title: Hierarchical context layer on top of Graphify — multi-project navigation with conversation indexing
body:
## Problem

Developers managing 10+ projects across multiple VPS servers hit a specific pain point that Graphify alone doesn't solve: **project-level navigation**. Graphify excels at code-level structure within a single project, but the agent still doesn't know *which* project to look at, where it's deployed, or what was discussed about it last week.

The result: every new session starts with the agent grepping the entire filesystem, SSHing into servers, and burning context before doing any real work.

## Solution: Hierarchical Context on top of Graphify

We built a three-level context hierarchy where Graphify serves as Level 1.5:

```
Level 0: Global Project Map     — 2KB, always loaded, lists all projects with paths
Level 1: Per-project CLAUDE.md  — 3-5KB, architecture + deployment + recent changes
Level 1.5: Graphify GRAPH_REPORT — code structure graph (your tool!)
Level 2: Source files            — only when needed
```

The agent navigates top-down: project map → project context → graph → specific file.

### What we added around Graphify

1. **Level 0 project map** in the agent's global instruction file — a table of all projects with local paths, VPS paths, and cross-project relationships. The agent reads this (~2KB) instead of grepping the disk.

2. **Conversation indexing** — a parser that converts Claude Code JSONL sessions and Claude Desktop exported chats into markdown with YAML frontmatter (date, project, topics, files touched). These become docs that Graphify can index, connecting conversations to code.

3. **VPS sync command** — pulls production code from remote servers to local mirrors, then runs `graphify --update` to keep the graph current.

4. **Graphify MCP for Claude Desktop** — added `graphify.serve` as an MCP server in Desktop config. Desktop automatically calls `query_graph` when asked about projects — no prompting needed.

## Test Results

Tested across Claude Code (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5) and Claude Desktop (Opus 4.7):

| Query | Without hierarchy | With hierarchy + Graphify |
|-------|------------------|--------------------------|
| "Architecture of Project A?" | 12 tool calls, reads 4+ files | 1 tool call (reads CLAUDE.md) |
| "Which projects use LiteLLM?" | 44 tool calls, missed 1 project | 2 tool calls, found all 3 |
| "Where is Project B deployed?" | 9 tool calls + SSH | 0 tool calls (answers from context) |
| Desktop: "Status of Project C?" | N/A | Auto-called `query_graph` twice, full answer |

The key finding isn't token savings — it's that **the agent stops being blind**. It knows where to look instead of searching everywhere.

## Working Code

Full implementation with templates, scripts, and multi-platform setup:
**https://github.com/CreatmanCEO/ai-context-hierarchy**

Includes:
- Level 0/1 templates for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI
- Claude Code JSONL session parser → markdown for Graphify indexing
- Claude Desktop export parser → markdown
- VPS sync command template

## What Graphify Could Do Natively

Some things that would make this pattern easier to adopt:

1. **Multi-project mode** — `graphify init --workspace` that creates a Level 0 index across sibling project directories, with per-project graphs linked together.

2. **Conversation ingestion** — accept Claude Code `.jsonl` files as a doc type in the detect/extract pipeline. The YAML frontmatter format (date, project, topics, files_touched) maps directly to graph nodes and edges.

3. **Remote source support** — `graphify add ssh://user@host:/path/` to index code living on remote servers without manual sync.

4. **Compact report mode** — a `--summary` flag that generates a 2-3KB executive summary instead of the full GRAPH_REPORT.md. For multi-project setups, the full report can be too large to load in context.

Happy to contribute PRs for any of these if there's interest.

## Setup (5 minutes)

```bash
# 1. Install graphify
pip install graphifyy

# 2. Clone the hierarchy templates
git clone https://github.com/CreatmanCEO/ai-context-hierarchy

# 3. Copy Level 0 template to your agent's global instructions
#    (customize with your projects)

# 4. Add CLAUDE.md to each project (Level 1)

# 5. Run graphify on each project (Level 1.5)
cd ~/project-a && /graphify .
cd ~/project-b && /graphify .
```

The agent now navigates your entire workspace without grepping blindly.

title: Add .mdx to DOC_EXTENSIONS for MDX-based static sites (Next.js, Docusaurus, Astro)
body:
## What

`graphifyy` (v0.4.21) hardcodes documentation file extensions to `{'.md', '.txt', '.rst'}`. As a result `.mdx` files are silently skipped during indexing, even when an entire docs/blog corpus is `.mdx`.

Looking at the relevant constant (best-guess based on observed behavior — let me know if I'm pointing at the wrong file):

```python
DOC_EXTENSIONS = {'.md', '.txt', '.rst'}
```

Adding `.mdx` would make the tool work cleanly for the large and growing population of MDX-driven static sites:

- **Next.js** content-collections / `app/blog/**/*.mdx`
- **Docusaurus** (`.mdx` is the default authoring format in v3+)
- **Astro** content collections
- **Gatsby** with `gatsby-plugin-mdx`
- **Storybook** docs (`*.stories.mdx`)

## Why it matters in practice

Real example: I'm running Graphify on a Next.js codebase with 67 blog posts, all `.mdx`. With the current extension set, **0 of 67** are indexed. The use case I was hoping to validate — semantic linking from blog content to backend code — can't even start.

MDX is structurally just Markdown with embedded JSX. The doc-extraction path should treat it the same as `.md`. The JSX components inside (`<Image />`, `<Callout />`, etc) can either be ignored or extracted as additional graph nodes, but baseline acceptance of the file extension would unblock most users.

## Suggested change

```python
DOC_EXTENSIONS = {'.md', '.mdx', '.txt', '.rst'}
```

If MDX needs special parsing logic to handle the JSX tags cleanly, a follow-up enhancement could parse them — but the conservative win is just accepting the extension and using the existing markdown parser; the JSX is already valid Markdown content from a text-extraction standpoint.

Happy to test against my codebase if a branch lands. Thanks for shipping the tool — the AST path on the engine repo (~800 nodes / 2K edges in 2.3s) was a clean install on Windows 11.

title: AST cache can still be written to nested src/graphify-out in 0.4.21
body:
### Summary

In `graphifyy 0.4.21`, the Codex skill flow for `/graphify .` can still create a nested cache directory when all code files live under `src/`:

```text
<project>/src/graphify-out/cache/
```

The final graph outputs are still written correctly to:

```text
<project>/graphify-out/
```

So this appears to affect AST/per-file cache placement only, not the main exported graph files.

### Environment

- Package: `graphifyy`
- Version: `0.4.21`
- Platform: Windows / PowerShell
- Invocation path: project root
- Project shape: Java/Spring-style repository with source files under `src/` and docs at the repo root

### Reproduction

Use the installed Codex skill flow for `/graphify .` on a repository where all code files share `src` as their common path prefix.

The relevant AST step in the installed Codex skill currently calls:

```python
result = extract(code_files)
```

With code files shaped like:

```text
src/main/java/...
src/main/resources/...
src/test/java/...
```

### Actual behavior

After the graph run, both directories exist:

```text
<project>/graphify-out/
<project>/src/graphify-out/cache/
```

The nested directory only contains AST cache files. In the observed run, the cache files under `<project>/src/graphify-out/cache/` corresponded to the code files under `src/`.

### Expected behavior

All graphify-generated outputs and caches should stay under:

```text
<project>/graphify-out/
```

The run should not create:

```text
<project>/src/graphify-out/
```

### Likely cause

`graphify.extract.extract()` infers a common root from the input paths when `cache_root` is not provided. If all code files are under `src/`, that inferred common root becomes `src`, so `save_cached()` writes AST cache files under:

```text
src/graphify-out/cache/
```

The `extract()` docstring already notes that callers should pass `cache_root=Path(".")` when running on a subdirectory so the cache stays at `./graphify-out/cache/`.

However, at least these call sites still appear to call `extract(code_files)` without an explicit `cache_root`:

- installed Codex skill AST extraction step
- `graphify.watch._rebuild_code()`, used by `graphify update .` / watch-style rebuilds

### Suggested fix

Either:

1. Pass an explicit project/output root at call sites:

```python
result = extract(code_files, cache_root=Path("."))
```

or:

2. Change `extract()` so its default cache output root is the invocation/output root, not the inferred common prefix of the input files.

This would avoid nested `graphify-out` directories in common repository layouts where all code is under `src/`.

title: fix(watch): rebuild continues when HTML viz exceeds MAX_NODES_FOR_VIZ
body:
Problem: _rebuild_code calls to_html() unconditionally, which raises ValueError for graphs exceeding MAX_NODES_FOR_VIZ (5000). The entire rebuild fails and returns False, even though AST extraction, clustering, and report generation all succeeded. Users with medium-to-large codebases can't use _rebuild_code at all; no graph.json / GRAPH_REPORT.md is produced.

Real-world impact: In a Presto Go monorepo (~1000 files), _rebuild_code reliably produces 5574 nodes (above 5000). This made the git post-commit hook a no-op: every code change raised the HTML-viz error, graph.json never got written, AI tools read 9-day-old stale data.

Fix: Wrap to_html() in its own try/except. When it raises:
1. Log a warning (don't fail the rebuild)
2. Delete stale graph.html from prev smaller run
3. Continue returning True - core products (graph.json + GRAPH_REPORT.md) are already written

Tests: Added tests/test_watch_rebuild_large_graph.py with 2 tests. All existing tests pass.

Alternative considered: --no-viz parameter; rejected because it requires callers (post-commit hook, CI) to know the threshold. Caller-agnostic fix is cleaner.

title: graphify update writes absolute paths into generated artifacts
body:
## Summary

`graphify update .` currently serializes absolute filesystem paths into the generated artifacts for code-only rebuilds.

The regression is specific to the `update` / `watch` rebuild path. Running the full `/graphify` workflow on a relative path still produces project-relative `source_file` values, but `graphify update .` does not.

## Affected outputs

- `graphify-out/graph.json` node and edge `source_file` fields
- `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` report title and any path-bearing sections
- `graphify-out/graph.html` title and node metadata
- `graphify-out/cache/*.json` AST cache entries

## Reproduction

1. Create a small repo with `pkg/a.py`.
2. From the repo root, run `graphify update .`.
3. Inspect `graphify-out/graph.json` or `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md`.

## Actual behavior

Generated outputs contain absolute paths such as:

- `/Users/alice/project/pkg/a.py`
- `# Graph Report - /Users/alice/project (...)`

This makes committed graph artifacts machine-specific and leaks local filesystem layout into reports, HTML, and cache files.

## Expected behavior

`graphify update .` should preserve project-relative paths, matching the rest of the pipeline:

- `pkg/a.py` in `source_file`
- a non-absolute report title for the project root
- no absolute project paths in `graphify-out/cache/*.json`

## Root cause

`graphify.watch._rebuild_code()` resolves the input path before running detection and report generation:

- `watch_path = watch_path.resolve()`
- `detect(watch_path, ...)` therefore returns absolute file paths
- the AST extractors serialize those absolute paths directly into `source_file`
- `report.generate(..., str(watch_path), ...)` also receives an absolute root label

## Scope

This issue is about path serialization only. The large-graph HTML failure path was already handled separately in `v0.4.23`.

title: fix(watch): keep update outputs project-relative
body:
## Summary

Fixes #433.

`graphify update` should keep generated paths project-relative for code-only rebuilds, matching the rest of the pipeline.

## Root cause

`graphify.watch._rebuild_code()` resolved the requested path before detection and report generation. That changed a relative invocation such as `graphify update .` into an absolute rebuild root, which then leaked absolute paths into:

- `graphify-out/graph.json` `source_file` fields
- `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` title and path-bearing sections
- `graphify-out/graph.html` title and node metadata
- `graphify-out/cache/*.json` AST cache entries

## What changed

- keep the cache root absolute, but run detection against the user-provided path so extractor inputs stay project-relative for normal `graphify update .` usage
- normalize merged rebuild payloads back to project-relative `source_file` values before report/JSON/HTML export
- render a non-absolute report root label for the common `.` case
- add watch rebuild regression tests for repo-root and subdirectory invocations

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_watch.py`
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_pipeline.py`
- manual smoke test: `.venv/bin/python -m graphify update .` in a temporary repo, verifying no absolute project paths in `graph.json`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, `graph.html`, or `graphify-out/cache/*.json`

title: Feature Request: Add Java Inheritance Relationship Support in Tree-sitter Parsing
body:
## Feature Request: Java-specific Inheritance support while treesitter parsing.

### Description

Currently, the tool supports extracting method call relationships for Java code. However, inheritance relationships (e.g., extends, implements) are not captured, which limits the completeness of the code graph for Java projects.

In contrast, inheritance relationships are already supported for other languages such as Python and C#.

### Problem Statement

When parsing Java code, the absence of inheritance edges leads to:

- Incomplete dependency graphs
- Reduced accuracy in code understanding and analysis
- Inconsistency across language support


### Expected Behavior
The parser should:

- Detect extends relationships between classes
- Detect implements relationships for interfaces
- Add corresponding edges in the extracted graph
- 
### Suggested Approach
Enhance Tree-sitter Java parsing logic to capture:
- class_declaration → superclass
- class_declaration → interfaces
Map these to inheritance edges similar to existing implementations in Python and C#

Optionally distinguish edge types:
- INHERITS_FROM
- IMPLEMENTS

title: _is_sensitive false-positives on directory names containing "secret"/"token"/"password" as substrings
body:
## Summary                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                      
  `graphify.detect._is_sensitive()` uses substring matching on the generic secrets pattern, causing false positives on any file path that contains    
  `secret`, `token`, `password`, `credential`, `passwd`, or `private_key` as a **substring** of a larger word. This silently drops legitimate source
  files from the graph with no warning to the user.                                                                                                   
                                                   
  ## Version                                                                                                                                          
            
  graphify 0.4.23 (graphifyy on PyPI), macOS 26.4, Python 3.13                                                                                        
                                                              
  ## Concrete failure case                     
                          
  My repo is named `daniel-ai-secretary` and contains an `AISecretary/` directory. Every file path through those directories matches `(secret)` inside
   "**secret**ary".                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                      
  Result on my repo:
  - Without workaround: `graphify update .` reports `0 code files found` and fails                                                                    
  - With `Path('.')` workaround: build succeeds but **7,023 nodes from `AISecretary/` are silently missing** because per-file checks still flag
  `AISecretary/Services/Foo.swift` as sensitive                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                      
  Other plausibly-affected names: any repo/dir containing `tokenizer`, `tokenize`, `password_manager`, `credentials_ui`, `secretariat`, `tokenized_*`,
   etc.                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                      
  ## Root cause                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                      
  `detect.py` line 36:                         
                                                                                                                                                      
  ```python                  
  re.compile(r'(credential|secret|passwd|password|token|private_key)', re.IGNORECASE),
                                                                                                                                                      
  No word boundaries. Matches secret inside Secretary, token inside tokenizer, password inside password_manager (the last is probably desired — but
  the substring match also catches safe collisions).                                                                                                  
                             
  Proposed fix                                 
                                                                                                                                                      
  Add \b word boundaries to that single pattern:
                                                                                                                                                      
  re.compile(r'\b(credential|secret|passwd|password|token|private_key)\b', re.IGNORECASE),
                                                                                                                                                      
  The other _SENSITIVE_PATTERNS entries (dotfiles, key extensions, id_rsa family, etc.) already have sufficient specificity and don't need changes.
                                                                                                                                                      
  Additional observations
                                                                                                                                                      
  1. When files are skipped as sensitive, the user isn't warned unless they inspect detected['skipped_sensitive'] in the dict. A repo with thousands
  of skipped files produces a silently-incomplete graph.                                                                                              
  2. _is_sensitive is called on the full path string (full = str(path)), so even using Path('.') as root doesn't fully help — per-file paths still
  contain the offending substrings. My project's workaround is a runtime monkey-patch of _SENSITIVE_PATTERNS[2], which isn't persistable.             
  3. Consider surfacing the skipped count at build-time when >N% of discovered files are dropped (e.g., WARNING: 84% of discovered files skipped as 
  sensitive — check patterns).                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                      
  Workaround for others hitting this           
                                                                                                                                                      
  import re, graphify.detect
  graphify.detect._SENSITIVE_PATTERNS[2] = re.compile(                                                                                                
      r'\b(credential|secret|passwd|password|token|private_key)\b',
      re.IGNORECASE                                                                                                                                   
  )

title: Node ID collisions when multiple files share the same stem (e.g. Program.cs)
body:
## Problem

`_make_id(stem, name)` uses only the file stem to generate node IDs. When a project has multiple files with the same name in different directories (e.g. `src/App1/Program.cs` and `src/App2/Program.cs`), their nodes collide — methods from both files merge into a single node, producing an incorrect graph.

This is common in .NET solutions where each project has its own `Program.cs`, `Startup.cs`, `AssemblyInfo.cs`, etc.

## Proposed Fix

Add a post-extraction pass that detects colliding node IDs (multiple nodes from different `source_file` paths sharing the same ID) and disambiguates them by prepending the parent directory name.

For example:
- `program_program` → `app1_program_program` and `app2_program_program`

## Impact

Tested on a .NET solution with 2 `Program.cs` files — nodes are now correctly separated.

I have a PR ready.

title: Stub nodes break cross-language inheritance edges
body:
## Problem

When C# code inherits from a type defined in another language (e.g. F#), the C# extractor creates a stub node with no `source_file` because it can't resolve the base type. The `inherits` edge points to this stub instead of the real definition node.

For example, `class SqliteBookStore : BookStore` creates a stub `bookstore` node, while the actual F# abstract class is `interfaces_bookstore` (from `Interfaces.fs`). The inheritance edge connects to the wrong node, breaking cross-language graph connectivity.

## Proposed Fix

Add a post-extraction pass that:
1. Identifies stub nodes (no `source_file`) that have a matching real definition (by label match)
2. Prioritizes definition files (`Interfaces.fs`, `Domain.fs`, `Types.fs`, `Contracts.fs`, `Abstractions.fs`)
3. Redirects all edges from the stub to the real definition node
4. Removes the stub

## Impact

Tested on a mixed F#/C# project — all `inherits` edges now point to real definitions instead of stubs. Cross-language graph connectivity significantly improved.

I have a PR ready.

title: fix: add BCL method blocklist to cross-file inference
body:
Fixes #437

## Summary

Adds a blocklist of ~120 common .NET BCL/framework method names (`Contains`, `Equals`, `ToString`, `Where`, `Select`, `Add`, `Remove`, `AddDbContext`, `AddSingleton`, `LogInformation`, etc.) that are skipped during cross-file call resolution.

Without this, the cross-file inference creates hundreds of false `INFERRED` edges because common method names match unintended nodes — e.g. `string.Contains()` matches an F# union case `EdgeRelation.Contains`.

## Impact

Tested on a mixed F#/C#/Blazor project (141 code files):
- False INFERRED edges: 538 → 362
- Top hub: `Contains` (false positive) → `BookService` (correct)

The blocklist follows the same pattern as the existing `_SKIP_LABELS` set but targets method names. It's conservative — only blocks names that are extremely common across .NET codebases and almost never represent meaningful cross-file relationships.

title: fix: disambiguate colliding node IDs from same-name files
body:
Fixes #438

## Summary

Adds a post-extraction pass that detects and resolves node ID collisions caused by files sharing the same stem (e.g. `Program.cs` in multiple directories).

`_make_id(stem, name)` uses only the filename stem, so `src/App1/Program.cs` and `src/App2/Program.cs` both produce `program_program`. This causes their methods and type nodes to silently merge into a single node.

The fix detects these collisions by grouping nodes by ID and checking if they come from different `source_file` paths. When a collision is found, all affected nodes are renamed by prepending the parent directory name (e.g. `app1_program_program` and `app2_program_program`).

## Impact

Common in .NET solutions where each project has its own `Program.cs`, `Startup.cs`, `AssemblyInfo.cs`, etc. Also affects any multi-module project with naming conventions that produce duplicate file stems.

title: fix: merge stub nodes with real cross-language definitions
body:
Fixes #439

## Summary

Adds a post-extraction pass that merges stub nodes (nodes with no `source_file`, created by the generic extractor for unresolved type references) with their actual definitions from other files.

When C# code inherits from a type defined in F# (e.g. `class SqliteBookStore : BookStore`), the C# extractor creates a stub node `bookstore` because it can't resolve the base type. Meanwhile, the F# extractor creates the real node `interfaces_bookstore` from `Interfaces.fs`. The `inherits` edge incorrectly points to the stub instead of the real definition.

The fix:
1. Finds stub nodes (no `source_file`) that have a matching real definition (by label match)
2. Prioritizes definition files (`Interfaces.fs`, `Domain.fs`, `Types.fs`, `Contracts.fs`, `Abstractions.fs`)
3. Redirects all edges from the stub to the real definition
4. Removes the stub node

## Impact

Tested on a mixed F#/C# project — all cross-language `inherits` edges now point to real definitions. This is particularly important for mixed-language codebases where interfaces/abstract types are defined in one language and implemented in another.

## Test Plan

- [x] Verified on a mixed F#/C# project with 8 cross-language inheritance relationships
- [x] All `inherits` edges now correctly point to real definitions

title: fix(cache): skip non-file source_file in save_semantic_cache
body:
## Summary

`save_semantic_cache` aborts a whole batch with `IsADirectoryError` when a subagent emits a node whose `source_file` happens to be a directory path instead of a file. Observed on a TS/NestJS corpus where a subagent attributed an abstract base to `src/common/database/abstracts/mongo/repositories` (the containing folder). `save_cached → file_hash → read_bytes` then crashes, so every other file in the batch fails to cache too.

This PR makes the save path tolerant:
- `save_cached(path, ...)` now no-ops when `path` is not a regular file.
- `save_semantic_cache(...)` uses `p.is_file()` instead of `p.exists()` so directories are silently skipped.

Real files in the same batch cache normally; the bogus entry is just dropped.

## Changes

- `graphify/cache.py` — 2 small defensive checks, docstring explaining the case.
- `tests/test_cache.py` — 3 new tests:
  - `test_save_cached_noop_on_directory`
  - `test_save_semantic_cache_skips_directory_source_file` (mixed batch: real file + directory)
  - `test_save_semantic_cache_skips_missing_file`

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_cache.py` — 15/15 pass (12 existing + 3 new)
- [x] Reproduced original bug on a 288-file NestJS corpus (22-file chunk aborted mid-save)
- [x] Verified patched version caches all files in the same corpus

title: Query seed-node selection matches image/doc captions, dominating BFS start for cross-cutting code queries
body:
## Context
On a mixed-media corpus (410 files: 297 code, 54 doc, 59 image), a cross-cutting query — *"which modules mutate `seg_result.planes` and in what call order"* — returned a 28-node subgraph in which the three seed nodes were all `*.png` golden-test renders whose captions happened to include both the strings "planes" and the project slug. The 15 actual mutation sites (across `rg_primary_segmentation.py`, `pipeline_core.py`, `pipeline.py`) were never surfaced.

## Repro
1. Build a graph on any corpus that includes test-fixture images with descriptive captions ("Territory render for 41 Shakespeare Ave, Hamilton — 7 planes, 8 ridges", etc.).
2. `/graphify query "modules mutating seg_result.planes call order"`
3. BFS seeds are picked by `sum(1 for t in terms if t in label)` in the skill's template — image nodes win because their summary-style labels contain multiple query terms.

## Root cause
Seed selection in `/graphify query` / `SKILL.md` is pure substring match on `label`. No weighting by `file_type`, degree, or confidence. Image nodes with rich summary labels out-score precise code nodes whose labels are just a symbol name.

## Expected
- For queries that reference code-centric concepts, seeds should prefer `file_type=code` nodes.
- Tie-breakers: node degree, connection to multiple communities, `confidence=EXTRACTED` on incoming edges.

## Proposed fix
Weight the seed score in the skill query template:

```python
def seed_score(nid, ndata):
    term_hits = sum(1 for t in terms if t in ndata.get('label','').lower())
    ft = ndata.get('file_type','')
    type_weight = {'code': 1.0, 'document': 0.7, 'paper': 0.7, 'image': 0.4}.get(ft, 0.5)
    degree_weight = min(G.degree(nid) / 20, 1.0)
    return term_hits * type_weight * (0.5 + 0.5 * degree_weight)
```

Optional: expose `--prefer-type code|doc|image` on the query command.

## Impact
Cross-cutting code queries — exactly the queries graphify markets as its strength over grep — currently underperform grep+synthesize subagents in a side-by-side A/B because of this seed-selection issue.

title: Leiden clustering on code-heavy graphs produces low-cohesion fragmentation (274 communities, cohesion 0.01)
body:
## Context
Building on a Python analysis-engine corpus (297 code files, 54 docs, 59 images → 8333 nodes, 19086 edges), Leiden community detection returned 274 communities. The top-10 communities (~4400 nodes total) all reported cohesion between 0.010 and 0.020 — i.e., most communities have edge density barely above random.

## Why this matters
- The skill's `GRAPH_REPORT.md` surfaces communities + god nodes as the primary navigation layer.
- When cohesion is ~0.01 across the top communities, the resulting labels are too broad to be useful ("Core Services & Viewer" holds 705 heterogeneous nodes).
- Downstream: community-labelled wiki articles become dumping grounds, not focused references.

## Root cause (hypothesis)
Code graphs are leaf-heavy: docstring summaries, helper functions, and per-file `__init__` nodes all attach to a small number of hubs with degree=1. Leiden's modularity score collapses because these leaves don't contribute to within-community density.

## Proposed fix
1. **Prune degree-1 leaves** before clustering, attach them back post-cluster to their single neighbour's community.
2. **Tune resolution parameter** — default Leiden resolution appears to be 1.0; for code graphs of 5K+ nodes, bumping to 1.5–2.0 yields fewer, denser communities in practice.
3. **Post-cluster merge step**: merge any community smaller than `N` nodes (e.g., 10) into its most-connected neighbour.
4. Optional: expose `--cluster-resolution` flag.

## Repro data
- Nodes: 8333, Edges: 19086
- Communities: 274 (avg 30 nodes)
- Top-10 community sizes: 705, 510, 506, 498, 478, 422, 342, 311, 292, 292
- Top-10 cohesion: all between 0.010 and 0.020

Happy to share a sanitized `graph.json` if useful.

title: HTML viz hard-refuses at >5000 nodes without WebGL fallback or aggregated view
body:
## Context
On an 8333-node graph, the skill pipeline prints:

```
Graph has 8333 nodes - too large for HTML viz. Use Obsidian vault instead.
```

and skips `graph.html` generation entirely. No fallback is offered beyond Obsidian (which requires a separate app) or the markdown wiki.

## Why this matters
The wiki is useful but is agent-oriented; for human exploration the interactive HTML graph is the primary artefact. Hitting the 5K ceiling on a mid-sized codebase (≤500 files) means visualisation is unavailable in exactly the situation where a knowledge graph is most valuable.

## Root cause
The ceiling appears to be hard-coded against vis.js DOM performance:

```python
if G.number_of_nodes() > 5000:
    print(f'Graph has {G.number_of_nodes()} nodes - too large for HTML viz.')
```

vis.js degrades past ~3–5K DOM nodes. But this is a renderer choice, not an inherent graph limit.

## Proposed fixes
Ranked by effort:

1. **Aggregated view** (cheapest): when above ceiling, emit an HTML that collapses each community to a meta-node, edges weighted by inter-community edge count. Click to expand into member nodes. Keeps vis.js.
2. **WebGL renderer option**: sigma.js or Cosmograph handle 50K+ nodes at 60fps. Ship as `--renderer webgl` flag.
3. **Explicit override**: `--force-html` for users who accept slow render.

Even #1 alone (aggregated view as default above ceiling) would eliminate the "no viz" outcome for mid-sized graphs.

## Repro
- 410 files → 8333 nodes → HTML refused.
- 5K ceiling is approximately 250-300 mid-complexity Python files.

title: save_semantic_cache crashes with IsADirectoryError when a node's source_file points at a directory
body:
## Context
During Step 3 Part C merge, `save_semantic_cache` aborted with:

```
File ".../graphify/cache.py", line 31, in file_hash
    raw = p.read_bytes()
  ...
IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: 'analysis-engine/data/quote_validation/sp_images'
```

The subagent that produced the offending chunk had written a node with `source_file = 'analysis-engine/data/quote_validation/sp_images'` (a directory, not a file). `file_hash` then tried to `read_bytes()` it.

## Impact
Semantic cache save failed → on re-run, all 410 files would be re-extracted rather than hitting cache. For large corpora this doubles the API cost of any update.

## Proposed fix (one-liner in `cache.py::file_hash`)

```python
def file_hash(p: Path, root: Path) -> str:
    if not p.is_file():   # new guard
        return ''         # or raise a catchable warning
    raw = p.read_bytes()
    ...
```

Alternatively, have `save_cached` skip paths that fail `is_file()` with a warning.

## Secondary consideration
The upstream reason is that a semantic-extraction subagent sometimes returns a directory string in `source_file` — prompt clarity could also be tightened. But defence-in-depth at the cache layer is the robust fix.

## Repro
Any corpus where a semantic subagent labels a group of images collectively with the containing directory as `source_file`. Triggered reliably on a corpus with multiple directories of example images.

title: Semantic subagent node labels are free-form summaries, poisoning label-based term matching
body:
## Context
The skill's extraction prompt allows semantic subagents to produce long summary-style labels, e.g.:

> *"Dataclass types for the DeepRoofPlane segmentation pipeline. Extracted from poi"*
> *"LiDAR point cloud segmentation result: 4 planes (P0-P4 labels), 0 ridges detecte"*

These summary labels then flood BFS seed selection because the query code ranks seeds by substring match against `label`:

```python
score = sum(1 for t in terms if t in ndata.get('label','').lower())
```

A 200-char summary label has dozens of token matches by accident. The AST pass, by contrast, produces stable symbol-name labels (`session_validatetoken`) that act as precise anchors.

## Related to #F1 (seed selection)
F1 fixes seed scoring; this issue fixes the underlying data so scoring has good raw material.

## Proposed fix
Split label vs. summary in the extraction schema:

```json
{
  "id": "session_validatetoken",
  "label": "ValidateToken",            // short symbol or canonical name
  "summary": "Dataclass types for ...", // verbose description (optional)
  "file_type": "code",
  ...
}
```

Update the extraction prompt:

> `label` is the short canonical name (function name, class name, concept noun phrase — max 6 words). Use the verbose description for `summary`, not `label`.

Downstream:
- Community labeler uses `label` for word-frequency aggregation (currently skewed by summary words).
- Query seed scoring uses `label` (precise) rather than `summary` (noisy).
- Wiki rendering shows `label` as heading, `summary` as preamble.

## Impact
Measured: on an 8333-node graph, the top-3 BFS seeds for every semantic query were summary-style nodes from the same 20 files. Precise symbol-name AST nodes were crowded out.

title: Per-image chunk rule forces one subagent per image — 59 images ≈ 59 agents, each ~28K tokens for ~5 nodes output
body:
## Context
Skill says:

> Split into chunks of 20-25 files each. **Each image gets its own chunk (vision needs separate context).**

On a 410-file corpus with 59 images, this produces 59 image chunks + 16 non-image chunks = **75 total subagents**. Measured token cost per image chunk: ~28-30K total tokens (system + instructions + single image + output), yielding ~4-7 nodes each.

## Why this is wasteful
Vision models handle multiple images per request fine, up to the model's image-count cap. The per-chunk instruction payload (~2K tokens from the shared instructions file + tool-call boilerplate) is paid 59 times instead of ~10. Back-of-envelope: batching 6 images per chunk would cut image-chunk overhead from 59 × 30K = 1.77M tokens to 10 × (2K instructions + 6 × ~3K per image + output) ≈ 210K tokens. ~8× reduction for the image pass.

## Proposed fix
Change the rule to:

> Split non-image files into chunks of 20-25 files each. Split images into chunks of 4-6 images each (shared instruction context; separate image inputs within the chunk).

Plus: document in the subagent prompt that the output JSON must include one `source_file` per image, so multi-image chunks still produce per-image nodes correctly.

## Secondary observation
Image-chunk output was fairly thin across this test (average 5 nodes + 5 edges per image). If that's representative, an even more aggressive batch (8-10 images per chunk) would be fine given context-window headroom.

## Measurement
- 59 image chunks × ~28K tokens each = ~1.65M tokens for images alone
- Output produced: ~310 nodes, ~300 edges, 59 hyperedges
- Per-image avg duration: 33s
- Implied cost per node from the image pass: ~5K tokens/node

A batched version would trade that for ~600 tokens/node — in line with the non-image chunks.

title: Duplicate nodes from parallel semantic subagents — IDs diverge across chunks
body:
## Summary

When running graphify on a multi-file corpus, parallel semantic subagents produce duplicate nodes for the same real-world entity. The three-layer deduplication system documented in `build.py` does not catch these because the duplicates have **different IDs** — deduplication is ID-keyed, and the LLM generates IDs freely per chunk.

## Root cause

`_make_id()` in `extract.py` produces stable, normalised IDs for AST extraction. Semantic subagents, however, generate their own IDs in free-form JSON. When the same entity is mentioned in two source files processed by different subagent chunks, the resulting IDs diverge:

| Entity label | IDs found in graph.json |
|---|---|
| `Quadrifoglio Verde (Four-Leaf Clover Emblem)` | `quadrifoglio_verde`, `quadrifoglio_verde_c2` |
| `Achille Varzi` | `achille_varzi`, `achille_varzi_c4` |
| `Ugo Gobbato` | `ugo_gobbato`, `ugo_gobbato_c2`, `ugo_gobbato_c4` |
| `1935 German Grand Prix` | `german_grand_prix_1935`, `german_gp_1935_c4` |
| `Alfa Romeo Giulia GTA` | `alfa_romeo_giulia_gta`, `alfa_romeo_giulia_1962_gta` |

Two patterns emerge:

1. **Chunk-suffix contamination** — subagents append their chunk number to the ID (e.g. `_c2`, `_c4`). This suggests the chunk index leaks into the LLM context and the model incorporates it into generated IDs.
2. **Label abbreviation variance** — different subagents independently abbreviate the same label differently (`german_grand_prix_1935` vs `german_gp_1935_c4`), which `_make_id()`-style normalisation would still diverge on if the label itself differs.

## Impact

Each duplicate node produces a separate Obsidian wiki page (e.g. `Achille Varzi.md` and `Achille Varzi_1.md`). In a 83-file corpus this produced **41 `_N`-suffixed duplicate pages** (out of 206 total nodes — ~20% duplication rate). Wikilinks in the vault point to both variants, creating broken or split graph navigation.

## Reproduction

Run graphify on any corpus where the same named entity (person, car model, organisation) appears across more than one source file, using more than one semantic subagent chunk. Check `graph.json` for nodes with identical `label` but different `id`.

```python
import json
from collections import defaultdict

g = json.loads(open("graphify-out/graph.json").read())
by_label = defaultdict(list)
for n in g["nodes"]:
    by_label[n["label"]].append(n["id"])
dupes = {k: v for k, v in by_label.items() if len(v) > 1}
print(dupes)
```

## Proposed fix

### Option A — Post-merge label deduplication in `build.py` (minimal change)

After collecting all semantic nodes, before calling `build_from_json()`, apply a label-normalisation pass:

```python
def _normalise_label(label: str) -> str:
    """Canonical key for deduplication — lowercase, punctuation stripped."""
    import re
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]", "", label.lower()).strip()

def deduplicate_by_label(nodes: list[dict], edges: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
    """
    Merge nodes that share a normalised label. Keep the node whose ID has no
    chunk suffix (no _c\\d+ pattern) and is shortest. Rewrite all edge
    source/target references to the surviving ID.
    """
    import re
    canonical: dict[str, dict] = {}   # norm_label -> surviving node
    remap: dict[str, str] = {}        # old_id -> surviving_id

    for node in nodes:
        key = _normalise_label(node["label"])
        existing = canonical.get(key)
        if existing is None:
            canonical[key] = node
        else:
            # Prefer the ID without a chunk suffix
            has_suffix = bool(re.search(r"_c\d+$", node["id"]))
            existing_has_suffix = bool(re.search(r"_c\d+$", existing["id"]))
            if has_suffix and not existing_has_suffix:
                remap[node["id"]] = existing["id"]
            elif existing_has_suffix and not has_suffix:
                remap[existing["id"]] = node["id"]
                canonical[key] = node
            else:
                # Both or neither have suffix — keep shorter ID
                if len(node["id"]) < len(existing["id"]):
                    remap[existing["id"]] = node["id"]
                    canonical[key] = node
                else:
                    remap[node["id"]] = existing["id"]

    deduped_nodes = list(canonical.values())
    deduped_edges = []
    for edge in edges:
        e = dict(edge)
        e["source"] = remap.get(e["source"], e["source"])
        e["target"] = remap.get(e["target"], e["target"])
        if e["source"] != e["target"]:  # drop self-loops created by merge
            deduped_edges.append(e)
    return deduped_nodes, deduped_edges
```

Call this in Part C of the skill merge step, before writing `.graphify_extract.json`.

### Option B — Fix subagent ID generation prompt (prevents the problem at source)

In the subagent prompt, add an explicit instruction:

```
Node IDs MUST be generated using this exact rule:
  id = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", label.lower()).strip("_")
Do NOT append chunk numbers, sequence numbers, or any suffix to the ID.
The ID must be deterministic from the label alone so the same entity
always produces the same ID regardless of which chunk processes it.
```

Option B prevents the `_c2`/`_c4` contamination entirely. Option A catches both contamination and abbreviation variance as a safety net. Both together would be robust.

## Environment

- graphifyy version: 0.3.6
- Corpus: 83 markdown files, ~30K words, 6 semantic subagent chunks
- Result: 191 nodes, 41 duplicate `_N` files in Obsidian vault output

title: sanitize_label crashes when node source_file is None (export.py:392)
body:
## Summary

`graphify/export.py:392` calls `sanitize_label(data.get("source_file", ""))`. When a node's `source_file` attribute is explicitly set to `None` (rather than the key being absent), `dict.get` returns `None` and `sanitize_label` raises `TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got NoneType`.

This happens in practice with concept nodes lifted from code AST — they carry an explicit `source_file=None` rather than omitting the key.

## Repro

```
graphify <any code repo> --directed
```

Fails during the vis-network HTML build step.

## Stack shape

```
File ".../graphify/export.py", line 392, in <listcomp>
    "source_file": sanitize_label(data.get("source_file", "")),
File ".../graphify/security.py", line ...
TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got NoneType
```

## One-line fix

Swap the `dict.get` default for an `or ""` fallback so both the missing-key and explicit-None cases are handled:

```python
"source_file": sanitize_label(data.get("source_file") or ""),
```

Same pattern applies at `export.py:548` and `export.py:642` where `data.get("source_file", "")` is used — they don't currently crash because the result is only string-concatenated, but will surface as `"None"` in output.

## Local workaround

Currently patched client-side via a SKILL.md override in my Claude Code harness (walks G.nodes and rewrites None source_file/label/file_type to empty strings before calling to_html).

title: file_hash crashes with IsADirectoryError when source_file points to a directory (cache.py:27)
body:
## Summary

`graphify/cache.py:27` inside `file_hash()` calls `p.read_bytes()`, which raises `IsADirectoryError` if `p` is a directory. This triggers during `save_semantic_cache` when a node's `source_file` attribute accidentally holds a directory path (e.g. module-level nodes in Python packages where the "source" is the package dir, not a specific `.py`).

## Repro

```
graphify <python-package-with-__init__.py> --directed
```

Cache save step crashes:

```
IsADirectoryError: [Errno 21] Is a directory: '/some/package/dir'
```

## Current code

```python
def file_hash(path: Path) -> str:
    p = Path(path)
    raw = p.read_bytes()    # line 27 — blows up on directories
    content = _body_content(raw) if p.suffix.lower() == ".md" else raw
    ...
```

## One-line fix

Guard with `is_file()` before reading:

```python
def file_hash(path: Path) -> str:
    p = Path(path)
    if not p.is_file():
        return ""   # skip sentinel; save_semantic_cache can filter out empty hashes
    raw = p.read_bytes()
    ...
```

Callers (e.g. `save_semantic_cache`) should treat the empty string as "skip, don't cache this entry" rather than hashing a non-file.

## Local workaround

Client-side filter in the SKILL.md dispatch that drops nodes/edges/hyperedges where `source_file` isn't a regular file before calling `save_semantic_cache` — verified on a recent `.claude/skills/` run (169 files cached with 0 drops when all source_files resolved to real files).

Companion issue: #454 (sanitize_label None crash in export.py) — same pattern of None/non-file source_file tripping downstream code.

title: feat: incremental graph updates, git diff mode, community auto-naming, smarter god nodes
body:
## What this PR does

Four targeted improvements to graph quality, usability, and performance — each self-contained in its own module.

---

## 1. Incremental Graph Updates (`build.py: patch_graph()`)

**Problem:** Every run rebuilds the entire graph from scratch, even when only one file changed. On large corpora this is wasteful — watch mode and git hooks re-extract all files even if 99% of them are unchanged.

**Fix:** New `patch_graph(G, stale_files, new_extractions)` function:
- Removes only the nodes and edges whose `source_file` is in `stale_files`
- Merges new extractions for those files into the existing graph in-place
- Unchanged files' nodes/edges remain untouched — zero re-extraction cost

```python
from graphify.build import patch_graph

# Only re-process the 2 files that changed
G = patch_graph(G, stale_files={"src/auth.py", "src/models.py"}, new_extractions=[...])
```

---

## 2. Smarter God Node Detection (`analyze.py: god_nodes()`)

**Problem:** `god_nodes()` ranked by raw degree, so a `utils.py` that gets imported everywhere would dominate — even though `import` edges carry no architectural meaning.

**Fix:** Weighted degree by relation type:

| Edge type | Weight |
|-----------|--------|
| `calls`, `inherits`, `implements` | 3× |
| `references`, `uses`, `shares_data_with` | 2× |
| `conceptually_related_to`, `semantically_similar_to`, `cites` | 1× |
| `imports`, `imports_from`, `contains`, `method` | 0 (excluded) |

This surfaces genuine coupling hubs. Each result now includes a `weighted_degree` field alongside `degree` for transparency.

---

## 3. Community Auto-Naming (`cluster.py: name_communities()`)

**Problem:** Communities were always named `"Community 0"`, `"Community 1"`, etc. — meaningless in the report and visualiser until the skill's LLM labelling step ran.

**Fix:** New `name_communities(G, communities)` heuristic (no LLM, no API cost):
1. Picks top 6 nodes per community by weighted degree
2. Tokenises their labels (camelCase → words, snake_case → words)
3. Filters stop words, picks top 1-2 most frequent meaningful terms
4. Returns readable names like `"Auth Pipeline"`, `"Data Loading"`, `"Model Training"`

The `cluster-only` CLI command now uses this automatically instead of generic placeholders. The skill can still refine labels in Step 5, but the initial report and HTML are immediately readable.

---

## 4. Git Diff Mode (`__main__.py: graphify diff`)

**Problem:** No way to see what changed in the *graph* between commits — only raw file diffs. This makes the graph useless during code review.

**Fix:** New `graphify diff [ref]` command:

```bash
graphify diff           # compare graph vs HEAD~1
graphify diff main      # compare graph vs main branch
graphify diff abc1234   # compare graph vs specific commit
graphify diff HEAD~3 --graph path/to/graph.json
```

How it works:
1. `git diff --name-only <ref>` identifies changed code files
2. `git show <ref>:<path>` retrieves old file content into temp files
3. AST-extracts old and new versions
4. Builds an "old" graph snapshot by replacing changed nodes/edges in the current graph
5. Calls existing `graph_diff()` and reports added/removed nodes and relationships

Example output:
```
Graph diff vs HEAD~1: 3 new nodes, 5 new edges, 1 node removed
Files inspected: src/auth.py, src/session.py

New nodes (3):
  + TokenRefreshHandler
  + SessionStore
  + validate_expiry

New relationships (5):
  + TokenRefreshHandler --calls--> SessionStore
  + validate_expiry --uses--> TokenStore
  ...
```

---

## Test plan

- [ ] `from graphify.build import patch_graph` — imports cleanly
- [ ] `from graphify.cluster import name_communities` — imports cleanly
- [ ] `from graphify.analyze import god_nodes, _EDGE_WEIGHTS` — imports cleanly
- [ ] `graphify cluster-only <path>` — communities now show human-readable names
- [ ] `graphify diff HEAD~1` — runs in a git repo with an existing `graphify-out/graph.json`
- [ ] `graphify diff` on a repo with no code changes — prints "No files changed" and exits cleanly
- [ ] Existing tests pass — no regressions to `build`, `cluster`, `analyze` interfaces

title: feat: add LSP/static analysis enhancement for complete call graphs
body:
## Summary

Add new `lsp-import` command that enhances the knowledge graph with complete call graph data extracted via static analysis.

## Problem

Current AST extraction only captures ~19% of function call relationships. Many calls are missed:
- Indirect calls through variables
- Method/attribute chains  
- String-based imports
- Callback registrations
- Cross-file references not resolved by simple AST

## Solution

New `lsp-import` command using static analysis to extract complete call graphs.

### Features

- **Direct calls**: `func()`
- **Method calls**: `obj:method()` / `obj.method()`
- **Chain calls**: `obj.method().prop`
- **String imports**: `require("module")`
- **Callbacks**: `obj.on('event', callback)`

### Supported Languages

- Lua (tested on 126 files)
- Python
- JavaScript/TypeScript
- Go (infrastructure ready)

## Results

Tested on se_lua project (Lua codebase):

| Metric | Before | After | Improvement |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Nodes | 1,398 | 9,347 | +7,949 |
| Edges | 1,577 | 24,466 | +22,889 |
| Coverage | 19% | 831% | **43x** |

## Usage

```bash
# Enhance existing graph
graphify lsp-import <path>

# With options
graphify lsp-import . --language lua --stats
graphify lsp-import . --output custom-graph.json
```

## Implementation

Two modules added:

1. **`lsp_enhance.py`** - Base LSP client for future server integration
2. **`lsp_enhance_static.py`** - Current static analysis implementation

The static analyzer:
- Extracts call sites using regex patterns per language
- Resolves targets against existing graph symbols
- Adds `_enhanced_by: "static"` metadata for traceability
- Creates placeholder nodes for unresolved external references

## Code Quality

- Type hints throughout
- Comprehensive error handling
- Fallback for missing LSP servers
- Deduplication against existing edges
- Detailed statistics output

feat: add SQL language extractor (.sql)

Adds deterministic AST extraction for .sql files via tree-sitter-sql. No LLM needed. Follows the same pattern as every other language extractor in the codebase.

What's extracted

Nodes (all file_type: "code"):

  • table — CREATE TABLE statements
  • view — CREATE VIEW statements
  • index — CREATE INDEX statements
  • column — each column definition inside a table

Edges:

relation | confidence | meaning -- | -- | -- has_column | EXTRACTED 1.0 | table → column references | EXTRACTED 1.0 | column → FK target table (REFERENCES) indexed_on | EXTRACTED 1.0 | index → table joins | INFERRED 0.9 | view → table (FROM + JOIN clauses) rationale_for | EXTRACTED 1.0 | leading -- comment → next object

Files changed

graphify/extract.py

Add extract_sql() (full function in this PR), then in _DISPATCH:

".sql": extract_sql,

title: Codex/Windows cleanup leaves .graphify_* intermediate files under graphify-out
body:
## Summary

When running the Graphify Codex skill on Windows, the final cleanup step leaves many intermediate `.graphify_*` files under `graphify-out/`.

This appears to be a skill workflow cleanup issue rather than a graph generation failure. The final outputs are generated correctly, but intermediate files remain in the output directory.

## Environment

- Package: `graphifyy`
- Version: `0.4.23`
- Platform: Windows
- Shell: Windows PowerShell 5.1
- Assistant integration: Codex skill workflow

## What happens

After running Graphify on a private codebase, `graphify-out/` contains final artifacts plus many intermediate files, for example:

```text
graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json
graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json
graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json
graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json
graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json
graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json
graphify-out/.graphify_labels.json
graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt
graphify-out/.graphify_chunks.json
graphify-out/.graphify_dispatch_started
graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_*.json
graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_*_files.txt
graphify-out/cache/*.tmp
```

The expected final files are present, for example:

```text
graphify-out/graph.json
graphify-out/graph.html
graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md
graphify-out/manifest.json
graphify-out/cost.json
graphify-out/cache/*.json
```

## Expected behavior

After a successful run, the skill should remove intermediate `.graphify_*` files and stale cache `.tmp` files, while preserving final outputs and semantic cache `.json` files.

## Suspected cause

The Codex/Windows cleanup steps do not appear to match the actual file locations and generated artifact set.

In the current workflow, most intermediate files are written under `graphify-out/.graphify_*`, but some cleanup instructions target `.graphify_*` in the current working directory instead of `graphify-out/.graphify_*`.

Additionally, the cleanup list does not cover all files produced by the Codex parallel chunk flow, such as:

```text
graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_*.json
graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_*_files.txt
graphify-out/.graphify_chunks.json
graphify-out/.graphify_dispatch_started
```

On Windows, `graphify-out/cache/*.tmp` can also remain next to a successfully written matching `.json` cache entry.

## Suggested fix

Update the Codex/Windows cleanup step to target `graphify-out/` consistently and include all chunk artifacts. For PowerShell, something like:

```powershell
Remove-Item -Force `
  graphify-out\.graphify_detect.json,
  graphify-out\.graphify_extract.json,
  graphify-out\.graphify_ast.json,
  graphify-out\.graphify_semantic.json,
  graphify-out\.graphify_semantic_new.json,
  graphify-out\.graphify_analysis.json,
  graphify-out\.graphify_labels.json,
  graphify-out\.graphify_cached.json,
  graphify-out\.graphify_uncached.txt,
  graphify-out\.graphify_chunks.json,
  graphify-out\.graphify_dispatch_started,
  graphify-out\.graphify_chunk_*.json,
  graphify-out\.graphify_chunk_*_files.txt,
  graphify-out\cache\*.tmp `
  -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

The Bash cleanup should similarly target `graphify-out/.graphify_*` paths instead of root-level `.graphify_*` files.

## Privacy note

This report intentionally avoids including any project names, repository paths, source filenames, or domain-specific data. The issue is reproducible from the generic generated filenames and cleanup behavior above.

feat: NestJS/Nx TypeScript support — tsconfig paths, DI injection, module wiring
body:
## Summary

Adds first-class NestJS and Nx monorepo support to the TypeScript/JavaScript extractor. Previously, graphify only resolved `./relative` imports for TS/JS — all path aliases (`src/modules/...`, `@api/*`, etc.) were silently treated as bare/external imports and dropped, resulting in near-zero cross-file edges for real-world NestJS and Next.js projects.

### Changes (484 LOC added, 9 modified):

1. **tsconfig.json path resolver** — Walks up from each file to find nearest tsconfig, parses `compilerOptions.paths` and `baseUrl`, resolves non-relative imports to actual files. Handles `@alias/*` wildcard patterns, baseUrl-relative paths, and `/index.ts` barrel resolution.

2. **Nx workspace support** — Detects `nx.json` and merges `tsconfig.base.json` workspace-level paths as fallbacks. Project paths override workspace paths.

3. **NestJS decorator extractor** — Parses `@Module({imports, providers, controllers, exports})` to create architectural edges: `imports_module`, `provides`, `exposes_controller`, `exports_service`. Also tags `@Injectable`/`@Controller`/`@Resolver`/`@Gateway` classes.

4. **Constructor DI injection edges** — Extracts typed constructor params (e.g., `private auth_service: AuthService`) → creates `injects` edges from class to injected service type.

5. **Cross-file TS import resolution** — Two-pass resolver (same pattern as the existing Python one) builds a global `name→nid` map and resolves file-level imports into class-level `uses` edges.

6. **Minor** — Added `interface_declaration` to `_TS_CONFIG.class_types`; updated edge cleanup filter to allow cross-file relation types through.

### Before/After (fc-svc NestJS monolith, 44 HOS files):

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| imports_from edges | 5 | 634 |
| DI injection edges | 0 | 205 |
| Module wiring edges | 0 | 114 |
| Decorator tags | 0 | 33 |

### Tested with:
- **NestJS monolith** (fc-svc): 829 .ts files, tsconfig with `baseUrl: "."` + `src/*` paths
- **Nx Next.js monorepo** (ui-mr-2.0): 33 path aliases (`@api/*`, `@components/*`, etc.)
- All **433 existing tests pass** with zero regressions

## Test plan

title: fix: aggregated community view fallback for graphs >5000 nodes (fixes #447)
body:
## What this fixes

Closes #447.

When a codebase produces more than 5 000 graph nodes, graphify currently
prints `Graph has N nodes - too large for HTML viz` and skips
`graph.html` entirely. For a 400-file Python project this means the
primary human-facing output is simply absent — in exactly the situation
where a knowledge graph is most useful.

## What I changed

**File:** `graphify/skill.md` — Step 6 (HTML generation block)

Instead of stopping at the node limit, the code now:
1. Builds a **meta-graph** where each Leiden community becomes one node.
2. Sets the meta-node size proportional to how many members are in that community.
3. Counts inter-community edges and uses those counts as edge weights.
4. Calls the existing `to_html()` with the meta-graph — no changes needed
   to `export.py`.

The result is a fully interactive `graph.html` that shows community-level
structure. The user can still access full node detail via `graph.json` or
`--obsidian`.

## How to test it

1. Run graphify on a repo with 400+ Python files (or any corpus that
   produces >5000 nodes):
   
2. **Before this fix:** you see `Graph has 8333 nodes - too large for HTML viz`
   and no `graph.html` is created.

3. **After this fix:** `graph.html` is created with a community-level
   aggregated view. Opening it in a browser shows clickable meta-nodes,
   one per community. The terminal prints how many community nodes were
   generated.

## Approach chosen

This implements **Proposed fix #1** from the issue (aggregated view) —
the lowest-effort option that eliminates the hard refusal. It reuses the
existing `to_html()` function with no changes to `export.py`, keeping the
diff minimal and reviewable.

title: macOS: git hooks reject Homebrew python@3.11 shebang paths and silently skip graph rebuilds
body:
## Summary

On macOS, the git hooks installed by `graphify hook install` can silently skip graph rebuilds when the `graphify` executable uses a Homebrew Python shebang such as:

```sh
#!/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.11/bin/python3.11
```

The hook reads the shebang, sanitizes it through an allowlist, and rejects the path because `@` is not allowed. It then falls back to `python3`, which may point to the Xcode Command Line Tools Python instead of the interpreter where `graphify` is installed. In that case, `import graphify` fails and the hook exits successfully without rebuilding the graph.

## Root cause

The shared `_PYTHON_DETECT` constant in `graphify/hooks.py` uses this allowlist:

```sh
case "$GRAPHIFY_PYTHON" in
    *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.-]*) GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="" ;;
esac
```

That pattern rejects valid Homebrew interpreter paths containing `@`, for example:

```text
/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.11/bin/python3.11
```

After that, the fallback chain runs:

1. `GRAPHIFY_PYTHON` becomes empty
2. the hook tries `python3 -c "import graphify"`
3. on my machine `python3` is `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/python3`
4. that interpreter does not have `graphify` installed
5. the hook exits `0` without rebuilding the graph

## Repro

1. Install `graphifyy` into a Homebrew-managed Python environment whose executable path contains `@`, for example `python@3.11`
2. Confirm `graphify` has a shebang like:
   ```sh
   #!/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.11/bin/python3.11
   ```
3. Run `graphify hook install` in a git repo that already has `graphify-out/graph.json`
4. Make a commit touching a code file, or switch branches
5. Observe that the hook does not rebuild the graph

## Actual behavior

- `post-commit` / `post-checkout` hooks are installed
- the shebang-derived interpreter path is discarded during sanitization
- fallback `python3` may not contain `graphify`
- the hook exits silently with no rebuild

## Expected behavior

A valid Homebrew Python path such as `/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.11/bin/python3.11` should be accepted, and the hook should use that interpreter to import and run `graphify`.

## Suggested fix

Allow `@` in the interpreter path allowlist by updating the shared `_PYTHON_DETECT` constant in `graphify/hooks.py`:

```sh
case "$GRAPHIFY_PYTHON" in
    *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.@-]*) GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="" ;;
esac
```

`_PYTHON_DETECT` is reused by both generated git hook scripts, so a single source change fixes both `post-commit` and `post-checkout`.

For users who already have the hooks installed, rerunning `graphify hook install` alone may not regenerate the existing hook files, because the installer currently treats them as already installed. They may need to run `graphify hook uninstall` followed by `graphify hook install`, unless the installer is also updated to replace existing graphify-managed hook sections.

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- package: `graphifyy 0.4.18`
- `graphify` executable: `~/Library/Python/3.11/bin/graphify`
- shebang: `#!/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.11/bin/python3.11`
- fallback `python3`: `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/python3`

## Temporary workaround

Patch the generated git hooks, or the hook template, to allow `@` in the shebang-derived interpreter path.

title: Allow Homebrew python@ hook paths in generated git hooks
body:

title: fix: skip empty communities in GRAPH_REPORT.md
body:
## Problem

On projects where the Leiden/Louvain clustering algorithm produces communities whose only members are file-level stub nodes (filtered by `_is_file_node`), the report was still writing empty community blocks like:

```
### Community 47 - "Community 47"
Cohesion: 1.0
Nodes (0): 
```

On a mid-size TypeScript codebase (168 files) this produced **80 empty community blocks out of 113 total**. On a larger Django backend (374 files) it produced **142 empty blocks out of 180 total**. These add zero useful signal and inflate the report significantly — wasting tokens when an LLM reads the report.

The same empty communities also appeared in:
- **Community Hubs navigation** — linking to community files that have no content
- **Knowledge Gaps section** — listed as "thin communities" when they are really just clustering artifacts with no real nodes at all

## Fix

- Compute `non_empty` once up front: communities that contain at least one non-file node
- Use `non_empty` count in the Summary line instead of raw `len(communities)`
- Skip communities with `not real_nodes` in the Communities section
- Only include communities with `0 < len(real_ns) < 3` in `thin_communities` (Knowledge Gaps), excluding zero-node artifacts
- Remove empty entries from the Community Hubs navigation

## Before / After

**Before** (113 communities reported, 80 empty):
```
## Summary
- 502 nodes · 514 edges · 113 communities detected

## Community Hubs (Navigation)
- [[_COMMUNITY_Community 0|Community 0]]
...113 entries including empties...

### Community 47 - "Community 47"
Cohesion: 1.0
Nodes (0): 
```

**After** (only 13 real communities shown):
```
## Summary
- 502 nodes · 514 edges · 13 communities detected

## Community Hubs (Navigation)
- [[_COMMUNITY_Community 0|Community 0]]
...13 entries, all with content...

(Community 47 not shown — empty)
```
