title: --obsidian: community labels with ., &, (, ) produce invalid Obsidian tags and break Dataview queries
body:
### Version                                                                                                   
                                                          
  graphifyy 0.7.0                                                                                               
  
  ### What I ran                                                                                                
                                                          
  ```                                    
  /graphify <some-folder> --obsidian
  ```                                                                                                           
  
  The graph clustered into communities and at least one community label contained                               
  characters that are not valid in Obsidian tag syntax — for example a label like
  `Foo Tool 1.2` (contains `.`) or `A & B` (contains `&`).                                                      
                                                                                                                
  ### What happened                                                                                             
                                                                                                                
  In `graphify-out/obsidian/_COMMUNITY_*.md`, the embedded Dataview block:                                      
                                         
  ```dataview                                                                                                   
  TABLE source_file, type FROM #community/Foo_Tool_1.2    
  SORT file.name ASC                                                                                            
  ```                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                
  …fails to parse with:                                                                                         
                                                          
  ```                                                                                                           
  Dataview: Error:                                        
  -- PARSING FAILED --------------------------------------------------
  > 1 | TABLE source_file, type FROM #community/Foo_Tool_1.2                                                    
      |                                                  ^                                                      
    2 | SORT file.name ASC                                                                                      
  Expected one of the following:                                                                                
  'and' or 'or', /FROM/i, EOF, FLATTEN <value> [AS <name>], ...
  ```                                                                                                           
                                                          
  Same failure mode for any community whose label contains `.`, `&`, `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, or `:`.                
                                                          
  ### Why                                                                                                       
                                                          
  Obsidian tag grammar accepts only `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` and `/` (for nesting). The                                  
  slugifier in `graphify/export.py` only replaces spaces with underscores; it
  doesn't strip other invalid characters. The same untreated string is also                                     
  written into the `tags:` frontmatter list on every node, so `FROM #community/...`                             
  queries can't match anything for those communities even when the dot-truncation                               
  isn't a parse error.                                                                                          
                                                                                                                
  ### Where in the source                                                                                       
                                                          
  `graphify/export.py` (v0.7.0) — four sites, all using the same pattern:                                       
                                                          
  | Line  | Context                                                                |                            
  | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | L72   | `comm_tag = f"community/{community_name.replace(' ', '_')}"` (node tag)|                            
  | L184  | `comm_tag_name = community_name.replace(" ", "_")`                     |                            
  | L188  | `… FROM #community/{comm_tag_name}` (Dataview block in community page) |
  | L235  | `"query": f"tag:#community/{label.replace(' ', '_')}"` (Canvas search) |                            
                                                                                                                
  ### Suggested fix                                                                                             
                                                                                                                
  Centralize tag slugification, e.g.:                                                                           
                                         
  ```python                                                                                                     
  import re                                               
                                         
  def _safe_tag_segment(name: str) -> str:
      # Obsidian tags allow only [A-Za-z0-9_-] and / for nesting.                                               
      # Replace spaces with underscores, then strip everything else.                                            
      cleaned = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_/-]", "", name.replace(" ", "_"))                                          
      return cleaned or "unnamed"                                                                               
  ```                                                                                                           
                                                          
  …and use it at all four sites that build `community/<slug>`.                                                  
                                                          
  Alternative (more robust against any character): rewrite the generated Dataview                               
  query to filter on the frontmatter field rather than the tag, since the
  frontmatter already stores the literal label:                                                                 
                                                                                                                
  ```dataview                                                                                                   
  TABLE source_file, type                                                                                       
  WHERE community = "Foo Tool 1.2"                        
  SORT file.name ASC                                                                                            
  ```
                                                                                                                
  That removes the slug-roundtrip entirely and works for any label.                                             
                                         
  ### Minimal repro                                                                                             
                                                          
  1. Create a folder with two text files that mention the same concept.                                         
  2. Force at least one community label to contain a `.` or `&`. The easiest way
     is to label the community manually after running `/graphify --cluster-only`.                               
     (Or just run on any corpus where the auto-generated labels happen to include                               
     a version number like "X 1.2".)                                                                            
  3. Run `/graphify <folder> --obsidian`.                                                                       
  4. Open the vault in Obsidian, install Dataview, open the affected                                            
     `_COMMUNITY_*.md`. The block fails to parse.                                                               
                                                                                                                
  ### Workaround                                                                                                
                                                                                                                
  Hand-edit each affected `_COMMUNITY_*.md` to use the `WHERE community = "..."`                                
  form shown above.

title: _load_tsconfig_aliases() doesn't follow tsconfig "extends" — SvelteKit/Nuxt/NestJS aliases silently dropped
body:
## Problem

`_load_tsconfig_aliases()` (extract.py) reads `compilerOptions.paths` from the
nearest `tsconfig.json` it finds, but does **not** follow the `extends` field.

This breaks alias resolution for any project that uses an extended tsconfig — which
is the modern default for SvelteKit, Nuxt, NestJS, Astro, T3 stack, and most
framework starters. In all of these, the user's `tsconfig.json` typically just
extends a framework-generated file, and the actual `paths` live in the parent.

The #575 fix works perfectly for projects that put `paths` directly in
`tsconfig.json`, but silently no-ops for the (much more common) extended case.

## Repro

SvelteKit project (`graphifyy 0.7.0`).

`tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "extends": "./.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json",
  "compilerOptions": { ... }   // no `paths`
}
```

`.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json` (auto-generated by `svelte-kit sync`):

```json
{
	"compilerOptions": {
		"paths": {
			"$lib": ["../src/lib"],
			"$lib/*": ["../src/lib/*"],
			"$partials": ["../src/partials"],
			"$partials/*": ["../src/partials/*"]
		}
	}
}
```

Project code uses these aliases everywhere:

```ts
import { db } from '$lib/server/database'
import RecommendationCarousel from '$lib/components/recommendations/recommendation-carousel.svelte'
```

**Observed:** `_load_tsconfig_aliases()` returns `{}` because the
project-root `tsconfig.json` has no `paths`. Every `$lib/*` and `$partials/*`
import falls into the bare-package branch and gets dropped.

**Impact in numbers** (1,966-file SvelteKit corpus, AST + Kimi semantic):

- 8,088 nodes, 11,179 edges built
- 1,705 communities (extreme fragmentation — most are 1-4 node singletons)
- 192 `.svelte` files appear with zero cross-file edges; ~150 of those are
  verifiably used in the live app (cross-checked with knip + grep)

## Root cause

`extract.py` `_load_tsconfig_aliases()`:

```python
data = json.loads(tsconfig.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
paths = data.get("compilerOptions", {}).get("paths", {})
# never inspects data.get("extends")
```

## Proposed fix

Resolve the `extends` chain before reading `paths`. Pseudocode:

```python
def _load_tsconfig_chain(path: Path, seen: set[Path] | None = None) -> dict:
    """Load a tsconfig and recursively merge from any `extends` parent.
    Child paths win over parent. Cycle-safe via `seen`."""
    seen = seen or set()
    if path in seen or not path.exists():
        return {}
    seen.add(path)
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    extends = data.get("extends")
    base = {}
    if extends:
        # extends can be relative path, absolute path, or a node-module name.
        # For now handle the common relative-path case; node_modules resolution
        # is a follow-up.
        ext_path = (path.parent / extends).resolve()
        if ext_path.is_dir():
            ext_path = ext_path / "tsconfig.json"
        elif ext_path.suffix == "":
            ext_path = ext_path.with_suffix(".json")
        base = _load_tsconfig_chain(ext_path, seen)
    # Deep-merge compilerOptions; child paths override parent.
    merged = {**base, **data}
    base_co = base.get("compilerOptions", {})
    own_co = data.get("compilerOptions", {})
    merged["compilerOptions"] = {**base_co, **own_co}
    if "paths" in own_co or "paths" in base_co:
        merged["compilerOptions"]["paths"] = {**base_co.get("paths", {}), **own_co.get("paths", {})}
    return merged
```

Then have `_load_tsconfig_aliases()` call `_load_tsconfig_chain()` and read
paths from the merged result.

## Frameworks affected by this gap

- **SvelteKit** — `extends` `.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json`
- **Nuxt 3/4** — `extends` `.nuxt/tsconfig.json`
- **NestJS** — `extends` `tsconfig.base.json`
- **Astro** — `extends` `astro/tsconfigs/...`
- Anything from `tsconfig/bases` (npm package) used by T3, monorepo templates
- Most monorepo setups (turborepo, nx) where leaf packages extend a root tsconfig

## Workaround

Manually copy the framework-generated `paths` into the project-root `tsconfig.json`.
Brittle (gets regenerated) and not always possible (SvelteKit overwrites
`.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json` on every `svelte-kit sync`).

title: .svelte markup-level dynamic imports invisible to AST extractor — {#await import('./X.svelte')} pattern dropped
body:
## Problem

Per #254, `.svelte` files were added to `CODE_EXTENSIONS` and dispatched to the
JS/TS extractor, with the maintainer noting "template blocks are skipped by the
parser gracefully." This works for imports inside the `<script>` block, but
silently drops imports inside the markup block — most notably the
canonical SvelteKit lazy-load pattern:

```svelte
{#await import('./recommendation-carousel.svelte') then { default: Carousel }}
  <Carousel ... />
{/await}
```

Because tree-sitter-javascript can't parse the surrounding `{#await ... then ... /await}`
mustache markup, it bails (or skips) before reaching the `import(...)` call.
The import is invisible to graphify, so the target component looks like an
orphan unless it's also imported elsewhere.

## Why this matters

This pattern is the standard SvelteKit code-splitting idiom — used to defer
loading of heavy components, popovers, modals, command palettes, lazy charts,
etc. In a SvelteKit codebase that leans on it heavily (modern apps targeting
small initial bundles), most component-to-component edges live in markup, not
in `<script>`.

## Repro

Any `.svelte` file with a markup-level dynamic import. Concrete example from
a 707-`.svelte`-file production SvelteKit codebase using `graphifyy 0.7.0`:

```svelte
<!-- src/lib/components/app-sidebar.svelte (excerpt) -->
<script lang="ts">
  // Dynamic loaded on demand to avoid hydration cost
  let CommandPalette: ... | undefined = $state()
  // ...
  if (open && !CommandPalette) {
    import('./command-palette.svelte').then((m) => (CommandPalette = m.default))
  }
</script>

{#if CommandPalette}
  <CommandPalette bind:open {menu} />
{/if}
```

```svelte
<!-- src/routes/(series)/[id]/(view)/+layout.svelte (excerpt) -->
{#await import('$lib/components/discover/queue-bar.svelte') then { default: QueueBar }}
  <QueueBar series_id={series.id} />
{/await}
```

In both cases the target `.svelte` shows up in graphify as an orphan despite
being live-loaded in production.

(Note: the first example's `import(...)` is technically inside `<script>` so
it should work in principle. Empirically it doesn't, suggesting tree-sitter-js
also struggles when the script block contains complex Svelte 5 runes like
`$state` mixed with dynamic imports. The second example is unambiguously
markup-level and definitely invisible.)

## Impact in numbers

Same SvelteKit corpus as #691:
- 707 `.svelte` source files
- 26 of them flagged as "no incoming edges in graph" by hand-rolled query
- After grep-verification: ~20 of those 26 are actually used via dynamic
  import (false positives ≈ 77%)
- Knip exhibits the same blind spot for the same reason

## Possible fixes (ordered by effort)

1. **Regex pre-pass** before handing the file to tree-sitter-js: scan the raw
   file for `import\(['"]([^'"]+)['"]\)` matches, emit `imports_from` edges
   from those, then continue with the existing JS extraction. ~20 lines, no new
   deps. False positives possible (matches inside string literals or comments)
   but rare in practice and lower-cost than missing them.

2. **Strip markup before parsing**: for `.svelte` files, extract just the
   `<script>` and `<script lang="ts">` blocks with a regex, concatenate, and
   feed to tree-sitter-js. Catches in-script dynamic imports reliably.
   Misses pure-markup dynamic imports.

3. **Add `tree-sitter-svelte`** as an optional language. Proper solution but
   requires shipping another grammar and writing a `LanguageConfig` for it.

(1) and (2) combined would solve ~95% of the problem at low cost.

title: feat(extract): markdown section-level source_location for doc nodes
body:
## Summary

Adds a deterministic Python markdown-section parser exposed as `graphify.extract.parse_markdown_sections(path)`, and updates the semantic-extraction skill prompts so LLM-emitted concept nodes from `.md` files carry `source_location: "L<start>-L<end>"` instead of `null`.

## Why

Currently doc nodes have `source_location: null`, so an agent answering a content question via graphify can locate the right file but not the right section. To answer it has to read the whole file — which defeats the context-bloat reason for using graphify in the first place. Code-AST nodes already get `source_location: "L33"` from tree-sitter; this brings doc nodes to parity so callers can target a `Read` with `offset`/`limit` instead of loading whole files.

This came out of a 3-way retrieval pilot where graphify scored 6/24 on content-recall queries vs 24/24 for direct CLAUDE.md routing and 20/24 for Qdrant semantic search. The discriminating issue was always the same: `query` returned the right node label and source-file pointer, but the agent then had to read the entire file to actually answer "what does this principle SAY". With section ranges, a 500-token targeted Read replaces a 5,000-token full-file load.

## What's new

### `parse_markdown_sections(path)` (graphify/extract.py)

Pure stdlib regex. Returns `[{label, level, start_line, end_line}, ...]` for each section. CommonMark-conformant fence handling:

- Opener indent must be 0–3 spaces (4+ spaces is an indented code block, not a fence).
- Closer must use the same fence char class (` `` ` vs `~~~`), be at least as long as the opener, and be followed only by whitespace (so an inner ` ```python ` info-string line inside a triple-backtick block is content, not a closer; and a 4-backtick block can legitimately contain a triple-backtick line as content).

Skips YAML frontmatter and fenced code blocks.

### Skill prompts (skill.md + 10 variants)

- Doc-instruction tells subagents to emit `L<start>-L<end>` for markdown concepts.
- Schema example shows `"source_location":"L1-L50"`. `null` still valid where no section applies.
- New `MARKDOWN_SECTIONS_JSON` placeholder: orchestrator pre-computes section ranges via `parse_markdown_sections` and substitutes into the subagent prompt. Subagents copy ranges verbatim from this map rather than recomputing — eliminates fabricated `L1-L9999`-style ranges.
- New Step B3 validation pass runs BEFORE `save_semantic_cache`, so bad ranges never enter the on-disk cache. Validates BOTH nodes and edges. Drops malformed (regex check), out-of-bounds (vs file line count), and fabricated (not in parser-derived sections) ranges to `null` with a stderr warning. Single-line refs (`start == end`) allowed without section match — they may legitimately point at a precise in-section line.

### `llm.py` direct LLM backend

Updated for parity with the skill prompts (same schema example + doc-instruction).

### `skill-vscode.md` NOT updated

That variant uses a stripped-down schema (no `source_file`, no `source_location`). TODO comment + note in CHANGELOG flag this as a separate follow-up — happy to scope it into a follow-up PR if you'd prefer.

## Tests

- New: `tests/test_markdown_sections.py` — 13 cases covering single header, multi-level, nested, no-headers, YAML frontmatter, no-trailing-newline, fenced-code, 4-backtick + inner triple, tilde-vs-backtick mix, 5-tilde + inner 3-tilde, info-string non-closer, 4-space-indent non-fence, 3-space-indent valid fence.
- All existing tests pass: `pytest tests/test_extract.py tests/test_chunking.py tests/test_validate.py` shows 49 passing (2 deselected on Windows due to symlink-privilege issues — pre-existing baseline; not introduced by this PR).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI runs and all green.
- [ ] Manual smoke: pick a 5–10 markdown-file folder, run `/graphify` (Claude Code) or `graphify <dir>` (CLI). Inspect `graph.json` — doc nodes should have `source_location: "L<n>-L<m>"` matching their source headers.
- [ ] Run `pytest tests/test_markdown_sections.py -v` — expect 13 passed.
- [ ] Spot-check one node's range against the source markdown headers in a real corpus.

## End-to-end validation (smoke test on real corpus)

Tested on 6 real-world markdown files (≈8K words total). A semantic subagent emitted **81 nodes + 77 edges**, all with `source_location` populated. The B3 validation pass dropped **0 bad ranges** — the `MARKDOWN_SECTIONS_JSON` binding is doing its job. Sample:

```
claude_goal_1_trading_wiki:    L12-L15  (the "Goal 1" subsection)
claude_goal_2_trading_manual:  L16-L27  (the "Goal 2" subsection)
soul_intellectual_courage:     L30-L32  (was previously unanswerable)
```

A previously failing content-recall query ("summarize the Intellectual Courage principle from SOUL") can now be answered by Reading 3 lines instead of 80.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Cache invalidation when `parse_markdown_sections` output changes between runs (currently the validator only checks new chunk results).
- Update `skill-vscode.md` schema to add `source_file` / `source_location` once the VS Code Copilot pipeline can handle the larger node payload.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:

title: Headless flow for semantic LLM extraction on a docs-only corpus?
body:
Hi — following up on your earlier guidance about the CI-as-sole-publisher model.

We're applying it to a huge Markdown-only corpus (no code) and ran into a gap. The CLI graphify update <path> does AST-only extraction, which produces no output for a docs-only repo. The full semantic extraction path (/graphify <path> --update) is implemented as a slash command that orchestrates Claude Code subagents — which means it can't run headlessly in CI.

So for our setup, the recommended workflow ("CI runs graphify --update on every merge to main") doesn't apply directly: there's no headless command that does semantic LLM extraction.

Could you clarify:

For a docs-only corpus, is there a headless / CLI path for semantic LLM extraction (calling the LLM directly from python -m graphify ...)?
If not, is the intended model: a designated human maintainer runs /graphify --update locally in Claude Code after each merge, and pushes the regenerated graph to master?
Is headless semantic extraction on the roadmap?
Thanks for the help so far — the CI-as-publisher model fits our needs well; we just want to wire it correctly.

title: _read_tsconfig_aliases() silently fails on tsconfig.json with comments — every JS/TS project hits this
body:
Follow-up to #691 (and the v0.7.1 fix). The `extends` chain is now followed correctly, but the underlying parser still uses `json.loads`, which raises on `//` line comments and trailing commas — i.e. on the de-facto format every TypeScript tool ships and every framework starter generates. The exception is swallowed by the bare `except Exception: return {}` at `extract.py:62-63`, so `_load_tsconfig_aliases()` returns `{}` and every aliased import falls into the bare-package branch, exactly as it did pre-#691.

## Repro (real project — 1,870-file SvelteKit app)

`tsconfig.json` — the only thing that matters is one trailing-line comment, generated as-is by `pnpm create svelte` / `npm create vite` / `nx` / NestJS / T3 / Astro:

```jsonc
{
  "extends": "./.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "skipLibCheck": true, // only way to make svelte-check not include node_modules
    "strict": true
  }
}
```

`.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json` (auto-generated by `svelte-kit sync`, has the actual paths):

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "paths": {
      "$lib": ["../src/lib"],
      "$lib/*": ["../src/lib/*"],
      "$partials": ["../src/partials"],
      "$partials/*": ["../src/partials/*"]
    }
  }
}
```

**Observed:**

```python
>>> from graphify.extract import _load_tsconfig_aliases
>>> _load_tsconfig_aliases(Path('src/lib/server'))
{}
```

The silent `except` at `extract.py:60-63` masks `json.JSONDecodeError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 22 column 25`.

**Expected** (what you get if `json.loads` is monkey-patched to strip `//` comments first):

```
$lib       -> /…/website/.svelte-kit/../src/lib
$partials  -> /…/website/.svelte-kit/../src/partials
$app/types -> /…/website/.svelte-kit/types/index.d.ts
```

So the extends-following logic from #691 *does* work — it's just unreachable in practice because the parent file fails to parse.

## How aliases are used in this codebase

These are exactly the imports the resolver needs to handle. All standard SvelteKit shapes:

```ts
// src/hooks.server.ts (TS, top-level alias usage)
import { connect_to_db, disconnect_from_db } from '$lib/server/database'
import { MBSQLError } from '$lib/server/database/series.mbsql'
import { auth_check } from '$lib/server/middleware/auth-check'
```

```ts
// src/app.d.ts (type-only imports — also alias-resolved)
import type { ListConfigurationSection } from '$lib/types/series-list-config'
import type { ContentRating } from '$lib/types/series-ui-options'
```

```svelte
<!-- src/lib/components/series/similar/similar-series-section.svelte (Svelte <script>) -->
import RecommendationCarousel from '$lib/components/recommendations/recommendation-carousel.svelte'
import ImageV2 from '$partials/Series/ImageV2.svelte'
import SimpleTooltip from '$partials/SimpleTooltip.svelte'
```

Repo-wide totals: **4,246** `$lib/...` imports, **478** `$partials/...` imports across `.ts` / `.svelte` files. Currently every one of them falls through to the bare-package branch.

## Impact

For our 1,870-file SvelteKit corpus on `graphifyy 0.7.2`:

- `imports_from` edges from `.svelte` files: **18** (essentially unchanged from v0.7.0's 18)
- `.svelte` orphan files: **314** (unchanged from v0.7.0's 314)
- Total edges: **11,179** (byte-identical to v0.7.0)

The v0.7.1/0.7.2 upgrade produced zero net new edges in our graph because the JSONC failure short-circuits everything before the new extends logic runs.

Note: the bare `except Exception: return {}` at `extract.py:60-63` made this surprisingly hard to diagnose — there's no signal anywhere that alias loading failed.

title: extract_svelte() regex fallback: alias paths skipped + synthetic IDs don't match real file nodes, so 100% of generated edges are dropped by build
body:
Follow-up to #692 (and the v0.7.1 fix). The regex fallback was added at `extract.py:1699-1732`, and a unit-level call confirms it does emit `dynamic_import` edges. But none of them survive into `graph.json`. Two independent bugs:

## Bug A — alias paths excluded by design

`extract.py:1712-1715`:

```python
for m in _re.finditer(r"""import\(\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]\s*\)""", src):
    raw = m.group(1)
    if not raw.startswith("."):
        continue   # ← skips $lib/…, $partials/…, ~/, @/, src/…, etc.
```

Only relative `./X` paths are kept. The original ticket explicitly listed both relative *and* aliased examples — and in real SvelteKit codebases the aliased form dominates.

## Bug B — synthetic node IDs use the **source** file's path, so edges never resolve

`extract.py:1711, 1716`:

```python
file_node_id = _make_id(path.stem, str(path))
node_id      = _make_id(raw,        str(path))   # path = the importer
```

But the real file nodes elsewhere in the graph are created with `_make_id(str(path))` where `path` is the **target** file (relative, no stem prefix). So:

```
real target node id    : src_partials_series_grid_card_series_card_library_svelte
regex-pass target id   : card_series_card_library_svelte_users_jippi_…_src_partials_series_grid_series_single_view_svelte
real source file id    : src_partials_series_grid_series_single_view_svelte
regex-pass source id   : series_single_view_users_jippi_…_src_partials_series_grid_series_single_view_svelte
```

`build_from_json` in `build.py:99-104` tries normalized fallback, then drops the edge:

```python
if src not in node_set or tgt not in node_set:
    continue  # skip edges to external/stdlib nodes
```

Both endpoints are phantom, so every `dynamic_import` edge from the regex pass is discarded. The phantom nodes themselves leak through (I see one labelled `./Card/series-card-library.svelte` orbiting nothing), but no edge connects to the real target file.

## Repro

```python
>>> from graphify.extract import extract_svelte
>>> r = extract_svelte(Path('src/partials/Series/Grid/series-single-view.svelte'))
>>> [e for e in r['edges'] if e['relation'] == 'dynamic_import']
[{'source': 'series_single_view_…', 'target': 'card_series_card_library_svelte_…', ...}]   # produced
```

Then in `graph.json`:

```bash
$ jq '[.links[] | select(.relation == "dynamic_import")] | length' graphify-out/graph.json
0
```

## Dynamic-import shapes seen in this codebase

A real SvelteKit app uses many flavors. The regex fallback needs to handle all of these. Counts from our 1,870-file corpus, then a minimal example for each:

| Shape | Where it lives | Count | Currently captured? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{#await import('$lib/...')}` | markup | 21 | no — Bug A |
| `{#await import('./...')}` | markup | 1 | no — Bug B |
| `import('$lib/...').then(...)` | `<script>` | 23 | no — Bug A (tree-sitter doesn't see alias as a file) |
| `import('./...').then(...)` | `<script>` | 2 | only via tree-sitter, not the regex pass |
| `typeof import('./...')` (type-only) | `<script>` | 5 | no |
| `typeof import('$lib/...')` (type-only) | `<script>` | 1 | no |

### Markup, aliased — 21 occurrences

```svelte
<!-- src/routes/(series)/[id=id]/(view)/+layout.svelte:263 -->
{#await import('$lib/components/discover/queue-bar.svelte') then { default: QueueBar }}
  <QueueBar series_id={series.id} />
{/await}

<!-- same file: $partials alias -->
{#await import('$partials/Catalog/SeriesEditBadge.svelte') then { default: CatalogSeriesEditBadge }}
  <CatalogSeriesEditBadge {series} />
{/await}
```

### Markup, relative — 1 occurrence

```svelte
<!-- src/partials/Series/Grid/series-single-view.svelte:63 -->
{#await import('./Card/series-card-library.svelte') then { default: SeriesCardLibrary }}
  <SeriesCardLibrary {series} library_entry={cardCtx.library_entry} />
{/await}
```

### Script, relative `.then()` — 2 occurrences

```svelte
<!-- src/lib/components/display-mode.svelte:47 -->
body_promise = import('./display-mode-body.svelte').then((m) => {
  body_component = m.default
})
```

This one *is* captured because tree-sitter-js sees the script body. It's the only category that works today.

### Script, relative inside `Promise.all` — same file, app-sidebar.svelte

```svelte
<!-- src/lib/components/app-sidebar.svelte:550-554 -->
void Promise.all([
  import('./change-locale.svelte'),
  import('./content-rating-selector.svelte'),
  import('./theme-picker.svelte'),
]).then(...)
```

### Script, type-only `typeof import(...)` — 6 occurrences

```svelte
<!-- src/lib/components/app-sidebar.svelte:515,522,535-539 -->
type AppSidebarModQueueComponentType = (typeof import('./app-sidebar-mod-queue.svelte'))['default']
let CommandPalette: (typeof import('./command-palette.svelte'))['default'] | undefined = $state()
let LanguagePicker = $state<Component<ComponentProps<typeof import('./change-locale.svelte').default>> | null>(null)
```

These are type positions, but in modern Svelte 5 + `$state()` they're load-bearing — the *runtime* `import('./command-palette.svelte').then(...)` lives a few lines below the type alias and is the only thing that actually loads the component. A graph that ignores `typeof import(...)` and gets the runtime `import(...)` is fine; one that misses both leaves the lazy-loaded component looking like a pure orphan.

## Impact

For our corpus, ~150 of the ~314 currently-orphaned `.svelte` files are reached only through the patterns above — the same population originally cited in #691/#692. None of those edges exist in the current graph.

title: GRAPH_REPORT.md community counts disagree across header, body, and rendered sections
body:
## Summary

The `GRAPH_REPORT.md` produced by the standard pipeline reports three different community counts in three places, with no documented relationship between them. As an end-user it is unclear which is "the" count, and they do not arithmetically reconcile.

## Repro

`graphifyy v0.7.0`, AST-only build (no LLM), Python codebase, default flags.

```
graphify .
```

## What I see

Header (line 8 of `GRAPH_REPORT.md`):

```
- 2360 nodes · 4006 edges · 161 communities detected
```

Body section heading (line 204):

```
## Communities (186 total, 44 thin omitted)
```

Rendered community sections actually present in the body: 142 (i.e. 186 − 44).

So the report exposes:

| Location | Number | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Header | 161 | "communities detected" |
| Body heading | 186 | "total" |
| Body content | 142 | (186 − 44 thin omitted) |

161, 186, and 142 don't reconcile via any arithmetic visible in the report. The thin-omission count (44) explains 186 → 142, but the gap between 161 ("detected") and 186 ("total") is unexplained.

## What I'd expect

Either:

1. A single canonical count surfaced consistently (e.g. header reports `total` matching the body), with a separate explicit line like `(N hidden as thin)` if filtering is applied; **or**
2. If "detected" and "total" genuinely measure different things (e.g. pre/post some merge/split pass), label them with that distinction in both places so users can tell which to trust.

Right now a reader looking at `GRAPH_REPORT.md` cannot answer "how many communities does this graph have?" without diving into the JSON or source.

## Notes

- Not blocking — graph itself is fine, this is a labeling/reporting clarity issue.
- Happy to test a fix against the same corpus if useful.

title: fix(antigravity): use .agent instead of .agents for Antigravity paths
body:
## Problem

Google Antigravity reads configuration from `.agent/` (no trailing 's'):
- Rules: `.agent/rules/`
- Workflows: `.agent/workflows/`
- Skills: `~/.agent/skills/`

The `graphify antigravity install` command was writing to `.agents/` (with a trailing 's'), causing all files to be placed in directories that Antigravity never reads. This meant the integration silently failed — no rules loaded, no workflow registered, no skill found.

## Fix

Changed all Antigravity-specific paths from `.agents` → `.agent`:

| Location | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| `_PLATFORM_CONFIG["antigravity"]["skill_dst"]` | `~/.agents/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` | `~/.agent/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` |
| `_ANTIGRAVITY_RULES_PATH` | `.agents/rules/graphify.md` | `.agent/rules/graphify.md` |
| `_ANTIGRAVITY_WORKFLOW_PATH` | `.agents/workflows/graphify.md` | `.agent/workflows/graphify.md` |
| Workflow content | `~/.agents/skills/...` | `~/.agent/skills/...` |
| Help text | `.agents/rules` | `.agent/rules` |

Other platforms that use `.agents/` (Codex, Gemini Windows) are **not** affected — only the Antigravity-specific code paths were changed.

## Testing

Ran `graphify antigravity install` after the fix — all files now land in the correct `.agent/` directories and are picked up by Antigravity.

title: Bug: graphify hook install loses community labels on rebuild
body:
## Description
When using `graphify hook install`, the post-commit hook triggers `_rebuild_code()` which overwrites human-readable community labels with generic placeholder names.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Run `/graphify .` — communities get human-readable labels (e.g. "Domain Models & Enums")
2. Install hook: `graphify hook install`
3. Make any code change and commit
4. Hook triggers rebuild → `GRAPH_REPORT.md` and `graph.html` now show generic `"Community N"` labels

## Root cause
- Full pipeline (Step 5) writes `.graphify_labels.json`, then Step 9 cleanup deletes it
- `_rebuild_code()` in `watch.py` hardcodes `labels = {cid: "Community " + str(cid)}` instead of reading persisted labels
- `graph.json` stores `community` IDs per node but no `community_labels` mapping

## Expected behavior
Hook rebuild should preserve human-readable community labels.

## Possible fix options
1. Don't delete `.graphify_labels.json` in Step 9 cleanup, and make `_rebuild_code()` read it
2. Or store `community_labels` directly inside `graph.json`

## Additional note
`.graphify_incremental.json` is also not cleaned up after `--update` — should be added to Step 9 cleanup.

title: Add Solidity AST extraction (.sol) via tree-sitter-solidity
body:
## Summary

Adds Solidity to the set of languages supported by graphify's deterministic AST extraction. Mirrors the existing pattern used for SQL: optional dependency, `_DISPATCH` registration, dedicated tree-sitter extractor.

- New `extract_solidity()` in `graphify/extract.py` (~280 lines, bespoke walk).
- `tree-sitter-solidity` added as an optional `solidity` extra (pinned `>=1.2.13,<2`) and bundled into the `all` extra.
- `.sol` registered in `_DISPATCH` and `detect.CODE_EXTENSIONS`.

## Coverage

**Nodes:** contract / interface / library declarations, free functions, functions / modifiers / constructors / fallback / receive, events, errors, structs, enums, state variables.

**Edges:** `defines`, `contains`, `inherits`, `imports`, `imports_from` (named imports + `using ... for ...`), `applies_modifier`, `emits`, `calls` (low-confidence `0.5` for member calls, full `1.0` for direct).

## Resolution quality

A pre-pass collects file-wide `decl_map` / `modifier_map` / `event_map` so that `inherits`, `applies_modifier`, and `emits` edges resolve to in-file definition nids instead of producing dangling bare-name targets.

`require` / `assert` / `revert` / `keccak256` / type conversions (`address(...)`, `uintN(...)`) are filtered from `calls`. `revert_statement` subtrees are skipped entirely so `revert NotOwner(...)` is not misclassified as a function call.

## Validation

- 21 new unit tests in `tests/test_multilang.py` (single-file fixture + multi-file fixture under `tests/fixtures/solidity/`). All pass.
- 525 unrelated tests still pass.
- Benchmarked on OpenZeppelin contracts (349 `.sol` files): 0 errors, ~0.8 ms/file, 7,148 nodes / 8,535 edges. Edge distribution: `contains` 40% · `calls` 35% · `imports_from` 10% · `inherits` 6% · `defines` 5% · `emits` 2% · `applies_modifier` 2%. ERC20 god-node check confirms `ERC20` as top, with `approve` / `transfer` / `transferFrom` next — matches the expected ERC20 surface.

## Out of scope (Phase 5+ candidates)

- Cross-file name resolution (single-file resolution only, by design — bare names for cross-file ancestors).
- Type-resolved member calls (currently flagged `INFERRED` 0.5 with `context: member_call`).
- Yul / inline assembly parsing.
- Natspec extraction (`@notice`, `@dev`).
- Storage read/write tracking.
- Reentrancy / external-call ordering analysis.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_multilang.py -k solidity -v` passes (21 tests).
- [ ] `pytest tests/` shows no regressions in non-Solidity tests.
- [ ] `pip install graphifyy[solidity]` then run `graphify` on a folder with `.sol` files — graph builds without errors.
- [ ] Spot-check OpenZeppelin or Uniswap V3 results for edge sanity.
