title: Add `.surql` (SurrealDB schema) support — tree-sitter grammar already on PyPI, clear extraction targets
body:
### Problem

Graphify gives AI assistants full visibility into app code and SQL schemas, but projects using SurrealDB are dark on the data layer. `.surql` files define tables, fields, indexes, events, and graph relations — none of which appear in the knowledge graph today.

### Why it's a low-effort addition

[`tree-sitter-surrealql`](https://github.com/Ce11an/tree-sitter-surrealql) is already published to PyPI, so it slots directly into the existing tree-sitter pipeline with no grammar work needed.

### What to extract — concrete example

From two real schema files:

```sql
-- organization.surql
DEFINE TABLE OVERWRITE organization SCHEMAFULL ...;
DEFINE FIELD OVERWRITE owner ON organization TYPE record<user>;
DEFINE INDEX OVERWRITE organization_slug_unique ON organization FIELDS slug UNIQUE;
DEFINE EVENT OVERWRITE setup_organization ON organization WHEN $event = "CREATE" THEN {
    RELATE $owner->employee_of->$org ...;
};

-- employee_of.surql
DEFINE TABLE OVERWRITE employee_of SCHEMAFULL
    TYPE RELATION FROM user TO organization ...;
DEFINE FIELD OVERWRITE role ON employee_of TYPE record<organization_role>;
```

Expected nodes and edges:

| Node | Edge | Target | Source |
|------|------|--------|--------|
| `organization` | `has_field` | `owner` | field definition |
| `owner` | `references` | `user` | `TYPE record<user>` |
| `employee_of` | `relation_from` | `user` | `TYPE RELATION FROM user` |
| `employee_of` | `relation_to` | `organization` | `TYPE RELATION ... TO organization` |
| `role` | `references` | `organization_role` | `TYPE record<organization_role>` |
| `setup_organization` | `event_on` | `organization` | `ON organization` |

The `TYPE RELATION FROM X TO Y` syntax is native graph-edge semantics — exactly what graphify models.

### Implementation path

Following the same pattern as the SQL extractor:

1. Add `tree-sitter-surrealql` to dependencies
2. Register `.surql` as a handled extension
3. Extract `DEFINE TABLE`, `DEFINE FIELD`, `DEFINE INDEX`, `DEFINE EVENT`, `DEFINE FUNCTION` nodes
4. Emit `references` edges for `TYPE record<T>` fields and `TYPE RELATION FROM X TO Y` declarations
5. Add fixture + test following `tests/fixtures/` pattern

title: Step 5 community labeling: sampling truncated member lists causes systematic mislabeling on large communities
body:
## Summary
Running the `/graphify` skill's `--update` + Step 5 (label communities) flow on a personal Obsidian vault (~110 files, session-log style journal), 10 of 25 communities with >=3 members ended up mislabeled: the assigned label described a minority theme (as little as ~10-15% of members) while the majority of the community covered unrelated topics.

## Root cause
Step 5 says: "For each community key, look at its node labels and write a 2-5 word plain-language name." It doesn't say to read the *full* member list. It's easy to only look at the first N members of `communities[cid]` for large communities (30-44 nodes in my case) to save context/output. Member-list order reflects insertion order from extraction, not relevance or centrality, so the first N members are often unrepresentative. Example: a 44-node community got labeled "Techo del Menu (Sonnet 4.6)" when that topic was only ~4 of the 44 nodes -- the other 40 covered 5+ unrelated topics.

## Why it's easy to fall into
This seems specific to journal/session-log style corpora (dated daily notes, changelogs): a single dated entry ("Session - 20 July") cross-references everything touched that day via wikilinks/backlinks, so Louvain clustering pulls unrelated topics into the same community through narrative adjacency rather than semantic similarity. Large communities in this kind of corpus are disproportionately likely to be genuine multi-topic mixes, which makes partial-sample labeling fail silently and confidently -- the resulting label reads clean and specific, so nothing about it signals it's wrong.

## Suggested fix
I patched my local copy of SKILL.md Step 5 to:
1. Explicitly require reading the full node-label list per community before writing a label -- never a head/sample slice.
2. 2. When the full list reveals a genuine topic mix rather than one coherent theme, prefer a compound label ("Topic A + Topic B (mixed)") over forcing a single-theme name.
3. 3. Call out the session-log/dated-entry corpus pattern specifically, since it's the most likely source of narrative-adjacency-driven community mixing.
Happy to open a PR with this SKILL.md wording if useful -- flagging the failure mode first in case there's a preferred fix (e.g. enforcing full-membership reads via a script rather than prose guidance alone).

title: fix(dedup): preserve same-source node attributes
body:
## Summary

- retain non-conflicting attributes when exact-ID nodes from the same source file collapse
- preserve the deterministic collision survivor for conflicting values
- keep cross-file references and genuine slugged-path ID collisions isolated
- document the dedup-enabled build contract

Fixes #2091.

## Root cause

The exact-ID pre-dedup pass selected one complete node dictionary and discarded the other. That made deterministic collision ranking work, but it also removed complementary AST/semantic data such as `summary` and `confidence_score` before NetworkX could merge attributes.

The fix gap-fills only missing keys from same-source duplicates. It does not import attributes from another source file, so the existing #1504 collision boundary remains intact.

## Impact

Default `dedup=True` builds now retain AST precision (`source_location`, `_origin`) and semantic enrichment (`summary`, `confidence_score`) on the surviving node. Existing survivor values still win genuine conflicts.

## Validation

- reproduced #2091 on current `v8` before the fix: `summary=None`, `confidence_score=None`
- `pytest tests/test_dedup.py -q --tb=short` on Python 3.10: 48 passed
- `pytest tests/ -q --tb=short` on Python 3.12: 3553 passed, 3 skipped
- `ruff check graphify/dedup.py graphify/build.py tests/test_dedup.py`
- all five `tools.skillgen` CI checks
- `graphify update .`

title: # fix(dedup): merge same-ID node attributes instead of discarding them (#2091)
body:
## What

On the default `dedup=True` path, when two nodes share an ID the pre-dedup step
kept one whole node dict and threw the other away. In the AST↔semantic case
(where `_semantic_id_remap` forces the AST node and the LLM node onto one ID so
they merge), the LLM's `summary` / `confidence_score` / `references` were
silently dropped — even though `build()`'s docstring promises a key-wise union.

The user already paid API credits for those summaries, and the only output was a
`note:` about the *label*, never mentioning the lost attributes.

## How

The survivor now **gap-fills** from the loser instead of replacing it wholesale:

- Only keys the survivor lacks are copied over (`setdefault`).
- Conflicting keys (`label`, `source_file`) still resolve to the survivor, so
  `_collision_rank` ordering and the collision reporting are unchanged.
- The first insert now copies (`dict(node)`) so caller-owned node dicts are never
  mutated.

Before: `dedup=True` → `summary=None`. After: `dedup=True` → `summary` preserved,
survivor's label still wins the conflict.

## Files

- `graphify/dedup.py` — gap-fill merge in the same-ID pre-dedup loop.
- `tests/test_dedup.py` — 3 tests: gap-fill preserves disjoint attrs,
  survivor wins on conflict, input nodes are not mutated.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — entry under `0.9.24 (unreleased)`.

## Reference

- Issue #2091
- Root cause: `graphify/dedup.py` same-ID collapse loop.

## Conclusion

`dedup=True` now yields at least the attribute set `dedup=False` does, with the
survivor winning genuine conflicts. No public API change; full suite green
(pre-existing unrelated `test_ollama_retry_cap.py` failures aside).

title: detect(): sensitive-file filter silently drops any path containing 'token', 'secret', 'password'…
body:
## Summary

`detect()` silently excludes any file whose **name or full path** contains `token`, `secret`, `credential`, `passwd`, `password`, or `private_key` — as a bare substring, with no word boundaries and no regard for file type.

In a markdown knowledge base this drops ordinary prose articles. Three files in my corpus had **never** been in the graph across many runs:

```
wiki/ai-token-economics.md         <- a heavily-linked hub node
wiki/privacy-tokens.md
wiki/chain-of-hope-tokenomics.md
```

The exclusion is invisible in normal use: the paths land in `skipped_sensitive`, but the `/graphify` skill flow only reports a *count* ("mention file count skipped, not the file names"), so nothing tells you *which* files vanished or why. I only found it by diffing the manifest against `ls wiki/`.

## Source

`graphify/detect.py` (v0.4.23):

```python
_SENSITIVE_PATTERNS = [
    ...
    re.compile(r'(credential|secret|passwd|password|token|private_key)', re.IGNORECASE),  # L36
    ...
]

def _is_sensitive(path: Path) -> bool:
    name = path.name
    full = str(path)
    return any(p.search(name) or p.search(full) for p in _SENSITIVE_PATTERNS)
```

Because `full = str(path)` is also tested, **one directory named e.g. `secrets/` or `password-reset/` silently removes an entire subtree** from the corpus.

## Reproduce

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.detect import _is_sensitive

_is_sensitive(Path("notes/ai-token-economics.md"))       # True  (expected False)
_is_sensitive(Path("docs/password-reset-design.md"))     # True  (expected False)
_is_sensitive(Path("research/tokenization.md"))          # True  (expected False)
```

## Second-order bug: `--update` then deletes the recovered nodes

This is the part that cost me the most time. If you work around the filter by force-including the files (so they appear in `graphify-out/manifest.json`), the next `--update` is **destructive**:

`detect_incremental()` still excludes them, so comparing against the manifest reports them as `deleted_files`, and the merge step runs `G_existing.remove_nodes_from(...)` — silently pruning ~70 nodes that had just been recovered. So the workaround makes the next incremental run worse than no workaround at all.

## Suggested fix

Exempt markdown-family extensions from the **broad keyword pattern only**, keeping every strict pattern (`.env`, `.pem`, `id_rsa`, `.netrc`, `aws_credentials`, …) applying to all files:

```python
_PROSE_EXTS = {".md", ".markdown", ".rst", ".org"}
_KEYWORD_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r'(credential|secret|passwd|password|token|private_key)', re.IGNORECASE)

def _is_sensitive(path: Path) -> bool:
    name, full = path.name, str(path)
    is_prose = path.suffix.lower() in _PROSE_EXTS
    for p in _SENSITIVE_PATTERNS:
        if is_prose and p.pattern == _KEYWORD_PATTERN.pattern:
            continue
        if p.search(name) or p.search(full):
            return True
    return False
```

Real secrets live in dotfiles, keys and configs — not in `.md` notes. I deliberately left `.txt` guarded, since `token.txt` / `access_token.txt` are plausible credential dumps.

Verified against my corpus: 98 -> 101 documents detected, `skipped_sensitive` empty, and all of `.env` / `.env.local` / `*.pem` / `secrets.json` / `api_token.json` / `credentials.yaml` / `id_rsa` / `.netrc` / `aws_credentials` / `token.txt` still correctly blocked.

Two smaller things that would have made this self-diagnosing:

1. **Match on the filename only**, not the full path — or at least only the path segment(s) below the corpus root. A parent directory name shouldn't silently disqualify a subtree.
2. **Name the skipped files** (behind a flag if you like). A bare count reads as "nothing important happened".

Happy to open a PR if the approach looks right.

title: Zero-node warning (#1666) fires on data .json that #1224 skips by design, so it always asks users to report intended behaviour
body:
## Summary

The zero-node warning added for #1666 fires on data-shaped `.json` files that `extract_json` skips **on purpose** per #1224. Because the skip is deliberate and deterministic, the warning's own escalation advice — *"A re-run will retry them (empties are no longer cached); if it persists, please report the file(s)"* — is guaranteed to trigger: it never stops persisting, so it reliably instructs users to report a settled design decision.

I hit this on a real repo and got as far as drafting the report before reading `extractors/json_config.py` and finding the behaviour is intended. That is the failure mode: the warning converts an intentional skip into an apparently-actionable bug.

## Reproduction

Any repo containing data JSON with no manifest-recognition key. On graphify 0.9.20:

```
warning: 8 source file(s) produced zero nodes and are absent from the graph:
stateful_corpus.json, stateless_corpus.json, underwrite_payload.json,
alfa-overview.json, alfa-underwriting.postman_collection.json (+3 more).
A re-run will retry them (empties are no longer cached); if it persists,
please report the file(s) (#1666).
```

Re-running `graphify update .` reproduces the identical list — as it must, since nothing about these files will ever change the outcome.

## Why these files are skipped (working as designed)

`extract_json` recognises a config/manifest by filename or a top-level key probe (`dependencies` / `extends` / `$ref` / `$schema` / `compilerOptions`), and deliberately skips everything else — per its docstring, AST-walking data JSON "produced hundreds of orphan key-nodes and duplicate communities that swamped real structure (#1224)".

Confirmed none of the 8 carries a probe key:

| file | top-level keys | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `benchmarks/stateful_corpus.json` | `_comment`, `now`, `scenarios`, `seed` | skip |
| `benchmarks/stateless_corpus.json` | `_comment`, `scenarios` | skip |
| `benchmarks/underwrite_payload.json` | `coverage`, `flight`, `live_context`, `sale` | skip |
| `deploy/grafana/dashboards/alfa-overview.json` | `annotations`, `panels`, `refresh`, `schemaVersion`, `tags` | skip |
| `portal/src/locales/{en,ru}.json` | `common`, `controls`, `coverage`, `cta`, `dashboard` | skip |
| `portal/public/postman/*.json` (×2) | `info`, `item`, `variable` / `_postman_variable_scope`, `id`, `name`, `values` | skip |

Worth noting the Grafana dashboard is a near-miss: it has `schemaVersion`, not `$schema`.

Size is not the trigger either — these run 690 B to 21 KB, far under the 1 MiB cap, and all parse cleanly.

## Suggested fix

Same shape as the resolution of #1689, which separated "no extractor exists" from "extractor ran and produced nothing":

Let `extract_json` distinguish *intentionally skipped* from *unexpectedly empty* — e.g. return a `skipped: "data-shaped json (#1224)"` marker alongside the empty node list — and have the zero-node warning exclude those files from the "please report" bucket. If they are still worth surfacing, a separate non-actionable line would do it without implying a defect:

```
note: 8 data .json file(s) were skipped by design (#1224) and are not in the graph.
```

That keeps the #1666 warning meaning what it was built to mean — *this is anomalous, tell us* — instead of firing on the one category where zero nodes is the correct answer.

## Minor, related

The warning advises `graphify extract --force`, which is correct but is not listed in `graphify --help` (which documents `update`, `cluster-only`, `path`, `explain`, `diagnose`, `watch`, …). `graphify extract --force .` does work. Running it without a path returns `error: must specify a path to scan or a --postgres DSN`, which reads like "unknown subcommand" and briefly convinced me the command did not exist. Listing `extract` in `--help` would remove the ambiguity.

## Environment

- graphify (`graphifyy`) 0.9.20, uv tool install, macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), Python 3.12
- Repo: ~500 source files, Python + Java + TypeScript + Rust

title: Emit a bare file node for deliberately-skipped data .json so it stays discoverable (without reintroducing #1224)
body:
## Summary

Data-shaped `.json` is deliberately skipped by `extract_json` (#1224 — AST-walking it exploded into orphan key-nodes), which is the right call for *structure*. But the current skip is total: the file contributes **no node at all**, so the path is absent from `graph.json` entirely and is unreachable from `query` / `explain` / `affected`.

Requesting a middle setting: emit a single **file node** for skipped data JSON — no key traversal, no children, no edges — so the file is discoverable without reintroducing #1224's node explosion.

## Why this matters (concrete case)

Our repo runs two implementations of the same underwriting engine (Python and a Java port) and pins their agreed behaviour in shared parity corpora:

- `benchmarks/stateful_corpus.json`
- `benchmarks/stateless_corpus.json`

These are the *contract* between the two implementations — CI has dedicated `parity`, `parity-java` and `parity-java-stateful` jobs that consume them. They are arguably the most decision-relevant files in the repo for any "do these two implementations agree?" question.

Neither has ever appeared in our graph. Our project convention (and our `CLAUDE.md`) routes codebase questions through `graphify query` first, so the practical result is that a parity question returns a confident, well-formed answer assembled entirely from the *implementations*, with no indication that the file defining the agreed behaviour exists at all.

That is the part worth weighing: the failure is not an empty result, which would prompt a fallback to grep. It is a plausible result with a silent hole. Same class of concern as the "if someone uses the warning's silence as evidence their corpus is fully covered" point raised in #1666.

The same applies to other data JSON that is meaningful at file granularity — i18n catalogues (`portal/src/locales/{en,ru}.json`), Grafana dashboards, Postman collections.

## Proposal

For a `.json` that fails manifest recognition, return exactly one node:

```json
{
  "id": "<path_qualified_id>",
  "label": "stateful_corpus.json",
  "file_type": "data",
  "source_file": "benchmarks/stateful_corpus.json",
  "source_location": "L1"
}
```

No key nodes, no nested traversal, no edges — the file node only. On our repo that is 8 nodes total, against the 561 orphan nodes #1224 was closed to prevent.

Benefits:

- `query` / `explain` can surface that the file exists and where it lives.
- Co-location edges (if any are derived elsewhere from directory structure) put it near the code that consumes it.
- It composes with #1666's warning: a file node is exactly the "every extractable file produces at least a file node" invariant quoted in that thread, so these files stop being anomalous and the warning stops firing on them — which would resolve the false-positive I filed alongside this.

If a blanket file node is too broad, gating it behind a flag (`--index-data-json`) or a size ceiling would still cover the case, though the value is highest when it is on by default — the whole problem is that the gap is invisible unless you already know to look for it.

## Alternative considered

Adding a probe key to our corpora (e.g. `$schema`) to make them manifest-recognised. Rejected: it would pull them down the manifest path and produce misleading dependency-shaped structure, and it asks every repo to mangle its data files to be visible to the tool.

## Environment

- graphify (`graphifyy`) 0.9.20, uv tool install, macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), Python 3.12
- Related: #1224 (the deliberate skip), #1666 (zero-node warning), #1689 (classified-as-code but no extractor)

title: TS/JS: methods inside a module-level object-literal export get no graph node at all (repository pattern)
fix: TS/JS object-literal repository methods get their own graph node
body:
Fixes #2110.

## What's broken

`const repo = { findX(...) {...}, y: async () => {...} }` at module scope produces exactly one graph node — for `repo` itself — and nothing for its methods. Every call into or out of such a method is invisible to `affected`/`explain`/the call graph.

This hits the common "repository object" pattern in TypeScript (`export const fooRepo = { findById() {...}, create() {...}, ... }`), used instead of a class when there's no instance state.

## Root cause

In `graphify/extractors/engine.py`, the module-level-const branch of `_js_extra_walk` (handling `lexical_declaration` with a value type of `object`/`array`/`as_expression`/`call_expression`/`new_expression`) creates a single node for the const and then unconditionally returns `True`. That return short-circuits the caller's default recursive descent into the const's children, so the object literal's own `pair`/`method_definition` children — the actual methods — are never visited by any code path.

The already-correct handling just above it, for class fields with function values (`class C { handler = () => {} }`), walks each member and gives it its own node + a `method` edge back to the class. This fix mirrors that pattern for the object-literal case.

## Fix

Walks the object literal's direct children when the const's value is `type == "object"`. For `method_definition` children (shorthand methods) and `pair` children whose value is a function/arrow-function, creates a member node scoped under the const's id, with a `method` edge from the const. New nodes are wired into `callable_def_nids`/`local_bound_names`/`function_bodies` the same way every other callable node is, so downstream call resolution and the indirect-dispatch guard treat them consistently with any other method.

## Testing

- New file `tests/test_js_object_literal_repository_methods.py`, 7 tests: shorthand + async shorthand + arrow-valued members all get nodes, the container still gets its own node, a `method` edge exists from container to each member, an in-body call resolves to a free-standing helper, and a same-file external call to `repo.findX()` resolves to the member node. (Cross-file resolution through an imported plain-object binding — as opposed to a `new Class()` instance, which `test_ts_receiver_member_calls.py` already covers — is a separate, broader concern out of scope here, matching #2023/#1985.)
- Full JS/TS-filtered suite: 675 passed.
- Full suite: 3344 passed, 167 skipped. 12 failures, all pre-existing environment-only gaps unrelated to this change (missing optional `openai`/`tree-sitter-hcl` deps, a wheel-build toolchain nuance) — none touch JS/TS.
- Verified against a real production 28-method repository object (not included, private codebase) — all 28 methods now correctly appear as nodes with correct line numbers; previously none did.

title: .graphifyinclude is dead code: loaded on every detect() run but never consumed
body:
### Summary

`.graphifyinclude` is dead code. The file is read from disk on every `detect()` run and its patterns are parsed, but the result is assigned to a local variable that is never read again. A user who creates a `.graphifyinclude` file gets a silent no-op: no effect on which files are indexed, no warning, and no field in the result dict.

### How it got here

`.graphifyinclude` was added in v0.6.6 (#583, CHANGELOG.md:1084) as a hidden-path allowlist ("opt specific hidden dirs into traversal, e.g. `.hermes/plans/**/*.md`"). It was wired into the `detect()` walk via two call sites:

```python
if (not d.startswith(".") or _could_contain_included_path(dp / d, root, include_patterns))
...
if p.name.startswith(".") and not _is_included(p, root, include_patterns):
```

Commit `df40e4d` (#873, "index dot dirs") removed the blanket dot-prefix exclusion and, with it, both of those consumer lines. It left the loader, both matcher helpers, and the assignment in place. Since then the chain is: file read, patterns parsed, local variable, discarded.

### Evidence (all references, repo-wide)

- `graphify/detect.py:1140` `_load_graphifyinclude(root)` — working loader (walks root to VCS-root, reads `.graphifyinclude`, parses via `_parse_gitignore_line`). Dead.
- `graphify/detect.py:1170` `_is_included(path, root, patterns)` — full gitignore-style matcher. **Zero callers.**
- `graphify/detect.py:1219` `_could_contain_included_path(...)` — directory-prefix matcher. **Zero callers.**
- `graphify/detect.py:1315` `include_patterns = _load_graphifyinclude(root)` — the only call site; value never read again (confirmed: `include_patterns` matches only this line plus the dead defs).
- `CHANGELOG.md:1084` — the v0.6.6 feature entry (the only user-facing promise).
- `CHANGELOG.md:664` — a v0.8.26 (#1087) anchored-pattern bugfix that was applied to `_is_included` while it was already dead.
- Tests: none on mainline. The original PR's tests and a `graphifyinclude_patterns` result key only exist on the old `origin/v5` branch; the v0.6.6 mainline squash landed the detect.py code without them, so nothing failed when the feature was later severed.

No references in README, cli.py, extract.py, watch.py, skill files, or tools. Even when live, the feature only ever affected `detect()`, never `extract.py` `collect_files`.

### Contrast: `.graphifyignore` is fully wired

Load at detect.py:1306, consumed for dir pruning (1385) and file filtering (1418), surfaced as `graphifyignore_patterns` in the result dict (1504), and mirrored in `extract.py` `collect_files` (5306+). That is the pattern an include feature would need to follow.

### User impact

Low severity but real: ~110 lines of maintained-but-dead code (it even received a bugfix while dead), real I/O on every scan, and a silent no-op for anyone who trusts the loader or the CHANGELOG entry. Minor wart: `.graphifyinclude` is not in `_SKIP_FILES` (detect.py:796), so the allowlist file itself shows up in the `unclassified` output.

### Proposed fix

Two coherent directions:

**Option A (preferred): remove the dead code.** Delete `_load_graphifyinclude`, `_is_included`, `_could_contain_included_path`, and detect.py:1315. Add a CHANGELOG erratum noting `.graphifyinclude` has been non-functional since #873. Optionally emit a one-line stderr note when a `.graphifyinclude` file is present, pointing users to `!` negations in `.graphifyignore` (which already provide re-include via last-match-wins) now that dot dirs are indexed by default. This removes the original motivation cleanly.

**Option B: re-implement as an ignore-override.** Make `.graphifyinclude` a re-include that can rescue paths excluded by `.gitignore`/`.graphifyignore`: check `_is_included` before recording `ignored` for dirs (1385) and files (1418), use `_could_contain_included_path` to exempt matching dirs from pruning, mirror in `extract.py` `collect_files`, add `graphifyinclude_patterns` to the result dict, and restore tests. Decisions to settle first: precedence vs CLI `--exclude` (currently wins over all ignore files, #947); whether include can rescue `_SKIP_DIRS` noise and `_is_sensitive` files (#583 said no, keep that); the gitignore parent-exclusion rule (a negation cannot rescue files under an excluded dir); and the `--code-only` and `watch.py` re-scan paths.

Given #873 already made the original hidden-dir use case moot and `!` in `.graphifyignore` covers the common "re-include" need, Option A is the lower-risk resolution unless there is demand for a distinct allowlist file.

title: fix: bound per-term query seed recovery
body:
## Summary

- keep per-term query seed recovery within `max_k`
- prioritize recovery candidates that cover more query terms
- preserve deterministic ordering and normalized-label deduplication

## Problem

`_pick_seeds()` caps the initial combined-score selection at `max_k`, but its second-stage `best_seed_by_term` recovery loop previously appended every distinct singleton winner without applying that cap.

That means a long natural-language query can create one traversal root per matching token. Generic exact-label winners then broaden BFS/DFS traversal and consume the output budget even though callers explicitly requested a bounded seed set.

The new regression test uses a self-contained synthetic graph. With `max_k=3`, the previous behavior returns four seeds: one dominant anchor plus three unique per-term recovery candidates. The bounded selector returns three.

## Root cause

The two-stage selection had inconsistent limits:

1. combined-score seeds respected `max_k`
2. per-term recovery iterated all winners in lexical term order and had no global limit

The recovery path was added for good reason: it prevents an incidental exact match from starving relevant substring-only terms (#1445), and remains important alongside coverage scaling (#1602). Removing it would reintroduce that failure mode.

## Change

Recovery now:

1. runs only while seed capacity remains
2. groups query terms by their singleton-winning node
3. prefers nodes that recover the most terms with one slot
4. breaks ties by combined score, label length, and node id
5. keeps the existing normalized-label deduplication from #1766

The initial combined-score selection, query scoring, endpoint resolution, and traversal algorithms are unchanged.

This also leaves the separate tied-score/community-diversification problem in #1303 out of scope.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest -q tests/test_serve.py` — 127 passed
- `uv run ruff check graphify/serve.py tests/test_serve.py`
- `git diff --check`
- `graphify update .` — code graph rebuilt successfully

The regression fixture and all public context are synthetic and self-contained.

Authored with Codex (GPT-5).

title: feat(extract): tree-sitter-based Dart extraction with source_location line anchors
body:
## What

Dart is currently the one mainstream language whose extractor emits `source_location: None` on every node and edge — `extract_dart` is a ~520-line regex extractor predating the generic tree-sitter framework, so Dart symbols can't be jumped to or read by line range downstream, unlike Java/Kotlin/Swift/etc.

This PR makes tree-sitter the primary Dart path, using the community [`tree-sitter-dart`](https://pypi.org/project/tree-sitter-dart/) grammar as a new optional `[dart]` extra (prebuilt wheels for win/macOS/Linux, x86+arm):

- **AST-driven with line anchors**: declarations (classes, mixins, enums, extension types, extensions, typedefs), imports/exports, `part of` redirection, annotations, and functions/factory constructors all come from the AST with `L{n}` anchors on nodes and edges.
- **Proven heuristics retained**: the Flutter-framework sweeps (Bloc events/emissions, Riverpod providers, navigation routes) and Dart 3 pattern-destructured variables — which the 0.1.x grammar still parses with ERROR nodes — stay on the existing regexes, now line-anchored via match offsets and scoped by the AST.
- **Regex fallback preserved verbatim**: without the extra installed, extraction falls back to the previous implementation unchanged (`_extract_dart_regex`) — the same optional-grammar pattern as `extract_pascal` (#781). No new required dependency.

## Fixes along the way

The AST also closes two regex false-positive classes:
- Declarations inside string literals (e.g. lint-test fixtures with code in `'''...'''`) no longer produce phantom class/function nodes.
- Multi-line named/optional parameter lists (`required String id,` sits at the 0–2-space indent the variable regex scans) no longer leak parameters as variable nodes, including a case that produced labels containing newlines.

## Validation

- All existing `tests/test_dart.py` expectations pass **on both paths** (grammar installed and absent); new tests cover anchor stamping, `part of` redirection with anchors, the extension family (named/anonymous/generic), named/optional parameters, factory vs named constructors, and generators.
- Ran against a large production Flutter codebase (2,780 `.dart` files): **100% of locally-defined nodes and all edges anchored**, 100% anchor spot-check (2,547 sampled symbols found on their anchored line), node counts within 0.5% of the regex baseline (the delta is the string-literal phantoms the AST correctly drops), and the tree-sitter path ran slightly faster than the regex path (~5s vs ~5s for the whole repo, same order).
- Error recovery verified: files the grammar can't fully parse still extract (localized ERROR nodes), and any walker exception falls back to the regex extractor per file, so a grammar gap can never cost a file entirely.

`uv.lock` regenerated with `uv lock` (adds `tree-sitter-dart` to the `all`/`dart` extras; the surrounding marker churn is current uv re-normalizing environment markers).

title: fix: preserve exact identifiers in query expansion
body:
## Summary

- preserve user-supplied code identifiers before graph-vocabulary expansion
- keep exact anchors in their original spelling and order without consuming the 12-token expansion budget
- render the updated query guidance for every supported split-skill runtime
- add a generator-level regression test covering all rendered query skills

## Root cause

The query skill currently builds the traversal query exclusively from lowercase
tokens selected from the graph vocabulary. This improves recall for natural-language
questions, but it can discard a precise identifier that the user already supplied.

For example, an exact anchor such as `CheckoutMatchingResult` can become the separate
terms `checkout matching result`. On a large graph, those broader terms may seed
unrelated nodes while the exact symbol is no longer guaranteed to participate in the
query.

## Change

The query-expansion flow now:

1. captures inline-code and identifier-shaped spans from the original question
2. preserves those anchors verbatim, in order, with deduplication
3. selects up to 12 additional terms from the graph vocabulary
4. builds the query with exact anchors first, followed by expanded terms
5. reports both lists so the transformation remains auditable

Exact anchors are user-provided rather than model-invented. A query can also proceed
with exact anchors when no additional vocabulary token is appropriate.

This is intentionally independent from #2113: that PR bounds the query engine's seed
recovery, while this PR prevents the skill layer from dropping precise identifiers
before the engine sees the query.

## Scope

This changes skill guidance and generated skill artifacts only. It does not modify
query scoring, traversal behavior, or graph construction.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest -q tests/test_skillgen.py tests/test_install_references.py tests/test_install_roundtrip.py`: 124 passed, 1 skipped
- `uv run ruff check tests/test_skillgen.py`
- `uv run python -m tools.skillgen --check`
- `uv run python -m tools.skillgen --audit-coverage`
- `uv run python -m tools.skillgen --schema-singleton`
- `uv run python -m tools.skillgen --monolith-roundtrip`
- `uv run python -m tools.skillgen --always-on-roundtrip`
- `git diff --check`
- `uv run graphify update .`

title: Feature Request: Native Tree-sitter Support for R
body:
## Summary

Graphify currently recognizes `.R` files but relies on semantic/LLM-based extraction rather than deterministic AST parsing. This limits the accuracy and reproducibility of the generated graph for R projects, particularly CRAN-style packages.

I would like to contribute native Tree-sitter-based support for R.

## Motivation

R remains a major language in statistics, data science, epidemiology, and bioinformatics, with tens of thousands of open-source packages on CRAN and many active research codebases.

While semantic extraction provides a useful high-level understanding, a native parser would provide:

* Deterministic extraction
* Fully local analysis (no model required)
* Better reproducibility
* More accurate symbol and call relationships
* Faster indexing
* Improved support for large repositories

## Proposed Scope (Initial PR)

To keep the implementation manageable, I propose starting with core language support only.

The initial implementation would extract:

* Function definitions (`<- function()` and `= function()`)
* Function calls
* Package-qualified calls (`pkg::fun`, `pkg:::fun`)
* `library()` and `require()` imports
* Source locations
* File/function relationships

The goal is to produce the same core graph entities available for other Tree-sitter-backed languages.

## Future Enhancements

Once the core extractor is stable, additional R-specific features could be added incrementally, for example:

* `DESCRIPTION` parsing
* `NAMESPACE` parsing
* Roxygen metadata
* Exported vs internal functions
* `testthat` relationships
* S3 generic/method links
* S4 support
* R6 classes
* Vignettes and package structure

These would likely be separate follow-up PRs rather than part of the initial implementation.

## Questions

Before starting implementation, I'd like to confirm:

1. Would maintainers be interested in native Tree-sitter support for R?
2. Is there any preferred architecture or extractor pattern I should follow beyond the existing language extractors?
3. Are there any planned changes to the extraction pipeline that I should be aware of before beginning work?

If there is interest, I'd be happy to work on the initial implementation and submit a PR.

title: fix: suppress warnings for intentionally skipped files
body:
Fixes #2107.

## Problem

The zero-node diagnostic treats every extractor result with no nodes as anomalous. Some extractors intentionally return an explicit `skipped` marker for recognized but non-graph input, such as data-only JSON documents, so those files currently produce a false warning that asks users to re-run and report them.

## Change

Exclude results carrying the extractor-level `skipped` marker from the anomalous zero-node warning. Actual empty extractor results remain uncached and still warn.

## Validation

- Added a regression using a top-level JSON records array
- Preserved the existing negative control for a genuinely anomalous empty Ruby extraction
- Python 3.10: `3609 passed, 3 skipped`
- Python 3.12: `3609 passed, 3 skipped`
- All five `tools.skillgen` integrity checks pass
- `ruff check graphify/extract.py tests/test_zero_node_no_cache.py` passes
- `graphify update .` completed: 11,961 nodes / 21,152 edges

This is intentionally scoped to the warning behavior; skipped data JSON remains absent from the graph by design.

refactor(build): share the graph-json loader and prefixed-merge across multi-repo paths
body:
## What

Pure refactor, no behavior change: `merge-graphs` and the global graph now share one persisted-graph loader (`build.load_graph_json`) and one prefixed-merge with external-node dedup (`build.merge_prefixed_into`).

Before this, the load-a-graph.json dance (size cap, legacy `edges`→`links` normalization, type coercion) existed in three copies — the global-graph load, `global_add`'s source load, and `merge-graphs` — and the external-dedup/remap/self-loop-skip merge lived only inside `global_add`. The copies had already drifted slightly (`merge-graphs` didn't apply the size cap consistently).

## Why now

This is the first of a 3-PR stack: the cluster-graphs feature (#2121) composes member graphs through exactly these two helpers, so extracting them first keeps that PR reviewable and guarantees the three multi-repo paths (merge-graphs, global graph, clusters) can't drift again.

One observable improvement (not a behavior change to valid inputs): `merge-graphs` on a malformed JSON input now prints `error: ...` and exits 1 instead of an unhandled traceback.

## Stack

1. **→ this PR** — shared graph-json loader
2. #2121 — cluster graphs (multi-repo linked graphs)
3. #2122 — multigraph mode (parallel relations)

## Testing

- Full suite passes (3,608 passed, 3 skipped).
- Covered by the existing `test_merge_graphs_cli.py` / global-graph tests; no test changes needed.

title: feat(cluster): cluster graphs — link multiple repos into one connected graph
body:
## What

`graphify cluster` — link several repos' graphs into one connected graph with **real cross-repo edges**, for ecosystems where the coupling lives in contracts a single-repo scan can't see: service A calls service B's HTTP API via an env-var URL, two repos share a database table, a wire-format type file is copy-mirrored between a client and a worker. (`merge-graphs` and `global` union graphs side by side; a cluster also *connects* them.)

- A committable `cluster.json` names members by **git URL** (paths resolve per machine via a gitignored local override, the spec's path hint, or origin-remote sibling auto-discovery) and declares links: `api_call`, `shared_resource`, `mirrored_file`, `depends_on`, `references` — each optionally `direction: "both"`, which materializes a real reverse edge.
- `cluster build` composes members under `tag::` namespaces into a **directed** graph and resolves links into `EXTRACTED` edges in a standard `graphify-out/graph.json`, so `query`/`path`/`explain`/`affected`/`export` work unchanged. Node selectors are `{repo, file|label|id}` — users never write raw graph ids. `cluster check` dry-runs resolution (exit 1 on errors) for CI.
- `auto_links.packages` connects a member's manifest dependencies to their unique cross-repo provider (package nodes gain normalized `package_key`/`dependency_keys`); ambiguous providers are warned and skipped, declared links take precedence.
- **Member back-references:** `cluster build` writes a portable `cluster-ref.json` into each member's `graphify-out/` (opt out with `--no-refs`; `cluster remove` cleans up its own entry). Inside a member repo, `query`/`path`/`explain`/`affected` accept `--cluster [NAME]`, no-match failures note the membership (CLI + MCP), and the search-nudge hook + installed skills surface it to assistants. All passive surfaces are fail-open; marker fields are sanitized before reaching assistant-facing output (the marker travels with clones and is untrusted).
- `affected` traverses the new `calls_api`/`mirrors` relations by default so impact analysis crosses repo boundaries (`depends_on` deliberately excluded — it predates clusters).

## Design notes reviewers will want

- **Direction is load-bearing and tested.** Members load with their stored source/target order and compose into a DiGraph — an undirected round-trip re-emits endpoints by node insertion order and silently flips caller/callee (the #760 failure mode this codebase has hit before). Regression test pins the exact flip case (callee listed before caller).
- **Failure paths are actionable and pre-write.** Corrupt/missing member graphs, empty clusters, self-composition (cluster dir as its own member), and same-name cluster collisions (URL-tracked and URL-less) all fail with remediation text *before* any output is written.
- **`graph_mode` is validated but restricted to `"simple"`** in this PR; PR 3 widens it to `"multi"`. The spec key, manifest stamp, and status line ship now so existing clusters won't force-rebuild when PR 3 lands. One transitional test asserts `"multi"` is rejected; PR 3 replaces it.
- Writing markers into member repos' worktrees is opt-out (`--no-refs`) and fail-soft; the cluster's own `graphify-out/` stays gitignored (each machine composes its own graph) while member markers are committable and travel.

## Stack

1. #2120 — shared graph-json loader (base of this branch)
2. **→ this PR** — cluster graphs
3. #2122 — multigraph mode (parallel relations)

Until PR 1 merges, this PR's diff includes PR 1's one refactor commit; I'll rebase onto `v8` as the stack lands.

## Testing

- Full suite: 3,717 passed, 3 skipped; skillgen drift validators clean.
- ~180 new tests across `test_cluster_{spec,build,cli,links,refs}.py` and `test_affected_cluster_relations.py`: spec validation, compose, selector resolution (including dotfiles, LLM-labeled graphs, and member-order-independent externals), link direction round-trips, marker lifecycle (write/backfill/conflict/removal/corruption), `--cluster` end-to-end on all four query surfaces, hook/MCP hints, and sanitization of hostile marker fields.

title: feat: multigraph mode — preserve parallel relations end to end
body:
## What

Multigraph mode: `graphify extract --multigraph` (and `graph_mode: "multi"` clusters) builds keyed `MultiDiGraph`s on stable content-derived edge keys, so **parallel relations between the same node pair survive end to end** — today a pair that both `calls` and `references` silently collapses to one edge at build time.

- **Build/merge:** `build_from_json`/`build`/`build_merge` gain a `multigraph` param; incremental merges infer the existing graph's format; the format is **sticky** across rebuilds including `--force`, and `--no-multigraph` is the explicit downgrade path (warns that parallels collapse). Conversion in either direction bypasses the no-change early exit and carries the existing graph forward — an earlier draft of conversion could replace an unchanged graph with an empty one; that's pinned by tests now.
- **Watch/global:** watch rebuilds detect a multigraph on disk and rebuild through the keyed path; `global add` promotes when either side is keyed.
- **Query surfaces:** `query`/MCP render one EDGE line per parallel edge, `get_neighbors` iterates `edge_datas` (a `relation_filter` can no longer return empty for relations that exist), `explain` lists every parallel connection, and `affected` groups hits per source reporting all matched relations — while keeping the honest def-line fallback when an edge carries no location.
- **Analyze/export:** `graph_diff` uses occurrence-level identity on multigraphs only; GraphML/Cypher/Canvas exports keep parallel edges (Cypher `MERGE`s on `graphify_key` stay idempotent; canvas edge ids are index-qualified).
- Simple graphs are untouched: the multigraph edge-sort tiebreak is gated so the simple-path build keeps upstream's exact sort and tie behavior.

The first commit is a standalone one-liner (peelable on request): watch's rebuild now passes `root=project_root` to `build_from_json`, aligning watch-produced graphs with `graphify build`'s root-relative `source_file` paths (#932).

## Stack

1. #2120 — shared graph-json loader
2. #2121 — cluster graphs (base of this branch)
3. **→ this PR** — multigraph mode

Until PRs 1–2 merge, this PR's diff includes their commits; I'll rebase onto `v8` as the stack lands. Note: this PR replaces PR 2's transitional `graph_mode` validation test (which asserted `"multi"` is rejected) with the final round-trip test — the "removed test" in the diff is that swap, not lost coverage.

## Testing

- Full suite: 3,736 passed, 3 skipped; skillgen validators clean.
- New `test_multigraph_build.py` plus multigraph tests in the extract-CLI, analyze, cluster, and affected suites: stable keys across rebuilds, incremental format inference, conversion both directions (content preserved, `--force` stickiness, downgrade warning), mixed graph-mode composition, parallel-relation surfacing on every query surface, and exporter round-trips.
