title: cluster-only prints "graph.json updated" when to_json refused to write
body:
## What happens

`graphify cluster-only <path>` on a large existing graph computed a clustering, declined to persist it, and then reported success:

```
[graphify] WARNING: new graph has 794784 nodes but existing graph.json has 794903 (net -119).
  Refusing to overwrite. Possible causes: missing chunk files from a previous session, or
  fuzzy dedup collapsed same-named symbols across files during an --update on an already-current
  graph. Run a full rebuild (/graphify .) to be safe, or pass force=True only if you have
  verified the reduction is legitimate.
Loading existing graph...
Graph: 794784 nodes, 1766987 edges
Re-clustering...
Done - 27088 communities. GRAPH_REPORT.md and graph.json updated.
```

Exit code **0**. `graph.json` was **not** written — its mtime was unchanged and only 1.1% of nodes carried a `community`. The guard did its job; the final line contradicts it.

`.graphify_labels.json`, its `.sig`, and `GRAPH_REPORT.md` **were** written, for the clustering that was discarded. So a successful-looking run leaves labels and report describing a clustering the graph does not contain. Anything downstream keyed to community ids is then silently wrong.

We only caught it because our runbook says to verify community coverage after clustering rather than trust the exit code — that habit exists because this cost us a full clustering run once before.

## Suggested fix

Either is enough, both would be better:

1. When `to_json` returns falsy, say so and exit non-zero — `graph.json NOT written: refusing to overwrite (net -119 nodes)` — rather than printing `graph.json updated`.
2. Don't persist labels, `.sig` or `GRAPH_REPORT.md` when the graph write was declined, so the outputs stay consistent with each other.

## Second, separate finding: the -119 is unexplained

The guard's own explanation does not fit our case, and we could not account for the reduction:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Duplicate node ids in `graph.json` | **0** (794,903 nodes, 794,903 distinct, all `str`) |
| `networkx.node_link_graph(raw, edges="links")` | **794,903 nodes, 1,768,522 edges** — no loss |
| `graphify.paths.load_node_link_graph` | same call, so also lossless |
| `prune_dangling_edges` | removes edges only, never nodes |
| graphify's own report after "Loading existing graph..." | **794,784 nodes, 1,766,987 edges** |

So 119 nodes and 1,535 edges disappear between reading the file and reaching the writer, inside graphify, on a graph that plain networkx round-trips intact. We did not use `force=True`, because "verify the reduction is legitimate" is not something we could honestly claim.

Workaround, in case it helps anyone else: load the graph yourself and drive the public API — `load_node_link_graph`, `cluster`, `remap_communities_to_previous`, `label_communities_by_hub`, then `to_json(G, communities, path, community_labels=labels)`. The node count reaching the writer then equals the count on disk, the guard has nothing to fire on, and the output keeps graphify's exact format (`community`, `community_name`, `norm_label`). That produced 100% community coverage on all 794,903 nodes.

Also worth noting for anyone using `cluster-only` to refresh an existing store: it clusters from scratch with no reference to previous membership. Ours renamed 22,507 of 28,004 communities by hub. Community ids are what authored per-cluster content is keyed to, so that is a total loss of that content unless you pass the old membership through `remap_communities_to_previous` yourself. Driving the API with that step gave us 88% retention on the same change.

Versions: graphify 0.9.30, networkx 3.6.1, Python 3.13, macOS.

title: SQL FK-reference edges use referencing-file stem instead of resolving to the defining file, producing dangling edges across multi-migration schemas
body:
### Summary
When a SQL migration file has a foreign-key reference to a table defined in an *earlier* migration file, the extractor stamps the target node ID using the **referencing file's stem** instead of resolving to the table's actual defining file. This produces edges pointing at node IDs that don't exist anywhere in the extraction, showing up as dangling-endpoint edges in `graphify.diagnostics.diagnose_extraction`.

### Repro
Given two migrations:
```sql
-- 001_initial_schema.sql
create table public.profiles (id uuid primary key, ...);
```
```sql
-- 008_expansion_tables.sql
create table public.household_members (
  profile_id uuid references public.profiles(id),
  ...
);
```

The extractor correctly creates:
- `supabase_migrations_001_initial_schema_public_profiles` (the real `profiles` table node)

But the FK reference edge from `008_expansion_tables.sql` targets:
- `008_expansion_tables_public_profiles` (does not exist — wrong file stem)

instead of resolving to `supabase_migrations_001_initial_schema_public_profiles`.

### Impact
On a real project (24 SQL migration files, Supabase/Postgres), this produced **92 dangling edges** — every migration that FKs into a table defined in an earlier file is affected (observed in `004`, `005`, `008`, `013`, `018`, `021`, `022` referencing tables from `001` and `008`). All 92 are legitimate schema relationships; none are false edges — the extractor just can't resolve the correct target node ID across files.

### Expected behavior
The SQL extractor should maintain a project-wide symbol table (table name → defining file/node ID) built during the AST pass, and resolve `references public.<table>(...)` targets against that table rather than stamping the target ID with the local file's stem.

### Environment
- graphifyy 0.9.30
- `tree_sitter_sql` installed via `graphifyy[sql]`
- Reproduced via `graphify.diagnostics.diagnose_extraction(extraction, directed=False, root='.')` on a 24-file Supabase migrations folder

title: AST extractor misses some named exports, producing dangling imports_from edges
body:
### Summary
The TypeScript/JS AST extractor doesn't always emit a node for every named export in a file — sibling exports in the same file are inconsistently covered. When another file imports the missed export, the resulting `imports_from` edge has no valid target node, showing up as a dangling-endpoint edge in `graphify.diagnostics.diagnose_extraction`.

### Repro
`src/lib/constants.ts` exports two constants:
```ts
export const CREDIT_RULES = { ... }
export const DISCLAIMER_SHORT = "..."
```

The extractor creates a node for `CREDIT_RULES` (`src_lib_constants_credit_rules`) but **no node for `DISCLAIMER_SHORT`**, despite both being top-level named exports in the same file, extracted in the same pass.

Consumers (`src/components/Disclaimer.tsx`, `src/components/Footer.tsx`) that `import { DISCLAIMER_SHORT } from '@/lib/constants'` produce `imports_from` edges targeting a node ID that was never created.

The same pattern affects `src/content/site.ts`'s `COMPLIANCE_SCRIPT` export, imported by `src/app/hgc-credits/page.tsx` and `src/app/orientation/page.tsx` — both edges dangle for the same reason.

### Impact
Small in isolated scope (6 dangling edges observed on a ~190-file TS/TSX codebase), but any file with multiple named exports is at risk of silently dropping some of them, understating the real fan-out of a shared constants/content module in the graph.

### Expected behavior
Every top-level named export in a parsed file should get a node, regardless of how many other exports exist in the same file or what shape the export takes (string template literal, object literal, etc.).

### Environment
- graphifyy 0.9.30
- TypeScript/TSX source files (Next.js App Router project)
- Reproduced via `graphify.diagnostics.diagnose_extraction(extraction, directed=False, root='.')`

title: feat: add gleam support
Relative import of a subpackage emits an abs-path slug imports_from target to a non-existent <pkg>.py
body:
A relative import of a sibling subpackage emits an `imports_from` edge whose target is an absolute-path-derived slug for a non-existent `<subpackage>.py`, instead of resolving to the subpackage's `__init__.py`.

## Repro (minimal, deterministic on 0.9.32)

```
proj/pyproject.toml
proj/src/mypkg/__init__.py                 (empty)
proj/src/mypkg/api/__init__.py             (empty)
proj/src/mypkg/api/routes/__init__.py      (empty)
proj/src/mypkg/graphs/__init__.py          -> def build_graph(): return {}
proj/src/mypkg/api/routes/health.py        -> from ...graphs import build_graph
```

`graphify update proj --no-cluster` produces two edges out of `health`:

```
src_mypkg_api_routes_health --imports_from--> <abs-scan-slug>_proj_src_mypkg_graphs_py   # BUG: graphs.py does not exist
src_mypkg_api_routes_health --imports-->      src_mypkg_graphs_init_build_graph           # correct
```

`graphs/` is a package (`graphs/__init__.py`), so the `imports_from` target should be `graphs/__init__.py`, which is exactly what the companion `imports` edge already resolves to. Instead it is a slug for a `graphs.py` that is not on disk.

## Why it matters

The endpoint is derived from the absolute scan path, so it is machine-specific and differs per checkout path. Committed graphs then show a spurious diff on every rebuild from a different location, the same reproducibility problem as #2262 and #2273. In a real repo this fails a fail-closed host-path check.

## Notes

- Specific to the relative form. An absolute import of the same subpackage (`from mypkg import graphs`) resolves correctly to the package `__init__`, no slug.
- Seen on a real Python src-layout package where several `from ...graphs import X` / `from ...services import X` lines each produced one of these.

## Suggested fix

Resolve a relative subpackage import to the subpackage's `__init__.py` (match what the `imports` edge does), or canonicalize/drop the node-less endpoint rather than leaving the absolute-derived slug.

title: `cli.py::dispatch_command` is ~2,560 lines — offering to split it if that's wanted
body:
We run graphify against a fairly large internal codebase and did a complexity pass over our
checkout. One number stood out far beyond everything else, so we thought it was worth reporting
rather than sitting on.

### Measurement

- `graphify/cli.py` is 2,777 lines; `dispatch_command` starts at line 215 and runs to the end —
  roughly **2,560 lines in a single function**, an `if cmd == … / elif cmd == …` chain.
- Across `graphify/`: **86 blocks at radon rank D or worse, 24 at rank F.** `dispatch_command`
  is the most extreme single item by a wide margin.

### Why we're opening an issue rather than a PR

A 2,500-line refactor arriving unsolicited is unreviewable, and we're aware this is your core
dispatch path — there may well be reasons for the shape it has that aren't visible from
outside. We'd rather ask than assume.

### What we'd offer

If a split is wanted, the low-risk decomposition is a command→handler table: each `elif` branch
becomes a named function, `dispatch_command` becomes a lookup. It's mechanical, it preserves
behaviour exactly, and it can land in reviewable slices (one command group per PR) instead of
one large diff. Happy to do that work if you want it — and equally happy to leave it alone if
this is deliberate.

Related: #130 asks for platform config to move out of `__main__.py`, so some appetite for
CLI-layer cleanup seems to exist. We also have #1928 open with you (graphify impact) — same
spirit: offered, not pushed.

title: Feat/hdl vhdl tcl extractors
Noise-dir list matches bare build by name alone: real project directories named build/ are silently dropped from the scan
body:
### Summary

`_SKIP_DIRS` contains the bare string `"build"`, and `_is_noise_dir` matches it on directory name alone with no corroborating evidence. Any real project directory literally named `build/` is silently excluded from the scan, with no warning and no way to override it from `.graphifyignore` (an ignore file cannot un-ignore a hard-skipped dir).

Found while remediating #2478 on the same repo. Different mechanism, same failure signature: files missing from the graph, exit code 0, nothing printed.

### Environment

- graphify (`graphifyy`) 0.9.12
- Windows 11, Python 3.x

### The check

```python
def _is_noise_dir(part: str, parent: "Path | None" = None) -> bool:
    """Return True if this directory name looks like a venv, cache, or dep dir."""
    if part in _SKIP_DIRS:
        return True
    if part == "snapshots":
        # Prune only when it looks like an actual JS/Vitest snapshot dir.
        ...
```

`_SKIP_DIRS` includes `build`, alongside `dist`, `out`, `target`, `coverage`, `env`, and others with the same problem.

Note that `snapshots` immediately below it does the right thing: it verifies before pruning (checks the parent directory name, then looks for an actual `*.snap` file, and keeps the directory when it cannot confirm). `build` gets no such treatment.

### Repro

A directory literally named `build/` containing a real source file:

```
.claude/skills/build/SKILL.md      # a real skill definition, ~4 KB of markdown
```

Scan the repo root, then check the manifest:

```python
>>> import json
>>> m = json.load(open('graphify-out/manifest.json'))
>>> ks = list(m['files'].keys())
>>> len(ks)
2159
>>> len([k for k in ks if 'skills' in k.replace('\\', '/')])
725
>>> [k for k in ks if '/build/' in k.replace('\\', '/')]
[]
```

725 sibling skill files indexed, zero from `build/`. The file exists, is a supported type, is not gitignored from graphify's perspective, and is not reported anywhere in the run output.

Adding a `.graphifyignore` negation does not help, because the prune happens during the `os.walk` descent (`if not _is_noise_dir(d, dp)`), before ignore-file logic sees the path.

### Why this matters more than it looks

`build` is not an unusual name for real source. Bazel/Buck repos have `BUILD` files and build tooling directories; monorepos commonly have a first-party `build/` package; plugin and skill systems (our case) name a directory after the verb it implements. The user has no signal that anything was skipped, so the graph is quietly incomplete and every downstream answer drawn from it is quietly wrong.

### Requests

1. **Corroborate before pruning, the way `snapshots` already does.** For `build`/`dist`/`out`/`target`, only prune when there is supporting evidence: a sibling build manifest (`package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `Makefile`, `pom.xml`) in the parent, or the directory being gitignored, or containing predominantly compiled/minified artifacts. When it cannot be confirmed, keep it.
2. **At minimum, report hard-skipped directories** that contained supported source files, at normal verbosity. A one-line `skipped noise dir: .claude/skills/build (1 supported file)` turns a silent hole into a five-second fix.
3. **Let `.graphifyignore` negations override the hard-skip list.** An explicit `!build/` from the user should win over a name heuristic.

Happy to send a PR for (1) modelled on the existing `snapshots` logic if that shape is agreeable.

title: Feature: expose connected components and cycles — networkx is already bundled
body:
**Version:** graphify 0.9.33 (pipx, Python 3.14.5, Windows)

## The gap

graphify already builds a directed graph and already ships `networkx` 3.6.1, but never
calls its connectivity primitives. Searching the installed package (80 `.py` files):

| symbol | files containing it |
|---|---|
| `connected_component` | **0** |
| `strongly_connected` | **0** |
| `in_degree` / `out_degree` | **0** |
| `dijkstra` | **0** |
| `leiden` / `louvain` | 7 / 6 |
| `betweenness` | 2 |

So community detection and centrality are covered, but connectivity is not — even though
`nx.weakly_connected_components` and `nx.strongly_connected_components` would run on the
graph already in memory, with no new dependency and no LLM.

## Two questions this would answer

**1. Weakly connected components → orphaned code.**
Nodes that no path reaches from the rest of the project. Running this externally on a
graphify graph of a Next.js repo (229 nodes) surfaced a component of 3 containing a React
component that nothing imports, and an isolated script — neither visible from `god-nodes`
or from community labels, because both metrics describe nodes that *are* connected.

**2. Strongly connected components → circular dependencies.**
A cycle means no member can be read, tested or replaced on its own. On a markdown-heavy
repo the same external run found a 9-file cycle spanning docs and automation:

```
STATUS.md -> fila.yml -> fila.py -> POST_02.md -> PAUTA_01.md -> CONTA.md -> STATUS.md
```

Five of the six edges were `EXTRACTED`. This is the kind of finding an onboarding agent
benefits from, and `GRAPH_REPORT.md` is the natural place for it.

## Suggested shape

```
graphify components         # weakly connected; flags the ones with no source files
graphify cycles             # strongly connected components of size > 1
```

and a short section in `GRAPH_REPORT.md`:

```
Components: 7 (largest 150 nodes, 66%)
Circular dependencies: 0
```

## One caveat worth designing around

Config files distort the count. In the Next.js repo above, 4 of the 7 components were
`package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `eslint.config.mjs` and `postcss.config.mjs` — each parses
into its own tree with no edge to source code, so they read as "orphans" while being
nothing of the sort. A component containing no `file_type: code` node could be labelled as
config rather than counted as orphaned code.

## Context

This came out of building a small external layer that post-processes `graph.json` for
exactly these questions, and then checking whether graphify already answered them. It does
not, but it is one import away from doing so — the extraction quality is already there, and
these would be a thin analysis pass on top rather than new machinery.

Happy to send a PR if the direction is welcome.

title: Filename-only "potentially sensitive" filter silently drops design-token files (tokens.css, tokens.contract.json)
body:
## Problem

A filename-word denylist silently excludes files from the graph. It matches on the **name only** —
the content is never inspected — so design-system files called `tokens.css` / `tokens.contract.json`
are treated as credentials and dropped.

Discovered on a monorepo whose design tokens are generated artifacts with fixed names: the generated
`tokens.css` and the committed `tokens.contract.json` were both absent from the graph, announced by a
single line:

```
[graphify extract] 1 file(s) skipped as potentially sensitive (rename or move if wrongly flagged): tokens.css
```

## Repro (deterministic on 0.9.34)

```bash
mkdir case && cd case
for n in tokens token mytokens design-tokens palette secrets credentials; do
  echo ':root{ --a: #fff; }' > "$n.css"
done
echo 'def f(): return 1' > tokens.py
echo '{"a":1}' > tokens.json
echo '{"a":1}' > plain.json
graphify extract . --code-only --no-cluster --out /tmp/out --force
```

```
[graphify extract] found 2 code, 0 docs, 0 papers, 0 images
[graphify extract] 2 file(s) not classified (no supported extension or shebang), skipped: mytokens.css, palette.css
[graphify extract] 6 file(s) skipped as potentially sensitive (rename or move if wrongly flagged):
      credentials.css, design-tokens.css, secrets.css, token.css, tokens.css, tokens.json
```

## The rule, as observed

| file | outcome |
|---|---|
| `tokens.css`, `token.css`, `design-tokens.css`, `secrets.css`, `credentials.css`, `tokens.json` | **skipped as sensitive** |
| `mytokens.css`, `palette.css` | not matched |
| `tokens.py` | **not** matched |
| `plain.json` | indexed |

Three properties, all of which look unintended:

1. **Content is never read.** An empty file named `token.css` is skipped; a file named `palette.css`
   containing a real API key is not. The check cannot do what its message claims.
2. **The match is word-boundary aware, which makes it worse, not better.** `design-tokens` matches
   (separator-delimited word `tokens`), `mytokens` does not. So the *more* conventionally named a
   design-token file is, the more likely it is to be dropped.
3. **It is extension-dependent.** `tokens.py` survives; `tokens.css` and `tokens.json` do not. Same
   word, same content-blindness, different outcome. (Also note `.css` is not a supported code
   extension at all — `palette.css` came back "not classified" — yet `tokens.css` still went down the
   sensitive path, so the check runs ahead of classification.)

## Why the suggested remedy does not work

The warning says *"rename or move if wrongly flagged"*. For a **generated** artifact that is not
available: the name is fixed by the generator and asserted by a drift guard in CI. Renaming it to
please a scanner would break the build that produces it. In a design-system repo, `tokens.*` is close
to the single most likely filename to exist.

## Suggested fix

Any of these would resolve it; roughly in order of preference:

1. **Inspect content.** Gate the skip on an actual secret-shaped match (high-entropy string, known key
   prefixes, `PRIVATE KEY` armor). A `:root{}` block of hex colours is not that.
2. **Drop `token` from the name denylist**, or require it to co-occur with a content signal.
   `secret`/`credential`/`password` are far less ambiguous than `token`, which is ordinary vocabulary
   in design systems, tokenizers, parsers and lexers.
3. **Make it overridable** — honour a `.graphifyignore`-style allowlist, or add
   `--no-sensitive-filter`. Today there is no flag to opt out; I checked `--help`.
4. **Raise the reporting.** One line in the middle of extraction output is easy to miss for a file
   that then simply does not exist in the graph. If a file is excluded, it is worth being loud.

Happy to send a PR for (1) or (3) if you have a preference on shape.

## Environment

`graphifyy` 0.9.34, macOS (darwin 25.5.0), Python 3.12, `--code-only` (no LLM backend involved).

title: `query` silently infers a context filter from the wording of the question and collapses the result to the seed nodes
body:
Two related defects in `query`, both of which turn a good answer into an empty-looking one
without saying anything is wrong. Measured on **0.9.34** (PyPI package `graphifyy`), Windows,
Python 3.13. I checked the 0.9.35 diff and neither is fixed there — see the version note at
the end.

## 1. A context filter is inferred from the question's wording, opt-out rather than opt-in

With no `--context` given, `_resolve_context_filters` falls back to `_infer_context_filters`
(`graphify/serve.py`), which matches the question's tokens against `_CONTEXT_HINTS`:

```python
_CONTEXT_HINTS = (
    ("call", ("call", "calls", "called", "invoke", "invokes", "invoked")),
    ("import", ("import", "imports", "imported", "module", "modules")),
    ("field", ("field", "fields", "member", "members", "property", "properties")),
    ("parameter_type", ("parameter", "parameters", "param", "params", "argument", "arguments")),
    ("return_type", ("return", "returns", "returned")),
    ("generic_arg", ("generic", "generics", "template", "templates")),
)
```

These are ordinary English words. Anyone asking a question in a natural way will hit them —
"which **modules** handle X", "what does this **return**", "the **property** that stores Y".
The result is a filter the user never asked for.

### Self-contained repro

Build a tiny graph — 81 nodes, none of whose edges carry a `context` attribute (this is the
normal shape of an LLM-extracted graph; see part 2):

```python
import json, os
os.makedirs("graphify-out", exist_ok=True)
nodes = [{"id": "payment_gateway", "label": "PaymentGateway",
          "source_file": "payment.py", "source_location": "L1", "community": 0}]
links = []
for i in range(60):
    nid = "helper_%02d" % i
    nodes.append({"id": nid, "label": "Helper%02d" % i,
                  "source_file": "helper%02d.py" % i, "source_location": "L1", "community": 0})
    links.append({"source": "payment_gateway", "target": nid, "relation": "uses"})
    if i % 3 == 0:
        nid2 = "leaf_%02d" % i
        nodes.append({"id": nid2, "label": "Leaf%02d" % i,
                      "source_file": "leaf%02d.py" % i, "source_location": "L1", "community": 0})
        links.append({"source": nid, "target": nid2, "relation": "uses"})
json.dump({"directed": False, "multigraph": False, "graph": {},
           "nodes": nodes, "links": links},
          open("graphify-out/graph.json", "w"))
```

Then ask the same question twice, differing only by the word "modules":

```
$ graphify query "PaymentGateway setup"
Traversal: BFS depth=2 | Start: ['PaymentGateway'] | 81 nodes found

$ graphify query "which modules handle PaymentGateway setup"
Traversal: BFS depth=2 | Start: ['PaymentGateway'] | Context: import (heuristic) | 1 nodes found
```

Same seed, same graph, same day: **81 nodes -> 1 node**. The traversal is reduced to the seed
itself.

The same thing on our real prose graph (4139 nodes, 10043 edges), where the seeds happen to
differ slightly but the collapse is identical:

```
$ graphify query "Open Cloud API key scopes DataStore setup"
... | 524 nodes found

$ graphify query "which modules handle Open Cloud API key scopes"
... | Context: import (heuristic) | 8 nodes found
```

8 is exactly the number of seed nodes.

### Why this is worse than it looks

The output does say `(heuristic)`, and I appreciate that it is labelled. But the failure mode
is **indistinguishable from a correct negative answer**. A caller — human or agent — sees a
short, confident result and concludes the graph does not contain the information. Nothing warns
that a filter just removed 99 % of the candidate set. In our own query log the phrasing that
triggers this is uncommon but not rare: **11 of 336 logged queries** contain a trigger word.

### Request

Either:

* make the inference **opt-in** (a flag, or only when the question also parses as a
  relational query), or
* keep it opt-out but **warn when the inferred filter removes most of the candidate set** —
  e.g. if filtering drops more than some fraction of reachable nodes, print the unfiltered
  count alongside it, or fall back to the unfiltered traversal and note that the filter was
  discarded.

The second is probably enough. The information needed is already computed.

## 2. `--context` filters on an edge attribute that LLM-built graphs almost never have

This is why part 1 collapses so completely, and it is a defect on its own.

`_filter_graph_by_context` keeps an edge only when `data.get("context")` is in the filter set:

```python
def _filter_graph_by_context(G, context_filters):
    filters = set(_normalize_context_filters(context_filters))
    if not filters:
        return G
    H = G.__class__()
    H.add_nodes_from(G.nodes(data=True))
    ...
        for u, v, data in G.edges(data=True):
            if data.get("context") in filters:
                H.add_edge(u, v, **data)
    return H
```

All nodes are carried over but only matching edges are, so any unmatched value leaves an
edgeless graph and BFS cannot leave the seeds.

In our LLM-extracted graph, **4 of 10043 edges** carry a `context` attribute at all (all four
with the value `call`). Our edges do carry a `relation` attribute — `uses`, `defines`,
`documents` and so on — but nothing reads it here. So every possible `--context` value collapses
the traversal:

```
$ graphify query "<question>"                    -> 524 nodes found
$ graphify query "<question>" --context call     -> Context: call (explicit)  | 8 nodes found
$ graphify query "<question>" --context field    -> Context: field (explicit) | 8 nodes found
```

There is an unfortunate interaction with the truncation banner, which recommends exactly this:

```
[!] TRUNCATED: showing 46 of 524 nodes (~2000-token budget). The answer may be among the
478 cut nodes - raise the token budget (CLI: --budget) or narrow the query
(e.g. context_filter=['call'], or get_node for a specific symbol).
```

Following that advice on an LLM-built graph takes you from 46 useful nodes to 8.

### Request

Either document that `--context` only applies to AST-extracted graphs, or fall back to matching
the relation name when no edge in the graph carries a `context` attribute. The second would make
the flag do the useful thing users expect it to do.

## Version note

Measured on 0.9.34. In 0.9.35 `_infer_context_filters`, `_filter_graph_by_context`,
`_normalize_context_filters` and the `--context` CLI parsing are unchanged, so both defects
stand. Note that 0.9.35 **widens** the trigger set — `_CONTEXT_HINTS` gains `"caller"` and
`"callers"` under `call` — so part 1 fires on more phrasings there, not fewer. 0.9.35 also
changes seed selection for questions containing relational verbs (#2507), so the seed lists in
my examples may differ on that version; the collapse itself does not depend on which seeds are
chosen.

Happy to test a branch. We have a 4139-node LLM-extracted graph and a 188-file code-extracted
one, plus a log of 336 real queries I can replay to give you a before/after distribution.

title: Elixir: imports edges target a bare module id that matches no node — every cross-module import edge is silently dropped at build (2,586 of 19,337 on a 900-file project)
body:
## Summary

The Elixir extractor emits `imports` edges whose target is the **bare normalized module name**, while the module node it should point at is registered under a **path-prefixed id**. The two never match, so `build_from_json` drops every cross-module import edge.

On a real 900-file Elixir/Phoenix project this silently discarded **2,586 of 19,337 extracted edges (13%)** — the entire internal module dependency graph. Nothing warns; the build reports success and the graph looks plausible. It is only visible via `graphify diagnose multigraph`.

Python does not have this bug, so this is Elixir-specific (details below).

## Repro

Two files, one aliasing the other:

```elixir
# lib/demo/accounts.ex
defmodule Demo.Accounts do
  def list_users, do: []
end

# lib/demo/web.ex
defmodule Demo.Web do
  alias Demo.Accounts

  def index, do: Accounts.list_users()
end
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import collect_files, extract

res = extract(collect_files(Path("lib")), cache_root=Path("."))
ids = {n["id"] for n in res["nodes"]}
for e in res["edges"]:
    flag = "  <-- DANGLING" if e["target"] not in ids else ""
    print(f"{e['source']} --{e['relation']}--> {e['target']}{flag}")
```

Output (graphify 0.9.36):

```
NODES:
  lib_demo_accounts                        label= accounts.ex
  lib_demo_accounts_demo_accounts          label= Demo.Accounts
  lib_demo_accounts_demo_accounts_list_users
  lib_demo_web                             label= web.ex
  lib_demo_web_demo_web                    label= Demo.Web
  lib_demo_web_demo_web_index

EDGES:
  lib_demo_accounts --contains--> lib_demo_accounts_demo_accounts
  lib_demo_accounts_demo_accounts --method--> lib_demo_accounts_demo_accounts_list_users
  lib_demo_web --contains--> lib_demo_web_demo_web
  lib_demo_web --imports--> demo_accounts        <-- DANGLING
  lib_demo_web_demo_web --method--> lib_demo_web_demo_web_index
```

**Expected:** `lib_demo_web --imports--> lib_demo_accounts_demo_accounts`
**Actual:** target is `demo_accounts`, which matches no node, and the edge is dropped at build.

## Root cause

`graphify/extractors/elixir.py` builds the module node id and the import target id with different arities:

```python
# L119 — module node: stem IS included
module_nid = _make_id(stem, module_name)      # -> lib_demo_accounts_demo_accounts

# L154 — import target: stem is NOT included
tgt_nid = _make_id(module_name)               # -> demo_accounts
```

L154 cannot know the stem on its own, because the defining file is usually a *different* file. The per-file filter at L226 correctly lets the unresolved edge through so a later pass can fix it:

```python
clean_edges = [e for e in edges if e["source"] in seen_ids and
               (e["target"] in seen_ids or e["relation"] == "imports")]
```

…but no later pass ever does. The cross-file resolver registry in `extract.py` (~L3173) registers Swift, Python, Ruby, TypeScript, C++ and ObjC — **there is no Elixir resolver**, so `.ex`/`.exs` never gets a resolution pass and the exemption becomes a permanent leak.

That is also why Python is unaffected — the same repro in Python resolves correctly:

```
pkg_web --imports--> pkg_accounts_accounts     # valid
pkg_web_index --calls--> pkg_accounts_accounts # valid
```

## Suggested fix

Register an Elixir cross-file resolver that rewrites unresolved `imports` targets to the node id of the module with that name. Matching on the **normalized module name of module-level nodes** is exact and needs no heuristics — `normalize(label) == target`.

Worth stressing: matching on **id suffix** instead is not safe. I tried it first on the real project and it mis-resolved badly — a bare target like `application` (from `use Application`) latches onto any node whose id ends in `_application`, including function nodes such as `..._oauthapplications_update_application`. Exact module-name matching gave 382/382 unambiguous resolutions on the same corpus where suffix matching produced 7 wrong ones.

Endpoints with no matching module are genuinely external (stdlib and hex: `Logger`, `Application`, `Gettext`, `Ecto.Query`, `Phoenix.Component`, `Ash.Resource`). On the project above that was 86 distinct modules / 859 edges — small enough to emit as leaf stub nodes, which keeps "who imports `Ecto.Query` directly" answerable without vendoring `deps/`.

For reference, on the 900-file project the corrected resolution gave:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| dangling endpoint edges | 3,445 | 0 |
| graph edges | 13,156 | 16,578 |
| `Boundary.Accounts` degree | 75 | 199 |
| communities (Louvain) | 966 | 666 |

`Boundary.Accounts` was under-reported by 62%, and ~300 communities were spurious fragments that rejoined once their import edges existed. Because god-node ranking and community detection both run on the degraded edge set, the report's headline conclusions were wrong, not merely incomplete.

## Secondary observation

In the Elixir repro above, `Accounts.list_users()` produces **no `calls` edge at all** — `extract_elixir()` returns `raw_calls: []`, so cross-module calls are never recorded even before resolution. Python emits `pkg_web_index --calls--> pkg_accounts_accounts` for the equivalent code. This looks like the same missing-resolver gap plus an extractor gap; happy to file it separately if you'd prefer it tracked on its own.

## Environment

- graphify (graphifyy) 0.9.36, Python 3.13, Linux
- Corpus: 865 `.ex`/`.exs` + 39 `.js`, Elixir/Phoenix/Ash

title: fix(skill): --update no longer over-reports unchanged files (#2459)
body:
## Summary

`graphify --update` reported far more changed files than were actually modified. `detect_incremental` defaults to `kind="semantic"`, which treats every file whose `semantic_hash` is empty (AST-extracted only, never semantically chunked) as changed on every run. On a real monorepo this flagged 811 files after ~25 merged PRs when only 173 had actually changed, and each false positive was re-dispatched to a semantic extraction sub-agent at real model/token cost.

The update flow now passes `kind="ast"` at all 16 call sites -- the 14 platform `--update` runbooks (generated from the shared `tools/skillgen` fragment), plus the aider and devin monoliths -- so the changed set matches actual content changes. The `graphify extract` incremental scan keeps its semantic re-queue contract (files with empty `semantic_hash` re-extract), now passed explicitly instead of relying on the default. A sanctioned-diff predicate keeps the monolith roundtrip guard in sync with the new call shape, and a guard test locks the runbooks to `kind="ast"`.

Fixes #2459

## Validation

- `python -m tools.skillgen --check` -- 134 artifacts match committed output and `expected/` (no drift).
- `uv run pytest tests/test_skillgen.py tests/test_detect.py tests/test_extract_cli.py` -- 327 passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_incremental.py tests/test_office_incremental.py tests/test_watch.py tests/test_watch_manifest_location.py tests/test_build.py` -- 196 passed, 3 skipped.
- New `test_runbook_update_flows_pass_kind_ast` guard: every shipped `--update` runbook and fragment passes `kind="ast"` (red before the fix, green after).
- New `test_detect_incremental_kind_ast_ignores_empty_semantic_hash` premise test: ast mode reports unchanged files with empty `semantic_hash` clean; semantic mode still re-queues them.
