title: _semantic_id_remap() is not idempotent for same-named dir/file pairs — legacy bare-stem form re-matches an already-migrated id and grows a duplicate prefix on every pass
body:
**graphify version:** 0.9.4 (pinned local fork tag `0.9.4+colfix1`, branch `v8`)

---

### Root cause

`_semantic_id_remap()` (`graphify/build.py`) re-derives a non-AST node's id from its `source_file`, matching against `_old_file_stems()` (legacy pre-#1504 id forms) to migrate old short-form ids to the current full-path-stem canonical form.

The function is documented and expected to be idempotent (safe to run on an already-migrated graph), but it is not: for any `source_file` where the immediate parent directory shares a name with the file's own stem (e.g. `cache/cache.py`, or `memory/memory.db`), the freshly computed canonical stem is a compound of the two identical segments (`cache_cache`, `memory_memory`). One of the legacy forms checked by `_old_file_stems()` is the bare file stem alone (`cache`, `memory`) — which is a real string prefix of that compound canonical stem.

On the first migration pass this is harmless: the old short id (e.g. `cache_get`) correctly migrates to the new canonical id (`cache_cache_get`). But on a *second* pass over the now-migrated id, the same bare-stem legacy form (`cache`) is checked again, `cache_cache_get`.startswith(`cache_`) is still true (because the canonical stem itself happens to start with that legacy form), so the function treats the already-canonical id as if it still needed migrating and glues on another `cache_` prefix — producing `cache_cache_cache_get`. Every subsequent pass repeats this, growing the prefix without bound.

Concretely reproduced with a `~`-prefixed `source_file` (`~/memory/memory.db`): `_norm_source_file()`'s absolute-path guard uses `os.path.isabs()`, which returns `False` for a `~`-prefixed path (tilde expansion is a shell/`os.path.expanduser` concern, not something `isabs` performs), so the path is treated as project-relative rather than being skipped as unresolvable. The resulting stem (`memory` + `memory` → `memory_memory`) then collides with the bare-stem legacy form (`memory`) exactly as described above. This is the trigger that surfaced the bug in production, but tracing the code shows the underlying defect is general: it reproduces identically for a plain in-repo file with no `~` involved at all, wherever a directory and its file share a name.

In production this was masked, not fixed: a downstream compensating control (a composition-guard that restores from backup on any unexplained node-id disappearance) reset the corrupted ids every scheduled run, so the growing-prefix symptom never accumulated past one cycle's worth. That is a compensating control on our side, not a fix in graphify itself.

### Reproduction

```python
from graphify.build import _semantic_id_remap

# Same-named in-repo directory/file pair — no ~ involved
nodes = [{"id": "cache_get", "source_file": "cache/cache.py", "type": "code"}]
r1 = _semantic_id_remap(nodes, ".")
print(r1)  # {'cache_get': 'cache_cache_get'}  -- correct first-pass migration

migrated_id = r1["cache_get"]
nodes2 = [{"id": migrated_id, "source_file": "cache/cache.py", "type": "code"}]
r2 = _semantic_id_remap(nodes2, ".")
print(r2)  # {'cache_cache_get': 'cache_cache_cache_get'}  -- BUG: re-migrates an
           # already-canonical id, growing the prefix. Should be {} (stable).
```

The `~`-path variant that surfaced this in production:

```python
nodes = [{"id": "memory_db", "source_file": "~/memory/memory.db", "type": "concept"}]
r1 = _semantic_id_remap(nodes, ".")
print(r1)  # {'memory_db': 'memory_memory_db'}

migrated_id = r1["memory_db"]
nodes2 = [{"id": migrated_id, "source_file": "~/memory/memory.db", "type": "concept"}]
r2 = _semantic_id_remap(nodes2, ".")
print(r2)  # {'memory_memory_db': 'memory_memory_memory_db'}  -- BUG
```

### Fix applied (in our fork, `0.9.4+colfix1` branch `v8`)

Added an "already canonical" short-circuit at the top of the per-node loop in `_semantic_id_remap()`, mirroring the guard the sibling function `graph_has_legacy_ids()` already carries a few lines below it (`norm == new_stem or norm.startswith(new_stem + "_")`) — that function was already protected against this exact class of false-positive; `_semantic_id_remap()` was missing the equivalent guard:

```python
norm_nid = _normalize_id(nid)
if norm_nid == new_stem or norm_nid.startswith(new_stem + "_"):
    continue  # already canonical
new_id: str | None = None
for old_stem in _old_file_stems(rel):
    ...
```

This closes the general re-matching class (verified idempotent for both the same-named-directory case and the `~`-path trigger case) without touching the first-pass migration behaviour, `_norm_source_file()`, or any other caller.

A narrower fix scoped only to the `~`-path trigger (expanding `~` before the `os.path.isabs()` check in `_norm_source_file()`, and skipping remap if the path still doesn't resolve under `root`) was considered and rejected as insufficient on its own: it would have left the same-named-directory case — which needs no `~` at all — live and unpatched. The chosen fix addresses both.

Two regression tests added to `tests/test_build.py`:
- `test_semantic_rekey_second_pass_is_idempotent_on_tilde_path`
- `test_semantic_rekey_second_pass_is_idempotent_on_same_named_dir`

Full test suite run clean apart from four pre-existing, unrelated failures (environment `GEMINI_API_KEY` leakage into backend-detection tests, and an `openai`-client `max_retries` default assertion) — none touch `build.py`, `ids.py`, or `_semantic_id_remap`/`graph_has_legacy_ids`, and are reproducible on the pre-fix state too.

### Cross-reference

Related prior migration work: #1504 (silent cross-chunk ID collision), #1509 (stem-rule inconsistency between `llm.py` and the skill's `extraction-spec.md`). This is a distinct mechanism from both — a non-idempotent legacy-id migration re-match, not a chunking collision or a stem-rule divergence — but touches the same id-canonicalization area.

Happy to open a PR with the fix + tests above against this repo if useful.

title: JS/TS extractor produces a large number of dangling-endpoint edges for external imports + destructuring exports
body:
## Summary
On a 981-file Next.js/TS corpus, `diagnose_extraction` reported **1657 dangling-endpoint edges**. I isolated the root cause into two classes:

## Class 1 (1605/1657, 97%) — external package/builtin imports, by design
Every `imports_from` edge is kept even when its target isn't a valid node (the "clean edges" step in `extract.py` keeps `tgt in valid_ids or edge["relation"] in ("imports","imports_from","re_exports")`, assuming cross-file resolution will happen later). But for external packages (react, next, `prisma/client`, `node:crypto`, ...) that resolution never happens because the package source is outside the scanned corpus. The health-check reports this as if it were corruption, but it's expected/structural.

**Suggestion:** have the health-check count edges whose target uses the extractor's external-reference prefix (`ref_` in this version) separately from genuinely-local unresolved edges — "external (expected)" vs. "local (needs investigation)". Would cut a lot of noise from the signal.

## Class 2 (52/1657, 3%) — destructuring-export node-ID collision, a real limitation
A pattern like `export const { auth, handlers, signIn, signOut } = NextAuth(config)` (NextAuth v5's own recommended boilerplate) collapses to a single combined node (e.g. `stem_handlers_auth_signin_signout`). A file that imports just one of those names individually (`import { auth } from './auth'`) looks for `stem_auth` — which never matches. The same pattern shows up with next-intl's own recommended `createNavigation()` boilerplate.

**Suggestion:** have the destructuring-export pattern emit one node per exported name (all sharing the same source location) instead of one combined node, so single-name imports resolve correctly.

## My own workaround (happy to share the approach)
As a post-build step I added a lightweight "external" stub node for every `ref_*` target — in the extractor's own extraction schema, without patching `site-packages`. Result: dangling edges dropped from 1657 to 52 (all Class 2). It also made the graph more informative (external dependency surface is now visible). Could be a good candidate for a built-in `--stub-external-imports` flag.

title: JavaScript resolver links block-scoped object-shorthand variables to unrelated functions
Cannot extract any file from a pnpm package whose pnpm-workspace.yaml declares packages: ['.']
body:
### Summary

graphify skips every source file of a pnpm package whose `pnpm-workspace.yaml` declares
`packages: ['.']`, then fails the whole rebuild. The value is passed unchanged to
`Path.glob('.')`, which is never a valid pattern in Python.

### Environment

- graphify 0.8.16 (`uv tool install graphifyy`)
- Python 3.10.20, macOS arm64
- The underlying `pathlib` behaviour also holds on 3.9 and 3.13, with a *different* exception
  on 3.13 — see below

### Symptom

```
warning: skipped .../src/users/domain/users.service.ts (IndexError: tuple index out of range)
... x99
Nothing to update or rebuild failed — check output above.
[graphify watch] Rebuild failed: tuple index out of range
```

No `graph.json` and no `GRAPH_REPORT.md` are produced. In the affected monorepo, 99 of the
126 `.ts` files in the workspace package were skipped, and 0 in a sibling package that has no
`packages:` key. The 27 survivors are the files with no bare import — relative-only imports,
or none at all.

### Minimal reproduction

```
repro/
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml    # packages:
│                          #   - '.'
├── package.json           # {"name": "repro"}
├── a.ts                   # export const a = 1
└── b.ts                   # import { z } from 'zod'
```

```
graphify update repro
```

`b.ts` is skipped with `IndexError: tuple index out of range`; `a.ts` extracts fine.

**The import must be a bare specifier.** `import { a } from './a'` does *not* trigger it —
relative specifiers (and tsconfig-alias ones) short-circuit before workspace resolution, in
`_resolve_js_module_path` (l.295-315). Only a bare specifier reaches
`_resolve_workspace_import`. `zod` need not be installed.

The core of it, without graphify:

```python
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> Path('/tmp').glob('.')
IndexError: tuple index out of range       # Python <= 3.12
ValueError: Unacceptable pattern: '.'      # Python >= 3.13
```

### Root cause

`extract.py:229`, in `_load_workspace_packages()`:

```python
for pattern in _workspace_globs(root / "pnpm-workspace.yaml"):
    for package_dir in root.glob(pattern):      # <- line 229
```

`_workspace_globs` (l.199) keeps any non-empty value that does not start with `!`, so `'.'`
reaches `Path.glob()` intact. `pathlib` normalises `'.'` to zero pattern parts, then indexes
`pattern_parts[0]`.

Call chain:
`extract_js` → `_extract_generic` → `walk` → `_import_js` → `_resolve_js_import_target`
→ `_resolve_js_module_path` → `_resolve_workspace_import` → `_load_workspace_packages` → 💥

`packages: ['.']` is valid and fairly common pnpm — it means the workspace root *is* the
package. Every file carrying at least one bare import inside such a package dies.

### Why reports of this may not look alike

On Python >= 3.13 the same bug surfaces as `ValueError: Unacceptable pattern`, not
`IndexError`. Worth keeping in mind when triaging duplicates.

### Proposed fix

```python
for pattern in _workspace_globs(root / "pnpm-workspace.yaml"):
    candidates = [root] if pattern in (".", "./") else root.glob(pattern)
    for package_dir in candidates:
```

Returning `root` rather than skipping the pattern matters: a bare `try/except` around the glob
would remove the crash but silently drop the root package from the workspace map, so imports
of that package would stop resolving.

Verified on the affected repository: all 124 `.ts` files under the package's `src/` now extract
(99 of them previously failed), the root package resolves by name, and a full run over the
monorepo yields 1589 nodes / 3211 edges / 100% EXTRACTED with zero skips.

### Minor, unrelated observation

`graphify update` reports the failure as `[graphify watch] Rebuild failed: ...`, because
`_rebuild_code` lives in `watch.py` and serves both paths. It sends you looking at the git hook
or at watch mode. A path-specific prefix would save some time.

title: fix(php): consolidated PHP support — member-call resolution, use-import handling, node identity, cross-language isolation, query seeding (#1682, #2615)
body:
Fixes #2615. Fixes #1682.

## What this PR is

This PR contains all PHP-support and resolution work from the [`lawnstarter/graphify`](https://github.com/lawnstarter/graphify) fork, in one review unit. It replaces our seven open PRs: #2492, #2502, #2503, #2505, #2506, #2516, #2536. We close those seven with pointers to this PR.

One PR is easier to review than seven stacked PRs. Four of the seven had strict merge-order constraints (2492 → 2502 → 2505 → 2506). This PR has none: it is based on the current `v8` head (`50556ba`, v0.9.39) and is 0 commits behind.

The full defect report, with all corpus measurements, is #2615.

## Contents, in four groups

The CHANGELOG on this branch lists every change under one `## 0.9.40 (unreleased)` section, in the same four groups.

### Group A — PHP member-call resolution, cross-language isolation, import-edge repair
(previously PRs #2492, #2502, #2503, #2505, #2506)

- PHP instance-method calls on a typed receiver now resolve: `$this->prop->method()` (including promoted constructor params), typed locals and params, nullsafe `?->`, and `(new Service())->method()`. Declared types bind at INFERRED 0.8. Inline `new` binds at EXTRACTED 1.0 when the written namespace corroborates the class. This is the #1682 fix.
- Refuse-don't-guess policy: no edge for untyped, union, intersection, or DNF receivers; ambiguous short names; undeclared methods; chained or array receivers; rebound or shadowed locals; anonymous classes; `self`/`static`/`parent`.
- PHP 8.1 first-class callables emit `indirect_call`, not `calls`. The syntax creates a `Closure`; it does not transfer control flow.
- PHP `imports` edges keep the written FQN, alias, and kind (`use_kind` / `alias` / `target_fqn` metadata). Group-form `use function A\{f};` no longer claims `f` as a class name.
- A `use Vendor\Sdk\Client;` claim is honored. A claim that names no in-corpus class refuses (subtractive, `PhpNameResolver`). A claim that matches a declared FQN binds to it, including through renaming aliases (additive). The declared-FQN facts persist in `graph.json` (`_php_class_fqns`), so the bindings survive `graphify update`.
- All member-call resolvers and receiver-type indexes are language-scoped. A TypeScript call can no longer bind a Python class, and a foreign same-name class no longer suppresses the correct edge. One shared `_is_owned_definition` predicate keys off the per-resolver suffix tuple, so registration and scoping cannot drift.
- `imports` edges no longer die beside a same-stem foreign file (Python, Rust, Zig, Elixir, PowerShell, Pascal, Bash).

### Group B — natural-language query seeding
(previously PR #2516; follow-ups to #2507)

- The relational-verb demotion that upstream 0.9.35 shipped is restructured: the vocabulary is derived from `_CONTEXT_HINTS` and `_CONTEXT_FILTER_ALIASES` instead of a hardcoded list, and is a strict superset of it (62 words vs 29). The five upstream #2507 tests pass unchanged.
- A query term that the top-ranked seed's label already covers claims no extra guaranteed seed. Generic nouns stop dragging hub nodes into the traversal.
- A heuristically inferred context filter that reaches nothing beyond the seeds relaxes to an unfiltered traversal, with an explicit header note. An explicit `--context` filter is always honored.

### Group C — PHP node identity and lookup
(previously PR #2536, plus two sibling fixes that PR deferred because they needed #2492/#2502; those dependencies are inside this PR)

- `interface`, `trait`, and `enum` declarations mint canonical nodes, exactly as `class` does.
- Imports resolve from their own `target_fqn` edge metadata, so an import of a name only written as `Foo::class` no longer dangles.
- A sourceless stub can no longer shadow a real declaration in `explain`, and `affected` applies the same rule, so the two commands agree.
- `parent::` / `self::` / `static::` calls refuse instead of naming their scope as the callee.
- A property assigned in the constructor body from a typed parameter types the receiver (the pre-promotion Laravel idiom). The class-wide poisoning discipline applies: any other write to the property refuses the binding.

### Group D — resolution gaps closed on top of the above
(never proposed upstream before; they depended on groups A and C)

- A PHP function call (`name(...)`) never binds to a method or a class-like node cross-file. Only functions are plausible targets at a function-call site. The case-insensitive fallback is retried with the same refusal.
- A receiver typed by an `interface`, `enum`, or `trait` binds to that declaration's own method. Implementations are never guessed. The declared-FQN pre-scan now covers all four declaration kinds, which also closes a full-vs-incremental parity hole.
- `graphify query` and `shortest_path` prefer a sourced node over a sourceless stub on exact score ties, as `explain` and `affected` already do. Tie-break only; no live score changes.

## Measured evidence

All numbers are from real builds of a 46.4k-node (later 48.5k-node) PHP 8.3 / Laravel production corpus. Details and attribution per fix are in #2615 and in the CHANGELOG entries.

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `LeadHunterService` inbound `calls` edges (#1682 repro) | 0 | resolved, INFERRED 0.8 |
| Fabricated inbound `calls` on one test method from Laravel's `event()` helper | 848 | ~0 (documented same-file residual) |
| Fabricated inbound `calls` on one model accessor from `parent::` calls | 1,698 | 0 |
| Interface/trait/enum declarations with a real node | 0 of 291 | 291 |
| Dangling `imports` edges | ~19,000 | removed |
| "callers of ChargeCustomerService" (3 grep-verified callers) | 1 node, 0 of 3 | 128 nodes, 3 of 3 |
| "what code uses ChargeCustomerService to charge a customer" | 2,286 nodes, 0 of 3 | 138 nodes, 3 of 3 |
| Full-rebuild `calls` edge delta with the final fixes | — | −1,341 fabricated, +2,398 legitimate |
| Wrong-edge family from ignored `use` claims (lawnstarter#16) | 3 wrong edges | 0 (differential: 3 deleted, 0 added, 0 re-pointed) |

## Behavior changes

1. A same-file PHP call through a typed receiver moves from EXTRACTED to INFERRED (0.8). The old EXTRACTED label came from a bare-name match that could not see the type.
2. A PHP 8.1 first-class callable moves from `calls` to `indirect_call`. Consumers that filter on `relation == "calls"` will not see these edges. `affected` output is unchanged.
3. Methods of a PHP interface, trait, or enum move from file-scoped ids to type-scoped ids, and their labels gain the leading member dot. A full `graphify update .` lands this consistently. A hook-driven incremental rebuild against a pre-fix graph drops (never repoints) stale-id edges until the next full update.
4. `caller` / `callers` queries that strand on a class node now relax to an unfiltered traversal, with the header note `Context: call (heuristic; relaxed — no matches beyond seeds)`.

## Composition with upstream 0.9.36–0.9.39

The fork tracked upstream continuously. Two syncs (0.9.36/0.9.37 and 0.9.38/0.9.39) are merged into this branch, and the compositions were verified:

- `extractors/engine.py`: the member-call defer condition is `_python_defer or _java_defer or _php_defer or (…)`. The Python and PHP disjuncts are mutually exclusive by construction: each reads state assigned only inside its own `config.ts_module` branch.
- `extract.py`, ObjC receiver index: this branch keeps the fork's `_is_owned_definition` gate (strictly stronger than the source-file truthiness test upstream narrowed) AND adds upstream's `not _is_protocol_declaration`. Upstream's three new ObjC suites pass on this composition.
- `serve.py`: upstream's hardcoded relational-verb list is replaced by the derived superset (group B above). This is the one place the branch deliberately restructures upstream code; it absorbs all of upstream's vocabulary and its five tests pass unchanged.
- Upstream's TypeScript origin gate (#2553) and the fork's language-ownership gates compose because both only remove candidates. One fork fixture gained the `import` statement real TypeScript requires.

## Tests

- Full suite on this branch: **4,478 passed, 42 skipped, 0 failed** (with the optional `openai` extra installed; without it, 4 `test_ollama_retry_cap.py` tests fail on import, an environment condition #2516's evidence already documented). One labeling test (`test_label_communities_batches_when_over_batch_size`) is known-flaky — it also flakes at the clean upstream baseline, per #2503's evidence — and passes in isolation and in this run.
- Roughly 8,600 of the ~10,800 added lines are tests: 18 new test files, plus additions to `tests/test_watch.py`. Every positive resolution test carries a same-named decoy asserted to get no edge. Positive scenarios have mirrored full-build and incremental-rebuild assertions.
- Each fix landed on the fork red-first. The per-fix red/green evidence is on the fork PRs, linked from [lawnstarter/graphify#56](https://github.com/lawnstarter/graphify/issues/56).

## Migration

- The version bumps to 0.9.40. This rolls the version-namespaced AST cache, which is required: cache entries are keyed by content hash within the version namespace, so a same-version rebuild replays pre-fix facts.
- PHP corpora (and polyglot corpora) must run `graphify update .` once to shed the fabricated edges and gain the new ones.
- The serve-side changes (group B, and the sourced tie-breaks) need no rebuild.

## Known gaps, all deliberate refusals

- `parent::` / `self::` / `static::` calls resolve to nothing. Binding them needs a base-class-aware pass through `inherits`; a decided spec exists ([lawnstarter/graphify#58](https://github.com/lawnstarter/graphify/issues/58)). We can propose it as a follow-up after this PR.
- A method reached through a `use`d trait, or inherited from a cross-file parent class, gets no edge. Docblock types are not read.
- A `event(...)` call in the same file as a class that declares an `event()` method still binds in-file (documented residual; it never reaches the cross-file pass).
- One suspected defect was investigated and written off with measured probes: [lawnstarter/graphify#55](https://github.com/lawnstarter/graphify/issues/55) (zero corpus occurrences of the precondition; the wrong edge is unreachable end-to-end).

## Shape of the branch

66 commits of fork history (including the two upstream-sync merges) plus one packaging commit (consolidated CHANGELOG section, version 0.9.40, one docs correction). A squash merge gives one clean change if you prefer that. For per-fix review, each superseded PR body remains available, and each commit carries provenance to its fork PR.

title: A single extraction emits `source_file` with mixed path separators (`src\lib\content.ts` and `src/pages/index.astro` in the same output) on Windows
body:
**Labels:** bug, windows, extract, node-identity **Version:** 0.9.38 (commit `10ad921`) **Environment:** Windows 11, Python 3.13.6 ## Summary When `extract()` is handed **relative** paths, the `source_file` written onto nodes keeps the native separator for some extractors and is normalised to POSIX for others — inside one extraction run. The graph then contains two spellings of the same directory layout, which is the fragmentation #683 described. ## Steps to reproduce ``` project/ src/lib/content.ts export function getPosts() { return []; } src/pages/index.astro --- import { getPosts } from '../lib/content'; const posts = getPosts(); ---

{posts.length}

``` Using the module's own documented entry point, with relative arguments: ``` $ python -m graphify.extract src/lib/content.ts src/pages/index.astro ``` ## Actual behavior ``` "id": "lib_content", "source_file": "src\\lib\\content.ts" "id": "lib_content_getposts", "source_file": "src\\lib\\content.ts" "id": "pages_index", "source_file": "src/pages/index.astro" "id": "src_pages_index_posts", "source_file": "src/pages/index.astro" ``` Two separator conventions in one document. The `.ts` nodes use `\`, the `.astro` nodes use `/`. ## Expected behavior Every `source_file` is the canonical root-relative **POSIX** form, matching what the CLI already produces. For contrast, the same project through the normal CLI path is correct: ``` $ python -m graphify extract . ... "id": "src_a", "source_file": "src/a.py" # POSIX, consistent ``` and passing an explicit `root` is also correct: ```python extract(paths, root=Path(".").resolve()) # source_file = "src/lib/content.ts" and "src/pages/index.astro" -- both POSIX ``` So the canonical behaviour exists; the relative-input path just misses the normalisation. ## Impact `source_file` is compared as a **string** in several places, so the two spellings are different files as far as graphify is concerned: - `build._norm_source_file` / `_abs_identity` keying - `build._build_prune_sets` / `_derive_prune_root` (the `prune_sources` no-op class of #1151, #2446) - `analyze.find_import_cycles`, which matches `data["source_file"]` against `G.nodes[...]["source_file"]` by equality — a backslash node never matches a POSIX edge - dedup and the semantic-cache key path (#2314) ## Reachability Reachable from the documented `python -m graphify.extract ...` entry point (`graphify/extract.py:6513-6523`), which calls `extract(paths)` with **no** `root`, and from any library caller following `ARCHITECTURE.md` (see issue_9.md — that document advertises `extract(path)` as the public API). The primary `graphify extract` CLI passes `root` and is **not** affected. ## Root cause The `source_file` value is taken from the input path as given, and only the explicit-`root` branch runs it through the POSIX normalisation. The inferred-root fallback (`graphify/extract.py:5197-5211`) computes a root but the per-extractor `source_file` assignment is not uniformly `as_posix()`-normalised — the `.astro` extractor happens to normalise, the shared `jsts` path does not. ## Suggested fix Normalise once, centrally, in the `extract()` post-pass that already walks every node to canonicalise IDs — rather than in each extractor: ```python for n in nodes: sf = n.get("source_file") if sf: n["source_file"] = PurePath(sf).as_posix() ``` That is the single choke point all extractors route through, so it also covers the ones not exercised here. ## Collateral evidence `tests/test_astro_import_ids.py::test_astro_relative_inputs_keep_canonical_ids` fails on Windows on a clean checkout for exactly this reason: ``` assert 'src\\lib\\content.ts' == 'src/lib/content.ts' ``` ## Related - #683 (CLOSED) — "path-separator inconsistency splits same file into 2 components". Same class, resurfaced on a different code path. - #2259 (OPEN) — `source_file` absolute on some runs, relative on others. Adjacent but distinct: this report is about the *separator*, within a single run.

title: GRAPH_REPORT.md header embeds the generator's absolute host path (same class as #2598)
body:
`GRAPH_REPORT.md`'s generated header embeds the absolute path of the machine that built it:

```
# Graph Report - /Users/<user>/dev/apps/<project>  (2026-08-03)
```

Source is `graphify/report.py:104`:

```python
f"# Graph Report - {root}  ({today})",
```

`root` is interpolated as given, so the header reflects whatever was passed on the command line: running `graphify update .` from inside the project yields `# Graph Report - .`, while passing an absolute root bakes the full host path into the file.

This is the same class as #2598, just fixed for `graph.html`'s `<title>`. `GRAPH_REPORT.md` is a tracked artifact in practice — of six repos here, four commit it, and one of those carries an absolute `/Users/...` path in its committed blob. The result is that the same graph produces different bytes on different machines, and the build machine's directory layout ends up in git history.

Suggested fix, mirroring #2598: prefer a project-relative label or the directory basename rather than interpolating `root` raw.

Notes for triage:
- #777 (closed) covered `manifest.json`, `.graphify_root` and `cache/ast/*.json`, but explicitly not `GRAPH_REPORT.md`.
- PR #778's title reads "use project-relative paths in manifest.json and GRAPH_REPORT.md", but its diff touches only `graphify/__main__.py` and `graphify/detect.py` — it never touches `report.py`, so the report header is not actually covered by it. That PR is also currently conflicting and last updated 2026-05-23.

Observed on 0.9.40.

title: Astro frontmatter variable nodes do not share their file node's ID stem, and can embed the absolute on-disk path in the node ID
body:
**Labels:** bug, extract, astro, node-identity **Version:** 0.9.40 ## Summary `extract_astro()` mints nodes for frontmatter variables using a different ID recipe than the one used for the enclosing file node. As a result: 1. The symbol node does **not** carry the file node's stem as a prefix, breaking the `_` convention the build layer relies on. 2. When the path handed to `extract()` is absolute and no `root` is passed, the **full absolute filesystem path** is baked into the symbol node's ID — the leak class of #1789 / #2197, still reachable in 0.9.38. ## Steps to reproduce `src/pages/index.astro`: ```astro --- import { getPosts } from '../lib/content'; const posts = getPosts(); ---

{posts.length}

``` ### 1. Stem mismatch (relative input) ```python extract([Path('src/lib/content.ts'), Path('src/pages/index.astro')]) ``` ``` id=lib_content # file node for content.ts id=lib_content_getposts # symbol -- correctly prefixed id=pages_index # file node for index.astro id=src_pages_index_posts # symbol -- NOT prefixed with "pages_index" ``` The file node is `pages_index` (2-component stem) but its own frontmatter variable is `src_pages_index_posts` (3-component). They no longer share a prefix. ### 2. Absolute path leak (absolute input, no root) ```python extract([Path('src/pages/index.astro').resolve()]) ``` ``` id=index # file node -- fine id=c_users_asus_appdata_local_temp_claude_c_users_asus_desktop_os_gra phify_accccdec_07ee_4c98_8664_8b2a39362228_scratchpad_astro_src_pa ges_index_posts # symbol -- LEAK ``` Note both nodes come from the *same* file: the file node was correctly anchored to `index`, the variable node was not anchored at all. ## Expected behavior The variable node should be `pages_index_posts` (case 1) and `index_posts` (case 2) — always `_`, never containing the absolute path. ## Reachability Case 1 is reachable from `python -m graphify.extract src/pages/index.astro ...` (`graphify/extract.py:6523` calls `extract(paths)` with no `root`) and from any library caller. Case 2 needs absolute inputs whose inferred common root sits below the project root — e.g. `extract([Path('/abs/src/pages/index.astro')])`, a single-file call. Passing an explicit `root` produces correct IDs in both cases: ```python extract(paths, root=Path('.').resolve()) # -> src_lib_content, src_lib_content_getposts, src_pages_index, src_pages_index_posts ``` so the main `graphify extract` CLI is **not** affected. This is a library-API / module-entry-point defect. ## Impact - `build._semantic_id_remap` and `graph_has_legacy_ids` relate a symbol to its file with `norm_nid.startswith(new_stem + "_")` (`build.py:630`, `build.py:1057`). A symbol that does not carry its file's stem is invisible to that logic and never migrates. - The `contains` edge still connects them, but ID-based reconciliation (dedup, incremental re-key, cache replay) treats them as unrelated. - Case 2 makes `graph.json` non-portable and leaks the local username. ## Suggested fix `extract_astro()` (`graphify/extract.py:1575`) should mint frontmatter symbol IDs from the same anchored stem the file node uses — i.e. reuse `_make_id(_file_stem(rel), name)` with the already-computed relative path, rather than deriving from the raw input path. The safest version is to have the `extract()` id-remap post-pass assert the invariant, so any extractor that drifts is caught: ```python # post-pass sanity: every symbol node must sit under its file node's stem assert sym_id.startswith(file_stem + "_"), (sym_id, file_stem) ``` ## Related - #1789 (CLOSED) — absolute scan path embedded in file/dir/project node IDs. This is the residual case for astro *symbol* nodes. - #2197 (CLOSED) — same leak class via `source_file`.

title: C#: members inside `#if` / `#else` blocks produce no nodes, and calls to them produce no edges
body:
## Summary

Any C# member declared inside a preprocessor conditional (`#if`, `#else`, `#elif`) is absent
from the graph. No node is created for it, and call sites that target it produce no `calls`
edge either — the call simply disappears.

This is not about picking the "wrong" branch: **neither** branch is extracted. A type whose
members are all guarded by `#if` ends up as a class node with no methods at all, so nothing
can ever point at those members.

Conditional compilation is common in multi-targeted libraries (`#if NET8_0_OR_GREATER`,
`#if NETFRAMEWORK`, `#if DEBUG`), so this silently removes real API surface from the graph.

## Reproducer

Two files, no dependencies, `net8.0`. `dotnet build -c Debug` → 0 warnings, 0 errors, so this
is not a case of invalid C#.

`Helper.cs`

```csharp
namespace Probe.Lib;

public static class Gated
{
    // control case: outside any preprocessor directive
    public static void Outside(string a) { }

#if NET8_0_OR_GREATER
    public static void InsideIf(string a) { }
#else
    public static void InsideElse(string a) { }
#endif

#if DEBUG
    public static void InsideDebug(string a) { }
#endif
}
```

`Caller.cs`

```csharp
namespace Probe.Lib;

public static class Caller
{
    public static void Drive()
    {
        Gated.Outside("x");
        Gated.InsideIf("x");
        Gated.InsideDebug("x");
    }
}
```

Run `graphify extract <dir>` on the directory holding the two `.cs` files.

**Expected:** member nodes for `Outside`, `InsideIf`, `InsideDebug` (and arguably
`InsideElse`), and three `calls` edges from `Drive`.

**Actual:**

```
member nodes: ['.Drive()', '.Outside()']
calls edges:  .Drive() -> .Outside()          (1 of 3)
```

`InsideIf`, `InsideElse` and `InsideDebug` have no node, and the two calls to them are
missing. The `Gated` class node exists and carries only `.Outside()`.

## Version span

Measured with the same reproducer on **0.9.8, 0.9.20, 0.9.34 and 0.9.39** — byte-identical
result in all four (2 member nodes, 1 `calls` edge). This is a long-standing gap, not a
regression in a recent release.

## Impact in a real code base

Counted across 8 separately extracted C# code bases (roughly 10 000 `.cs` files),
**not sampled**:

* Method declarations that sit below a preprocessor directive in the syntax tree: **233**
* Of these, **at least 99 have no member node in the graph.**

Method: for every `.cs` file in each graph that contains `#if`, the file is parsed with
tree-sitter and every `method_declaration` whose ancestors include a `preproc_*` node is
checked against the member nodes recorded for that file. The check matches on the member
**name**, so a guarded method whose name also occurs outside the block counts as "present" —
99 is therefore a **lower bound**, not an exact figure.

A concrete consequence from that code base: a public static helper class exposes its `Setup`
entry point only inside `#if NET8_0_OR_GREATER` / `#else`. The class node exists and carries
its nine unguarded members, but `Setup` is absent — so the five call sites that invoke it can
never be connected to it, and "who calls `Setup`?" is unanswerable.

## Notes on what is *not* claimed here

* No claim about which branch *should* win. Extracting the members of every branch would
  already be a large improvement over dropping all of them; picking a branch by defined
  symbols is a separate design question.
* The cause was not traced in the extractor source. The reproducer localises the behaviour,
  nothing more.
* Non-method members (properties, fields, nested types) inside conditionals were not
  examined; the count above covers `method_declaration` only.

title: `export wiki` Audit Trail double-counts intra-community edges, systematically understating the AMBIGUOUS share
body:
**Labels:** bug, export, wiki, reporting
**Version:** 0.9.40

## Summary

Every community article ends with an "Audit Trail" section reporting the
EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS split of that community's edges. The counting loop visits
each edge once **per endpoint inside the community**, so:

- an edge with **both** endpoints in the community is counted **twice**
- an edge crossing out of the community is counted **once**

Since intra-community edges are overwhelmingly the high-confidence `EXTRACTED` ones (that is
what makes a community a community) and cross-community edges are disproportionately the
uncertain ones, the reported percentages are biased *towards* confidence in exactly the
direction that matters least for a reviewer.

`AMBIGUOUS` is documented in `ARCHITECTURE.md` as "flagged for human review", so this
under-reports the review burden.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
import networkx as nx
from graphify.wiki import _community_article

G = nx.Graph()
for n in ['a', 'b', 'c', 'x']:
    G.add_node(n, label=n, source_file='f.py')

G.add_edge('a', 'b', relation='calls', confidence='EXTRACTED')   # intra
G.add_edge('b', 'c', relation='calls', confidence='EXTRACTED')   # intra
G.add_edge('c', 'x', relation='calls', confidence='AMBIGUOUS')   # cross

article = _community_article(
    G, 0, ['a', 'b', 'c'], 'Core', {0: 'Core', 1: 'Other'},
    None, {'a': 0, 'b': 0, 'c': 0, 'x': 1}, {},
)
print(article[article.index('## Audit Trail'):])
```

## Actual behavior

```
## Audit Trail

- EXTRACTED: 4 (80%)
- INFERRED: 0 (0%)
- AMBIGUOUS: 1 (20%)
```

There are only **3** edges. `EXTRACTED: 4` counts two edges twice.

## Expected behavior

```
- EXTRACTED: 2 (67%)
- INFERRED: 0 (0%)
- AMBIGUOUS: 1 (33%)
```

## Root cause

`graphify/wiki.py:77-82`:

```python
conf_counts: Counter = Counter()
for nid in nodes:
    for neighbor in G.neighbors(nid):
        ed = edge_data(G, nid, neighbor)
        conf_counts[ed.get("confidence", "EXTRACTED")] += 1
total_edges = sum(conf_counts.values()) or 1
```

Iterating `nodes × neighbors` visits the pair `(a, b)` once as `a→b` and again as `b→a` when
both are in `nodes`. Nothing deduplicates the unordered pair.

## Suggested fix

Count each edge once by normalising the endpoint pair:

```python
conf_counts: Counter = Counter()
member = set(nodes)
seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
for nid in nodes:
    for neighbor in G.neighbors(nid):
        key = (nid, neighbor) if nid <= neighbor else (neighbor, nid)
        if key in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(key)
        conf_counts[edge_data(G, nid, neighbor).get("confidence", "EXTRACTED")] += 1
total_edges = sum(conf_counts.values()) or 1
```

(`member` is not strictly needed for the fix, but if the intent is "edges belonging to this
community" rather than "edges touching it", the cross-community ones should be excluded too —
worth confirming which is meant, since the section sits under a community heading.)

## Note on a nearby counter

`_cross_community_links` (`graphify/wiki.py:51-59`) is **not** affected: a cross-community
edge has only one endpoint in `nodes`, so it is naturally counted once.

## Related

- #2597 (OPEN), #2386 (OPEN), #2006 (OPEN) — other `export wiki` defects; none covers the
  audit-trail arithmetic.

title: `ARCHITECTURE.md` documents six functions that do not exist and the wrong signature for `extract()`
body:
**Labels:** bug, docs
**Version:** 0.9.40

## Summary

The "Module responsibilities" table in `ARCHITECTURE.md` is the entry point for anyone using
graphify as a library (and for agents, which `AGENTS.md` directs at the docs first). Six of
its sixteen documented functions do not exist, and the one signature it gives in prose is
wrong.

## Steps to reproduce

```python
import importlib

spec = [
    ('graphify.detect', 'collect_files'),   ('graphify.extract', 'extract'),
    ('graphify.build', 'build_graph'),      ('graphify.cluster', 'cluster'),
    ('graphify.analyze', 'analyze'),        ('graphify.report', 'render_report'),
    ('graphify.export', 'export'),          ('graphify.callflow_html', 'write_callflow_html'),
    ('graphify.ingest', 'ingest'),          ('graphify.cache', 'check_semantic_cache'),
    ('graphify.cache', 'save_semantic_cache'), ('graphify.security', 'validate_url'),
    ('graphify.validate', 'validate_extraction'), ('graphify.serve', 'start_server'),
    ('graphify.watch', 'watch'),            ('graphify.benchmark', 'run_benchmark'),
]
for mod, fn in spec:
    m = importlib.import_module(mod)
    print(('OK     ' if hasattr(m, fn) else 'MISSING'), f'{mod}.{fn}')
```

## Actual behavior

```
MISSING graphify.detect.collect_files
OK      graphify.extract.extract
MISSING graphify.build.build_graph
OK      graphify.cluster.cluster
MISSING graphify.analyze.analyze
MISSING graphify.report.render_report
MISSING graphify.export.export
OK      graphify.callflow_html.write_callflow_html
OK      graphify.ingest.ingest
OK      graphify.cache.check_semantic_cache
OK      graphify.cache.save_semantic_cache
OK      graphify.security.validate_url
OK      graphify.validate.validate_extraction
MISSING graphify.serve.start_server
OK      graphify.watch.watch
OK      graphify.benchmark.run_benchmark
```

Additionally, the pipeline diagram and table give `extract()` as `extract(path)` —
"file path → `{nodes, edges}` dict". The real signature takes a **list**:

```python
>>> from graphify.extract import extract
>>> extract(Path("a.py"))
TypeError: 'WindowsPath' object is not iterable
```

It is `extract(paths: list[Path], root=None, ...)`.

## Expected behavior

The table names functions that exist, with correct signatures.

## Actual names (for the fix)

| Documented | Actual |
|---|---|
| `detect.collect_files(root)` | `detect.detect(root)`; `collect_files` lives in `graphify.extract` |
| `extract.extract(path)` | `extract.extract(paths: list[Path], root=None, ...)` |
| `build.build_graph(extractions)` | `build.build(...)` / `build.build_from_json(...)` |
| `analyze.analyze(G)` | no single entry point — `god_nodes`, `surprising_connections`, `suggest_questions`, `graph_diff`, `find_import_cycles` |
| `report.render_report(G, analysis)` | `report.generate(...)` |
| `export.export(G, out_dir, ...)` | `export.to_json` / `to_wiki` / `to_cypher` / `to_html` … |
| `serve.start_server(graph_path)` | not present under that name |

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

The `root=` parameter that `ARCHITECTURE.md` omits from `extract()` is exactly the one whose
absence produces the defects in issue_4.md and issue_5.md — a caller following this document
would call `extract(paths)` with no root and silently get non-canonical `source_file` values
and absolute paths baked into node IDs. The doc is steering library users onto the buggy path.

## Suggested fix

Regenerate the table from the actual public surface, and add a docs test that imports each
documented symbol so the table cannot rot again:

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("mod,fn", _parse_architecture_table())
def test_architecture_table_symbols_exist(mod, fn):
    assert hasattr(importlib.import_module(mod), fn)
```

title: The `#2126` shell-allowlist regression tests pass vacuously on Windows — `_shell_verdict` mangles the glob before bash ever sees it
body:
**Labels:** bug, tests, windows, security-testing
**Version:** 0.9.40
**Environment:** Windows 11, Git Bash 5.2.37, Python 3.13.6

## Summary

`tests/test_hooks.py` guards the post-commit hook's interpreter allowlist — the fix for
#2126, and the guard that stops `;`, backticks and `$(...)` reaching a shell. On Windows the
helper that runs the glob passes the pattern through `subprocess` as an argv element, and
Windows argv quoting rewrites the backslashes inside the bracket expression. bash receives a
**different** pattern, one that matches nothing.

Consequences, both bad in opposite directions:

- `test_python_detect_allowlists_still_reject_shell_metacharacters` **fails** (4 params) —
  a false alarm claiming the allowlist accepts `foo;rm -rf /`.
- `test_file_path_allowlist_accepts_windows_backslash_path` and
  `test_shebang_allowlist_accepts_windows_backslash_path` **pass vacuously** — the pattern
  matches nothing, so "ACCEPTED" is guaranteed regardless of what the allowlist says. The
  #2126 regression test provides no coverage on the platform #2126 was about.

**The shipped hook is correct.** I verified it separately. This is purely a test-harness
defect — but one that disables a security regression test on the affected platform.

## Steps to reproduce

```
$ pytest tests/test_hooks.py -q -k allowlist
```

```
FAILED tests/test_hooks.py::test_python_detect_allowlists_still_reject_shell_metacharacters[foo;rm -rf /]
FAILED tests/test_hooks.py::test_python_detect_allowlists_still_reject_shell_metacharacters[foo`id`]
FAILED tests/test_hooks.py::test_python_detect_allowlists_still_reject_shell_metacharacters[foo$(id)]
FAILED tests/test_hooks.py::test_python_detect_allowlists_still_reject_shell_metacharacters[foo$IFS]
E   AssertionError: _FROM_FILE="" allowlist wrongly accepted dangerous input 'foo;rm -rf /'
```

### Demonstrating that the harness, not the hook, is wrong

Through `_shell_verdict`'s `subprocess.run([...])` path, **every** input is ACCEPTED — even
`/usr/bin/python3`, which the allowlist must accept, and `foo;rm -rf /`, which it must
reject. A pattern that never matches anything:

```
'foo;rm -rf /'                        -> ACCEPTED
'foo`id`'                             -> ACCEPTED
'foo$(id)'                            -> ACCEPTED
'C:\Users\u\.venv\Scripts\python.exe' -> ACCEPTED
'/usr/bin/python3'                    -> ACCEPTED
```

Writing the *same* case arm to a `.sh` file and running `bash case_test.sh <input>` — which
is how the hook actually executes — gives the correct answers:

```
$ cat case_test.sh
case "$1" in
  *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.@:\\-]*) echo REJECTED ;;
  *) echo ACCEPTED ;;
esac

foo;rm -rf /                          REJECTED
foo`id`                               REJECTED
foo$(id)                              REJECTED
foo$IFS                               REJECTED
C:\Users\u\.venv\Scripts\python.exe   ACCEPTED
/usr/bin/python3                      ACCEPTED
C:/Users/u/python.exe                 ACCEPTED
```

Both the #2126 property (Windows paths accepted) and the injection property (metacharacters
rejected) hold.

## Root cause

`tests/test_hooks.py:463-473`:

```python
def _shell_verdict(pattern: str, candidate: str) -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["bash", "-c", f'case "$1" in\n{pattern}) echo REJECTED ;;\n*) echo ACCEPTED ;;\nesac', "_", candidate],
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
```

On Windows, `subprocess` has no `execve`; the argument list is joined into a single command
string by `subprocess.list2cmdline`, whose rules double backslashes that precede a quote and
otherwise pass them through. The pattern contains `\\` inside a bracket expression, so what
`bash.exe` parses is not what was passed. `assert result.returncode == 0` does not catch it,
because a mangled-but-still-valid `case` arm exits 0.

## Suggested fix

Write the snippet to a file and invoke `bash script.sh <candidate>` — no shell-metacharacter
payload transits argv:

```python
def _shell_verdict(pattern: str, candidate: str, tmp_path) -> str:
    script = tmp_path / "case_test.sh"
    script.write_text(
        f'case "$1" in\n  {pattern}) echo REJECTED ;;\n  *) echo ACCEPTED ;;\nesac\n',
        encoding="utf-8", newline="\n",
    )
    result = subprocess.run(["bash", str(script), candidate],
                            capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    return result.stdout.strip()
```

This also matches how the hook runs in production (a script file read by bash), so the test
exercises the real code path.

To stop the vacuous-pass failure mode returning, add a control assertion to the accept tests:

```python
# sanity: the pattern must actually be capable of rejecting something,
# otherwise an ACCEPTED verdict proves nothing
assert _shell_verdict(pattern, "foo;rm -rf /", tmp_path) == "REJECTED"
```

## Related

- #2126 (CLOSED) — the fix these tests were written to guard.

title: `test_detect_surfaces_unreadable_dir_instead_of_silent_skip` calls `os.geteuid()`, which does not exist on Windows
body:
**Labels:** bug, tests, windows, good first issue
**Version:** 0.9.40

## Summary

The test uses `os.geteuid()` to skip itself when running as root (a `chmod 000` directory is
still readable by root, so the test would be meaningless). `os.geteuid` is POSIX-only, so on
Windows the guard itself raises before the test can decide anything.

## Steps to reproduce

```
$ pytest tests/test_detect.py::test_detect_surfaces_unreadable_dir_instead_of_silent_skip -q
```

## Actual behavior

```
    def test_detect_surfaces_unreadable_dir_instead_of_silent_skip(tmp_path, capsys):
        import os
>       if os.geteuid() == 0:
           ^^^^^^^^^^
E       AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'geteuid'. Did you mean: 'getpid'?

tests\test_detect.py:2453: AttributeError
```

## Expected behavior

Skipped on Windows. The test's premise — a directory made unreadable with `chmod 000` — does
not hold there either: Windows ignores POSIX mode bits, so even with a working `geteuid`
shim the directory would remain readable and the test would fail on its real assertion.

## Root cause

`tests/test_detect.py:2453`. `os.geteuid` is defined only on Unix.

## Suggested fix

Guard on the capability rather than adding a shim, so the test is skipped for both reasons it
cannot run on Windows:

```python
@pytest.mark.skipif(
    not hasattr(os, "geteuid"),
    reason="POSIX-only: relies on chmod 000 being enforced and on geteuid()",
)
def test_detect_surfaces_unreadable_dir_instead_of_silent_skip(tmp_path, capsys):
    if os.geteuid() == 0:
        pytest.skip("root bypasses chmod 000")
    ...
```

A repo-wide grep shows this is the only occurrence, so the fix is self-contained:

```
$ grep -rn "geteuid" tests/
tests/test_detect.py:2453:    if os.geteuid() == 0:
```

title: `to_obsidian`: case-only filename collisions silently overwrite node notes on case-insensitive filesystems
body:
## Case-only filename collisions overwrite each other

In `export.py::to_obsidian()`, the filename dedup map is keyed on the exact-case name (v0.8.37, lines 867-876):

```python
node_filename: dict[str, str] = {}
seen_names: dict[str, int] = {}
for node_id, data in G.nodes(data=True):
    base = safe_name(data.get("label", node_id))
    if base in seen_names:          # <-- case-SENSITIVE membership test
        seen_names[base] += 1
        node_filename[node_id] = f"{base}_{seen_names[base]}"
    else:
        seen_names[base] = 0
        node_filename[node_id] = base
```

Two nodes whose labels differ only in case produce two distinct keys, so no `_1` suffix is added — but on a case-insensitive filesystem they resolve to the **same path**, and the second `write_text` silently overwrites the first. One node's note is lost, and the `[[wikilink]]` to it from other notes points at a file whose on-disk casing came from whichever node wrote last.

Note that `safe_name()` strips `/` and `:`, which *increases* the collision rate — `api/analyze Endpoint` and `api:analyze endpoint` both collapse toward the same stem.

### Observed

7 collisions in one 1,729-node export:

| Node A | Node B |
|---|---|
| `apianalyze Endpoint` | `apianalyze endpoint` |
| `SprintSelector Component` | `SprintSelector component` |
| `workflowclaude Context Key` | `workflowclaude context key` |
| `brainstorm_sessions Table` | `brainstorm_sessions table` |
| `idea-flow Service (3026)` | `idea-flow service (3026)` |
| `Lifecycle Spine And Runtime Truth Contract` | `Lifecycle Spine and Runtime Truth Contract` |
| `workflow Shared-Context Heartbeat` | `workflow shared-context heartbeat` |

The output directory holds **1,899** `.md` files against **1,729** nodes + **177** community notes = 1,906 expected — i.e. **7 fewer** files than expected. That shortfall is *exactly* the collision count above, which is what silent overwrite looks like from the outside.

### Minimal reproduction

Four nodes, two case-only pairs, run through the exact `safe_name` + dedup logic above:

```
CURRENT   filenames=['apianalyze Endpoint', 'apianalyze endpoint',
                     'SprintSelector Component', 'SprintSelector component']
          files on disk = 2 of 4 nodes  -> 2 LOST
          unresolved links: ['apianalyze endpoint', 'SprintSelector component']
```

### Suggested fix — verified against the same reproduction

Key the dedup on the casefolded name while keeping the original for display:

```python
key = base.casefold()
if key in seen_names:
    seen_names[key] += 1
    node_filename[node_id] = f"{base}_{seen_names[key]}"
else:
    seen_names[key] = 0
    node_filename[node_id] = base
```

```
PROPOSED  filenames=['apianalyze Endpoint', 'apianalyze endpoint_1',
                     'SprintSelector Component', 'SprintSelector component_1']
          files on disk = 4 of 4 nodes  -> 0 LOST
          unresolved links: []
```

This is also correct on case-sensitive filesystems — it just adds a suffix where Linux would have allowed two distinct files. If that's undesirable, gate it behind a platform check or an `--assume-case-insensitive-fs` flag; defaulting to safe seems better than defaulting to silent loss.

### Severity

Low in practice for Obsidian users: Obsidian resolves wikilinks case-insensitively, so the surviving file still answers links aimed at the lost one. In the export above, **0** of 1,799 distinct link targets is genuinely unresolved — the loss is completely invisible from inside the app. That is the argument for fixing it rather than against: seven nodes have no note and nothing anywhere surfaces it.

### Environment

- `graphifyy` 0.8.37, Python 3.11
- macOS 26.6.1 (Darwin 25.6.0), APFS — case-insensitivity confirmed empirically, not assumed
- Graph: 1,729 nodes / 2,077 edges / 177 communities

title: Locked pypdf 6.13.3 carries six text-extraction DoS advisories on the exact extract_text() path graphify uses; the 50 MiB cap and `except Exception` do not mitigate them
body:
## Summary

`uv.lock` pins `pypdf 6.13.3`, and `pyproject.toml` floors it at `>=6.12.0`. That version has **six** known advisories, and every one of them is an unbounded-CPU or unbounded-memory bug **in PDF text extraction** — which is exactly and only what graphify uses pypdf for.

`SECURITY.md` already states that source files are attacker-controlled ("During the semantic pass, source files are attacker-controlled text mixed into the LLM context"), so a corpus containing a hostile PDF is inside the documented threat model. Point `/graphify` at a repo, a shared drive, or a downloaded dataset containing one crafted PDF and `graphify extract` hangs or balloons.

This is filed publicly because these are already-public CVEs with published fixes, and because private vulnerability reporting on this repo returns HTTP 500 (#2011).

## The advisories

All six are reachable through `page.extract_text()`:

| ID | CVE | Impact | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|---|
| PYSEC-2026-3610 | CVE-2026-59937 | Long runtimes — repeated malformed cross-reference streams | 6.14.0 |
| PYSEC-2026-3611 | CVE-2026-59938 | Large memory use — images declaring sizes far larger than the actual data | 6.14.0 |
| PYSEC-2026-3612 | CVE-2026-59936 | **Infinite loop** — unterminated inline image, "as done when extracting the page text" | 6.14.1 |
| PYSEC-2026-3613 | CVE-2026-59935 | **Infinite loop** — same, via the ASCII85 / ASCIIHex filters | 6.14.2 |
| PYSEC-2026-3655 | CVE-2026-71870 | Large memory use — oversized `/ToUnicode` font entry, "for example during text extraction" | 6.15.0 |
| PYSEC-2026-3656 | CVE-2026-71852 | Long runtimes + large memory — oversized font width entries, "for example during text extraction" | 6.15.0 |

Two of the upstream advisories name page-text extraction as the triggering operation in their own text.

## The call path

`graphify/detect.py:529`:

```python
def extract_pdf_text(path: Path) -> str:
    """Extract plain text from a PDF file using pypdf."""
    if not _file_within_size_cap(path):
        return ""
    try:
        from pypdf import PdfReader
        reader = PdfReader(str(path))
        pages = []
        for page in reader.pages:
            text = page.extract_text()      # <- every advisory above lands here
            if text:
                pages.append(text)
        return "\n".join(pages)
    except Exception:
        return ""
```

Reached from two places, so both the scan and the semantic pass are exposed:

- `detect.py:779` — word counting during corpus scan
- `llm.py:506` — document text for the semantic pass

## Why the existing guards do not cover it

**The size cap does not apply.** `_file_within_size_cap` rejects files over 50 MiB on disk, but every one of these is an *amplification* bug: a small, well-formed-looking PDF produces the runaway loop or allocation. A 20 KB file passes the cap and still hangs.

**`except Exception` does not catch a hang.** It converts the two memory advisories into a silent `return ""` — the document is dropped from the graph with no warning, which is its own quiet failure — but an infinite loop never raises, so PYSEC-2026-3612 and -3613 wedge the process. There is no `signal.alarm`, timeout, or subprocess isolation anywhere on this path (`grep -n "signal.alarm\|SIGALRM\|timeout" graphify/detect.py` returns nothing).

Worth noting the project already defends against precisely this class for Office files — `_zip_within_caps` exists to stop zip/XML bombs in `.docx`. PDF simply has no equivalent, and here the mitigation is free because upstream already shipped it.

**CI did not surface it.** The `security-scan` job runs `pip-audit --strict` with `continue-on-error: true`, so the finding is reported and then discarded. On current `v8`:

```
$ uv run --frozen pip-audit --strict
Found 34 known vulnerabilities in 7 packages
```

## Suggested fix

Raise the floor past all six and refresh the lock:

```toml
pdf = ["pypdf>=6.15.0", "markdownify"]
```

(`>=6.15.0` clears every advisory in the table; the highest fix version is 6.15.0.) The same string appears twice — in the `pdf` extra and in `all` — so both need it, and `uv lock` then moves `uv.lock` off 6.13.3.

I am happy to send that PR if you want it — say the word and I will open one. Holding off because a lockfile bump is a maintainer call, and the same audit run flags six other packages where the judgement is genuinely yours:

- `pillow 12.2.0` — 12 advisories, but graphify never imports PIL directly (it arrives transitively via matplotlib/umap), so the exposure is materially weaker than pypdf's.
- `cryptography`, `setuptools`, `soupsieve`, `yt-dlp`, `pip` — the rest of the 34, none on an obvious attacker-reachable path.

A separate question worth its own issue if you'd rather: `extract_pdf_text` swallowing `MemoryError` into `return ""` means a PDF can vanish from the graph silently. Even after the bump, a wall-clock guard on that path would turn "hangs forever" into "skips one file loudly."

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| graphify | `v8` @ `26128ab` (0.9.40) |
| pypdf | 6.13.3 (from committed `uv.lock`) |
| Verified with | `uv run --frozen pip-audit`, advisory text from the OSV records |

title: graphify opencode install does not copy skill file to ~/.config/opencode/skills/graphify/SKILL.md
body:
## Bug

`graphify opencode install` only writes the AGENTS.md section and the `tool.execute.before` plugin, but does **not** copy the skill file (`skill-opencode.md`) to `~/.config/opencode/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`. As a result, the `/graphify` command is unavailable in OpenCode — the skill is never discovered.

## Root cause

In `install.py`, `graphify opencode install` (without `--project`) calls `_agents_install(Path("."), "opencode")` (line 2265):

```python
# line 2259-2265
elif cmd in ("aider", "codex", "opencode", "claw", "droid", "trae", "trae-cn", "hermes"):
    subcmd = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ""
    if subcmd == "install":
        if "--project" in sys.argv[3:]:
            _project_install(cmd, Path("."))
        else:
            _agents_install(Path("."), cmd)  # <-- no _copy_skill_file
```

`_agents_install` (line 1470) only writes the AGENTS.md section + plugin, it never calls `_copy_skill_file`.

Compare with `_amp_install` (line 1518) and `_agents_platform_install` (line 1529), which **both** call `_copy_skill_file` before `_agents_install`:

```python
def _amp_install(project_dir):
    _amp_legacy_cleanup()
    _copy_skill_file("amp")           # <-- copies skill
    _agents_install(project_dir, "amp")

def _agents_platform_install(project_dir):
    _copy_skill_file("agents")        # <-- copies skill
    _agents_install(project_dir, "agents")
```

The platform config at line 338 already defines the correct destination:

```python
"opencode": {
    "skill_file": "skill-opencode.md",
    "skill_dst": Path(".config") / "opencode" / "skills" / "graphify" / "SKILL.md",
    ...
},
```

But no code path for `graphify opencode install` ever uses `skill_dst` to copy the file.

## Environment

- graphifyy 0.9.40 (installed via `uv tool install graphifyy`)
- macOS (nix-darwin)
- OpenCode

## Install output (actual)

```
$ graphify opencode install
graphify section written to /Users/luda/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md
  .opencode/plugins/graphify.js  ->  tool.execute.before hook written
  .opencode/opencode.json  ->  plugin registered

Opencode will now check the knowledge graph before answering
codebase questions and rebuild it after code changes.
```

No mention of skill file copy. `~/.config/opencode/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` does not exist after install.

## Expected output

Should also copy the skill file:

```
  skills/graphify/SKILL.md  ->  skill file written
```

## Suggested fix

Either:
1. Add a dedicated `_opencode_install` function (like `_amp_install`) that calls `_copy_skill_file("opencode")` before `_agents_install`, or
2. Add `_copy_skill_file(platform)` inside `_agents_install` for platforms that have a `skill_dst` (opencode, codex, etc.)

## Workaround

Manual copy after install:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/skills/graphify/references
cp <graphify-package>/skill-opencode.md ~/.config/opencode/skills/graphify/SKILL.md
cp <graphify-package>/skills/opencode/references/*.md ~/.config/opencode/skills/graphify/references/
```

title: fix(csharp): bind a call on a constructed generic type (`Bag<T>.Make()`)
body:
Fixes #2624 (the part still open on 0.9.86).

## Summary

`Bag<Payload>.Make()` gets no `calls` edge. The *receiver* is a constructed generic type, which tree-sitter wraps in a `generic_name`, and the C# member-call handler only captured a receiver that was a plain `identifier`. The receiver was dropped, so `_resolve_csharp_member_calls` had nothing to bind.

The rest of #2624 (type arguments on the method name: `Registry.Fetch<Payload>()`, `box.Read<Payload>()`, `Local<Payload>()`) is already fixed on v8 by #3406's `_csharp_bare_call_name`. This PR was first written before that landed; it is now rebased onto 0.9.86 and reduced to the one case still broken.

## Change

`graphify/extractors/engine.py`: a member call's receiver may also be a `generic_name`, read through `_csharp_bare_call_name` (the type-argument list off), so `Bag<Payload>.Make()` binds like any `Type.M()`. Type nodes are stored under the bare name. C# only; nothing else reads this branch.

This does not loosen resolution: the receiver still goes through receiver typing and the god-node guard, so an untypable receiver still gets no edge.

## Tests

Five tests appended to `tests/test_csharp_member_calls.py`. `test_constructed_generic_type_as_receiver` fails on clean 0.9.86 and passes here; the other four (explicit type argument on a type receiver and on a typed local, `Local<T>()` / `this.Local<T>()`, and the #1609 guard through a generic call) pass on 0.9.86 and stay as regression tests for #2624. The generic-receiver test is split across two files on purpose: in one file the callee resolves by an in-file label match and never reaches receiver typing.

```text
python -m pytest tests/test_csharp*.py -q          # 209 passed (0.9.86 without the fix: 1 failed)
python -m pytest tests -q                          # with my other 5 refreshed PRs applied: 3 failed, 7324 passed, 33 skipped; clean 0.9.86 on this machine: the same 3 failed, 7300 passed
python -m ruff check graphify/extractors/engine.py tests/test_csharp_member_calls.py   # All checks passed
```

The 3 failures (`test_absolute_path_lookup_skips_getcwd` x2, `test_3357_minimal_reproduction_no_config_emits_calls_edge`) fail on clean 0.9.86 on this Windows machine too.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01B8gwEpjajiWHVW3c9smuKf

title: fix(skill): clean up needs_update, not .needs_update
body:
Fixes #2440.

## Summary

`--watch` writes `graphify-out/needs_update` when it sees a doc/paper/image change it cannot re-extract without an LLM, and the read hook then treats the graph as stale for every source read while that file exists. The documented escape hatch is a full rebuild through the skill, whose step 9 cleans the flag up.

Step 9 deleted `graphify-out/.needs_update` — with a leading dot, which nothing writes. The `rm` matched nothing, so the real flag survived a complete, successful rebuild and every later Read kept getting the stale nudge. `graphify update` does clear it (`watch.py`), so the CLI path worked while the documented skill path silently did not.

The dot looks accidental rather than a second flag: the line directly above cleans dotted temp files (`.graphify_detect.json`, `.graphify_extract.json`, …), and the same fragment's own prose already writes `graphify-out/needs_update` without one.

## Changes

- Three skillgen fragments (`core/core.md`, `core/aider.md`, `core/devin.md`) drop the dot. The 32 rendered artifacts follow from `python -m tools.skillgen` and `--bless`; all 35 generated-line changes are that one line, and the two Windows ones are the PowerShell form skillgen derives itself.
- `gen.py` gains `_is_needs_update_flag_fix_line`, registered in `_SANCTIONED_MONOLITH_DIFFS`. The aider/devin monoliths are diffed against the pinned pristine v8 blob and every deviation has to be an enumerated change-class, so the round-trip guard fails without it. Same shape as the existing predicates.
- The PowerShell translator test used the old dotted line as its "translates exactly" example; updated so it still mirrors a real corpus line.

## Tests

`test_skill_cleanup_targets_the_flag_the_code_actually_writes` asserts the two halves agree: `watch.py` and `cli.py` name the undotted flag, and no rendered artifact references a dotted one. Confirmed it fails with the fragments reverted:

```
AssertionError: graphify/skill-agents.md cleans up '.needs_update', which nothing ever writes
```

`uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_skillgen.py -q` — 65 passed.

`uv run --no-sync python -m tools.skillgen --check` — 134 artifacts match committed output and `expected/`. `--audit-coverage`, `--schema-singleton`, `--monolith-roundtrip` and `--always-on-roundtrip` all OK (the git-show validators need `origin/v8` fetched locally or they skip).

`uv run --no-sync ruff check tools/skillgen/gen.py tests/test_skillgen.py` — passed.

Full suite: 22 failed, 4300 passed, 13 skipped, against a clean `v8` baseline of 22 failed, 4299 passed, 13 skipped — the same 22 in both runs, all pre-existing and platform-sensitive on this Windows machine. The +1 is the new test.

I did not run the `--watch` → touch a doc → rebuild sequence end to end; the evidence here is the filename mismatch between what the code writes and reads and what the skill deletes, established from the source.

title: fix(opencode): install user-scope skill
body:
Fixes #2670

## What
Make the `graphify opencode install` subcommand install Graphify's OpenCode skill at the user-scope location:
`~/.config/opencode/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`.

## Why
The command previously configured the project integration (`AGENTS.md`, plugin, and OpenCode config) but did not copy the skill itself. That left the documented OpenCode user-scope installation incomplete.

## How
- Route the OpenCode subcommand through dedicated install and uninstall handlers.
