title: Semantic extraction silently truncates every file at 20,000 characters (_FILE_CHAR_CAP), no warning
body:
## Summary

Semantic (LLM) extraction silently reads only the first 20,000 characters of every file (`_FILE_CHAR_CAP = 20_000` in `graphify/llm.py`), with no warning and no error. For files well above that size — a long `CLAUDE.md`, a design doc, a project plan — this means most of the file's content is invisible to the graph, silently.

## Environment

- Installed: `graphifyy` 0.8.31 (`pip show graphifyy`)
- Confirmed still present on `main` / latest release (0.9.66, 2026-09-22): `_FILE_CHAR_CAP = 20_000` at `graphify/llm.py:30`, used unconditionally in `_read_files` (truncates before building the prompt) and in the token-estimate helpers around line 2090-2134.

## Reproduction

1. Create/point at any prose file (`.md`) larger than 20,000 characters — a `CLAUDE.md` accumulated over months of a real project is a common case.
2. Run `/graphify --update` (or `extract_corpus_parallel(...)` directly) with `GEMINI_API_KEY` set.
3. Compare `len(open(file).read())` against the node count graphify produces for that file.

## Actual behavior

- The extraction call returns `failed_chunks: 0` and a normal-looking result — nothing signals truncation.
- Real case: a 229,319-character `CLAUDE.md` (project history/decisions) was read up to character 20,000 (8.7% of the file) and produced 11 nodes. Once manually split into <18k-char chunks at heading boundaries and re-extracted, the same file produced 215 nodes — the other 91.3% of the file had simply never reached the model.
- Across one real corpus (~430 files), 29 documents exceeded the cap; some plans were seen as low as 8.7%–50% of their actual content, all without any indication in the CLI output.

## Expected behavior

At minimum: print a warning (like the existing "extraction warning: N issues" pattern) whenever a file is truncated by `_FILE_CHAR_CAP`, naming the file and the percentage lost. Ideally: split an oversized file into multiple chunks (the same way the corpus itself is already chunked across files) and extract each chunk, merging nodes back onto the original `source_file` — this is what we ended up implementing as a workaround.

## Workaround we're using

A small script that: audits which files exceed the cap, splits each one into <18k-char tramos (cutting on markdown `## ` headings, falling back to line breaks for an oversized single section), extracts each tramo with `extract_corpus_parallel`, and reassigns any node whose `source_file` the model pointed elsewhere back to the correct original document (by checking which candidate document's text mentions the node's label). Happy to share it if useful, but a native fix (at least the warning) would remove the need for every user to discover this independently.

## Related

Not a duplicate of the shrink-guard issues (#3579, #3580, #2229, #2976) — this is upstream of those, in extraction input, not in the merge/write path. No existing issue found for `_FILE_CHAR_CAP` / truncation / "20000" in search.

title: Default dedup=True + force=True on every normal run leaves the #479 shrink guard permanently bypassed unless --no-dedup is known and passed
body:
## Summary

`graphify <path>` (and its internal alias `graphify extract <path>`) defaults to `dedup=True`, and on any normal successful run writes with `force=True` regardless of dedup outcome — meaning the #479 shrink guard in `to_json()` never actually engages unless the user already knows to pass `--no-dedup`. A carefully built, curated graph can be silently shrunk by a routine `graphify .` with zero warning.

## Environment

Confirmed against a fresh install of `graphifyy==0.9.66` in an isolated venv (latest release as of today) — not a stale-version report. Also present, in a cruder form (no `--no-dedup` escape hatch existed at all), in `0.8.31`.

## What happened

A project's `graphify-out/graph.json` was carefully built by hand via `build_merge(..., dedup=False)` (the documented workaround for #2881/#3094-style cross-file dedup) to 6,319 nodes / 9,240 edges, with curated (non-default) community labels and real Gemini token spend. Running `graphify . --no-viz` right after — no subcommand, no flags beyond `--no-viz` — silently rewrote it to 5,412 nodes / 7,056 edges. No warning, no error, no diff summary.

## Root cause (traced in `graphify/cli.py`, v0.9.66)

1. A bare positional path is rewritten to `extract` internally:
```python
elif Path(cmd).exists() or cmd in (".", "..") or cmd.startswith(("./", "../", "/", "~")):
    # User ran `graphify <path>` directly — treat as `graphify extract <path>`.
    sys.argv.insert(2, sys.argv[1])
    sys.argv[1] = "extract"
    _reenter_main()
```
2. `extract`'s default is `dedup=not no_dedup` → `dedup=True` unless `--no-dedup` is explicitly passed:
```python
G = _build_merge([merged], graph_path=existing_graph_path, ..., dedup=not no_dedup, ...)
# or, full build:
G = _build([merged], dedup=not no_dedup, ...)
```
3. The write is *always* forced on a normal run:
```python
_force_write = cli_allow_partial or not _extraction_incomplete
...
_to_json(G, communities, str(graph_json_path), force=_force_write, ...)
```
`_extraction_incomplete` is only `True` when a chunk genuinely failed — on a clean run it's `False`, so `_force_write` is `True`. The in-line comment even says this is intentional: *"force=True bypasses the #479 shrink guard entirely. A full build legitimately shrinks (fuzzy dedup collapse, deleted code) so it keeps force=True"*.

`--no-dedup` *does* give real protection (it makes `build_merge` raise `ValueError` and abort *before* any write, per the comment at line ~4508 referencing #2881) — but it's opt-in, unadvertised on a normal run, and not the default even though the shrink guard the library ships and documents is otherwise dead code without it.

## What saved us

`backup_if_protected()` (`graphify/export.py`) snapshots `graph.json` + report + labels + manifest to `graphify-out/{YYYY-MM-DD}/` before an overwrite, *if* the existing graph has a `.graphify_semantic_marker` or a curated (non-default) label — both were true here, so today's damage was recoverable. But this is a single dated folder, overwritten in place if it differs from what's already there: a second accidental run on the same day would have backed up the already-damaged state over the good one, with no way back. `GRAPHIFY_NO_BACKUP=1` disables it entirely. It's a nice safety net, not a substitute for the shrink guard actually being armed by default.

## Suggested fix

Pick one (or both):
- Default `--no-dedup`'s shrink-guard protection to *on* regardless of `dedup`/`--no-dedup` — i.e. decouple "skip fuzzy merging" from "verify the write doesn't silently drop nodes from untouched files." The two are orthogonal concerns bundled into one flag today.
- At minimum, print a warning before a forced write that shrinks the graph (`new_n < existing_n`) even when `force=True`, instead of writing silently — so a user gets *some* signal, even if they don't want the run to abort.

## Related

Not a duplicate: #2881 (closed) added the `--no-dedup` escape hatch but the *default* path (what the README/quickstart and the `/graphify` Claude Code skill's own `references/update.md` actually invoke) still ships the unsafe default. #3579/#3580/#2229/#2976 discuss the shrink guard failing to fire on other, unrelated code paths — this is specifically about the guard being deliberately bypassed with `force=True` on the default/most common invocation.

title: `_pick_winner` can discard a real declaration in favour of a source-less stub
body:
### Summary

In `graphify/dedup.py`, `_pick_winner()` chooses which of several colliding node records survives, ranking them by `_content_richness()`. That richness score explicitly ignores `source_file` and `source_location` (they're listed in `_RICHNESS_IGNORED_KEYS`) — which are precisely the fields that distinguish a real, located declaration from a placeholder.

The result: a node with no `source_file` at all can out-score and replace the genuine declaration it collides with, purely because it happens to carry one or two extra bookkeeping keys (e.g. `external`, `type`, `_origin`).

### Reproduction

Run against an unmodified `dedup.py`:

```python
from graphify.dedup import _content_richness, _pick_winner

real = {
    "id": "docs_guide_setup", "label": "Setup", "file_type": "concept",
    "source_file": "docs/guide.md", "source_location": "L12",
    "attributes": {"kind": "section"},
}
stub = {
    "id": "setup", "label": "Setup", "file_type": "concept",
    "source_file": "", "type": "external", "external": True,
    "_origin": "semantic",
}

print(_content_richness(real))      # 2
print(_content_richness(stub))      # 3
print(_pick_winner([real, stub]))   # -> the stub wins
```

Observed: `_pick_winner` returns the stub (`id: "setup"`), discarding the record that has an actual file and line.

Expected: the record with a real `source_file` should win. Provenance is a stronger signal of canonicity than incidental field count.

### Scope (checked, not assumed)

This does **not** affect code graphs. Both passes of `deduplicate_entities()` skip `file_type == "code"` nodes (`if _is_code(node): continue`), so `_pick_winner` is never reached for code symbols. The exposure is non-code node types — `concept`, `document`, `paper`, `image` — i.e. the semantic/document extraction path.

I mention this because I initially suspected this bug explained a missing function in a Rust graph, and that turned out to be wrong: the function was never missing, and the cause was elsewhere entirely. The scoring flaw above is real and reproducible on its own merits, but I don't want to overstate its blast radius.

### Suggested fix

Add a provenance tiebreak ahead of richness, so a node with a real source location always beats one without:

```python
def _score(n: dict) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    has_suffix = bool(_CHUNK_SUFFIX.search(n["id"]))
    no_source = 0 if n.get("source_file") else 1
    return (1 if has_suffix else 0, no_source, -_content_richness(n), len(n["id"]))
```

(Original: `return (1 if has_suffix else 0, -_content_richness(n), len(n["id"]))`)

This preserves the existing ordering in every case where both records have — or both lack — provenance, and only changes the outcome in the ambiguous case the bug concerns.

### Environment

- graphify `0.9.65` (PyPI package `graphifyy`)
- Python 3.14, Windows 10

---

title: Incremental --update silently loses cross-file edges; --force does not repair it, only deleting graphify-out does
body:
### Summary

A graph maintained with `--update` ends up missing edges that a clean build produces — predominantly cross-file `imports` / `imports_from`, plus some `calls`. `--force` does **not** repair it. Only deleting the `graphify-out` directory and rebuilding yields a graph equal to a clean build.

This is silent: nothing in the output indicates the graph is incomplete, and `graph.json` gives a consumer no way to tell.

### Measurement

Project: ~130 Python files, 3,277 nodes. Comparison is against a full build of the *same* source copied to a clean directory, diffing on `(source_file, label)` pairs rather than node ids (ids are root-dependent, so an id diff is meaningless across roots).

| Build method | Node difference | Edge difference |
|---|---|---|
| maintained with `--update` | 0 | **65 missing** |
| `--force` over that same directory | 0 | **64 missing** |
| `graphify-out` deleted, then rebuilt | 0 | **0** |

Relation breakdown of the 65 missing edges:

```
imports        41
imports_from   19
calls           5
```

Every missing edge originates in a file that had been re-extracted by an
earlier `--update`. Examples:

```
reachability.py --imports--> _parser_for()          (source_spans.py)
reachability.py --imports--> function_spans()       (source_spans.py)
validation.py   --imports--> _parser_for()          (source_spans.py)
attacker_value_ranking.py --imports--> is_file_node()  (graph_data.py)
```

### Expected

`--update` should produce a graph equivalent to a full build of the same source, or `--force` should repair one that has diverged.

### Actual

Re-extracting a changed file appears not to re-resolve that file's edges into *other* files. The stale state survives `--force` and is only cleared by removing the output directory.

### Why it matters

Any consumer that walks `imports`/`imports_from` (dependency analysis, supply-chain reach) undercounts, and anything walking `calls` can produce false negatives — a reachability query returning "no path" when a path exists in the source. Since the loss happens during the build, it leaves no trace in `graph.json`, so it cannot be detected by inspecting the graph alone.

### Reproduction

1. Build a graph for a multi-file project.
2. Edit a file that imports from several others; run `graphify <path> --update --code-only`. Repeat a few times across different files.
3. Copy the source to a clean directory and build it fresh.
4. Diff the two graphs on `(source_file, label)` node keys and `(source_key, target_key, relation)` edge keys.

### Environment

- graphify `0.9.65` (PyPI `graphifyy`)
- Python 3.14, Windows 10

### Possibly related

- #2391 (`calls` deleted by `references` on the same pair) — a different mechanism; the drift above is measured *after* accounting for that.
- #3354 (no build timestamp / commit recorded) — with no build provenance in `graph.json`, a drifted graph is indistinguishable from a current one.

title: Top-level module X.py and package X/ are conflated, producing phantom import cycles
body:
### Summary

When a project contains both a top-level module `X.py` and a package directory `X/`, graphify treats them as the same node. Imports *into the package* are attributed to the script, which fabricates import cycles that do not exist in the code.

This is a common Python layout — an entry-point script named after the package it launches.

### Reproduction

`OWASP/Nettacker` at current HEAD has exactly this shape:

```
nettacker.py          <- 123-byte entry point script
nettacker/            <- the package
nettacker/logger.py
nettacker/main.py
nettacker/core/app.py
```

The actual imports are acyclic:

```python
# nettacker.py
from nettacker.main import run

# nettacker/main.py
from nettacker.core.app import Nettacker

# nettacker/core/app.py
from nettacker import logger          # -> nettacker/logger.py, i.e. the PACKAGE
```

`from nettacker import logger` resolves to `nettacker/logger.py`. It has nothing to do with the top-level `nettacker.py`, which never mentions `logger` at all (`grep -c logger nettacker.py` → 0).

### Actual

`GRAPH_REPORT.md` reports three cycles, all rooted in the same conflation:

```
- 3-file cycle: nettacker.py -> nettacker/main.py -> nettacker/core/app.py -> nettacker.py
- 4-file cycle: nettacker.py -> nettacker/main.py -> nettacker/core/app.py -> nettacker/core/die.py -> nettacker.py
- 4-file cycle: nettacker.py -> nettacker/main.py -> nettacker/core/app.py -> nettacker/core/module.py -> nettacker.py
```

### Expected

`nettacker.py` and the package `nettacker/` should be distinct nodes. An import of `nettacker.<submodule>` should resolve to the package, and no cycle should be reported for this project.

### Why it matters

"Import Cycles" is presented as a finding worth acting on, and a circular import is normally a genuine design problem — so a false one sends a reader looking for a defect that isn't there. Worse, anything consuming `graph.json` for reachability inherits the phantom edge silently: the script appears to participate in call paths it has no part in.

Reproduced on a 1,786-node graph of the project above; the same shape will occur in any repo using the `foo.py` + `foo/` entry-point layout.

### Environment

- graphify `0.9.65` (PyPI `graphifyy`)
- Python 3.14, Windows 10
- Command: `graphify <path> --code-only` then `graphify cluster-only <path> --no-label`

title: JavaScript: calls through a CommonJS destructured require are never resolved (express: 63 call edges from 11,733 call sites)
body:
### Summary

For CommonJS code, graphify resolves the *import* of a function but not *calls through the imported binding*. The result is that JavaScript projects get almost no `calls` edges, while the same analysis on other languages produces one to two orders of magnitude more.

### Measurement

Same command on eight well-known repos (`graphify <path> --code-only`, then `cluster-only --no-label`). Call sites counted by walking each file's tree-sitter AST for the language's own call node type; call edges counted from `graph.json`:

| Repo | Language | Call sites | `calls` edges | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JamesNK/Newtonsoft.Json | C# | 48,070 | 13,487 | 28% |
| google/gson | Java | 23,468 | 5,337 | 23% |
| spf13/cobra | Go | 4,430 | 934 | 21% |
| BurntSushi/ripgrep | Rust | 17,103 | 3,270 | 19% |
| psf/requests | Python | 2,687 | 453 | 17% |
| gin-gonic/gin | Go | 9,414 | 1,346 | 14% |
| pallets/flask | Python | 3,963 | 386 | 10% |
| **expressjs/express** | **JavaScript** | **11,733** | **63** | **1%** |

express's whole graph contains 11 `calls` and 52 `indirect_call` edges across 404 nodes and 119 callable nodes.

### Concrete case

`expressjs/express` at current HEAD:

```js
// lib/utils.js:61
exports.normalizeType = function(type){ ... };

// lib/response.js:27
var normalizeType = require('./utils').normalizeType;

// lib/response.js:587
this.set('Content-Type', normalizeType(key).value);
```

Everything here is literal: a literal require path, a literal property, and a plain identifier call.

In the resulting `graph.json`, the node `lib_utils_normalizetype` has exactly two incoming edges:

```
response.js --imports--> normalizeType()
lib/utils.js --contains--> normalizeType()
```

There is **no `calls` edge** from `lib/response.js` to `normalizeType()`, even though the import was resolved correctly — so the resolver clearly knows where the symbol lives.

### Expected

A `calls` edge from the calling function in `lib/response.js` to `normalizeType()` in `lib/utils.js`.

### Why it matters

The import edge being present while the call edge is missing means the information needed to resolve the call is already available; only the call-site binding is not being made. Any consumer doing reachability or call-graph work on JavaScript gets a graph that is essentially call-free — a "no path found" result on a JS project currently means very little.

The `var x = require('./m').x` destructuring form is extremely common in CommonJS, so this is likely not an edge case.

### Environment

- graphify `0.9.65` (PyPI `graphifyy`)
- Python 3.14, Windows 10
- `expressjs/express` default branch, shallow clone 2026-09-22

title: Windows: update/query fail with "can't open file" after PYTHONHASHSEED re-exec (uv tool install)
body:
### What happens

On Windows, when graphify is installed with `uv tool install graphifyy`, every command that pins the hash seed fails immediately. That includes `graphify update .` and `graphify query ...`:

```
~\AppData\Roaming\uv\python\cpython-3.11-windows-x86_64-none\python.exe: can't open file '~\\.local\\bin\\graphify': [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

Commands that don't re-exec, such as `graphify --help`, work fine.

### Cause

The hash-seed pin added in #3641 re-execs like this (`graphify/__main__.py`, around L525):

```python
os.execvpe(sys.executable, [sys.executable, *sys.argv], {**os.environ, "PYTHONHASHSEED": "0"})
```

On Windows, uv installs the console script as a launcher `.exe`. There, `sys.argv[0]` is `~\.local\bin\graphify` (no extension, and not a Python file), so `python <argv[0]>` has nothing to run. The same will likely happen with pip/pipx console-script `.exe` launchers on Windows.

### Suggested fix

Re-exec as a module so it doesn't depend on `argv[0]`:

```python
os.execvpe(sys.executable, [sys.executable, "-m", "graphify", *sys.argv[1:]], {**os.environ, "PYTHONHASHSEED": "0"})
```

### Workaround

Set `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` before running graphify. This skips the re-exec.

### Environment
- graphifyy 0.9.66 (installed with `uv tool install "graphifyy[sql]"`)
- uv 0.12.5
- Windows 11 (10.0.26220), PowerShell 5.1
- Python 3.11 (uv-managed)

title: fix(cli): re-exec the hash seed pin as a module, not by replaying argv[0]
body:
Fixes #3779 — a regression in my own #3743 (issue #3641), reported within a day of the 0.9.66 release shipping. Sorry about that.

`_pin_hash_seed_if_needed` re-execs like this:
```python
os.execvpe(sys.executable, [sys.executable, *sys.argv], {**os.environ, "PYTHONHASHSEED": "0"})
```
This replays `sys.argv[0]` as the script path for the interpreter to run. That works for a POSIX console-script wrapper or a `python -m graphify` invocation — both real, runnable Python content — but not for a uv/pip/pipx console-script launcher on Windows, which installs as a native `.exe` stub with no such content. The interpreter has nothing to open, and every command this function touches (`update`/`extract`/`cluster-only`/`label`) failed outright with `can't open file` the moment it tried to pin the seed.

Fix (the issue's own suggestion, which is correct and minimal): re-exec via `-m graphify` instead, which never depends on `argv[0]` being anything runnable at all:
```python
os.execvpe(sys.executable, [sys.executable, "-m", "graphify", *sys.argv[1:]], {**os.environ, "PYTHONHASHSEED": "0"})
```
This also now matches the exact invocation shape the existing end-to-end test for this function (`test_update_still_runs_end_to_end_with_hashseed_unset`) was already exercising.

Verified the failure mode empirically before touching anything — simulated a non-Python launcher stub path as `argv[0]` and confirmed it broke pre-fix (`can't open file`) and is fixed post-fix. Updated the existing probe assertions to the new argv shape and added a dedicated regression test that drives the probe with a launcher stub path that isn't even a real file, confirming the fix no longer depends on it being runnable — the exact shape of the Windows uv-launcher scenario. Full suite is green aside from 16 pre-existing failures in the newly-added Erlang/R/Solidity/VB.NET extractor tests, caused by their optional grammar packages not being installed in my dev environment — unrelated to this change (confirmed via `python -c "import tree_sitter_r"` etc. all failing with `ModuleNotFoundError`, and confirmed these packages weren't needed by any branch cut before the 0.9.66 release landed).

title: fix(detect): break manifest key duplicate collapse ties by seen time, not iteration order
body:
Fixes #1964, specifically the still-live gap flagged in [this new comment](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/issues/1964#issuecomment-5787265856) from @cabgab-dev.

The original symptom in this issue (absolute-path manifest keys breaking incremental detection across clones/CI) looked fixed on current `v8` when I checked earlier — `save_manifest(root=...)` relativizes keys, and `load_manifest(root=...)` re-anchors them, both citing "the #777/#1964 portability guarantee". But a manifest written across a *mix* of call sites — some passing `root`, some not (an outdated installed skill runbook, for one) — can still end up with both an absolute and a relative key for the same file, each carrying different data.

Both `load_manifest` and `save_manifest`'s relativize step already canonicalize every raw key through a dict comprehension, which does correctly collapse the two forms down to one entry — but keeps whichever raw key happens to *iterate last* in the on-disk JSON, an artifact of arbitrary key order with no relation to which entry is actually current. A fresher hash can get silently discarded in favor of a stale one purely because of how the duplicate keys happened to accumulate, which is exactly @cabgab-dev's reported symptom: `detect_incremental()` sometimes reads the stale duplicate and under-reports genuine changes (146 files missing from the semantic cache reported as "2 files changed").

Reproduced directly: built a manifest with one stale absolute-keyed entry and one fresh relative-keyed entry for the same file, and confirmed via `load_manifest` that swapping their on-disk JSON order flips which one survives — the collapse really is order-dependent today.

Fixed with a small shared helper, `_collapse_manifest_duplicates`, used at both collapse sites. It breaks a collision by each entry's own `seen` timestamp (present specifically to record when an entry was last confirmed current) when both sides have one and disagree, falling back to the historical last-wins behavior for legacy/partial entries with no `seen` field — so this only changes behavior for the exact ambiguous case it's meant to fix.

Two regression tests in `tests/test_detect.py`, each checked in both on-disk key orderings to prove the fix is order-independent, both confirmed to fail against pre-fix code via `git stash` first. Full suite is green aside from the same 16 pre-existing failures from the newly-added Erlang/R/Solidity/VB.NET extractor tests (missing optional grammar packages in my dev environment, unrelated to this change — already noted on #3780).

title: Rust: a type used above its declaration stays a sourceless stub when the name is defined in 2+ files
body:
### What happened?

In Rust, a type reference that appears above the type's declaration in the same file becomes a sourceless stub node. That is expected at first: `ensure_named_node` in `extractors/rust.py` only resolves names already in `seen_ids`, so a forward reference looks the same as a cross-file one.

The stub is never folded back if another file defines a type with the same name. `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` in `extract.py` rewires a stub only when exactly one definition with that label exists in the whole corpus. As a result the edge points at a stub instead of the struct defined a few lines further down in the same file.

The practical effect is that `graphify affected` and `graphify explain` on the real struct silently miss those users. It is common in any codebase with parallel modules: per-platform implementations, `v1`/`v2` modules, or a type mirrored between a Rust backend and a TS frontend. In our ~600-file Tauri repo (a macOS and a Windows engine that share type names), it leaves 140 stubs holding 300 edges. Every one of them is for a label defined in two or more files, and none is for a unique label, whose stubs do get rewired. One struct's biggest consumer (a function taking it as a parameter, declared above the struct) is missing from `affected` entirely.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
mkdir repro && cd repro && git init -q && mkdir src
cat > src/engine_a.rs <<'EOF'
fn before(s: &Sink) {}

struct Sink {
    n: u32,
}

fn after(s: &Sink) {}
EOF
cat > src/engine_b.rs <<'EOF'
struct Sink {
    n: u32,
}
EOF
graphify update .
```

Then list the `Sink` nodes and the `references` edges into them from `graphify-out/graph.json`.

### Error output or graph output

With both files:

```
node src_engine_a_sink | source_file='src/engine_a.rs' L3
node src_engine_b_sink | source_file='src/engine_b.rs' L1
node sink              | source_file=''
edge src_engine_a_after  -> src_engine_a_sink   L7
edge src_engine_a_before -> sink                L1    <- should be src_engine_a_sink
```

Control, with `src/engine_b.rs` deleted and the graph rebuilt from scratch: the stub is rewired as expected.

```
[('src_engine_a_sink', 'src/engine_a.rs')]
[('src_engine_a_after', 'src_engine_a_sink'), ('src_engine_a_before', 'src_engine_a_sink')]
```

In a larger corpus the stubs also collide across files, and `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids` bakes the file stem into their IDs (`..._engine_a_rs_sink`). They then look like a third real `Sink` in `explain`.

### Graphify version

0.9.66 (`graphifyy` from PyPI)

### Environment

macOS 27.0 arm64, Python 3.11.13 (uv tool install). The code path is platform-independent.

### Additional context

Two possible fixes. Either one alone would resolve the repro:

1. **Same-file forward references:** pre-scan a file's top-level type declarations (`struct_item`, `enum_item`, `trait_item`, `type_item`, `union_item`) before the main walk, so `ensure_named_node` resolves them regardless of order.
2. **Ambiguous labels:** when a stub's label has several definitions, prefer the one whose `source_file` equals the stub's `origin_file` (already recorded on the stub) before giving up.

The first fixes it at the source. The second is a smaller change in the rewire pass. Both cover only the same-file case, which seems right: a genuine cross-file reference to an ambiguous name has no single correct target, so it should stay a stub.

Related: #1402 (closed) fixed a different cause of the same phantom-stub symptom (sourced stubs blocking the rewire). This one is sourceless stubs that the uniqueness rule declines.

title: fix: prevent phantom cycles from package-module name collisions
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3777 by retracting provisional Python `imports_from` edges when package-form imports are successfully resolved to submodules.

Previously, an import such as:

```python
from nettacker import logger
```

could produce both:

```text
app.py → nettacker.py
app.py → nettacker/logger.py
```

when a `nettacker.py` module and `nettacker/` package coexisted. The incorrect provisional edge could create phantom import cycles.

## What changed

* Retract the provisional `context="import"` edge when the same import site resolves to a submodule on disk.
* Match provisional edges using canonical source paths and source locations.
* Preserve the existing `submodule_import` resolution behavior and edge metadata.
* Handle multi-imports, semicolon-separated imports, relative imports, and namespace packages.
* Leave standalone module imports unchanged.

## Tests

Added regression coverage for:

* Package/module collision reproducing #3777
* Nested package/module collisions
* Namespace package submodule imports
* Standalone module imports

Verified with:

```text
pytest tests/test_python_import_resolution.py
9 passed
```

Also verified `git diff --check` passes cleanly.

title: detect_incremental() uses a single global manifest for all subdirectories — --update on one subfolder reports files from the last-graphed folder as deleted
body:
## Bug: `detect_incremental()` uses a single global manifest for all subdirectories — `--update` on one subfolder reports every file from the last-graphed folder as deleted

**Version:** graphifyy 0.3.28

### What happened

Running the skill's `--update` flow on one subdirectory of a large repo (e.g. `workflows/`) after a previous full run had graphed a *different* subdirectory (e.g. `experts/`) causes `deleted_files` in the incremental-detect result to list hundreds of paths from that unrelated, previously-graphed folder.

Live case: `--update` on `workflows/` (a workspace with ~15 top-level graphed subfolders, each run via `/graphify <subfolder>`) returned `deleted_files` containing 230+ paths under `experts/rechts-kanzlei/...` — none of which are under `workflows/` and none of which were actually deleted. The last folder graphed before this run was `experts/`.

### Root cause

In `graphify/detect.py`, the manifest path is a module-level constant:

```python
_MANIFEST_PATH = "graphify-out/manifest.json"
```

`load_manifest()` / `save_manifest()` both default to this single flat path regardless of which `root` was passed to `detect_incremental(root)`. Every `/graphify <subfolder> --update` run in a multi-subfolder workspace reads and writes the *same* manifest file, so the manifest only ever reflects whichever subfolder was graphed most recently. The comparison in `detect_incremental()`:

```python
current_files = {f for flist in full["files"].values() for f in flist}
deleted_files = [f for f in manifest if f not in current_files]
```

flags every manifest entry not under the *current* run's file set as deleted — including entries that were never under `root` to begin with.

### Impact

If the caller (e.g. the skill's `--update` flow) prunes graph nodes whose `source_file` is in `deleted_files`, this can silently remove nodes belonging to an *unrelated* subfolder's graph, depending on which graph is currently loaded. In our case the prune step happened to target the just-loaded subfolder graph, which contained none of the flagged paths, so the visible symptom was only a wrong "N files deleted" count in the diff report — but the mechanism is a correctness bug regardless of the specific graph layout, and could delete real nodes in a different call pattern (e.g. running `--update` against the *root* graph, or against a subfolder whose graph overlaps the previously-graphed one).

### Suggested fix

Scope the manifest path to `root` by default (e.g. `graphify-out/<sanitized-root>/manifest.json`, falling back to the existing flat path for the root-level `.` invocation to avoid a migration step for existing single-folder setups). Additionally, filter `deleted_files` to only include manifest entries that were ever under `root`, as defense in depth against a stale or manually merged manifest.

Happy to share a patch if useful — we worked around it locally by scoping `_MANIFEST_PATH` per-root and adding the under-root filter to `deleted_files`.

title: fix(dedup): give a real source location priority over richness in pick_winner
body:
Fixes #3775.

`_pick_winner()` picks the canonical survivor among colliding node records, ranked by `_content_richness()`. That score deliberately excludes `source_file`/`source_location` (per #3372, richness compares actual content, not placement) — but that means it has no way to tell a real, located declaration apart from a source-less stub that happens to carry a couple of incidental bookkeeping keys (`external`/`type`/`_origin`). The stub can out-score and replace the genuine record purely on field count.

Reproduced the issue's own exact repro directly against fresh `upstream/v8` in an isolated worktree before touching anything: a stub with `source_file: ""` (richness 3) beats a real node with `source_file`/`source_location` set (richness 2), and `_pick_winner` returns the stub.

Fix (the issue's own suggestion, correct and minimal): add a provenance tiebreak to the scoring tuple, ahead of richness but after the existing chunk-suffix check — a node with a real `source_file` always wins over one without. Only changes the outcome when the two sides disagree on provenance; every case where both (or neither) side has a source file keeps the exact `#3372` richness-then-length ordering.

Scoped correctly: code-type nodes never reach `_pick_winner` at all (`deduplicate_entities` skips `file_type == "code"`), so this only affects concept/document/paper/image nodes from the semantic extraction path — confirmed, not assumed.

Two regression tests in `tests/test_dedup_survivor_richness.py`: the issue's exact repro (checked in both argument orders), and a companion confirming the tiebreak stays inert when both candidates already carry a source file (proving the fix doesn't disturb the existing `#3372` ordering). The first test checked to fail against pre-fix code via `git stash` first. Full suite is green aside from the same 16 pre-existing failures from the Erlang/R/Solidity/VB.NET extractor tests needing optional grammar packages not installed in my environment (unrelated, already noted on other recent PRs).

title: Terraform secret redaction misses the name/value-pair idiom (AWS environment/secrets lists)
body:
Follow-up from #3762 (which extended secret redaction to list values).

The redaction keys off the attribute/map KEY matching `_SENSITIVE_KEY_RE` (password/secret/token/…). It does **not** catch the AWS name/value-pair idiom where the sensitive info is in a `value` paired with a `name`:

```hcl
environment = [
  { name = "DB_PASSWORD", value = "hunter2" },   # value leaks
]
secrets = [{ name = "API_KEY", valueFrom = "..." }]
```

Here the map keys are literally `name`/`value`/`valueFrom` — none match the sensitive-key set — so `hunter2` is captured into graph.json and the MCP surface verbatim. This is a **pre-existing limitation of key-name matching** (the map form `x = { name = "PASSWORD", value = "..." }` misses it too), not a regression from #3762; #3762 correctly closed the list-recursion gap it targeted.

Fix idea: when a map/object has both a `name`-like key and a `value`/`valueFrom` key, and the `name`'s literal value matches `_SENSITIVE_KEY_RE`, redact the paired `value`. Scope to ECS/Batch `containerDefinitions[].environment`/`secrets` and the generic `[{name,value}]` shape. Keep it conservative (only redact when the name literal is clearly a secret) to avoid over-redacting ordinary name/value config.

title: fix(hook-guard): fire the search nudge at most once per session
body:
Fixes #3756.

The strict read arm already blocks a raw file read at most once per session through an atomic marker (\`_mark_session_denied\`), but the search arm (\`kind == "search"\`) printed \`_SEARCH_NUDGE\` on every single matching Bash/Grep call with no session check at all. Measured on a real deployment: 12,094 nudges across 250 sessions, 99% repeats (median 34/session, max 968), ~600k wasted tokens.

Generalized the existing one-time claim mechanism into a small shared helper (\`_claim_session_marker\`) keyed on an arbitrary marker key and suffix, used by both the original strict deny and a new \`_mark_session_search_nudged\`.

Two details from the issue's own analysis, both preserved:
- **Keyed on \`session_id\` + \`agent_id\`, not \`session_id\` alone.** Verified via the official Claude Code hooks docs that \`agent_id\` is a real field, present only inside subagent hook calls. A subagent (including a fork) inherits the parent's \`session_id\` but starts with an empty context — keying on \`session_id\` alone would silently starve every subagent of the nudge, and would also let a fork that searched first consume the parent's own claim.
- **Claim only after deciding to nudge.** The matcher is \`Bash|Grep\`, so this arm runs on every Bash call; claiming before deciding would let an unrelated command (e.g. \`git status\`) spend the claim on nothing.

**A real bug I caught in my own first draft:** gating the nudge itself directly on the claim succeeding broke 11 existing tests, since several of them omit \`session_id\` from the payload — an empty key always fails to claim, so the nudge silently stopped firing at all for that case. Fixed by explicitly failing open when \`session_id\` is absent (always nudge, the pre-fix behavior), matching this function's own stated fail-open design, and only gating on the claim when a real \`session_id\` is present.

Five new regression tests in \`tests/test_hook_guard.py\`: same-session repeat stays silent, a different session still gets its own first nudge, a subagent sharing its parent's session still gets its own nudge via \`agent_id\`, a missing \`session_id\` still fails open, and an unrelated Bash call never spends the claim. The primary dedup test checked against pre-fix code via \`git stash\` first — correctly failed there. Full suite is green aside from the same 16 pre-existing failures from the Erlang/R/Solidity/VB.NET extractor tests needing optional grammar packages not installed in my environment (unrelated, already noted on other recent PRs).

title: feat(config): let projects declare languages for ambiguous extensions via .graphifyrc
body:
Carries the original `.graphifyrc` language-override work from #3075 by @abhay-codes07 onto the current `v8` base, preserving its commit authorship and messages, then layers the reviewed follow-up fixes developed while maintaining it in the pfBlockerNG fork.

## Relationship to #3075

- #3075 is the original implementation and remains the source of this branch's first two commits; both retain @abhay-codes07's authorship and commit messages.
- While carrying that work in the pfBlockerNG fork, we found follow-up fixes and opened [abhay-codes07/graphify#1](https://github.com/abhay-codes07/graphify/pull/1) directly against the original author's branch.
- This PR combines #3075, those follow-ups, and the small current-`v8` conflict/fixture adaptation into one tested branch. It is a current-base integration candidate, not a claim of original authorship; maintainers can choose whichever review/merge shape is easiest.

The automated integration rebuild consumes open PRs against this repository. Keeping the full stack represented here prevents the downstream build from dropping the follow-up fixes while #3075 remains open.


## The problem

`.inc` is hard-mapped to the Pascal extractor, but it means "include file" in whatever language a project actually uses: PHP on pfSense/pfBlockerNG, Pascal in a Delphi tree, SQL or assembly elsewhere. A PHP `.inc` parsed as Pascal doesn't fail loudly — it yields a handful of incidental nodes, so the graph looks populated while the real code is missing from it. The same ambiguity affects `.h` (C vs C++) and `.m` (Objective-C vs MATLAB).

pfBlockerNG depends on this: its `.graphifyrc` sets `language.inc=php` to parse 21 PHP include files (`pfblockerng.inc`, `pfblockerng_extra.inc`, etc.) into the tracked knowledge graph. Without the override, those 21 files contribute ~29 incidental (mis-parsed-as-Pascal) nodes; with it, they contribute the real corpus.

## The change

- `graphify/rcfile.py` (new): owns all `.graphifyrc` parsing — `viz_node_limit` (unchanged contract) plus `language.<ext>=<language-or-explicit-extension>`. Unknown keys are ignored (forward-compatible); malformed lines/values raise `ValueError` naming the offending line.
- Overrides are **thread-local**, not process-global, so two concurrent extractions (e.g. an MCP server handling multiple roots) never cross-contaminate which extractor a `.inc`/`.m`/`.h` gets.
- `graphify/hooks.py`'s `_load_graphifyrc` now delegates to `rcfile.load_graphifyrc`, keeping `viz_node_limit` working for existing callers/tests unchanged.
- `detect.py`, `extract.py`, `symbol_resolution.py`, `extractors/{resolution,csharp,ocaml,robot}.py`, `resolver_registry.py`, and `watch.py` all consult `effective_suffix()` so the override is honored consistently in classification, extraction, cross-file import/call resolution, and live graph refresh (edit `.graphifyrc` → the next `graphify watch`/`update` re-dispatches affected files).
- Explicit extensions (`language.tpl=.ets`) are validated against the known code/doc extension set at parse time.

## Testing

- `tests/test_language_overrides.py`, `tests/test_language_override_lifecycle.py`, `tests/test_pr10_csharp_overrides.py`, `tests/test_pr10_resolution_overrides.py`, `tests/test_pr10_watch_overrides.py` (new, cover the override contract end to end: parsing, thread-local activation, extraction/import/resolution dispatch, and watch-triggered re-extraction on `.graphifyrc` changes).
- `tests/test_backend_extras.py`, `tests/test_extract.py`, `tests/test_hooks.py` (existing upstream coverage, kept green — `test_hooks.py` in particular is upstream's own `.graphifyrc`/`viz_node_limit` contract test).

Rebased cleanly onto `v8` (0.9.67) with one manual conflict resolution in `graphify/extractors/resolution.py::_collect_python_symbol_resolution_facts`: upstream's absolute-import work added `ambiguous_python_modules = ambiguous_python_modules or set()` immediately before the `py_paths` filter that this stack changes from `path.suffix == ".py"` to `effective_suffix(path) == ".py"`. Both changes are independent and were combined (kept upstream's normalization, applied the override-aware suffix check). One pre-existing fixture in `test_language_overrides.py` was updated: it declared `.tpl=r` to exercise the "declared-but-no-extractor" warning path, but upstream 0.9.6x added a real (optional-dependency-gated) `.r` extractor since this stack was first written, so that scenario now hits the "dependency is missing" warning instead of "no AST extractor". Swapped the fixture to `.tpl=.ets` (ArkTS, a recognized code extension with no registered extractor today), which preserves the original invariant under test.

## Functional verification

Rebuilding pfBlockerNG's tree with this branch (`graphify update .`) against its `.graphifyrc` (`language.inc=php`) produces 940 nodes across all 21 `.inc` files (9 of them contributing more than one node), versus ~29 nodes without the override.

title: feat(llm): add agy-cli backend (Antigravity CLI, key-free Gemini)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an **`agy-cli`** LLM backend that routes semantic extraction and community labeling through the locally installed Antigravity CLI (`agy`) in headless mode — the same way `claude-cli` routes through `claude -p`.

**Why:** Gemini users without a `GEMINI_API_KEY` currently have no path. The standalone `gemini` CLI no longer works for individual accounts (`IneligibleTierError: This client is no longer supported for Gemini Code Assist for individuals … migrate to the Antigravity suite`), so an Antigravity subscription is now the key-free way to run Gemini.

**How it works** (mirrors `_call_claude_cli`):
- `agy -p=<prompt> --output-format json --model <id> --dangerously-skip-permissions [--json-schema …] [--add-dir …]`, prompt attached to `-p=` (a detached `-p` makes agy swallow the next argument).
- Extraction enforces structure with `--json-schema` instead of a replacement system prompt (agy has none). Every array declares `items` — Gemini rejects schemas without it. Labeling/dedup calls keep their plain-text prompt (no schema).
- Envelope handling: prefer `structured_output` when present, fall back to parsing `response`; a **zero exit code can still carry `status: "ERROR"`**, so status is checked and the `error` text is surfaced. Usage maps `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens` / `output_tokens`; pricing is 0 (subscription).
- Default model `gemini-3.8-flash-low`; override with `GRAPHIFY_AGY_CLI_MODEL`. Serial by default like `claude-cli`; opt in with `GRAPHIFY_AGY_CLI_PARALLEL=1`.
- CLI validation checks that `agy` is on `$PATH` (same branch shape as `claude-cli`) instead of falling through to the AWS-credentials error path.
- Images are passed by path with `--add-dir`, like `claude-cli`.
- Docs: README backend list + env-var table, CHANGELOG, and one sentence in the skill (via `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md`, artifacts regenerated with `--bless`) naming `claude-cli` / `agy-cli` as key-free alternatives to the Gemini API.

title: Fix: emit OpenCode 2 plugin and drop stale config entry
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3732.

OpenCode 2 does not run V1 plugin implementations. `graphify install --platform opencode` still wrote the V1 shape:

```js
export const GraphifyPlugin = async ({ directory }) => ({
  "tool.execute.before": async (input, output) => { /* ... */ },
})
```

so the installed plugin fails to load with:

> Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function.

OpenCode 2 requires a default export with an `id` and a `setup(ctx)` function, registers hooks on the owning domain (`ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", ...)`), names the command tool `shell` (not `bash`), and exposes the location as `ctx.location.directory`.

The V1 installer also registered the plugin in `.opencode/opencode.json` under the `plugin` key as a bare relative path:

```json
{ "plugin": [".opencode/plugins/graphify.js"] }
```

OpenCode 2 treats a bare specifier as an npm package spec, tries to install it, and fails:

> NpmInstallFailedError (cause: Error: Could not read package.json: Error: ENOTDIR: not a directory, open '.../.opencode/plugins/graphify.js/package.json')

OpenCode 2 already auto-discovers direct `.js`/`.ts` files under `.opencode/plugins/`, so no config entry is needed.

### Changes

- Port `_OPENCODE_PLUGIN_JS` to the V2 API: default export + `setup(ctx)`, `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", ...)`, `shell` tool, `ctx.location.directory`.
- Stop writing the `.opencode/opencode.json` entry; remove any legacy `plugin`/`plugins` entry on install and uninstall.
- Update tests and the `graphify --help` description.

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation

- [ ] Security fix

```text
# 131 passed, 1 skipped

uv run --frozen ruff check graphify/install.py graphify/__main__.py tests/test_install.py
# All checks passed!
```

Manual, on OpenCode 2.0.15:

```text
graphify install --platform opencode      # from a project dir
opencode plugin list
# ID        VERSION  SOURCE
# graphify  local    .../.opencode/plugins/graphify.js

opencode api get /api/plugin              # graphify: active, 0 failed plugins
```

The shell reminder still fires: a `shell` command returned the `[graphify]` reminder line when `graphify-out/graph.json` existed.

title: Python: module.func() calls into an external (never-parsed) package emit no calls edge at all — only the file-level import survives
body:
## Summary

`_resolve_python_member_calls`'s module arm (introduced in #1883, extended in #3430, further scoped in #2447) resolves `module.func()` calls, but only when `module` is a **local** file this build parsed. When `module` is a genuine third-party/stdlib import — the target node is `external: true`, with no source ever read — the resolver silently drops the call site entirely. No `calls` edge is ever emitted from the calling *function* into that dependency; the only edge that exists at all is the whole-file `import`/`imports_from` statement, sourced from the *file* node at the *import line*, which can't say which function (if any) ever calls into it, or where.

This is a distinct cause from #2447's A/B/C — those are all about a *local* module failing to resolve due to an id mismatch or an unreachable caller scope. Here the import edge and its target are both already correct; the resolver bails because an external target structurally can never satisfy `t in contains_children`, by design (graphify never parses external source, so it has no children to have).

## Root cause

`extract.py`, `_resolve_python_member_calls`, the module arm (module-arm.org line ~3656 in `graphifyy==0.9.65`):

```python
rkey = _key(receiver)
caller_file = file_of_node.get(caller)
file_aliases = import_alias_by_filenode.get(caller_file, {})
mods = [t for t in imported_by_filenode.get(caller_file, ())
        if t in contains_children
        and (_module_stem_key(t) == rkey or file_aliases.get(t) == rkey)]
if len(mods) != 1:  # not an imported module, or ambiguous -> bail
    continue
children = contains_children[mods[0]].get(_key(callee), [])
if len(children) != 1:  # absent or ambiguous callable -> bail
    continue
_emit_call(caller, children[0], rc)
```

`t in contains_children` requires the imported target to itself be the *source* of at least one `contains` edge — i.e. graphify parsed it and found declarations inside it. An external package's stub node never has this, by construction, so `mods` is always `[]` for a genuinely external receiver, and the branch falls straight through with nothing emitted. There's no separate arm for "the receiver resolves to exactly one imported *external* module — can't resolve the specific symbol, but the call site itself, at this function, at this line, is a real fact."

## Minimal reproduction

```
app.py
```
```python
import requests


def fetch_data(url):
    return requests.get(url)


def unrelated():
    return 1
```

`graphify.extract.extract()` (AST-only, `--code-only`, no LLM) on this single file produces:

```
nodes: app_fetch_data, app_unrelated, app (file), requests (external)
edges:
  imports        app        -> requests   (source_location: L1)
  contains       app        -> app_fetch_data
  contains       app        -> app_unrelated
```

**Expected:** a `calls` edge `app_fetch_data -> requests`, sourced at `L5` (the actual call site).
**Actual:** absent. The only edge touching `requests` is the file-level import statement at `L1`.

## Impact

Any reachability/call-graph analysis built on this data (blast-radius, taint-tracing from an entry point to a third-party sink, "does untrusted input reach code we can't audit") cannot tell *which* function in a file uses an import, or *whether* a specific code path (e.g. a request handler) ever reaches a given dependency — only that the file imports it somewhere. On a real request-heavy codebase this collapses to near-universal noise (every file that imports `requests` "reaches" it, regardless of which function actually calls it), which is functionally the same false-positive shape as an earlier fixed issue where a bare import statement was treated as if it were an executed call path.

Measured on the real `psf/requests` project (1,265 nodes, 2,444 edges pre-fix): **zero** `calls` edges into any of its 35 external targets exist at all — every one of the 171 edges touching an external node is `imports`/`imports_from`, sourced from a file node.

## Suggested fix

Add a fallback arm, after the existing local-module arm bails (`mods == []`, not ambiguous): if the receiver matches exactly one of the caller's imported targets that is *not* in `contains_children` (i.e. genuinely unresolvable further, external or otherwise), emit a `calls` edge from the real caller function, at the real call-site location, directly to that import target — the same identity `_emit_call` already uses for the local case, just without trying to resolve past it to a specific member.

One implementation wrinkle found while verifying a local patch: at the point this resolver runs, an external stub's node does not yet exist in `node_by_id` (its node is materialized in a later pass), so gating the new arm on the `external` field silently matches nothing. Matching the import target's *id* directly (rather than looking up the node and checking a field on it) avoids the ordering dependency — it can only ever succeed on an exact id match, so it can't accidentally absorb an unrelated node.

Verified this shape of fix against `psf/requests`: 53 new `calls` edges appeared, each at a real call-site line (spot-checked several by hand against the source — e.g. `_basic_auth_str()` in `src/requests/auth.py` correctly resolves to `warnings` at line 45, the real `warnings.warn(...)` call), zero regressions against the pre-fix graph's other 2,444 edges (identical `contains`/`references`/`imports`/`method`/etc. counts, no edge removed).

## Related

- #1883 — introduced this resolver, local-module case only.
- #3430 — fixed a local-module id-mismatch case within the same arm.
- #2447 — three further local-module bail causes in the same arm, still open. This report is a fourth, independent cause specific to genuinely external (never-parsed) targets, not a local-module id or scope problem.

## Environment

- `graphifyy==0.9.65` (PyPI)
- Windows 11
- AST-only extraction (`--code-only`), no LLM, no semantic pass

title: GRAPH_REPORT.md: community Nodes listing includes rationale/concept nodes, so docstring fragments print as node names
body:
## Summary

`GRAPH_REPORT.md`'s per-community `Nodes (N): ...` listing includes `rationale` (docstring-fragment) and `concept` nodes as if they were real code declarations, so a community's node list can read like raw docstring prose — e.g. on `code2flow` (a real, small Python project):

```
### Community 14 - "Community 14"
Cohesion: 0.09
Nodes (13): Node, Check whether this variable is what the call is acting on. For example, if we…, Names exist largely for unit tests and deterministic node sorting :rtype: str, ...
```

`"Names exist largely for unit tests and deterministic node sorting :rtype: str"` is the literal docstring of `code2flow/model.py`'s `Node.name()` method (`file_type: "rationale"`), not a node name. It's listed as if it were one, and it also inflates the community's reported size (`len(real_nodes)`, which counts it).

## Root cause

This is the same bug class as the closed #1768 (`suggest_questions()` vs `report.py`'s Knowledge Gaps disagreeing over a missing `rationale` filter) — but a third, still-unfixed spot, inside `report.py` itself this time.

`report.py`, the community-rendering loop (~line 284):
```python
# Filter method/function stubs from display - they're structural noise
real_nodes = [n for n in nodes if not _ifn(G, n)]
```
`_ifn` is `_is_file_node` (imported from `.analyze`) — it excludes file nodes only.

Compare the Knowledge Gaps section, ~30 lines later in the *same function*:
```python
isolated = [
    n for n in G.nodes()
    if G.degree(n) <= 1
    and not _is_file_node(G, n)
    and not _is_concept_node(G, n)
    and G.nodes[n].get("file_type") != "rationale"
]
```
This one correctly excludes file, concept, *and* rationale nodes — the exact exclusion set #1768 established as the right one for report.py. The community-listing loop was never given the same treatment, so rationale (and concept) nodes still leak into `Nodes (N): ...` even though the codebase already knows how to filter them out, a few lines below.

## Minimal reproduction

```
pip install graphifyy
git clone https://github.com/scottrogowski/code2flow
graphify code2flow --code-only --no-label
```
Open `code2flow/graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` and look at any community whose members include a `Node`/model-style class with docstrings — several communities list docstring text (including truncated `…` mid-sentence, and `:param`/`:rtype:` Sphinx directives) directly in the `Nodes (N): ...` line.

## Suggested fix

```python
real_nodes = [
    n for n in nodes
    if not _is_file_node(G, n)
    and not _is_concept_node(G, n)
    and G.nodes[n].get("file_type") != "rationale"
]
```
i.e. reuse the exact filter the Knowledge Gaps section already applies, in the community-rendering loop too.

## Related

- #1768 — same missing-rationale-filter pattern, different location (`analyze.py` vs `report.py`'s own Knowledge Gaps section). Fixed there; this is the one place inside `report.py` that fix didn't reach.
- #751 / #2206 — about *reducing* how often rationale nodes get created in the first place; this report is about *display filtering* given that they exist, which is needed regardless of how that's resolved.

## Environment

- `graphifyy==0.9.65` (PyPI)
- Windows 11
- AST-only extraction (`--code-only --no-label`), no LLM

body:
## What

Adds an `omp` install platform so graphify's skill can be installed where Oh My Pi (OMP) actually reads agent skills from: `~/.omp/agent/skills/graphify` (global) and `.omp/agent/skills/graphify` (project scope).

## Why

OMP mirrors pi's agent layout under `~/.omp`, not the legacy `~/.pi` path the `pi` platform writes. `graphify install --platform omp` therefore failed as an unknown platform, leaving OMP without a graphify skill while every other platform had one. `omp` was already reserved in the CLI command set as a no-op placeholder; this gives it its implementation.

## Changes

- `_PLATFORM_CONFIG`: new `omp` entry reusing pi's skill bundle (`skill-pi.md` + pi's `references/` sidecar) — OMP uses the same skill format, so a second bundle would only drift.
- `_CLI_INSTALL_COMMANDS`: register `omp`.
- `_project_install` / `_project_uninstall`: join the skill-only project group (copilot, pi, kimi, agents).
- `dispatch_install_cli`: the pi-twin `graphify omp [install|uninstall]` subcommand.
- `tests/test_omp_platform.py`: destinations, bundle reuse, end-to-end install/uninstall via the CLI, subcommand behavior, the unknown-platform error listing omp, and `uninstall_all` parity with pi (the global flag form leaves the user-scope skill to the platform subcommand, exactly as it does for pi).

## Test plan

- New suite: 8/8 green (red before the production change).
- Install regression suites: `test_agents_platform`, `test_antigravity_install`, `test_uninstall_scope`, `test_wheel_packaging`, `test_apm_fallback_version`, `test_atomic_version_stamp` — 174 passed.

title: [Bug]: Windows: `_pin_hash_seed_if_needed` re-exec returns before the command finishes, or segfaults
body:
### What happened?

`graphify extract` / `update` / `cluster-only` / `label` re-exec themselves via `os.execvpe` to
pin `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` (#3641, #3779) when the caller has not set it. On Windows `os.exec*` does
not replace the process: CPython starts a new process and the calling one exits. The caller
therefore sees the command finish immediately while the real work continues detached, and in
some runs the process crashes instead.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
Repro (Git Bash, any small corpus, `PYTHONHASHSEED` unset):

rm -rf graphify-out
env -u PYTHONHASHSEED python -m graphify extract . --code-only; echo "exit=$?"
ls graphify-out/graph.json


Observed over three runs:
- exit 0 after ~0.5 s, `graph.json` absent on return, appears a few seconds later (the detached
  child finished it);
- exit 139 (segmentation fault / access violation), no output (twice).
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Effect: any script that runs `extract` and then reads `graph.json` (or runs `cluster-only`) fails
intermittently on Windows. Setting `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` before calling graphify avoids the re-exec
and everything works.

Suggested fix: on Windows (`os.name == "nt"`), run the child with
`subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "graphify", *sys.argv[1:]], env=...)` and
`sys.exit(result.returncode)` instead of `os.execvpe`, so the parent waits and propagates the
exit status.
```

### Graphify version

_No response_

### Environment

graphify 0.9.67 (pip `graphifyy`), Python 3.13.1, Windows 10 (10.0.19045)

### Additional context

_No response_

GRAPH_REPORT.md offers 'undocumented components' as a possible cause on graphs that structurally cannot have one
body:
## Summary

`GRAPH_REPORT.md`'s Knowledge Gaps section always offers the same two possible explanations for an isolated node, regardless of whether the graph could ever actually support one of them:

> These have ≤1 connection - possible missing edges or undocumented components.

"Undocumented components" only means anything when a semantic layer exists — document/paper/image nodes an LLM extracted meaning from, where an isolated node genuinely could be "mentioned but never explained further." A code-only graph (`--code-only`, or any run where semantic extraction never happened) has no such layer at all: there is nothing to be "undocumented" about, ever, on that graph. Offering it as a live possibility on every report regardless is misleading — a reader with a pure-code graph has no way to know that half the explanation offered to them can never be true.

Verified across 12 real code-only projects in this run: 0/12 ever had a document/paper/image node, and 100% of their isolated-node messages still offered "undocumented components" as if it might apply.

## Root cause

`report.py`, the Knowledge Gaps section:
```python
lines.append(
    "  These have ≤1 connection - possible missing edges or undocumented components. "
    ...
)
```
This string is unconditional — it never checks whether the graph has anything that could BE undocumented.

## Suggested fix

The information needed is already in the graph, no new build-time flag required — `VALID_FILE_TYPES` (`validate.py`) already distinguishes `document`/`paper`/`image` from `code`/`rationale`/`concept`:
```python
has_semantic_layer = any(
    G.nodes[n].get("file_type") in ("document", "paper", "image")
    for n in G.nodes()
)
reason = (
    "possible missing edges or undocumented components"
    if has_semantic_layer else "possible missing edges"
)
lines.append(f"  These have ≤1 connection - {reason}. ...")
```

Patched and verified locally: regenerated all 12 real code-only projects' `GRAPH_REPORT.md` — every one now reads "possible missing edges" only, with no wording claiming a possibility the graph structurally cannot have.

## Related

- #3794 — same section, a different defect (rationale/concept nodes leaking into counts rather than the wording being unconditional).
- #1768 — established that this exact function has repeatedly needed its counting/wording tightened against rationale/concept/semantic distinctions.

## Environment

- `graphifyy==0.9.65` (PyPI)
- Windows 11
- AST-only extraction (`--code-only --no-label`), no LLM

title: Bash extractor: record script invocations (python3 x.py, bash y.sh) as edges
body:
The bash extractor records functions, `source` imports and calls between functions, but not the
programs a script runs. In a pipeline driven by a shell script, that is most of what the script does:

    python3 scripts/stage_one.py --client "$C"
    bash scripts/other_step.sh "$C"
    "$PYTHON" scripts/stage_two.py

None of these produce an edge today, so `graphify path "runner.sh" "stage_one.py"` finds nothing and the
orchestrator looks disconnected from every stage it runs.

Checked on 0.8.44 and 0.9.67 (graphify/extractors/bash.py): on a 2,000+ line orchestrator script the
extractor produced 20 nodes and 30 edges (defines 18, calls 11, contains 1) and zero edges to other files.

Suggestion: when a command's first word is an interpreter (python, python3, bash, sh, node, or a
variable like "$PYTHON") and an argument is a path to a file in the repo, add an `invokes` edge from
the script to that file. Plain `./path/to/tool` could be treated the same way.

title: graphify export falkordb: MERGE without an index causes O(n²) push, 100x slowdown on large graphs
body:
## What happened

Pushing a 167,428-node / 209,215-edge graph (`graphify export falkordb --push falkordb://localhost:6379`) started fast (~10,000 node upserts/60s) and then collapsed to ~100 upserts/300s partway through, with the FalkorDB container pegged at ~97% CPU. Total wall time for the full push was multiple hours.

## Root cause

`push_to_falkordb` in `graphify/exporters/graphdb.py` issues, per node:

```python
graph.query(
    f"MERGE (n:{ftype} {{id: $id}}) SET n += $props",
    {"id": node_id, "props": props},
)
```

No index is created on `(label, id)` before this loop runs. Without one, `MERGE` on the match pattern does a full label scan to check for an existing node, so each upsert costs O(current nodes with that label) — the whole push is O(n²) in the number of nodes per label.

## Workaround (confirmed fix)

Creating one index per label before the push restores linear-time throughput:

```
for label in <distinct capitalized file_type labels in the graph>; do
  redis-cli -p 6379 GRAPH.QUERY <graph_name> "CREATE INDEX FOR (n:$label) ON (n.id)"
done
```

Verified on the graph above: after adding the indexes, throughput recovered to the original ~10,000 upserts/60s rate for the remainder of the push.

## Suggested fix

Have `push_to_falkordb` (and the equivalent Neo4j path, if it has the same gap) create `CREATE INDEX FOR (n:<label>) ON (n.id)` for each distinct node label present in the graph before the node-upsert loop runs, the same way a `CREATE CONSTRAINT`/index-first pattern is standard for bulk Cypher loads. This is idempotent and safe to run on every push, including re-runs against an already-populated graph.

## Environment

- `graphifyy` 0.9.67
- FalkorDB (`falkordb/falkordb:latest`, Docker)
- Graph: 167,428 nodes across 6 labels (Code, Concept, Document, Image, Paper, Rationale), 209,215 edges

title: install --platform claude: registration block is written through a symlinked ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, with no opt-out
body:
graphifyy 0.9.67, macOS arm64, installed via `uv tool install graphifyy`.

## What happened

`graphify install --platform claude` printed:

```
  skill installed  ->  ~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md
  CLAUDE.md        ->  skill registered in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
```

On this machine `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is a symlink:

```
$ ls -l ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
lrwxr-xr-x  ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md -> ~/AGENTS.md
```

`_write_always_on_block` opens the path in text mode, so the block was appended to the **symlink target** — a top-level rules document that is the single source of truth for this setup and is deliberately kept outside `~/.claude`. The output named `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, so nothing in it suggested a file elsewhere had been modified. I only found it by diffing the rules file afterwards.

The docstring around `install.py:394` already anticipates symlinked `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (nix/home-manager, chezmoi, stow) — but only for the case where the write *fails*. When the symlink is writable, the write silently lands wherever it points.

## Repro

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/t/.claude && printf '# my rules\n' > /tmp/t/rules.md
ln -s /tmp/t/rules.md /tmp/t/.claude/CLAUDE.md
HOME=/tmp/t graphify install --platform claude
tail -5 /tmp/t/rules.md   # graphify block is here, not in a file named CLAUDE.md
```

## Asks

1. **Resolve the symlink in the output.** `skill registered in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md -> ~/AGENTS.md` would have made this a non-event.
2. **An opt-out.** `claude_md` is a hardcoded `True` in `_PLATFORM_CONFIG["claude"]` with no CLI flag to skip it, so there is no supported way to install the skill without touching the rules file. A `--no-claude-md` (or `--skill-only`) flag would cover both the symlink case and anyone who keeps their rules file under strict change control.
3. **Consider whether the block is still needed for this platform.** Claude Code auto-discovers `~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` and surfaces the skill by its frontmatter `description:` — the skill was listed and invocable with the registration block removed. If that holds generally, the always-on block is redundant for `--platform claude` and could default to off there.

## Related: a tuned `description:` does not survive an upgrade

Adjacent to #3144. The packaged `description:` is broad ("Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content"), which in practice makes the skill trigger on ordinary code questions where a knowledge graph is not wanted. Narrowing `description:` fixes that, but every `install`/upgrade overwrites it — the `.bak` is announced, which helps, yet the narrowing has to be re-applied by hand each time.

Would you take a patch that preserves an existing frontmatter `description:` on re-install (or gates it behind `--keep-local-description`)? Happy to send one.

title: [Bug]: Maven POM ingestion drops most inter-module `depends_on` edges: inherited groupId and `${...}` properties are not resolved
body:
### What happened?

## Summary
  
  `_parse_pom` (`graphify/manifest_ingest.py`) builds each module's package id and each
  dependency's id from the literal text of the POM. Two common Maven patterns make those ids
  disagree, so the `depends_on` edge points at a node that doesn't exist and is pruned as dangling
  by `build_from_json`:

  1. **Inherited groupId.** A module that takes its `groupId` from `<parent>` — the norm in a
     multi-module reactor — gets the bare id `artifactId`, because `root.findtext("groupId")` only
     reads the module's own top-level element:

     ```python
     gid = root.findtext("groupId")          # None when inherited from <parent>
     name = f"{gid}:{aid}" if gid else aid   # -> "livy-server", not "org.apache.livy:livy-server"
     ```

     Dependencies on it always carry a groupId (Maven requires it), so they are emitted as
     `org.apache.livy:livy-server` and never match. **Such a module can never be the target of an
     edge.**

  2. **Unresolved properties.** `${project.groupId}`, `${scala.binary.version}` and any other
     property are kept verbatim in dependency coordinates (`${project.groupId}:livy-rsc`,
     `livy-core_${scala.binary.version}`), while the target module's own id is written out
     (`org.apache.livy:livy-rsc`). No match, no edge.

  The failure is silent: nodes for every module are created, only the edges are missing.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
apache/livy` (21 modules) shows both causes in one file.

  
  git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/apache/livy.git
  cd livy && graphify update .
  graphify explain "livy-server"
  

  `server/pom.xml` declares four internal dependencies; the graph keeps one:

  | Dependency | `groupId` | `artifactId` | Target's own id | Edge |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `livy-test-lib` | `org.apache.livy` | `livy-test-lib` | `org.apache.livy:livy-test-lib` | ✅ |
  | `livy-rsc` | `${project.groupId}` | `livy-rsc` | `org.apache.livy:livy-rsc` | ❌ (2) |
  | `livy-core` | `${project.groupId}` | `livy-core_${scala.binary.version}` | `livy-core-parent` / `livy-core_2.12` | ❌ (1, 2) |
  | `livy-repl` | `org.apache.livy` | `livy-repl_${scala.binary.version}` | `livy-repl-parent` / `livy-repl_2.12` | ❌ (1, 2) |

  Across the repo:

  - The POMs declare **55** inter-module dependencies; the graph contains **18** `depends_on`
    edges between modules.
  - 8 of the 25 module nodes inherit their groupId (`livy-server`, `livy-core-parent`,
    `livy-repl-parent`, `livy-scala-api-parent`, `livy-integration-test`, `livy-assembly`,
    `livy-beeline`, `livy-coverage-report`). **None of the 18 edges targets any of them.**
  - Asked "which modules depend on `livy-core`?", the graph answers none; the POMs list 8.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Inter-module dependencies resolve to their module nodes, as they would under Maven's own effective-POM rules.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.67

### Environment

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_
