title: [Feature]: Stable way for external tools to supply community labels
body:
### Problem or use case

I name communities with an external tool and hand the names to graphify through `.graphify_labels.json`. It works: `cluster-only` picks them up and the report, `graph.json` and `graph.html` all use them.

The catch is that `cluster-only` only keeps a saved label if `.graphify_labels.json.sig` matches `graphify.cluster.community_member_sigs`. I had to copy that function byte for byte. If it ever changes, every external label quietly turns back into a hub name, with no error.

### Proposed solution

Either of these would do:

1. Treat the labels file and its `.sig` as a supported format: document it and add a test that pins `community_member_sigs`.
2. Add `graphify label --from names.json`, which takes a `{cid: name}` map and writes the `.sig` itself, so outside tools never have to touch the hash.

### Alternatives considered

Adding another LLM backend doesn't help. The open labeling bugs (#3671, #3747) come from free-text generation itself.

### Area

Graph building or querying

### Additional context

My tool is [jev-graphify](https://github.com/190ibrahim/jev-graphify). It doesn't generate names. It builds candidates from the graph (hub, classes, files, common words) and has [TypeSafe Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai) pick one, so there are no empty or cut-off names. It uses no LLM key.

On a ROS 2 repo (5,025 nodes, 247 communities) it named 237 communities in about 9 seconds for $0.02, and `cluster-only` kept all of them. So far it has only been tested on that one codebase.

Happy to open a PR for either option if you're open to it.

title: [Bug]: deduplicate_entities drops every pre-existing self-loop once it merges any node
body:
### What happened?

When `deduplicate_entities` merges at least one pair of nodes, it rewrites every edge and keeps only those with `source != target`. So every self-loop in the graph is dropped, including ones the merge had nothing to do with: recursive calls from the AST pass, and self-referencing foreign keys from `--postgres` (a `parent_id` on a `categories` table, for instance).

https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/4c735618f3d56fd622c2049771584621c31ba9ff/graphify/dedup.py#L1033

```python
        if e["source"] != e["target"]:
            deduped_edges.append(e)
```

In practice this hits incremental `graphify extract` runs with a semantic pass: the LLM often returns a duplicate concept, dedup merges it, and all self-loops disappear. A later code-only run brings back only the self-loops of files it re-extracts — the Postgres schema is introspected on every run, so the FK self-loops return, but a recursive call stays missing until its file changes. The graph's edges therefore depend on whether an unrelated merge happened in the last run.

Expected: only self-loops created by the merge itself are dropped (an edge `a → b` whose endpoints merge into one node). Pre-existing self-loops are kept — the rule graphify already follows elsewhere: the doc remap in `build.py` ("Drop only self-loops the remap itself collapsed … leave any pre-existing self-loop alone", [build.py#L1018](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/4c735618f3d56fd622c2049771584621c31ba9ff/graphify/build.py#L1018)), and the Swift-extension merge keeping untouched edges verbatim (#2538, [extract.py#L3434](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/4c735618f3d56fd622c2049771584621c31ba9ff/graphify/extract.py#L3434)).

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
cat > repro_selfloops.py <<'EOF'
from graphify.dedup import deduplicate_entities

nodes = [
    {"id": "walk", "label": "walk()", "source_file": "src/tree.py", "file_type": "code"},
    {"id": "categories", "label": "categories", "source_file": "schema.sql", "file_type": "code"},
    # two same-label concepts from one document: the exact pass merges them
    {"id": "cache", "label": "Cache", "source_file": "docs/guide.md", "file_type": "concept"},
    {"id": "cache_2", "label": "cache", "source_file": "docs/guide.md", "file_type": "concept"},
]
edges = [
    {"source": "walk", "target": "walk", "relation": "calls"},                   # recursive call
    {"source": "categories", "target": "categories", "relation": "references"},  # self-referencing FK
    {"source": "cache_2", "target": "walk", "relation": "references"},
]

def loops(es):
    return [(e["source"], e["relation"]) for e in es if e["source"] == e["target"]]

print("self-loops in:     ", loops(edges))
_, merged = deduplicate_entities([dict(n) for n in nodes], [dict(e) for e in edges], communities={})
print("after a merge:     ", loops(merged))
_, unmerged = deduplicate_entities([dict(n) for n in nodes[:3]], [dict(e) for e in edges[:2]], communities={})
print("with nothing to merge:", loops(unmerged))
EOF
python repro_selfloops.py
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
self-loops in:      [('walk', 'calls'), ('categories', 'references')]
[graphify] Deduplicated 1 node(s) (1 exact).
after a merge:      []
with nothing to merge: [('walk', 'calls'), ('categories', 'references')]
```

### Graphify version

0.9.61 (the same filter is on `v8` at 4c73561)

### Environment

macOS 27, Python 3.13.11, uv tool install

### Additional context

A possible fix, in the same spirit as the doc remap — keep an edge that was already a self-loop before the remap:

```python
        e["source"] = remap.get(src, src)
        e["target"] = remap.get(tgt, tgt)
        # Remove legacy keys so they don't leak into edge attrs in graph.json.
        e.pop("from", None)
        e.pop("to", None)
        if e["source"] != e["target"] or src == tgt:
            deduped_edges.append(e)
```

Until then we wrap `deduplicate_entities` and re-append the incoming self-loops whose node survived the merge.

title: MCP query tools: single-word seeding crosses domains, default budget truncates most results
body:
graphifyy 0.9.67, `graphify.serve` MCP, graph of 167k nodes / 889 communities built from a mixed book corpus.

**1. Seeding matches single words from the question.**
`query_graph("incidence algebra derivations poset")` seeds on `Poset`, `Incidence`, `Derivations`, `Algebra`. `Incidence` resolves to a node from a biostatistics book, so the BFS pulls in an unrelated community. The same happens with "quantum", which matches a quantum machine learning book for a question about quantum Grassmannians. Related to #2384 and #2381, which cover other seed-selection failures; this one is about cross-domain single-token matches. Suggestion: try multi-word phrase matches against labels first, and fall back to single tokens only when no phrase matches.

**2. The default token budget drops 85-90% of nodes.**
With the default budget, the two queries above showed 35 of 240 and 41 of 400 nodes. The truncation warning is clear, but this is the effect #2530 describes, measured on a 167k-node graph. A larger default (or ranking nodes by relevance to the question before cutting) would help agents that do not retry.

**3. `shortest_path` resolves fuzzy labels to whole-document nodes.**
`shortest_path("quantum Grassmannian", "incidence algebra")` resolved the source to a book-title node. Returning the resolved endpoints, or several candidate matches, would make the result easier to interpret.

title: fix: preserve cross-file edges during incremental updates
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3776 

Fixes the loss of cross-file `imports` and `calls` edges when re-extracting files during incremental updates.

Previously, symbol resolution only indexed freshly extracted nodes. When a changed file imported or called a symbol defined in an unchanged file, the target symbol was unavailable during resolution and the edge was silently skipped.

## Changes

* Pass `resolution_context_nodes` into the symbol-resolution pipeline.
* Include unchanged-file symbols when building the resolution index.
* Ensure freshly extracted nodes take precedence over resolution-context nodes.
* Preserve existing incremental edge reconciliation and removed-import pruning behavior.
* Add a regression test covering cross-file imports and calls to an unchanged file.

## Validation

* `pytest tests/test_incremental.py` — 11 passed
* `pytest tests/test_symbol_resolution.py tests/test_python_import_resolution.py tests/test_forwarding_review_findings.py tests/test_imported_export_forwarding.py` — 66 passed
* `pytest tests/test_js_import_resolution.py` — 71 passed
* `pytest -k "incremental or resolution" tests/test_watch.py` — 36 passed, 1 skipped
* `git diff --check` — clean

## Scope

This PR addresses the symbol-resolution issue causing `imports` and `calls` to disappear during incremental updates.

The separate non-relative `imports_from` target-canonicalization issue is not included in this change.

title: fix(cobol): detect fixed-format source that carries sequence numbers
body:
## What

The COBOL fixed/free format detector counts a line as fixed-format only when its first six columns are **blank** (`^ {6}[ *\-/ ]`). But legacy mainframe COBOL â€” the main reason a COBOL extractor exists â€” puts a **sequence number** in columns 1-6. Such a file scores zero fixed markers and is misclassified as free-format.

In free mode the code is taken verbatim (no column-8 slice), so the sequence number stays glued to the statement. `000400 MAIN-PARA.` then no longer matches the paragraph anchor `^(NAME)(?: SECTION)?\s*\.\s*$`, and **the entire procedure layer disappears**: a seven-line program with two paragraphs and a `PERFORM` collapses to just the file and program nodes â€” zero paragraphs, zero `calls` edges â€” silently.

```
$ extract_cobol(seq_numbered.cob)   # before
  program=[PAYROLL] paragraphs=[] calls=0     # 2 nodes total
$ extract_cobol(seq_numbered.cob)   # after
  program=[PAYROLL] paragraphs=[MAIN-PARA, INIT-PARA] calls=1
```

## Fix

Count a fixed-format marker when the six-column sequence area is **six spaces OR six digits**, followed by a valid indicator column (space = code, `*`/`/` = comment, `-` = continuation, `D` = debug): `^(?: {6}|\d{6})[ *\-/dD]`. Once the file is correctly read as fixed-format, the existing column-8..72 slice already strips the sequence number and indicator, so paragraphs and `PERFORM`s resolve normally.

A six-digit prefix is not something free-format code begins a line with, so blank-sequence fixed-format and genuinely free-format source are both unaffected (verified).

## Verification

- Reproduced: a sequence-numbered program yielded only 2 nodes and 0 `calls` before.
- The new regression test asserts the program, both paragraphs, and the `PERFORM` `calls` edge â€” and **fails on the old detector**.
- Blank-sequence fixed-format and free-format inputs still extract their paragraphs and calls (no regression). All COBOL extractor tests pass.

title: fix(cobol): link both endpoints of a PERFORM ... THRU range
body:
## What

`PERFORM A THRU Z` (and `THROUGH`) runs the whole paragraph range A..Z, but the PERFORM pattern captured only the first name â€” so a `calls` edge was emitted to `A` and the range-end `Z` got **none**. "What performs Z?" then answered nothing even though this paragraph does, and any reachability walk stopped short of the range's tail. THRU-based flow is common in legacy COBOL.

```
PERFORM A-PARA THRU Z-PARA   # before: calls -> A-PARA only
                             # after:  calls -> A-PARA AND Z-PARA
```

## Fix

Capture the optional `THRU`/`THROUGH` target in the PERFORM pattern and enqueue both endpoints for resolution against the paragraph table. Intermediate paragraphs in the range are not individually linked (that would need paragraph source ordering); the two endpoints are the reliable, common signal and both now resolve. A plain `PERFORM A` is unchanged.

## Verification

Regression test: `PERFORM A-PARA THRU Z-PARA` now links `MAIN-PARA` to both `A-PARA` and `Z-PARA`, and **fails on the old single-capture pattern**. All COBOL extractor tests pass.

Previously, enum members, properties, and methods could collide with actual type names during C# type resolution. The initial fix introduced a `contains`-edge requirement, which caused a regression for partial/cross-repo graphs that do not contain structural `contains` edges.

This update removes that requirement and instead excludes nodes that are targets of member-specific relations.

title: fix(cli): wait for the hash-seed re-exec on Windows instead of os.execvpe (#3799)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3799.

On Windows `os.exec*` does not replace the process: CPython spawns a new one and the calling process exits immediately. So `update` / `extract` / `cluster-only` / `label` (the commands that pin `PYTHONHASHSEED` via `_pin_hash_seed_if_needed`) returned before `graph.json` was written, and the exiting parent intermittently died with an access violation (exit 139 / `0xC0000005`).

This PR moves the re-exec into a small `_reexec(argv, env)` helper:

- **POSIX:** unchanged, a real `os.execvpe`.
- **Windows:** runs the child with `subprocess.run`, waits for it, and exits with the child's return code (as suggested in the issue).

The existing `OSError` fallback (keep running without the pin) still applies to both branches.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## How was this tested?

Windows 11, Python 3.12, graphify 0.9.67 (pip `graphifyy`), small TSX corpus, `PYTHONHASHSEED` unset:

```text
before: python -m graphify update .   -> 6/6 runs exit 139 (Windows fatal exception: access violation in os.execvpe)
after:  python -m graphify update .   -> 8/8 runs exit 0, graph.json present when the command returns

pytest tests/test_pin_hash_seed.py      -> 10 passed
full suite, before vs after this change (same machine): identical failure set, except
  tests/test_pin_hash_seed.py::test_update_still_runs_end_to_end_with_hashseed_unset
  which fails on Windows before this change and passes after it.
  (The remaining failures are pre-existing on Windows / missing optional extras and
  unrelated to this change.)
```

Test changes: the subprocess probes now stub `_reexec` instead of `os.execvpe` (so on a Windows CI runner they never spawn a real child), and two unit tests cover the POSIX `execvpe` branch and the Windows wait-and-propagate branch.

title: fix(terraform): redact secret-named variable defaults and output values
body:
## What does this PR do?

Terraform secret redaction (#3644, #3762) keys off the attribute name, so it misses a secret named by the block label. `variable` and `output` blocks keep the secret's name in their label and the literal under a generic key (`default` for a variable, `value` for an output). This input:

```hcl
variable "db_password" {
  type    = string
  default = "hunter2"
}
output "admin_token" {
  value = "tok-123"
}
```

wrote `"default": "hunter2"` and `"value": "tok-123"` into `graph.json`, and the MCP `query`/`get_node` surface returned them unredacted. A `password = ...` attribute in the same file was already redacted.

The fix is in `graphify/extractors/terraform.py`, where attributes are attached to their owner block. For a `variable` or `output` block, it redacts `default`/`value` in two cases: the block label matches the existing `_SENSITIVE_KEY_RE`, or the block sets Terraform's own `sensitive = true`. Ordinary variables and outputs such as `variable "region"` and `output "bucket_name"` are unchanged. All other keys on the block, such as `type`, stay visible.

This PR does not overlap #3787, which covers the `{ name = "DB_PASSWORD", value = ... }` pair idiom. This PR covers the block-label and `sensitive = true` cases.

title: fix(wiki): keep an article labelled index from overwriting index.md
body:
## What does this PR do?

`to_wiki` writes `index.md` as the catalog, but the slug-dedup set never reserved that name. An article whose label slugs to `index` was written to `index.md` and then overwritten by the catalog. This happens with a god node labelled `index()` (a common web view), a community that the default hub labeler names after one, or an `Index` god node on a case-insensitive filesystem. The catalog entry for that article then linked back to the catalog itself (`[index()](index.md)`), and `to_wiki` still counted the lost article as written.

Reproduced end to end with a small Python project whose `index()` view calls four helpers, then `graphify update .` and `graphify export wiki`:

```text
v8:  wiki/ has no article for index(); index.md lists "- [index()](index.md) — 5 connections"
fix: wiki/index_2.md holds the index() article; index.md lists "- [index()](index_2.md) — 5 connections"
```

Fix, in `graphify/wiki.py`:

title: [Bug]: Codex Step B3 can overwrite in-memory semantic results with an empty disk merge
body:
## What happened?

The Codex skill has incompatible result-collection instructions between Step B2 and the shared Step B3. This affects host-agent semantic extraction for documents, papers, and images.

Step B2 instructs the parent to collect returned JSON in memory and write `graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json`. It explicitly says there are no per-chunk files and that Step B3's disk-based success checks do not apply.

However, Step B3 still:

1. Requires `.graphify_chunk_NN.json` files as the success signal and recommends a Claude-specific `general-purpose` agent when they are missing.
2. Unconditionally runs a disk-based merge over `.graphify_chunk_*.json`, then overwrites `.graphify_semantic_new.json`.

Consequently, following B3's checks can incorrectly classify successful Codex results as failures. Skipping only those checks, as B2 instructs, is insufficient: running the subsequent merge with no chunk files overwrites the collected results with empty arrays.

Expected: Codex follows the same file-based semantic extraction pipeline as Claude. Each write-capable subagent writes its extraction JSON directly to the assigned absolute CHUNK_PATH (.graphify_chunk_NN.json), and the parent uses the shared Step B3 to validate, collect, cache, and merge those files without losing results. B2 and B3 must agree on this contract.

## Source references

Confirmed against current `v8` commit `4c735618f3d56fd622c2049771584621c31ba9ff`:

- [Codex B2 generator fragment](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/4c735618f3d56fd622c2049771584621c31ba9ff/tools/skillgen/fragments/dispatch/codex-agenttask.md#L13-L18)
- [Shared B3 generator fragment](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/4c735618f3d56fd622c2049771584621c31ba9ff/tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md#L214-L250)
- [Generated Codex skill](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/4c735618f3d56fd622c2049771584621c31ba9ff/graphify/skill-codex.md#L265-L313)
- [Existing Codex regression test](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/4c735618f3d56fd622c2049771584621c31ba9ff/tests/test_skillgen.py#L303-L316) checks the memory-collection wording and B2 dispatch, but does not verify compatibility with B3.

## Steps to reproduce

From a checkout of the commit above, run the following standard-library-only script. It seeds a minimal B2 output and executes the actual B3 merge snippet from the generated skill in a temporary directory. It does not run an LLM or modify the repository.

```sh
python - <<'PY'
import json
import os
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

skill = Path('graphify/skill-codex.md').read_text()
b3 = skill.split('**Step B3 - Collect, cache, and merge**', 1)[1]
merge_code = b3.split('import json, glob\n', 1)[1].split('\n"\n```', 1)[0]
merge_code = 'import json, glob\n' + merge_code.replace('\\"', '"')
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='graphify-codex-repro-') as root:
    os.chdir(root)
    Path('graphify-out').mkdir()
    target = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json')
    target.write_text(json.dumps({
        'nodes': [{'id': 'doc_example', 'label': 'Example'}],
        'edges': [], 'hyperedges': [],
        'input_tokens': 0, 'output_tokens': 0,
    }))
    print('Before B3:', len(json.loads(target.read_text())['nodes']), 'node(s)')
    exec(compile(merge_code, '<actual Step B3 merge snippet>', 'exec'))
    after = json.loads(target.read_text())
    print('After B3:', len(after['nodes']), 'node(s)')
    assert after['nodes'] == []
PY
```

## Observed output

```text
Before B3: 1 node(s)
Merged 0 chunks: 0 in / 0 out tokens
After B3: 0 node(s)
```

This is a deterministic reproduction of the merge-snippet data loss, not a claim that every Codex run follows the conflicting instructions in the same way. An agent may compensate for the contradiction, but the documented pipeline should not require that inference.

## Version and environment

- Graphify: `0.9.67`, current `v8` commit linked above.
- Host: Codex; reproduction executed on Linux with Python, using only the standard library.
- Scope: host-agent semantic extraction. The reproduction does not exercise code-only AST extraction or the direct LLM backend path.

## Related work and proposed fix

- #804 is related prior work: its description mentions normalizing returned Codex JSON into chunk files. It was closed without a GitHub merge; the conflicting instructions are still present in current `v8`.
- #273 concerns the `wait` / `wait_agent` tool name, a separate issue.
- #2746 changes extraction prompts for Claw/Kiro/Pi while retaining Codex's inline-return contract.
- #3681 concerns token-usage observability; any change here should avoid unnecessarily overlapping that work.

Updated proposal: align Codex with Claude's existing file-based pipeline rather than introduce a separate in-memory collection path.

- Update Codex Step B2 to dispatch write-capable subagents with an absolute CHUNK_PATH for each chunk. Each subagent writes its JSON directly to that file; the parent waits for completion and proceeds to the shared Step B3.
- Use the same extraction prompt source as Claude, including the extraction rules, JSON schema, and CHUNK_PATH output contract.
- Keep the shared B3 collection/cache/merge code and Part C AST/semantic merge. Adapt only platform-specific tool invocation and recovery wording to the tools available in each host; do not create a Codex-only collection or merge implementation.
- Update the generator sources and regenerate the affected skill artifacts and snapshots.
- Replace regression assertions that require Codex's in-memory/compact behavior with checks for shared extraction instructions, direct chunk-file output, and identical collection/cache/merge behavior for the same chunk fixtures. Include a small live Codex subagent check that confirms the assigned chunk files are created and consumed by the shared pipeline.

This supersedes the original proposal to preserve in-memory collection. The reported B2/B3 inconsistency and reproduction remain applicable to the linked affected revision. The reproduction demonstrates the old contract mismatch; the fix should prevent it by making B2 produce the chunk files B3 expects. Token-usage observability remains separate work tracked by #3681.

title: [Bug]: Markdown wikilink index (_build_link_index) ignores .graphifyignore, walks ignored dirs and hangs update on large data trees
body:
### What happened?

The vault-wide wikilink fallback added in #2875 (v0.9.48), `extractors/markdown.py::_build_link_index`, walks the entire scan root with `os.walk`. It prunes only dot-directories and `detect._SKIP_DIRS`. It never consults `.graphifyignore`/`.gitignore`, so it descends into directories that `detect()` correctly excludes.

This has two effects:

1. **Hang on repos with a large ignored data directory.** My repo has a local `data/` tree (Parquet partitions, millions of directories) listed in `.graphifyignore`. `detect()` prunes it, but `graphify update .` never finishes:
   - Each `ProcessPoolExecutor` worker builds its own index. The cache is per-process, so six workers walk `data/` concurrently and sit in D state (`__lock_buffer`) with directory fds open under `data/...`. I observed 50+ minutes stuck at "AST extraction: 700/770".
   - On a warm cache it still hangs in the parent process. `watch._reconcile_markdown_links` re-parses every Markdown file on each full rebuild, and that reaches `_build_link_index` again.
   - The post-commit hook hits its 600s timeout on every commit and leaves a stale `.rebuild.lock`.
   - The same commit in a clean checkout without the local `data/` tree finishes in ~51s.
2. **Links resolve into ignored files.** A bare `[[name]]` can resolve to a document under an ignored directory, and the extractor emits a `references` edge to it.

The docstring says the index uses "the same corpus boundary the scanner draws", but the scanner also applies ignore files.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
mkdir repro && cd repro && git init -q
printf 'bigdata/\n' > .graphifyignore
mkdir -p notes/a notes/b bigdata/x/y/z
printf '# Hub\n\nSee [[target]] and [[secret]].\n' > notes/a/hub.md
printf '# Target\n' > notes/b/target.md
printf '# Ignored\n' > bigdata/x/y/z/secret.md
for i in $(seq 1 200); do mkdir -p bigdata/part=$i; done
```

```python
import os
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.detect import detect
from graphify.extract import extract

root = Path(".").resolve()
files = [p for g in detect(root)["files"].values() for p in g]
print("detect includes bigdata/:", any("/bigdata/" in str(p) for p in files))  # False

visited, _walk = [], os.walk
def spy(top, *a, **k):
    for dp, dn, fn in _walk(top, *a, **k):
        visited.append(os.path.relpath(dp, root))
        yield dp, dn, fn
os.walk = spy
out = extract([root / "notes/a/hub.md", root / "notes/b/target.md"], cache_root=root)
os.walk = _walk
print("dirs walked under ignored bigdata/:", sum(v.startswith("bigdata") for v in visited))
for e in out["edges"]:
    if e.get("relation") == "references":
        print(e["source"], "->", e["target"])
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
detect includes bigdata/: False
dirs walked under ignored bigdata/: 204
notes_a_hub -> notes_b_target
notes_a_hub -> bigdata_x_y_z_secret
```

Stack of the hung warm-cache `graphify update .` (from `faulthandler.dump_traceback_later`):

```text
File "<frozen os>", line 373 in walk
File ".../graphify/extractors/markdown.py", line 156 in _build_link_index
File ".../graphify/extractors/markdown.py", line 185 in _vault_lookup
File ".../graphify/extractors/markdown.py", line 251 in _resolve_markdown_link
File ".../graphify/extractors/markdown.py", line 414 in add_link
File ".../graphify/extractors/markdown.py", line 465 in extract_markdown
File ".../graphify/extract.py", line 191 in _safe_extract
File ".../graphify/extract.py", line 6901 in _safe_extract_with_xaml_root
File ".../graphify/watch.py", line 632 in _reconcile_markdown_links
File ".../graphify/watch.py", line 1029 in _reconcile_existing_graph
File ".../graphify/watch.py", line 1868 in _rebuild_code
File ".../graphify/cli.py", line 2445 in dispatch_command
```

### Graphify version

0.9.67. The same code is on `main` as of 2026-09-25.

### Environment

Linux 6.8 (Ubuntu), Python 3.12.3, graphify installed with `uv tool`.

### Additional context

**Suggested fix:** prune the index walk with `graphify.detect.ignored_predicate(root)`. It already mirrors `detect()`'s ignore decisions for a single path. Apply it to child directories so ignored subtrees are never descended, and to candidate files. I verified this locally by monkeypatching `_build_link_index`:
- full `graphify update .` on the real repo: 50s, where the unpatched run never finished
- index walk: 138 directories instead of the whole `data/` tree
- the resulting graph contains no nodes from ignored paths

```python
from graphify.detect import _SKIP_DIRS, ignored_predicate

def _build_link_index(root):
    ignored = ignored_predicate(root)
    index = {}
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        dp = Path(dirpath)
        dirnames[:] = sorted(
            d for d in dirnames
            if not d.startswith(".") and d not in _SKIP_DIRS and not ignored(dp / d)
        )
        for fname in filenames:
            if Path(fname).suffix.lower() not in _MD_LINKABLE_EXTS:
                continue
            abs_path = dp / fname
            if ignored(abs_path):
                continue
            rel = os.path.relpath(str(abs_path), str(root)).replace("\\", "/")
            index.setdefault(_nfc(fname), []).append((rel.count("/"), _nfc(rel), abs_path))
    return index
```

Related:
- #2415 takes a different approach: it builds the index from the files that `detect()` already found, which avoids a second walk entirely.
- #3045 may be the same symptom (hang after the AST phase), but no cause is identified there.

title: fix(manifest_ingest): resolve inherited groupId and ${...} properties in pom.xml (#3806)
body:
Fixes #3806.

`_parse_pom` built module and dependency ids from the literal POM text, so two common Maven patterns produced ids that never matched and the `depends_on` edges were pruned as dangling:

1. **Inherited groupId**: a module with no top-level `<groupId>` now falls back to `<parent><groupId>` (version works the same way with `<parent><version>`).
2. **`${...}` properties**: groupId/artifactId/version of the module and of each dependency are resolved against the POM's own `<properties>` plus `project.groupId`, `project.artifactId`, `project.version`, `project.parent.groupId` and `project.parent.version`. Placeholders that can't be resolved from the same file (for example, a property only defined in a parent POM) are kept as-is, which matches the current behaviour.

## Tests
- Added `test_pom_inherits_groupid_and_resolves_properties` to `tests/test_manifest_ingest.py`. It covers the parsed ids and the edges that survive `build_from_json` across three modules.
- RED→GREEN: the new test fails on `v8` (`'acme-server' == 'org.acme:acme-server'`) and passes with this change.
- `pytest tests/test_manifest_ingest.py`: 14 passed.
- Full suite: `5539 passed, 62 failed, 259 skipped`. The same 62 tests (VB.NET, Terraform and similar optional-grammar extractors) fail on the base commit in my environment too. None of them are manifest tests.
- `ruff check` on the two changed files: clean.

## Real-world check (apache/livy, the repro from the issue)
Ran `extract` + `build_from_json` over all 25 `pom.xml` files:
- before: 18 `depends_on` edges
- after: 39 `depends_on` edges

Some edges are still missing because `scala.binary.version` is only defined in the root POM, and this change doesn't do cross-file parent-property inheritance.

title: [Bug]: graphify prs <number> fetches diffs for all open PRs, and drops graph impact on non-default base branches
body:
### What happened?

Running `graphify prs <number>` to inspect a single PR has two issues in `graphify/prs.py`:

1. **Unnecessary network I/O:** `cmd_prs` calls `attach_graph_impact(prs, graph_path, repo)` on the entire list of open PRs (up to 50) before checking `pr_number`. Inspecting one PR triggers up to 50 concurrent `gh pr diff` executions in a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, adding 10–30 seconds of latency and consuming rate limits to compute impact for PRs that are never rendered.
2. **Graph impact is skipped for PRs targeting a non-default base branch:** `attach_graph_impact` filters candidates with `actionable = [pr for pr in prs if pr.status != "WRONG-BASE"]`. If an inspected PR targets `main` when the repo default is `v8` (or targets any feature branch), it is excluded from `actionable`. Its diff is never fetched, so `files_changed`, `communities_touched`, and `nodes_affected` remain empty, and `render_pr_detail` prints no graph impact section.

Additionally, `fetch_prs` hardcodes `limit=50`. If an open PR was updated earlier and falls outside the top 50, `graphify prs <number>` exits with `PR #<number> not found in open PRs` instead of attempting an individual lookup via `gh pr view`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Ensure a local `graphify-out/graph.json` exists.
2. Pick any open PR targeting a non-default base branch (or run on a PR where `base != expected_base`).
3. Run `graphify prs <number>`.

### Error output or graph output

- Inspecting a single PR takes 15–30s while `gh pr diff` runs in parallel for all open PRs in the background.
- The output for a PR targeting another base branch omits graph impact:

```text
  PR #3600  ·  WRONG-BASE
  feat: update config
  
  branch:  user:patch-1  ->  main
  author:  user
  updated: 5d ago
  CI:      ✓ SUCCESS

(no graph impact or changed files shown, despite graph.json existing)
```

### Expected behavior

1. When `pr_number` is provided, graph impact calculation should only run for the target PR.
2. `render_pr_detail` should display changed files and blast radius regardless of the PR's target base branch.
3. If `<number>` is not in the first 50 results from `gh pr list`, fall back to fetching that specific PR with `gh pr view`.

### Graphify version

0.9.67 (active v8 branch at 4c73561)

### Environment

Platform-independent (Linux, macOS, Windows). Python 3.10–3.14.

### Suggested fix

In `cmd_prs` (`graphify/prs.py`):
- Find the requested `match` PR first (fetching directly via `gh pr view` if not present in `prs`).
- If `pr_number is not None`, pass only `[match]` into `attach_graph_impact` without filtering out `"WRONG-BASE"`.

title: fix(dedup): preserve pre-existing self-loops during entity deduplication
body:
Closes #3809

### Summary
When `deduplicate_entities` merges at least one node, it rewires edges and discards any edge where `e["source"] == e["target"]`. This inadvertently dropped pre-existing self-loops (such as recursive AST `calls` edges or self-referencing foreign key `references` edges) that were unrelated to the merge.

### Changes
- In `graphify/dedup.py`, updated the edge filter condition to `if e["source"] != e["target"] or src == tgt:`.
- Self-loops resulting from the collapse of two distinct merged nodes (`src != tgt`) continue to be dropped as before.
- Pre-existing self-loops (`src == tgt`) are preserved. If a merged node carried a self-loop, the edge is rewired to the surviving canonical node.
- Added regression tests in `tests/test_dedup.py` verifying that:
  1. Recursive calls and self-referencing foreign keys survive an unrelated concept merge.
  2. A pre-existing self-loop on a merged node rewires onto the survivor.

title: fix(markdown): respect ignore rules when building wikilink index (#3822)
body:
## Summary

`_build_link_index` in `graphify/extractors/markdown.py` indexes document basenames for Obsidian wikilink fallback resolution. Previously, it walked the scan root with `os.walk` and only pruned dot-directories and `_SKIP_DIRS`, bypassing `.graphifyignore` and `.gitignore`.

This caused extraction workers to hang for extended periods descending into large ignored subdirectories (e.g. data trees or build directories), while also allowing wikilinks to resolve to documents inside ignored folders.

## Changes

- Prune subdirectories in `dirnames[:]` and skip candidate files in `_build_link_index` using `graphify.detect.ignored_predicate(root)`.
- Added a regression test in `tests/test_languages.py` verifying that ignored directory trees are not traversed and that wikilinks cannot bind to files inside ignored paths.

title: Gate the undocumented components reason on a real semantic layer
body:
Fixes #3801.

## Summary

`GRAPH_REPORT.md`'s Knowledge Gaps section always offered "undocumented components" as a possible reason for an isolated node, regardless of whether the graph could ever actually have one. That phrase only means anything when a semantic layer exists — `document`/`paper`/`image` nodes an LLM extracted meaning from, where an isolated node genuinely could be "mentioned but never explained further." A code-only graph (`--code-only`, or any run where semantic extraction never happened) has no such nodes at all, so offering it as a live possibility on every report is misleading.

## Fix

The reason now checks whether any node in the graph carries a `document`/`paper`/`image` `file_type` before including that clause, reusing the same `VALID_FILE_TYPES` distinction `validate.py` already draws between the semantic layer and `code`/`rationale`/`concept` nodes — no new build-time flag needed, matching the issue's own suggested fix.

## Testing

- Added two regression tests to `tests/test_report_gap_thresholds.py`: one confirming a code+concept-only graph's isolated-node message omits "undocumented components" and keeps "possible missing edges", and one confirming adding a single `document` node elsewhere in the same graph brings the fuller reason back.
- Confirmed the first test fails against pre-fix code via `git stash`.
- Full `test_report.py`/`test_report_gap_thresholds.py` suite passes.
- Full project test suite passes (only pre-existing, unrelated failures remain: four extractor test files needing optional `tree-sitter-language-pack` grammars not installed in this environment).
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check` passes.

title: fix: scope PR graph impact to requested PR
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3824.

When inspecting a single PR with `graphify prs <number>`, Graphify previously calculated graph impact for the entire list of open PRs and skipped impact calculation for `WRONG-BASE` PRs.

This change makes detail mode targeted and preserves graph impact regardless of the PR's base branch.

## Changes

* Resolve the requested PR before calculating graph impact.
* Fetch diffs only for the requested PR in detail mode.
* Calculate graph impact for `WRONG-BASE` PRs when explicitly inspected.
* Fall back to `gh pr view <number>` when the requested PR is outside the first 50 open PRs.
* Preserve open-PR semantics by rejecting closed and merged PRs from the fallback lookup.
* Centralize GitHub PR JSON parsing to avoid duplicated logic.
* Add regression tests covering the affected behavior.

## Validation

* `pytest tests/test_prs.py` — **65 passed**

title: PHP: inter-class member calls are silently dropped, and language builtins (e.g. `empty()`) get mis-wired to same-name internal methods
body:
## Environment
- graphify 0.9.65 (also reviewed 0.9.66/0.9.67 release notes — no PHP member-call resolver mentioned)
- Corpus: a ~52 MB Symfony PHP bundle (11,007 nodes / 32,817 edges after extraction), `--code-only` mode

## Problem A — PHP member calls are silently dropped

`extract.py` ships member-call resolvers for Swift, Python, TypeScript, C++, C#, Java… but there is **no `_resolve_php_member_calls`**. A PHP call like:

```php
$this->emailSender->prepareAndSendEmail($action);
```

produces no edge at all. Empirical check on our graph: `EmailSender::prepareAndSendEmail` has **0 incoming edges from other files** while at least two services call it — all 18 of its incoming `calls` edges are intra-file self-calls.

Notably, the cross-repo parking mechanism **already exists** (`_park_unresolved_member_call` -> `metadata.unresolved_calls`, ref #3152) but is never invoked for PHP. Our full graph contains **zero** parked entries with `"lang": "php"` — the calls are dropped with no trace instead of being parked.

## Problem B — builtins get mis-wired to same-name internal methods

`_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` rebinds a call to the single internal method sharing the callee's name. PHP language builtins collide with that rule:

- ~**200 calls to `empty()`** (language construct) across ~150 files are wired to an internal method `ParseCollectionPaginator::empty()` — including 24 false edges from two god-node services alone.
- Same risk class for common names: `execute`, `handle`, `format`.

So the graph is wrong in both directions: **missing edges** on real inter-class calls, **polluted edges** on builtin names.

## Impact on a real corpus

A local post-processor (tree-sitter-php, same parking format) recovered on this single bundle:

- **-454 false edges** removed (builtin rewiring)
- **+1,566 real edges** added (typed-property member calls, interface -> implementations)
- **6,558 calls parked** in `metadata.unresolved_calls` (previously dropped silently)

## Suggested fix

1. Add a PHP member-call resolver: receiver type from typed/promoted constructor properties + `$this->method()` self-calls; interface calls -> all implementations.
2. Park unresolved PHP member calls in `metadata.unresolved_calls` (same payload format as other languages, `"lang": "php"`) so `merge-graphs` can finish the edges.
3. Never rewire a builtin callee name (`empty`, `count`, `strlen`, ...) to an internal method — consult a builtin list per language before rewiring.

## Repro

Any PHP corpus containing `$this->someTypedProperty->method()`: the edge is absent from `graph.json` and nothing appears in `metadata.unresolved_calls` for the caller. Then add a second method named `empty` anywhere in the corpus and observe `empty()` calls being wired to it.

Happy to share our local post-processor (pure post-processing on `graph.json`, idempotent) if useful as a reference implementation.

title: fix(ingest): classify a URL by its host, not by text it contains
body:
## What does this PR do?

`graphify.ingest._detect_url_type` decides how `ingest()` fetches a URL. It tested substrings of the whole URL, so `"x.com" in url` matched every host that merely ends in those letters, and a site name anywhere in the path or query was enough:

| URL | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/abc123/paper.pdf?dl=1` | tweet | pdf |
| `https://www.netflix.com/title/80057281` | tweet | webpage |
| `https://www.linux.com/news/` | tweet | webpage |
| `https://developer.box.com/guides/` | tweet | webpage |
| `https://x.com.example.org/status/1` | tweet | webpage |
| `https://example.org/why-arxiv.org-matters` | arxiv | webpage |
| `https://example.org/?ref=github.com` | github | webpage |
| `https://example.org/embed?src=youtube.com` | youtube | webpage |

A tweet classification loses the page. `_fetch_tweet` rewrites the URL with `url.replace("x.com", "twitter.com")` (`https://www.dropbotwitter.com/...`) and asks the Twitter oEmbed endpoint for it. When that lookup fails, `ingest()` saves a note that says only `Tweet at <url> (could not fetch content)`. The tweet check also runs before the `.pdf` check, so a Dropbox-shared paper is never downloaded. The same holds for any `*x.com` host: wix.com, max.com, vox.com, fedex.com and others.

The fix parses the URL once and matches the host itself or a subdomain of it (`_host_is`). `x.com`, `twitter.com`, `mobile.twitter.com`, `arxiv.org`, `export.arxiv.org`, `github.com`, `youtube.com` and `youtu.be` keep their types. `hostname` is already lowercased by `urlparse`, and a trailing root dot is dropped. The pdf/image/webpage checks after it are unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## How was this tested?

`tests/test_ingest_url_type.py` is new:

- the known hosts keep their type (9 cases, including subdomains and an upper-case host);
- look-alike hosts and names in the path or query no longer match (8 cases);
- `ingest()` on a Dropbox PDF link downloads it through `safe_fetch` and never calls the text fetch. `validate_url` and the fetchers are stubbed, so the test needs no network.

9 of the 18 fail on `v8`, all 8 look-alike cases and the Dropbox routing test. The 9 that pass are the known hosts.

title: feat: add optional LLM semantic judgment + JEV decision layers
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds two **optional** judgment layers on top of graphify's deterministic heuristics, so the "judgment" outputs (surprising_connections, suggest_questions, community labels, dedup tiebreaks) can be boosted by a language model and/or a structured decision service — while the **default behavior stays byte-identical** (both layers are off unless opted in, and every failure falls back to the original heuristic path).

1. **LLM semantic layer** (graphify/semantic_judge.py, new): reuses the existing llm.py backend/provider machinery.
   - reorder_surprises: asks the model whether each surprise-connection candidate is a "real surprise" (yes/weak/no), reranks candidates, keeps all candidates.
   - refine_questions: filters low-value suggested questions and rewrites wording when the model proposes better phrasing (no_signal untouched).
   - validate_community_labels: checks an LLM-produced community name against member labels; falls back to the hub label when the score is poor (<= 0.75).
   - Outbound payloads are **metadata only** (labels, relations, confidence, member labels) — never source code.
2. **JEV decision layer** (graphify/jev_decide.py, new, stdlib-only): a lightweight TypeSafe System One client (jev_noul / jev_choice / jev_score).
   - dedup._jev_tiebreak (CLI --dedup-jev): resolves 75–92 fuzzy-window candidate pairs; union only when p > 0.75.
   - analyze.surprising_connections: JEV keep/drop gate on heuristic candidates (used when the LLM semantic layer is off — the two are mutually exclusive via a semantic_on switch).
   - analyze.suggest_questions: JEV value filter (score + confidence threshold).
   - Fail-open everywhere: no key, timeout, transport error, bad JSON or low confidence → None → caller falls back to the deterministic original.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature

## How was this tested?

- New tests: tests/test_semantic_judge.py (22), tests/test_jev_decide.py (18), plus JEV coverage added to tests/test_analyze.py and tests/test_dedup.py.
- .venv Python 3.12 / pytest 9.0.3: tests/test_semantic_judge.py tests/test_jev_decide.py tests/test_analyze.py tests/test_dedup.py → 197 passed.
- Full suite on this machine: 5877 passed, 16 failures from missing optional tree-sitter language packs (erlang/r/solidity/vbnet) — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.
- E2E: with no key, surprising_connections / suggest_questions / --dedup-jev output is byte-identical to baseline (fail-open verified); with a real key the JEV judgments fire (only metadata leaves the machine).

title: fix(detect): keep tables in place and read all text in docx sidecars
body:
## What does this PR do?

`graphify.detect.docx_to_markdown` writes the markdown sidecar that a `.docx` file is extracted from. It had three problems:

- **Tables moved to the end.** It wrote every paragraph first and then appended all tables, so a table lost the heading it belongs to and ended up after the last section.
- **Missing text.** `Paragraph.text` reads only the runs directly under a paragraph. So tracked insertions (`w:ins`), content controls (`w:sdt`, which is how forms and templates hold their values), simple fields, smart tags and text boxes were dropped.
- **Broken table rows.** A cell's text went into its row as is: a line break in a cell split the markdown row, and a `|` in a cell added a column.

One document, before and after:

```text
before                          after
# Pricing                       # Pricing
# Notes                         | Plan | Price |
- First item                    | --- | --- |
The fee is  euros.              | Basic \| Pro | 10 EUR per month |
Client:                         # Notes
Host                            - First item
| Plan | Price |                The fee is twelve euros.
| --- | --- |                   Client: Acme
| Basic | Pro | 10 EUR          Host
per month |                     Callout
```

The document has the table under `# Pricing`, a tracked change (`ten` deleted, `twelve` inserted), a content control holding `Acme`, and a text box `Callout`.

The change:

- `docx_to_markdown` walks `doc.element.body` in document order. A table is written where it stands, in the same header / separator / rows form as before, and python-docx's `row.cells` still keeps merged cells aligned to the grid.
- `_docx_paragraph_text` reads the text of every run in the paragraph. It skips runs under a tracked deletion, moved-away text, a ruby guide, a text box, or the `mc:Fallback` copy Word writes of each text box. A text box's paragraphs follow the paragraph that anchors it, once.
- Content controls and custom XML are looked through for paragraphs, tables and rows.
- `_docx_cell_markdown` puts a cell on one line (line breaks and paragraphs become spaces), flattens a nested table into the cell once, and escapes `|` as `\|`.

Headings, list items, plain and empty paragraphs are written exactly as before.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## How was this tested?

`tests/test_docx_to_markdown.py` is new, with 5 tests on real `.docx` files built with python-docx:

- headings, a list item, plain, empty and tab-stop paragraphs keep their markdown exactly;
- a table stays under its heading;
- a cell with a pipe, a line break and a second paragraph stays on its row;
- a nested table is flattened into its cell once;
- a tracked insertion, inline and block content controls and a text box are read, while the deleted text and the text box's fallback copy are not.

4 of the 5 fail on `v8`; the one that passes is the plain-paragraph test, which pins that the output did not change there. Each of 9 mutants of the new code is caught by a failing test: tables dropped, pipes not escaped, cell whitespace kept, deletions read, text box runs read inline, fallback copy read, text boxes not emitted, content controls skipped, nested table dropped.

title: TS workspace resolution picks a main/types target outside the corpus (built dist/) and drops the edge
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.64 (Linux, pnpm workspace, TypeScript)

**What happens.** A workspace package that declares `"main": "./dist/index.js"` (no `exports` map) resolves to its built `dist/index.js` whenever the package has been built locally. `dist/` is outside the corpus (gitignored), so the target node doesn't exist and the import edge is dropped. On a fresh clone (no `dist/`) the same imports resolve to `src/index.ts` and the edges exist — so the graph depends on whether the developer ran a build.

**Where.** `extractors/resolution.py`: `_package_entry_candidates` returns `svelte`/`module`/`main`/`types` targets before the `src/index` fallback, and `_resolve_workspace_import` returns the first candidate that `is_file()`. A built `dist/index.js` exists, so it wins.

**Measured** (same commit, 3 packages × ~360 app import lines; file-level recall of a symbol's users vs `git grep`, 2 × 200 random symbols):
- with `dist/` present: cross-package recall 1–2%, 0 app → package barrel edges
- without `dist/` (clean clone): cross-package recall 31–38%, all 360 app import lines reach `packages/*/src/index.ts`

**Suggested fix.** Treat a candidate that is not in the corpus (gitignored / not a detected source file) as missing and fall through to the next one — the same fall-through #3487 added for `exports` conditions. The `main`/`types` fallback path doesn't get it today.

**Workaround we shipped.** An `exports` map with a `source` condition first (`"source": "./src/index.ts"`), which your `_EXPORT_CONDITION_PRIORITY` ranks first while Node/TS/Metro/esbuild ignore it.

title: Kotlin: annotations and primary-constructor properties are not extracted (JPA relationships lost)
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.68 (also 0.9.15)

## Problem

The tree-sitter engine harvests declaration annotations only for Java/Groovy
(`_java_annotation_names`, gated on those languages). Kotlin nests annotations
differently — `modifiers -> annotation -> user_type` for `@Entity`, or
`annotation -> constructor_invocation -> user_type` for `@OneToMany(...)` — so
nothing is emitted for Kotlin. In addition:

- primary-constructor `val`/`var` parameters (the idiomatic place for Kotlin
  entity fields) get no node, type edge, or annotation edge at all;
- class-body `property_declaration`s attach their type edge to the class, with
  no per-property node, so field-level annotations have nowhere to attach.

For Kotlin JPA/Spring code this drops essentially the whole domain model.

## Repro

```kotlin
import jakarta.persistence.*

@Entity
@Table(name = "orders")
class Order(
    @Id @GeneratedValue val id: Long? = null,
    @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY) val customer: Customer,
    @Column(nullable = false) var status: String
) {
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "order")
    var lines: MutableList<OrderLine> = mutableListOf()

    @get:Transient
    val total: Int get() = 0
}

@Entity class Customer(@Id val id: Long)
@Entity class OrderLine(@Id val id: Long, @ManyToOne val order: Order)
```

`graphify extract . --code-only`

**Actual (0.9.68):** 4 nodes / 4 edges — three `contains` edges and
`Order -references/generic_arg-> OrderLine`.

**Expected:** class annotation edges (`Order -> Entity`, `Order -> Table`),
per-field nodes (`Order -defines/field-> .customer`, …), field type edges
(`.customer -> Customer`, `.order -> Order`), and field annotation edges
(`.customer -> ManyToOne`, `.status -> Column`, `.id -> Id`,
`.lines -> OneToMany`, `.total -> Transient`). With the patch below: 20 nodes /
27 edges, 13 of them `attribute` edges.

## Proposed fix

We've been running the attached patch in production since 0.9.15, and it's now
rebased onto 0.9.68. It adds `_kotlin_annotation_names`, `_kotlin_member_name`
and `_kotlin_param_type_node` helpers, and emits:

1. class-level annotation edges (`references`, `context="attribute"`);
2. a `.name` node per primary-constructor `val`/`var`, with type + annotation edges;
3. a `.name` node per class-body property (its type edges move from the class to
   the property; initializer call collection is unchanged);
4. function/getter annotation edges for Kotlin.

Happy to open a PR with tests if this direction is welcome. One open question:
Java annotations are now import-qualified (`jakarta.persistence.Entity`), while
this patch still emits the simple name for Kotlin. Aligning the two would be a
natural follow-up.

<details><summary>Patch against 0.9.68 (graphify/extractors/engine.py)</summary>

```diff
--- a/graphify/extractors/engine.py
+++ b/graphify/extractors/engine.py
@@ -791,6 +791,70 @@
             return c
     return None
 
+def _kotlin_annotation_names(declaration_node, source: bytes) -> list[str]:
+    """Collect annotation names from a Kotlin declaration's `modifiers` child.
+    Kotlin nests the annotated type under `annotation -> user_type` (no args,
+    e.g. `@Entity`) or `annotation -> constructor_invocation -> user_type`
+    (with args, e.g. `@OneToMany(...)`), unlike Java's flat
+    `marker_annotation`/`annotation` with a direct name field. So
+    `_java_annotation_names` finds nothing on a Kotlin node, and its call sites
+    are gated to java/groovy anyway. Mirror it for Kotlin here.
+    """
+    names: list[str] = []
+    modifiers = None
+    for child in declaration_node.children:
+        if child.type == "modifiers":
+            modifiers = child
+            break
+    if modifiers is None:
+        return names
+    for anno in modifiers.children:
+        if anno.type != "annotation":
+            continue
+        user_type_node = None
+        for c in anno.children:
+            if c.type == "user_type":
+                user_type_node = c
+                break
+            if c.type == "constructor_invocation":
+                for cc in c.children:
+                    if cc.type == "user_type":
+                        user_type_node = cc
+                        break
+                break
+        if user_type_node is None:
+            continue
+        name = _kotlin_user_type_name(user_type_node, source)
+        if name:
+            names.append(name)
+    return names
+
+def _kotlin_member_name(node, source: bytes) -> str | None:
+    """Property/param name for a Kotlin `class_parameter` (direct identifier) or
+    `property_declaration` (`variable_declaration -> identifier`)."""
+    if node.type == "class_parameter":
+        for c in node.children:
+            if c.type in ("identifier", "simple_identifier"):
+                return _read_text(c, source)
+        return None
+    for c in node.children:
+        if c.type == "variable_declaration":
+            for cc in c.children:
+                if cc.type in ("identifier", "simple_identifier"):
+                    return _read_text(cc, source)
+    return None
+
+def _kotlin_param_type_node(cp):
+    """The `user_type` node of a Kotlin `class_parameter`, unwrapping `nullable_type`."""
+    for c in cp.children:
+        if c.type == "user_type":
+            return c
+        if c.type == "nullable_type":
+            for cc in c.children:
+                if cc.type == "user_type":
+                    return cc
+    return None
+
 def _kotlin_function_return_type_node(func_node):
     """Find the return-type node of a Kotlin function_declaration (the type after `: ` post-params)."""
     saw_params = False
@@ -4097,6 +4161,54 @@
                                             target = ensure_named_node(ref_name, line)
                                             add_edge(class_nid, target, "references", line,
                                                      context="generic_arg")
+
+                # Class-level annotations (@Entity, @MappedSuperclass, @Embeddable,
+                # …). The Java harvester at the class site is gated to java/groovy,
+                # so Kotlin annotations never became edges. Emit the same
+                # references/attribute edges here.
+                for anno_name in _kotlin_annotation_names(node, source):
+                    target_nid = ensure_named_node(anno_name, line)
+                    if target_nid != class_nid:
+                        add_edge(class_nid, target_nid, "references", line,
+                                 context="attribute")
+
+                # Primary-constructor `val`/`var` params are properties with no
+                # walk-visited node of their own (class-body property_declarations
+                # are handled during recursion). Give each its own node + type +
+                # annotation edges (@Column, @Id, @ManyToOne, @OneToMany, …),
+                # parallel to class-body properties, so JPA mapping/relationship
+                # annotations are queryable per field. Path is
+                # primary_constructor -> class_parameters -> class_parameter.
+                for child in node.children:
+                    if child.type != "primary_constructor":
+                        continue
+                    for cps in child.children:
+                        if cps.type != "class_parameters":
+                            continue
+                        for cp in cps.children:
+                            if cp.type != "class_parameter":
+                                continue
+                            mline = cp.start_point[0] + 1
+                            pname = _kotlin_member_name(cp, source)
+                            pnid = class_nid
+                            if pname:
+                                pnid = _make_id(class_nid, pname)
+                                add_node(pnid, f".{pname}", mline)
+                                add_edge(class_nid, pnid, "defines", mline,
+                                         context="field")
+                            ptype = _kotlin_param_type_node(cp)
+                            if ptype is not None:
+                                prefs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
+                                _kotlin_collect_type_refs(ptype, source, False, prefs)
+                                for ref_name, role in prefs:
+                                    ctx = "generic_arg" if role == "generic_arg" else "field"
+                                    tgt = ensure_named_node(ref_name, mline)
+                                    if tgt != pnid:
+                                        add_edge(pnid, tgt, "references", mline, context=ctx)
+                            for anno_name in _kotlin_annotation_names(cp, source):
+                                tgt = ensure_named_node(anno_name, mline)
+                                if tgt != pnid:
+                                    add_edge(pnid, tgt, "references", mline, context="attribute")
 
             # Ruby: `class Dog < Animal` puts the base class in the `superclass`
             # field (a `<` token followed by a constant or scope_resolution).
@@ -4764,16 +4876,30 @@
             # Field-type references stay class-gated: top-level properties keep
             # their pre-#2565 (no-references) behavior unchanged.
             if parent_class_nid:
+                line = node.start_point[0] + 1
+                # Give the property its own node (parallels method nodes: `.name`),
+                # so its type + annotations attach per-property rather than lumping
+                # onto the class. Falls back to the class if the name is unresolvable
+                # (e.g. destructuring `val (a, b) = ...`).
+                prop_name = _kotlin_member_name(node, source)
+                prop_nid = parent_class_nid
+                if prop_name:
+                    prop_nid = _make_id(parent_class_nid, prop_name)
+                    add_node(prop_nid, f".{prop_name}", line)
+                    add_edge(parent_class_nid, prop_nid, "defines", line, context="field")
                 type_node = _kotlin_property_type_node(node)
                 if type_node is not None:
-                    line = node.start_point[0] + 1
                     refs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
                     _kotlin_collect_type_refs(type_node, source, False, refs)
                     for ref_name, role in refs:
                         ctx = "generic_arg" if role == "generic_arg" else "field"
                         target_nid = ensure_named_node(ref_name, line)
-                        if target_nid != parent_class_nid:
-                            add_edge(parent_class_nid, target_nid, "references", line, context=ctx)
+                        if target_nid != prop_nid:
+                            add_edge(prop_nid, target_nid, "references", line, context=ctx)
+                for anno_name in _kotlin_annotation_names(node, source):
+                    target_nid = ensure_named_node(anno_name, line)
+                    if target_nid != prop_nid:
+                        add_edge(prop_nid, target_nid, "references", line, context="attribute")
             # #2565: seed the initializer into initializer_nodes so walk_calls
             # collects its calls (`val repo = createRepo()`), which previously
             # died at the `return` below. Seeding the WHOLE expression (not just
@@ -5217,6 +5343,16 @@
                         add_edge(func_nid, target_nid, "references", line,
                                  context="attribute")
                         annotation_targets.add(target_nid)
+
+            # Kotlin function/getter annotations (e.g. @Transient on a computed
+            # property getter). Members with their own node attach here; the Java
+            # site above is java-only.
+            if config.ts_module == "tree_sitter_kotlin":
+                for anno_name in _kotlin_annotation_names(node, source):
+                    target_nid = ensure_named_node(anno_name, line)
+                    if target_nid != func_nid:
+                        add_edge(func_nid, target_nid, "references", line,
+                                 context="attribute")
 
             if config.ts_module == "tree_sitter_php":
                 params_container = None
```

title: Reuse the shared real node filter in the community listing loop
body:
Fixes #3794.

## Summary

`GRAPH_REPORT.md`'s per-community `Nodes (N): ...` listing only excluded file nodes from display, so a `rationale` (docstring-fragment) node or a `concept` node leaked into the list as if it were a real code declaration — on a real project this printed raw docstring prose, including mid-sentence truncation and Sphinx `:param:`/`:rtype:` directives, as if they were node names, and inflated the reported community size since the count is `len(real_nodes)`.

The Knowledge Gaps section a few lines below in the same function already excludes file, concept, *and* rationale nodes — the correct set #1768 established for this function. The community-listing loop was never given the same treatment; this is the third spot with this exact missing-filter pattern (#1768, then a Knowledge Gaps spot, now this one).

## Fix

Rather than patching only the display line, this consolidates every "is this a real node" check the function makes — the summary's thin/shown counts, the community listing, and the Gaps section's isolated/thin-community counts — onto one shared `_real_node` predicate. Fixing only the display line while leaving the count computations on the narrower file-only filter would have reintroduced the exact header-vs-render disagreement #3148 fixed, since a community made up entirely of rationale/concept nodes would still count toward "shown" even though nothing real is rendered for it.

## Testing

- Added `test_community_listing_excludes_rationale_and_concept_nodes` to `tests/test_report_gap_thresholds.py`, reproducing the issue's own repro shape (code nodes + a rationale node + a concept node in one community) — confirmed it reproduces the issue's exact example output against pre-fix code via `git stash`.
- Full `test_report.py`/`test_report_gap_thresholds.py` plus every other test file touching `report.py` (`test_semantic_similarity.py`, `test_hypergraph.py`, `test_labeling.py`, `test_pipeline.py`, `test_confidence.py`) passes — 108 tests.
- Full project test suite passes. One pre-existing, unrelated failure was found during this work (`tests/test_incremental.py::test_update_preserves_cross_file_imports_and_calls_to_unchanged_file`) — confirmed via a separate clean `upstream/v8` worktree that it fails identically without any of this PR's changes, so it's not introduced here; flagging separately.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check` passes.
