title: PHP Class::method() static calls without an explicit 'use' import stay INFERRED instead of EXTRACTED
body:
## Summary

For PHP, a type-qualified static call `ClassName::method()` is emitted as `INFERRED` (confidence_score 0.85) instead of `EXTRACTED` (1.0) whenever the caller and callee classes share a namespace and therefore have no explicit `use` import statement — even though the receiver type is named explicitly in source text.

Other languages' member-call resolvers (Swift `_resolve_swift_member_calls`, Python `_resolve_python_member_calls`, C++, Java, C#, Kotlin) all promote a **type-qualified** call (`Type.staticMethod()`) to `EXTRACTED` regardless of import evidence — see the comment at `extract.py` around line 3821-3824:

```python
# A type-qualified call (`Type.staticMethod()`) names the receiver type
# explicitly in source, so it is an exact reference — EXTRACTED, matching
# the Python qualified-class-method pass (#1533). An instance call whose
# receiver type came from local inference (`obj.method()`) stays INFERRED.
```

PHP has no equivalent dedicated resolver. `scoped_call_expression` (`Class::method()`) calls fall through to the generic cross-file name resolver (`extract.py` ~L8380-8444), which gates `EXTRACTED` purely on `has_import_evidence` (an explicit `use` statement or matching import edge). Same-namespace PHP classes never need a `use` import for each other, so every same-namespace static call gets stuck at `INFERRED` 0.85 even though the class name is written right there in the call.

## Repro

```php
// app/StoreClass/LogApi.php
namespace App\StoreClass;

class LogApi
{
    public static function logIncoming($flag_log, $endpoint_log, $request_log = [], $response_log = []): LogApiModel
    {
        $request_log = is_array($request_log) ? LogActivity::sanitize($request_log) : $request_log;
        ...
    }
}
```

`LogActivity` lives in the same `App\StoreClass` namespace, so there's no `use App\StoreClass\LogActivity;` line. The resulting edge:

```json
{
  "source": "app_storeclass_logapi_logapi_logincoming",
  "target": "app_storeclass_logactivity_logactivity",
  "relation": "calls",
  "_origin": "ast",
  "confidence": "INFERRED",
  "confidence_score": 0.85,
  "context": "call",
  "source_file": "app/StoreClass/LogApi.php",
  "source_location": "L20"
}
```

Ran a corpus-wide sweep on a Laravel app (585 PHP `INFERRED` `_origin:ast` `calls` edges): 83 of them were genuine `Class::method()` scoped calls (confirmed by checking the source line at `source_location` for a `\b[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_\\]*::\s*\w+\s*\(` pattern with no `$obj->method(` on the same line) — all should have been `EXTRACTED`. The remaining 500 were true `$obj->method()` instance calls where the receiver type is inferred, correctly left as `INFERRED`.

## Expected

A PHP `scoped_call_expression` (`ClassName::method()`, including `self::`, `static::`, `parent::` resolved to a concrete class) should be treated as type-qualified and promoted to `EXTRACTED`/1.0 the same way the Swift/Python/C++/Java/C#/Kotlin member-call resolvers already do, independent of whether an explicit `use` import exists — same-namespace classes legitimately never have one.

## Suggested fix

Add a PHP-specific resolver (or extend the generic one) that inspects the raw call node type before falling back to name-only resolution: if it's `scoped_call_expression` with an uppercase/class-like left-hand identifier, set `confidence="EXTRACTED"`, `confidence_score=1.0` regardless of `has_import_evidence`, mirroring the existing `type_qualified` branches at extract.py:3830, 4121, 4287, 4509, 4880.

## Environment

- `graphifyy` 0.9.69
- Detected via `/graphify` skill incremental `--update` on a Laravel 12 / PHP 8.5 codebase

title: [Feature]: Apache AGE (PostgreSQL) backend — push, incremental sync, branches, and retrieval
body:
## Problem or use case

Graphify already pushes to Neo4j and FalkorDB, but there is no PostgreSQL path. Many teams already run Postgres and can add the Apache AGE extension without standing up a dedicated graph database. Additionally, the current pushers are one-shot full syncs — there's no persisted notion of *which commit* a pushed graph represents, so incremental updates, branch-aware graphs, and historical checkpoints aren't possible on any backend.

## Proposed solution

A complete Apache AGE backend, built and tested on a branch of my fork:

- `graphify export age --push postgresql://user@host/db` — deletion-safe push (stale nodes/edges removed in the same transaction), idempotent via MERGE, batched via PREPARE/EXECUTE with UNWIND payloads; property indexes created automatically (GIN on `properties` + btree expression indexes on `id`/`source_file`)
- A registry layer (plain SQL tables): stable `repository_id` (uuid5 of normalized remote URL), owner resolution, per-repo default-branch graph naming — so two repos pushed without `--graph-name` never collide
- Logical snapshots + a reversible `graph_diff()` — incremental pushes apply only the delta (O(changed) instead of O(graph))
- Branch support: feature branches push as diff chains against the base snapshot; `graphify age materialize|reap` manages their AGE graphs; rebase/force-push detection fails closed
- Retrieval: `--age postgresql://... [--graph-name NAME]` on `query`/`path`/`explain` — fetches into NetworkX and reuses the exact same scoring/formatting code as the file backend (backend parity enforced via sorted traversal)
- Agent-facing Cypher contract pinned in `docs/AGE_SCHEMA.md` with live-tested queries

Design and rationale are documented in `docs/AGE_PLAN.md` (phased plan with live-spike findings). New `age` extra: `uv tool install "graphifyy[age]"` (psycopg[binary]); `AGE_PASSWORD`/`PGPASSWORD` preferred over embedding credentials in `--push`, matching the `NEO4J_PASSWORD`/`FALKORDB_PASSWORD` convention.

## Alternatives considered

- SQL-only property tables — rejected; loses Cypher and the graph-query ergonomics agents get from the neo4j/falkordb backends
- Neo4j/FalkorDB themselves — require dedicated infra; AGE rides on Postgres users already run
- Reusing the existing `postgres` extra — it carries `tree-sitter-sql` (corpus parsing), which push doesn't need; `age` stays lean (`psycopg[binary]` only). Happy to fold into `postgres` if you'd rather not add an extra.

## Compatibility / behavior impact

No change to extraction, node/edge IDs, graph.json schema, or incremental updates — all AGE code paths are opt-in (`export age` / `--age` flag). One shared-code change: `analyze.graph_diff()` gains `properties`/`changed_nodes`/`changed_edges` keys (additive). `serve.py` BFS/DFS/subgraph traversal is now `sorted()` so answers don't depend on backend edge-insertion order. pyproject gains the `age` extra.

## Additional context

Implementation is complete on `e4c5/graphify`, branch `apache-age-backend`, current with v8/0.9.69 — ~40 phased commits mirroring the FalkorDB PR (#1176) convention of one branch/PR per feature. AI-assisted implementation; commits carry Co-Authored-By trailers per the authorship convention.

Heads-up on size: +9.2k lines total, but the reviewable core is ~3.2k production lines — the rest is ~3.9k tests (13 files: tier-1 pure/mocked unit tests + tier-2/3 live integration), ~1.6k design docs, and ~600 generated skill artifacts (regenerated via `tools.skillgen --bless`). The commits are phased (exporter → registry → snapshots → branches → retrieval) so the PR reviews commit-by-commit.

Verification already run: full suite 6184 passed; live integration suite green against the pinned `apache/age` digest image, PostgreSQL 18.1 / AGE 1.7.0 (962 passed); ruff clean; pyright adds zero errors beyond the 2 pre-existing in graphdb.py.

title: fix(php): resolve Class::method() static calls to the actual method
body:
Fixes #3872.

## Root cause

`scoped_call_expression` (`Helper::format()`) was handled in the shared engine's PHP branch by using the **scope** text as the callee name:

```python
elif node.type == "scoped_call_expression":
    # Static method call: Helper::format() → callee = "Helper"
    scope_node = node.child_by_field_name("scope")
    if scope_node:
        callee_name = _read_text(scope_node, source)
```

So `Helper::format()` was extracted as a bare call to `"Helper"`, not `"format"`. It also never set `is_member_call`, so it fell straight into the generic cross-file bare-name resolver, which matches by label — and `Helper` the class is itself a labeled node. The result: every PHP static call resolved to the **class definition**, never the actual method, and picked up whatever confidence the bare-name resolver's import-evidence gate produced (INFERRED 0.85, since same-namespace PHP classes never need a `use` import for each other).

Verified against a Laravel app: `ChartColors::palette()` calls across 8 files all resolved their `calls` edge target to the `ChartColors` class node, never `.palette()`.

## Fix

- `extractors/engine.py`: `scoped_call_expression` now captures the real method name (`name` field) as the callee, the scope text as the receiver, and marks it a member call — same shape as the C++ `qualified_identifier` / Java `method_invocation` branches just above it.
- `extract.py`: new `_resolve_php_member_calls`, registered via the existing `LanguageResolver` framework, mirroring `_resolve_java_member_calls`. Binds:
  - `self::` / `static::` → enclosing class (exact)
  - `parent::` → through a single `inherits` edge (exact)
  - `Class::` → the class's own method, when the class is declared in-corpus and unambiguous (exact — the receiver is named explicitly in source)
  - a dynamic scope (`$var::method()`) is left unresolved rather than guessed, consistent with the #543/#1219 god-node guard
  - all resolved edges are `EXTRACTED`/1.0, matching the existing type-qualified promotion other languages already get (Swift/Python/C++/Java/C#/Kotlin)

`member_call_expression` (`$obj->method()`) behavior is unchanged — still unresolved, as before this patch (no receiver-typed PHP resolver existed for instance calls; this fix only targets scoped `::` calls).

## Tests

- Updated `test_php_object_creation.py::test_existing_static_call_edges_are_unchanged` → renamed/rewritten as `test_static_call_resolves_to_the_actual_method_not_the_class`, since the old assertion encoded the bug (`"Baz" in target_label` was true only because the target *was* the class).
- Added `tests/test_php_static_call_resolution.py`: same-namespace no-import case (the exact #3872 repro), `self::`/`static::`, `parent::`, dynamic-scope no-phantom-edge, and an explicit no-regression check that `$obj->method()` stays unresolved.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -q`: 6044 passed, 14 skipped (pre-existing/unrelated), 0 failed.

## Real-world validation

Ran the patched extractor over a 1027-file Laravel `app/` corpus (no crashes, 8 parallel workers): `calls` edge confidence distribution went from before (INFERRED-heavy for scoped calls) to `3383 EXTRACTED / 553 INFERRED`, with `EXTRACTED` targets now landing on the actual called methods (spot-checked a random sample of 12).

title: feat: Apache AGE (PostgreSQL) backend — push, incremental sync, branches, and retrieval
body:
## What does this PR do?

Implements #3873 — an Apache AGE (PostgreSQL extension) backend for graphify, giving the project a Postgres-native path alongside Neo4j and FalkorDB, plus the machinery none of the existing pushers have: incremental sync, snapshots, and branch-aware graphs.

Phased commits (each milestone reviewable on its own):

- **Phase 0–1 — exporter**: `push_to_age()` in `graphify/exporters/graphdb.py` — deletion-safe reconcile in the push transaction, batched PREPARE/EXECUTE + UNWIND, auto-created property indexes (GIN + per-prop btree expression), live-spike findings baked in (`cypher()` graph name must be a literal; `SET n +=` rejects parameterized maps). Wired as `graphify export age --push postgresql://...` behind a new `age` extra (`psycopg[binary]`).
- **Phase 2 — registry**: `graphify/age_registry.py` — plain-SQL registry (repos/snapshots/branches/diff tables, versioned idempotent migrations), stable `repository_id` = uuid5(normalized remote URL), per-repo default graph names so repos can't collide.
- **Phase 3 — snapshots + incremental sync**: `graphify/age_snapshots.py` + a reversible extension of `analyze.graph_diff()` (adds `properties`/`changed_nodes`/`changed_edges`; additive keys only). Push applies O(changed) once a snapshot exists.
- **Phase 4 — branches**: `graphify/age_branches.py` — feature branches push as validated diff chains over the base snapshot; `graphify age materialize|reap`; rebase/force-push detection fails closed into a fresh revision generation.
- **Phase 5–6 — retrieval + agent contract**: `graphify/age_backend.py` (`fetch_graph_from_age` → NetworkX → identical scoring/formatting as the file backend) behind `--age postgresql://... [--graph-name NAME]` on `query`/`path`/`explain`; `docs/AGE_SCHEMA.md` pins the Cypher contract with live-tested fixtures.

Docs: `docs/AGE_PLAN.md` (full design + spike findings), `docs/AGE_SCHEMA.md` (agent query contract). Generated skills regenerated via `tools.skillgen --bless` (`export age` step + `--age` usage lines).

## Type of change

- [x] New feature

## Verification & Invariants

Invariants this code protects and how:

- **Deletion-safe reconcile**: stale nodes/edges deleted in the *same transaction* as upserts — readers never see a partial graph. Covered by live integration tests (`test_age_integration.py`) that push, mutate, re-push, and assert row counts.
- **Provenance/direction**: undirected `nx.Graph` edges recover extracted direction via `_src`/`_tgt` (same idiom as `build.py`/`serve.py`); a relabeled node is deleted under its *old* label.
- **Fail-closed**: ambiguous first-push default-branch resolution is a hard error, not a guess; `schema_version`/`extraction_config_hash` mismatch refuses to extend a diff chain; non-contiguous diff chains raise.
- **Untrusted input**: graph name → `sql.Literal`; table/label identifiers → `sql.Identifier`; Cypher labels/relations whitelisted to `[A-Za-z0-9_]`/`[A-Z0-9_]`; full-props attribute keys must match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` before entering the Cypher SET clause; payloads via `sql.Literal(json.dumps(...))`; no `shell=True` anywhere (git calls are arg-list subprocesses with timeouts).
- **Determinism**: `serve.py` traversal is `sorted()` so answers don't depend on backend row-scan order.
- **Credentials**: `AGE_PASSWORD`/`PGPASSWORD` preferred over `--password`/DSN-embedded secrets, matching the neo4j/falkordb convention.

- [x] Reproduced the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the smallest fix necessary. (Feature-sized: one concern — AGE backend support — carried as phased commits per the one-branch-one-PR-per-feature convention.)
- [x] Added a regression test (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description synchronized with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any limitations / unsupported cases explicitly.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv sync --all-extras --frozen
uv run --frozen pytest tests/ -q --tb=short            # 6184 passed, 74 skipped
uv run --frozen ruff check .                            # clean
uv run --frozen pyright                                 # AGE files: only the 2 pre-existing upstream graphdb.py errors remain
uv run --frozen python -m tools.skillgen --check        # 134 artifacts in sync

# Live tier-2/3 suite (cannot run in CI — needs a real AGE instance):
docker run -d --name graphify-age -p 5432:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=graphify_test \
  apache/age@sha256:4241e2d8bb86a6b2ea44e9ad06c73856e12b209de295124603a599dd7feb70eb
uv run --frozen pytest tests/ -q -k age                 # 962 passed, live Apache AGE 1.7.0 / PostgreSQL 18.1
```

Test layout mirrors the FalkorDB suite: tier-1 unit tests are pure/mocked and run everywhere; tier-2/3 integration tests auto-skip without a reachable AGE (service-identifying `LOAD 'age'` probe, `AGE_HOST`/`AGE_PORT`/`AGE_DB`/`AGE_USER`/`AGE_PASSWORD` overrides).

## Limitations / unsupported cases

- `fetch_graph_from_age` loads the whole named graph into NetworkX — same cost profile as loading graph.json, documented choice (server-side filtering would mean reimplementing scoring in Cypher).
- `serve.py`/MCP is not AGE-wired (agents query AGE directly via the pinned contract) — deferred, see plan doc Phase 6.
- `--full-props` pushes only scalar attributes whose keys are valid Cypher identifiers; others are dropped (no rewrite, to avoid silent collisions).
- `age` extra overlaps `postgres` extra on `psycopg[binary]` — kept lean (no tree-sitter-sql) deliberately; can fold into `postgres` if preferred.

title: fix(csharp): don't collect tuple element names as type references
body:
Fixes #3796

### Problem
A named tuple type `(int mode, string label)` parses as a `tuple_type` whose `tuple_element` children carry both a `type` and a `name` field. `_csharp_collect_type_refs` walked every named child, so the element **names** were collected as type references, minted as sourceless placeholder nodes and emitted `references` edges — one junk "type" node per element, repeated in every file that declares such a signature (the issue reports five junk nodes from a single 5-element tuple return).

### Fix
Only the `type` field of each `tuple_element` should feed type-reference collection; the `name` is an identifier, not a type reference. The collector now descends into the element's `type` field only, skipping the name.

### Tests
- New: `tests/test_csharp_tuple_type_refs.py` — asserts no node is minted and no `references` edge targets an element name.
- Existing C# suite (106 tests across member nodes / generic callsites / interface dispatch / object creation / enum members / field generics) all pass.

title: path: no route through a contains edge — file-to-file dependency via a shared symbol reports no path
body:
## Summary

`graphify path <fileA> <fileB>` reports "No directed path found" for a real, direct, single-hop dependency between two files — not because of a direction-flip in a stored edge (that's #2309, fixed in 0.9.31), but because the edge needed to complete the route **does not exist in either direction**. `contains` edges only go file → symbol; there is no symbol → file edge, so a route like `a.py --imports--> helper() [defined in b.py]` can never reach `b.py`.

## Repro

Given:
- `a.py` does `from b import helper` and calls it
- `helper()` is defined in `b.py`

The graph then has:
```
a.py --imports--> helper()      (EXTRACTED)
b.py --contains--> helper()     (EXTRACTED)
```

Both edges point **into** `helper()`. There is no edge from `helper()` back out to `b.py` (or to `a.py`), so `nx.shortest_path` over the digraph `path` builds (from raw `contains`/`imports` edges) can never find `a.py -> helper() -> b.py`, even though `graphify explain a.py` and `graphify explain b.py` both correctly show the real edges on either side.

Reproduced on a real repo (graphifyy 0.9.69, code-only extraction, ~22k nodes / 53k edges): a module doing `from engine import get_bot` and calling it. `explain` on both files is accurate. `path fileA.py fileB.py` → "No directed path found between...". `--undirected` doesn't help either — it returns a longer, wrong detour through an unrelated file instead of the trivial 2-hop route, because undirected search has no reason to prefer the real containment edge over any other 2-hop U-turn through a shared node.

## Root cause

`path`'s traversal graph is built directly from the graph's raw symbol-level `contains`/`imports` edges. `contains` is directionally asymmetric for reachability purposes (file → symbol only), so any file-to-file question that must route *through* a symbol node (the common case — most cross-file dependencies are "file A imports a symbol defined in file B") has no directed edge to complete the hop back out to the target file.

This is a different failure mode from #2309 (which was a *rendering* bug — the true direction existed in `_src`/`_tgt` but was displayed backwards, fixed in 0.9.31 by reading those markers). Here the edge to complete the route is structurally absent, so correct direction-reading doesn't help.

## Existing correct pattern already in the codebase

`analyze.find_import_cycles()` solves the equivalent file-level problem correctly: it collapses symbol-level nodes to their parent file via the `source_file` attribute, and builds the file-level digraph from `imports_from`/`re_exports` edges — which carry a `source_file` attribute that resolves the true file→file direction — instead of from raw `contains` edges. `path`/`query` don't reuse this; they operate on the raw symbol graph.

## Suggested fix

When both `path` endpoints resolve to file nodes (the common CLI usage — `graphify path some/file.py other/file.py`), build the traversal graph the same way `find_import_cycles` does (collapse to `source_file`, route over `imports_from`/`re_exports`), instead of over the raw symbol digraph. That would make the trivial "does A depend on B" case — probably the single most common use of `path` — actually work.

## Environment

- graphifyy 0.9.69 (PyPI), Python 3.12
- `graphify extract . --code-only` (no LLM backend configured)
- Graph: ~22k nodes / 53k edges

Happy to share a minimal synthetic repo reproducing this in isolation if useful — the example above is genericized from a real internal codebase.

title: fix(detect): keep foreign manifest keys in their own path syntax
body:
## What does this PR do?

Follow-ups found while reviewing the recent manifest-key fixes for #1964.

- `_to_absolute_from_storage` normalized a foreign-platform absolute key with `os.path.normpath`, which applies the *current* platform's rules. On Windows, `/home/u/foo.py` became `\home\u\foo.py`, which POSIX cannot read back (`posixpath` does not treat `\` as a separator). The docstring also said such keys "pass through unchanged", which was not true. A new `_normpath_own_flavor` still collapses `.`/`..`, but under the key's own syntax: `ntpath` for a drive letter or leading backslash, `posixpath` for a leading `/` the current platform does not consider absolute. Every platform now canonicalizes a given key to the same string.
- `test_save_manifest_relativize_step_collapses_seeded_duplicates` never reached `save_manifest`'s own duplicate collapse. `save_manifest` calls `load_manifest` first, which already removes the duplicate, so the test still passed with the save side reverted to last-wins. The test now stubs `load_manifest` to hand over the un-collapsed rows.
- Type hints on `_collapse_manifest_duplicates`, matching its sibling helpers.

The ingest fix that was originally part of this PR is now in #3880, per the one-concern-per-PR rule.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a manifest key canonicalizes to the same string on every platform, and a foreign key is never rewritten into a form its own platform cannot read (#1964's cross-platform scope; Windows portability per CONTRIBUTING).

Persisted state: foreign-platform keys were mostly *not* persisted in the rewritten form, because `save_manifest` drops seeded rows whose file does not exist locally. The user-visible effect was the rewritten key returned by `load_manifest`. No migration is needed.

title: fix(ingest): rewrite only the host when normalizing a tweet URL for oEmbed
body:
## What does this PR do?

`_fetch_tweet` normalized a tweet URL for oEmbed with `url.replace("x.com", "twitter.com")` over the whole URL. This is the same bug class `dd65345` fixed in `_detect_url_type` ("classify a URL by its host, not by text it contains"):

- "x.com" in the path or query was rewritten too: a `?next=https://x.com/...` link was changed, and a handle like `dropbox.com_fan` became `dropbotwitter.com_fan`, so oEmbed was asked about a different URL.

It now parses the URL and rewrites the host only, reusing the `_host_is` helper from `_detect_url_type` (so `x.com` and its subdomains, e.g. `mobile.x.com` -> `mobile.twitter.com`).

Split out of #3879 per the one-concern-per-PR rule.

title: `_rebuild_lock` is a no-op on Windows, so the #1037 race is still unfixed there
body:
## Summary

`graphify.watch._rebuild_lock` falls back to `yield True` when `fcntl` can't be imported. Its docstring says so: *"Falls back to a no-op yield(True) on platforms without fcntl (Windows)."* So on Windows every caller "gets" the lock and concurrent rebuilds are never serialized.

#1037 was reported on Windows 11 and proposed "Serialize via `flock` (POSIX) or `msvcrt.locking` (Windows)". Only the POSIX half landed, so the race described there still exists on Windows in 0.9.61.

## Environment

- graphifyy 0.9.61, Python 3.13.3
- Windows 11 Pro (build 26200), Git for Windows (Git Bash); commits and pulls also via GitHub Desktop 3.6.6 (bundled git 2.53.0)

## Reproduction

```python
import subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.watch import _rebuild_lock

out = Path("graphify-out")
with _rebuild_lock(out) as a:
    with _rebuild_lock(out) as b:
        print("nested:", a, b)

holder = subprocess.Popen(
    [sys.executable, "-c",
     "import time; from pathlib import Path; from graphify.watch import _rebuild_lock\n"
     "with _rebuild_lock(Path('graphify-out')) as g:\n"
     "    print('holder', g, flush=True); time.sleep(5)"],
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
holder.stdout.readline()
with _rebuild_lock(out) as c:
    print("second process while holder runs:", c)
holder.wait()
```

Output on Windows:

```
nested: True True
second process while holder runs: True
```

`graphify-out/.rebuild.lock` is never created. With `fcntl` I'd expect `True False` and `False`.

## Why it matters

On Windows these paths all run unserialized:

- post-commit and post-checkout rebuilds fired back-to-back. The installed post-checkout hook even says *"The flock inside _rebuild_code still prevents pile-ups when commit + checkout fire back-to-back"*, which doesn't hold on Windows.
- a hook rebuild plus a manual `graphify update`: `cli.py` calls `_rebuild_code(..., block_on_lock=True)`, which doesn't wait here.
- the #1059 pending queue: since the lock is always acquired, contenders never defer to the running rebuild; each runs its own.

All of them write the same fixed temp file `graphify-out/.graph.tmp.json`, `os.replace` it onto `graph.json`, then write `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, `.graphify_labels.json` and `.sig`. Two overlapping rebuilds can therefore:

- fail with a JSON parse error (the #1037 symptom) or a `PermissionError` from `os.replace`, visible only in the log
- leave `graph.json` and the report/labels from different runs
- leave the graph at an older commit if the older rebuild finishes last

I haven't captured a fresh corruption on 0.9.61; the list above follows from the code path and the original #1037 report.

## Suggested fix

Take a Windows byte-range lock on the same `.rebuild.lock` with `msvcrt.locking`: `LK_NBLCK` for the non-blocking case, and a retry loop for `blocking=True` (`LK_LOCK` gives up after 10 attempts). Windows releases the lock when the handle closes or the process dies, so no stale-lock cleanup is needed, same as flock.

One caveat: Windows byte-range locks are mandatory, so locking byte 0 would stop external pollers from reading the PID written there. Locking a byte past the payload (for example at a large fixed offset) avoids that.

As defense in depth, a per-process temp name such as `.graph.tmp.<pid>.json` would stop overlapping writers from clobbering each other's temp file even when the lock is missing.

## Current workaround

Our `post-merge` hook waits 60 s before running `graphify update`, so a just-started hook rebuild can finish, then runs it once more 60 s later to overwrite a possibly stale result. It works in practice but only narrows the window.

title: hook-guard search: no project-membership gate — Bash/Grep that only touch out-of-project paths still get the MANDATORY nudge
body:
## Summary

The `search` arm of `graphify hook-guard` (matcher `Bash|Grep`) nudges on every search
while `graphify-out/graph.json` exists, regardless of **where** the search points. The
`read` arm already skips out-of-project targets (#1840 (a)); the `search` arm has no
equivalent gate.

## Versions

- First observed on 0.9.20.
- **Reproduced on v0.9.69** (latest, installed via pipx). In `graphify/cli.py`, the
  `if kind == "search":` branch (~line 856) decides only on
  `_bash_invokes_search(cmd_str)` (the #3121 tokenizer) or `pattern` for the Grep tool,
  plus `out_path("graph.json").is_file()`. No path is inspected. The `read` branch right
  below it has the #1840 (a) `relative_to(root)` gate.

## Repro

From a project root that has `graphify-out/graph.json`, pipe hook payloads straight into
the guard (`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` set to that root):

```sh
printf '%s' '{"tool_input":{"command":"grep -n foo /some/other/repo/README.md"}}' \
  | graphify hook-guard search
```

Results on v0.9.69 (paths anonymized; the real runs used sibling repos and a
home-directory folder outside the project):

| Payload | Target | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Bash `grep -n foo /some/other/repo/README.md` | outside the project | nudge |
| Bash `grep -n localhost /etc/hosts` | outside the project | nudge |
| Grep tool, `path` = absolute dir outside the project | outside the project | nudge |
| Bash `grep -rn X app/` | inside the project | nudge (expected) |
| Bash `echo "add flag support"` | not a search | silent (#3121 fix works) |
| `hook-guard read`, `file_path` = a `.py` outside the project | outside the project | silent (#1840 gate works) |

The same kind of out-of-project target is ignored by `read` but nudged by `search`.
In Claude Code, the injected `_SEARCH_NUDGE` ("MANDATORY: … You MUST run
`graphify query` …") reaches the agent although nothing searched belongs to the graph.

## Impact

In one real session, the agent ran searches over data exports and sibling repositories
from inside a graphified project, and received the nudge about 30 times. The token cost
is small; the real problem is the wording. "MANDATORY" pushed the agent into one
`graphify query` about unrelated data, which returned unrelated code. The volume issues
#3435 and #3756 get worse because of this.

## Proposal

Mirror #1840 (a) in the search arm:

- **Grep tool:** apply the same `relative_to(root)` check to `path`. When `path` is
  absent, the search is project-wide, so keep nudging.
- **Bash:** decide **per executed search**, never from the command as a whole. Collecting
  path-like tokens across the whole command causes false silences: in
  `grep foo /tmp/x; rg foo`, the second search runs over the project. For each search
  command found by the #3121 tokenizer:
  - apply `cd` and `VAR=value` in order;
  - drop output redirections (`>`, `2>&1`), but keep input ones (`<`);
  - do not treat the pattern argument as a path (unless `-e`/`-f` supplies the pattern);
  - resolve relative targets against the effective cwd;
  - a search with no target means the cwd, or, when fed by a pipe, the upstream
    commands' paths.
  Skip the nudge only when **every** search's targets are outside the root. Keep nudging
  when anything is uncertain: an unresolved variable, `$(...)`, backticks, a heredoc, a
  subshell, `xargs` feeding a search, or `cd -`.
- Optional: a config knob for in-project non-code directories to exclude (for example
  data dumps), since those are not in the graph either.

## Workaround in use

A small wrapper, set as the `Bash|Grep` hook command, applies the rule above. It pipes the
original stdin to `graphify hook-guard search` unless every search is provably outside
the project, and it never blocks. Parse errors and uncertainty forward the call; if
graphify itself is missing or times out, the nudge is simply lost.

We tested it on 42 cases, all passing: in-project and out-of-project paths, mixed commands,
`cd` changing the base, variables assigned before or after use, output and input
redirections, `git -C … grep`, `find … -exec grep`, pipes into `grep`, `xargs`, `$(...)`,
subshells, quoted paths with spaces, and the Grep tool with and without `path`. The first
version of the wrapper used the whole-command rule and silenced 5 searches over project
code, which is why the proposal above is per-search.

title: fix(watch): serialize _rebuild_lock on Windows via msvcrt (#3881)
body:
### Closes #3881.

## Problem

On Windows, `_rebuild_lock` in `graphify/watch.py` catches `ImportError` when importing `fcntl` and immediately falls back to `yield True`. Because `fcntl` does not exist on Windows, every caller is handed the lock simultaneously.

When git hooks (like `post-commit` and `post-checkout` back-to-back) or a background watcher and an explicit `graphify update` run at roughly the same time on Windows, they execute concurrently. Both write to `.graph.tmp.json` without synchronization and attempt `os.replace` onto `graph.json`, causing `PermissionError: [WinError 32]`, truncated JSON files, or mismatched community labels across rebuilds.

The original lock issue (#1037) was reported on Windows, but only the POSIX `fcntl.flock` half landed. Additionally, four lock tests in `tests/test_watch.py` and three pending queue tests were marked `skipif(sys.platform == "win32")`, so Windows CI never ran the locking test suite.

## RCA

In `graphify/watch.py`:
```python
try:
    import fcntl
except ImportError:
    yield True
    return
```
On Windows, `fcntl` is never available. The early return bypassed lock creation, acquisition, PID writing, and cleanup entirely.

## Fix

1. **Stdlib Windows file locking (`msvcrt.locking`)**:
   When `fcntl` is unavailable, use Python's built-in `msvcrt` module on Windows.
   - Non-blocking (`blocking=False`): Calls `msvcrt.locking(fh.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_NBLCK, 1)`. If already locked, raises `OSError`, caught to yield `False`.
   - Blocking (`blocking=True`): Loops with a short 50ms sleep until `LK_NBLCK` succeeds, avoiding `msvcrt.LK_LOCK`'s 10-second timeout.
   - Unlock: Calls `msvcrt.locking(fh.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)` in `finally:`.
   - Kernel safety: Windows automatically releases byte-range locks if the holding process crashes or is terminated.

2. **Byte offset past PID payload (`_win_lock_offset = 4096`)**:
   Windows byte-range locks are mandatory. If byte 0 is locked, external pollers attempting to read the holder PID from `.rebuild.lock` hit `PermissionError: [Errno 13]`. Locking 1 byte at offset 4096 preserves concurrent read access to byte 0 while enforcing strict mutual exclusion.

3. **Enable tests on Windows**:
   Removed `skipif(win32)` from the 4 lock tests and 3 pending queue tests in `tests/test_watch.py`, and added `test_rebuild_lock_blocks_concurrent_process` to assert that a second process is rejected when the lock is held.

## Verification/Test Suite

### Before fix (Windows 11, Python 3.14):
Running a holder subprocess with a concurrent non-blocking caller:
```text
[*] Testing _rebuild_lock in: C:\Users\harsha\AppData\Local\Temp\tmptqo4ovrx\graphify-out
[*] Holder process status: HOLDER_ACQUIRED True
[*] Second caller non-blocking acquisition result: True
[FAIL] Issue #3881 reproduced! Both processes acquired the lock simultaneously.
```

### After fix (Windows 11, Python 3.14):
```text
[*] Testing _rebuild_lock in: C:\Users\harsha\AppData\Local\Temp\tmppsk29nce\graphify-out
[*] Holder process status: HOLDER_ACQUIRED True
[*] Second caller non-blocking acquisition result: False
[*] External reader successfully read PID: 19168
[SUCCESS] Lock correctly serialized concurrent processes.
```

### Test suite:
```text
$ uv run pytest tests/test_watch.py -k "test_rebuild_lock or pending or contention or drains" -v
tests/test_watch.py::test_rebuild_lock_writes_pid_with_newline PASSED      [ 10%]
tests/test_watch.py::test_rebuild_lock_removed_after_release PASSED        [ 20%]
tests/test_watch.py::test_rebuild_lock_does_not_accumulate_pids_across_runs PASSED [ 30%]
tests/test_watch.py::test_rebuild_lock_non_blocking_does_not_clobber_holder PASSED [ 40%]
tests/test_watch.py::test_rebuild_lock_blocks_concurrent_process PASSED    [ 50%]
tests/test_watch.py::test_queue_and_drain_pending_round_trip PASSED        [ 60%]
tests/test_watch.py::test_drain_pending_dedupes_and_skips_blank_lines PASSED [ 70%]
tests/test_watch.py::test_queue_pending_noop_on_empty_list PASSED          [ 80%]
tests/test_watch.py::test_rebuild_code_queues_on_lock_contention PASSED    [ 90%]
tests/test_watch.py::test_rebuild_code_merges_pending_on_acquire PASSED    [100%]

```

title: Kotlin: class property with an annotation and no explicit type drops the whole file (UnboundLocalError: 'line' unbound)
body:
## Summary

A Kotlin class property that carries an **annotation and no explicit type** crashes the Kotlin extractor, and `_safe_extract` then **drops the entire file** from the graph (0 nodes, 0 edges for that file). It is silent apart from a single `warning: skipped …` line on stderr.

## Environment

- graphify **0.9.70** (latest on PyPI at time of writing), installed with `uv tool install graphifyy`
- `tree_sitter_kotlin` **1.1.0**
- Python 3.11.16, Linux x86-64 (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8)
- Trigger: `graphify update .` (the AST-only path; **no LLM needed** to reproduce)

## Minimal reproduction

`Repro.kt`:

```kotlin
class Repro {
    @Volatile
    var counter = 0
}
```

```console
$ GRAPHIFY_DEBUG=1 graphify update .
Re-extracting code files in . (no LLM needed)...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../graphify/extract.py", line 192, in _safe_extract
    return extractor(path)
  File ".../graphify/extract.py", line 2852, in extract_kotlin
    return _extract_generic(path, _KOTLIN_CONFIG)
  File ".../graphify/extractors/engine.py", line 5813, in _extract_generic
    walk(root)
  File ".../graphify/extractors/engine.py", line 5811, in walk
    walk(child, parent_class_nid=None)
  File ".../graphify/extractors/engine.py", line 4618, in walk
    walk(child, parent_class_nid=class_nid)
  File ".../graphify/extractors/engine.py", line 4870, in walk
    target_nid = ensure_named_node(anno_name, line)
                                   ^^^^^^^^^
UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'line' where it is not associated with a value
  warning: skipped /tmp/gf-min/Repro.kt (UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'line' where it is not associated with a value)
[graphify watch] Rebuilt: 0 nodes, 0 edges, 0 communities
```

Control — the same property **without** the annotation extracts fine:

```kotlin
class Control {
    var counter = 0
}
```

```console
$ GRAPHIFY_DEBUG=1 graphify update .
[graphify watch] Rebuilt: 2 nodes, 1 edges, 1 communities
```

## Root cause

`engine.py`, in the `property_declaration` branch for `tree_sitter_kotlin` (~line 4853): `line` is assigned **only inside** `if type_node is not None:`, but it is then used unconditionally by the annotation loop further down:

```python
if (config.ts_module == "tree_sitter_kotlin" and t == "property_declaration"):
    if parent_class_nid:
        type_node = _kotlin_property_type_node(node)
        if type_node is not None:
            line = node.start_point[0] + 1          # ← assigned here only
            refs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
            ...
        annotation_targets: set[str] = set()
        for anno_name, anno_raw in _kotlin_annotation_names(node, source):
            target_nid = ensure_named_node(anno_name, line)   # ← may be unbound
            if target_nid != parent_class_nid and target_nid not in annotation_targets:
                add_edge(parent_class_nid, target_nid, "references", line, context="attribute")
```

When the property has no explicit type node (`val x = 0`, `var counter = 0`, i.e. inferred type) **and** at least one annotation, `line` is never bound.

A minimal fix is to hoist the assignment above the `if type_node is not None:` branch (or compute it inside the annotation loop), e.g.:

```python
if parent_class_nid:
    line = node.start_point[0] + 1
    type_node = _kotlin_property_type_node(node)
    ...
```

## Impact

The failure is not limited to the property: **the whole file is discarded**, so every symbol, call edge and class in it disappears from `graph.json` without further notice. Downstream, `graphify query`, `path`, `affected` and `explain` then return empty or misleading results for that file's symbols — a wrong "nothing references this" is easy to conclude.

Real case: in a 70-file Kotlin Android project, 4 files were dropped this way (`FaceView.kt`, `FaceRuntime.kt`, `AndroidAudio.kt`, `AudioStreams.kt`) — i.e. the whole Android layer of the app is absent from the graph while the rest of the code is present.

Two secondary observations worth noting:

1. On a **second** `graphify update` run the warning is not repeated (files come from the incremental cache), so the loss is easy to miss.
2. Developers can set `GRAPHIFY_DEBUG=1` to get the traceback — that was the only way to find this, since the default path prints just one line.

Happy to test a patch if that helps.

title: feat: generalize unresolvable call tracking for better observability (#3665)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3665

This PR addresses unresolvable call observability in `graphify/extract.py`. Instead of silently discarding unresolvable calls and drop sites with bare `continue` statements (which leaves callers indistinguishable in `graph.json` from callers that make no calls), calls dropped without a resolvable target are now explicitly recorded on the caller node's metadata:

- **Generalized call recording**: Replaces `_park_unresolved_member_call` with a generalized `_record_unresolved_call` function storing structured dictionaries tracking `callee`, `reason`, `lang`, `receiver_type`, and `line`.
- **Bounded metadata & truncation tracking**: Strictly preserves the `_MAX_PARKED_CALLS_PER_NODE` (64) boundary. Any excess unresolvable calls increment an explicit `unresolved_calls_truncated` counter key on node metadata rather than being silently dropped.
- **Cross-file resolution drop sites**: Instruments the cross-file call resolution loop to record dropped calls across:
  - `no_candidates` (resolves the #3665 reproduction for dictionary/registry dispatch and `getattr`)
  - `cross_language_mismatch`
  - `go_import_mismatch`
  - `elixir_scope_mismatch`
  - `csharp_member_target`
  - `unresolved_ambiguity`
  - `source_less_stub`
  - `missing_import_evidence`
- **Multi-language member calls**: Connected across Python, Swift, TypeScript, C++, C#, PHP, Java, Objective-C, Go, and Kotlin member-call extraction sites with `reason="external_unresolved"`.
- **Backwards compatibility**: `_park_unresolved_member_call` is retained as a drop-in wrapper defaulting to `reason="external_unresolved"`.
- **Rebased on latest upstream**: Single clean commit rebased on top of `v0.9.89` (`e8eb76e7`) with no merge conflicts or branch drift.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [x] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Preserved invariants**: Strictly enforces node metadata boundaries at 64 entries with an explicit `unresolved_calls_truncated` counter tracking overflow. No synthetic or guessed edges are emitted.
- [x] **Backwards compatibility**: Callers of `_park_unresolved_member_call` continue to function unchanged.
- [x] **Comprehensive tests**: Added unit and end-to-end integration tests in `tests/test_cross_repo_member_calls.py` covering:
  - Schema validation, deduplication, and truncation counters.
  - End-to-end `graph.json` serialization (`test_graph_json_records_reason_and_truncation_counter`).
  - Python reproduction regression test matching #3665 (`test_python_unresolved_call_drop_sites_3665`).
  - Python typed receiver member-call extraction test (`test_python_typed_receiver_external_member_call`).

## How was this tested?

title: [Bug]: SQL: CREATE TABLEs inside BEGIN; … COMMIT; still dropped when a DO $$ … END $$; block makes tree-sitter-sql emit a top-level block (follow-up to #2953)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`extract_sql` silently drops every `CREATE TABLE` inside a `BEGIN; … COMMIT;` transaction when the transaction also contains a `DO $$ … END $$;` block.

tree-sitter-sql parses `BEGIN;` as the opener of a `block` that closes on the `END` of the DO body. The top-level node is then `block` instead of `transaction`. Since #2953, the top-level dispatch in `graphify/extractors/sql.py` walks `statement`, `transaction`, `ERROR` and a few Firebird types, but not `block`, so nothing inside it is extracted. The `create_table` nodes are still in the tree, under the `block`. No error or warning is printed.

**Expected:** `users` is extracted as a table node.
**Actual:** only the file node is produced.

Real-world impact: on an 850-line PostgreSQL `schema.sql` (PL/pgSQL trigger functions plus a few idempotent `DO $$` blocks), 8 of the 11 `CREATE TABLE` statements and all their triggers are missing from the graph.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
1. Save as `repro.sql`:


BEGIN;

CREATE TABLE users (
    id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY
);

DO $$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_trigger WHERE tgname = 't') THEN
        CREATE TRIGGER t BEFORE UPDATE ON users
        FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION touch();
    END IF;
END $$;

COMMIT;


2. Run in a fresh env:


uvx --from 'graphifyy[sql]==0.9.70' python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract_sql
print([n['label'] for n in extract_sql(Path('repro.sql'))['nodes']])
"


3. Control case: replace `BEGIN;` with `BEGIN TRANSACTION;` (equivalent in PostgreSQL) and run again. `users` is now extracted.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
No traceback: the failure is silent.


# BEGIN;
['repro.sql']

# BEGIN TRANSACTION;
['repro.sql', 'users']


Top-level nodes of the tree-sitter-sql parse (type, start row, end row):


# BEGIN;
[('block', 1, 12), ('ERROR', 12, 12), ('ERROR', 13, 15)]

# BEGIN TRANSACTION;
[('transaction', 1, 15)]
```

### Graphify version

0.9.70

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

- tree-sitter-sql 0.3.11, py-tree-sitter 0.25.2
- Also reproduced on graphifyy 0.9.53 (`uv tool install 'graphifyy[sql]==0.9.53'`)
- Reproduced on 0.9.70 in a clean throwaway env (`uvx --from 'graphifyy[sql]==0.9.70'`), not from a git checkout of `v8`
- No provider environment variables set: this is AST-only extraction, no LLM involved

### Additional context

Related:
- #2953: `BEGIN; … COMMIT;` wrapping (the case this follows up)
- #1910, #2180: PL/pgSQL `ERROR` nodes

title: [Bug]: Python: from-importing a function that has a nested def makes every module.func() call from that file lose its calls edge (0.9.58+)
body:
**What happened?**

Since 0.9.58, if a file does `from pkg import mod` and also `from pkg.mod import f`, where `f` is a function
that contains a nested `def`, **every** `mod.<anything>()` call in that file loses its `calls` edge. 0.9.57
resolves them. Still reproduces on 0.9.70 and on `v8@4c21b15e9b`.

Root cause (found by instrumenting the resolver; the intermediate edge does not survive to `graph.json`):
since #3410 an outer function with a nested def is the source of a `contains` edge. The module arm of
`_resolve_python_member_calls` treats any `imports` target that has `contains` children as a candidate module:

```python
mods = [t for t in imported_by_filenode.get(caller_file, ())
        if t in contains_children
        and (_module_stem_key(t) == rkey or file_aliases.get(t) == rkey)]
if len(mods) != 1:  # not an imported module, or ambiguous -> bail
    continue
```

The `imports views -> sort_todos` edge makes `sort_todos` a candidate, and `_module_stem_key` takes the stem
of its *file* (`store`), which matches the receiver. So `mods == [store.py, sort_todos]`, and the resolver
bails as ambiguous.

**Steps to reproduce**

```shell
mkdir -p repro/app/api repro/app/services && cd repro
touch app/api/__init__.py app/services/__init__.py
cat > app/services/store.py <<'EOF'
def sort_todos(todos):
    def key(t):
        return t
    return sorted(todos, key=key)


def parse_todo_file(path):
    return path
EOF
cat > app/api/views.py <<'EOF'
from services import store
from services.store import sort_todos


def get_archived_panel():
    return store.parse_todo_file(1)


def board():
    return sort_todos([])
EOF
git init -q . && graphify update .
```

**Error output or graph output**

```text
calls edges from app/api/views.py
0.9.57:  board() -> sort_todos(); get_archived_panel() -> parse_todo_file()
0.9.58, 0.9.62, 0.9.66, 0.9.70:  board() -> sort_todos()        <- parse_todo_file() lost
controls: without the nested `def key` in sort_todos -> both edges on every version
```

**Suggested fix (one line, verified):** a node that is itself contained by another node is not a module:

```diff
             mods = [t for t in imported_by_filenode.get(caller_file, ())
                     if t in contains_children
+                    and t not in file_of_node
                     and (_module_stem_key(t) == rkey or file_aliases.get(t) == rkey)]
```

On a 485-file Python subtree of our repo this line alone restores exactly the 8 lost `mod.func()` edges
and adds or removes nothing else (full graph diff, 0.9.70 vs 0.9.70 + this line: +8 `calls`, −0). On the
whole ~2,470-file repo, combined with the fix from the companion issue, the 8 are recovered and no edge is
removed.

**Version:** 0.9.58 → 0.9.70 (last good: 0.9.57) · **OS:** macOS · **Python:** 3.11 · **Install:** uv
(`uv venv` + `uv pip install graphifyy==<v>`; reproduced on a clean fixture, no LLM backend)

**Additional context:** related but different: #2447 (other causes in the same arm), #2428 / PR #2429 (alias
stem; the un-aliased repro above is not covered by #2429), #3272 (package-form import outside the package tree).

title: [Bug]: Python: a class used in a type annotation turns calls to its constructor into no edge at all (0.9.62+)
body:
**What happened?**

Since 0.9.62, calling a project class whose name also appears in a type annotation in the same file drops the
`calls` edge to its constructor. 0.9.61 and older resolve it. Still reproduces on 0.9.70 and on `v8@4c21b15e9b`.

Two shapes, same root:

- **A. annotation in another function:** the annotation leaves a sourceless stub node `Parser` in the file.
  In `extractors/engine.py` the in-file resolution binds `Parser()` to that stub. Then neither branch runs, so
  the call is emitted neither as an edge nor as a raw call:

  ```python
  external_stub_target = bool(tgt_nid and not nid_to_sf.get(tgt_nid))
  if tgt_nid and not external_stub_target:
      ...  # emits calls
  elif callee_name and not tgt_nid:
      ...  # raw_call for cross-file resolution
  ```
  Before #3156 the edge to the stub was emitted and later remapped to the real class.

- **B. annotation in the same function** (`def detect(self) -> Parser: return Parser()`): even when the call
  reaches the cross-file pass, it is skipped because the pair already has the annotation edge:
  `if tgt != caller and (caller, tgt) not in existing_pairs:` (extract.py). Before, the in-file `calls` and the
  generic `references` collapsed in build (`_GENERIC_RELATIONS`, specific beats generic).

**Steps to reproduce**

```shell
mkdir -p repro/app/engines/transcript && cd repro
touch app/engines/__init__.py app/engines/transcript/__init__.py
cat > app/engines/transcript/parser.py <<'EOF'
class Parser:
    def feed(self, line):
        return line
EOF
cat > app/engines/engine.py <<'EOF'
from typing import Optional

from engines.transcript.parser import Parser


class Engine:
    def detect(self):                    # shape A
        return Parser()

    def get_parser(self) -> Optional[Parser]:
        return None

    def make(self) -> Parser:            # shape B
        return Parser()
EOF
git init -q . && graphify update .
```

**Error output or graph output**

```text
edges from app/engines/engine.py
0.9.57, 0.9.61:  calls .detect()->Parser; calls .make()->Parser; references .get_parser()->Parser
0.9.62, 0.9.70:  references .get_parser()->Parser; references .make()->Parser   <- both calls lost
0.9.70 + shape-A fix:        calls .detect()->Parser; references .get_parser(); references .make()
0.9.70 + shape-A + B fixes:  calls .detect()->Parser; calls .make()->Parser; references .get_parser()
controls: no annotation -> calls on every version;
          external class (fastapi.HTTPException) annotated + called -> only references on 0.9.62+ (the #3156
          intent), unchanged by the patches below
```

**Suggested fix, measured on 0.9.70:**

- Shape A, one line in `extractors/engine.py`: let a call bound to a sourceless stub fall through to
  cross-file resolution, where the #3156 guard still drops truly external targets:

  ```diff
  -                elif callee_name and not tgt_nid:
  +                elif callee_name and (not tgt_nid or external_stub_target):
  ```

  Restores shape A (12 of 48 lost constructor edges in our repo). External-class control unchanged.

- Shape B: a pair that has only generic edges (`references`/`uses`/`mentions`) should not block a `calls`,
  which build then collapses. We tried this (a `generic_only_pairs` set checked next to `existing_pairs` in
  the direct-call branch). It recovers the other 36, but it is wider than the regression: it also turns 223
  long-standing `uses`/`references` pairs into `calls`. We checked all of them by AST and each one is a real
  call site, so it looks correct, but it is a behavior change beyond 0.9.61. Leaving that decision to you.

**Version:** 0.9.62 → 0.9.70 (last good: 0.9.61) · **OS:** macOS · **Python:** 3.11 · **Install:** uv
(clean fixture, no LLM backend)

**Additional context:** introduced alongside #3156 (0.9.62). Not covered by #3405 or #2447.

title: [Feature]: out-of-tree graph store keyed by repository, shared across worktrees
body:
### Problem or use case

I'd like graphify to keep its graphs outside the repositories it indexes, in a per-user store. I want the graphs. What I don't want is `graphify-out/` inside other people's repos, or a set of workarounds I have to maintain to keep it out.

On a typical day I clone about ten repositories and open around three git worktrees in each, one per agent task. Since graphify writes `graphify-out/` into the checkout, every clone and every worktree needs its own handling:

- The output has to be ignored somewhere, and the repo's `.gitignore` isn't mine to edit. So it goes into `.git/info/exclude` or a global excludes file, without a trailing slash in case it's a symlink.
- A fresh worktree has no graph, and rebuilding one per worktree costs time and LLM calls. Copying the primary checkout's graph in doesn't help: incremental extraction then treats the whole corpus as changed (#2654).
- A symlink from each worktree to the primary checkout's `graphify-out` needs a `post-checkout` hook in `init.templateDir`. That hook doesn't fire in repos that set their own `core.hooksPath`. An `update` from the worktree also writes straight through the link into the primary graph.
- An absolute `GRAPHIFY_OUT` is one global value with no per-repo key. The skill ignores it anyway (#2571).

Each of these works on its own terms. Together they are a pile of glue per clone, just to read someone else's code with a graph.

### Proposed solution

My proposal is an opt-in store mode. Graphs live in a per-user directory keyed by repository, nothing is written to the working tree, and one global setting turns it on. After that a new clone or worktree needs no preparation.

I read through v8 to check how much this touches. Most of it already works with an absolute `GRAPHIFY_OUT`, so the design is mostly about computing that value per repo:

1. Resolution happens in `graphify/paths.py` at import time, and the first match wins. If `GRAPHIFY_OUT` is set, nothing changes. If an in-tree `graphify-out/` already exists at the repo top, nothing changes either, so teams that commit their graph are not affected. If store mode is on, the result is `<store>/<key>`. Otherwise it stays `graphify-out`. The resolved value is absolute and goes into `GRAPHIFY_OUT`, so the modules that copy the constant at import keep working as they are.
2. Store mode is enabled with `GRAPHIFY_STORE=1` or with `{"store": true}` in `~/.graphify/config.json`. The config file is there because git hooks run from GUI clients don't see the shell environment. The default location is `~/.graphify/store/`, next to the per-user state graphify already keeps, and `GRAPHIFY_STORE_DIR` overrides it.
3. The key is the repo directory name plus a short hash of `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`. That gives every linked worktree of a clone the same key. Outside git, the hash comes from the absolute cwd. Each entry also writes an `origin.json` with the common dir, the primary worktree path and the remote URL, for listing and pruning later.
4. Worktrees share the clone's graph read-only. Read commands, hook-guard and MCP work from any worktree. Write commands (`extract`, `update`, `watch`, `cluster-only`) exit with a message pointing at the primary checkout. The existing worktree guard in the hooks already skips rebuilds there. Since `source_file` paths are relative to the scan root, a graph built in the primary checkout resolves fine from a worktree. In store mode `.graphify_root` is always written absolute. This would also cover the read-side fallback from #2064.
5. A new `graphify where` command prints the resolved output dir exactly as the process sees it. It is the only new CLI surface, and the skill uses it to find the graph.
6. The skill and the always-on text stop hardcoding the path. Each bash block starts with `GFY_OUT="$(graphify where 2>/dev/null || echo graphify-out)"`, and every literal `graphify-out/` becomes `"$GFY_OUT"/`. Inline Python gets the path from an env var, never through string interpolation. In default mode `graphify where` prints `graphify-out`, so current behaviour doesn't change. This overlaps with #1054 and #2720, and I'd rather work with those authors than open a competing change.
7. `graphify store list` shows each entry with its origin, size and last write, and flags orphans whose clone is gone. `graphify store prune` removes orphans and is a dry run by default.
8. In store mode `hook install` doesn't write the `.gitattributes` merge-driver line, since there is no in-tree graph to merge. Nothing else in the hooks changes.

I'd split the work into three PRs, each useful on its own:

1. Resolution, the key, `origin.json`, the write guard in linked worktrees, and `graphify where`. Tests would use real `git worktree add` fixtures, like the existing worktree-guard test in `test_hooks.py`. CLI, hooks and MCP users get the benefit from this one alone.
2. Skill fragments, always-on blocks and the agent text in `install.py` switch to `graphify where`, including the `--bless` run and the sanctioned always-on edits.
3. `graphify store list` and `graphify store prune`.

A few things I'm not sure about:

- Should store mode stay opt-in, or become the default in some later major version?
- Is a shared read-only graph the right policy for worktrees? The alternative is an opt-in per-worktree graph keyed by `--git-dir`, seeded from the clone's graph once #2654 is fixed.
- Is `~/.graphify/store/` a good default, or would you prefer `$XDG_DATA_HOME/graphify/` on Linux? I wouldn't put it under a cache dir, because the semantic pass costs money to rebuild.

### Alternatives considered

- `graphify remote` (#1751, #1752) moves the data out, but the repo still gets a `graphify-out` symlink, a committed `.graphify/` config and a `.gitignore` edit. That fits a team sharing one graph. It doesn't fit leaving someone else's repo untouched.
- Making the skill honour `GRAPHIFY_OUT` (#1054, #2720) is needed, and step 6 builds on it. It is still one global value with no per-repo key, though.
- The worktree fallback in #2064 lets read commands use the primary checkout's graph. It covers part of step 4, but not the in-tree writes or the skill.
- #686 asked for worktree support earlier and got `GRAPHIFY_OUT`, which leads back to the points above.

### Area

CLI or installation

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this. If the design looks right to you, I'll start with the first PR, and I'm happy to change any part of it before that.

title: [Bug]: Maven POM ingestion does not resolve properties inherited from a parent POM
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Follow-up to #3806, which v0.9.68 fixed for inherited `groupId` and a POM's own `${...}`
  properties — thanks, that already recovers a lot. One case from that report is still open.

  ## Problem
  
  `_parse_pom` resolves `${...}` only against the `<properties>` of the POM being parsed and the
  built-in `project.*` values. A property defined in a **parent** POM and used in a child stays
  literal, so the dependency does not match the module node and the `depends_on` edge is dropped.

  This is how most Scala multi-module projects suffix their artifacts: `scala.binary.version`
  lives in the root POM and every module depends on `foo_${scala.binary.version}`.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/apache/livy.git
  graphify explain "livy-server"
  
  
  - `scala.binary.version` is defined only in the root `pom.xml`; `server/pom.xml` uses it 17
    times.
  - The module nodes resolve (`org.apache.livy:livy-core_2.12`, `livy-core_2.13`), but
    `server/pom.xml` still looks up `livy-core_${scala.binary.version}`.
  - Result: `livy-server → livy-core` and `livy-server → livy-repl` are missing, and no module is
    shown depending on `livy-core`, while 8 declare it.
  - Overall, v0.9.70 keeps 39 of the 55 inter-module dependencies the POMs declare (v0.9.67 kept
    18).
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
- `scala.binary.version` is defined only in the root `pom.xml`; `server/pom.xml` uses it 17

  - Result: `livy-server → livy-core` and `livy-server → livy-repl` are missing, and no module is
    shown depending on `livy-core`, while 8 declare it.
  - Overall, v0.9.70 keeps 39 of the 55 inter-module dependencies the POMs declare (v0.9.67 kept
```

title: fix: guard search hook by project membership
body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #3882 by making the search hook aware of whether a search target is inside or outside the Graphify project.

The implementation introduces a single lightweight Bash parser and intermediate representation (IR) shared by both search detection and project-membership analysis. This avoids maintaining two independent tokenization paths while preserving the existing #3121 behavior.

### Key changes

* Added a shared `_parse_bash()` representation for shell commands.
* Refactored `_bash_invokes_search()` to consume the shared parser.
* Added project-membership analysis for search targets.
* Tracks:

  * `cd` / effective working directory
  * environment variable assignments
  * input redirections
  * known pipeline producers
  * search-specific command arguments
* Handles `grep`, `rg`, `find`, `fd`, and `git grep` target semantics.
* Added conservative handling for uncertain shell constructs:

  * unresolved variables and shell parameters
  * command substitutions and backticks
  * subshells
  * heredocs
  * `xargs`
  * `cd -`
  * unknown pipeline producers
  * Windows drive-relative paths
* Preserves the existing nudge-only behavior; search hooks never deny execution.

### Safety invariant

The hook suppresses the search nudge **only when every executed search is provably targeting something outside the project**.

If any search is inside the project or cannot be resolved with certainty, the nudge is preserved.

### Testing

Added 18 focused tests covering:

* direct search targets
* outside-project searches
* mixed searches
* `cd` state tracking
* redirections
* pipelines
* search flags and pattern separation
* shell uncertainty
* Windows path handling
* fail-open behavior

Full relevant hook/search suite:

**206 passed, 0 failed**

Existing tests were left unchanged.

title: fix(hook): bound soft nudges per agent (carries #3443)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Carries #3443 by @L4XB onto the current `v8` base, preserving its commit authorship and message, then adds one follow-up commit that closes three gaps found while running it downstream. Refs #3435, #3756, #2984.

### Relationship to #3443

- #3443 is the original implementation and remains the source of this branch's first commit, which keeps @L4XB's authorship and commit message.
- The follow-up was described in [a review comment on #3443](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/pull/3443#issuecomment-5868350642), with an offer to open it as a PR against @L4XB's branch.
- This PR combines both into one tested branch on current `v8`. It is an integration candidate, not a claim of original authorship; maintainers can merge whichever shape is easiest, and this can be closed if the follow-up lands in #3443 directly.

### The follow-up

1. **Subagents get their own budget.** Claude Code subagent tool calls carry the parent's `session_id` and are distinguished only by `agent_id` ([hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#common-input-fields)). Keying the counter on `session_id` alone lets the parent exhaust the budget before a subagent, which starts with an empty context, sees a nudge. The marker is now keyed on `session_id` plus a 16-character SHA-256 prefix of `agent_id` when present, so long ids cannot truncate two agents into one key.
2. **The query stamp no longer silences agents that never queried.** `last_query_stamp` is project-wide and cannot say which agent ran `query`/`explain`/`path`. Each agent's first nudge now fires regardless of the stamp; the stamp silences the later ones. Calls without a `session_id` keep the stamp-only behavior.
3. **The stale-graph notice is bounded.** `_READ_NUDGE_STALE` fired on every read of a file edited after the last build. It now draws on the same per-agent budget.

`_nudge_allowed` takes the hook payload instead of a session id so it can read `agent_id`. The strict-mode deny is unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariants: each agent (session, or subagent within it) sees its first nudge; after that, nudges stop while the query stamp is fresh and after `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_NUDGE_CAP` per agent; the strict deny still fires at most once per session; any marker error fails open.

`test_fresh_query_stamp_suppresses_deny` changes accordingly: with a fresh stamp there is still no deny, the session's first nudge fires, and the second read is silent. New tests cover per-agent budgets (including 64-character session ids), a subagent's first nudge after the parent queried, the stamp without a `session_id`, and the stale notice sharing the budget. They were run red against #3443 alone before the follow-up.

Known limitation (inherited from #3443): the counter is an unlocked read-modify-write, so concurrent hook processes for the same agent can exceed the cap slightly. They cannot suppress an agent's first nudge.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run pytest -q

  Erlang/R/Solidity/VB.NET extractors and Ollama backend not installed locally)
uv run ruff check .
  All checks passed!
```

Also deployed downstream and checked live under Oh My Pi: after `graphify query`, the parent session's next grep was silent, and a freshly spawned subagent still received its first nudge, with separate markers under `graphify-out/cache/hook_sessions/`.

- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).

title: [Feature]: Persistent Light/Dark Theme Preference for Graph Visualization
body: ### Description The generated `graph.html` visualization currently defaults to a dark theme. It would be useful to support a persistent **light/dark theme preference**, especially for users working in environments where light mode is preferred. Ideally, Graphify should provide a theme toggle in the generated visualization and remember the user's selection between sessions. ### Proposed behavior Add a theme selector/toggle with at least: * ☀️ Light * 🌙 Dark * 🖥️ System The selected theme should be persisted using browser storage (for example, `localStorage`) so that reopening the generated `graph.html` preserves the user's preference. ### Expected behavior For example: ```text First visit ↓ Use system preference ↓ User selects "Light" ↓ Save preference to localStorage ↓ Next time graph.html is opened ↓ Automatically use Light mode ``` ### Additional considerations The theme should apply consistently to: * Graph/canvas background * Sidebar * Search box * Search results * Node/edge information panels * Legend * Statistics panel * Checkboxes and controls * Text and secondary text * Borders and separators * Hover/selected states It would also be useful if the default behavior could follow the operating system's `prefers-color-scheme` setting when no explicit preference has been saved. ### Possible implementation A simple implementation could use CSS variables: ```css :root { --bg: #ffffff; --panel-bg: #f8f9fa; --text: #222222; --secondary-text: #666666; --border: #d9dee5; } [data-theme="dark"] { --bg: #0f0f1a; --panel-bg: #1a1a2e; --text: #e0e0e0; --secondary-text: #aaa; --border: #333; } ``` And persist the selection: ```javascript localStorage.setItem("graphify-theme", theme); ``` On startup: ```javascript const savedTheme = localStorage.getItem("graphify-theme"); if (savedTheme) { document.documentElement.dataset.theme = savedTheme; } else if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches ``` ### Proposed solution ### Proposed solution Add a theme selector to the generated `graph.html` with three options: * **Light** * **Dark** * **System** — follows the user's OS/browser preference The selected theme should be stored in `localStorage` so the preference persists when the generated HTML file is reopened. The implementation could use CSS variables for theme-dependent colors and JavaScript to switch between themes. When no preference has been saved, Graphify should respect the browser's `prefers-color-scheme` setting. The theme should cover the entire visualization UI, including the graph background, sidebar, search, legend, statistics, controls, text, borders, and hover/selection states. This would allow users to choose their preferred appearance without modifying the generated HTML or Graphify's source code. ### Alternatives considered _No response_ ### Area Graph building or querying ### Are you willing to submit a PR? Yes, but I will need guidance ### Compatibility / behavior impact ### Additional context _No response_

title: feat(cli): refresh stale skills after a package upgrade (#1805)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Upgrading graphify (`uv tool upgrade graphifyy`, `pip install -U graphifyy`) replaces the package but leaves every installed skill on the old version. `graphify install` only refreshes the platform it detects, so on a machine with several agents, codex, opencode, gemini and the rest keep running outdated instructions until each one is reinstalled by hand. I ran into this on my own setup, where the Gemini copy was several minor releases behind the package without anything saying so to the agent.

#1805 improved the warning, but the warning goes to the terminal and the agent reading the skill never sees it. This PR fixes the drift itself: on the first CLI run after an upgrade, graphify re-copies every user-scope skill whose `.graphify_version` stamp is older than the running package. That includes `graphify update`, which is often the first command run after an upgrade (or the only one, from a git hook), so nobody has to run `graphify --version` or anything else first. It is on by default, and `GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1` turns it off for pinned or centrally managed skill directories.

The refresh only acts when it can be sure the result is right:

- It only touches copies graphify installed itself (stamp and `SKILL.md` both present) and never installs anything new.
- A stamp newer than the package is left alone, so nothing gets downgraded (#1568).
- A directory that two installers write to is skipped, because the stamp doesn't record which variant is there. That covers copilot and `graphify vscode install`, gemini and agents on Windows, and two platform dirs symlinked to the same real directory. Pairs that differ only by host OS (claude/windows) get the variant a plain `graphify install` would pick.
- A locally edited `SKILL.md` is kept as `SKILL.md.bak` via the existing `_copy_skill_file` backup (#3144).
- Output goes to stderr, one line per refreshed directory plus the `.bak` notice, so `--json` and the MCP stdio server stay clean.
- A failed refresh never breaks the command the user actually ran. The stamp stays old, so the existing version warning still names the manual fix.
- `install`, `uninstall`, `hook-check` and `hook-guard` skip the refresh.

### Locking

Once the CLI writes skill directories on its own, two graphify processes can end up writing the same one: several agents starting right after an upgrade, or a refresh running while the user runs `graphify install` or `uninstall`. Every writer stages through the same fixed `SKILL.md.tmp` / `references.tmp` names, so they would write through each other, and an uninstall racing a refresh could see the skill put back.

Install, uninstall and the refresh now take one lock per skill directory:

- It is an OS file lock (`flock` on POSIX, `msvcrt.locking` on Windows). The OS releases it however the holder exits, so a crash or a kill never leaves a directory locked and there is no staleness timeout to tune.
- The lock file lives under `~/.cache/graphify/skill-locks/`, keyed by the resolved skill path, not inside the skill directory. A project install leaves nothing in the repository, and uninstall never has to delete a file another process may still hold. The file is never deleted.
- Install and uninstall wait for the lock. The refresh doesn't: it skips a directory another process holds and reads the stamp again once it has the lock, so a directory that was refreshed or uninstalled in the meantime is left alone.
- Where locking isn't available (a file system that refuses to lock, no writable cache directory), install and uninstall run unlocked as they did before this PR, and the refresh leaves the skill to the version warning.

Two small related changes: the version warning now also checks the gemini skill, which it missed because gemini isn't in `_PLATFORM_CONFIG`, and the vscode skill path is factored into `_vscode_skill_destination()` so install, uninstall and the refresh share one definition. The README env var table and the version-mismatch troubleshooting entry mention the new behaviour.

**Limitations:** only user-scope skills are refreshed. Project-scoped installs (`--project`) and the shared directories listed above still rely on the warning and a manual `graphify install --platform <name>`. The refresh runs on the CLI's first invocation after the upgrade, not at install time, since pip and uv offer no post-install hook for wheels.

title: fix(opencode): dual v1+v2 plugin + absolute file:// registration
body:
## What does this PR do?

`graphify opencode install` writes `.opencode/plugins/graphify.js` using only the v1 plugin API, so OpenCode v2 refuses to load it:

```
failed to load plugin <path> : Plugin must export a default definition with an id and
an effect or setup function (cause: SchemaError(Missing key at ["default"]))
```

The installer also registers the plugin in `.opencode/opencode.json` under the **bare relative path** `".opencode/plugins/graphify.js"`. OpenCode v2 resolves a bare specifier as an npm package spec and fails:

```
NpmInstallFailedError (cause: Error: Could not read package.json:
  ENOENT .../.opencode/plugins/graphify.js/package.json)
```

So on v2 the integration is dead on arrival — one error or the other fires from the directory you open OpenCode in.

Fixes both in one file:

- Port `_OPENCODE_PLUGIN_JS` to a **single dual entrypoint**: a v2 default export (`{ id, setup }`) that prepends the reminder via `ctx.shell.hook("create.before", event)`, **plus** the v1 named export (`"tool.execute.before"`) kept alongside, so the same file still loads on v1. The v2 path walks up from the hook's `event.cwd` so the reminder also fires when the first command runs from a subdirectory.
- Register the plugin by its resolved **`file://` URI** (the form the Kilo installer already uses) instead of a bare relative path. Uninstall drops both the URI form and any legacy bare relative entry, so an old `opencode.json` cannot keep tripping v2's npm-spec resolution.

Refs #3554, #3732. Note: this overlaps #3819 (dual entrypoint) and #3792 (drop the stale config entry); this PR does both, keeps v1 compatibility, and registers the plugin explicitly rather than relying on auto-discovery.

The invariant: `graphify opencode install` must produce a plugin that loads and injects on **both** OpenCode v1 and v2, from any project directory, without leaving a config entry that v2 misparses.
