title: fix(maven): resolve properties inherited from a parent POM (#3890)
body:
## Summary

`_parse_pom` now resolves `${...}` against the `<parent>` chain, so a property
declared only in the root POM (e.g. `scala.binary.version`) reaches every module
that uses it:

```text
_parse_pom(text, pom)
  _inherited_pom_properties   # walk <parent>/<relativePath> chain, outermost first
  own <properties>            # override inherited
  project.* builtins          # setdefault
  expand aid/gid/version/deps # module may suffix its own artifactId too
 ```

 - Chain follows Maven's <relativePath> rule: declared path, default ../pom.xml,
   <relativePath/> = repository parent (stop, inherit nothing).
 - Cycle-safe (seen-set + depth cap); unparseable/missing ancestors are skipped.
 - Unknown keys stay literal so unresolvable references remain visible instead of
   silently dropping the dependency.

 Evidence

 - Before: 5 of the 10 new tests fail at HEAD — livy-server's dependency on
   livy-core_${scala.binary.version} stays literal (pkg_..._livy_core_scala_binary_version)
   and the depends_on edge is dropped.
 - After: tests/test_manifest_ingest.py 24 passed, including the #3806
   regression test; livy-shaped layout resolves 17/17 scala.binary.version uses
   in server/pom.xml and the livy-server → livy-core_2.12 edge survives
   build_from_json. ruff check clean.


Fixes: #3890

title: fix(extract): ignore contained symbols when resolving imported modules (#3887)
body:
Fixes #3887

### Summary

In `_resolve_python_member_calls`, candidate imported modules matching a receiver name (`module.func()`) are gathered from the caller file's `imported_by_filenode` targets:

```python
mods = [t for t in imported_by_filenode.get(caller_file, ())
        if t in contains_children
        and (_module_stem_key(t) == rkey or file_aliases.get(t) == rkey)]
```

when a file imports both a module (`from services import store`) and a function from that module (`from services.store import sort_todos`), and `sort_todos` contains a nested function (`def key(t): ...`):
1. PR #3410 added `contains` edges from enclosing functions to their nested functions, so `sort_todos in contains_children` evaluates to `True`.
2. `_module_stem_key(sort_todos)` looks at the node's `source_file` (`services/store.py`), whose stem is `"store"`.
3. `mods` ends up with two entries: the module file node `services/store.py` and the function node `sort_todos`.
4. Because `len(mods) == 2 != 1`, the god-node ambiguity guard bails out, silently dropping the `calls` edge for every `store.<func>()` call in that caller.

### Fix
Filter out nodes that are themselves contained inside another node by adding `and t not in file_of_node`.

`file_of_node` is already populated on line 3903 for all `contains` edges (`file_of_node[tgt] = src`). Top-level file and module nodes are never the target of a `contains` edge, so `t not in file_of_node` is `True` strictly for genuine module/file nodes and `False` for any symbol (function, method, class) defined inside a file.

### Evidence/verification

#### Before Fix
Running extraction on a caller importing both `store` and `sort_todos` (with nested `def key` in `sort_todos`):
```text
$ uv run python contribution-docs/reproduction-scripts/reproduce_issue_3887.py
============================================================
Issue #3887 Reproduction Results:
Extracted Calls Edges:
  board() -> sort_todos()

[FAILED] get_archived_panel() -> parse_todo_file() call edge MISSING!
```

#### After Fix
With `and t not in file_of_node`:
```text
$ uv run python contribution-docs/reproduction-scripts/reproduce_issue_3887.py
============================================================
Issue #3887 Reproduction Results:
Extracted Calls Edges:
  board() -> sort_todos()
  get_archived_panel() -> parse_todo_file()

[PASSED] get_archived_panel() -> parse_todo_file() call edge FOUND.
```

### Verification
- Added regression test `test_python_module_call_resolves_when_same_file_imports_function_with_nested_def` in `tests/test_extract.py`.
- Ran `uv run pytest tests/test_extract.py -k "nested_def or test_python_module_qualified_call"` (3 passed in 0.98s).
- Ran all Python member call tests in `test_extract.py` (31 passed in 1.53s).
- Ran `uv run ruff check graphify/extract.py tests/test_extract.py` (clean).
- Ran `uv run python -m tools.skillgen --check` (134 artifacts match).

title: fix(kotlin): hoist property line calculation to prevent UnboundLocalError on annotated properties (#3884)
body:
Fixes #3884

### Summary

When extracting Kotlin class properties in `engine.py`, properties with an annotation and an inferred/implicit type (e.g. `@Volatile var counter = 0` or `@Inject val id = 1`) crashed with:
`UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'line' where it is not associated with a value`.

Because `_safe_extract` catches extractor crashes and returns empty results, the entire `.kt` file was silently dropped from the graph (0 nodes, 0 edges).

### Root Cause
In `graphify/extractors/engine.py` (around line 4844), `line = node.start_point[0] + 1` was defined only within `if type_node is not None:`. When a property has no explicit type node, `type_node` is `None`, so `line` was never assigned before being passed to `ensure_named_node(anno_name, line)` in the subsequent annotation loop.

### Fix
Hoist `line = node.start_point[0] + 1` to the top of the `if parent_class_nid:` block, matching the pattern used in the adjacent Swift extractor. This ensures `line` is unconditionally available for both explicit-type properties and inferred-type properties.

### Evidence

#### Before Fix
```text
$ uv run python contribution-docs/reproduction-scripts/reproduce_issue_3884.py
  warning: skipped C:\Users\...\Repro.kt (UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'line' where it is not associated with a value)
============================================================
Issue #3884 Reproduction Results:
Extracted nodes count: 0
Extracted edges count: 0

[FAILED] Entire Kotlin file was DROPPED (0 nodes, 0 edges)!
```

#### After Fix
```text
$ uv run python contribution-docs/reproduction-scripts/reproduce_issue_3884.py
============================================================
Issue #3884 Reproduction Results:
Extracted nodes count: 3
Extracted edges count: 2
  Node: repro (Repro.kt)
  Node: repro_repro (Repro)
  Node: volatile (Volatile)
  Edge: repro --contains--> repro_repro
  Edge: repro_repro --references--> volatile

[PASSED] Class extracted and annotation edge created cleanly.
```

title: fix(sql): walk block nodes so DDL before a DO block is extracted
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3886.

If a migration opens with a bare `BEGIN;` and later has a `DO $$ ... END $$;` block, tree-sitter-sql treats everything from that `BEGIN` up to the `END` of the DO body as a single `block` node. The top-level loop in `extract_sql` handled `statement` and `transaction` but not `block`, so every `CREATE TABLE` inside it got skipped without any error. That's why the reporter's schema only showed the tables that came after the DO block.

Here's the tree for the reduced repro:

```
block ['keyword_begin', ';', 'statement', ';', 'ERROR', 'keyword_end']
ERROR []
;
ERROR ['dollar_quote', ';', 'keyword_commit', ';']
```

The fix adds a `block` branch that walks the node, the same way `transaction` is already handled. `walk()` already recurses and `_add_node` dedupes by id, so nothing new is needed past the dispatch.

title: fix(extract): keep constructor calls that hit a same-file annotation stub
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3888.

If a class shows up in a type annotation (Python) or a generic argument (C#) earlier in a file, that reference creates a source-less stub with the class name. A later `Parser()` or `new Widget()` in the same file then finds the stub in the local lookup, gets treated as an external stub, and is dropped. It isn't emitted locally and it never reaches cross-file resolution either. That's where the constructor edges went missing after 0.9.62.

```python
from typing import Optional
from app.engines.transcript import Parser

class Engine:
    def detect(self): return Parser()          # no `calls` edge on 0.9.70
    def get_parser(self) -> Optional[Parser]: ...
```

The fix sends these calls to cross-file resolution too. That pass already refuses source-less targets (#3156), so the stub itself still can't turn into a calls hub.

Two guards go with it:

- **Evidence for rescued calls.** None of these calls produced an edge before, so a rescued call only binds when there's evidence for the target: an import of it, or for C# the namespace / `using` scope (through `CsharpNameResolver`, the same one the reference edges use). Otherwise a file that imports `com.lib.Client`, or has `using System.Collections.Generic`, would end up binding `new Client()` / `new List<int>()` to some unrelated class with the same name in the repo.
- **C# `new X()` never targets a member.** Object creations are tagged, and `case_of` / `defines` targets are dropped from their candidates. It's the same exclusion the C# type-definition index uses (#3815). This follows @JensD's suggestion in the issue. Without it, `new List<int>()` binds to an enum member called `List`.

## Type of change

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a constructor call to a project class keeps its `calls` edge whether or not the class was also used in an annotation, and a call that had no edge before only gains one when the target is backed by an import or by namespace scope.

title: fix(extract): parse only Astro frontmatter and scripts in the AST pass
body:
## What does this PR do?

`extract_astro` fed the whole `.astro` file to the JavaScript grammar. The template is not JS, so almost every page was reported as a syntax error ("first error at line 1/2 … no symbols extracted"). Symbols that tree-sitter could not recover past the template were dropped. Fixes #2788, and covers the "`.astro` script blocks are parsed unmasked" half of #3337. The `window`/`globalThis` half is not touched.

The AST pass now runs on a masked copy of the file, the same approach as `_vue_mask_non_script` and `_php_mask_to_script_blocks`:

- The frontmatter body and JS `<script>` bodies are kept verbatim. Every other character becomes a space, keeping `\r`/`\n`, so byte offsets and `source_location` still match the original file.
- The masked source is parsed with the TS grammar, which is Astro's default script language and a superset of JS, after `_normalize_ts_import_types`.
- `<script>` tags whose `type` is not JS are blanked too, because their bodies are not statements. That covers anything other than no type, `module`, `text/javascript` or `application/javascript`, for example `application/ld+json`.
- The character right after a kept region (the `<` of `</script>`) becomes `;`, so two scripts on one line don't merge into one statement. This doesn't change the length.

The existing regex import rescue (static and dynamic imports) is unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: every node extracted from a `.astro` file keeps a `source_location` that points at its line in the original file. The mask never inserts or removes characters, and the new test asserts `L5` and `L15` for a frontmatter function and a client-script function.

Persisted state: AST cache entries built before this change hold the old, poorer results for `.astro` files. They are keyed on file content, so they only refresh when a file changes or the cache is cleared.

Limitation: expressions inside the template (`{items.map(...)}`) are not parsed. They weren't meaningfully before either, since they sat inside the ERROR region. Imports inside them are still recovered by the regex pass.

title: fix(rust): resolve a forward-referenced type to its local declaration
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3782.

A Rust struct, enum or trait used above its declaration got a sourceless stub: `ensure_named_node` only resolves names already in `seen_ids`. `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` folds it back only for a corpus-unique label, so a same-named type in another file leaves the edge on the stub.

`extract_rust` now pre-scans the file's `struct_item`/`enum_item`/`trait_item` names before `walk()` (the Verilog, SQL and Bash pre-scan idiom), and `ensure_named_node` resolves against them.

- Only these three items are pre-registered: a `type` alias or `union` without an `impl` never becomes a node, so its references would be dropped as dangling.
- The scan never goes deeper than `walk()` (no function, static or const bodies), so every registered id becomes a node.
- Option 2 (the stub's `origin_file` in the rewire) would cover other extractors too; a natural `extract.py` follow-up.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a reference above a same-file struct, enum or trait, spelled the same and alone on its casefolded id, resolves like one below it; anything else keeps v8's per-file result.

Known limitation: resolution is flat per file and keeps only the last path segment, inheriting its errors: qualified paths (`io::Error`, `imp::Child`), `Self::X` without alias, generic parameters, `mod` scopes. On tokio 2 of 85 moved references are wrong (`imp::Child`); on 351 crates of a local cargo registry, roughly 85 of 2,279 (201 in the suspect classes). title: [Bug]: Wikilinks to note names that contain a dot ([[note.en]], [[v1.2 release]]) produce no references edge
body:
### What happened?

A wikilink whose target note name contains a dot is dropped: `[[note.en]]`, `[[v1.2 release]]`, `[[2026.09.27]]`, `[[Mr. Smith]]` and `[[sub/deep.fr|alias]]` produce no `references` edge, although `note.en.md` (etc.) exists and is a node in the graph.

Expected: the same edge an extension-less wikilink gets (`[[plain]]` -> `plain.md`). Dotted note names occur naturally: language suffixes, versions, dates, initials.

Cause: `_resolve_markdown_link` in `graphify/extractors/markdown.py` appends `.md` only when `Path(target).suffix == ""`. For `note.en` the suffix is `.en`, which is not in `_MD_LINKABLE_EXTS`, so the function returns `None` before the sibling or vault-wide lookup runs. Its docstring says extension-less wikilink targets are treated as sibling `.md`; a dotted note name never reaches that branch. An inline link with the full file name, `[x](./inline.en.md)` in the reproduction below, resolves fine.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p vault/notes/sub vault/other && cd vault
printf '# Hub\n\nSee [[note.en]], [[v1.2 release]], [[2026.09.27]], [[Mr. Smith]], [[plain]], [[sub/deep.fr|deep]].\nInline: [x](./inline.en.md)\n' > notes/hub.md
echo '# Note' > notes/note.en.md
echo '# Inline' > notes/inline.en.md
echo '# Deep' > notes/sub/deep.fr.md
echo '# Mr' > "notes/Mr. Smith.md"
echo '# Daily' > other/2026.09.27.md
echo '# Plain' > other/plain.md
echo '# Release' > "other/v1.2 release.md"
graphify update .
# then list the references edges of notes/hub.md in graphify-out/graph.json
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
notes/hub.md -> notes/inline.en.md
notes/hub.md -> other/plain.md
2 references edges; expected 7 (the five dotted wikilinks are missing)
```

### Graphify version

0.9.71 (v8 @ d6eaa8a); also on 0.9.70 (v8 @ 4c21b15)

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

AST-only path (`graphify update`), no API key involved. Reproduced on a clean checkout of v8.

### Additional context

On a real 3,300-note Obsidian vault, 1,523 of 12,329 wikilinks (12.4%) have a dotted target of this kind (mostly language-suffixed notes such as `name.en`), and the `<name>.md` note exists in every case. On Python 3.14, where `Path("Mr.").suffix == "."`, a trailing-dot link such as `[[Mr.]]` is lost the same way (it resolves on 3.12).

I have a small fix (for wikilinks only, retry `<name>.md` when that note exists, without overriding an indexable literal file beside the link, such as `pic.png` beside `pic.png.md`) and can open a PR.

title: fix(markdown): resolve wikilinks to note names that contain a dot (#3904)
body:
## What does this PR do?

<!-- Describe the problem and the change. Link the relevant issue when one exists. -->

Fixes #3904.

Wikilinks to note names containing a dot (`[[note.en]]`, `[[v1.2 release]]`, `[[Mr. Smith]]`) produced no `references` edge: `Path("note.en").suffix` is `.en`, so `_resolve_markdown_link` skipped the `.md` completion and returned `None`.

For wikilinks only, a target whose suffix is not a document extension is now retried as `<name>.md` through the existing sibling-then-vault resolution, and kept only when that document exists. A literal file beside the link whose type graphify indexes (`detect.classify_file`, whether or not `.graphifyignore` excludes it) keeps precedence: `[[pic.png]]` beside `pic.png` and `pic.png.md` still yields no edge. On Python 3.14, where `Path("Mr.").suffix == "."`, this also restores `[[Mr.]]`, which v8 drops there.

Note: #2949 edits the same `if suffix not in _MD_LINKABLE_EXTS:` line (code-file links); whichever lands second needs a rebase. An existing literal file beside the link keeps precedence in both.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

<!-- What invariant does this code protect? How do you prove your change doesn't break it? What generated or persisted state could your change invalidate? -->

Invariant: a dotted wikilink yields an edge only to an existing `<name>.md`, never in place of an indexable literal file beside the link; inline/reference links and document suffixes resolve as before.

- `test_markdown_wikilink_dotted_note_name`: sibling, vault-wide, path-qualified with alias. Fails on v8.
- `test_markdown_dotted_link_without_note_stays_skipped`: `[[missing.en]]`, `[[image.png]]`, inline `[note](note.en)` give no edge; red without the existence check or the wikilink-only condition.
- `test_markdown_dotted_wikilink_literal_file_keeps_precedence`: `pic.png` + `pic.png.md` give no edge; a raw `thirteen.en` + `thirteen.en.md` give the note. Fails without the precedence check, and on v8.

Persisted state: the AST cache is namespaced by package version (`graphify/cache.py`), so a release re-extracts markdown. Incremental `graphify update` picks up dotted targets created after the first build and drops deleted ones.

New filesystem access: `is_file()` on the literal and on `<name>.md`; for a literal `.html`/`.yaml`/`.yml`/`.skill`, `classify_file` reads the file (its paper check), uncached, although that branch never returns None; plus the existing once-per-run vault index when the sibling misses, which a vault of dotted wikilinks only did not build on v8 (that index honours `.graphifyignore` since #3822).

Known limitation: the literal-file check looks beside the link only, so `[[pic.png]]` written in another folder than `pic.png` + `pic.png.md` resolves to the note. `[[notes.txt]]` meaning `notes.txt.md` resolves from the same folder (its path id coincides with the note's) but not from another folder, on v8 as here. A natural follow-up would be the same `<name>.md` fallback for document suffixes whose literal file is missing.

title: fix(solidity): extract file-level free functions and their calls
body:
## What does this PR do?

File-level **free functions** have been valid Solidity since 0.7 (used heavily for pure utility helpers), but the extractor only descended into named type declarations — `contract`, `library`, `interface`, `abstract contract`. Any `function` declared directly at source-unit scope, **and every call made from its body**, was dropped entirely. A file made only of free functions produced *no nodes at all*, so its whole call subgraph was invisible.

```solidity
function halve(uint x)   pure returns (uint) { return x / 2; }
function quarter(uint x) pure returns (uint) { return halve(halve(x)); }
```
Before: 0 function nodes, 0 edges. After: both functions extracted and `quarter → halve` linked.

The fix walks source-unit `function_definition` nodes, emits each as a file-contained callable node, and resolves an unambiguous same-file free-function call to a `calls` edge.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant protected: **extraction completeness** — a valid, source-backed declaration must not silently vanish. The fix stays **fail-closed**: a member call (`Lib.f()`) is parked as a `raw_call` for cross-file resolution rather than guessed, and calls that would cross into contract scope are left unresolved rather than mis-linked. Node ids are derived from `stem + kind + name + arity:signature`, so they are deterministic and stable across rebuilds (no filesystem/line-number dependence).

The Blade extractor recognised `@include`, `<livewire:>` components, and `wire:click` bindings — but not `@extends`. title: fix(vbnet): resolve type/module-qualified calls to their target method
body:
## What does this PR do?

The VB.NET invocation resolver only fired for **self / unqualified** receivers — `Me`, `MyClass`, the enclosing type, or a bare name. A call *qualified by a type or module name* matched nothing and produced no edge at all:

```vbnet
Namespace Demo
  Public Module Helpers
    Public Sub Log()
    End Sub
  End Module
  Public Class Service
    Public Sub Run()
      Helpers.Log()      ' <- dropped: no calls edge to Helpers.Log
    End Sub
  End Class
End Namespace
```

Calling a shared `Module` `Sub` via `Helpers.Log()` is idiomatic VB.NET, so the graph was missing a whole class of real call edges, leaving callers disconnected from the module methods they invoke.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant protected: **extraction completeness without guessed relationships**. I map each declared type/module's short name to its `owner_key`, then resolve a qualified call against the *receiver's* owner (the map that already keys same-type methods), falling back to the existing `raw_calls` mechanism for cross-file partial-type merging. The resolver stays **fail-closed**:

- A call through a **value receiver** (a local variable, e.g. `obj.Save()`) has no statically known owner and is left unresolved — never guessed into a false edge (covered by a dedicated test).
- Cross-file resolution keeps its existing "exactly one candidate" guard, so no ambiguous edge is emitted.

Self/unqualified resolution is unchanged. Node ids and ownership keys are derived from names (no filesystem/ordering dependence), so extraction stays deterministic.

title: [Bug]: a virtual-workspace-root Cargo.toml is re-reported as "produced zero nodes" and re-extracted on every run
body:
## Symptom

In a **virtual** Cargo workspace — root `Cargo.toml` declares `[workspace]` members and no `[package]` — every `graphify update .` prints this pair, verbatim, forever:

```
  AST extraction: 1/1 uncached files (100%)
  warning: 1 source file(s) produced zero nodes and are absent from the graph: Cargo.toml. A re-run will retry them (empties are no longer cached); if it persists, please report the file(s) (#1666).
```

A second run prints the same two lines. In a fresh corpus the file is not recorded in `manifest.json` at all, while the crate manifests are:

```
$ python3 -c "import json;m=json.load(open('graphify-out/manifest.json'));[print(repr(k),repr(v['ast_hash'])) for k,v in m.items()]"
'crates/a/Cargo.toml' 'e5669eadddf158022994cfc50f79ec52'
'crates/a/src/lib.rs' 'ba96bc9d26fd26c2697e47c67e3d3c65'
```

In a corpus that has been through older versions the entry survives as the one and only un-hashed entry — measured on a 12-crate workspace:

```
$ python3 -c "import json;m=json.load(open('graphify-out/manifest.json'));print([k for k,v in m.items() if not v.get('ast_hash')])"
['Cargo.toml']
```

## The empty result is intentional

`manifest_ingest.py::_parse_cargo` emits nothing for a virtual workspace root, on purpose:

> A virtual workspace root (`[workspace]`, no `[package]`) declares no package of its own — emit nothing rather than a fabricated node.

So the ingest is right and the *reporting* is what collides:

1. A file that is empty-by-design is indistinguishable from a file whose extraction silently failed, so the #1666 bucket can never be empty. That bucket is the only place a genuinely dropped file would surface — a permanent, unsolvable entry in it teaches the reader to skip the line, which is the opposite of what it is for.
2. "empties are no longer cached" (post-#2543/#3679) turns that into permanent work: the file is re-detected and re-extracted on every single run and never reaches a cached state, so `AST extraction: N/N uncached files (100%)` is the steady state in any workspace of this shape.

## Minimal repro (0.9.67, Python 3.14, Linux)

```
$ mkdir -p m/crates/a/src && cd m
$ printf '[workspace]\nmembers = ["crates/a"]\nresolver = "2"\n'        > Cargo.toml
$ printf '[package]\nname = "a"\nversion = "0.1.0"\nedition = "2021"\n' > crates/a/Cargo.toml
$ printf 'pub fn f() -> u32 { 1 }\n'                                    > crates/a/src/lib.rs
$ graphify update .
  AST extraction: 1/1 uncached files (100%)
  warning: 1 source file(s) produced zero nodes and are absent from the graph: Cargo.toml. ...
[graphify watch] Rebuilt: 3 nodes, 1 edges, 2 communities

$ graphify update .   # and again, and again
  AST extraction: 1/1 uncached files (100%)
  warning: 1 source file(s) produced zero nodes and are absent from the graph: Cargo.toml. ...
```

## Measured on a real repo

`tessella` (Rust, 12-crate workspace, 0.9.67): 3771 nodes / 9096 links (`links`, not `edges`).

- No node in `graph.json` has `source_file == "Cargo.toml"`. The 12 `crates/*/Cargo.toml` files each contribute exactly 1 package node, and all 28 `depends_on` links come from them. Net value of the root manifest in the graph: **0 nodes, 0 links**.
- The single un-hashed `manifest.json` entry in the whole corpus is that file (see above), in this workspace and in a second workspace of the same shape (`musivum`).

## Workaround we are shipping

A `.graphifyignore` entry `/Cargo.toml`, which removes the permanent warning and the permanent re-extraction at a measured cost of 0 nodes / 0 links (verified by diffing `graph.json` before/after — the only change is that the warning disappears). We would rather delete that line when this is fixed.

## Ask

- Suppress the zero-node warning for paths that `is_package_manifest_path()` recognises *and* that the ingest deliberately leaves empty — `manifest_ingest` knows the difference; the warning path does not.
- Or split the bucket into "no extractable content (by design)" vs "extraction produced nothing (suspect)" and cache the former so it is not re-extracted every run.
- Either way, `AST extraction: N/N uncached files (100%)` should not be the permanent steady state for a repo that is fully extracted.

title: [Bug]: .cu/.cuh: CUDA kernel files trip the syntax-error warning on file-scope macro invocations, and macro-defined kernel bodies are never extracted
body:
## Symptom

`.cu` / `.cuh` sit in the `native` family next to `.cpp`/`.metal` and are extracted with `extract_cpp` (`extract.py`: `".cu": "native", ".cuh": "native"` in the extension-family table, `".cu": extract_cpp, ".cuh": extract_cpp` in the extension→extractor table), so the standard shape of a hand-written CUDA kernel file — file-scope invocations of a macro, with the kernel body living inside the macro definition — lands in the syntax-error bucket:

```
  warning: 10 file(s) had syntax errors and may be partially extracted: crates/candle-kernels/src/affine.cu (first error at line 32, no symbols extracted), crates/candle-kernels/src/binary.cu (first error at line 1, no symbols extracted), crates/candle-kernels/src/cast.cu (first error at line 5, 5 symbol(s) extracted), crates/candle-kernels/src/conv.cu (first error at line 6, 12 symbol(s) extracted), crates/candle-kernels/src/fill.cu (first error at line 5, 14 symbol(s) extracted) (+5 more)
```

## What the trigger actually is (reduced)

A file-scope macro invocation is not a valid C++ statement, and that is the whole trigger:

```
$ cat a_invoke_only.cu
OP(float, k_f32)
$ cat b_macro_def.cu
#define OP(T, NAME) extern "C" __global__ void NAME(const T* in) {}
OP(float, k_f32)
$ cat c_arch_guard.cu
#define OP(T, NAME) extern "C" __global__ void NAME(const T* in) {}
#if __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 800
OP(float, k_f32)
#endif
$ cat d_launch.cu
void run(float* d) { my_kernel<<<1, 256>>>(d); }

$ graphify update .
  warning: 3 file(s) had syntax errors and may be partially extracted: a_invoke_only.cu (first error at line 1, no symbols extracted), b_macro_def.cu (first error at line 2, no symbols extracted), c_arch_guard.cu (first error at line 3, no symbols extracted)
[graphify watch] Rebuilt: 5 nodes, 1 edges, 4 communities
```

- `d_launch.cu` — `<<<1, 256>>>` launch syntax plus a `__global__`-kernel call — parses **cleanly** and yields `run()`. The launch syntax is not the trigger.
- `c_arch_guard.cu` — the `#if __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 800` guard is not the trigger either; the reported line is the invocation.

Also reduced separately: `.cuh` files that contain only `#define`s yield their file node and nothing else.

## Impact, measured on a real repo

`tessella/crates/candle-kernels/src` — 14 files (11 `.cu`, 3 `.cuh`), 0.9.67: they contribute **273 nodes and 812 links**, so the warning overstates the damage — 10 of the 14 do yield symbols:

```
quantized.cu 186   cuda_utils.cuh 24   reduce.cu 13   conv.cu 11   fill.cu 10
unary.cu 8         compatibility.cuh 6 indexing.cu 5  cast.cu 3    sort.cu 3
```

(The 259 symbol nodes above come from those 10 files; the remaining 4 files contribute their file node and nothing else, so they are the only real losses — and the second item is the one that matters.)

- `affine.cu` (7 file-scope invocations), `binary.cu` (84), `ternary.cu` (21) — the invocation is the only content, so 112 kernel names exist in the sources and none of them is a node.
- `binary_op_macros.cuh` — the file that *defines* `BINARY_OP` / `BINARY_OP_OUT`, i.e. where a large part of the kernels' bodies actually live. No C++ AST walk can see a body inside a `#define`, so the graph cannot answer "what does `badd_bf16` call" or "which kernel lists exist".

So a repo asking GPU-path questions reads the syntax-error line as "these files are missing", when the truth is "these files are present, 10 of them are extracted, and the kernel bodies defined through macros are outside the AST".

## Ask

1. Do not report the CUDA macro-invocation idiom as a *syntax error*: either treat `.cu`/`.cuh` as a language with its own handling (at minimum stop counting file-scope macro invocations as parse failures), or put the truth in the warning ("no symbols extracted; the file may define its kernels through macros").
2. Consider extracting file-scope macro invocations as symbol evidence — `BINARY_OP(__nv_bfloat16, badd_bf16, x + y)` names a kernel that exists in the compiled artifact, and for many of these names it is the only place the name appears.
3. Minor and unreduced: `binary.cu` reports `first error at line 1` while its first invocation is at line 5 (our other files report the correct line — `i_nospace_include.cu` 4, `j_many_invokes.cu` 5, `k_cmp_arg.cu` 2). Flagging it in case it points at something in error recovery.

title: [Feature]: acknowledging an expected warning per path — .graphifyignore is the only lever today and it deletes that file nodes and links (273/812 measured)
body:
## Symptom

The only supported way to silence a per-file warning is an entry in `.graphifyignore`, and an ignore entry removes the file from the corpus — so **every node and link that file produced disappears from `graph.json`**. For a file that is extracted mostly correctly and merely trips the warning, that is a strictly worse outcome than the warning itself:

```
  warning: 10 file(s) had syntax errors and may be partially extracted: crates/candle-kernels/src/affine.cu (first error at line 32, no symbols extracted), ... crates/candle-kernels/src/conv.cu (first error at line 6, 12 symbol(s) extracted), crates/candle-kernels/src/fill.cu (first error at line 5, 14 symbol(s) extracted) (+5 more)
```

`conv.cu` yields 12 symbols. Silencing the line for it costs those 12 nodes, and there is no syntax that removes the message while keeping the extraction.

## Minimal repro (no CUDA involved)

```
$ cat src/macros.h
#define MAKE_KERNEL(TYPE, NAME, EXPR) \
    void NAME(TYPE x) {               \
        (void)(EXPR);                 \
    }

$ cat src/code.cpp
#include "macros.h"

MAKE_KERNEL(int, add_i32, x + 1)
MAKE_KERNEL(float, add_f32, x + 1.0f)

int kept_function(int a) { return a + 1; }

$ graphify update .
  warning: 1 file(s) had syntax errors and may be partially extracted: src/code.cpp (first error at line 3, 1 symbol(s) extracted)
[graphify watch] Rebuilt: 3 nodes, 2 edges, 1 communities
```

`extract_cpp` returns `nodes = [code.cpp, kept_function()]` with `parse_errors = {"first_error_line": 3, "multiline_error": true}`. The file is not a loss: this is the #2551 gate firing because a file-scope macro invocation dissolved into a multi-line ERROR region. Adding `src/code.cpp` to `.graphifyignore` to clean the log would delete `kept_function()` as well.

## Measured cost of the ignore entry (real repo)

In `crates/candle-kernels/src` the same trade-off is 14 CUDA files contributing **273 nodes and 812 links** (0.9.67). The warning names 10 of them; 7 extract between 4 and 15 symbols each (`cast.cu` 5, `conv.cu` 12, `fill.cu` 14, `indexing.cu` 7, `reduce.cu` 15, `sort.cu` 4, `unary.cu` 9). Verified by diffing the canonical node and link sets of `graph.json` before/after adding the ignore entry: the sets differ by exactly those 273 nodes and 812 links, so the only lever available today deletes real data. A `#` comment above the entry helps the next human reading the file; it does not help the CI log, and it does not exist for the reader who never opens `.graphifyignore`.

Related: #3911 (the CUDA-specific report: why these files trip the warning at all).

## Ask

A way to acknowledge expected noise for a path **without** removing it from the corpus. Any of these shapes would work:

1. A CLI flag — `--warn-level` / `--no-syntax-warnings` / `--quiet-warnings` — leaving the counts reachable via `--verbose`.
2. A per-path allowlist: a `.graphifyallow` file, or a directive inside `.graphifyignore` (e.g. `!warnings-ok: path/*` or `hide-warn: path`) that mutes the log line for those files while they keep being extracted.
3. A configuration key (e.g. `[warnings] syntax_errors = "mute:path/*"`), whatever fits the existing configuration model.

For our repo the difference is binary: with a suppression that keeps the files, the log is clean **and** the graph keeps the GPU execution path; without one, we have to choose between a perma-noisy log and 273 missing nodes.

Happy to test a build or open a PR if you point at the intended shape.

title: [Bug]: path resolves an ambiguous endpoint to one node without refusing; <file>::<symbol> and node id do not select the node asked for
body:
### What happened?

`graphify path` does not refuse an ambiguous endpoint the way `explain` does, and the two other ways to disambiguate (`<file>::<symbol>` and the full node id) do not select the node asked for.

1. **Bare ambiguous label:** `path` resolves it to one candidate and prints a confident route, exit 0. The tied-score warning goes to stderr and names no candidates; `explain` on the same label lists both ids.
2. **`<file>::<symbol>`:** `explain` tells the user to "Retry with path::symbol", but `path` resolves `src/b.ts::.nonce()` to the *file* node `b.ts`, not the method.
3. **Full node id:** the route ends at the containing class (`BetaClient`), not at the method node given.

Expected: an ambiguous endpoint is refused with the candidate ids (as `explain` does), and the `path::symbol` form and node id resolve to the node named, so the route ends there.

Related: #1969 (`explain` silently resolving ambiguity, where it notes `path` warns). This is the other half: the warning `path` emits is not a refusal.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p src
cat > src/a.ts <<'X'
export class AlphaClient { nonce() { return 1 } }
X
cat > src/b.ts <<'X'
export class BetaClient { nonce() { return 2 } }
X
cat > src/main.ts <<'X'
import { AlphaClient } from './a'
import { BetaClient } from './b'
export function run() { new AlphaClient(); new BetaClient() }
X
graphify extract . --code-only --force && graphify cluster-only . --no-label

graphify path "run()" ".nonce()"                          # 1
graphify explain ".nonce()"                               # for comparison
graphify path "run()" "src/b.ts::.nonce()" --undirected   # 2
graphify path "run()" src_b_betaclient_nonce              # 3
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
# 1  (exit 0; the warning is on stderr)
warning: target match was ambiguous (top score 12994.1, runner-up 12994.1)
Shortest path (2 hops):
  run() --calls [EXTRACTED]--> AlphaClient --method [EXTRACTED]--> .nonce()

# explain, same label
Ambiguous: '.nonce()' matches 2 nodes in different files.
  src/a.ts   id: src_a_alphaclient_nonce
  src/b.ts   id: src_b_betaclient_nonce
Retry with path::symbol using one of the paths above (e.g. <path>::.nonce()) or the full node id.

# 2  (without --undirected: "No directed path found")
Shortest path (2 hops):
  run() --calls [EXTRACTED]--> BetaClient <--contains [EXTRACTED]-- b.ts

# 3
Shortest path (1 hops):
  run() --calls [EXTRACTED]--> BetaClient
```

Found on real repos where this matters (a method name defined on two classes in different files; one repo has six `.cleanup()` nodes): the confident route through the wrong candidate is what a script or agent reads.

### Graphify version

0.9.64

### Additional Environment Details

macOS 26.6, Python 3.14.2 (not in the dropdown, so I picked 3.13), run via `uvx --from graphifyy==0.9.64`. Clean checkout of the repro above; the environment was stripped with `env -i` (no provider variables set).

title: Node Info panel shows "Type: unknown" / "Source: -" for every node (field name mismatch in generated graph.html)
body:
## Bug: Node Info panel shows `Type: unknown` and `Source: -` for every node (field name mismatch in generated `graph.html`) ### Summary In the generated `graph.html` visualization, clicking any node shows a **Node Info** panel where `Type` is always `unknown` and `Source` is always `-`, even though the underlying `graph.json` has correct `file_type` and `source_file` values for every node. Root cause: the Node Info click handler reads node fields with a **leading underscore** (`n._file_type`, `n._source_file`, `n._community_name`, `n._degree`), but the node objects embedded in the HTML (and in `graph.json`) use the **non-underscore** keys (`file_type`, `source_file`, `community_name`, `degree`). ### Version - `graphifyy` **0.9.71** (installed via `uvx --from graphifyy graphify`) ### Evidence **Generated `graph.html` — Node Info handler (reads `_`-prefixed keys):** ```js document.getElementById('info-content').innerHTML = `
${esc(n.label)}
Type: ${esc(n._file_type || 'unknown')}
Community: ${esc(n._community_name)}
Source: ${esc(n._source_file || '-')}
Degree: ${n._degree}
``` **The embedded node data in the same `graph.html` (and in `graph.json`) uses non-underscore keys.** Counting occurrences in the generated HTML: ``` 502 "community_name": 502 "degree": 502 "file_type": 502 "source_file": ``` (zero occurrences of `_file_type` / `_source_file` / `_community_name` / `_degree` in the data.) **A sample node object (`graph.json`):** ```json { "id": "packages_app_src_leaddetailview", "label": "LeadDetailView.tsx", "community_name": "LeadDetailView.tsx", "file_type": "code", "source_file": "packages/app/src/LeadDetailView.tsx", "source_location": "L1" } ``` Keys present: `id, label, _origin, community, community_name, file_type, norm_label, source_file, source_location`. There is **no** `_file_type`, `_source_file`, `_community_name`, or `_degree`. ### Impact - Every node's Node Info shows `Type: unknown` and `Source: -`, making the panel effectively useless for identifying what a node is or where it lives — which is one of the main navigation affordances of the HTML export. - Affects all languages/repos, since it's purely a field-name mismatch in the generator. ### Expected Node Info should read the same keys that are emitted into the node objects, e.g.: ```js
Type: ${esc(n.file_type || 'unknown')}
Community: ${esc(n.community_name)}
Source: ${esc(n.source_file || '-')}
Degree: ${n.degree}
``` ### Suggested fix In the HTML generator template, drop the leading underscore from the four Node Info fields (`_file_type` → `file_type`, `_source_file` → `source_file`, `_community_name` → `community_name`, `_degree` → `degree`) — or, conversely, emit the node objects with underscore-prefixed keys. The two sides just need to agree; the non-underscore form matches `graph.json`, so aligning the handler to the data is the smaller change. ### Notes - `Community` may appear correct in some builds via the vis.js tooltip/title, but the click-panel handler is still inconsistent with the emitted data. - Happy to send a PR aligning the handler to the non-underscore keys if useful.

title: fix(kotlin): keep annotated inferred properties in the graph
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3884.

A Kotlin class property that has an annotation and no explicit type crashes the extractor, and `_safe_extract` then drops the entire file from the graph. The reported case is:

```kotlin
class Repro {
    @Volatile
    var counter = 0

    fun ping() { }
}
```

`graphify update` prints one warning and keeps going:

```text
warning: skipped Repro.kt (UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'line' where it is not associated with a value)
```

The class, the property, `ping()`, and every other symbol in that file are absent (0 nodes, 0 edges). A second `graphify update` does not repeat the warning, because the failure is recorded on `failed_sources` and the empty result is what the incremental path sees. In the report's Android project this removed 4 of 70 Kotlin files, including the whole Android layer, while the rest of the graph looked fine.

### Cause

In the Kotlin `property_declaration` handler, `line = node.start_point[0] + 1` was assigned only inside `if type_node is not None`. The annotation loop below that branch always reads `line`.

`_kotlin_property_type_node` looks for a `user_type` / `nullable_type` / `type_reference`. `@Volatile var counter = 0` has none: the type is inferred from `0`. So `line` is never bound, the annotation loop raises `UnboundLocalError`, and `_safe_extract` returns an empty result for the file.

### Change

Assign `line` once, before the type-node check, still inside `if parent_class_nid`. That is the same expression the explicit-type path already used. The type-reference walk and the initializer seeding are unchanged.

After the fix the file stays in the graph, `ping()` is still a method of `Repro`, and `@Volatile` is a `references` edge with `context="attribute"`, which is what an annotated property with an explicit type already produced.

### What this does not change

- A property with an explicit type (`@Volatile var counter: Int = 0`) still emits the same attribute edge. `line` is still the property node's start line.
- A property with no annotation never entered the loop, so it still emits no annotation edge.
- Top-level properties stay class-gated. The annotation loop is still inside `if parent_class_nid`, so a file-level `@Volatile val counter = 0` still does not get a `references` edge, and it never hit this crash.
- Use-site targets (`@field:Volatile`, `@get:JvmName("count")`) and argument forms (`@Suppress("NAME")`) already had their names parsed by `_kotlin_annotation_names`. An inferred-type property with one of those used to drop the file; it now gets the same attribute edge. The use-site keyword itself is not turned into a node.
- Primary-constructor parameters are a different path and are not touched. `class Repro(@Volatile var inferred = 0)` does not parse as a `class_parameter` in tree-sitter-kotlin (the parameter is an `ERROR` node). That is a pre-existing grammar miss, not this bug.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: an extractor exception on one declaration must not discard the rest of the file, and an annotation on an inferred-type property must be recorded the same way as an annotation on an explicit type.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

`test_kotlin_annotated_inferred_property_keeps_the_file` fails on the parent commit: `failed_sources == ['Repro.kt']` and stderr reports the `UnboundLocalError`. With this commit it requires the file to be extracted, the sibling `ping()` method edge to survive, and a `Repro` → `Volatile` `references` edge with `context="attribute"`. The explicit-type control passes on both the parent and this commit.

No persisted graph or cache format changes. AST extraction stays deterministic. No skill fragments were edited, so skillgen was not regenerated.

## How was this tested?

Windows, Python 3.12, branch `fix/3884-kotlin-annotated-property` based on `v8` @ `d6eaa8a` (0.9.71).

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_kotlin_grammar.py::test_kotlin_annotated_inferred_property_keeps_the_file tests/test_kotlin_grammar.py::test_kotlin_annotated_explicit_type_property_still_references -q
# before the hoist: 1 failed (failed_sources == ['Repro.kt']), 1 passed
# after the hoist: 2 passed

uv run pytest tests/test_kotlin_grammar.py -q
# 25 passed

uv run ruff check graphify/extractors/engine.py tests/test_kotlin_grammar.py
# All checks passed

uv run pre-commit run --files graphify/extractors/engine.py tests/test_kotlin_grammar.py
# skillgen --check passed
# ruff passed

uv run pytest tests/ -q --tb=line
# 5913 passed, 115 skipped, 47 failed
```

The 47 full-suite failures are from this Windows environment, not from the Kotlin change. They are missing optional extractors (`tree-sitter-language-pack`, solidity, vb-dotnet), POSIX-only APIs (`os.mkfifo`, `socket.AF_UNIX`), path-separator and console-encoding checks, a file lock on a deleted cwd, and `openai` not installed. None are in `tests/test_kotlin_grammar.py`.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. Not applicable: no skill fragment changed. `skillgen --check` passed.
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

title: fix(cuda): normalize CUDA syntax and recover macro-generated kernels (#3911)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3911 by adding CUDA-aware normalization and recovery for kernel functions declared through macros.

CUDA kernel macros such as:

```cpp
#define AFFINE_KERNEL(NAME, TYPE) \
    __global__ void NAME##_##TYPE() {}

AFFINE_KERNEL(foo, float);
```

could cause Tree-sitter to report false C++ syntax errors because the preprocessor-level macro invocation is not directly represented as a valid C++ AST construct.

This change normalizes those invocations before parsing while recovering the generated kernel nodes from the original source.

## What changed

* Added CUDA source normalization for:

  * CUDA qualifiers
  * kernel launch configurations (`<<<...>>>`)
  * recognized CUDA kernel macro invocations
* Added balanced CUDA macro argument parsing supporting nested `()`, `[]`, and `{}`.
* Added token-pasting resolution for generated kernel names such as `NAME##_##TYPE`.
* Added macro-generated kernel node and `contains` edge recovery.
* Preserved original byte offsets and line positions during normalization.
* Added non-code span detection so macros inside:

  * multiline block comments
  * single-line block comments
  * `//` comments
  * string literals
  * character literals
    are ignored.
* Preserved genuine C++ syntax errors instead of suppressing them.
* Added deduplication against kernels already discovered through AST extraction.

## Tests

Added comprehensive CUDA regression coverage for:

* Typed CUDA kernel macros
* Token pasting
* Multiline macro definitions/invocations
* Nested macro arguments
* CRLF/LF preservation
* Comments and string literals
* Commented-out macro definitions
* Ordinary non-CUDA macros
* AST + macro deduplication
* Malformed macro invocations
* Genuine syntax-error retention
* Multiple kernel macro invocations

### Verification

* **101 tests passed, 0 failed**
* CUDA regression suite: **32 passed**
* C++/CLI & nested extraction: **23 passed**
* Parse-warning tests: **10 passed**
* Extract CLI: **34 passed**
* Extractor registry: **2 passed**
* `git diff --cached --check`: **clean**
* `python -m graphify update .`: **successful**

The change is scoped to CUDA extraction/normalization and its regression tests.

title: MCP server: silent wrong matches on ambiguous/near-miss names, noisy query_graph, misleading list_prs error
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.71 (installed via `uv tool`), `graphify-mcp` over stdio, started with an explicit `graph.json` path.
**Codebase:** PHP / Symfony bundle, ~11k nodes / ~33k edges, 614 communities.

## 1. `get_node` silently picks one match for an ambiguous name

- **Steps:** `get_node(label="edit")` on a graph where several classes define `edit()`.
- **Actual:** returns a single node (`Controller/VisitController.php L427`) with no hint that other candidates exist.
- **Expected:** a list of the candidates (path + line), or an explicit "ambiguous, N matches" error. The caller can't tell whether the answer is the right `edit()`.

## 2. `get_node` silently resolves a non-existent name to a different node

- **Steps:** `get_node(label="MailController")` when no `MailController` exists in the codebase.
- **Actual:** returns `EmailController` as if it were an exact match.
- **Expected:** "no exact match", optionally followed by fuzzy suggestions clearly labelled as such.

Side note: the `path::symbol` form works (`Controller/VisitController.php::edit` → found). `get_node(node_id=...)` does not find a generated-looking id for a non-existent symbol, which is correct.

## 3. `query_graph` is dominated by god nodes

- **Steps:** `query_graph(question="who sends the convocation emails?")`, default depth 3.
- **Actual:** BFS starts from 5 seeds and reaches 2,708 nodes. The output is TRUNCATED and mostly made of the highest-degree nodes (framework interfaces, core entities, enums). With `token_budget=8000` it is still truncated (240 of 2,708). With `context_filter=['call']` only 20 nodes remain, all unrelated test helpers.
- **Expected:** rank results by relevance or distance to the seeds rather than degree, or damp hubs during traversal (similar to `exclude_hubs_percentile` in `god_nodes`).

## 4. `get_community` returns no community label

`get_community(3)` returns "Community 3 (205 nodes)" with no name or summary. A generated label (e.g. dominant class or directory) would make the output usable.

## 5. `list_prs` reports "gh CLI not found" when the real issue is repo detection

- **Steps:** `list_prs()` with no `repo` argument, the server started on a `graph.json` outside any git repo.
- **Actual:** `Error: gh CLI not found or not authenticated. Run: gh auth login`. gh is installed and authenticated. Passing `repo=owner/name` makes it work. `get_pr_impact` with the same `repo` works too.
- **Expected:** an error such as "could not detect repository; pass `repo=`".

## 6. Minor: `get_neighbors` truncation hides incoming edges

With the default budget, outgoing edges are listed first, so all incoming edges (callers) are cut off on high-degree nodes. Listing incoming edges first, or balancing both directions, would help.

title: fix(hooks): refuse a core.hooksPath that leaves the repository
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3869.

`graphify hook install` asks git for the hooks directory via `git rev-parse --git-path hooks`. That follows `core.hooksPath`. If the value is an absolute path, or a relative path that resolves outside the checkout, install created that directory and wrote `post-commit` and `post-checkout` there, mode `0755`. `hook status` created the directory too.

I checked this on a temporary repo before the fix. Both an absolute path and a `../` path received those two files outside the tree. A normal `git clone` did not copy `core.hooksPath`. The report's snippet (`git config core.hooksPath` around the old line numbers) is stale. The current code is `_hooks_dir`.

The files written are Graphify's own hook script. `viz_node_limit` from `.graphifyrc` is parsed as an integer before it is embedded, so the repository does not choose the script body. Git already runs whatever is configured at `core.hooksPath` on commit. This bug is the extra write. It is not repository-chosen code execution, and the CVSS 8.5 score on the issue does not fit. I said that on the issue.

### Change

A resolved hooks path is accepted only when it is inside the repository (so `.husky` and a normal `.git/hooks` still work) or when it is exactly git's own hooks directory. The second case matters for a linked worktree: with `core.hooksPath` unset, `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` points at the main repo's `.git/hooks`, which is outside the worktree root.

Anything else is refused, with a stderr line, and install uses `<common-git-dir>/hooks` instead. The outside directory is not created.

Clearing the setting with `git -c core.hooksPath=` is not used. An empty value makes `--git-path hooks` print `./`.

### Limitation

A `core.hooksPath` that someone set on purpose to a shared directory outside the repo is no longer honored. Install goes to the default git hooks directory and says so. In-repo paths are unchanged.

title: feat(extract): InterSystems ObjectScript extractor (.cls/.mac/.inc/.rtn)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an AST extractor for **InterSystems ObjectScript** (`.cls` UDL classes, `.mac`/`.rtn` routines, `.inc` macro includes) behind a new optional extra `objectscript`, using `tree-sitter-objectscript` (InterSystems' own grammar; abi3 wheels for macOS/Linux/Windows, no C toolchain). Today `.cls` files are parsed as Salesforce Apex and routines are skipped.

**Routing.** `.cls` is already Apex and `.inc` is already Pascal, so both keep their suffix defaults and are *content-routed* in `_get_extractor`, following the existing `.h`/`.m` pattern: a cheap byte scan (`_is_objectscript_class` / `_is_objectscript_include`, first 256 KB, grammar-free) reroutes only files that positively look like ObjectScript (line-leading `Class Pkg.Name`; `#define`/`$$$`/`$Func(`/`##class(`/`%RO` export header). A C-style `.inc` header guard stays on Pascal. `.mac`/`.rtn` are plain dispatch entries. `.int` (compiler output that duplicates every `.mac`/`.cls` symbol) is deliberately not dispatched.

**What the graph gets.** Classes (short-name label, full dotted name in `metadata.full_name`), methods/classmethods, properties, parameters, XData, indices, foreign keys, relationships, queries, triggers; `Extends` → `inherits`; typed `references` (`field`/`parameter_type`/`return_type`/`type`); `Include`/`#include` → `includes`; macros (`$$$NAME`) and routine labels as callable nodes. Body pass: `..M()`, `##class(X).M()` (→ `references` + cross-file `calls`), `%New` → `instantiates`, `$$L^R` / `Do L^R` / `Goto` → routine calls, `$$$MACRO` → `uses`, `$ClassMethod("X","M")` → INFERRED. XData attribute references (`targetClass=`, `ClassName=` …) are **INFERRED only**.

**Cross-file resolution.** Every ObjectScript raw call is tagged `language="objectscript"` and `is_qualified_call=True` (it names its own target scope), and the shared bare-name pass skips qualified calls next to its existing `is_member_call`/`is_mixin` skips, so it never binds them; the registered `objectscript_calls` language resolver retargets external-class/include stubs onto unique definitions and resolves qualified calls (EXTRACTED), inherited/`##super()` calls (INFERRED) and macro uses. No `_LANG_FAMILY_BY_EXT` entries were added on purpose: the suffix-keyed family tables cannot express the shared `.cls`/`.inc`, and a partial entry would drop legitimate cross-suffix edges (see "Limitations").

Related: the grammar's own `tree-sitter` pin is stale (ABI 15 needs ≥0.25), reported upstream as intersystems/tree-sitter-objectscript#56; the extra therefore pins `tree-sitter>=0.25` explicitly.

## Type of change

- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariants protected and how they are proven:
- **Existing Apex and Pascal corpora are unchanged.** `tests/fixtures/sample.cls`/`sample.trigger` still route to `extract_apex`; a Pascal `.inc` and a C-style `.inc` still route to `extract_pascal` (`test_get_extractor_keeps_apex_and_pascal`, `test_is_objectscript_include_rejects_plain_c_header`, `test_apex_and_pascal_end_to_end_unchanged`, plus the existing Apex/Pascal suites).
- **Provenance.** XData/string-derived references are never EXTRACTED; cross-file `calls` are EXTRACTED only with qualified evidence; stubs carry `source_file: ""` and the full dotted label so `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` can never mis-merge `%Persistent` onto a user `Persistent` (`test_objectscript_xdata_reference_is_inferred_not_extracted`, `test_objectscript_cross_file_end_to_end`, `test_objectscript_resolver_prefers_extracted_over_inferred_call`).
- **Determinism / robustness.** Child iteration order only, no environment reads; explicit-stack body walk; ERROR nodes traversed; empty files, garbage, 1 MB+ XData handled (`test_objectscript_strings_and_garbage_do_not_create_phantoms`, `test_objectscript_pound_if_expression_body_is_not_dropped`).
- **Persisted state invalidated.** `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 4 → 5, because `.cls`/`.inc` results cached at this version were produced by Apex/Pascal.

## Limitations / unsupported cases

- Language-family tables are suffix-keyed, so the shared `.cls`/`.inc` cannot be given an ObjectScript family; ObjectScript stays family-less like Apex and Pascal (raw calls are protected by `is_member_call` instead).

- Pascal's unit lookup still rglobs `*.inc`; it only serves Pascal `uses` clauses, so ObjectScript includes are inert there.
- Grammar-side: a class-level `[ Language = python ]` and some `[`-contains expressions are rejected by tree-sitter-objectscript 1.9.22; such files are reported by the existing partial-extraction warning and still yield their remaining symbols.

title: docs: document labeling `--batch-size` vs context window, `--missing-only`, `export html` node limit
body:
Fixes #3859

## Problem

- The README suggested `--batch-size 200` "for large graphs", but the default of 100 (`_LABEL_BATCH_SIZE`) is already sized for a ~16k context window, and a batch that overflows the context is not retried: `_label_batch_with_retry` only splits on unparseable/incomplete replies, so the batch is logged as failed and its communities keep their hub-derived names.
- `--missing-only` was only in `--help`, and does not do what one might expect after re-clustering.
- `export html` hard-codes `node_limit = 5000` (overridable with `--node-limit`) and does not read `GRAPHIFY_VIZ_NODE_LIMIT`, which `cluster-only`, `update` and `watch` honour. The variable was not listed in the env table.

## Changes (docs + help strings only, no behaviour change)

- `README.md`: drop `--batch-size 200` from the example; add notes on `--batch-size` vs context window (~150 tokens per community; default 100 ≈ 16k, `--batch-size 40` for 8k) and on `--missing-only`; add `export html` / `--node-limit` examples; add `GRAPHIFY_VIZ_NODE_LIMIT` to the env table; update the ">5000 nodes" troubleshooting entry (graphs above the limit now get an aggregated one-node-per-community view instead of failing).
- `graphify/__main__.py`: the same points, briefly, in the `--batch-size`, `--missing-only` and `export html` help lines.

## Verification

- Checked against current `v8` (0.9.72), not only 0.9.69: `llm.py` (`_community_label_lines`, `_label_batch_with_retry`: `max_tokens = 256 + 48 × n`, only `JSONDecodeError`/`ValueError` trigger a split), `cli.py` (`missing_only` branch, reuse branch persisting hub names, `export html` `node_limit = 5000`), `exporters/html.py` (`_viz_node_limit`, aggregation above the limit), `watch.py` (`_reconcile_graph_html`).
- Rule of thumb measured without any LLM call, using `_community_label_lines` on a real 1,733-community graph (cl100k tokenizer): prompt line mean 85 / p90 167 tokens per community, so ~150 per community with the reply reservation. In practice, on an 8192-token model, batches of 100 hit 14,822 tokens and 8 of 18 failed; with `--batch-size 40` a batch stayed around 6k tokens.
- `graphify --help` output checked; `uv run pytest tests/test_cli_help.py tests/test_labeling.py tests/test_backend_extras.py tests/test_export.py` → 107 passed; `uv run ruff check graphify/__main__.py` clean. Full `uv run pytest tests`: 23 failures (Erlang/R/Solidity/VB.NET extractors, `test_ollama_retry_cap`), the same 23 on unmodified `v8` in this environment.

## Out of scope

title: Svelte: every .svelte file reports a syntax error at line 1; functions inside <script> are never extracted (extract_svelte feeds the whole file to the JS grammar)
body:
## Summary

`extract_svelte` calls `_extract_generic(path, _JS_CONFIG)` on the raw `.svelte` file. The HTML template is not JavaScript, so tree-sitter hits a top-level ERROR at line 1 and never reaches `function_declaration` nodes inside `<script>`. Only imports survive, via the regex rescue pass. On a SvelteKit app with 394 components, every single one was flagged "syntax errors and may be partially extracted".

This is the same failure mode as #2788 / PR #3902 for Astro. Vue already avoids it via `_vue_mask_non_script`.

## Reproduce (graphify 0.9.71, macOS, Python 3.13)

```
mkdir t && cd t
printf '<script>\n  import { foo } from "./x";\n  let n = 1;\n  function bump() { n++; }\n</script>\n<button onclick={bump}>{n}</button>\n' > A.svelte
graphify extract . --code-only --no-cluster
```

Output:

```
warning: 1 file(s) had syntax errors and may be partially extracted: A.svelte (first error at line 1, 1 symbol(s) extracted)
wrote graphify-out/graph.json — 2 nodes, 1 edges
```

`bump()` is missing. Same result with `<script lang="ts">` and with Svelte 5 runes (`$state`, `$props`).

## Fix that works locally

Mirror `extract_vue`: mask non-script regions with `_vue_mask_non_script` (regex is generic `<script …>…</script>`), pick `_JS_CONFIG` when `lang` is js/jsx else `_TS_CONFIG`, run `_normalize_ts_import_types`, and pass `source_override=` to `_extract_generic`. The existing regex import-rescue stays as-is.

```python
src = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
masked, lang = _vue_mask_non_script(src)
cfg = _JS_CONFIG if lang in ("js", "jsx") else _TS_CONFIG
mb = masked.encode("utf-8")
if cfg is _TS_CONFIG:
    mb = _normalize_ts_import_types(mb) or mb
result = _extract_generic(path, cfg, source_override=mb)
```

Results on a real SvelteKit repo (658 code files, 394 `.svelte`):

| | files with parse errors | nodes | edges |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 394 | 1829 | 3816 |
| after | 0 | 3377 | 5921 |

Minimal repro above: 2 nodes / 1 edge -> 3 nodes / 3 edges (`bump()` present). Line numbers stay correct because the mask preserves `\n`.

Happy to open a PR if useful.

title: feat(extract): allow acknowledging expected syntax error warnings per path (#3912)
body:
Closes #3912.

### Summary
Previously, the only way to silence the partial-extraction syntax error warning (\warning: N file(s) had syntax errors and may be partially extracted: ...\) was an entry in \.graphifyignore\. However, ignoring a file completely excludes it from the corpus, discarding all extracted nodes and edges even when the file was mostly successfully parsed.

This PR introduces warning suppression mechanisms without excluding files from the corpus:
1. **\.graphifyallow\ / \.graphifywarnignore\**: Placing glob patterns in \.graphifyallow\ (or \.graphifywarnignore\) at the scan root acknowledges expected syntax errors for matching paths, suppressing the warning while keeping all extracted nodes and links.
2. **\suppress_syntax_warnings\ parameter in \extract()\**: Allows programmatic suppression with a list of patterns or \True\ to silence all syntax error warnings.
3. **\GRAPHIFY_QUIET_SYNTAX_WARNINGS\ env var**: Enables silencing syntax error warnings via environment configuration.

### Tests
- Added test coverage in \	ests/test_partial_extraction_warning.py\ covering:
  - Suppression via \.graphifyallow\ and verifying nodes/edges are preserved in the graph.
  - Verification that suppression is scoped and non-matching files still trigger warnings.
  - Suppression via \.graphifywarnignore\.
  - Suppression via \suppress_syntax_warnings\ list and boolean parameters.
  - Suppression via \GRAPHIFY_QUIET_SYNTAX_WARNINGS\ environment variable.

title: fix(manifest): treat virtual-workspace-root Cargo.toml as skipped by design (#3910)
body:
Closes #3910

### Root Cause
In a virtual Cargo workspace, the root `Cargo.toml` specifies a `[workspace]` table without a `[package]` table:
1. `_parse_cargo` returned `None`, causing `extract_package_manifest` to return `{"nodes": [], "edges": []}` without any `skipped` marker.
2. In `extract()`:
   - Files with 0 nodes and no `skipped` marker triggered the `#1666` warning: `warning: 1 source file(s) produced zero nodes and are absent from the graph: Cargo.toml...`.
   - The file was classified under `_failed_sources`, causing `cli.py` to drop it from `manifest.json` and retry extraction on every subsequent run.
   - Neither sequential nor parallel extraction cached zero-node results lacking `nodes`.

### Fix
1. In `graphify/manifest_ingest.py`: Return `{"name": None, "skipped": "virtual workspace root Cargo.toml"}` from `_parse_cargo` when `[workspace]` is present without a package name, and pass through `{"nodes": [], "edges": [], "skipped": ...}` from `extract_package_manifest`.
2. In `graphify/extract.py`: Allow caching extraction results when `result.get("skipped")` is present even if `nodes` is empty (`result.get("nodes") or result.get("skipped")`).
3. In `tests/test_manifest_ingest.py`: Verified that virtual workspace manifests emit no zero-node warnings, are not flagged in `failed_sources`, and are cached.

_resolve_java_member_calls looks a member call up only on the receiver's declared type. title: fix(java): resolve calls to inherited methods and super
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3931.

Member calls were only matched against the receiver's own type, so `this.start()`, `super.close()` or `worker.start()` got no edge when the method lives in a superclass. The resolver now walks up the `extends` chain from the receiver type and takes the nearest declaration; `super` starts at the direct superclass. There is no edge when an ancestor lies outside the corpus, belongs to another language or points back at the class itself, or when more than one declaration is found.
