title: fix(cluster): keep hub-only neighbours with their hub under --exclude-hubs
body:
## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #919, where `--exclude-hubs` came from.

Related: #446 proposes pruning degree-1 leaves attached to a hub before partitioning in the *default* path and reattaching them afterwards. This PR is narrower. It only fixes the `--exclude-hubs` path, where nodes whose only neighbours are the excluded hubs are already left out of the partition and currently come back as singletons. I haven't tested how it would interact with that proposal, which has no PR yet. #1800 shows `--exclude-hubs` in regular use, and community counts there will change with this fix (fewer singletons).

With `--exclude-hubs P`, `cluster()` removes the hubs from the subgraph it partitions ([`cluster.py#L272-L275`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cluster.py#L272-L275)), then reattaches each hub to its neighbours' majority community ([`#L289-L305`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cluster.py#L289-L305)).

A node whose **only** neighbours are hubs is not an isolate in `G`, so it skips the isolate handling ([`#L273`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cluster.py#L273)). But it has degree 0 in the subgraph that is actually partitioned ([`#L274-L275`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/cluster.py#L274-L275)), so it comes back from the partition as a **singleton community**, cut off from the only nodes it connects to. In practice they are mostly nodes tied to a hub by `contains`, `imports` or `rationale_for` edges: local symbols of a hub file with no other edge, dependency entries of a manifest, rationale notes. For example:
- on the #919 codebase at p99, the 25 are 14 entries of `package.json`, 1 constant in `src/lib/firebase.ts`, and 10 local, non-exported types and constants of `src/components/ui/index.tsx`, the hub file from #919 (`ButtonVariant`, `DialogProps`, `BUTTON_SIZES`, …), whose only edge is `contains`;
- on graphify's own graph they include private helpers of `extract.py` and `watch.py`.

Minimal reproducer:

```python
import networkx as nx
from graphify.cluster import cluster

G = nx.Graph()
for group in (["a1", "a2", "a3", "a4"], ["b1", "b2", "b3", "b4"]):
    G.add_edges_from((u, v) for i, u in enumerate(group) for v in group[i + 1:])
G.add_edges_from(("H", n) for n in ["a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "b1", "l1", "l2", "l3"])  # l1-l3 hang off H only
print(sorted(cluster(G, exclude_hubs_percentile=90).values(), key=len))
# v8 (0.9.71):  [['l1'], ['l2'], ['l3'], ['b1', 'b2', 'b3', 'b4'], ['H', 'a1', 'a2', 'a3', 'a4']]
# this branch: [['b1', 'b2', 'b3', 'b4'], ['H', 'a1', 'a2', 'a3', 'a4', 'l1', 'l2', 'l3']]
```

Measured on 0.9.71 (`d6eaa8a`), graphs built with `graphify extract <dir> --code-only` and loaded the way `cluster-only` loads them. "Stranded" means singletons whose non-self neighbours are all excluded hubs.

**graphify's own `graphify/` package** (3,182 nodes, 7,784 edges):

| `--exclude-hubs` | hubs | Leiden: communities | Leiden: stranded | Louvain: communities | Louvain: stranded |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | 0 | 156 → 156 | 0 → 0 | 146 → 146 | 0 → 0 |
| 99 | 32 | 293 → 247 | 64 → 0 | 289 → 237 | 64 → 0 |
| 95 | 158 | 616 → 357 | 279 → 0 | 609 → 357 | 279 → 0 |
| 90 | 297 | 946 → 486 | 479 → 0 | 948 → 488 | 477 → 0 |

**The React/TS codebase from #919**, at its current state ([neo1777/marzio1777 @ `0aa0333`](https://github.com/neo1777/marzio1777/tree/0aa0333), 626 nodes; #919 used an older, larger graph):

| `--exclude-hubs` | hubs | Leiden: communities | Leiden: stranded | Louvain: communities | Louvain: stranded |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| — | 0 | 21 → 21 | 0 → 0 | 24 → 24 | 0 → 0 |
| 99 | 7 | 47 → 22 | 25 → 0 | 49 → 22 | 25 → 0 |
| 95 | 32 | 100 → 27 | 76 → 0 | 100 → 27 | 76 → 0 |
| 90 | 62 | 192 → 41 | 154 → 0 | 193 → 41 | 153 → 0 |

(before → after. Each cell is a single `cluster()` run with graphify's fixed seed (42), as a user gets it. Leiden = `graspologic-native` 1.3.1, Louvain = the networkx fallback. "hubs" = graphify's own rule, degree above the percentile. The one singleton left on graphify's graph is a true isolate, there before and after.)

On graphify's graph the community count drops by less than the number of stranded nodes (Leiden, p99: 293 − 64 = 229, but 247 measured). The hub communities, grown by their former singletons, are split again by the existing passes: with Leiden, 19, 20 and 19 more communities come from split passes than on `v8` at p99, p95 and p90 (3 more at p95 and p90 on the #919 codebase). That accounts for most of the gap. The rest comes from the partitioner itself: at p99 one stranded node has a self-loop that on `v8` was part of the first-pass input, and removing a single edge is enough to change the first partition slightly, so single-run differences of a community or two are not attributable to the fix.

On #919 I reported 261 / 518 / 678 communities at p99 / 95 / 90 and read the growth as over-splitting. That was a different graph, built with 0.8.11 on an older state of the codebase, and I didn't keep it, so I can't say how much of that growth was stranded nodes.

**The change.** Nodes whose non-self neighbours are all excluded hubs are held out of the partition. After the hubs are reattached, they are placed with the same majority vote the hubs use, with ties going to the lowest community id, as for hubs. Since all their neighbours are hubs and every hub is placed by then, the vote always has a winner. They are placed in sorted order, so the result stays deterministic. The `cluster()` docstring now mentions it.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: excluding a hub from partitioning must not leave the nodes that connect only to it in communities of their own.

What changes in behaviour, only when `--exclude-hubs` is set:
- the stranded nodes join their hub's community instead of staying alone;
- **a hub's placement can change too.** On `v8` each stranded singleton was a community that could win a hub's majority vote. Now only real communities vote.
- a hub's community grows by its private members, so it can now cross the oversize or cohesion threshold and be split by the existing passes.

What doesn't change:
- default output (no `--exclude-hubs`) is identical;
- true isolates, and nodes whose only edge is a self-loop, keep their own community.

Not covered: two or more nodes that hang off a hub *and* link to each other (a pair, a chain). They form their own component in the partitioned subgraph, so they come back as a small community rather than a singleton, and they are left as they are.

- [x] Read CONTRIBUTING.md.
- [x] Reproduced the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Smallest fix: two blocks in `cluster()` plus a docstring line, no signature change.
- [x] Regression tests in a new `tests/test_cluster_exclude_hubs.py`, kept separate so it doesn't collide with other open PRs that touch `tests/test_cluster.py`, e.g. #2388:
  - `test_exclude_hubs_keeps_hub_only_neighbours_with_their_hub` fails on `v8`;
  - `..._hub_only_neighbour_with_self_loop_joins_its_hub` fails on `v8`;
  - three boundary tests pass before and after: true isolates, self-loop-only nodes, and percentile 100 (no hubs, identical to the default).
- [x] Description kept in sync with the implementation.
- [x] Limitations documented above.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_cluster_exclude_hubs.py tests/test_cluster.py tests/test_god_nodes_exclude_hubs.py -q   # 28 passed, 2 skipped
# same three files with graspologic-native installed (Leiden path)                                           # 28 passed, 2 skipped
uv run pytest tests/ -q                          # 6013 passed, 101 skipped, 23 failed (see below)
uv run ruff check .                              # all checks passed
uv run pyright graphify/cluster.py               # same 3 errors as on v8, none new
```

The full-suite failures are the Erlang, R, Solidity, VB.NET and ollama tests (`openai` and the optional grammars aren't installed without `--all-extras`). They fail identically on a clean `v8`. I also applied this branch together with #2388 on `d6eaa8a`: it merges cleanly and the cluster tests pass.

The before/after tables come from a small script that runs `cluster()` at each percentile and counts the stranded singletons: https://gist.github.com/neo1777/9b68c8c24b553af37396781fe1f81da4 (with a `run.sh` that regenerates every number in this description from public sources).

The branch is based on `v8` at `1cd9a36` (0.9.72); the measurements above ran on 0.9.71 (`d6eaa8a`), and `cluster.py` is unchanged between the two.

Environment: Python 3.12.3, uv 0.11.23, Linux Mint 22.3. The "before" columns come from `graphifyy` 0.9.71 from PyPI, the "after" columns from this branch, on the same graphs.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] ~~Generated skill artifacts~~: not touched.
- [x] Deterministic: stranded nodes are placed in sorted order; the new tests pass under `PYTHONHASHSEED` 0, 1, 2, 42.
- [x] No unsafe interpolation.
- [x] No API keys or local-only graph data.
- [x] AI authorship disclosed in the commit (`Co-Authored-By`).

title: fix(analyze): make the cross-repo/directory surprise bonus match its reason
body:
## What does this PR do?

`surprising_connections` gives an edge +2 and the reason **"connects across different repos/directories"** when its two endpoints have different top-level directories. The helper that computes the directory, [`_top_level_dir()`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/analyze.py#L216-L218), returns the **whole path** when there is no `/`:

```python
return path.split("/")[0] if "/" in path else path
```

So two files at the scan root always have "different top-level directories". I noticed it on a flat folder of Markdown notes, where every surprise carried that reason. Any surprising edge between two root-level files gets it, e.g. between a function in `main.py` and one in `utils.py`, unless the existing suppression of INFERRED `calls`/`uses` edges applies. Minimal reproducer, AST only, on 0.9.71:

```bash
mkdir flat && cd flat
printf 'class Store:\n    def save(self, item):\n        return item\n' > store.py
printf 'from store import Store\n\ndef handle(item):\n    return Store().save(item)\n' > service.py
printf 'from service import handle\n\ndef endpoint(req):\n    return handle(req)\n' > api.py
cd .. && graphify extract flat --code-only --out flat
python -c "import json; [print(s['source_files'], '->', s['why']) for s in json.load(open('flat/graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json'))['surprises']]"
```

```text
# v8 (d6eaa8a)
['service.py', 'store.py'] -> connects across different repos/directories; bridges separate communities
['api.py', 'service.py'] -> connects across different repos/directories
# this branch
['service.py', 'store.py'] -> bridges separate communities
['api.py', 'service.py'] -> cross-file semantic connection
```

(`cross-file semantic connection` is the existing fallback text when no bonus applies, [`analyze.py#L345`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/analyze.py#L345).)

The change, all in `analyze.py`:

1. **A path without `/` maps to `"."`** (the scan root). I use `"."` rather than `""` on purpose. `_norm_source_file` ([`build.py#L375-L399`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/build.py#L375-L399)) leaves a file *outside* the scan root absolute, and its first component is `""`. A root file and an out-of-root file must stay distinct, as they are today.
2. **Backslashes and a leading `./` are normalized** inside the helper. `build_from_json` already converts backslashes (it keeps `./`), but `serve.py`'s `_load_graph()` calls `node_link_graph` directly ([`serve.py#L73`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/serve.py#L73)). Without this, `pkg\a.py` and `lib\b.py` would both become `"."` after change 1.
3. **The comparison key becomes `(node["repo"], top-level dir)`** ([`analyze.py#L266-L269`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/analyze.py#L266-L269)). `merge-graphs` and `global add` keep `source_file` repo-relative and tag each node with `repo` ([`build.py#L2391`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/d6eaa8aae8df155874ebb1044302c055c286342a/graphify/build.py#L2391)), so two repos can share directory names. The tag is set in `prefix_graph_for_global()`. Without this, change 1 would drop the bonus on a real cross-repo edge between two root-level files, which today gets it only because the filenames differ.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: the bonus, and the reason text, apply only when the two endpoints really are in different top-level directories, or in different repos.

What changes in behaviour:
- **Single-repo graphs.** Edges between root-level files no longer get +2 and the false reason. Nodes have no `repo`, and a plain `dir/file` path gives the same top-level directory as before. The only other differences are two rare path forms:
  - backslash paths, which on `v8` compared as whole strings (`build_from_json` converts them anyway; `_load_graph()` doesn't);
  - `./dir/file` paths, which on `v8` all mapped to `"."`. `extract` doesn't produce them.

  Both now resolve to their real top-level directory.
- **Merged graphs.** A cross-repo edge now gets the bonus whenever the two repos differ. On `v8` it depended on directory names: `src/x.py` (repo A) → `src/y.py` (repo B) didn't get it, while `src/x.py` → `lib/y.py` did. Edges between two root-level files of the *same* repo stop getting it, as in single-repo graphs. This changes the surprise ranking of merged graphs. I think it's the behaviour the reason text describes, but it's your call.

- [x] Read CONTRIBUTING.md.
- [x] Reproduced the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Smallest fix I could find that doesn't regress merged graphs (one helper, one comparison).
- [x] Regression tests in `tests/test_analyze.py`:
  - the flat case, which fails on `v8`;
  - merged graphs, and backslash and `./` paths, which also fail on `v8`;
  - two pins that pass before and after: a root file vs a subdirectory file, and a root file vs an out-of-root absolute path.
- [x] Description kept in sync with the implementation.
- [x] Limitations: a `./`-prefixed path is treated like its unprefixed form. `external` nodes of merged graphs have no `repo` (same as today).

No existing issue: I found this while testing on a flat corpus. I searched the title, body and comments of all issues and PRs, open and closed (for `_top_level_dir`, surprise score, cross-repo, flat directory and root-level files), and the code of every PR branch that touches `_top_level_dir`; none changes its behaviour.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_analyze.py -q                        # 55 passed
uv run pytest tests/test_*merge*.py tests/test_*global*.py tests/test_serve*.py tests/test_report*.py -q   # 282 passed, 2 skipped
uv run pytest tests/ -q                                       # 6014 passed, 101 skipped, 23 failed (see below)
uv run ruff check .                                           # all checks passed
uv run pyright graphify/analyze.py                            # same 2 errors as on v8, none new
```

The full-suite failures are the Erlang, R, Solidity, VB.NET and ollama tests: I ran `uv sync` without `--all-extras`, so `openai` and the optional grammars are missing. They fail identically on a clean `v8` checkout. The new tests also pass under `PYTHONHASHSEED` 0, 1, 2 and 42.

The branch is based on `v8` at `1cd9a36` (0.9.72); the reproducer above ran on 0.9.71 (`d6eaa8a`), and `analyze.py` is unchanged between the two.

Environment: Python 3.12.3, uv 0.11.23, Linux Mint 22.3; `graphifyy` 0.9.71 from PyPI for the reproducer (Leiden via `graspologic-native` 1.3.1, and the same output with the Louvain fallback).

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] ~~Generated skill artifacts~~: not touched.
- [x] Deterministic: pure string handling, no ambient state.
- [x] No unsafe interpolation.
- [x] No API keys or local graph data included.

title: fix(path): resolve path::symbol and node-id endpoints before scoring (#3913)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3913.

`graphify path` and the MCP `shortest_path` tool picked both endpoints with token scoring alone, so they misread the forms `explain` already understands:

- a bare label shared by symbols in several files (`.nonce()` on `AlphaClient` and `BetaClient`) got routed to one of them silently, with only a score-tie warning;
- `src/b.ts::.nonce()` scored the path half and landed on the file node;
- a full node id got tokenized and resolved to its containing class.

Both entry points now go through one helper, `_resolve_path_endpoint`. If the query hits one of `_find_node`'s exact tiers (path::symbol, node id, exact label or source path), that node is used as-is. If the hits span several files, the query is refused with the same candidate list `explain` prints. Queries with no exact hit (multi-word or partial labels) still fall through to `_score_nodes` as before.

Two same-named symbols in one file are refused too. `path::symbol` can't separate them, so the message lists their locations and ids and asks for the node id. A plain file path such as `src/b.ts` still resolves to the file node.

While I was there, I also fixed the retry hint to suggest `<path>::<label>` using the node's own label. Before, it echoed the query, which gave `<path>::index.ts::foo()` for a path-scoped query. `explain` now prints the same shared message instead of its own copy.

Repro from the issue, after the fix:

```text
$ graphify path "run()" ".nonce()"
Ambiguous: '.nonce()' matches 2 nodes in different files.
  src/b.ts
    id: src_b_betaclient_nonce
  src/a.ts
    id: src_a_alphaclient_nonce
Retry with path::symbol using one of the paths above (e.g. <path>::.nonce()) or the full node id.

$ graphify path "run()" "src/b.ts::.nonce()"
Shortest path (2 hops):
  run() --calls [EXTRACTED]--> BetaClient --method [EXTRACTED]--> .nonce()

$ graphify path "run()" "src_b_betaclient_nonce"
Shortest path (2 hops):
  run() --calls [EXTRACTED]--> BetaClient --method [EXTRACTED]--> .nonce()
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a `path` endpoint that names a node exactly resolves to that node, and one that could mean nodes in different files is refused instead of guessed. Plain label, file path and multi-word queries keep working as before. Nothing persisted changes: this only affects how queries against an existing `graph.json` are resolved.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Limitations:

- Queries that only match through scoring (partial or multi-word labels) behave as before: the top score wins, with the existing tie warning.
- `get_node` / `get_neighbors` are unchanged. They already refuse cross-file ambiguity, but two same-named symbols in one file still resolve to the first one there. I left that out to keep this PR on `path`.

## How was this tested?

```text
# new tests against the v8 serve.py / cli.py (tests from this branch)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_path_cli.py
9 failed, 10 passed

# with the fix
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_path_cli.py tests/test_serve.py
173 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
6170 passed, 14 skipped
```

I also ran the issue's two-file repro (`AlphaClient` / `BetaClient` in `src/a.ts` and `src/b.ts`) through `graphify extract`, then `graphify path` and `graphify explain`. The output is above.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments.
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

Note: I used Claude Code while working on this fix. I reviewed and ran all of it myself.

title: docs(readme): document label-reuse sidecar and Leiden/Louvain fallback
body:
Addresses items 3 and 5 of #3859 (items 1, 2, and 4 are already covered by #3926).

## What

Three README additions, README-only (+4/−2):

1. **Concepts table** — the Communities row no longer presents Leiden as the only algorithm; it now notes the silent networkx Louvain fallback when the optional `leiden` extra is not installed.
2. **Extras table, `leiden` row** — documents the fallback and that switching algorithms reshuffles every community, so a full `graphify label` run is needed for fresh names.
3. **New "Label reuse after re-clustering" callout** next to the existing "Community names" one — documents `.graphify_labels.json.sig`: a saved label is reused only while its community's membership signature is unchanged; changed or new communities get hub-derived placeholder names until `graphify label` runs again; after the community set changes (a different `--resolution`, or installing the `leiden` extra), a full `graphify label` is the only way to refresh every name.

## Why

From #3859: the `.sig` sidecar decides which labels survive a re-cluster but was not documented anywhere in the README (cf. #3808), and the README described Leiden as the clustering algorithm without mentioning the Louvain fallback — each cost the reporter a failed run or a wrong assumption.

## How checked

- Facts verified against the code: the `.graphify_labels.json` + `.sig` write/reuse path in `graphify/cli.py` (`community_member_sigs` reuse guard, hub-fill for changed communities), the graspologic → networkx Louvain fallback chain in `graphify/cluster.py::_partition`, and the `leiden` extra in `pyproject.toml`.
- `uv run pre-commit run --files README.md` — passes (skillgen-check Passed; ruff has no files to check).
- Tables keep their column counts; no trailing whitespace; no other files touched.

title: fix(scala): extract Scala 3 enum definitions, their cases and methods
body:
## Problem

A Scala 3 `enum` produces **no nodes at all**. `enum_definition` was missing from the Scala `class_types`, so the enum type, its cases, and any methods declared in its body all vanish from the graph, and a reference to the enum resolves to nothing.

```scala
enum Color { case Red, Green, Blue }
enum Op[A] {
  case Add(x: Int, y: Int)
  case Noop
  def run: A = ???
}
```

Before this change the whole graph for that file is just the file node — `Color`, `Op`, every case, and `run` are all absent. Every other language with enums (Java's `enum_constant` #1719, Kotlin's `enum_entry` #1738, Swift, TypeScript) emits a node per member with a `case_of` edge; Scala was the odd one out.

## Implementation

- Add `enum_definition` to `_SCALA_CONFIG.class_types` so the enum gets a node and the class heritage/body machinery runs for it.
- Add `enum_body` to `_SCALA_CONFIG.body_fallback_child_types` — an enum wraps its members in `enum_body`, not `template_body`, so the body walk needs it to reach the enum's methods and cases.
- Add `_scala_extra_walk`, dispatched for `tree_sitter_scala`, to emit a node plus a `case_of` edge per case. Cases nest under an `enum_case_definitions` wrapper as `simple_enum_case` (`case Red`) or `full_enum_case` (`case Add(x: Int)`); both carry the case name as an `identifier` child. This mirrors the existing Java/Kotlin/Swift enum-member handlers.

## Verification

- New regression test `test_scala_enum_definition_cases_and_methods` — fails on the pre-fix code (no `Color`/`Op`/case nodes), passes after.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -q` — 6100 passed, 15 skipped.
- `uv run ruff check .` — clean.
- `uv run pyright` — no new errors introduced (error count unchanged against the pre-existing baseline).

## Limitations

Case constructor parameter types (`case Add(x: Int)`) and per-case `extends` arguments are not linked; the case node and its `case_of` edge are the fix for the dropped members.

title: fix(rust): emit a node per enum variant with a case_of edge
body:
## Problem

The `enum_item` handler walked each variant only to collect its payload type references (`Click(Logger)` → `Logger`), but never emitted a node for the variant itself. So an enum produced a node for the type with **no members at all** — a leaf whose variants are absent from the graph.

```rust
enum Shape { Circle(f64), Square { side: f64 }, Empty }
```

`Circle`, `Square`, and `Empty` never became nodes. Every other language with enums (Java's `enum_constant` #1719, Kotlin's `enum_entry` #1738, Swift, Scala) emits a node per member with a `case_of` edge; Rust was missing it.

## Implementation

In the existing `enum_variant` loop in `extract_rust`, emit a node plus a `case_of` edge per variant, keyed on the variant's `identifier` child, alongside the existing payload-type walk. Tuple variants (`Circle(f64)`), struct variants (`Square { side: f64 }`), unit variants (`Empty`), and discriminant variants (`Colored = 1`) all carry the name as the first `identifier`.

## Verification

- New regression test `test_rust_enum_variants_emit_case_of_nodes` (against the existing `sample.rs` `GraphEvent` fixture) — fails pre-fix, passes after. The existing `test_rust_enum_variant_references` still passes, confirming payload-type references coexist with the new variant nodes.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -q` — 6100 passed, 15 skipped.
- `uv run ruff check .` — clean.
- `uv run pyright` — no new errors.

title: fix(cpp): extract enum / enum class specifiers and their enumerators
body:
## Problem

An `enum` or `enum class` produces **no nodes at all**. `enum_specifier` was missing from the C++ `class_types`, so the enum type and every enumerator vanish from the graph — even though `struct`/`class` specifiers sitting right next to them are extracted normally.

```cpp
struct Point { int x; };            // extracted: Point, x
enum class Color { Red, Green, Blue };  // dropped entirely
enum Old { X, Y };                      // dropped entirely
```

Every other language with enums (Java's `enum_constant` #1719, Swift, Scala) emits a node per member with a `case_of` edge; C++ dropped the whole type.

## Implementation

- Add `enum_specifier` to `_CPP_CONFIG.class_types`. Its name and body sit on the same `name`/`body` fields as `struct_specifier` (`type_identifier` + `enumerator_list`), so the type gets a node and its body is walked with no other config changes.
- Add `_cpp_extra_walk`, dispatched for `tree_sitter_cpp`, to emit a node plus a `case_of` edge per `enumerator` (`Red`, `Green = 2`), keyed on the enumerator's `name` field.

Anonymous enums (`typedef enum { A, B } Flag;`) carry no `type_identifier` name and are skipped by the existing name guard rather than emitting a nameless node.

## Verification

- New regression test `test_cpp_enum_specifier_members_are_extracted` — fails pre-fix, passes after; also asserts the anonymous `typedef enum` is skipped and that struct extraction is unaffected.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -q` — 6100 passed, 15 skipped.
- `uv run ruff check .` — clean.
- `uv run pyright` — no new errors.

## Limitations

Enumerator initializer expressions and the enum's underlying type (`enum class Color : uint8_t`) are not linked; the member nodes and their `case_of` edges are the fix for the dropped type. Anonymous enums remain unnamed and are intentionally skipped.

title: fix(zig): emit a node per enum member with a case_of edge
body:
## Problem

The enum body walk only emitted an enum's methods; its members — the `container_field` nodes (`red`, `north = 0`) — were dropped, so an `enum { red, green, blue }` produced a node for the enum with **no members at all**, leaving it a leaf.

```zig
const Color = enum { red, green, blue };
const Dir = enum(u8) { north = 0, south };
```

`red`/`green`/`blue` and `north`/`south` never became nodes. Every other language with enums (Java's `enum_constant` #1719, Swift, Scala, Rust) emits a node per member with a `case_of` edge; Zig was missing it. Enum *methods* were already captured (#prior work), only the members were absent.

## Implementation

Add a `container_field` branch to the Zig `walk`, emitting a node plus a `case_of` edge per member, keyed on the field's `name` field. The branch is gated on the immediate `enum_declaration` parent so struct and tagged-union fields — which share the `container_field` node shape — stay untouched.

## Verification

- New regression test `test_zig_enum_members_emit_case_of_nodes` — fails pre-fix, passes after; also asserts struct fields (`Point { x, y }`) are not turned into nodes/`case_of` edges. The existing `test_zig_enum_and_union_methods_are_extracted` still passes.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -q` — 6100 passed, 15 skipped.
- `uv run ruff check .` — clean.
- `uv run pyright` — no new errors.

## Limitations

Tagged-union fields (`union(enum) { a: i32 }`) are intentionally left as-is — only `enum_declaration` members are treated as cases. Member value expressions (`north = 0`) are not linked.

title: SKILL.md never tells the user that graphify-out/ was written into their working tree
body:
`graphify/skill.md` walks the agent through ten steps and never mentions the user's version control once. Verified at HEAD of `v8` today, not only on an installed copy: in the whole 41,732-byte file, "git" as a standalone word does not appear, nor does "gitignore", "working tree" or "version control". The seven occurrences of the string are all `github.com` — the Step 0 clone flow — plus a sponsors link.

The consequence is small but it lands on every run inside a repository. Step 9 is titled "Save manifest, update cost tracker, clean up, and report", and the report it produces describes the graph: nodes, communities, cost. It never says that a directory now exists in the working tree, what is in it, or that the project has a decision to make about it.

And the user cannot reliably find out for themselves, because the project's own answer is in a state they have no way to read off their own disk. The README's Team setup section says "the `graphify-out/` directory is gitignored by default" and shows `git add -f` for the queryable products. But nothing in the skill writes that ignore entry, and #722 — still open — asks for exactly the shipped `graphify-out/.gitignore` that would make the sentence true. So one of two things is happening on any given machine, and the user is not told which: either their own ignore rules already cover the directory and it is invisible to `git status`, or nothing covers it and a pile of machine-local files (`.graphify_root`, `.graphify_python`, `.graphify_analysis.json`, the AST cache, the `needs_update` flag) is sitting there untracked. The first case is the quiet one, and it is the one where a report line is the only channel left.

The surrounding decision is not obvious either, and it is spread across places a first-time user will not have read: the README's Team setup section, #1867 (with PR #1866) on the recommendations being incomplete, #722 on the missing shipped ignore file, and #2407 — a user asking the question directly.

So the ask here is not a policy; the policy is being worked out in those issues. It is one line of output at the point where the tool already speaks to the user:

> In Step 9's report, when the scan root is inside a git working tree, state that `graphify-out/` was created or updated there, and point at the Team setup section for what to force-add and what to leave machine-local.

Three reasons for putting it in Step 9 rather than in a code path. It costs nothing while #722 is undecided: reporting what was written is true under every outcome of that discussion. The agent reading SKILL.md is the only participant that knows both facts at the same moment — that the run just wrote into the tree, and that the tree is a repository. And it is the one remedy that works in both of the two states above, including the one where `git status` stays silent.

I am reporting this rather than sending a patch because the exact wording depends on where #722 lands; happy to open a PR against whichever shape you prefer.

title: AST extraction: Svelte 5 script blocks and TypeScript export type * produce partial graphs
body:
## Version

graphify 0.9.72 (uv tool upgrade graphifyy reports Nothing to upgrade), Python 3.10, macOS.

## Minimal reproduction

`index.ts`:
```ts
export type * from "./types.js";
```
`types.ts`:
```ts
export type FetchFn = typeof globalThis.fetch;
```

`Example.svelte`:
```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  let { value = 0 }: { value?: number } = $props();
  const doubled = $derived(value * 2);
  function increment() { value += 1; }
</script>
<button onclick={increment}>{doubled}</button>
```

Run structural extraction using `graphify.extract.extract([Path("index.ts"), Path("Example.svelte")], parallel=False)` or a code-only extraction.

## Observed

The TypeScript barrel reports a syntax error on `export type *` and no symbols. Svelte files report syntax errors at `<script>` (line 1), and larger Svelte 5 templates can emit spurious `if()` function nodes from markup. On our application the health warning listed 175 partially extracted files, mostly Svelte, plus unresolved barrel symbols. Named type exports (or removal of unused type re-exports) avoid the barrel error, but not Svelte template errors.

## Expected

Support TS 5 type-star exports. Parse Svelte script blocks as TS/JS and Svelte markup with a compatible grammar, preserving original source locations; template `{#if}` blocks must not become functions. Parser gaps should be clearly recorded in the graph/report, since they skew cohesion and hub rankings.

title: Windows + uv: Step 1 pins an ephemeral uv cache interpreter, and the subcommand guard still parses graphify.exe as a shebang
body:
Two interpreter-resolution defects in the `SKILL.md` installed by
`graphify install --platform claude`. Both are still present in v0.9.72
(`graphify/skill.md` at that tag: Step 1 lines 73 and 89 for the uv half,
line 673 for the guard; the only change to this file since v0.9.61 is the
`.graphify_root` write).

Related: #1619 (A1 reports the guard half; its PR #1962 was closed without
merging), #2183 (same guard, pipx `-E` shebang), #513 (same `head -1` on
`graphify.exe`, but in the post-commit hook, closed). The uv-cache half below
does not appear in any of them.

## 1. Step 1's uv branch resolves a throwaway cache environment

Step 1 tries uv first:

```bash
_UV_PY=$(uv tool run --from graphifyy python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)" 2>/dev/null)
```

`uv tool run` does not run inside the environment created by
`uv tool install graphifyy`. It provisions a separate, cached environment and
reports that one. On Windows 11 with graphify installed via
`uv tool install graphifyy`:

```
$ uv tool run --from graphifyy python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)"
Downloading graphifyy (1.4MiB)
Installed 30 packages in 1.84s
%LOCALAPPDATA%\uv\cache\archive-v0\<hash>\Scripts\python.exe

$ uv tool dir
%APPDATA%\uv\tools
```

The persistent interpreter the CLI actually runs from is
`%APPDATA%\uv\tools\graphifyy\Scripts\python.exe`. The cache path is written to
`graphify-out/.graphify_python` and every later step is pinned to it. Two
consequences:

- The cache entry can be evicted (`uv cache clean`, `uv cache prune`), and the
  sidecar then points at nothing.
- It can be a **different graphify version** than the installed CLI: in the run
  above it downloaded the latest release while the installed tool was older. The
  skill steps and the `graphify` CLI then silently disagree on versions.

The `import graphify` check does not catch either case, because the cache
interpreter imports fine on the day it is resolved.

## 2. The subcommand guard parses a PE binary as a shebang

"Interpreter guard for subcommands" still does:

```bash
PYTHON=$(head -1 "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" | tr -d '#!')
case "$PYTHON" in *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.@-]*) PYTHON="python3" ;; esac
```

On Windows the launcher is a console-script `.exe` (first two bytes `MZ`). In my
run (Claude Code, Git Bash) this produced
`command substitution: ignored null byte in input` and exit 127: the binary
bytes were executed as a command. When the allowlist does catch it, the
fallback is `python3`, which on Windows is often the Microsoft Store stub
(as #1619 describes). Either way nothing validates the result before it is
written to `.graphify_python`. Step 1 does better here: its shebang branch
gates the candidate on `"$_SHEBANG" -c "import graphify"` before accepting it.
The guard is the same parse without the gate, so the two blocks already
disagree.

## Expected

A resolved interpreter should be the durable environment the CLI runs from, and
it should be proven to import graphify before it is persisted.

## Proposal (both blocks)

1. Resolve the persistent tool environment directly, before any run-once
   command:
   `"$(uv tool dir)/graphifyy/Scripts/python.exe"` (Windows) or
   `"$(uv tool dir)/graphifyy/bin/python"` (POSIX); likewise
   `pipx environment --value PIPX_LOCAL_VENVS` for pipx.
2. Only parse a shebang when the launcher is a text script: skip it if the path
   ends in `.exe` or the first two bytes are `MZ`.
3. Reject any candidate whose path contains a uv cache segment
   (`/cache/archive-v0/`), and drop `uv tool run --from graphifyy` as a source
   of the interpreter path.
4. Gate every candidate on `"$PY" -c "import graphify"` and apply the same
   resolution function in Step 1 and in the guard, so the two cannot drift again
   (#2183 shows they already have).

The `find_graphify_python` function in #1619 covers points 1, 2 and 4; point 3
is the new part.

Environment: observed on graphifyy 0.9.55 installed with `uv tool install`,
skill installed with `graphify install --platform claude`, Claude Code on
Windows 11 (Git Bash); now on 0.9.65. Upstream text checked against v0.9.72.

title: update.md prints the whole detect_incremental result to stdout, flooding the agent's context
body:
The first code block of "For --update" in `references/update.md` (unchanged
through v0.9.72, line 17) both persists and prints the incremental detection
result:

```python
result = detect_incremental(Path('INPUT_PATH'))
new_total = result.get('new_total', 0)
print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
Path('graphify-out/.graphify_incremental.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
```

The result carries every file path in the corpus (`files`) plus the changed
subset (`new_files`). On a ~940-file corpus that print was roughly a thousand
indented paths.

**Why it matters in this skill specifically:** the reader of that stdout is not a
person scrolling a terminal, it is the agent's context window. Every later step
already reads `.graphify_incremental.json` from disk, so the print duplicates
the most verbose artifact of the pipeline into the scarcest resource, at the
start of a flow that still has to dispatch subagents and run the merge.

**It also contradicts the full build.** Step 2 of `SKILL.md` handles the
equivalent `detect()` result with an explicit "Do NOT cat or print the JSON",
followed by a short per-category summary. The incremental path is the only one
that dumps it.

**Observed vs expected:** observed, a full JSON dump of every path. Expected,
only what the next decision depends on, with the data left on disk, the same
as Step 2.

**Proposal:** replace the dump with a summary, keeping the sidecar write as is:

```python
nf = result.get('new_files', {})
print(json.dumps({
    'new_total': new_total,
    'deleted': len(result.get('deleted_files', [])),
    'new_by_type': {t: len(v) for t, v in nf.items()},
    'total_files': result.get('total_files'),
    'total_words': result.get('total_words'),
    'skipped_sensitive': result.get('skipped_sensitive', []),
}, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
print('Full result: graphify-out/.graphify_incremental.json')
```

I ran the whole `--update` flow with this substitution and every later step
behaved identically, since none of them read stdout.

The same pattern may be worth a pass elsewhere in the generated skills: any
block that writes a sidecar and also prints it in full.

Environment: observed on graphifyy 0.9.55, `graphify install --platform claude`,
Claude Code on Windows 11; now on 0.9.65. Block checked unchanged in v0.9.72.

title: --update: break down a mass change by top-level directory before dispatching extraction
body:
When `--update` reports that most of the corpus changed, the flow goes straight
from detection to chunking and subagent dispatch. Nothing prompts a check of
*where* the change is, and a manifest diff cannot tell "this content was
rewritten" from "this content just entered the scan root": both are simply
absent from the manifest.

Related, but a different cause: #2459 and #2033 (false "changed" reports from
`kind="semantic"`), #2870 and #2908 (files *leaving* scope), #2239 (other
pre-dispatch gaps on `--update`). This issue is about genuinely new files that
are new only because the corpus boundary moved.

## What happened

Six days after a build, `--update` reported **799 of 936 files** new or changed.
That reads as "the corpus was rewritten" and seems to justify a large extraction.

Grouping the changed documents by their first path component under the scan
root showed that **240 of 277 changed documents (3.31 of 4.14 MB) sat in one
folder that had been moved into the scan root** a few days earlier. Nothing in
it was knowledge the graph was meant to hold. Adding that folder to
`.graphifyignore` took the corpus from 936 to 289 files and the pending work
from 799 to 152 files.

The breakdown took one short script. Without it, the run would have dispatched
several times more subagents than needed, on content that should not have been
in the graph.

## Expected

Before spending on a diff that covers most of the corpus, show the shape of the
change so the user can tell a boundary change from a content change.

## Proposal (`references/update.md`, between the detection block and the
`code_only` check)

When `new_total` exceeds a fraction of the corpus (for example half of
`total_files`):

1. Group `new_files` by first path component relative to the scan root (files
   directly in the root count as `(root)`), with file count and total size per
   group. The full build already does this: Step 2 of `SKILL.md`, when
   `total_files` > 500, ranks the top 5 first-level subdirectories and asks which
   one to run on before continuing. `--update` has no equivalent gate, although
   a large diff costs the same as a large build.
2. Print the top groups and ask whether the dominant one is intended corpus or a
   directory that was moved or cloned in.
3. If it should be excluded, offer to append it to `.graphifyignore` and rerun
   detection before any chunking.

This is cheap (no LLM, one pass over paths already in
`.graphify_incremental.json`) and runs only when the diff is large enough to be
expensive.

Environment: observed on graphifyy 0.9.55, `graphify install --platform claude`,
Claude Code on Windows 11; now on 0.9.65. `references/update.md` checked in
v0.9.72: no such step (the file is unchanged since v0.9.61).

title: Code files that yield no symbols (data-only .js) enter the graph as isolated nodes, silently
body:
Routing is by extension: `.js` is `code`, code goes to the AST pass only, and
semantic extraction never sees it (Step B0 selects only
`document`/`paper`/`image`). For a **pure data file**, a literal array or object
with no functions, classes or imports, the AST finds nothing to extract. The
file enters the graph as a bare file node and its content contributes nothing.
Nothing in the flow reports it.

Related: #2214 (structured YAML/JSON data forced through the LLM, the opposite
routing problem), #728 (isolated dead-weight nodes from bundled/synthetic
files), #1692 / #3521 (unclassified files now surfaced; these files are
classified, so they are not covered), #3155 (file-level provenance for data
JSON).

## Measured on a real corpus

After a full rebuild, **88 degree-0 nodes represented 3.10 MB and ~369,500
words, 39.5% of the corpus, with not one edge**. They were large domain data
files: question banks (~45,000 lines in total) and reference catalogues,
including a ~13,000-row code table. A three-paragraph README contributed more to
the graph than all of them, purely because of the file extension. The health
check passed, since a degree-0 node is not an integrity error.

## Minimal reproduction (v0.9.65; identical on 0.9.61 and 0.9.55)

Seven one-line files, each holding the same two-element array of objects:

```js
const BANK = [...];                // v_const.js
var BANK = [...];                  // v_var.js
window.BANK = [...];               // v_window.js
module.exports = [...];            // v_cjs.js
export default [...];              // v_esm_default.js
export const BANK = [...];         // v_esm_named.js
window.APP.bank = [...];           // v_ns.js
```

`extract()` followed by `build_from_json()`:

```
graphifyy 0.9.65 graph nodes 9 edges 2
v_cjs.js           nodes=1 v_cjs.js(deg 0)
v_const.js         nodes=2 v_const.js(deg 1), BANK(deg 1)
v_esm_default.js   nodes=1 v_esm_default.js(deg 0)
v_esm_named.js     nodes=2 v_esm_named.js(deg 1), BANK(deg 1)
v_ns.js            nodes=1 v_ns.js(deg 0)
v_var.js           nodes=1 v_var.js(deg 0)
v_window.js        nodes=1 v_window.js(deg 0)
```

Five of the seven common ways to write a data file produce one isolated node.
The other two produce one node for the binding name. None carries anything from
the data itself.

## Expected

A code file that yields no symbols should be reported, because "this file has
no symbols" and "this file is data the AST cannot read" look identical in the
output.

## Proposal

1. **After Part A (`SKILL.md`)**, flag code files whose extraction produced only
   a file node (or a file node plus bindings with no functions/classes), and
   print their count and total size next to the AST summary:
   `N code files yielded no symbols (X MB); they may be data rather than code`.
2. **Offer to route those files through semantic extraction** as documents
   (add them to the Part B file list), the same way video is re-routed to
   documents after transcription.
3. **In `GRAPH_REPORT.md`**, give isolated *file* nodes their size. The report's
   "isolated nodes" section (reworked through #3548, #3794 and #3801 in
   v0.9.72) deliberately excludes file nodes, so a 400 KB data file with zero
   edges is invisible there. A large isolated file node is the signature of
   this failure; a small one usually is not.

Environment: observed on graphifyy 0.9.55, `graphify install --platform claude`,
Claude Code on Windows 11. Reproduction above re-run on 0.9.65; `report.py`
and the skill checked at v0.9.72.

title: extraction-spec has no rule for referencing nodes outside the chunk: agents copy id fragments or mint stub nodes, and replace-on-re-extract deletes real content
body:
The subagent prompt in `references/extraction-spec.md` says how to build ids for
entities in the chunk's own files, and the merge in `references/update.md` relies
on `source_file` for replace-on-re-extract. The spec's `source_file RULE` fixes
the *spelling* of the value ("EXACTLY as it appears in FILE_LIST"), but nothing
tells a subagent what to do when a file in its chunk refers to an entity that
lives in a file *outside* its `FILE_LIST`, and nothing on the merge side
enforces membership. In one `--update` run that gap produced two separate
silent failures.

Related: #3253 and #537 (subagents can only relate files inside their own
`FILE_LIST`), #1895 / #2217 / #2260 (out-of-scope `source_file`, guarded in the
LLM backend path but not in the skill's subagent path), #3004 and #1711
(replace-on-re-extract losing content by other routes).

## Failure 1: an id prefix is used as a complete id

To let chunks link to nodes owned by other chunks, the dispatching agent listed
the id *prefixes* those nodes share (the stem part of `{stem}_{entity}`).
Several subagents used the prefix verbatim as a target id. **115 edges** pointed
at ids that do not and cannot exist. They validate as well-formed strings and
only disappear when the graph is built, as dangling endpoints.

The spec's id rule invites this: it defines ids as stem plus entity, so a stem
reads like a usable id. Step 4.5's health check reports dangling endpoints after
the fact, but by then the edges are already gone.

## Failure 2: a stub node for a foreign file triggers destructive replace

Another subagent, asked only to *reference* three documents handled elsewhere,
defined its own stub node for each so that its edges would not dangle, with
`source_file` set to those documents. That is locally reasonable. But
`build_merge` drops every existing node whose `source_file` appears in the
incoming extraction, so the merge would have **deleted 23 rich nodes** extracted
earlier for those three documents and replaced them with three stubs.

Nothing would have reported it: node count still rises, the health check passes.
It was caught by reading the subagent's summary, not by any check. The skill's
Part B3 merge and the `build_merge` call in `update.md` do not compare incoming
`source_file` values against the files dispatched this run. The cache write does
(`allowed_source_files=uncached`), which is the check #1895 describes for the
backend path.

## Expected

A subagent should never be able to change nodes for a file it was not given, and
a cross-chunk reference should either resolve to a real id or be reported, not
silently dropped.

## Proposal

**`references/extraction-spec.md`, prompt text:**

- Never create a node whose `source_file` is not in `FILE_LIST`. A reference to
  something outside the chunk is expressed as an edge only.
- A dangling cross-chunk reference is acceptable; the controller resolves it.
- If the prompt ever gives example ids, give complete ids, and state that a stem
  or prefix on its own is never a valid id.

**`SKILL.md` Step B3 and `references/update.md`, before `build_merge`:**

- Drop (or re-attribute to the containing file) any incoming node, edge or
  hyperedge whose `source_file` is not in the set dispatched this run, and print
  how many were dropped per file. The same invariant #2217 proposes for the
  backend path.
- Optionally, resolve unresolved edge targets centrally against the full id
  space (existing graph + all chunks), where it is known, instead of relying on
  each agent's reconstruction of ids it cannot see.

**`references/update.md`, prose:** state that replace-on-re-extract makes
`source_file` a destructive key, so every node's `source_file` must name the
file the node actually came from.

Environment: observed on graphifyy 0.9.55, `graphify install --platform claude`,
Claude Code on Windows 11; now on 0.9.65. Spec and merge flow checked in
v0.9.72 (both files unchanged since v0.9.61): no such rule or check. #2260,
still open, would add the dispatched-set check to the LLM backend path only.

title: semantically_similar_to is scoped to one chunk, so similarity across chunks is never emitted, and plain string metrics miss it in a reconciliation pass
body:
The subagent prompt in `references/extraction-spec.md` (unchanged through
v0.9.72) says:

> Semantic similarity: if two concepts in this chunk solve the same problem ...

Chunks are dispatched in parallel and no subagent sees another's output, so a
similarity whose two ends land in different chunks cannot be emitted by
construction. Agents are not missing these edges, they are unable to produce
them, and each agent's output still reads as having followed the instruction.

Related: #65 (same diagnosis; closed after v0.3.17 added same-directory
grouping in Step B1, while "a full global linking pass remains on the table"),
#7 (local embeddings, open) and its PR #1126 (closed without merging), #537.
This report adds a concrete case from the current pipeline and what worked when
I built the controller-side pass.

## Concrete case

A project's most consequential design rule is stated in two different data files
(two different directories, so same-directory grouping does not help). Both were
extracted correctly as `rationale` nodes, but in different chunks. Each has one
edge, to its own file; they are not connected to each other and ended up in
different communities. The graph holds the same fact twice and does not know it.

The more the corpus is split, the more of the cross-cutting edges fall between
chunks, so more parallelism means a sparser semantic layer.

## Proposal

1. **Reconciliation pass after Step B3 collection, before Part C.** With all
   chunks in hand, compare `rationale`/`concept` node text across *different*
   source files, and emit `semantically_similar_to` edges marked `INFERRED` with a
   score derived from the measured similarity. Report the candidate pairs rather
   than writing silently, since this is inference over content the controller
   did not author.
2. **Amend the spec wording** so agents know the cross-chunk case is handled
   elsewhere.

## What I learned implementing (1)

I checked the pass against the known pair above, chosen before picking a
metric:

- **Word-shingle Jaccard** found 5 pairs and missed the known pair. Shingles
  measure near-verbatim copying; two texts stating one rule in different words
  share almost no trigrams.
- **TF-IDF cosine** found 32 pairs and still missed it (0.371 against a 0.42
  threshold). Both texts are long and surround the shared core with their own
  material, which dilutes the cosine.
- What identified it was **the number of rare terms in common** (nine
  low-frequency terms). Accepting a pair on *either* a strong cosine *or* a high
  rare-term overlap with a moderate cosine caught it and added 12 more true
  pairs, with no false positives on manual review.

Two things seem worth carrying into any implementation, embeddings included:
score paraphrase by shared low-frequency vocabulary, not string overlap, with a
second acceptance path for long texts whose similarity is concentrated; and
validate against a known pair fixed in advance, because 5 pairs and 32 pairs
both looked like success.

Environment: observed on graphifyy 0.9.55, `graphify install --platform claude`,
Claude Code on Windows 11; now on 0.9.65. Spec wording and absence of a linking
pass checked in v0.9.72.

title: fix(extractors): extract Kotlin annotations and constructor properties (#3835)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3835 by restoring Kotlin annotation and property dependency extraction while preserving Graphify's existing class-level JVM graph model.

### Changes

* Extract Kotlin declaration annotations from classes, constructor properties, functions, and properties.
* Support Kotlin use-site targets such as `@get:Transient`.
* Support bracketed annotations such as `@get:[Transient VisibleForTesting]`.
* Extract annotation class literals such as `Customer::class`.
* Restore `field` references for primary-constructor `val`/`var` properties.
* Restore `generic_arg` references for generic constructor and class-body properties.
* Handle annotations on property getters/setters.
* Preserve the distinction between constructor properties and plain constructor parameters.
* Avoid introducing Kotlin property/member nodes.

### Tests

* `pytest tests/test_kotlin_grammar.py tests/test_kotlin_object_literal.py` — 42 passed
* `pytest tests/test_languages.py -k "kotlin or java"` — 46 passed
* `git diff --check` — clean

### Architectural Notes

This implementation intentionally uses Graphify's existing class-level dependency representation:

```text
Order --references(context="field")--> Customer
Order --references(context="generic_arg")--> OrderLine
Order --references(context="attribute")--> ManyToOne
Order --references(context="attribute")--> Customer
```

It does not introduce Kotlin-specific property/member nodes, avoiding inconsistencies with the existing Java/Kotlin JVM graph model and type-resolution infrastructure.

title: fix(install): name the symlink target when writing CLAUDE.md (#3805)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Refs #3805 (ask 1 only).

When `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is a symlink, `install` writes the registration block into the file the link points to, but the output only named the link:

```text
  CLAUDE.md        ->  skill registered in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
```

So a rules file somewhere else got changed and nothing in the output said so. This adds a small `_shown_path` helper that prints `link -> target` when the path is a symlink, and uses it in the three places that report a write to that file: `skill registered in`, `created at`, and the project-scoped `registration removed from`. Paths that aren't symlinks print the same as before.

The issue's repro, after the fix:

```text
$ mkdir -p /tmp/t/.claude && printf '# my rules\n' > /tmp/t/rules.md
$ ln -s /tmp/t/rules.md /tmp/t/.claude/CLAUDE.md
$ HOME=/tmp/t graphify install --platform claude | grep CLAUDE.md
  CLAUDE.md        ->  skill registered in /tmp/t/.claude/CLAUDE.md -> /tmp/t/rules.md
```

The link itself is left alone, and the block still goes into `rules.md` exactly as before. The only change is in what gets printed.

title: fix(hooks): report hooks written by an older release as out of date (#3771)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Refs #3771.

Upgrading the package never touches hooks that are already on disk. So a repo that ran `graphify hook install` before a hook fix (for example the #2253 console-window launcher) keeps running the old script. Until now, `graphify hook status` still said `installed`, so nothing told the user the hook was stale.

`status` now compares the graphify block in each hook with the current template and reports blocks from an older release:

```text
$ graphify hook status        # repo whose hooks were written by 0.9.25
post-commit: installed (out of date: run `graphify hook install` to refresh it)
post-checkout: installed (out of date: run `graphify hook install` to refresh it)
merge driver: registered

$ graphify hook install
post-commit: updated existing post-commit hook at .../.git/hooks/post-commit
post-checkout: updated existing post-checkout hook at .../.git/hooks/post-checkout
merge driver: already registered (graphify-out/graph.json merge=graphify)

$ graphify hook status
post-commit: installed
post-checkout: installed
merge driver: registered
```

Before this change, the first `status` printed `installed` for both hooks.

The comparison only looks at the text between the start and end markers, so user content around the block doesn't count. It also ignores the two values that differ per install: the `_PINNED` interpreter path and the `GRAPHIFY_VIZ_NODE_LIMIT` export. `status` already checks the viz limit against `.graphifyrc` separately. The refresh itself needed no change, because `hook install` already rewrites an existing block in place.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: `hook status` says plain `installed` only when the installed graphify block is the one the current release would write, apart from its per-install values.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Limitations:

- This makes stale hooks visible. It does not refresh them automatically, because nothing runs when the package is upgraded. Each repo still needs `graphify hook install`. Refreshing automatically (for example from the hook itself) would be a bigger change, so I left it for you to decide.
- Hooks copied from an `init.templateDir` template are checked once they are in a repo, but the template itself is not checked or updated.
- A block with no end marker is not flagged. `hook install` can't rewrite those in place either.

## How was this tested?

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_hooks.py -k "<the 3 new tests>"

title: fix(install): keep a symlinked instructions file on uninstall
body:
## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to the review on #3950 ([comment](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/pull/3950#issuecomment-5911729158)). Refs #3805.

When removing graphify's section leaves an instructions file empty, uninstall deletes the file. If that file is a symlink, only the link gets deleted. The graphify section stays in the file the link points to, and the user loses their link.

Repro with a project whose `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to an empty `dotfiles/rules.md`:

```text
$ graphify install --project      # writes "# graphify" into dotfiles/rules.md through the link
$ graphify uninstall --project

# v8
  CLAUDE.md        ->  deleted .claude/CLAUDE.md
.claude/CLAUDE.md exists: no     dotfiles/rules.md still has "# graphify": yes

# this branch
  CLAUDE.md        ->  graphify skill registration removed from .claude/CLAUDE.md
.claude/CLAUDE.md exists: yes    dotfiles/rules.md still has "# graphify": no
```

The fix: when the path is a symlink, uninstall writes the cleaned content through it instead of unlinking. Regular files that end up empty are still deleted as before. The same `if cleaned: write / else: unlink` pattern is in six places, and all six get the same one-line change:

- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` skill registration (`_remove_claude_skill_registration`)
- `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.local.md` (`_strip_graphify_md_section`)
- `GEMINI.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CODEBUDDY.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`

title: fix(skillgen): print a summary of detect_incremental in the update runbook (#3944)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3944.

The first block of `references/update.md` persisted the incremental detection
result and also printed it in full:

```python
print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
```

`result` carries every file path in the corpus (`files`) plus the changed subset
(`new_files`). The reader of that stdout is the agent's context window, and every
later step reads `graphify-out/.graphify_incremental.json` from disk, so the dump
only copied the most verbose artifact of the pipeline into its scarcest resource,
at the start of a flow that still has to dispatch subagents and run the merge.
Step 2 of the core already says "Do NOT cat or print the JSON" for `detect()`;

title: fix(skillgen): pass root= to extract() in Step 3 Part A (#3727)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Addresses the first suggested change in #3727 (the skill half). The identity
check and the health-check baseline proposed there are separate work and are not
part of this PR, so the issue should stay open.

`extract()` uses `cache_root` as the fallback anchor for `source_file` and node
ids when `root` is not given (#1941). The CLI passes both
(`{"cache_root": out_root, "root": target}`), but Step 3 Part A of the skill
still called:

```python
result = extract(code_files, cache_root=Path('INPUT_PATH'))
```

That is harmless while the cache sits in the scan root. The trap is that the two
parameters look alike and this block gets adapted: pointing only the cache
somewhere else (the documented `--out` case) re-anchors every code node. The
node count does not move, every id is renamed, and every cached edge from a
document concept into code is left dangling, so the shrink guard cannot see it.
In the rebuild that prompted the issue, 1328 code-node ids changed and 313
cached edges dangled with no error.

The call now reads:

```python
result = extract(code_files, cache_root=Path('INPUT_PATH'), root=Path('INPUT_PATH'))
```

plus a three-line comment in the block saying which argument anchors ids.

Only `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md` is edited by hand. The 14 split-host
skill bodies and their `expected/` twins are regenerated (+4/-1 lines each).

Invariant: node ids and `source_file` are anchored on the scan root, never on
where the cache happens to live. As written, the rendered call is behaviour
preserving (both values are the scan root), so existing graphs, manifests and
cache entries are not invalidated; it only stops being a trap when the cache is
relocated. No library code changes.

title: fix(label): keep labels already named when a nested retry fails to parse
body:
## Problem

`_label_batch_with_retry` retries the ids a truncated reply left out (#3671) from inside the `try` that guards the batch's own parse. When one of those retries still won't parse, its error is caught by *this* batch's `except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError)` branch, which then:

1. re-splits the whole batch and asks the backend again for ids it has already named, and
2. if the re-split fails the same way, lets the error escape, so `label_communities` skips the batch and loses every name in it, including the ones already parsed.

The split after a parse failure (#1278) has a related problem. If one half fails at the base case, the error escapes before the other half's names are returned.

Example: a batch of 4 whose reply names only 2 ids before it is truncated, where one of the 2 missing ids never parses. On `v8` the batch makes 5 backend calls, asks again for the 2 ids it already had, and still loses all 4 names. With this change it makes 3 calls and keeps 3 names.

## Change

- The batch's own reply is still parsed inside the `try`.
- The missing ids are now retried outside it, one half at a time. After a parse failure every id counts as missing, so this is still the plain #1278 split.
- A half that still won't parse is recorded, and the other half still runs.
- The batch re-raises (the first parse error) only when none of it could be named. `label_communities` still skips a batch that yields nothing.
- The stderr diagnostic at the base case, the partial-reply handling (#3671) and the depth cap are unchanged.

## Verification

New tests in `tests/test_label_retry.py`:

- `test_a_missing_id_that_never_parses_keeps_the_labels_already_had` checks the partial reply case. It also asserts the backend is not asked again for ids it already named.
- `test_a_half_that_never_parses_does_not_discard_the_other_half` checks the split case.
- `test_a_batch_that_never_parses_still_raises` checks that the error still reaches the caller when nothing could be named.

Before the fix, the first two fail with `ValueError: label response is not parseable JSON`, which drops every name. The third passes before and after.

Commands run:

- `uv run pytest tests/test_label_retry.py tests/test_labeling.py -q`: 41 passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -q`: 6009 passed, 102 skipped, 24 failed.
  - 23 of the failures also fail on unmodified `v8` in this environment. They are the Erlang, R, Solidity and VB.NET extractor tests (their grammar packages are not installed by a plain `uv sync`) and `test_ollama_retry_cap.py` (`openai` is not installed).
  - The 24th, `test_incremental_mtime_collision.py::test_same_size_rewrite_in_one_tick_is_requeued`, is timing-sensitive. It failed only in the full run on a heavily loaded machine and passes when run on its own.
- `uv run ruff check .`: all checks passed.
- `uv run pyright graphify/llm.py tests/test_label_retry.py`: same 25 errors as unmodified `v8`, none new.

## Scope and limits

The change is limited to `_label_batch_with_retry`. It does not change `max_tokens` budgeting; #3755 addresses that separately and touches the same function, so one of the two may need a small rebase. I did not add a CHANGELOG entry because release batches appear to be written by maintainers.

title: fix(export): index (label, id) before the graph DB push upsert loop
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the O(n²) node-upsert loop in the graph DB exporters by creating an index on the `MERGE` match pattern before any node is written.

Both `push_to_falkordb` and `push_to_neo4j` upsert every node with:

```python
MERGE (n:<Label> {id: $id}) SET n += $props
```

That matches on `(label, id)`, but neither path created an index on that pattern first. Without one, the engine scans every node already carrying the label to decide whether the node already exists, so each upsert costs `O(nodes with that label)` and the whole push degrades to `O(n²)` in nodes-per-label. In the report on [#3804](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/issues/3804) (167,428 nodes / 209,215 edges across 6 labels) throughput collapsed from ~10,000 node upserts/60s to ~100 upserts/300s partway through, with FalkorDB at ~97% CPU and a multi-hour total wall time.

The change creates one index per distinct label up front, before the upsert loop:

```cypher
-- FalkorDB
CREATE INDEX FOR (n:<Label>) ON (n.id)

-- Neo4j
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:<Label>) ON (n.id)
```

`_distinct_node_labels()` derives the label set exactly the way the two push loops derive `ftype` (`.capitalize()`, then `[^A-Za-z0-9_]` stripped, falling back to `Entity`), so every label a `MERGE` matches against is covered — including the fallback label a node with an unusable `file_type` would be written under.

Refs [#3804](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/issues/3804).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: **no `MERGE` in either push path may run before its label is indexed.** Without it a bulk push silently costs a full label scan per node, and the only symptom is throughput — the push still reports success.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

The regression tests assert against the Cypher that reaches the server, using fake `falkordb` / `neo4j` clients, so they need no database and run in the default CI:

- One index per distinct label is issued, and the **last** index precedes the **first** `MERGE`.
- Stated as the property itself rather than a fixed call order: scanning the recorded Cypher, every `MERGE (n:<Label>` must have seen a `CREATE INDEX` for that label earlier in the stream.
- `_distinct_node_labels()` cannot emit a label the `MERGE` loop would never write (an all-punctuation `file_type` collapses to the `Entity` fallback, matching `_safe_label`).
- A `CREATE INDEX` that raises does not abort the push — every node and edge is still upserted.

Against the unpatched `graphdb.py` all 5 tests fail, and one reports the failure in the shape of the bug itself:

```
E  AssertionError: MERGE on unindexed label Code: MERGE (n:Code {id: $id}) SET n += $props
```

Limitations / unsupported cases:

- Neo4j index creation uses `IF NOT EXISTS` so re-pushes stay idempotent. **FalkorDB's `CREATE INDEX` has no such clause**, so a re-push against an already-indexed graph gets an error back. That is caught and ignored deliberately: a redundant index is a performance detail, and failing an otherwise valid push over it would be worse. The push is unchanged in that case apart from the (already-optimized) query cost.
- Creating an index on a large, already-populated graph is itself not free. That cost is paid once and is bounded per label, which is the trade this issue is asking for.
- Only the index statements are new. Node/edge property payloads, label sanitization, community attachment, and the `MERGE`-based idempotency of the push itself are untouched.

## How was the tested?

Commands actually run:

```text
uvx ruff@0.15.14 check --config pyproject.toml graphify/exporters/graphdb.py tests/test_graphdb_push_indexes.py
# All checks passed!

python -m pytest tests/test_graphdb_push_indexes.py -q
# 5 passed

# Prove the regression test demonstrates the old failure:
git stash push graphify/exporters/graphdb.py
python -m pytest tests/test_graphdb_push_indexes.py -q
# 5 failed
git stash pop
python -m pytest tests/test_graphdb_push_indexes.py -q
# 5 passed

# No regression in the surrounding export suites (baseline is identical with and
# without the change; those failures are pre-existing in this environment):
python -m pytest tests/test_cli_export.py -q
# 47 failed, 5 passed  — both with and without the change
```

Notes on the environment: `pyright` reports only `reportMissingImports` for `neo4j`, `falkordb` and `pytest` — optional dependencies that are not installed here. There are no type errors in the changed code.

`tests/test_falkordb_integration.py` skips here (no FalkorDB server reachable), which is why the new tests use fake clients rather than adding to that file — they need to run in CI, which starts no external services.

- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python). — Labels are passed through the same `[^A-Za-z0-9_]` allowlist the push loops already apply to `ftype`, so nothing new is interpolated into Cypher.
