title: feat(prs): export human-readable review artifacts
body:
## What does this PR do?

Graphify's PR dashboard shows changed files and community impact, but a reviewer still has to reconstruct behavior from the raw diff. This adds `graphify prs <number> --review`, which exports a revision-pinned `review.json` and self-contained `review.html` under `GRAPHIFY_OUT/reviews/pr-<number>/`.

The review starts with collapsible change stories: focused before/after dependency graphs and, with `--infer`, cited plain-language pseudocode through Graphify's existing backend. Reviewers can then expand the blast radius, affected communities, relationships/confidence, and fixed base/head source excerpts. A local comparison is available through `graphify prs --review --base <ref> --head <ref>`.

Source collection reads committed Git objects into isolated temporary snapshots. Both sides use the same structural extraction/build pipeline; graph comparison, incoming traversal, and clustering reuse existing helpers. The bounded directed SVG presentation shares positions across the two snapshots and works offline without JavaScript, a CDN, or new dependencies. Existing PR, export, and MCP paths retain their behavior.

[Whiteboard](https://github.com/devdotfast/whiteboard) inspired the guided explanation and source attachment approach. This contribution implements that reading experience as portable Graphify artifacts.
<details>
<summary>Example reading experience: graphs, pseudocode and blast radius</summary>

This demonstration uses the [committed Python test fixture](https://github.com/mikkelkrogsholm/graphify/blob/ebc01b88d9cdd7efe323038bee0883ba83c9ef3a/tests/test_review_source.py). Its topology was extracted by the actual review builder. Pseudocode comes from an explicitly mocked, authored model reply and remains `INFERRED`.

**Before**

```text
When signing in:
    Create a session
    Return the session
```

**After**

```text
When signing in:
    If MFA is required:
        Return an MFA challenge

    Create a session
    Return the session
```

The after-change dependency graph includes an added `challenge()` call. Arrows represent structural dependencies. The actual HTML artifact uses directed SVG with shared before/after positions; this Mermaid excerpt makes the topology visible inside the PR.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    app["app.py"] -->|imports| authenticate["authenticate()"]
    login["login()"] -->|calls| authenticate
    authenticate -->|calls| challenge["challenge() · added"]
    authenticate -->|calls| session["create_session()"]
    style challenge fill:#eaf7ed,stroke:#277a43
```

The blast-radius view retains the unchanged `login()` caller and `app.py` importer as potential upstream dependents. Relationships, affected communities, fixed-revision source excerpts and coverage can be expanded separately.

</details>


Try it:

```bash
graphify prs 42 --review
graphify prs 42 --review --infer --backend ollama --model <configured-model>
graphify prs --review --base origin/v8 --head HEAD
```

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the review gap and identified the invariant.
- [x] Kept the feature within three source/analysis/rendering boundaries and a small PR dispatch change.
- [x] Added isolated boundary tests and regression coverage for snapshot path aliases, first-line file/symbol collisions, and several methods changed in one hunk.
- [x] Kept this description synchronized with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented limitations and unsupported cases.

<details>
<summary>Implementation boundaries and evidence handling</summary>

Inferred explanations stay review-local and retain `INFERRED` confidence. Citation validation checks supplied IDs and source sides; it does not prove semantic correctness. Source-only changes remain visible even when graph topology does not change. Collection preserves the user's checkout/index and canonical graph/cache. Backend unavailability, failure, or abstention leaves the deterministic artifact usable.

Git paths, source/model text, subprocess arguments, and HTML are treated as data. Collection excludes sensitive/ignored files, symlinks/gitlinks, nonportable paths, binary/non-UTF-8 blobs, and oversized content, with disclosed coverage. Git external diff/textconv, replacement objects and grafts are disabled. Invalid filename bytes cannot alias valid source paths; physical LF lines, terminators and Git modes are retained. Marker-based generated-directory and directory-only ignore decisions precede source admission, with unreadable ignore rules failing closed. HTML escapes untrusted content and has a restrictive CSP.

</details>

## How was this tested?

A main review and two independent adversarial reviews covered only the addition, followed by a focused repair pass. Repairs include source-identity and collection boundaries, output symlink/rollback handling, model validation/status, and connected accessible blast-radius graphs. The tests include 63 additional regression cases across the adversarial repair pass and automated-review follow-up. The follow-up fixes failed-source diagnostic normalization and decorator-only Python change mapping. It also states the trusted local output-directory boundary explicitly; static symlink checks do not prevent a hostile concurrent process from replacing directory ancestors. The end-to-end regression now enters through `prs.cmd_prs` and generates actual artifacts, covering the route that the sampled formal check did not exercise.

After the October 12 upstream sync, the full suite on Python 3.12 passes: **7,273 passed, 133 skipped, 1,864 warnings** (371.44 seconds). Focused contribution/PR/architecture checks on Python 3.12.2, 3.10.20, and 3.13.13: **214 passed on each** (113 warnings per run). The only Git conflict was in README.md: keep upstream’s documentation-link replacement for the old command reference and our human-readable review section. Output assumes no adversarial process concurrently changes the checkout or output directories; do not run elevated in an attacker-writable directory. Missing merge-base history in a shallow clone fails explicitly and must be fetched first. Windows execution and live model-provider calls remain unverified locally. Upstream CI exercises Linux on Python 3.10, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14; the full suite was run locally on macOS and Python 3.12, and 214 focused tests pass on both Python 3.10.20 and 3.13.13.

title: `hook-guard read` skips any path containing a directory with the same name as the last segment of `GRAPHIFY_OUT`
body:
## Summary

When `GRAPHIFY_OUT` is a nested path whose last segment is a common name (e.g. `artifacts/graphify`), `graphify hook-guard read` silently skips the read nudge for **every** file under any directory with that name, not just the output directory. Example: `tools/graphify/notes.md` or `.codex/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`.

## Version / environment

- graphifyy 0.9.69
- Windows 11, Claude Code PreToolUse hook (should be platform-independent)
- `GRAPHIFY_OUT=artifacts/graphify`

## Reproduction

From a project root containing `artifacts/graphify/graph.json`:

```bash
export GRAPHIFY_OUT=artifacts/graphify

# expected: no nudge (this is the output dir) -> OK
echo '{"tool_name":"Read","tool_input":{"file_path":"artifacts/graphify/GRAPH_REPORT.md"}}' | graphify hook-guard read

# expected: nudge (regular indexed source file) -> OK
echo '{"tool_name":"Read","tool_input":{"file_path":"src/app.py"}}' | graphify hook-guard read

# expected: nudge, actual: no output
echo '{"tool_name":"Read","tool_input":{"file_path":"tools/graphify/notes.md"}}' | graphify hook-guard read
echo '{"tool_name":"Read","tool_input":{"file_path":"tools/graphify/helper.py"}}' | graphify hook-guard read
```

The files under `tools/graphify/` are in the graph (`source_file` present in `graph.json`), so they should be nudged like any other file.

## Cause

In `_run_hook_guard` (`cli.py`), the `read` branch has this check:

```python
under_out = "graphify-out/" in j or (GRAPHIFY_OUT_NAME.lower() + "/") in j
```

`GRAPHIFY_OUT_NAME` is `os.path.basename(GRAPHIFY_OUT)`, which is `graphify` here. So the check becomes a substring test for `graphify/` anywhere in the path. The `"graphify-out/"` literal has the same issue for any directory named `graphify-out` outside the project's real output dir, but that is less likely to happen in practice.

This looks like the same pattern as #2273 (`detect.py`, closed), but in the hook guard, which that fix did not cover.

## Suggested fix

Compare against the resolved output directory instead of a bare name substring. Something like:

```python
out_dir = out_path().resolve()
def _is_under_out(v: str) -> bool:
    try:
        p = Path(v)
        p = (root / p) if _is_cwd_relative(v) else p
        p.resolve().relative_to(out_dir)
        return True
    except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError):
        return False
under_out = any(_is_under_out(v) for v in (file_path, path) if v)
```

The Glob `pattern` field (e.g. `artifacts/graphify/**`) could keep a prefix match against the output dir's project-relative path.

## Impact

Fails open: tools are never blocked, only the nudge is lost. In our repo this dropped the nudge for 11 indexed files (all of `tools/graphify/`), plus a skill directory. Because of this, we kept the old inline hook for `Read|Glob` and only switched `Bash|Grep` to `hook-guard search`, which works well. Thanks for #522 and #3121!

title: fix(ruby): capture paren-less self-send calls
body:
## Problem

A receiver-less Ruby method call written **without parentheses** — the most common call form in idiomatic Ruby — is dropped from the call graph:

```ruby
class Widget
  def run
    build        # a method call on self: NO edge was emitted
  end
  def build; end
end
```

Tree-sitter parses that `build` as a bare `identifier`, structurally identical to a local-variable read (`x`). The call-walk only inspected `call` nodes, so `build(1)`, `self.build` and `build arg` each produced a `calls` edge while the bare `build` produced nothing — not even a `raw_call`. A `module` of mutually-calling helpers could end up with no internal edges at all, and the existing Ruby bare-call promotion path in `ruby_resolution.py` had nothing to promote.

## Implementation

Mirror Ruby's own disambiguation rule: a bare identifier is a send on `self` **unless** a local or parameter of that name is in scope.

- `_ruby_local_names` collects the bound names of a method body — parameters, assignment targets, block parameters, `for` variables and `rescue` captures.
- In the call-walk, a bare `identifier` whose name is not one of those (and is not the `method`/`receiver` field of a `call`) is routed through the normal callee path as a non-member call. It then resolves in-file (`EXTRACTED`) or becomes a `raw_call` the Ruby resolver can prove/promote.

The collector is deliberately over-inclusive, so a missed binding only **suppresses** a candidate call (fail-closed) rather than inventing a wrong edge. All changes are gated on `tree_sitter_ruby`, so no other language is affected.

### Limitations
A receiver-position send (`logger.info` where `logger` is itself a paren-less send) is left for a follow-up and stays unresolved rather than guessed.

## Verification

- `tests/test_ruby_bare_self_send_calls.py` (new): the self-send, cross-`module` and mixed-in cases are captured; the negatives (a local, a parameter and a block parameter that shadow a method name) must **not** become calls; `self.build` and bare `build` do not double an edge. The positive specs fail on `v8`, pass with the fix.
- `uv run pytest tests/` — full suite green (6175 passed, 15 skipped; the DNS-bound `test_security.py` and the built-wheel test need network/a wheel).
- `uv run ruff check .` clean; `uv run pyright` adds zero new errors.

title: fix(typescript): extract abstract method signatures
body:
## Problem

An abstract class's method was dropped from the graph, while the identical contract on an `interface` was kept:

```ts
interface Drawable { draw(): void; }      // draw -> node (method_signature)
abstract class Shape { abstract area(): number; }  // area -> dropped (abstract_method_signature)
```

So the base of an `abstract class` kept only its concrete methods, a polymorphic `shape.area()` had no declaration to resolve to, and the overridden contract had no node to carry it.

## Implementation

An abstract method is the same kind of contract as an interface method: a subclass must implement it. `interface` methods (`method_signature`) were already a TS function type; abstract methods parse as `abstract_method_signature`, which was not.

Add `abstract_method_signature` to the TypeScript function types (inherited by the TSX config). Its name sits on the same `name` field as `method_signature`, so nothing else is needed.

### Limitations
Abstract **fields** (`public_field_definition` with `abstract`) are left as-is, matching concrete fields, which are not nodes either. Scope is abstract methods only.

## Verification

- `tests/test_ts_abstract_methods.py` (new): the abstract method becomes a node; a concrete method and a free function calling it both resolve to it; parity with the interface method it mirrors. All fail on `v8`, pass with the fix.
- `uv run pytest tests/` — full suite green (6175 passed, 15 skipped). Existing TS suites (`test_ts_inheritance`, `test_ts_namespace`, `test_typescript_enum_members`, `test_ts_decorators`) unchanged.
- `uv run ruff check .` clean; `uv run pyright` adds zero new errors.

title: fix(scala): extract deferred (abstract) method declarations
body:
## Problem

A bodyless `def area: Double` parses as `function_declaration`; a `def` **with** a body is `function_definition`. Only the latter was a Scala function type, so every deferred (abstract) method was dropped.

```scala
trait Shape {
  def area: Double          // dropped
  def name(): String        // dropped
  def describe: String = name()   // kept — but its call had no target
}
```

In Scala this is the common case, not an edge case: a `trait` used as an interface is entirely deferred defs, so the whole contract vanished — the trait had no method nodes, and a concrete method calling a deferred one had no target to link to. The same held for an `abstract class`'s abstract members.

## Implementation

Add `function_declaration` to the Scala function types. A bodyless `def` only occurs inside a `trait`/`abstract class` body, so it is always a method declaration; its name sits on the same `name` field as `function_definition`.

## Verification

- `tests/test_scala_abstract_methods.py` (new): deferred methods (with and without a parameter list) become nodes in both a `trait` and an `abstract class`; a pure-interface trait keeps every contract method; a call to a deferred method now resolves. All fail on `v8`, pass with the fix.
- `uv run pytest tests/` — full suite green (6175 passed, 15 skipped). `test_scala_self_type` and the Scala cases in `test_languages` unchanged.
- `uv run ruff check .` clean; `uv run pyright` adds zero new errors.

title: fix(cpp): treat a member-function declaration as a method, not a field
body:
## Problem

Inside a class body a `virtual double area() = 0;` (pure virtual), a `virtual void draw();` and a plain prototype `int run();` all parse as a `field_declaration` whose declarator is a `function_declarator`. The field branch recognised that shape only to skip emitting a type reference — it still emitted a node for every declarator as a **data member** (a bare `area` label with a `defines`/field edge).

Consequences:
- a pure-virtual interface class had no method nodes, only phantom fields;
- a header-declared method and its out-of-line/overriding definition did not share one node (`area` field vs `.area()` method);
- a call to such a method resolved to a field-shaped node.

## Implementation

In the field-declaration branch, emit a `function_declarator` with the same shape a defined method uses — a `.name()` label, a `method` edge, and callable — so the declaration and its definition collapse to one method node (parity with the Java/TypeScript/Scala abstract-method contract). A genuine data member still gets its `defines` field edge.

## Verification

- `tests/test_cpp_method_declarations.py` (new): pure-virtual / declared-virtual / prototype members become method nodes; a data member stays a field; the decl/def merge keeps one node and a call through it resolves. All fail on `v8`, pass with the fix.
- This corrects the label of every header-declared method, so a few existing cross-file assertions that expected the old bare `bar`/`run` field label now expect `.bar()`/`.run()` (`test_cpp_objc_cross_file_calls`, `test_languages`). The resolved call edges (source, target, confidence) are unchanged, and the decl/def merge still produces exactly one node carrying the definition site.
- `uv run pytest tests/` — full suite green (6175 passed, 15 skipped).
- `uv run ruff check .` clean; `uv run pyright` adds zero new errors.

title: feat(extract): add Prismio (.psm) support

title: feat(extract): add Prismio (.psm) support
body:
## Problem

Graphify has no support for [Prismio](https://github.com/prismio-lang/prismio) (`.psm`). A Prismio project produces no code graph at all.

## Implementation

Prismio has no tree-sitter grammar, so this is a dependency-free scanner in the style of the COBOL extractor (`graphify/extractors/prismio.py`): comments and string text are blanked (offsets preserved, `${...}` interpolation kept), then a token pass reads the declarations and scans bodies for calls.

**Nodes:** files, functions, `prop`s, `extern fn`s, methods, structs, enums and variants, traits, `impl` blocks, top-level `let`s.

**Edges:**
- `contains`, `method`, `imports_from` (every import form: `a.b`, selective `a.b.name`, `as`, `{x, y} from dir`, `* from dir`, `a.*`, resolved by walking up to the project root).
- `implements` / `references` from `impl` blocks, and `references` from parameter/return types, struct fields, enum payloads, trait bounds and `Type { .. }` literals (generic parameters are never looked up).
- `calls`: bare calls, plus `recv.f(x)` / `Type.f(x)` via a second resolver once the receiver's type is known (parameter, `self`, annotated or constructed `let`, or a type named in the call). Prismio resolves those to a method of the type *or* a free function taking it first, so both are searched among the caller's own file and its **direct** imports (Prismio imports are not transitive), and bound only when exactly one matches the arity. `Type.f()` is `EXTRACTED`; receiver-typed calls are `INFERRED` (0.8).

Wired through the facade, `LANGUAGE_EXTRACTORS`, the dispatch table, `_LANG_FAMILY_BY_EXT`, `analyze._cross_language`, `detect.CODE_EXTENSIONS`, and two registered `LanguageResolver`s. No new dependency or extra.

## Fail-closed boundaries

- Overloaded same-file names are never guessed; a name bound to two types in one function, call-result receivers and field receivers are not typed and stay unbound.
- Ambiguous candidates (e.g. two traits both defining `pick` for one type) produce no edge.
- Unbound `impl`/type names (built-ins such as `Int`, std outside the scanned tree) are dropped together with their placeholder node: no phantom stubs.
- An import naming no file on disk produces no edge. `.ums` build manifests are out of scope.

## Verification

- `tests/test_prismio_extractor.py` (15 tests) + `tests/fixtures/new_languages/sample.psm`. Each behaviour was mutation-checked (reverting the fix makes its test fail): overload-id collisions, the member-call resolver, import visibility, overload guessing, generic shadowing.
- **Full suite** (`pytest tests -n 8`): 5801 passed, 57 failed. The *same 57* fail on untouched `v8` in the same environment (the optional terraform / vbnet / solidity grammars are not installed there); this branch adds exactly 15 passing tests and no new failures.
- `ruff check` clean; pyright clean on the new files.
- Real-world: Prismio's own `src/` + `std/` (73 files) -> ~3.6k nodes, ~14k edges, 0 stubs, 0 duplicate ids. All 606 `.psm` files in the repo (including deliberately-invalid programs) extract without error, <0.1 s per file. 4,320 randomly truncated/mutated real files raise nothing.
- Incremental parity: after editing two files (one adding a cross-file call), `graphify update` yields exactly the same nodes and edges as a fresh build.
- Found and fixed along the way: overloads differing only by punctuation (`Int` vs `Int?`) shared a node id because `make_id` drops punctuation, silently losing about half of `std/io.psm`'s `print` overloads.

## Known limits

No type inference beyond the cases above, so method-style calls on call results or fields (`a.b().c()`) are intentionally unlinked. pyright still reports pre-existing errors in `extract.py`; none are in the new code.

title: fix(rust): stop prelude types becoming god nodes and label constructors
body:
Fixes two Rust extraction issues that make the language's own primitives read as core abstractions.

## 1. Prelude types become god nodes

`_LANGUAGE_BUILTIN_GLOBALS` covers ECMAScript/Python/Swift builtins but held no Rust standard-library type. Every `Option<T>`, `Vec<T>`, `String`, `Result` annotation was extracted as a domain type and resolved onto a few canonical nodes carrying corpus-wide degree. On a ~1,200-file workspace `String` was the #1 node with ~1,700 edges; `Option` and `Vec` each produced hundreds of per-file stubs.

This adds a Rust-only `_RUST_BUILTIN_TYPES` set — kept separate from the shared set so the same names still resolve as user types in other languages (Python `pathlib.Path`, a Kotlin `Result`) — and skips those names in the Rust type-reference collector and call collector.

The filter is definition-aware. A file that defines its own `struct Result<T>` shadows the prelude, and its references are kept. This is pinned by a test and by the existing `tests/fixtures/sample.rs`, which defines a local `Result`.

## 2. Tuple-struct construction counted as a call

`ClientId(id)` was emitted as `calls`, so a newtype used as a key everywhere read as the top call hub. A construction targets a data definition, not a callable. It is now emitted as `references` with `context="constructor"` in both the in-file and cross-file paths. A real function call still emits `calls`.

## Tests

New `tests/test_rust_builtin_type_hubs.py`:

- prelude types produce no node; a user-defined type still does
- cross-file and same-file construction become `references[constructor]`
- a real function call stays `calls`
- a locally defined prelude-named type keeps its references

`uv run pytest -q`: 6064 passed, 102 skipped. The 26 failures are pre-existing on a clean `v8` checkout (missing optional extractor dependencies for erlang/R/solidity/VB.NET, plus environment-specific ollama/install tests); I confirmed this by running the same set with the change stashed.

`uv run ruff check` and `uv run pyright` are clean on the changed files.


Fixes #3974.

title: Rust: standard-library types become god nodes; tuple-struct construction counted as a call
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs in the Rust extractor make the language's own standard-library types look like the most central abstractions in a graph.

### 1. Prelude types become god nodes

`_LANGUAGE_BUILTIN_GLOBALS` covers ECMAScript / Python / Swift builtins but contains no Rust standard-library type. Every `Option<T>`, `Vec<T>`, `String`, `Result` annotation is therefore extracted as a domain type and resolved onto a small number of canonical nodes carrying corpus-wide degree.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Run `graphify .` (or `graphify extract`) over a non-trivial Rust workspace.
2. Open `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` and read the "God Nodes" section.

Observed on a ~1,200-file workspace: `String` was the #1 node with ~1,700 edges. `Option` and `Vec` each produced hundreds of per-file stub nodes, and the "Suggested Questions" section asked why `String` bridged almost every community.

### 2. Tuple-struct construction counted as a call

`ClientId(id)` is emitted as a `calls` edge. A newtype used as a map key throughout the codebase therefore reads as the top call hub, even though it is only ever constructed.

## Expected

- Rust prelude / std types should not become cross-cutting graph hubs.
- Constructing a data definition should not be counted as a function call.

## Notes

A file may legitimately shadow a prelude name (its own `struct Result<T>`). The fix must keep references to a type the file actually defines, so a bare name filter is not sufficient.

title: fix(php): stop language constructs binding to same-named methods (#3830)
body:
### what does this pr do?

fixes the builtin half of #3830. empty(), isset(), eval() and die() are language constructs, but tree-sitter-php parses them as a plain function_call_expression and the call pass resolves them by name. a reserved word is a legal method name since php 7, so any class with a method called empty picks up every empty($x) in the repo. same file the edge is EXTRACTED, other files get INFERRED through the case-insensitive fold. the symfony corpus in the issue had about 200 of these on one paginator method.

the php branch now drops the callee for these before the in-file lookup and before raw_calls, same thing _GO_PREDECLARED_FUNCS does for go. php only, bare calls only, and it takes the whole call-shaped keyword list from the php manual (array, die, empty, eval, exit, isset, list, unset) so it doesnt depend on which of them the pinned grammar gives its own node type. $bag->empty() is a member call and still resolves.

the member call half of #3830 is #3391. #2617 refuses methods for php function calls across files, this one is narrower and also covers the same-file EXTRACTED edges.

### verification & invariants

a call to a php language construct never produces a calls edge. the method that shares the name, member calls into it, and calls nested inside the construct like empty($this->load()) are unchanged. the tests cover all of those plus EMPTY() in upper case and a genuine cross-file function call.

title: build_merge: re-extracting one doc silently drops another doc's hyperedge when both share an id (attach_hyperedges de-dups by id alone)
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.73 (also 0.9.6)

## Summary

Hyperedge ids are chosen per extraction, so two different documents can emit hyperedges with the same `id`. A full build keeps both. An incremental `build_merge` that re-extracts **only one** of the two documents silently drops the **other** document's hyperedge, even though that document was not re-extracted.

The cause is that `build_merge` carries forward the existing hyperedges of untouched files through `export.attach_hyperedges`. That function de-duplicates by `id` alone (`seen_ids`), so a carried hyperedge loses to any new-chunk hyperedge with the same id from a different `source_file`.

Seen in the wild on a ~14k-node graph: two docs (an ADR and a plan describing the same mechanism) both produced `public_pool_invariant_enforcement`.

## Reproduction (self-contained)

```python
import json, os, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.build import build_merge
from graphify.export import to_json
from graphify.cluster import cluster

d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); os.chdir(d)
(d / "a.md").write_text("# A\n\nAlpha.\n"); (d / "b.md").write_text("# B\n\nBeta.\n")
Path("graphify-out").mkdir()

def node(i, sf): return {"id": i, "label": i, "file_type": "concept", "source_file": sf}
def he(sf, members): return {"id": "shared_flow", "label": f"Flow in {sf}", "relation": "participate_in",
                             "nodes": members, "source_file": sf, "confidence": "INFERRED", "confidence_score": 0.8}
a, b = ["a_one", "a_two", "a_three"], ["b_one", "b_two", "b_three"]

# 1. full build: both hyperedges kept
G = build_merge([{"nodes": [node(i, "a.md") for i in a] + [node(i, "b.md") for i in b], "edges": [],
                  "hyperedges": [he("a.md", a), he("b.md", b)]}],
                graph_path="graphify-out/graph.json", root=".", dedup=False)
to_json(G, cluster(G), "graphify-out/graph.json", force=True)
print([(h["id"], h["source_file"]) for h in json.load(open("graphify-out/graph.json"))["hyperedges"]])
# [('shared_flow', 'a.md'), ('shared_flow', 'b.md')]

# 2. re-extract ONLY b.md
G = build_merge([{"nodes": [node(i, "b.md") for i in b], "edges": [], "hyperedges": [he("b.md", b)]}],
                graph_path="graphify-out/graph.json", root=".", dedup=False)
print([(h["id"], h["source_file"]) for h in G.graph["hyperedges"]])
# [('shared_flow', 'b.md')]   <- a.md's hyperedge is gone, though a.md was not touched
```

**Expected:** after step 2, both hyperedges are present: `a.md`'s carried unchanged and `b.md`'s replaced.
**Actual:** `a.md`'s hyperedge is silently dropped.

## Suggested fix

Treat a hyperedge's identity as `(id, source_file)` rather than `id` when de-duplicating carried hyperedges in `attach_hyperedges` / `build_merge`, which is consistent with the replace-per-source rule `build_merge` already applies. Alternatively, namespace hyperedge ids by source file at extraction time.

title: [Bug]: ollama + library path silently drops ~96% of edges: no source_file backfill, on_chunk_done fires after the checkpoint and without the chunk's allowlist, #2973 recovery is case-sensitive, and MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is inert
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README
- [x] I searched existing issues (closest matches: #2973 closed, #2314, #2217, #1757, #1939 — none covers the four points below)

### What happened?

We run graphify nightly over a ~21k-document corpus (Markdown + PDF, mostly Italian prose, not code) with a small local model, calling `extract_corpus_parallel()` as a library rather than through the CLI. The resulting graphs are far emptier than the extraction work we pay for. The gap traces to four separate things on the ollama/cache path. They compound, so I am filing them together — happy to split if you prefer.

Expected: a chunk the model answered successfully persists its nodes **and** its edges, or says what it dropped.
Actual: on this backend a successful chunk routinely persists nothing at all, silently, and is re-extracted and dropped again the next night.

Across our nightly logs, **394 of 1163 completed chunks persisted zero cache entries** (33.9%), each logged as a success.

---

#### 1. Nothing backfills `source_file` on edges, and `save_semantic_cache` drops every item without one

The extraction schema asks the model for `source_file` on nodes *and* edges (`llm.py:510`). A small local model fills it on nodes and forgets it on edges. Measured on our corpus with `qwen2.5:14b`: **nodes 99%, edges 4%**.

`save_semantic_cache` groups by that field and skips anything missing it (`cache.py:1463-1477`):

```python
for e in edges:
    e = _normalized(e)
    src = e.get("source_file", "")
    if src:
        by_file[src]["edges"].append(e)
```

No `else`, no counter, no warning. **96% of the edges the model just produced never reach the cache.** On the next incremental run those files are cache hits — with almost no edges — so the loss is permanent, not retried.

The information needed to repair this is already in hand and costs no model call: an edge's `source`/`target` are node ids from the same chunk, and those nodes do carry `source_file`. A deterministic pass took our edge coverage from **4% to 99%**:

```python
nsrc = {n["id"]: n["source_file"] for n in nodes if n.get("source_file")}
for e in edges:
    if not e.get("source_file"):
        v = nsrc.get(e.get("source")) or nsrc.get(e.get("target"))
        if v:
            e["source_file"] = v
```

Suggestion: do this inside `extract_corpus_parallel` before `_checkpoint_chunk`, and `warn()` with a count for whatever still has no `source_file`, instead of dropping it silently.

#### 2. `on_chunk_done` cannot persist a corrected chunk without defeating #2973 and #1757

A caller that wants to apply the fix above must re-persist the chunk, and the callback makes that impossible to do correctly:

- `_checkpoint_chunk(result, chunk)` runs **before** `on_chunk_done(idx, total, result)` (`llm.py:2729-2730`), so a callback can only write *after* the uncorrected version is already on disk.
- The callback signature is `(idx, total, chunk_result)`. It never receives `chunk`, so the caller **cannot reconstruct `allowed = [unit_path(item) for item in chunk]`** — the exact value `_checkpoint_chunk` passes as `allowed_source_files`.

Without that list the caller's `save_semantic_cache` runs with `allowed_source_files=None`, which disables both:

- **#2973's basename recovery** — `_recover_group_path` is gated on `allowed_paths is not None` (`cache.py:1510`), so an unresolvable `source_file` is skipped rather than recovered;
- **the #1757 scope guard** — a stray `source_file` can clobber another file's complete entry.

So the caller's write is strictly worse than the checkpoint it overwrites, and nothing in the callback's arguments allows better.

Suggestion: pass the chunk's resolved paths to the callback — `on_chunk_done(idx, total, result, allowed)`, or an `allowed=` kwarg keeping the old arity working — and/or offer a hook that runs *before* `_checkpoint_chunk` so a caller can correct `result` in place and let the library persist it with the right scope.

#### 3. #2973's basename recovery is exact-match, so a lowercasing model is never recovered

`_recover_group_path` matches on `ap.name == cache_path.name` (`cache.py:1512`):

```python
candidates = [ap for ap in allowed_paths if ap.name == cache_path.name]
if len(candidates) == 1:
```

Our model's dominant `source_file` failure is not a mangled basename — it **lowercases the path and drops intermediate directories**. When the basename itself contains uppercase (`g0/SPEC-CONGELATA.md`), the exact comparison finds zero candidates and the group falls through to the silent skip, although a case-insensitive comparison would have matched exactly one file in the chunk.

Suggestion: when the exact match yields nothing, retry with `ap.name.casefold() == cache_path.name.casefold()`, keeping the same "recover only if exactly one candidate" rule. Conservative, and one extra pass over a list at most `chunk_size` long.

#### 4. `GRAPHIFY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` has no effect on the ollama backend

`_call_openai_compat` sends the cap as `max_completion_tokens` (`llm.py:1408`). Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint ignores that field. Measured against ollama directly, same model and server, only the field name changed:

| field sent | value asked | completion_tokens returned | finish_reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_completion_tokens` | 15 | **195** | `stop` |
| `max_tokens` | 15 | **15** | `length` |

Consequence: the output cap a user sets is silently inert on ollama, so `--api-timeout` is the only thing bounding generation. It also makes the `finish_reason == "length"` path at `llm.py:1485` unreachable there, so the adaptive "retry with smaller input" signal never fires. In our run with `GRAPHIFY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=3000`, a two-file chunk returned **6722** output tokens.

Suggestion: in the ollama branch — where `extra_body` is already being assembled — also set `kwargs["max_tokens"] = max_completion_tokens`.

Related, minor: the `num_ctx` derived at `llm.py:1443` is capped by the server's `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`. We requested 14000 and `/api/ps` reported `context_length: 11000`, so the derived value is a request and not a guarantee; a note to that effect in the comment would help.

---

#### Why these matter together

Each is survivable with a hosted model that fills `source_file` on every item. Together, on a small local model, a nightly incremental run can bill a full extraction and persist almost none of its edges while reporting success. Ours did exactly that for weeks.

### Steps to reproduce

Extract as a library (not via the CLI) against a local ollama:

    export OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11436/v1
    export GRAPHIFY_OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=14000
    export GRAPHIFY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=3000
    export GRAPHIFY_TOKEN_BUDGET=7000

then, in Python:

    from pathlib import Path
    from graphify.llm import extract_corpus_parallel

    files = [Path("docs/a.md"), Path("docs/sub/B-UPPER.md")]   # prose, not code
    r = extract_corpus_parallel(files, backend="ollama", model="qwen2.5:14b",
                                root=Path("."), max_concurrency=1, token_budget=7000)

    n, e = r["nodes"], r["edges"]
    print("nodes with source_file:", sum(1 for x in n if x.get("source_file")), "/", len(n))
    print("edges with source_file:", sum(1 for x in e if x.get("source_file")), "/", len(e))
    print("output tokens:", r["output_tokens"], "(cap asked: 3000)")

Point 4 on its own, no graphify involved — send the same request twice, changing only the field name, and compare `usage.completion_tokens`:

    curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11436/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"model":"qwen2.5:14b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"List 60 Italian city names, comma separated."}],"max_completion_tokens":15,"stream":false}'

    curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11436/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"model":"qwen2.5:14b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"List 60 Italian city names, comma separated."}],"max_tokens":15,"stream":false}'

### Error output or graph output

```text
# point 4, measured:
max_completion_tokens=15  ->  195 tokens, finish_reason "stop"
max_tokens=15             ->   15 tokens, finish_reason "length"

# a real two-file chunk, GRAPHIFY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=3000:
input_tokens 6572   output_tokens 6722

# our nightly, aggregated from its own logs:
chunks persisting >0 cache entries:  769
chunks persisting  0 cache entries:  394   (33.9%, each logged as a success)

# the silent skip itself produces no output at all — that absence is the report.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.73 (every line number above is from the installed 0.9.73 wheel; the behavior was first seen on 0.8.18)

### Operating System

Linux

### Additional context

Backend `ollama`, model `qwen2.5:14b` (Q4_K_M), 3× Tesla P40, Ubuntu. Corpus ~21k documents, mostly Italian prose. Points 1-3 are read from the 0.9.73 source; point 4 is measured against the live server as shown above.

title: feat(extract): support Verilog header files (.vh)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Verilog headers ending in `.vh` are currently skipped by detection and extractor dispatch. Register them with the existing Verilog parser so detection, extraction, incremental updates, and watch rebuilds include them.

Fixes #3749.

title: fix(extract): parse only Svelte script blocks in the AST pass (#3928)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3928. `extract_svelte` called `_extract_generic(path, _JS_CONFIG)` on the raw `.svelte` file. The markup is not JavaScript, so tree-sitter produced a top-level ERROR at line 1 and never reached the declarations inside `<script>` — every component was reported as "had syntax errors and may be partially extracted", and only imports survived, via the existing regex rescue pass.

This is the same failure `extract_astro` had, fixed in #3902 (`f9a6893`), and that `extract_vue` already avoids. This change gives Svelte the same treatment: blank everything outside the `<script>` bodies (keeping `\r`/`\n`, so AST locations still match the original file) and parse only those bodies.

Details:

- **Grammar follows the first block's `lang`**: `js`/`jsx` → JS, `ts` or unset → TS (a superset of JS, and Svelte's own default), mirroring `extract_vue`.
- **Both script blocks are parsed** — the instance block plus Svelte 5 `<script module>` / Svelte 4 `<script context="module">`.
- **Non-JS `type` scripts are blanked** (`application/ld+json` and friends): their bodies are data, not statements, and would only add parse errors — same rule as the Astro masker.
- **A script region is terminated in place of the following `<`**, so two blocks on one line do not run together into a single statement (the case `test_extract_astro_scripts_on_one_line_do_not_merge` covers for Astro).
- **The regex import rescue is unchanged.** It still covers template-layer dynamic imports (`{#await import('./X.svelte')}`), which the AST pass cannot see. An import that both passes now resolve yields the same `(source, target, relation)` edge twice, which `build.dedupe_edges` collapses — identical to the Astro path's behaviour today (verified: both emit 2, both collapse to 1).

`_svelte_mask_non_script` mirrors `_astro_mask_non_script`, and the two share the script-tag and non-JS-type patterns instead of duplicating them (`_ASTRO_SCRIPT_RE` / `_ASTRO_NON_JS_TYPE_RE` now alias the shared constants — no behaviour change). Happy to drop that bit of sharing and keep the Astro lines untouched if you'd rather the diff stayed strictly inside `extract_svelte`.

Also covers the Svelte half of #3942: because the markup is blanked, a template `{#if}` no longer mints a spurious `if()` function node. That issue's other half (`export type *`) is not touched here.

### Measured

The issue's minimal repro, `graphify extract . --code-only --no-cluster`:

| | files flagged with syntax errors | result |
|---|---|---|
| before | 1 of 1 | `2 nodes, 1 edges` — `bump()` missing |
| after | 0 of 1 | `3 nodes, 3 edges` — `bump()` present |

A small SvelteKit-shaped corpus (runes `$state`/`$derived`/`$effect`/`$props`, `{#snippet}`/`{@render}`, `context="module"`, TS type aliases, a `ld+json` block, `<style>`):

| | files with parse errors | nodes | edges |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 3 of 3 | 7 | 6 |
| after | **0 of 3** | 14 | 17 |

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: **deterministic AST extraction must not silently drop symbols a file really declares.** A `.svelte` file's `<script>` body is ordinary JS/TS; feeding the surrounding markup to the JS grammar turned a fully extractable file into a line-1 parse error plus a near-empty node set, and the only signal was a warning that is easy to miss in a large run.

Nothing persisted is invalidated: node ids are unchanged (they derive from the path and symbol name, and masking preserves offsets, so `source_location` values still point at the original lines). The graph gains the symbols that were previously dropped, which is a growth, not a shrink, so the anti-shrink guard is not implicated.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Limitations, stated explicitly:

- An **unterminated** `<script>` (no closing tag) extracts nothing. It matched nothing before either (zero symbols, parse error), so this is not a regression; it is malformed Svelte and the tag regex requires a close.
- `lang="jsx"` maps to the JS grammar for symmetry with `extract_vue`; Svelte itself does not support JSX, so this should never fire in practice.
- Markup-layer expressions are deliberately *not* code to the AST pass. Dynamic imports there are still recovered by regex; nothing else in the template is extracted.

## How was this tested?

```text
# the issue's own repro, before and after
graphify extract . --code-only --no-cluster

# new regression tests (8)
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_svelte_extraction.py -q          # 8 passed

# regression semantics: with the extract.py change stashed, 4 of the 8 fail
git stash push graphify/extract.py && uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_svelte_extraction.py -q
#   4 failed, 3 passed   (the import tests pass either way — they guard against
#   the masking costing imports the rescue pass already recovered)

# neighbours of this code path
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_astro_extraction.py tests/test_astro_import_ids.py \
  tests/test_js_import_resolution.py tests/test_import_extension_resolution.py \
  tests/test_partial_extraction_warning.py tests/test_languages.py tests/test_extract.py -q

# full suite, lint, types
uv run --frozen pytest tests/ -q
uv run --frozen ruff check .          # clean
uv run --frozen pyright graphify/extract.py
```

Environment: Windows 11, Python 3.12 (uv-managed), `uv sync --all-extras --frozen`.

Full suite on this branch: **52 failed, 6125 passed, 62 skipped**. To be sure none of that is mine, I ran the full suite a second time on a clean worktree checked out at the merge base (`ef4450d`) and diffed the two failure lists. **No test fails on this branch that passes at the merge base**, with one apparent exception that is a property of the checkout path, not of the change:

- `test_install.py::test_codex_hook_command_is_a_real_cli_subcommand` fails in my main checkout and passes in the worktree. The reason is that my checkout lives under `D:\Download2\Open Source Con\…`: the test does `command.split()` on the registered hook command and asserts `parts[1]` is a known subcommand, so the space in the directory name makes it read `'Source'`. The worktree happens to sit under a space-free temp path. It fails identically on unmodified code at the same path, so it is unrelated to this PR (and is the same class of problem as #2581).

Everything else failing is pre-existing and nowhere near extraction — `test_hooks.py` (12), `test_skillgen.py` (11), `test_non_regular_files.py` (5), `test_extract.py` parallel-fallback (5), skillgen path-injection (3), `test_install.py` (3), plus singles in watch, uninstall scope, atomic writes, terraform, and unicode wikilink normalization. **No Svelte or Astro test is among them.**

Cross-platform notes (CONTRIBUTING #13): the masker preserves `\r` and `\n`, so CRLF files keep correct line numbers; verified explicitly, along with a UTF-8 BOM file, an empty file, a markup-only file, a style-only file, two scripts on one line, and a Vue-3.3-style attribute containing `>` (`generic="T extends Record<string, unknown>"`). All extract cleanly with no parse errors.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). — the masker is a pure function of the file's bytes.
