title: fix(llm): backfill edge source_file, add casefold recovery, pass allowed to on_chunk_done, and set ollama max_tokens (#3982)
body:
Resolves #3982

### Root Cause
1. **Missing Edge source_file**: Local / weaker LLMs (such as small models via Ollama) frequently emit edges without a `source_file` field. During semantic cache grouping in `save_semantic_cache`, items without `source_file` are skipped.
2. **Casefold recovery**: Model drift or case inconsistencies (e.g. `WEIRD_NAMED_FILE.py` vs `weird_named_file.py`) caused `_recover_group_path` in `graphify/cache.py` to fail basename matching and drop valid cache items.
3. **Single-file chunk attribution**: In single-file chunks, any un-attributed items unambiguously belong to that single dispatched file.
4. **`on_chunk_done` callback signature**: Callers running `extract_corpus_parallel` as a library did not receive the chunk allowlist (`allowed`), preventing proper downstream scoping / caching and risking unintended cache drops.
5. **Ollama `max_tokens` vs `max_completion_tokens`**: Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint ignores `max_completion_tokens` and only respects `max_tokens` (or `options: {num_predict: ...}`).

### Changes
- **Edge source_file backfill & single-file chunk attribution** (`graphify/llm.py`):
  - In single-file chunks, attribute missing `source_file` on nodes, edges, and hyperedges to the lone file.
  - In multi-file chunks, backfill missing edge `source_file` from endpoint node source files (`source` or `target`).
  - Emit a warning with count if edges remain un-attributed.
- **Casefold recovery** (`graphify/cache.py`):
  - If exact basename matching fails in `_recover_group_path`, fall back to case-insensitive basename matching against `allowed_paths`.
- **`on_chunk_done` callback** (`graphify/llm.py`):
  - Pass `allowed=[unit_path(item) for item in chunk]` to `on_chunk_done` with backwards-compatible fallback for 3-argument callbacks.
- **Ollama `max_tokens`** (`graphify/llm.py`):
  - When `backend == "ollama"` in `_call_openai_compat`, supply `kwargs["max_tokens"] = max_completion_tokens`.
- **Tests**:
  - Added unit tests for edge `source_file` backfill and `on_chunk_done` in `tests/test_chunking.py`.
  - Added unit tests for case-insensitive basename recovery in `tests/test_semantic_cache_basename_recovery.py`.
  - Added unit tests for Ollama `max_tokens` parameter in `tests/test_llm_backends.py`.

title: fix(build): preserve same-id hyperedges from untouched files during build_merge (#3981)
body:
Fixes #3981

### Problem
Hyperedge IDs are emitted per document extraction, meaning two distinct documents can emit hyperedges with the same ID (e.g., `shared_flow` or a common invariant name).
A full build keeps both hyperedges. However, during incremental `build_merge`:
1. `_new_hyperedge_ids = {he.get("id") for chunk in new_chunks ...}` keyed only on hyperedge ID.
2. Carried hyperedges from untouched files were checked against `_new_hyperedge_ids`:
   ```python
   if he.get("id") and he.get("id") in _new_hyperedge_ids:
       continue
   ```
   When document B was re-extracted and produced a hyperedge with ID `shared_flow`, document A's untouched `shared_flow` was silently dropped.
3. Similarly, `attach_hyperedges` deduplicated incoming hyperedges using `seen_ids = {h["id"] ...}`, dropping valid hyperedges from other files that shared an ID.

### Solution
1. In `build_merge()`, treat hyperedge identity as `(id, normalized_source_file)` (falling back to `id` if `source_file` is absent). Re-extracting a file now only replaces that file's hyperedges, preserving same-ID hyperedges belonging to untouched files.
2. In `attach_hyperedges()`, deduplicate by `(id, source_file)` when `source_file` is present (falling back to `id` if absent).
3. Added unit tests in `tests/test_build_merge_hyperedges_and_prune.py` and `tests/test_hypergraph.py` verifying preservation across re-extracts and deduplication behavior.

title: fix(skill): a partly-read file is no longer a silent, permanent loss
body:
## Summary

`graphify install` + `/graphify --update .` never enters `llm.py`, so #1369's oversized-file guard does not apply. Step 3 Part B hands files to `general-purpose` subagents, and the Read tool returns **at most 2000 lines per call while reporting no error when it truncates**. A subagent that read only the head of a long file still writes a well-formed chunk, so Step B3's success signal ("chunk exists and parses") was never evidence of coverage.

Three behaviours turned that into permanent loss rather than a miss:

1. `build_merge`'s replace-on-re-extract drops every existing node whose `source_file` is the re-extracted file, then re-adds only what the subagent returned — so the unread tail was **deleted**.
2. The run **reported success** — valid JSON, chunk on disk, no warning.
3. The manifest recorded `semantic_hash`, so the file was **never retried**.

On the reported 4165-line archive: 103 nodes covering ~31%, **90 of 131 `###` entries with no surviving node**, and every later run skipped it.

@Ryanm218's follow-up measured a second mechanism that made the obvious fix insufficient, and this PR implements both bounds rather than only the `>2000` solo rule: a **590-line** plan extracted to **zero nodes**, which no Read-cap guard explains. File-count-only chunking (20–25 files) dilutes attention across the chunk.

## What changed

All edits are in `tools/skillgen/fragments/`, so the 13 disk-dispatching hosts pick them up from one edit and the generated artifacts are regenerated by `python -m tools.skillgen` (no hand-editing of `graphify/skill*.md`).

**1. `references/shared/extraction-spec.md` + `-compact.md`** — the prompt states the cap, forbids emitting nodes for a partly-read file and says why (replace-on-re-extract deletes first), and asks the subagent for a top-level `coverage` map of `file -> lines read`. The field is in the emitted schema, not just the prose. Both variants are covered: fixing only the verbose one would leave codex/claw/kiro/pi silently half-reading.

**2. `core/core.md` Step B1** — a chunk is bounded by **both** limits (20–25 files **and** ~6000 total lines), and a file past 2000 lines gets a chunk to itself.

**3. `core/core.md` Step B3.5** (new) — compares each reported coverage against the file's real length, names what was short, and writes the list to `.graphify_partial.txt`. That list is then handed to the two places that decide whether a file is ever looked at again:

- `save_semantic_cache(..., partial_source_files=...)` → the entry is stamped `partial: True`, which `load_cached` treats as a **miss**
- `_stamped_manifest_files(..., partial_source_files=...)` → left **unstamped**, so `detect_incremental` re-queues it

Both parameters already exist and are already used by the library path for a truncated LLM response (#933, #1950, #3203). This PR wires the skill path to the same contract rather than inventing a second one, so the next `--update` re-dispatches the file and replace-on-re-extract swaps the partial node set for a complete one.

## Why this is safe

- **Fail-safe in the direction that loses nothing.** No `coverage` reported → no file flagged. A flagged file is re-read, never trusted. Nodes already extracted for those files are kept — they are still true.
- **No library behaviour change.** The diff outside `tools/skillgen/fragments` is generated markdown. `cache.py` / `cli.py` already implement partial handling and are covered by `tests/test_partial_cache.py`.
- **All five skillgen guards pass**: `--check`, `--audit-coverage`, `--schema-singleton`, `--monolith-roundtrip`, `--always-on-roundtrip`. The monolith round-trip is untouched because the two monoliths (aider, devin) extract sequentially one file at a time and never chunk — see below.
- **Windows render verified**: the new inline python is inside the supported `$(cat ...) -c` form, so `_core_to_powershell` translates it to a here-string and the strict translator still rejects unknown bash. `test_windows_python_step_bodies_match_posix_verbatim` covers parity.

## Tests

The two load-bearing tests **execute the emitted python** rather than matching its source, per the #2126/#2641 convention that static assertions gave this class of bug no coverage:

- `test_coverage_check_flags_a_partly_read_file_and_clears_a_complete_one` — runs Step B3.5 against a real `graphify-out`, asserts the short file is named with `read 10 of 50 lines` and written to `.graphify_partial.txt`, then that a full count clears the warning.
- `test_a_partly_read_file_is_cached_as_a_miss_so_the_next_update_retries_it` — round-trips the **real** semantic cache: after the cache write, `check_semantic_cache` must return the partly-read file as **uncached** while the fully-read file still hits.

That second test is the one that matters, because the loss was permanent precisely *because* the file was served from cache forever. Verified non-vacuous: reverting just the `partial_source_files=` argument makes the same round trip return an empty uncached list.

Plus prompt-contract tests asserting both spec variants carry the rule, and that Step B1 keeps both bounds.

Full suite: `6020 passed`. The 52 failures in this environment are pre-existing on `origin/v8` (symlink/mtime/timing on Windows) — I diffed the failing set against a stashed baseline and my change adds none; the one apparent delta, `test_same_size_rewrite_in_one_tick_is_requeued`, passes 3/3 in isolation.

## Known gap

`codex` collects subagent results in memory with no per-chunk files, so Step B3.5 has nothing to compare against — it gets the prompt-layer fix but not the machine gate. The two monoliths (`aider`, `devin`) extract sequentially per file and never chunk, so the attention-dilution half does not apply to them; they would still want the read-completely rule, which I left out to keep this diff to the reported path. Happy to follow up on either.

Fixes #2225

title: [Bug]: ollama branch overwrites extra_body, so GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING and providers.json extra_body are silently inert; plus no JSON mode and no seed, so extraction is not reproducible (73 vs 34 nodes on identical input)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README
- [x] I searched existing issues. #1621 (closed) added `GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING`; nobody noticed the ollama branch overwrites it. #3680 asks for `extra_headers` in providers.json, which is adjacent but different. No issue covers reproducibility or a seed.

### What happened?

We run graphify nightly over a ~21k-document corpus with a local model (`ollama` + `qwen2.5:14b`, 3× Tesla P40). To get usable extraction we have ended up **wrapping the `openai.OpenAI` client in our own code** to inject two fields into every request. We would much rather not maintain a monkeypatch of a third-party library's private call path, so here is why we have to, with the measurements.

Three separate things on the ollama branch, one of which is a plain bug.

---

#### 1. The ollama branch **replaces** `extra_body`, so `GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING` is silently inert there

`_call_openai_compat` builds `extra_body` through a chain of `if/elif` (`llm.py:1419-1427`):

```python
if extra_body is not None:
    kwargs["extra_body"] = extra_body            # custom provider's own extra_body
elif "moonshot" in base_url:
    kwargs["extra_body"] = {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}
elif _thinking_disabled_via_env():               # GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING
    kwargs["extra_body"] = {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}
```

and then, further down, unconditionally for ollama (`llm.py:1473`):

```python
    kwargs["extra_body"] = {"options": {"num_ctx": num_ctx}, "keep_alive": keep_alive}
```

That is an assignment, not a merge. So on the ollama backend:

- `GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING=1` has **no effect at all** — it is documented as a user choice in `_thinking_disabled_via_env`'s own docstring, and on this backend it is discarded a few lines later;
- a custom provider's `extra_body` from `providers.json` is discarded too, although the comment at `llm.py:1416-1418` explicitly promises the opposite ("When supplied, it wins over the moonshot default — the user has explicitly chosen the request shape for their endpoint"). The example in that comment is `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false` **for a self-hosted Qwen**, i.e. exactly the local-model case this branch breaks.

Fix is a merge instead of a replacement:

```python
    _eb = dict(kwargs.get("extra_body") or {})
    _eb.setdefault("options", {})["num_ctx"] = num_ctx
    _eb["keep_alive"] = keep_alive
    kwargs["extra_body"] = _eb
```

#### 2. No way to force JSON mode, and the difference is large

Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint supports `response_format={"type": "json_object"}`, which constrains generation to valid JSON. graphify does not send it on any path (`grep -rn response_format` in 0.9.73 finds only `_json_object_candidates`, the tolerant *parser*), and there is no flag to ask for it.

Measured on the same two documents, same prompt, same model, only that field added:

| | nodes | edges | output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| without `response_format` | 39 | 30 | 3,238 |
| with `response_format` | 73 | 73 | 7,856 |

Tolerant parsing recovers *a* JSON object from prose, but it cannot recover the content the model never emitted because it drifted out of JSON.

#### 3. No seed, so extraction is not reproducible — which makes any A/B comparison meaningless

There is no `seed` anywhere in the package (`grep -c '"seed"' llm.py` → 0). Ollama accepts `options.seed`, and with `temperature: 0` already in the ollama BACKENDS entry a fixed seed would make extraction reproducible.

Without it, we measured this — **identical input, identical prompt, identical configuration, same server, consecutive runs**:

```
run 1 :  73 nodes /  73 edges /  7,856 output tokens / 1,125 s
run 2 :  34 nodes /  18 edges /  2,404 output tokens /   321 s
```

Input was byte-identical (6,715 prompt tokens, 2,687-character system prompt, verified equal), so this is not truncation — the generation itself varies by 3.3× in length and 4× in edge count. Environment checked to rule out the obvious causes: `temperature: 0` is configured **and sent**, `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1`, `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=0`, `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=f16`.

The consequence is not only ours: **graphify's own quality comparisons on a local backend cannot be trusted at n=1**. A `seed` (and surfacing it in the docs) would fix that for everyone.

---

#### Why we are reporting this rather than just patching it

We also have to replace `_EXTRACTION_SYSTEM`, a private module global, because our corpus is Italian prose rather than code and the shipped prompt extracts ~1 node per document on it. There is no supported way to extend or replace it: no environment variable, no parameter, and `--prompt-file` only selects the *cache namespace*, not the prompt. So every integration like ours ends up reaching into module internals — and silently loses whatever the next release adds to that prompt. (We just caught ourselves dropping 0.9.73's own `<untrusted_source>` SECURITY paragraph that way, which would have turned our corpus into an instruction channel. That one is on us, but a supported hook would have prevented it.)

A documented extension point — a parameter, an env var, or a documented "append to the system prompt" hook — would let integrators stop monkeypatching private internals.

### Steps to reproduce

Point 1, no model needed — inspect the request graphify builds:

    GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING=1 python - <<'PY'
    # observe that kwargs["extra_body"] ends up as
    #   {"options": {...}, "keep_alive": "..."}
    # with no "thinking" key, on the ollama branch
    PY

or simply read `llm.py:1419-1427` against `llm.py:1473`.

Point 3, two identical runs against a local ollama:

    export OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11436/v1
    export GRAPHIFY_TOKEN_BUDGET=7000
    for i in 1 2; do
      python -c '
    from pathlib import Path
    from graphify.llm import extract_corpus_parallel
    r = extract_corpus_parallel([Path("a.md"), Path("b.md")], backend="ollama",
                                model="qwen2.5:14b", root=Path("."),
                                max_concurrency=1, token_budget=7000)
    print(len(r["nodes"]), len(r["edges"]), r["input_tokens"], r["output_tokens"])'
    done

### Error output or graph output

```text
# point 3, two consecutive runs, identical input (6,715 prompt tokens both times):
73 73 6715 7856
34 18 6715 2404

# point 2, same documents and prompt, only response_format added:
without: 39 nodes, 30 edges, 3238 output tokens
with   : 73 nodes, 73 edges, 7856 output tokens

# point 1 produces no error at all — the env var is simply discarded. That is the report.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.73

### Operating System

Linux

### Additional context

Backend `ollama`, model `qwen2.5:14b` (Q4_K_M), 3× Tesla P40, Ubuntu, `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=11000`. Corpus ~21k documents, mostly Italian prose. Related to our #3982 (the cache/`source_file` side of the same local-model path) and to the closed #1621, which introduced the env var that point 1 shows is inert here.

title: [Bug]: _ensure_stat_index binds to the first root per process while the index is keyed by absolute path — a multi-root process gets wrong hashes and atexit writes the corruption to disk (184 cached files reported as 0)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README
- [x] I searched existing issues. #3847 (closed) is about *where* `stat-index.json` lands on `extract --out`; #2974 (closed) is about `atexit` recreating a deleted directory. Neither covers the first-root binding below, which corrupts hashes across projects and survives in 0.9.73.

### What happened?

`_ensure_stat_index` binds the stat index to the **first** root a process ever sees and then returns forever, while the index is keyed by the file's **absolute** path — but `file_hash` is computed from the content *plus the path relative to the root*. Any process that touches two different roots therefore gets, from the second root onward, hashes computed under the first root. And because `atexit` flushes the accumulated index into whatever `_GRAPHIFY_OUT` points at when the process exits, the corruption is **written to disk** and outlives the process.

`cache.py:329-333`:

```python
def _ensure_stat_index(root: Path) -> None:
    global _stat_index, _stat_index_root, _stat_index_dirty
    if _stat_index_root is not None:
        return                      # bound to the FIRST root, for the life of the process
```

and the key omits the root:

```python
abs_key = str(p.resolve())          # does NOT contain the root
entry = _stat_index.get(abs_key)
if entry and entry["size"] == st.st_size and entry["mtime_ns"] == st.st_mtime_ns:
    return entry["hash"]            # hash computed under a DIFFERENT root
```

What this does in practice, measured on our install:

```
_cache/<project-A>/cache/stat-index.json   5,960 entries, 1.34 MB
   containing paths belonging to projects B and C, which share nothing with A
```

and the user-visible effect for project A:

```
before deleting the poisoned index :  574 files,   0 in cache,    0 nodes
after  deleting the poisoned index :  574 files, 184 in cache, 1,990 nodes
```

**199 cache entries were on disk and invisible.** Had we run a rebuild in that state we would have written an empty graph over a good one (1,911 nodes).

The failure is silent in both directions: on read you are served cache that is not yours; on write you deposit an entry under a key nobody will ever look up. Nothing warns.

### Why this is easy to hit

The CLI is safe — it runs one root per process. But anyone who uses the library across projects is not, and the natural shape is the dangerous one:

```python
# WRONG, and nothing says so
for name, root in projects:
    gc._GRAPHIFY_OUT = str(CACHE / name)
    gc.check_semantic_cache(files, root=root)      # 2nd iteration onward: wrong hashes
```

Resetting the globals by hand between iterations is **not** enough, because the `atexit` handler stays registered and still writes the accumulated index into the last `_GRAPHIFY_OUT` at exit. We verified that: reads came back correct, and the file on disk was still poisoned.

We hit this twice in four days before understanding it, both times noticed only because a number did not add up between two measurements of the same thing.

### Suggested fixes, in order of preference

1. **Key the index by `(root, absolute path)`**, or store the root in the entry and ignore entries whose root differs. This makes multi-root processes correct rather than merely documented.
2. **Keep a dict of indexes per root** instead of one bound index, and flush each to its own location.
3. At minimum: **`warn()` when `_ensure_stat_index` is called with a root different from the bound one** — a one-line change that turns a silent wrong answer into a visible one — and say in the API docs that one process must touch one root.

### Steps to reproduce

    import graphify.cache as gc
    from pathlib import Path

    # two roots, same file content, different relative paths
    # run both in ONE process, as a library user naturally would
    for name, root in [("A", Path("/corpus/a")), ("B", Path("/corpus/b"))]:
        gc._GRAPHIFY_OUT = f"/tmp/out/{name}"
        print(name, gc.file_hash(root / "doc.md", root=root))

    # the second hash is computed under root A: it is the SAME value, although the
    # relative path differs, so it must not be.
    # then inspect /tmp/out/B/cache/stat-index.json and observe it contains
    # absolute paths from corpus A.

Detection on an existing install — a healthy index contains only paths under its own project's source:

    python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]));print(len(d));[print(' ',k) for k in list(d)[:3]]" \
      <graphify-out>/cache/stat-index.json

### Error output or graph output

```text
# poisoned index belonging to project A:
5,960 entries, 1.34 MB
  /corpus/other-project/00-INDEX.md
  /corpus/yet-another/journal/...

# same project, before and after deleting that file:
before:  574 files,   0 in cache,    0 nodes
after :  574 files, 184 in cache, 1,990 nodes

# no warning is emitted in either state — that silence is the report.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.73 (the binding at `cache.py:331` is unchanged from 0.8.18, where we first hit it)

### Operating System

Linux

### Additional context

`stat-index.json` is derived cache, so deleting it is a safe workaround — it regenerates at the cost of recomputing hashes. We now run one subprocess per project, which also works. Both are workarounds for something the library could make correct; option 3 alone would have saved us two incidents.

title: feat(semantic): add cross-chunk semantic similarity reconciliation (#3948)
body:
Closes #3948.

### Problem
In parallel chunked semantic extraction (Step B1/B2), subagents receive an isolated list of files and prompt instructions scoping semantic similarity strictly to their assigned chunk:
> *"Semantic similarity: if two concepts in this chunk solve the same problem..."*

Because subagents operate without shared visibility, identical or paraphrased concepts and design rules residing in different chunks/directories can never be connected by construction. After subagent dispatch, Step B3 only aggregated per-chunk JSONs without any cross-chunk similarity reconciliation. Furthermore, as reported in #3948, naive string overlap (e.g. shingle Jaccard) misses paraphrased rules due to near-zero shared trigrams, while standard TF-IDF cosine suffers dilution when shared principles are surrounded by lengthy document-specific text.

### Solution
1. **Spec & Prompt Guidance**:
   Updated `references/extraction-spec.md` (and `-compact.md`) to clarify that chunk-level subagents extract intra-chunk relationships, while cross-chunk conceptual similarity is reconciled globally after collection.
2. **Reconciliation Module (`graphify/semantic_similarity.py`)**:
   Implemented `reconcile_semantic_similarity(nodes, edges, ...)` comparing `concept` and `rationale` nodes across *different* `source_file`s using a dual-path acceptance strategy:
   - **Path 1 (High Cosine)**: TF-IDF cosine similarity $\ge 0.65$
   - **Path 2 (Rare-term Vocabulary Overlap)**: Moderate cosine combined with shared low-frequency / rare vocabulary, capturing concentrated paraphrases across long documents without false positives.
   - Emits `semantically_similar_to` (`INFERRED`) edges with discrete confidence scores (`0.65`–`0.95`) aligned with the spec rubric.
   - Idempotent and non-duplicating (respects existing connections).
   - Surfaces candidate pairs to stderr during reconciliation.
3. **Pipeline Integration**:
   - Added `reconcile_semantic_similarity` to Step B3 merge in `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md` (and re-rendered all supported host skills via `python -m tools.skillgen`).
   - Wired into `extract_corpus_parallel()` in `graphify/llm.py` for headless and library usage.
4. **Validation**:
   - Added unit and integration tests in `tests/test_semantic_similarity.py` covering high-cosine pairs, rare-term paraphrase detection, same-source-file exclusion, idempotence, existing-edge preservation, and reporting.
   - All 5 skillgen guards pass (`--check`, `--audit-coverage`, `--schema-singleton`, `--monolith-roundtrip`, `--always-on-roundtrip`).
   - Ran `graphify update .` to keep the codebase graph up to date.

title: [Bug]: Lua colon-method calls (obj:method()) are dropped from the call graph
body:
### Summary

Lua colon-method calls (`obj:method()`) are never recorded as call edges. A call to a sibling method via `self:other()` — the standard way one method of a Lua "class" (metatable) invokes another — is silently dropped from the call graph. Dot calls (`M.helper()`) and plain calls (`helper()`) work; only the colon form is affected.

### Version / commit

`v8` @ `ef4450d` (v0.9.73)

### Environment

macOS (darwin 24.6), Python 3.13, tree-sitter-lua via default `uv sync`.

### Minimal reproduction

```lua
-- animal.lua
local Animal = {}

function Animal:speak()
    return self:describe()
end

function Animal:describe()
    return self.name
end
```

```python
from graphify.extract import extract
r = extract(["animal.lua"])
calls = [(e["source"], e["target"]) for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "calls"]
```

### Expected

A `calls` edge `Animal:speak` → `Animal:describe`.

### Actual

No `calls` edge is emitted. Both methods are present as nodes, but the colon call between them is dropped.

### Root cause

A colon call parses as a `method_index_expression` whose callee is in the `method` field and whose receiver is in the `table` field. `_LUA_CONFIG` set `call_accessor_field="name"` (and no object field), so `child_by_field_name("name")` returned `None` and the callee name was never captured.

### Scope

A clean checkout reproduces. `self:` receivers can be resolved against the enclosing method's own table; an arbitrary-object receiver (`other:m()`) stays unresolved (no false binding).

title: [Bug]: PowerShell method calls ($this.M(), [Type]::M()) are dropped from the call graph
body:
### Summary

PowerShell method calls are never recorded as call edges. A call like `$this.Square(3)` from one class method to another — or the static `[Calc]::Make()` form — is silently dropped from the call graph. Only bare command/function invocations (`Helper`) are captured.

### Version / commit

`v8` @ `ef4450d` (v0.9.73)

### Environment

macOS (darwin 24.6), Python 3.13, tree-sitter-powershell via default `uv sync`.

### Minimal reproduction

```powershell
# calc.ps1
class Calc {
    [int] Square([int]$x) { return $x * $x }
    [int] Run() { return $this.Square(3) }
}
```

```python
from graphify.extract import extract_powershell
r = extract_powershell("calc.ps1")
calls = [(e["source"], e["target"]) for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "calls"]
```

### Expected

A `calls` edge `.Run()` → `.Square()`.

### Actual

No `calls` edge. Both methods are present as nodes, but every method invocation is dropped.

### Root cause

The call walker in `graphify/extractors/powershell.py` only handles `command` nodes. A method call parses as an `invokation_expression` (callee in the `member_name` child, args in `argument_list`), which was never visited. A bare property read (`$this.Name`) is a separate `member_access` node and correctly produces no call.

### Scope

A clean checkout reproduces. Member calls should resolve only to methods (not to a free function sharing the name), to avoid false edges on unknown receivers.

title: [Bug]: Erlang local function references (fun Name/Arity) are dropped from the call graph
body:
### Summary

Erlang local function references (`fun Name/Arity`) are never recorded in the call graph. Passing a local function as a callback — `lists:map(fun helper/1, L)`, `spawn(fun loop/0)`, etc., one of the most common idioms in Erlang/OTP — produces no edge, even though the reference names exactly one function.

### Version / commit

`v8` @ `ef4450d` (v0.9.73)

### Environment

macOS (darwin 24.6), Python 3.13, tree-sitter erlang via `tree_sitter_language_pack`.

### Minimal reproduction

```erlang
%% worker.erl
-module(worker).
-export([run/0]).
run() -> lists:map(fun helper/1, [1, 2, 3]).
helper(X) -> X + 1.
```

```python
from graphify.extract import extract
r = extract(["worker.erl"])
edges = [(e["source"], e["target"], e["relation"]) for e in r["edges"]
         if e["relation"] in ("calls", "indirect_call")]
```

### Expected

An `indirect_call` edge `run/0` → `helper/1` (the function is referenced to be invoked, not called on the spot).

### Actual

No edge. `helper/1` is present as a node, but the `fun helper/1` reference is dropped.

### Root cause

The body walker in `graphify/extractors/erlang.py` only handles `call` nodes. A `fun Name/Arity` reference parses as an `internal_fun` node (name in the `fun` field, arity in the `arity` field), which was never visited.

### Scope

A clean checkout reproduces. The arity is part of the reference, so resolution stays exact (a `fun helper/0` must not bind to `helper/1`). Remote references (`fun mod:f/2`, `external_fun`) name an explicit module and belong to the separate cross-file remote-call boundary; they remain unresolved here.

title: fix(lua): resolve colon-method calls (obj:method())
body:
## Problem

Lua colon-method calls (`obj:method()`) are never recorded as call edges. A method invoking a sibling via `self:other()` — the standard way one method of a Lua "class" (metatable) calls another — is silently dropped from the call graph. Dot calls (`M.helper()`) and plain calls (`helper()`) already work; only the colon form is affected.

Fixes #3991.

## Root cause

A colon call parses as a `method_index_expression` whose callee is in the `method` field and whose receiver is in the `table` field. `_LUA_CONFIG` set `call_accessor_field="name"` (and no object field), so `child_by_field_name("name")` returned `None`, the callee name was never captured, and the call was dropped.

## Implementation

- Point `_LUA_CONFIG` at the real fields: `call_accessor_field="method"`, `call_accessor_object_field="table"`.
- Build a per-file map of each method's enclosing table (`Animal` for `Animal:speak`). When a colon call's receiver is the literal `self`, rewrite the bare method name to its table-qualified label (`Animal:other`) so it resolves through the existing `label_to_nid` map — matching either a colon- or dot-defined sibling.
- Fail-closed: a colon call on any other receiver (`other:m()`, a chained receiver) is left unqualified and deferred, so it can never bind by bare name to an unrelated top-level function.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/test_lua_method_calls.py tests/test_lua_import.py -q` — 13 passed. The two positive tests fail on pre-fix `v8` and pass with the fix; the fail-closed and dot/plain-call controls hold both ways.
- `uv run pytest tests -q` (full suite) — green.
- `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run pyright` — clean (0 errors added).

## Limitations

Only the literal `self` receiver is resolved. A call through a variable (`a = Animal; a:m()`) or a remote receiver is intentionally left unresolved rather than guessed.

title: fix(powershell): record method calls ($this.M(), [Type]::M())
body:
## Problem

PowerShell method calls are never recorded as call edges. A call like `$this.Square(3)` between class methods — or the static `[Calc]::Make()` form — is silently dropped from the call graph. Only bare command/function invocations (`Helper`) were captured.

Fixes #3992.

## Root cause

The call walker in `graphify/extractors/powershell.py` only handled `command` nodes. A method call parses as an `invokation_expression` (callee in the `member_name` child, args in `argument_list`), which was never visited.

## Implementation

- Handle `invokation_expression` in the call walk: read the `member_name` and resolve it, mirroring the existing command path.
- Resolve member names against a **method-only** label map (nodes whose label is dot-prefixed, `.M()`), so a member call binds to a method and never to a free function that happens to share the name. On an unknown receiver this is fail-closed (no edge rather than a wrong one).
- A bare property read (`$this.Name`) is a separate `member_access` node and still correctly produces no call.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/test_languages.py -k powershell -q` — 27 passed. The two positive tests fail on pre-fix `v8` and pass with the fix; the fail-closed and command-call controls hold both ways.
- `uv run pytest tests -q` (full suite) — green.
- `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run pyright` — clean.

title: fix(erlang): record local fun references (fun Name/Arity)
body:
## Problem

Erlang local function references (`fun Name/Arity`) are never recorded in the call graph. Passing a local function as a callback — `lists:map(fun helper/1, L)`, `spawn(fun loop/0)`, etc., one of the most common idioms in Erlang/OTP — produced no edge, even though the reference names exactly one function.

Fixes #3993.

## Root cause

The body walker in `graphify/extractors/erlang.py` only handled `call` nodes. A `fun Name/Arity` reference parses as an `internal_fun` node (name in the `fun` field, arity in the `arity` field), which was never visited.

## Implementation

Handle `internal_fun`: resolve the reference by exact name and arity against the module's function table and emit an `indirect_call` edge — the function is handed off to be invoked, not called on the spot (the same relation the engine uses for by-name callbacks elsewhere). `add_edge` already dedups and drops self-edges.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest tests/test_erlang_extractor.py -q` — 9 passed. The positive test fails on pre-fix `v8` and passes with the fix; the arity, direct-call, and anonymous-fun controls hold both ways.
- `uv run pytest tests -q` (full suite) — green.
- `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run pyright` — clean (0 errors).

## Limitations

Remote references (`fun mod:f/2`, node type `external_fun`) name an explicit module and belong to the separate cross-file remote-call boundary; they remain unresolved here. Anonymous `fun ... end` bodies are still walked for the direct calls inside them.

title: fix(build): keep a same-id hyperedge from an untouched file on update
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3981.

`build_merge` carries forward the hyperedges of files that weren't re-extracted, but it skipped any carried hyperedge whose `id` also appeared in the new chunks, whichever file the new one came from ([`build.py#L2159`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/ef4450d9c28acb2b8cdc22d369c1777b77148eef/graphify/build.py#L2159)). Hyperedge ids are chosen per extraction, so two docs can both emit `shared_flow`. A full build keeps both, but re-extracting only `b.md` silently drops `a.md`'s.

One note on the diagnosis in the issue: it points at `export.attach_hyperedges`, but `build_merge` hasn't called that since the fix for #3102 (3378ae8), which moved the same id-only check into `build_merge`'s own carry loop. That loop is what this PR changes. `attach_hyperedges` is untouched.

The check now matches on `(id, source_file)`. The new side's `source_file` goes through `_norm_source_file` exactly like the carried side already does, and an empty `source_file` counts as missing. A hyperedge re-emitted from the same file (relative or absolute path), or a source-less one re-emitted without a source, still replaces the carried copy as before. `merge_raw_extraction` (the `--no-cluster` path) already replaces hyperedges per source with no id-only check, so the two paths now agree.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: on an incremental update, a hyperedge is replaced only when its own source file is re-extracted (replace-per-source, like nodes and edges), so `--update` ends with the same hyperedge set a full build would.

Behavior change: after an update, `graph.json` can now hold two hyperedges with the same `id` from different files. A full build already writes exactly that (step 1 of the repro in #3981).

Not changed here, and worth a follow-up if you agree:
- `watch.py` has the same id-only skip when it preserves hyperedges ([`watch.py#L1082`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/ef4450d9c28acb2b8cdc22d369c1777b77148eef/graphify/watch.py#L1082)). The AST-only rebuild there doesn't produce hyperedges today, so the check has nothing to match.
- `merge-graphs` dedups collected hyperedges by id through `attach_hyperedges`, so two same-id hyperedges inside one input graph would still collapse there.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

## How was this tested?

Two tests in `tests/test_build_merge_hyperedges_and_prune.py`. One is the regression from the issue. The other covers the re-emissions that must still replace the carried copy (same file in absolute form, and source-less with an empty `source_file`). I checked that each part of the new key matters: reverting to id-only, deleting the check, skipping the normalization, or dropping the empty-as-missing rule each makes one of the two tests fail.

Windows 11, Python 3.11, `uv sync --frozen`:

```text
# reporter's script from #3981, step 2 output
before (ef4450d): [('shared_flow', 'b.md')]
after:            [('shared_flow', 'a.md'), ('shared_flow', 'b.md')]

uv run pytest tests/test_build_merge_hyperedges_and_prune.py -k "shares_an_id or re_emits"
  ef4450d:     1 failed, 1 passed
               AssertionError: assert ['flow B v2'] == ['flow A', 'flow B v2']
  this branch: 2 passed

uv run pytest tests/ -q
  ef4450d:     65 failed, 5978 passed, 145 skipped
  this branch: 65 failed, 5980 passed, 145 skipped   (run as two halves)
  (the 65 failing test ids are identical on both; they already fail on a clean
   checkout on this Windows machine, e.g. hooks, cp1252 decoding, deleting the
   cwd. None are in build/merge/hyperedge tests. The +2 are the new tests.)

uv run ruff check .                  All checks passed!
uv run pyright graphify/build.py     13 errors before and after, none in the changed lines
python -m tools.skillgen --check / --audit-coverage / --schema-singleton /
  --monolith-roundtrip / --always-on-roundtrip    all ok
```

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (n/a, no fragment changes)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed that no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

title: Kotlin extractor throws UnboundLocalError on large files with nested lambdas
body:
## Description
Graphify fails to parse several Kotlin files with `UnboundLocalError` in the Kotlin extractor, producing incomplete graph nodes/edges.

## Affected patterns
- Large classes (~500–2000 LOC) with many nested lambdas and anonymous callbacks
- Android callbacks (SensorEventListener, LocationCallback, Handler/Runnable)
- Sealed classes with extensive `when` branches combined with nested lambdas
- Partial extraction observed in some medium-sized files

## Root cause
The Python-based Kotlin AST visitor raises `UnboundLocalError` when traversing deeply nested anonymous callbacks/lambdas. The exception interrupts file traversal, so symbols after the failure point are not extracted.

## Impact
- Missing code nodes/edges for affected files
- Incomplete cross-file relationships
- Extraction appears to skip affected files entirely in severe cases

## Reproduction
1. Process a Kotlin codebase containing large classes with nested anonymous listeners/lambdas
2. Run extraction (`graphify update .`)
3. Observe `UnboundLocalError` during Kotlin parsing and missing nodes for those files

## Expected
Kotlin files parse without internal extractor errors regardless of nesting depth or LOC.

## Environment
- graphifyy 0.9.70
- Python 3.10.17

## Notes
Likely an initialization/order bug in the Kotlin extractor visitor (use of a local variable before assignment in a branch). The issue is in the extractor, not the input files.

title: `graphify label` / `cluster-only` silently drops parallel edges (rebuilds the graph as a simple nx.Graph and writes it back)
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.73 (also seen on 0.9.16)

**What happens**

`graphify label .` and `graphify cluster-only .` reload `graph.json` with
`build_from_json(_raw, directed=_directed)` (`cli.py`, around line 2101), which creates
a simple `nx.Graph()` (`build.py`, around line 1031). A simple graph keeps **one edge
per node pair**, so when `graph.json` contains two edges between the same pair
(for example an `imports` edge and a `calls` edge between the same two nodes, or
edges added by an external tool), all but one are lost when the command writes
`graph.json` back. Nothing is printed about it.

This looks like the same root cause that #2074 fixed for `graphify path` (loading
with `"multigraph": True` so parallel links "survive load instead of being silently
collapsed last-writer-wins"), but the `cluster-only` / `label` path still loads a
simple graph and then **writes it back to disk**, so the loss is persistent.

**Minimal reproduction (0.9.73)**

```bash
mkdir -p repro/graphify-out && cd repro
cat > graphify-out/graph.json <<'JSON'
{"directed": false, "multigraph": false, "graph": {}, "nodes": [
 {"id": "a", "label": "a", "file_type": "code", "source_file": "a.py"},
 {"id": "b", "label": "b", "file_type": "code", "source_file": "a.py"},
 {"id": "c", "label": "c", "file_type": "code", "source_file": "a.py"}],
 "links": [
 {"source": "a", "target": "b", "relation": "imports", "confidence": "EXTRACTED", "source_file": "a.py"},
 {"source": "a", "target": "b", "relation": "calls",   "confidence": "EXTRACTED", "source_file": "a.py"},
 {"source": "b", "target": "c", "relation": "calls",   "confidence": "EXTRACTED", "source_file": "a.py"}]}
JSON
uvx --from graphifyy==0.9.73 graphify cluster-only .
```

Output says `Graph: 3 nodes, 2 edges`. Before: 3 links. After: 2 links —
`(a, b, calls)` is gone from `graph.json`.

**Measured on a real graph** (~45,600 nodes, 0.9.16, `label`): 69,784 edges before,
69,462 after. 322 edges lost, none with a missing endpoint, and every one of them
was a second edge on a node pair that stayed connected by another edge.

**Expected**

Re-clustering / labeling should not change the edge set. Either keep parallel
edges (load into a `MultiGraph` as #2074 does, or cluster on a simple projection
and write the original link list back), or at least warn with the number of edges
that will be collapsed.

**Workaround we use:** re-adding the extra edges after every `label` run.

**Side note (separate, minor):** running the command via `uvx --from graphifyy==<newer>`
also rewrote the user's installed Claude skill (`~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`
and `references/`) to the newer packaged version. `SKILL.md` got a `.bak`, but
`references/` did not. It was unexpected for a `cluster-only` run. Happy to open
that as its own issue if useful.

title: fix(resolution): prefer source entry over built dist in workspace packages (#3834)
body:
Fixes #3834.

### Problem
A workspace package declaring `"main": "./dist/index.js"` (or `"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"`, etc.) without an `exports` map resolves to its built `dist/index.js` whenever the package has been built locally. Because build output directories like `dist/` are outside the indexed corpus (and in `_SKIP_DIRS`), the target node is absent from the graph and the import edge is silently dropped. On a clean clone without `dist/`, resolution fell through to `src/index`, causing graph extraction to depend on whether local build artifacts were present.

### Solution
In `_resolve_workspace_import` within `graphify/extractors/resolution.py`:
- Identify when a resolved candidate falls within a known build-output directory (`dist`, `build`, `target`, `out`, `dist-protected`) relative to the package directory.
- Defer build-output matches as fallback candidates so that source candidates (`src/index`, bare `index`) are tried first.
- If a source candidate exists, it is selected regardless of whether local build outputs exist. If no source candidate exists, the build artifact remains as a fallback.
- Added regression tests in `tests/test_js_import_resolution.py`.

title: Elixir extractor: unqualified bare-name calls attach to unrelated same-named nodes, producing fake god nodes
body:
# Upstream issue draft for Graphify-Labs/graphify

Title: **Elixir extractor: unqualified bare-name calls attach to unrelated same-named nodes, producing fake god nodes**

## Summary

The Elixir AST extractor resolves unqualified function calls by bare name, ignoring import scope and arity. When a name is defined somewhere in the repo (so a definition-anchored node exists) and *called* elsewhere as a DSL/framework function, every call site attaches to the definition node. One node can collect hundreds of false `calls` edges, become the #1 god node, and distort Louvain clustering.

## Observed (repo: Elixir umbrella, ~10 apps, migrations under `priv/repo/migrations/`; graphifyy 0.9.56)

- `table()` — node anchored at `apps/ecosystem_web/lib/ecosystem_web/components/core_components.ex:677` (a Phoenix function component). Collected **690 `calls` edges whose `source_file` is a migration file** (`change()`/`up()`/`down()` callers across 8 apps) — these are Ecto.Migration `table/2` usages. Result: 691-edge #1 god node, clustered with migrations instead of UI components.
- `remove()` — anchored at an ETS registry helper (`agent_session_registry.ex:91`); 106 edges from migrations (Ecto.Migration `remove/1`).
- `execute()` — two separate definition-anchored nodes (a mix task and a seeds file) each collected migration `execute/1` edges (54 + 38).
- `create()` ×4, `add()`, `index()` — same pattern (Ecto.Migration DSL, anchored in unrelated manager/notification/config files).
- `select()` — anchored at a domain function (`membership.ex:12`); 147 edges from other apps' Ecto.Query pipelines.
- `build()` — anchored at a test factory; 109 edges from other apps' factory usages (ExMachina `build/2`).
- `push_flash()` — anchored at one LiveView; 89 edges from other components (Phoenix.LiveView `push_flash/3`).

## Root cause

Call-edge resolution does not consider the caller's imports/aliases. The only node that exists for a bare name is wherever the name happens to be *defined*; unqualified DSL calls therefore join it.

## Suggested fix (either)

1. Resolve unqualified calls against the caller module's `import`/`alias`/`require` set before matching a node, or
2. When the call-site file differs from the def-site file and the bare name matches a known DSL surface (Ecto.Migration, Ecto.Query, Kernel, ExMachina, Phoenix.LiveView), emit a qualified external-dependency node (e.g. `ecto_migration_table`, label "Ecto.Migration table/2") instead of joining the definition node.

## Workaround we used (happy to contribute)

Detection: any node whose `source_file` is not a migration context but whose incident edges are >50% from migration paths (degree ≥ 5), plus known framework names with >20 cross-file `calls` edges. Repair: re-point those edges to external DSL nodes (`confidence: INFERRED, 0.95`), keep the definition node's real local edges, re-cluster. 1,212 edges re-pointed across 13 nodes; god-node list went from 4/10 artifacts to a clean ranking. Script available on request.

title: [Bug]: Dart conditional import/export links only the default URI, dropping the platform implementation
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

The Dart extractor only links the **default** URI of a configurable (conditional) `import`/`export` directive. Every `if (...)` alternative is dropped:

```dart
// lib/service.dart
export 'service_stub.dart'
    if (dart.library.io) 'service_io.dart';
```

produces a single `exports` edge to `service_stub.dart`; there is no edge to `service_io.dart`.

This is the standard Flutter facade pattern for platform-specific code, and the stub is usually an empty placeholder while the real implementation lives in the `if` branch. As a result the implementation file becomes unreachable through the facade: everything that imports `service.dart` appears to depend only on the stub, and `explain`/`path` on the implementation file see no link from the facade or its importers.

Expected: one edge per URI in the directive - the default one plus each conditional alternative (`service_stub.dart` and `service_io.dart` above). The same applies to conditional `import` directives.

Cause: both patterns in `graphify/extractors/dart.py` (section "6. Imports and Exports") match only the first quoted string after `import`/`export`:

```python
r"""^\s*export\s+['"]([^'"]+)['"]"""
```

Note that a condition may itself contain a string literal (`if (app.flavor == 'prod') 'flags_prod.dart'`), so a naive "all quoted strings in the directive" approach would mint a bogus `prod` node.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p repro/lib && cd repro
printf "export 'service_stub.dart'\n    if (dart.library.io) 'service_io.dart';\n" > lib/service.dart
printf "class Service {}\n" > lib/service_stub.dart
printf "class Service {\n  void connect() {}\n}\n" > lib/service_io.dart

python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract_dart
for e in extract_dart(Path("lib/service.dart"))["edges"]:
    print(e["relation"], "->", e["target"])
PY
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
exports -> service_stub_dart
```

Expected:

```text
exports -> service_stub_dart
exports -> service_io_dart
```

On a real Flutter app (~300 Dart files) all four such facades in the project were affected: the graph had no edge from any facade to its `*_io.dart` implementation.

### Graphify version

0.9.73 (reproduced on `v8` @ e10df08 / 0.9.74 as well - the Dart extractor is unchanged there)

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables are needed - this is pure AST/regex extraction. Reproduced from a clean checkout of `v8`.

title: fix(dart): link every URI of a configurable import/export (#4002)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4002.

The Dart extractor matched `import`/`export` directives only up to the first quoted string, so every `if (...)` alternative of a configurable directive was dropped:

```dart
export 'service_stub.dart' if (dart.library.io) 'service_io.dart';
```

produced only `exports -> service_stub.dart`. In the usual Flutter facade the stub is an empty placeholder and the real implementation lives in the conditional branch, so the implementation was unreachable from the facade and everything importing it.

Change (section "6. Imports and Exports" of `graphify/extractors/dart.py`):

- the whole directive is parsed: default URI, then any number of `if (<dotted.name> [== '<value>']) '<uri>'` branches (single or double quotes, across line breaks);
- the default URI keeps exactly the edge it had before (same relation, no context);
- each alternative gets the same relation (`imports`/`exports`) tagged `context="conditional_uri"` and its own `source_location`, so consumers can tell the platform-selected branches from the default one;
- a string literal inside the condition (`if (app.flavor == 'prod')`) is part of the URI test and is not emitted as a URI.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: an import/export edge is emitted for every library URI the directive names, and only for those. The default-URI edge is unchanged (same target, relation, line, no context), so existing graphs and caches do not change for non-configurable directives; only new `conditional_uri` edges (and their target stub nodes) appear for configurable ones. No persisted-state format change.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Limitations: URIs are still minted as unresolved targets keyed by the URI string, exactly like the default URI today; resolving Dart URIs to file nodes is #2329 / #2570 and out of scope here. String interpolation in a URI is not valid Dart and is not handled.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_dart.py -k conditional   # on unpatched v8: 1 failed (regression test reproduces the bug)
uv run pytest tests/test_dart.py tests/test_extract.py   # with the fix: 242 passed, 4 skipped
uv run pytest tests -q   # 6136 passed, 102 skipped, 28 failed - the same 28 fail on unpatched v8
                         # (erlang / r / solidity / vbnet extractors, ollama retry cap; local environment)
uv run ruff check .      # All checks passed
uv run pyright graphify/extractors/dart.py   # 0 errors
```

Also ran `graphify extract . --code-only` on a ~300-file Flutter app: all four conditional-export facades in the project now link to their `*_io.dart` implementations (before: no edge from any facade to its implementation).

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

title: fix(path): route through a contains edge back out to its file (#3878)
body:
Fixes #3878.

`contains` only runs file → symbol. A route that reaches a symbol via an `imports`/`calls`/`references` hop had no edge back out to the file that defines it, so a file-to-file dependency that must route through a shared symbol — the common case for cross-file dependencies — reported "No directed path found" even though both halves of the route existed in the graph.

Fix: add the implied reverse hop (symbol → its containing file) to `path`'s own directed traversal graph, for routing purposes only. The printed segment still recovers the real stored `contains` edge and its true direction from the graph, same as any other hop, so the output stays honest about what is actually stored — it just lets the route continue instead of dead-ending.

Scoped to the directed case (`path`'s default). `--undirected` already treats every edge as bidirectional, so this doesn't touch that branch.

Verified: reproduced the issue's exact edge shape (file --imports--> symbol, other-file --contains--> symbol, no direct file-to-file edge) against a fresh synthetic graph, confirmed "No directed path found" pre-fix, confirmed a correct 2-hop route post-fix. New regression test added to `tests/test_path_cli.py`, confirmed to fail against pre-fix code. Full suite passes (only the pre-existing unrelated extractor failures for erlang/r/solidity/vbnet, all due to missing optional tree-sitter packages).

title: fix(cache): rebind the stat index on a cache root switch (#3989)
body:
Fixes #3989.

`_ensure_stat_index` bound to the first root/cache_root a process ever saw and returned immediately for every later call, for the life of the process. A read for a later root silently came from the first root's file, and at exit the accumulated in-memory index — now holding entries for every root ever touched — was written back into the first root's file alone, poisoning it with paths from unrelated projects (exactly as measured in the issue: a project's own `stat-index.json` filling up with paths from two other, unrelated projects).

Went with the issue's preferred fix (option 2: a correct per-root index, not just a warning) plus the minimum-fix warning (option 3) on top:

- On a call naming a different cache root than the one currently bound, flush the outgoing root's own pending entries to its own file, then load the new root fresh — so each root's file only ever holds that root's own entries, and revisiting an earlier root in the same process reloads its real state instead of starting empty or staying bound to whatever is current.
- Warn (`RuntimeWarning`) on the switch, so a library caller crossing project roots in one process sees it rather than losing the fastpath silently.
- The resolved stat-index path is captured at bind time rather than re-derived from the live out-directory at flush time — a caller following the documented "set the out directory, then call" pattern has already pointed it at the new root by the time the switch is noticed, so re-deriving then would flush the outgoing root's entries into the new root's file instead of its own.

The CLI path (one root per process) is unaffected — this only changes behavior when a second distinct root is actually seen in the same process.

Verified: reproduced the issue's exact two-project repro shape, confirmed pre-fix that the second project's file ends up empty/missing and the first project's file gets polluted with the second project's paths; confirmed post-fix each project gets its own correct file and the switch is warned. New tests added in `tests/test_stat_index_multi_root.py`, confirmed to fail against pre-fix code. Full suite passes (only the pre-existing unrelated extractor failures for erlang/r/solidity/vbnet, all due to missing optional tree-sitter packages) — ran the existing cache/detect/stat-index test files individually too, all green (the fix does add `RuntimeWarning` noise to a few existing tests that share process state across unrelated `tmp_path` roots without resetting between tests, which is expected and non-fatal — no test asserts on warning count).

title: fix(merge-graphs): restore the previous merged community via --previous (#3858)
body:
Fixes #3858.

`merge-graphs` offsets each input's own communities into a shared id space so they don't fuse into one meta-node (#3014). In a multi-source pipeline, that per-source partition is what the input graph's `community` field holds — it has no relation to the previous **merged** clustering `.graphify_labels.json`/`.graphify_labels.json.sig` were actually written against. `cluster-only`'s label-reuse remap reads that `community` field as "the previous clustering" and silently mismatches almost every community, since it's actually fresh per-source ids — exactly the breakage measured in the issue (1,130/1,709 communities renamed by hub on one real pipeline).

Implements the first of the issue's two suggested fixes: `merge-graphs --previous <previous-merged-graph.json>` reads a prior merged output and restores its real `community` value onto each node that survives the merge, by node id, before the per-source offset is ever written out. A node with no match in the previous file (new since the last merge) gets no `community` rather than keeping an unrelated per-source offset. The per-source partition stays available regardless, in `local_community`.

This productizes the issue's own 10-line workaround script directly into the command.

Verified: two new regression tests in `tests/test_merge_graphs_cli.py` covering the exact shape (a real previous merged clustering restored by id vs. the fresh per-source offset, and a new node correctly getting no stale community), confirmed to fail against pre-fix code. Full suite passes (only the pre-existing unrelated extractor failures for erlang/r/solidity/vbnet, all due to missing optional tree-sitter packages).

title: feat(bash): record a script's invocation of another script as an edge (#3802)
body:
Fixes #3802.

The bash extractor recorded functions, `source` imports, and calls between functions, but nothing for the programs a script actually runs. In a pipeline driven by a shell script that's most of what the script does, so an orchestrator looked disconnected from every stage it runs — `graphify path "runner.sh" "stage_one.py"` found nothing even though the dependency is right there on the page.

Implements the issue's suggested heuristic: when a command's first word is a known interpreter (`python`, `python3`, `python2`, `node`, `nodejs`, `ruby`, `perl`) or a bare variable standing in for one (`"$PYTHON" scripts/stage_two.py`), and an argument resolves to an existing file in the repo with a recognized script extension, emit an `invokes` edge (INFERRED) from the calling scope to that file.

Kept entirely separate from the existing bash-to-bash runner handling (`bash`/`sh`/`zsh`/`ksh`/`dash` plus direct `./script.sh` invocation), which still emits its own `calls` edge unchanged — this is purely additive, not a rewrite of the existing logic, so it can't regress the `.sh`-to-`.sh` path.

Gated on the target actually existing on disk, same as every other heuristic edge in this file, so a plain command that happens to take a `.py`-looking argument (`cp`, a custom tool) is never mistaken for an interpreter invocation.

Verified against the issue's exact example:
```
PYTHON="python3"
python3 scripts/stage_one.py --client "$C"
bash scripts/other_step.sh "$C"
"$PYTHON" scripts/stage_two.py
```
now produces `invokes` edges to both `.py` stages (plus the existing `calls` edge to the `.sh` stage), and `graphify path "runner.sh" "stage_one.py"` finds the route:
```
Shortest path (2 hops):
  runner.sh --contains--> runner.sh script --invokes--> stage_one.py
```

Six new regression tests in `tests/test_extract.py`, confirmed to fail against pre-fix code (except the two negative cases, which hold either way). Full suite passes (only the pre-existing unrelated extractor failures for erlang/r/solidity/vbnet, all due to missing optional tree-sitter packages).

title: [Feature]: Dart part files should keep their own file node (linked to the library), not vanish from the graph
body:
### Problem or use case

A Dart `part of` file has no node of its own in the graph. Since #1098 the extractor redirects the part's declarations to the parent library (good - one library, one id namespace), but it also drops the part's file node entirely (`test_roadmap_bug_fixes` asserts "No child file node should be created").

As a result a real, scanned source file cannot be looked up by name:

```text
$ graphify explain "bg_account_runtime.dart"
No node matching 'bg_account_runtime.dart' found.
```

`path` cannot start from or reach it either. In Flutter apps parts are commonly used to split one large library across several big files (in our app: a 2,500-line `part of 'background_service_entry.dart'` and four `part of 'mail_dao.dart'` files), so these are exactly the files an assistant wants to ask about before reading them. Today the only way is to know which library owns the part and ask about the library instead.

### Proposed solution

Keep the redirect, but keep the part's file node too:

- the part gets its regular file node (`id` from its own path, `label` = file name, `source_file` = the part);
- `library --includes--> part`, anchored on the `part of` line;
- `part --contains--> declaration` for every declaration the library `defines` from this part.

Declaration ids stay in the library's namespace and the library's `defines` edges are unchanged, so the split that #1098 fixed does not come back. `explain "<part>.dart"` then lists the part's declarations and its library.

### Alternatives considered

- Status quo + documenting "ask the parent library": works, but every consumer has to know the `part of` structure in advance.
- Moving `defines` from the library to the part: would re-split the library's namespace and break the redirect contract, so no.

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

- Node/edge ids: no existing id changes. Adds one file node per part file plus `includes` and `contains` edges.
- graph.json schema / cache semantics: unchanged (`includes` is already used by the Blade extractor). Existing graphs pick the new nodes up on the next rebuild.
- `test_roadmap_bug_fixes` currently asserts the part has no node; that assertion has to flip to "the part has its own node, its declarations are still defined by the library".

### Additional context

Found together with #4002 on a ~300-file Flutter app (graphify 0.9.73; the extractor is unchanged on `v8` @ e10df08 / 0.9.74).

title: feat(extract): warn when a cleanly parsed file yields no symbols (#3946)
body:
Addresses the first of #3946's three proposals: making a symbol-free extraction visible.

A code file that parses with zero errors but still produces nothing beyond its own bare file node is usually a plain data literal the AST extractor has nothing to model (`const BANK = [...]`, `module.exports = [...]`), not a code file that legitimately has no symbols. Those two cases looked identical in the output — the file silently entered the graph as an isolated, zero-edge node, and nothing reported it. The issue measured 88 such nodes on a real corpus, 3.10 MB / ~369,500 words, 39.5% of the corpus, with not one edge among them.

Added a complementary check right next to the existing syntax-error warning, gated on the opposite condition (no `parse_errors` and no extractor `error`) so the two can never double-report the same file — a file already explained by a genuine parse error or a missing optional dependency (the `tree-sitter-*-not-installed` case) is excluded here.

Scoped deliberately narrower than the issue's own repro: only flags a file whose extraction produced **nothing but the file node itself** (the `module.exports = [...]`, `export default [...]`, `window.X = [...]`, bare `var X = [...]` shapes — 5 of the issue's 7 examples). Left out the "file node plus a binding with no functions/classes" case (`const BANK = [...]`, `export const BANK = [...]`) for now, since reliably distinguishing a plain binding from a real symbol (a class, say) across every language extractor without false positives is a bigger, separate piece of work — happy to follow up if that's wanted.

The issue's other two proposals (re-routing symbol-free files through semantic extraction as documents, and giving isolated file nodes their size in `GRAPH_REPORT.md`) are bigger behavioral/design changes not attempted here.

Verified against the issue's exact 7-file reproduction — the new warning correctly names the 5 fully-symbol-free files and stays silent on the 2 that produce a binding node. Four new regression tests in `tests/test_partial_extraction_warning.py`, confirmed to fail against pre-fix code (except the two negative-case tests, which hold either way). Full suite passes (only the pre-existing unrelated extractor failures for erlang/r/solidity/vbnet, all due to missing optional tree-sitter packages — confirmed those files are correctly excluded from the new warning too, since they carry an extractor `error`, not a clean empty parse).

title: fix(export): stop cluster-only/label from dropping parallel edges (#3999)
body:
Fixes #3999.

`cluster-only`/`label` reload an existing `graph.json` into a simple `Graph` to re-cluster (`build_from_json`), which keeps one edge per node pair. Writing that same graph back out then silently dropped a second edge on any pair that stayed connected by another — an `imports` edge and a `calls` edge between the same two nodes, say. A real corpus measured in the issue lost 322 edges this way across one run, every one of them a second edge on a pair that stayed connected by the other.

Went with the issue's own suggested alternative ("cluster on a simple projection and write the original link list back") rather than changing `build_from_json`'s graph type globally — that function is the core graph loader used everywhere (`query`, `explain`, `serve`, `analyze`, clustering, scoring, ...), so switching it to a `MultiGraph` across the board would be a much larger, riskier change than this bug warrants, and community is purely a node attribute — re-clustering never needs to add or remove an edge in the first place.

Added an `original_links` parameter to `export.to_json`: when given, it writes back every original link verbatim instead of re-deriving the link list from the simple graph, dropping only a link whose endpoint no longer exists in the graph. Wired `cluster-only`/`label` to pass the links already loaded from the input file. This also sidesteps any endpoint-order canonicalization undirected storage would otherwise apply when deriving the link list from `G`, since the original links keep their exact stored endpoint order. The parameter is opt-in and defaults to `None` (previous behavior) — a fresh extraction build has no prior links to preserve, since the graph it just built is the only authoritative source, so every other caller of `to_json` is unaffected.

Verified against the issue's exact minimal reproduction — before: 3 links, after this fix: still 3 links (previously 2, with `(a, b, calls)` silently gone). Three new regression tests (one through the real `cluster-only` CLI command, one direct unit test on `to_json`), confirmed to fail against pre-fix code. Full suite passes (only the pre-existing unrelated extractor failures for erlang/r/solidity/vbnet, all due to missing optional tree-sitter packages).

(The issue's side note about `uvx --from graphifyy==<newer>` unexpectedly rewriting the installed Claude skill is a separate concern and not addressed here.)

title: fix(python): bind self and super calls within the caller's class chain
body:
### what does this pr do?

self.save() in one class gets wired to the save() of a different class whenever another class in the same file also defines save(). self, cls and super are exempt from the python member-call defer because the receiver is the callers own instance, but the lookup they fall through to is the file-wide label_to_nid, which keeps only the last definition of each name. so the last class declared in the file wins, and the edge comes out EXTRACTED.

found it by running the same call through two declaration orders, the target flipped with the order. on httpx at b5addb6 (23 files, 305 calls edges) 40 calls edges sat on the wrong method. the whole sync Client chain (get, post, ... -> request -> send -> send_handling_auth -> send_handling_redirects -> send_single_request) pointed into AsyncClient, which _client.py declares later. every super().__init__() in _exceptions.py pointed at RequestNotRead.__init__, the last __init__ in that file, and AsyncClient.__init__ called itself. graphify itself has the same fake recursion in security.py from super().redirect_request().

the call now resolves against the enclosing class first, then its in-file bases nearest first, with super skipping the class itself. same order the objc resolver already uses for self. two bases on one level that both define the method is an mro tie, so neither gets bound. a method of a class outside the chain is never the target. a module-level function stored on the instance (self.handler = handler) still binds like before, its not a method of any class.

ts, swift and ruby bind this.save() and self.save() the same last-writer way. they dont record the receiver at that point in the engine, so those are separate prs.

### type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

### verification & invariants

a self, cls or super call never binds to a method of a class outside the callers own class chain. a nested def follows the enclosing methods self. calls whose receiver is anything else take the existing paths unchanged, and the cross-file pass is not touched.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

### how was this tested?

windows 11 arm64, python 3.14, venv from uv sync --all-extras.

```text
python -m pytest tests/test_extract.py -k python_self    5 passed, 4 of them fail on v8 (the stored-callable one passes on both)
python -m pytest tests/test_python*.py tests/test_extract.py tests/test_languages.py tests/test_multilang.py tests/test_build.py tests/test_analyze.py    949 passed, 2 failed (both fail on v8 too: windows MAX_PATH and cp1252 locale)
python -m pytest tests/<file> per file                    every failing test also fails the same way on unpatched v8 on this box (windows only: read-only replace, cp1252 locale, fifo/unix socket/symlink setup, deleting cwd, install paths, hook git setup)
python -m ruff check .                                    all checks passed
python -m pyright graphify/extractors/engine.py           34 errors, the same 34 as v8
```

httpx b5addb6, extract() over httpx/*.py, before vs after, spot checked against the source:

```text
calls edges          305 -> 299   (40 removed, 34 added)
Client.get           -> AsyncClient.request       now Client.request
Client.send          -> AsyncClient.send_handling_auth   now Client.send_handling_auth
RequestError.__init__ -> RequestNotRead.__init__  now HTTPError.__init__
AsyncClient.__init__  -> AsyncClient.__init__     now BaseClient.__init__
DataField.render     -> FileField.render_data     now DataField.render_data
```

title: fix(js): bind this calls to the caller's own class
body:
### what does this pr do?

stacked on the python self-call pr (fix(python): bind self and super calls within the caller's class chain), so the first commit here is that one. only the second commit is new, happy to rebase once that lands.

follow up to the python self-call fix, same bug in js and ts. this.save() in one class is resolved through the file-wide label_to_nid, which keeps only the last definition of each name, so it lands on the save() of whichever class the file declares last, as EXTRACTED.

a this or super call never moves off a method its own class defines. calls the own class doesnt define, and every other receiver, take the same path as before.

## What does this PR do?

Closes #4008.

Since #1098 a `part of` file's declarations are redirected to the parent library, so one library has one id namespace. The redirect also dropped the part's own file node, so a scanned source file could not be found by name:

title: fix(extract): refuse a dedup shrink unless the user accepts it
body:
## What does this PR do?

A finished `graphify extract` must not replace `graph.json` when dedup is what made the graph smaller. Fixes #3774.

`graphify <path>` rewrites itself to `extract`. A complete run then calls `to_json(..., force=True)`, so the #479 node-count check never runs. Dedup is on by default, and `build_merge` also skips its own shrink check while dedup is on. A graph built with dedup off can be rewritten smaller, with no error.

This change counts nodes dedup merged away (`build()` sets `_dedup_collapsed`, popped before `to_json` so it is not stored). If the new node count is still below the saved count after nodes removed for deleted files are subtracted, the command exits before `to_json` and leaves `graph.json` as it was. The message names the old count, the new count, and `--allow-dedup-shrink`.

`--allow-dedup-shrink` writes that smaller graph. A deleted file still writes with no extra flag. `--allow-partial` stays the flag for an incomplete extraction. `--no-dedup` still skips dedup. Dedup matching is unchanged (that is #3094).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: a complete extract does not overwrite a larger `graph.json` when the extra loss is a dedup merge. A file deletion still overwrites. Persistent graph state is the file on disk; a refused run does not stamp the manifest, because the process exits before that write.
