title: fix(elixir): scope unqualified calls to imported and used modules
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4001.

The shared cross-file call pass resolves an unqualified call by bare name against every definition in the corpus ([`extract.py#L8404`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/e10df08877f8819a625a1afa38c3297a31fda296/graphify/extract.py#L8404)). That's wrong for Elixir: an unqualified call can only reach the caller's own module, Kernel, or a module the file `import`s or `use`s. So every migration's `table(:users)`, which comes from Ecto.Migration via `use Ecto.Migration`, became a `calls` edge to whatever project function happened to be named `table`. In the report, a Phoenix component collected 690 of these edges and became the top god node. This isn't limited to DSLs. On #2556, @norbu09 measured the cross-file Elixir calls this pass produced on a 904-file app as 207, "mostly noise" (`users → count`, `attrs → required`).

The Elixir extractor now records on each raw call the modules its file names in `import` or `use`. `alias` and `require` don't bring functions into scope, so they're left out. The shared pass then keeps only candidates whose file defines one of those modules, and leaves the call unresolved otherwise. The filter sits right after the existing Go `import_path` filter, which works the same way. The per-file module index is built from `resolution_nodes` using the `_elixir_module` marker that #3603 already carries through the incremental allow-lists, so it also holds on `graphify update`.

Repro: five files through `extract()`. A migration with `use Ecto.Migration` + `table(:users)`; `core_components.ex` defining `table/1`; `helpers.ex` defining `fmt/1`; `user.ex` with `import MyApp.Helpers` + `fmt(x)`; `other.ex` calling `fmt(x)` with no import.

```text
before (e10df08):
  change() (20240101000000_create_users.exs) --calls[INFERRED 0.85]--> table() (core_components.ex)
  go() (other.ex)   --calls[INFERRED 0.85]--> fmt() (helpers.ex)
  show() (user.ex)  --calls[INFERRED 0.85]--> fmt() (helpers.ex)
after:
  show() (user.ex)  --calls[INFERRED 0.85]--> fmt() (helpers.ex)
```

Known limits, left out on purpose:
- If a `use` macro imports another module indirectly (`use MyAppWeb, :live_view` importing `CoreComponents`), that import isn't in the source, so bare calls into it are no longer resolved. This is the same fail-closed trade as the JS/TS import gate in #1659.
- An `import` written with an alias's short name (`alias MyApp.Helpers` then `import Helpers`) and an `import` inside a function body don't count as scope yet, so those calls also stay unresolved.
- Scoping is per file: a candidate counts if its file defines an imported top-level module. That only over-matches when a file defines several top-level modules.
- Matches inside the import scope stay `INFERRED`. The Go branch promotes its matches to `EXTRACTED`; I kept this PR to removing the false edges.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: an unqualified Elixir call resolves across files only to a definition that is in scope for the caller, meaning its file defines a module the caller imports or uses. Same-file calls are still resolved by the extractor and are unchanged, as are qualified `Mod.fun()` calls, which the shared pass already skips.

title: [Bug]: one C# partial class drops every recursive call in the graph, in every language
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

When a corpus contains a C# `partial class` split across two files (the default WinForms/WPF shape: `Form1.cs` + `Form1.Designer.cs`), every recursive `calls` self-loop disappears from `graph.json` — in Python, TypeScript, Java and C# alike, not only in the C# files.

`_merge_csharp_partial_class_nodes` (`graphify/extract.py`) collapses the partial halves, then rewrites **every** edge in the corpus and skips any edge whose endpoints are equal after the remap:

```python
for e in all_edges:
    src = remap.get(e.get("source"), e.get("source"))
    tgt = remap.get(e.get("target"), e.get("target"))
    if src == tgt:
        continue
```

That drops every pre-existing self-loop, not only the ones the merge creates. The same loop also dedups edges it never rewrote on `(src, tgt, relation, source_file, source_location)`, a key that ignores confidence/context, so it can prune legitimate parallel edges elsewhere.

**Expected:** only self-loops created by the merge itself (two distinct halves collapsing) are dropped, and edges the merge does not remap come out unchanged. That is the rule the Swift extension merge already follows (#2538) and the one `deduplicate_entities` adopted in #3809 (fixed in 0.9.69). Recursive calls are meant to be kept — `build_from_json` preserves them.

On real code (`graphify update --force --no-cluster`, v0.9.74):

| corpus | recursive `calls` self-loops |
|---|---|
| google/gson `gson/src/main` (pure Java) | 22 |
| same + the two 3-line `Form1` partial files from the steps below | **0** |
| JamesNK/Newtonsoft.Json `Src/Newtonsoft.Json` (has real partials, e.g. `JsonWriter` + `JsonWriter.Async`) | **0** (206 once the merge stops dropping them) |

For example, `GsonTypes.canonicalize()` → itself is lost from Gson.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir repro && cd repro
printf 'def walk(node):\n    for child in node.children:\n        walk(child)\n' > tree.py
printf 'public partial class Form1 {\n    public Form1() { }\n}\n' > Form1.cs
printf 'public partial class Form1 {\n    private void InitializeComponent() { }\n}\n' > Form1.Designer.cs

graphify update . --force --no-cluster
python -c "import json; g=json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); print([(e['source'], e['relation'], e['target']) for e in g['links'] if e['source'] == e['target']])"

# remove the two partial files and rebuild
rm Form1.cs Form1.Designer.cs
graphify update . --force --no-cluster
python -c "import json; g=json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); print([(e['source'], e['relation'], e['target']) for e in g['links'] if e['source'] == e['target']])"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
--- with Form1.cs + Form1.Designer.cs ---
[]
--- after deleting the two C# files ---
[('tree_walk', 'calls', 'tree_walk')]
```

### Graphify version

0.9.74 (e10df08)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables set (AST-only `graphify update`). A clean checkout of `v8` at `e10df08` reproduces it.

### Additional context

The merge's docstring scopes it to class-level nodes ("Member node ids are left untouched — only the class-level nodes collapse"), but the edge rewrite loop runs over the whole corpus, so edges from every language pass through it.

I have a fix with regression tests ready and will open a PR right after this.

title: fix(extract): keep recursive calls when merging C# partial classes
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4016.

`_merge_csharp_partial_class_nodes` collapses the halves of a C# `partial class` onto one node, then rewrites every edge in the corpus. It skipped every edge whose endpoints were equal after the remap, so one partial class split across two files erased every recursive `calls` self-loop in the repo — in every language — and it deduped edges it never rewrote on a key that ignores confidence/context.

This applies the two rules graphify already uses for the same situation elsewhere:

- an edge the merge does not remap is kept verbatim and never deduped — the Swift extension merge rule (#2538);
- a self-loop is dropped only when two distinct endpoints collapse into one node — the `deduplicate_entities` rule (#3809). A self-loop that existed before the merge, including one on a merged-away half, is rewired onto the canonical node instead of being dropped.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: **a merge pass may only drop the self-loops it creates itself; every edge it does not remap comes out exactly as it went in.**

- `test_partial_class_keeps_recursive_calls_in_other_languages` — Python + TypeScript recursion survives a partial merge (real `extract()`).
- `test_partial_class_keeps_recursive_call_inside_a_half` — a recursive C# method inside a half keeps its self-call (real `extract()`).
- `test_merge_drops_only_the_self_loops_it_creates` — untouched self-loop kept; self-loop on the merged-away half rewired to the canonical node; the collapsed half→half edge still dropped.
- `test_merge_does_not_dedup_edges_it_never_rewrote` — two untouched parallel edges that differ only in confidence both survive.

All four fail with `graphify/extract.py` from `v8` and pass with this change. The existing #2332 / #2411 partial-class tests are unchanged and pass.

Persisted state: after the next rebuild, `graph.json` for a corpus with a split partial class gains back its recursive `calls` self-loops (and any parallel edges the old dedup pruned). No node ids change; no edge the merge does not touch is altered.

title: fix(extract): parse .luau with tree-sitter-luau and resolve require() through Rojo projects (#2520)
body:
## Problem

Two things kept Roblox/Luau repositories out of the graph.

**1. Grammar.** `.luau` files are dispatched to `tree-sitter-lua`. Luau is a typed superset of Lua 5.1, and the plain Lua grammar has no rule for `export type`, if-expressions (`if c then a else b`), `::` casts, generics, string interpolation, `+=`, or `continue`. When the parser meets one of them the file is extracted only in part, and in typed Roblox code (`--!strict`) that is most files. This is #2520.

**2. Requires.** On a Rojo project a `require` names an *instance*, not a file: `require(ReplicatedStorage.Shared.Util.Logger)` or `require(script.Parent.Config)` only becomes a file through the `"$path"` mounts of the Rojo `*.project.json`. The Lua import handler reads the argument as a dotted module name, so nearly every such require ended on an external stub and the graph had no file-to-file dependencies.

Measured on a 1,648-file Roblox repository (258k lines, every file `--!strict`), `graphify extract . --code-only` on 0.9.74:

| | tree-sitter-lua (current) | tree-sitter-luau (commit 1) |
|---|---|---|
| files reported "had syntax errors and may be partially extracted" | 954 / 1,648 | 10 |
| declared functions present in the graph | 6,902 / 9,482 (72.8%) | 8,986 / 9,482 (94.8%) |
| nodes / edges | 9,636 / 15,837 | 11,644 / 18,877 |

And on a 933-file Rojo game with one `default.project.json`:

| | commit 1 | commits 1 + 2 |
|---|---|---|
| external nodes | 837 | 37 |
| `imports` edges | 4,460 | 5,089 |
| `imports` edges landing on a file node | 1,781 | 4,901 (96.3%) |
| `imports` edges landing on an external | 2,679 | 188 |

Before commit 2, most of the 1,781 "resolved" edges came from accidental hits of the dotted-path probe (including case-insensitive matches on macOS). After it, the remaining externals are vendor packages that are not checked out (React, Flipper, ReactRoblox, TopbarPlus, ProfileStore), dynamic requires (`require(module)`, `WaitForChild(name)`) and instances with no script behind them.

## Implementation

### Commit 1: `tree-sitter-luau` for `.luau`

- `pyproject.toml`: add `tree-sitter-luau>=1.2,<2` ([tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-luau](https://github.com/tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-luau), MIT, abi3 wheels for macOS x86_64/arm64, manylinux x86_64/aarch64, musllinux, Windows amd64/arm64). `uv.lock` updated with `uv lock`.
- `graphify/extract.py`: `_LUAU_CONFIG = dataclasses.replace(_LUA_CONFIG, ts_module="tree_sitter_luau")` and `extract_luau()`. The Luau grammar emits the same node types the Lua walk already consumes (`function_declaration`, `function_call`, `variable_declaration`, `method_index_expression`), so the config is shared and only the grammar changes. `.luau` now dispatches to `extract_luau`; `.lua` and `.toc` keep `extract_lua`; the language-name map gains `"luau"`.
- `tests/fixtures/sample.luau`: extended with the Luau-only constructs above, with functions declared after them.
- `tests/test_languages.py`: five Luau tests. `test_luau_no_parse_errors` and `test_luau_finds_functions_after_luau_only_syntax` fail on `v8` before this change; `test_luau_and_lua_use_distinct_grammars` pins the dispatch.
- `README.md`: grammar count 37 → 38.

### Commit 2: resolve `require()` through Rojo project files

- `graphify/extractors/luau_facts.py` (new): per-file AST facts for Luau results, stored in the AST cache under `result["luau_module"]`: every `require` argument, every `local` binding with its visible byte range, and the fields of a top-level `return { … }`, each reduced to an instance-path chain (`GetService`, `WaitForChild`, `FindFirstChild`, `FindFirstAncestor`, `.X`, `["X"]`, `.Parent`, casts, parentheses; `if`/`and`/`or` as alternatives). It lives under `extractors/` because importing `graphify.rojo_resolution` from `engine.py` would create a cycle.
- `graphify/extractors/engine.py`: +7 lines, Luau results carry the facts.
- `graphify/rojo_resolution.py` (new): the repo-level pass. It loads the nearest `*.project.json` at or below the scan root (nested project files, `{"optional": …}`, most specific mount wins), evaluates each chain against the mounts (`script`, local aliases, locator modules that return a table of instance paths, the `LocalPlayer.PlayerScripts`/`PlayerGui` runtime aliases, `PlayerModule`), maps the instance back to the script Rojo syncs there (`X.luau`, `.server`/`.client` variants, `X/init.luau`), and rebuilds the file's `imports` edges:
  - a resolved require becomes an `imports` edge to that file node, stamped with `target_file` like any resolved import;
  - an instance with no script behind it becomes an external node named after the instance path;
  - a dynamic require keeps today's target;
  - `.lua` files, and `.luau` files with no project file above them, are untouched.
- `graphify/extract.py`: registers the pass as a `LanguageResolver("luau_rojo_requires", {".luau"}, …)` through `run_language_resolvers`, right after the per-file merge and **before** the id-remap, so `target_file` canonicalization (#2169) also works for a target outside an incremental batch. The tail registry runs after the remap and would be too late.
- `tests/fixtures/rojo_project/`: a minimal `default.project.json` (Shared and Server mounts, an absent `Packages` vendor folder) and eight sources (`.server.luau`, `init.luau`, a locator module, one `.lua`).
- `tests/test_rojo_resolution.py`: nine tests in the style of `test_languages.py`, running the full `extract()` on the fixture. Seven fail on commit 1 alone; the two that pass (`.lua` file, project file above the scan root) pin today's behaviour.
- `README.md`: one paragraph after the Terraform one.

### Commit 3: Lua-family gates in `engine.py`

Giving `.luau` its own grammar had silently taken it out of four Lua-only engine paths, which gate on `config.ts_module == "tree_sitter_lua"`: bare `require(...)` statements (no `imports` edge), the `self:` method rewrite (bound to an unrelated bare function), the `lua_self_table` lookup and the #3991 fail-closed guard for colon calls on unknown receivers. `engine.py` now has `_LUA_FAMILY = frozenset({"tree_sitter_lua", "tree_sitter_luau"})` and the four gates test membership in it. New fixture `tests/fixtures/sample_methods.luau` and three tests in `tests/test_languages.py` (`test_luau_bare_require_statement_is_an_import`, `test_luau_self_colon_call_binds_to_the_table_method`, `test_luau_colon_call_on_unknown_receiver_is_fail_closed`); all three fail on commits 1 + 2 and pass with this one. On the 933-file game, call edges go from 18,460 to 18,536; imports are unchanged.

## Verification

Commands run (macOS arm64, Python 3.12, `uv sync`):

```
uv run pytest tests/test_languages.py tests/test_rojo_resolution.py -q
uv run pytest tests/ -q --ignore=tests/test_languages.py
uv run ruff check graphify/ tests/
uv run pyright graphify/rojo_resolution.py graphify/extractors/luau_facts.py
uv run pyright graphify/extract.py graphify/extractors/engine.py
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --check
```

- `test_languages.py` + `test_rojo_resolution.py`: 442 passed, 20 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_swift_extension_across_files_merges_into_canonical_type`, which writes to `/private/tmp` and is blocked by the sandbox the suite ran in; it passes outside the sandbox and fails identically on untouched `v8`.
- `tests/test_rojo_resolution.py` alone: 9 passed (7 fail on commit 1 alone). The three commit-3 tests fail on commits 1 + 2 and pass on the branch.
- Rest of the suite: 36 failed, 5,710 passed, 82 skipped. The same 36 tests fail identically on `v8` (erlang, r, security, solidity, vbnet, ollama retry cap, non-regular files: environment or grammar related, most of them needing network the sandbox denies), so the branch introduces no new failure.
- `ruff check graphify/ tests/`: clean. `pyright` on the two new modules: 0 errors; `extract.py` (119) and `engine.py` (33) keep exactly the errors they have on `v8`, none new. `tools.skillgen --check`: OK.

## Limitations

- Only project files at or below the scan root count. Scanning a subfolder of a Rojo repository gives the plain-Lua behaviour for its requires.
- Bindings are lexical by byte range, not flow-sensitive: a local reassigned later keeps its declaration value. Values coming out of `pcall`, function calls or table mutation fail closed (the require stays on the Lua handler's target).
- `.luaurc` aliases (`@self`, `@pkg`) are not resolved. String requires resolve only relative to the file (Lune style, `./` and `../`).
- `FindFirstChild(name, true)` (recursive) is treated as unresolvable.
- Resolved edges stay `EXTRACTED` with score 1.0, as for the Lua handler.
- The 10 files still flagged on the real repository contain constructs the Luau grammar itself rejects; they are reported by the existing partial-parse warning, not silently dropped.

Closes #2520.

title: build_from_json collapses same-file, same-label nodes at different locations (even with dedup=False) — regression vs 0.8.31
body:
## Summary

`build_from_json` (and therefore `build_merge(..., dedup=False)`) collapses nodes that share the same `source_file` and the same `label` but sit at different `source_location`s. In 0.8.31 they are all kept; in 0.9.74 only one survives. This is **not** the cross-file merge from #3094 — the nodes are in the same file and the control below (same label, different file) is preserved.

Typical victims: a JSON key that appears at several nesting levels (`name` at `L2` and `L5` of one `plugin.json`), and a heading repeated in two sections of one Markdown document. They are distinct nodes with distinct ids and locations, but they get merged even though `dedup=False` was requested.

## Minimal reproduction

```python
from graphify.build import build_from_json

def node(i, label, ft, src, loc):
    return {"id": i, "label": label, "file_type": ft, "source_file": src, "source_location": loc}

nodes = [
    node("pkg_name",        "name",  "code",     "pkg/plugin.json", "L2"),
    node("pkg_author_name", "name",  "code",     "pkg/plugin.json", "L5"),
    node("doc_s1_notes",    "Notas", "document", "docs/plan.md",    "L10"),
    node("doc_s2_notes",    "Notas", "document", "docs/plan.md",    "L80"),
    node("other_name",      "name",  "code",     "pkg/other.json",  "L2"),   # control: other file
]
G = build_from_json({"nodes": nodes, "edges": [], "hyperedges": []})
print(len(nodes), "->", G.number_of_nodes(), sorted({n["id"] for n in nodes} - set(G.nodes)))
```

| version | result |
|---|---|
| 0.8.31 | `5 -> 5`, nothing lost |
| 0.9.74 | `5 -> 3`, lost `['doc_s2_notes', 'pkg_name']` |

## Real-world impact

On an existing, hand-curated graph (6,412 nodes / 9,308 edges), re-loading its own `graph.json` through `build_from_json` gives 6,119 nodes / 8,562 edges on 0.9.74 (0.8.31: unchanged). 286 nodes and 746 edges disappear; 284 of those 286 have a surviving node with the same `source_file` + label (210 code, 49 document, 11 rationale). None of them come from deleted files.

Consequence: `build_merge(new_chunks, graph_path=..., dedup=False)` with an *empty* chunk raises the #479 guard (`build_merge would drop 217 node(s) from sources that were neither re-extracted nor pruned`) and refuses to write. The guard does its job, but it means an existing graph can no longer be merged incrementally on 0.9.74 without losing nodes, even with `dedup=False`.

## What I did not verify

I suspect the `(source_file, label)` key used by the ghost-duplicate merge pass in `build_from_json` (#1145 / #2068) but I have not confirmed that this is the code path. I also did not check intermediate versions between 0.8.31 and 0.9.74, so I can't say which release introduced it.

## Expected

Nodes at different `source_location`s with different ids should survive `dedup=False`, or the collapse should be limited to the AST-vs-LLM twin case it was designed for (and be opt-out).

Environment: Windows 11, Python 3.14, `graphifyy` 0.8.31 vs 0.9.74 (fresh venv).

first slice of #2474, following the plan @nadiadatepe-eng and @Baziar agreed there. dispatch_command is one 3,800 line if/elif chain, big enough that pyright reports it as too complex to analyze and skips the whole body, so none of the cli dispatch is type checked today.

graphify/commands/registry.py maps a command to a "module:function" handler that is imported only when the command runs. dispatch_command(cmd) stays the public entry point, checks the table first and falls through to the remaining chain, so the rest can move a slice at a time. this slice moves the eight smallest branches verbatim: prs, hook, hook-check, hook-guard, watch, check-update, clone and benchmark. handlers take no arguments, still read sys.argv and exit the same way, and helpers that stay in cli.py (_run_hook_guard, _clone_repo, _default_graph_path, _enforce_graph_size_cap_or_exit) are imported at call time.

the porting rules for later slices are in graphify/commands/__init__.py. next would be the mid-size branches, extract last and on its own like the thread said.

title: Zig: error set declarations are dropped entirely
body:
## Summary

A Zig error set declared as `const E = error{ A, B };` is extracted as *nothing* — neither the error type node nor its members appear in the graph.

## Repro

```zig
const FileError = error{ NotFound, PermissionDenied };
fn open() FileError!void { return error.NotFound; }
```

Extracting this file yields a node for `open()` but no `FileError` node and no members.

## Cause

`const E = error{...}` parses as a `variable_declaration` whose value node is an `error_set_declaration`. The `variable_declaration` handler only recognises `struct_declaration`, `enum_declaration`, `union_declaration`, `builtin_function` and `field_expression` as value nodes, so the whole declaration falls through and is lost.

## Expected

An error set is a named enumeration of error values — the direct parallel of a Zig `enum`. It should emit the type node plus a node and a `case_of` edge per member, exactly like enum members already do (and like Java #1719 / Swift / Scala enums).

I have a fix ready with a regression test.

title: PHP: 8.1 enum cases are dropped (no case_of edges)
body:
## Summary

A PHP 8.1 `enum` captures its type and methods but drops all of its cases, leaving the enum a caseless leaf.

## Repro

```php
<?php
enum Suit: string {
    case Hearts = 'H';
    case Spades = 'S';
    public function color(): string { return 'x'; }
}
```

The graph has `Suit`, `Suit::color()`, but no `Hearts`/`Spades` nodes and no `case_of` edges.

## Cause

`enum_declaration` is in the PHP `class_types`, so the type and its methods are walked, but the cases nest in the `enum_declaration_list` body as `enum_case` nodes that no handler visits. Every other enum language already emits a node + `case_of` per member via a language extra-walk (Java #1719 `enum_constant`, Kotlin `enum_entry`, Swift, Scala, C++ `enumerator`); PHP has none.

## Expected

Emit a node and a `case_of` edge per `enum_case`, for both backed (`: string`) and pure enums. Methods must stay intact.

Fix + regression test ready.

title: Elixir: defmacro/defmacrop/defguard/defguardp definitions are dropped
body:
## Summary

Elixir macros and guard macros are not extracted. A module's `defmacro`, `defmacrop`, `defguard` and `defguardp` definitions produce no nodes, and a call to a locally-defined macro resolves to nothing.

## Repro

```elixir
defmodule MyMod do
  defmacro trace(expr) do
    quote do: unquote(expr)
  end
  defguard is_even(x) when is_integer(x) and rem(x, 2) == 0
  def run(x) do
    trace(x)
  end
end
```

`run()` is captured but `trace`/`is_even` are missing, and there is no `run -> trace` edge.

## Cause

Only `def`/`defp` are handled in the call-keyword dispatch. `defmacro`/`defmacrop`/`defguard`/`defguardp` share the exact same head shape (a `call` head, optionally wrapped in a `when` binary_operator) but fall through to the generic recursion and are dropped.

## Expected

Treat them like `def`/`defp` — macros and guard macros are named, invocable members. They are already in the call-pass skip-keyword set, so their own keyword is never mistaken for a call.

Fix + regression test ready.

title: Rust: macro_rules! definitions are dropped and their invocations never resolve
body:
## Summary

A `macro_rules!` macro is not extracted: it never becomes a node, and a `name!(...)` invocation of a locally-defined macro resolves to nothing.

## Repro

```rust
macro_rules! my_vec {
    ($($x:expr),*) => { vec![$($x),*] };
}
fn build() -> Vec<i32> {
    my_vec!(1, 2, 3)
}
```

No `my_vec` node, no `build -> my_vec` edge.

## Cause

The `macro_definition` node type has no branch in the walker, so the macro is dropped. Invocations are `macro_invocation` nodes (never `call_expression`), which `walk_calls` doesn't handle, so even if the definition existed there would be nothing linking to it.

## Expected

Emit a node per `macro_definition` and resolve a bare `name!` invocation to it with a `calls` edge. A macro and a function can share a name (`vec!` vs `vec`), so macros should be tracked separately / id-qualified to avoid cross-binding. A scoped invocation (`log::info!`) is cross-crate and should stay unresolved (fail-closed).

Fix + regression tests ready.

title: fix(zig): extract error set declarations and their members
body:
Fixes #4021.

### Problem
A Zig error set (`const E = error{ A, B };`) was dropped entirely — both the error type and its members vanished from the graph.

`const E = error{...}` parses as a `variable_declaration` whose value is an `error_set_declaration`. That value node type wasn't among the recognised forms, so the whole declaration fell through the `variable_declaration` handler.

### Fix
Recognise `error_set_declaration` and emit the type node plus a node and a `case_of` edge per member identifier. An error set is a named enumeration of error values — the direct parallel of a Zig `enum` — so this mirrors the existing enum-member handling (and Java #1719 / Swift / Scala). Struct and union fields are untouched.

### Tests
Adds `test_zig_error_set_members_emit_case_of_nodes`, which fails on current `v8` (the whole declaration was dropped) and passes with the fix. Full suite green (6233 passed, only the DNS-sandboxed `test_security.py` env tests excluded); `ruff` and `pyright` clean on the touched file.

title: fix(php): extract enum cases with case_of edges
body:
Fixes #4022.

### Problem
A PHP 8.1 `enum` captured its type and methods but dropped all of its cases, leaving the enum a caseless leaf. `enum_declaration` is in the PHP `class_types`, so the type and methods are walked, but the cases nest in the `enum_declaration_list` body as `enum_case` nodes that no handler visited.

### Fix
Add a PHP extra-walk that emits a node plus a `case_of` edge per `enum_case`, keyed off the case's `name` field, and dispatch it from the engine for `tree_sitter_php`. This brings PHP to parity with Java #1719 (`enum_constant`), Kotlin (`enum_entry`), Swift, Scala, and C++ (`enumerator`). Backed enums (`: string`) and pure enums are both handled; enum methods are untouched.

### Tests
Adds `test_php_enum_cases_have_case_of_edge` (backed + pure enum, methods still present), which fails on current `v8` and passes with the fix. Full suite green (6233 passed, security env tests excluded); `ruff` clean; `pyright` on `engine.py` unchanged from baseline (0 added).

title: fix(elixir): extract defmacro and defguard definitions
body:
Fixes #4023.

### Problem
`defmacro`/`defmacrop` (macros) and `defguard`/`defguardp` (guard macros) were dropped entirely: the member never became a node, and a call to a locally-defined macro had nothing to resolve to. They define named, invocable members with the same head shape as `def`/`defp` (a `call` head, optionally wrapped in a `when` binary_operator), but only `def`/`defp` were handled — the rest fell through to the generic recursion.

### Fix
Handle the four keywords in the same branch as `def`/`defp`. They are already listed in the call-pass skip-keyword set, so their defining keyword is never mistaken for a call.

### Tests
Adds `test_elixir_defmacro_and_defguard_are_extracted`, which checks the macro, private macro, and guard become nodes and that a call to a local macro now resolves. Fails on current `v8`, passes with the fix. Full suite green (6233 passed, security env tests excluded); `ruff` and `pyright` clean on the touched file.

title: fix(rust): extract macro_rules! definitions and resolve their invocations
body:
Fixes #4024.

### Problem
A `macro_rules!` macro was dropped entirely: it never became a node, and a `name!(...)` invocation of it (a `macro_invocation`, never a `call_expression`) had nothing to resolve to. The `macro_definition` node type had no branch, and `walk_calls` didn't handle `macro_invocation`.

### Fix
Emit a node per `macro_definition` and resolve a bare `name!` invocation to it with a `calls` edge. Macros are tracked in their own name registry rather than the function/type label map, because a macro and a function can share a name (`vec!` vs `vec`); the node id is macro-qualified for the same reason and the label carries a `!`. A scoped invocation (`log::info!`) is cross-module/crate and stays unresolved (fail-closed), matching how scoped calls are already handled.

### Tests
Adds `tests/test_rust_macro_rules.py`: the dropped definition, the resolved local invocation, name coexistence with a same-named function, and the unresolved scoped case. The three positive tests fail on current `v8` and pass with the fix. Full suite green (6233 passed, security env tests excluded); `ruff` clean; `pyright` on `rust.py` unchanged from baseline (0 added).

title: fix(llm): merge ollama num_ctx into extra_body instead of replacing it (#3988)
body:

Part of #3988 (item 1 only).

title: fix(swift): bind self and super calls within the caller's class chain
body:
### what does this pr do?

stacked on #4011 (python) and #4012 (js), it reuses their _self_call_target. only the last commit is new, happy to rebase once those land.

self.save(), a bare save() (implicit self) and super.ping() in a swift method go through the file-wide label_to_nid, which keeps only the last definition of each name, so they land on whichever class the file declares last, as EXTRACTED.

on Alamofire at bda9ed5 (Source/, 44 files, 665 calls edges) 46 calls edges changed: 33 wrong ones moved to the right method and 13 wrong ones dropped. DataRequest.init, UploadRequest.reset, WebSocketRequest.cancel and friends calling super were recorded as calling themselves. URLEncodedFormEncoder's keyed container calls went to the unkeyed container, and DataRequest.serializingResponse went to DownloadTask.response.

swift inherits edges exist at bind time, so this uses the same in-file chain walk as python: own class first, then bases nearest first, super skips the class itself. a method of a class outside the chain is never the target. free functions, constructors and calls from an extension of the same type resolve exactly as before.

one gap that was already there: an extension of a nested type (extension URLEncodedFormEncoder.KeyedContainer) gets a different node id than the nested class, so those calls now get no in-file edge instead of the wrong one.

a self, super or implicit-self call never binds to a method of a class outside the callers own class chain. calls that resolve to something that is not a method of another class keep their old target.

title: [Bug]: Swift: a call through an injected protocol dead-ends at the requirement, so the conformer's method is unreachable
body:
Title: [Bug]: Swift: a call through an injected protocol dead-ends at the requirement, so the conformer's method is unreachable

## What happened?

Since #3673 a call on a protocol-typed property resolves to the protocol's own requirement node, which is right. But nothing joins that requirement to the method of the type that conforms to it, so every edge walk through an injected dependency stops at the protocol. C# had the same gap for interfaces and #3003 closed it with a `dispatches_to` edge; Swift never got one.

Expected: with exactly one conformer, the requirement's method links to the conformer's method, as `IReport.Build()` links to `Report.Build()` in C#.

## Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p probe/Core probe/Services probe/App
cat > probe/Core/Store.swift <<'SW'
protocol Store { func fetch() async throws -> [Item] }
struct Item { let id: Int }
SW
cat > probe/Services/RemoteStore.swift <<'SW'
struct RemoteStore: Store {
    func fetch() async throws -> [Item] { try decode() }
    func decode() throws -> [Item] { [] }
}
SW
cat > probe/App/ItemModel.swift <<'SW'
final class ItemModel {
    private let store: Store
    init(store: Store) { self.store = store }
    func load() async throws -> [Item] { try await store.fetch() }
}
SW
cd probe && graphify update . --no-cluster && graphify explain "Store.swift::fetch"
```

## Error output or graph output

```text
$ graphify update . --no-cluster
[graphify watch] Rebuilt (no clustering): 13 nodes, 19 edges
$ graphify explain "Store.swift::fetch"
Node: .fetch()
  ID:        core_store_store_fetch
  Source:    Core/Store.swift L1
  Degree:    3

Connections (3):
  --> Item [references] [EXTRACTED] Core/Store.swift:L1
  <-- Store [method] [EXTRACTED] Core/Store.swift:L1
  <-- .load() [calls] [INFERRED] App/ItemModel.swift:L4
```

No edge reaches `Services/RemoteStore.swift`'s `.fetch()`, so `RemoteStore.decode()` is unreachable from `ItemModel.load()`. On a real app (GAURAV-1313/roomy, 298 Swift files, four protocols injected as `any P`) the same cut sits at every protocol seam; e.g. `CleanupStore.run()` never reaches `DeletionService.merge()`.

## Graphify version

0.9.74 (v8 at 0b60d47)

## Operating System

macOS

title: refactor(csharp): lift interface dispatch into a language-agnostic core
body:
## What does this PR do?

Moves the single-implementer dispatch mechanism out of `graphify/csharp_dispatch.py` into a new `graphify/interface_dispatch.py`, with the file-suffix gate as a keyword parameter (`resolve_interface_dispatch(..., suffixes=)`). `csharp_dispatch.py` keeps its public names (`resolve_csharp_interface_dispatch`, `_method_label`, `DISPATCH_RELATION`) and becomes the `.cs` gate over the core. The registration in `extract.py` is untouched.

Why: Swift protocols have exactly the shape #3003 fixed for C# interfaces. Since #3673 a call through an injected protocol lands on the requirement node, and the conformer's method is unreachable from it. The follow-up PR adds a 46-line `.swift` gate over this core instead of a second copy of the algorithm, following the rule from the #3729 review: reuse the existing resolver rather than re-implement a subset of it.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [x] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: for every corpus, the edges this pass emits are identical before and after. The body of `resolve_interface_dispatch` is the old function verbatim; the only edit is the module constant `_CSHARP_SUFFIXES` becoming the `suffixes` parameter, which the C# gate passes as `(".cs",)`. Which pairs qualify, the edge's fields, and the dedup are unchanged. No persisted or generated state is involved: the pass runs in memory after extraction.

- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.

- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly. Nothing new; the docstring keeps the out-of-scope list from #3005 (abstract base classes, interface hierarchies).

title: feat(swift): dispatch a protocol requirement to its single conformer
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4032.

Links a Swift protocol requirement to the method of its single conformer with a member-level `dispatches_to` edge: the Swift twin of #3003.

Builds on #4034, the refactor that lifts the C# mechanism into `graphify.interface_dispatch`; cherry-pick that commit first. This PR is one commit on top of it: 3 files, +322, nothing removed.

**Symptom.** Since #3673, `store.fetch()` on an injected `Store` resolves to the protocol's own `.fetch()` requirement, which is what the call site names. The conforming `RemoteStore.fetch()` is a separate node and nothing joins the two, so every edge walk through an injected dependency (`query`, `explain`, the graph view) stops at the protocol.

```swift
// Core/Store.swift
protocol Store { func fetch() async throws -> [Item] }
// Services/RemoteStore.swift
struct RemoteStore: Store {
    func fetch() async throws -> [Item] { try decode() }
    func decode() throws -> [Item] { [] }
}
// App/ItemModel.swift
final class ItemModel {
    private let store: Store
    func load() async throws -> [Item] { try await store.fetch() }
}
```

On `v8`: `ItemModel.load() --calls--> Store.fetch() [INFERRED]`, and `RemoteStore.decode()` is unreachable from `load()`.

**Root cause.** `csharp_dispatch.py` linked an interface requirement to its implementation for `.cs` files only. No pass did it for Swift; `dispatches_to` appeared nowhere else.

**Fix.**
- `graphify/swift_dispatch.py` (new, 46 lines): the `.swift` gate over `resolve_interface_dispatch`.
- `graphify/extract.py` (+10): registers `swift_protocol_dispatch` right after `csharp_interface_dispatch`.
- `tests/test_swift_protocol_dispatch.py` (new): 17 cases.

The edge is per method, not per call site, so one edge reconnects every caller of the requirement. It is additive: the `calls` edge to the requirement stays. Confidence is `INFERRED` 0.9, as in #3005: the target is forced once there is a single conformer, but the source text never names it.

**Before and after, rendered by graphify's own viewer.** The `CleanupStore` → `Cleaner` → `DeletionService` neighbourhood of roomy, cut from each build's `graph.json` and drawn with `graphify cluster-only`, same node positions on both sides. On `v8` the three `Cleaner` requirements have no edge to `DeletionService`'s methods; on this branch the three dashed (`INFERRED`) `dispatches_to` edges join them. The self-loop on `DeletionService.merge()` in both panels is a separate, pre-existing resolution bug (a qualified call to a method with the caller's name resolves to the caller), reported separately.

![roomy before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GAURAV-1313/graphify/assets-swift-dispatch/swift-dispatch/roomy-graph-before-after.png)

**Measured**, resolver registration on and off, same checkout:

| corpus | nodes | edges | `dispatches_to` | conformer method reachable from the caller |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 files: protocol, `extension RemoteRepository: Repository`, `@MainActor` consumer | 18 → 18 | 25 → 27 | 0 → 2 | no → yes |
| SwiftUI app: `@StateObject` store, actor cache, enum state | 36 → 36 | 58 → 59 | 0 → 1 | no → yes |
| [GAURAV-1313/roomy](https://github.com/GAURAV-1313/roomy), 298 Swift files, 4 protocols injected as `any P`, `graphify update --no-cluster` | 2,910 → 2,910 | 6,221 → 6,226 | 0 → 5 | 5 callers, e.g. `CleanupStore.run()` → `DeletionService.*` |

On roomy, `graphify explain "DeletionService.swift::merge"` gains the line `--> .merge() [dispatches_to] [INFERRED] …/DeletionService.swift:L15`.

**One note from the roomy run, and a question.** Two of its four protocols (`Cleaner`, `LibraryChangeSource`) really have two conformers each: the app type and a test fake in `RoomyTests`. The fakes are `final class X: P` with `P` declared in another file, so the per-file classifier emits them as `inherits` (the limit below), the guard counts one conformer, and the edges land. The other two protocols have struct fakes, which are counted, and get no edge, which is the guard as written. Once the classifier is fixed, all four have 2+ conformers and this app gets zero edges unless a conformer declared in a test target is treated differently. I'd rather have your call on that than decide it in code.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: an edge is drawn only when the corpus forces the target. The protocol has exactly one `implements` conformer, that conformer owns exactly one method with the requirement's name, and both the protocol and the conformer are declared in `.swift` files. Anything else leaves the graph exactly as extracted: a protocol with 0 or 2+ conformers, a conformer with 0 or 2+ same-named methods, a protocol-extension default nobody overrides (folded into the protocol's own node, so the conformer owns no candidate), a builtin protocol (`View`, `Codable`: sourceless stubs that never pass the declared-in guard), and a same-named Kotlin class that binds to the protocol by name.

- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary. The mechanism is not re-implemented; the gate is 46 lines plus a 10-line registration.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test. 17 cases: cross-file positive, reachability through the injected dependency, the call to the requirement is kept, edge shape, extension-declared conformance, same-file class conformer, two conformers → nothing, no matching member → nothing, protocol-extension default → nothing, overriding a default → links, builtin protocol skipped while a static requirement links, subclassing out of scope, protocol inheritance not walked, Kotlin same-name conformer → nothing, a C# corpus untouched by this pass, registration order. 9 fail on the base without this commit (every positive case); 8 are negative controls that pass on both.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly:
  - Swift spells a superclass and a protocol identically in a class's inheritance list, and `_swift_classify_base` only knows the protocols declared in the file it is extracting, so `final class C: P` with `P` in another file is emitted as `inherits` and this pass does not see it. Pinned by `test_class_conformer_of_a_protocol_in_another_file_is_a_known_limit`. Struct/enum/actor conformers, same-file classes and `extension C: P` are covered. Fixing the classifier is a separate change; it is also a wrong `inherits` edge on its own.
  - Protocol inheritance is not walked transitively, as in C#. Subclassing a class is an `inherits` edge and a different bet, so it is out of scope.
  - Property requirements are not dispatched; the pass keys on `method` edges, as the C# one does.

this branch:  13 nodes, 20 edges

                <-- .load() [calls] [INFERRED] App/ItemModel.swift:L4

title: fix(extract): keep Scala file-scope val/var type references (#2054)
body:
## Problem

Scala 3 drops the boilerplate wrapper: `val`/`var` can be written directly at file scope with no enclosing `object`/`class`/`trait`. The `val_definition`/`var_definition` type-reference dispatch was gated on `and parent_class_nid`, so a file-scope binding produced **no node and no edge of any kind**, while the byte-identical definition nested one level inside any container resolved correctly.

The missing container was the only difference. I verified this against tree-sitter-scala 0.26.0 before writing the fix — both positions parse to the same node type carrying the same `type` field:

```
class_definition
  template_body
    val_definition  fields=[(identifier, pattern), (type_identifier, type), (string, value)]
compilation_unit
  val_definition    fields=[(identifier, pattern), (type_identifier, type), (string, value)]
```

This is the Scala instance of a generic defect in the walker's default recursion path that had already caused and been fixed once for Python (#1050) — a position that legitimately has no container must fall back to the file node rather than be skipped.

## Implementation

One anchor fallback in the existing dispatch, reusing the `owner_nid = parent_class_nid or file_nid` idiom already present in the property branch above:

- drop `and parent_class_nid` from the gate
- compute `owner_nid = parent_class_nid or file_nid`
- emit the edge from `owner_nid`, and move the self-reference guard onto the same anchor so a file-scope binding cannot mint an edge from the file node to itself

Class-nested bindings are untouched; a regression test pins that case explicitly.

## Scope

Edges only. No new node type, no config change, no skillgen output (`_SCALA_CONFIG` registers none of these node types — they are handled ad-hoc in the walker).

## Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/test_scala_top_level_binding.py -q     # 8 passed
uv run pytest tests/ -q                                   # 28 failed, 6144 passed, 101 skipped
uv run ruff check .                                       # All checks passed!
uv run pyright                                            # 635 errors
```

- **6 of the 8 new tests fail on the pre-fix tree.** The 2 that pass either way are deliberate: the in-class control (must not regress) and the self-edge guard (trivially empty before the fix, meaningful after it).
- **The 28 failures are byte-identical to the clean-tree baseline** (`28 failed, 6136 passed`), which I captured on an unmodified checkout and diffed test-id-by-test-id. They are missing tree-sitter grammars for erlang/R/solidity/vbnet plus ollama retry tests, and none touch Scala.
- **pyright is at parity**: 635 errors before and after. That is pre-existing debt in this repo, not something this change introduces or claims to fix.

New tests cover: file-scope `val` and `var`, the in-class control, a file-scope type that resolves to a real declaration elsewhere, the no-self-edge guard, `EXTRACTED` confidence tagging, non-null `source_location`, and that a generic annotation keeps its `generic_arg` context distinct from a plain `field` one.

## Limitations

- A file-scope binding attributes its type reference to the **file** node, so several file-scope bindings of the same type produce parallel edges from that one node. This is the same shape the existing `contains`-from-file model already produces; collapsing them would need a node for the binding itself, which is out of scope here.
- Node counts grow very slightly on corpora that use Scala 3 file-scope bindings. Expected and correct — those definitions were previously absent entirely.

title: fix(extract): walk Scala type_definition right-hand sides (#2049)
body:
> **Stacked on #4036.** This branch is #4036 plus one commit. The reviewable unit is
> the **top commit** (`879dfd3`); the commit below it is #4036 verbatim and is not
> part of this change. This PR targets `v8` only because GitHub cannot base a PR on
> a fork branch. If you would rather review the combined diff, the net effect of
> this commit alone is: widen one dispatch tuple by one node type, and add two node
> types to one walker whitelist.

## Problem

A type alias (`type Alias = List[Int]`), an `opaque type`, and a `match type` all declare a dependency on the types they name — but the type-reference dispatch only fired for `val_definition`/`var_definition`, so these produced **zero `references` edges of any kind, in any context**. That is the asymmetry with `val`/`var`, whose annotation *is* walked:

```scala
trait Repo:
  type Alias = List[Int]
  opaque type Id = Long
  type Elem[X] = X match
    case String => Char
```

`match_type` needed a second, independent change: the type-reference walker's own recursion whitelist did not know `match_type`/`type_case_clause`, so **even a correctly dispatched call on a match type's right-hand side would still resolve nothing.**

## Implementation

Two small changes:

1. **Widen the dispatch tuple** to include `type_definition`. I verified the RHS field name against tree-sitter-scala 0.26.0 *before* writing the fix — all three forms carry it under the same `type` field the `val`/`var` path already reads, so the existing walk applies verbatim with no new handler:

   ```
   type_definition  fields=[(type_identifier, name), (generic_type, type)]   # type Alias = List[Int]
   type_definition  fields=[(type_identifier, name), (type_identifier, type)]  # opaque type Id = Long
   type_definition  fields=[(type_identifier, name), (type_parameters, ...), (match_type, type)]
   ```

2. **Add `match_type`/`type_case_clause` to the walker whitelist**, recursing over named children exactly as `compound_type` is already handled. A case clause names two real types — the one it discriminates on and the one it yields — and both are collected.

File-scope aliases inherit the anchor fallback from #4036; without it, an alias at file scope is still dropped by the separate missing-container defect that PR fixes.

## Scope

**Edges only.** The alias itself still gets no node of its own. That is a separate, already-accepted tradeoff shared with `val`/`given` bindings, and I deliberately left it alone rather than widening this PR. No new node type, no config change.

## Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/test_scala_type_definition.py -q     # 10 passed
uv run pytest tests/ -q                                   # 28 failed, 6154 passed, 101 skipped
uv run ruff check .                                       # All checks passed!
uv run pyright                                            # 635 errors
```

- **8 of the 10 new tests fail on the pre-fix tree** (confirmed by stashing the `engine.py` change and re-running).
- **The 28 failures are byte-identical to the clean-tree baseline** (`28 failed, 6136 passed`), diffed test-id-by-test-id. They are missing tree-sitter grammars for erlang/R/solidity/vbnet plus ollama retry tests; none touch Scala.
- **pyright is at parity**: 635 errors before and after — pre-existing debt in this repo.

Tests cover all three alias forms in-trait and at file scope, the `generic_type` argument split, the `match_type` result *and* matched type, that the shared `val` context split is preserved rather than flattened, `EXTRACTED` tagging with a source location, and the self-edge guard.

title: fix(extract): resolve Scala context bounds to references edges (#2046)
body:
> **Stacked on #4036 and #4037.** This branch is those two plus one commit. The
> reviewable unit is the **top commit** (`e293b64`); the two below it are #4036 and
> #4037 verbatim. This PR targets `v8` only because GitHub cannot base a PR on a fork
> branch. The net effect of the top commit alone is: add one helper function, and call
> it from one place.

## Problem

`def sort[A: Ordering]` desugars to an implicit `Ordering[A]`, so a context bound is a real dependency the function has on that typeclass — and the `[A: Ordering]` form is the idiomatic spelling, more common in modern Scala than the `(implicit ...)` it compiles to. `context_bound` was not referenced anywhere in the extractor, so the dependency was invisible wherever it appeared.

Two grammar shapes drive the implementation. I verified both against tree-sitter-scala 0.26.0 before writing the fix:

- **`context_bound` is a direct child of `type_parameters`**, one per bound, sitting alongside the type parameter's own `identifier`. That means the walk belongs in the existing per-function Scala block and needs no new handler — exactly as the issue anticipated.

  ```
  type_parameters  fields=[(identifier, name), (':', bound), (context_bound, bound)]
    identifier     "A"
    context_bound  fields=[(type_identifier, type)]
      type_identifier  "Ordering"
  ```

- **A higher-kinded parameter nests a further `type_parameters`** for its own arity brackets, so the walk must recurse rather than read direct children only — otherwise *both* bounds on `def program[F[_]: Async: Temporal]` are missed.

  ```
  type_parameters  fields=[(identifier, name), (type_parameters, type_parameters),
                           (':', bound), (context_bound, bound), (':', bound), (context_bound, bound)]
  ```

## Implementation

A `_scala_collect_context_bounds` helper next to the existing `_scala_collect_type_refs`, called from the per-function Scala block. Bounds get their own `type_bound` context rather than reusing `parameter_type`, so a consumer can tell a typeclass constraint from a parameter annotation.

**`upper_bound` (`[T <: Comparable[T]]`) is deliberately not matched.** It is a distinct node type, and a subtype constraint is not a dependency — emitting an edge there would assert something the source does not say.

### One trap worth flagging

`type_parameters` and `parameters` carry the **same field name** (`"parameters"`) on `function_definition`:

```
function_definition fields=[(identifier, name), (type_parameters, parameters),
                            (parameters, parameters), (generic_type, return_type), ...]
```

So `child_by_field_name("parameters")` returns whichever comes first — the type parameters. The bounds are therefore located **by node type, never by field name**; a field lookup here would read the function's real parameters as if they were bounds. A regression test pins that `xs: List[A]` still resolves under `parameter_type` and never under `type_bound`.

## Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/test_scala_context_bounds.py -q        # 10 passed
uv run pytest tests/ -q                                   # 28 failed, 6164 passed, 101 skipped
uv run ruff check .                                       # All checks passed!
uv run pyright                                            # 635 errors
```

- **6 of the 10 new tests fail on the pre-fix tree** (confirmed by stashing the `engine.py` change and re-running). The other 4 are deliberate negative/guard cases: unbounded type parameter, upper bound only, the field-name trap, and the self-edge guard.
- **The 28 failures are byte-identical to the clean-tree baseline** (`28 failed, 6136 passed`), diffed test-id-by-test-id — missing tree-sitter grammars for erlang/R/solidity/vbnet plus ollama retry tests. None touch Scala.
- **pyright is at parity**: 635 errors before and after.

Tests cover a single bound, several bounds, the nested `F[_]` case, the distinct `type_bound` context, the two negative cases (unbounded / upper bound), the field-name trap, a class member (`[K: Ordering]`), `EXTRACTED` tagging with a source location, and the self-edge guard.

## Limitations

- Only `def`/`function_definition` is handled, matching where the per-function Scala block already lives. A context bound on a class-level type parameter (`class Foo[A: Ordering]`) is still not walked; that is a separate dispatch and I left it out rather than widening this PR.
- The emitted bound type goes through the same `ensure_named_node` resolution as every other reference, so an unbound typeclass resolves to a sourceless stub for the corpus rewire to collapse later — the normal path.

title: fix(opencode): load the plugin on OpenCode 2 and refresh installed copies (#3554, #3732)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3554 and #3732.

`graphify opencode install` writes a plugin in the OpenCode 1 shape. On OpenCode 2 that install fails twice on every start. This is the server log of OpenCode 2.0.22 opened in a project that graphify 0.9.74 set up:

```text
failed to load plugin target=<project>/.opencode/plugins/graphify.js
  PluginModule.LoadError: Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function.
  (cause: SchemaError(Missing key at ["default"]))
failed to load plugin target=.opencode/plugins/graphify.js
  NpmInstallFailedError (cause: Error: Could not read package.json: Error: ENOTDIR: not a directory,
  open '<project>/.opencode/plugins/graphify.js/package.json')
```

The first error is the plugin file, which only has a named export. The second is the `"plugin": [".opencode/plugins/graphify.js"]` entry in `.opencode/opencode.json`: OpenCode 2 reads a bare path as an npm package name.

There are three changes.

**1. One plugin file for both runtimes.** The default export has `id`, `setup(ctx)` for OpenCode 2 and `server()` for OpenCode 1. Each runtime ignores the other's function. On OpenCode 2 the command tool is called `shell`, and the server is a background service that outlives a session, so the reminder is tracked per session there. The file imports nothing from an opencode package, because a plain file in `.opencode/plugins/` can't resolve one.

The plugin id carries the file's own location (`graphify-<hash>`). OpenCode loads `.opencode/plugins/` from the project and from each directory above it, and OpenCode 2 fails a second plugin with the same id: `Duplicate plugin ID: graphify`, shown as "1 plugin failed". With one install in `~` and one in a project, that happened in every such project. The copies share one record of who was reminded, so a command still gets a single reminder. On OpenCode 1 two copies used to add it twice.

**2. No opencode.json entry.** Both runtimes load every file in `.opencode/plugins/` on their own (OpenCode 1.2.0 and later), so the entry is not needed. Install no longer writes it. Install and uninstall remove the entry older releases wrote, under `plugin` or `plugins`, and leave everything else in the file alone. If the file has comments, it is not rewritten, because that would drop them. Install prints what to remove instead.

**3. Installed copies are refreshed.** Upgrading graphify does not touch a plugin that is already on disk. So someone who upgrades OpenCode keeps both errors until they find out they have to run the install again in each project. The CLI now rewrites an old-shape plugin on its next run, next to the stale-skill refresh from #1805:

```text
$ graphify --version
graphify: refreshed <project>/.opencode/plugins/graphify.js so OpenCode 2 can load it; set GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1 to disable
graphify <version>
$ graphify --version
graphify <version>
```

So nobody has to reinstall by hand: each project is upgraded the first time graphify runs in it after the upgrade, whether that is a `graphify query`, an `update`, or the post-commit hook.

It looks in the working directory and in the home directory. Home matters because `graphify opencode install` run from `~` puts the plugin in `~/.opencode/plugins/` (#1412), and OpenCode loads that one for every project below home. That is how I ran into this. `GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1` turns it off, the same switch as the skill refresh.

An old plugin is replaced only when the `opencode` on PATH reports 1.3.4 or later. Older OpenCode 1 releases can't load the new file, and the plugin they have still works, so it stays. The version is asked once (`opencode --version`), and only when an old plugin is actually found. If there is no `opencode` on PATH, nothing is replaced.

Only a plugin that graphify wrote is touched. The stale entry is also dropped when the plugin next to it is already current, because a checkout can bring `opencode.json` back on its own. If the rewrite fails, for example in a read-only checkout, the command still runs and stderr gets one `graphify: could not refresh ...` line. The rewrite takes the same per-directory lock as the skill refresh, without waiting, and both files are replaced with a temp file and one rename (`write_text_atomic`), so OpenCode, which watches them, never sees half a plugin.

### About the other open PRs

#3792, #3819 and #3896 are open for the same issues, so I checked what was still missing before sending another one:

- #3819 imports `Plugin` from `@opencode/plugin`. I tried that import in a small plugin of my own: OpenCode 2.0.22 fails with `Cannot find package '@opencode/plugin'`. That matches the comment on that PR. It also keeps the bare config entry.
- #3792 and #3896 export `{ id, setup }` without `server()`. OpenCode 1.18.34 rejects a default export like that with `must default export an object with server()`, and 1.18.34 is still npm `latest`.
- None of them touches a plugin that is already installed.

Happy to rebase on top of one of them or to split this up if you prefer a different order.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: after `graphify opencode install`, and after any graphify CLI run in a project that has an older install, OpenCode 1 (1.3.4 and later) and OpenCode 2 both load `.opencode/plugins/graphify.js` without an error, and the first shell command of a session carries the reminder.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Limitations:

- OpenCode 1 before 1.3.4 can't load the new file. Those releases call every export as a function, and OpenCode 2 needs the default export to be an object, so one file can't serve both. I took the releases that read `server()` from a default export (1.3.4, March 2026) as the floor. I got this from the OpenCode source. I did not run a release that old.
- The refresh leaves such an old OpenCode alone, but an explicit `graphify opencode install` there still writes a plugin that release can't load.
- The refresh needs `opencode` on PATH to ask for the version. Where it isn't (some hook environments, a desktop-only install), nothing is refreshed and `graphify opencode install` is still the way.
- This is the first refresh that writes inside a project. The skill refresh from #1805 only writes under the user's home. If `.opencode/plugins/graphify.js` or `.opencode/opencode.json` is tracked in git, the first graphify run after the upgrade leaves them modified, also when that run comes from the post-commit hook.
- The refresh only looks in the working directory and in home. A plugin in some other parent directory is refreshed when graphify next runs there.
- Only `.opencode/opencode.json` is cleaned, as before. An entry that someone moved to `opencode.jsonc` or to the global config stays, and so does an entry in a file with comments.
- A plugin that was edited by hand is replaced too, if it still starts with graphify's header and has no default export. OpenCode 2 could not load it either way.
- An `opencode.json` that only held graphify's entry is left as `{}`, the same as uninstall did before.

## How was this tested?

```text
# new and changed tests against the unchanged v8 sources
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_opencode_plugin_refresh.py tests/test_install.py -k opencode
47 failed, 9 passed

# with the fix
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_opencode_plugin_refresh.py tests/test_install.py tests/test_install_strings.py tests/test_skill_auto_refresh.py
204 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
6339 passed, 14 skipped

.venv/bin/ruff check graphify/install.py graphify/__main__.py tests/test_install.py tests/test_opencode_plugin_refresh.py
All checks passed!

.venv/bin/pyright graphify/install.py graphify/__main__.py
5 errors (the same 5 as on v8, none in the changed lines)
```

Three tests drive the installed file with node the way each runtime calls it: one for OpenCode 2, one for OpenCode 1, and one with two copies of the file at different paths. They are skipped when node is missing, like the node tests in `test_export.py`.

I also ran both runtimes for real, each with its own XDG directories, in a scratch project that has `graphify-out/graph.json`:

- OpenCode 2.0.22 with the 0.9.74 install: the two errors at the top.
- `graphify --version` from this branch in that project: the refresh line shown above, nothing on the second run, and `opencode.json` no longer has the entry.
- The same refresh with no `opencode` on PATH, and with a fake `opencode` that prints `1.3.3`: the old plugin and the entry stay as they are.
- OpenCode 2.0.22 again: the plugin loads with no error. I asked for two shell commands. The server log shows what was spawned:

  ```text
  echo "[graphify] knowledge graph at graphify-out/. For focused questions, ..." ; echo first-call
  echo second-call
  ```

- OpenCode 1.18.34 with a fresh `graphify opencode install` from this branch, so with no `opencode.json` at all: the plugin is discovered, the first `bash` call got the reminder and the second did not.
- Two copies, one in the parent directory and one in the project. OpenCode 2.0.22 lists both as `active` (with a shared id the second one was `failed: Duplicate plugin ID: graphify`), and the first shell command carries one reminder. OpenCode 1.18.34 loads both, and the first `bash` command carries one reminder.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments.
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

Note: I used Claude Code while working on this fix. I reviewed and ran all of it myself.

title: hook-guard reminders always say `graphify-out/graph.json`, even when `GRAPHIFY_OUT` points elsewhere
body:
## Summary

When the output directory is customized with `GRAPHIFY_OUT`, `graphify hook-guard` correctly uses the custom directory to decide *whether* to emit a reminder, but the reminder text itself still names `graphify-out/graph.json`. This request asks for the reminder text to name the effective output location instead.

## Current Behavior

Observed with graphifyy 0.9.74 on Windows 11, Claude Code PreToolUse hooks:

- `hook-guard read` and `hook-guard search` resolve the output directory from `GRAPHIFY_OUT` (via `out_path()`) for their decisions: graph existence, output-directory exclusion (#3959 fix works as expected), staleness.
- The `additionalContext` text they emit is fixed. All three reminders begin with or contain `graphify-out/graph.json`:
  - normal read reminder: `MANDATORY: graphify-out/graph.json exists. You MUST run graphify before reading source files. ...`
  - stale read reminder: `graphify-out/graph.json exists but may be STALE for this file ...`
  - search reminder: `MANDATORY: graphify-out/graph.json exists. You MUST run graphify query ... before grepping raw files. ...`
- The texts are module-level constants in `graphify/cli.py` (`_READ_NUDGE`, `_READ_NUDGE_STALE`, `_SEARCH_NUDGE`), built once at import time, and written unchanged by `_run_hook_guard`.
- We could not find an environment variable, CLI option, config file or template that changes this text in 0.9.74. (`hook-guard` accepts only the kind argument and `--strict`.)

## Example

| | Value |
|---|---|
| Configuration | `GRAPHIFY_OUT=artifacts/graphify` |
| Actual graph | `artifacts/graphify/graph.json` |
| No `graphify-out/` directory | true |
| Current reminder | `graphify-out/graph.json exists ...` |
| Expected reminder | `artifacts/graphify/graph.json exists ...` |

## Why This Is Inconsistent

The reminder is gated on the custom graph existing, then tells the agent a different path exists. In a project with no `graphify-out/` directory, the reminder names a file that is not there, while the hook's own decision was based on the configured location. An agent that follows the text literally (for example to read the graph or the report next to it) is pointed at the wrong directory.

## Expected Behavior

- With the default output directory, reminder text stays as it is today.
- When the output directory is customized through a supported mechanism (`GRAPHIFY_OUT`), every hook-guard reminder that names the graph location names the effective location instead (e.g. `artifacts/graphify/graph.json`).

How this is implemented (formatting at emit time, a helper, a template, etc.) is left to the maintainers.

## Scope

- `hook-guard read`: normal and stale reminders.
- `hook-guard search`: reminder.
- Possibly related, for the maintainers to decide: `_GEMINI_NUDGE_TEXT` (`hook-guard gemini`) also names `graphify-out/`. Not observed by us; listed only for completeness.

## Non-Goals

- No change to path containment / output-directory exclusion (#3959 fix).
- No change to when reminders fire, stale detection, `--strict` / `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT`, or fail-open behavior (always exit 0).
- Not asking for fully customizable reminder text.
- No change to installers or CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md sections written by `graphify install`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: With `GRAPHIFY_OUT` unset, the read, stale and search reminders are byte-identical to 0.9.74.
- AC2: With `GRAPHIFY_OUT=artifacts/graphify` and `artifacts/graphify/graph.json` present, the normal read reminder names `artifacts/graphify/graph.json` and does not contain `graphify-out/`.
- AC3: Same setup, a target file newer than `graph.json`: the stale reminder names `artifacts/graphify/graph.json`.
- AC4: Same setup, a search command (e.g. `grep -rn x .`): the search reminder names `artifacts/graphify/graph.json`.
- AC5: For the same inputs, whether a reminder is emitted is unchanged from 0.9.74 (e.g. reads under `artifacts/graphify/` still emit nothing; `tools/graphify/x.md` still emits a reminder).
- AC6: Exit code stays 0, nothing on stderr, and `--strict` / `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT` behave as in 0.9.74.
- AC7: The stdout JSON shape (`hookSpecificOutput.hookEventName`, `additionalContext`) is unchanged.

(Open question for maintainers: whether an absolute `GRAPHIFY_OUT` should be shown as given, or relative to the project root.)

## Environment

- graphifyy 0.9.74 (PyPI), Python 3.10.11, Windows 11
- Claude Code 2.1.287, PreToolUse hooks calling `graphify.exe hook-guard read` / `hook-guard search`
- `GRAPHIFY_OUT=artifacts/graphify`

## Reproduction

Read-only; does not build or update the graph.

1. In a project with an existing graph at `artifacts/graphify/graph.json` and no `graphify-out/` directory, set `GRAPHIFY_OUT=artifacts/graphify`.
2. Pipe valid JSON to the guard (generate it with a JSON library so Windows backslashes are escaped):
   `{"tool_name":"Read","tool_input":{"file_path":"src/app.py"}}` → `graphify hook-guard read`
3. Observe stdout: `additionalContext` starts with `MANDATORY: graphify-out/graph.json exists.`
4. Repeat with `{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"grep -rn x ."}}` → `graphify hook-guard search`; same path in the text.
5. Make the target file newer than `graph.json` (or use one that already is) and repeat step 2; the stale reminder also names `graphify-out/graph.json`.

## Additional Evidence

- A 22-case run of `hook-guard read|search` on 0.9.74 with `GRAPHIFY_OUT=artifacts/graphify` matched the expected nudge/no-nudge outcome in 22/22 cases, including the #3959 cases (`tools/graphify/…`, `.codex/skills/graphify/…`). The only issue left in that run was the path named in the text.
- Related: #3959 (output-directory exclusion with a custom `GRAPHIFY_OUT`), fixed in 0.9.74 via #3964.

title: AST extraction emits source_location=L1 for zero-byte source files (unsatisfiable provenance anchor)
body:
## Summary

AST extraction emits a provenance anchor for zero-byte source files:

```
source_file  = empty.py
file_type    = code
_origin      = ast
source_location = L1
```

`empty.py` is 0 bytes / 0 lines, so `L1` designates a line that does not exist. The anchor is unsatisfiable by construction: it can neither be resolved nor rejected by reading the file.

## Versions tested

| version | behavior |
|---|---|
| `graphifyy 0.9.72` | reproduces |
| `graphifyy 0.9.74` | reproduces (identical) |

Behavior is identical on both versions — 0.9.74 does not change it.

## Minimal fixture

Two files, one of them empty:

```
fixture/
  empty.py      0 bytes
  witness.py    VALUE = 1
```

## Commands

```bash
graphify extract ./fixture --out ./out --code-only
```

## Expected result

`empty.py` contains no code, so it should produce no code node. A file with 0 lines cannot carry a `source_location`.

## Actual result

```text
wrote graph.json: 2 nodes, 0 edges, 2 communities
```

Nodes emitted:

```text
id=empty     file_type=code  _origin=ast  source_file=empty.py    source_location=L1
id=witness   file_type=code  _origin=ast  source_file=witness.py  source_location=L1
```

`witness.py` has 1 line, so `L1` is correct there. Only the zero-byte file produces the impossible anchor.

## Why `L1` is invalid for a 0-byte file

`source_location` is a provenance anchor: it must designate a line that actually exists in the target file. For a 0-byte file:

- the file has 0 lines;
- `L1` designates a non-existent line;
- no line range is valid, so no anchor can be emitted at all.

Any provenance validator that compares `source_location` against the real file length will reject this. The node is therefore unusable for provenance purposes regardless of how the validator is configured.

## Impact

Affects any project containing zero-byte Python files — in practice, any Python package, since `__init__.py` files are frequently empty. Because the anchor is provably unsatisfiable, such nodes block strict provenance validation of the whole graph.

## Suggested fixes

Any one of these would resolve it:

1. do not emit a node for a 0-byte file;
2. emit the node without `source_location`;
3. emit the node as `file_type=file` instead of `code`.

## Environment

```text
graphify 0.9.72 / 0.9.74
Python 3.13
Windows
```

title: fix(hook-guard): name the effective graph.json when GRAPHIFY_OUT is customized
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4040. `hook-guard read` and `hook-guard search` decide whether to nudge from the configured output dir (`GRAPHIFY_OUT`), but the reminder text always said `graphify-out/graph.json`. With `GRAPHIFY_OUT=artifacts/graphify` the agent was told about a file that does not exist. The reminders now name the effective `graph.json`.

Implementation: a small helper `_nudge_for_out()` in `graphify/cli.py` rewrites the path in the read, stale-read and search reminders at emit time, using `out_path("graph.json")`. With the default output dir it returns the constant unchanged, so the default output is byte-identical. `_GEMINI_NUDGE_TEXT` (names `graphify-out/` generally, not observed in the issue) is left alone to keep this PR to one concern.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI

title: fix(extract): track calls to external Python modules
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3793.

`import requests` followed by `requests.get()` inside a function now records a `calls` edge from that function to the external module at the call line. The file-level import remains. Aliases work too, including when a separate `from` import shares the module or source line.

The fallback requires one exact plain-import binding and a conservative lexical check. Parameters, rebindings, type aliases and explicit dynamic namespace operations suppress it. Parsed local modules continue to resolve to their definitions; no external member nodes are invented. The AST cache schema changes so old raw facts are re-extracted.

title: fix(deps): cap tree-sitter-dm <0.26
body:
## Problem

The `dm` and `all` extras declare `tree-sitter-dm` with no upper bound. The **0.26.0** DreamMaker grammar changed the type-path node shape, so `extract_dm()` no longer finds type definitions — a `.dm` file comes back with only its own file node (verified: `/datum/weapon` etc. missing; grammar parses fine, but the node shape the extractor walks changed).

`uv.lock` pins `0.25.1`, so local dev and CI are unaffected. But a fresh `uvx --from graphifyy[all]` / `uvx --from graphifyy[dm]` resolves from PyPI with no constraint and pulls `0.26.0`, **silently breaking DM extraction for end users**.

## Fix

Cap both extras to `>=0.25,<0.26` (matching the existing `tree-sitter-cpp>=0.23,<0.25` pin style). `uv.lock` continues to resolve `0.25.1`; the full DM test suite stays green.

Found while running the 0.9.75 both-interpreter churn gate (a freshly-built 3.13 venv pulled 0.26.0 and 9 `test_dm_*` tests failed; pinning 0.25.1 made them pass).

A follow-up to re-support the 0.26.0 node shape in `extract_dm()` can lift the cap later.

title: Off-rubric INFERRED confidence_score still emitted at 9 sites; the #2813 guard does not cover them
body:
Follow-up to #2813 / #2823. Same class: INFERRED edges that carry a `confidence_score` outside the documented rubric (0.55 / 0.65 / 0.75 / 0.85 / 0.95), in places the guard test from that fix does not look at.

Found on `v8` @ 48d7c0e (0.9.75). Nine emission sites, all explicitly INFERRED:

| File | Line | Score |
|---|---|---|
| `graphify/cross_repo_calls.py` | 238 | 0.8 |
| `graphify/cross_repo_types.py` | 68 | 0.9 |
| `graphify/interface_dispatch.py` | 153 | 0.9 |
| `graphify/extract.py` | 3926, 4218, 4384, 4606, 4816, 5007 | 0.8, the else branch of `1.0 if type_qualified else 0.8` (and `1.0 if exact else 0.8` for Java) |

In each `extract.py` ternary the other branch is EXTRACTED / 1.0, so only the INFERRED side is off the scale.

## Why the existing guard misses them

`test_no_module_hardcodes_an_off_rubric_inferred_score` is parametrized over four files and matches the literal text `"confidence_score": 0.8,`. The ternary branches in `extract.py` are not that text, and `cross_repo_calls.py`, `cross_repo_types.py` and `interface_dispatch.py` are not in the list.

## Reproduce

```shell
grep -rnE 'confidence_score' graphify/*.py | grep -E '0\.8|0\.9'
```

This also prints a few score consumers (`.get("confidence_score", ...)` fallbacks) next to the nine emission lines above.

## Proposed fix

I have a patch ready and will open a PR that links here:

- Snap the nine sites to 0.85, following the #2813 precedent. 0.8 and 0.9 sit between rubric tiers, so 0.85 is the conservative same-tier choice. If you would rather have 0.95 for the two 0.9 sites, say so and I will change it.
- Replace the file-list guard with one that parses every `.py` under `graphify/` and checks dict values, keyword args, assignments and ternary branches.

EXTRACTED / 1.0 and AMBIGUOUS / 0.2 stay allowed. No edge targets, relations or tiers change.
