title: feat: Grok Build support (skill, AGENTS.md, hooks)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds [Grok Build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build) (xAI's `grok` CLI) as a graphify platform. It follows the existing platform patterns rather than introducing a new design: install scoping is the same as **amp / agents**, and the hook is wired the way **Codex**'s is, using **Claude Code**'s `hook-guard` entries.

Closes #2228

### Why

Grok already picks graphify up today through its Claude compat layer (a normal `graphify install` lands in `.claude/skills` / `CLAUDE.md`, which Grok scans). What doesn't work is:
- **Hooks load but never fire.** Grok sends camelCase payloads (`toolName` / `toolInput` / `sessionId`, and `read_file` uses `target_file`), so `hook-guard` silently prints nothing.
- **The semantic step assumes Claude's Agent tool** (`subagent_type="general-purpose"`), which Grok's subagent API doesn't take.

This PR adds a native grok path so both work properly rather than by accident.

### What's added

**1. Skill + AGENTS.md** (`feat: add Grok Build skill and AGENTS.md integration`)

| Command | Writes |
|---|---|
| `graphify install --platform grok` | skill only, at `$GROK_HOME/skills/graphify/` (default `~/.grok/skills`), like `--platform amp` |
| `graphify grok install` | that user skill plus the `## graphify` section in `./AGENTS.md` (like `graphify amp install`) |
| `graphify grok install --project` | `./.grok/skills/graphify/` plus AGENTS.md (via `_project_install`'s amp/codex group) |
| `graphify grok uninstall [--project]`, `graphify uninstall` | reverse the above |

- **Skillgen slot.** Grok's subagent tool (`spawn_subagent`) can't take Pi's `subagent_type="general-purpose"` dispatch, because Grok rejects built-in types passed by name ([docs](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/blob/main/crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/16-subagents.md)). A new platform key, `semantic = "subagents" | "sequential"`, therefore renders Part B as in-session sequential extraction for grok, using 18 `@@SEM_*@@` slots (12 in `core/core.md`, 6 in `references/shared/`). The fragments live in `tools/skillgen/fragments/semantic/{subagents,sequential}/`; the `subagents/` fragments are the original text, extracted verbatim.
- **Grok's Part B renames an invalid chunk** to `.json.invalid` so the merge skips it. The all-cached case (still run B3) now comes from v8's shared fix, which the sequential fragment follows too.
- **Other platforms are unchanged.** Every non-grok generated file is byte-identical.
- **Why AGENTS.md:** Grok reads both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, so writing CLAUDE.md too would duplicate the section. GROK.md is not a documented instruction file. `.grok/rules` is loaded in addition to AGENTS.md.
- **`tests/conftest.py`** now also clears `GROK_HOME`, next to `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so the suite can never write into a contributor's real Grok home.

**2. Hooks** (`feat: add Grok Build hook support`)
- **Installer.** `graphify grok install [--project]` registers `_claude_pretooluse_hooks()` (matchers `Bash|Grep` → `graphify hook-guard search` and `Read|Glob` → `graphify hook-guard read`, timeout 10) in `.grok/hooks/graphify.json`.
- **detect.** `.grok/hooks/graphify.json` is added to the graphify-written files `detect` skips (#4057), so a project install doesn't get indexed.
  - It is called from `_agents_install` exactly where the Codex hook is installed: merged, backed up, with the absolute exe for a user install and the bare `graphify` for `--project` (#3129).
  - Grok maps Claude matcher names to its own tools (Bash→`run_terminal_command`, Read→`read_file`, Grep→`grep`, Glob→`list_dir`).
  - Grok accepts `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` and `permissionDecision` ([10-hooks.md](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/blob/main/crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/10-hooks.md)), so it gets the real nudge, not Codex's no-op `hook-check` (#651).
- **Guard (`graphify/cli.py`).** `hook-guard` reads Grok's camelCase keys (`toolInput` / `toolName` / `sessionId`) when `tool_input` / `tool_name` / `session_id` are absent. It uses `read_file`'s `target_file` as the target and accepts `read_file` alongside `Read` for the opt-in strict block. The Claude Code path is unchanged, because snake_case keys always win.
- **Own hook file.** Grok loads every `.grok/hooks/*.json`, so graphify uses its own file rather than a shared one like `.codex/hooks.json`. Uninstall deletes the file once it has no hooks left, together with its graphify-only `.graphify-bak`, and prunes empty `.grok/hooks` and `.grok` directories. Non-graphify entries in the file are preserved.

### How to use it

```bash
graphify grok install            # user skill + AGENTS.md + .grok/hooks/graphify.json
graphify grok install --project  # project skill (.grok/skills) instead; commit .grok/ and AGENTS.md
grok --trust                     # once per project, or /hooks-trust inside a session
graphify update .                # build graphify-out/ (AST, no LLM); or /graphify . inside Grok
```

Grok loads project AGENTS.md, project skills and project hooks **only in a trusted folder**. The installer prints this hint.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [x] Refactor (skillgen semantic slot; no output change for existing hosts)
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariants**
- Every non-grok generated artifact (`graphify/skill-*.md`, `graphify/skills/*/references/`, `graphify/always_on/`, `tools/skillgen/expected/`) is byte-identical to v8.
- The grok skill contains no Agent-tool / `subagent_type` instructions.
- The Claude Code / Codebuddy hook payload path is unchanged.
- The guard always exits 0 and fails open: bad JSON, a non-dict `toolInput`, an empty `sessionId` or a marker-write failure never blocks.
- The strict block fires at most once per session.
- Install and uninstall are idempotent, preserve user content in AGENTS.md and the hook file, and refuse to rewrite a malformed hook file.

**Two existing tests had to change:**
- `test_skillgen.py::#1461` now also accepts the sequential wording, and still requires "do not stall".
- The consolidation-allowlist test now includes grok, because its renamed Part B heading needs an allowlist entry, as kilo's and vscode's do.

**Other notes**
- `--audit-coverage` uses amp's v8 body as Grok's baseline, the same as for `agents`.
- `skill-grok.md` is added to pyproject package-data.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant. (Before this change, `hook-guard` printed nothing for a Grok-shaped payload.)
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test. (`tests/test_grok_platform.py`, 22 tests; `tests/test_grok_hooks.py`, 31 tests. The env is isolated.)
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

### End-to-end test (grok CLI 1.0.46, no model calls)

The test used a fresh venv with this branch installed editable, plus a throwaway `HOME`/`GROK_HOME` and a sample repo.

- **Installs:** `install --platform grok`, `grok install` and `grok install --project` write the expected skill paths, a single AGENTS.md section and `.grok/hooks/graphify.json`.
- **Untrusted folder:** `grok inspect` shows `Skills: graphify user` and 0 instructions / 0 hooks.
- **Trusted folder (`grok --trust inspect` / `grok inspect --json`):**
  - `AGENTS.md` loads as a project instruction.
  - `graphify` shows as a project skill; the project copy overrides the user copy.
  - Hooks: `matcher=Bash|Grep` → `graphify hook-guard search` and `matcher=Read|Glob` → `graphify hook-guard read`, both from the project.
- **graphify itself:** `graphify update .`, `graphify query "how does login check the password"` and `graphify path handle_login get_user` work.
- **Hook commands:** Grok-documented payloads were piped into the exact commands in `.grok/hooks/graphify.json`. Every exit code is 0.
  - `read_file`, the `grep` tool, and a `run_terminal_command` running `grep -r` get the nudge.
  - `ls`, `list_dir` of a directory, an out-of-project read, `web_search` and bad JSON are silent.
  - With `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT=1`: the first read in a session is denied once, then nudged; a new session is denied again; an empty session id is never blocked.
- **Uninstall:** `grok uninstall --project` and then `grok uninstall` remove the skills, the section, the hook file and `.grok/`. `grok inspect` then shows 0 skills, instructions and hooks.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv sync --all-extras --frozen
uv run python -m tools.skillgen && uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless   # no diff
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --check                # OK, 143 artifacts
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --audit-coverage       # OK
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --always-on-roundtrip  # OK
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --monolith-roundtrip   # OK
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --schema-singleton     # OK
uv run pytest -q tests/test_grok_platform.py tests/test_grok_hooks.py tests/test_hook_strict.py tests/test_skillgen.py tests/test_install_roundtrip.py
uv run pytest -q          # 3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14 (all extras): only the 9 DM tests fail, same as clean v8 with tree-sitter-dm 0.26.0
uv run ruff check .       # clean
uv run pyright            # 636 errors, the identical set to upstream v8 (no new errors)
# e2e: graphify grok install [--project]; grok inspect; grok --trust inspect; grok inspect --json;
#      graphify update .; graphify query/path; hook commands fed Grok payloads; graphify grok uninstall [--project]
```

## Limitations

- Tested live on Linux with Grok Build 1.0.46 (hooks and a full `/graphify .` run, including the all-cached path; results in the PR comments). Not tested on Windows/PowerShell.
- Grok only loads project `AGENTS.md`, skills and hooks in a trusted folder (`grok --trust`).

title: fix(extract): stop walking JSON Schema files as config manifests (#2255)
body:
## Problem

`_is_config_json()` decides whether a `.json` file is worth AST-walking. It matches by filename first, then falls back to a root-key probe:

```python
_CONFIG_JSON_KEYS = frozenset({
    "dependencies", ..., "extends", "$ref", "$schema", "compilerOptions",
})
```

`$schema` belongs in that set — configs legitimately carry it. But it is also the **defining marker of a JSON Schema**, so every schema document satisfied the probe and was walked in full. That re-opens the keyword-node explosion #1224 closed for data JSON.

Measured impact from the report: one 160 KB contract contributed **362 nodes** labelled with bare schema keywords (`description` ×113, `type` ×83, `$ref` ×53, `required` ×20, `properties` ×20, …) plus ~12 schema-only communities, which pollutes clustering, god-node analysis and `GRAPH_REPORT.md` — 13% of a 2,725-node graph.

A minimal reproduction of my own (a 20-line schema with `$id` + `$defs`) already yields 34 nodes / 34 edges, with `description` ×7 and `type` ×7 as graph nodes.

## Implementation

Two changes, both ahead of the existing probe:

1. **Drop `$ref` from the probe keys.** A root-level `$ref` is a schema construct and never a config signal. Unambiguous — no real config has one.

2. **Return `False` when the root object carries `$schema` *plus* a schema-definition marker** (`$defs`, `definitions`, or `$id`). This is what separates *"this file IS a schema"* from *"this config POINTS AT a schema"*: the latter points `$schema` at its own tool's schema (`biomejs.dev`, `docs.renovatebot.com`) and never carries these markers.

The root keys are now collected once into a set, so the schema check and the config probe read the file the same way instead of walking the root twice.

### Why this is low-risk

The filename branches run **before** the probe, so `biome.json` / `renovate.json` / `angular.json` / `package.json` / `tsconfig.json` never depended on it. Only arbitrarily-named files did.

I built a control matrix and ran it before and after — every config shape keeps **byte-identical node counts**:

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `biome.json` (`$schema` + config keys) | True, 4 nodes | True, 4 nodes |
| `renovate.json` (`$schema` + `extends`) | True, 4 nodes | True, 4 nodes |
| `package.json` / `tsconfig.json` | True, 5 / 3 | True, 5 / 3 |
| `foo.eslintrc.json` / `api.tsconfig.json` | True, 3 / 3 | True, 3 / 3 |
| `custom.config.json` (probe: `extends`) | True, 4 nodes | True, 4 nodes |
| `weird.json` (probe: `compilerOptions`) | True, 3 nodes | True, 3 nodes |
| `contracts/events-v1.json` (`$schema`+`$defs`) | **True, 5 nodes** | **False, 0** |
| `ref.json` (root `$ref`) | **True, 2 nodes** | **False, 0** |

I deliberately used the **structural** markers rather than inspecting the `$schema` *value* for `json-schema.org`. The value check is tempting but unreliable (a custom meta-schema can be a local path) and it would make classification depend on URL substring matching — worse for the determinism invariant than spec-defined key names.

## Documented limitation

A hand-written schema carrying `$schema` but **no** `$defs` / `definitions` / `$id` is still walked. Closing that needs a keyword-density heuristic, which risks skipping a real config whose keys happen to overlap schema vocabulary — the worse error, since it drops structure silently, exactly what #1224 was about.

Rather than guess, it is documented in the `_is_config_json` docstring and pinned by `test_minimal_schema_without_defs_or_id_is_still_walked`, so closing it later is a deliberate change with a test rather than an accident. Happy to attempt the heuristic if you'd prefer fuller coverage.

Also updated the now-inaccurate `extract_json` docstring, which still advertised `$ref` as a probe signal.

## Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/test_json_schema_config.py -q    # 14 passed
uv run pytest tests/ -q                              # 28 failed, 6262 passed, 101 skipped
uv run ruff check .                                  # All checks passed!
uv run pyright                                       # 636 errors
```

- **5 of the 14 new tests fail on the pre-fix tree** (confirmed by reverting `json_config.py` and re-running). The other 9 are deliberate: config-side guards against over-correcting, plus the documented-limit case.
- **Baseline captured on a clean v0.9.75 checkout: `28 failed, 6248 passed, 101 skipped`.** The 28 failures are **byte-identical** between the two runs — diffed test-id-by-test-id, not compared by count. title: zig: tagged-union variants are dropped from the graph
body:
## What happens

A Zig tagged union keeps its methods but loses every variant. Given:

```zig
const Shape = union(enum) {
    circle: f64,
    rectangle: struct { w: f64, h: f64 },
    point,

    pub fn area(self: Shape) f64 { return 0; }
};
```

the graph has `Shape` and `.area()` but no `circle` / `rectangle` / `point`, so the union sits as a near-memberless leaf.

## Why

The `container_field` branch in `graphify/extractors/zig.py` only fires when the field's parent is an `enum_declaration`. A tagged union's variants are `container_field` nodes under a `union_declaration`, so they fall through and are never emitted.

## Expected

A tagged union's variants are its discriminant cases — the same shape as enum members — so each should become a node with a `case_of` edge to the union, matching enums (Java #1719, Swift, Scala) and the Zig enum / error-set handling already in place. A bare `union { ... }` has typed data fields (not cases) and should stay untouched, like a struct's fields.

title: fix(zig): emit a node per tagged-union variant with a case_of edge
body:
Closes #4049

## Problem

A Zig tagged union keeps its methods but drops every variant:

```zig
const Shape = union(enum) {
    circle: f64,
    rectangle: struct { w: f64, h: f64 },
    point,
    pub fn area(self: Shape) f64 { return 0; }
};
```

The graph gets `Shape` and `.area()` but none of `circle` / `rectangle` / `point`.

## Cause

The `container_field` branch in `zig.py` only fires for an `enum_declaration` parent. A tagged union's variants are `container_field` nodes under a `union_declaration`, so they were never emitted.

## Fix

A tagged union's variants are its discriminant cases — the same shape as enum members — so emit a node + `case_of` edge per variant, exactly like the existing enum and error-set handling (and Java #1719 / Swift / Scala). Gated by `_is_tagged_union`, which keys off the `(enum)` / `(Tag)` parenthesis: a bare `union { ... }` has typed data fields, not cases, so — like a struct's fields — it stays untouched.

## Tests

Added `test_zig_tagged_union_variants_emit_case_of_nodes`: asserts each variant of a `union(enum)` and a `union(Tag)` becomes a node with a `case_of` edge, and that a bare `union { ... }` mints no variant nodes. The test fails on current `v8` and passes with the fix. Full suite: 6345 passed, 15 skipped. `ruff` and `pyright` clean on the touched files.

title: cpp: a named union is dropped from the graph entirely
body:
## What happens

A named C++ `union` and everything it declares produce no nodes at all — the whole type vanishes. Given:

```cpp
union Value { int i; float f; };
struct Point { int x; };
```

the graph has `Point` (and its members) but no `Value`, `i`, or `f`.

## Why

`union_specifier` is missing from `_CPP_CONFIG.class_types` in `graphify/extract.py`. `class_specifier`, `struct_specifier`, and `enum_specifier` are all present, so classes/structs/enums become type nodes while a union falls through and is dropped.

## Expected

A `union_specifier` is a class-like container with the identical name/body fields as `struct_specifier` (`type_identifier` + `field_declaration_list`), so a named union should become a type node with its data members, like a struct. An anonymous union (no `type_identifier`) should be skipped, like an anonymous enum.

title: fix(cpp): extract union specifiers as class-like type nodes
body:
Closes #4051

## Problem

A named C++ `union` is dropped from the graph entirely — the type and all its members vanish:

```cpp
union Value { int i; float f; };
struct Point { int x; };
```

`Point` and its members are in the graph; `Value` / `i` / `f` are not.

## Cause

`union_specifier` was missing from `_CPP_CONFIG.class_types`. `class_specifier`, `struct_specifier`, and `enum_specifier` are all there, so a union was the only class-like container that fell through and was dropped.

## Fix

Add `union_specifier` to `class_types`. It shares struct_specifier's name/body fields (`type_identifier` + `field_declaration_list`), so the existing generic container handling gives it a type node, a `contains` edge from its file, and a data member per field — exactly like a struct. An anonymous union has no `type_identifier` and is skipped by the existing name guard, like an anonymous enum.

## Tests

Added `test_cpp_union_specifier_is_extracted`: a named union becomes a type node with `defines` edges to its members, and a `typedef union { ... } Anon` mints no nameless node. Fails on current `v8`, passes with the fix. Full suite: 6345 passed, 15 skipped. `ruff` clean; `pyright` on extract.py unchanged (119 errors before and after, 0 added).

title: vbnet: enum members use a contains edge instead of case_of
body:
## What happens

A VB.NET enum's members are linked to the enum with a `contains` edge, while every other language with enums emits `case_of`:

```vbnet
Public Enum Color
    Red
    Green
    Blue
End Enum
```

`Red` / `Green` / `Blue` become nodes, but under `contains`, not `case_of`.

## Why

In `graphify/extractors/vbnet.py`, `enum_member` nodes are emitted through the same `add_data_member` helper as real class fields, which always adds a `contains` edge. VB.NET is the lone outlier — Java (#1719), C#, Swift, Scala, C++, Rust, Zig, PHP all emit `case_of` per enum member.

## Why it matters

The relation is not cosmetic. `case_of` (and `defines`) targets are excluded from `New X()` / `new X()` constructor binding (`_member_nids` in `extract.py`). Because VB.NET enum members are `contains`, an enum member whose name matches a type can be mis-resolved as that type's constructor.

## Expected

An enum member is a discriminant case, so it should get a `case_of` edge, like every other language. Real class fields keep `contains`.

title: fix(vbnet): link enum members with case_of instead of contains
body:
Closes #4053

## Problem

A VB.NET enum's members hang off the enum with a `contains` edge, while every other language with enums emits `case_of`:

```vbnet
Public Enum Color
    Red
    Green
    Blue
End Enum
```

## Cause

`enum_member` nodes went through the same `add_data_member` helper as real class fields, which always emits `contains`. VB.NET was the only language still doing this (Java #1719, C#, Swift, Scala, C++, Rust, Zig, PHP all use `case_of`).

## Why it matters

The relation carries resolution semantics, not just a label. `case_of` and `defines` targets are excluded from `New X()` constructor binding (`_member_nids` in `extract.py`); as `contains`, a VB.NET enum member whose name matches a type could be mis-bound as that type's constructor.

## Fix

Give `add_data_member` an optional `relation` argument (default `contains`) and pass `case_of` for the `enum_member` path only. Real class fields are untouched.

## Tests

Added `test_vbnet_enum_members_emit_case_of_not_contains`: enum members get `case_of` (and not `contains`), while a real class field keeps `contains` (and not `case_of`). Fails on current `v8`, passes with the fix. Full suite: 6345 passed, 15 skipped. `ruff` and `pyright` clean on the touched file.

title: pascal: an enumerated type is dropped from the graph entirely
body:
## What happens

A Pascal/Delphi enumerated type and all of its values produce no nodes at all — the whole type vanishes. Given:

```pascal
type
  TColor = (clRed, clGreen, clBlue);
```

the graph has nothing for `TColor`, `clRed`, `clGreen`, or `clBlue`.

## Why

In `graphify/extractors/pascal.py`, the `declType` handler only emits a node when the type's kind is `declClass`, `declIntf`, or `declHelper`. An enumerated type parses as `declType -> type -> declEnum -> declEnumValue`, which matches none of those, so the declaration falls through to a plain child walk and is dropped.

## Expected

An enumerated type is a named type whose values are its cases. It should become a type node with a `case_of` edge per value, matching every other language with enums (Java #1719 / C# / Swift / Scala) and the existing class/interface handling.

Note: this is the AST (tree-sitter-pascal) path, which is the AST-quality extractor; the regex fallback used when tree-sitter-pascal isn't installed only models classes/interfaces and is out of scope here.

title: fix(pascal): extract enumerated types and their values
body:
Closes #4055

## Problem

A Pascal/Delphi enumerated type and all of its values are dropped from the graph — the whole type vanishes:

```pascal
type
  TColor = (clRed, clGreen, clBlue);
```

Nothing for `TColor` / `clRed` / `clGreen` / `clBlue` reaches the graph.

## Cause

The `declType` handler only emits a node for `declClass` / `declIntf` / `declHelper` kinds. An enumerated type parses as `declType -> type -> declEnum -> declEnumValue`, so it matched nothing and fell through to a bare child walk that emits no node.

## Fix

Detect a `declEnum` under the `declType`'s `type` child and emit the type node (with a `contains` edge from its unit/file) plus a `case_of` edge per `declEnumValue` — the Pascal parity of the Java #1719 / C# / Swift / Scala enum handling. Class/interface/helper handling is unchanged, and a record type still extracts as before.

This fixes the tree-sitter (`tree-sitter-pascal`) path, which is the AST-quality extractor. The regex fallback (used only when tree-sitter-pascal isn't installed) models just classes/interfaces and is intentionally left as-is.

## Tests

Added `test_pascal_enum_type_and_values_are_extracted` (guarded on `tree_sitter_pascal` being installed, since the AST path is required): the enum type and each value become nodes, with a `case_of` edge per value. Fails on current `v8`, passes with the fix. Full suite: 6345 passed, 15 skipped. `ruff` and `pyright` clean on the touched file.

title: fix(elixir): scope import/use to the declaring module, not the file
body:
## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #4015 (shipped in 0.9.75). It fixes the finding the graphify-labs review raised on that PR: "One mutable call-scope list is shared by every module and call in a file".

The finding is real. #4015 collected every `import`/`use` in a file into one list, so an import in one module leaked into a sibling module in the same file. Elixir scopes `import`/`use` to the module body it appears in and to modules nested in it. Repro on `v8` (48d7c0e):

```elixir
# lib/my_app/pair.ex           (MyApp.Helpers.fmt/1 lives in helpers.ex)
defmodule MyApp.Importer do
  import MyApp.Helpers
  def show(x) do fmt(x) end          # in scope: should bind
  defmodule Nested do
    def inner(x) do fmt(x) end       # nested, inherits the import: should bind
  end
end

defmodule MyApp.Sibling do
  def go(x) do fmt(x) end            # no import: must not bind, but did
end
```

The extractor now records `import`/`use` targets per enclosing module, with the file's top level as its own scope. Each call's `elixir_call_scope` is built from its own module, the modules enclosing it, and the top level. Each raw call also gets its own list instead of sharing one mutable list with every other call in the file. Separately, a module nested in a same-named module (`defmodule Foo do defmodule Foo do`) gets the same node id, so the walk up the enclosing chain stops at a module it has already visited. Without that guard, extraction of such a file never terminates (checked: it hangs until killed).

Nothing changes in the shared resolver beyond its comment. The candidate side, which keeps candidates whose file defines an in-scope top-level module, is the same as in #4015.

- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.

## How was this tested?

New test `test_import_is_scoped_to_the_module_that_declares_it` in `tests/test_elixir_unqualified_call_scope.py`. It uses the shape above and asserts `show → fmt` and `inner → fmt` bind while `go → fmt` does not.

I also checked that each piece matters. Keying all imports to the file again, or not walking enclosing modules, each makes the new test fail. Dropping the visited-set guard makes the self-nested case hang.

title: `extract()` raises `ValueError` on Windows when a symbol-less file and `root` are on different drives (regression in 0.9.75)
body:
## Summary

The "cleanly parsed code file yields no symbols" warning added in 0.9.75 (#4009, fixes #3946) builds the displayed path with an unguarded `os.path.relpath` in `graphify/extract.py`:

```python
_symbolless_files.append((os.path.relpath(str(_p), str(root)).replace("\\", "/"), _size))
```

On Windows `os.path.relpath` raises `ValueError: path is on mount 'D:', start on mount 'C:'` when the file and `root` are on different drives, so a diagnostic warning aborts the whole extraction.

The automated review on #4009 already flagged this risk ("`os.path.relpath` can raise `ValueError` and crash `extract()` for out-of-root paths on Windows", medium severity). This issue adds a concrete reproduction, the affected tests, and a verified fix.

## Environment

Windows 11, Python 3.12.13, graphify v0.9.75 (`48d7c0e8`).

## Reproduction

`root` is not passed, so `extract()` falls back to `cache_root` (`elif cache_root is not None: root = cache_root`).

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract

p = Path(r"D:\proj\a.py")   # contains only: "# comment\nX = 1\n"  -> the file yields exactly 1 node
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:   # %TEMP% is on C:
    extract([p], cache_root=Path(td))
```

Result on v0.9.75:

```
ValueError: path is on mount 'D:', start on mount 'C:'
```

- On v0.9.74 the same call succeeds.
- On v0.9.75 the same call succeeds when `root=p.parent` is passed explicitly.
- The test suite hits it too when the checkout is on a different drive from `%TEMP%`: `tests/test_languages.py::test_objc_bridging_header_not_isolated` and `tests/test_languages.py::test_objc_paired_no_dangling_edges` fail, because the `_corpus()` helper passes only `cache_root=<tmp dir>`. A clean v0.9.75 checkout on `D:` gives 2 failed; the same checkout on `C:` gives 2 passed.

## Scope

- The `graphify extract` CLI is not affected: it passes `root=target` explicitly (`ast_kwargs: dict = {"cache_root": out_root, "root": target}`). Checked end to end with the repo on `D:`, `GRAPHIFY_OUT` on `C:` and one symbol-less `.py` file: the warning is printed, `graph.json` is written, exit code 0.
- Affected: callers of `extract()` that pass `cache_root` without `root` on a different drive from the scanned files, and the test suite on Windows checkouts outside the temp drive.

## Suggested fix

```python
try:
    _rel = os.path.relpath(str(_p), str(root)).replace("\\", "/")
except ValueError:          # different drive on Windows
    _rel = _p.as_posix()
_symbolless_files.append((_rel, _size))
```

Applied to a clean v0.9.75 checkout on `D:`: the reproduction above succeeds, the `-k objc` tests in `tests/test_languages.py` pass (33 passed), and `tests/test_partial_extraction_warning.py` passes (11 passed).

title: [Feature]: skill.md — "Do not skip steps" contradicts the documented skips; shouted MANDATORY Agent-tool line; API-key note stated twice
body:
### Problem or use case

`graphify/skill.md` (generated from `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md`) gives the agent instructions that conflict:

1. **"Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps."** (`skill.md:59`, `core.md:56`) follows the fast path at `:53`, which says to **skip Steps 1–5 entirely** when `graphify-out/graph.json` exists and the request is a question. The steps then skip conditionally themselves (Step 0 only for a URL or several paths — "A plain local path skips this step"; Part B has its own "skip Part B entirely" fast path). An agent that follows instructions literally must break one of them; "do not skip" is the absolute one, so the cost is a needless rebuild instead of a `graphify query`.
2. **`:214`** — "**MANDATORY: You MUST use the Agent tool here. Reading files yourself one-by-one is forbidden … If you do not use the Agent tool you are doing this wrong.**" Current Claude models follow instructions closely and tend to over-apply stacked caps/absolutes — here, spawning subagents even when the code-only fast path or a tiny doc set makes Part B unnecessary. The reason (5–10× faster) is the load-bearing part.
3. **API-key note stated twice** — `:163` and `:170` say the same thing in two blockquotes, and #2513 reports the claim itself is inaccurate (`llm.py` `detect_backend()`). Whatever #2513 settles should appear once.

### Proposed solution

In `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md`, then `uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`:

1. Replace "Follow these steps in order. Do not skip steps." with: "Run the steps in order. Skip a step only where it says so (the fast path above, Step 0 for a plain local path, Part B for a code-only corpus)."
2. Replace the MANDATORY line with: "Dispatch semantic extraction with the Agent tool — one subagent per chunk; it is 5–10× faster than reading files yourself. Skip this when the Part B fast path applies."
3. Merge the two API-key blockquotes into one, using whatever wording #2513 lands on.

### Alternatives considered

Fix only the contradiction in (1) and keep the absolute wording in (2) — resolves the conflict but keeps the over-application risk. Splitting the skill (#1641) is complementary, not a substitute.

### Area

Skills or assistant integrations

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

No, I just wanted to request it

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Generated skills only (every `graphify/skill*.md` built from `core.md` changes on regenerate). No effect on node/edge IDs, cache semantics, graph.json schema, MCP output, or incremental updates.

### Additional context

Related: #2513, #1641, #3768. Found in 0.9.53; confirmed unchanged on `v8` HEAD (`core.md:50/56/167`).

title: fix(detect): skip graphify's own installed skill folders (#4057)
body:

graphify's own `graphify/skills/<host>/` tree, a top-level `skills/graphify/` and your other skills/rules are still indexed. The tests cover those cases and run every installer in `install.py`, so a platform that writes a new file fails them.

title: feat: cache Graphify context outside the repository
body:
I work on multiple projects where `main` changes frequently.

My usual workflow looks like this:

1. Generate a Graphify map of the repository.
2. Use `graph.json`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and the visualization as context for my coding agent.
3. Before starting another contribution, sync my local branch with the latest upstream `main`.
4. Continue working from the updated codebase.

The problem is that Graphify's generated files are local-only and usually ignored by Git. In some Git workflows, such as resetting or cleaning the local repository while syncing with upstream, this local Graphify context can be removed.

I then have to generate the graph again.

Graphify already supports `--update`, which is useful when the existing graph is still available. The problem is when the local graph itself is lost during repository maintenance.

Would it make sense for Graphify to support storing its local graph outside the repository?

For example:

```text
~/.graphify/projects/<repository>/
```

The repository could then reference that local graph instead of depending entirely on `graphify-out/` inside the working tree.

This could allow a workflow like:

```text
clone/sync repository
        ↓
Graphify finds the existing local graph
        ↓
detect changed files
        ↓
update only what changed
```

Instead of:

```text
clone/sync repository
        ↓
local Graphify output is gone
        ↓
build the project graph again
```

The exact implementation could be different. The main idea is simply to make Graphify's local knowledge persistent across branch resets, upstream syncs, or other Git operations that replace or clean the working tree.

This would be especially useful for contributors working on fast-moving repositories, where pulling or resetting to the latest upstream branch happens frequently.

Is there already a recommended workflow for this, or would persistent repository-level local storage be useful?

title: Rust: `const _` gets its file's node ID, so the file node is relabelled `_` and gains a self-loop
body:
Version: graphifyy 0.9.69

An anonymous Rust constant (`const _: () = assert!(...);`, the usual compile-time assertion) gets the same node ID as the file that declares it. When the graph is built, the constant's label and location replace the file node's, and the file's `contains` edge to the constant becomes a self-loop.

Repro, `src/codec.rs`:

```rust
use core::fmt;

pub const WIDTH: usize = 8;

const _: () = assert!(WIDTH == 1 << 3);

pub fn encode() {}
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract
from graphify.build import build_from_json

r = extract([Path("src/codec.rs")], cache_root=Path("."))
G = build_from_json(r, root=".", directed=False)
```

`extract()` emits two nodes with the ID `src_codec`:

```
N src_codec 'codec.rs' L1
N src_codec '_' L5
E src_codec contains src_codec L5
```

After `build_from_json`, `G.nodes["src_codec"]` has label `_` and `source_location` `L5`, and `(src_codec, src_codec)` is a self-loop.

Cause: `extractors/rust.py` (the `static_item` / `const_item` branch) builds the ID with `_make_id(stem, item_name)`. `make_id` strips `_` from each part, so the name `_` becomes empty, the join gives `src_codec_`, and `normalize_id` strips the trailing underscore. The result is the bare stem, which is also what `_file_node_id` returns for the file.

Effect on a real project: the file node is shown as `_`. Every import and `contains` edge of the file is attached to it, so a module with a few imports ranks as a god node and a cross-community bridge in `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and the graph health check reports a self-loop.

Possible fix: skip `const _` / `static _` in the Rust extractor, since an anonymous constant can't be referenced. Alternatively, have `make_id` refuse a part that strips to empty, so no symbol can collapse onto its file's ID.

title: fix(dedup): keep unstamped document nodes apart across files
body:
## What does this PR do?

An unstamped document or rationale node stays in its own source file when another file has the same label. Fixes #3094.

`deduplicate_entities` pass 1 groups equal normalized labels, then unions the cross-file residue without calling `_crossfile_fileanchored_blocked`. The fuzzy pass already calls that function, so near-matches stay apart (#1284). Equal labels never reach it. #296 let unstamped `document` and `rationale` nodes into that residue, and the 0.9.66 check still collapses five of those nodes to two on 0.9.75 (`48d7c0e`).

Each cross-file union now calls the existing block, including the protected-id branches. Pairs the block still allows are joined to each other, so two concept nodes beside a blocked document stay one node. The same-file loop, `_reads_as_file_entity`, and the fuzzy pass are unchanged.

- [ ] Security fix

The invariant: a `document` or `rationale` node is not merged into a node from another source file. A same-file duplicate still becomes one node. Two `concept` nodes with the same label still become one node. No graph file is written by these tests.

The assertion also requires one `concept` and one `document`, so a patch that only skips the join from the document winner (leaving three nodes) fails it too. title: [Bug]: export html/neo4j/falkordb/canvas, merge-driver and global add reverse stored edge direction
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Several commands that reload `graph.json` reverse the direction of stored edges. Some write the reversal to disk: the git merge driver rewrites the committed `graph.json`, and `global add` writes `~/.graphify/global-graph.json`.

`graph.json` is written with `"directed": false`. The real direction is in each link's arc order (`source` → `target`, since #563), or in `_src`/`_tgt` on older files (#2309). A plain undirected `json_graph.node_link_graph()` load re-orders each edge's endpoints by node-list position. **An edge comes back reversed exactly when its target node comes before its source node in the node list.** On graphify's own `graph.json` that is 21,098 of 26,727 links (79%). It is deterministic, so the output looks stable.

Several readers already handle this with the `_src = link.get("_src", link["source"])` idiom: `query`, `path`/`explain`, `affected`, `merge-graphs` and the MCP server (#1174, #2261, #2309, #2487). These paths still don't:

| Path | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| merge driver (`graphify hook install`) | `paths.load_node_link_graph` + raw `node_link_data` write in `merge-driver` | **Rewrites the committed graph.json reversed**, even when merging three identical copies. Later readers take it as truth. |
| `global add` | undirected load in `global_graph.global_add` | `~/.graphify/global-graph.json` stored reversed; `path` on the global graph gives wrong routes. |
| `graphify update` / `watch` / git hooks | `watch._reconcile_graph_html` → `load_node_link_graph` | graph.html arrows backwards after any topology change (one 1-function edit: 14/19 arrows reversed). |
| `export html` | export loader in `cli.py` | graph.html arrows backwards. |
| `export neo4j` / `export falkordb` (cypher.txt and `--push`) | export loader; `to_cypher`, `push_to_neo4j`, `push_to_falkordb` ignore `_src`/`_tgt` | `(a)-[:CALLS]->(b)` written as `(b)-[:CALLS]->(a)`, so "who calls X" queries return callees. |
| `export obsidian` → `graph.canvas` | export loader; `to_canvas` ignores `_src`/`_tgt` | Canvas arrows backwards. |

Expected: every output keeps the direction stored in `graph.json`.

Not affected: `cluster-only`/`label` HTML (rebuilt via `build_from_json`), and the readers listed above. `export graphml` declares `edgedefault="undirected"`, so it drops direction rather than contradicting it.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p repro/graphify-out && cd repro
cat > graphify-out/graph.json <<'EOF'
{"directed": false, "multigraph": false, "graph": {},
 "nodes": [{"id": "normalize", "label": "normalize()", "file_type": "code", "source_file": "util.py"},
           {"id": "tokenize", "label": "tokenize()", "file_type": "code", "source_file": "util.py"}],
 "links": [{"source": "tokenize", "target": "normalize", "relation": "calls", "confidence": "EXTRACTED"}]}
EOF
# graph.json: tokenize calls normalize. The callee is listed first in "nodes".

graphify export neo4j
grep CALLS graphify-out/cypher.txt

graphify export html
grep -o '"from": *"[a-z]*", *"to": *"[a-z]*"' graphify-out/graph.html

# merge driver, three identical inputs
cp graphify-out/graph.json base.json; cp base.json cur.json; cp base.json other.json
graphify merge-driver base.json cur.json other.json
python3 -c "import json; [print(l['source'], '->', l['target']) for l in json.load(open('cur.json'))['links']]"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
MATCH (a {id: 'normalize'}), (b {id: 'tokenize'}) MERGE (a)-[:CALLS {confidence: 'EXTRACTED'}]->(b);
"from": "normalize", "to": "tokenize"
normalize -> tokenize
```

All three should be `tokenize` → `normalize`.

### Graphify version

0.9.75 (v8 @ 48d7c0e)

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables set. Reproduced on a clean checkout of v8 at 48d7c0e and with the `uv tool` install of 0.9.75.

### Additional context

**Proposed fix (I'm happy to send PRs):**
- Add one helper that copies arc order into `_src`/`_tgt`, keeping any existing markers. It is the same idiom `query` and `merge-graphs` already use inline.
- Call it in `paths.load_node_link_graph`, the `export` loader and `global_add`.
- Make `to_cypher`, `to_canvas` and `push_to_*` read `data.get("_src", u)` / `data.get("_tgt", v)`, as `to_html` already does.
- Have the merge driver pop the markers back into arc order before writing, as `to_json` does.

I've prototyped this with regression tests for each path above. Each test fails on v8 and passes with the fix, and the full suite is otherwise unchanged.

Forcing a directed load instead would break Obsidian/wiki output: `DiGraph.neighbors()` returns successors only, so notes lose their incoming links.

I'd split it into two PRs:
1. Loaders, exporters and the merge driver.
2. `global add`. That one also has to remap `_src`/`_tgt` when it merges external-library nodes shared between repos. Today it only rewires the edge endpoints, so markers can name a node that no longer exists, and that already happens on v8 for files that carry markers.

**Existing outputs after a fix:**
- A graph.json already rewritten by the merge driver: `graphify update` repairs code edges. Semantic edges are carried over, so they need re-extraction.
- `global-graph.json`: `global add` skips unchanged repos, so it needs `global remove <tag>` and then `global add`.
- graph.html: an unchanged `update` doesn't re-render it, so it needs `graphify export html`.

Related: #3495, which covers the same `"directed": false` mismatch from the external-consumer side. #3022 moves `global_add` onto a new loader, but with `preserve_direction=False`, so it keeps this reversal.

AI disclosure: I investigated this and wrote the reproduction and prototype with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), and verified them myself.

title: [Bug]: graph_diff reports "no changes" when a call is reversed (skill --update summary)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`analyze.graph_diff` reports `no changes` when a call reverses (a calls b becomes b calls a). The skill's `--update` flow uses it for the "what changed" summary (`tools/skillgen/fragments/references/shared/update.md`, plus the `aider` and `devin` core fragments). A reversed call is therefore invisible to the user.

There are two causes:
1. `graph_diff` keys undirected edges by sorted endpoint pair, so `a→b` and `b→a` produce the same key.
2. The skill loads `G_old` with a plain `json_graph.node_link_graph()` call, which loses the arc-order direction (see #4066). So even a direction-aware diff would have nothing to compare.

Expected: a reversed call shows as one removed and one new edge, with the correct `source`/`target`.

Measured through the skill's own code on a two-file project:

| Edit | Shown on 0.9.75 | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| no edit | no changes | no changes |
| call reversed | **no changes** | 1 new, 1 removed edge |
| lines inserted above functions | no changes | no changes |
| new call added | 1 new edge | 1 new edge |

Low severity: it only affects the update summary, not the graph.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
python - <<'EOF'
import networkx as nx
from graphify.analyze import graph_diff

def g(src, tgt):
    G = nx.Graph()
    G.add_node("normalize", label="normalize()")
    G.add_node("tokenize", label="tokenize()")
    G.add_edge(src, tgt, relation="calls", _src=src, _tgt=tgt)
    return G

print(graph_diff(g("tokenize", "normalize"), g("normalize", "tokenize")))
EOF
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
{'new_nodes': [], 'removed_nodes': [], 'new_edges': [], 'removed_edges': [], 'summary': 'no changes'}
```

### Graphify version

0.9.75 (v8 @ 48d7c0e)

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables set. Reproduced on a clean checkout.

### Additional context

**Proposed fix (I'm happy to send a PR after #4066):**
- Count an edge as reversed only when both graphs carry `_src`/`_tgt` and the markers differ. In that case it appears in both `new_edges` and `removed_edges`.
- Report `source`/`target` from the markers.
- Have the skill fragments load `G_old` through `paths.load_node_link_graph` and regenerate them with skillgen.

Gating on markers keeps today's output for callers that don't stamp them, which matters for the proposed public `graph_diff` in #164. The naive fix (key every edge by `_src`/`_tgt`) gives false positives today, because `G_old` comes back without markers.

Prototyped with a regression test that fails on v8 and passes with the fix. The no-edit and line-shift cases above still report no changes.

title: fix(extract): keep an unresolved base off a class in another language
body:
## What does this PR do?

An unresolved base stays on its sourceless stub when the only same-label class is in another language. Fixes #2207.

`extract` calls `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` once for the whole corpus. A stub has no source file. One type candidate for that label is copied onto every edge that names the stub. The function path already requires a shared language family. The type path does not, so `class User(Base)` inherits a TypeScript `Base`, and `Command::SUCCESS` can land on a TypeScript `Command` class.

The apply loop now skips that write when the edge file and the candidate file both have a language family and the families differ. A same-language unique match still moves. One stub can still bind a same-language referrer while the other language stays on the stub. The exact list and the case-folded list both go through this loop.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: a missing base does not attach to a same-named type in another language. A same-language unique class still absorbs the stub. The built-in `Exception` guard stays per edge.

- Decoy: `test_rewire_cross_language_block_is_per_edge` failed on that same tree with `assert 'frontend_widget' == 'widget'` (the PHP edge moved too). The test also requires the TypeScript edge to take the TypeScript class, so dropping the candidate for the whole stub fails it. The BookStore fixture failed the same way: the target `source_file` was `interfaces.py`.
- Left alone: the function-path family check (#1781), `_names_own_builtin_base` (#2812), `_is_type_like_definition`, and the C# same-file remap skip.
- Limitations: a base declared in one language and subclassed by the same name in another stays unbound. The BookStore fixture now expects the sourceless stub. A file whose suffix has no language family still rewires.

title: AST extractor resolves member calls to same-named local functions (produces false self-loop edges)
body:
## Summary

The AST extractor resolves a **member call whose method name matches a function declared in the same file to that local function**, instead of to a method on the receiver's type. The result is a false `calls` self-loop edge on the local function.

Reproduced on `graphify 0.9.74`, graphify `update .` (AST-only path), TypeScript sources.

## Repro

### Case A — DOM method

```ts
// packages/portal/src/components/ui.tsx
export function confirm(message: string): boolean {
    return window.confirm(message);
}
```

`window.confirm` is a `Window` method. The graph records `confirm()` in `ui.tsx` as calling **itself** (`calls` edge, source == target).

### Case B — class field receiver

```ts
// packages/web/src/ChatClient.ts
close(): void {
    // ...
    const socket = this.socket;
    if (socket) {
        this.detach(socket);
        socket.close();   // WebSocket.close()
    }
}
```

`socket.close()` is `WebSocket.prototype.close`. The graph records `ChatClient.close()` as calling **itself**.

## Diagnosis

The resolution appears to ignore the receiver expression and match on the member name alone:

- `window.confirm(message)` → matches local `confirm` (wrong)
- `socket.close()` → matches own method `close` (wrong)
- `this.emitStatus(...)`, `this.clearTimers(...)`, `this.detach(...)` → resolve **correctly** (the receiver is `this`, and those names don't collide)

So the failure is specifically **receiver-scoped name collision on a non-`this` receiver**. `this.method()` and module-level calls resolve correctly; `expr.method()` where `expr` is not `this` does not consult `expr`'s type.

## Impact

Small in edge count but visible in every health report, because these surface as `self_loop_edges` in:

```
graphify diagnose multigraph
```

In the repro repo, 2 of 387 `calls` edges are misresolved this way. They are indistinguishable from genuine recursion, so a reader has to open the source to classify each self-loop. That is the real cost: the diagnostic cannot be trusted as a regression signal without manual triage.

## Suggested fix

When resolving `receiver.method(...)`:

1. If `receiver` is `this`/`self`, resolve against the enclosing class/struct — current behaviour is already correct here.
2. Otherwise, resolve against the inferred type of `receiver`. For known globals (`window`, `document`, `console`, `globalThis`, `process`) consult the ambient/global type rather than local scope.
3. Only fall back to a same-file name match when the receiver type is unknown **and** no matching symbol is reachable on the receiver — and in that fallback, prefer emitting no edge over a self-loop.

Also worth considering: the `Window.confirm` / `WebSocket.close` cases would both be fixed by seeding ambient lib types (`lib.dom.d.ts`) as known symbol sources.

## Related

`graphify diagnose multigraph` reports `self_loop_edges` without distinguishing genuine recursion from misresolution. Tagging the provenance (e.g. `relation_source: lexical | inferred`) would let consumers filter, and would have made this triagable without reading source.

title: fix(extract): don't emit L1 for zero-byte files
body:
A 0-byte file has no line 1, but its file node was still getting `source_location: L1`. Now the shared tree-sitter path (`_extract_generic`) sets it to `None` when the source is empty, the same way other location-less file nodes look. The node stays, since an empty `__init__.py` is a real module that other files import.

That one guard covers every language on the generic path (Python, JS/TS, Java, C/C++, C#, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Lua, Vue/Svelte). Go, Rust, Zig, Elixir, Julia, Bash, PowerShell, R and Solidity have their own extractors and still emit L1 for empty files. I left those out to keep this small; happy to follow up.

Closes #4041

Testing: the new regression test fails on v8 and passes here. Full suite is green on 3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14. Live before/after against v8 on the issue fixture and on a small package with empty `__init__.py` files, through update, report, html and the other exports: the only change is that those nodes now have `None` instead of `L1`.

title: fix(export): preserve stored edge direction when reloading graph.json (#4066)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4066 (loaders, exporters and the merge driver; `global add` follows in a separate PR).

`graph.json` is written `"directed": false` and stores direction in arc order (#563), or in `_src`/`_tgt` on legacy files (#2309). A plain undirected `node_link_graph` load re-orders each edge's endpoints by node-list position. Every link whose target comes before its source in the node list therefore came back reversed: 79% of links on graphify's own graph.

`query`, `path`/`explain`, `affected`, `merge-graphs` and the MCP server already restore direction. This PR fixes the rest:

- **Loaders.** New `paths.restore_arc_direction(data)` stamps `_src`/`_tgt` from arc order and keeps existing markers. It's the idiom `query` and `merge-graphs` already use inline. It's applied in `load_node_link_graph` (used by the `update`/`watch`/hook HTML re-render, the merge driver, benchmark and callflow) and in the `export` loader.
- **Writers that emit direction.** `to_cypher`, `to_canvas`, `push_to_neo4j` and `push_to_falkordb` now read `data.get("_src", u)` / `data.get("_tgt", v)`, as `to_html` already does.
- **Merge driver.** Pops the markers back into arc order before writing, as `to_json` does. The committed `graph.json` keeps the post-#563 convention, with no markers left in the file.
- **ARCHITECTURE.md.** New "Edge direction in graph.json" section that documents the convention and how to load and read direction, so new readers don't reintroduce the bug.

Forcing a directed load instead was rejected. It breaks Obsidian/wiki output, because `DiGraph.neighbors()` returns successors only and notes lose their incoming links.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** every output keeps the direction stored in `graph.json`. Arc order is the direction, and legacy `_src`/`_tgt` markers win where present.

`tests/test_export_direction.py` has 8 tests: the loader, `export html`, `cypher.txt`, `neo4j --push`, `falkordb --push` (fake SDKs, no database), the Obsidian canvas, `watch._reconcile_graph_html`, and the merge driver (arc order, no markers left). The fixture covers three cases: an edge listed callee-first (reversed today), one listed caller-first (must stay as is), and a legacy-marker link. **All 8 fail on `v8` on the direction assert and pass with this change.**

**Persisted state this fix cannot repair by itself:**
- A `graph.json` already rewritten by the merge driver can't be detected from the file alone.
  - Code edges: `graphify update` repairs them. They are rebuilt from source, and the no-change check compares link source/target.
  - Semantic edges: these are carried over unchanged, so they need fresh semantic extraction of the affected files.
- An existing `graph.html` is not re-rendered by an unchanged `update` (`_reconcile_graph_html` returns early when the HTML exists and isn't marked stale). Run `graphify export html`.
- `cypher.txt` and canvas files: re-run the matching `graphify export`.
- **Neo4j / FalkorDB contents: a re-push does not remove the reversed relationships.** `push_to_*` and `cypher.txt` only `MERGE`, and `MERGE (a)-[r:CALLS]->(b)` matches on direction. A re-push therefore adds the correct relationship and keeps the old reversed one. Clear the graphify-pushed data (or drop the FalkorDB graph) before re-pushing.

**Limitations / out of scope:**
- `global add` (separate PR; it also needs `_src`/`_tgt` remapped during external-node dedup).
- `graph_diff` (#4067).
- `export graphml` declares `edgedefault="undirected"`, so it drops direction rather than contradicting it.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

title: Solidity enum values use `contains` instead of `case_of`
fix(solidity): link enum values with case_of instead of contains
body:
## Problem
Closes #4089.

A Solidity enum linked its values to the enum with a `contains` edge — the relation used for real declared members like struct fields. Every other language with enums emits `case_of` per value (Java #1719, C#, Swift, Rust, VB.NET #4054). Solidity was the lone remaining outlier.

## Implementation
One-line relation change in `graphify/extractors/solidity.py`: the `enum_value` edge now uses `case_of` instead of `contains`. Struct fields, state variables, events and errors are untouched — they are real declarations and keep `contains`.

This is not cosmetic: `case_of` targets are excluded from constructor binding (`_member_nids` in `extract.py`), so an enum value named like a type can no longer be mistaken for a constructable member.

## Verification
- Added `test_solidity_enum_values_emit_case_of_not_contains` — asserts enum values get `case_of` (not `contains`) while a struct field keeps `contains`. Verified it FAILS on pre-fix v8 and passes with the change.
- `uv run pytest tests/` → 6491 passed, 15 skipped (security/wheel env-only tests deselected).
- `ruff check` clean, `pyright` clean on the changed file.

## Limitations
No behavioural change for struct/event/error members, which correctly remain `contains`.

title: PowerShell enum members use `contains` instead of `case_of`
body:
### Version / commit

v8 @ 35adf43 (v0.9.76)

### What happens

A PowerShell enum links its members to the enum with a `contains` edge, the same relation used for real declared members. Every other language that has enums emits a `case_of` edge per member — Java (#1719), C#, Swift, Rust, and VB.NET (#4054). PowerShell is now one of the last extractors still using `contains` for enum members.

### Minimal reproduction

```powershell
# status.ps1
enum Status {
    Active
    Paused
    Closed
}
```

```python
from graphify.extractors import extract_powershell
r = extract_powershell("status.ps1")
for e in r["edges"]:
    if e["relation"] in ("case_of", "contains"):
        print(e["relation"], e["source"], "->", e["target"])
```

### Expected

`Status -> Active/Paused/Closed` as `case_of`.

### Actual

`Status -> Active/Paused/Closed` as `contains`.

### Why it matters

`case_of` targets are deliberately excluded from constructor binding (`_member_nids` in `extract.py`), so an enum member whose name collides with a type can currently be mistaken for a constructable member. It also breaks the cross-language invariant downstream consumers rely on to tell enum cases apart from declared members.

title: SQL: a trigger is not linked to the function it EXECUTEs
body:
### Version / commit

v8 @ 35adf43 (v0.9.76)

### What happens

A `CREATE TRIGGER` is linked to the table it fires on (`triggers` edge) but **not** to the function it runs. The `EXECUTE FUNCTION` / `EXECUTE PROCEDURE` clause — the entire reason the trigger exists — is ignored, so the trigger→routine dependency is missing from the graph.

### Minimal reproduction

```sql
-- schema.sql
CREATE TABLE users (id INT);
CREATE FUNCTION log_it() RETURNS TRIGGER AS 'SELECT 1';
CREATE TRIGGER audit_ins AFTER INSERT ON users
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION log_it();
```

```python
from graphify.extractors import extract_sql
r = extract_sql("schema.sql")
for e in r["edges"]:
    print(e["relation"], e["source"], "->", e["target"])
```

### Expected

An edge from `audit_ins` to the `log_it()` function (alongside the existing `triggers` edge to `users`).

### Actual

Only `audit_ins --triggers--> users`. No edge to `log_it()` at all; the function it executes is invisible as a dependency.

### Why it matters

The function is the trigger's payload — change-impact and call-graph analysis that start from a modified function completely miss the triggers that invoke it. SQL already models structural references (`reads_from`, `indexes`, `triggers`); the executed routine is the one that was left out.

title: fix(sql): link a trigger to the function it executes
body:
## Problem
Closes #4093.

A `CREATE TRIGGER` was linked to its ON table but not to the function it runs. The `EXECUTE FUNCTION` / `EXECUTE PROCEDURE` clause was ignored, so the trigger→routine dependency — the trigger's whole reason to exist — was missing from the graph.

## Implementation
In `graphify/extractors/sql.py`:
- Register function/procedure node ids in a `routine_nids` map (mirroring the existing `table_nids`).
- In the `create_trigger` branch, read the `object_reference` that follows `EXECUTE` and emit an `executes` edge from the trigger to that routine. The ON table is captured before `EXECUTE` appears, so this reads the routine, not the table.

Resolution is name-based against routines defined in the same file (a trigger's function is declared before it). When the routine is not in this file the edge is **skipped** rather than guessing a cross-file target or minting a bare-name stub that could never rewire onto a `name()` function node — consistent with the project's fail-closed stance.

`executes` is a new relation string, consistent with the existing non-semantic SQL relations (`triggers`, `indexes`, `reads_from`).

## Verification
- Added `test_sql_trigger_links_to_the_function_it_executes` (resolved case — verified it FAILS on pre-fix v8) and `test_sql_trigger_executing_an_undefined_function_fails_closed` (guards the no-stub behaviour).
- Existing trigger tests still pass (their functions are not defined in-file, so no edge is added).
- `uv run pytest tests/` → 6492 passed, 15 skipped (security/wheel env-only tests deselected).
- `ruff check` clean; `pyright` adds no new errors (4 pre-existing baseline errors unchanged).

## Limitations
Cross-file trigger→function links are intentionally not emitted (fail-closed). Firebird `fb_proc_or_trigger` and the ERROR-recovery trigger path are out of scope; this covers the cleanly-parsed `CREATE TRIGGER ... EXECUTE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE` form.

title: Objective-C: C-style enum (and typedef enum) declarations are dropped
body:
### Version / commit

v8 @ 35adf43 (v0.9.76)

### What happens

The Objective-C extractor emits `@interface`, `@implementation` and `@protocol` type nodes, but plain `enum` and `typedef enum` definitions are dropped entirely — the enum type **and** all of its members are missing from the graph. Every other language with enums emits a type node plus a `case_of` edge per member (Java #1719, C++ #3939, Swift).

### Minimal reproduction

```objc
// Color.m
#import <Foundation/Foundation.h>
enum Color { Red, Green, Blue };
typedef enum { North, South } Direction;
```

```python
from graphify.extractors import extract_objc
r = extract_objc("Color.m")
print([n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]])
```

### Expected

`Color` and `Direction` type nodes, each with `case_of` edges to its members.

### Actual

Neither the enum types nor their members appear; only the file node (and any classes) are emitted.

### Why it matters

ObjC enums are everywhere in real codebases; a `[Color]`-typed field or a `switch` over an enum has no type to point at. Unlike C (whose `class_types` is empty by design), the ObjC extractor is object-oriented and already models named types, so enums are an inconsistency within its own model.

### Note

The `NS_ENUM`/`NS_OPTIONS` macro spelling is a separate matter: tree-sitter-objc parses it into an ERROR subtree, so it has no clean AST and is out of scope here. This is about the plain C-style `enum` / `typedef enum` forms, which parse cleanly.

title: fix(objc): extract C-style enum declarations
body:
## Problem
Closes #4095.

The Objective-C extractor already emits `@interface`, `@implementation` and `@protocol` type nodes, but plain `enum` and `typedef enum` definitions were dropped entirely — both the enum type and all of its enumerators were invisible.

## Implementation
In `graphify/extractors/objc.py`:
- Add an `enum_specifier` branch for a named C-style enum (`enum Color { Red, Green };`).
- Add a `type_definition` branch for the `typedef enum { ... } Name;` / `typedef enum Tag { ... } Name;` forms, where the name callers reference is the typedef alias.
- A shared `_emit_enum` helper emits the type node (`contains` from the file) plus a node and a `case_of` edge per enumerator — the same shape every other language with enums uses (Java #1719, C++ #3939, Swift).
- A nameless enum (`enum { A, B };`) and a bodyless reference (`enum X y;`) are skipped so no phantom node is minted.

## Verification
- Added `tests/test_objc_enum_declarations.py` (plain enum, typedef enum alias, and the skip/no-phantom case). Verified the positive tests FAIL on pre-fix v8 and pass with the change.
- `uv run pytest tests/` → 6493 passed, 15 skipped (security/wheel env-only tests deselected).
- `ruff check` clean; `pyright` clean (0 errors on the changed file, unchanged from baseline).

## Limitations
`NS_ENUM`/`NS_OPTIONS` are macro calls that tree-sitter-objc parses into ERROR subtrees — there is no clean AST to read, so they remain unsupported (documented in the test). This covers the plain C-style `enum` / `typedef enum` forms, which parse cleanly.

title: [Bug]: gemini silently omits most files in a single oversized chunk (token_budget=60000 default) — not truncation
body:
## Pre-flight

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

## What happened?

`extract_corpus_parallel()` defaults to `token_budget=60_000`. With a
doc-heavy corpus that packs every dispatched document into a **single chunk**,
and `gemini-3-flash-preview` then returns a syntactically valid response that
covers only a fraction of the files. graphify detects this correctly and warns:

```
[graphify extract] semantic extraction on 30 files via gemini...
[graphify extract] chunk 1/1 done
[graphify] WARNING: 24/30 dispatched file(s) produced no nodes and are absent
from the graph: copilot-instructions.md, opencode.yml, CONTRIBUTING.md, ...
The model returned a response but omitted them; a re-run will retry them.
[graphify extract] semantic extraction is incomplete: 24 dispatched file(s)
produced no nodes and 0 came back truncated or hollow.
```

The important detail is that final clause: **0 truncated, 0 hollow**. The
response is complete and well-formed — it just silently omits 24 of the 30
files. The whole-corpus single chunk is what triggers it.

Two things then compound:

1. A re-run "retries them" — which re-sends the same oversized chunk, which
   omits the same files. That loop is what presents to users as *the semantic
   index never finishing*, rather than as a coverage bug.
2. With library defaults (600 s/request, 6 SDK retries on 429, bisect depth 3)
   a single worst-case chunk can burn ~80 minutes with no stage-level ceiling.

The README Troubleshooting entry for *"extraction was incomplete ... refusing to
overwrite"* attributes this to the model's **output-token limit** being "cut off
mid-string", and calls the warnings "noisy but not data loss". That diagnosis
doesn't match this case — output was 1,899 tokens, nowhere near a cap, and
graphify explicitly reports nothing truncated. The advice to lower
`--token-budget` is still correct and does fix it, so credit where due; but the
stated cause sends you looking for an output-cap problem that isn't there.

## Steps to reproduce

30 markdown/config documents (24 MB repo, 213 code files — code is AST-only and
never reaches the model). Only chunking changes between the two runs:

```bash
# Arm A — library default
graphify extract . --backend gemini --model gemini-3-flash-preview --force \
  --max-concurrency 1 --api-timeout 180

# Arm B — only difference is chunk size
graphify extract . --backend gemini --model gemini-3-flash-preview --force \
  --max-concurrency 1 --api-timeout 180 --token-budget 15000
```

## Error output or graph output

| `--token-budget` | chunks | docs with no nodes | input tok | output tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60000 (default) | 1 | **24 / 30** | 59,989 | 1,899 (3.2%) |
| 15000 | 4 | **3 / 30** | 62,425 | 9,068 (14.5%) |

Identical corpus, identical model, ~62K input tokens both arms — output rose
4.8x purely from splitting. Coverage went 20% → 90%.

A cheap pre-flight health signal that found this: the **output:input token
ratio** in `graphify-out/cost.json`. Backtracking through my own run history,
every run that "never finished" sat at 3–8%; every healthy run sat at 35–65%.

## Graphify version

0.9.75

## Operating System

Linux

## Anything else?

- Not model-specific in the sense of quality — `gpt-oss:120b` via Ollama cloud
  did not show this collapse at a similar chunk size, but `gpt-oss:20b` and
  `granite4.2` did produce hollow/prose output in earlier testing. The common
  factor looks like chunk size.
- The README's own remedy example uses `--token-budget 4000`, which is further
  in the direction that works.
- Possible improvements, if useful:
  - Lower the default `token_budget`, or derive it from corpus size rather than
    a fixed 60K.
  - When files are omitted but the response is *not* truncated, say so
    explicitly — "the model returned a short but valid response; N files were
    not addressed" is far more actionable than a retry that cannot succeed.
  - Consider capping retries for this specific case, since retrying an
    unchanged chunk against the same model reproduces the same omission.

Happy to provide the corpus or test harness if useful.

title: fix(security): raise dependency security floors
body:
## Summary

Raise dependency security floors to address specific advisories while preserving existing compatibility pins. The release checkout used for validation was v0.9.76; this is not a claim that these vulnerabilities uniquely affect that release.

- Update `uv.lock` for anyio, cryptography, PyJWT, pypdf, soupsieve, urllib3 and virtualenv, with required transitive updates.
- Add minimum patched versions to uv constraints and a pip constraints file; raise the declared pypdf minimum for PDF/all extras.
- Apply available Debian updates in the Docker build, upgrade build-time pip, enforce security constraints and run `pip check`.
- Remove build-only pip from the runtime image to eliminate findings in its vendored libraries. Runtime pip-based installation is intentionally no longer available.

No CI workflow changes are included.

## Dependency advisories

The following HIGH/CRITICAL findings in the saved Trivy report motivate each dependency floor. These are dependency findings, not claims that every affected code path is reachable in Graphify.

| Dependency | Previous lock → security floor | Advisories addressed |
|---|---|---|
| anyio | 4.13.0 → 4.14.2 | [CVE-2026-63374](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-63374) |
| cryptography | 49.0.0 → 50.0.0 | [CVE-2026-69247 / GHSA-g6cj-pr64-35w5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g6cj-pr64-35w5) |
| PyJWT | 2.13.0 → 2.14.0 | [CVE-2026-102268](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-102268), [CVE-2026-102266](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-102266), [CVE-2026-102267](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-102267), [CVE-2026-102271](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-102271), [CVE-2026-102272](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-102272), [CVE-2026-102273](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-102273) |
| pypdf | 6.18.1 → 6.19.0 | [CVE-2026-102998](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-102998), [CVE-2026-102999](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-102999), [CVE-2026-103000](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-103000) |
| soupsieve | 2.8.3 → 2.8.4 | [CVE-2026-49476](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-49476), [CVE-2026-49477](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-49477) |
| urllib3 | 2.7.0 → 2.8.0 | [CVE-2026-97687](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-97687), [CVE-2026-97689](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-97689) |
| virtualenv (development dependency) | 21.3.3 → 21.7.13 | [CVE-2026-102925](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-102925), [CVE-2026-102930](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-102930), [CVE-2026-102937](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2026-102937) |

### Why cryptography requires a major-version bump

The [upstream advisory GHSA-g6cj-pr64-35w5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g6cj-pr64-35w5) explicitly lists **`>=44.0.0,<50.0.0` as affected** and **`50.0.0` as the first patched version** for CVE-2026-69247. PKCS#7 EnvelopedData decryption exposes a Bleichenbacher oracle through distinguishable errors and timing; the fix is described in [upstream PR #15369](https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/pull/15369).

The previous lock contains 49.0.0. As checked on 2026-10-08, [PyPI](https://pypi.org/pypi/cryptography/json) publishes no patched 49.x release, so staying within major 49 cannot remediate this advisory. The 50.0.0 floor is the first fixed release, not an arbitrary upgrade to the latest major.

**Compatibility validation remains incomplete:** the focused tests below do not substitute for the full supported test matrix. Full-matrix validation is still required before landing this major bump. This documentation update does not change the current `cryptography>=50.0.0` constraints or claim that an upper bound has been added.

## Validation

- Focused security, MCP, HTTP server and PDF regression tests: **305 passed, 1 skipped**.
- `uv lock`, locked dependency sync, Docker build with `--pull`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Isolated container CLI `--help` smoke test passed (no network, read-only filesystem, dropped capabilities).
- Trivy 0.70.0 with the 2026-10-05 database:
  - Lockfile, including dev dependencies: **0 critical / 0 high**, 2 medium findings remain.
  - Container Python packages: **0 vulnerability findings**.
  - Container Debian packages: **44 high findings remain**, with no fixed versions reported by this database snapshot.

This does not claim complete container remediation. Remaining OS findings need vendor fixes or a separately tested base-image strategy. Full test suite and all optional integrations were not tested.

## Follow-up security recommendations

The existing CI runs non-blocking Bandit and pip-audit. Keep both, and consider adding:

1. Trivy filesystem scanning of locked dependencies (including dev dependencies), configuration and secrets.
2. Trivy scanning of the built container's OS/Python packages and image configuration.
3. Semgrep application-focused security rules, excluding non-production corpora from the production gate.
4. JSON report artifacts uploaded even on scan failures; initially report-only, then enforce reviewed thresholds after triage.

A local Semgrep Community scan found five XML-parser hardening recommendations and eleven SHA-1 warnings in application code. These require separate review: existing XML guards and non-cryptographic hash uses mean findings are not automatically confirmed exploitable vulnerabilities. No Semgrep-driven source changes are included here.

title: test(pascal): cover the valued enumerated form (clRed = 1, clGreen = 2)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4071.

Pascal enum extraction landed in #4056 with a test for the plain form only (`TColor = (clRed, clGreen, clBlue)`). This adds a test for the valued form:

```pascal
TColor = (clRed = 1, clGreen = 2);
```

The explicit ordinal nests under `declEnumValue -> defaultValue -> literalNumber`, beside the value's `identifier`. The new test, `test_pascal_valued_enum_literals_are_not_nodes`, asserts:

- `TColor`, `clRed` and `clGreen` are nodes;
- neither literal (`1`, `2`) is a node;
- the `case_of` targets from `TColor` are exactly `{clRed, clGreen}`, so no value is labelled `clRed = 1` and no edge points at a literal.

Test-only: the extractor already reads just the `identifier` child of each `declEnumValue`, so no change to `graphify/extractors/pascal.py` was needed.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** an enum value's node is named by its identifier alone; an explicit ordinal never leaks into the label or becomes a node of its own.

Since the test passes on `v8` without a code change, I checked that it can fail by breaking the extractor two ways, restoring it after each:

| Extractor | Result |
| --- | --- |
| version from before #4056 (`b462631^`) | fails: `TColor`, `clRed`, `clGreen` all missing |
| mutated to `value_name = _read(value)` (whole `declEnumValue` text) | fails: labels become `clRed = 1` / `clGreen = 2` |
| unmodified `v8` | passes |

**Limitation:** both failing runs trip the first assertion (the expected labels). The "no literal node" assertion and the exact `case_of` set have not been observed failing on their own; they guard a regression that would emit the literal as a separate node.

Nothing generated or persisted is affected; the test writes only to `tmp_path`.

title: fix(skill): simplify credential and dispatch guidance

## What does this PR do?
