title: feat(qml): add bounded Qt 6 and QML static analysis
body:
## What does this PR do?

Add bounded Qt 6/QML static analysis to Graphify's existing Python pipeline. QML files and Qt's meta-object/event mechanisms need scoped source facts and resolution beyond generic C++ parsing. This contribution preserves provenance and uncertainty from extraction through incremental refresh, persisted graphs and consumers.

The supported static profiles include:

- QML declarations, imports, bindings, handlers and embedded/external JavaScript scopes, with original byte ranges and explicit ambiguous/unavailable outcomes.
- Literal `qmldir`, `.qmltypes`, QRC, CMake and qmake metadata, accepted import/module membership and packaged components independent of use.
- Native Qt declarations (`Q_PROPERTY`, `Q_INVOKABLE`, `QML_ELEMENT` and supported related macros), signals/slots, connect/disconnect sites and emissions. Connection facts remain distinct from direct calls.
- Both QML/C++ integration directions: registered/context APIs exposed to QML and supported literal C++ loading/access to source-resolved QML objects.
- Full/incremental parity, stale-fact removal, retained prior products on failure, logical edge direction and graph/export/search/assistant transport.

The QML parser is optional: `graphifyy[qml]` uses pinned `tree-sitter-language-pack==0.11.0`, also used by existing R/Erlang extras. Ordinary analysis neither executes project code/build hooks nor requires a Qt SDK. Qt 6.5/6.8 are source fixture profiles, not installed SDK certification.

Shared source-identity, constructor authority, direction, cache/publication and cross-platform fixture/CI changes remain because Qt acceptance depends on them. The contribution is substantial; [the scope and review order](https://github.com/SlinkyRamey/graphify/blob/1a7768dca95c1e365070a216a0a629b006350be8/docs/qt-qml/UPSTREAM_CONTRIBUTION.md) and [code reference](https://github.com/SlinkyRamey/graphify/blob/1a7768dca95c1e365070a216a0a629b006350be8/docs/qt-qml/CODE_REFERENCE.md) identify the responsibility boundaries. Independent fork repository policy, Windows Codex hook transport, community recovery, selection redesign and middle-button navigation are excluded. The upstream installer and viewer selection/navigation remain their baseline implementations. Aggregate internal/external source-edge counts remain narrowly as the Qt packaged-component membership prerequisite.

Related #1716 and overlapping proposal #1748. I inspected #1748 at `7b38d4c2e2226b1db826a26774c7a5f299b8d62f`; it already covers QML objects/members and C++ registration aliases. This implementation uses a separately documented parser decision and extends scoped resolution, metadata, native event mechanisms, reverse access and incremental/consumer contracts. The common extractor, facade and packaging files overlap, so maintainers need an explicit integration decision before combining the proposals. This PR does not automatically supersede #1748 or certify its reported tests.

title: fix(update): refuse a saved semantic id when the total grows
body:
## What does this PR do?

A saved semantic node id must still be in the graph when `graphify update` or `to_json` writes, even if the node total grew.

`to_json` in `graphify/export.py` compares `new_n < existing_n` and only when force-write is false. `graphify update` writes a temp file with `force=True`, then `_check_shrink` in `graphify/watch.py` returns success at `len(new_nodes) >= len(existing_nodes)`. Five new AST nodes can replace one lost rationale id and the total still rises. A sourceless stub such as `pathlib_Path` keeps a semantic count flat, and a rebuilt `src/app.ts` was treated as a reason to drop the rationale node on that file.

`_lost_saved_semantic_nodes` returns saved nodes for which `_is_ast_tier` is false, the id is absent from the new graph, and `source_file` is not in the deleted set. `to_json` calls it inside `if not force`. `_check_shrink` calls it after the force-write return and the legacy deletion return, and before the larger-total return. The deleted set is the files the user removed. The rebuilt set is not passed. A legacy semantic id that `build_from_json` rewrites to its canonical stem, including a bare doc id folded into its `_doc` twin, is the same node.

Related to #2229. This does not use a closing keyword: a hyperedge that disappears while every saved semantic id remains is still written.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

- Reproduced on v8 at `35adf43`: `pytest tests/test_watch.py::test_check_shrink_refuses_lost_semantic_id_when_total_grows tests/test_export.py::test_to_json_refuses_lost_semantic_id_when_total_grows -q` failed with `assert True is False` on both. The saved graph has 4 nodes, including `rationale_lost`. The new graph has 7 nodes, drops that id, and adds a sourceless `pathlib_Path` stub. `src/app.ts` is in the rebuilt set and not in the deleted set. `graph.json` lost `rationale_lost`.
- Decoy: a total compare returns true because 7 > 4. A semantic count stays at 2 because the stub fills the slot. An excuse that trusts the rebuilt set returns true because `src/app.ts` was rebuilt. The test passes `rebuilt_sources={"src/app.ts"}` and asserts the write is refused and `rationale_lost` is still in the file.
- Left alone: force-write on a complete extract, `--allow-dedup-shrink`, and dedup matching. Those are #3774 and #3094.
- Limitations: a hyperedge that disappears while every saved semantic id remains still writes. An AST rename can drop a hyperedge for that reason, so hyperedge ids are not part of this check.

title: [Bug]: All-cached semantic run skips Step B3, so Part C fails on missing .graphify_semantic.json
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

When every doc, paper and image in the corpus hits the semantic cache, the generated skill tells the agent "If all files are cached, skip to Part C directly". Part C reads `graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json` unconditionally, but the only Part B step that writes that file is the Step B3 merge. The second `/graphify` run on an unchanged mixed corpus (code plus docs) therefore fails in Part C with `FileNotFoundError`.

The obvious workaround is to write an empty `.graphify_semantic.json`, as the code-only fast path does. That gets past Part C but silently drops every cached semantic node, because B3 is also the step that merges `.graphify_cached.json` in.

**Expected:** Part C runs, and the extraction contains the cached nodes.

**Where it lives:**
- `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md`, the sentence right after the Step B0 block.
- Rendered into every split host (`graphify/skill.md`, `skill-codex.md`, `skill-windows.md` and the rest).
- The monolith hosts `skill-aider.md` and `skill-devin.md` carry the same sentence, but `--monolith-roundtrip` pins their bodies to the v8 baseline.

**Related gap: stale chunk files.** B3 merges every `graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_*.json` it finds, and chunks are only removed by the final cleanup step. A run that is interrupted after dispatch leaves its chunks behind, and the next run merges them as if they were fresh. That includes an all-cached run, once it goes through B3.

**Proposed fix (PR to follow):** the change touches only the source fragment, with artifacts regenerated by `python -m tools.skillgen --bless`.
1. Replace "skip to Part C directly" with: skip Steps B1 and B2 but still run Step B3's commands, and do not write an empty `.graphify_semantic.json`.
2. In the Step B0 block, delete any `.graphify_chunk_*.json` before dispatch. Nothing has been dispatched at that point, so any chunk on disk is a leftover.
3. Add regression tests:
   - a text check that every split host routes the all-cached case through B3;
   - a behavioural test that runs the rendered B0, B3 and Part C Python blocks against an all-cached corpus with a stale chunk on disk.

   Both tests fail on current `v8` and pass with the fix.

**Out of scope:** the aider and devin monoliths. Changing them needs a sanctioned round-trip change, which can be a follow-up.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# Corpus with at least one document, e.g. notes.md
/graphify ./corpus        # first run: notes.md is extracted and cached
/graphify ./corpus        # second run, nothing changed
#   Step B0 prints: Cache: 1 files hit, 0 files need extraction
```

title: fix(detect): scope incremental manifest anchoring to prevent false deletions (#3785)
body:
### Summary
Fixes #3785.

In multi-directory workspaces or repositories where distinct subdirectories are graphed or updated independently (e.g. \/graphify workflows\, \/graphify experts\, or \--update\ on subfolders):
1. When a manifest is stored at \<workspace>/graphify-out/manifest.json\, stored keys are relative to \<workspace>\. Running an incremental scan on a subfolder (\workflows/\) previously caused \load_manifest(..., root=workflows)\ to re-anchor those keys against \workflows/\, creating invalid paths that failed disk checks and were falsely reported as deleted.
2. \detect_incremental()\ iterated over all rows in the loaded manifest without verifying whether the entries actually belonged to \oot\.

### Fix
1. **Manifest Storage Anchor Resolution (\_manifest_storage_anchor\)**: When a manifest resides under \<workspace>/graphify-out/manifest.json\ and \oot\ is a subfolder of \<workspace>\, stored relative keys are anchored to \<workspace>\ rather than the subfolder root. \_to_absolute_from_storage\ remains completely pure with zero filesystem I/O.
2. **Root Containment Guard**: In \detect_incremental()\, manifest entries outside \oot\ are skipped (\if not _in_root(f): continue\), ensuring files belonging to other subfolders or parent directories are never falsely reported as \deleted_files\ or \excluded_files\.
3. **No Filesystem Traversal or Slug Overrides**: Eliminates speculative ancestor traversal and preserves default un-slugged manifest locations so \--out\ and CLI workflows continue to operate as expected.

### Verification
- Standalone reproduction script \eproduce_issue_3785.py\ passes: 0 false deletions, 0 false exclusions across both subfolder update scenarios.

- CLI extract test suite: \uv run pytest tests/test_extract_cli.py\ (34 passed, 0 failures).
- Pre-commit checks: \skillgen --check\ and \uff\ passed.

title: fix(js): extract methods on exported objects to resolve CommonJS calls (#3778)
body:
### Summary
Fixes #3778.

In Express-style CommonJS architectures (and similar Node.js packages), core methods are assigned to module-level objects that are subsequently exported:
```js
// response.js
var normalizeType = require('./utils').normalizeType;
var res = Object.create(http.ServerResponse.prototype);

res.format = function(obj) {
    this.set('Content-Type', normalizeType(key).value);
};

module.exports = res;
```

Previously, `_js_extra_walk` only captured `exports.x = fn` and `<Class>.prototype.x = fn`. Top-level member assignments on objects (`res.format = fn`) were skipped to prevent phantom god-nodes (#1077). Consequently:
1. `res.format` never received a node.
2. Its AST body was never appended to `function_bodies`.
3. `walk_calls` never walked the method body.
4. Calls made inside those methods (such as `normalizeType(...)`) were never extracted, resulting in 0 resolved call edges despite valid destructured `require` statements.

### Fix
1. **Detect Exported Objects**: Added `_js_find_exported_objects(program_node, source)` to identify top-level identifiers exported via CommonJS or ESM (`module.exports = res`, `exports = module.exports = ...`, `exports.response = res`, `module.exports = { res }`, etc.).
2. **Method Extraction on Exported Objects**: Handled `kind == "object"` in `_js_extra_walk` when `owner_name` is exported. We emit the owner node, method node `.{member}()`, `method` edge, and append the method body to `function_bodies` so `walk_calls` scans all call expressions inside.
3. **Preserve Guard #1077**: Arbitrary local objects that are not exported (`const obj = {}; obj.whatever = () => 1;`) continue to be skipped, keeping the phantom god-node guard intact.

### Verification
- **Reproduction**: Tested with minimal reproduction script mirroring Express `response.js` calling `utils.normalizeType`. Confirmed method node and cross-file `calls` edge are emitted.
- **Test Suite**:
  - Added unit test `test_extract_js_exported_object_member_assignment_and_calls` in `tests/test_extract.py`.
  - All 54 JavaScript extract tests pass cleanly (`uv run pytest tests/test_extract.py tests/test_languages.py -k "js"`).
  - Phantom god-node guard test `test_extract_js_arbitrary_member_assignment_not_captured` passes.

title: [Bug]: graph.html renders nothing when a label contains an unclosed <!-- followed by <script
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`graphify update .` writes a `graph.html` that renders nothing — an empty page, no graph, no legend — whenever the node labels contain an unclosed `<!--` followed, later in the embedded JSON, by `<script`.

**Expected:** the page opens and draws the graph, whatever text the labels happen to carry.

**Actual:** the document is empty and the browser console reports `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'` in `graph.html`. An HTML parser finds only **one** inline `<script>` element instead of two: everything after the data block has been swallowed as script text.

**Cause.** The graph is embedded as JSON inside a `<script>` element, and the escaping only neutralises `</`:

```python
# graphify/exporters/html.py, ~line 617
def _js_safe(obj) -> str:
    return json.dumps(obj).replace("</", "<\\/")
```

Inside a script element the HTML tokenizer does not care about quotes — it reacts to three sequences: `<!--`, `<script` and `</script`. An unclosed `<!--` moves it to *script data escaped*, a later `<script` moves it to *script data **double** escaped*, and in that state the real `</script>` no longer closes the element ([HTML spec, script data double escaped state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#script-data-double-escaped-state)). The rest of the document becomes part of the script, which is then a syntax error, so nothing runs and nothing renders.

A closed `<!-- … -->` inside a single label is harmless: the `-->` returns the tokenizer to the normal state. It takes an **unclosed** opener — which is exactly what label truncation produces — followed by a `<script` in a later label.

**How I hit it.** Under 0.8.19 this happened on an ordinary repository with no crafted input: fenced ` ```vue ` blocks in the markdown became nodes labelled `code:vue (<!-- components/… the panel t)` (truncated, so the comment is never closed) and `code:vue (<script setup>)`. 0.9.76 no longer extracts fenced blocks as nodes, so that particular path is gone — but the escaping is unchanged, and a heading or a symbol name reaches the same place. The minimal repro below fails on 0.9.76 today.

**Suggested fix:** escape the `<` itself, not the `</` pair. JavaScript reads `\u003c` as `<`, so labels still display `<script setup>` while the HTML tokenizer never sees the sequence:

```python
def _js_safe(obj) -> str:
    return json.dumps(obj).replace("<", "\\u003c")
```

The same one-line helper is duplicated in `graphify/tree_html.py` and `graphify/callflow_html.py` and has the same gap.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
1. mkdir repro && cd repro

2. Create guide.md with exactly this content (the <!-- is deliberately never closed,
   and the <script heading must come after it):

# Guide

## An unclosed <!-- opener in a heading

Prose.

## Then a <script setup> heading

More prose.

3. Create hello.js so the corpus has a code file:

export function hello() {
  return "hi";
}

4. graphify update .

5. Open graphify-out/graph.html in a browser: the page is blank.
   The console shows SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'.

Checking it without a browser (any HTML parser does):

  node -e "const {JSDOM}=require('jsdom');const d=new JSDOM(require('fs').readFileSync('graphify-out/graph.html','utf8'));console.log([...d.window.document.querySelectorAll('script')].length)"

  prints 2 on a healthy page (vis-network + the data block) and 1 here, because the
  closing </script> was not recognised.

Swapping the two headings so that <script setup> comes first, or closing the comment
as <!-- comment -->, produces a working page: the order and the unclosed opener are
what matter.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Browser console on opening graphify-out/graph.html:

  Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'   (graph.html)

Parsing the same file with a standards HTML parser (jsdom):

  inline <script> elements found: 1   (expected 2)
  block 1: SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'
  body elements: 17                   (18 on a page that is not broken)

The embedded data, as written into graph.html:

  {"id": "guide_md_h2_1", "label": "An unclosed <!-- opener in a heading", ...}
  {"id": "guide_md_h2_2", "label": "Then a <script setup> heading", ...}

Both sequences reach the document verbatim; only "</" would have been escaped.

CLI output is normal and reports no problem:

  [graphify watch] Rebuilt: 12 nodes, 11 edges, 3 communities
  [graphify watch] graph.json, graph.html and GRAPH_REPORT.md updated in graphify-out
```

### Graphify version

0.9.76

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.1

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

- graphify **0.9.76**, installed with `uv tool install graphifyy` (uv 0.11.16); the tool's interpreter is Python 3.14.5.
- Windows 11, PowerShell and Git Bash alike.
- **No provider environment variables set**: no `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. The run is AST-only, no LLM involved, and the embedded labels come straight from the markdown headings.
- **A clean checkout reproduces it**: the repro above is an empty directory with two files and nothing else — no config, no `.graphifyignore`, no cache.
- First seen on 0.8.19 in a real repository, where fenced `vue` blocks in the docs produced the two labels by themselves; still reproducible on 0.9.76 with the minimal case.

### Additional context

The escaping has been tightened once before, in `a523509` ("fix(tree): escape title, header, and JSON blob in emit_html"), which mirrored `_js_safe()` into `tree_html.py`. That change covered `</` only, so all three copies share the same gap today:

- `graphify/exporters/html.py` (~line 617) — the one this report is about;
- `graphify/tree_html.py`;
- `graphify/callflow_html.py`.

It does not look exploitable: `</script` is already neutralised, so hostile content cannot close the element and inject markup. The effect is a graph page that silently will not render — which, with the CLI reporting success, is hard to attribute without reading the HTML.

A regression test would be cheap: generate a graph whose labels contain `<!--` and `<script`, then assert that neither sequence appears inside the `<script>` block of the output (or, stronger, that an HTML parser finds both inline scripts).

I can open a PR with the one-line change in all three files plus that test, if it is welcome.

title: fix(export): escape every "<" in JSON embedded in <script> blocks
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4124.

`graph.html` (and `GRAPH_TREE.html`) embed graph data as JSON inside a `<script>` element. The escaping only neutralised `</`, so an unclosed `<!--` followed later by `<script` reached the document verbatim. That moves the HTML tokenizer into the [script data double escaped state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#script-data-double-escaped-state), where the real `</script>` no longer closes the element: the rest of the page is swallowed as script text, it fails with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'`, and nothing renders while the CLI reports success.

The fix escapes every `<` as `\u003c` instead of only the `</` pair. JSON and JavaScript decode `\u003c` back to `<`, so labels display unchanged, but the tokenizer never sees `<!--`, `<script` or `</script` inside the data block.

Changed:
- `graphify/exporters/html.py`: `_js_safe()` (nodes, edges, legend, hyperedges).
- `graphify/tree_html.py`: the inline escape in `emit_html()`.

**Correction to the issue:** the issue listed `graphify/callflow_html.py` as a third copy. It is not affected: its inline `<script>` is static code and embeds no graph data, so it is left unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** JSON embedded in an inline `<script>` must never be able to change the HTML tokenizer's state, whatever text node labels carry. With no raw `<` in the payload, none of the three sequences the tokenizer reacts to (`<!--`, `<script`, `</script`) can appear.

**Regression tests** (both fail on `v8` and pass with the fix):
- `tests/test_export.py::test_to_html_escapes_script_data_sequences_in_embedded_json`: labels containing `<!--` and `<script` in nodes, edges, legend and hyperedges. Asserts no raw `<` in any embedded JSON block and that labels still decode to the original text.
- `tests/test_tree_html.py::test_emit_html_escapes_script_data_sequences_in_embedded_json`: same check for `emit_html()`, plus a JSON round-trip.

**End-to-end check:** ran `graphify update` on the minimal repro from #4124 (`guide.md` + `hello.js`) and parsed the page with jsdom:

| Page | Inline `<script>` elements | Script syntax |
|---|---|---|
| Before the fix | 1 | `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'` |
| After the fix | 2 | ok |

**Generated/persisted state:** only the HTML output changes, and it is rewritten on the next run. `graph.json`, caches and the manifest are untouched.

**Limitations:** only `<` is escaped. `>` and `&` cannot change the tokenizer state inside script data, and `json.dumps` already escapes non-ASCII characters (including U+2028/U+2029).

title: Julia: functions with a `where` clause are dropped entirely
body:
### Version / commit
v0.9.77 (v8 @ 5c7b847)

### Environment
macOS, Python 3.13, clean checkout of `v8`.

### What happens
Any Julia method written with a `where` clause is silently dropped from the graph — no node, no `defines` edge, and none of the calls made from its body are recorded.

`where` constraints are everywhere in idiomatic generic Julia, so this erases a large fraction of a real codebase's functions.

### Minimal reproduction
```julia
# where.jl
function combine(a::Vector{T}, b::Vector{T}) where {T<:Number}
    merge_all(a, b)
end
function merge_all(a, b)
    return a
end
```

```python
from graphify.extract import extract_julia
r = extract_julia("where.jl")
print([n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]])
# -> ['where.jl', 'merge_all()']   # 'combine()' is missing
print([(e["source"], e["target"]) for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "calls"])
# -> []                            # combine -> merge_all lost
```

### Expected vs actual
- **Expected:** a `combine()` node with a `calls` edge to `merge_all`.
- **Actual:** `combine` is absent and its body call vanishes.

### Root cause
The signature reader only looks for a direct `call_expression` child of the `signature` node, but a `where` method wraps the call head in a `where_expression`, so the name is never found and the definition falls through.

A clean checkout of `v8` reproduces it. Fix PR to follow.

title: fix(julia): extract functions with where-clause signatures
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4126.

A Julia method written with a `where` clause — `function f(x::T) where T ... end` — was dropped entirely: no node, no `defines` edge, and every call made from its body was lost. Since `where` constraints are pervasive in idiomatic generic Julia, this silently erased a large share of a typical codebase's functions.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Root cause

`_func_name_from_signature` scanned the `signature` node's children for a direct `call_expression` to read the function name from. But a parametric method nests the call head one level deeper:

```
signature
  where_expression
    call_expression      <- the actual `f(...)` head
    where
    identifier / curly_expression
```

With no direct `call_expression` child, the name came back `None` and the whole `function_definition` was skipped.

## Implementation

Unwrap `where_expression` (recursively, to cover stacked `f(x) where T where U`) before reading the call head. Plain and short-function signatures take the existing path unchanged, so the fix is additive.

### Version / commit
v0.9.77 (v8 @ 5c7b847)

### Environment
macOS, Python 3.13, clean checkout of `v8`.

### What happens
A parametric type declaration is dropped from the graph entirely — no node, and for the subtyping form no inherits edge either. The non-parametric forms (`struct Box`, `abstract type Shape`, `Dog <: Animal`) all work; only the `{...}` parameter list breaks it. Parametric types are the backbone of generic Julia.

### Minimal reproduction
```julia
# params.jl
struct Box{T}
    value::T
end
abstract type Shape{T} end
struct Sq{T} <: Shape{T}
end
```

```python
from graphify.extract import extract_julia
r = extract_julia("params.jl")
print([n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]])
# -> ['params.jl']   # Box, Shape, Sq all missing
```

### Expected vs actual
- **Expected:** `Box`, `Shape`, and `Sq` nodes, with `Sq --inherits--> Shape`.
- **Actual:** none of the three types appear.

### Root cause
The type-head reader only recognises a plain `identifier`. A parametric head is a `parametrized_type_expression` (its leading `identifier` is the real name), which matched neither the bare nor the `binary_expression` (subtyping) branch, so the name came back `None` and the type was skipped.

A clean checkout of `v8` reproduces it. Fix PR to follow.

title: fix(julia): extract parametric type definitions
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4128.

`struct Box{T}` and `abstract type Shape{T}` were dropped from the graph entirely — no node, no inherits edge. The non-parametric forms all work; only the `{...}` type-parameter list broke extraction. Since generics are the backbone of idiomatic Julia, this silently erased a large share of a typical codebase's types.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Root cause

The type-head reader (`_type_head_names`) only recognised a plain `identifier`. A parametric declaration exposes a `parametrized_type_expression` whose leading `identifier` is the real name:

```
type_head
  parametrized_type_expression   # Box{T}
    identifier                   # Box   <- the name
    curly_expression             # {T}
```

That matched neither the bare branch nor the `binary_expression` (subtyping) branch, so the name came back `None` and the `struct_definition` / `abstract_definition` was skipped. The subtyping form `Sq{T} <: Shape{T}` hit the same gap for its parametric operand.

## Implementation

Add a small `_type_name` helper that resolves an operand through `parametrized_type_expression` to its leading identifier, and use it in both the bare and subtyping branches. Non-parametric declarations keep the existing behaviour.

title: Scala: given...with instance methods leak to the file and collide with same-named trait methods
body:
### Version / commit
v0.9.77 (v8 @ 5c7b847)

### Environment
macOS, Python 3.13, clean checkout of `v8`.

### What happens
A Scala 3 `given name: T with { ... }` instance owns method implementations, but it is not modelled as a container. Its methods leak to the file node, and when a given method shares a name with a method of the trait it implements (the normal case — it IS the implementation), the leaked file-level node collides with the trait's method node. The trait node then wrongly carries the given's call/reference edges, corrupting the graph.

### Minimal reproduction
```scala
// given.scala
trait Show[A]:
  def show(a: A): String

given intShow: Show[Int] with
  def show(a: Int): String = helper(a)
  def helper(a: Int): String = a.toString
```

```python
from graphify.extract import extract_scala
r = extract_scala("given.scala")
print([n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]])
# -> no 'intShow' node; a stray file-level 'helper' appears
print([(e["source"], e["target"]) for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "calls"])
# the show -> helper call is attributed to the TRAIT's show node, not the given's
```

### Expected vs actual
- **Expected:** an `intShow` node owning `show`/`helper`; the `show -> helper` call stays inside the given; the trait node is untouched.
- **Actual:** no given node; methods leak to the file; the trait `show` node is polluted with the given's edges.

### Root cause
`given_definition` is absent from the Scala `class_types`, so the engine never opens a scope for its `with_template_body`; the members are walked as if they were file-level definitions and their ids collide with equally-named trait members.

A clean checkout of `v8` reproduces it. Fix PR to follow.

title: fix(scala): model given...with instances so their methods don't collide
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4130.

A Scala 3 `given name: T with { ... }` instance owns method implementations, but `given_definition` was not in the Scala `class_types`, so its body was never a scope. Its methods leaked to the file node, and because a given method normally shares its name with the trait method it implements, the leaked file-level node **collided** with the trait's method node — the trait ended up carrying the given's call/reference edges, corrupting the graph.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Root cause

The engine only opens a child scope (and namespaces members under it) for node types in `config.class_types`. `given_definition` was missing, so:

```
given intShow: Show[Int] with
  def show(a: Int) ...     # minted as file-level `<stem>_show`
  def helper(a: Int) ...   # minted as file-level `<stem>_helper`
```

`<stem>_show` is exactly the id the trait's `show` already owns → collision; the given's `show -> helper` call then lands on the trait node.

## Implementation

Two additions to `_SCALA_CONFIG`:
- `given_definition` → `class_types` (the given is named by its `identifier`, e.g. `intShow`).
- `with_template_body` → `body_fallback_child_types` (where a `given ... with` wraps its members).

The given now becomes its own node owning its methods. Fail-safe edges:
- **Anonymous** given (`given Show[Int] with ...`, no name) → skipped rather than leaked (strictly better than the previous collision).
- **Alias** given (`given x: T = expr`, no body) → simply yields a node.

## Verification & Invariants

- [x] **Reproduced** and identified the invariant (a given's members must be namespaced under it; the trait must stay clean).

title: Elixir: defdelegate function definitions are dropped
body:
### Version / commit
v0.9.77 (v8 @ 5c7b847)

### Environment
macOS, Python 3.13, clean checkout of `v8`.

### What happens
`defdelegate name(args), to: Mod` defines a real, public module function (it forwards its body to another module), but it is not extracted. The delegated function never becomes a node, and an intra-module call to it resolves to nothing — so parts of a module's public surface vanish from the graph.

### Minimal reproduction
```elixir
# facade.ex
defmodule Facade do
  defdelegate start(x), to: Worker
  defdelegate stop(x), to: Worker, as: :halt

  def run(x) do
    start(x)
    stop(x)
  end
end
```

```python
from graphify.extract import extract_elixir
r = extract_elixir("facade.ex")
print(sorted((n.get("label") or "").rstrip("()") for n in r["nodes"]))
# -> ['Facade', 'facade.ex', 'run']   # start / stop missing
print([(e["source"], e["target"]) for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "calls"])
# -> []   # run -> start, run -> stop unresolved
```

### Expected vs actual
- **Expected:** `start` and `stop` function nodes, with `run --calls--> start` and `run --calls--> stop`.
- **Actual:** the delegated functions are absent and the calls dangle.

### Root cause
`defdelegate` has the same `call` head shape as `def` (its first argument is the function signature), but it is not in the def-handling keyword set, so it falls through to the generic recursion and is dropped.

A clean checkout of `v8` reproduces it. Fix PR to follow.

title: fix(elixir): extract defdelegate function definitions
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4132.

`defdelegate name(args), to: Mod` defines a real, public module function (it forwards its body to another module), but it was dropped: the delegated function was never a node and intra-module calls to it had nothing to resolve to. Delegation is a common public-API idiom, so whole slices of a module's surface went missing.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Root cause

`defdelegate` has the identical `call` head shape as `def`/`defp` — the first argument is the function signature:

```
call
  identifier "defdelegate"
  arguments
    call "start(x)"     <- the signature
    keywords "to: Worker"
```

But it was absent from the keyword branch that turns such heads into member nodes, so it fell through to the generic recursion and vanished.

- Handle `defdelegate` in the same branch as `def`/`defp` (the existing signature reader already pulls the name out of the leading `call` argument and ignores the `to:`/`as:` keyword list).
- Add `defdelegate` to `_SKIP_KEYWORDS` so the call pass never mistakes the `defdelegate` keyword itself for a call.

title: fix(affected): accept qualified seeds, exit nonzero on a miss or tie
body:
## What does this PR do?

`graphify affected` had no way to name one of two same-named methods, and it reported a failed lookup as success. On httpx, `Client` and `AsyncClient` both define `.send()` in `httpx/_client.py`:

- `affected "Client.send"`, `affected "httpx/_client.py::Client.send"` and `affected ".send()"` print `No unique node match for ...` on stdout and exit 0. A script reads that as "nothing depends on this".
- `affected send` resolves to a sourceless stub `Send`, left by a `send: Send` annotation in tests/conftest.py, and lists its 10 annotation users. Three real definitions are named `send`.

The change is in seed resolution in `graphify/affected.py` and in the `affected` branch of `graphify/cli.py`. The traversal, `affected_nodes`, is unchanged.

**Qualified seeds.** `Class.method`, `path::Class.method`, `path::function` and `path::Class` now resolve.

- The path goes through the same `_as_repo_relative` normalization as a file-path seed and restricts the node's own `source_file`. The exact spelling wins. A case- or Unicode-insensitive match is used only when no file has the exact spelling, and when it matches several files the result is a tie.
- The class must own the member through a `method` or `contains` edge. Direction is read from the `_src`/`_tgt` markers the way serve.py reads them. Label text alone never picks the owner.
- When several owners with the requested name own a matching member, the result is a tie.
- A qualified query is answered from its scope before any unrestricted label, so a Markdown heading `# Client.send` cannot stand in for the method. A miss inside a path scope is final.
- A two-level chain such as `Outer.Inner.run` is refused with a hint to use `Inner.run`, `path::Inner.run` or a node id.

**Fail closed.** Resolution runs in tiers: exact id, qualified, exact label, bare name, source path, substring. A tier resolves the seed only when it has exactly one candidate. A miss prints `No unique node match for X` to stderr and exits 1. A tie prints each candidate's label, `file:line` and node id to stderr and exits 1. After a name tier ties, the substring tier no longer runs.

**Real definitions beat stubs.** In each tier, source-backed nodes outrank sourceless ones. A method label such as `.send()` also answers to `send`. Other labels keep their leading dot, so a `.config` file does not tie with `Config`.

`format_affected` raises a new `SeedResolutionError` instead of returning the miss text, and the CLI turns it into exit 1. `resolve_seed` keeps its `str | None` return. `explain` and `path` resolve through `serve._find_node_tiers` and are unchanged.

### Behavior changes users will see

I resolved every node label under 80 characters, plus its bare forms, with v8 and with this branch (httpx: 3,235 seeds, Flask: 3,134).

- A miss or a tie now exits 1 and prints to stderr. One existing test expected exit 0 on a miss and now expects 1.
- A bare name shared by a function and methods is now a tie: 10 httpx names (`get`, `post`, `put`, ...) and 16 Flask names. `get()` and `httpx/_api.py::get` still resolve to the function.
- Stubs no longer answer for names that real definitions carry. 14 seeds moved from a stub to a real node and 9 to a candidate list. Flask's `affected copy` used to resolve to the stdlib `copy` stub and now resolves to `AppContext.copy`. Flask's `before_app_request` now resolves to `Blueprint.before_app_request`, which has no inbound edges; v8's stub carried one decorator use that the extractor had bound to it.
- 102 seeds that used to miss now resolve (44 httpx, 58 Flask), almost all bare method names that one class defines.
- I also tried every owned member in both graphs as `Owner.member` and `path::Owner.member`. None resolved to the wrong node. The 168 misses are httpx Markdown headings whose own labels contain a dot.

### Limitations

- One ownership level only, and inherited members are not followed. Name the class that defines the method.
- A member whose own label contains a dot (some Markdown headings) cannot be named as `Owner.member`. Use its node id.
- A `::` left half with no separator, no matching file and whitespace in it is treated as prose, as on v8. Adding `./` makes it a path.
- A left half that names an extensionless file in the graph is a path. So a root file named `Invoice` scopes `Invoice::Line` to itself; v8 resolved that query by substring.
- A plain file-path seed (no `::`) keeps v8's case-insensitive comparison.
- `affected_nodes` on an undirected graph still reads direction from edge iteration order, as on v8. The CLI always loads a directed graph, so only library callers are affected.
- Seen while testing and not changed here: `explain "Client.send"` on httpx returns a rationale node, and `path "no_such_symbol_xyz" httpx_models_response` routes from a docs node and exits 0.

Related: #3485 (`path::Symbol` for explain), #3913 and #3935 (path endpoint refusal), #1669 (member seeding), #2309 (`_src`/`_tgt` markers), #2706 and #2707 (path-form seeds).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: `affected` walks from exactly one node, and only from a node the query names unambiguously. A query that names no node, or several, exits nonzero with the reason on stderr. The resolver never picks one of several candidates, and a sourceless stub never answers for a name that source-backed definitions carry. A `path::` query whose left half has a separator or names a file never resolves outside that file.

Persisted state: none. `affected` reads graph.json and writes nothing, and extraction is untouched. Fixture graphs built by v8 and by this branch have identical node and edge sets, and an incremental update matched a clean rebuild.

- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

## How was this tested?

Linux only. Windows was not tested. The path half of a `path::` seed goes through the same `_as_repo_relative` helper as a file-path seed, but I did not run it on Windows.

```text
# vbnet extractors plus the ollama retry tests, all from missing optional dependencies)
uv run --offline pytest tests -q
v8:     30 failed, 6452 passed, 105 skipped
branch: 30 failed, 6474 passed, 105 skipped

uv run --offline ruff check .    All checks passed!
uv run --offline pyright         637 errors on v8 and on this branch

# httpx (2,239 nodes), graphify affected <seed>
seed                            v8                           this PR
Client.send                     miss, exit 0                 .send() L879, 9 hits, exit 0
httpx/_client.py::Client.send   miss, exit 0                 .send() L879, 9 hits, exit 0
AsyncClient.send                miss, exit 0                 .send() L1594, 9 hits, exit 0
send                            stub Send, 10 hits, exit 0   3 candidates, exit 1
.send()                         miss, exit 0                 2 candidates, exit 1
get_environment_proxies         9 hits, exit 0               9 hits, exit 0
httpx/_utils.py                 98 hits, exit 0              98 hits, exit 0
httpx/_missing.py::Client.send  miss, exit 0                 miss, exit 1
no_such_symbol_xyz              miss, exit 0                 miss, exit 1
```

```text
$ graphify affected send
Ambiguous seed send: 3 nodes match.
- .send() httpx/_client.py:L879 (id: httpx_client_client_send)
- .send() httpx/_client.py:L1594 (id: httpx_client_asyncclient_send)
- send() httpx/_transports/asgi.py:L148 (id: httpx_transports_asgi_asgitransport_handle_async_request_send)
Pass one of the ids above, or narrow the seed as Class.method or path::symbol.
```

### Rust verification on a v0.9.89 graph

Reproduced the public four-file Cargo fixture in [#4439](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/issues/4439) on Linux. The graph contains a source-backed `Invoice` and the sourceless `invoice` import stub. Reading the same graph, v0.9.89's `affected Invoice` reports no unique match and exits 0. This PR at `d480fe3` resolves the declaration and reports `make()` as affected. A missing name exits 1 on stderr.

A separate fixture with an `Invoice` struct and an `Invoice` enum variant produces a genuine tie. This PR lists both source-backed candidates and their ids on stderr and exits 1. Each explicit id resolves. Both fixtures' graph bytes remain unchanged by the queries.

The contributor [reports](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/pull/4134#issuecomment-6155764787) 401 correct resolutions and two genuine ties among 403 affected names in a private Cargo workspace. Those corpus figures are contributor evidence; the workspace is unavailable for independent verification. `explain Invoice` remains ambiguous in the public fixture, as documented above. Its resolver and Rust import-edge extraction are unchanged by this PR.

<details>
<summary>Edge-case fixtures through the CLI (v8 vs this PR)</summary>

```text

unrelated class Handle in other.py, pkg.py::handle.send:             miss, exit 0     ->  nested send(), exit 0
```

Qualified resolution on graphs with many same-named owners stays linear: 2,000 classes named `Client` resolve `Client.send` in 0.03 s, and a 16,000-edge undirected graph resolves in 0.12 s. Two tests cap the ownership lookups and whole-graph edge scans.

title: fix(rust): expand grouped use declarations into import bindings
body:
## What does this PR do?

`use crate::util::{parse, render};` produces one import edge to `util`; neither binding gets its own edge. A root group such as `use {a::b, c};` produces no edge.

This expands each grouped `use` into the bindings of the equivalent plain declarations. It uses v8's existing import-target rule, preserving path text, aliases, comments, spacing, glob imports and nested `self` bindings. Each edge comes from the file node at the binding's line. Plain declarations and call edges stay unchanged.

title: fix(python): let package imports pass a same-named type stub
body:
## What does this PR do?

In a src-layout repo, a Python package import could not reach the package when a type with the same case-folded name was referenced from another file.

In Flask (d73fa1c), the tests do `import flask` and annotate `app: flask.Flask`. The annotation leaves a sourceless stub for the type `Flask`. Node ids are case-folded, so the stub's id is `flask`, the same id as the dotted-module alias for `src/flask/__init__.py`. `_repoint_python_package_imports` (#2072) refuses any alias that already exists as a node id, so it never repointed `import flask` or `from flask import ...`. No file under `tests/` had an import edge to `src/flask/__init__.py`, and `affected` on the package listed no tests.

The refusal protects a real case: when a scan-root `pkg.py` exists, the resolver binds `import pkg` to it, and the nested `src/pkg` alias must not take that edge. This PR keeps the refusal for any id held by a node with a `source_file`. It ignores the collision only when all of these hold:

- Every node with that id is sourceless.
- The alias names exactly one scanned Python source or type-source file, with a valid dotted name: exact `.py` or `.pyi` suffix, every path component an NFKC-stable identifier (so `src/shop.v2/` never spells `shop.v2`).
- The import statement, NFKC-normalized the way Python reads identifiers, spells the module exactly like that file's dotted path (`flask`, not `Flask`).
- The edge has no `target_file`, so the resolver's own pick is never replaced.
- Exactly one node holds the destination file id, and its `source_file` is the alias file. If `__init__.h` or `__init__.pyi` shares the id, the edge stays where v8 put it.
- The top-level name is not a standard-library or built-in module name. The names come from a fixed constant, `_PYTHON_STUB_IMPORT_STDLIB_MODULE_NAMES` (333 names), the union of `sys.stdlib_module_names | sys.builtin_module_names` on CPython 3.10, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14, not from the running interpreter. It is a deliberate superset.
- On disk, the file must win a conservative finder model for that dotted name within its own path root. The check reads directory listings, not the scan, so files excluded by `.graphifyignore` still count. A package directory on the way must have no same-named module beside it, and the file must come first in finder order (extension modules, `.py`, `.pyc`, `.pyi`). Extension modules are matched by a fixed pattern (`<name>.so`, `<name>.pyd`, `<name>.<tag>.so`, `<name>.<tag>.pyd`), not by the host's `EXTENSION_SUFFIXES`.
- Nothing else can be found first for the top-level name: no `<top>` directory and no `<top>` module file of any of those kinds in the scan root or in the importer's non-package ancestors, scanned or not. A root `shop.py` therefore keeps `import shop.core` off `src/shop/core.py`.
- Every directory these checks need could be listed. A listing error counts as unknown and the edge keeps its v8 target.

To check the spelling, `_suppress_ambiguous_python_imports` leaves the raw module name it already reads on kept import edges as `_python_import_spelling`. `_repoint_python_package_imports` pops it from every edge, so it never reaches graph.json.

The stub and its `references` edges are not touched, and member-call resolution (`flask.redirect(...)`) is unchanged.

One side effect: Flask's tests had 16 `calls` edges to an external `flask` node (`flask.redirect()`, `flask.Flask()`, ...), created by the #3793 external-module path. Because `import flask` now reaches a real file, that path no longer applies and those 16 edges are gone. They pointed at a stub that claimed the in-repo package was external. Resolving those calls through the package is a separate change.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Rebased onto v0.9.88, `a9860f7`. The conflict repair retains upstream language overrides and package-initializer handling. The new 333-name stub exclusion has its own name; upstream's 218-name set remains unchanged for existing sibling-import rules. No cache-schema change is needed because the spelling marker is generated after cache reads and removed before output.

Invariant: a sourceless stub no longer keeps an exactly spelled import away from the one scanned module it names. The exception applies only when every condition above holds; otherwise the edge keeps its v8 target. It never overrides a real node, a resolver-stamped `target_file`, an ambiguous module name, a shared destination id, a file that cannot spell the import, a file that loses on disk inside its own tree, a shadowing entry in the scan root or the importer's ancestors, or a directory that cannot be listed.

The checks do not model the whole import system. They do not consult site-packages, PYTHONPATH, `.pth` files, custom importers, zip imports, or the relative order of the candidate's root and the importer's roots.

Determinism: the result depends only on the corpus on disk. Two tests run one corpus under different host values and get identical graphs: one patches `importlib.machinery.EXTENSION_SUFFIXES` to the 3.13 and 3.10 lists, the other patches `sys.stdlib_module_names` and `sys.builtin_module_names`.

Persisted state: no cache format change. `_python_import_spelling` is set after the per-file cache is written and popped before output; none of the rebuilt corpus graphs contains it.

title: fix(extract): honor tsconfig customConditions for workspace exports
body:
## What does this PR do?

Workspace package imports ignore the importer's `compilerOptions.customConditions`. For example, zod puts its checked-in TypeScript source behind `"@zod/source"`, alongside runtime exports that exist only after a build. On current v8, 229 distinct zod file/specifier sites still resolve to no file.

This adds a conservative fallback after the existing workspace resolution walk. It preserves every source file that walk reaches, including the dist-to-src fallback from #4485. Only an import left unresolved or on build output can change.

The fallback reads the importer's nearest tsconfig.json or jsconfig.json, merges relative or absolute `extends` parents in TypeScript's order, and caches completed merges per extraction run. It handles an exact exports entry whose first condition key is active in that importer and whose value names an in-package TypeScript implementation. Extension substitutions follow TypeScript 5.9.3. Declarations and JavaScript-only targets are refused.

It keeps v8's result when the config or target is uncertain:

- Unknown, missing, malformed, cyclic, or package-name config inheritance; symlinked configs or importer directories.
- JSONC stripping that would change any string, including an extends path. Conditions must also appear verbatim as string literals in the config that sets them. The shared JSONC parser is unchanged.
- A resolution mode that does not read exports, or `resolvePackageJsonExports: false`.
- Any `baseUrl`, `outDir`, or `declarationDir`; nonempty module suffixes; matching `paths` keys; or path-option templates.
- Nested condition objects, arrays, null targets, numeric keys, wildcard requests, or requests ending in `/`.
- Targets with traversal, backslashes, empty or node_modules segments, symlinks, or build-output locations.

Numeric-key rejection uses string checks, so an arbitrarily long key cannot raise an integer-conversion exception.

## Verification against v0.9.92

Base: `86c57be8204673c2a1b9849a3292a7dd3ab373d8`.
Candidate: `c1e5dcb9e8d32ae966d5757f05315a5214ad0d4b`.

The diff adds 1,192 lines across three files. It preserves both sets of tests at the rebase conflict and adds cases for source-twin priority, JSONC strings, numeric-key limits, and lexical importer paths.

- The final 63 custom-condition cases produce **13 failures and 50 passes on unmodified v8**, then **63 passes on this branch**. Six related JS/TS test files pass all **240 tests**.
- New review regressions also failed before their fixes: four JSONC cases, one huge numeric key, and two symlinked importer paths.
- Full suite: v8 **8,208 passed, 149 skipped**. Branch **8,271 passed, 149 skipped**.
- Ruff passes. Pyright reports the same **678 errors and 4 warnings** on both versions, with identical normalized diagnostic multisets.
- AST-only `graphify update . --no-cluster` completes.
- Independent GPT-6-Astra review approves the code. Its 54-fixture matrix has 18 changed resolutions, all matching TypeScript 5.9.3. It also checks same-process config/cache changes and real CLI/watch incremental behavior.

Fresh CLI extractions used `extract --code-only --no-cluster --no-dedup --max-workers 1` with separate output directories for baseline and candidate. The TypeScript 5.9.3 oracle uses each importer's own config and module resolution mode.

| Repository | Import recall before | Import recall after | Import precision before | Import precision after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| zod | 665/891 = 74.6% | 891/891 = 100% | 665/677 = 98.23% | 891/903 = 98.67% |
| hono | 843/843 = 100% | 843/843 = 100% | 843/846 = 99.65% | 843/846 = 99.65% |
| express | 149/153 = 97.4% | 149/153 = 97.4% | 149/149 = 100% | 149/149 = 100% |

These scores cover immediate file import pairs within mapped oracle files. They do not measure symbol or call precision. Zod maps 891 of 896 oracle pairs; hono maps 843 of 860; express maps all 153. The existing 12 zod and 3 hono false-positive pairs remain unchanged.

All **229 changed zod file/specifier sites** were unresolved on v8 and match TypeScript's selected file on this branch. Zod keeps all 5,922 existing nodes with all attributes unchanged, and all existing edges except 203 imports_from edges to the external `ref_zod` stub. In particular, all 1,903 existing imports to source files retain every attribute. Its graph changes from 10,004 to 10,090 edges and adds six external symbol stubs. Hono and express graph.json files are byte-identical.

## Limits

This deliberately supports fewer shapes than TypeScript. Existing v8 source targets always win, even where its fixed condition priority or source-twin heuristic differs from TypeScript. Solution-style `references`, package.json `imports` conditions, JavaScript-only custom targets, and the refused shapes above remain outside this fallback.

Importer edits followed by changed-paths rebuilds match full CLI rebuilds in independent fixtures. Config-only edits can stay stale until a full `graphify update`, matching the existing alias-loader limitation. Windows was not tested; symlink tests skip where symlinks are unavailable.

The full suites ran with the development dependency group and an isolated SQL grammar. Other optional-dependency tests can skip. No generated skill sources changed. Both material AI contributors are disclosed in the commit metadata.

title: fix(global): preserve stored edge direction in global add (#4066)
body:
## What does this PR do?

This is the separate `global add` PR announced in #4088. #4088 fixed the other reloaders in #4066 and listed `global add` as a follow-up, because it changes persisted user state (`~/.graphify/global-graph.json`) and needs an extra fix in the external-node dedup.

`global add` loads a repo's `graph.json` with a plain undirected `node_link_graph`. As in #4066, every link whose target comes before its source in the node list comes back reversed. Here the reversal is written to `~/.graphify/global-graph.json`, so `path` and every other direction-aware reader of the global graph follow the wrong direction.

Changes, all in `global_graph.global_add`:

- **Load.** Call `paths.restore_arc_direction` (added in #4088) before `node_link_graph`, as the export loader and `load_node_link_graph` now do. `prefix_graph_for_global` already rewrites `_src`/`_tgt` when it prefixes IDs, so the markers survive into the global graph.
- **External-node dedup.** When a repo's external node (no `source_file`, e.g. `requests`) is deduplicated onto one already in the global graph, `remap` rewires the edge endpoints but not `_src`/`_tgt`. Repo B's edge ends at `A::requests` while its `_tgt` still names `B::requests`, a node that no longer exists, so direction-aware readers follow the marker to nowhere. The markers are now remapped along with the endpoints. This already happens on `v8` for graph.json files that carry legacy markers. Stamping on load would make it happen for every repo, so the two changes ship together.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** every edge in `global-graph.json` keeps the direction stored in the source repo's `graph.json`, and its `_src`/`_tgt` markers name nodes that exist in the global graph.

Two new tests in `tests/test_export_direction.py`, the #4066 regression file from #4088:
- `test_global_add_persists_stored_direction` uses that file's fixture: a link listed callee-first (reversed today), one listed caller-first (must stay as is) and a legacy-marker link.
- `test_global_add_dedup_remaps_direction_markers`: two repos share an external `requests` node. Both edges must point from the caller to `A::requests`, and every marker must name an existing node.

**Both fail on `v8` on the direction assert and pass with this change.**

**Persisted state this fix cannot repair by itself:** an existing `~/.graphify/global-graph.json` keeps its reversed edges. `global add` skips a repo whose `graph.json` hash is unchanged, so users must run `graphify global remove <tag>` and then `graphify global add` again for each repo.

**Open question for review:** `global-graph.json` now keeps the stamped `_src`/`_tgt` markers. It is written with raw `node_link_data`, and every direction-aware reader honours the markers. If you would rather it follow the `graph.json` convention (arc order is the direction, no markers), `_save_global_graph` can pop them back the way `to_json` and the merge driver do. I left that out to keep this PR to the fix.

**Overlap:** #3022 also edits `global_add` (moves it onto a new `load_graph_json`) with `preserve_direction=False`, so it keeps the reversal. Whichever lands second needs a small rebase. On top of #3022 this PR becomes `preserve_direction=True` plus the dedup marker remap, which is still needed.

title: Java: methods and calls inside anonymous class bodies are dropped
fix(java): capture methods and calls inside anonymous class bodies
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4139.

A Java/Groovy anonymous class (`new Runnable() { … }`) contributed nothing to the graph: its methods were not nodes and every call made inside them was dropped. Anonymous listeners/callbacks are routine in Java, so this silently erased a large slice of the call graph. Kotlin's equivalent (`object : Foo { … }`, #2347) is already handled — this brings Java to parity.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Root cause

The anonymous body hangs off an `object_creation_expression` as a `class_body`:

```
object_creation_expression   new Runnable() { … }
  type: Runnable
  class_body
    method_declaration        public void run() { helper(); }
```

`object_creation_expression` is not in `class_types` and the function branch never recurses into bodies, so the `run()` method — and its call to `helper()` — were never visited. This is the exact shape Kotlin #2347 fixed for `object_literal`.

## Implementation

Mirror the Kotlin #2347 handling in the same function-body section: scan the body for anonymous classes (an `object_creation_expression` with a `class_body`), without crossing a nested `method_declaration`/`lambda_expression` boundary and without descending into a found one; emit an owner node per anonymous class (id qualified by enclosing function + base type + line, so two in one method can't collide); add a `contains` edge from the enclosing method; and walk the `class_body` like the class branch so members and their calls flow through the normal machinery.

**Fail-closed limitation (documented):** the base type is recorded only as the node's label, not an `implements`/`inherits` edge. A Java anonymous class usually realises a library interface or class whose kind is unknowable from this file, and the guidelines prefer withholding a guessed relationship over asserting one — so no subtype edge is emitted.

## Verification & Invariants

- [x] **Read** CONTRIBUTING.md.
- [x] **Reproduced** and identified the invariant (an anonymous class's members and their calls must appear in the graph).
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** that mirrors the established Kotlin pattern (one file, `graphify/extractors/engine.py`).
- [x] Added **regression tests** that fail on pre-fix `v8` and pass after.
- [x] Documented the fail-closed subtype-edge limitation above.

title: Fortran: named generic interfaces are dropped, so calls to the generic name dangle
body:
### Version / commit
v0.9.77 (v8 @ 5c7b847)

### Environment
macOS, Python 3.13, clean checkout of `v8`.

### What happens
A named generic interface (`interface area; module procedure area_circle, area_square; end interface`) names a callable that dispatches to its specific procedures. The interface is never turned into a node, so a call to the generic name produces no edge (a Fortran function call only resolves to an in-file node), and the dispatch set is invisible — even though the specific procedures themselves are extracted. Generic interfaces and operator overload sets are routine in scientific Fortran.

### Minimal reproduction
```fortran
! shapes.f90
module shapes
  interface area
    module procedure area_circle, area_square
  end interface
contains
  real function area_circle(r)
    real :: r
    area_circle = r
  end function
  real function area_square(s)
    real :: s
    area_square = s
  end function
  subroutine report(x)
    real :: x, a
    a = area(x)
  end subroutine
end module
```

```python
from graphify.extract import extract_fortran
r = extract_fortran("shapes.f90")
print([n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]])
# -> no 'area()' node
print([(e["source"], e["target"]) for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "calls"])
# -> []   # report -> area is lost
```

### Expected vs actual
- **Expected:** an `area` node that dispatches to `area_circle`/`area_square`, and a `report -> area` call edge.
- **Actual:** the generic interface is absent and the call dangles.

### Root cause
`fortran.py` has no handler for `interface` nodes; a named generic interface's `name` is never emitted. A direct call to a specific procedure resolves fine, so this is specific to the generic name.

A clean checkout of `v8` reproduces it. Fix PR to follow.

title: fix(fortran): extract named generic interfaces as callable nodes
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4141.

A named generic interface (`interface area; module procedure area_circle, area_square; end interface`) names a callable that dispatches to its specific procedures by argument type. The interface block was never turned into a node, so a call to the generic name dangled (a Fortran function call_expression only resolves to an in-file node) and the dispatch set was invisible — even though the specific procedures were extracted. Generic interfaces and operator overload sets are routine in scientific Fortran.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Root cause

`fortran.py`'s `walk()` had no `interface` branch, so a named generic interface fell through to the default recursion and its `name` (`area`) was never emitted:

```
interface
  interface_statement
    name: area                 <- never noded
  procedure_statement
    procedure_kind: module procedure
    method_name: area_circle
    method_name: area_square
```

Because a function `call_expression` only emits a `calls` edge when the callee resolves to an in-file node, `a = area(x)` produced nothing.

## Implementation

Handle `interface` in `walk()`:
- **Named** generic interface → emit a node for the generic name, and record `(generic, specific_procedure)` pairs; after the walk, link them with `dispatches_to` edges (resolved via the same `ensure_named_node` path as type-bound procedures, so a procedure from another module becomes a collapsible sourceless stub rather than a dangling edge). The existing call resolution then binds `area(x)` to the new node.
- **Unnamed** abstract/explicit interface → recurse as before, so its procedure declarations are still extracted (unchanged).

## Verification & Invariants

- [x] **Reproduced** and identified the invariant (a generic interface name must be a callable node so calls resolve; no dangling edges).
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** (one file, `graphify/extractors/fortran.py`).
- [x] Added a **regression test** that fails on pre-fix `v8` and passes after.
- [x] Documented behaviour: cross-module specific procedures resolve to sourceless stubs (consistent with type-bound procedures).

## How was this tested?

```text
python -m pytest tests/ -q -k fortran        # 16 passed

# 6555 passed, 15 skipped
```

`graph.json` already stores `built_at_commit`, but the MCP server dropped it on load, so `graph_stats` only showed counts. title: [Bug]: UTF-16 source files extract to nothing, and Windows-1252 names are cut short, with no warning
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

The extractors hand tree-sitter the raw file bytes, and tree-sitter reads them as UTF-8. Two encodings that real Windows projects still contain go wrong, and nothing is printed either way:

- **UTF-16 with a BOM** (what Visual Studio saves as "Unicode", what Windows PowerShell 5.1 `Out-File` and `>` write, what older SSMS scripts are): the file gets its file node and nothing else. No classes, no methods, no calls.
- **Windows-1252** (Notepad's old ANSI default): `CaféOrder` is stored as `Caf\xE9Order`. `\xE9` is not UTF-8, so the identifier is cut at that byte and the class comes out as `Order`, with node id `order_shop_order` instead of `order_shop_caféorder`.

The regex-based readers (Svelte, Vue, Astro, Dart, Razor, ...) read with `errors="replace"`, so UTF-16 turns into replacement characters there too. Three secondary passes (`_is_spock_file`, `_extract_spock_fallback`, `_augment_cpp_string_tests`) call `read_text(errors="replace")` with no encoding, so they follow the host locale and read the same file differently on Windows and Linux.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
python - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
src = "namespace Shop {\n  public class CaféOrder {\n    public void Pay() { Charge(); }\n    public void Charge() { }\n  }\n}\n"
for name, data in {"utf8": src.encode("utf-8"), "cp1252": src.encode("cp1252"), "utf16": src.encode("utf-16")}.items():
    d = Path("enc_" + name); d.mkdir(exist_ok=True); (d / "Order.cs").write_bytes(data)
EOF
graphify update enc_utf8 --force --no-cluster
graphify update enc_cp1252 --force --no-cluster
graphify update enc_utf16 --force --no-cluster
# then compare the node labels in each enc_*/graphify-out/graph.json
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Same C# / Java / Python file, saved four ways, `graphify update --force --no-cluster` on 0.9.77:

lang  encoding       calls  nodes found
cs    utf-8              1  .Charge(), .Pay(), .Send(), CaféOrder, Invoice, Shop
cs    utf-8 + BOM        1  .Charge(), .Pay(), .Send(), CaféOrder, Invoice, Shop
cs    windows-1252       1  .Charge(), .Pay(), .Send(), Invoice, Order, Shop
cs    utf-16 + BOM       0  (nothing)
java  utf-8              1  .charge(), .pay(), CaféOrder
java  windows-1252       1  .charge(), .pay(), Order
java  utf-16 + BOM       0  (nothing)
py    utf-8              1  .charge(), .pay(), .send(), CaféOrder, Invoice
py    windows-1252       1  .charge(), .pay(), .send(), Invoice, Order
py    utf-16 + BOM       0  (nothing)

No warning is printed in any row.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.77 (5c7b847)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

AST-only `update`, no provider environment variables set. A clean checkout of `v8` at `5c7b847` reproduces it.

### Additional context

`detect._read_ignore_text` already solves the same problem for ignore files (UTF-8 first, then UTF-16 by BOM, then a fallback with a one-time warning). Source files never got the same treatment. I have a fix with regression tests ready and will open a PR right after this.

title: fix(extract): decode UTF-16 and non-UTF-8 source files before parsing
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4145.

tree-sitter reads its input as UTF-8, and every extractor handed it the raw file bytes. A UTF-16 file (Visual Studio "Unicode", Windows PowerShell 5.1 `Out-File`) produced only its file node, and a Windows-1252 identifier was cut at its first non-UTF-8 byte (`CaféOrder` → `Order`). Both were silent.

This adds two helpers in `extractors/base.py` and routes every source read in extraction through them:

- `_read_source_bytes(path, *, warn=True)`: valid UTF-8, with or without a BOM, is returned **byte for byte** (an `isascii()` fast path, then a strict UTF-8 check). A UTF-16/UTF-32 file with a BOM is decoded exactly and re-encoded as UTF-8. Anything else is decoded as cp1252, then latin-1 (which cannot fail), and a warning names the file once per process.
- `_read_source_text(path, *, warn=True)`: the same, as `str`. For valid UTF-8 it returns exactly what `path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` did, including universal-newline translation and a kept BOM, so the regex extractors see the same text as before.

59 read sites in 34 files now use them: 31 tree-sitter `read_bytes()` reads and 28 `read_text(..., errors="replace")` reads. Two of those are in the semantic pass: `llm._file_to_text` (a document sent whole) and its token estimate now use the same reader as `file_slice.unit_source_text` (a document cut into slices), so a document reads the same whichever path it takes. Secondary passes that re-read a file its extractor already read (cross-file resolution, rationale, Spock/Catch2 fallbacks, XAML code-behind) pass `warn=False`, so one bad file gives one warning. That includes three reads (`_is_spock_file`, `_extract_spock_fallback`, `_augment_cpp_string_tests`) that had no `encoding=` at all and so depended on the host locale.

Left as they are on purpose: binary readers (`.dmi`, Delphi binary forms), XML project files that declare their own encoding (`.csproj`, `.slnx`, `.xaml`, Lazarus `.lpk`), header sniffers (`_is_objc_header`, `_is_cpp_header`), and JSON/YAML config reads (`tsconfig`, `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** the same source text gives the same graph whatever encoding the file was saved in, and every file that was valid UTF-8 gives exactly the graph it gave before.

- Valid UTF-8 is never re-encoded: `_read_source_bytes` returns the original `bytes` object, so node ids, byte offsets and source locations of existing files cannot move. Checked on all 453 `.py` files of this repo (313 contain non-ASCII): every one byte-identical to `read_bytes()`.
- The fallback is a fixed `("cp1252", "latin-1")`, not `locale.getpreferredencoding()`. `_read_ignore_text` uses the host encoding, which is fine for ignore rules that never leave the machine, but node ids are persisted and shared, and CONTRIBUTING asks that extraction not depend on ambient state. A test pins this by monkeypatching the locale.
- `FF FE 00 00` is both the UTF-32-LE BOM and a UTF-16-LE BOM followed by U+0000; a failed UTF-32 decode falls through to UTF-16 (tested).
- Line numbers are unchanged in every case (decoding never adds or removes a line), so `source_location` stays correct.
- Persisted state: the cache key is the hash of the file bytes and the cache directory carries the package version, so the empty/truncated results cached for non-UTF-8 files by older versions are not reused after upgrading. UTF-8 files hash the same and extract the same.
- Cost: reading those 8.4 MB took 46 ms instead of 35 ms (best of 5).

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Limitations:** a file in a third legacy encoding (Shift-JIS, GBK, cp1251, ...) is still decoded as cp1252/latin-1. Its names come out whole but mis-spelled, and the warning names the file so it can be re-saved as UTF-8. UTF-16 without a BOM is not detected.

## How was this tested?

New `tests/test_source_file_encoding.py`, 42 tests:
- decoder: UTF-8 (with/without BOM, CRLF, empty) passed through byte for byte; UTF-16 LE/BE and UTF-32 LE/BE decoded exactly with no warning; the `FF FE 00 00` case; cp1252 read whole and warned once; `warn=False` silent; latin-1 fallback for a byte cp1252 does not define; locale independence; `_read_source_text` equals `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` for CRLF, lone CR and BOM.
- extraction: C#, Java and Python saved as UTF-16 LE, UTF-16 BE, UTF-32 and cp1252 give exactly the UTF-8 graph (same node ids, same edges); a cp1252 file warns once across all passes; a UTF-16 Python file's import call resolves across files; UTF-16 SQL, PowerShell and Svelte are extracted; a UTF-16 Spock spec keeps its feature methods; a UTF-16 Catch2 `TEST_CASE` is recovered.
- semantic pass: for UTF-8, UTF-8 + BOM, UTF-16 and cp1252, `llm._file_to_text` and `file_slice.unit_source_text` return the same text.

Before the fix (upstream `5c7b847` with only the helpers added, so the decoder tests can import), all 19 extraction tests fail; without the `llm.py` change the UTF-16 and cp1252 reader-agreement cases fail; with the fix all 42 pass.

```text
uv sync --all-extras --frozen
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_source_file_encoding.py -q          # 42 passed
uv run --frozen pytest tests -q                                       # 6622 passed, 23 failed; the same 23 fail on clean v8 5c7b847 on Windows (FIFO/socket/POSIX-path tests)
uv run --frozen ruff check graphify tests/test_source_file_encoding.py  # All checks passed
uv run --frozen bandit -q -ll <changed files>                         # same 7 findings as v8 (B314 x4, B324 x3), none new
uv run --frozen pyright <changed files>                               # 199 errors, identical to v8 file by file; llm.py/file_slice.py 11 = v8; new test file 0
graphify update <dir> --force --no-cluster                            # table from the issue: every row now matches UTF-8
```

Windows 11, Python 3.12.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (not applicable, no skill sources changed)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

title: [Bug]: Cross-drive syntax-error warning can abort extraction on Windows
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

A source file with recoverable syntax errors can abort extraction when its path and the scan root are on different Windows drives. The syntax-error warning calls `os.path.relpath` for its display path, and the resulting `ValueError` escapes instead of returning the extracted graph and warning.

The expected behavior is to return the graph and report the partial-extraction warning with a usable source path. The adjacent warning for a clean file without symbols already handles this drive condition.

### Steps to reproduce

Use this Lua input as `broken.lua`:

```lua
local t = {
function f() end
```

Call `graphify.extract.extract([source], root=scan_root)` with the included source and scan root on different Windows drives. This report's execution used a controlled macOS probe: the real extraction entry point ran on this fixture, while the source/root `relpath` conversion used `ntpath.relpath` with different drives. A same-drive extraction is the control.

The path operation can be checked independently on any platform:

```python
import ntpath
ntpath.relpath("D:/included/broken.lua", "C:/scan-root")
```

### Error output or graph output

Path-sanitized controlled-probe result:

```text
ValueError: path is on mount 'D:', start on mount 'C:'
```

The exception escapes the syntax-warning display conversion in `graphify/extract.py`; the extraction call returns no graph and does not emit the intended warning.

### Graphify version

0.9.77; source inspected at `5c7b84792f453582676548185aaec3824d51dfe2` on `v8`.

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

The source snapshot was tested with local Python dependencies. The cross-drive operation was simulated with Windows path semantics; this is not a native Windows run. No model request is needed. The earlier cache portability path contained the same exception before the warning failed. No written AST cache file was inventoried, and this report makes no cache-file creation claim.

### Additional context
