title: fix(deps): raise tree-sitter runtime floor to >=0.25 for ABI 15 grammars
body:
## Summary

The declared runtime floor `tree-sitter>=0.23.0,<0.26` is lower than any runtime that can load the grammars this same file allows. This PR floors the runtime at the oldest release that supports the grammars we already ship.

## The problem

`tree-sitter` 0.23 and 0.24 report `LANGUAGE_VERSION = 14`. The grammars pinned alongside them ship ABI 15:

| package | pin | resolves to | ABI |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree-sitter-javascript` | `>=0.23,<0.26` | 0.25.0 | 15 |
| `tree-sitter-powershell` | `>=0.26,<0.28` | 0.26.4 | 15 |
| `tree-sitter-scala` | `>=0.23,<0.27` | 0.26.0 | 15 |

So the constraint set admits a resolution where the runtime cannot load the grammars. Every parse then fails with `Incompatible Language version 15`. I reproduced this locally: 61 test failures from that single error, 390 in total once knock-on effects are counted.

A resolver is free to land there. Demonstrated with `uv pip compile`:

```
# with the current floor
tree-sitter==0.23.2            <- ABI 14
tree-sitter-javascript==0.25.0 <- ABI 15   => broken pair

# with >=0.25
tree-sitter==0.25.2            <- ABI 15
tree-sitter-javascript==0.25.0 <- ABI 15   => consistent
```

The grammar versions are identical in both rows. Only the runtime is constrained differently.

## The fix

Floor the runtime at `>=0.25`, the oldest release supporting ABI 15.

## This does not change the locked resolution

`uv.lock` already resolved `tree-sitter` to `0.25.2`. Re-locking after this change edits exactly one line — the recorded `specifier` string — and leaves all 201 resolved versions byte-identical:

```
-    { name = "tree-sitter", specifier = ">=0.23.0,<0.26" },
+    { name = "tree-sitter", specifier = ">=0.25,<0.26" },
```

The floor had simply lagged the lock.

## Scope and impact

Worth being precise about what this does and does not fix:

- **CI was never red.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `uv sync --all-extras --frozen`, which uses the lock and already got 0.25.2.
- **This only affects resolution from `pyproject.toml`** — `uv tool install`, `pip install graphifyy`, and long-lived environments where grammars get upgraded without the runtime.
- On a correctly resolved tree the suite goes from **390 failed / 3841 passed** to **8 failed / 4480 passed**.

The 8 residual failures are environmental, not code defects:

- 7 × `tests/test_security.py` — the sandbox resolver returns `198.18.0.8` for `example.com` (RFC 2544 benchmark range, classified `is_private=True`), so the SSRF guard in `graphify/security.py` correctly blocks it. The guard is behaving as designed; the tests assume real DNS.
- 1 × `tests/test_extract.py::test_collect_files_skips_hidden` — the checkout path itself contains a dot-directory component, and the assertion walks absolute path parts. Passes when run from a non-hidden checkout.

## Testing

- `uv lock --check` clean
- `uv sync --all-extras` resolves `tree-sitter==0.25.2`, `LANGUAGE_VERSION = 15`, ABI-15 JavaScript grammar loads
- Full suite: 4480 passed, 8 failed (environmental, listed above)

Two files: `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`.

title: fix(extract): keep syntax warnings from aborting cross-drive scans
body:
A recoverable syntax error can abort extraction when the included source file and scan root are on different Windows drives. The parser has already produced nodes, but the partial-extraction warning's `relpath` call raises `ValueError` before `extract()` returns its graph.

Catch that display-path error and use the source path with forward slashes. Normal same-drive warning paths stay relative. Graph identities, node/edge data and cache keys do not change.

- After the fix, the cross-drive path returns the same nodes and edges as the normal-path control. The warning preserves the first error line and uses a readable source path. The control checks that same-drive warnings stay relative and that the symbol-less warning does not fire for this parse-error fixture.
- Windows drive semantics are simulated with real `ntpath.relpath`. This is not a native Windows run.

title: [Bug]: graphify update spends ~10 s recomputing the same source-path identities (~150k calls for <1k files)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Every `graphify update` reconciles the existing graph in `_reconcile_existing_graph` (watch.py). That pass asks `_StoredSourcePaths.identity()` for each node, edge and hyperedge's `source_file`, several times per item (`is_evicted` against several identity sets, `in_watch_root`, `rebase_preserved`). Each call rebuilds `Path` objects and runs an `os.path.abspath`.

A graph has far fewer distinct source files than items, and the answer depends only on the stored path plus roots that are fixed once `_StoredSourcePaths.__init__` returns. So almost all of that work is the same computation repeated.

On graphify's own repo (975 files, ~18.7k nodes, ~38k edges), one no-change `update` makes 150,594 `identity()` calls and 152,470 `absolute_identity()` calls for fewer than 1k distinct `source_file` values. The reconcile step alone takes ~10 s of every update, including the post-commit hook rebuild.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
git clone https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify && cd graphify
PYTHONHASHSEED=0 graphify update . --force
# profile a second, no-change run (PYTHONHASHSEED set so graphify does not re-exec itself):
PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python -c "import cProfile, sys; from graphify.__main__ import main; sys.argv = ['graphify', 'update', '.']; cProfile.run('main()', 'u.prof')"
python -c "import pstats; pstats.Stats('u.prof').sort_stats('cumulative').print_stats('watch.py', 8)"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
No-change `graphify update .` on graphify's own repo, 0.9.77:

_reconcile_existing_graph   ~10 s (22.6 s cumulative under cProfile)
identity()                  150,594 calls
absolute_identity()         152,470 calls
is_evicted()                114,060 calls
distinct source_file values < 1,000

Timed without the profiler, wrapping only _reconcile_existing_graph: 10.29 s and 10.03 s on two runs.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.77 (5c7b847)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

AST-only `update`, no provider environment variables set, PYTHONHASHSEED=0. A clean checkout of `v8` at `5c7b847` reproduces it.

### Additional context

The graph output is not affected, only time. I have a fix ready (cache the answer per source file for the lifetime of the `_StoredSourcePaths` instance; graph.json byte-identical with and without it) and will open a PR right after this.

title: perf(watch): compute each stored source path's identity once per update
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4150.

`_reconcile_existing_graph` asks `_StoredSourcePaths.identity()` for every node, edge and hyperedge's `source_file`, several times per item. On graphify's own repo that is ~150k calls for fewer than 1k distinct files, each rebuilding `Path` objects and running an `os.path.abspath`.

`identity()` and `in_watch_root()` now remember their answer per `source_file` for the lifetime of the instance (one reconcile pass). The answer depends only on the stored path and on `project_root`, `watch_root`, `existing_source_root` and `legacy_watch_relative`. All four are fixed by the end of `__init__` and never reassigned, and `__init__` itself never calls `identity()`, so nothing is cached against half-initialised roots. Non-string values skip the cache. The uncached computation is unchanged, kept as `_identity_uncached`.

title: [Bug]: PowerShell member calls bind to another class with the same method name
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

When two PowerShell classes define the same method name, `$this.Pick()` in `Alpha.Run` produces a definite call edge to `Beta.Pick`. This makes the graph show a dependency on the wrong class.

The expected call is `Alpha.Run -> Alpha.Pick`. Member calls should retain the receiver's class identity; a receiver that cannot be established should remain unresolved rather than selecting another class by method name.

### Steps to reproduce

Save the following as `two_classes.ps1`:

```powershell
class Alpha {
 [int] Pick() { return 1 }
 [int] Run() { return $this.Pick() }
}
class Beta {
 [int] Pick() { return 2 }
 [int] Run() { return $this.Pick() }
}
```

Run the source extractor directly, without an AST cache:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extractors.powershell import extract_powershell

result = extract_powershell(Path("two_classes.ps1"))
for edge in result["edges"]:
    if edge.get("relation") == "calls":
        print(edge["source"], "->", edge["target"])
```

Compare the class-qualified node IDs, since both method nodes have the label `.Pick()`.

### Error output or graph output

Class-normalized call edges from the real source extractor:

```text
Alpha.Run -> Beta.Pick  (EXTRACTED)
Beta.Run -> Beta.Pick   (EXTRACTED)
```

The fixture parses without tree-sitter errors. An explicit `[Alpha]::Make()` likewise selects `Beta.Make` when both classes declare `Make`.

### Graphify version

0.9.77; tested source `5c7b84792f453582676548185aaec3824d51dfe2` on `v8`.

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

Python 3.12.11, tree-sitter 0.25.2 and tree-sitter-powershell 0.26.4, using a source snapshot with local dependencies. PowerShell source is parsed, not executed. The direct extractor probe bypasses the corpus AST cache and needs no model request.

### Additional context

#3992 and #3995 fixed previously dropped member calls; that fix is present. This report concerns the remaining receiver-identity error, not missing PowerShell support. Variable type inference, cross-file dispatch and bare-command/function name collisions are separate scope.

title: fix(extract): clear false file provenance from rescued imports
body:
# fix(extract): keep unresolved rescued imports free of false file provenance

Regex-rescued imports can emit unresolved package names, missing relative files, and browser import URLs as node `source_file` values. Downstream consumers then treat references such as `unknown-package` or `/node_modules/.vite/deps/react.js` as real source files.

Mark only stubs emitted by the unresolved-target branch and clear their file claim after the existing ID canonicalization pass. Keep the specifier label and importing-file edge evidence. Delaying the clearing preserves portable IDs for unresolved relative imports; the existing Astro portability regression remains unchanged.

Validation: 86 focused tests and five language subcases pass, including JS, TS, Svelte, Astro, Vue, resolved local imports, portable IDs and warm AST cache reuse. The new regression fails before the repair. Isolated full-corpus CLI builds on 0.9.49 and 0.9.77 pass cold and retained source-path validation and querying while preserving every node ID and edge. Installed runtimes were not modified. title: [Bug]: changed-files rebuild (hook/watch) evicts placeholder nodes for files that were never scanned
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

An extractor can mint a node for a file that is not in the checkout: the target of an unresolved dynamic import (`import('./queue.js')`), or a project a `.sln` / `.slnx` / `<ProjectReference>` names. The node carries the missing path as its `source_file`, but it is the referring file's output (label `./queue.js`, edges only from the referrer).

On a changed-files rebuild (`_rebuild_code(changed_paths=...)`, used by the post-commit hook and `graphify watch`), the corpus sweep in `_reconcile_existing_graph` reads that missing path as a deleted source and evicts the node. The unchanged referrer's preserved edges to it then dangle and are dropped. A full rebuild of the same tree keeps both, so after every hook or watch rebuild the graph silently differs from a full rebuild, and it flips back on the next `graphify update`.

This goes against CONTRIBUTING ("Cross-file edges: must be preserved during incremental updates") and against the intent of #1795 ("require deletion evidence before evicting a missing source"): a path that was never scanned has no deletion evidence.

On graphify's own repo (975 files, v8 5c7b847), editing one unrelated file and running the changed-files rebuild loses 8 nodes and 15 edges compared with a full rebuild of the same tree: the placeholders for `tests/fixtures/dynamic_import.ts`'s missing `./queue.js`, `./mayaEngine.js`, `./staticHelper`, and the `.csproj` projects `sample.sln`, `sample.slnx` and `sample.csproj` reference.

Related to #3570 (same symptom class); the commenters there found that cause fixed by 32b209a, and this is a different mechanism that still reproduces on 0.9.77.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
cat > repro.py <<'EOF'
import json, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.watch import _rebuild_code

def placeholder(c):
    g = json.loads((c / "graphify-out/graph.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    nodes = [n["id"] for n in g["nodes"] if n.get("source_file", "").endswith("queue.js")]
    edges = [(e["source"], e["relation"]) for e in g["links"] if e["target"] in nodes]
    return nodes, edges

if __name__ == "__main__":
    c = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "corpus"; c.mkdir()
    (c / "app.ts").write_text("export async function load() {\n  return import('./queue.js');\n}\n")
    (c / "other.ts").write_text("export function other() {\n  return 1;\n}\n")
    _rebuild_code(c, no_cluster=True, acquire_lock=False, force=True)
    print("full rebuild:              ", placeholder(c))
    (c / "other.ts").write_text("export function other() {\n  return 2;\n}\n")
    _rebuild_code(c, changed_paths=[Path("other.ts")], no_cluster=True, acquire_lock=False, force=True)
    print("changed-files (other.ts):  ", placeholder(c))
    _rebuild_code(c, no_cluster=True, acquire_lock=False, force=True)
    print("full rebuild, same tree:   ", placeholder(c))
EOF
PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python repro.py
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
full rebuild:               (['queue'], [('app_load', 'imports_from'), ('app', 'dynamic_import')])
changed-files (other.ts):   ([], [])
full rebuild, same tree:    (['queue'], [('app_load', 'imports_from'), ('app', 'dynamic_import')])

On graphify's own repo, after a one-file edit: changed-files rebuild 18,617 nodes / 37,920 edges vs full rebuild of the same tree 18,625 / 37,935.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.77 (5c7b847)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

AST-only, no provider environment variables, PYTHONHASHSEED=0. A clean checkout of `v8` at `5c7b847` reproduces it. Found while comparing changed-files and full rebuilds of graphify's own repo.

### Additional context

Fix ready: use the previous scan (manifest.json, rewritten only after reconcile) as the deletion evidence. A missing path that was in the last scan is evicted as before; one that was never scanned is kept while a referrer that is not re-extracted this run still points at it. No manifest: old behaviour. PR right after this.

title: fix(watch): keep placeholder nodes for never-scanned files on incremental rebuilds
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4160.

A changed-files rebuild (post-commit hook, `graphify watch`) evicted nodes whose `source_file` is a path that was never in the checkout: placeholders the REFERRING file mints for an unresolved dynamic import (`import('./queue.js')`) or for a project a `.sln` / `.slnx` / `<ProjectReference>` names. The corpus sweep read the missing path as a deleted source, so the unchanged referrer's preserved edges to the placeholder dangled and were dropped, while a full rebuild of the same tree keeps both.

`_referenced_unscanned_identities` (watch.py) uses the previous scan as the deletion evidence #1795 asks for. `manifest.json` is only rewritten after reconcile, so during reconcile it is the last scan:
- a missing path listed in it was a real file: evicted, as before;
- a missing path never listed in it cannot have been deleted: its nodes are kept while a referrer that is **not** re-extracted this run still points at them (a re-extracted referrer re-emits them, or not, itself);
- a missing path is only kept if it looks like a referrer's placeholder: none of its nodes has a `source_location` and it is the `source_file` of no edge. An extracted file always has one or the other (its file node, symbols, `contains` edges), so a real deleted file is evicted even if the manifest is stale or lost its entry;
- no readable manifest, or one that lists none of today's files (anchored elsewhere): the old behaviour, unchanged.

The check runs in both sweep branches (a placeholder path without an extension, `./staticHelper`, goes through the non-AST branch). It is computed once, lazily, only when a missing source is met.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** a changed-files rebuild must give the graph a full rebuild of the same tree gives (CONTRIBUTING: cross-file edges must be preserved during incremental updates), and a source with deletion evidence is still evicted.

Parity on graphify's own repo (975 files): three identical copies, each fully built by v8, then the same change; A = full rebuild, B = changed-files rebuild with this PR, C = changed-files rebuild on v8. Compared node-by-node and edge-by-edge with every attribute (community fields excluded, they depend on the whole graph):

| change | v8 changed-files vs full | this PR vs full |
|---|---|---|
| edit `graphify/manifest.py` | 8 nodes, 15 edges missing | identical, all attributes |
| add a new module | 8 nodes, 15 edges missing | identical, all attributes |
| delete `graphify/file_slice.py` (7 importers) | 10 nodes / 19 edges differ | 2 / 4 differ, every one of them also differs on v8 |

What this PR does not change, and is already on v8: after a delete, the deleted file's unchanged importers keep their old edges into it. (One earlier edit run also showed 126 external stub nodes, `posixpath` etc., whose `_origin` differed between full and changed-files rebuilds on v8 and on this PR alike; the final run above did not reproduce it, and this PR does not touch `_origin`.)

Two alternatives were measured and rejected: re-extracting the referrers (a partial batch extracts differently from the full corpus: on the delete case it added 2 nodes a full rebuild does not have), and telling placeholders apart by label/location (a `<ProjectReference>` placeholder is labelled with the file name, like a real empty file).

- Persisted state: placeholder nodes and their edges now survive incremental runs, as they do in full rebuilds. Nothing else changes.

- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

## How was this tested?

`tests/test_incremental_unscanned_placeholders.py`:
- an unresolved `import('./queue.js')` placeholder and its edges survive an incremental rebuild of an unrelated file, and the result equals a full rebuild of the same tree (fails on v8: the placeholder is gone);
- a scanned file that is deleted is still evicted;
- without `manifest.json` the old eviction is kept;
- a manifest that lists none of today's files is no evidence (old eviction);
- a really deleted, extracted file whose manifest entry was lost is still evicted (the stale-manifest case the review bot raised; the last two fail on the first commit, 69ee389, and pass with 7340762).

title: [Bug]: R: a function named only with symbols (`%||%`, `%>%`) gets its file's node ID, and extract_r then loops forever
body:
Version: graphifyy 0.9.77, Windows 11, Python 3.14.5; `graphify/extractors/r.py` is unchanged on master (5c7b84792f).

`extract_r` never returns on an R file that defines an infix operator whose name contains no letter or digit, provided some function in the file calls anything not defined in the file. A file whose only content is the base-R null-coalescing fallback is enough:

```r
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extractors.r import extract_r
extract_r(Path("ops.R"))   # never returns
```

`` `%>%` <- function(lhs, rhs) rhs(lhs) `` followed by any function containing a call hangs the same way. In `graphify update` this shows up as worker processes at 100% CPU and no `graph.json`.

**Cause.** This is the R twin of #4064. `declare_function()` builds the ID with `_make_id(owner, name)`, the symbol-only name normalises to nothing, and the ID comes out equal to `owner`. The file node is added first, so the operator node is dropped as a duplicate, and `scope_parent[file_id] = file_id` is recorded. `resolve_local()` (line 383) then walks up `scope_parent` looking for any callee it cannot find locally (`is.null` above), reaches the file, and maps the file to itself on every step.

The top-level variable branch (line 358) has the same collision without the hang: `` `%||%` <- rlang::`%||%` `` produces no node at all.

**Fix, tested against master's `r.py`.** Omitting the node, which is how 28675a19 fixed Rust's `const _`, would be wrong here: an R operator is a real function that other code calls. In `declare_function()`, give a symbol-only name an ID of its own instead:

```python
nid = _make_id(owner, name)
if nid == owner:  # name made only of symbols, e.g. `%||%`
    nid = _make_id(owner, "op", "".join(f"{ord(c):x}" for c in name))
```

With this change both repros above return in about 30 ms, the operator appears as its own node (`` `%>%`() ``, contained by the file), and none of the 52 files of a real R codebase (19 of which carry the `%||%` fallback) hangs any longer. The same treatment applies at line 358.

A cycle guard in `resolve_local()` (stop when `scope_parent.get(scope) == scope`) also ends the hang. On its own it leaves the operator silently missing from the graph, so it is a belt to the fix above rather than a substitute for it.

title: [Bug]: C# scope_chain metadata differs between CRLF and LF checkouts of the same commit (71% of nodes on Newtonsoft.Json)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

C# namespace scope ids, stored in node metadata as `scope_chain` (and `scope_id` on using directives), are built as `f"s{node.start_byte}"` (`graphify/extractors/engine.py`, the `namespace_declaration` and `file_scoped_namespace_declaration` branches). A CRLF checkout has one more byte per line than an LF checkout of the same file, so the same namespace gets a different id: `s27` vs `s30` in the repro below.

So a Windows developer with `core.autocrlf=true` and a Linux/macOS developer (or CI) produce a different graph.json for the same commit. On Newtonsoft.Json's `Src/Newtonsoft.Json` (242 `.cs` files), 3,096 of 4,352 nodes (71%) differ between a CRLF and an LF copy, all in this metadata. Edges are identical, so resolution itself is fine, but a committed graph.json churns whenever it is rebuilt on a machine with the other line-ending setting.

These two lines are the only places a byte offset reaches persisted graph data.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
cat > repro.py <<'EOF'
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract

src = "// Weapons.\nusing System;\n\nnamespace Game.Combat\n{\n    public class Weapon\n    {\n        public void Hit() {}\n    }\n}\n"
for name, nl in (("lf", "\n"), ("crlf", "\r\n")):
    root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / name; root.mkdir()
    p = root / "Weapon.cs"; p.write_bytes(src.replace("\n", nl).encode())
    r = extract([p], root=root, cache_root=root)
    print(f"{name:5}", sorted({n['label']: (n.get('metadata') or {}).get('scope_chain') for n in r['nodes'] if (n.get('metadata') or {}).get('scope_chain')}.items()))
EOF
python repro.py
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
lf    [('.Hit()', ['s27']), ('Weapon', ['s27'])]
crlf  [('.Hit()', ['s30']), ('Weapon', ['s30'])]

Newtonsoft.Json Src (CRLF copy vs LF copy, `graphify update --force --no-cluster`): 4,352 nodes, 3,096 with different metadata; 11,627 edges, all identical.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.77 (5c7b847)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

AST-only, no provider environment variables, PYTHONHASHSEED=0. A clean checkout of `v8` at `5c7b847` reproduces it. Found by building the same repo once with CRLF and once with LF line endings.

### Additional context

Fix ready: use row:column (`node.start_point`) instead of `start_byte`. It is equally unique and identical for CRLF and LF; the ids are only compared within one file, so resolution is unchanged. PR right after this.

title: fix(csharp): make namespace scope ids independent of line endings
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4164.

C# namespace scope ids (the `scope_chain` node metadata, and `scope_id` on using directives, that a namespace-scoped `using` is matched against) were `f"s{node.start_byte}"`. A CRLF checkout (Windows, `core.autocrlf=true`) has one more byte per line than an LF checkout of the same commit, so the two wrote different metadata into graph.json.

`_csharp_scope_id(node)` now returns `s{row}:{column}` from `node.start_point`, used by both namespace branches. A line ending only adds a byte at the end of a line, so row and column are the same for CRLF and LF, and a position is just as unique as a byte offset. The ids are only compared within the same file (`CsharpNameResolver._using_in_scope`), so resolution does not change.

These two sites were the only byte offsets that reached persisted graph data (`grep start_byte}` over `graphify/`).

title: 0.9.77: update fails with "File name too long" on export default base64 string + tsconfig baseUrl
body:
After upgrading from 0.8.11 to 0.9.77, `graphify update .` fails on our repo with:

```
[graphify watch] Rebuild failed: [Errno 63] File name too long: '/Users/.../data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo...
```

We have a few JS files that just export a base64 logo (`export default 'data:image/png;base64,...'`), and the project's tsconfig has `"baseUrl": "."`. Looks like the exported string gets treated as an import path, then resolved against baseUrl, and the `is_file()` check blows up because the path is longer than PATH_MAX. The whole rebuild stops instead of just skipping the file.

Repro:

```bash
mkdir -p repro/src && cd repro
echo '{ "compilerOptions": { "baseUrl": "." } }' > tsconfig.json
printf "export default 'data:image/png;base64,%s'\n" "$(printf 'A%.0s' $(seq 1 1100))" > src/logo.js
graphify update .
```

Without the tsconfig (or with a short string) it works, but there's still a weird import edge to `ref_data_image` in the graph.

Stack:

```
extract.py:864 _import_js
extractors/resolution.py:829 _resolve_js_import_target
extractors/resolution.py:788 _resolve_js_module_path
extractors/resolution.py:341 _resolve_tsconfig_alias
extractors/resolution.py:40 _resolve_js_import_path
  candidate.is_file()
OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long
```

I guess `_import_js` shouldn't pick up the string for `export default ...` (only for `export ... from '...'`), and catching OSError around `is_file()` would probably be a good idea anyway (Python 3.10 doesn't ignore ENAMETOOLONG there).

macOS, Python 3.10.20, graphifyy 0.9.77 via uv tool. Going back to 0.8.11 for now.

title: fix(csharp): resolve calls through casts and interface-typed properties
body:
Part of #3797. Two of the dropped C# call shapes from the issue:

- `((IStore)_obj).Save()` / `(_obj as IStore).Save()` got no `calls` edge. The receiver capture didn't handle a parenthesized cast, so the call never reached the member resolver. The cast's type is now used as the receiver, so it resolves like `IStore.Save()`.
- `IStore Store => ...; Store.Save()` resolved to the concrete `Store.Save()`, because a capitalised receiver was looked up as a type name first. A field/property/local of that name shadows the type in C#, so the recorded `receiver_type` is now tried first, with the type-name lookup as fallback.

The `?.` case was already fixed by #3976.

Left out the partial-class case: it only misses when another class has a method with the same name, and fixing it (~8 lines) changes how every unqualified C# call gets resolved, so it felt riskier. Happy to send it as a separate PR if you want it.

title: feat(install): add moca platform (skill to ~/.config/moca/skills)
body:
## What

Adds a `moca` platform to `graphify install --platform moca` / `graphify moca install|uninstall`.

[moca](https://github.com/adeotek/moca) (MIT) — Mo Coding Agent — is a terminal coding agent shipped as one static Go binary that loads Agent-Skills-standard `SKILL.md` files unchanged (verified against graphify's own skill in its ecosystem-compatibility corpus). It reads:

- user scope: `~/.config/moca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/moca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`)
- project scope: `<project>/.moca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (loaded for a trusted workdir)

It has its own instructions file (`~/.config/moca/AGENTS.md`, plus a trusted workdir's `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`) which graphify does not write into, and no plugin/hook surface — a skill-only registration like `pi` / `agents`.

## Why

moca ships a **create-only** seeded copy of this skill (0.9.93: `SKILL.md` + `references/`) at `~/.config/moca/skills/graphify/` and never refreshes it. That copy carries no `.graphify_version`, so graphify cannot even warn that it is stale. This platform entry writes the current skill to the directory moca actually reads, plus the version stamp graphify's own stale-skill check and auto-refresh key on.

moca's docs already name it as the refresh route: [docs/specs/external-tools.md](https://github.com/adeotek/moca/blob/main/docs/specs/external-tools.md).

## How

- `_PLATFORM_CONFIG["moca"]` reuses claude's split bundle (`skill.md`, byte-identical to pi's) plus the `references/` sidecar.
- `_platform_skill_destination`: user scope honors `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (moca resolves its config dir that way, falling back to `~/.config`); project scope is `.moca/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`.
- `_project_install` / `_project_uninstall`: added to the skill-only tuple.
- CLI dispatch (`graphify moca install|uninstall`), both help-text lists, and the README platform table.
- `tests/test_moca.py`: platform registration, both scope destinations (incl. the XDG override), installed layout (SKILL.md + references), uninstall, CLI dispatch, help text.

## Verification

Rebased onto current `v8` (the branch was 407 commits behind; the only conflict was the hand-maintained `--help` platform list that #4655 replaced with a derived expression — that line is dropped and `moca` is picked up from `_PLATFORM_CONFIG`).

`tests/test_moca.py` (15 tests) plus the install / references / round-trip / help / wheel suites pass; `ruff check` clean.

## Notes

- Part B of the skill (subagent-based semantic extraction) can't run in moca v1 — it has no subagent tool — so the neutral claude/pi bundle is reused rather than adding a new variant. Happy to follow maintainer preference if a moca-specific variant is wanted.
- Drafted with an AI coding assistant; tested locally before submission.

title: fix(detect): drop a previous checkout's absolute manifest keys
body:
## What does this PR do?

A re-clone must not keep absolute manifest keys that point at the previous checkout.

`save_manifest` drops a row when `Path(f).exists()` is false, so a move is already clean. A re-clone copies `graphify-out/` while the old checkout is still on disk, so that check keeps the old absolute keys. The scan prune then skips them because `_in_root` is false, and `_to_relative_for_storage` writes them absolute again. They never share a stored key with the new relative rows, so both halves stay. The drop runs only when `scan_corpus` is set. A subset save omits it and keeps every live out-of-root row (#917).

`_previous_checkout_absolute_keys` drops a group only when `_to_relative_for_storage` would keep the keys absolute, at least two of them share one directory prefix, and each path under that prefix is a relative key this save writes. The longest suffix wins, so `src/c.py` beats `c.py`. `save_manifest` calls it only when `scan_corpus` is set, after the exists check and before the #1908 scan prune. A row that relativizes into the storage root is not a candidate, so a sibling directory from #3785 stays.

Related to #3581. This does not use a closing keyword. Part 2 of that issue, `graph.json` after `--force`, is not in this diff. #3583 is a different path spelling and is not touched.

title: [Bug]: Markdown links to a file name with a space ([x](My%20Note.md), [x](<My Note.md>)) produce no references edge
body:
### What happened?

A markdown link to a document whose file name contains a space is dropped. CommonMark allows two ways to write such a destination, and neither one resolves:

- percent-encoded: `[x](My%20Note.md)`, `[r]: Ref%20Two.md`
- angle brackets: `[x](<My Note.md>)`, `[x](<My Note.md> "title")`, `[r]: <Ref One.md>`

Expected: the same `references` edge that `[[My Note]]` already gets. Editors such as Obsidian write the percent-encoded form when wikilinks are turned off and links use relative paths.

Cause, in `graphify/extractors/markdown.py`:

- `_MD_INLINE_LINK_RE` captures `<?([^)\s>]+)>?` and `_MD_REF_DEF_RE` captures `<?([^\s>]+)>?`. Inside angle brackets the capture stops at the first space, so `<My Note.md>` becomes `My`, which then resolves to a nonexistent `My.md`.
- `_resolve_markdown_link` never decodes the destination, so `My%20Note.md` is looked up literally.

In both cases the edge keeps an id derived from a path that does not exist and drops at build.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p vault/notes/sub && cd vault
printf '# Hub\n\nInline: [a](My%%20Note.md), [b](<sub/Deep Note.md>), [c](<Titled Note.md> "title")\nReference: [d][r1], [e][r2]\nWikilink: [[My Note]]\n\n[r1]: <Ref One.md>\n[r2]: Ref%%20Two.md\n' > notes/hub.md
echo '# My Note' > "notes/My Note.md"
echo '# Deep' > "notes/sub/Deep Note.md"
echo '# Titled' > "notes/Titled Note.md"
echo '# Ref one' > "notes/Ref One.md"
echo '# Ref two' > "notes/Ref Two.md"
graphify update .
# then list the references edges of notes/hub.md in graphify-out/graph.json
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
notes/hub.md -> notes/My Note.md
1 references edges; expected 5
```

The one edge that survives comes from the wikilink `[[My Note]]`. The five markdown links are all lost.

### Graphify version

0.9.79 (v8 @ f765dcb)

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone), `uv sync --all-extras`

### Additional Environment Details

AST-only path (`graphify update`), no API key involved.

### Additional context

I have a small fix and can open a PR:

- capture the whole `<...>` destination in both regexes;
- percent-decode inline and reference destinations (wikilinks stay verbatim).

A file whose name literally contains the escape (`100%25.md` on disk) keeps precedence, so no encoded link loses a file it reaches today.

title: fix(markdown): resolve links to file names that contain a space (#4177)
body:
## What does this PR do?

<!-- Describe the problem and the change. Link the relevant issue when one exists. -->

Fixes #4177.

Markdown links to a file name with a space produced no `references` edge. CommonMark writes such a destination in one of two ways, and both were lost:

- `[x](<My Note.md>)`: the inline regex captured `<?([^)\s>]+)>?` and the reference-definition regex `<?([^\s>]+)>?`, so the capture stopped at the space and `My` resolved to a nonexistent `My.md`;
- `[x](My%20Note.md)`: the destination was never decoded.

The fix touches `graphify/extractors/markdown.py` only:

- Both regexes try a whole `<...>` destination first (spaces allowed; no line break, `<` or `>`). After the `>`, the inline regex accepts only a CommonMark title (`"…"`, `'…'`, or `(…)` without a nested parenthesis), and the reference-definition regex requires a title opener or the end of the line. An unclosed `<` therefore falls back to the bare form and does not swallow the links after it on the line.
- Inline and reference destinations are percent-decoded after the anchor and query are stripped. A file whose name literally contains the escape keeps precedence, with or without the `.md` completion (`[x](100%25)` beside `100%25.md`). The external-link guard runs again on the decoded form, so `%2F%2Fhost/...` stays external. Wikilinks stay verbatim, as Obsidian writes them.

Which links change target: bracketed destinations that v8 cut short, at a space or a `)`. `<a b.md>` used to reach `a.md` when that file existed; it now reaches `a b.md`, the name CommonMark reads between the brackets.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

<!-- What invariant does this code protect? How do you prove your change doesn't break it? What generated or persisted state could your change invalidate? -->

Invariant:
- A destination that is neither bracketed nor percent-encoded resolves exactly as on v8.
- A percent-encoded bare destination never loses a literal file it reached on v8.
- A spaced destination, bracketed or encoded, now reaches its existing document.
- Wikilinks are unchanged.

Tests:
- `test_markdown_link_destination_with_spaces`: inline encoded, inline bracketed with a title, reference bracketed and reference encoded, with no ghost targets. It fails on v8.
- `test_markdown_link_forms_keep_their_existing_targets`: a literal `100%25.md` reached by `[x](100%25.md)` and by `[y](100%25)`; `[[My%20Note]]` not decoded into `My Note.md`; `[a](<b.md) -> [c](d.md)` and `[e](<f.md) -> (see [g](h.md))` still reaching all four files. It checks the exact set of real targets and passes on v8, as it should.
- `test_markdown_decoded_link_stays_external`: `%2F%2Fhost%2Fshare%2Fx.md` and an encoded `https://` URL resolve to nothing. On v8 they stayed undecoded, as dangling relative paths.

Six mutations each turn one of these tests red:
- no literal precedence;
- precedence without the `.md` completion;
- decoding wikilinks;
- no second external guard;
- a permissive title after `>`;
- a `(…)` title that allows a nested `(`.

Persisted state: the AST cache is namespaced by package version (`graphify/cache.py`), so a release re-extracts markdown.

New filesystem access: one `is_file()` per destination that contains `%` and changes when decoded.

Known limitations:
- Inline links keep their relative semantics. Obsidian's "shortest path" and "absolute path in vault" link formats resolve only when they happen to be relative to the linking file, as on v8.
- Backslash escapes are not unescaped, as on v8. This applies in a destination (`[x](a\)b.md)`, `<a\>b.md>`). It also applies in a title: a spaced bracketed destination whose title holds an escaped quote or parenthesis is still cut at the space.

title: fix(python): keep TYPE_CHECKING-only imports out of import cycles (#3159)
body:
## What does this PR do?

<!-- Describe the problem and the change. Link the relevant issue when one exists. -->

Fixes #3159. An import under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` never runs, yet it became an `imports_from` edge, so Import Cycles listed impossible cycles. It is now stamped `type_only`, the marker `find_import_cycles` already skips for TypeScript `import type` (#3123); the edge stays in the graph. This follows the approach proposed in the 29 Aug comment on the issue. `else:` and `if not TYPE_CHECKING:` stay runtime.

Stamping alone would hide real cycles: when `build_from_json` or `dedupe_edges` collapses the edges of one file pair, the marker of one edge can land on an import that runs (`from . import b` plus a guarded `from .b import B`). A collapsed edge is now `type_only` only if every import folded into it is. This also fixes the same hidden cycle for TypeScript `import type` next to a value import. In the default undirected graph, the reverse-direction duplicate that #1061 drops is the other file's import, so it leaves the surviving edge's marker alone and #3123's `import type` cycles stay gone.

### What happened?

#2873 added typed stub nodes (`external: true`, `source_file: ""`) for imports of stdlib / third-party modules. The stubs are minted without an `_origin` stamp. On the next `update`, the #2334 tier backfill stamps every unstamped loaded item by shape, and a stub has no `L<line>` location, so it is stamped `semantic`. Expected: the external stubs after any update are exactly the ones a fresh build of the same tree has.

```shell
mkdir demo && cd demo
printf 'import bisect\nimport json\n\n\ndef find(xs, x):\n    return bisect.bisect_left(xs, x)\n' > a.py
graphify update . --no-cluster && graphify update . --no-cluster    # second run stamps the stubs

graphify update . --no-cluster      # the default clustered update ends the same way
```

title: [Bug]: --no-cluster graph.json keeps edges to undeclared nodes; markdown ones embed the checkout path
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

#2873 made every edge endpoint in graph.json a declared node. The clustered path gets that from `build_from_json`, which mints a stub for an external import and drops every other edge it cannot attach. The raw `--no-cluster` writers skip `build_from_json`:

- `graphify update --no-cluster` only mints the import stubs, so any other dangling edge is written as is. The common case is a markdown link to a document that does not exist: `extract_markdown` keeps it dangling on purpose ("must stay dangling") and builds the target id from the absolute resolved path, so graph.json carries the checkout folder and the OS username.
- `graphify extract --no-cluster` does neither, so `import os` is written as an edge to an undeclared `os` node.

Every loader (networkx `node_link_graph`) turns each missing endpoint into an attribute-less phantom node, and the same repo gives different edge ids in every clone.

Expected: a `--no-cluster` graph.json follows the same endpoint rules as the clustered one (no undeclared endpoint, no checkout path).

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir demo && cd demo
printf 'import os\n\n\ndef home():\n    return os.getcwd()\n' > app.py
printf '# Demo\n\nSee [the guide](docs/guide.md) and [[Roadmap]].\n' > README.md
graphify update . --no-cluster
# every link whose target is not in nodes[]:
python -c "import json; g=json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); ids={n['id'] for n in g['nodes']}; print([(e['relation'], e['target']) for e in g['links'] if e['target'] not in ids])"

# same folder, extract path:
rm -rf graphify-out && graphify extract . --code-only --no-cluster
```

```text
update                           dangling=0
```

### Pre-flight checks

### What happened?

An AST cache entry is keyed by its own file's content. When `pkg/slice.py` is renamed or deleted, the unchanged importer `pkg/user.py` is a cache hit, and the hit replays its import edges as they were resolved while `slice.py` existed: target id minted from the absolute path, `target_file` stamped to the old file.

extract()'s id remap only maps stamped targets that exist (a missing one is kept "dangling, exactly as before", which is right for a fresh speculative stamp), so the edge keeps the absolute-path id and the #2873 stub node is minted with it. graph.json then holds the checkout folder and the OS username, and a warm update differs from a cold build of the same tree (cold gives `pkg_slice`).

Expected: a warm update gives the same graph as a cold build after an imported module is renamed or deleted, with no checkout path in any id.

```shell
printf 'def cut(p):\n    return p\n' > pkg/slice.py
printf 'from pkg.slice import cut\n\n\ndef go(p):\n    return cut(p)\n' > pkg/user.py
graphify update . --no-cluster
```

title: fix(cache): treat an AST hit whose import target is gone as a miss
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4184.

`save_cached` (ast kind) now records the `target_file` stamps that name an existing file when the entry is written, under `_cached_target_files` (made portable with the same anchoring as the entry's ids, #2257). `load_cached` pops that list and returns a miss if any recorded file is gone, so the importer is extracted again and resolves exactly as on a cold build.

- Stamps that did not exist at write time (speculative targets) are not recorded, so they never cause a miss.
- Entries without the list load as before.
- The list never reaches extraction results (popped on load).

Not done: remapping a missing target to its root-relative id inside extract(). File ids carry no extension, so that could bind a Python import to a same-stem file in another language — the false edge the existing "keep its raw id dangling" comment guards against.

title: [Bug]: Windows console script (graphify.exe) always runs AST extraction on one core
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

#3754 (for #3669) skips the process pool when spawn workers cannot re-import `__main__`, by checking `os.path.isfile(__main__.__file__)`. The pip/uv console script on Windows is a launcher exe with a zipped `__main__.py`, so `__main__.__file__` is `...\Scripts\graphify.exe\__main__.py`, which is not a file on disk. Every `graphify update` / `graphify extract` from the normal Windows command therefore prints

> note: running AST extraction sequentially — a parallel pool needs an importable __main__ to relaunch workers, which a stdin (`… | python -`), `python -c`, or REPL invocation does not have.

and extracts on one core, although the caller is none of those.

The pool would work: `__main__.__spec__.name` is `"__main__"`, so `multiprocessing.spawn.get_preparation_data` passes the module NAME to the worker (`init_main_from_name`), and `_fixup_main_from_name("__main__")` returns without touching `__main__` (its comment: "__main__.py files for packages, directories, zip archives, etc ... we don't even try").

Expected: the console script gets the same pool as `python -m graphify`.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# Windows, graphify installed with uv tool / pip (console script graphify.exe)
graphify update <repo> --no-cluster --force          # prints the "running AST extraction sequentially" note
python -m graphify update <repo> --no-cluster --force   # same code, real __main__ file: "[12 workers]"

# what _spawn_cannot_reimport_main sees under graphify.exe:
#   __main__.__file__  = '...\Scripts\graphify.exe\__main__.py'   (os.path.isfile -> False)
#   __main__.__spec__.name = '__main__'
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Cold build of graphify's own repo with graphify.exe, alternated (18,832 nodes / 39,422 edges every run):

v8 f765dcb (sequential):           44.3 s   39.6 s   38.9 s
with the pool allowed (12 workers): 28.1 s   26.5 s   26.3 s

graph.json identical (all attributes).
```

0.9.79 (f765dcb)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider keys set. 12-thread laptop. Reproduces on a clean checkout with the console script installed into a venv.

### Additional context

Found while comparing a 1-worker build against a parallel one: the plain graphify.exe run printed the stdin note. #3620 (open) adds a different pre-pool guard and does not change this check. A fix is ready; PR right after this.

title: fix(extract): let the Windows console script use the extraction pool
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4186.

`_spawn_cannot_reimport_main` now returns False when `__main__` has a module spec, mirroring `multiprocessing.spawn.get_preparation_data`: such a `__main__` is re-imported by NAME, never by path, and a spec named `__main__` is skipped in the worker altogether. That covers the pip/uv console script on Windows (`graphify.exe`, whose `__file__` is a zip member inside the exe) and `python -m`.

stdin, `-c` and the REPL have no spec, so #3669's behaviour is unchanged for them. The two existing stdin/REPL tests now also set `__spec__ = None`, as a real stdin caller has; before, they inherited the test runner's own `__main__` spec.

Worker count is unchanged: still `os.cpu_count()` (or `GRAPHIFY_MAX_WORKERS`), capped by the number of uncached files, and a 1-worker pool still falls back to sequential (#2173), so 1-core machines and the Windows post-commit hook (`GRAPHIFY_MAX_WORKERS=1`) behave as before.

title: [Bug]: --no-cluster graph.json carries extracted_sources (absolute input paths) and failed_sources
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`extract()` returns `extracted_sources` (#3411) and `failed_sources` (#2543) next to nodes/edges. They steer the current run and hold the absolute paths of its inputs. The raw `--no-cluster` writers dump the extraction as graph.json, so:

- every `graphify extract --no-cluster` writes `extracted_sources` (one absolute path per input file, i.e. the checkout folder and the OS username) into graph.json;
- the first `graphify update --no-cluster` (no graph.json yet) writes both keys. A rebuild of the same tree drops them again and adds a `hyperedges` key the first build lacked, so the first build and a rebuild write different top-level keys.

The clustered path is not affected (it writes through `build_from_json`). Nothing reads these keys back from graph.json; `build_merge` / `merge_raw_extraction` use them from the in-memory extraction.

Expected: a --no-cluster graph.json holds no absolute input paths, and its top-level keys do not depend on whether it is the first build.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir demo && cd demo
printf 'import os\n\n\ndef home():\n    return os.getcwd()\n' > app.py
graphify extract . --code-only --no-cluster
python -c "import json; g=json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); print(sorted(k for k in g if k not in ('nodes','links','edges')), g.get('extracted_sources'))"

rm -rf graphify-out
graphify update . --no-cluster            # first build: extracted_sources + failed_sources present
graphify update . --no-cluster --force    # rebuild: both gone, hyperedges added
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
extract --no-cluster keys: ['extracted_sources', 'hyperedges', 'input_tokens', 'output_tokens']
extracted_sources = ['C:\\Users\\<user>\\...\\demo\\app.py']

update --no-cluster, first build: ['directed', 'extracted_sources', 'failed_sources', 'input_tokens', 'output_tokens']
update --no-cluster, rebuild:     ['directed', 'hyperedges', 'input_tokens', 'output_tokens']

On graphify's own tests/fixtures corpus the first build's extracted_sources lists 116 absolute paths.
```

0.9.79 (f765dcb)

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

built from source (git clone)

No provider keys set. Reproduces on a clean checkout and in a fresh empty folder (steps above).

title: [Bug]: MCP query_graph and shortest_path rebuild a copy of the whole graph on every call
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

On a warm MCP server, most of a `query_graph` call and nearly all of a `shortest_path` call is spent rebuilding a structure that is the same for every call on the same graph:

- `_query_graph_text` calls `_traversal_view(G)`, which copies every edge of the loaded DiGraph into a new undirected graph on every query (~38k `add_edge` per query on graphify's own graph).
- `_shortest_path_text` builds a sorted `nx.DiGraph` (or `nx.Graph` with `undirected=true`) from every edge on every call (sorted for the deterministic route, #2074). The path search itself takes under 1 ms.

The `_traversal_view` docstring chose this on purpose ("A fresh copy per query rather than a cached one ... only the edge dicts are duplicated"), i.e. for memory/simplicity, not correctness. The trigram index already uses the safe alternative: build once and cache on `G.graph`, which a hot reload invalidates by swapping in a new graph object.

Expected: build each structure once per loaded graph; answers unchanged.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# graphify's own repo, built graph (18,865 nodes / 38,458 edges)
python - <<'EOF'
import time, statistics, graphify.serve as S
G = S._load_graph("graphify-out/graph.json"); S._get_trigram_index(G)   # what the server does at load
t=[]
for _ in range(10):
    s=time.perf_counter(); S._shortest_path_text(G, {"source": "load_cached", "target": "save_cached"}); t.append(time.perf_counter()-s)
print("shortest_path median ms", statistics.median(t)*1000)
EOF
# profile: almost all time is building the sorted DiGraph; nx.shortest_path on it is < 1 ms.
# same for query_graph: ~half the call is _traversal_view copying every edge.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
shortest_path: ~93 ms of a ~108 ms call is building the sorted DiGraph; nx.shortest_path on it: 0.24 ms
query_graph: _traversal_view = ~half of a warm call (406,495 add_edge calls over 10 queries)

Warm-server medians on graphify's own graph (v8 f765dcb): query_graph 270-430 ms, shortest_path 100-235 ms (laptop, varies with thermal state).
```

0.9.79 (f765dcb)

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

built from source (git clone)

No provider keys set. Measured in-process on the MCP code path (`_load_graph` + `_query_graph_text` / `_shortest_path_text`).

title: perf(serve): build the MCP traversal view and shortest-path graphs once per graph
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4191.

- `_traversal_view(G)` builds the undirected view once per graph object and caches it on `G.graph["_traversal_view"]`.
- New `_path_search_graph(G, undirected)` holds the sorted DiGraph / Graph `_shortest_path_text` used to rebuild per call, cached per direction on `G.graph["_path_search_graphs"]`. Its body is the old inline code, comments included, so #2074's deterministic route and #3878's reverse `contains` hops are unchanged.

Same pattern as the trigram index: a hot reload swaps in a new `G`, so a cached structure never outlives its graph.

**About the design note this changes.** `_traversal_view`'s docstring said: "A fresh copy per query rather than a cached one: `_filter_graph_by_context` already copies per query when a filter applies, and the copy shares node data dicts with `G`, so only the edge dicts are duplicated." That was a memory/simplicity trade-off. The numbers below show the per-call copy is most of a warm query and the cache costs ~27 MB, so this PR flips it and updates the docstring. Happy to drop either half if you prefer to keep the old trade-off.

**Why sharing is safe.** Nothing writes to the cached structures (checked every function on the path with an AST scan for add/remove/update/setdefault/pop/item assignment):
- `_filter_graph_by_context` builds a new graph when a filter applies and never touches its input;
- `_bfs`, `_dfs`, `_complete_induced_edges`, `_subgraph_to_text` only read (their writes go to local sets/dicts), and none reads `.graph`;
- only `nx.shortest_path` reads the path graphs.
Each structure has a single call site.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [x] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

(performance; no behaviour change)

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** every `query_graph` / `shortest_path` answer is byte-identical to a freshly built structure, in any order of calls, and a reloaded graph never sees the previous graph's structures.

graphify's own graph (18,865 nodes / 38,458 edges). The same calls run interleaved in one process with the cache cleared (= v8 behaviour) vs kept, so thermal drift hits both sides; outputs asserted equal on every call (240 calls):

| MCP call | v8 (median) | this PR (median) | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_graph`, no filter (n=120) | 430 ms | 266 ms | 1.6x |
| `query_graph`, "what calls X" heuristic filter (n=30) | 428 ms | 274 ms | 1.6x |
| `shortest_path`, directed (n=45) | 235 ms | 0.8 ms | ~300x |
| `shortest_path`, `undirected=true` (n=45) | 137 ms | 0.8 ms | ~170x |

Separate processes (v8 vs PR, alternated, 2 runs each; 80 queries + 30 paths; all outputs identical across the 4 processes):

| | v8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| warm `query_graph` median | 367 / 269 ms | 164 / 166 ms |
| warm `shortest_path` median | 117 / 103 ms | 0.2 / 0.2 ms |
| first `query_graph` call (pays the one build) | 220 / 142 ms | 168 / 143 ms |
| RSS after load | 123 MB | 123 MB |
| RSS after the 110 calls | 204 MB | 231 MB (+27 MB: view +8, both path graphs +24) |

(An earlier run on a hotter machine gave the same ratios: 524 -> 316 ms, 211 -> 0.8 ms.)

title: [Bug]: extract() resolves the same paths ~24k times and the call tie-break re-parses candidate paths on every site
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Profiling a no-change `graphify update` on graphify's own repo shows two pieces of repeated path work that do not depend on anything that changes during the run:

1. `extract()`'s id remap calls `Path.resolve()` on the same file paths once per input, once per `target_file`-stamped edge (`_raw_tp.resolve()`, `stem_forms.get(Path(tf).resolve())`) and once per node (`prefix_remap.get(Path(sf).resolve())`): 23,819 calls from `extract()` itself for ~1k distinct files.
2. `paths._path_proximity_winner` (the #1553 god-node tie-break) builds a `PurePosixPath` for every candidate's parent directory, twice (same-directory tier and common-prefix tier), on every ambiguous call site. A common name brings the same candidate files back on every site: 226,809 Path objects per update.

Expected: each distinct path resolved/parsed once; same graph.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
git clone https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify && cd graphify
graphify update . --force                      # first build
python -c "import cProfile,sys; from graphify.__main__ import main; sys.argv=['graphify','update','.','--force']; cProfile.run('main()','u.prof')"
python -c "import pstats; p=pstats.Stats('u.prof'); p.sort_stats('cumulative'); p.print_callers('pathlib.py.*\\(resolve\\)'); p.print_callees('_path_proximity_winner')"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Path.resolve <- extract()            23,819 calls
_path_proximity_winner  1,649 calls -> PurePosixPath.__new__ 226,809 calls

Wall time of the whole update (not profiled), graphify's repo, 18,830 nodes: cold ~28 s, no-change ~21-25 s.
```

0.9.79 (f765dcb)

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

title: perf(extract): resolve and parse each path once in the id remap and call tie-break
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4194.

- `extract()`: the id remap now resolves each distinct path once through a local memo (`_resolved`), instead of once per input, per `target_file`-stamped edge and per node. A hit returns the same `Path` the call would; a path that raises is never stored, so every existing `try/except` behaves as before. The memo lives for one `extract()` call only.
- `paths._path_proximity_winner`: the parent-directory parse of each candidate path is memoized (`_parent_parts`, `functools.lru_cache(maxsize=65536)`). Equal part-tuples are exactly equal `PurePosixPath(...).parent` values, so the same-file, same-directory and longest-common-prefix tiers decide as before.

title: [Bug]: C#: name resolver ignores enclosing namespaces
[Feature]: Python: obj.method() on an annotated parameter or a constructor-bound local produces no calls edge
body:
### Problem or use case

`affected`, `explain` and `shortest_path` miss most Python method callers. `_resolve_python_member_calls` resolves `ClassName.method()` (#1446) and `module.func()` (#1883), and #4176 is adding `self.attr.method()`. A plain local receiver never gets a `calls` edge, even when the function itself names its class:

```python
from ._models import Request
from ._client import Client

def send(request: Request):       # annotated parameter
    request.read()                 # no edge to Request.read

def build():
    client = Client()              # constructor binding
    client.send()                  # no edge to Client.send

def get(url):
    with Client() as client:       # context manager on a constructor
        return client.get(url)     # no edge to Client.get
```

Measured against jedi on v8 @ f765dcb (jedi `goto` on every call inside every function, kept when the target is defined in the repo):

| repo | real calls graphify finds | `obj.method()` calls found |
|---|---|---|
| httpx | 301 / 437 (68.9%) | 0 / 98 |
| click (`src/click`) | 376 / 502 (74.9%) | 2 / 85 |

### Proposed solution

Type the receiver from the function's own code, only when it is certain: a parameter annotation (`X`, `"X"`, `Optional[X]`, `typing.Optional[X]`, `X | None`), `x = X(...)` / `x: X`, or `with X(...) as x`. Any other binding of the name in the function (factory call, loop, unpacking, a second class, lambda parameter, match capture, ...) drops the type. Resolve with the existing class/method index and the same origin gate as the TS receiver arm (#2553): the class name is unique and the class is defined in, imported into, or in a module imported by the caller's file. Otherwise no edge.

### Alternatives considered

- Resolve `obj.method()` by method name alone: rejected, that is the god-node collision the shared pass deliberately skips (#543/#1219).
- Return-type inference (`x = make_client()`): bigger, needs cross-file return types; left out.
- Run jedi/pyright as a resolver: new heavy dependency and not deterministic across environments.

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

- Adds `INFERRED` `calls` edges only (confidence_score 0.85). No node, id or existing edge changes.
- Raw calls gain `receiver_type` (the key Ruby already uses), so the AST cache schema goes 5 -> 6 and old warm caches re-extract.
- graph.json schema, generated skills and MCP output formats unchanged. Incremental updates behave the same (warm == cold).

### Additional context

PR ready right after this issue. 0.9.79 (f765dcb), Windows 11, Python 3.12.12, built from source.

title: feat(python): resolve obj.method() through an annotated parameter or constructor-bound local
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4197.

**Extractor** (`graphify/extractors/engine.py`): for every Python function, `_python_local_class_bindings` builds `{name -> class}` from
- parameter annotations: `X`, `mod.X` (last part), `"X"`, `Optional[X]`, `typing.Optional[X]`, `X | None`;
- `x = X(...)` and `x: X = ...`;
- `with X(...) as x`.

A name gets no type as soon as anything makes it unsure: a second, different class; a rebind from a non-constructor (`x = make()`); `for x in`, `except ... as x`, tuple unpacking (also `with A() as (x, y)`), `+=`, walrus, `global`/`nonlocal`, `import x`, a `match` capture (`case x:`), `*x` / `**x` parameters. Containers (`list[X]`, `Optional[list[X]]`) give no type.
Scopes: a nested `def` is its own caller and is not read, except that a `nonlocal x` inside it drops `x`. Calls inside a lambda or a nested class body are attributed to the enclosing function, so every name a lambda or class body binds is dropped (`lambda c: c.send()` inside `def f(c: Client)` gets no edge).
A member call whose receiver has a type gets `receiver_type` on its raw call (same key Ruby already uses).

**Resolver** (`graphify/extract.py`, `_resolve_python_member_calls`): a new arm before the class arm emits `caller -> Class.method` only when
1. the class name is defined exactly once in the corpus (the class arm's single-definition guard),
2. the class is defined in the caller's file, imported into it by name, or lives in a module it imports (the #2553 origin gate), and
3. the method is the class's own.

Otherwise no edge. Confidence `INFERRED`, `confidence_score` 0.85 (the rubric value the shared call pass uses), because the type comes from an annotation or a constructor, not from the call. A typed receiver never falls through to the module arm.

**Cache** (`graphify/cache.py`): `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 5 -> 6, so a cache written before this re-extracts instead of keeping raw calls without `receiver_type`.

Complements #4176 (`self.attr.method()`): different arm in the same function.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a new `calls` edge is emitted only when the receiver's class is certain from the function's own code and the class is unique and visible from the caller. Every other case emits nothing, as before (fail-closed).
Persisted state it could invalidate: AST cache entries (schema bumped, so they re-extract).

Measured on three real repos, v8 vs this branch, cold `graphify update <repo> --no-cluster --force`:

| repo | real calls found (vs jedi) | `obj.method()` found | new edges | new edges correct | edges lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| httpx | 68.9% -> **77.3%** | 0 -> **37** / 98 | +39 | 39 | 0 |
| click | 74.9% -> **80.3%** | 2 -> **29** / 85 | +102 | 102 | 0 |
| flask | n/a | n/a | +12 | 12 | 0 |

"Correct" = jedi `goto` at the exact call site lands on the same file, class and method. 152 of 153 confirmed that way. The other one, `with Client(...) as client: client.request(...)` in `httpx/_api.py`, jedi cannot follow through `Client.__enter__`'s TypeVar return; checked by hand, it is `Client.request`.
Node counts identical. Every other edge identical (a few ids built from the checkout's absolute path differ only because the two copies sit in different folders).

Build time, cold, median of interleaved runs: httpx 3.58 -> 3.67 s (7 runs), click 4.51 -> 4.57 s (3), flask 4.01 -> 4.02 s (7). Same within noise.

- [x] Added a **regression test**: 10 tests in `tests/test_python_typed_receiver_calls.py`. On v8, 7 fail (every case that should link); the 3 "must not link" guards pass on both.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.

**Limitations (no edge, same as before):**
- Module-qualified annotation through a module import (`from . import models` + `m: models.Request`): that import edge points at the package / module id, not the class's file, so the origin gate cannot prove the class is visible.
- Return-type inference (`x = make_client()`), attribute receivers (`self.x.m()`, #4176), inherited methods.
- `with X(...) as x` assumes `X.__enter__` returns `self`. True for every with-binding edge in the three repos above (all checked).

title: AMBIGUOUS edges distort Suggested Questions + clustering (false-positive bridges)
body:
## Context

Working through a trace of a cross-community bridge surfaced by `GRAPH_REPORT.md` → **Suggested Questions**, I hit a case where `graphify` correctly tagged an edge as `AMBIGUOUS` (confidence 0.35, `conceptually_related_to`, `source_location: null`) but the downstream pipeline still treated it as a signal:

- **Suggested Questions** asked the user to explain the AMBIGUOUS relationship as if it were real.
- **Louvain clustering** merged the two end-doc clusters into one community because the AMBIGUOUS edge contributed to modularity.

End result: a confirmed false positive consumed exploration time, and a 27-node community was shaped around noise.

### Example (anonymized to the pattern, not the specific repo)

Two unrelated planning docs — one about a BE PATCH endpoint for a video-evaluation feature, one about a department-hierarchy schema refactor — have **zero cross-references** in prose but share surface structure (Goal / Architecture / File Map / Phase templates, same tech stack, same `superpowers:...` sub-skill hint). The LLM semantic extractor inferred `conceptually_related_to` at **confidence 0.35** / `source_location: null`.

The AMBIGUOUS flag worked perfectly — the problem is only that *consumers* of the graph (`suggest_questions`, `cluster`) weight it the same as EXTRACTED/INFERRED edges.

## Proposals

### 1. `suggest_questions` should skip or demote AMBIGUOUS edges

Currently (`graphify.analyze.suggest_questions`) a bridge with `confidence == AMBIGUOUS` is phrased identically to a high-confidence one:
> "What is the exact relationship between A and B? _Edge tagged AMBIGUOUS (relation: conceptually_related_to) - confidence is low._"

The disclaimer is good, but the question still spends user attention. Two options:

- **(a)** Skip AMBIGUOUS-only bridges unless the user passes `--include-ambiguous`.
- **(b)** Still emit the question but **suppress it from the top-N** and append it in a separate "Low-confidence hints" section at the bottom of the report, so the user sees it after the real signal.

My preference: **(b)**, keeps the audit trail without burying real bridges.

### 2. Clustering should weight AMBIGUOUS edges below EXTRACTED/INFERRED

Louvain modularity in `graphify.cluster` currently reads `weight` from the raw `confidence_score` (0.35 for AMBIGUOUS in my case). Two cheap wins:

- Multiply AMBIGUOUS weight by a configurable factor (default **0.5**) *before* passing to `nx.community.louvain_communities(..., weight='weight')`.
- Expose it as `cluster(G, ambiguous_scale=0.5)` so power users can bump it to 0.0 (drop entirely) or 1.0 (current behavior).

This keeps the community graph more faithful to EXTRACTED structure without changing the edge data itself. Users exploring via `/graphify path` still see the AMBIGUOUS edge; only the auto-cluster stops being warped by it.

## Backward compatibility

Both changes are additive (new flags, defaults preserve existing behavior if you choose `ambiguous_scale=1.0`). Nothing in the schema or output file format changes.

## Related

- Honesty Rules in `SKILL.md` already say "Never invent an edge. If unsure, use AMBIGUOUS." This proposal just **completes the loop** by making downstream consumers honor the confidence tier.
- `confidence_score` is already written to `graph.json` — this is a pure consumer-side change.

Happy to open a PR for either or both if the maintainers agree with the direction.

title: pre-#1504 scheme detection: suggest  automatically on same-name node collisions
body:
## Context

While tracing a `betweenness=0.047` bridge in a mid-sized TypeScript monorepo (17k+ nodes, 1,400 communities), the top God Node showed up as a cross-community hub between three communities — Controllers (Finance/Admin), Acquisition Survey Domain, and a doc-cluster.

Running `graphify path`/`graphify explain` revealed the bridge was fake: a function `assertClubAccess()` in `permissions.ts` had `.getById()` as a neighbor, but the `.getById()` node was labeled as living in **"Acquisition Survey Domain"** community — in reality the edge was to `team.controller.ts:L25` `.getById()`, which was a **same-name method-ID collision** across controllers. The old (pre-#1504) node-ID scheme glued all `.getById()` into one node, and clustering + labeling fell apart.

After a fresh rebuild (delete `manifest.json` → full re-extract) with path-qualified IDs:
- Node count: 17,580 → 14,011
- Communities: 1,399 → 1,087 (tighter clusters)
- `assertClubAccess()` degree: 5 → 4, now **single community** (Controllers Core)

The bug + collision warning fired correctly:
```
[graphify] note: this graph uses the pre-#1504 node-ID scheme;
rebuild with `graphify extract --force` to get path-qualified IDs
(fixes same-name-file collisions).
```

Problem: this notice only appears on `graphify query`/`path`/`explain` output, not on `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and `graphify extract --force` isn't actually a CLI command (`graphify update --force` is the real path, and even that doesn't trigger a re-extract — just overrides shrink-guard). The user has to delete `manifest.json` manually, which is an unobvious operation.

## Proposals

### 1. Expose a dedicated rebuild subcommand

Something like `graphify rebuild [--path .]` that:
- Backs up `manifest.json` to `.manifest-backup-<ts>.json`
- Deletes `manifest.json` + `.graphify_old.json`
- Triggers the full detect → extract → merge pipeline with `root=` relative paths (same as current `--update`)
- Prints "Semantic cache preserved: X/Y files" at the end

Rationale: semantic re-extraction stayed 100% cache-hit in my case (288/288 docs), so the rebuild cost was only AST (seconds, no tokens). The command *looks* expensive but almost never is.

### 2. Surface the pre-#1504 banner inside `GRAPH_REPORT.md`

Right now, users who read the report but never run `query` miss the warning. Add a top-of-report block:
```markdown
> ⚠️ **Graph uses pre-#1504 node-ID scheme.** Same-name files/methods may collide, inflating betweenness
> and distorting community membership. Run `graphify rebuild` to regenerate with path-qualified IDs.
> (Likely cost: seconds + 0 tokens if your semantic cache is intact.)
```

Check for the collision by looking for duplicate `label` with different `source_file` in `graph.json` nodes — if the duplicate rate > 0.5%, print the banner.

### 3. (Optional) Suggested Questions / Surprising Connections should flag collision-driven bridges

High-betweenness nodes whose degree is dominated by same-label-different-source neighbors are statistical artifacts. If `(unique source_files among neighbors) / degree < 0.5`, demote the question to "likely a node-ID collision — run `graphify rebuild`."

## Why this matters

Users new to graphify see the bridge, trust the clustering, and run queries against noise. The remediation path exists but is buried in a single-line note; the warning + fix flow should be loud enough that users don't trace a false bridge for 20 minutes before finding the escape hatch.

Happy to send a PR for #1 (the subcommand) if the direction looks right.

title: PHP extractor misses PHP 8.5 void casts and match arms
body:
## Summary

The PHP AST extractor still emits partial-extraction warnings for valid PHP 8.5 syntax. In a PHP 8.5 application, Graphify 0.9.80 with tree-sitter-php 0.24.1 reports no symbols for seven files containing `(void) SomeClass::someMethod(...)`, and a multiline parse error for a `return (string) match (...) { EnumCase => ... }` expression. The same repository produced ten warning candidates on Graphify 0.9.57; 0.9.80 reduces that to eight but does not cover these constructs.

Minimal syntax examples:

```php
<?php
(void) SomeClass::someMethod($argument);

return (string) match ($mode) {
    SomeEnum::First => $object->first(),
    SomeEnum::Second => $object->second(),
};
```

PHP 8.5 accepts these forms. The current grammar reports an ERROR on the class name after `(void)` and fails to parse enum-qualified match arms in this return/cast context, which prevents useful file-level symbols from being extracted.

## Expected behavior

The PHP extractor should parse these valid PHP 8.5 constructs and retain surrounding declarations, calls, and relationships. Please add parser regression tests for the snippets above; merely suppressing warnings would hide missing graph coverage.

## Environment

- PHP 8.5.2
- Graphify 0.9.80 (also compared against 0.9.57)
- tree-sitter-php 0.24.1

Repository evidence is from 8fold/site-mastering-the-mundane.apps issue #217. No application source was changed to work around the parser limitation.
