title: fix(csharp): resolve types from enclosing namespaces
body:
## Summary

Fixes C# type resolution for types declared in enclosing namespaces.

Previously, `CsharpNameResolver` only searched the declaring namespace, global namespace, and `using` namespaces. As a result, types available through C#'s enclosing-namespace lookup were unresolved and could fall back to sourceless stubs.

### What changed

- Added an enclosing-namespace fallback to `CsharpNameResolver.resolve_type_name()`.
- Searches enclosing namespaces from innermost to outermost.
- Keeps the existing `_scopes_for()` and ambiguity behavior unchanged.
- Resolves types consistently across:
  - Dotted namespaces
  - Nested namespace blocks
  - File-scoped namespaces
- Adds regression coverage for:
  - `references`
  - `inherits`
  - Constructor `calls`
  - Multi-level namespace shadowing
  - Existing resolution controls

### Verification

- `49` C# type-resolution tests passed
- `61` object-creation/.NET tests passed
- `15` C# language tests passed
- Ruff passed
- Pyright passed
- Full test suite: `6274 passed, 344 skipped, 55 failed`
- The 55 full-suite failures were confirmed to be unrelated Windows platform/optional-dependency failures.

Fixes #4196

title: Weakly-connected / "Knowledge Gaps" signal doesn't filter AST-origin declarations without a () suffix — false positives dominate
body:
`suggest_questions()` and the `GRAPH_REPORT.md` "Knowledge Gaps" section both treat `degree(n) <= 1` as "possible documentation gap," filtered only by `_is_file_node`, `_is_concept_node`, and `file_type != "rationale"` (`analyze.py:549-563`, `report.py:327`, shared via `_real_node`).

`_is_file_node` (`analyze.py:65-90`) only recognizes three shapes: a label matching its own filename, a `.method()` stub, or a bare `function_name()` stub. `_is_concept_node` (`analyze.py:183-193`) only excludes nodes with an empty or extension-less `source_file`.

Neither catches a plain AST declaration whose label has no trailing `()` — e.g. a TypeScript `type`/`interface` alias, an enum member, a local `const`, or a JSON config key — even when it has a real `source_file` and `_origin == "ast"`, and even when its only edge is the `contains` edge from its own file.

Concrete repro: in a Next.js/Medusa monorepo, three file-local row-shape types declared back-to-back:

```ts
type TabRow = { id: string; ... };
type ContributionRow = { id: string; ... };
type TabRecognition = { vendor_id: string; ... };
```

(used only as `manager.execute<ContributionRow[]>(...)` generic parameters, never exported) — each got exactly one `contains` edge and were then surfaced by `suggest_questions()` as "What connects `ContributionRow`, `TabRecognition`, `TabRow` to the rest of the system? — 1,556 weakly-connected nodes found — possible documentation gaps." They are not a gap; they're working as designed.

This isn't a one-off: in a ~5,000-node graph of that repo, **1,718 of 2,033 weakly-connected nodes have `_origin == "ast"`**, vs. 260 `_origin == "semantic"` (docs/PRD-derived) and 55 untagged. Manually sampling 26 of the *semantic* ones found zero confirmed real gaps too (mostly risk-register table rows and section headings) — but the AST-origin majority is the larger, more mechanically-fixable false-positive source.

**Suggested fix:** have `_is_file_node` (or a sibling check) also exclude any node with `_origin == "ast"` whose only edge is a single `contains` edge from its declaring file — regardless of whether the label ends in `()`. That one change would remove the great majority of the 1,718 false positives in our graph without touching the semantic/doc side of gap detection.

---
(graphify version: graphifyy 0.9.79, installed via `uv tool install`)

title: [Bug]: Elixir: qualified remote calls (`Mod.fun()`, `Alias.fun()`) produce no calls edge, or bind to the caller's own same-named function
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

While working on a project, I used graphify to build a code map of a mid-sized Phoenix application. The module graph came out almost empty: modules that clearly depend on each other had no `calls` edges between them. I narrowed it down to how the Elixir extractor handles remote calls.

In Elixir, most cross-module calls are qualified: `MyApp.Accounts.get_user(id)`, or `Accounts.get_user(id)` after `alias MyApp.Accounts`. `import` is used much less (mostly for framework helpers). graphify only links unqualified calls: those inside the same module, and those into modules brought in with `import`/`use`. Every qualified call is either dropped or, worse, attached to the wrong function.

Failing scenarios (all from the reproduction below):

| # | Code (inside `App.Web` / `App.Admin`) | Expected edge | Actual |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `App.Accounts.get_user(id)` (fully qualified) | `show -> App.Accounts.get_user` (EXTRACTED) | **no edge** |
| 2 | `alias App.Accounts` … `Accounts.get_user(id)` | `show_aliased -> App.Accounts.get_user` (EXTRACTED) | **no edge** |
| 6 | `App.Repo.insert(x)` in a module that also defines its own `insert/1` | `save -> App.Repo.insert` | **wrong edge** `save -> App.Admin.insert`, marked **EXTRACTED** |

Working controls, for comparison:

| # | Code | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | `import App.Repo` … `insert(attrs)` | `create -> App.Repo.insert` (INFERRED) ✓ |
| 4 | local call `build(attrs)` | `create_local -> build` (EXTRACTED) ✓ |

Scenario 6 is the most harmful one. A remote call becomes an EXTRACTED edge to an unrelated local function, so the graph states a false fact with full confidence. This is a common shape in Phoenix code: a context module with `create/1` or `insert/1` that calls `Repo.insert/1`, or a LiveView `update/2` that calls `Map.update/3`.

On the real project, `lib/` contains about 14,100 qualified call sites into the project's own modules. graphify produced about 1,100 cross-module call edges in total, almost all of them through `import`, so the module-level dependency graph was unusable.

**Where it happens** (`v8`, `graphify/extractors/elixir.py`)

- `walk_calls` (L298): for a call whose first child is a `dot` node, it splits the dot text and keeps only `parts[-1]` (L319). `App.Accounts.get_user` becomes `get_user`, and the module qualifier is discarded.
- The bare name is then looked up in the file's own `label_to_nid` (L325). If the file defines a function with that name, the call binds to it as EXTRACTED (scenario 6).
- Otherwise it goes to `raw_calls` with `is_member_call: True` and `elixir_call_scope` (L340). The cross-file pass in `extract.py` (L8871) only keeps candidates from modules that are `import`ed or `use`d in scope. `alias` is deliberately excluded, and a fully qualified module never enters the scope, so scenarios 1 and 2 get no edge.

The import-scope filter (from #4001) is correct for unqualified calls. The problem is that qualified calls never get a resolution path of their own: the qualifier that identifies the target exactly is thrown away first.

**Suggested fix**

1. In `walk_calls`, keep the receiver of a `dot` call: the module part (`App.Accounts`), separate from the function name.
2. Expand the receiver with the module's lexical alias table (`alias A.B`, `alias A.B, as: C`, `alias A.{B, C}`, `__MODULE__`). The extractor already parses aliases for the `imports` edges.
3. If the expanded module is defined in the corpus and has a function with that name, emit an EXTRACTED edge to exactly that definition, like the type-qualified passes for Swift and Go.
4. If the module is not in the corpus (`Repo` from Ecto, `Enum`, `Map`, …), emit nothing. Never fall back to the bare-name `label_to_nid` lookup for a qualified call. This matches "prefer fail-closed behavior over guessed relationships".
5. Calls on a variable receiver (`mod.fun()`, `conn.assigns`) cannot be resolved statically and should stay unlinked.

Related: #1883 (Python qualified calls), #2550 (Kotlin), #1313 (Go), #4001 and #3565 (Elixir).


### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p repro/lib/app && cd repro

cat > lib/app/accounts.ex <<'EOF'
defmodule App.Accounts do
  def get_user(id) do
    {:user, id}
  end
end
EOF

cat > lib/app/repo.ex <<'EOF'
defmodule App.Repo do
  def insert(changeset) do
    {:ok, changeset}
  end
end
EOF

cat > lib/app/web.ex <<'EOF'
defmodule App.Web do
  alias App.Accounts
  import App.Repo

  # 1. fully qualified remote call
  def show(id) do
    App.Accounts.get_user(id)
  end

  # 2. remote call through an alias
  def show_aliased(id) do
    Accounts.get_user(id)
  end

  # 3. control: unqualified call to an imported function
  def create(attrs) do
    insert(attrs)
  end

  # 4. control: local call
  def create_local(attrs) do
    build(attrs)
  end

  defp build(attrs) do
    attrs
  end
end
EOF

cat > lib/app/admin.ex <<'EOF'
defmodule App.Admin do
  # 6. qualified call to App.Repo.insert/1 from a module with its own insert/1
  def save(x) do
    App.Repo.insert(x)
  end

  def insert(x) do
    x
  end
end
EOF

uvx --python 3.13 --from graphifyy==0.9.80 graphify extract lib --code-only --no-cluster --out out

python3 -c "
import json
g = json.load(open('out/graphify-out/graph.json'))
for e in g['edges']:
    if e['relation'] not in ('contains', 'method'):
        print(e['source'], e['relation'], e['target'], e.get('source_location'), e.get('confidence'))
"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
app_admin_app_admin_save calls app_admin_app_admin_insert L4 EXTRACTED      <- wrong: the call is App.Repo.insert
app_web imports app_accounts L2 EXTRACTED
app_web imports app_repo L3 EXTRACTED
app_web_app_web_create_local calls app_web_app_web_build L22 EXTRACTED      <- ok (local)
app_web_app_web_create calls app_repo_app_repo_insert L17 INFERRED          <- ok (import)

missing: app_web_app_web_show         calls app_accounts_app_accounts_get_user   (L7)
missing: app_web_app_web_show_aliased calls app_accounts_app_accounts_get_user   (L12)
```

### Graphify version

0.9.80

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables set (`--code-only`, no LLM). Reproduced in a fresh directory containing only the four files above.


### Additional context

Function bodies written as one-liners (`def f(x), do: ...`) are not walked at all; see the separate issue below. To isolate this bug, the reproduction uses `do ... end` bodies only.

title: [Bug]: Elixir: calls inside one-line function bodies (`def f(x), do: g(x)`) are never collected
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

While working on a project, I found that calls inside keyword-form function bodies are missing from the graph. `def a(x), do: b(x)` produces the node `a()`, but no `calls` edge to `b()`, even though `b` is defined in the same module. One-line definitions are idiomatic Elixir (delegating wrappers, guards, small helpers), so a real code base loses a large share of its local call edges.

**Where it happens** (`v8`, `graphify/extractors/elixir.py`)

A function body is registered for `walk_calls` only when the definition has a `do_block` child (L252-253, `if do_block_node: function_bodies.append(...)`). The keyword form `, do: expr` has no `do_block` node. Its body is the value of the `do:` pair in the call's `arguments` keywords, so it is never walked.

**Suggested fix**

When a `def`/`defp`/`defmacro`/… has no `do_block`, take the value of the `do:` keyword in its arguments as the body and walk it the same way. The same applies to `else:`/`rescue:` keywords if they are handled for block bodies.


### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p repro2/lib && cd repro2
cat > lib/short.ex <<'EOF'
defmodule App.Short do
  def a(x), do: b(x)

  def b(x) do
    x
  end
end
EOF
uvx --python 3.13 --from graphifyy==0.9.80 graphify extract lib --code-only --no-cluster --out out
python3 -c "
import json
g = json.load(open('out/graphify-out/graph.json'))
print([(e['source'], e['target']) for e in g['edges'] if e['relation'] == 'calls'])
"
```

title: fix(python): link constructor calls to the __init__ they run
body:
## What does this PR do?

Related issue: #4209.

`Foo(...)` reaches the class node but stops before its initializer. `affected`, `query` and `path` traverse calls rather than class-to-method ownership, so a change to something `Foo.__init__` calls can miss the constructor's callers and their tests.

This adds an `INFERRED` calls edge from the caller to the nearest initializer in a supported class chain, with score 0.85 and `context: "constructor"`. The existing edge to the class stays. For example, `build() -> CachedStore()` now also reaches the inherited `Store.__init__`, so `affected "open_db()"` finds `build()` and `test_build()`.

The pass requires an extracted class call, an unambiguous source binding, and a plain module-level class chain with at most one base per class. It refuses decorated classes or initializers, metaclasses, custom allocation, ambiguous or conditional bindings, stdlib name collisions, initializer ID collisions, and source patterns that can replace construction behavior. Unsupported cases add nothing. Analysis exceptions also add nothing.

Three private node attributes store class-chain and call-binding facts. Incremental merges remove the derived constructor edges and relink them over the merged graph. AST cache schema advances from 27 to 28. Existing nodes and edges keep all other attributes.

Cache coordination: v8 schema 27 includes its Python member-result, injected-field, native declaration and Rust import facts. This branch uses schema 28 for constructor-entry facts. It preserves all prior facts, package-version and grammar namespaces, language-override salts and separate sibling-import rules.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: only source-backed, unambiguous constructor calls in the supported static subset gain an initializer edge. Existing graph output stays unchanged apart from the derived edges and stored facts.

Rebased onto v0.9.96, `dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3`. Resolved the cache schema conflict and kept both the new upstream cost-recording helper and the constructor-aware prune signature. Constructor proof rules and all 271 constructor tests are unchanged. The branch retains upstream's Python member-result and injected-field inference, explicit type aliases, native declaration changes, no-change update shortcuts, finalized-build stamps, and watch timeouts.

Fresh full builds of seven repositories preserve every baseline node and edge attribute except the three private facts. They add 703 constructor edges. An independent Python `ast` derivation confirms all 703. SCIP can judge 586, and all 586 agree on the class, inheritance chain and initializer. The existing SCIP indexes refer to unchanged source snapshots; mappings use unique file, label and location anchors in the fresh graphs, with no missing or ambiguous anchors.

- [x] Read CONTRIBUTING.md.
- [x] Reproduced the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Kept the change scoped to constructor entry edges.
- [x] Added regression and boundary tests.
- [x] Synchronized this description with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented unsupported cases.

Limitations:

- Call sites require an actual `.py` extension, even when `.graphifyrc` declares another extension as Python. Remapped files can still supply classes and initializers for `.py` callers.
- These are static rules. Another module can still replace a class or initializer through mutation or dynamic behavior the rules do not model.
- Unsupported syntax gives up correct edges. Multiple inheritance, external bases, nested classes, re-exports and overloaded initializers are excluded.
- The pass preserves v8's incremental graph behavior. Existing stale base or caller edges can prevent an addition until a full rebuild.
- Undirected builds can collapse a factory method's class-call edge into the class's method-membership edge. A later unrelated or no-change `build_merge` drops the inferred constructor edge because its class-call evidence no longer exists. Directed graphs retain both directions.
- Stored facts add about 0.2 to 3.2 percent to the historical corpus graph files. Clustering can assign different communities when new edges appear.
- Windows was not tested.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run --offline --no-sync pytest tests/test_python_constructor_init.py -q
  current v8: 95 failed, 176 passed
  this PR: 271 passed

uv run --offline --no-sync pytest tests -q
  current v8: 8677 passed, 159 skipped, 1 xfailed, no failures
  this PR: 8948 passed, 159 skipped, 1 xfailed, no failures

uv run --offline --no-sync ruff check .
  clean
uv run --offline --no-sync pyright --outputjson
  685 errors, 4 warnings, identical diagnostics to current v8

uv run --offline graphify update <repo> --no-cluster
  added constructor edges: flask 3, requests 3, httpx 56, rich 506,
    langchain-core 100, yt-dlp 17, fastapi 18
  all existing nodes and edges preserved

graphify affected "open_db()" --depth 4
  v8: initializer only
  this PR: initializer, build(), test_build(), importing test file
  after a caller edit: incremental and clean graphs have equal nodes and edges
```

The full suites use an isolated SQL grammar through `PYTHONPATH`. Both revisions have the same 159 skips and one expected failure.

GPT-6-Astra at high reasoning reviewed candidate `6025149b3cd9d84758040b8b57f7130bd5cd02e5` and found no implementation blockers. Its source audit confirms that all six non-cache PR patches match the previously reviewed version. The new upstream cost, timeout, no-change and build-stamp helpers match baseline exactly.

The strict comparison passes 679 paired stages: 553 retained stages, 30 new v0.9.96 mixed stages, 88 native-override stages and eight watch skip/stamp/timeout stages. Every baseline edge attribute and all node attributes except the three constructor facts are preserved. Native overrides allow no exclusions. Added edges must be calls from actual `.py` sources with constructor context, INFERRED confidence and score 0.85. Exact constructor sets are required, including all retained 354 positive and 199 negative stages.

The new fixtures exercise injected fields, exact member names, scalar method-result bindings and refusals for rebound, wrapped, union and container producers. They preserve explicit aliases and native declarations through cold/warm extraction, both graph directions, built/raw merges, changed-file watch and pruning. Semantic records, hyperedges, saved labels, pending labels, signatures and sweep counts retain their baseline attributes. Cache 27-to-28 retirement, parser/grammar namespaces, opaque identities, provenance and stdlib separation pass.

No-change and identical-content touch paths preserve state without invoking extraction. Main-thread SIGALRM and worker-thread Timer behavior preserve baseline timeout behavior. A truncated graph publication receives no new build stamp; the next run attempts extraction and refuses corrupt JSON as baseline does. The fixture explicitly removes its injected corrupt temporary graph before testing a successful full rebuild. This does not claim automatic repair of corrupt JSON.

The independent focused upstream command passes 214 tests with no skips. Solidity remains unavailable in an inherited fixture, and no new Solidity or Robot Framework coverage is claimed. SQL uses the isolated optional grammar. Windows was not tested. Natural clustering can still change when new edges appear.

Windows was not tested. No generated skill fragments changed.

- [x] Included no API keys or local graph artifacts.

title: Python constructor calls do not reach the initializer they run
body:
Python constructor calls stop at the class node, hiding the initializer's dependencies from change-impact traversal.

## Reproduction on current v8

Verified on v0.9.80, commit `6478eb7`, with Python 3.13 on Linux. Build these files with `graphify update <fixture> --no-cluster`:

```python
# pkg/storage.py
def open_db(path):
    return path

class Store:
    def __init__(self, path):
        self.db = open_db(path)

# pkg/cache.py
from pkg.storage import Store

class CachedStore(Store):
    pass

# pkg/service.py
from pkg.cache import CachedStore

def build(path):
    return CachedStore(path)

# tests/test_service.py
from pkg.service import build

def test_build():
    build("test.db")
```

`graphify affected "open_db()" --depth 4 --graph <fixture>/graphify-out/graph.json` finds `Store.__init__` but misses `build()` and `test_build()`. The call graph has `build -> CachedStore` and `Store.__init__ -> open_db`, with no call edge joining them.

## Constructor fix

PR #4208 adds an inferred constructor-entry edge when a supported source binding and class chain identify the initializer. It preserves the class edge and every other existing node and edge. The fixture then reaches the initializer, `build()`, its importing test file, and `test_build()`. Incremental output after editing the caller matches a clean rebuild.

Fresh comparisons against `6478eb7` add 703 constructor edges across seven pinned repositories: Flask 3, requests 3, httpx 56, rich 506, langchain-core 100, yt-dlp 17 and FastAPI 18. All 703 agree with an independent Python `ast` derivation. All 586 that SCIP can judge agree on the called class, inheritance chain and initializer. Every pre-existing node and edge remains identical.

This is a restricted static subset. Decorators, metaclasses, custom allocation, multiple inheritance, ambiguous bindings, external bases and known mutation patterns add no edge. Cross-module dynamic mutation remains a documented limitation.

## Why it matters for test impact

A separate [runtime-trace study](https://github.com/krishhgg/jev-map/tree/main/benchmarks/07-popular-repos) measured Flask and yt-dlp tests against pinned source revisions. Historical v8 graphs reached only 4 of 3,482 sampled Flask test/function pairs and 20 of 606 yt-dlp pairs. A broader prototype combining receiver typing, constructor entry and pytest fixture dependencies reached 1,699 and 358 respectively. Those are historical prototype results, not the results of this constructor PR or current v0.9.80.

Constructor entry is one missing link in that chain. Since the study, upstream has added `self.attr.method()` support in #4176 and annotated/constructor-bound local receiver support in #4198. Those changes are already present in the base used to verify this PR. Remaining opportunities include inherited methods, factory return types and pytest fixture dependency edges through the nearest `conftest.py` chain.

Related: #2041, #2860, #2417, #2586 and #1499.

title: fix(elixir): emit calls edges for keyword-form def bodies
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4207.

One-line Elixir definitions (`def a(x), do: b(x)`) have no `do_block` node: tree-sitter-elixir puts the keyword body in the `arguments` node's trailing `keywords` child, as the value of the `pair` whose keyword is `do:`. The extractor only registered `do_block` bodies in `function_bodies` for the call-walk pass, so every call inside a keyword-form body was silently dropped from the graph — a real codebase loses a large share of its local call edges.

The fix: when a `def`/`defp`/`defmacro`/`defmacrop`/`defguard`/`defguardp` has no `do_block`, take the value of the `do:` pair in its `arguments` as the body and walk it the same way (new `_get_do_keyword_body` helper, mirroring the existing `_get_defimpl_target` pair-walking style).

## Changes

| File | Change |
| ---- | ------ |
| `graphify/extractors/elixir.py` | Add `_get_do_keyword_body()` helper; in the `def`-family branch, fall back to the `do:` keyword-pair value when `do_block_node` is absent (+32 lines) |
| `tests/test_elixir_keyword_def_calls.py` | New regression tests: keyword-form call edge, `when`-guarded keyword head, no dangling edges for undefined callees, block-form unchanged (+70 lines) |

Invariant protected: every defined function whose body the extractor recognizes gets its calls walked exactly once, so `calls` edges reflect the source. Limitation: only the `do:` keyword is handled; `else:`/`rescue:` keyword bodies are not walked, matching the block form which only walks `do_block` children.

title: fix(php): parse PHP 8.5 (void) casts and casted match expressions
body:
Closes #4202

tree-sitter-php can't parse PHP 8.5's `(void)` cast, or a cast placed directly before `match (...)` (`return (string) match (...) {...}`). That's true for the pinned version and for 0.25.1, which I tried as well. The statement ends up in an ERROR node, the file gets the partial-extraction warning, and a call behind `(void)` can disappear (for example `(void) Cache::warm()` inside a method).

This is a workaround until the grammar supports these. Before parsing, `extract_php` replaces those casts with spaces of the same length, so byte offsets and line numbers stay exactly the same. It doesn't touch anything inside strings, heredocs/nowdocs, comments or inline HTML; it uses the original parse tree to check that. Files that don't contain the pattern are parsed exactly as before.

Limits: only `(void)` and the scalar casts (`string`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `array`, `object`, plus their aliases) right before `match (` are handled. Other PHP 8.5 syntax the grammar doesn't support yet isn't covered.

Testing: new `tests/test_php_unparsed_casts.py` with 5 tests. The 3 positive ones fail on current v8. The full suite on 3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14 shows the same failures as v8. Ruff is clean and pyright shows no new findings. With `graphify update --no-cluster` on the issue snippet and a set of `(void)`/`match` files, the syntax-error warnings are gone, and the output matches v8 run on copies with the casts removed. On guzzle, monolog, flysystem, saloon and PHP-Parser the graphs are identical. saloon and PHP-Parser have `(void)` in docblocks and strings, and those were left untouched.

AI-assisted (Grok Bot); each commit carries a Co-Authored-By line.

title: fix(elixir): resolve qualified and aliased remote calls
body:
Closes #4206

The Elixir extractor threw away the module part of a remote call and kept only the function name. So `App.Accounts.get_user(id)` and `Accounts.get_user(id)` (after `alias App.Accounts`) got no `calls` edge at all, and `App.Repo.insert(x)` inside a module with its own `insert/1` was linked to that local function as EXTRACTED. The same went for `Map.update(...)`, `Enum.map(...)`, `conn.assigns` and so on whenever the caller's module had a function with that name.

Now `walk_calls` keeps the receiver when it's a module name and expands it through the alias table in scope (`alias A.B`, `alias A.B, as: C`, `alias A.{B, C}`, aliases inside a function body, the implicit alias of a nested `defmodule`, and `__MODULE__`). If that module is in the same file the edge is made right there. Otherwise the call goes to a new `elixir_qualified_calls` resolver, which links it only when exactly one top-level module in the corpus has that name and that module defines the function. Modules outside the corpus get nothing. A qualified call never goes through the bare-name lookup anymore, and calls on a variable (`mod.fun()`, `conn.assigns`, `fun.(x)`) or an Erlang module (`:ets.new`) stay unlinked. Unqualified, import/use and local calls work the same as before.

Limits: arity isn't checked, so `Mod.fun/1` and `Mod.fun/2` both point at the `fun` node. A nested module defined in another file (`App.Web.Helpers` declared inside `App.Web`) isn't a cross-file target, same as for the existing import-target pass. `require A, as: B` isn't treated as an alias, and dynamic receivers like `Module.concat(...)` aren't resolved.

Testing: new `tests/test_elixir_qualified_calls.py` with 11 tests. 9 of them fail on current v8; the nested-module and import/local control tests pass on both. The full suite on 3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14 shows the same failures as v8. Ruff is clean and pyright shows no new findings. The issue's repro now gives exactly the expected edges, also after an incremental `graphify update`. On hexpm, plausible/analytics and phoenix the Elixir `calls` edges went from 3464 to 4811, 2892 to 5091 and 1163 to 1439. Nothing outside `.ex`/`.exs` changed. I spot-checked a sample of the new edges and they're correct. Every removed edge was a remote or variable call that had been bound to a same-named local function.

AI-assisted (Grok Bot); each commit carries a Co-Authored-By line.

title: fix(cluster,analyze,report): isolate AMBIGUOUS edges from top-N and modularity
body:
Closes #4199.

## 요약
AMBIGUOUS edge (LLM 추론, confidence ~0.35) 가 Leiden 모듈러리티로 독립 cluster 를 묶거나 Suggested Questions top-N 을 잠식하던 문제 수정. cluster() ambiguous_scale 파라미터 (default 0.5, env override), suggest_questions `low_confidence` 플래그, report.py 분리 렌더링.

## 변경
- `graphify/cluster.py` — `ambiguous_scale: float = 0.5` kwarg + `GRAPHIFY_AMBIGUOUS_SCALE` env override. 원본 graph 는 복사 후 수정 (`/graphify path`/`explain` 영향 없음). AMBIGUOUS edge 없는 corpus 는 copy skip.
- `graphify/analyze.py` — `suggest_questions()` 가 `ambiguous_edge` 질문에 `low_confidence=True` 플래그 추가. #3849 interleave contract 유지 (metadata-only).
- `graphify/report.py` — 플래그된 entry 를 `### Low-confidence Hints` 서브섹션으로 분리 렌더링. AMBIGUOUS 없으면 섹션 자체 미출력.

## 테스트
- `tests/test_cluster_ambiguous_scale.py` (신규, 7 tests): default scale 가중치 감쇄, scale=0.0 valid partition 유지, scale=1.0 no-op, env override + malformed fail-soft, 원본 graph 불변, no-AMBIGUOUS corpus copy skip
- `tests/test_suggest_questions_ambiguous.py` (신규, 4 tests): 모든 ambiguous_edge 가 플래그 보유, 타 type 은 미보유
- `tests/test_analyze.py::test_suggest_questions_diversity_preserves_limit_and_candidates` relax (optional `low_confidence` 키 허용)
- 전체 suite: **3030 passed, 34 skipped** (pre-existing `test_built_wheel_ships_the_full_skill_payload` 는 `build` dev-dep missing 로 환경 이슈, 본 PR 무관)

## Motivation (English)

Tracing a betweenness-0.047 bridge in a 14k-node monorepo revealed both ends joined by a single `AMBIGUOUS` edge (`confidence_score=0.35`, `source_location=null`). The LLM extractor had tagged it correctly — but downstream (a) consumed user attention via top-N and (b) pulled two independent 5-node doc clusters into one community. This PR teaches the three consumers (clustering, question generation, report) to honor the existing `AMBIGUOUS` tag.

## Backward compatibility

- Public API: new kwarg has default; existing callers unaffected unless they inspect question dict keys for strict equality.
- Partition outputs: default `0.5` is a behavior change on graphs with AMBIGUOUS edges. Byte-identical legacy behavior: `ambiguous_scale=1.0` or `GRAPHIFY_AMBIGUOUS_SCALE=1.0`.
- Report format: new subsection only when AMBIGUOUS edges present. EXTRACTED/INFERRED-only corpora produce identical output.

Honesty-rule compliance: AMBIGUOUS edges are not deleted or re-tagged. Only modularity weighting is scaled; presentation relocated; audit trail intact.

title: feat(cli,report): add graphify rebuild + surface pre-#1504 collision banner
body:
Closes #4200.

## 요약
pre-#1504 node-ID scheme (same-name file/method collision) 전수 재추출을 명시적 subcommand 로 노출. `graphify rebuild <path>` 는 manifest 백업/삭제 후 전체 재추출 트리거. semantic cache 는 보존 → docs/papers/images replay, code 만 re-AST. GRAPH_REPORT.md 상단에 collision 배너 자동 추가.

## 변경
- `graphify/cli.py` — 신규 `rebuild <path>` subcommand. `manifest.json` 을 `.manifest-backup-<ts>.json` 으로 백업 후 삭제, 기존 `_rebuild_code` 호출. `cache/` 디렉토리는 untouched 라 semantic 재추출 비용 0.
- `graphify/__main__.py` — help text 에 `rebuild` 등록.
- `graphify/report.py` — `_label_collision_percent()` helper + 상단 `⚠️` 배너. duplicate label with different `source_file` 가 structural node 의 0.5% 이상일 때 활성. concept node (empty source_file) 와 label 없는 node 는 제외.

## 테스트
- `tests/test_rebuild_cmd.py` (신규, 2 tests): manifest 백업 + `_rebuild_code` delegation, no-manifest 환경에서도 실행
- `tests/test_report_collision_banner.py` (신규, 6 tests): collision percent helper (unique/colliding/concept/missing-field), banner 출력/미출력 양방향
- 기존 `test_cluster.py`/`test_analyze.py` 89/89 pass + 2 skipped

## Motivation (English)

Full re-extract today requires users to delete `manifest.json` by hand — an unobvious operation hidden behind a one-line note that only appears on `query`/`path`/`explain` output, never on `GRAPH_REPORT.md`. In practice full rebuild is cheap: the semantic cache is content+prompt hashed, so docs/papers/images replay from disk; only code re-ASTs (seconds, no tokens). The gap is purely in surface area.

This PR:
1. Gives users a one-liner (`graphify rebuild`) that does the right thing (back up → delete manifest → re-extract), with no risk of losing the semantic cache.
2. Puts the collision warning in `GRAPH_REPORT.md` so readers who never run `query` still see it, and the remediation is in the same paragraph.

## Backward compatibility

- Existing `update` subcommand unchanged.
- No schema/output format changes except the optional banner block at the top of `GRAPH_REPORT.md` — only renders when a collision is actually detected.
- No new dependencies.

Honesty-rule compliance: the banner is a *diagnostic*, not an edit. Nodes/edges in `graph.json` are untouched; the fix (if the user runs it) rebuilds with path-qualified IDs through the normal pipeline.

title: [Bug]: C#: nested types imported with `using static` are never resolved
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`using static Demo.Layer;` makes the nested types of `Layer` usable without a qualifier, not only its static members. Code that keeps its classes inside static holder classes typically relies on this: `new Record()` where `Record` is declared as `Layer.Record`.

graphify does not resolve such a name at all:

* The C# type-definition index skips nested types (`extractors/csharp.py`, `_build_csharp_type_def_index()`, line 44: `if metadata.get("is_nested_type"): continue`).
* `CsharpNameResolver` only takes `using_kind` `namespace` and `alias` from the import edges (lines 243–252). A `using static` edge (`using_kind: "static"`) is ignored. #1466, which introduced the resolver, says so on purpose: "`using static N.T;` is ignored (it imports members, not a namespace/type)". C# also imports the nested types of `T` with it.

This also keeps the #3888 fix (#3901, released in 0.9.74) from bringing constructor edges back. A `new X()` rescued from a same-file stub is bound only with import or namespace/`using` evidence from that resolver (`extract.py` lines 8703 and 8870). For a nested type the resolver never has any, so the call is still dropped. 0.9.55 bound these calls by name alone, which found the right class but also bound calls the code cannot see (see the controls).

Type references to nested types (`public Record Current;`) end on a sourceless placeholder on both 0.9.55 and 0.9.79, including from inside the holder class.

Expected: `new Record()` and `Record` as a type resolve to `Demo.Layer.Record` when the file has `using static Demo.Layer;` or the code sits inside `Layer`. They stay unresolved when neither is the case.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
Seven files, nothing else needed.

`Lib/Layer.cs`

namespace Demo
{
    public static partial class Layer
    {
        public partial class Record
        {
        }

        public class Queue
        {
        }
    }
}


`Lib/Deep.cs`

namespace Demo
{
    public static partial class Print
    {
        public static partial class Engine
        {
            public class Info
            {
            }
        }
    }
}


`App/Static.cs` (imports the holder with `using static`)

using static Demo.Layer;

namespace Demo
{
    public class Holder
    {
        public Record Current;

        public object MakeS() { return new Record(); }
    }
}


`App/Inside.cs` (code inside the holder class)

namespace Demo
{
    public static partial class Layer
    {
        public class Builder
        {
            public Record Last;

            public object MakeI() { return new Record(); }
        }
    }
}


`App/DeepUse.cs` (two levels of nesting)

using static Demo.Print.Engine;

namespace Demo
{
    public class Reader
    {
        public Info Last;

        public object MakeD() { return new Info(); }
    }
}


`App/NoImport.cs` (control: `Record` is not visible here, this file would not compile)

namespace Demo
{
    public class Stranger
    {
        public Record Current;

        public object MakeX() { return new Record(); }
    }
}


`App/Framework.cs` (control: this is `System.Collections.Generic.Queue<T>`, not `Demo.Layer.Queue`)

using System.Collections.Generic;

namespace Other
{
    public class User
    {
        public Queue<int> Items;

        public object MakeQ() { return new Queue<int>(); }
    }
}


Then, in the folder containing `Lib/` and `App/`:


graphify extract . --code-only


and look at the `calls` edges leaving the five `Make*()` methods in `graphify-out/graph.json`.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
"real" means the definition in `Lib/`.


                                0.9.55             0.9.79
MakeS()  calls Record           real               (no edge)
MakeI()  calls Record           real               (no edge)
MakeD()  calls Info             real               (no edge)
MakeX()  calls Record           real   <- wrong    (no edge)     control, not visible
MakeQ()  calls Queue            real   <- wrong    (no edge)     control, framework type


The `references` edges of `Holder`, `Builder`, `Reader`, `Stranger` and `User` point to a sourceless placeholder on both versions.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.79 (latest release); compared with 0.9.55

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.1

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

Python 3.14.6 (the version list in the form ends at 3.13). graphify installed with `uv venv` + `uv pip install graphifyy==0.9.79` (0.9.55 the same way), not with `uv tool install`.

### Additional context

**Size in two real C# code bases** (raw `graph.json`, unpatched releases, same source tree):

* Code base 1 (1,288 `.cs` files): `new X()` (caller, class) pairs with a `calls` edge to a class defined in the code base go from 2,106 on 0.9.55 to 1,307 on 0.9.79. Of the 830 pairs that have neither a `calls` nor a `references` edge on 0.9.79, 825 target a nested type and the calling file has a `using static` directive. I did not analyse the other 5.
* Code base 2 (143 `.cs` files): 156 on 0.9.55, 95 on 0.9.79. All 61 lost pairs target a nested type, and each calling file has a `using static` directive.

"Has a `using static` directive" was counted per file, not matched against the specific holder type. Every counted site was matched against its source line (`new <Name>` at the reported line).

**Suggested fix, measured, test suite not run**

The diff below only covers the constructor case. In the rescued-call branch, when the resolver returns nothing for a C# `new X()`, it binds to the single candidate that is a nested type whose holder class the caller can see: imported with `using static` (holder name built through the whole holder chain, so `using static Demo.Print.Engine;` works) or enclosing the caller. Everything else is left as it is.


```diff
--- a/graphify/extract.py
+++ b/graphify/extract.py
@@ -7494,6 +7494,89 @@
 _PARALLEL_THRESHOLD = 20
 
 
+def _csharp_build_nested_index(all_nodes: list[dict], all_edges: list[dict]):
+    """Holder type of each nested C# type, the parent chain of each member, and the
+    `using static` imports per file -- all read from edges the extractor already emits."""
+    by_id = {n.get("id"): n for n in all_nodes if isinstance(n.get("id"), str)}
+
+    def _type_key(node: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
+        md = node.get("metadata") or {}
+        ns = md.get("namespace", "") if isinstance(md, dict) else ""
+        return (ns if isinstance(ns, str) else "", str(node.get("label") or ""))
+
+    container: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
+    parent: dict[str, str] = {}
+    static_usings: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str, str | None]]] = {}
+    for edge in all_edges:
+        rel = edge.get("relation")
+        src = by_id.get(edge.get("source"))
+        tgt = by_id.get(edge.get("target"))
+        if src is None:
+            continue
+        if rel in ("contains", "method") and tgt is not None:
+            label = str(src.get("label") or "")
+            if (
+                src.get("source_file")
+                and src.get("type") != "namespace"
+                and not label.endswith((".cs", ")"))
+            ):
+                parent.setdefault(tgt["id"], src["id"])
+                md = tgt.get("metadata") or {}
+                if rel == "contains" and isinstance(md, dict) and md.get("is_nested_type"):
+                    container[tgt["id"]] = _type_key(src)
+        elif rel == "imports":
+            md = edge.get("metadata") or {}
+            if isinstance(md, dict) and md.get("using_kind") == "static" and isinstance(md.get("target_fqn"), str):
+                static_usings.setdefault(str(src.get("source_file") or ""), []).append(
+                    (md["target_fqn"], md.get("scope_kind") or "file", md.get("scope_id"))
+                )
+    return by_id, container, parent, static_usings, _type_key
+
+
+def _csharp_nested_visible(idx, resolver, caller_node: dict, candidates: list[str]) -> str | None:
+    """The single candidate that is a nested type whose holder type the caller can see:
+    imported with `using static`, or enclosing the caller."""
+    by_id, container, parent, static_usings, type_key = idx
+    imported = {
+        fqn
+        for fqn, kind, scope_id in static_usings.get(str(caller_node.get("source_file") or ""), [])
+        if resolver._using_in_scope(kind, scope_id, caller_node)
+    }
+    enclosing: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
+    cur, seen = caller_node.get("id"), set()
+    while cur in parent and cur not in seen:
+        seen.add(cur)
+        cur = parent[cur]
+        enclosing.add(type_key(by_id[cur]))
+    def _fqn(nid: str, depth: int = 0) -> str:
+        # Full name through the holder chain (`Demo.Print.Engine`).
+        node = by_id[nid]
+        outer = parent.get(nid)
+        if outer is not None and outer in by_id and nid in container and depth < 16:
+            return f"{_fqn(outer, depth + 1)}.{node.get('label')}"
+        ns, label = type_key(node)
+        return f"{ns}.{label}" if ns else label
+
+    hits = []
+    for cand in candidates:
+        key = container.get(cand)
+        if key is None:
+            continue
+        outer = parent.get(cand)
+        fqn = _fqn(outer) if outer in by_id else (f"{key[0]}.{key[1]}" if key[0] else key[1])
+        if fqn in imported or key in enclosing:
+            hits.append((fqn, cand))
+    # The parts of one partial nested type are separate nodes here; they are the
+    # same type, so they count once. Bind to the first part by source file, the
+    # same tie-break the C# type-definition index uses.
+    if len({fqn for fqn, _ in hits}) != 1:
+        return None
+    return min(
+        (cand for _, cand in hits),
+        key=lambda nid: (str(by_id[nid].get("source_file") or ""), str(by_id[nid].get("source_location") or ""), nid),
+    )
+
+
 def extract(
     paths: list[Path],
     cache_root: Path | None = None,
@@ -8641,6 +8724,7 @@
                 str(n.get("label", ""))
             )
     _csharp_stub_resolver: CsharpNameResolver | None = None  # built on first use
+    _csharp_nested_idx = None  # built on first use
     for rc in all_raw_calls:
         if rc.get("_ambiguous_python_import"):
             continue
@@ -8711,6 +8795,18 @@
             if scoped in candidates:
                 candidates = [scoped]
                 stub_scope_hit = True
+            elif scoped is None and rc.get("csharp_new") and caller_node is not None:
+                # Nested types are not in the type-definition index, so the resolver
+                # cannot see `new Record()` for `Layer.Record` even when the caller
+                # imports `Layer` with `using static` or sits inside `Layer`.
+                if _csharp_nested_idx is None:
+                    _csharp_nested_idx = _csharp_build_nested_index(all_nodes, all_edges)
+                nested_hit = _csharp_nested_visible(
+                    _csharp_nested_idx, _csharp_stub_resolver, caller_node, candidates
+                )
+                if nested_hit is not None:
+                    candidates = [nested_hit]
+                    stub_scope_hit = True
         # Cross-language guard: never bind a call to a definition in a different
         # language family. Name-only matching was resolving a TSX callback passed
         # by name to a same-named Kotlin method in the Android half of the repo
```
Edit: the first version of this diff required exactly one visible candidate. That misses a nested type declared `partial` across two files, because each part is its own node at this stage (for example a generated part and a hand-written part). The diff above treats parts with the same holder and name as one type and binds to the first part by source file, the same tie-break the type-definition index uses. I checked it on the repro (with a second `partial` part of `Layer.Record` added) and on a real case of that shape. The counts below were measured with the first version, so they are a lower bound for the corrected one.

Measured against unpatched 0.9.79 (the patched build differs from the unpatched one only in `extract.py`):

* Repro: `MakeS`, `MakeI` and `MakeD` get their `calls` edge to the real definition. `MakeX` and `MakeQ` get none.
* Eight graphs built from real code, including the two code bases above: the patch only adds `calls` edges, 927 in total (829 + 71 + 25 + 2, nothing in the other four graphs). Each one is at a `new <Name>` source line and points to a nested type. No edge is removed, and no edge moves to a different target.
* Code base 1: 1,307 -> 2,133 pairs (0.9.55: 2,106). Code base 2: 95 -> 161 (0.9.55: 156).
* Of the pairs 0.9.55 had, 10 in code base 1 stay without an edge. 8 of them are calls whose file imports a holder type of the same name in a different namespace. The patch does not bind those because the imported holder does not contain the type. I did not check how that code compiles.

Type references to nested types are not touched by this diff. Teaching `CsharpNameResolver` about `using static` targets and the enclosing type chain would probably cover both. I have not built or measured that.

All measurements: AST extraction only, no LLM.

Related: #3888, #3901, #1466, #4196.

title: [Feature]: one test that pins graph.json invariance for every extractor (checkout folder, rebuild, line endings)
body:
### Problem or use case

The same source tree should always give the same graph.json. Seven recent bugs broke that in one of four ways, and each was found by diffing two builds by hand:

| way it broke | issues |
|---|---|
| checkout path (and OS username) inside an id or a graph.json key | #4152, #4154, #4156, #4182, #4188 |
| a rebuild of an unchanged tree writes a different graph than the first build | #4180, #4188 |
| CRLF checkout gives different ids than LF | #4164 |
| raw `--no-cluster` edge points at a node that is never declared | #4182 |

Each fix added a narrow test for its own extractor or write path. Nothing checks the invariant across all extractors, so the next extractor, or the next change to a write path, can bring the same bug back without any test failing.

### Proposed solution

One test file that builds the whole `tests/fixtures` corpus (every language with an extractor) through the real CLI, in `--no-cluster` and clustered mode, and compares every node and edge with all attributes:

- two copies in different folders give the same graph;
- the checkout folder name appears nowhere in graph.json;
- a cold build and a rebuild of the unchanged tree are the same (top-level keys too);
- an LF copy and a CRLF copy give the same graph;
- every raw edge endpoint is a declared node;
- the corpus is not trivially empty (guards against a silent empty build).

Community ids are left out of the comparison (they come from clustering; #3761 covers that).

### Alternatives considered

- Keep adding one narrow test per bug: that is what happened seven times, and it only protects the one extractor each bug was found in.
- A CI job that builds a real repo and diffs: slower, needs network, and harder to run locally than a pytest file on the fixtures already in the repo.

### Area

Developer experience or CI

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Test only. No change to node/edge ids, cache, graph.json schema, skills, MCP output or incremental updates. Adds about 20 s to the suite.

### Additional context

Written and checked against 0.9.80 (6478eb7): 12/12 pass. Against 0.9.79 the three checks covered by #4180/#4182/#4188 fail, which is the point. PR right after this issue. Windows 11, Python 3.12.12.

title: test: pin graph.json invariance across checkout folder, rebuild and line endings
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4217.

Adds `tests/test_graph_invariance.py`. It builds the whole `tests/fixtures` corpus (every extractor) through the real CLI (`python -m graphify update <dir> --force`, with and without `--no-cluster`) and checks the invariants that #4152, #4154, #4156, #4164, #4180, #4182 and #4188 each broke for one extractor or write path:

| test | catches |
|---|---|
| `test_checkout_folder_does_not_change_the_graph` | checkout path inside an id (#4152, #4154, #4156) |
| `test_graph_never_contains_the_checkout_path` | path in ids, edges or top-level keys (#4182, #4188) |
| `test_rebuilding_an_unchanged_tree_changes_nothing` | first build != rebuild (#4180, #4188) |
| `test_line_endings_do_not_change_the_graph` | CRLF ids != LF ids (#4164) |
| `test_every_edge_endpoint_is_a_declared_node` | raw edges to undeclared nodes (#4182) |
| `test_fixture_corpus_is_not_trivial` | a silent empty build passing everything above |

Each runs for `no_cluster` and `clustered` (12 cases). Builds are shared through a module fixture, so the whole file takes about 20 s. Community ids are excluded from the comparison; clustering determinism is #3761's job.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: the same source tree gives the same graph.json whatever folder it is in, however many times it is rebuilt, and whatever its line endings; and the raw graph never references a node it does not declare.
Persisted state it could invalidate: none (test only, builds in pytest tmp dirs, leaves the repo clean).

Proof that it catches the real bugs:

| graphify | result |
|---|---|
| 0.9.79 (before #4181, #4183, #4189) | 3 failed, 9 passed: path in graph.json, rebuild != build, undeclared endpoints (all `no_cluster`) |
| 0.9.80 (6478eb7) | **12 passed**, ~20 s |

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.

- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.

**Limitations:** community ids are not compared (see #3761). Binary and non-UTF-8 fixture files are copied as-is in the CRLF copy. The corpus is `tests/fixtures`, so a language without a fixture is not covered until it gets one.

## How was this tested?

```text

pyright tests/test_graph_invariance.py                     # 0 errors
```

- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (this test is that check).

title: docs: add guidance for contributors using AI coding agents
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a short "Working with AI Coding Agents" section to CONTRIBUTING.md, under Pull Requests.

The rules that matter most for AI-assisted PRs already exist in this guide but are spread across several sections: branch off `upstream/v8`, one concern per PR, regression tests that fail before the fix, never hand-edit generated skill files, run pytest/ruff/pyright, and disclose AI help with `Co-Authored-By:`. This section collects them in one place so a contributor, or the agent they point at this file, finds them together. It adds no new policy; every bullet restates an existing rule.

title: [Bug]: Python AST extraction merges same-named nested classes under different parents
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Graphify gives distinct nested Python classes the same node ID when they have the same name in one file but different enclosing classes. It emits one class node with multiple `contains` parents, losing the other definition and conflating relationships to it.

In `xai-org/x-algorithm`, `phoenix/xrex/cutedsl/ranker_fa4/tile_scheduler.py` defines five different nested `Params` classes. A focused extraction produced one `...tile_scheduler_params` node, sourced to the first definition, with `contains` edges from multiple enclosing scheduler classes. A consumer that requires one lexical parent per symbol cannot process this graph; a consumer that accepts it may attribute definitions and references to the wrong class.

Source example: https://github.com/xai-org/x-algorithm/blob/78460ca8b65c57ddd3a05f9217c8aaeba214b628/phoenix/xrex/cutedsl/ranker\_fa4/tile\_scheduler.py

The likely cause is that the class ID is built from the file stem, namespace stack, and class name, but omits the enclosing class identity. The `contains` edge does use the enclosing class identity. The same ID construction remains in the v0.9.80 source; I reproduced the behavior at runtime on 0.9.77, not 0.9.80.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from graphify.extract import extract

with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    root = Path(tmp)
    source = root / "scheduler.py"
    source.write_text(
        "class Forward:\n"
        "    class Params:\n"
        "        pass\n"
        "\n"
        "class Backward:\n"
        "    class Params:\n"
        "        pass\n"
    )
    result = extract([source], root=root, cache_root=root / "cache", parallel=False)
    print([(n["id"], n.get("source_location"))
           for n in result["nodes"] if n.get("label") == "Params"])
    print([(e["source"], e["target"])
           for e in result["edges"]
           if e.get("relation") == "contains" and e.get("target") == "scheduler_params"])
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Actual output:


[('scheduler_params', 'L2')]
[('scheduler_forward', 'scheduler_params'),
 ('scheduler_backward', 'scheduler_params')]


Expected: two distinct `Params` nodes, each with its own source location and exactly one enclosing class. References to either nested class should resolve to the corresponding node.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.77

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.13.7

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

_No response_

### Additional context

title: [Feature]: Python: self.m() / super().m() / cls.m() get no calls edge when m is defined on a base class in another file
body:
### Problem or use case

The in-file pass (`_self_call_target`) walks base classes declared in the same file, so this works:

```python
class Base:
    def m(self): ...

class C(Base):
    def run(self):
        return self.m()      # C.run -> Base.m  (same file: edge)
```

When the base class is imported from another module, the call gets no edge at all:

```python
# flask/app.py
from .sansio.app import App

class Flask(App):
    def __init__(self, ...):
        super().__init__(...)            # no edge to App.__init__
        self.add_url_rule(...)           # no edge to App.add_url_rule (defined on App)

    def handle_exception(self, e):
        handler = self._find_error_handler(...)   # no edge to App._find_error_handler
```

That is the normal shape of any project that splits a base class into its own module, so `affected App._find_error_handler` misses its callers in subclasses. Measured against jedi on 0.9.80, Flask has 162 / 243 real call pairs (66.7%), the lowest of httpx / click / flask, and inherited calls are a large part of the gap.

### Proposed solution

In `_resolve_python_member_calls`, for a `self.m()`, `cls.m()` or bare `super().m()` raw call the in-file pass could not bind, walk the caller's class up its `inherits` edges and bind the first class that owns `m` (nearest first, as in the MRO). Fail closed, no edge, when the order is not certain:
- a class with two or more bases (MRO across files is not modelled),
- a base the edge list cannot show (`mod.Base`, `Generic[T]`, a call; only bare-name bases become `inherits` edges),
- a base outside the corpus, or a self-loop base,
- the caller's own base is neither defined in nor imported by the caller's file,
- `super(Cls, obj).m()` with arguments (its MRO starts after `Cls`, not after the caller's class).

### Alternatives considered

- Bind `self.m()` to any method named `m` in the corpus: the god-node collision the shared pass skips on purpose.
- Model the full C3 MRO across files: possible, but multiple inheritance across modules is rare in practice and much harder to get exactly right; single inheritance covers the cases measured.

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

- Adds `calls` edges only (EXTRACTED, the same rule the in-file base walk already uses). No node id or existing edge changes.
- Python class nodes with a base that is not a bare name get `metadata.python_opaque_bases: true`; that key is forwarded on changed-files rebuilds like `ruby_lookup_unsafe`.
- Raw calls gain `_python_super_args` for `super(...)` with arguments. AST cache schema 6 -> 7.
- A changed-files rebuild gives the same edges as a full build (tested both ways).

### Additional context

PR right after this issue. 0.9.80 (6478eb7), Windows 11, Python 3.12.12.

title: feat(python): resolve self/cls/super() calls to a base-class method in another file
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4221.

**Resolver** (`graphify/extract.py`, `_resolve_python_member_calls`): a new arm for `self.m()`, `cls.m()` and bare `super().m()` raw calls (the ones the in-file `_self_call_target` walk could not bind). `_inherited_method` starts at the caller's class (skipping it for `super`), and walks up `inherits` edges, binding the first class whose own methods include `m`. It returns no edge when:
- a class on the chain has 0 or 2+ bases (multiple inheritance: MRO order across files is not modelled),
- a class has `metadata.python_opaque_bases` (it has a base that is not an `inherits` edge),
- a base is outside the corpus (no `source_file`) or is the class itself,
- the caller's own base is neither defined in nor imported by the caller's file (same origin gate as the typed-receiver arm, #2553).

The arm is additive: when it finds nothing, the raw call continues exactly as before. Confidence is EXTRACTED, the same as the in-file base walk it extends across files.

**Changed-files rebuilds**: there, a base class in an unchanged file is still a name stub when the resolver runs (the full build has already rewired it). The arm runs `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` on *copies* of the inherits edges, so both builds walk the same chain; the real edges are not touched. Hops after the first trust the `inherits` edges, because a changed-files rebuild carries an unchanged class's `inherits` edges but not its imports.

**Extractor** (`graphify/extractors/engine.py`):
- a Python class whose bases include a non-name (`mod.Base`, `Generic[T]`, a call, `*bases`) gets `metadata.python_opaque_bases = True` (keyword arguments like `metaclass=` do not count);
- a `super(...)` call with arguments gets `_python_super_args` on its raw call.

**Forwarding** (`graphify/cli.py`, `graphify/watch.py`): `python_opaque_bases` joins the metadata keys already forwarded for unchanged context nodes (next to `ruby_lookup_unsafe`).

**Cache** (`graphify/cache.py`): `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 6 -> 7.

Complements #2737 (resolving the `inherits` edges themselves): with it, more chains have real edges to walk; classes with a module-qualified or generic base stay excluded here until their MRO position is modelled.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a new `calls` edge is emitted only when a single-inheritance chain makes the target certain; everything else emits nothing, as before. A changed-files rebuild gives the same `calls` edges as a full build.
Persisted state it could invalidate: AST cache entries (schema bumped) and class-node metadata (new key, forwarded on changed-files rebuilds).

Measured on three repos, 0.9.80 vs this branch, cold `graphify update <repo> --no-cluster --force`:

| repo | real calls found (vs jedi) | new edges | new edges correct (jedi) | edges lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flask | 66.7% -> **71.6%** (162 -> 174 / 243) | +12 | 12 | 0 |
| httpx | 78.5% -> 78.9% | +2 | 2 | 0 |
| click | 80.3% -> 80.7% | +2 | 2 | 0 |

"Correct" = jedi `goto` at the exact call site lands on the same file, class and method: 16 / 16.
Every refused call on click and flask was traced to its stop rule; the large groups are a `module.Class` base (`class AliasedGroup(click.Group)`, which has no `inherits` edge at all), class attributes that hold a class (`self.response_class(...)`, not a method), and bases outside the corpus (`dict`, `ABC`).

Changed-files rebuild vs full build on flask (`watch._rebuild_code`, changing one file): `app.py`, `sansio/app.py`, `sansio/scaffold.py` each give the same inherited-call edges as a fresh full build.

Build time, cold, median of 5 interleaved runs: flask 6.15 -> 6.10 s, httpx 6.47 -> 5.98 s, click 7.67 -> 7.89 s. Same within noise.

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test**: 8 tests in `tests/test_python_inherited_method_calls.py`. On 0.9.80, the 5 that expect an edge fail; the 3 "no edge" guards pass on both. The two changed-files tests also fail if `python_opaque_bases` is not forwarded, and the cache test fails if the schema stays at 6.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Limitations (no edge, same as before):** multiple inheritance; bases written as `mod.Base` / `Generic[T]`; methods reached through a nested function's `self` (a closure); class attributes holding a callable; `super(Cls, obj)` with arguments. A subclass that assigns `self.m = ...` would shadow an inherited method at runtime; like the in-file walk, this is not modelled.

## How was this tested?

title: [Feature]: link a substituted template-literal import() to the modules its pattern can load (INFERRED) instead of dropping it
body:
### Problem or use case

`import()` with a substituted template literal is skipped on purpose since 563ee80 ("skip dynamic template literals in import() args"), which removed a garbage edge to a path containing the literal `${name}`. The side effect is that a module loaded only this way gets no inbound edge at all, so it reads as unreachable/dead code, and `affected` and reachability questions miss it.

Real case (NestJS service, TypeScript monorepo):

```ts
// apps/backend/src/email/email.service.ts
const templateModule = await import(`./templates/${lang}/${templateName}.template`);
```

`templates/<lang>/<name>.template.ts` holds 61 modules (10 languages). They are really used: our staging logs show emails rendered from them. Yet in the graph none had an edge from the service that loads them, and 59 of the 61 had no inbound edge at all (the other 2 are imported by a spec). Static dead-code tools share the blind spot (knip's docs recommend declaring such files as `entry`), so two tools agreeing is not evidence here.

### Proposed solution

When the template literal has substitutions, treat it as a glob instead of dropping it, fail-closed:

- only relative specifiers (`./`, `../`);
- each `${...}` becomes `*`, i.e. exactly one path segment (no `**`); static text is glob-escaped;
- the last segment must keep some static text: `` `./handlers/${name}` `` still produces no edge, so `test_ts_dynamic_template_literal_skipped` keeps passing unchanged;
- extensions follow the static-import rules (runtime suffix substituted like TypeScript, otherwise source extensions appended);
- above a cap (128 matches) the pattern is considered too broad and links nothing.

Each match gets an `imports_from` edge with `deferred: true`, `confidence: "INFERRED"`, `confidence_score: 0.85` and a `dynamic_pattern` attribute holding the readable pattern (`./templates/*/*.template`). The runtime loads one module of the set, so these stay visibly inferred, never EXTRACTED.

I have this implemented on top of v0.9.79 (`_link_dynamic_import_pattern` in `extractors/engine.py`, `_expand_js_dynamic_import_pattern` in `extractors/resolution.py`) with 5 tests: all matches linked, edges INFERRED with the pattern, `./${x}` links nothing, non-relative links nothing, over-cap links nothing. Full suite: no new failure compared to plain v0.9.79 in my environment (the same 68 failures, all from missing optional extras). On the repo above it adds 61 edges, all from that one call site; no other pattern in the repo matched.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep skipping and rely on per-project configuration (what knip does with `entry`): pushes the knowledge to every user, and the graph stays wrong by default.
- Emit EXTRACTED edges: rejected, the runtime picks one module, so it would overstate certainty.
- Link only the first match or the folder node: loses which modules are candidates.

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

- Node/edge IDs: unchanged; target IDs are the same `_make_id` of the resolved file as static imports.
- graph.json schema: new optional edge attribute `dynamic_pattern`; edges are ordinary `imports_from` + `deferred`.
- Cache: JS/TS files bypass the AST cache, so no cache semantics change.
- Incremental updates: the edges are owned by the importer file. With a changed-files rebuild (hook / watch), a new module added to the folder is linked only once the importer is re-extracted; a full `graphify update` picks it up. Happy to discuss whether that is acceptable or needs handling.

### Additional context

Related but distinct: #2575 / #2584 / #3210 (plain-string dynamic imports, fixed). Version 0.9.79, macOS, Python 3.14.

title: [Bug]: Python: `from pkg.wrappers import X as XBase` inside a local wrappers.py resolves to that same file (class inherits from itself)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

An absolute import of a package outside the corpus resolves to the importing file itself when that file has the same name as the module's last part.

`_resolve_cross_file_imports` tries the exact dotted path, then a unique path suffix, then a bare-stem index of the last part. For `from werkzeug.wrappers import Request as RequestBase` written inside flask's own `src/flask/wrappers.py`, the first two find nothing (werkzeug is not in the corpus) and the bare stem `wrappers` is that very file. The import is then treated as importing `Request` from `wrappers.py`, so:

- `class Request(RequestBase)` gets `inherits` rewired onto itself (`Request -> Request`),
- every use of the alias becomes a `uses` / `references` edge to the local class instead of the external one.

A module cannot import its own names, so any target equal to the importing file is wrong.

Real projects with this shape (a module that subclasses a library class from a same-named library module):

| project | file | line | v8 edge |
|---|---|---|---|
| flask | src/flask/wrappers.py | `class Request(RequestBase)` (werkzeug.wrappers.Request) | Request inherits Request |
| flask | src/flask/wrappers.py | `class Response(ResponseBase)` | Response inherits Response |
| typer | typer/testing.py | `class CliRunner(ClickCliRunner)` (click.testing.CliRunner) | CliRunner inherits CliRunner |
| joblib (loky) | backend/queues.py | `class Queue(mp_Queue)`, `class SimpleQueue(mp_SimpleQueue)` (multiprocessing.queues) | Queue inherits Queue, SimpleQueue inherits SimpleQueue |

Scanning the 16,890 .py files of a typical venv's site-packages: 208 files import from an outside module whose last part equals their own name, 83 classes inherit such a name, 7 with the same name as the base (self-loop).

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p demo/pkg && cd demo
touch pkg/__init__.py
cat > pkg/wrappers.py <<'EOF'
from werkzeug.wrappers import Request as RequestBase


class Request(RequestBase):
    pass


def wrap(req: RequestBase) -> RequestBase:
    return RequestBase(req)
EOF
graphify update . --no-cluster
python -c "import json; g=json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); n={x['id']:x['label'] for x in g['nodes']}; [print(e['relation'], n[e['source']], '->', n.get(e['target'])) for e in g.get('links', g.get('edges', [])) if e['relation'] in ('inherits','uses','references')]"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
inherits    Request -> Request          (self-loop; expected: Request -> RequestBase stub)
references  wrap()  -> Request          (expected: -> RequestBase stub)
uses        wrap()  -> Request          (expected: no edge to the local class)
```

### Graphify version

0.9.80 (6478eb7)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No LLM keys; AST only. Clean checkout of v8 @ 6478eb7 reproduces.

### Additional context

Different from #2374 / #2401 (self-loops made by `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes`; this one is made earlier, in `_resolve_cross_file_imports`) and from #3445 (which file the bare-stem fallback picks: with proximity, the importer itself is still the nearest candidate). PR right after this issue.

title: fix(python): never resolve an absolute import to the module that contains it
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4224.

In `_resolve_cross_file_imports` (`graphify/extractors/resolution.py`), once an import's target module is found, return early when that module is the importing file itself. A module cannot import its own names; only the bare-stem fallback reaches this case, for a package outside the corpus whose last part equals the importer's own name (`from werkzeug.wrappers import Request` inside a local `wrappers.py`). The import then stays unresolved, exactly like any other external import, so the `inherits` / `references` edges keep their stub (`RequestBase`) and no `uses` edge is drawn to the local class.

The fallback order itself is unchanged (so this composes with #3445, which changes how the bare-stem candidate is chosen).

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: an import edge, and every `uses` / `references` / `inherits` repoint derived from it, never points from a file into that same file through an import.
Persisted state it could invalidate: none. This pass runs on every build over the per-file results; nothing it decides is cached per file, so no cache schema change.

0.9.80 vs this branch, cold `graphify update <dir> --no-cluster --force`, every edge compared:

| project | edges changed | what changed |
|---|---|---|
| flask | 2 | `Request -> Request`, `Response -> Response` become `-> RequestBase`, `-> ResponseBase` stubs |
| typer | 1 | `CliRunner -> CliRunner` becomes `-> ClickCliRunner` stub |
| joblib | 2 | `Queue -> Queue`, `SimpleQueue -> SimpleQueue` become `-> mp_Queue`, `-> mp_SimpleQueue` stubs |
| httpx | 0 | — |
| click | 0 | — |

No other node or edge changed in any of the five. (joblib keeps 2 other self-loops, `ResourceTracker as _ResourceTracker` and `Popen as _Popen`; those come from `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` folding `_X` onto `X`, which is #2374 / #2401.)

title: [Bug]: Python typed-receiver calls get no edge inside a nested function or a nested class's method
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

The typed-receiver arm of `_resolve_python_member_calls` (#4198) checks that the receiver's class is defined in, or imported into, the caller's file. It finds the caller's file with `_file_node`, which returns the caller's **first** `contains` parent. For a top-level function or a method that parent is the file, but for a nested function it is the enclosing function, and for a method of a nested class it is the outer class. The check then compares a function (or class) id with the file's imports, fails, and the call gets no edge, although the extractor stamped the right `receiver_type`.

Nested typed callbacks are common, e.g. click's option factories:

```python
# click/decorators.py
def confirmation_option(*param_decls, **kwargs):
    def callback(ctx: Context, param: Parameter, value: bool) -> None:
        if not value:
            ctx.abort()            # receiver_type: Context, but no edge to Context.abort
```

Measured against jedi on 0.9.80: click has 10 such calls (`ctx.exit()`, `ctx.abort()`, ...), rich 4; all 14 are real calls jedi resolves to the same method.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p demo/pkg && cd demo
touch pkg/__init__.py
printf 'class Client:\n    def send(self):\n        return 1\n' > pkg/client.py
cat > pkg/use.py <<'EOF'
from .client import Client

def top(c: Client):
```

title: [Feature]: TS/JS: `this.field.method()` gets no calls edge when the field is a class field (`private repo: Repo`), only when it is a constructor parameter
body:
### Problem or use case

`_resolve_typescript_member_calls` types `this.repo.findById()` from a per-file `name -> Type` table. That table gets constructor parameter properties (#1316), `const x = new Foo()` locals and typed parameters (#1630), but never class fields. The way most NestJS, Angular and TypeORM classes hold their collaborators is a field (shapes taken from NestJS, hono and TypeORM, combined into one class):

```ts
export class Example {
  protected cookieSigner: CookieSigner | undefined;
  private readonly logger = new Logger('HttpAdapter');
  #root: Node = new Node();
  declare readonly manager: MongoEntityManager;

  handle() {
    this.cookieSigner?.sign(...);   // no edge
    this.logger.log(...);           // no edge
    this.#root.insert(...);         // no edge
    this.manager.find(...);         // no edge
  }
}
```

Measured with the TypeScript compiler as ground truth (`checker.getSymbolAtLocation` on every call inside every named function; kept when the target is a function/method/class in the repo), on 0.9.80:

| repo | `this.x.method()` calls found | of the misses, field declared as a class field |
|---|---|---|
| NestJS (`packages/`, 664 files) | 156 / 326 (47.9%) | 140 of 164 |
| TypeORM (`packages/typeorm/src`, 496 files) | 360 / 558 (64.5%) | 155 of 188 |

So `affected Injector.loadPerContext` and similar miss most callers in these codebases.

### Proposed solution

In `_ts_receiver_type_table`, also record class fields (`public_field_definition` / `field_definition`):
- `name: T` and `name?: T` -> `T` (same single-`type_identifier` rule as typed parameters);
- `name: T | undefined` / `T | null` -> `T`;
- an untyped field initialized with `new T(...)` -> `T`;
- `#private` fields keyed by their `#name`, the receiver the extractor already records for `this.#name.m()`;
- `static` fields skipped (they are read as `Cls.field`).

Arrays, generics and real unions stay untyped, and the existing #2553 origin gate decides as before.

### Alternatives considered

- A full type checker (run tsc): heavy dependency, needs installed packages, not deterministic across environments.
- Keying fields separately from locals: the table is per file and first-binding-wins today for every source; fields follow the same rule, with constructor parameter properties still winning.

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Adds `INFERRED` `calls` edges only (0.85, as the existing table entries). No node, id or existing edge changes. JS/TS files bypass the AST cache, so no cache schema change. Changed-files rebuilds give the same edges as a full build (checked).

### Additional context

PR right after this issue. 0.9.80 (6478eb7), Windows 11, Python 3.12.12, TypeScript 5.9.3 for the ground truth.

title: feat(ts): type `this.field` receivers from class field declarations
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4230.

`_ts_receiver_type_table` (`graphify/extractors/engine.py`) now also reads class fields, so `this.repo.findById()` resolves when `repo` is declared on the class, not only when it is a constructor parameter property. Fields go into a per-class table (`ts_type_table["fields"][Class][field]`), not the per-file name table. Only a `this.x.m()` call (marked `ts_this_field` on its raw call) reads it, through the caller's own class, so two classes in one file with a same-named field keep their own types. Field types read:

- `repo: Repo`, `repo?: Repo`, `declare readonly repo: Repo` -> `Repo` (the existing single-`type_identifier` rule);
- `repo: Repo | undefined` / `| null` -> `Repo`;
- `logger = new Logger(...)` (no annotation) -> `Logger`;
- `#root: Node` -> keyed `#root`, which is the receiver the extractor already records for `this.#root.insert()`;
- `static` fields are skipped (`this.x` inside an instance method never reads them).

Arrays, generics and two-class unions stay untyped. Every other receiver (locals, parameters, constructor parameter properties) uses the file table exactly as before. The #2553 origin gate and the confidence (`INFERRED`, 0.85) are unchanged.

In `_resolve_typescript_member_calls`, a type name defined more than once gives no edge, even when the caller's import names the exact one. Windows
