title: fix(csharp): resolve nested types imported with using static
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4216.

C# nested types imported through `using static` were not being resolved by the type resolver, causing references and constructor calls to remain unresolved.

### What changed

- Track `using static` imports within their existing namespace/file scope.
- Build a separate index for nested types by their containing type.
- Resolve static-imported nested types without expanding the existing top-level type index.
- Support multi-level nested types such as `using static Demo.Print.Engine;`.
- Handle nested types declared inside partial holder classes.
- Preserve ambiguity safety when multiple static imports expose the same nested type.

### Validation

- `pytest tests/test_csharp_type_resolution.py -q` — 52 passed
- `pytest tests/test_csharp_partial_classes.py -q` — 13 passed
- `pytest tests/test_csharp_member_calls.py -q` — 45 passed
- `pytest -k "csharp" -q` — 211 passed, 8 skipped
- `graphify update .` — successful
- `git diff --check` — clean

The existing top-level type index and static import graph edges are unchanged.

title: AST cache ignores the tree-sitter grammar version: stale extractions survive a grammar upgrade
body:
## Summary

The AST cache key does not include the tree-sitter grammar version. After upgrading a grammar package (for example `tree-sitter-swift` 0.7.2 → 0.7.4), `extract()` keeps returning the results produced by the old grammar for every file whose content and path are unchanged. That includes results the new grammar would have fixed.

`cache_dir()` namespaces AST entries by graphify's own version and cache schema (`ast/v{version}-s{schema}`). `file_hash()` covers the file content and its relative path. Neither of these changes when only the grammar package changes.

## Reproduction (graphifyy 0.9.80)

`src/Badge.swift`:

```swift
final class Badge {
    #if os(iOS)
    func iosOnly() {}
    #endif
    func update() {}
}
```

`repro.py`:

```python
import sys
from importlib.metadata import version
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract

root, cache = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
ast = extract([root / "Badge.swift"], cache_root=cache, root=root)
owned = sorted(e["target"] for e in ast["edges"] if e["relation"] == "method")
print(f"tree-sitter-swift {version('tree-sitter-swift')}: methods owned by Badge = {owned}")
```

Run it three times:

```
# 1) fresh cache, tree-sitter-swift 0.7.2 (cannot parse #if inside a type body)
tree-sitter-swift 0.7.2: methods owned by Badge = []
# 2) same cache, after upgrading to tree-sitter-swift 0.7.4
tree-sitter-swift 0.7.4: methods owned by Badge = []
# 3) empty cache, tree-sitter-swift 0.7.4
tree-sitter-swift 0.7.4: methods owned by Badge = ['badge_badge_iosonly', 'badge_badge_update']
```

Run 2 serves the 0.7.2 extraction from the cache, so the upgrade has no effect until the cache is deleted or the source file changes. Nothing reports that the cached entry came from a different grammar.

## Impact

We found this while comparing two graphs built from the same Swift sources. One environment had upgraded `tree-sitter-swift`, but its warm cache still held the 0.7.2 results. As a result, roughly 400 members were detached from their types and their call edges were missing, even though the installed grammar parsed the files correctly.

## Suggested fix

Include the version of the grammar used for each language in the AST cache namespace or key, for example the installed `tree-sitter-<lang>` distribution version and the `tree-sitter` runtime version. A content-only key is not enough, because the extractor's output depends on the grammar.

## Workaround

Key `cache_root` by the grammar versions on the caller side, for example `<cache>/ts{tree_sitter}-swift{tree_sitter_swift}`.

Environment: graphifyy 0.9.80, tree-sitter 0.25.2, tree-sitter-swift 0.7.2 / 0.7.4, Python 3.11, macOS.

title: [Bug]: Rust: an in-file call binds to any same-named function, so `Matcher::new()` reaches `Printer::new()` and `Arc::new(x)` reaches the file's own `new`
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`extract_rust` binds a call inside one file by the callee's bare name alone (`label_to_nid.get(callee_name)` in `walk_calls`, `graphify/extractors/rust.py`). The index holds every node in the file, last one wins, and the call's shape is ignored:

- `Matcher::new()` goes to whichever `fn new` the file defines last, even `impl Printer`'s.
- `Arc::new(x)`, `Vec::default()`, `String::from(..)` (std types) go to the file's own `new` / `default` / `from`.
- `self.go()` goes to another type's `go` when both types live in the file.
- `drop(x)` (a free call) goes to `impl Drop`'s method; `x.total()` (a method call) goes to a free `fn total`.

All these edges are `calls`, `EXTRACTED`, confidence 1.0.

Measured against rust-analyzer (go-to-definition at every call inside every `fn`), 0.9.80, `calls` edges whose both ends are in `.rs` files:

| repo | calls edges | correct | wrong: another fn in the repo | wrong: real target is std or a dependency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ripgrep | 3129 | 1852 | 970 | 262 (39.4% wrong) |
| bat | 774 | 602 | 98 | 40 (17.8% wrong) |
| fd | 181 | 148 | 9 | 20 (16.0% wrong) |

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p demo/src && cd demo
cat > src/lib.rs <<'EOF'
use std::sync::Arc;

pub struct Matcher;
pub struct Printer;

impl Matcher {
    pub fn new() -> Matcher { Matcher }
}

impl Printer {
    pub fn new() -> Printer { Printer }
}

pub fn make_matcher() -> Matcher { Matcher::new() }
pub fn share(m: Matcher) -> Arc<Matcher> { Arc::new(m) }
EOF
graphify update . --no-cluster
python -c "import json; g=json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); n={x['id']:(x['label'],x.get('source_location')) for x in g['nodes']}; [print(n[e['source']], '->', n[e['target']]) for e in g.get('links', g.get('edges', [])) if e['relation']=='calls']"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
('make_matcher()', 'L14') -> ('.new()', 'L11')   # wrong: Printer::new, the call is Matcher::new (L7)
('share()', 'L15') -> ('.new()', 'L11')          # wrong: std's Arc::new, not Printer::new

Expected: ('make_matcher()', 'L14') -> ('.new()', 'L7') and no edge from share().
```

### Graphify version

0.9.80 (6478eb7)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No LLM keys; AST only. Clean checkout of v8 @ 6478eb7 reproduces.

### Additional context

The call already says which type it means (`Matcher::`, `Self::`, `self.` inside `impl Matcher`), and the extractor knows each method's impl type, so the in-file match can be restricted to that type's methods. Related but different: #2313 (the shared builtin-name list), #2774 (node ids merged by bare name), #2135 (lowercase `module::f()` across files). PR right after this issue.

title: fix(rust): bind an in-file call to the type it names, not to any same-named function
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4237.

In `extract_rust` (`graphify/extractors/rust.py`), the in-file call match now follows the call's shape:

- `Type::f()` and `Self::f()` bind only to `f` in an `impl Type` block of the same file. The type is the last path segment without generic arguments (`crate::a::Matcher`, `Vec::<u8>`, `io::Error`, `i32`), on both the call and the impl. With no such method there is no in-file edge, except `Enum::Variant(x)`, which still gets its `references` (constructor) edge to the variant node.
- `self.f()` binds only to `f` on the caller's own impl type. With no such method in the file it now reaches the existing cross-file `self` pass (#2234) instead of another type's `f`.
- A bare `f()` binds only to a free function or a type (tuple struct / variant constructor), never to a method. `x.f()` binds only to a method, never to a free function.

Module paths (`fs::read`, `self::helper`) keep the old match.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: an in-file `Type::f()` / `Self::f()` / `self.f()` edge goes to a method of that type; a free call never reaches a method and a method call never reaches a free function.
Persisted state it could invalidate: AST cache entries for `.rs` files. The cache directory is keyed by package version (`cache/ast/v{version}-s{schema}`), so the next release re-extracts; no schema bump needed (no new persisted field).

Against rust-analyzer 1.97.1 (go-to-definition at every call inside every `fn`), 0.9.80 vs this branch, cold `graphify update <dir> --no-cluster --force`, `calls` edges with both ends in `.rs` files:

| repo | wrong edges | wrong share | correct edges | calls found |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ripgrep | 1232 -> **532** | 39.4% -> **18.9%** | 1852 -> **2236** | 40.5% -> **48.2%** |
| bat | 138 -> **36** | 17.8% -> **5.0%** | 602 -> **655** | 65.8% -> **71.5%** |
| fd | 29 -> **9** | 16.0% -> **5.4%** | 148 -> **154** | 34.4% -> **35.8%** |

"Calls found": (caller, callee) pairs rust-analyzer resolves to a `fn` in the repo that the graph also has. Correct edges go up because `B::new()` now reaches `B::new` instead of the last `new` in the file.

Correct (caller, callee) pairs lost: ripgrep 1, bat 0, fd 0. The one is `Default::default()` in a globset test: a trait-qualified call whose target depends on the variable's type (`let set: GlobSet`), so the old edge was the bare-name guess landing right.

New pairs rust-analyzer does not confirm: ripgrep 25, bat 0, fd 0. All are `x.f()` calls with an untyped receiver, which this PR leaves as a bare-name guess; with methods and free functions in separate indexes, the guess now lands on a different method in those 25 cases (for example `searcher.search_path()` in `crates/core/search.rs`, whose target is `Searcher::search_path` in `crates/searcher`, now reaching the local `SearchWorker::search_path`; before, the name matched the caller itself and the edge was dropped). Over all `x.f()` / `expr.f()` / `self.field.f()` edges in ripgrep: wrong 659 -> 502, correct 560 -> 646.

Changed-files rebuild vs full build (`watch._rebuild_code`, bat, changing `src/printer.rs`): 1118 / 1118 / 1118 `calls` edges, identical.

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary (the in-file match in `walk_calls`, plus the method index it reads).
- [x] Added a **regression test**: `tests/test_rust_in_file_call_binding.py`, 7 tests; 6 fail on 0.9.80, `test_enum_variant_constructor_is_still_a_reference` passes on both.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Limitations:** `x.f()` with a receiver that is not `self` is still bound by name in-file (a typed-receiver pass is the follow-up). Trait-qualified calls (`Default::default()`, `From::from(x)`) and `<T as Trait>::f()` get no in-file edge. `Type::f()` where `impl Type` is in another file still gets no edge, as before.

## How was this tested?

Project venv (Python 3.12.12, graphify from this branch via PYTHONPATH), Windows 11; rust-analyzer 1.97.1 for the ground truth:

title: fix(cache): namespace AST cache by tree-sitter grammar versions (#4236)
body:
## Summary
- The AST cache key did not include the tree-sitter grammar version, so upgrading a grammar package (e.g. tree-sitter-swift 0.7.2 -> 0.7.4) kept serving stale extractions for every unchanged file until the cache was manually deleted (#4236).
- The AST cache directory is now namespaced as `cache/ast/v{graphifyy}-s{schema}-g{grammar_fingerprint}/` where the fingerprint is a short sha256 of the installed `tree-sitter` runtime and every `tree-sitter-*` distribution version (memoized per process).
- A grammar upgrade now automatically moves extract() to a fresh directory; the stale-dir sweep cleans the old one.

## Test plan
- `tests/test_grammar_cache_key.py`: dir is grammar-namespaced and its suffix equals the fingerprint; upgrading a grammar changes the returned cache dir end-to-end; fingerprint is stable for an unchanged set and changes on version bump.
- `ruff check` clean on both files; existing `cache_dir` callers/layout audited (no bypass of `cache_dir()`).

Fixes #4236

title: [Bug]: Skill detect()/detect_incremental() calls ignore the persisted --no-gitignore and --exclude settings (.graphify_build.json)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

#1886, #2027 and #1971 made `--exclude` and `--no-gitignore` persist in `graphify-out/.graphify_build.json`. `graphify update`, `--watch` and the hook read them back (`_read_build_excludes` / `_read_build_gitignore` in `watch.py`).

The skill pipeline does not. `skill.md` Step 2 calls `detect(Path('INPUT_PATH'))`, and `references/update.md` calls `detect_incremental(Path('INPUT_PATH'))`. Both use the defaults: `gitignore=True` and no `extra_excludes`. I checked this on `v8` at `6478eb7`.

So when a corpus was built with `--no-gitignore`, a skill-driven `--update`:

- **Drops every opted-in git-ignored file from the scan.** `detect_incremental` puts them in `excluded_files`, because they still exist on disk. The runbook prunes only `deleted_files`, so their nodes stay in `graph.json`. But `save_manifest(..., scan_corpus=...)` drops their manifest rows. Their nodes then go stale, and the next CLI run re-extracts all of them, which costs LLM tokens for docs.
- **Re-includes paths excluded with `--exclude`.** This is #1886 again, on the skill path.

Expected: the skill honors the same persisted options as the CLI.

Our case: an Obsidian knowledge base whose `wiki/` folder is deliberately git-ignored (not versioned) but belongs in the graph. The README says `--no-gitignore` is the way to do this, and it works for the CLI.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p /tmp/gfy-repro/notes /tmp/gfy-repro/docs && cd /tmp/gfy-repro && git init -q
printf 'notes/\n' > .gitignore
echo '# A note' > notes/a.md; echo '# B doc' > docs/b.md; echo '# Skip me' > docs/skip.md
python -I - <<'EOF'   # the graphifyy 0.9.80 environment
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.watch import _write_build_config, _read_build_gitignore, _read_build_excludes
from graphify.detect import detect, detect_incremental, save_manifest
root, out = Path('.'), Path('graphify-out')
# What `graphify extract . --no-gitignore --exclude docs/skip.md` persists:
_write_build_config(out, excludes=['docs/skip.md'], gitignore=False)
print('persisted:', (out / '.graphify_build.json').read_text())
rel = lambda fs: sorted(str(Path(f).resolve().relative_to(Path.cwd().resolve())) for f in fs)
# CLI update/watch/hook path (watch.py) honors the persisted options:
cli = detect(root, gitignore=_read_build_gitignore(out), extra_excludes=_read_build_excludes(out) or None)
print('CLI-path detect():       ', rel(f for v in cli['files'].values() for f in v))
save_manifest(cli['files'], root=str(root.resolve()))
# Skill path, verbatim from skill.md Step 2 / references/update.md:
sk = detect(Path('.'))
print('skill detect():          ', rel(f for v in sk['files'].values() for f in v))
inc = detect_incremental(Path('.'))
print('skill detect_incremental: new =', rel(f for v in inc['new_files'].values() for f in v),
      '| excluded_files =', rel(inc['excluded_files']), '| deleted_files =', inc['deleted_files'])
EOF
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
persisted: {"excludes": ["docs/skip.md"], "gitignore": false}
CLI-path detect():        ['docs/b.md', 'notes/a.md']
skill detect():           ['docs/b.md', 'docs/skip.md']
skill detect_incremental: new = ['docs/skip.md'] | excluded_files = ['notes/a.md'] | deleted_files = []
```

The skill path drops `notes/a.md` (git-ignored, but opted in) and re-includes `docs/skip.md` (excluded).

### Graphify version

0.9.80

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional context

Two possible fixes:

1. In `skill.md` Step 2 and `references/update.md`, for every platform copy, read the persisted options and pass them:
   ```python
   from graphify.watch import _read_build_gitignore, _read_build_excludes
   out = Path('graphify-out')
   detect(Path('INPUT_PATH'), gitignore=_read_build_gitignore(out),
          extra_excludes=_read_build_excludes(out) or None)
   ```
2. Make `detect()` and `detect_incremental()` fall back to the persisted values when the caller passes nothing, for example with `gitignore: bool | None = None`. That fixes every caller in one place, including third-party scripts that follow the runbook.

Option 2 looks safer, because the skill has many platform copies of these calls.

title: [Bug]: `graphify export svg` writes a graph.svg that is not well-formed XML when a label contains a control character
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

A node or community label that contains a C0 control character (an ANSI escape from a pasted terminal capture, a form feed used as a section separator, a NUL) ends up in `graph.svg`. XML 1.0 forbids those characters, so the file is not well-formed. `graphify export svg` still prints `graph.svg written` and exits 0.

The same graph exports a well-formed `graph.graphml`. #2897 made `to_graphml` strip these characters and left `to_svg` out, for a reason given in #2899: `to_svg` does not crash, matplotlib only warns about a missing glyph and draws a box. That holds for a label without a pair of `$` (between two of them, a control character can make matplotlib read invalid mathtext and `to_svg` raise `ValueError`), but the file it writes is not valid XML, and the command reports success.

Expected: a well-formed `graph.svg`, with the control character dropped from the drawn text, as `to_graphml` does.

Cause, in `graphify/export.py`: `to_svg` hands the raw node labels to `nx.draw_networkx_labels` and the raw community label to `mpatches.Patch`. With the default `svg.fonttype`, matplotlib's SVG backend writes each drawn string into a comment (`<!-- text -->`). Its comment escaping handles `&`, `<`, `>` and `--`, not control characters. `_strip_xml_illegal` is only called from `to_graphml`.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir svg-repro && cd svg-repro
printf '# Notes\n\n## Build \033[31mlog capture\033[0m\n\nSome text.\n\n## Deploy\n\nSee [[Notes]].\n' > notes.md
printf 'def helper():\n    return 1\n\ndef main():\n    return helper()\n' > app.py
graphify update .
graphify export svg
xmllint --noout graphify-out/graph.svg
graphify export graphml
xmllint --noout graphify-out/graph.graphml
```

The legend takes the same path. On a project with no control character in any heading, `graphify export svg --labels labels.json` with `{"0": "Core \^[[0mmodule", "1": "Other\^Lgroup"}` gives the same `xmllint` error (`<!-- Core [0mmodule (4) -->`).

### Error output or graph output

```text
.../graphify/export.py:1409: UserWarning: Glyph 27 () missing from font(s) DejaVu Sans.
  plt.savefig(output_path, format="svg", bbox_inches="tight",
graph.svg written - embeds in Obsidian, Notion, GitHub READMEs
graphify-out/graph.svg:513: parser error : xmlParseComment: invalid xmlChar value 27
     <!-- Build [31mlog capture[0m -->
```

The parentheses of the warning hold the ESC character. `xmllint` exits 1 on `graph.svg` and 0 on `graph.graphml`. The heading becomes the node `Build \x1b[31mlog capture\x1b[0m` in `graph.json`.

### Graphify version

0.9.80 (v8 @ 6478eb7)

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

`uv sync --all-extras --frozen`, matplotlib 3.10.9 (the `uv.lock` version); the same file is malformed with matplotlib 3.11.2. AST-only path (`graphify update`), no API key involved. Reproduced on a clean checkout of v8 at 6478eb7 (no local change).

### Additional context

I have a small fix and can open a PR: pass the node labels and the legend text through `_strip_xml_illegal` in `to_svg`, with a regression test next to the #2897 tests.

title: [Bug]: An ignore pattern without a slash is matched against the whole path: `*` crosses `/`, and `!dir/` brings the directory back without its files
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

gitignore compares a pattern that has no slash with the name of each file or directory, and with nothing else. `_is_ignored` also compares it with the entry's whole relative path, with every cumulative path prefix, and with the name of every ancestor directory. Three consequences, visible in `graphify update`:

- `*` crosses `/`: `test_*.py` ignores `test_helpers/util.py`, and `doc*.md` ignores `docs/api.md`.
- A directory re-included with `!dir/` comes back without its files, because they still match the broad pattern through their ancestor's name. `.*` followed by `!.github/` drops `.github/scripts/release.py`. github/gitignore's `Global/Tags.gitignore` (`tags`, then `!tags/`) drops every file under a `tags/` directory.
- The other way round, `!name` also re-includes the files below a directory called `name`: with `*.py` then `!vendor`, `vendor/a.py` is kept. git ignores it, because `!vendor` only re-includes the entry called `vendor`. The same goes after `*`: a bare `!dir` brings the directory back, its files still match `*`, and git needs `!dir/**` as well for them (the README's `!src/` and `!src/**`).

The README describes `.graphifyignore` as "same syntax as `.gitignore`, including `!` negation". `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` keeps the files of the first two cases and ignores `vendor/a.py` in the third.

Cause, in `graphify/detect.py`, `_is_ignored` -> `_eval` -> `_matches`, the branch for patterns without a slash: it tries `fnmatch(rel, p)`, then the entry's name, then `fnmatch(part, p)` and `fnmatch(prefix, p)` for every ancestor segment. `_is_ignored` already evaluates each ancestor on its own, top-down, so the entry's name is all this branch needs. `!dir/` only applies to directories, so it can never rescue a file that matches through its ancestor's name. Anchored patterns were made segment-wise in #1975; this branch was left as it was.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir demo && cd demo && git init -q
mkdir -p .github/scripts test_helpers src/tags
echo 'def release(): pass' > .github/scripts/release.py
echo 'def helper(): pass' > test_helpers/util.py
echo 'def handle(): pass' > src/tags/handler.py
echo 'def main(): pass' > app.py
printf '.*\n!.github/\ntest_*.py\ntags\n!tags/\n' > .graphifyignore
graphify update .
python3 -c "import json; print(sorted({n['source_file'] for n in json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json'))['nodes'] if n.get('source_file')}))"
cp .graphifyignore .gitignore
git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- '*.py'
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
graphify keeps: ['app.py']
git keeps:      .github/scripts/release.py, app.py, src/tags/handler.py, test_helpers/util.py
```

Three of the four files are dropped. None of them matches a pattern by its own name.

### Graphify version

0.9.80 (v8 @ 6478eb7)

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone), `uv sync --all-extras`

### Additional Environment Details

AST-only path (`graphify update`), no API key involved. git 2.54.

### Additional context

I have a small fix and can open a PR: in the branch for patterns without a slash, compare the entry's NFC name only, and drop the path, prefix and ancestor-segment comparisons, together with the root-relative path that was only computed for them. Anchored patterns and the parent-exclusion walk stay as they are. It comes with 14 tests: 12 fail on v8 and all 14 pass with the fix (the other two are controls that must keep passing). The third consequence changes for anyone who relied on it: after `*`, a bare `!dir` no longer brings the directory's files back, as in git. `!dir/` plus `!dir/**`, or `!vendor/**/*.py` in the example above, is the spelling that works in git and keeps working here. A short README note says why a re-included directory needs both lines after `*`.

title: [Bug]: An unqualified call in Java, C#, Scala and C++ is bound to the last same-named method of the file, not the one in the caller's class
fix(export): strip control characters from the labels drawn into graph.svg (#4241)
body:
## What does this PR do?

<!-- Describe the problem and the change. Link the relevant issue when one exists. -->

Fixes #4241.

`graphify export svg` wrote a `graph.svg` that is not well-formed XML when a node or community label held a C0 control character, yet reported success. matplotlib copies each drawn string into a comment and escapes `&`, `<`, `>` and `--`, not control characters. #2897 made `to_graphml` strip them; `to_svg` was left out as, for a label without a pair of `$`, it does not crash (matplotlib warns about a missing glyph, #2899), but the file is invalid XML.

Node labels and legend text go through `_strip_xml_illegal`, as in `to_graphml`: tab, LF and CR stay, other C0 controls go. A non-string label is `str()`-ed first, as networkx does. Two commits, each green on its own; the second only matters for a node without a `label`, which graphify already reports as missing a required field and draws by its id.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation

title: C#: calls bind to enum members of the same name (follow-up to #3795)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

#3795 is fixed for type references: base types and parameter types no longer resolve to enum
members. Calls still do. Invoking a delegate-typed field gets a `calls` edge to an enum member
that shares the field's name.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
`Eval.cs`:


namespace Demo
{
    public delegate float Curve(float t);
    public class Eval
    {
        public enum Kind { Linear, Delegate }
        public Kind Mode;
        public Curve Delegate;
        public float Evaluate(float t)
        {
            switch (Mode) { case Kind.Delegate: return Delegate != null ? Delegate(t) : t; default: return t; }
        }
    }
}


`graphify extract . --code-only`
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
### Actual


eval_demo_eval_evaluate --calls--> eval_demo_kind_delegate


`eval_demo_kind_delegate` is the enum member `Kind.Delegate`.

### Expected

No `calls` edge to `Kind.Delegate`. An enum member (or a property) can never be the target of a
call. `Delegate(t)` invokes the field; with no project method to point at, it gets no edge (or an
`unresolved_calls` entry).
```

### Graphify version

0.9.80

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

pip

### Additional Environment Details

_No response_

### Additional context

In a ~120-file Unity project, 5 calls still land on enum members on 0.9.80. The other shapes
are `inj.Handles[i].Pause()` landing on an enum member `Pause`, and
`store.Vector2[idx] = new Vector2(...)` (also `Vector3`, `Quaternion`) landing on enum members of
those names. Excluding enum members and properties from call-target lookup, as #3795 did for type
lookup, would cover all of them.

title: C#: calls through a member chain, through element access, or inside a constructor produce no edge (follow-up to #3797)
[Bug]: C#: an external type referenced from several files gets one placeholder node per file
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

A type the corpus uses but does not declare (`List<T>`, `System.Type`, Unity's `VisualElement`)
gets a separate sourceless placeholder node in every file that mentions it, with the file's name
in its id. Queries for the type return a dozen identical nodes, and nothing connects the files
that share it.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
`A.cs`:


using System.Collections.Generic;
namespace Demo
{
    public class A { public List<int> Items; }
}


`B.cs`:


using System.Collections.Generic;
namespace Demo
{
    public class B { public List<string> Names; }
}
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
### Actual


a_demo_a --references--> a_cs_list
b_demo_b --references--> b_cs_list


These are two nodes labelled `List`. `System.Type` does the same: referenced from `User.cs` and
`Channel.cs`, it becomes `user_cs_type` and `channel_cs_type`.

### Expected

One placeholder per external type, keyed by its name (or its qualified name when the `using`s say
which one), shared by every file that references it.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.80

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

pip

### Additional Environment Details

_No response_

### Additional context

In a ~120-file Unity project, 349 placeholder nodes fold into far fewer on 0.9.80; in a 42-file
one, 116. When the folded nodes keep all their edges, the most-used Unity types (`Vector2`,
`VisualElement`) become the top god nodes. So whatever fixes the identity should probably keep a
placeholder's `inherits`/`implements` edges and think twice about counting plain `references`
toward degree. That is a separate design question; the duplication is the bug.

title: [Bug]: a method that constructs its own declaring type loses its `method` edge
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

A static factory that calls its own type's constructor has a `calls` edge to the type. Its type
should also have a `method` edge to it. Only one survives, apparently because edges are kept one
per node pair. The method is then invisible to anything that walks a type's members (member
lookup, `explain` on the type, call resolution into it).

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
`Report.cs`:


namespace Demo
{
    public sealed class Report
    {
        public string Verb;
        public static Report Fault(string verb) { return new Report { Verb = verb }; }
        public static string NotImplementedJson(string verb) { return verb; }
        public string ToJson() { return Verb; }
    }
}
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
### Actual


report_demo_report --method--> report_demo_report_notimplementedjson
report_demo_report --method--> report_demo_report_tojson
report_demo_report_fault --calls--> report_demo_report


`Report` has no `method` edge to `Fault`.

### Expected

Both edges: `report_demo_report --method--> report_demo_report_fault` and the `calls` edge back.
Or, if one edge per pair is a deliberate invariant, a structural edge (`method`, `contains`)
should win over a `calls` edge in the opposite direction.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.80

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

pip

### Additional Environment Details

_No response_

### Additional context

7 methods in a 42-file project and 11 in a ~120-file one. The mechanism (one edge per node pair,
last write wins) is probably not C#-specific: any edge between a type and its own member, in
either direction, can replace the structural one.

title: [Bug]: C#: a generic and a non-generic type of the same name share one node
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`Effect` and `Effect<T>` get the same node id, so the generic's declaration and the non-generic's
merge, and `Effect<T> : Effect` becomes a self-loop.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
`Effects.cs`:


namespace Demo
{
    public abstract class Effect { public virtual int ReadSlot(string p) { return 0; } }
    public abstract class Effect<T> : Effect where T : unmanaged { }
    public abstract class Tween<T> : Effect<T> where T : unmanaged
    {
        public override int ReadSlot(string p) { return base.ReadSlot(p) + 1; }
    }
}
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
### Actual


effects_demo_effect --inherits--> effects_demo_effect
effects_demo_tween --inherits--> effects_demo_effect


### Expected

Two nodes, for example `effects_demo_effect` and `effects_demo_effect_1` (the arity in the id,
the way C# metadata names it ``Effect`1``), with `Effect<T> --inherits--> Effect` and
`Tween<T> --inherits--> Effect<T>`.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.80

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

pip

### Additional Environment Details

_No response_

### Additional context

The generic-over-non-generic base pair is a common C# pattern (`Effect<T> : Effect`,
`Comparer<T> : Comparer`). Every subclass then appears to inherit the non-generic base directly,
and members declared on the generic land on the same node as the non-generic's.

title: fix(detect): match unanchored ignore patterns against the entry name only (#4242)
body:
## What does this PR do?

<!-- Describe the problem and the change. Link the relevant issue when one exists. -->

Fixes #4242. gitignore matches a pattern without a slash against an entry's name only. `_is_ignored` also matched it against the whole relative path, each prefix and every ancestor's name, so `*` crossed `/` (`test_*.py` ignored `test_helpers/util.py`); a directory re-included with `!dir/` came back without its files (`.*` then `!.github/` dropped `.github/scripts/release.py`; github/gitignore's `Global/Tags.gitignore` did the same to a `tags/` directory); and `!name` re-included the files below a directory called `name` (`*.py` then `!vendor` kept `vendor/a.py`).

The unanchored branch of `_matches` now compares the entry's NFC name only (the unanchored counterpart of #1975); `_is_ignored` already tests each ancestor top-down. Anchored patterns and the parent-exclusion rule are unchanged. Three commits: the fix with its tests; the removal of `_segments`, its cache and the root-relative path `_eval` computed for these patterns, which have no reader left; a README note on re-including a directory after `*`.

As in git (gitignore(5)), `!dir` now re-includes the directory called `dir`, not its files: after `*`, write `!dir/` and `!dir/**` (the README's `!src/` + `!src/**`). A bare `!dir` used to bring the files back. Of 545 public `.graphifyignore` files scanned, one does that for directories (two, absent from its committed tree); if they exist locally, their files leave that graph. The other way round, a file that a pattern hid only because its `*` crossed `/` is now indexed, as git indexes it: `service-account*.json` no longer hides `service-account-keys/prod.json` (write `service-account*/` to ignore that directory). 78 such patterns appear in 50 of the 545 files; their committed trees show no file that moves, local-only directories are not seen.

title: fix(extract): bind an unqualified call to the caller's own class in Java, C#, Scala and C++ (#4243)
body:
## What does this PR do?

<!-- Describe the problem and the change. Link the relevant issue when one exists. -->

Fixes #4243. Related: #2041 (umbrella), point 4.

In Java, C#, Scala and C++, `b()` inside a method was bound to the last method named `b` in the file, whatever its class: with a nested `Inner.b()` declared after `Outer.b()`, `Outer.a()` got an EXTRACTED edge to `Inner.b()` (Guava's `Synchronized.java`: 195 of 213 `delegate()` call edges on `SynchronizedTable.delegate`).

The call now goes to the nearest class that declares the name, as `_self_call_target` does for `self`/`this`. Three commits: the caller's own class; its bases declared in the file; the classes around it.

## Type of change

<!-- What invariant does this code protect? How do you prove your change doesn't break it? What generated or persisted state could your change invalidate? -->

- A supertype outside the file is not seen, so an inherited method can lose to an enclosing class that declares the name (3 wrong of the 21 call sites that step out past a class: `get()` in `WeakReference` subclasses, wrong on v8 too).

title: R extractor hangs forever on a backtick-quoted operator whose body calls a non-local function
body:
**Repro** (graphify 0.9.73, Python 3.14, macOS): a file `m1.R` containing

```r
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a
```

`extract_r()` never returns, so `graphify update` hangs indefinitely with no output. Without the call (`` `%||%` <- function(a, b) a ``), or with an ordinary name (`f <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a`), the file extracts instantly.

**Cause:** `_make_id(owner, "%||%")` strips every non-identifier character, so the function's id equals the file id (`_make_id('m1', '%||%') == 'm1'`). `declare_function` then sets `scope_parent[file_id] = file_id`, and `resolve_local()` in `extractors/r.py` (around line 385) loops forever on `scope = scope_parent.get(scope)` whenever a called name such as `is.null` is not defined locally.

**Suggested fix:** give symbol-only names a distinct id (e.g. encode the operator characters), and/or stop `resolve_local()` when a scope's parent is itself or has already been visited.

title: fix(csharp): never let a call bind to a same-named enum member (#4245)
body:
Fixes #4245.

#3795 is fixed for TYPE references (a base type or parameter type no longer resolves to a same-named enum member). Calls still could. The reported shape: invoking a delegate-typed field whose name happens to match one of its own enum's cases got a `calls` edge to the case instead of no edge — an enum member can never be the target of a call.

Traced this to **two** separate places, neither of which had the exclusion #3795 already applies for type lookup:

1. `graphify/extractors/engine.py`'s per-file `label_to_nid` — the shared bare-name-to-node map used by Ruby, C#, Java, Kotlin and more (per its own comment) to resolve a same-file call. No exclusion for a node that's the target of a `case_of` edge (the relation every one of those languages already emits per enum case).
2. The shared cross-file call resolver in `graphify/extract.py` already excludes a `case_of`/`defines` target as a candidate — but only for `rc.get("csharp_new")` (what `new X()` constructs), not for an ordinary C# call. Widened the same exclusion to any C# call.

Also threaded an optional `edges` parameter through `symbol_resolution.build_label_index` (defaulting to `None`, so its two existing call sites with just `nodes` are untouched) so it can apply the same exclusion when edges are available — kept for symmetry with the other two fixes even though the live pipeline doesn't currently route through that function.

Scoped to `case_of` targets only (not `defines`/property targets) for the per-file map, since the three repro shapes in the issue are all enum cases, and a `defines` target can legitimately be a callable variable in some other language that shares this same per-file map (e.g. a JS/Dart arrow function assigned to a variable) — didn't want to guess at a broader exclusion without a concrete failing case for it.

Verified against the issue's exact repro (the `Delegate(t)` case) and a control case (`Handles[i].Pause()` against a same-named `State.Pause` enum member elsewhere in the corpus, confirming the fix doesn't make a genuine call unresolved). Two new regression tests in `tests/test_csharp_enum_members.py`, confirmed to fail against pre-fix code (the control passes either way). Full suite passes clean with no failures at all once run with the correct module resolution (confirmed the one run that showed 26 failures was the editable-install trap — subprocess-based tests picking up a different checkout — not a real regression).

title: fix(csharp): give a generic and a non-generic type separate ids (#4249)
body:
Fixes #4249.

`name` is just the bare identifier for a C# type declaration; a `type_parameter_list` is a separate sibling node, so `Effect` and `Effect<T>` minted the exact same id and merged into one node. The common base-pair shape (`Effect<T> : Effect`, `Comparer<T> : Comparer`) then showed as a self-loop, and any member declared on the generic landed on the same node as the non-generic one.

Folds the declared arity into the id the same way C# metadata itself names a generic type (`` Effect`1 ``), so each arity gets its own node. The label is untouched (still just "Effect"), and a non-generic declaration (arity 0) keeps today's id exactly — no change for the overwhelmingly common case.

Also extended the same arity-awareness to a same-file `base_list` reference, so `Tween<T> : Effect<T>` (both in the same file) resolves to a real definition rather than a dangling stub or, worse, the unrelated non-generic sibling.

**Disclosed limitation, not fixed here:** the cross-file type index this extractor shares with ordinary type references (`_build_csharp_type_def_index` / `CsharpNameResolver`, from #3795/#3815) still picks one arbitrary candidate when more than one same-named definition exists for a namespace — it has no arity concept at all. So a generic subtype whose same-named generic base lives in a *different file* may still resolve to the wrong arity sibling rather than failing to resolve outright. Making that shared index arity-aware would mean adding arity to node metadata and threading a desired-arity parameter through every one of its callers (field/property/parameter/return type references, qualified calls, aliasing) — a meaningfully larger change I didn't want to risk alongside this fix. The node collapse and the resulting self-loop — the actual reported defect — are fixed regardless, in both the same-file and cross-file case (the nodes are always separate now; only which specific cross-file sibling an edge names can still be imprecise).

Verified against the issue's exact repro: before, one `Effect` node with `effects_demo_effect --inherits--> effects_demo_effect` (self-loop). After, two nodes and no self-loop; `Tween<T>`'s inherits edge (same file) correctly reaches the generic `Effect<T>` node, not the non-generic one. Two new regression tests in `tests/test_csharp_type_resolution.py`, confirmed to fail against pre-fix code. Full suite passes clean with correct module resolution (one unrelated, pre-existing Erlang cross-file-call gap is visible now that `tree-sitter-language-pack` is actually installed in this environment — untouched by this change, not something this PR causes or fixes).

title: fix(build): keep a method edge when a member constructs its own type
body:
Fixes #4248.

`Report.Fault()` belongs to `Report`, and the body also does `new Report()`. That is a `method` edge one way and a `calls` edge back. The default graph only keeps one edge between two nodes, and the call was the one that stuck. `Report` then had no `method` edge to `Fault`, so looking up the type's members skipped it.

A `method` or `contains` edge now wins when the other edge is a `calls` edge going the other way. A directed graph still keeps both, since those are two different edges. Edges that point the same way are unchanged.

On the usual undirected graph, `Fault --calls--> Report` is the edge that gets dropped.

title: fix(csharp): resolve calls through member chains, element access and constructors
body:
Closes #4246

Three more C# call shapes got no `calls` edge when the callee lived in another file: a call through a field of a typed receiver (`run.Sequence.Apply()`), a call on an array or list element (`_configs[i].WriteIds()`), and any call inside a constructor, since constructor bodies were never walked for calls at all.

Now the C# extractor records `[type of run, "Sequence"]` for a member chain and the element type for `xs[i].M()` (from `T[]`, `List<T>`, `IList<T>` or `IReadOnlyList<T>` fields, properties, parameters and locals, with the same scoping and shadowing rules as other receivers). `_resolve_csharp_member_calls` resolves the root type, looks up the field's declared type on that class or its bases through the field tables C# already exports, and then finds the method there like any other typed receiver. If any step is unknown or ambiguous there's no edge. Constructor bodies are walked now too, and since constructors have no node of their own, their calls come from the type node (the issue mentioned that as an option). `this.M()` and `base.M()` inside a constructor resolve through that type. Chains and element access that already bound within the same file are left as they were.

Limits: chains are only one field deep (`a.B.C.M()` and `this.a.B.M()` stay unresolved), and element access only works on a plain identifier (`this._items[i]` and `run.Items[i]` don't resolve). A constructor's call to a method of its own class shares a node pair with the existing `method` edge, so the cross-file pass skips it. Walking constructor bodies also adds the usual call-site `references` edges (for example, generic args of `CreateMap<A, B>()` inside an AutoMapper `Profile` constructor). Constructor calls also go through v8's existing name lookup for `new X()`, so the one wrong binding that already exists on v8 (`new System.ArgumentNullException` linking to AutoMapper's own internal `ArgumentNullException`, 11 edges) picks up 2 more from constructors.

Testing: new `tests/test_csharp_member_chain_calls.py` with 12 tests. The 6 positive ones fail on current v8, and the ambiguity, unknown-type, type-parameter, nested-list and #3797 control tests guard against wrong edges. The full suite on 3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14 has the same failures as v8. Ruff is clean and pyright shows no new findings. The three repros from the issue now give exactly the expected edges, and `Other.WriteIds` gets nothing. On MediatR, Polly, Newtonsoft.Json and AutoMapper the C# `calls` edges went from 469 to 480, 5483 to 5546, 14252 to 14421 and 3479 to 3537, with none removed. I spot-checked a sample of the new edges against the source and they were right.

AI-assisted (Grok Bot); each commit carries a Co-Authored-By line.

title: fix: make the test suite pass on Windows
body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes `uv run pytest tests` pass on Windows (10, Python 3.12), where it previously failed 29 tests. One real bug in `graphify/paths.py`; everything else is test-side.

**Real bug:** `_atomic_replace` (used by `write_text_atomic`) hands a read-only destination to `os_replace_with_fallback`. On Windows `os.replace` raises `PermissionError` for it, the fallback catches that and renames the destination aside, and the read-only file is silently overwritten. `test_atomic_writes::test_write_text_atomic_refuses_a_readonly_destination_without_leaking_a_temp` documents the intended behaviour (refuse). `_atomic_replace` now raises `PermissionError` for a read-only regular file on Windows (`os.name == "nt"`); POSIX behaviour is unchanged. The check is deliberately not in the shared `os_replace_with_fallback`, because install/cache/export callers must still be able to replace their own copies, which can be read-only (a regression test pins that).

**Test-side (no behaviour change on POSIX):**
- `encoding="utf-8"` where text was read/written with the cp1252 default
- compare home-relative paths where Git Bash prints MSYS-style (`/tmp/...`) paths
- pin `platform.system` to Linux in modules that assert the POSIX skill layout (gemini and hermes intentionally install elsewhere on Windows); the install roundtrip redirects `LOCALAPPDATA` into tmp so it cannot touch a real one
- `as_posix()` for expected portable `source_file` paths (terraform)
- add `USERPROFILE`/`SYSTEMROOT` to a subprocess env allowlist (`Path.home()` ignores `HOME` on Windows)
- shorten a directory name so the cache path stays under `MAX_PATH` (C include)
- retry a directory rename that a scanner can briefly block (`test_cli_export`)
- stamp the manifest row's `seen` explicitly instead of relying on a fast disk (`test_incremental_mtime_collision`); the gate only distrusts an mtime within 50 ms of `seen`, so the test failed whenever `save_manifest` took longer than that
- skip tests that need FIFOs, unix sockets, unprivileged symlinks, a deletable cwd, or a POSIX `python3` in `bash` when the platform lacks them (10 tests skip on Windows)

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Tests or CI

## Verification & Invariants

- Invariant: an atomic write never silently replaces a destination the user marked read-only, and never leaves a temp file behind (Windows). Covered by the existing `test_atomic_writes` test, which failed before this change. `os_replace_with_fallback` itself still replaces a read-only destination, covered by a new test.
- No generated or persisted state is affected; no skill fragments touched.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test. (existing test covers the `paths.py` fix)
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Limitations: the 10 tests that now skip on Windows no longer guard that code path there. Not run on Linux or macOS; the changes are meant to be no-ops on POSIX, but CI should confirm. `tests/test_skillgen_input_path_injection.py::test_step1_still_resolves_a_legitimate_path` now skips on Windows unless `bash` has a `python3` that can import graphify (e.g. WSL).

## How was this tested?

```text

uv run pytest tests -v        # Python 3.10.22: 6630 passed, 196 skipped, 0 failed

# Full suite before the review follow-up (dde1ec7):
uv run pytest tests -v        # Python 3.12.10: 6628 passed, 197 skipped, 0 failed
uv run pytest tests -v        # Python 3.13.16: 6628 passed, 197 skipped, 0 failed

# After the follow-up, the files it touches, on Python 3.13.16:
uv run pytest tests/test_atomic_writes.py tests/test_paths.py tests/test_install.py   tests/test_install_roundtrip.py tests/test_skill_auto_refresh.py   tests/test_install_references.py tests/test_uninstall_scope.py   # 290 passed, 8 skipped

ruff check <changed files>    # All checks passed
pyright graphify/paths.py     # 0 errors
```

title: Import builder resolves bare  to a same-stem local module (captures stdlib)
body:
## Summary

`graphify`'s import-graph builder resolves a bare `import <name>` to a local module that shares the same stem, which captures **stdlib imports as if they pointed at local files**.

## Repro

In a repo with a file at `pipeline/common/logging.py` (any module whose stem collides with a stdlib top-level name), a bare `import logging` anywhere in the tree is recorded as an edge whose target resolves to that local `pipeline/common/logging.py`, not to stdlib `logging`.

Measured on one real corpus before we worked around it:

- `logging`: 853 edges landed on `pipeline/common/logging.py`
- `types`: 60 edges → `pipeline/common/types.py`
- `io`: 9 edges → `pipeline/common/io.py`
- total 922 fabricated stdlib→local edges

## Why it's wrong

A bare import resolves from `sys.path`, so a module nested under the repo root can never be its target. The result is a fabricated import cycle and `logging.py` becoming the graph's top hub.

## Suggested fix

Prefer a real path/package match over a bare-stem match when resolving an import target. The local workaround we currently carry is a post-extraction filter (`filter_stdlib_name_collision_edges`), which we'd like to delete once upstream resolves bare-stem imports correctly.

_Reported by a downstream consumer of the graphify CLI (pipx `graphifyy`)._

title: Stub-rewire pass does not fire: cross-module refs to a single located type stay unbound
body:
## Summary

The stub-rewire pass (`_rewire_unique_stub_nodes`) does not fire, so cross-module references to a single located type never bind to the real definition.

## Repro

- A class `Settings` is defined exactly once at `config/settings/_models.py:38` (node `config_settings_models_settings`).
- 159 per-file `Settings` stub nodes (338 links) are emitted across the tree.
- The stub-rewire pass (`graphify/extract.py:2165`, called once at `:6128`) should bind those stubs to the single located definition, but after the build the stubs remain unbound.

## Candidate-count hypothesis

Two candidate causes were recorded by the reporting team (on their internal card GRAPHIFY-007): the pass is keyed on the bare name while the located definition is keyed on a module-qualified path, so the key never matches; and/or the pass runs before all located definitions are indexed, so the singleton lookup sees zero candidates. A minimal reproduction is one class plus one cross-module reference.

## Impact

Downstream code that relies on graph edges to trace "who uses `Settings`" sees 338 links to stubs and none to the real class, which defeats the stub-rewire feature.

_Reported by a downstream consumer of the graphify CLI (pipx `graphifyy`)._

title: feat(extract,detect): Apps Script, CSS/SCSS design tokens and an explicit secrets-filter override (#2498, #2698, #3473)
body:
Consolidates the outstanding fixes for three issues into one branch, rebased onto current `v8`. Every referenced PR was raised against an older `v8` revision and no longer applies; this is the single, current version. One previous version of this PR was self-reviewed and two real issues were found and fixed before opening (see **Review notes** below).

## What this fixes

### #2698 — classify `.gs`, `.css` and extensionless config files
- **`.gs` (Google Apps Script) is now code**: routed to the JavaScript extractor, the JS language/resolution family, the AST-cache bypass set and the rebuild hook. A GLSL/Gosu marker guard (`#version `, `gl_Position`, `EmitVertex`, `uses java.` …) leaves a real geometry shader / Gosu file without an extractor rather than force-parsing it as JS.
- **`.css` / `.scss` / `.less` are code.**
- **Well-known extensionless config/build files** (`.htaccess`, `Dockerfile`, `Makefile`, `Procfile`, `Vagrantfile`, …) are classified by filename as documents instead of being dropped as "not classified".

### #3473 — design-token systems were invisible to the graph
- New `graphify/extractors/css.py`: a brace-aware, comment/string-aware, dependency-free scan. It emits a node per custom-property definition in a root/theme context (`:root`, `:host`, `html`, `body`, `[data-theme…]`, `.dark`, `.theme-*`, `@theme`), a `defines_token` edge per definition, and collects `var(--x)` uses.
- Uses resolve to a same-file definition, or to exactly one cross-file definition; ambiguous or missing uses emit nothing (no fan-out).
- A custom property declared **locally** (outside a root context, e.g. a component overriding a theme token) shadows a same-named global, so no false cross-file edge is invented — while a file that also declares the token in `:root` keeps its own same-file edge.
- Wired through the incremental cache (`raw_token_uses`) and both id-remap passes; warm and cold extraction agree.

### #2498 — the filename-only secrets filter silently drops design-token files
The report has two distinct halves:
- **`.css` case (reporting defect):** `tokens.css` is now genuinely graphable, so the misleading "skipped as potentially sensitive" message for an unsupported extension is gone.
- **`tokens.json` / `tokens.contract.json` (real data loss):** `#3527` deliberately keeps bare plural `tokens` in data files excluded, so rather than weaken the default the fix is the **explicit override** the issue asked for (option 3): a wildcard-free `!path` entry in `.graphifyignore` (or `--exclude`) now overrides **only the Stage-3 name heuristic**.
  - A specific Stage-2 key file (`.env`, `id_rsa`, `server.pem`) or a credential-store directory is **never** rescued.
  - Glob entries (`!*.json`) are ignored, so a broad opt-in cannot silently start ingesting credential stores.
  - An entry is anchored to its own directory and matched case-sensitively; a leading `/` is anchor-exact, per gitignore semantics.
  - Only the **explicit** `.graphifyignore`/`--exclude` set is consulted — never `.gitignore`.
  - Default posture is unchanged: `tokens.json`, `oauth_token.json`, `api_token.txt`, `credentials.json`, `.token`, `secrets.json` all stay skipped unless explicitly overridden.
- **The skip is no longer silent:** `GRAPH_REPORT.md` gains a `## Skipped Files` section listing every excluded file by name, and the CLI skip notice names the escape hatch.

## PRs this supersedes

| PR | Subject | Status here |
|----|---------|-------------|
| #2747 | `.gs` only, minimal | superseded by the `.gs` support here |
| #3505 | `.gs` (comprehensive) | folded in |
| #3480 | CSS/SCSS design tokens | folded in, plus the local-shadow fix |
| #3067 | CSS/HTML UI + JS linkage | superseded by the token-focused design here |
| #2240 | Twig + SCSS | SCSS half superseded; Twig is out of scope for these issues |
| #1921 | `.graphifyinclude` override | superseded by `.graphifyignore` negation (`.graphifyinclude` was removed in #2112) |
| #3605 | closed omnibus | superseded |

All of the above no longer merge onto `v8`; this branch applies cleanly on `v8` @ `5b74d7d`.

## Review notes (self-review before opening)
Two independent verification passes were run. They caught and this branch fixes:
1. The override was initially reading the *merged* ignore set (including `.gitignore` and nested anchors) and matching case-insensitively — i.e. broader than the "exact `.graphifyignore` path" it promised. It now uses the explicit pattern set only, is anchor-scoped, and case-sensitive.
2. `var()` resolution initially ignored local custom-property shadowing, inventing false `EXTRACTED` `uses_token` edges between a component override and a theme token. Fixed, then narrowed so a file that also defines the token in `:root` keeps its same-file edge.

## Tests

New / extended:
- `tests/test_gs_apps_script.py` — `.gs` routing, GLSL/Gosu guard, node parity with `.js`.
- `tests/test_css.py` — CSS/SCSS/Less classification, token extraction, comments/strings/urls/nesting/themes, cross-file resolution, same-file precedence, local shadowing, warm cache.
- `tests/test_detect.py` — explicit-negation rescue, `.gitignore`-only negation does not rescue, anchor scoping, leading-slash anchoring, wildcard entries do not rescue, Stage-1/2 never rescued, dotfile classification.
- `tests/test_report.py` — `## Skipped Files` present/absent.

Local results (`v8` @ `5b74d7d`, Python 3.12, Windows):
- Focused suites: `test_detect.py` 304 passed / 1 skipped, `test_css.py` 25 passed, `test_report.py` 21 passed, `test_gs_apps_script.py` 10 passed, `test_extract.py` 289 passed / 4 skipped.
- `ruff check` on all changed files: clean.
- Full suite: **6699 passed, 24 failed, 184 skipped**. All 24 failures reproduce identically on a clean `v8` checkout — they are pre-existing Windows/environment failures (no `os.mkfifo`, read-only-file semantics, missing home dir under a stripped env, cp1252 unicode, and gemini/hermes install + watch/hook timing). None is in a file this branch touches.

## Known limitations
- The `.gs` sniff scans the first 256 KiB for GLSL/Gosu markers; a genuine Apps Script file that literally contains one of those substrings in a string or comment is left without an extractor (same outcome as MATLAB `.m`). Kept from #3505's conservative design.
- Tailwind-style utility-class → token inference is deliberately **not** attempted; only unambiguous `var()` references are resolved.
- The CSS extractor is `.css`/`.scss`/`.less`, not Sass indented syntax; `@import url(...)` prose is not resolved.

title: [Bug]: `path` answers a `file::symbol` endpoint from a same-name symbol in another file when the file holds no such symbol (exit 0, warning only)
body:
### What happened?

`graphify path` accepts a `file::symbol` endpoint whose file holds no such symbol and answers from a same-name symbol in **another** file. The route is printed on stdout, the only signal is a score warning on stderr, and the exit code is 0. `explain` handles the same qualifier correctly ("No node matching …").

A qualifier is the caller's way of saying "this file, not the others"; falling back to a score over the bare name returns a route from a module the caller explicitly excluded. The printed route carries labels only (no file, no node id), so it looks exactly like a correct answer. An agent that ignores stderr, or a wrapper that keeps stdout only, reads it as a confirmed call chain. On a real project (34k nodes, about two labels in three shared — every Next.js `route.ts` exports the same handful of names) this is the common case, not a corner.

### Steps to reproduce

Five files, no LLM:

```
src/billing/route.ts   import { chargeCard } from './charge';
                       export function readRoute(id: string) { return chargeCard(id); }
src/billing/charge.ts  export function chargeCard(id: string) { return `charged:${id}`; }
src/seats/route.ts     import { SeatInput } from './schema';
                       export function readRoute(id: string) { return SeatInput.parse(id); }
                       export function buildManifest() { return SeatInput; }
src/seats/schema.ts    export const SeatInput = { parse: (x: string) => x };
src/admin/route.ts     export function listAdmins() { return []; }
```

```
graphify update .          # 11 nodes, 11 edges
graphify path "src/admin/route.ts::readRoute" "chargeCard"
```

`src/admin/route.ts` defines no `readRoute`.

### Error output or graph output

```
$ graphify path "readRoute" "chargeCard"
Ambiguous: 'readRoute' matches 2 nodes in different files.        # correct: refused, exit 1
  src/seats/route.ts
    id: src_seats_route_readroute
  src/billing/route.ts
    id: src_billing_route_readroute
Retry with path::symbol using one of the paths above (e.g. <path>::readRoute()) or the full node id.

$ graphify path "src/admin/route.ts::readRoute" "chargeCard"
Shortest path (1 hops):
  readRoute() --calls [EXTRACTED]--> chargeCard()
warning: source match was ambiguous (top score 249.797, runner-up 249.797)     # stderr
exit=0

$ graphify explain "src/admin/route.ts::readRoute"
No node matching 'src/admin/route.ts::readRoute' found.            # correct
```

### Expected behavior

`path` with a qualifier that matches no node behaves like `explain`: it reports that `src/admin/route.ts` holds no `readRoute` (ideally listing the files that do) and exits non-zero.

Two small additions would make every answer checkable:

1. print the node id (or `file:line`) next to each label in the `path` output;
2. exit non-zero whenever the "match was ambiguous" warning fires on an explicitly qualified endpoint.

### Graphify version

0.9.82 (PyPI `graphifyy`). Same behaviour on 0.9.77.

### Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu)

### Python Version

3.14.4

### Installation Method

`pip install graphifyy==0.9.82` in a fresh venv (0.9.77 via pipx)

### Additional Environment Details

Related, not duplicates: #1969 (`explain` resolves ambiguous terms silently), #3917 (MCP: silent wrong matches on ambiguous names), #3485 (closed; `explain` ambiguity message).

title: [Feature]: symbol-level reference edges for value reads (constants, schemas) in JS/TS, not only file-level `imports`
body:
### Problem or use case

A function that reads an imported value (a constant, a schema object) has no edge to it: the graph holds only `file --imports--> symbol`. The function is reachable from the value only through `contains`, so impact questions stop at the file.

Reproduction (0.9.82, five TypeScript files, no LLM — the same project as in #4264):

```
src/seats/route.ts     import { SeatInput } from './schema';
                       export function readRoute(id: string) { return SeatInput.parse(id); }
                       export function buildManifest() { return SeatInput; }
src/seats/schema.ts    export const SeatInput = { parse: (x: string) => x };
```

```
$ graphify path "buildManifest" "SeatInput"
Shortest path (2 hops):
  buildManifest() <--contains [EXTRACTED]-- seats/route.ts --imports [EXTRACTED]--> SeatInput

$ graphify affected "SeatInput" --depth 2
Affected nodes for SeatInput
Relations: calls, indirect_call, references, imports, imports_from, dynamic_import, re_exports, inherits, extends, implements, uses, mixes_in, embeds, requires
Depth: 2
- seats/route.ts [imports] src/seats/route.ts:L1
```

`buildManifest()` and `readRoute()` both use `SeatInput` in their bodies. Consequences:

- `affected SeatInput` stops at the file: it cannot tell which of the file's functions are affected (in a 600-line module, that is the question);
- `path fn → const` always answers through the file, whether or not that function touches the value — a function in the same file that never uses it would get the identical route.

The `affected` relation list already names `references` and `uses`; in this reproduction neither is emitted for the value reads, while calls are (`readRoute() --calls--> chargeCard()` in the sibling module).

### Proposed solution

Emit `references` (or `uses`) from the enclosing function / method / class to an imported or module-level identifier it reads — the same resolution `calls` already does for call expressions, extended to identifier reads (`SeatInput`, `SeatInput.parse`, a constant passed as an argument; type-position uses could be optional).

### Alternatives considered

Confirming each file-level lead with a language server or `rg` after the graph query — that is what we do today; it works, but it means the graph cannot answer "which functions depend on this value" on its own.

### Area

AST extraction (JS/TS), `path` / `affected`

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Not at the moment.

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Additive edges: node ids unchanged, edge count grows. `affected` and `path` would return symbol-level results where they return file-level ones today, so default output for existing queries changes (more rows in `affected`, shorter routes in `path`).

### Additional context

Related, not a duplicate: #3252 (class/type references across files never rewire to the canonical definition) — this request is about value reads inside a function body.

Smaller note on the same output: the default `path` is documented as directed, yet the route above walks `contains` against its direction (`buildManifest() <--contains-- seats/route.ts`), and `--undirected` returns the same route. If containment is deliberately bidirectional, saying so in `--help` would help.

title: fix(csharp): type a var from the called method's return type
body:
Closes #4266

`var report = ServiceFactory.Get<IReport>(scope); report.Build()` got no `calls` edge to `IReport.Build`, while the same code with `IReport report = ...` did. A `var` was only typed when its initializer was `new T()`, and the factory usually lives in another file, so the extractor can't see its return type anyway.

Now the C# extractor records `var x = R.M<A>(...)` (with `R` a type name, a typed local/field/parameter, `this`, or no receiver) as a deferred receiver `[R, M, type args]` on calls made through `x`, and each method's declared return type and type-parameter count goes into the per-file tables C# already exports for the cross-file pass. `_resolve_csharp_member_calls` finds `M` on `R` (or its bases) the same way it finds any member call, and types `x` as `M`'s return type: `T Get<T>()` called as `Get<IReport>()` gives `IReport`, `List<T> CreateList<T>()` gives `List`, and `Widget Make()` gives `Widget`. There's no edge if `M` isn't declared in the corpus, if more than one overload is left after matching the number of type arguments, if the type argument is inferred, or if the return type is a class-level type parameter (`Box<T>.Value()`).

Limits: only a plain invocation as the initializer is handled. `await`, `?.`, chained calls (`a.B().C()`) and a generic receiver (`Factory<T>.Get()`) stay untyped. The variable's type is resolved with the same name lookup typed locals already use, so it carries over that lookup's existing gaps. On Polly, calls through a non-generic `ResiliencePipeline` end up on `ResiliencePipeline<T>`'s method of the same name, because the two types share one node (#4249); an explicitly typed `ResiliencePipeline p` does the same on v8.

Testing: new `tests/test_csharp_var_call_return_type.py` with 9 tests. The 4 positive ones (generic factory in the same file and across files, non-generic return, `List<T>` return) fail on current v8. The overload, missing-declaration, inferred-generic, class-type-parameter and explicit-type/`new` control tests make sure no wrong edges show up. The full suite on 3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14 has the same failures as v8. Ruff is clean and pyright shows no new findings. The issue's repro now gives `Consumer.Run() -> IReport.Build()` for both the one-file and two-file layouts. On MediatR, Polly, Newtonsoft.Json and AutoMapper the C# `calls` edges went from 477 to 477, 5284 to 5483, 14419 to 14423 and 3526 to 3534, with none removed. I checked a sample of the new edges against the source.

AI-assisted (Grok Bot); each commit carries a Co-Authored-By line.

title: Qualified annotation httpx.Response binds to unrelated local class _Response (EXTRACTED, 1.0)
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.83, `graphify update .`

## What happens

A Python annotation with a qualified external type, `httpx.Response`, gets a `references` edge to an unrelated local class named `_Response` in a test file. The edge is tagged `EXTRACTED` with confidence 1.0, although the code never mentions that class.

## Minimal repro

`app/client.py`

```python
import httpx


def read_body(response: httpx.Response) -> bytes:
    return response.content
```

`tests/test_fake.py`

```python
class _Response:
    """Stand-in for a urllib response."""

    def read(self):
        return b""
```

Run `graphify update .`. The graph then contains:

```
app_client_read_body --references--> tests_test_fake_response   EXTRACTED 1.0 ast L4
```

## Expected

No edge, or an edge to an external `httpx.Response` node. The `httpx.` qualifier means the annotation cannot name the local class.

## Likely cause

From reading the source (not verified with a patch): the annotation resolver appears to discard the qualifier (`engine.py`, around lines 112-116). The stub-rewiring step then strips leading underscores when it matches labels (`extract.py`, around lines 3456 and 3478), so `Response` and `_Response` compare equal and the one unique local definition is chosen.

## Impact

It creates false dependencies from production code to test code and presents them as certain, so impact analysis (`graphify affected`, `query`) can mislead.

body:
`hook-guard read` returns early unless the target's extension is in `_HOOK_SOURCE_EXTS` (`graphify/cli.py`, also on v8). PowerShell isn't in that list, although `detect.py` treats `.ps1`, `.psm1` and `.psd1` as code and they are extracted into the graph. So in a PowerShell repo the Read/Glob nudge never fires, only the search one does.

Repro (0.9.83): in a repo with a built `graphify-out/graph.json`, pipe `{"tool_name":"Read","tool_input":{"file_path":"script.ps1"}}` into `graphify hook-guard read`. Nothing is printed; the same payload with `server.js` prints the nudge.

Adding `.ps1` and `.psm1` to the tuple fixes it here. Other languages from `CODE_EXTENSIONS` seem to be missing too (`.dart`, `.ex`, `.sql`, ...), so deriving the list from there might be the better fix.

Fixes #4271. `graphify hook-guard read` returned early for `.ps1`, `.psm1`, and `.psd1` targets because the extension gate `_HOOK_SOURCE_EXTS` (`graphify/cli.py`) did not list them — even though `detect.py` classifies those extensions as code (`CODE_EXTENSIONS`) and they are extracted into the graph. In a PowerShell repo the Read/Glob nudge therefore never fired, only the search one did. This PR adds the three PowerShell extensions to `_HOOK_SOURCE_EXTS` and adds regression coverage in `tests/test_hook_guard.py`.
