title: `_rebuild_lock` unlinks `.rebuild.lock` on release, so two rebuilds can hold the lock at once (POSIX)
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.82 (same code in 0.8.40) · macOS (Darwin 25.2) · Python 3.11

## What happens

`graphify/watch.py` `_rebuild_lock` opens `graphify-out/.rebuild.lock` (L200), takes `fcntl.flock` (L209), and on release calls `LOCK_UN` (L244) and then **unlinks the path** (L254-258).

`flock` locks the open file (the inode), not the path. Once the path is unlinked while another process is already waiting on the old inode, a later caller creates a new inode and locks it immediately:

1. A holds the lock.
2. B, a blocking waiter (`graphify update` → `_rebuild_code(..., block_on_lock=True)`, cli.py:2563), opens the path → inode X and waits in `flock`.
3. A finishes: `LOCK_UN`, then `unlink(path)`. B now holds the lock on X, which no longer has a path.
4. C (another `graphify update`, a post-commit/post-checkout hook, or `watch`) opens the path → new inode Y → `flock` succeeds at once.

B and C are now both inside `_rebuild_code` and write the same outputs (`.graph.tmp.json`, `graph.json`, the report). This only needs one blocking waiter plus any later caller, so two terminals/agents running `graphify update` on the same repo are enough.

## Repro (no git repo needed)

```python
import multiprocessing as mp, tempfile, time
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.watch import _rebuild_lock

def holder(out, name, hold, q):
    with _rebuild_lock(out, blocking=True) as got:
        q.put((name, "enter", time.monotonic()))
        time.sleep(hold)
        q.put((name, "exit", time.monotonic()))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "graphify-out"
    q = mp.Queue()
    a = mp.Process(target=holder, args=(out, "A", 1.0, q)); a.start(); time.sleep(0.3)
    b = mp.Process(target=holder, args=(out, "B", 1.5, q)); b.start()   # waits on inode X
    a.join(); time.sleep(0.3)                                            # A unlocks + unlinks; B acquires X
    c = mp.Process(target=holder, args=(out, "C", 0.5, q)); c.start()   # new inode Y
    b.join(); c.join()
    ev = sorted((q.get() for _ in range(6)), key=lambda e: e[2])
    for n, k, t in ev:
        print(f"{t - ev[0][2]:5.2f}s {n} {k}")
```

Output on 0.9.82:

```
 0.00s A enter
 1.00s A exit
 1.00s B enter
 1.38s C enter      <- C enters while B is still holding the lock
 1.88s C exit
 2.50s B exit
```

## Expected

At most one holder of the rebuild lock at a time.

## Possible fixes

- Keep the lock file on release (rewrite/truncate the PID line instead of unlinking). Tools that currently poll for the file's absence could try a non-blocking `flock`, or read an explicit "done" marker.
- Or keep unlink-on-release but make acquisition robust: after `flock` succeeds, compare `os.fstat(fh.fileno()).st_ino` with `os.stat(lock_path).st_ino` and retry when they differ (or when the path is gone).

Related: #858 (unlink was added there for the stale-PID problem), #1037, #1059, #3881.

Workaround we use for now: serialize every call through a lock file that is never removed, e.g. `/usr/bin/lockf -k .git/graphify-update.lock graphify update .` on macOS (`flock` from util-linux on Linux).

title: Full-corpus rebuild requests are dropped on lock contention (log says "changes queued"), and a full rebuild never drains late incremental work
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.82 · macOS 26.2 (arm64) · Python 3.11.15
**Related:** #1059 (incremental requests are now queued — this is the part that fix left out), #4273 (separate lock bug)

## What happens

`_rebuild_code` in `graphify/watch.py` queues only incremental requests before trying the non-blocking lock:

- L1602-1603: `if changed_paths is not None and not block_on_lock: _queue_pending(...)`
- L1604-1608: if the lock is busy, it prints `Rebuild already in progress for ... - changes queued.` and returns `False`.
- L1627-1631: the late-arrival drain runs only `if merged is not None`, i.e. only when the lock holder was an incremental rebuild ("A full rebuild already saw everything").

That leaves two gaps.

**1. A full-corpus request that loses the lock is dropped, and the log says it was queued.**
The post-checkout hook body (`hooks.py:280`, `_rebuild_code(_root, force=_force)`) and `watch` (`watch.py:2624`, `_rebuild_code(watch_path)`) both ask for a full rebuild with the non-blocking lock. If a post-commit rebuild (or anything else) holds the lock at that moment, nothing is queued, the call returns `False`, and the message still says `changes queued`. The running incremental rebuild covers only its own changed paths, so the files the checkout touched never reach the graph.

**2. Incremental work queued while a full rebuild runs is not applied by that rebuild.**
"A full rebuild already saw everything" holds only for files changed before it walked the corpus. A post-commit hook that fires after the walk queues its paths in `.pending_changes`; the full rebuild then skips the drain, so those paths stay queued and are missing from the graph until some later rebuild happens to run.

## Repro (no git repo needed)

Gap 1 (`repro_full_rebuild_drop.py`):

```python
import multiprocessing as mp, tempfile, time
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.watch import _rebuild_code, _rebuild_lock

def hold(out, seconds):
    with _rebuild_lock(out, blocking=True):
        time.sleep(seconds)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    (root / "a.py").write_text("def f():\n    return 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    out = root / "graphify-out"
    p = mp.Process(target=hold, args=(out, 2.0)); p.start(); time.sleep(0.5)
    full_ok = _rebuild_code(root)                     # post-checkout / watch call
    print("full rebuild returned:", full_ok, "| queued:", (out / ".pending_changes").exists())
    inc_ok = _rebuild_code(root, changed_paths=[root / "a.py"])   # post-commit call
    print("incremental rebuild returned:", inc_ok, "| queued:", (out / ".pending_changes").exists())
    p.join()
```

Output:

```
[graphify watch] Rebuild already in progress for /private/var/.../tmpwuqtopc8 - changes queued.
full rebuild returned: False | queued: False
[graphify watch] Rebuild already in progress for /private/var/.../tmpwuqtopc8 - changes queued.
incremental rebuild returned: False | queued: True
```

Gap 2 (`repro_late_incremental.py`) — the inner full rebuild is slowed after it writes the graph, so the incremental call arrives after the walk:

```python
import json, multiprocessing as mp, tempfile, time
from pathlib import Path
import graphify.watch as w
ORIG = w._rebuild_code

def slow_full(root):
    def slowed(watch_path, **kw):
        if kw.get("acquire_lock") is False and kw.get("changed_paths") is None:
            ok = ORIG(watch_path, **kw); time.sleep(2.0); return ok
        return ORIG(watch_path, **kw)
    w._rebuild_code = slowed   # the outer call looks up the inner call by global name
    ORIG(root)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    (root / "a.py").write_text("def f():\n    return 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    out = root / "graphify-out"
    p = mp.Process(target=slow_full, args=(root,)); p.start(); time.sleep(1.0)
    (root / "a.py").write_text("def f():\n    return 1\n\ndef g_added_late():\n    return 2\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print("incremental returned:", ORIG(root, changed_paths=[root / "a.py"]),
          "| queued:", (out / ".pending_changes").exists())
    p.join()
    labels = {str(n.get("label", "")) for n in json.loads((out / "graph.json").read_text())["nodes"]}
    print("after full rebuild finished -> pending still queued:", (out / ".pending_changes").exists(),
          "| g_added_late in graph:", any("g_added_late" in l for l in labels))
```

Output:

```
[graphify watch] Rebuild already in progress for /private/var/.../tmpoedfeyzl - changes queued.
incremental returned: False | queued: True
after full rebuild finished -> pending still queued: True | g_added_late in graph: False
```

## Expected

- A full request that cannot take the lock is recorded (for example a "full" marker next to `.pending_changes`), and the lock holder runs one more full pass before releasing.
- After any rebuild finishes — full or incremental — the holder drains `.pending_changes` that arrived during the run.
- The "changes queued" message is printed only when something was actually queued.

title: feat(skill): run the pipeline as `graphify pipeline` subcommands, no inline Python (#197)
body:
## What this fixes

Closes the remaining work in #197.

The Graphify agent skill delivered **every** pipeline step — and, on demand, every reference flow — as inline Python inside a bash string:

```bash
$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
import json
from graphify.detect import detect
# ... 10-20 lines of Python, with # comments
"
```

In Claude Code that trips two content-based approval heuristics **once per step**:

1. **`command_substitution`** — from `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)`.
2. **"Newline followed by `#` inside a quoted argument"** — from the multi-line Python comments.

Neither can be satisfied by permission allow-rules, so a single run cost roughly **30 manual "Yes" clicks** and the skill was close to unusable without hand-patching it.

## How it's fixed

Every step is now a plain console command. The step bodies live in a new `graphify/pipeline.py` and are exposed as `graphify pipeline <step>`:

| Old inline block | New command |
|---|---|
| `detect(...)` + write sidecar | `graphify pipeline detect <path>` |
| `collect_files` + `extract` | `graphify pipeline extract-ast <path>` |
| empty `.graphify_semantic.json` | `graphify pipeline empty-semantic` |
| `check_semantic_cache(...)` | `graphify pipeline cache-check <path> --prompt-file SPEC` |
| chunk merge | `graphify pipeline merge-chunks` |
| `save_semantic_cache(...)` | `graphify pipeline save-cache <path> --prompt-file SPEC` |
| cached+new merge | `graphify pipeline merge-semantic` |
| AST+semantic merge | `graphify pipeline merge-extraction` |
| build/cluster/analyze/report | `graphify pipeline build <path> [--directed]` |
| health check | `graphify pipeline diagnose <path>` |
| curated labels | `graphify pipeline label <path> --labels '<json>'` |
| manifest + cost | `graphify pipeline save-manifest <path>` |
| cleanup | `graphify pipeline cleanup` |

The on-demand reference flows are converted the same way, with seven more steps plus existing commands:

- **query** → `graphify pipeline vocab`, `graphify query`, `graphify path`, `graphify explain`, `graphify save-result`
- **update** → `graphify pipeline detect-incremental | code-only-check | empty-extract | update-merge | graph-diff`
- **add / watch** → `graphify add`, `graphify watch` (now parses `--debounce` and defaults to the `.graphify_root` marker)
- **transcribe** → `graphify pipeline transcribe`
- **exports (MCP)** → the `graphify-mcp` console script instead of `-m graphify.serve`

Because every step is a console-script call, `Bash(graphify *)` becomes an allowlistable prefix, the `cat`-to-interpreter indirection disappears, and the security surface shrinks: arguments go through argparse instead of being interpolated into a Python string.

### The skill is generated — the fragment is the source of truth

`graphify/skill*.md` and `graphify/skills/*/references/*.md` are rendered from `tools/skillgen/fragments/` by `python -m tools.skillgen`. The edits are in the fragments (`core/core.md`, `references/**`, `query-stub/default.md`); the ~200 generated artifacts and the `expected/` snapshots are regenerated and blessed (`python -m tools.skillgen --bless`).

## Verification

- **Byte-identical output.** The old inline-Python blocks and the new subcommands were run side by side on a real corpus: `.graphify_detect.json`, `.graphify_ast.json`, `.graphify_semantic.json`, `.graphify_extract.json`, `.graphify_analysis.json`, `graph.json`, `manifest.json`, and `GRAPH_REPORT.md` are all identical (report modulo its timestamp). Same graph, different delivery.
- **No new test failures.** Rebased onto `v8` (`e8eb76e7`, 0.9.89). Full suite in this environment: 7911 passed, 216 skipped, 10 failed; all 10 fail identically on a clean `upstream/v8` (3 `test_hooks`, 1 wheel build, 2 `os.getcwd` subprocess, 1 `@/` alias resolution, 3 `test_ingest_url_type` Windows symlink `readlink`), none in code this PR touches.
- **New tests.** `tests/test_pipeline_cli.py` (pipeline steps end to end, including the incremental-update flow, the `#479` shrink guard + `--force`, `--no-gitignore`, `GRAPHIFY_OUT`, and the boolean-flag/positional parsing) and `tests/test_skill_no_inline_python.py` (a drift guard that fails if any split host or reference reintroduces an inline `-c` block).
- **Reviewed twice by a separate agent**; all findings fixed (nested `graphify-out` from a wrong `cache_root`, `merge-chunks` erroring on the all-cached path, `--no-gitignore`/`--force` silently dropped, a boolean flag swallowing the following path, non-numeric label keys crashing, `GRAPHIFY_OUT` ignored, stale fallback prose, and the MCP config caveat).

## Known blocker / deliberately out of scope: the aider & devin monoliths

`skill-aider.md` and `skill-devin.md` still contain inline Python (37 and 39 `-c` blocks). **This is not a capability gap — it's a deliberately isolated, high-blast-radius change**, and it is not what #197 reports (those are Aider and Devin, not Claude Code).

Why they're separate:

1. **They aren't generated from `core.md` + references.** `gen.render()` returns `_read_fragment("core/{aider|devin}.md")` verbatim — each is a **hand-maintained 1,300–1,400-line single file** that duplicates the entire pipeline *and* every reference flow inline. Converting them is the same work as everything in this PR, repeated twice.

2. **They're frozen against a pinned v8 blob.** `monolith_roundtrip` (`tools/skillgen/gen.py:1232`) diffs the rendered monolith against `roundtrip_ref` (a pinned v8 commit) and requires **every non-blank changed line** to match a predicate in `_SANCTIONED_MONOLITH_DIFFS` (19 predicates). So a conversion there also has to add a new sanctioned-diff predicate and re-validate the round-trip — the guard exists precisely to stop arbitrary drift, and touching it is a wide, cross-cutting change.

3. **Different hosts.** Aider and Devin have their own delivery mechanism; the Claude Code heuristics in #197 don't apply to them.

I chose to keep this PR scoped, correct, and low-risk rather than fold a 76-block rewrite of two frozen files into it. The monolith conversion is a clean follow-up PR on its own.

## Scope summary

- ✅ **Claude Code skill set** (`skill.md` + `skills/claude/references/*`): zero inline Python, zero `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)`. Only Step 1's one-time interpreter *detection* remains (inherent to installing/detecting graphify, and it is a single block, not per-step).
- ✅ **All other split hosts** (Codex, Windows, opencode, kilo, copilot, claw, droid, amp, trae, kiro, pi, vscode, agents) and **all references**: zero non-bootstrap inline `-c`.
- ⏭️ **aider/devin monoliths**: unchanged, tracked as a follow-up (see above).

Ref #114 (which fixed only the `save_query_result` block).

title: fix(watch): don't drop full rebuilds when the lock is busy (#4274)
body:
Fixes #4274.

## Problem

#1059 made incremental rebuild requests survive lock contention by queueing their paths in `.pending_changes`. Two gaps remained in `_rebuild_code`:

1. **Full-corpus requests were dropped.** A full request (post-checkout hook, `watch`) that lost the non-blocking lock queued nothing, returned `False`, and still logged `changes queued`. The lock holder only covered its own change set, so files touched by the checkout never reached the graph.
2. **Full rebuilds never drained late work.** The late-arrival drain was skipped for full rebuilds ("a full rebuild already saw everything"), but that only holds for files changed before the corpus walk. Paths a post-commit hook queued after the walk stayed in `.pending_changes` until some unrelated rebuild ran.

## Fix

- A full request that cannot take the lock leaves a `.pending_full` marker beside `.pending_changes` (`_queue_pending_full` / `_drain_pending_full`).
- When the lock holder starts, a queued marker upgrades the run to a full rebuild (which supersedes queued incremental paths).
- The late-arrival drain now runs after every rebuild, full or incremental. A marker that appears mid-run triggers one more full pass; queued paths trigger an incremental pass. Still bounded by `_PENDING_DRAIN_MAX_PASSES`.
- `changes queued` is printed only when something was actually queued (an empty change set now logs `nothing to queue`).

**Behaviour change worth noting:** an incremental holder that finds a full request waiting now does a full rebuild instead of its incremental one. Slower for that one run, but it's the only way the full request gets honoured.

## Verification

- Both repro scripts from #4274 pass after the change: the contended full request leaves the marker, and the late `g_added_late` function lands in `graph.json` with `.pending_changes` empty afterwards.
- 5 new regression tests in `tests/test_watch.py`. All 5 fail on `v8` HEAD and pass with this change:
  - full request queues a marker on contention
  - empty change set does not claim "changes queued"
  - incremental holder runs a full pass for a marker queued mid-run
  - incremental holder upgrades to full when a marker is already queued
  - full rebuild drains incremental work queued mid-run
- `tests/test_watch.py`: 186 passed, 3 skipped. Hook/watch/rebuild subset (`-k "hook or watch or rebuild or pending"`): 615 passed, 13 skipped.

Thanks to @Ethan-JY-Park for the detailed report and repro scripts.

title: fix(watch): close the rebuild lock unlink-vs-flock race (#4273)
body:
Fixes #4273.

`flock` locks the open file's inode, not the path. Release unlinked the path after unlocking, so a blocked waiter already parked in `flock()` could end up holding the lock on an orphaned inode with no path at all, while a later caller opened the path fresh, got a brand-new inode that was never locked, and acquired it immediately — two callers running the rebuild at once, writing the same outputs.

Went with the second of the issue's two suggested fixes (keep unlink-on-release, make acquisition robust), since the first (keep the lock file, truncate/rewrite the PID instead) would change the "poll for absence" contract external tooling already relies on:

1. **Reordered release**: unlink now happens *before* `flock(LOCK_UN)` on the POSIX path. `flock` only ever wakes a blocked waiter at the unlock call, so doing the unlink first guarantees it has already happened by the time any waiter's `flock()` can return — this closes the exact gap where a stat-based check could read the path as still valid moments before it disappears under it. (Confirmed this ordering matters empirically: the stat-check alone, with the old unlock-then-unlink order, did *not* fix the race — the window was still open.)
2. **Stat-based verification on top of the reorder**: after `flock` succeeds, compare the locked file's `(st_dev, st_ino)` against whatever currently lives at the path; retry against a fresh `open()` when they differ or the path is gone. Bounded (100 attempts) so a pathological unlink/recreate storm gives up rather than spinning forever, with the same outcome as losing the non-blocking race.

Windows (`msvcrt`) is untouched — byte-range locks there are tied to an open handle in a way that already prevents this, and the issue is explicitly POSIX-specific.

Verified against the issue's own exact repro script (multiprocessing, no git repo needed): before, `C` reliably entered while `B` still held the lock across every run; after, `C` only enters once `B` exits, across every run. New regression test in `tests/test_watch.py` mirroring the same repro shape, confirmed to fail reliably against pre-fix code (3/3 runs) and pass reliably with the fix (3/3 runs). Full suite passes (only the one pre-existing, unrelated Erlang cross-file-call gap, visible now that `tree-sitter-language-pack` is installed in this environment).

title: Git hook doesn't update the graph for files with non-English characters in their name
body:
## What's happening

If you use graphify's git hooks (`graphify hook install`), the graph is supposed to update itself every time you commit.

But if the file you changed has a name with non-English characters, like `naïve.py`, `données/app.py`, `用户.py` or `сервис.py`, your changes never make it into the graph. Files with plain English names in the same commit update just fine.

There's no error or warning. The log says the graph was rebuilt, so you'd have no idea anything was missing.

## How to see it for yourself

1. Make a new folder with two files: `plain.py` and `naïve.py`
2. Run `git init`, commit everything, then run `graphify update .` and `graphify hook install`
3. Add a new function to both files and commit again
4. Look at the graph: the new function in `plain.py` is there, but the one in `naïve.py` isn't

## Why it happens

When the hook asks git which files changed, git writes non-English names in an escaped form, so `naïve.py` comes out as `"na\303\257ve.py"`. The hook takes that literally, can't find a file with that name, and quietly skips it.

## What should happen

Files should update in the graph no matter what characters are in their name.

## Workaround for now

Run this once and git will print file names normally:

```
git config --global core.quotePath false
```

Running `graphify update .` also fixes the graph, since it rebuilds everything.

## Who this affects

Anyone using the git hooks on a project with non-English file or folder names, which covers a lot of projects in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian, French, German and more.

---

**Version:** graphify 0.9.84 (current `v8`) · macOS 26.4 · Python 3.14

title: fix(hooks): pick up changed files with non-ASCII names (#4278)
body:
Fixes #4278.

## What this fixes

The git hook wasn't updating the graph for files with non-English characters in their name (like `naïve.py` or `用户.py`). Git was handing the hook an escaped version of the name, the hook couldn't find a file called that, and the change was quietly skipped.

## What changed

- The hook now asks git for file names as they really are, so `naïve.py` comes through as `naïve.py`.
- A few rare names still get escaped by git (names with quotes or backslashes in them). The hook now decodes those back to the real name too.

## How I tested it

- Made a real git repo with the hooks installed and committed changes to `plain.py`, `naïve.py`, `中文/用户.py` and `say "hi".py`. Before this fix only `plain.py` was updated in the graph. After it, all four are.
- Added tests: one runs a real git commit and checks the hook gets every file name right, and one checks the decoding on its own. They fail on the current `v8` and pass with this change.
- Full test suite passes.

## Heads up

People who already have the hooks installed need to run `graphify hook install` again to get the fix. `graphify hook status` already tells them their hook is out of date.

title: fix(extract): explain a semantic omission that was not a truncation (#4101)
body:
Addresses the second of #4101's suggested improvements: making the message actionable when a chunk omission is not a truncation problem.

With a doc-heavy corpus packed into a single oversized chunk, the model can return a complete, well-formed response that simply omits some of the dispatched files — zero truncated, zero hollow, just incomplete coverage. The existing message ("a re-run will retry them") reads as transient, but re-sending the same chunk at the same `--token-budget` reproduces the exact same omission every time. With library-default timeouts and retries, a retry loop on an oversized chunk can burn a very long time while presenting as "the semantic index never finishes," when it's actually a coverage gap at the current chunk size — the issue's own measurement showed coverage going from 20% to 90% purely by lowering `--token-budget` from 60000 to 15000, no other change.

Added a conditional note to the existing "semantic extraction is incomplete" message: only when every omission this run came from a chunk that did **not** truncate, it now says so explicitly and points at `--token-budget` as the lever that actually helps. Every other case (including a mix of omission + truncation in the same run, where the omission is no longer provably a pure coverage gap) keeps the exact existing message, unchanged.

Scoped to this one message-wording improvement. The issue's other two suggestions (lowering the default `token_budget` or deriving it from corpus size, and capping retries for this specific case) are behavior changes with real tuning tradeoffs across different models/corpora that I didn't want to guess at without the kind of real-world measurement the issue's author has — this is a real-API-dependent LLM pipeline I can't easily verify tuning changes for in this environment.

Verified via this repo's existing mock-based test harness (`tests/test_hollow_chunks_arm_shrink_guard.py`, no real LLM API needed — it stubs `extract_corpus_parallel` directly). Three new regression tests: the note fires with the token-budget pointer on a pure-omission run, stays silent on a truncated run, and stays silent when omission and truncation occur together. Confirmed to fail against pre-fix code (the two negative-case tests hold either way). Full suite passes (excluding one known slow, network-dependent test file unrelated to this change — `test_skillgen_input_path_injection.py`, which spawns real subprocesses that attempt a PyPI fallback install in this sandboxed environment; also confirmed the one other failure in a targeted rerun was the pre-existing editable-install-trap, not a regression).

title: Node IDs drop the file extension (and doc IDs the path), so distinct entities in x.py/x.html or a/x.md/b/x.md collide and one is lost
body:
On 0.9.83, `graphify extract --backend claude-cli` warns (`dedup.py:505`):

```
node 'firmware_lib_portal' is minted by two different files — keeping 'portal.py' from 'firmware/lib/portal.py', dropping 'Brick provisioning portal (portal.html)' from 'firmware/lib/portal.html'
node 'protocol' is minted by two different files — keeping 'protocol' from 'docs/protocol.md', dropping 'protocol (top-level)' from 'docs/firmware/protocol.md'
```

Both are two distinct entities, not one entity seen twice:

1. **Extension dropped.** `portal.py` and `portal.html` sit side by side; the ID is derived from the path stem. A Python module and the HTML page it serves share a stem by convention (same for `x.ts`/`x.css`, `x.c`/`x.h`, `x.py`/`x.md`).
2. **Path dropped.** For the doc nodes the ID is the bare name `protocol`, so a repo-level `docs/protocol.md` and a subsystem `docs/firmware/protocol.md` collide.

The suggested workaround (extract per subfolder, then `merge-graphs`) cannot help case 1 — both files are in the same folder — and is heavy for case 2. This differs from #3352 (one concept attributed to the wrong page): here two concepts become one.

It recurs on every full rebuild. Across four repos we lose 10+ nodes per build this way, mostly where a component's `README.md` and the code it documents collide (10 such warnings in our largest repo alone).

**Suggestion:** include the extension in file-derived IDs (e.g. `…_portal_py` / `…_portal_html`), and give semantic doc nodes a path-qualified ID — or disambiguate on collision instead of dropping.

Environment: graphifyy 0.9.83, Linux, Python 3.14, claude-cli backend (Sonnet), `--token-budget 4500`.

title: fix(dedup): keep distinct files that mint the same node id (#4281)
body:
Fixes #4281

## What does this PR do?
Two distinct files can derive the same node id (`portal.py`/`portal.html`, or a bare `protocol` from `docs/protocol.md` and `docs/firmware/protocol.md`). Dedup collapsed them to one node with a warning, losing a real entity on every rebuild. Now each file keeps its own node: the best-ranked file keeps the id, the others get a path- or extension-qualified id (`firmware_lib_portal_html`), and their edges follow. Ids no file derives from its own path still collapse with the existing warning.

## Type of change
- [x] Bug fix

## How was this tested?
- tests/test_dedup.py (107 passed), including new tests for both cases and order-independence; two old tests that asserted the "one entity is lost" behavior were updated
- Full suite: only pre-existing failures (test_hooks shebang test fails without this change; some test_extract tests fail under -n 4 with or without it)
- Checked through build() with semantic nodes matching the issue

title: [Bug]: Rust: a cross-file reference to a type with impl blocks in other files stays a sourceless stub
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

A Rust type that is declared once and has `impl` blocks in other files gets one sourced node per file: the declaration (`struct Thing` in `a.rs`) and one node per `impl Thing { ... }` block (in `b.rs`). Only the declaration node carries `_rust_declaration_count`.

A cross-file reference to the type (`use crate::a::Thing;` and `fn make(t: Thing)` in `c.rs`) is emitted as a sourceless stub by `ensure_named_node` in `extractors/rust.py`, as expected. `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` in `extract.py` should then collapse that stub onto the declaration. It doesn't: `real_by_label` holds two type-like candidates for `Thing` (the declaration and the `impl` node), so `len(candidates) != 1` and the stub is left unresolved. In a larger corpus, `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids` then bakes the referencing file into the stub ids (`..._tests_roles_rs_role`, `..._src_generate_rs_matchsetup`). They then appear as extra, sourceless copies of the type in `explain` and in the report.

**Expected:** the reference binds to `src_a_thing`. The name is not genuinely ambiguous: there is exactly one declaration, and the other candidate is an `impl` block for that same type, not a rival definition.

**Actual:** `src_c_make` references a sourceless `thing` stub, and so do the `imports_from` edges from `src_b` and `src_c`.

In a ~60-file Rust/Bevy workspace this left 34 sourceless stubs for just 3 types (`Attributes` ×15, `MatchSetup` ×12, `Role` ×7). `MatchSetup`'s declaration had 4 edges instead of 24, so `affected`/`explain` on it silently missed most of its users.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p repro/src && cd repro
cat > src/a.rs <<'EOF'
pub struct Thing {
    pub n: u32,
}
EOF
cat > src/b.rs <<'EOF'
use crate::a::Thing;

impl Thing {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Thing { n: 0 }
    }
}
EOF
cat > src/c.rs <<'EOF'
use crate::a::Thing;

pub fn make(t: Thing) -> u32 {
    t.n
}
EOF
graphify update .
```

Then list the `Thing` nodes, and the edges into them, from `graphify-out/graph.json`.

### Error output or graph output

```text
node src_a_thing      source_file="src/a.rs" L1   (_rust_declaration_count = 1)
node src_b_thing      source_file="src/b.rs" L3   (impl block)
node src_b_thing_new  source_file="src/b.rs" L4
node thing            source_file=""              <- sourceless stub

edge src_b      -> thing   imports_from  L1      <- should be src_a_thing
edge src_c      -> thing   imports_from  L1      <- should be src_a_thing
edge src_c_make -> thing   references    L3      <- should be src_a_thing
```

Control: with `src/b.rs` removed (no `impl` block elsewhere), the stub is rewired as expected:

```text
src_c      -> src_a_thing  imports_from
src_c_make -> src_a_thing  references
sourceless Thing stubs: 0
```

### Graphify version

0.9.84. Also reproduced on a clean checkout of `v8` at `1d1e03b`.

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.15.0. Not in the dropdown; it's the interpreter uv picked for both the tool install and the clean checkout.

### Installation Method

`uv tool install` (recommended). Also reproduced from source: `git clone` of `v8`, then `uv sync` and `uv run python -m graphify update <repro>`.

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables are set. The run is `graphify update .`, which is AST-only and uses no LLM backend. A clean checkout of `v8` reproduces it.

### Additional context

Related but different causes of the same phantom-stub symptom:
- #3782: same-file forward reference when the name is declared in 2+ files. That fix covers the same-file case only, and the issue notes that "a genuine cross-file reference to an ambiguous name has no single correct target". This case isn't genuinely ambiguous.
- #1402: sourced stubs blocking the rewire.

Possible fix, in `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes`, right after the exact-label lookup:

```python
candidates = real_by_label.get(_node_label_key(stub), [])
if len(candidates) > 1:
    declared = [c for c in candidates if c.get("_rust_declaration_count")]
    if len(declared) == 1:
        candidates = declared
```

This stays fail-closed. It only fires when exactly one candidate is a declaration, so two real `struct Sink` declarations in parallel modules still leave the stub unresolved, as in #3782. I've applied it locally: it removes all 34 stubs, with the same edge count and no dangling edges. I haven't run the upstream test suite against it.

title: fix(extract): bind Rust stubs past impl blocks to the single declaration
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4283.

A Rust type that is declared once and has `impl` blocks in other files gets one node per file: the `struct`/`enum`/`trait` declaration, plus one node per `impl Thing { … }` block. A cross-file reference to the type is emitted as a sourceless stub. `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` should then collapse that stub onto the declaration, but it requires exactly one type-like candidate per label. The `impl` nodes count as candidates too, so the rewire gave up and left the reference on the stub. In a ~60-file Rust workspace this left 34 sourceless stubs for 3 types, and `explain`/`affected` on those types missed most of their users.

The change applies when an exact-label lookup returns several candidates, all of them Rust nodes (`_lang_family(...) == "rust"`), and exactly one of them carries `_rust_declaration_count == 1`. In that case the stub binds to that one. Only struct/enum/trait declarations set that marker in `extractors/rust.py`; `impl` nodes never do. Nothing else in the rewire pass changes.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** a stub is only bound when the target is unambiguous. One Rust declaration plus any number of Rust `impl` blocks is one type, so it binds. These cases stay ambiguous, and the stub is kept (fail-closed):
- two or more declarations of the same name, whether in separate nodes or folded into one node by same-file inline modules (`_rust_declaration_count == 2`);
- a same-named candidate in another language. The marker only tells a Rust declaration from a Rust `impl` block; it says nothing about, for example, a TypeScript class. This is the same rule the split-impl-block pass already uses (see the `declared_type_count` comment in `extract.py`): "2+ declarations sharing a bare name means the name itself is genuinely ambiguous; 0 or 1 means every same-labeled node … is safe to pool". It also stays consistent with #3782, where a genuine cross-file reference to a twice-declared name keeps its stub.

**Tests**, all in `tests/test_multilang.py`:
- `test_rust_cross_file_reference_skips_impl_blocks_in_other_files`: the #4283 repro (`a.rs` declares `Thing`, `b.rs` has `impl Thing`, `c.rs` references it), checked cold and from the warm cache. It **fails on `v8` without the fix** ("sourceless Thing stub left behind") and passes with it.
- Fail-closed guards, which must keep the sourceless stub:
  - `test_rust_cross_file_reference_to_twice_declared_type_keeps_its_stub`: two real `struct Thing` declarations.
  - `test_rust_declaration_tiebreak_keeps_stub_beside_another_language`: a Rust `struct Thing` plus a TypeScript `class Thing`.
  - `test_rust_declaration_tiebreak_keeps_stub_for_declarations_folded_in_one_node`: `mod x { struct Thing }` and `mod y { struct Thing }` in one file, plus an `impl Thing` elsewhere.

  The last two were added after the automated review (second commit, `d2a5d8f`). Both **fail on the first commit (`52dcf0c`)** and pass now. All three guards pass on unmodified `v8`.

**Persisted state:** none is invalidated. The change only affects which existing node a stub's edges are redirected to during extraction. Graphs built before this change keep their stubs until the next `graphify update`.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Limitations:**
- The tiebreak only runs when every candidate is a Rust node, so other languages, and mixed-language name clashes, behave exactly as before.
- A reference to a name with two or more real declarations still stays a stub, by design. This includes cfg-gated twins in one file (`#[cfg(unix)] struct X; #[cfg(windows)] struct X;`), which fold into one node with a count of 2, the same as the split-impl-block pass treats them.
- Not covered here: the fully qualified `crate::b::X` tie-break mentioned in the #3782 follow-up comment.

## How was this tested?

On Windows 11, from a clone of `v8` at `1d1e03b` (full history).

First commit (`52dcf0c`), Python 3.12.15:

```text
uv sync --all-extras --frozen -p 3.12
uv run pytest tests/test_multilang.py -q -k "impl_blocks_in_other_files or twice_declared"   # unmodified v8: 1 failed, 1 passed; with the fix: 2 passed
uv run --frozen pytest tests/ -q --tb=short                                                   # 7063 passed, 32 skipped, 12 failed (see below)
uv run --frozen pyright                                                                       # 602 errors, same 602 on unmodified v8; none in the changed lines
```

Final code (`d2a5d8f`), on Python 3.10 and 3.13 as the welcome comment asks:

```text
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_multilang.py -q -k "impl_blocks_in_other_files or twice_declared or tiebreak"   # 4 passed; with 52dcf0c's extract.py: 2 failed, 2 passed; with unmodified v8: 1 failed (the regression test), 3 passed
uv sync --all-extras --frozen -p 3.10 && uv run --frozen -p 3.10 pytest tests/ -q --tb=short   # 7077 passed, 31 skipped, 1 failed (test_hooks, see below)
uv sync --all-extras --frozen -p 3.13 && uv run --frozen -p 3.13 pytest tests/ -q --tb=short   # 7076 passed, 32 skipped, 1 failed (test_hooks, see below)
uv run --frozen ruff check .                                                                  # All checks passed!
```

Failures that come from my local environment, not from this change:
- **`tests/test_skillgen.py` (11 tests on the first run):** my first clone was shallow, so the `v8` baseline blobs were missing. CI uses `fetch-depth: 0` for the same reason. After `git fetch --unshallow`, all of them pass.
- **`tests/test_hooks.py::test_shebang_parse_requires_leading_hash_bang`:** fails identically on unmodified `v8` at `1d1e03b` on this machine. The resolved interpreter path is a Windows sandbox `/tmp` mapping that doesn't end with the expected home-relative path.

I also ran `graphify update .` on the #4283 repro and on a ~60-file Rust/Bevy workspace. The repro's `make()` now references `src_a_thing`. The workspace went from 1373 to 1339 nodes (the 34 stubs are gone), with the same edge count and no dangling edges.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. Not applicable: no skill fragments or generated files are touched.
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

title: Rust extractor: lossy structure and name-only call resolution (generic impls, traits, mods, use-lists, receivers)
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.7.0 (`graphify/extract.py`, `extract_rust`)

`extract_rust` loses most of the structure of idiomatic Rust. Reproduced with this file:

```rust
use std::fmt::{self, Display};
pub trait Reader { fn read(&self) -> u8; fn skip(&self) { helper(); } }
pub struct Foo<T> { x: T }
impl<T> Foo<T> { pub fn new(x: T) -> Self { Self { x } } pub fn go(&self) { Self::new(1); helper(); } }
impl Display for Foo<u8> { fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result { Ok(()) } }
impl Reader for Foo<u8> { fn read(&self) -> u8 { 0 } }
mod inner { pub fn helper() {} pub struct Foo; }
pub fn helper() { inner::helper(); println!("x"); }
pub type Alias = u8; pub const K: u8 = 1; macro_rules! m { () => {} }
```

## Structure problems

1. **Generic impls create orphan nodes.** `impl<T> Foo<T>` / `impl Foo<u8>` produce nodes `Foo<T>` / `Foo<u8>`, separate from the `Foo` struct node. Methods hang off the orphans.
2. **Trait is dropped from `impl Trait for Type`.** No `implements` edge; trait impls look like inherent impls, and several impls of the same method name for one type (e.g. three `impl From<_> for E`) share one ID scheme.
3. **`trait_item` returns without descending.** Trait methods produce no nodes, so calls from default method bodies (`skip -> helper`) are lost.
4. **IDs ignore the inline `mod` path, and are case-folded.** `inner::helper` and top-level `helper` get the same ID, as do `inner::Foo` and `Foo`; nodes merge and `inner::helper()` becomes a dropped self-call. Because `_make_id` lower-cases, `const ITEM` and `fn item()` also collide (first label wins). Across files, `_file_stem` is `parent.stem`, so every `src/lib.rs` shares `src.lib`.
5. **Missing node kinds:** `mod`, `type`, `const`, `static`, `union`, `macro_rules!`.
6. **`use` handling is lossy:** `use std::fmt::{self, Display}` yields one edge (the text before `{`), losing `Display`; nested/aliased lists are not flattened.

## Call-resolution problems

The extractor resolves calls by bare name only (`label_to_nid[name.lower()]`, last definition wins), ignoring qualifiers and receivers, so on a real workspace most edges for common names are wrong. Examples found by auditing the old output line by line:

- `Vec::new()`, `Cursor::new(..)`, `HashMap::new()`, `u64::from(x)`, `Default::default()` are linked to any local `fn new` / `fn from` / `fn default`.
- `v.len()` / `s.is_empty()` / `file.seek(..)` on std types are linked to local methods with the same name.
- `Value::Inline(..)` / `VrIndex(..)` (enum variant / tuple-struct constructors) are linked to a function named `inline` / the type node.
- `validator.enter_item(..)` is linked to an unrelated free `fn enter_item`, not the method on `validator`'s type.
- Conversely, true calls are missed: `self.m()` when several types in the file define `m`, `Type::f()` when `Type` has several impls, trait-qualified calls (`Seek::seek(&mut s)`), calls through generic bounds (`V: Trait`), `if let Some(x) = x`, loop/closure variables, and everything crossing a file boundary other than by unique name.

## Patch

I have a patch (`extract_rust` replacement + a small Rust pass in `extract()` for cross-file resolution) and 10 regression tests. Happy to open a PR. Summary of the behaviour:

- IDs scoped by file path + `mod` path and tagged by kind; generics stripped so `impl<T> Foo<T>` attaches to `Foo`; `implements` edges (also cross-file); trait methods as nodes; nodes for mod/type/const/static/macro; use-trees flattened.
- Calls resolved with light receiver-type inference (parameters, typed/constructor `let`, struct field types, `Self`, fn/method return types with `Result`/`Option`/`Box`/`Arc` unwrapped, `if let Some(x)`, generic bounds, `for`/closure element types over `Vec`/slice/array). When a call can reach several impls, an edge goes to each candidate with `INFERRED` confidence. Calls on external types (`Vec::new`, `u64::from`, ...) and enum-variant/tuple-struct constructors produce no edge. Typed calls whose type lives in another file are resolved in a cross-file pass.

## Measured on a real workspace

179 `.rs` files (a DICOM parser; calls counted over the whole graph, incl. cross-file), old extractor vs patched:

| | old | patched |
|---|---|---|
| nodes (in-file extraction) | 2658 | 5782+ |
| `calls` edges | 3544 | 4607 (2482 EXTRACTED, 2125 INFERRED) |

The 134 old call edges that disappear were classified by source line: 68 `Type::f()` on external types, 43 enum-variant/tuple-struct constructors and chains on external types, 23 `recv.f()` on std types (`len`/`is_empty`/`seek`/`read`) — plus 4 `validator.enter_*` calls that used to point at the wrong free function and now point at the method. None was a `Type::f()` call on a type defined in the workspace.

## Remaining limit

Where the type is only known to a real type checker (results of `.map(..)` / `.collect()`, macro-generated code), no edge is emitted rather than a guessed one.

title: [Feature]: graph.html sidebar: show full text for truncated names and explain the community count
body: ### Problem or use case The graph.html sidebar is 280px wide and truncates long text with an ellipsis, with no way to read the full value: - community names in the Communities legend - search results - neighbor links in the Node Info panel On graphify's own graph, 126 of 283 community labels (45%) are truncated (measured in Chrome: scrollWidth > clientWidth on .legend-label). With that many communities, the sidebar is the main way to navigate, so unreadable names make it hard to find the right one. The number next to each community (e.g. "145") also has no label or tooltip, so it isn't clear that it's the community's node count. - Before ### Proposed solution Show a tooltip with the full text when hovering a truncated name, and a "N nodes" tooltip on the legend count. - Reuse the existing vis-network `vis-tooltip` style, so it matches the canvas tooltips, with the same ~100ms delay. - Show it only when the text is actually truncated; always show it for the count, since that one explains the number. - Set the tooltip text via textContent only I have a working branch (~40 lines in graphify/exporters/html.py plus regression tests, including a label with & " ' < > to confirm nothing is interpreted as HTML). - After ### Alternatives considered - Native `title` attributes: smaller change (~4 lines), but the browser adds a noticeable delay and the look doesn't match the viewer. Happy to switch to this if you prefer a smaller change. - Expanding the truncated name in place on hover (CSS white-space: normal): no tooltip needed, but the list shifts while hovering. ### Area Graph building or querying ### Are you willing to submit a PR? Yes, I can work on this ### Compatibility / behavior impact Viewer-only change. No effect on node/edge IDs, cache semantics, graph.json schema, generated skills, MCP output, or incremental updates. The embedded graph data in graph.html is unchanged; only the sidebar script gains the tooltip logic. ### Additional context Branch: https://github.com/hassannzidan/graphify/tree/hassan/legend-tooltips I'll open a PR right after this issue. title: fix(extract): qualify nested class node IDs with parent class scope
body:
Fixes #4220

### Summary
When extracting nested classes with the same name across different parent classes (e.g. `Forward.Params` and `Backward.Params`), node IDs previously collided because `_make_id(stem, ".".join(namespace_stack), class_name)` did not incorporate the enclosing class scope. This caused the second class definition to be discarded by `seen_ids` and produced multiple `contains` edges pointing to a single node.

### Changes
- In `graphify/extractors/engine.py`, prefix `class_nid` with `parent_class_nid` when present (except for Ruby which resolves full namespace qualification).
- Added regression tests in `tests/test_python_nested_classes.py` covering same-named nested classes under different parents, multi-level nesting, and recursive nesting.

title: graphify affected <ClassName> returns no results for Dart/Flutter symbols
body:
## What happened?

`graphify affected "<ClassName>"` returns "No affected nodes found" for Dart/Flutter projects, even when the class is imported by hundreds of files. `graphify query "<ClassName>"` works correctly (finds related nodes), but the reverse traversal that `affected` depends on is blind.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
# On any Dart/Flutter project with a graph already built
graphify affected "DatabaseWrapper"
# → No affected nodes found.
```

## Error output or graph output

```
Affected nodes for DatabaseWrapper
Relations: calls, references, imports, imports_from, re_exports, inherits, extends, implements, uses, mixes_in, embeds
Depth: 2
No affected nodes found.
```

## Measured impact

On a real Flutter project (12 104 nodes, 12 420 edges):

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total symbols defined via `defines` edges | 4 793 |
| Symbols reachable by `affected` **before** | **100 (2.1 %)** |
| Symbols reachable by `affected` **after** (with fix) | **4 793 (100 %)** |
| Symbols gained | 4 693 (+97.9 %) |

## Root cause

`DEFAULT_AFFECTED_RELATIONS` in `graphify/affected.py` does not include `"defines"`.

In Dart (and Python, Go, and other file-module languages), the AST extractor emits a `defines` edge from the source file to each declared symbol (class, function, etc.). External files that use the symbol import the *file* — so the symbol node's only incoming edge is `defines`. Because `defines` is excluded from the whitelist, the reverse traversal terminates at depth 0 with no results.

```python
# In the graph: the class node has exactly 1 incoming edge
{
  "relation": "defines",
  "source": "database_database_wrapper",
  "target": "database_database_wrapper_databasewrapper"
}

# But DEFAULT_AFFECTED_RELATIONS skips it:
DEFAULT_AFFECTED_RELATIONS = (
    "calls",
    "references",
    "imports",
    # ...  "defines" is NOT here
)
```

## Related

- **#2329** — "Dart imports are never resolved to file nodes" (the import-resolution side)
- **#2570** — PR adding `_resolve_dart_import_target` (complementary; both are needed for full Dart `affected` support)

## Environment

- Graphify version: 0.9.76 (v8 branch)
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Python Version: 3.13
- Installation Method: uv tool install

title: feat(query): --seed to start the traversal at given nodes

Resolves #4293 (related: #445, #2381, #2384, #3810).

This PR adds `--seed X` (repeatable) to `graphify query`. The caller can choose where the traversal starts instead of
using the question's keyword matches. The use case: an external ranker picks where to start, and graphify's graph does
the expansion. The ranker could be embeddings, a hybrid or learned retriever, or an agent that already knows the
relevant file. This is the same retrieve-then-expand shape that `BENCHMARKS.md` describes for graph-expand, exposed on
the CLI.

```
graphify query "how are tokens refreshed?" --seed backend/app/core/security.py --seed refresh_token
```

Behaviour:
- **One interpretation of a node reference.** Each value resolves exactly as `affected` resolves its seed
  (`affected.resolve_seed`): node id, unique label, callable name with or without `()`, or a repo-relative or absolute
  file path. An absolute path is anchored to the graph's own root, using the same derivation as `affected` (#2706), so
  it works from any cwd.
- **Fail closed.** A value that does not resolve to exactly one node is listed in the header as

title: fix(affected): add defines to DEFAULT_AFFECTED_RELATIONS (dart lang)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `"defines"` to `DEFAULT_AFFECTED_RELATIONS` so that `graphify affected "<Symbol>"` can walk from a class/function symbol back to its defining file, and onward to all files that import it.

Fixes #4288.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant**: A symbol with a `defines` edge from its source file must be reachable by the reverse traversal. The defining file (and transitively, its importers) are affected by changes to the symbol.

**Measured on a real Dart/Flutter project (12 104 nodes, 12 420 edges):**

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Symbols reachable by `affected` | 100 (2.1 %) | 4 793 (100 %) |
| Symbols unreachable | 4 693 (97.9 %) | 0 (0 %) |

**Regression test**: `tests/test_affected_defines.py` — 10 tests covering:
- Symbol → defines → file → imports → consumer chain
- `defines` relation reported in `AffectedHit.via_relation`
- Symbol with ONLY `defines` incoming (the pure Dart case)
- Depth limits respected (`depth=1` returns only the defining file)
- `--relation calls` excludes `defines` (backward compat)
- File-level seed unaffected (backward compat)
- Python module pattern works too
- Existing non-defines relations (`references`) unaffected
- `defines` is in `DEFAULT_AFFECTED_RELATIONS` (sanity)

All 10 tests fail pre-fix, pass post-fix. All 64 existing affected tests remain green.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_affected_defines.py -xvs
uv run pytest tests/test_affected_member_seed.py tests/test_affected_cli.py -xvs
uv run pytest tests/test_indirect_dispatch.py tests/test_js_dynamic_import_affected.py -xvs
uv run pytest tests/ -q
uv run ruff check graphify/affected.py tests/test_affected_defines.py
uv run pyright graphify/affected.py
```

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (N/A — no skill changes)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

## Limitations

- **Granularity is file-level, not symbol-level**: `affected "<Symbol>"` returns all files that import the defining module, not just those using the specific symbol. This is a conservative over-approximation — safe for blast-radius analysis, and strictly better than returning 0 nodes.
- **Full Dart consumer visibility requires #2570**: Without the import-resolution fix from #2570, `affected "<Symbol>"` returns the defining file but not its transitive consumers. This PR finds the defining file; #2570 finds the consumers. Both are needed for complete Dart/Flutter `affected` support — this PR without #2570 is a partial fix. Reviewers should prioritize merging #2570 alongside or shortly after this PR.

## Side-effects analysis

| Concern | Checked | Result |
|---------|---------|--------|
| Interaction with `method`/`contains` relations | ✅ | None — `defines` goes file→symbol, `contains` goes dir→file or class→method. Different directions, no overlap. |
| Performance | ✅ | One more string in a tuple. No graph format or extractor changes. |
| `--relation` filter | ✅ | `--relation calls` excludes `defines` — tested in `test_defines_excluded_by_relation_filter` |
| File-level seed (`affected "<file>"`) | ✅ | Unchanged — tested in `test_file_seed_unaffected_by_defines_change` |
| Existing non-defines relations (`references`, etc.) | ✅ | Unchanged — tested in `test_non_defines_relations_still_work` |
| All 64 existing affected tests | ✅ | Green |
| Real project cross-reference | ✅ | 699/700 source files on disk, 100/100 sampled symbols found in source code |
| Graph staleness | ✅ | Only 1 of 700 source files missing from disk (deleted since graph build) |

## Pre-existing issues not introduced by this PR

- `pyright` reports 2 `reportAttributeAccessIssue` errors on `graphify/affected.py` lines 218 and 236 (`Cannot access attribute "out_edges" / "in_edges" for class "Graph[Unknown]"`). These are pre-existing — `nx.Graph` has these attributes at runtime but they are absent from the NetworkX type stubs. The same errors appear on the unmodified `v8` branch. This PR does not introduce or change them.

title: feat(export): show truncated sidebar names and legend node counts on hover in graph.html
body: Fixes #4286 ## What does this PR do? The 280px sidebar in `graph.html` truncates community names in the legend, search results and Node Info neighbor links with a CSS ellipsis, and gives no way to read the full text. The number next to each legend entry has no label saying it's a node count. On graphify's own graph, 126 of 283 legend labels (45%) are truncated. This adds one shared tooltip to the sidebar script in `graphify/exporters/html.py` (+46 lines, no existing lines changed): - **Reuses the existing look.** It's a single `div.vis-tooltip`, the class vis-network already styles for node tooltips, and it uses the same 100ms `tooltipDelay`. It overrides only wrapping: one line up to 360px, then it wraps between words (`overflow-wrap: break-word`). It's positioned near the cursor and kept inside the viewport. - **Shows only when needed.** Legend names, `.search-item` and `.neighbor-link` show it only when the text is actually truncated (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`). For a legend row, hovering anywhere except the count (checkbox, dot, gaps, padding) counts as hovering the name, and moving within the row doesn't hide or restart the tooltip. `.legend-count` always shows it, as "N nodes" / "1 node", because there it explains the number rather than completing cut-off text. - **Uses one delegated listener** on `document` (`mouseover` / `mouseout`, plus `mousedown` to hide it). Rows rebuilt later by search or `showInfo()` are covered without rebinding. Hiding it also clears its text. - **No `title` attributes**, so the browser's native tooltip doesn't stack on top. The full text is still in the DOM, because the ellipsis only hides it visually. - Before - After It's independent of #3457. That PR touches `focusNode` and community reveal; this one adds a separate block and changes no existing lines. With `git merge-tree`, `html.py` merges cleanly with #3457 in either order. The only conflict, in `tests/test_export.py`, already exists between #3457 and current v8, and this branch adds none. ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Tests or CI - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Security fix ## Verification & Invariants **Escaping invariant (#1838 / #3686):** a label goes through exactly one escaping step, the one its sink needs. The tooltip text is set only with `textContent`, read from the element's own text, so it adds no new `innerHTML` sink and no extra escaping layer. `& " ' < >` show literally. The legend label is still HTML-escaped once in Python for its existing `innerHTML` sink, and the browser decodes it once into the DOM text the tooltip reads. The `esc()` neighbor-link path from #1838 is unchanged. **Persisted state:** none is affected. `graph.json`, node/edge ids, cache, skills and MCP output don't change; only the generated `graph.html` does. **Tests** (in `tests/test_export.py`). They run the real generated `graph.html` script in Node.js against small DOM mocks (`_run_sidebar_harness`), and are skipped only when `node` is missing. Here they ran. The mock elements have `offsetWidth`/`offsetHeight` (200x30) and the window is 1280x800, so the positioning math is checked rather than producing `NaNpx`. - `test_to_html_legend_label_escaped_once_without_title`: the legend label is HTML-escaped exactly once for its `innerHTML` sink (no `&`), adds no tags, carries no `title` attribute, and its DOM text (what the tooltip shows) is the raw label. It already passes on v8 and guards the invariant the tooltip depends on. - `test_to_html_sidebar_tooltip_shows_truncated_text_and_node_counts`: - exactly one `.vis-tooltip` exists; - a truncated legend label, search item and neighbor link each show the full label `Team "A" & B 'c' ` literally, with `innerHTML` never written; - non-truncated rows show nothing; - counts show "3 nodes" / "1 node" even when not truncated; - the tooltip is placed 12px right of and 16px below the cursor (`left: 112px; top: 116px` for a hover at 100,100); - on mouseout it is hidden **and emptied**; - no `left`/`top` value ever contains `NaN`; - the wrap overrides are present. It **fails on current v8** and passes on this branch. - `test_to_html_sidebar_tooltip_stays_inside_viewport_near_edges`: a hover near the right edge is clamped to `left: 1076px`, and one near the bottom edge flips above the cursor (`top: 752px`). Every position keeps the 200x30 tooltip fully inside the 1280x800 viewport. - `test_to_html_legend_row_hover_shows_label_anywhere_but_count`: on a parent-linked mock row (checkbox + dot + label + count inside `.legend-item`): - hovering the padding, dot or checkbox shows the truncated name; - moving between those children never hides the tooltip; - the count still shows "3 nodes"; - a name that fits shows nothing from anywhere on its row, while its count still shows "1 node"; - leaving the row hides and empties the tooltip. Without the review follow-up's `html.py` changes, the tooltip test and the row test fail: the text stays after mouseout, the row padding, dot and checkbox show no tooltip, and moving within the row hides it. Without the mock sizes, the positioning assertions fail with `left: NaNpx`, and the edge test also gets `top: 806px`, past the bottom of the window. **Limitations:** - **Mouse only:** there's no tooltip on keyboard focus or on touch devices. - **Screen readers:** they read the full names, but the count is still a bare number, as it is today. - **Narrow viewports:** below about 368px wide, the 360px tooltip can overflow the right edge. - **Measured in Chrome:** the 45% figure is from Chrome 155 on Windows 11 (Segoe UI, 12px). Other fonts and platforms will differ. - [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/v8/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide. - [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant. - [ ] Made the **smallest fix** necessary. A 4-line native-`title` version would be smaller; this one was chosen for the consistent look and delay and for showing only on truncated text. Happy to switch if you prefer the smaller change. - [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test. - [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation. - [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly. ## How was this tested? Windows 11 Pro 25H2, Python 3.14.5, Node v24.15.0, on v8 @ 1d1e03b. ```text $ uv run pytest tests/test_export.py -q -rs 72 passed, 1 warning in 5.68s (no skips; the 6 Node-driven tests ran: test_to_html_show_info_runtime_renders_node_fields, test_to_html_aggregated_community_nodes_runtime, test_to_html_legend_label_escaped_once_without_title, test_to_html_sidebar_tooltip_shows_truncated_text_and_node_counts, test_to_html_sidebar_tooltip_stays_inside_viewport_near_edges, test_to_html_legend_row_hover_shows_label_anywhere_but_count) $ uv run pytest tests -q 2 failed, 6822 passed, 226 skipped, 1560 warnings in 561.37s (0:09:21) FAILED tests/test_extract.py::test_c_include_out_of_root_target_id_is_deterministic_across_checkout_paths FAILED tests/test_hooks.py::test_shebang_parse_requires_leading_hash_bang Both are environment-specific and unrelated: - test_c_include... hits the Windows MAX_PATH limit in the pytest tmp dir (FileNotFoundError on a long cache path); it fails the same way on pristine v8. - test_shebang_parse... fails only under `uv run` (resolves the interpreter to .venv\Scripts\python.exe) and passes when run with the venv's python directly, on both v8 and this branch. title: [Feature]: let graphify query start from caller-chosen nodes (--seed)
body:
### Problem or use case

Keyword seed selection keeps coming up: #445 (image and doc captions win the seeds), #2381 (test and doc rationale
nodes take over the seeds), #2384 (local variables win the seeds), #3810 (single words from the question cross
domains). Each of those asks for smarter automatic seeding.

Often, though, the caller already knows where to start: an agent that has the file open, a user who knows the symbol,
or an external retriever (embeddings, hybrid search, a learned ranker). Today there is no way to tell `query` "start
here". You have to word the question so the keyword scorer happens to land there.

### Proposed solution

`graphify query "<question>" --seed X [--seed Y ...]`

- Each value resolves exactly as `affected` resolves its seed (`affected.resolve_seed`): node id, unique label,
  callable name, or a repo-relative or absolute file path anchored to the graph's root. There is one interpretation of
  a node reference.
- It fails closed. Values that do not resolve to exactly one node are listed as skipped. If none resolve, the command
  reports it and does not fall back to keyword seeds.
- The header shows `Start (given): [...]`. Without `--seed`, nothing changes.

Implemented in #4289 (62 lines and 7 tests; it passes on Python 3.10 and 3.13).

### Alternatives considered

- **Better automatic seed scoring** (the issues above): worthwhile and complementary. `--seed` is an escape hatch that
  works whatever the scorer does.
- **`explain X` and `path A B`:** they start from a node, but neither gives a question-scoped traversal with `--budget`
  and `--context`.
- **Configurable seed exclusion** (#2381): it fixes one cause, not the case where the caller already knows the start.

### Area

Graph building or querying

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this (already open: #4289)

title: [Bug]: TS: a class field's type leaks to every same-named receiver in its file, so `A.run` binds `this.repo.save()` to `RepoB.save`
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Since 18682e8 (#4231, my PR) `_ts_receiver_type_table` types class fields, but it writes them into the per-file receiver table (`name -> Type`, first binding wins). That table is keyed by the bare name for the whole file, so a field's type reaches every receiver with that name in the file: with two classes in one file that each have a `repo` field of a different type, both classes' `this.repo` take one type, and `A.run` binds `this.repo.save()` to `RepoB.save`. It also types any local that happens to share a field's name.

The graphify-labs bot flagged this on #4231 and the PR had a second commit scoping fields per class, but only the first commit shipped in 0.9.81.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir demo && cd demo
printf 'export class RepoA { save(): void {} }\nexport class RepoB { save(): void {} }\n' > repos.ts
printf 'import { RepoA, RepoB } from "./repos";\nexport class A {\n  repo: RepoA;\n  run(): void { this.repo.save(); }\n}\nexport class B {\n  repo: RepoB;\n  run(): void { this.repo.save(); }\n}\n' > svc.ts
graphify update . --no-cluster
python -c "import json; g=json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); n={x['id']:x['label'] for x in g['nodes']}; o={e['target']:n[e['source']] for e in g.get('links',g.get('edges',[])) if e['relation']=='method'}; [print(o.get(e['source']), n[e['source']], '->', o.get(e['target']), n[e['target']]) for e in g.get('links', g.get('edges', [])) if e['relation']=='calls']"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
A .run() -> RepoB .save()     # wrong: A.repo is RepoA
B .run() -> RepoB .save()

Expected: `A .run() -> RepoA .save()` and `B .run() -> RepoB .save()`.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.84 (1d1e03b4)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No LLM keys; AST only. Clean checkout of v8 @ 1d1e03b4 (0.9.84) reproduces.

### Additional context

Follow-up to #4231. PR right after this issue.

title: [Bug]: TS: `c.foo()` gets no edge when the class declares `#foo` before `foo`
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`foo()` and `#foo()` on one class get the same node id (ids drop `#`), labeled after whichever is declared first. Since 27df0f9 (#4233, my PR), `_resolve_typescript_member_calls` skips a match whose label and the call disagree on a leading `#`. So when `#foo` comes first, the shared node is labeled `.#foo()` and the public call `c.foo()` gets no edge at all; with `foo` first it resolves.

In hono, `Context.newResponse` is a public arrow property with no node of its own: it is folded into the `.#newResponse()` node. On 0.9.84 the three `c.newResponse()` calls (`errorHandler` in `src/hono-base.ts`, `streamSSE`, `stream`) get no edge.

The graphify-labs bot flagged this on #4233 and the PR had a second commit removing the guard, but only the first commit shipped in 0.9.81.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir demo && cd demo
printf 'export class Ctx {\n  #foo(): number { return 2; }\n  foo(): number { return 1; }\n}\n' > ctx.ts
printf 'import { Ctx } from "./ctx";\nexport function make(c: Ctx): number { return c.foo(); }\n' > use.ts
graphify update . --no-cluster
python -c "import json; g=json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); n={x['id']:x['label'] for x in g['nodes']}; print([(n[e['source']], n[e['target']]) for e in g.get('links', g.get('edges', [])) if e['relation']=='calls'])"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
[]

Expected: `[('make()', '.#foo()')]`, the one node graphify has for `foo` / `#foo` (as it gives when `foo` is declared first).
```

0.9.84 (1d1e03b4)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

built from source (git clone)

title: [Feature]: Rust: `x.method()` and `self.field.method()` get no calls edge across files, and in-file they bind by bare name
body:
### Problem or use case

Rust method calls on anything other than `self` are never resolved across files: the shared pass skips every member call, and `_resolve_rust_self_member_calls` handles only `self.m()` ("a non-self receiver needs local type inference this pass does not attempt, left for a future extension"). Inside one file, `x.m()` binds to whichever method named `m` the file defines, with no regard for `x`'s type.

```rust
// src/search.rs
use crate::matcher::Matcher;

pub struct Searcher { matcher: Matcher }

impl Searcher {
    pub fn search(&self) -> usize { self.matcher.find() }   // no edge
}

pub fn by_param(m: &Matcher) -> usize { m.find() }          // no edge

pub fn by_let() -> usize {
    let m = Matcher::new();
    m.find()                                                // no edge
}
```

Measured against rust-analyzer (go-to-definition at every call inside every `fn`), 0.9.84:

| repo | `x.m()` calls found | `self.field.m()` calls found | all calls found | `calls` edges that are wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ripgrep | 225 / 1029 (21.9%) | 54 / 255 (21.2%) | 48.2% | 532 of 2808 (18.9%) |
| bat | 29 / 84 (34.5%) | 1 / 11 | 71.5% | 36 of 722 |
| fd | 10 / 177 (5.6%) | 1 / 2 | 35.8% | 9 of 166 |

Most of the remaining wrong edges in ripgrep (502 of 532) are in-file bare-name matches of `x.m()` / `self.field.m()` / `expr.m()`.

### Proposed solution

The type of a receiver is usually written in the source: a typed parameter (`m: &Matcher`), a `let` with a type or with `Type::new()` / `Type { .. }`, a struct field (`matcher: Arc<Matcher>`), or the declared return type of the function or method that produced it (`-> Self`, `-> io::Result<Matcher>` followed by `?`). Record those facts in the extractor and resolve `x.m()` to that type's method in a corpus pass next to the `self.` one, the same way the Python, TS, C# and C++ resolvers use declared types. A receiver whose type is not known gets no edge rather than a bare-name guess.

### Alternatives considered

- Running rust-analyzer: heavy, needs a toolchain and a cargo build graph, not deterministic across environments.
- Keeping the in-file bare-name match as a fallback: on ripgrep, after typing, the matches it still makes are right 45 times and wrong 125 times.

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Rust only. No node or edge ids change. `.rs` nodes gain three attributes (`_rust_ret`, `_rust_ret_ok`, `_rust_fields`) and Rust raw calls a `rust_receiver` field, so the AST cache schema goes 7 -> 8 to retire entries written without them, and the three markers are forwarded on changed-files rebuilds next to `_rust_impl_key` (changed-files rebuild == full build on ripgrep and fd). Rust `calls` edges change: new INFERRED edges for typed receivers, and an untyped `x.m()` no longer gets an EXTRACTED in-file bare-name edge. No generated skills or MCP output format change.

### Additional context

Follow-up to #4237 / #4238 (in-file Rust call binding, shipped in 0.9.82). PR right after this issue.

title: fix(ts): scope class-field receiver types to the field's own class
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4294. Follow-up to #4231: this is that PR's second commit (the fix for the graphify-labs bot's finding), which did not ship in 0.9.81, plus two cases it missed.

- `_ts_receiver_type_table` (`graphify/extractors/engine.py`) records each class's field types from declared fields, constructor parameter properties, `this.x = param` / `this.x = new T()` in the constructor, and `get x(): T` / `set x(v: T)`. They go on the class node (`_ts_fields`; static fields apart in `_ts_static_fields`), never into the per-file name table.
- A `this.x.m()` call (marked `ts_this_field`, plus `ts_static_this` inside a static method) in a method of a known class reads that class's fields, then its bases' through `inherits` (`_resolve_typescript_member_calls`, `graphify/extract.py`). It never falls back to the file table, which would hand it another class's field or a local that shares the name. An inherited field's type is judged by the declaring file's imports.
- `const { x } = this` / `const { x: y } = this` in the enclosing function (or around an arrow function holding the call) mark `x.m()` / `y.m()` the same way, since they read the field.
- Classes are matched like node ids (casefolded): `class UsecaseVisitor` and `const usecaseVisitor` in one file are one node, labeled after either name.
- Fields of an unnamed class (`export default class { .. }`) stay in the file table, which its class-less methods still read, as on 0.9.84.
- A changed-files rebuild forwards `_ts_fields` / `_ts_static_fields` and the unchanged files' import edges (`watch.py`, `cli.py`), so an inherited field from an unchanged file resolves as in a full build.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: `this.x` (or a name destructured from `this`) in a method of a known class is typed by that class's fields or its bases', never by another class's field or a same-named local.
Persisted state it could invalidate: none in the AST cache (JS/TS files bypass it, `_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`). graph.json class nodes gain `_ts_fields` / `_ts_static_fields`.

0.9.84 vs this branch, cold `graphify update <dir> --no-cluster --force`, every `calls` edge that differs:

| repo | edges removed | edges added | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| TypeORM (`packages/typeorm/src`) | 2 | 95 | 92 added edges are in the compiler's list and 3 (`this.expressionMap.setMainAlias` / `createAlias` in `SelectQueryBuilder`) were confirmed with the compiler at the call site, e.g. 50 `this.broadcaster.broadcast*()` calls in the query runners through `this.broadcaster = new Broadcaster(this)` in their constructors, and `this.mongoQueryRunner.*()` in `MongoEntityManager`. The 2 removed are `embeddedMetadata.create()` on a local `const embeddedMetadata = embeddedMetadatas.shift()` that took the class's field type by name (the compiler resolves them to `EmbeddedMetadata.create` too, so they were right by coincidence) |
| NestJS (`packages/`) | 0 | 16 | 10 in the compiler's list (e.g. 5 `this.ctx.writeToStdout()`, `this.exceptionHandler.handle()`, `this.instanceLinksHost.get()`, and `this.staticInstanceRef?.error()` in a static method); 6 are `this.localInstance?.log()`-style calls to the `LoggerService` interface through the `get localInstance(): LoggerService` getter, confirmed at the call site |
| excalidraw (`packages/`) | 1 | 10 | checked by reading (the compiler setup here cannot load its workspace aliases): `this.library.*` -> `Library` (`this.library = new Library(this)`), `this.elements` / `this.appState` `.isEmpty()` / `.applyTo()` -> `ElementsDelta` / `AppStateDelta` (constructor parameter properties, also inherited by `HistoryDelta`), `creator.clear()` / `navigator.clear()` after `const { creator, navigator } = this`. Removed: `creator.clear()` -> `AppFlowchart.clear`, an in-file name match to the class's own property (wrong) |
| hono, mermaid, typescript-eslint | 0 | 0 | — |

Against the TypeScript compiler, `this.x.method()` calls found: TypeORM 79.6% -> **96.1%**, NestJS 78.5% -> **81.6%**, hono unchanged (all calls found: TypeORM 65.7% -> 67.0%, NestJS 80.9% -> 81.3%).

Changed-files rebuild vs full build (`watch._rebuild_code`), NestJS, changing `packages/core/nest-application.ts` (its fields come from a base class in an unchanged file) and `packages/core/injector/module-ref.ts`: 2195 / 2195 / 2195 `calls` edges each, identical. (On excalidraw a changed-files rebuild of `App.tsx` drops that file's cross-package edges: 506 on clean 0.9.84 and the same 506 here; unrelated to this change.)

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.

- [x] Added a **regression test**: on 0.9.84 6 fail: `test_same_named_fields_in_two_classes_of_one_file_keep_their_own_type`, `test_field_destructured_from_this_types_the_local`, `test_constructor_declared_fields_stay_with_their_class`, `test_field_declared_on_a_base_class_in_another_file`, `test_accessor_types_this_field_calls`, `test_static_method_reads_static_fields`; guards that pass on both: `test_class_sharing_its_node_with_a_same_named_value_keeps_its_fields`, `test_unnamed_class_field_still_types_this_field_calls`, `test_inherited_field_of_a_package_type_emits_no_edge`.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4295. Follow-up to #4233: this is that PR's second commit (the fix for the graphify-labs bot's finding), which did not ship in 0.9.81.

A call written `c.foo()` can only mean a public member, so the edge to that node is kept.

The extractor marks a member node `_ts_public_twin` when its class declares both `#name` and a public `name` (a method or a property, e.g. hono's `newResponse` arrow property, which has no node of its own). A public call reaches a `#`-labeled node only when it carries the mark, so `c.run()` on a class that declares only `#run` (its public `run` inherited from a base) gets no edge to the private method. The mark is on the node and is forwarded on changed-files rebuilds (`watch.py`, `cli.py`).
