title: feat(rust): resolve `x.method()` and `self.field.method()` through the receiver's declared type
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4296.

`extract_rust` (`graphify/extractors/rust.py`) now records:
- on each `fn` node, its return type: `_rust_ret` (`-> Self`, `-> Foo`, `-> Box<Foo>`/`Arc<Foo>`/`Rc<Foo>`) and `_rust_ret_ok` (the `T` of `-> Result<T, _>` / `io::Result<T>` / `Option<T>`);
- on each struct node, its field types (`_rust_fields`; `Box`/`Arc`/`Rc` deref to the inner type);
- on each `x.m()` raw call, how the receiver's type is found (`rust_receiver`): a typed parameter (closures included) or `let`, `Type { .. }`, a struct field, the return of `T::f()` / `f()` / `y.m()`, unwrapped by `?` / `.unwrap()` / `.expect()`, through `.clone()`.

`_resolve_rust_typed_member_calls` (`graphify/extract.py`, registered after the `self.` pass) evaluates that over the corpus and binds the call to the type's method, `INFERRED` 0.85. Every step must be unique: a type or free function defined more than once is narrowed to the caller's file, then its crate; a method name must match one method across the type's impl blocks in that crate. A file's crate is the deepest crate root above it, the roots being the directories that hold a `src/` of some `.rs` file in the corpus (so a `tests` module inside `src/` and a crate's own `tests/` / `benches/` / `examples/` stay with it).

Precision rules: a type written with a path only counts when the path is crate-local (`crate::`, `self::`, `super::`), since `fs::DirEntry` or `walkdir::DirEntry` must not reach the crate's own `DirEntry`; a type parameter never names a type; a name rebound without a type (an untyped closure parameter, `for x in`, `if let Some(x)`, a match arm, a tuple pattern) hides the outer binding from after its value on, so `for x in x.iter()` still types the `x` in `x.iter()`. A non-`self` receiver with no known type no longer binds by bare name in-file.

The three node markers are forwarded on changed-files rebuilds next to `_rust_impl_key` in `watch.py` and `cli.py`.

title: feat(html): add a light/dark/system theme toggle to graph.html
body:
Closes #3894

graph.html now has a small Light / Dark / System toggle at the top of the sidebar, and the choice is remembered.

The page colors that were hardcoded in the stylesheet (background, sidebar, search box and results, node info panel, legend, stats, checkboxes, text, borders, hover states) are now CSS variables under `:root`. Their values are exactly the old dark colors, and a `[data-theme="light"]` block overrides them. A small inline script in `<head>` reads `localStorage['graphify-theme']` and sets `data-theme` before first paint, so the page doesn't flash. System follows `prefers-color-scheme` and updates live through a `matchMedia` change listener. Every `localStorage` access is wrapped in try/catch, because it can throw under `file://` or in privacy modes. Node labels are white per node, so switching themes also updates the label color (dark labels in light mode). The canvas just shows the page background. Community colors stay as they were.

The default stays dark when nothing is saved, not System, so nobody's current look changes. The issue suggested defaulting to the OS setting, and that's a one-line change if you'd rather have it.

Limits: hyperedge shading and its label keep their fixed indigo colors in both themes. The toggle row pushes the rest of the sidebar down by about 37px. No new dependencies. The output is still deterministic.

Testing: new `tests/test_html_theme.py` with 6 tests covering the variables and their dark values, the light override, the toggle buttons, the try/catch around localStorage, the head script and determinism. 5 of them fail on current v8, and the determinism one passes on both. The existing Node-harness tests in `test_export.py` pass. The full suite on 3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14 has the same failures as v8. Ruff is clean. On a real MediatR graph (1630 nodes) I rendered both v8 and this branch in headless Chromium. The default canvas is pixel-identical to v8, and the sidebar is identical apart from the 37px shift. Light, System (with emulated light and dark schemes, plus a live switch) and a reload with a saved choice all behave as expected, with no console errors on either build.

title: perf(resolution): skip os.getcwd() in the path-memo key for absolute paths
body:
## What does this PR do?

`_source_key` and `_resolve_cached` key their memo on the path and the cwd. They call `os.getcwd()` on every lookup, hit or miss.

On a private 900-file repo, `graphify extract --code-only` calls `os.getcwd()` 215k times. With this PR it calls it 51 times. `os.getcwd()` is a syscall, and I measured 30 to 40us per call on macOS. The cache key took longer than the resolution it saved.

An absolute path resolves the same from any cwd. This PR keys it with an empty cwd. A relative path still keys on the cwd, so a `chdir` still misses the cache.

The check is `Path.is_absolute()`, so host rules apply. A driveless `\x` on Windows depends on the current drive and stays keyed on the cwd.

The memo came in with cd8d99b2f.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [x] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a memo hit returns what `Path.resolve()` returned for that path from the same cwd. A relative path depends on the cwd and keeps it in the key. An absolute path does not depend on it.

- `graph.json` is byte-identical to `v8` on three corpora, three cold runs each: two commits of the private repo, and this repo's own source.
- The new tests fail on `v8` and pass here. They also fail against a mutant that drops the cwd for every path.
- No persisted state changes. The memo lives in process only, and `extract()` clears it at the start of each run.
- Security: path handling, so reviewed against SECURITY.md. No trust boundary changes. An absolute and a relative key cannot collide, since `os.getcwd()` never returns an empty string.
- Not run on Windows. The driveless case rests on `Path.is_absolute()` semantics.

title: perf(resolution): walk each JS/TS tree once when collecting symbol facts
body:
## What does this PR do?

`_collect_js_symbol_resolution_facts` walks every parsed JS/TS tree in full four times. Each pass keeps only a few node types. On a private 900-file repo with about 400 JS/TS files that is 7.8M node visits.

This PR walks each tree once and keeps the nodes of the six types those passes filter on, in walk order. The passes then iterate that short list. Each fact list is filled by one pass only, so fact order does not change.

`_walk_js_tree` also moves from a `.children` stack to a `TreeCursor`, which skips building a child list at every node. A cursor cannot move above the node it starts from, so the walks that start inside a tree stay inside that subtree. These are the function-body walks, and the import and export nodes passed to `_js_named_specifiers`.

This overlaps #3353, which also indexes JS nodes once and frees each tree after use. This PR is smaller and does not change memory behavior. I will close this if #3353 lands first.

title: fix(extract): parse TS 5 export type star re-exports (#3942)
body:
Addresses the TypeScript half of #3942 (the Svelte half already shipped in v0.9.76 via #3984).

`export type * from "./x"` (TS 5.0's type-only star re-export) has no equivalent in `tree-sitter-typescript` 0.23 — currently the latest release on PyPI, confirmed by checking available versions. The grammar raises an `ERROR` node on the `type` keyword in this exact position, and the whole file is dropped, losing every symbol in it, not just the one statement. A barrel file that only re-exports types this way reported a syntax error and contributed nothing to the graph.

The construct is erased at compile time, the same as `import type` / `export type { X }` (both already handled correctly), so the graph only needs the re-export edge, not the type-only distinction. Added `_normalize_ts_export_type_star`, which blanks out just the `type` keyword — same byte length, same offsets — before parsing, so the grammar reads the ordinary, already-supported `export * from "./x"` form instead. Threaded into `extract_js`'s existing TS source-normalization chain (alongside the existing `import(...)` type-argument workaround, composing cleanly with it since they target disjoint syntax).

Unlike that existing workaround, this prefix is never ambiguous with a runtime expression (`export type *` can only ever mean the type-only star re-export), so no AST-based disambiguation pass is needed — a direct regex match is sufficient and safe.

Verified against the issue's exact repro: before, `index.ts` reported a syntax error and extracted zero symbols; after, it correctly produces a re-export edge to `types.ts`, and `types.ts`'s own `FetchFn` type survives. Confirmed the already-working named form (`export type { X } from "./y"`) is untouched — still correctly stamped `type_only` for import-cycle exclusion (#1241/#3123). Four new regression tests in `tests/test_ts_export_type_star.py`, confirmed to fail against pre-fix code (import error, since the function didn't exist). Full suite passes clean — the only failures were the known editable-install-trap pattern (confirmed via a targeted rerun with correct module resolution: 110/110 pass) plus one pre-existing unrelated Erlang gap.

title: [Bug]: Java: a bare `m()` or `field.m()` inherited from a class in another file gets no calls edge when the name is not unique
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Inside a subclass, Java code calls inherited members without `this.`:

```java
// Base.java
abstract class Base {
    protected Gateway gateway;
    protected boolean isRegistered(Object o) { return o != null; }
}

// Child.java
class Child extends Base {
    boolean check(Object o) { return isRegistered(o); }   // no edge
    void pay() { gateway.charge(); }                       // no edge
}
```

- `isRegistered(o)`: the in-file pass (#4252) looks at the caller's class and its bases *in the same file* only (its docstring: "A supertype outside this file is invisible"). The call then goes to the shared cross-file pass, which binds a bare name only when one definition exists in the whole corpus. As soon as another class also has an `isRegistered`, the call gets no edge, although `extends Base` says exactly which one it is.
- `gateway.charge()`: the receiver type table holds the class's own fields and the in-file bases' fields. A field declared on a base class in another file types nothing; #3151 fixed this for `this.gateway.charge()` only.

Expected: `isRegistered(o)` -> `Base.isRegistered`, `gateway.charge()` -> `Gateway.charge`, the nearest supertype that declares the name, as javac binds it.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir demo && cd demo
cat > Base.java <<'EOF'
abstract class Base {
    protected Gateway gateway;
    protected boolean isRegistered(Object o) { return o != null; }
}
EOF
cat > Child.java <<'EOF'
class Child extends Base {
    boolean check(Object o) { return isRegistered(o); }
    void pay() { gateway.charge(); }
}
EOF
echo 'class Gateway { void charge() {} }' > Gateway.java
echo 'class Audit { void charge() {} boolean isRegistered(Object o) { return false; } }' > Audit.java
graphify update . --no-cluster
python -c "import json; g=json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); print([(e['source'], e['target']) for e in g['links'] if e['relation']=='calls'])"


Output: `[]`. Expected `(child_child_check, base_base_isregistered)` and `(child_child_pay, gateway_gateway_charge)`.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
No error. The two `calls` edges are missing.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.84 (1d1e03b4)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

Windows 11, Python 3.12, graphify 0.9.84 from source (v8 1d1e03b4).

### Additional context

Measured against javac (the element javac binds at every method call inside every method, `src/main/java` of each project), 0.9.84:

| project | all calls found | bare `f()` calls found | `field.m()` calls found |
|---|---|---|---|
| jackson-core | 77.9% | 87.9% | 34.2% |
| commons-io | 82.1% | 83.0% | 70.6% |
| jsoup | 81.4% | 79.4% | 67.6% |
| commons-lang | 86.3% | 88.8% | 61.0% |

In jackson-core, 368 of the missed `field.m()` calls are fields like `_streamReadConstraints` declared on `ParserBase`, and 219 missed `f()` calls are methods like `_reportUnsupportedOperation()` declared on a parent class.

Related: #4252 (in-file bases, shipped), #3151 (`this.field` on a superclass, shipped). PR right after this issue.

title: fix(java): resolve bare calls and field receivers inherited from a supertype in another file
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4304.

- `_resolve_java_member_calls` now also takes Java bare calls (`m()`) the file could not bind: it looks the name up on the caller's supertypes, `EXTRACTED` like `super.m()`: first up the superclass chain, nearest declaration wins (Java's "class wins": a superclass method beats an interface default at any depth), then the interfaces level by level. Two interfaces declaring it on one level bind nothing. A constructor name (`new Base()`) is skipped.
- A plain receiver (`gateway.charge()`) that is not a parameter, a local (typed or `var`), a lambda / catch / for-each / resource / pattern variable, or a field of the class or its in-file bases is now marked `receiver_unbound` by the extractor (`_java_bound_names`). The resolver then types it from a field declared on a supertype (#3151's tables), so a local named like the inherited field still wins.
- `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 7 -> 8, so cached Java results without the marker are re-extracted.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a bare `m()` / `field.m()` binds to the member javac would bind when the nearest supertype declaring the name is unique; a name the method or class declares itself is never retyped.

Against javac on 6 projects (`src/main/java`), 0.9.84 vs this branch, cold `graphify update <dir> --no-cluster --force`:

| project | all calls found | edges added | added edges javac confirms | edges lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| jackson-core | 77.9% -> **96.5%** | 729 | 700 (+20 by reading, 9 wrong) | 0 |
| commons-io | 82.1% -> **84.6%** | 64 | 64 | 0 |

| gson | 88.4% -> 88.5% | 2 | 2 | 0 |
| commons-text | 78.2% -> 78.6% | 2 | 2 | 0 |

The 10 wrong ones are all overloads split across levels: `isEnabled(StreamWriteFeature)` is declared on `GeneratorBase` but `JsonGeneratorBase` declares `isEnabled(JsonWriteFeature)`, and graphify keeps one node per method name with no parameter types, so the nearer one wins. `_method_on_type_or_bases` (`this.m()`, typed receivers) works the same way today.

title: [Feature]: Java: a call on a call (`builder().size(3).build()`), on `new T()` or on a cast gets no calls edge
body:
### Problem or use case

When a Java receiver is itself an expression, the call gets no `calls` edge, even though every step's type is written in the source as a method's declared return type:

```java
// Builder.java
class Builder {
    Builder size(int n) { return this; }
    Product build() { return new Product(); }
}
// Client.java
class Client {
    void run(Object o) {
        Factory.builder().size(3).build().ship();   // only Factory.builder() is linked
        new Builder().size(1);                      // no edge
        ((Builder) o).build();                      // no edge
    }
}
```

The Java extractor keeps a receiver only when it is a name, `this`, `super` or `this.field`; for any other receiver the raw call has `receiver: None` and `_resolve_java_member_calls` skips it. Fluent builders, `getX().getY()` accessors and `new T().m()` are common Java style.

Measured against javac (the element javac binds at every method call inside every method, `src/main/java`), 0.9.84:

| project | chained `a().b()` calls found | `new T().m()` / cast receivers found |
|---|---|---|
| jsoup | 0 / 117 | 0 / 30 |
| commons-io | 1 / 38 | 0 / 12 |
| commons-lang | 0 / 37 | 0 / 6 |
| gson | 0 / 13 | 0 / 11 |
| jackson-core | 0 / 12 | 0 / 20 |
| commons-text | 0 / 11 | - |
| **all six** | **1 / 228 (0.4%)** | **0 / 79** |

### Proposed solution

Put each method's declared return type on its node, record the shape of an expression receiver in the raw call, and type it step by step in `_resolve_java_member_calls`, the way C# chains already resolve (#4258). A step whose type is unknown (a library type, a type parameter, an untyped `var`) ends the chain with no edge.

### Alternatives considered

Binding the last call by bare name: wrong whenever two classes share a method name, the case `_java_defer` exists for.

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Java only. No node or edge ids change. Java method nodes gain `_java_ret` and Java raw calls a `java_receiver_chain` field, so the AST cache schema goes 7 -> 8, and `_java_ret` is forwarded on changed-files rebuilds next to `_rust_impl_key`. New INFERRED `calls` edges only; no edge is removed. No generated skills or MCP output format change.

### Additional context

Related: #1770 / #4258 (C# chains, shipped). PR right after this issue.

title: feat(java): resolve calls on chained, `new` and cast receivers through declared return types
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4306.

- The Java extractor puts each method's declared return type on its node (`_java_ret`, same filter as receiver types: no library types, no type parameters; overloads sharing a node keep it only when they all declare it).
- A member call whose receiver is a call, `new T()`, a cast or a parenthesized one of those gets `java_receiver_chain`, e.g. `["call", "size", ["call", "builder", ["type", "Factory"]]]`. A name at the start of the chain is replaced by its declared type from the method's table, or kept as a type when it is capitalized and undeclared (`Factory.builder()`), as for plain receivers.
- `_resolve_java_member_calls` walks the chain: each call is looked up on the type so far (`_method_on_type_or_bases`), its `_java_ret` gives the next type. A return type declared in several files (a nested `Builder` in many classes) is taken from the file of the method that returns it, or not at all. Edges are `INFERRED` 0.85, like other typed receivers.
- `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 7 -> 8; `_java_ret` is forwarded on changed-files rebuilds next to `_rust_impl_key` in `watch.py` and `cli.py`.

`test_inherited_field_resolves_and_chained_receiver_stays_deferred` asserted that `factory.create().charge()` gets no edge because the chain "carries no declared type"; `create()` declares `Gateway`, so it now resolves and the test (renamed `..._follows_return_type`) asserts the edge.

## Type of change

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a call on an expression receiver gets an edge only when every step's type is declared in the corpus and unique (or unique in the returning file); otherwise none.

Against javac on 6 projects (`src/main/java`), 0.9.84 vs this branch, cold `graphify update <dir> --no-cluster --force`:

| project | all calls found | chained calls found | edges added | added edges right | edges lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| jsoup | 81.4% -> **84.3%** | 0.0% -> **66.7%** | 144 | 143 | 0 |
| commons-lang | 86.3% -> **88.4%** | 0.0% -> **89.2%** | 84 | 84 | 0 |
| commons-io | 82.1% -> **83.9%** | 2.6% -> **42.1%** | 35 | 35 | 0 |
| gson | 88.4% -> **91.1%** | 0.0% -> **100%** | 34 | 34 | 0 |
| commons-text | 78.2% -> **80.3%** | 0.0% -> **90.9%** | 19 | 19 | 0 |
| jackson-core | 77.9% -> 78.2% | 0.0% -> **75.0%** | 17 | 17 | 0 |

All six: chained calls 1/228 -> **159/228**, `new T().m()` / cast receivers 0/79 -> **46/79**; 333 edges added, 0 removed. 308 are confirmed by javac; 24 more are calls made inside constructors (mostly builder chains in `this(builder()...)`), which my comparison missed because javac names a constructor `<init>` and graphify names it after its class; I checked those by reading; 1 is wrong: jsoup's `el.attr("xmlns").equals(..)` — `Node.attr(String)` returns `String` but `Element`'s own `attr` overloads return `Element`, and graphify keeps one node per method name.

Changed-files rebuild == full build: `test_chain_through_an_unchanged_file_survives_a_changed_files_rebuild` (fails without the forwarded marker).

Build time, 2 runs each: no change (commons-lang 10.9-11.9 s both, jsoup 5.2-5.3 s both).

title: skill.md: shell injection through `LABELS_DICT` and `INPUT_PATH` in `python -c "..."` blocks, plus three smaller robustness gaps (v0.9.84)
body:
Found while vendoring `graphify/skill.md` from v0.9.84 into a project (an automated review flagged these;
I then checked each against the file). Items 1, 2, and 5 are reproduced. Items 3 and 4 are from reading
the text, not from running it.

## 1. Community labels are spliced into a double-quoted shell string (reproduced)

Step 5 has `labels = LABELS_DICT` inside `python -c "..."`. The labels are chosen by the model from node
labels, which come from the corpus (docs, comments, file names). In a double-quoted shell string, `$(...)`
and backticks run before Python sees the text:

```bash
python3 -c "
labels = {0: 'Attention Mechanism', 1: 'Data $(touch LABEL_MARKER) Loading'}
print('python saw:', labels)
"
# python saw: {0: 'Attention Mechanism', 1: 'Data  Loading'}
# and LABEL_MARKER now exists
```

So a corpus that gets the model to emit such a label runs a command as the user. Step 1 already avoids
this with a quoted heredoc (`<<'GRAPHIFY_ROOT_EOF'`, with a comment explaining why); Step 5 doesn't.

## 2. `INPUT_PATH` has the same problem in Steps 2, 3, 4, 5, and 9 (reproduced)

`Path('INPUT_PATH')` is substituted into `python -c "..."` the same way:

```bash
python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; print('path:', Path('./proj$(touch PATH_MARKER)'))"
# PATH_MARKER now exists
```

The comment in Step 1 says a bare path in a command line "would let a malicious path execute as shell
code"; the later steps don't follow it.

Suggested fix for 1 and 2: pass the values through a quoted heredoc (`python3 - <<'EOF' ... EOF`) or
through environment variables or `sys.argv`, never by substituting text into a double-quoted script.

## 3. Step 5 carries on after the shrink guard refuses (from reading)

Step 4 exits with `SystemExit(1)` when `to_json` returns `False`. Step 5 prints the same error and
continues, after it has already written `GRAPH_REPORT.md` and `.graphify_labels.json`, so they can
describe a graph that `graph.json` doesn't contain. Step 4's own comment says to write the report only
when the graph was written.

## 4. The chunk merge aborts on invalid JSON (from reading)

Step B3 says "If a subagent failed or returned invalid JSON, print a warning and skip that chunk - do
not abort", but the merge script does `d = json.loads(Path(c).read_text(...))` with no `try`, so one
bad chunk raises and stops the merge.

## 5. The interpreter path is word-split (reproduced)

`$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c ...` is unquoted in every block, so an interpreter path with a
space (a home directory like `/Users/First Last/...`) is split into two words:

```text
no such file or directory: .../a
```

`"$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)"` fixes it.

## Environment

`graphifyy` v0.9.84, the package's `graphify/skill.md`. I only read that file. The other `skill-*.md`
variants (and v1.0.0's, which has a different layout) may have the same patterns; I haven't looked.

title: fix(julia): extract return-typed, qualified, operator and functor methods; broadcast/pipe calls
body:
Follow-up to #4126/#4128 (a041fac), which handled `where` clauses and parametric types. These Julia definitions and calls were still dropped:

- **Return-type annotations:** `function f(x)::Float64` wraps the call head in a `typed_expression`. `_unwrap_call_expression` now unwraps `where` and `::T` wrappers in any combination.
- **Qualified, operator and functor methods:** a new `_def_name` handles `Base.show(...)`, `Base.:+(...)`, bare `+(...)` and functors `(c::Circle)(x)`. The node id uses the bare name, so all methods of one generic function share a node and in-file calls resolve to it. The label keeps the qualifier (`Base.show()`), and functors get `(Circle)()`. This applies to `function` definitions, short `f(x) = ...` definitions and macro names.
- **Calls:** `walk_calls` now emits `calls` edges for broadcasts (`helper.(xs)`) and pipes (`x |> helper`, `xs .|> helper`).

## Tests
There are three new tests in `tests/test_languages.py` covering all of the above, plus parametric struct inheritance with no type-parameter nodes. All 22 Julia tests pass.

## Real-world check: AbstractTrees.jl v0.4.5
I ran the extractor before this change (`b4e6307`) and after it on the same 19 `.jl` files in [AbstractTrees.jl](https://github.com/JuliaCollections/AbstractTrees.jl):

| | Before → after |
|---|---|
| Nodes | **+47** (none lost) |
| Edges | **+221** |
| `calls` edges | **+142** |

The added nodes are method definitions that were previously dropped, mostly packages extending `Base` and `AbstractTrees` interfaces:

- `src/cursors.jl` (20 → 27 nodes, 68 → 136 calls): `Base.iterate()`, `Base.length()`, `Base.size()`, `Base.eltype()`, `Base.getindex()`, `Base.IteratorSize()`, `Base.IteratorEltype()`
- `src/base.jl`: `Base.show()`
- `test/examples/*.jl`: interface implementations such as `AbstractTrees.children()`, `AbstractTrees.nodevalue()` and `AbstractTrees.printnode()`. Before this change, `onenode.jl` and `onetree.jl` had no call edges at all.

Most of the extra `calls` edges come from the bodies of these methods, which were never walked before. A full `graphify update .` on the package builds cleanly (242 nodes, 392 edges, 25 communities).

title: fix(query): fallback BFS/DFS traversal omits relationships between visited nodes
body:
## Summary

Cubic identified a correctness bug in Graphify's generated query instructions.

The inline NetworkX fallback for `/graphify query` records graph edges only when traversal discovers a previously unvisited node.

This can omit valid relationships between already visited nodes, producing incomplete answers even when the underlying graph contains the missing edges.

## Affected file

`graphify/skills/codex/references/query.md`

Original downstream finding: `.codex/skills/graphify/references/query.md`, approximately line 133.

**Priority:** P2

## Root cause

Both BFS and DFS couple edge recording to node discovery.

In BFS, an edge is appended only when the neighboring node is absent from `subgraph_nodes`.

DFS similarly appends an edge only when the neighbor has not yet been visited.

However, a graph can contain multiple relationships connecting nodes already discovered during traversal.

Node visitation should control whether traversal expands a node again, not whether an existing relationship is included in the result.

## Minimal example

Consider a graph with three nodes:

- A
- B
- C

And three relationships:

- A → B
- B → C
- A → C

If A, B, and C are already selected as starting nodes, the BFS fallback records no edges between them because each target is already discovered.

The graph contains three valid relationships, but the traversal result can contain zero.

## Expected behavior

The fallback traversal should preserve all relevant relationships between included nodes, within the configured traversal depth and output budget.

## Actual behavior

Relationships to previously discovered nodes may be omitted, resulting in incomplete graph context.

## Suggested fix

1. Separate edge collection from node-discovery logic.
2. Use the visited set only to control traversal expansion.
3. Record all relevant traversed relationships.
4. Preserve edge direction and relationship metadata.
5. Avoid duplicate edges.
6. Add regression coverage for BFS, DFS, seeded nodes, cycles, and cross-links.
7. Update the authoritative skill-generation source and regenerate the affected artifacts.

## Verification

This issue was identified through static review of the generated workflow. The example above demonstrates the suspected failure mechanism; an automated regression test should confirm the behavior before implementing the fix.

I would be happy to contribute a PR addressing this issue.

title: fix(skill): complete induced subgraph in query fallback
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4314.

The inline NetworkX fallback for `/graphify query` recorded an edge only when BFS/DFS discovered an *unvisited* neighbour, so an edge between two already-visited nodes (two seeds, a triangle chord, a cycle arc, a cross-link) was dropped. The fallback returned a traversal tree rather than the induced subgraph over the node set it reports.

`graphify query` had the identical defect and already fixed it in #2323 via `graphify.serve._complete_induced_edges`; the inline fallback now mirrors that completion.

Reproduced on `v8` with the issue's example (seeds A/B/C; edges A→B, B→C, A→C):

| case | before | after |
|------|--------|-------|
| BFS, three seeds | 0 edges | 3 edges |
| DFS, three seeds | 2 edges (missing B→C) | 3 edges |
| BFS, single seed | 2 edges (missing B→C) | 3 edges |

## Changes

- `tools/skillgen/fragments/references/query/default.md`, `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/aider.md`, `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/devin.md`: add an induced-edge completion pass after the BFS/DFS walk. The visited set controls expansion only; edges are completed over the visited set (ordered-pair keys when directed, unordered `frozenset` otherwise; self-loops skipped; duplicates collapsed; edges incident to unvisited nodes excluded).

title: [Bug]: dedup _norm strips combining marks, so distinct Indic-script labels collapse into one node
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?


`graphify.dedup._norm` builds the dedup key with `re.sub(r"[\W_]+", " ", ...)`. In Python's `re`, `\w` matches only `str.isalnum()` characters plus `_`. Unicode combining marks (categories Mn/Mc: Devanagari/Tamil/Thai vowel signs, viramas, anusvara, etc.) are not alphanumeric, so they are treated as separators and deleted.

For Indic-script labels this destroys the word:

| label | `_norm(label)` |
|---|---|
| `हिंदी` | `ह द` |
| `कि` | `क` |
| `की` | `क` |
| `के` | `क` |

Consequences:

1. **False exact merge (Pass 1).** Three distinct same-file nodes labelled `कि`, `की`, `के` all share the key `क`, so they are merged into a single node and two entities are silently lost. Edges are rewired onto the survivor.
2. **Wrong fuzzy scoring (Pass 2).** Entropy gate, MinHash shingles and Jaro-Winkler all run over the mangled string, so unrelated Indic labels can score as near-duplicates and genuine ones are judged on the wrong text.

Expected: a label's vowel signs and viramas are part of the word. Different words must keep different keys; punctuation/underscore/whitespace should still collapse to a single space as before.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
from graphify.dedup import _norm, deduplicate_entities
print("norm:", ascii(_norm("\u0939\u093f\u0902\u0926\u0940")))
labels = [("h1", "\u0915\u093f"), ("h2", "\u0915\u0940"), ("h3", "\u0915\u0947")]
nodes = [dict(id=i, label=l, source_file="a.md", file_type="concept") for i, l in labels]
out, _ = deduplicate_entities(nodes, [], communities={})
print("survivors:", sorted(n["id"] for n in out))
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
norm: '\u0939 \u0926'
[graphify] Deduplicated 2 node(s) (2 exact).
survivors: ['h1']
(graphifyy) PS C:\Users\suraj\Desktop\projects\graphify>
```

### Graphify version

0.9.84

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.11

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

title: fix(dedup): keep combining marks in label normalization so Indic words don't collapse
body:
Fixes: #4317 

`graphify.dedup._norm` built the dedup key with `re.sub(r"[\W_]+", " ", ...)`. Python's `\w` does not match Unicode combining marks (categories Mn/Mc: vowel signs, viramas, anusvara), so they were deleted as if they were punctuation:

| label | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `हिंदी` | `ह द` | `हिंदी` |
| `कि` / `की` / `के` | `क` (all three) | distinct |

Three distinct same-file nodes `कि`, `की`, `के` shared one key, so Pass 1 merged them and two entities were silently lost. Entropy, MinHash shingles and Jaro-Winkler also ran on the mangled text.

**Implementation:** `_norm` now walks the NFKC-casefolded label and keeps a character if it is alphanumeric **or** a combining mark (`unicodedata.category(ch)` starts with `M`). Everything else, including `_`, still collapses to a single space, with leading/trailing separators trimmed. Two files changed: `graphify/dedup.py` (+`_is_label_char`, rewritten `_norm`) and `tests/test_dedup.py` (4 tests).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** two labels that differ in a vowel sign or virama are different words and must not share a dedup key; labels differing only by case, punctuation, underscores or whitespace still must.

**Persisted state:** none changed. `_norm` only computes in-memory dedup keys (and `norm_cache`); nothing here is written to `graph.json`, node IDs or the cache. A graph rebuilt after this change may keep Indic nodes that were previously (wrongly) merged, which is the intended correction.

- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.

**Regression tests (`tests/test_dedup.py`):**
- `test_norm_keeps_combining_marks` and `test_distinct_indic_words_are_not_exact_merged` **fail on unmodified v8** (`'ह द' != 'हिंदी'`, `['h1'] != ['h1','h2','h3']`) and pass with the fix.
- `test_norm_still_separates_punctuation_for_latin` and `test_identical_indic_labels_still_exact_merge` pin behaviour that must not change.

**Differential check:** old vs new `_norm` on ~190k random strings (ASCII, Latin-1/Extended, Cyrillic, CJK, ZWSP, em dash, ideographic space, emoji) containing no combining marks: 0 mismatches.

## Limitations / unsupported cases

- ZWJ/ZWNJ (category Cf) still act as separators, so Indic conjuncts written with an explicit joiner are split at the joiner.
- Casefolding can introduce a mark (e.g. Turkish `İ` → `i` + U+0307). That mark is now kept instead of turned into a space; `İstanbul` and `Istanbul` still do not share a key (they did not before either).
- Out of scope: `graphify.ids.normalize_id` has the same `[^\w]+` shape but produces persisted node IDs, so changing it needs a separate migration discussion. `build.deduplicate_by_label` carries the recipe too but is dormant (not called from `build()`).
- Only Devanagari and Tamil are exercised in tests; other mark-dependent scripts (Bengali, Telugu, Thai, Arabic harakat, Hebrew niqqud) follow from the same category rule but are not individually tested.

title: fix: write graph.json as one line of compact JSON (#3413)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #3413.

`graphify-out/graph.json` was written pretty-printed (`indent=2`). For a mid-size repo that is roughly a million lines, so every PR that commits a rebuilt graph reports 50k–160k changed lines.

GitHub does honor `linguist-generated=true`: the file is collapsed in the Files changed view and left out of the language statistics. It still counts every changed line toward the PR's additions/deletions totals, though, and no other attribute changes that either. Measured on pfBlockerNG/pfBlockerNG with `linguist-generated=true` in place, adding `-diff`, removing it, and marking the file `binary` all produced the same counts (for example +158987 −157008 for `graph.json` alone on one PR). This is why #3575 (attribute-only, closed by its author) could not fix #3413. Only the content of the file changes the count: one line of compact JSON shows as +1 −1.

This PR writes `graph.json` as one line of compact JSON (`separators=(",", ":")`, no indent) by default, at every writer of a project graph. There is no flag, env var, or config option. Readers are unaffected (`json.load`). Each site keeps its existing `ensure_ascii` and trailing-newline behaviour, so only whitespace changes.

### Writers changed

- `export.to_json` (clustered build, `update`, `cluster-only`, etc.)
- `watch._json_text` — candidate text for the `update --no-cluster` path
- `cli._prune_graph_json_sources` — `--no-cluster` exclusion prune
- `merge-driver` output (the committed graph.json)
- `merge-graphs --out`
- `extract --no-cluster`
- `global_graph._save_global_graph` — same node-link shape as a project graph; changed for consistency
- `paths.write_json_atomic` gains a `compact=` keyword used by the above

Left alone on purpose: manifest, `.graphify_labels.json`, `.graphify_analysis.json`, global manifest, Obsidian/canvas exports, installer configs, `reflect` sidecars and the skill files. They are not a project graph.json and are not what bloats PR diffs. The skill snippets that write `.graphify_*.json` intermediates are untouched.

### Existing indented graphs

`update` decides "nothing changed" by comparing parsed data (`_canonical_graph_for_compare`, `_canonical_topology_for_compare`), not bytes. An already-committed indented `graph.json` would therefore compare equal to the freshly built candidate and be left indented forever. `_rebuild_code` now checks whether the existing file is a single line; if not, the unchanged-graph / unchanged-topology skips are bypassed and the graph is rewritten compact once. A compact, unchanged graph is still left untouched.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant protected: a project graph.json is one line, round-trips to the same data, and an unchanged compact graph is not rewritten.

`tests/test_compact_graph_json.py` (new, 12 cases) drives real builds and CLI subprocesses:

- `to_json`, clustered `update`, `update --no-cluster`, `extract --no-cluster`, `merge-graphs`, prune, global graph: output is exactly one line with compact separators and loads to the expected nodes/edges.
- `merge-driver` on two compact inputs: one line, union of nodes and links.
- An existing indented graph is rewritten compact by `update` (clustered and no-cluster), with identical nodes/links.
- Guard: an already-compact unchanged graph is not rewritten (inode and mtime unchanged).

Red/green, same unchanged test file (`git hash-object` 6673ef56cb441291b6355343e446ac9d3168ed61 before and after):

- Unmodified `upstream/v8` (b4e6307): `10 failed, 2 passed` (the 2 passes are the "compact graph left untouched" guards). Failures are e.g. `graph.json spans 82 lines`, `cur.json spans 41 lines`.
- Writers changed but `update` legacy handling not yet added: the two `test_update_rewrites_existing_indented_graph_compact` cases fail with `graph.json spans 82 lines` / `67 lines`, proving that the data-equality skip alone leaves an indented graph in place.
- With this change: `12 passed`.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_compact_graph_json.py -q          # red on v8: 10 failed, 2 passed; green: 12 passed
uv run pytest tests -q -k "merge_driver or merge_graphs or global"   # 83 passed, 7 skipped
uv run pytest tests -q                                      # 6965 passed, 168 skipped, 1 failed
uvx ruff check <touched files>                              # All checks passed
```

The one failure, `tests/test_extract.py::test_collect_files_skips_hidden`, fails identically on unmodified `upstream/v8` in the same checkout (the worktree lives under a hidden directory), so it is unrelated.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] No skill fragments touched, so no skillgen run needed.
- [x] Extraction remains deterministic; only the serialized whitespace changes.
- [x] No unsafe interpolation into shell/Python.
- [x] No API keys or local-only graph data included.
- [x] AI authorship disclosed in the commit (`Co-Authored-By: Claude`).

Limitations: the first `update` after upgrading rewrites an existing indented graph.json once (one large diff in that commit), after which diffs are one line. The file is no longer human-readable without a formatter (`python -m json.tool`, `jq .`).

title: fix(explain): refuse a name that several nodes of one file carry
body:
## What does this PR do?

`explain` and the MCP `get_node` / `get_neighbors` tools refuse a name only when its winning match tier spans several source files. When several nodes of **one** file carry the name, the tie is broken by graph iteration order and one node is printed as the answer, with nothing saying a choice was made. `path` already refuses that case (#3913, #3935) and lists the node ids.

Two shapes seen on real graphs:

- Two classes of one module each define a method with the same name (`WebSocketRequestHandler.vmsg()` and `WebSocketServer.vmsg()` in one Python file). `explain ".vmsg()"` printed one of them.
- Per-file import stubs carry no `source_file`, so every stub of `EntityManagerInterface` counts as the same "file". `explain "EntityManagerInterface"` printed the stub of one test file, with that stub's degree.

Measured on three real PHP/JS/Python graphs (4.8k to 36.5k nodes), on 1,500 node labels drawn at random from each: 4, 12 and 22 labels resolved this way, silently.

**Change.** One helper, `_tier_refusal`, now decides whether the winning tier names a single node. `_resolve_single_node` (`explain`, `get_node`, `get_neighbors`) and `_resolve_path_endpoint` (`path`, `shortest_path`) both call it, so the four lookups refuse the same names with the same messages. A plain file path keeps its exception: its tier is the file node followed by its members, which is precedence, not a tie.

The `explain` CLI now resolves through `_resolve_single_node` instead of its own copy of the cross-file check. Exit codes are unchanged here (a refusal still exits 1, a miss still exits 0); distinct exit codes are a separate PR.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a lookup by name answers with a node only when the name designates exactly one node; otherwise it lists the candidates and their ids. The answer never depends on node order in graph.json.

Persisted state: none. Read-only commands.

title: fix(cli): give lookups distinct exit codes for ambiguous and missing names
body:
## What does this PR do?

**Depends on #4320** (stacked on that branch, so this PR's diff also shows its commit; the change proposed here is the last commit, 13dc240).

A script, or an agent driving the CLI, cannot tell from the exit code whether a lookup answered:

| Command | Answer | Ambiguous name | No matching node | Any other error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `explain` (v8) | 0 | 1 | **0** | 1 |
| `path` (v8) | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `query` (v8) | 0 | n/a | **0** | 1 |

`explain` and `query` report a miss with the same exit status as an answer, and `path` reports an ambiguity, a miss and a missing graph file with the same status.

This gives the refusals their own codes:

| Command | Answer | Ambiguous name | No matching node | Any other error |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `explain`, `path`, `query` | 0 | **3** | **4** | 1 (unchanged) |

- `explain`: a refusal that lists candidates exits 3, a miss exits 4 (was 0).
- `path`: an ambiguous endpoint, or both endpoints resolving to the same node, exits 3; an endpoint that matches nothing, including a `file::symbol` whose file defines no such symbol (#4264), exits 4. "No path found" between two existing nodes is still an answer and still exits 0.
- `query`: `No matching nodes found.` exits 4 (was 0).

The messages and the streams they go to are unchanged. The codes are named once in `cli.py` (`EXIT_AMBIGUOUS`, `EXIT_NOT_FOUND`). Ambiguity is told apart from a miss by `serve._is_ambiguity_refusal`, which checks the prefix that `_ambiguity_message` and `_same_file_ambiguity_message` now share through one constant, so the classification cannot drift from the messages. `--help` and the README's "Using the graph directly" section document the codes.

### Behavior changes users will see

- `explain` and `query` on a name that matches nothing now exit 4 instead of 0. Six tests in `tests/test_cli_export.py` ran `query "test"` / `explain "test"` against a fixture with no such node and asserted exit 0; they now look up `Transformer`, a node the fixture has, so they still prove the command ran against the right graph.
- Tests that pinned a refusal to exit 1 now expect the named constant.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: the exit code of a lookup says which of three outcomes happened (answer, ambiguous name, no match), and is never 0 unless an answer was printed.

Persisted state: none.

title: feat(query): add --strict to refuse a question that names no node
body:
## What does this PR do?

**Depends on #4321** (and through it #4320): stacked on that branch for the exit codes, so this PR's diff also shows their commits; the change proposed here is the last commit, 5452c26.

Adds `graphify query --strict`. Without the flag nothing changes.

`query` picks its traversal roots from the question's keywords. On a natural-language question those roots can be unrelated to the question, and the output does not say so. On a 36k-node PHP graph, `query "how does a host listing page reach the database"` started from an enum constant `LISTING`, a `page()` helper of a manual test script, the `Host` entity, an enum constant `DATABASES` and an unrelated test file, then printed 74 of 7,314 reached nodes. Nothing in the output says that four of the five roots are word collisions, so an agent cannot tell that answer from a good one.

`--strict` is for callers that would rather get a refusal than a guess:

- The question must name one node outright, with the forms `path` endpoints already accept exactly: a node id, an exact label, a file path, or `path::Symbol`. The traversal starts from that node only.
- A name that matches several nodes is refused with the candidates, exit 3 (the `explain` / `path` refusal).
- A question that names no node is refused, exit 4, with the next step:

```text
No node is named exactly 'how does a host listing page reach the database'. --strict starts only from a node the question names outright: its id, its exact label, its file path, or path::Symbol.
Look one up with: graphify explain "<path>::<Symbol>"
Connect two with: graphify path "<A>" "<B>"
Without --strict, query seeds from keywords, which may be off-topic.
```

**Implementation.** The exact-name part of `_resolve_path_endpoint` becomes `_resolve_exact_node`, which `path` and `query --strict` both call, so there is one definition of "names a node outright"; `path` keeps its score fallback after it. The keyword seeding moves unchanged into `_question_seeds`, and `_query_graph_text` takes an optional `start_nodes` that bypasses it. Rendering, budget, context filters and BFS/DFS are untouched.

Relation to #4289 (`--seed`): that PR lets an external ranker pass seeds next to a question and skips unresolved ones. `--strict` is the fail-closed reading of the question itself, and resolves through the same functions as `explain` / `path` rather than `affected.resolve_seed`. They can coexist.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: with `--strict`, `query` either traverses from the single node the question names, or prints a refusal and exits nonzero. It never seeds from a keyword match.

Persisted state: none.

title: fix(explain,query): say how to get the full answer when output is cut
body:
## What does this PR do?

A truncated answer says how much was cut, but not how to get the rest:

- `explain` lists the 20 most connected neighbors, then `... and N more` and a by-file summary. There is no option to list them all.
- `query` (CLI and MCP `query_graph`) and the MCP `get_neighbors` / `get_community` tools say "raise the token budget" without the value that would return everything, so a caller retries with a guess and may be cut again.

This PR:

- adds `explain --all`, which lists every connection. The cut line now reads `... and 5 more (--all lists all 25)`.
- puts the exact budget for the complete output in the truncation notice of `_subgraph_to_text` and `_cut_lines_to_budget`: `raise the token budget to 271125 to get all 7314 (CLI: --budget 271125, MCP: token_budget=271125)`. The value comes from the same 3-chars-per-token rule that does the cut. For `query` it is the smallest budget at which every node line fits, past which edges are never dropped (#2601, #2784), so the output is complete (possibly with the existing "complete answer over budget" notice). The tests check that this budget returns every node and edge and that one token less still truncates.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: every truncated `explain` / `query` / `get_neighbors` / `get_community` output states the total and an option that returns all of it.

title: docs(always-on): say large graph.json diffs in pull requests are expected
body:
A committed `graphify-out/graph.json` is rewritten whole on every build, so its pull-request diffs are large by design. Assistants reviewing such PRs flag the diff as churn and propose shrinking the graph or skipping the rebuild hooks, which defeats keeping the graph current.

This adds one rule to the Claude, AGENTS.md and Gemini always-on blocks, after the `graphify update` line:

> A committed graphify-out/graph.json is rewritten whole on every build, so a large diff to it in a pull request is expected. Do not flag it as churn or suggest skipping the graph rebuild or its hooks.

The change is recorded as a sanctioned skillgen edit, and the regenerated `always_on/*.md` and `expected/` files are included. All skillgen guards (`--check`, `--always-on-roundtrip`, `--audit-coverage`, `--monolith-roundtrip`) pass, as do `tests/test_skillgen.py` and `tests/test_install_strings.py`. #4319 (compact one-line `graph.json`) changes how these diffs look but not whether they happen.

title: [Bug]: OpenAI-compatible backends crash on null token counts in usage ('<' not supported between 'NoneType' and 'int')
body:
### What happened?

Semantic extraction through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint fails on every chunk when the endpoint returns a `usage` object whose token counts are `null`. The model's response itself is fine, but the whole chunk is discarded:

```
[graphify] chunk 1/1 failed: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'
```

`_call_openai_compat` only guards against `usage` being absent, not against its fields being `None`:

```python
# graphify/llm.py (v8, lines 1486-1487)
result["input_tokens"] = resp.usage.prompt_tokens if resp.usage else 0
result["output_tokens"] = resp.usage.completion_tokens if resp.usage else 0
...
output_tokens = result["output_tokens"]
if output_tokens < 50 and backend == "ollama":   # line 1500 -> TypeError
```

The comparison runs for every backend (the `backend == "ollama"` test is second), so any OpenAI-compatible gateway that reports `"completion_tokens": null` breaks, including custom providers from `~/.graphify/providers.json`. Even without that comparison, the `None` would fail later in the per-chunk merge (`merged["output_tokens"] += result.get("output_tokens", 0)`).

`_call_azure` has the same two lines (1888-1889).

### Steps to reproduce

No network needed; a fake client that returns null token counts reproduces it:

```python
import json
from types import SimpleNamespace as NS
import openai
from graphify import llm

body = json.dumps({"nodes": [{"id": "a", "label": "A"}], "edges": [], "hyperedges": []})

class Fake:
    def __init__(self, **kw):
        create = lambda **k: NS(
            choices=[NS(message=NS(content=body), finish_reason="stop")],
            usage=NS(prompt_tokens=None, completion_tokens=None),
        )
        self.chat = NS(completions=NS(create=create))

openai.OpenAI = Fake
llm._call_openai_compat("https://example.invalid/v1", "k", "m", "text", backend="openai")
# TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'
```

In real use: add a custom provider pointing at a gateway that omits token counts, then run `graphify extract <docs-folder> --backend <that-provider>`.

### Error output or graph output

```
[graphify extract] semantic extraction on 30 files via openai-custom...
[graphify] chunk 1/1 failed: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'
[graphify] WARNING: 1/1 semantic chunk(s) failed — see errors above. Partial results returned.
[graphify] WARNING: 30/30 dispatched file(s) produced no nodes and are absent from the graph: ...
[graphify extract] error: all semantic chunks failed for backend 'openai-custom' (30 uncached files) - see per-chunk errors above.
```

The second warning ("The model returned a response but omitted them") is misleading here: the model did return content; graphify dropped it while reading token counts.

### Proposed solution

Coerce null counts to 0 where the response is read, in both OpenAI-shaped paths:

```diff
-    result["input_tokens"] = resp.usage.prompt_tokens if resp.usage else 0
-    result["output_tokens"] = resp.usage.completion_tokens if resp.usage else 0
+    result["input_tokens"] = (resp.usage.prompt_tokens or 0) if resp.usage else 0
+    result["output_tokens"] = (resp.usage.completion_tokens or 0) if resp.usage else 0
```

This matches what the `claude-cli` path already does (`int(usage.get("output_tokens", 0) or 0)`). The Anthropic (`resp.usage.input_tokens`) and Bedrock (`usage.get("inputTokens", 0)`) paths have the same shape and may deserve the same guard, though I have not seen them fail.

With this patch applied locally to `_call_openai_compat` and `_call_azure`, a parametrized test over `usage` = `(None, None)`, `(120, None)`, `(120, 80)` and `usage=None` passes (it fails with the `TypeError` above before the patch). Happy to open a PR with the fix and the test.

One side effect worth noting: cost tracking reports 0 tokens for such endpoints. That seems acceptable (the data is not available), but a one-time warning might be friendlier than silent zeros.

### Graphify version

0.9.85

### Operating System

macOS (Darwin 25.6.0)

### Python Version

3.14

### Installation Method

`uv tool install "graphifyy[openai]"`

### Additional Environment Details

Custom provider defined in `~/.graphify/providers.json` (OpenAI-compatible gateway), `openai` Python package 3.28.0.

title: fix(dedup): rank a relative source_file against the scan root, not the CWD (#4281)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4281. Fixes the subdirectory case @gmos found in #4282 ([comment](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/pull/4282#issuecomment-6101831797)), which is still on v8 in 0.9.85. It does not touch the remaining `a/x.md` vs `b/x.md` case.

By dedup time a node's `source_file` is already root-relative, but `_rank_path` still called `.resolve()` on it, which prepends the CWD. When graphify starts from a subdirectory of the root, the renamed `x.html` node gets its own id but none of its edges.

```diff
 _rank_path(source_file, root)
-  if root and normalized:
+  if root and normalized and normalized is absolute:
     return normalized.resolve().relative_to(root)
   return normalized
```

Run from `root/firmware`:

| | node key | edge key | edge lands on |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | `firmware/firmware/lib/portal.html` | `firmware/lib/portal.html` | `firmware_lib_portal` |
| after | `firmware/lib/portal.html` | `firmware/lib/portal.html` | `firmware_lib_portal_html` |

I left `_source_key` in `extractors/resolution.py` alone. At extraction time a relative path is still CWD-relative, so resolving it there is right. The `_rank_path` docstring said it mirrored `_source_key`; it now says how they differ.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

A node and the edges from its file must get the same `_rank_path` key, whatever directory graphify runs from.

The regression test is #4282's absolute-edge-path test plus `monkeypatch.chdir(root / "firmware")`. It is committed before the fix, so checking out `f369742` alone shows it failing.

`_collision_rank` uses the same key, so the winner of a collision between relative paths no longer depends on the CWD either. Nothing persisted changes; the keys exist only inside dedup.

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test**.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

## How was this tested?

```text

uv run --python 3.10 pytest tests/test_dedup.py    # 109 passed

uv run ruff check .                                # all checks passed
uv run pyright graphify/dedup.py                   # 5 errors, the same 5 as on v8
```

## Limitations

Reverting the one condition restores the old behavior. Only dedup is affected. A relative path containing `..` is no longer normalized here; nodes are relativized before dedup, so stored paths shouldn't contain one.

title: feat(extract): symbol-level references for JS/TS value reads (#4265)
body:
## Problem

A function body that reads an imported or module-level value (a constant, a schema object, a value handed to a call) had no edge to it: the graph carried only `file --imports--> symbol`, so the function was reachable from the value only through `contains` and `affected` / `path` stopped at the file.

```
$ graphify path "buildManifest" "SeatInput"
buildManifest() <--contains-- seats/route.ts --imports--> SeatInput

$ graphify affected "SeatInput" --depth 2
- seats/route.ts [imports] src/seats/route.ts:L1
```

Both `readRoute()` and `buildManifest()` read `SeatInput`; neither appeared in `affected`, and every same-file function looked identical whether or not it touched the value.

## Implementation

Extend the existing JS/TS symbol-resolution fact pass (`graphify/extractors/resolution.py`) — the same mechanism that already resolves aliased-import `calls` — to emit `references` use facts (context `value`) from the enclosing function / arrow-const / class method to a value it reads:

- **Imported values** resolve through the file's import/alias table: `SeatInput`, `SeatInput.parse(...)`, a constant passed as an argument.
- **Same-file module-level values** resolve against the file's own symbol nodes.
- **Excluded (fail-closed):** reads shadowed by any local binding in the scope, import/export clause names, type positions, and names the scope also invokes as a call/JSX tag. That last guard matters: a second edge for an invoked `(caller, target)` pair would make the relation-blind cross-file call dedup in `extract()` skip the real `calls` edge — caught by the JSX cross-file test.
- `_js_top_level_function_bodies` is refactored onto a new `_js_top_level_function_nodes` (behaviour-preserving) so the value-read pass can see a function's parameters.

Additive: node ids unchanged, edge count grows.

## Verification

The issue's reproduction now resolves at symbol level:

```
$ graphify path "buildManifest" "SeatInput"
Shortest path (1 hops):
  buildManifest() --references [EXTRACTED]--> SeatInput

$ graphify affected "SeatInput" --depth 2
- route.ts [imports] src/seats/route.ts:L1
- buildManifest() [references] src/seats/route.ts:L3
- readRoute() [references] src/seats/route.ts:L2
```

`tests/test_js_value_reference_edges.py` adds regression tests: imported read, member read, arrow-const, class method, same-file value, parameter/local shadowing, invoked-name guard, and a JSX cross-file `calls` regression guard. The positive assertions fail on `upstream/v8` and pass with the change.

Commands actually run:

- `python -m pytest tests/ -q` → `6910 passed, 199 skipped, 7 failed`
- `python -m ruff check .` → clean

The same 7 tests fail identically on a clean `upstream/v8` checkout in this environment (git hooks / wheel-build / `os.getcwd()` subprocess tests); none touch JS/TS extraction. `pyright` is not installed in this environment, so it was not run.

## Limitations / unsupported cases

- Type-position uses are not value reads; they keep flowing through the existing type-reference passes.
- A value read inside a nested function is attributed to the enclosing top-level function (mirrors the existing `calls` facts pass).
- Namespace-member reads (`ns.foo`) reference `ns`, not the specific member.

Closes #4265.

title: [Bug]: `graphify uninstall --purge` deletes the whole project when `GRAPHIFY_OUT` is set but empty (or `.`)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?


`graphify uninstall --purge` is documented to delete `graphify-out/` (README: "add `--purge` to also delete `graphify-out/`"). When `GRAPHIFY_OUT` is set to an empty string, or to `.`, it instead runs `shutil.rmtree` on the **project folder itself**: source, `.git`, everything. It asks for no confirmation and prints only `/  ->  deleted (--purge)`.

| `GRAPHIFY_OUT` | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| unset / `graphify-out` | delete `./graphify-out/` | deletes `./graphify-out/` ✅ |
| `""` (set but empty) | treat as unset, delete `./graphify-out/` | **deletes the whole project** |
| `.` | refuse, since it is the project | **deletes the whole project** |

Without `--purge` the bad value still misroutes output: `out_path()` resolves into the project root, so `graph.json`, `cache/` and reports are written there instead of `graphify-out/`.

**Root cause** (`v8` @ b4e6307):
- `graphify/paths.py:28`: `GRAPHIFY_OUT = os.environ.get("GRAPHIFY_OUT", "graphify-out")`. The default only applies when the variable is *missing*; a set-but-empty value comes through as `""`. Then `GRAPHIFY_OUT_NAME` (`paths.py:397`) becomes `'.'` and `out_path()` (`paths.py:400`) points at the project root.
- `graphify/install.py:2143-2148`, the purge block in `uninstall_all()`: `out = pd / _GRAPHIFY_OUT` gives `Path(".") / ""`, which is `Path(".")`. Then `rmtree(out)` runs, with no check that `out` is inside the project and not the project itself.
- The same pattern appears in the git-hook rebuild bodies, `graphify/hooks.py:224` and `:299`. They read `os.environ.get('GRAPHIFY_OUT', 'graphify-out')` directly and miss `graphify-out/.graphify_root` when the value is empty. This doesn't delete anything, but it's the same bug.

**How an empty value happens in practice:** a `.env` entry left blank (`GRAPHIFY_OUT=`), docker-compose `GRAPHIFY_OUT=${GRAPHIFY_OUT}` when the host variable is unset, a CI variable defined with an empty value, or `export GRAPHIFY_OUT=` in a shell profile.


### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# Safe: neither step deletes anything. Run in bash from a graphify checkout or any env with graphify installed.

# 1. The path arithmetic the purge relies on:
python -c "from pathlib import Path; print(repr(Path('.') / ''), repr(Path('.') / '.'))"

# 2. What graphify resolves the output dir to:
GRAPHIFY_OUT= python -c "import graphify.paths as p; print(repr(p.GRAPHIFY_OUT), repr(p.GRAPHIFY_OUT_NAME), p.out_path('graph.json'))"
GRAPHIFY_OUT=. python -c "import graphify.paths as p; print(repr(p.GRAPHIFY_OUT), repr(p.GRAPHIFY_OUT_NAME), p.out_path('graph.json'))"
python -c "import graphify.paths as p; print(repr(p.GRAPHIFY_OUT), repr(p.GRAPHIFY_OUT_NAME), p.out_path('graph.json'))"

# 3. With either bad value, `graphify uninstall --purge` then calls rmtree(Path(".")).
#    WARNING: please don't confirm this in a real folder. Besides deleting the project,
#    `graphify uninstall` removes graphify from every agent platform on the machine.
#    Confirmed only in a throwaway temp project, with the platform uninstallers stubbed out.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
# step 1
WindowsPath('.') WindowsPath('.')

# step 2: empty, dot, unset
'' '.' graph.json
'.' '.' graph.json
'graphify-out' 'graphify-out' graphify-out\graph.json

# step 3: uninstall --purge with GRAPHIFY_OUT="" (temp project)
  /  ->  deleted (--purge)
# the project directory, including src/, no longer exists
```

### Graphify version

0.9.85 (v8 @ b4e6307)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

Python 3.14.5 (the dropdown has no 3.14 option). No provider/LLM environment variables are involved. A clean checkout of `v8` @ b4e6307 reproduces it. The code path is platform-independent, so it likely affects Linux and macOS the same way.


### Additional context

Likely also affected (not verified): `GRAPHIFY_OUT=..` (purge target would be the project's parent) and an absolute `GRAPHIFY_OUT` pointing at the project or one of its parents, since the purge has no containment check.

I have a fix with regression tests ready: it treats a blank value as unset, rejects `.`/`..` in `paths.py`, and adds a guard in `uninstall_all()` that refuses to purge the project, its parents, home or a filesystem root before anything is uninstalled. I'll open a PR that references this issue.

title: fix(install): never let uninstall --purge delete the project when GRAPHIFY_OUT is empty or "."
body:
Fixes #4328

## What does this PR do?

`graphify uninstall --purge` ran `rmtree(pd / GRAPHIFY_OUT)`. When `GRAPHIFY_OUT` was set but empty (a blank `.env` / docker-compose / CI entry) or set to `.`, that path was the project itself, and the whole project was deleted. The empty value also sent every output file (`out_path()`) into the project root.

Two independent layers:

1. **`graphify/paths.py`**: the new `_out_from_env()` strips the value and treats a blank `GRAPHIFY_OUT` as unset. A value that normalizes to `.` or to only `..` parts falls back to `graphify-out` with a stderr warning. Every other value is returned unchanged (after the strip), so custom relative and absolute output dirs (#686, #1423) behave as before. `GRAPHIFY_OUT_NAME` and `out_path()` derive from it.
2. **`graphify/install.py`**: `_unsafe_purge_reason()` refuses a purge target that is the project or any parent of it, the home folder or any parent of it, or a filesystem root. `uninstall_all()` runs this check **first**, before any platform uninstaller, so a refused purge exits 1 with nothing changed instead of leaving graphify half-uninstalled. This guard holds on its own, for example for an absolute `GRAPHIFY_OUT` that points at the project. It protects only the purge: such a value still sends normal output into the project root (see Limitations).

Also, the post-commit / post-checkout rebuild bodies in `graphify/hooks.py` now take the output dir from `graphify.paths` instead of re-reading the env var. Before, an empty value made them look for `.graphify_root` in the repo root. The hooks' shell gates already used `${GRAPHIFY_OUT:-graphify-out}`, which handles the empty case.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** `uninstall --purge` deletes only the output directory. It never deletes the project, an ancestor of it, the home directory or a filesystem root, whatever `GRAPHIFY_OUT` holds. A refused purge changes nothing.

`tests/test_uninstall_purge_safety.py` (new, 29 tests) runs the real `uninstall_all(purge=True)` on a `tmp_path` project with every platform uninstaller and `graphify.hooks.uninstall` stubbed. It uses the conftest sandbox home and clears `GRAPHIFY_OUT` first. It doesn't reload modules: it resolves the value through `paths._out_from_env()` and patches `install._GRAPHIFY_OUT`.
- `""`, `"   "`, `"."`, `".."`: only `graphify-out/` is removed, and the project and `src/` survive.
- An absolute path equal to the project, its parent, or the home dir is refused with `SystemExit(1)`. Nothing is deleted, and **no uninstaller stub was called**.
- Layer 1 bypassed (`install._GRAPHIFY_OUT = ""` / `"."`): still refused.
- Default, a custom relative dir, and a custom absolute dir outside the project are still purged.
- Filesystem roots are tested on the pure helper only, so a regression can never hand a real root to `rmtree`.

`tests/test_hooks.py`: one new test, run for both hooks. It runs the shipped root-resolution snippet in a fresh process with `GRAPHIFY_OUT=""` and checks that it still finds `graphify-out/.graphify_root`.

There are 31 new tests: 29 in `tests/test_uninstall_purge_safety.py`, plus the hook test above, which runs for both hooks. With the source changes stashed, 29 of them fail (27 in the new file plus both hook runs). The 2 that pass cover behavior this PR keeps: the default purge and uninstall without `--purge`. Among the failures, the bypass tests actually deleted the tmp project, and the hook test missed `.graphify_root`.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Limitations:**
- A value of only spaces makes the post-checkout hook's shell gate (`[ -d "${GRAPHIFY_OUT:-graphify-out}" ]`) skip the rebuild. It deletes nothing, and I left it out of scope.
- `_out_from_env()` can't know the project path at import time, so an absolute `GRAPHIFY_OUT` that points at the project (or a parent of it) isn't caught by layer 1. Only `--purge` is guarded against it: the purge is refused. Without `--purge`, `graph.json`, `cache/` and the reports are still written into the project root, as before this PR. Fixing that needs a project-aware check wherever the output dir is resolved, so I left it for a separate change.

**Related:** #3207 (open) would let `.graphifyrc` persist the output dir in a committed file. With this guard, a repo-supplied value still can't make `--purge` delete the project.

## How was this tested?

Windows 11, Python 3.14.5, `v8` @ b4e6307.

```text
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_uninstall_purge_safety.py tests/test_hooks.py -q
  -> all 31 new tests pass (with the source changes stashed, 29 fail: 27 in the new file + 2 hook runs)
uv run --frozen pytest tests -q
  -> 6922 passed, 227 skipped, 4 failed. The same 4 fail on unmodified v8 @ b4e6307:
     test_extract.py::test_c_include_out_of_root_target_id_is_deterministic_across_checkout_paths
     test_hooks.py::test_shebang_parse_requires_leading_hash_bang
     test_resolve_memoization.py::test_absolute_path_lookup_skips_getcwd
     test_source_key_memoization.py::test_absolute_path_lookup_skips_getcwd
uv run --frozen ruff check .                      -> All checks passed
uv run --frozen pyright <changed files>           -> 0 errors
uv run --frozen pre-commit run --files <changed>  -> skillgen-check, ruff: Passed
```

I also ran the real purge on a throwaway temp project with the platform uninstallers stubbed. Before the fix, `GRAPHIFY_OUT=""` and `"."` deleted the project. After it, both remove only `graphify-out/`, and the default case is unchanged. I also installed the hooks into a temp git repo and confirmed both generated hooks contain `from graphify.paths import GRAPHIFY_OUT as _out`. I never ran `graphify uninstall` itself.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. *(N/A: no skill fragments changed; `skillgen --check` passes.)*
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

**Suggested CHANGELOG entry** (not added; maintainers usually write these at release):
> Fix: `graphify uninstall --purge` no longer deletes the whole project when `GRAPHIFY_OUT` is set but empty or set to `.`/`..`. A blank value now means the default `graphify-out`, and `.`/`..` fall back to it with a warning. The purge refuses (exit 1, nothing changed) any target that is the project, a parent of it, the home folder or a filesystem root. The git hooks now resolve the output dir the same way (#4328).

title: [Bug]: `affected` on an overriding method misses every caller that reaches it through the base or interface method
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

A call site names the declared type, so its `calls` edge points at the base or interface member: `walker.walk(v)` with `v: NodeVisitor` links to `NodeVisitor.head`. At runtime it runs whichever override the object has. Nothing links an override to the member it overrides, so `graphify affected` on the override walks only the callers that name the subclass, and every caller through the base type is missing.

```java
interface NodeVisitor { void head(String n); }
class Printer implements NodeVisitor { public void head(String n) {} }
class Walker { void walk(NodeVisitor v) { v.head("x"); } }
```

```console
$ graphify affected printer_printer_head
Affected nodes for .head()
...
No affected nodes found.
```

`Walker.walk` runs `Printer.head`. (The node id is used because `Printer.head` as a name is #4134's subject.)

Expected: Changing `Printer.head` affects `Walker.walk`: the callers of the member an override overrides are callers of the override too.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
Save the three classes as `NodeVisitor.java`, `Printer.java`, `Walker.java`, run `graphify update .`, then `graphify affected printer_printer_head`. With this fix: `- .walk() [calls] Walker.java:L1`.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
No error. `affected` prints `No affected nodes found.` for the overriding method.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.85 (b4e6307b)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

Windows 11, Python 3.12, graphify 0.9.85 from source (v8 b4e6307b).

### Additional context

For every method that overrides a supertype member, javac's callers that reach it only through that member (Java, `src/main/java`), and how many `affected(method, depth 1)` lists, 0.9.85:

| project | callers through the overridden member (files) | listed |
|---|---|---|
| jackson-core | 1125 | 6 (1%) |
| commons-io | 637 | 0 (0%) |

title: fix(affected): walk the callers of the supertype member an overriding method overrides
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4330.

`affected_nodes` now treats a method's overridden members as stepping stones. When the walk reaches a method node, it finds the method's class (incoming `method` edge), that class's supertypes (`inherits` / `extends` / `implements`, transitively), and their same-named members, and walks those members' callers at the same depth. The overridden member itself is not reported (it did not change), unless a real edge reaches it too (a base overload calling the abstract member shares its node). It runs at query time: no new edges, no graph or cache change, every language with those edges (Java, TypeScript, Python, Kotlin, C#, ...).

This is class-hierarchy analysis: a caller bound to `Base.m` is listed for every override of `m`, since any of them can run there.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a caller bound to a member that a method overrides is affected by that method, at the depth of a direct caller.

Against javac (callers of each overriding method that reach it only through the member it overrides, by file), 0.9.85 vs this branch, `affected(method, depth=1)`:

| project | callers through the overridden member | listed before | listed after |
|---|---|---|---|
| jackson-core | 1125 | 6 (1%) | **707 (63%)** |
| commons-io | 637 | 0 (0%) | **480 (75%)** |
| jsoup | 452 | 3 (1%) | **298 (66%)** |
| commons-lang | 341 | 1 (0%) | **160 (47%)** |

The rest are calls with no `calls` edge at all (receiver types graphify does not resolve yet), not the walk. TypeScript, callers of overridden members on graphify's own edges: TypeORM 1737 missed -> 0, NestJS 98 -> 0.

Cost, every method of the project as a seed, depth 2: jackson-core 0.01 -> 0.30 ms per query, jsoup 0.02 -> 0.12 ms, TypeORM 0.01 -> 0.14 ms; mean hits per seed 3.5 -> 6.3 / 4.2 -> 6.1 / 2.2 -> 3.7.

title: [Feature]: Python: calls on a pytest fixture parameter (`runner.invoke()`) get no calls edge
body:
### Problem or use case

A test names a fixture as a parameter and pytest passes in what the fixture returns:

```python
# tests/conftest.py
@pytest.fixture
def runner():
    return CliRunner()

# tests/test_basic.py
def test_help(runner):
    result = runner.invoke(cli, ["--help"])   # no edge to CliRunner.invoke
```

The parameter has no annotation, so `_python_local_class_bindings` leaves it untyped and `runner.invoke()` gets no edge. Tests are where this pattern lives, so the graph cannot tell which tests exercise `CliRunner.invoke`, and `graphify affected` on it lists none of them.

Measured on graphify 0.9.85: in click's test suite, 413 member calls go through the `runner` fixture (`return CliRunner()` in `tests/conftest.py`), and none has a `calls` edge.

### Proposed solution

Mark each `@pytest.fixture` function with the class it returns (return annotation, including `Iterator[T]` / `Generator[T, ...]` for yield fixtures, else a single class in every `return` / `yield`), mark calls on an untouched, unannotated parameter of a test or fixture in a test module / conftest.py, and resolve them in `_resolve_python_member_calls` against the fixture pytest itself would pick: the test's own module, then the conftest.py of its directory and of each directory above it. The class goes through the existing typed-receiver gate, judged from the fixture's file.

### Alternatives considered

Requiring `runner: CliRunner` annotations in tests: few suites annotate fixture parameters.

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Python only. No node or edge ids change. Fixture function nodes gain `_py_fixture` and Python raw calls a `_python_fixture_param` marker, so the AST cache schema goes 7 -> 8; `_py_fixture` and the unchanged files' import edges are forwarded on changed-files rebuilds. New INFERRED `calls` edges only, none removed. No generated skills or MCP output format change.

### Additional context

Found while measuring `graphify affected` against real test suites (a crash inserted in a function; the failing tests are the truth): test -> fixture -> code paths were cut at the fixture parameter. PR right after this issue.
