title: [Bug]: Python files can disappear from the graph when a class is used before it's defined
body:
## What's happening

In some Python projects, whole files go missing from the graph, and the classes inside them get tangled up. There's no error, so it's easy to miss.

I noticed it on [rich](https://github.com/Textualize/rich): when I ran `graphify update rich/rich`, two of its main files, `markdown.py` and `syntax.py`, weren't in the graph at all.

When it happens:

- the file itself disappears from the graph
- the class with the same name as the file ends up "containing" itself and every other class in the file
- other files that import it look like they import the class instead of the file
- some calls made from inside that file are quietly left out

## When it happens

All three of these at once:

1. The file is directly in the folder you point graphify at, not in a subfolder
2. It has a class with the same name as the file, like `Widget` in `widget.py`
3. Something earlier in that file mentions the class before it's defined, like a type hint `w: Widget`

Naming a file after its main class is pretty common, like `console.py` with `Console`, so this shows up in real projects.

## How to see it for yourself

Make a folder with these two files and run `graphify update .`:

`widget.py`
```python
from __future__ import annotations

class Helper:
    def make(self, w: Widget) -> None:
        w.draw()

class Widget:
    def draw(self):
        return 1
```

`app.py`
```python
from widget import Widget

def use(w: Widget):
    w.draw()
```

Then look at `graphify-out/graph.json`:

- there's no `widget.py` node
- `Widget` "contains" itself and `Helper`
- `app.py` imports `Widget` the class instead of `widget.py` the file
- the call from `Helper.make` to `Widget.draw` is missing, while the same call from `app.py` is there

## What should happen

`widget.py` should be in the graph like any other file, and the `Widget` it mentions should just point to the class defined lower down in the same file.

## How much it matters

I checked graphify's call links against [Jedi](https://github.com/davidhalter/jedi) on rich. On 0.9.85, with this fixed, graphify finds **54 more correct calls**, going from 64.6% to 68.6%, with no wrong links added and none lost. Both missing files come back too.

---

**Version:** graphify 0.9.85 · macOS 26.4 · Python 3.14

title: [Bug]: graphify reads files that git's global ignore file hides
body:
## What's happening

graphify skips files listed in a project's `.gitignore`, but it doesn't look at git's global ignore file. So a file that git ignores on your machine can still end up in the graph.

I noticed it because a local settings file showed up in graphify's file list, even though git ignores it. The rule for it lives in my global ignore file at `~/.config/git/ignore`, not in the project's `.gitignore`.

The global ignore file is where a lot of people keep rules for local settings and secret files, so they don't have to add them to every project. graphify reading those files is the part that worries me.

## How to see it for yourself

```bash
mkdir demo && cd demo && git init
echo 'x = 1' > a.py
echo 'SECRET = "abc"' > secret.py
echo 'secret.py' > ~/my-ignore
git config core.excludesFile ~/my-ignore

git status --short        # secret.py isn't listed, git ignores it
graphify update .
```

`secret.py` is in `graphify-out/graph.json`.

I used `git config` inside the repo so the example doesn't touch your global settings. It's the same setting git uses for the global ignore file, and `~/.config/git/ignore` behaves the same way.

## What should happen

If git ignores a file, graphify should skip it too, the same way it already does for `.gitignore` and `.git/info/exclude`. `--no-gitignore` could keep turning this off like it does for the others.

This came up before as a suggestion in #1363, but only the fix for `.gitignore` and `.graphifyignore` working together went in.

---

**Version:** graphify 0.9.85 · macOS 26.4 · Python 3.14

title: [Feature]: Python: reading a `@property` (`response.text`) gets no edge to its getter
body:
### Problem or use case

A Python property is a method that runs on attribute access:

```python
class Response:
    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        return self.content.decode(self.encoding)

def show(r: Response):
    return r.text          # runs Response.text, no edge
```

graphify links calls, and `r.text` is not a call, so nothing points at `Response.text`. The getter looks unused, `explain` lists no readers, and `graphify affected` on it misses every reader. Properties hold real logic in most libraries (URL parsing, encodings, lazy attributes).

Measured on graphify 0.9.85: httpx declares 54 properties, click 24, flask 19; reads of them on a typed receiver get no edge (httpx 65 such reader -> property pairs, flask 37, click 26).

### Proposed solution

Mark `@property` / `@cached_property` / `@x.getter` methods, record attribute reads whose receiver is typed the way member calls already are (`self`, a typed local or parameter, a `self.X` field bound to one class), and resolve them through `_resolve_python_member_calls`, keeping only targets that are properties. The edge is `references` with context `property_read`, as #3120 does for C# member reads, so `calls` stays call sites only.

### Alternatives considered

A `calls` edge: the getter does run, but a read is not a call site, and mixing them would change what call-graph queries return.

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Python only. No node or edge ids change. Property methods gain `_py_property` and Python raw calls gain attribute-read entries (`_python_attr_read`), so the AST cache schema goes 7 -> 8; `_py_property` is forwarded on changed-files rebuilds. New `references` edges with context `property_read` only; `calls` edges unchanged. No generated skills or MCP output format change.

### Additional context

Found while measuring `graphify affected` against real test suites (a crash inserted in a function; the failing tests are the truth): in httpx, many test -> code paths go through properties (`url.host`, `response.encoding`). PR right after this issue.

title: feat(python): link reads of a `@property` to its getter
body:
## What does this PR do?

title: feat(extract): add EJS (.ejs) template extractor
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3811 (same gap as #2511).

`.ejs` is in `CODE_EXTENSIONS` but had no AST extractor, so an Express/Node app's
server-rendered views were counted as code and contributed nothing to the graph
(the `#1689` "no AST extractor" warning). They are not dumb HTML: they carry
`<% %>` scriptlets (including `require`/`import`), inline `<script>` blocks, and
`<%- include('partials/_page-header') %>` composition.

Adds `extract_ejs`. A `.ejs` file fed whole to the JS grammar is one top-level
ERROR that loses every symbol (the `.svelte` lesson of #3928), so the extractor
masks the template down to the JavaScript it can actually read — the bodies of
code tags (`<% %>` / `<%_ %>`) and of JS `<script>` blocks — and parses them with
the TS grammar, the same strategy `.svelte`/`.vue`/`.astro` use. Output
expressions (`<%= %>`/`<%- %>`), comments (`<%# %>`) and markup are blanked while
preserving line numbers; an output tag inside a `<script>` body is replaced by a
length-preserving `0` so the surrounding statement still parses.

Two regex passes then add what no JS grammar can see: dynamic `import('./X')`
calls written in a scriptlet, and the EJS `<%- include('partial') %>` composition
edge an Express view graph is built on, resolved to the real partial `.ejs` file.

`.ejs` is wired into `_DISPATCH`, the `jsts` language family, the JS
resolve/cache sets, and the hook source extensions.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature

## Verification & Invariants

- `.ejs` no longer trips the `#1689` warning; it produces nodes and edges.
- Masking preserves byte offsets and line numbers (regression-tested), so
  `source_location` still points at the original lines.
- Include resolution mirrors the existing Svelte/Vue/Astro regex rescue: a
  relative hit is stamped with `target_file` (no absolute-path ghost stub,
  #2195), and an unresolved bare/views-root include keeps a stub so the edge is
  never dropped.
- Deterministic: no ambient state, no ENV dependence.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_ejs_extractor.py \
  tests/test_extract.py tests/test_languages.py tests/test_detect.py \
  tests/test_import_extension_resolution.py tests/test_svelte_extraction.py \
  tests/test_vue_extraction.py tests/test_astro_extraction.py \
  tests/test_astro_import_ids.py tests/test_blade_extractor.py \
  tests/test_cjs_module_extension.py tests/test_typescript_module_extensions.py \
  tests/test_package_json_subpath_imports.py -q
# 1219 passed, 25 skipped

uv run ruff check <changed files>   # All checks passed
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --check   # check OK
```

The one failing test on this base (`test_unmapped_at_alias_resolution.py::test_3357...`)
also fails on `upstream/v8` without this change (host VCS-root interference); it is
unrelated.

title: graphify now respects git's global ignore file
body:
Fixes #4335.

## What this fixes

You can tell git to ignore files in each project with a `.gitignore`, or once for your whole computer with git's global ignore file. graphify was respecting the first one but not the second, so a file you hid using the computer-wide list could still end up in your graph.

That global list is usually where people put local settings and other private files, so it's the one that matters most here.

## What changed

graphify now reads git's global ignore file too, the same way git does:

- if you've set one with `git config core.excludesFile`, it uses that
- if not, it uses git's default spot, `~/.config/git/ignore`
- your project's own `.gitignore` still wins, so a `!` rule there can bring a file back in, same as git
- `--no-gitignore` turns it off along with the other git ignore rules
- it only kicks in inside a git repo, like git

## How I tested it

- Ran the example from the issue. Before this change `secret.py` showed up in the graph, now it doesn't.
- Added tests for a custom `core.excludesFile`, the default `~/.config/git/ignore`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, a project `!` rule beating the global one, `--no-gitignore`, and a folder that isn't a git repo. They fail on the current `v8` and pass with this change.
- Full test suite passes.

## Heads up

This means what graphify picks up can now depend on your global git settings, not just files in the project. That's the point of the fix, and it's the same thing git does, but it's worth knowing if two people get slightly different file lists.

title: fix(llm): coerce null token counts to 0 across backends

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4325.

Some OpenAI-compatible gateways return a `usage` object whose token-count fields are `null`. The backend readers only guarded against `usage` being absent, not against its fields being `None`, so `result["input_tokens"]` / `result["output_tokens"]` became `None` and crashed extraction for the whole chunk:

- `_call_openai_compat`: `TypeError: '<' not supported between 'NoneType' and 'int'` at the ollama low-token warning (`output_tokens < 50` runs for every backend — the `backend == "ollama"` check is second).

title: [Feature]: `graphify benchmark` measures answer size but never whether the answer is right
body:
### Problem or use case

`graphify benchmark` reports how many tokens a query costs versus reading the corpus. Nothing measures whether the answer contains what the question needed, so a change to query scoring, seeding or rendering can make answers smaller and worse and the benchmark calls it a win. Twenty-odd open PRs change how `query` ranks or renders (#2403, #3284, #3417, #3636, ...), and there is no shared number to compare them by.

I built such a number from a public set with known answers: the 177 SWE-bench Lite issues of django, pytest, sphinx, requests, flask, pylint, seaborn, xarray and astropy, each repo built at the commit its issues were filed against, the issue title as the question and the files the real fix changed as the right answer. `query_graph` with the MCP defaults (BFS, depth 3, ~2000 tokens), graphify 0.9.85:

| | right file is the first file shown | in the first 3 | in the first 5 | anywhere in the answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `query_graph` | 25% | 34% | 38% | 62% |
| BM25 over the repo's .py files (reference) | 32% | 56% | 64% | 92% in the top 50 |

The same set run against some open query PRs (each applied on its own base, same graphs):

| | first 5 | answers carrying "Complete answer over budget" (full issue text as the question) |
|---|---|---|
| 0.9.85 | 38% | 55 of 177 |
| #2403 (no test-path seeds) | 51% | 38 |
| #3417 (ranking rewrite) | 51% | 146 |
| #3284 | 39% | 61 |
| #3636 | 38% | 55 |

### Proposed solution

`graphify benchmark --questions FILE`: a JSON list or JSON Lines of `{"question": ..., "files": [...]}`. Each question goes through `query_graph` as the MCP tool runs it; the report gives how often an expected file is the first file shown, in the first 3 and 5 files, anywhere, and the answer size. `--json` for raw per-question results, `--depth` / `--budget` to match other settings. A project's own history supplies questions: issue titles and the files their fixes changed.

### Alternatives considered

A separate harness outside the repo (what produced the tables above): nobody running or reviewing a query change has it, and it drifts from the real `query_graph` path.

### Area

Graph building or querying

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

CLI and docs only. `graphify benchmark` without `--questions` is unchanged; no graph, cache, extraction or MCP output change.

### Additional context

Questions built from SWE-bench Lite (problem statement title, files of the gold patch), each repo checked out at the most common base commit of its instances. PR right after this issue.

title: fix(python): keep file node when a class is type-hinted before it's defined (#4334)
body:
Fixes #4334

**What changed**

In `_extract_generic` (`graphify/extractors/engine.py`), a forward reference like `w: Widget` before `class Widget` in `widget.py` minted a bare `widget` stub, which is the same id the file node gets once paths are made relative, so the file node got swallowed and `Widget` ended up "containing" itself and `Helper`. Now the stub is still emitted exactly as before, but after the walk, if the name turns out to be a class defined in this file, references get rewired to that class and the stub is dropped. Anything else (an imported `Widget`, or a `def widget()` with the same id) is left on v8's sourceless-stub path for the cross-file rewire.

**How I tested it**

- New `tests/test_python_forward_ref_file_id.py`: the issue repro (single file + with an importer), `pkg/widget.py` importing `Widget` from `.base` (no dangling edges, `use()` links to `base.Widget`), and a `def widget()` with no class (no reference to the function).
- Ran the issue's 2-file repro with `graphify update .` (fresh `graphify-out`) before and after:
  - before: no `widget.py` node, `Widget contains Widget/Helper`, `app imports_from Widget`, no `Helper.make -> draw` call
  - after: `widget.py` node is back and contains both classes, `app.py` imports_from the file, `.make() calls .draw()` shows up
- Also checked live: `pkg/widget.py` + `from .base import Widget` and the `def widget()` case both give the same graph as v8.
- `ruff check` clean. Full suite on py3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14: the only failures (`test_dm_*` and 7 `test_security` safe_fetch/validate_url tests) fail the same way on v8 too.

One note: in the 2-file repro the file node's id comes out as `widget_py_widget` rather than `widget`. That's because `app.py`'s own `Widget` stub still collides, and v8 already does exactly the same thing even without the forward ref, so I left it alone here.

_I used an AI assistant (Grok Bot) to help write this; I reviewed and tested the change myself._

title: fix(skills): improve installation and output path handling
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes four installation and path-handling issues in Graphify's generated agent integrations.

### Changes

**1. Guard missing Graphify executables in Codex hooks**

- Generated hooks previously invoked `graphify hook-check` even when Graphify was unavailable.
- Add POSIX and Windows command guards that skip execution when Graphify is missing.
- Preserve failure exit codes when the installed executable runs unsuccessfully.

**2. Support interpreter paths containing spaces**

- Quote the saved Python interpreter substitution in both add/watch command examples.
- Prevent executable paths containing spaces from being split into separate shell arguments.

**3. Correct multi-repository clone and merge paths**

- Use explicit, quoted clone destinations with `graphify clone --out`.
- Build each repository's graph at its own location.
- Merge the corresponding `graphify-out/graph.json` files.
- Stop the workflow when cloning or extraction fails.
- Avoid capturing the multiline human-readable output of `graphify clone` as a path.

**4. Report the actual graph output location**

- Correct the skill completion message to report the resolved current-working-directory `graphify-out` path.
- Avoid incorrectly reporting the scanned input directory as the output destination.

All affected generated skill artifacts and expected snapshots were regenerated from the authoritative sources.

## Regression tests

Added or updated tests covering:

- Missing Graphify executable in generated hooks.
- POSIX and Windows hook command behavior.
- Interpreter paths containing spaces.
- Clone destinations and multiline CLI output.
- Failed clone operations stopping downstream commands.
- Correct graph completion output paths.

## Verification

- Full pytest suite: **7,171 passed, 15 skipped** (run before the final clone-workflow correction).
- Focused installation/path tests: **152 passed**.
- Final clone-workflow regression tests: **9 passed**.
- Ruff: **Passed**.

- Skillgen coverage and consistency checks: **Passed**.

Native PowerShell execution was unavailable in the macOS test environment. Windows hook coverage validates the generated command and its expected path-handling behavior.

## Related issues

title: [Bug]: /graphify skill "Step 1 - Ensure graphify is installed" exits 0 and leaves empty graphify-out files when a write fails; .graphify_root readers trim folder names
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Step 1 of the `/graphify` skill ("Step 1 - Ensure graphify is installed") saves two files that every later step depends on:

- `graphify-out/.graphify_python`: which Python to run
- `graphify-out/.graphify_root`: which folder is being scanned

There are two bugs around these files.

**Bug 1: Step 1 reports success when it can't write them**

Actual: Step 1 writes each file with `open(path, 'w').write(...)`. Opening the file creates it right away, so when the write fails (for example on a full disk), Python prints `OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device`, but the empty file stays behind and Step 1 exits 0. After that:

- Every later step runs `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "..."`, which becomes an empty command. Bash prints `bash: : command not found`, and nothing points back to Step 1 or the full disk.
- `graphify update` with no path reads the empty `.graphify_root` as `Path("")`, which is the current directory, so it rebuilds whatever folder you're in instead of the project, without a warning.

The Windows version of Step 1 does the same: `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText` throws, PowerShell prints the error, and the script keeps going.

Expected: if Step 1 can't write a file, it exits non-zero with a message naming the file (for example `could not write graphify-out/.graphify_root (disk full?)`), and it doesn't leave an empty file behind.

**Bug 2: readers trim spaces off the saved folder name**

Actual: Linux and macOS allow a folder name to end with a space, such as `proj `. Step 1 saves the path exactly, but `graphify update` (`cli.py`), `_infer_merge_root` (`build.py`) and both git hook scripts (`hooks.py`) read it back with `.strip()` and get `proj`. If a `proj` folder also exists, they work on that folder instead.

Expected: readers use the path exactly as Step 1 saved it. They only remove a UTF-8 byte-order mark (added by Windows PowerShell 5.1, see #3028) and a trailing newline.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
Linux, from the root of a `v8` checkout (commit `b4e6307`). No root access needed. The full disk is a private 2 MB filesystem that disappears when the command ends.

**Setup (both bugs):** save Step 1 from the skill to a script.


python3 - > /tmp/step1.sh <<'EOF'
import re
text = open("graphify/skill.md").read()
blocks = re.findall(r"\n(.*?)\n", text, re.S)
print(next(b for b in blocks if "graphify_root" in b))
EOF


**Bug 1: run Step 1 on a full disk**


unshare -rm bash -c '
  mkdir -p /tmp/fullfs && mount -t tmpfs -o size=2M tmpfs /tmp/fullfs
  mkdir -p "/tmp/fullfs/work/my project"
  dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/fullfs/fill bs=64k 2>/dev/null   # fill the disk
  cd /tmp/fullfs/work
  sed "s|^INPUT_PATH\$|/tmp/fullfs/work/my project|" /tmp/step1.sh > /dev/shm/step1.sh
  bash /dev/shm/step1.sh; echo "Step 1 exit code: $?"
  stat -c "%s bytes  %n" graphify-out/.graphify_python graphify-out/.graphify_root
  $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "print(1)"; echo "next step exit code: $?"
'


Output:


OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device      (printed twice)
Step 1 exit code: 0
0 bytes  graphify-out/.graphify_python
0 bytes  graphify-out/.graphify_root
bash: line 9: : command not found
next step exit code: 127


**Bug 2: a folder name ending in a space**


mkdir -p /tmp/sp/"proj " /tmp/sp/proj && cd /tmp/sp
sed "s|^INPUT_PATH\$|/tmp/sp/proj |" /tmp/step1.sh | bash
python3 -c "
from pathlib import Path
saved = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_root').read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig')
print('Step 1 saved:', repr(saved))
print('readers get: ', repr(saved.strip()))
"


Output:


Step 1 saved: '/tmp/sp/proj '
readers get:  '/tmp/sp/proj'


`/tmp/sp/proj` is a different, existing folder, so `graphify update` and the git hooks would work on it instead of `proj `.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
**Bug 1: what Step 1 prints on a full disk**

Python reports both failed writes, but only as "Exception ignored" while shutting down, so neither the command nor Step 1 fails:


Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='graphify-out/.graphify_python' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='/tmp/fullfs/work/graphify-out/.graphify_root' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
Step 1 exit code: 0


What's left on disk, and what the next step prints:


0 bytes  graphify-out/.graphify_python
0 bytes  graphify-out/.graphify_root
bash: line 9: : command not found
next step exit code: 127


How an empty `.graphify_root` is read by `graphify update` (no path):


Path("") -> current directory


**Bug 2: the saved folder vs. what readers get**


Step 1 saved: '/tmp/sp/proj '
readers get:  '/tmp/sp/proj'      <- a different folder that exists


There's no graph output to show: both bugs happen before or around the graph build, by pointing it at the wrong folder or stopping it with an unclear error.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.85 (v8 branch, commit b4e6307)

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

- Provider environment variables: none set (no OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GRAPHIFY_* or similar). Neither bug involves a provider: both happen in Step 1's file writes and in the readers of `.graphify_root`, before any extraction.
- Clean checkout: yes. Both bugs reproduced in a fresh worktree of `upstream/v8` at `b4e6307`, with no local changes.
- OS: Fedora 43 (Linux, x86_64), bash 5.3. Bug 2 also applies to macOS. Windows doesn't allow trailing spaces in folder names, but its Step 1 has the same write problem as Bug 1 (`WriteAllText` throws and the script continues).
- Full disk was simulated with a private 2 MB tmpfs (`unshare -rm`), as in the steps above. I first hit Bug 1 on a real full `/tmp` while running the test suite.


### Additional context

**Where the code is (line numbers on `v8` at `b4e6307`)**

Bug 1, where Step 1 writes the files. The skill text is generated from these fragments, so a fix goes here and then `python -m tools.skillgen --bless`:

- `tools/skillgen/fragments/shell/posix.md` lines 32-40: writes `.graphify_python` and `.graphify_root` with `open(...).write(...)`
- `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/aider.md` and `core/devin.md`: their own copies of Step 1 (ending at lines 100 and 113)
- `tools/skillgen/fragments/shell/powershell.md` lines 59 and 68: the Windows Step 1, writing both files with `WriteAllText`

Bug 2, the readers that call `.strip()` on `.graphify_root`:

- `graphify/cli.py` line 2552: `graphify update` with no path
- `graphify/build.py` line 624: `_infer_merge_root`
- `graphify/hooks.py` lines 227 and 302: the post-commit and post-checkout hook scripts. These are templates copied into `.git/hooks`, so hooks that are already installed keep the old code until they're reinstalled.

**How I found it**

While running the test suite for #4309, `/tmp` filled up, because some tests create a ~168 MB home folder each. After that, `test_step1_still_resolves_a_legitimate_path` started failing with the repo folder where the project folder should be. The cause was Bug 1: Step 1 had left `.graphify_root` empty, and the test read `Path("")`, which resolves to the current directory.

**Related**

- #4309: its PR adds `read_scan_root()`, which reads `.graphify_root` with `.strip()` like the readers above. Whichever fix lands second should update it.
- #3028: why the readers decode with `utf-8-sig` (Windows PowerShell 5.1 adds a byte-order mark). A fix should keep that.

I'm happy to send a PR for both bugs.

title: [Bug]: `graphify benchmark` counts its own copy of the query, not the answer query_graph returns
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`graphify benchmark` reports how many tokens a query costs, but it never asks `query_graph`. `_query_subgraph_tokens` in `graphify/benchmark.py` runs its own copy of the query: seeds are the 3 labels with the most substring hits, then a BFS with **no token budget**, printed in its own line format. The real `query_graph` (the MCP tool and `graphify query`) picks seeds differently (exact / prefix / substring tiers, source and rationale matches, the gap window), stops at the ~2000-token budget and adds its notices. So the number is not what an agent pays.

Example, flask, "what are the core abstractions": the benchmark counts 10,361 tokens. `query_graph` answers with 2 nodes (~61 tokens):

```console
Traversal: BFS depth=3 | Start: ['click_core'] | 2 nodes found

NODE click_core [src= loc= community=]
NODE cli.py [src=src/flask/cli.py loc=L1 community=]
EDGE cli.py --imports_from [EXTRACTED context=import]--> click_core at=src/flask/cli.py:L15
```

Expected: the benchmark measures the answer `query_graph` returns for each question (MCP defaults: BFS, depth 3, ~2000-token budget).

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
git clone https://github.com/pallets/flask && cd flask
graphify update . --no-cluster
graphify benchmark graphify-out/graph.json
graphify query "what are the core abstractions"     # compare its size with the benchmark's line for that question
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Average tokens per sample question (the benchmark's 4 chars/token), graphs built with 0.9.85:

| graph | benchmark says | query_graph really returns |
|---|---|---|
| requests (1,352 nodes) | ~8,807 (10.2x fewer) | ~2,780 (32.4x fewer) |
| flask (2,080) | ~12,824 (10.8x) | ~1,224 (113.3x) |
| pytest (5,809) | ~4,918 (78.7x) | ~2,521 (153.6x) |
| django (45,984) | ~278,990 (11.0x) | ~1,619 (1893.5x) |

It is wrong in both directions: with the 177 SWE-bench Lite issue titles of these repos (plus sphinx, pylint, seaborn, xarray, astropy) as questions, the benchmark's median is 767 tokens and the real answers' median is 1,634.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.85 (b4e6307b)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No LLM keys; AST only. Windows 11, Python 3.12. Clean checkout of v8 @ b4e6307b (0.9.85) reproduces.

### Additional context

Related: #2674 (same function, None-label crash, fixed). #4341 is about answer quality, this one about answer size. PR right after this issue.

title: fix(benchmark): count the tokens of the answer query_graph returns
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4347.

- `benchmark.py`: `_query_subgraph_tokens` returns the token estimate of `_query_graph_text(G, question, mode="bfs", depth=3, token_budget=2000)`, the function behind the MCP `query_graph` tool and `graphify query`, and 0 when it answers "No matching nodes found.". The copy of the query (own seeds, unbudgeted BFS, own line format) is removed; `token_budget` is a new keyword, defaulting to the MCP default.

The size cap and the `edges` -> `links` normalization (#2212) come along unchanged. title: feat(ingest): ingest REA reverse-engineering output (JavaScript Application Graph)
body:
## What

Adds a graphify ingester for [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea)'s **JavaScript Application Graph** (JAG). REA reverse-engineers shipped apps (native binaries, JS/Electron, .NET, WASM) and emits a canonical, evidence-bearing graph; this turns that into a queryable graphify graph:

```bash
graphify extract --rea app.jag.json
# then: graphify query / path / explain over a reverse-engineered app
```

graphify maps code you *have source for*; this lets you do the same for code you *don't*.

## How

- **`graphify/rea_ingest.py`** — `ingest_rea_jag(doc, source_file="")` → `{nodes, edges}`:
  - JAG node kinds → graphify `file_type` (structural artifacts → `code`; process/IPC boundaries like package/IPC-channel/contextBridge → `concept`).
  - JAG relations (`contains/loads/imports/calls/invokes/sends/exposes/handles/maps_to/persists_to/observed_as/changed_from`) → graphify's relation vocab, with the **original relation preserved** in the edge context (`rea:<relation>`).
  - REA epistemic state → confidence: `observed` → `EXTRACTED`, `inferred` → `INFERRED` (score capped); `unavailable` edges dropped.
  - **Endpoint-safe**: mints `rea_external` stubs so no edge dangles. Graph-wide `coverage`/`limitations` attached to root-node metadata.
- **CLI**: `graphify extract --rea <jag.json>` merges alongside the AST/semantic/postgres/cargo sources (mirrors the existing ingesters).
- Tests: `tests/test_rea_ingest.py` (8) + `tests/fixtures/rea_jag_sample.json`.

## Status / notes

- **Draft** — built against REA's documented JAG contract (`docs/javascript-application-graph.md`) plus a synthetic fixture. Should be **validated against a real `rea ... --json` export** before merge; field-name aliases are accepted where the prose contract is slightly ambiguous.
- Licensing: REA is MIT; this consumes its JSON *contract*, not its code.
- Follow-up: native-binary findings (functions/calls/symbols) as a second ingestion slice.

title: fix(julia): name parametric functors by their type, not the variable
body:
Follow-up to #4310 (shipped in 0.9.86). This fixes the advisory finding the Graphify review flagged on that PR at `julia.py:197`.

## Bug
For a parametric functor definition, the type sits in a `parametrized_type_expression`. `_def_name` took the last `identifier` in the typed expression, which there is the **variable**, not the type:

| Definition | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `(b::Box)(x, y) = x` | `(Box)()` | `(Box)()` |
| `(b::Box{T})(x) where T = x` | `(b)()` ❌ | `(Box)()` |

The bogus `b#call` node also split methods of one functor across two nodes, which defeats the shared-node-per-generic-function design.

## Fix
`_def_name` now reads the last operand (an `identifier` or a `parametrized_type_expression`) through the existing `_type_name_of` helper, which already unwraps `Box{T}` for struct heads.

## Tests
`test_julia_parametric_functor_uses_type_not_variable` covers `(b::Box{T})`, `(b::Box)` and `(::Box{T})`, and asserts that all three share one `(Box)()` node. The test fails without the fix (`['(b)()', '(Box)()']`). All 466 tests in `tests/test_languages.py` pass.

title: fix(transcribe): include video transcripts in semantic extraction
body:
## Summary

Fix two bugs in Graphify's video/audio transcription workflow that affect first builds and downstream semantic extraction.

Previously:

1. The Whisper prompt instructions referenced god-node labels that were unavailable during first builds.
2. Successfully transcribed video files were recorded in `.graphify_transcripts.json` but omitted from `.graphify_detect.json`, which Step B0 uses to determine semantic extraction inputs.

As a result, transcription could rely on nonexistent context, and valid video transcripts could be silently excluded from graph extraction.

## Changes

**1. Fix first-build Whisper prompt generation**

- Generate domain hints only from genuinely available corpus context, such as readable documents or README files.
- Use previous analysis only when available and relevant to the current corpus.
- Fall back to a generic transcription prompt when reliable context is unavailable.
- Avoid depending on god-node analysis that has not yet been generated.

**2. Include video transcripts in semantic extraction**

- Add `update_detect_with_transcripts()` to synchronize successful transcript paths with the detection inventory.
- Record valid transcripts in `files.document` before Step B0.
- Replace the transcript manifest with the current run's successful transcripts.
- Remove stale generated transcript entries.
- Exclude missing, invalid, duplicate, and out-of-directory transcript paths.
- Preserve original source documents and other detection metadata.
- Stop before semantic extraction when either sidecar update fails.

**3. Regenerate skill artifacts**

- Update the authoritative shared transcription fragment.
- Regenerate the transcription

title: fix: Step 1 fails loudly instead of leaving empty marker files; readers keep .graphify_root exactly (#4346)
body:
**Stacked on #4344. Please review that one first.** The first 8 commits here belong to #4344. This PR adds the last 4.

With both applied, Step 1 does two things: it refuses a scan path with a line break (#4344), and it fails loudly when a write fails (this PR). `read_scan_root()` from #4344 now calls `read_root_marker()` from this PR, so one function decides how the marker is read.

> **In short:** on a full disk, Step 1 left `.graphify_python` and `.graphify_root` empty and still exited 0, and six readers trimmed spaces off the saved folder (`proj ` became a sibling `proj`). Now Step 1 writes safely and fails loudly, and every reader keeps the folder name exactly. Fixes #4346.
>
> **To review:** about 180 hand-written lines in 11 files (list below). The other 32 changed files are regenerated by `uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`, and `--check` confirms they match the sources.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4346.

Step 1 of the `/graphify` skill saves two files that every later step reads: `.graphify_python` (which Python to run) and `.graphify_root` (which folder to scan).

**1. Step 1 said "done" even when it couldn't save them.** On a full disk it left both files empty and exited 0. The next step failed with `bash: : command not found`, and `graphify update` rebuilt the current folder instead of the project. Now Step 1:

```text
deletes last run's files
writes each file to a temp file, then renames it into place
on any error: cleans up, says which file, exits 1
```

So after Step 1, both files are complete and from this run, or Step 1 failed and said so. The Windows Step 1 does the same.

**2. Six readers used `.strip()` on the saved folder.** A folder named `proj ` (legal on Linux and macOS) came back as `proj`. A new `read_root_marker()` removes only a byte-order mark (#3028) and a final newline, and every reader uses it: `graphify update`, `build.py`, `watch.py`, `reflect.py` and the two git hooks. `graphify update` now also stops on an empty `.graphify_root` instead of guessing.

### How to review

| File | What changed |
|---|---|
| `tools/skillgen/fragments/shell/posix.md` | Step 1 writes both files in one Python call (35 lines) |
| `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/aider.md`, `core/devin.md` | the same Step 1 block, copied |
| `tools/skillgen/fragments/shell/powershell.md` | the Windows Step 1 (23 lines) |
| `graphify/paths.py` | new `read_root_marker()` (11 lines) |
| `graphify/cli.py`, `build.py`, `watch.py`, `reflect.py`, `hooks.py` | each reader switches to it (1–15 lines each) |
| `tools/skillgen/gen.py` | the exact list of changed lines the monolith check allows |
| `tests/test_graphify_root_marker.py`, `tests/test_skillgen_input_path_injection.py` | the tests |

Skip `graphify/skill*.md`, `graphify/skills/**` and `tools/skillgen/expected/**`. They're generated.

### Evidence: before and after

Step 1 with `ulimit -f 0`, so every write fails the way it does on a full disk:

```text
v8:           Step 1 exit code 0, .graphify_python and .graphify_root left empty
this branch:  "could not write graphify-out/.graphify_python (File too large; is the disk full?)",
              exit code 1, no files left behind
```

`graphify update` with the saved folder `proj ` and a sibling `proj`:

```text
v8:           rebuilds proj (the wrong folder)
this branch:  rebuilds proj  (the saved folder)
```

<details>
<summary>Reproduce bug 1</summary>

From a checkout of `v8`:

```bash
python3 - > /tmp/step1.sh <<'EOF'
import re
text = open("graphify/skill.md").read()
print(next(b for b in re.findall(r"```bash\n(.*?)\n```", text, re.S) if "graphify_root" in b))
EOF
mkdir -p "/tmp/s1/my project" && cd /tmp/s1
sed -e "s|^INPUT_PATH\$|/tmp/s1/my project|" \
    -e "s|^mkdir -p graphify-out\$|mkdir -p graphify-out\ntrap '' XFSZ; ulimit -f 0|" /tmp/step1.sh | bash
echo "exit: $?"; wc -c graphify-out/.graphify_*      # exit 0, two empty files
```

</details>

### Commits

```text
d8baf79  tests for both bugs
96aa478  Step 1 saves its files safely and fails loudly (bash, aider, devin, Windows)
2d3e236  graphify update, build.py and the hooks read the folder exactly
378d4b2  watch.py and reflect.py too, plus a test that catches any new .strip() reader
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**The rule:** if `.graphify_python` or `.graphify_root` exists and isn't empty, it holds what this run of Step 1 found, and every reader gets that exact value.

**Enforced by:**

- **Step 1 failing a write:** all three bash copies run under `ulimit -f 0` with old files present. Each must exit non-zero, name the file and leave nothing behind. The Windows Step 1 gets the same test under `pwsh`, with a directory blocking its temp file (`ulimit` stops pwsh itself from starting on CI). That test skips where `pwsh` isn't installed.
- **Readers:** `proj ` and `proj` stay apart in `read_root_marker()`, `build.py`, the hooks and `graphify update`. A guard test fails if any module reads a file as `utf-8-sig` and then calls `.strip()`.

All of these fail on `v8` and pass on this branch.

**What changes for existing setups:**

- Installed git hooks keep the old code until `graphify hook install` is run again.
- `graphify update` with an **empty** `.graphify_root` now exits 1. A **missing** one still falls back to the current folder.

**Limitations:** not tested on Windows PowerShell 5.1. The Windows Step 1 ran under PowerShell 7.4.6 on Linux.

title: [Bug]: C/C++ `#include "x.h"` only resolves next to the including file — headers reached through include paths become file-less stub nodes (40% of includes in an STM32Cube project)
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.86 (also seen on 0.9.9), macOS, Python 3.12, AST extraction (`graphify update .` and the skill's Part A).

## Summary

`_resolve_c_include_path` (`graphify/extractors/resolution.py`) only tries `Path(includer).parent / raw`. C projects rarely keep headers next to the file that includes them. Usually headers sit in a separate include directory (`Inc/` + `Src/`, `include/` + `src/`, `-I` paths from the build). When the sibling lookup fails, the edge falls back to the bare stem id, and:

- if the header has a same-stem `.c` (the normal `foo.h` / `foo.c` pair), the stem is ambiguous and the edge lands on a **stub node with no `source_file`**;
- if the stem is unique, it happens to resolve by name.

So the commonest C layout gets the worst result, and no warning is printed.

## Minimal repro

```
proj/
  Core/Inc/adc.h               int adc_read(void);
  Core/Src/adc.c               #include "adc.h"
  app/nfc.h                    int nfc_poll(void);
  app/test/support/harness.c   #include "nfc.h"
                               #include "adc.h"
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract
from graphify.build import build_from_json
files = [Path(p) for p in ("Core/Inc/adc.h", "Core/Src/adc.c", "app/nfc.h", "app/test/support/harness.c")]
G = build_from_json(extract(files, cache_root=Path(".")), root=".", directed=True)
for u, v, d in G.edges(data=True):
    if d.get("relation") == "imports":
        print(G.nodes[u].get("source_file"), d.get("source_location"), "->", v, repr(G.nodes[v].get("source_file")))
```

Actual (0.9.86):
```
Core/Src/adc.c L1 -> adc ''                    # stub, no file
app/test/support/harness.c L2 -> adc ''        # stub, no file
app/test/support/harness.c L1 -> app_nfc 'app/nfc.h'
```
Expected: both `adc.h` includes → the `Core/Inc/adc.h` file node.

## Impact on a real project

The project is a firmware monorepo: an STM32CubeWL modem (`Core/Inc` + `Core/Src`, the HAL, LoRaWAN and Sigfox stacks) plus an MSP430 application whose host tests include the application headers through `-I`. Of 1,052 quoted includes that resolve to a tracked file:

| | 0.9.86 | 0.9.9 |
|---|---|---|
| correct file node | 627 | 692 |
| file-less stub node | 425 | 144 missing |
| a wrong file node | 0 | 197 (`adc.h` → `adc.c`, a header → a Markdown doc with the same stem) |

0.9.86 no longer points includes at wrong files (thanks!), but 40% of the include structure is still disconnected.

## Suggested fix

When the sibling lookup fails, search the corpus before falling back to the stem, roughly like the compiler's `-I` search:

1. If a `compile_commands.json` exists, try its `-I` directories in order (exact).
2. Otherwise, take the scanned files whose path ends with `/<raw>` (same file name and any directory parts in `raw`), and pick the one sharing the **longest directory prefix** with the including file. A tie stays unresolved; don't guess.
3. Only when no exact-case candidate exists, retry case-insensitively (macOS/Windows builds find `msp430fr2476.h` as `msp430FR2476.h`).

We run step 2 + 3 as a post-processing pass on `graph.json` (about 40 lines, re-resolving each `#include` line from the source). It resolves all 1,052 includes, with no false matches on the system headers (55) or the 18 ambiguous names. Happy to turn it into a PR against `resolution.py` if this approach is acceptable.

## Also noticed (separate, minor)

The standard C++ guard in C headers triggers a false "syntax errors … no symbols extracted" warning (184 headers here; every STM32Cube header has it):

```c
#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif
...
#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

The outcome is the same as for an unguarded header: C headers yield no symbols in either case (typedefs and prototypes are not modelled). So the warning is noise, but it makes real parse errors easy to miss.

title: [Bug]: PowerShell dot-source (. file.ps1) creates no imports edge, and script-scope calls are dropped
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.63 · Microsoft Windows 11 Home Single Language · Python 3.11.9

## Summary

In PowerShell files, two common cross-file patterns produce no edges:

1. **Dot-sourcing** another script (`. "$PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1"`) creates no `imports` edge from the caller file to the sourced file. Dot-sourcing is PowerShell's equivalent of an import, so the file-level dependency is lost.
2. **Calls made at script scope** (outside any `function`) are dropped. Only calls inside a function body get an edge.

Calls *inside* functions do resolve across files (as `INFERRED`), so the gap is limited to these two cases. They are the usual shape of PowerShell entry-point scripts: dot-source a library at the top, then call its functions at script scope.

## Minimal repro

`lib.ps1`:
```powershell
function Get-Answer { return 42 }
```

`main.ps1`:
```powershell
. "$PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1"
function Invoke-Main { Get-Answer }
Invoke-Main
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract
d = Path(r"<folder with the two files>")
r = extract([d / "main.ps1", d / "lib.ps1"], cache_root=d)
print([n["id"] for n in r["nodes"]])
for e in r["edges"]:
    print(e["source"], e["relation"], e["target"], e.get("confidence"))
```

Actual output:
```
['main', 'main_invoke_main', 'lib', 'lib_get_answer']
main contains main_invoke_main EXTRACTED
lib contains lib_get_answer EXTRACTED
main_invoke_main calls lib_get_answer INFERRED
```

## Expected

In addition to the edges above:
- `main imports lib` (EXTRACTED), from the dot-source line.
- `main calls main_invoke_main`, from the script-scope call on line 3 (with the file node as the caller).

## Impact

In a real repo (a few PowerShell build/flash scripts that dot-source a shared `toolchain.ps1` and a helper module), the graph showed the scripts as unconnected. Every `--update` that re-extracted those files dropped any hand-added edges, so they had to be re-added after each run.

Related, but different: #3992 and #4158 (PowerShell method-call resolution).

title: [Bug]: query prints per-term guaranteed seeds in alphabetical order, burying the answer file on multi-term queries
body:
### Problem

`_pick_seeds` guarantees one seed per query term (#1445) and appends those seeds in `sorted(best_seed_by_term)`,
which is alphabetical term order. `_subgraph_to_text` prints seeds first. So on a multi-term query, a weak match on an
early-alphabet term is printed ahead of a specific term's exact match, and the answer file can fall below what an
agent reads first.

A minimal case: the query `alpha bravo charlie apple zebra` on a graph where all five are exact labels and eight
more labels contain `apple`. The start line is `['alpha', 'bravo', 'zebra', 'apple', 'charlie']`, so the common term's
seed is printed before the rare exact match `charlie`.

### Measured

I measured this on AST-only graphs (`graphify update --no-cluster`) with graphify's own `_score_query`, `_pick_seeds`
and `_query_graph_text`, on graphify 0.9.86 (v8 a5ba60d). hit@5 = the answer file is among the first 5 files
`graphify query` prints:
- 114 Django issues from SWE-bench Lite; the answer is the file the official fix changed. Queried by the title plus
  the first 400 characters: **hit@5 53**. Yet a start node lies in the answer file on **83** of them.
- In those misses the answer's seed usually sits at positions 6-10, after per-term seeds ordered alphabetically.

### Proposal

Order the guaranteed seeds by the strength of each term's best match:
- `_score_query` already ranks each term's winner with `(-singleton score, -degree, label length, node id)`, and the
  singleton score carries the term's IDF weight.
- `_score_query` would return that order (`term_order`), and `_pick_seeds` would iterate it, keeping the sorted
  order when `term_order` is not given.
- The same seeds are picked, the traversal reaches the same nodes, and the order stays deterministic.

| set | hit@3 v8 / proposed | hit@5 v8 / proposed |
|---|---|---|
| Django issues, title + 400 chars (114) | 53 / 58 | 53 / **63** |
| Django issues, title only (114) | 46 / 48 | 54 / 55 |
| full-stack-fastapi-template, 100 questions | 29 / 33 | 36 / 37 |

Per question, hit@5 moved +10/-0, +4/-3 and +1/-0 on those three sets. The
[evaluation script and data](https://github.com/devkancheti4-design/model-d-graphify/tree/master/bench/graphify-seed)
reproduce every number above.

I have a PR ready, with tests that fail on v8 and pass with the change.

title: fix(query): order the per-term guaranteed seeds by match strength (#4357)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4357.

`_pick_seeds` guarantees one seed per query term (#1445), but it appended those seeds in `sorted(best_seed_by_term)`,

title: Hook install/uninstall identifies graphify's hooks by the substring "graphify" and drops whole hook groups, including other commands in them
body:
**Summary**

When graphify installs or removes its own `PreToolUse` hooks, it identifies them by checking whether the case-sensitive substring `graphify` occurs anywhere in the stringified hook group. For Claude Code and CodeBuddy the group must additionally use one of the matchers recognised by the removal filter (`Glob|Grep`, `Bash`, `Bash|Grep`, `Read|Glob`; the current install writes `Bash|Grep` and `Read|Glob`); for Codex there is no matcher restriction. Every group that passes this filter is removed as a whole, including other commands in it and unrelated groups whose command path happens to contain `graphify`. The uninstall path rewrites the settings file without creating a backup.

**Where** (v0.9.84, `graphify/install.py`)

- Claude: `_install_claude_hook` L2078 and `_strip_graphify_hook` L2102 - `h.get("matcher") in ("Glob|Grep", "Bash", "Bash|Grep", "Read|Glob") and "graphify" in str(h)`. Install writes through `_write_settings_with_backup` (L2080); uninstall writes with `settings_path.write_text(json.dumps(settings, indent=2), ...)` at L2106.
- Codex: L1770 and L1790 - `"graphify" not in str(h)`, no matcher restriction.
- Gemini (`BeforeTool`): L1012 and L1026; CodeBuddy: L2261 and L2275 (same matcher restriction as for Claude Code).
- Permalink: https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/2cb81c6fd5ec0758453606a3a76e516e893199b4/graphify/install.py#L2078-L2106

For Claude Code, the hooks are installed by `graphify claude install [--project]` and removed by `graphify claude uninstall [--project]` and by `graphify uninstall`.

**Why it matters**

`str(h)` covers the whole group (`{"matcher": ..., "hooks": [...]}`), not graphify's individual command, so:

1. If a user adds their own command to the `hooks` array of one of graphify's groups, the whole group is removed on the next hook install or uninstall, including the user's command.
2. A separate group of another tool that uses one of the four matchers above (any matcher for Codex) and whose command path contains `graphify` (for example a script under a folder named `graphify-notes`) is removed as well.
3. Uninstall does not create or update a `.graphify-bak` of the settings file, so recovering the removed entries depends on an earlier backup or version control. The file is also re-serialised with `json.dumps(settings, indent=2)`, which escapes non-ASCII characters and changes the indentation to two spaces.

Guard hooks (security, formatting, audit) are typical entries in these files, and a guard that disappears without a specific message is easy to miss.

**Minimal reproduction**

1. Run `graphify claude install --project` so that `.claude/settings.json` contains graphify's `PreToolUse` groups.
2. Add your own command as a second object in the `hooks` array of graphify's `Bash|Grep` group. Add a separate `PreToolUse` group with matcher `Bash` whose command path contains `graphify` (e.g. `python /tools/graphify-notes/check.py`).
3. Run `graphify claude uninstall --project` in the same project directory.

Expected: only graphify's own commands are removed; your command and the unrelated group stay.
Actual: both groups are removed completely, and no backup of the previous settings file is written.

**Suggested fix**

1. Identify graphify's commands inside the individual `hooks[]` elements instead of matching `str(group)`, covering the variants it writes (`hook-guard search`, `hook-guard read` with optional `--strict`, `hook-guard gemini`, `hook-check`, with the emitted executable path). Remove only those commands and drop a group only when it becomes empty.
2. Optionally tag graphify's entries with a dedicated marker so they can be found unambiguously (if the host accepts the extra field).
3. Use `_write_settings_with_backup` (or an equivalent single backup) on the uninstall paths too.
4. In `_strip_graphify_hook`, guard `h.get(...)` against non-dict entries (a string entry raises `AttributeError`; the install path already checks `isinstance(h, dict)`).

**Environment**

graphify 0.9.84 (code re-checked on the release commit above). Windows 11, Claude Code. Found during an internal security review.

title: `install`/`uninstall` still rewrite line endings of CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and related files (remaining paths after #3741)
body:
**Summary**

#3741 fixed the CRLF conversion in `_register_always_on_block` and in the Gemini install path. The remaining writers listed below still use `Path.write_text` without `newline=""`, and all of them read existing files through `Path.read_text`, which normalises CRLF to LF before the text is modified. When these paths rewrite an existing file, its line endings are normalised to CRLF or LF depending on platform and writer; the original convention is not reliably preserved. (An install that changes nothing, or an uninstall without a graphify section, leaves the file untouched.)

**Where** (v0.9.84, `graphify/install.py`)

- Still without `newline=""`: `claude_install` L2047, `_agents_install` L1809, `codebuddy_install` L2238, `_strip_graphify_md_section` L2216 (uninstall of CLAUDE.md), `_agents_uninstall` L1983 (AGENTS.md), `gemini_uninstall` L1060, `vscode_install` L1117 (L1120 creates a new file), `vscode_uninstall` L1160, `codebuddy_uninstall` L2311.
- Fixed in #3741: `_register_always_on_block` L498-L533 and `gemini_install` L935-L948 - but these still read with `read_text(encoding="utf-8")`.
- Permalink: https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/2cb81c6fd5ec0758453606a3a76e516e893199b4/graphify/install.py#L2197-L2218

**Why it matters**

On Windows, these writes convert the normalised LF text to CRLF whenever a rewrite happens. That changes the bytes of an LF file in the working tree and can show up as an every-line diff where git does not normalise line endings (with `* text eol=lf`, `git diff` may hide it). On Linux/macOS a CRLF file loses its `\r` the same way. For `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, which are often shared and reviewed, that can hide the real change in noise and trip line-ending checks.

**Minimal reproduction** (Windows, Git Bash, Python 3.12)

1. In a project directory, create `CLAUDE.md` with LF line endings (`printf 'a
b
' > CLAUDE.md`).
2. Run `graphify claude install`, then `graphify uninstall`.
3. Inspect the file (`file CLAUDE.md`).

Expected: only the graphify block is added and later removed; the remaining lines keep LF.
Actual: the file is rewritten with CRLF line endings. The same read-modify-write pattern in isolation (`read_text`, append, `write_text`) turns both LF and CRLF input into CRLF on Windows with the default write, or into LF with `newline=""`; neither choice preserves both input conventions.

**Suggested fix**

Read the existing file without newline translation (`open(..., newline="")`, or read bytes and decode; `Path.read_text(newline=...)` needs Python 3.13), detect its line ending, write the new block with that ending (the helpers currently join with a hard-coded `
`), and write with `newline=""` everywhere. A single helper used by all install/uninstall writers would cover the remaining paths and keep them from drifting apart again. A round-trip test per writer (LF file and CRLF file in, same endings out, only the graphify block changed) would pin it.

**Environment**

graphify 0.9.84 (release commit above). Windows 11, Claude Code. Found during an internal security review.

title: Semantic extraction and labeling pick a cloud backend from ambient API keys (and `claude -p` as a fallback) without an explicit opt-in
body:
**Summary**

When the headless CLI needs semantic extraction, community labeling or `--dedup-llm` and no backend was supplied, graphify auto-detects one from environment settings, checking the built-in cloud providers before Ollama. If labeling finds no backend, it falls back to the `claude` CLI when that is on `PATH`. The README documents the order, but there is no general switch that requires a cloud backend to be named explicitly. #3300 / #3305 raise this for Bedrock only; this issue is the general case.

**Where**

- `graphify/llm.py` L3190-L3220 `detect_backend()`: gemini -> kimi -> claude -> openai -> deepseek -> azure -> bedrock (selected by the presence of `AWS_PROFILE` / `AWS_REGION` / `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`) -> ollama; custom registered backends are checked after Ollama.
- Callers that use it when no backend is given: `graphify/cli.py` L3869-L3871 (`extract`), `graphify/llm.py` L1970 (library `extract_files_direct`), L3548 (labels).
- `graphify/llm.py` L3551-L3559: `if not backend and _claude_cli_available(): backend = "claude-cli"`, which runs `claude -p` with the prompt on stdin (L2947-L2974).
- README "Data residency" (L613) describes the order.
- Permalink: https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/2cb81c6fd5ec0758453606a3a76e516e893199b4/graphify/llm.py#L3190-L3220

**Why it matters**

API keys in a developer environment are often there for other tools (a coding assistant, a notebook, CI). A user who runs `graphify extract .` without `--backend`, expecting a local run, can send the content of uncached documents (and image data where the backend supports it) to the automatically selected cloud provider. The CLI prints `semantic extraction on N files via <backend>` just before the requests, but it does not ask for confirmation or say which environment setting selected the backend. When community labeling runs with no backend configured and `claude` on `PATH`, the community node labels are passed to `claude -p`; there the CLI only prints `Labeling communities...`.

For private or customer repositories this is a consent question rather than a bug. Today a user has to manage the backend selection or skip the LLM work: explicitly select a local backend, configure Ollama while keeping the earlier cloud selectors out of graphify's environment, use `--code-only` without `--dedup-llm`, or use `cluster-only --no-label` on an existing graph.

**Suggested fix**

1. Treat cloud backends as opt-in: use one only if it is named (`--backend <name>`, or a new setting such as a `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND` environment variable or config key). Without that, use a configured local backend (Ollama), otherwise skip the semantic step with a clear message (the AST pass keeps working).
2. If auto-detection is kept for convenience, say in the existing line which environment setting selected the backend and how to change it, and honour a "none" switch (as proposed in #3305) for every backend, not only Bedrock.
3. Treat the `claude -p` fallback the same way, since it normally sends the prompt to a hosted model: it should need the same opt-in.
4. Mention the opt-in in the skill text so the host agent does not suggest a cloud run on its own.

Compatibility: an opt-in would require users who rely on auto-detection today to pass `--backend` (or set the new setting) once; a one-line hint when a key is found but not used would make that easy.

**Environment**

graphify 0.9.84 (release commit above). Windows 11, Claude Code. Found during an internal security review.

title: fix(dedup): path-qualify semantic ids that dropped the directory (#4281)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4281. Builds on #4371 (warning wording).

Semantic extraction sometimes drops the folder from an id, so `a/x.md` and `b/x.md` both emit `x`. Dedup then merged them and one real document was lost. This PR gives each file its own path-qualified id (`a_x`, `b_x`), unless the bare id is only a mention of another document.

Three different things produce the same collision:

| Shape | Example | Right result |
|---|---|---|
| two real documents | `a/x.md` and `b/x.md` each emit their own `x` | two nodes, `a_x` and `b_x` |
| a mention of another document | `docs/firmware/protocol.md` emits `protocol` and points at it | one node: the reference ends on `docs/protocol.md` |
| one entity described in two documents | `sender` in `docs/a.md` and `docs/b.md` | one node, both documents point at it |

The id alone can't tell these apart: in all three, two files emit one id. What differs is the graph around it. A mention is a path-slice id that another node of its own file points at. In the entity case the id is not a path slice, and for two real documents the id is a slice but nothing in the file points at it.

### The rule

```text
for each id shared by files with different full path stems:
  candidates = nodes whose id is a SHORTER path slice of their own file
               (not AST-tier, not an absolute source_file)
  drop from candidates every MENTION:
      the node is the target of a `references` edge from another node of its own file
      AND its id is itself a path slice of that file          # names a document
  if 2+ files remain, and no remaining file's full stem equals the id:
      rename each node to <full stem of its own file> + rest of id
      edges and hyperedges follow by their own source_file
      references from OTHER files stay on the bare id, with one warning per id
```

The same mention evidence also makes a mention lose survivor ties in `_collision_rank`, so a real document outranks it whatever the label lengths are.

```diff
 deduplicate_entities
   _disambiguate_defining_collisions        # x.py vs x.html (#4282)
+  _path_qualify_dropped_collisions         # a/x.md vs b/x.md
+    _mentions                              # own-file `references` + path-slice id
   exact-id collapse
+    _mentions
     _collision_rank(node, root, mentions)  # a mention ranks as a reference
```

The path-slice gate matters. Ordinary entity ids such as `x_intro` are also the target of intra-file `references` edges. Without the gate, `x_intro` would be skipped from the rename and two real documents would collapse, and the ranking would change survivors for unrelated collisions. `test_reference_evidence_does_not_change_survivors_of_other_collisions` pins this: v8 and this PR keep `a/x.md`'s `x_intro`; an ungated version flips to `c.md`'s.

### Cases

Seven hand-built semantic fragments, run through `graphify.build.build()` on v8, on the first version of this PR (f8c2451), and now.

| case | correct | v8 | PR before (f8c2451) | PR now | covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D: two real docs | 4 nodes, edges within each file | `b/x.md` dropped | ok | ok | `test_path_dropped_through_build` |
| R: mention of another doc | 2 nodes, firmware doc references `docs/protocol.md` | ok, because the mention's label is shorter | self-link: `docs_firmware_protocol` references itself | ok | `test_reference_to_another_file_does_not_become_a_second_document` |
| R_noedge: same, no edge | same 2 nodes, no edge | ok | ok | ok | `test_mention_without_an_edge_gives_the_same_two_documents` |
| R_toplevel: plus a top-level `protocol.md` | 3 nodes, one per file | top-level document dropped | same | same (known) | `test_top_level_collision_keeps_todays_result` |
| F: reference from a third file | no `x`; `c.md`'s edge not pinned on one file | `c_note` pinned on `a_x` as EXTRACTED, `b/x.md` dropped | ok | ok | `test_path_dropped_foreign_reference_edge_is_dropped_by_build` |
| R_labelswap: R with the labels swapped | same as R | `docs/protocol.md` dropped, self-link | self-link | ok | `test_reference_outcome_does_not_depend_on_label_length` |
| G: one entity in two docs | 3 nodes, `sender` once | ok | ok | ok | `test_entity_described_in_two_documents_collapses_to_one_node` |

Totals: v8 3 of 7 right, first version 4 of 7, now 6 of 7. False facts (a self-link, or an extra node): 1, 2, 0. EXTRACTED edges on the wrong node: 2, 2, 0.

### Existing tests this PR changes

The collapse for these inputs was pinned in #1504 and #4282. This PR reverses it for path-dropped ids, because the maintainer's comment on #4281 says the remaining `a/x.md` vs `b/x.md` case "still needs a path-qualified id".

| Test | Before | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_cross_chunk_id_collision_emits_warning` (#1504) | id `readme_booking_service` on `module-a/README.md` and `module-b/README.md` | id `booking_service` on both | The old id is a path slice of both files, so it is now renamed. `booking_service` is not, so the collapse and the warning are still covered. Assertions are unchanged. |
| `test_bare_id_across_different_paths_still_collapses_with_warning` | asserted one node and a WARNING | renamed `test_bare_id_across_different_paths_is_path_qualified`; asserts `docs_protocol` and `docs_firmware_protocol`, and no `minted by two different files` | With no `references` edge there is no evidence that either copy is a mention, so both files are renamed. The docstring points to the case where the edge exists (R), which stays one node. |

All other existing `test_path_dropped_*` tests are unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

One id per real entity. A reference must not become a new entity, and a real document must not be dropped. Renames depend only on the input: groups, members and warnings are visited in sorted order, and nothing reads the hash seed or the input order.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Code only: no schema, cache or file-format change. Reverting restores the old collapse for newly extracted bare ids.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. It applies only to semantic nodes whose id is a shorter path slice shared across files. On a rebuild, a corpus with such collisions gets more nodes than before (two documents instead of one), and saved queries or notes that use the bare `x` find `a_x` and `b_x` instead. #4371 is independent: the two PRs merge in either order without conflicts (`git merge-tree`).

**Limitations**

- The mention evidence is inferred from the edges an LLM chose to emit. A missing or reversed `references` edge gives no evidence, so both files are renamed (R_noedge). With a reversed edge, the reference can still end up as a self-link.
- A real document whose own node is linked to its file-level id the same way (an entity named like its file) reads as a mention, and that collision collapses as on v8.
- R_toplevel stays wrong: with a top-level `protocol.md` that also mints `protocol`, one real document is still dropped by the label tiebreak. It is a separate collision, and a test pins today's result.
- If two or more other files also mint the mention's id, the mention stays on the bare id and `build_from_json` folds it into its own file's page, which gives a self-link and no warning. This is the same outcome as the first version of this PR.
- A reference to the bare id from a third file (`c.md -> x`) cannot be attributed to one file. The edge is left on `x`, one warning is printed per id, and `build()` then drops it because no node `x` exists.
- For `imports`, `imports_from` and `re_exports` edges, `build_from_json` mints an external stub node for the missing target. An import-family edge to a renamed bare id leaves a phantom external node `x`. Checked by hand; there is no test.
- Absolute `source_file` values (no root, outside the root, or a Windows path on POSIX) are never qualified, so checkout paths cannot leak into ids (#502, #2197, #2618). Those collisions stay on collapse-and-warn.
- AST-tier nodes are not touched. Hyperedge members given as dicts are not rewritten, as in the #4282 pass.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_dedup.py`: the five cases R, R_labelswap, R_noedge, R_toplevel and G from the table, plus `test_reference_evidence_does_not_change_survivors_of_other_collisions` (the survivor gate). The first version of this PR already added tests for keeping both files, order independence, foreign references, absolute paths, a lone id, the build path, a rebuild, and a bare id that names an existing file. On the rebased branch before the final change, R and R_labelswap fail and the rest pass. With an ungated version of the evidence, only the survivor-gate test fails.

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_dedup.py -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pytest-4281   -> 130 passed
uv run pytest tests -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pytest-4281                 -> 7594 passed, 14 skipped
uv run ruff check .                                                    -> All checks passed
uv run pyright                                                         -> 626 errors repo-wide, 626 on upstream/v8
                                                                          dedup.py + test_dedup.py: 5 before, 5 after
.venv/bin/graphify update .                                            -> graph updated
git checkout uv.lock                                                   (uv run rewrites it)
```
