title: [Bug]:  C#: nested partial types are never merged, and `Foo` / `Foo<T>` partials are merged into one
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?


`_merge_csharp_partial_class_nodes` (#2332) collapses the halves of a top-level `partial` type into one node. Its
grouping key is wrong in two cases:

1. **Nested partial types are skipped on purpose** (`md.get("is_nested_type")` → `continue`), because their node ids
   do not carry the enclosing type. A nested partial type split across files stays split: each half is its own type
   node and owns only its own members.
2. **The key is `(namespace, label)`, and the label has no arity.** `partial class Box` and `partial class Box<T>`
   are distinct types with distinct ids since #4249, but this pass folds them back into one node.

Every lookup through the type then sees only one half, or sees two candidates and gives up:

* `base.M()` from a derived class gets no edge when `M` is declared in the other half of the base.
* A receiver-typed call (`engine.Stop()`) into the type gets no edge.
* An unqualified call from one half into a member of the other half gets no edge as soon as a method of the same
  name exists on any other type. The in-file own-class binding (#4252) cannot see the other file, and the
  cross-file pass then has several candidates. This also affects **top-level** partial types: the existing test
  `test_cross_half_unqualified_in_class_call_resolves` passes only because its method name is unique in the corpus.

**Expected** for the repro below:

```
Engine: 1 node   [['.Start()', '.Stop()']]
Box:    2 nodes  [['.Plain()'], ['.Typed()']]
calls:  Caller.Run() -> Engine.Start()
        Caller.Run() -> Engine.Stop()
        Engine.Start() -> Engine.Stop()
        Turbo.Reset() -> Machine.Reset()
        Turbo.Stop() -> Engine.Stop()
```

**Scale.** On a proprietary C# corpus of eight graphs, built with graphifyy 0.9.86 from PyPI, graphify's own output
(no post-processing): **1 592** `base.M()` call sites in classes whose base is a nested type declared in the corpus
get no edge because `M` is declared in another half of the nested partial base. Measured by matching `base.<Name>(`
in every `.cs` file that holds methods in the graph, assigning each line to the enclosing method by start line, and
checking for a `calls` edge from that method to a `.<Name>()` node. With a change that keys the merge on the
enclosing chain, those 1 592 drop to 0, and the call sites of that kind with an edge go from 466 to 2 235.

The pass's docstring and `test_nested_partial_not_merged` describe the nested exclusion as deliberate, to avoid
merging same-named nested types under different outers. Keying on the enclosing chain and the arity avoids that
without excluding nested types.

Two things showed up while trying such a change locally, worth knowing for a fix:

* **A placeholder base next to the real base.** Halves may repeat the base list, and each half resolves it in its
  own file's scope. In the repro, `Kit.cs` names the sibling `Machine` without `using static` and leaves a
  placeholder; `Kit.Engine.cs` resolves the real `Kit.Machine`. Today the two halves are separate nodes, so
  `Turbo.Reset() -> Machine.Reset()` resolves through one of them. Once they merge, the type has two bases named
  `Machine`, and that edge is lost unless the placeholder is dropped when a real base of the same name sits next to
  it.
* **Cache.** A new merge key stored on the nodes needs an `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` bump; replayed old entries would keep
  nested halves split and `Box` / `Box<T>` merged.

Not part of this issue: a base written qualified (`class Turbo : Kit.Engine`), or a sibling nested type used as a
base without `using static`, resolves to a placeholder, also for non-partial types. That is the remainder discussed
under #4216.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir partial-repro && cd partial-repro

cat > Demo.csproj <<'EOF'
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup><TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework></PropertyGroup>
</Project>
EOF

cat > Kit.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo
{
    public static partial class Kit
    {
        public class Machine
        {
            public virtual void Reset() { }
        }

        public partial class Engine : Machine
        {
            public virtual void Stop() { }
        }
    }
}
EOF

cat > Kit.Engine.cs <<'EOF'
using static Demo.Kit;

namespace Demo
{
    public static partial class Kit
    {
        public partial class Engine : Machine
        {
            public void Start() { Stop(); }
        }
    }
}
EOF

cat > Turbo.cs <<'EOF'
using static Demo.Kit;

namespace Demo
{
    public class Turbo : Engine
    {
        public override void Stop() { base.Stop(); }
        public override void Reset() { base.Reset(); }
    }
}
EOF

cat > Caller.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo
{
    public class Caller
    {
        public void Run(Kit.Engine engine) { engine.Start(); engine.Stop(); }
    }
}
EOF

# Same method names on an unrelated type.
cat > Pump.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo
{
    public class Pump
    {
        public void Start() { }
        public virtual void Stop() { }
        public virtual void Reset() { }
    }
}
EOF

cat > Box.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo
{
    public partial class Box { public void Plain() { } }
}
EOF

cat > BoxOfT.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo
{
    public partial class Box<T> { public void Typed() { } }
}
EOF

# Optional: the snippet compiles as-is (0 warnings, 0 errors).
dotnet build -nologo -v q

cat > show.py <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract

r = extract(sorted(Path(".").glob("*.cs")), root=Path(".").resolve(), cache_root=Path(".cache"))
N = {n["id"]: n for n in r["nodes"]}
own = {e["target"]: e["source"] for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "method"}
q = lambda i: N[own[i]]["label"] + N[i]["label"] if i in own else N[i]["label"]
for lab in ("Engine", "Box"):
    ns = [n for n in r["nodes"] if n["label"] == lab and n.get("source_file")]
    print(f"{lab}: {len(ns)} node(s):",
          [sorted(N[m]["label"] for m, o in own.items() if o == n["id"]) for n in ns])
print("calls:", sorted(f"{q(e['source'])} -> {q(e['target'])}"
                       for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "calls"))
EOF

uv run --no-project --isolated --python 3.13 --with graphifyy==0.9.86 python show.py
```

### Error output or graph output
```text
Engine: 2 node(s): [['.Stop()'], ['.Start()']]
Box: 1 node(s): [['.Plain()', '.Typed()']]
calls: ['Turbo.Reset() -> Machine.Reset()']
```

### Graphify version

0.9.86

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

pip

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables set; extraction is AST-only. Reproduced with graphifyy 0.9.86 from PyPI on
Python 3.13.14 (`uv run --isolated`, as above) and 3.14.6 (pip into a fresh venv), and on a clean checkout of `v8`
at `a5ba60d`.


### Additional context

_No response_

title: fix(csharp): merge nested and generic partial types by their full type path (#4363)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4363.

`_merge_csharp_partial_class_nodes` grouped partial halves by `(namespace, label)` and skipped nested types. This PR
keys the merge on the type's full path inside its namespace, and fixes the two places where a merged type was still
not treated as one type.

1. **Key on the type path** (`graphify/extractors/engine.py`, `graphify/extract.py`). The C# extractor records each
   type's path inside its namespace, enclosing types first, each with its arity: `Kit.Engine`, `` Outer`1.Inner ``.
   Partial types carry it as `metadata.type_path`. The merge groups by `(assembly, namespace, type_path)`:
   * nested halves now merge, but only under the same enclosing chain (`OuterA.Inner` and `OuterB.Inner` stay apart);
   * `Box` and `Box<T>` stay apart (#4249), top-level or as an enclosing type;
   * a nested type whose path is unknown stays unmerged, as before; so does a node that two declarations in one
     file share (same-named nested types under different outers already collide on one id), since no single path
     is right for it.
2. **Unqualified call into the other half** (`extract.py`, cross-file call pass). The in-file own-class binding
   (#4252) cannot see a partial type's other file. When the cross-file pass has several candidates for a C#
   unqualified call and exactly one is a member of the caller's own type, it binds that one (`EXTRACTED`, as the
   in-file binding does). A tie, for example overloads, falls through to the existing tie-breakers unchanged. This
   also fixes top-level partial types whenever a method of the same name exists elsewhere in the corpus.
3. **Placeholder base next to the real base** (`extract.py`, new `_drop_shadowed_csharp_partial_bases`, runs after C#
   type resolution). Halves may repeat the base list, and each half resolves it in its own file's scope. If the base
   is a sibling nested type and only one half's file has `using static` for the holder, the other half leaves a
   placeholder. Once the halves merge, the type has two same-named bases, and `base.M()` through it loses its edge.
   A placeholder spelled with the bare name is the unresolved spelling of the resolved base, so the pass drops it.
   One whose edge is marked `qualified` (`Other.IFoo`), or whose name is a `using` alias in that half's file, can
   be a different type that only shares the simple name, and stays. Without this step, change 1 would lose edges
   that v8 has; in the issue's repro it is `Turbo.Reset() -> Machine.Reset()`.
4. **`_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 8 -> 9** (`graphify/cache.py`), so cached C# results without `type_path` are re-extracted.
   Replayed, they would keep nested halves split and fold `Box` / `Box<T>` together.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** the halves of one C# partial type, in one assembly, are one type node; declarations that are distinct
types (other enclosing type, other arity, other namespace, other assembly) are never merged. A lookup through the
type sees the members of every half.

**Persisted state:** `metadata.type_path` is new on C# partial type nodes; the schema bump retires AST cache entries
without it. No other cache or output format changes. `ARCHITECTURE.md` gets a paragraph on the merge key, next to
the one on Python nested class ids.

**Determinism:** `type_path` is built from the AST walk of one file; the merge key and the canonical half (sorted by
source file, location, id) do not depend on file order or environment.

**Effect on a real corpus.** A proprietary C# corpus of eight graphs, each built twice from the same source tree:
graphifyy 0.9.86 from PyPI, and the same files with this change. Compared is graphify's own output, before any
post-processing of ours. Unit: a `calls` pair, i.e. (source file, label) of the caller and of the callee,
deduplicated; pairs whose callee has no `source_file` are not counted.

* **Gained: 26 270 pairs.** 26 238 of them are in one graph; the other seven gain 22, 6, 4, 0, 0, 0 and 0.
* **Lost: 619 C# pairs**, all accounted for:
  * 449 are replaced by a pair from the same caller to a method **of the same name** elsewhere:
    * 201: the new callee is an override in a type derived from the old callee's type;
    * 197: the new callee is in the same type, in another half (an overload that the merge now puts in one type);
    * 50: constructor calls whose old callee was the node of a half that is now merged into the type;
    * 1: not classified.
  * 170 differ from the new callee only by a leading underscore (`Foo()` / `_Foo()`). Both names in one type already
    share one node id on 0.9.86; which label the edge reports depends on which half the node comes from. This PR does
    not change that collision.
* 3 further pairs are lost in one non-C# file. The code paths changed here only run for `.cs` files and C# raw calls.
* `base.M()` call sites in classes whose base is a nested type declared in the corpus (measured as described in
  #4363): "method declared in another half of the base" **1 592 -> 0**; call sites with an edge **466 -> 2 235**.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test**: 13 new tests in `tests/test_csharp_partial_classes.py`; 10 fail on v8, 3 are guards (see below).
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Limitations:**

* A base written qualified (`class Turbo : Kit.Engine`), or a sibling nested base without `using static`, still
  resolves to a placeholder, also for non-partial types (the #4216 remainder). Change 3 only removes such a
  placeholder when a real base of the same name sits next to it.
* Two same-named nested types under different outers **in one file** already share one node id on v8; this PR does
  not change that, and leaves such a node unmerged.
* A merged type that keeps a qualified or aliased placeholder base next to a real base of the same simple name still
  has two bases, so a lookup through its base chain can still bail there.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_csharp_partial_classes.py`; each fails on v8 and passes with this change:

* `test_nested_partial_halves_merge_under_the_same_outer`
* `test_nested_partial_cross_half_unqualified_call_resolves`
* `test_cross_half_unqualified_call_beats_a_same_named_method_elsewhere` (top-level partial plus a same-named decoy)
* `test_nested_partial_base_call_resolves_into_the_other_half`
* `test_receiver_typed_calls_resolve_into_both_nested_halves`
* `test_same_named_nested_partials_under_different_outers_not_merged`
* `test_deeply_nested_partials_key_on_the_whole_enclosing_chain`
* `test_generic_and_non_generic_partials_not_merged`
* `test_base_named_by_two_halves_resolves_once`
* `test_schema_bump_retires_csharp_entries_cached_without_type_path` (also fails with the schema left at 8)

Guards, passing on v8, for cases a merge must not break (added after the automated review; the first two fail on this
PR's first commit):

* `test_nested_types_sharing_an_id_in_one_file_are_not_merged`
* `test_qualified_or_aliased_base_is_not_dropped_as_shadowed`
* `test_receiver_qualified_calls_are_not_rebound_to_the_own_type`

The tests that rely on name lookup include an unrelated type with the same method names; without it, the
corpus-wide unique-name fallback produces the edge and the test passes for the wrong reason.

Changed tests: `test_nested_partial_not_merged` is removed; it asserted the old exclusion, which the first two new
tests replace. In `tests/test_csharp_type_resolution.py::test_csharp_using_static_on_partial_holder_class`,
`len(shared_defs) == 2` ("nested partial SharedNested declarations remain unmerged") is now `== 1`, and the merged
node is still contained by the holder.

Commands run on Windows, Python 3.14.6 unless noted, after `uv sync --all-extras`:

```text
$ uv run pytest tests -q
  this branch:  8 failed, 7270 passed, 70 skipped
  v8 (a5ba60d): 19 failed, 7256 passed, 70 skipped (run before the 3 guards were added)
                = the same 8, plus the 10 new tests and the 1 changed test that need this change
  the same 8 on both:
    test_hooks.py::test_shebang_parse_requires_leading_hash_bang
    test_non_regular_files.py::test_char_device_is_rejected
    test_partial_extraction_warning.py::test_warning_carries_no_hardcoded_issue_number
    test_resolve_memoization.py::test_absolute_path_lookup_skips_getcwd
    test_skillgen_input_path_injection.py::test_step1_still_resolves_a_legitimate_path (3 parameters)
    test_source_key_memoization.py::test_absolute_path_lookup_skips_getcwd

$ uv run --isolated --no-project --python 3.10 --with-editable . --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_csharp*.py -q
  216 passed            (same with --python 3.13)

$ uv run pytest tests/test_csharp_partial_classes.py tests/test_csharp_type_resolution.py -q   # code at a5ba60d
  11 failed, 74 passed  (the 10 new tests and the 1 changed one; the 3 guards pass)

$ uv run ruff check .
  All checks passed!

$ uv run pyright
  618 errors on v8 and on this branch; no new findings

$ git diff --check
  clean
```

The repro from #4363, run with this branch:

```text
Engine: 1 node(s): [['.Start()', '.Stop()']]
Box: 2 node(s): [['.Plain()'], ['.Typed()']]
calls: ['Caller.Run() -> Engine.Start()', 'Caller.Run() -> Engine.Stop()', 'Engine.Start() -> Engine.Stop()', 'Turbo.Reset() -> Machine.Reset()', 'Turbo.Stop() -> Engine.Stop()']
```

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (No skill fragments changed.)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.

title: [Feature]: Add ABAP Cloud (abapGit) and SAP CAP CDS language support
body:
### Problem or use case

Graphify's file classifier (`graphify/detect.py`) decides file type purely by looking up `path.suffix` (the final extension) against `CODE_EXTENSIONS`/`DOC_EXTENSIONS`. There's no entry for SAP's ABAP Cloud (abapGit-serialized) repository objects or CAP (Cloud Application Programming Model) sources, so an entire, widely-used enterprise stack is **silently skipped during `detect()` with no warning** — same failure class as any unrecognized-extension gap, but it blanks out whole directories rather than a handful of files.

Concretely, these extensions produce `classify_file() -> None` today and never reach `graphify-out/manifest.json` at all:
- ABAP Cloud / abapGit: `.abap`, `.asddls`, `.asdcls`, `.asbdef`, `.baseinfo`, `.srvdsrv`, and the generic `.xml` used for every abapGit object's ADT-metadata sidecar (`.clas.xml`, `.ddls.xml`, `.dcls.xml`, `.intf.xml`, `.prog.xml`, `.tabl.xml`, `.dtel.xml`, `.doma.xml`, `.msag.xml`, `.devc.xml`, `.bdef.xml`, `.srvb.xml`, `.g4ba.xml`, `.xslt.xml`, `.fugr.*.xml`, etc.)
- SAP CAP: `.cds` (the core data-model/service-definition language)
- Adjacent SAP BTP artifacts: `.hdbmigrationtable` (HANA table DDL), `.mtaext` (MTA extension descriptors), `.edmx` (OData metadata)

Validated this on a real SAP BTP + ABAP Cloud repo (CAP Node.js backend + an `abap/` folder with ABAP Cloud objects): `/graphify .` produced a graph with **zero nodes** for the entire `abap/` tree (~150 files: classes, CDS views, access-control roles, behavior definitions, function groups) and for `db/data-model.cds`, every `*.cds` service/annotation file, every `.hdbmigrationtable`, and the UI5 `.properties`/`.mtaext`/`.edmx` files — with no error, no `skipped_sensitive` entry, nothing in the corpus summary hinting anything was dropped. The only way I found it was diffing `find .` against `manifest.json` by hand.

### Proposed solution

1. Add the extensions above to the classification tables. Since there's no tree-sitter grammar for ABAP or CDS in the AST dispatch table, the simplest correct fix is classifying them as `DOCUMENT` so they flow through the existing LLM semantic-extraction path (same mechanism already used for `.md`/`.txt`) rather than gating this on writing a full AST extractor first. I validated this: after adding the extensions to `DOC_EXTENSIONS` and running semantic extraction over ~200 previously-invisible files, I got real, useful nodes/edges — ABAP classes and their call graphs, CDS view base-entity references, DCLS access-control grants, HANA tables linked back to the CDS entities they implement, etc. A dedicated AST extractor (tree-sitter has an ABAP grammar, and CDS is close enough to SQL DDL) would obviously do better, but even the fallback closes the "totally invisible" gap.
2. Clarify or harden the node-ID rule in the extraction prompt for abapGit's compound-extension convention, where one logical object spans several sibling files (e.g. `zknsf_i_ratings.ddls.asddls` + `.ddls.xml` + `.ddls.baseinfo` are all the *same* CDS view). The current "drop only the final extension, keep the rest of the filename as the stem" rule is ambiguous here — different parallel-extraction chunks independently guessed different stems for the same object (some kept the `.ddls`/`.bdef`/`.clas` segment, others additionally baked `_asddls_`/`_baseinfo_`/`_xml_`/`_abap_` into the id), producing duplicate/fragmented nodes and dropped cross-chunk edges that I had to find and merge by hand afterward.
3. Surface unclassified files in the corpus summary — a `skipped_unclassified: N` count (distinct from `skipped_sensitive`) would have told me immediately that a whole ecosystem went ungraphed, instead of discovering it by manual diff.

### Alternatives considered

- Renaming/copying the ABAP/CDS files to a recognized extension before scanning — works around the classifier but pollutes the repo and loses the real file-type information in the resulting graph.
- Monkeypatching `graphify.detect` at runtime for one project — not durable across `--update` runs or other projects, and doesn't help anyone else hitting the same gap.

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

No, I just wanted to request it

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Purely additive: new extensions added to the classification sets, no change to how any currently-recognized extension is classified, no change to the node/edge ID scheme for existing languages, no change to `graph.json` schema or MCP output. One thing worth calling out in release notes: repos that already contain ABAP/CDS files will see new nodes/edges appear after upgrading and running `--update`, since files that were always present but invisible will now be picked up as "new."

### Additional context

Happy to share the exact extension list and the specific duplicate-ID patterns I hit (and how I resolved them) if that's useful for scoping the fix — didn't want to paste a large diff into the issue body unprompted.

title: [Bug]: graphify_node silently resolves qualified Python symbols to unrelated semantic matches
body: ### Pre-flight checks - [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README ### What happened? When querying Python callables through Graphify MCP, short callable labels resolve correctly, but qualified Python symbols can silently fall back to unrelated semantic matches. The tool still returns a successful response with `resolved: semantic`, even though the returned node is unrelated to the requested symbol. This can mislead agent workflows that use the result for architecture analysis, callers, tests, dependencies, or change-impact analysis. Expected behavior: Qualified Python symbols should either resolve to the intended callable, return explicit candidates, or return an unresolved/ambiguous result. Actual behavior: Qualified names can resolve to an unrelated semantic node while still appearing successful. ### Steps to reproduce ```shell Repository: chapaevv123/miden-preflight Indexed commit: d93970586a74aaef96a4e41b8bf00c15da6a4fd8 1. Query: graphify_node(symbol="main()", strict_calls=true) This correctly resolves to: src/miden_preflight/cli.py main() 2. Query: graphify_node(symbol="miden_preflight.cli.main", strict_calls=true) This returns an unrelated test symbol while reporting `resolved: semantic`. 3. Query: graphify_node(symbol="scan()", strict_calls=true) This correctly resolves to: src/miden_preflight/engine.py scan() 4. Query: graphify_node(symbol="miden_preflight.engine.scan", strict_calls=true) This returns an unrelated GitHub Actions workflow node while reporting `resolved: semantic`. The repository package entry point is declared in: pyproject.toml miden_preflight.cli:main ``` ### Error output or graph output ```text Correct short-name resolutions: main() → src/miden_preflight/cli.py → main() scan() → src/miden_preflight/engine.py → scan() Incorrect qualified-name resolutions: miden_preflight.cli.main → unrelated test symbol → resolved: semantic miden_preflight.engine.scan → unrelated .github/workflows/preflight.yml node → resolved: semantic The important part is that both incorrect lookups return success rather than an unresolved or ambiguous result. ``` ### Graphify version _No response_ ### Operating System Windows ### Python Version 3.11 ### Installation Method uv tool install (recommended) ### Additional Environment Details Graphify MCP connected through Codex. Repository tested: chapaevv123/miden-preflight Indexed commit: d93970586a74aaef96a4e41b8bf00c15da6a4fd8 Environment: Windows 10 Python 3.11 Codex MCP client No provider API keys or special environment variables are required to reproduce this issue. The issue was reproduced repeatedly against the same indexed repository state. ### Additional context I reproduced this against a real indexed repository and cross-checked the returned nodes against the source at the exact indexed commit. The key concern is not that semantic search is fuzzy, but that qualified symbol lookups can return an unrelated node while still appearing successful. A short GIF reproduction is attached above.

title: fix(serve): resolve qualified Python names like pkg.mod.func (#4366)
body:
Asking for `miden_preflight.cli.main` (or `miden_preflight.engine.scan`) found nothing, even though `main()`/`scan()` resolve fine. The dotted name tokenizes to `miden_preflight cli main`, which matches no label. The issue's `graphify_node` / `resolved: semantic` output comes from a wrapper outside this repo. Upstream `get_node`/`get_neighbors`/`explain` already fail closed with "No node matching…", so the wrong match itself doesn't come from here. Still, the qualified name should resolve.

**What changed** (`graphify/serve.py`): in `_find_node_tiers`, a dotted Python symbol (`pkg.mod.func`, `pkg.mod.func()`, or the `pkg.mod:func` entry-point form) is now mapped onto the existing `path::symbol` lookup. It checks `pkg/mod.py` and then `pkg/mod/__init__.py`, suffix-matched, so `src/` layouts work. It's skipped when the raw query already exactly matches a node label, and when nothing matches it falls through to the old tiers. `_tier_refusal` treats a dotted hit as a symbol tier and not a file query, so a function plus a same-named method in that module come back as `Ambiguous` (for `get_node`/`explain` and `path` alike) instead of one of them being picked.

**Testing**
- Live, on chapaevv123/miden-preflight @ d939705 after `graphify update .`: `miden_preflight.cli.main` and `miden_preflight.cli:main` now resolve to `src/miden_preflight/cli.py` `main()` L26, and `miden_preflight.engine.scan` resolves to `engine.py` `scan()` L158. Before, all three gave "No node matching". `main()` itself is still ambiguous because `role_model.py` also defines one, same as before.
- Added two tests in `tests/test_serve.py`. Both fail on v8 and pass here.
- ruff is clean. Full suite on 3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14: the only failures are the 16 that already fail on v8 (9 `test_dm_*`, 7 `test_security` safe_fetch/validate_url).

Not covered: `pkg.mod.Class.method`. Use `path::.method()` or the node id for that.

Fixes #4366

title: feat(hook): show the graph nodes behind a nudged call, and tighten its wording
body:
Follow-up to #3443, which shipped in 0.9.87. That PR decides **when** the soft nudge fires. This one changes **what a firing nudge says**: in our downstream build, agents still treated it as noise within the budget. The change was first offered to #3443's branch as L4XB/graphify#1, but #3443 landed without it, so it is proposed here directly on `v8`.

**What changes**
- **Call-specific hint.** A firing nudge, and the strict-mode deny, ends with a command built from the call and up to five matching graph nodes with file and line:
  ```
  Start with: `graphify explain "load_config()"`
  What the graph already has for this call:
  - load_config() (src/app.py L10)
  ```
  For a search, the terms come from the Grep `pattern` or the pattern argument of `grep`/`rg`/`ag`/`ack`. Value-taking flags such as `-t`/`-g`/`-A` are skipped, `find`/`fd` are excluded because they match file names, and a grep fed by a pipe is excluded because it filters output, not code. For a read, the hint lists the file's symbols in line order. An exact label match suggests `explain`; anything else suggests `query`. Terms shorter than 5 characters only match exactly, so `src` does not list every path.
- **Cheap and fail-safe.** The hint scans `graph.json` labels directly instead of loading the query stack, which cost about 1.5 s per hook call on a 15k-node graph. Measured: 0.3–0.5 s on 3k–15k-node graphs. Graphs over 24 MiB, a malformed graph, no match, or any error all return the unchanged nudge. Graph text is sanitised to one line with no control characters or backticks and a capped length, because `graph.json` is repository content.
- **Narrower wording.** "…or to modify/debug specific lines" excused nearly every targeted read. The nudge and the deny now allow raw reads only once the exact file and lines are known.
- **Always-on rule.** The Claude, AGENTS.md and Gemini blocks now say to query "before your first grep, search or source-file read for a codebase question", to put the rule in every subagent prompt that explores code, and to read raw files only for lines the graph or an earlier read already located. This is recorded as a sanctioned skillgen edit (`_QUERY_FIRST_EDIT`) next to `_GRAPH_DIFF_EDIT`. The Kiro and Antigravity blocks use different sentences and are unchanged.

**Why:** in session logs, the nudge got 28–41 deliveries per session against 0–2 `graphify` calls, and the model's reasoning never mentioned it. On a real repo, `rg 'stripHiddenWrappers'` now gets `graphify explain "stripHiddenWrappers()"` plus its file and line.

**Tests:** new cases in `tests/test_hook_guard.py` and `tests/test_hook_strict.py` cover hint content and ranking, the 5-node cap, flag parsing, path-only and short-term non-matches, hostile labels, malformed and oversized graphs, and the deny hint. All skillgen guards pass (`--check`, `--always-on-roundtrip`, `--audit-coverage`, `--monolith-roundtrip`), and the hook, install-string and skillgen tests pass (236).

title: fix(powershell): dot-source quoted/$PSScriptRoot paths and script-scope calls (#4356)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4356. Two gaps in `graphify/extractors/powershell.py` dropped edges from ordinary PowerShell scripts:

1. **Dot-source with a quoted or `$PSScriptRoot` path.** The handler only read the path when tree-sitter parsed it as `command_name`. `. "$PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1"` and `. '.\lib.ps1'` parse as `string_literal`, and unquoted `. $PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1` as `path_command_name`, so no `imports_from` edge was emitted. The fix accepts all three node types and strips surrounding quotes; the existing basename logic handles the rest.
2. **Calls at script scope.** `walk_calls` ran only over function/method bodies, so commands in a script's main body produced no `calls` edge and no `raw_call`. The fix also walks the file root with the file node as the caller. `walk_calls` already stops at `function_statement`/`class_statement`, so function bodies are not walked twice.

Also bumps `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 8 -> 9 so cached results for unchanged `.ps1` files are re-extracted (same approach as c68d167).

| Dot-source form | v8 (0.9.86) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `. ./lib.ps1`, `. .\lib.ps1` | edge | edge |
| `. "$PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1"` | none | edge |
| `. $PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1` | none | edge |
| `. '.\lib.ps1'` | none | edge |
| `. (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "lib.ps1")` | none | none (runtime-only path, see limitations) |

Invariant: a `.ps1` file that dot-sources another file gets an `imports_from` edge for every statically known path, and every command it invokes, in a function or at script scope, appears exactly once as a `calls` edge or `raw_call` attributed to the right caller. Calls inside a function must stay attributed to that function, not to the file; the control test `test_powershell_script_scope_walk_does_not_duplicate_function_calls` covers this.

Persisted state: AST cache entries written by schema 8 are invalidated by the schema bump.
