title: fix: preserve directed explain edges and guard agent graph guidance
body:
## Summary

Fix three issues in Graphify's explanation and generated agent workflows: missing incoming relationships in directed graph explanations, skipped query vocabulary expansion, and unsafe assumptions around automatic graph updates.

### 1. Preserve directed and parallel relationships in explanations

The inline `/graphify explain` fallback previously used `G.neighbors(nid)`, which returns only outgoing neighbors for directed graphs.

The CLI handled incoming and outgoing neighbors but collapsed parallel relationships by retrieving a single edge per node pair.

**Changes:**

- Enumerate both incoming and outgoing edges for directed graphs.
- Preserve parallel relationships in `MultiDiGraph`.
- Preserve edge direction, relationship type, confidence, and available edge metadata.
- De-duplicate self-loop relationships.
- Preserve the existing undirected inline explanation output.
- Add explicit `graphify explain --all` support to display every relationship instead of the default first 20.
- Preserve the existing grouped summary when the default output is truncated.
- Keep query-log connection counts consistent with the full relationship set.

### 2. Require graph vocabulary expansion before querying

The generated `AGENTS.md` instructions previously directed agents to query using the user's raw natural-language question without first applying Graphify's existing constrained vocabulary workflow.

**Changes:**

- Check that an existing graph is available.
- Expand natural-language questions against the graph's actual node-label vocabulary before querying.
- Use only vocabulary supported by the graph, avoiding invented terms.
- Handle questions with no matching vocabulary without issuing a broad or guessed query.
- Preserve the user's original question for user-facing answers and saved results.
- Clarify the ordering of graph check → vocabulary expansion → query.

### 3. Guard automatic graph updates

The generated `AGENTS.md` instructions previously recommended running `graphify update .` after code changes without checking whether a graph existed. They also did not clearly distinguish local AST updates from semantic extraction that can involve an LLM/API.

**Changes:**

- Automatically run the code-only `graphify update .` workflow only when `graphify-out/graph.json` already exists.
- Avoid silently initializing a missing graph.
- Distinguish AST-only CLI updates from the semantic `/graphify --update` workflow.
- Require an explicit user request before semantic refreshes that may invoke configured LLM/API services.
- Skip updates when no relevant content changed.
- Instruct agents to preserve existing graph and cache state after failed updates.

## Skill generation

Updated authoritative sources and regenerated the affected artifacts:

- Shared query reference.
- Always-on `AGENTS.md` instruction fragment.
- Aider and Devin monolith source fragments.
- Generated query references for the supported platforms.
- Generated always-on and monolith artifacts.
- Matching skill-generator expected snapshots.

The monolith round-trip validator also verifies that Aider and Devin use the approved shared explanation block rather than accepting arbitrary changes to that section.

## Regression tests

Added or updated coverage for:

- Incoming-only and outgoing-only directed relationships.
- Bidirectional relationships.
- Parallel edges and edge metadata.
- Self-loop de-duplication.
- Undirected explanation compatibility.
- Default 20-relationship limit and grouped truncation summary.
- Explicit `--all` output with more than 20 relationships.
- Generated `AGENTS.md` vocabulary-expansion sequence.
- Missing-graph protection.
- Code-only versus semantic update guidance.
- Aider and Devin monolith consistency.

New regressions were reproduced before their corresponding fixes and passed afterward.

## Verification

- Focused CLI, installer, and skill-generation tests: **210 passed**.
- Full pytest suite: **6,966 passed, 168 skipped**.
- Ruff: **Passed**.
- Skill-generation consistency: **134 artifacts match**.
- Monolith round-trip: **Passed**.
- Always-on round-trip: **Passed**.
- Schema singleton: **Passed**.
- Coverage audit: **Passed**.
- `git diff --check`: **Passed**.

Repository-wide Pyright remains non-clean due to existing diagnostics. The CLI complexity diagnostic was confirmed against the committed baseline; no new diagnostics were reported for the new renderer, generator changes, or regression tests.

No external LLM/API calls or graph-initialization operations were performed during verification.

## Related context

Adjacent issues: #849 (relationship direction), #483 (semantic-refresh opt-in), and #1114 (graph-first agent guidance).

This PR does not claim to resolve those broader issues.

The previously submitted BFS/DFS traversal fix (#4315) and incremental-update fix (#4313) are outside this PR's scope.

## AI contribution disclosure

OpenAI Codex materially assisted with investigation, implementation, regression testing, and verification. The contributor reviewed the code changes and test results. AI co-author attribution is included in the commit metadata.

title: fix(dedup): say what an id-collision merge actually drops (#4281)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4281. Fixes the misleading warning the reporter hit.

When two files mint one id, dedup keeps one node and merges the other into it. The warning claimed that "the dropped node is lost" and that the id "does not identify a single entity", for every such collision. On the reporter's corpus that was wrong: none of their 16 remaining warnings was a lost document. They were one entity described in two documents, or a reference to another file, and merging them was correct. This PR rewords the warning to say what the merge did. It does not change which node survives.

```text
_report_id_collision(nid, survivor, loser)        # cross-file branch only
  survivor defines the id, loser does not  -> silent          (unchanged)
  head = "kept <survivor> from <file>, merged <loser> from <file> into it"
  if _defines_id(survivor) or _defines_id(loser)
    "the id comes from a file path: either a reference to the kept file (merge is right)
     or a separate document (its own label and attributes are lost; edges stay)
     -> advise 'graphify extract' per subfolder"
  else
    "the id comes from neither path: probably one entity described in both files"
```

Edges stay on the kept node because both nodes have the same id. What is dropped is the merged node's own label and attributes.

Real stderr, before and after (both from `deduplicate_entities`):

`protocol` in `docs/protocol.md` and `docs/firmware/protocol.md`

```diff
-[graphify] WARNING: node 'protocol' is minted by two different files — keeping 'Protocol' from 'docs/protocol.md', dropping 'protocol (top-level)' from 'docs/firmware/protocol.md'. An ID is derived from the source path plus the entity name, so this one does not identify a single entity and the dropped node is lost. To keep them distinct, run 'graphify extract' per subfolder and merge with 'graphify merge-graphs'.
+[graphify] WARNING: node 'protocol' is minted by two different files: kept 'Protocol' from 'docs/protocol.md', merged 'protocol (top-level)' from 'docs/firmware/protocol.md' into it. The id comes from a file path, so the merged node is either a reference to the kept file (then the merge is right) or a separate document (then its own label and attributes are lost; its edges stay on the kept node). To keep separate documents apart, run 'graphify extract' per subfolder and merge with 'graphify merge-graphs'.
```

`sender` in `docs/a.md` and `docs/b.md`

```diff
-[graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files — keeping 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', dropping 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md'. An ID is derived from the source path plus the entity name, so this one does not identify a single entity and the dropped node is lost. To keep them distinct, run 'graphify extract' per subfolder and merge with 'graphify merge-graphs'.
+[graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files: kept 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', merged 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md' into it. The id comes from neither path, so this is probably one entity described in both files. The merged node's own label and attributes are not kept; its edges stay on the kept node.
```

Severity is unchanged. `WARNING` and the phrase "minted by two different files" are kept, so `test_issue_3472_source_file_collision.py` and the #1504 test pass without edits.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The warning must not claim more than the merge did. After a collision, one node is kept, the other node's own label and attributes are dropped, and its edges stay on the kept node. Survivor choice is unchanged: it still comes from `_collision_rank`, and the order of the input still does not matter (#1851).

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. The change is stderr text plus a docstring. No persisted state, cache or graph.json field is touched.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Only the text of the cross-file collision warning changes. Anything that greps stderr for the old words ("is lost", "does not identify a single entity", "dropping") will no longer match. In this repo only `dedup.py` contained them; the CHANGELOG line for #1504 describes the older warning and is left as it is.

**Limitations**

- The text cannot tell a reference from a second document when the id comes from a path. It says both are possible. Telling them apart needs edge evidence and is out of scope here (it is the separate fix for the path-qualified id case in #4281).
- "Probably one entity" for an id that comes from neither path is an inference, not a fact. Two real documents can also share such an id; the merged node's label and attributes are then lost.
- Severity stays `WARNING`. The reporter asked for something milder, but `test_issue_3472` asserts `WARNING` for a non-path id, so lowering it would change an existing test.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_dedup.py`:

| Test | Before the fix | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_collision_warning_for_path_slice_id_is_conditional` (`protocol`) | fails | passes |
| `test_collision_warning_for_non_path_id_says_what_is_kept` (`sender`) | fails | passes |
| `test_collision_warning_wording_keeps_the_same_survivor` | passes | passes |
| `test_collision_warning_for_path_derived_id_that_is_not_a_slice` (`x_intro` from `a/x.md` and `b/x.md`) | fails | passes |

The third test pins that the survivor is the same in both input orders; it is a guard, so it is expected to pass before the fix.

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_dedup.py -q -k collision_warning   -> before the fix: 3 failed, 1 passed
uv run pytest tests -q                                       -> 7581 passed, 14 skipped
uv run ruff check .                                          -> All checks passed
uv run pyright                                               -> 626 errors repo-wide, 626 before this change
                                                                dedup.py + test_dedup.py: 5 before, 5 after
git checkout uv.lock                                         (uv run rewrites it)
```

pyright is not clean on this repo. This PR adds no errors: the repo-wide and touched-file counts are unchanged.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (N/A: no skill fragments touched.)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). (Wording only; the survivor test runs both input orders.)
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python). (Labels and paths are interpolated into a stderr message only, as before.)
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

title: fix(install): preserve line endings of CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and siblings (#4360)
body:
## What this fixes

Closes #4360.

`#3741` stopped two writers from *translating* line endings on write (`newline=""`), but every install/uninstall path in the issue still **reads** through `Path.read_text`, which opens in universal-newline mode and folds `\r\n` to `\n` before graphify's block is merged. The later write then re-emitted the platform default, so a read-modify-write normalised the **whole** file:

- On **Windows**, an LF file gained CRLF on every line.
- On **Linux/macOS**, a CRLF file lost its `\r`.

For `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`, which are shared and reviewed, that buries the real one-block change in an every-line diff and can trip line-ending checks.

### Confirmed real on `v8` (0.9.87)

The issue's minimal repro, run end-to-end through the real CLI:

```
$ printf 'a\nb\n' > CLAUDE.md        # LF file
$ graphify claude install
$ file CLAUDE.md                      # -> CRLF line terminators   (bug)
$ graphify uninstall
$ file CLAUDE.md                      # -> still CRLF              (bug)
```

Function-level check on Windows showed `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `CODEBUDDY.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` all flipping LF → CRLF after install, and staying CRLF after uninstall.

## The fix

One shared read/write pair, used by every listed writer so the read and write sides can no longer drift apart:

- `_read_keep_newline(path) -> (text, newline)` — reads **bytes** (bypassing universal-newline translation), detects the file's dominant ending (`\r\n` or `\n`), and returns bare-`\n` text so the existing `_replace_or_append_section` / `_remove_marker_section` helpers keep working unchanged.
- `_write_keep_newline(path, text, newline)` — converts bare `\n` to the detected ending and writes with `newline=""`, so nothing is translated on the way out. A fresh file (no prior convention) is written LF, matching what the other writers already emit.

### Writers updated

| Path | Install | Uninstall |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CLAUDE.md` | `claude_install` | `_strip_graphify_md_section` |
| `AGENTS.md` | `_agents_install` | `_agents_uninstall` |
| `GEMINI.md` | `gemini_install`* | `gemini_uninstall` |
| `CODEBUDDY.md` | `codebuddy_install` | `codebuddy_uninstall` |
| `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | `vscode_install` (new-file branch too) | `vscode_uninstall` |
| `# graphify` H1 registration | `_register_always_on_block`* | `_remove_claude_skill_registration` |

\* the two `#3741` paths are included: they had the write side fixed but still read through `read_text`, so a CRLF file was still normalised to LF on any host. Fixing the read side closes that gap.

As a small simplification, the installers now reuse the already-read `content` for the "already configured (no change)" comparison instead of re-reading the file.

## Tests

New `tests/test_install_line_endings.py`:

- A **round-trip test per writer** (claude, agents, gemini, codebuddy, vscode, always-on registration, `_strip_graphify_md_section`): the file is seeded with an LF body and again with a CRLF body; after install only the graphify block changed and every line keeps the original ending; after uninstall the bytes equal the original exactly.
- A fresh-file test asserting LF (not platform CRLF).
- Direct unit tests for `_read_keep_newline` / `_write_keep_newline`.

The bug is observable in the file bytes on any host OS (LF input fails on Windows, CRLF input fails on Linux), so the tests are not platform-gated.

Verification:

- New tests pass: `17 passed`.
- **Pre-fix**, the same suite fails `11` cases — confirming the tests pin the bug.
- Existing install/uninstall suites unaffected: `253 passed, 3 skipped`; the wider 5-file run has byte-identical pass/fail sets before and after the change.
- `ruff check` clean.

## Scope

Only the read-modify-write writers listed in the issue (plus the `#3741` read side). Graphify-owned rule files that aren't shared/reviewed (`kiro`, `antigravity`, `cursor`, `devin`) and the JSON settings writers are unchanged.

title: fix(install): remove only graphify's own hook entries, keep others (#4359)
body:
## What this fixes

Closes #4359.

When graphify installed or removed its `PreToolUse` / `BeforeTool` hooks, it identified its own hooks with `"graphify" in str(group)` over the **whole group dict**. `str(group)` covers `{"matcher": ..., "hooks": [...]}`, not graphify's individual command, so:

1. A user command added to the `hooks` array of one of graphify's groups was removed **with the group** on the next install/uninstall.
2. An unrelated group whose command path merely contained the word `graphify` (e.g. `python /tools/graphify-notes/check.py`) was removed too.
3. Uninstall rewrote the settings file with no backup, and `_strip_graphify_hook` raised `AttributeError` on a non-dict entry.

### Confirmed real on `v8` (0.9.87)

```
// graphify claude install --project
// add your own command to graphify's Bash|Grep group
// add a separate group: python /tools/graphify-notes/check.py
$ graphify claude uninstall --project
user linter kept?       False      (bug)
unrelated group kept?   False      (bug)
backup written?         False      (bug)
non-dict entry result:  AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'
```

## The fix

Hook entries are now matched at the **entry** level, not the group level:

- `_is_graphify_hook_command(command)` — true when a command invokes graphify's own `hook-guard <search|read|gemini>` / `hook-check` subcommands, or references `graphify-out/` (which identifies the pre-#522 inline bash guard, so legacy entries are still cleaned up).
- `_is_graphify_hook_entry(entry)` — the entry is a `type: "command"` hook whose command matches the above. Non-dict / non-command entries are never graphify's (and no longer crash uninstall).
- `_strip_graphify_hooks(groups)` — removes only graphify's entries from each group, keeps every other entry, and drops a group **only** once it has nothing left. Non-dict groups and non-list `hooks` pass through untouched; a group with no graphify entry is never rewritten.

Applied to all four hook hosts, install and uninstall, so the filters stay in step:

| Host | Install | Uninstall |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude | `_install_claude_hook` | `_strip_graphify_hook` |
| CodeBuddy | `_install_codebuddy_hook` | `_uninstall_codebuddy_hook` |
| Codex | `_install_codex_hook` | `_uninstall_codex_hook` |
| Gemini | `_install_gemini_hook` | `_uninstall_gemini_hook` |

The uninstall paths now write through `_write_settings_with_backup`, so they keep the same rolling `.graphify-bak` that install already did.

## Tests

New `tests/test_install_hook_identity.py`:

- Per host, uninstall keeps a user command sharing graphify's group **and** an unrelated group whose path contains `graphify`, while removing graphify's own commands, and writes a backup.
- Per host, a non-dict entry in the hook array does not crash uninstall and is preserved.
- The pre-#522 bash guard is replaced on install, and re-install stays idempotent.
- Unit tests for `_is_graphify_hook_command` (recognises graphify's variants + legacy, rejects `graphify-notes`-style paths) and `_strip_graphify_hooks` (keeps user entries, drops only emptied groups, passes malformed shapes through).

Verification:

- New tests pass: `19 passed`; **pre-fix** the same suite fails `16` cases.
- Existing suites unaffected: `160 passed, 3 skipped` (settings-merge + install + new).
- End-to-end via the CLI repro above: user command and unrelated group survive, graphify guards removed, backup written.
- `ruff check` clean.

title: Automated issue triage: auto-label new issues (area/ + kind/ + good first issue suggestion)
body:
## What

Automated first-pass triage for issues: when an issue is opened, label it from a
small, fixed taxonomy so it is immediately findable, and surface a good first issue
for newcomers.

## Why

- We have ~700 open issues, and almost all carry only `bug`/`enhancement` from the
  template. `good first issue` exists but is effectively unused, so a newcomer has no
  obvious place to start.
- Maintainers spend real time on the same first-pass reads: "is this a bug or a
  question, which area, is it beginner-friendly".
- This is now routine for production-grade open-source projects, and the economics
  just changed: classifier models are extremely fast and cheap. TypeSafe's System One
  model returns a typed decision in ~100 ms and bills input tokens only, and the fast
  tier of every provider is comparable. Scoring every issue costs almost nothing.

## Proposal

On `issues: opened` / `reopened`:

1. Stamp `status/need-triage` so nothing is lost.
2. One classifier call picks `area/*` and `kind/*` **from a fixed allowlist**.
3. Apply those, set `status/bot-triaged`, remove `status/need-triage`.
4. `good first issue` is only **suggested** in a comment (plus `status/gfi-suggested`)
   for a maintainer to confirm. A wrong beginner task is worse than none.

Failure is fail-open: no key, timeout, or bad output means no labels and the issue
keeps `status/need-triage`. It cannot mislabel.

### Label fields

- `area/*`: extract, build, analyze, query, export, cli, install, watch, llm, ci,
  docs, other
- `kind/*`: bug, feature, docs, question, refactor, performance, other
- `status/*`: need-triage, bot-triaged, gfi-suggested

Existing labels (`bug`, `enhancement`, `good first issue`, ...) stay as they are.

### Model

Runs on TypeSafe **System One (Jev)** — typed `choice`/`noul` questions where the
options are the allowlist, so the model cannot emit a label we did not define. An
ordered `TRIAGE_MODEL` list lets it fall back to any OpenAI-compatible model
(OpenAI, Gemini, ...), so a rate-limited provider never blocks triage. The model is
configurable; a default is picked and everything can be changed later.

## Rollout

Started in a fork and verified with real issues. Then a `TRIAGE_DRY_RUN` canary:
the bot comments the proposed labels and changes nothing, so maintainers can review
a batch before it goes live. Rollback is just unsetting the variable.

An implementation PR is on the way.

title: feat(triage): auto-label new issues with an allowlisted classifier (System One / Jev + model fallback)
body:
# feat(triage): auto-label new issues with an allowlisted classifier (System One / Jev + model fallback) Closes #4374 ## Summary Adds automated first-pass triage for issues. When an issue is opened it gets `status/need-triage`, then a classifier picks `area/*` and `kind/*` from a **fixed allowlist**, applies them, sets `status/bot-triaged`, and **suggests** `good first issue` in a comment for a maintainer to confirm. It runs on TypeSafe's **System One** model (Jev) — a first-class backend, not an afterthought — and falls back to any OpenAI-compatible model if configured. **Purely additive: 13 new files, no existing file modified.** ## Why We sit at ~700 open issues and almost all carry only `bug`/`enhancement` from the template, so `good first issue` is effectively unused and a newcomer has no obvious starting point. A first-pass classifier fixes that. This is what most production-grade open-source projects do now. And the economics just changed: classifier models have become extremely fast and cheap — a System One (Jev) call returns a typed decision in a few hundred milliseconds and bills input tokens only ($0.042 per Mtok), and the fast tier of every provider is similar. Scoring every new issue is a rounding error in cost and latency, so there is no reason a newcomer should land on an unlabelled tracker. ## What it does ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Issue opened / reopened] --> B[Ensure labels exist
idempotent] B --> C[Stamp status/need-triage on open] C --> D{Has area/* or status/bot-triaged?} D -- yes --> E[Skip: already triaged] D -- no --> F[Classify
allowlist + typed/JSON output] F --> G{Usable decision?} G -- no --> H[Fail open: keep status/need-triage] G -- yes --> I[Apply area/* + kind/* + status/bot-triaged] I --> J{Good first issue?} J -- yes --> K[Add status/gfi-suggested + suggestion comment] J -- no --> L[Done] ``` The whole flow is **one ordered job**, so there is no race between stamping and classifying. Untrusted issue text reaches the model but never a shell (it travels via an env var into the classifier's stdin). ## How it classifies The classifier does not ask one broad "label this issue" question. It decomposes into atomic, allowlisted decisions and lets **code** compose them — the pattern that makes model output reliable: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph State S1[title] --- S2[body] --- S3[existing labels] end subgraph Q[Typed questions / allowlist] Q1[kind: choice over kind/*] Q2[area: choice over area/*] Q3[area_secondary: choice or none] Q4[good_first_issue: noul] end State --> Q --> M[Classifier model] M --> Ans[Typed answers + confidence] Ans --> Code[code: cap areas, threshold GFI,
map confidence to high/medium/low] Code --> Out[area/* + kind/* + status/*] ``` The model can only ever choose from the allowlist. Anything else is dropped, so a hallucinated label cannot reach the repository. Failures (no key, timeout, network error, malformed output) produce no labels at all — the issue simply keeps `status/need-triage`. It **fails open** and cannot mislabel. ## Label fields Each triaged issue gets **one `kind/*`**, **one or two `area/*`**, and `status/bot-triaged`: - **`area/*`** (where the work lands): `extract`, `build`, `analyze`, `query`, `export`, `cli`, `install`, `watch`, `llm`, `ci`, `docs`, `other` - **`kind/*`** (what the issue is): `bug`, `feature`, `docs`, `question`, `refactor`, `performance`, `other` - **`status/*`** (workflow state, never model-chosen): `need-triage`, `bot-triaged`, `gfi-suggested` Pre-existing labels (`bug`, `enhancement`, `good first issue`, ...) are untouched. ## Model capabilities — System One (Jev) and a fallback chain The classifier has two engines behind one interface, chosen per candidate: | Engine | Providers | Output | Guarantee | |---|---|---|---| | **System One** | TypeSafe (Jev) | typed `choice` / `noul` answers + confidence | options are the allowlist → the API itself cannot emit an unknown label | | **Chat** | OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Groq, OpenRouter, Kimi, Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible gateway | JSON | validated against the allowlist in code | ```mermaid flowchart TD K[TRIAGE_MODEL ordered list] --> C1{Candidate: provider + model} C1 -->|typesafe| T[System One: Choice / Noul
typed, no type errors] C1 -->|openai / gemini / ...| O[Chat: JSON validated against allowlist] T --> R{Usable decision?} O --> R R -- yes --> Apply[Apply labels + status] R -- no, more candidates --> C1 R -- no, list exhausted --> FO[Fail open: keep status/need-triage] ``` `TRIAGE_MODEL` is an ordered list, each entry `[provider:]model`, so a rate-limited or slow provider never blocks triage: ``` TRIAGE_MODEL = "typesafe:jev-latest, openai:gpt-4.1-mini" ``` ### System One / Jev integration (recommended) Graphify is standardising on System One models for classification, so Jev is a first-class backend. Jev is **not a chat model**: `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` takes typed `questions` and returns typed `answers` with calibrated confidence. Triage maps directly onto its primitives: | Jev question | Type | Maps to | |---|---|---| | `kind` | `choice`, criteria = `kind/*` | the `kind/*` label | | `area` | `choice`, criteria = `area/*` | the primary `area/*` label | | `area_secondary` | `choice`, `area/*` + `none` | an optional second `area/*` | | `good_first_issue` | `noul` | GFI suggestion (probability >= 0.5) | Because a Choice's options *are* the label allowlist, Jev's output is type-safe by construction, and each answer's calibrated `confidence` is mapped to `high`/`medium`/`low`. Enable it with one secret (`TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, alias `JEV_API_KEY`); model defaults to `jev-latest`. Docs: . ## Evaluation on real issues `tools/triage/eval_classifier.py` is a provider-agnostic harness. It runs the exact code path the workflow uses against 18 hand-labeled real Graphify issues (`tools/triage/eval_dataset.json`) and reports accuracy, soft (probability) accuracy, latency, tokens and cost. Method, a per-issue table for every engine, the disagreement analysis and the raw request/response traces are in `tools/triage/EVAL.md`. Because the harness takes `--provider`/`--model`, the same 18 issues were run through System One and through two Gemini Flash tiers, so the comparison is apples-to-apples: | Engine | `kind` top-1 | `area` top-1 | soft p(kind) | mean latency | p50 | input tok/req | cost / 1k issues | failed | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **System One (`jev-latest`)** | 88.9% | 77.8% (83.3% contained) | **0.87** | **392 ms** | **380 ms** | 1,665 | **$0.070** | **0/18** | | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | 94.4% | 83.3% | n/a | 1,076 ms | 1,019 ms | 905 | $0.420 | 0/18 | | `gemini-3.8-flash` | 84.6%\* | 92.3%\* | n/a | 5,132 ms | 4,391 ms | 658 | $0.651 | 5/18 | \* Gemini 3.8 Flash completed only 13 of 18 requests on a free-tier key (5 came back `429`/`503`); under the workflow those issues simply keep `status/need-triage`. **Speed and cost, on identical issues.** The recommended backend returns a decision in **392 ms against 1,076 ms** for the fast Gemini tier and **5,132 ms** for the flagship Flash, so it is **2.7x to 13x faster**, at **6x to 9x lower cost per issue** ($0.07 vs $0.42 and $0.65 per 1,000 issues). System One returns a typed decision in a single round trip and bills input only, while a chat model spends completion tokens thinking before it emits JSON. That is exactly where the extra latency and cost go. **Accuracy is a wash at this sample size,** and this PR does not pretend otherwise: with 18 issues, one issue is 5.6 points, so Flash-Lite's one-extra-`kind` edge is a single case. What System One adds beyond top-1 is a **calibrated probability per label** (the source of the 0.87 soft accuracy and the `high`/`medium`/`low` confidence the workflow can filter on) plus a guarantee by construction that a label outside the allowlist cannot come back, since the Choice options *are* the allowlist. A chat model returns a JSON string that has to be re-validated in code. No OpenAI model was run: no OpenAI key was available to this evaluation. The harness supports it unchanged (`--provider openai --model gpt-4.1-mini`). Example trace (issue #4361, System One, 359 ms). Note that the labels in the response are the same strings the request offered as `criteria`, and that `good_first_issue` is a probability the code thresholds rather than a yes/no the model asserts: ```json // request (abridged) {"model": "jev-latest", "state": {"issue": {"number": 4361, "title": "...", "body": "...", "existing_labels": []}}, "questions": {"kind": {"type": "choice", "criteria": {"kind/bug": "...", "kind/feature": "..."}}, "area": {"type": "choice", "criteria": {"area/extract": "...", "...": "..."}}, "good_first_issue": {"type": "noul", "criteria": {"true": "...", "false": "..."}}}} // response {"model": "jev-1.13.0", "answers": {"kind": {"choice": "kind/bug", "confidence": 0.76, "probabilities": {"kind/bug": 0.79, "kind/feature": 0.14, "...": 0.0}}, "area": {"choice": "area/llm", "confidence": 1.0, "probabilities": {"area/llm": 1.0, "...": 0.0}}, "good_first_issue": {"noul": 0.3}}, "usage": {"input_tokens": 1784, "output_tokens": 354}} ``` Full verbatim traces for System One and for Gemini, side by side, are in EVAL.md. Every disagreement is on an issue where the taxonomy itself is arguable: #4469 (performance vs feature), #525 (docs vs question), #4341 (cli vs query), #1177 (docs vs install). The model's confidence flags exactly those, with clean issues coming back `high` and ambiguous ones `low`. Nothing was mislabelled into a label outside the allowlist. End to end, the exact CLI the workflow runs returns the expected decision, and the fallback chain recovers when the first model errors: ```text TRIAGE_MODEL=typesafe:jev-latest -> {"action":"triaged","provider":"typesafe","model":"jev-latest", "area":["area/extract"],"kind":"kind/bug","good_first_issue":true,"confidence":"high"} TRIAGE_MODEL=typesafe:jev-no-such-model,typesafe:jev-latest -> {"action":"triaged","provider":"typesafe","model":"jev-latest", ...} # fell through ``` ## Thanks Thanks to [@omsenjalia](https://github.com/omsenjalia), who provided the TypeSafe System One API key used for this evaluation. Without it this PR would have shipped with a "should be fast and cheap" claim instead of measured latency, tokens, cost and accuracy on real issues. ## Live results Also deployed to a fork and exercised with real issues. | Issue | Applied labels | |---|---| | `[Bug]: uninstall --purge deletes the project when GRAPHIFY_OUT is empty` | `area/cli`, `kind/bug`, `status/bot-triaged` | | `Typo in README quickstart` | `area/docs`, `kind/docs`, `status/bot-triaged`, `status/gfi-suggested` (+ suggestion comment) | | `Add support for the Grok CLI as a platform` | `area/install`, `kind/feature`, `status/bot-triaged` | | `How do I exclude a folder from indexing?` | `area/extract`, `kind/question`, `status/bot-triaged` | The `good first issue` label was **not** auto-applied — it was suggested on the docs typo and left for a maintainer, exactly as intended. Reopening an already triaged issue re-ran nothing (idempotent). The fallback chain was proven live: a rate-limited primary model fell through to the next model and still produced the right labels. ## Files | File | Role | |---|---| | `.github/workflows/issue-triage.yml` | The bot (supports `TRIAGE_DRY_RUN` canary) | | `.github/workflows/labels-sync.yml` | Create/update labels from the taxonomy | | `.github/workflows/workflow-lint.yml` | `actionlint` on the two workflows | | `tools/triage/taxonomy.py` | Single source of truth for the label set | | `tools/triage/classify.py` | System One + chat engines, allowlist, fallback, fail-open | | `tools/triage/sync_labels.py` | Idempotent label creation | | `tools/triage/eval_classifier.py` | Opt-in, provider-agnostic benchmark: labeled issues -> accuracy, latency, cost | | `tools/triage/eval_dataset.json` | The 18 labeled real issues the benchmark scores against | | `tools/triage/EVAL.md` | Evaluation method and measured results | | `tools/triage/README.md` | Operator/config reference | | `tools/triage/IMPLEMENTATION.md` | Adoption guide (prereqs, wiring, rollout) | | `tools/triage/__init__.py`, `tests/test_triage.py` | Package + tests | ## Safe rollout 1. **Fork / dry run** — verified above. 2. **`TRIAGE_DRY_RUN=true`** — the bot comments the proposed labels and changes nothing; review a batch against maintainer judgement. 3. **Live** — apply `area/`+`kind/`+`bot-triaged`; GFI stays suggestion-only. 4. Optional: promote GFI to auto-apply later once trusted. Rollback is non-destructive: set `TRIAGE_DRY_RUN`, or delete the workflow. ## Configuration | Settings | Name | Meaning | Default | |---|---|---|---| | Secrets | `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` (alias `JEV_API_KEY`) | System One key | — | | Secrets | `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` / ... | chat provider key | — | | Variables | `TRIAGE_MODEL` | model, or a comma-separated fallback list | provider default | | Variables | `TRIAGE_BASE_URL` | override base URL | provider endpoint | | Variables | `TRIAGE_MAX_TOKENS` | chat completion budget | `2048` | | Variables | `TRIAGE_DRY_RUN` | report proposed labels only | unset | ## Testing - `tests/test_triage.py`: **62 tests** — allowlist enforcement, fail-open, provider detection, the System One question/answer mapping, request shape, the fallback chain, bounded reads, the TOCTOU guard, and the eval fixture's labels (no network). Runs inside the existing CI matrix with no extra setup. - `actionlint` and `ruff` clean. - `tools/triage/eval_classifier.py` is the opt-in, paid accuracy/latency/cost benchmark, and doubles as the head-to-head against chat models; it is deliberately not part of CI. ## Review response The Graphify review bot flagged one advisory finding, which is fixed in this commit: - **TOCTOU: the apply step removed `area/`/`kind/` labels a maintainer added after the triage check.** The check step decided "needs triage", the model ran, and the apply step then removed every `area/`/`kind/` label it did not want, so a human who labelled the issue in that window lost their label. The check step now snapshots the labels, the apply step diffs the live labels against that snapshot, and if anything new appeared it backs off and leaves `status/need-triage` for a human. Labels that were already on the issue when triage started (a stale `kind/` from an earlier bot run) are still replaced, which is what the documented re-triage flow needs. The advisory unbounded-read patterns are fixed as well: model replies, the issue payload on stdin and the label-sync response are read with an explicit cap, following the same shape as the caps already used in `graphify/llm.py`. ## Safety - Minimal token scopes: `contents: read`, `issues: write`. - The API key is a repo secret, read only inside the classifier process. - Prompt injection contained: untrusted text never reaches a shell, the model can only pick from the allowlist, and no model-authored text is echoed into comments (the GFI note is fixed wording). - `good first issue` is never auto-applied. - The bot never removes a label it did not add. It snapshots the labels before the model runs and backs off if a maintainer labelled the issue in the meantime, so the issue keeps `status/need-triage` for a human instead of losing their label. ## Notes / open questions - The workflow files must land on the default branch (`v8`) for `issues` events. - Repo settings: Actions token `read/write`, Issues enabled (the guide covers both). - Open: run on Jev only, or Jev-with-fallback by default? Keep GFI suggested-only or auto-apply after a trusted period? Add `priority/*` in a follow-up? ## Checklist - [x] Additive only (13 new files, nothing existing modified) - [x] Tests added and passing (`pytest tests/test_triage.py`) - [x] Lint clean (`ruff`, `actionlint`) - [x] Evaluated on real issues with measured accuracy, latency and cost - [x] Fails open; never mislabels - [x] No secrets in the change - [x] Adoption/rollout documented (`tools/triage/IMPLEMENTATION.md`)

title: feat(llm): opt-in backend selection, disable switch, and honest auto-detect (#4361)
body:
## What this addresses

Closes #4361.

`detect_backend()` chooses a cloud provider purely from whichever API key is set in the environment (Gemini → Kimi → Claude → OpenAI → DeepSeek → Azure → Bedrock → Ollama), and community labeling additionally falls back to `claude -p` when the CLI is on `PATH`. Keys in a developer environment are often there for other tools (a coding assistant, a notebook, CI), so a bare `graphify extract .` could send the contents of uncached documents to a provider the user did not intend.

### Confirmed real on `v8` (0.9.87)

With a dummy `GEMINI_API_KEY` in the environment and no `--backend`:

```
$ graphify extract .            # repo also contains notes.md
[graphify extract] semantic extraction on 1 files via gemini...   # no hint why
```

## The fix

This takes the issue's alternative #2 — keep auto-detection, but make it honest and give it a real off switch — rather than flipping cloud use to opt-in, which would break every existing key-less `graphify extract` flow. The mechanism the issue names for #1 (`GRAPHIFY_BACKEND`) is added either way, so opting a run in or out is one line.

- **`GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=<name>`** selects a backend explicitly and wins over ambient keys.
- **`GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none`** (also `off` / `disable` / `disabled`) disables every LLM backend, including the `claude -p` labeling fallback. `graphify extract` keeps the local AST pass, prints what it held back, and exits 0 — the code-only graph is still built:

  ```
  $ GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none graphify extract .
  [graphify extract] GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none: skipping LLM work (1 non-code file(s) and LLM dedup kept out); indexing code only.
  ```

- **Auto-detection is announced**: it prints the exact variable that chose the provider and how to override or disable it:

  ```
  [graphify] using backend 'gemini' (auto-detected from GEMINI_API_KEY); pass --backend or set GRAPHIFY_BACKEND to choose explicitly, or GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none to disable LLM work.
  ```

- **The `claude -p` labeling fallback is announced** and opt-out-able. It is kept (not removed) because silently downgrading real labels to `Community N` is the regression it was added to prevent.
- `extract_files_direct()` raises a clear `ValueError` naming `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND` when a library caller would otherwise auto-detect a disabled backend.

Implementation: `detect_backend_with_source()` now carries the detection logic and returns `(backend, source)`; `detect_backend()` delegates to it. `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND` is added to `backend_detection_env_vars()` so tests (and the conftest isolator) treat it as a detection input. README data-residency note updated. `claude-cli` is not the target of a disable bypass elsewhere; the two auto-detect call sites (CLI `extract`, library `extract_files_direct`) and the label path all honour it.

## Tests

New `tests/test_backend_opt_in.py`:

- `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=<name>` beats an ambient key.
- `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND` set to each disable sentinel → `detect_backend()` is `None`, `backend_disabled_by_env()` is true.
- Auto-detection names the ambient variable (`auto-detected from GEMINI_API_KEY`).
- `extract_files_direct(backend=None)` raises naming `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND` when disabled.
- `generate_community_labels` returns placeholders and never contacts `label_communities` (so never reaches `claude -p`) when disabled — asserted by call count, so it fails pre-fix.

Verification:

- New tests: `9 passed`; **pre-fix** `8` of them fail.
- Related suites unaffected: `235 passed` (backend detection/isolation, llm backends, ollama, provider registry, extract CLI, labeling).
- CLI end-to-end: `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none` writes a code-only graph and exits 0; the auto-detect message names the source.
- `ruff check` clean.

## Not done (maintainer call)

The issue's primary suggestion (#1) — making cloud use strictly opt-in, so an unnamed backend skips the semantic step by default — is a behavior change for every existing user. This PR leaves auto-detection on by default and adds `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND` as the explicit selector, so flipping the default is a one-line follow-up if maintainers want it. Happy to do that in this PR or a follow-up.

title: fix(extract): resolve quoted dot-source and script-scope calls in PowerShell
body:
## What & Why

Fixes the two gaps reported in #4356 for PowerShell entry-point scripts.

1. **Quoted/interpolated dot-source had no edge.** The dot-source handler read its
   operand only from a `command_name` child of `command_name_expr`. A bare path
   (`. ./Shared.psm1`) parses that way, but a quoted or interpolated one
   (`. "$PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1"`) parses as a `string_literal`, so the lookup
   returned nothing and no `imports_from` edge was emitted. The operand is now
   taken from either a `command_name` or a `string_literal`, and a small helper
   (`_dot_source_module_stem`) strips the quotes, a leading variable reference
   (`$PSScriptRoot` / `${PSScriptRoot}` / `$env:DIR`), directory components and the
   extension, yielding the same stem the library file's node id uses.

2. **Script-scope calls were dropped.** `walk_calls` ran only over the bodies
   collected in `function_bodies`, so a command at file scope never became a
   `calls` edge (`main calls main_invoke_main` was missing). `walk_calls` now also
   runs once over the whole tree with the file node as the caller; it still stops
   at `function_statement` / `class_statement`, so the per-body passes are not
   repeated and no edge is emitted twice.

Together these cover the usual PowerShell entry-point shape: dot-source a library
at the top of the script, then call its functions at file scope.

Fixes #4356

## How Tested

Two focused regression tests added in `tests/test_languages.py`:

- `test_powershell_quoted_dot_source_emits_import_edge` — the quoted dot-source
  resolves to the library stem (`. "$PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1"` → `lib`).
- `test_powershell_script_scope_call_emits_calls_edge` — a top-level call is
  attributed to the file node (`("main.ps1", "Invoke-Main")`).

Each was confirmed to fail with the extractor fix reverted, and to pass with it
(the repo's CI runs on this fork):

- fix + tests → all green (`pytest`: 7323 passed, 14 skipped, on 3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14)
- tests only, fix reverted → `2 failed, 7322 passed, 14 skipped`,
  `FAILED ... test_powershell_quoted_dot_source_emits_import_edge`,
  `FAILED ... test_powershell_script_scope_call_emits_calls_edge`

Also run:

```
uv run ruff check .        # All checks passed
uv run pyright             # 1 error, pre-existing at HEAD~ (same _make_id
                           # argument, unchanged by this diff); no new errors
```

The parser assumptions behind the fix were checked directly against
`tree-sitter-powershell` 0.26.4: for `. "$PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1"` the
`command_name_expr` child is a `string_literal` (text `"$PSScriptRoot\lib.ps1"`),
and the top-level `Invoke-Main` is a `command` reachable from the root.

## Limitations

- A dot-source whose operand is a bare variable with no literal tail (`. "$path"`)
  still yields no edge — nothing can be resolved statically. Behavior is
  unchanged there.
- Calls inside file-scope `begin`/`process`/`end` blocks are attributed to the
  file node by the new pass.

title: feat(pi): add a native Pi guard extension that also loads in Oh My Pi
body:
## Summary

Graphify already installs a Pi *skill* (`graphify pi install`), but Pi has no `PreToolUse` hook, so the hook-guard policy that Claude Code, Codex and others get never runs there. This adds a native Pi extension that runs the installed `graphify hook-guard` before Pi's tool calls.

- `graphify/pi/` is a Pi package (`package.json` with a `pi.extensions` entry, plus `index.ts`) shipped inside the wheel and sdist. It imports only Node built-ins, so it loads straight from site-packages with no `node_modules`.
- On `tool_call` for `read`, `grep`, `find` and search-style `bash`, it calls `graphify hook-guard read|search` with a Claude-shaped payload. A strict-mode (`GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT=1`) denial becomes a `{block, reason}` result. Guidance is sent as one `<system-reminder source="graphify">` steering message. All graph decisions stay in the existing Python policy.
- `graphify pi guard install|uninstall` delegates to Pi's own `pi install|remove <package dir>`. `graphify pi guard path` prints the directory.
- Safety bounds:
  - Only local targets inside the project are checked.
  - The hook uses the first `graphify` on an absolute `PATH` entry outside the project, so there is no project-local fallback.
  - Each call has a 256 KiB input cap, a 64 KiB output cap and a 2 s `SIGKILL` budget.
  - In-flight calls are cancelled on session navigation and new runs.
  - Every failure fails open.

### Oh My Pi

Oh My Pi reads the same `pi` manifest key, so the same package loads there with `omp plugin install "$(graphify pi guard path)"`. On OMP, guidance uses its passive tool-call context channel instead of a steering message. OMP's `glob` and `;`-separated targets are handled too. This supersedes #3506, which shipped an OMP-only package.

## Testing

- `tests/pi.test.ts` (bun, 19 tests) drives the real extension against the real installed `graphify` CLI. It covers nudges, the strict denial, out-of-project and remote targets, `~`/`@` paths, `PATH` shadowing and symlinked executables, timeouts, output and input caps, cancellation on navigation, unmapped tools, and Pi vs OMP delivery. The new `pi-guard` CI job runs it.
- `tests/test_pi_guard_install.py` covers `pi guard path`, delegation to `pi install`/`pi remove` with exit-code propagation, and a missing `pi`.
- Full pytest suite: 7376 passed, 185 skipped.
- Manual tests with a non-editable install of the built package:
  - **Pi 0.85.1:** `graphify pi guard install` registered the package. A Pi SDK session loaded it from that registration and got nudges for `grep`/`find`/`bash`/`read` and the one-time strict denial.
  - **Oh My Pi 18.10.1:** `omp plugin install "$(graphify pi guard path)"` gave the same results.

title: [Bug]: Solidity: calls, `super` calls and modifiers inherited from a base contract get no edge
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

The Solidity extractor binds a bare call `f()` and a modifier `onlyX` only to members of the contract that makes the call. Almost every real contract calls into its bases (`_msgSender()` from `Context`, `onlyOwner` from `Ownable`, `super.supportsInterface()`), and those calls get no edge, so `explain` / `affected` on a base-contract function miss every derived contract that uses it.

```solidity
// Ownable.sol
import {Context} from "./Context.sol";
abstract contract Ownable is Context {
    modifier onlyOwner() { _checkOwner(); _; }
    function _checkOwner() internal view { require(owner() == _msgSender()); }   // _msgSender: no edge
}
// Vault.sol
import {Ownable} from "./Ownable.sol";
contract Vault is Ownable {
    function sweep() external onlyOwner { }                                     // onlyOwner: no edge
}
```

`super.f()` is lost twice over: it is never resolved, and tree-sitter-solidity parses `x || super.f(y)` (the usual `supportsInterface` shape) as a call of `(x || super).f`.

**Expected:** Each such call or modifier links to the member solc resolves it to: the first declaration in the caller contract's C3 linearization (for `super.f()`, the first one after the caller's own contract).

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
Save the two files above (plus a `Context.sol` declaring `_msgSender()`), run `graphify update . --no-cluster`, and look for `calls` / `uses` edges out of `_checkOwner()` and `sweep()`.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Answer key: solc's AST (`referencedDeclaration` of every call, modifier invocation and `super` call). Graphify 0.9.87, `graphify update . --no-cluster`:

| repo | inherited `f()` | inherited modifier | `super.f()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenZeppelin contracts (`contracts/`, solc 0.8.28) | 0 of 237 | 0 of 29 | 0 of 71 |
| Uniswap v3-core (`contracts/`, solc 0.7.6) | 0 of 1 | 0 of 7 | — |
| solmate (`src/`, solc 0.8.15) | 0 of 6 | 0 of 7 | — |

Calls inside one contract are found (75-100%).
```

### Graphify version

0.9.87 (7536dc06)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No LLM keys; AST only. Windows 11, Python 3.12. Clean checkout of v8 @ 7536dc06 (0.9.87) reproduces. Answer key: solc 0.8.28 / 0.8.15 / 0.7.6 via solc-js.

### Additional context

Related: #3906 and #4090 (other Solidity fixes). Library calls, `using for` calls, typed receivers, `emit` and `revert` are separate gaps I will file on their own. PR right after this issue.

title: Python: `@x.setter`/`@x.getter`/`@x.deleter` mint a sourceless stub node and a false decorator edge
body:
**Version/commit:** v0.9.87 (v8 @ 7536dc0)
**Environment:** macOS, Python 3.13, `uv sync --all-extras`

### Problem
The Python decorator-reference pass (#2154) runs `ensure_named_node` on a decorator's head symbol. For the property-descriptor protocol decorators `@x.setter` / `@x.getter` / `@x.deleter`, the head symbol is `setter`/`getter`/`deleter` — not a corpus symbol. So every property with a setter/deleter (or a `@x.getter` redefinition) fabricates a sourceless stub node (`setter`/`getter`/`deleter`, empty `source_file`) and a `references` (context=decorator) edge onto it.

This is the same fabrication the builtin-decorator noise list already guards against for `@property`/`@staticmethod`, and it violates the provenance rule (a node with no source file).

### Reproduction
```python
class Config:
    @property
    def name(self): return self._n
    @name.setter
    def name(self, v): self._n = v
```

### Expected
No decorator edge and no sourceless stub for `@name.setter` (the accessor protocol is not a reference to a symbol named `setter`).

### Actual
A sourceless node labeled `setter` and a `references` edge `Config.name -> setter`.

Fix PR to follow.

### Problem
PEP 673 `Self` names the enclosing class, not a corpus symbol, but the Python type-ref pass treats the bare identifier `Self` (and the `typing.Self` tail) as a type reference and runs it through the sourceless-stub path. ```

`Self` is dropped, exactly as the `-> "Builder"` string self forward-ref is already left unresolved. No sourceless `self` node.

### Actual
A sourceless node labeled `Self` (id `self`) with a `references` edge from the method.

title: feat(solidity): resolve calls, `super` calls and modifiers inherited from base contracts
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4379.

- `extractors/solidity.py`, extractor: a bare `f()` / `this.f()` the caller's contract does not declare, a `super.f()` and a modifier the contract does not declare are recorded as raw calls (`solidity_call`: `inherited` / `super` / `modifier`, with the call's argument count). Callables carry `metadata.arity`. Modifiers on constructors, `receive` and `fallback` are read too (only functions were).
- `_callee_text`: tree-sitter-solidity parses `x || super.f(y)` as a call of `(x || super).f`; the right-most operand is read as the receiver.
- `resolve_solidity_inherited_calls`, registered right after `solidity_type_references` (it walks the `inherits` edges that pass binds): takes the caller contract's C3 linearization (`contract C is A, B` -> C, B, A, as solc), and links to the first contract that declares the name (functions also by argument count); `super.f()` starts after the caller's contract. Several same-arity overloads in that contract are ambiguous and get no edge. Edges are `calls` / `uses` (as for same-contract calls and modifiers), EXTRACTED.
- `extract.py`: the shared corpus-wide name match skips these raw calls, so a name no base declares is never bound to some other contract's function.
- `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 10 -> 11 (Solidity extraction output changed).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a Solidity call or modifier binds to the declaration solc binds it to, searched only through the caller contract's own bases.

Answer key: solc's AST over each repo (every call's / modifier's / `super` call's `referencedDeclaration`), graphify `update . --no-cluster`, 0.9.87 vs this branch:

| repo | inherited `f()` | inherited modifier | `super.f()` | all compiler references found |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OpenZeppelin contracts | 0 -> 237 of 237 | 0 -> 29 of 29 | 0 -> 68 of 71 | 34.5% -> 46.5% |
| Uniswap v3-core | 0 -> 1 of 1 | 0 -> 7 of 7 | — | 31.2% -> 36.8% |
| solmate | 0 -> 6 of 6 | 0 -> 7 of 7 | — | 32.2% -> 43.5% |

Edges between two functions/modifiers that solc does not have: solmate 4 -> 4, Uniswap 10 -> 10 (both: contract-level `using` edges, unchanged), OpenZeppelin 147 -> 155. The 8 new ones are real calls drawn from a merged node: `_grantRole` and `grantRole` (same parameters) get one node id, so a call made in `_grantRole` shows on `grantRole`. That id collision exists on 0.9.87 for 85 such pairs in OpenZeppelin; I will open it separately.

Not covered here (separate PRs): library calls `Lib.f()`, `using L for T` calls, calls on a typed receiver `token.f()`, `emit E()` and `revert Err()`.

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test**: `tests/test_solidity_inherited_calls.py`, 8 tests (base function in another file, base modifier two levels up, `super` chain, `super` inside `||`, last-listed base wins, same-arity overloads left unbound, no corpus-wide name match, changed-files rebuild equals full build). 7 fail on 0.9.87; the no-name-match guard passes on both.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Limitations:** overloads are told apart by argument count only (same count, different types = no edge); a base contract must bind through the existing type pass (declared in the same file or an imported one).

body:
Fixes #4380.

### Problem
The Python decorator-reference pass (#2154) runs `ensure_named_node` on a decorator's head symbol. For the property-descriptor protocol `@x.setter` / `@x.getter` / `@x.deleter`, the head symbol is `setter`/`getter`/`deleter` — not a corpus symbol — so every property with a setter/deleter (or a `@x.getter` redefinition) fabricates a sourceless stub node and a false `references` (context=decorator) edge onto it. title: fix(go): drop generic type parameters from signature type references
body:
Fixes #4383.

title: [Bug]: graphify update false positive on semantic nodes deduplicated into canonical AST twins
body:
### Pre-flight checks
- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?
When updating an existing graph via `graphify update .`, `build_from_json()` dedupes semantic nodes that share `(source_file, label)` with a canonical AST node (per `#1145 (extended)`: non-AST nodes sharing `(source_file, label)` with an AST node have their ghost IDs removed from the graph, and their edges are rewired to the canonical node).

However, the shrink guard `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes(saved_nodes, new_nodes, deleted_sources)` checks whether any saved semantic node is missing from `new_nodes` only by looking up `node_id in new_ids` and legacy stem renames (`_renamed_present`). Because the ghost ID was intentionally pruned during deduplication, `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes()` falsely classifies the deduplicated node as "lost".

The shrink guard then aborts the update with:
```text
[graphify] WARNING: Refusing to overwrite — saved semantic node(s) are missing from the new graph: src/models/user.ts:User.
Nothing to update or rebuild failed
```
requiring `--force` even though no symbols were lost.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Build a graph where a symbol has a semantic node (e.g. `id: "src/models/user.ts:User"`, `label: "User"`, `source_file: "src/models/user.ts"`, `_origin: "semantic"`).
2. Run `graphify update .` to perform an AST-only code rebuild.
3. The AST extractor emits the canonical AST node for `User` (`_origin: "ast"`).
4. `build_from_json()` collapses the semantic ghost node into the AST canonical node.
5. `_check_shrink()` runs `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes()`, which reports `src/models/user.ts:User` as lost and aborts with exit code 1.

### Error output or graph output
```text
[graphify] WARNING: Refusing to overwrite — saved semantic node(s) are missing from the new graph: src/models/user.ts:User.
Nothing to update or rebuild failed
```

### Graphify version
0.9.87

### Operating System
Windows / Linux / macOS

### Python Version
3.11 / 3.12 / 3.13

title: [Bug]: LLM field variations (file/path -> source_file, relationship -> relation) trigger false extraction schema warnings
body:
### Pre-flight checks
- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?
When loading or validating semantic extractions, LLMs frequently emit `"file"`, `"path"`, or `"filepath"` instead of `"source_file"` on nodes, and `"relationship"` instead of `"relation"` on edges.

title: fix(build): exempt deduplicated AST-twin semantic nodes from shrink guard and fold LLM node/edge field aliases
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4389
Fixes #4390

1. **Exempt deduplicated AST-twin semantic nodes from the shrink guard** (#4389):
   `build_from_json()` folds a non-AST node into a canonical AST node that shares its `(source_file, label)` (#1145 extended), so the semantic ghost id disappears even though the symbol survives. `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes()` only looked up ids, so it reported the folded node as lost and `graphify update` / `to_json()` refused to write without `--force`.
   The guard now indexes new nodes by `(_norm_source_file(source_file), label)` and excuses a missing saved semantic node when that key holds a new node. It uses the same rules as the dedup:
   - only strict `_origin == "ast"` nodes count as canonical (#2334), so a non-AST or drifted semantic node cannot excuse a loss;
   - keys shared by 2+ AST nodes are ambiguous (same as `_loc_collisions`) and excuse nothing;
   - a truthy non-string `source_file` is skipped instead of raising.
2. **Fold LLM node and edge field aliases** (#4390):
   - `_fold_node_aliases()`: folds `file`, `path` and `filepath` onto `source_file` (first non-blank alias wins) before `validate_extraction()`.
   - `_fold_edge_aliases()`: folds `relationship` onto `relation`, after the existing `type` fold.
   - A canonical field that is already set always wins. Docstrings updated to match.

### Known limitation (out of scope)

`build_from_json()` has two other dedup passes that also drop a semantic ghost id, and the shrink guard still reports those as lost:
- method ghosts remapped to a single AST method (#3705), e.g. `get_pairs` → `.get_pairs()`;
- file-mention ghosts remapped by label to an AST file node (#3344), e.g. `App.tsx` with `source_file: notes.md`.

Both still make `to_json()` refuse the write. I kept this PR to the `(source_file, label)` case; happy to follow up separately.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The end-to-end positive tests fail on `v8` and pass on this branch.
  - `tests/test_alias_folding.py` (7 tests).

title: [Bug]: PDF and image URL captures can overwrite an earlier file
body:
### Pre-flight checks

### What happened?

Adding two PDF or image URLs that produce the same sanitized filename writes both downloads to one corpus path. For example, URLs with the same host and `.pdf` path but different query strings select the same destination. The second successful capture replaces the first file's bytes, and both calls report that path. I expect both captures to remain available at distinct paths, with each returned path naming its own saved bytes.

This is supported by the `v8` source: the filename uses the URL host and path, omits the query, and the PDF and image routes write directly to that filename. I have not run the example below against Graphify.

### Steps to reproduce

The following is a deterministic local example using mocked validation and downloads. It does not make a network request. Run it from a source checkout with Graphify installed:

```shell
python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from unittest.mock import patch
import graphify.ingest as ingest_mod

first_url = "https://example.org/report.pdf?revision=one"
second_url = "https://example.org/report.pdf?revision=two"
payloads = {first_url: b"first PDF", second_url: b"second PDF"}

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    target = Path(directory)
    with patch.object(ingest_mod, "validate_url"), patch.object(
        ingest_mod, "safe_fetch", side_effect=lambda url: payloads[url]
    ):
        first = ingest_mod.ingest(first_url, target)
        second = ingest_mod.ingest(second_url, target)
    print(first.name, second.name)
    print(first.read_bytes())
    print(sorted(path.name for path in target.iterdir()))
PY
```

The image route uses the same binary writer; two `.png` URLs with a shared host/path and different queries have the same naming collision.

### Error output or graph output

No command output or graph was captured. The source predicts the following final three lines for the mocked PDF example, after its download status messages (filename is path-sanitized), because both calls select `example_org_report_pdf.pdf` and the second write replaces its contents:

```text

b'second PDF'
['example_org_report_pdf.pdf']
```

There is no exception to warn that the first capture was replaced.

title: feat(dispatch): link interface members to every implementer, not just one (#3800)
body:
## What does this PR do?

`resolve_interface_dispatch` (the shared mechanism behind both the C# and Swift `dispatches_to` passes, #3003 / #3673) bailed out entirely whenever an interface or protocol had more than one implementer — the exact scenario #3800 reports. For a static structural graph, "what can this call reach" has an answer of **all** implementers, not none; stopping at the interface for the common multi-implementer case left most injected-dependency chains permanently cut.

This links the interface member to **every** implementer that owns it unambiguously, instead of only firing when there is exactly one. Each implementer is still checked independently against the existing single-owner guard (an implementer that itself declares two methods of the same name is skipped on its own, without suppressing its siblings). Confidence falls as the candidate set grows, using the extraction rubric's own discrete INFERRED tiers: 0.85 (1 implementer, unchanged) → 0.75 (2) → 0.65 floor (3+).

Scope: this addresses only the first half of #3800 (`dispatches_to` edges to every implementation). The second half of that issue — a `calls`/`accesses` edge for property reads through an interface-typed receiver (e.g. `c.Count`) — is a different mechanism (property-access resolution in the extractors, not this post-pass) and is left for a separate PR to keep this change to one concern.

Fixes #3800 (partially — see Scope above).

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

This is additive (existing call edge to the interface member is untouched) and purely INFERRED, so it cannot turn a real EXTRACTED fact into something else, and it cannot regress the existing single-implementer case (count=1 still scores 0.85, covered by the pre-existing tests).

title: feat(go): resolve member calls through typed parameters and struct fields (#3368)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Go's extractor marks every non-package-alias selector call (`p.cfg.Format()`, `limiter.Allow()`) `is_member_call=True`, and the shared cross-file resolver (`resolve_cross_file_raw_calls`) drops every member call unconditionally — the same conservative default every language with this gap uses, since a bare method name alone collides across a corpus. No Go-specific resolver existed to answer it instead, so a member call through a typed parameter, receiver, or struct field produced **no `calls` edge at all**. As #3368 shows on a real service codebase, that's most cross-component calls in typical Go code built on structs and interfaces.

This adds a Go-specific resolver, `graphify/go_resolution.py`, following the same pattern as the existing C#/Ruby/Kotlin receiver-typed resolvers:

1. The extractor (`graphify/extractors/go.py`) now builds two small tables while parsing each file: `go_local_types` (caller -> `{name: declared type's node id}`, from a receiver or parameter) and `go_struct_fields` (type -> `{field: declared type's node id}`, from that type's own field declarations). Both only ever hold a **bare, same-package** declared type (`_go_bare_local_type`) — a slice, map, func, generic instantiation, or package-qualified type is left out, never guessed.
2. `resolve_go_member_calls` walks a member call's dotted receiver chain (`p.cfg`, `a.b.inner`) segment by segment through these tables to the type it bottoms out at, then looks up the called method on that type via the existing `method` edges. A miss at any step — ambiguous, untypable, or out of scope — leaves the call unresolved rather than guessing.
3. Emitted edges are `INFERRED` at `0.85` ("strong inference"): the receiver's type is proven structurally, but the call site itself never names it — the same tier C#'s `recv.M()` case uses.

### Scope

This covers the issue's Patterns A–C (parameter, struct field, and multi-segment field-chain receivers), for same-package declared types. Explicitly **out of scope**, left as follow-up (matching how the issue itself phases the work):

- **A package-qualified receiver/field type** (`pkg.Type`, e.g. the issue's own `uploader.IProfileUploader` example). Resolving that needs the cross-package qualified-type machinery `_resolve_go_type_references` already owns — a second, narrower copy of that logic here would duplicate it rather than reuse it.
- **A local variable's inferred type** (`x := &Foo{}`). Only a parameter, receiver, or field with an explicit declared type carries one in these tables.
- **Interface dispatch (Pattern D / Steps 4–5)**. Go has no `implements` keyword, so even after this fix, a call that resolves onto an *interface* method still stops there. Comparing method sets to find which structs satisfy which interfaces, then following `interface_dispatch.py`'s existing dispatch pattern from there, is a separate, larger change.

Fixes #3368 (partially — see Scope).

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Additive only: every new edge is `INFERRED`, nothing existing is repointed or removed, and an unresolved chain produces no edge (never a wrong one). Determinism: resolution is a pure function of the extracted tables and `method` edges — no ambient state, no network, no ordering dependency (merging per-file tables is keyed by full node ids, so file iteration order can't change the result).

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue's root cause (traced to `go.py`'s `walk_calls` / the shared resolver's unconditional `is_member_call` skip) and verified end-to-end with the issue's own example shapes (typed parameter, struct field, 3-segment chain, package-qualified type) before writing the fix.
- [x] Made a **focused fix**: one new module (`go_resolution.py`) plus additive-only extraction-side table building; no existing node/edge shape is changed, only two new per-file dict keys and one new raw-call field (`member_receiver`) are added.
- [x] Added **regression tests**: `tests/test_go_member_calls.py` (9 cases) covering a typed-parameter receiver, cross-file struct-field resolution over an *ambiguous* bare method name (proves the fix isn't just riding the engine's existing same-file bare-name fallback), confidence tier, 3-segment chains, package-qualified types staying unresolved, generic type-parameter fields not being chased, an undeclared field producing no edge, edge dedup, and a non-Go corpus being untouched.
- [x] Documented limitations explicitly (see Scope above and the module docstring in `go_resolution.py`).

title: Source-less external placeholders that lose their last edge without a file being deleted are never collected (after #4247 upgrade, and on every edit that drops the last reference)
body:
### Pre-flight checks
- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

A source-less node (external-type placeholder such as `List`, or a namespace node such as `system_collections_generic`) that loses its last edge stays in `graph.json` permanently at degree 0. This happens when the edge goes away because a file was **re-extracted**, not deleted.

There are two paths, both on 0.9.88:

1. **Upgrade across #4247 (0.9.84).** The per-file stubs (`a_cs_list`, `b_cs_list`) are replaced by one shared `list` placeholder. Re-extraction re-points the edges, but the old stubs are left behind at degree 0.
   - This happens with incremental runs and with `extract --force --code-only`. `--code-only` on an existing graph always merges (`merge_existing_graph = incremental_mode or (code_only and existing_graph_path.exists())`, cli.py:3737).
   - On our real C# backend graph, a `--force --code-only` rebuild after 0.9.70 → 0.9.88 left **41,709 orphans out of 116,039 nodes**. For example, there were 4,233 `Task` nodes at degree 0 next to one shared `task` node with 12,458 edges.
   - Communities went from 13,249 to 43,319, almost all of them singletons. `query_graph`/`get_node` for `Task`/`List` returned thousands of dead hits.
2. **Steady state.** When the last file that references an external type or namespace is *edited* so that it no longer references it, the shared placeholder stays at degree 0 forever. This is ongoing accumulation, not just a one-off migration artefact.

As far as I can tell from the 0.9.88 source, the cause is:
- `build_merge` drops existing nodes and edges *owned by* re-extracted sources (by `source_file`, build.py ~2220). A source-less placeholder is owned by nobody, so it survives with no edges.
- The orphan sweep added for #2807 (build.py ~2483–2531) only runs inside `if prune_sources:`, so it only runs when files are deleted or excluded.
- Even when it does run, it spares `_isolated_before`: source-less nodes that are already at degree 0 when the sweep starts. That is computed *after* the re-extracted sources' old edges are gone, so these nodes count as "already isolated" and are kept.

`--force` does not help (see path 1). The only way to clear them is to delete `graph.json` and rebuild from scratch, which loses the semantic/curated layer. Alternatively you can prune by hand.

### Steps to reproduce

Path 1 (upgrade):
```shell
mkdir -p repro/src && cd repro
printf 'using System.Collections.Generic;\nnamespace Demo\n{\n    public class A { public List<int> Items; }\n}\n'   > src/A.cs
printf 'using System.Collections.Generic;\nnamespace Demo\n{\n    public class B { public List<string> Names; }\n}\n' > src/B.cs
uvx --from "graphifyy==0.9.70" graphify extract src --code-only
uvx --from "graphifyy==0.9.88" graphify extract src --force --code-only
```

Path 2 (steady state, 0.9.88 only):
```shell
rm -rf src/graphify-out
uvx --from "graphifyy==0.9.88" graphify extract src --code-only      # fresh build
printf 'namespace Demo\n{\n    public class A { public int[] Items; }\n}\n'     > src/A.cs
printf 'namespace Demo\n{\n    public class B { public string[] Names; }\n}\n'  > src/B.cs
uvx --from "graphifyy==0.9.88" graphify extract src --code-only      # incremental: both files edited, nothing deleted
```

### Error output or graph output

Source-less nodes and their degree after each step:

```text
Path 1
0.9.70 extract                      nodes 8  a_cs_list(1) b_cs_list(1) system_collections_generic(2)
0.9.88 extract --force --code-only  nodes 9  list(2) a_cs_list(0) b_cs_list(0) system_collections_generic(2)
0.9.88 incremental (touch A.cs)     nodes 9  list(2) a_cs_list(0) b_cs_list(0) system_collections_generic(2)
control: fresh 0.9.88 from scratch  nodes 7  list(2) system_collections_generic(2)

Path 2
fresh 0.9.88                        nodes 7  list(2) system_collections_generic(2)
incremental, A+B drop List          nodes 7  list(0) system_collections_generic(0)
control: fresh from scratch         nodes 5  (no source-less nodes)
```

Expected: incremental and `--force --code-only` end with the same node set as a from-scratch build (7 and 5 respectively).

### Graphify version
0.9.88 (upgraded from 0.9.70)

### Operating System
openSUSE Leap 16.0 (x86_64)

### Python Version
3.13.13

### Installation Method
`uv tool install "graphifyy[openai,mcp]"` (uv 0.11.16); repro uses `uvx`

### Additional Environment Details
Large C# monorepo (~430 csproj, ~116k nodes before cleanup). The graph is served through `graphify serve`, rebuilt incrementally every night and with `--force --code-only` once a week.

### Additional context

Possible fix directions (your call, of course):
- Run the source-less/degree-0 sweep after **every** merge, not only when `prune_sources` is non-empty.
- Snapshot `_isolated_before` from the graph **as loaded from disk** (before the re-extracted sources' nodes and edges are dropped). Nodes that were isolated in the stored graph would still be protected, which is the rationale in the code comment. Nodes isolated *by this run's rebind* would be collected, matching the #2807 reasoning that "a node with neither a source_file nor an edge names nothing and connects nothing".
- Optionally, a one-time migration sweep when the stored `graphify_version` predates #4247, for graphs whose stubs were already orphaned by an earlier run.

For now we pruned our graph once by hand with exactly the #2807 criterion (no `source_file`, `file_type == "code"`, degree 0), then ran `cluster-only` + `label`. Result: 116,039 → 74,330 nodes, edges unchanged, 43,319 → 1,610 communities. Path 2 means the orphans will build up again without a fix upstream.

title: [Feature]: Extract Objective-C NS_ENUM and NS_OPTIONS declarations
body:
### Problem or use case

Graphify recognizes ordinary Objective-C enums, but skips enum and option types declared with `NS_ENUM` or `NS_OPTIONS`. Their names and values are missing from the graph, even in files that Graphify already recognizes as Objective-C.

For example, save this as `Window.h`:

```objc
#import <Foundation/Foundation.h>

typedef NS_ENUM(NSInteger, WindowState) {
    WindowStateClosed,
    WindowStateOpen,
};

typedef NS_OPTIONS(NSUInteger, WindowOptions) {
    WindowOptionsResizable = 1 << 0,
    WindowOptionsClosable = 1 << 1,
};
```

The Objective-C extractor currently produces no enum types or members for these declarations. The inspected `v8` snapshot, [`a9860f7`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/commit/a9860f70dc3cc2e9c2d8cb923484cfa0592b9067), explicitly leaves both macros unsupported.

To inspect the result directly, without the extraction cache:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extractors.objc import extract_objc

result = extract_objc(Path("Window.h"))
print([node["label"] for node in result["nodes"]])
```

### Proposed solution

Include `WindowState`, `WindowOptions`, and their members in the graph, using the same type nodes and `case_of` edges as ordinary enums. Keep their source locations and skip malformed declarations without losing valid neighboring declarations.

This would cover the two named macros in files already routed to the Objective-C extractor. It would not add general preprocessor expansion or evaluate enum values.

### Alternatives considered

Writing the declarations as ordinary enums makes them visible today, but changing application source just to build a graph is not a useful workaround.

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact
