title: Kotlin: generic type parameters (`<T>`) leak as a sourceless god node `t`
body:
**Version/commit:** v0.9.88 (v8 @ a9860f7)
**Environment:** macOS, Python 3.13, `uv sync --all-extras`

### Problem
`_kotlin_collect_type_refs` appends the bare `T`/`R` identifiers used in a generic signature or property type as type references and runs them through the sourceless-stub path. Every generic class/function in the corpus then collapses its `T` onto one bare `t` node — a god node. Single-letter type params are not in the analyzer's builtin-noise filter, so these hubs pollute god-node rankings. C#, Java, TypeScript, and Go already exclude their type parameters (the just-shipped Go #4383 is the same fix).

### Reproduction
```kotlin
class Box<T>(val v: T) {
    fun get(): T? = v
    fun <R> map(f: (T) -> R): R? = null
}
```

### Expected
`T`/`R` dropped (local bindings); genuine user types and the generic container head still reference.

### Actual
Sourceless nodes `t`/`r` with `references` edges from the class/functions.

Fix PR to follow.

`_kotlin_collect_type_refs` appends the bare `T`/`R` identifiers used in a generic signature or property type as type references and runs them through the sourceless-stub path. title: fix(dedup): keep a dropped-folder doc next to a top-level same-id file (#4281)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4281. Closes the gap named in the review of #4371: "a bare id that names an actual input file, e.g. a top-level protocol.md next to docs/protocol.md". Stacks cleanly with #4371 in either order.

When the LLM drops the folder, `protocol.md`, `docs/protocol.md` and `docs/firmware/protocol.md` all mint `protocol`. #4362 skips any group whose bare id names an input file, because the id may be a reference to that file. So the collapse ran and one real document was dropped:

```diff
 nodes after build
   docs_protocol            docs/protocol.md
   docs_firmware_protocol   docs/firmware/protocol.md
+  protocol                 protocol.md        (v8: dropped)

 edges
-  docs_firmware_protocol -> docs_protocol
+  docs_firmware_protocol -> protocol
```

The id alone can't tell "my own page with the folder dropped" from "a reference to protocol.md". The rest of the file can: a file that only refers to protocol.md still has its own page node.

```text
for each id shared across files:
  the file whose full stem IS the id (protocol.md) keeps it and counts toward the group
  for each other file with that bare id:
    if the file has no other node spelled with its own full stem:
      the bare id is its page: rename to <full stem> + rest of id
    else:
      it may be a reference: leave it to the collapse, as before

survivor ranking:
  a bare path slice from a file that has its own page ranks as a reference,
  so protocol.md's node survives whatever the labels are
```

```diff
 deduplicate_entities
   _path_qualify_dropped_collisions
+    _own_page_files                         # file has a node spelled with its own full stem
-    skip the group if the bare id names an input file
+    decide per file: no own page -> rename, own page -> collapse
   exact-id collapse
-    mentions = _mentions(...)
+    mentions = _mentions(...) | _slice_references(...)
     _collision_rank(node, root, mentions)
```

### Existing tests this PR changes

| Test | Before | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_top_level_collision_keeps_todays_result` | 2 nodes; its docstring says "KNOWN LIMITATION, pinned so a change is noticed" | renamed `test_top_level_file_keeps_its_own_node_next_to_dropped_folder_docs`; 3 nodes, the firmware reference ends on `protocol` | this is the fixed case |
| `test_bare_id_naming_an_existing_file_is_not_renamed` | three files, each with a single `protocol`, collapse to 1 node | renamed `test_bare_ids_in_three_files_keep_one_node_per_file`; 3 nodes, no collision warning | none of the three files has another page, so each bare id is that file's page. The collapse was the data loss |

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

One node per real document. A reference must not become a new document, and a real document must not be dropped. The result does not depend on input order or label length.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Code only: no schema, cache or file-format change.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. It changes only groups where an input file is named by the bare id, and survivor choice only for a bare path slice from a file that has its own page. On a rebuild, such a corpus gets one more document node, and a saved query for `protocol` finds the top-level file.

**Limitations**

- If the LLM drops the folder AND emits another node spelled with the file's full stem (`docs_protocol_header`), the file counts as having its own page and gets the collapse it got before. `test_dropped_folder_doc_with_own_stem_entity_falls_back_to_collapse` pins this.
- In R_toplevel one warning still prints: the firmware file's mention of `protocol` collapses into the top-level node. That merge is right, the warning is noise.

title: [Bug]: C#: a partial type loses the members of a half when its file stem collides with another file (`Spec.cs` / `_Spec.cs`, `Cfg/Helpers.cs` / `Cfg_Helpers.cs`)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?


Two file paths can mint the same file stem: a leading underscore is dropped (`Spec.cs` and `_Spec.cs`), and a
directory separator becomes `_` (`Cfg/Helpers.cs` and `Cfg_Helpers.cs`). The type ids in those files then collide,
and `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids` salts them apart by path. That part works.

It goes wrong when one of the colliding types is a `partial` type with a half in a third file. In `extract()`,
`_merge_csharp_partial_class_nodes` runs BEFORE `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids`:

1. The merge picks the canonical half and rewires the edges of the other halves onto the canonical id. That id is
   still the colliding, unsalted one.
2. The disambiguation remaps an edge endpoint by `(id, source_file of the edge)`. The rewired edges carry the
   source_file of the half they came from, not of the canonical half. The lookup misses, and since the id is
   ambiguous, the fallback does not apply either. The edges stay on an id that no node has any more.

Result:

* The members declared in the third half have no owning type (no `method` edge).
* That half's file has no `contains` edge to the type.
* If both colliding files declare a half of the same partial type (same id in two files), the merge does not
  remove the second node (it only removes nodes whose id differs from the canonical one). The disambiguation then
  splits them again, so the type stays two nodes.
* The merge removes merged-away halves by id. If an unrelated node in another file shares that id, it is removed
  too. Example: `Cfg/Helpers.cs` holds a half of `App.Cfg`, and `Cfg.cs` holds a method
  `Helpers.App.Cfg()`. Both mint the same id; the method disappears from the graph, and its `calls` edge now
  starts at the type `Cfg`. (Not in the repro below; the PR adds it as a test.)

The repro shows the first three symptoms in two shapes. Case 1 (`Cfg`) has no underscore at all.

**Expected:**

```text
Cfg    1 node(s) [['.Alpha()', '.Beta()', '.Gamma()']]
Spec   1 node(s) [['.Copy()', '.Move()']]
_Spec  1 node(s) [['.Extra()']]
methods without owner: []
```

**Scale.** On a proprietary C# corpus of eight graphs, built with graphifyy 0.9.88 from PyPI (graphify's own output,
no post-processing), 60 C# method nodes have no `method` edge. All 60 are in one graph, which has 5 file groups with
a colliding stem (1 leading underscore, 4 directory separator vs. underscore). The other seven graphs have no such
group and no method without an owner.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p partial-collide && cd partial-collide
mkdir -p Cfg generated

cat > Demo.csproj <<'EOF'
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup><TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework></PropertyGroup>
</Project>
EOF

# Case 1: "Cfg/Helpers.cs" and "Cfg_Helpers.cs" mint the same file stem.
cat > Cfg/Helpers.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo { public partial class Cfg { public void Alpha() { } } }
EOF
cat > Cfg_Helpers.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo { public partial class Cfg { public void Beta() { } } }
EOF
cat > generated/Cfg.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo { public partial class Cfg { public void Gamma() { Alpha(); Beta(); } } }
EOF

# Case 2: "Spec.cs" and "_Spec.cs" mint the same file stem.
cat > Spec.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo { public partial class Spec { public int Size; } }
EOF
cat > _Spec.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo { public class _Spec : Spec { public void Extra() { Move(); } } }
EOF
cat > generated/Spec.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo { public partial class Spec { public void Move() { } public void Copy() { } } }
EOF

graphify update .

python - <<'EOF'
import json
g = json.load(open("graphify-out/graph.json", encoding="utf-8"))
edges = g.get("links") or g.get("edges")
nodes = {n["id"]: n for n in g["nodes"]}
owned = {}
for e in edges:
    if e["relation"] == "method":
        owned.setdefault(e["source"], []).append(nodes[e["target"]]["label"])
for label in ("Cfg", "Spec", "_Spec"):
    halves = [sorted(owned.get(n["id"], [])) for n in g["nodes"] if n["label"] == label]
    print(f"{label:6} {len(halves)} node(s) {halves}")
has_owner = {e["target"] for e in edges if e["relation"] == "method"}
print("methods without owner:", sorted(n["label"] for n in g["nodes"]
      if n["label"].endswith("()") and n["id"] not in has_owner))
EOF
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Cfg    2 node(s) [['.Alpha()'], ['.Beta()']]
Spec   1 node(s) [[]]
_Spec  1 node(s) [['.Extra()']]
methods without owner: ['.Copy()', '.Gamma()', '.Move()']


No warning is printed; the build exits 0.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.88

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

pip

### Additional Environment Details

Windows 11. graphifyy 0.9.88 from PyPI, installed with `uv pip install` into a fresh virtual environment with
Python 3.13.14. Same output with Python 3.14.6.

### Additional context

Running the disambiguation before the merge fixes all three symptoms in the repro: every edge is still on its own
half when the colliding ids are salted, and the merge then joins the halves by type path, whatever their ids are.
A PR with this change and regression tests follows.

This issue does not change how ids are minted. The underlying normalization (leading underscore dropped, separator
and underscore equal) is the same that #3302 and #2810 describe for other languages.

title: fix(csharp): salt colliding ids before the partial merge, so a half keeps its members (#4411)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4411.

In `extract()`, `_merge_csharp_partial_class_nodes` ran before `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids`. When a partial
type's id collides with a type in another file (two files with the same stem: `Spec.cs` / `_Spec.cs`,
`Cfg/Helpers.cs` / `Cfg_Helpers.cs`), the merge rewired the edges of every half onto the canonical half's id while
that id was still ambiguous. The disambiguation remaps endpoints by `(id, source_file of the edge)`; for edges that
came from another half that key does not exist, so they stayed on an id no node had afterwards. The half's members
lost their owner, its file lost its `contains` edge, and when both colliding files declared a half of the same type,
the type stayed two nodes. And because the merge removes merged-away halves by id, an unrelated node in another file
that shared a half's id was removed with it (in the new test, a method `Helpers.App.Cfg()` next to a half of
`App.Cfg`; its `calls` edge moved onto the type).

This PR swaps the two calls (`graphify/extract.py`), so ids are salted apart while every edge still sits on its own
half, and the merge then joins the halves by type path (#4364), whatever their ids are. The merge's docstring and
`ARCHITECTURE.md` state the new order. No other code changes. Four regression tests; the test module's docstring
now names the type-path key that #4364 introduced.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** after the merge, every edge of every half of a C# partial type ends on a live node, and the halves
of one type in one assembly are one node, also when the type's id collides with a node in another file.

**Why the order is safe:** the disambiguation renames only ids that two or more source files share. Halves of a
partial type are in different files, so before this PR they either had distinct ids (unchanged by the
disambiguation) or the colliding case that this PR fixes. The merge groups by `metadata.type_path`, not by id, and
maps node ids to files through the same node dicts the disambiguation renamed in place, so its assembly probe sees
the new ids. Without a collision, the ids, and therefore the merge, are the same as before.

**Persisted state:** none. No node metadata, id or cache format changes; no schema bump.

**Determinism:** the salt is a function of the path; the canonical half is still chosen by (source file, location,
id).

**Effect on a real corpus.** A proprietary C# corpus of eight graphs, each built twice from the same source tree:
graphifyy 0.9.88 from PyPI, and the same files with this change. Compared is graphify's own output. Unit: an edge
pair, i.e. (source file, label) of both ends, deduplicated, per relation.

* One graph has 5 colliding file groups (1 leading underscore, 4 directory separator vs. underscore). There:
  * C# methods without a `method` edge: 60 -> 0.
  * `method` +96 / -36, `contains` +37 / -1, `references` +470 / -468, `defines` +3 / -0, `calls` +20 / -0.
  * Every lost pair (36 + 1 + 468) is the same edge with the same other end, now on the merged type node instead of
    one of the split halves. No other pair is lost.
  * The 20 new `calls` pairs go into members of the previously split types; 1 checked against the source line
    (`new X()` on that line).
* The other seven graphs have no colliding group. Their C# nodes and pairs are identical in both builds. Two
  differences there do not come from this change:
  * 8 `.sql` file nodes appear only in the branch build, because my branch environment has the optional SQL
    grammar installed (`uv sync --all-extras`) and the PyPI install does not.
  * 3 `calls` pairs differ in one HTML file. That file's output also differs between two builds of 0.9.88 from
    PyPI (19 pairs).

## Limitations

* This PR does not change how ids are minted. Two files still collide on their stem, and their nodes keep the
  path-salted ids they had before (#3302 and #2810 describe the normalization for other languages).
* `_merge_swift_extensions` also runs before the disambiguation. I did not examine whether Swift extensions have the

title: [Bug]: Ollama ignores graphify's context size, so docs come back empty
body:
## What's happening

I tried `graphify extract --backend ollama` with qwen2.5:14b on a few docs, and none of them made it into the graph. Every try, the model wrote a plain summary of the docs instead of JSON, and graphify gave up after 3 retries.

graphify works out a context size for each chunk and sends it to Ollama as `num_ctx`. But it sends it to Ollama's `/v1` address, and that address ignores it. So Ollama just uses its own default, which is 4096 on my machine, and cuts off the rest of the prompt. That cuts off the part asking for JSON, so the model answers in plain text.

You can see it in graphify's own output. It says `tokens: 4,096 in` even though the docs were a lot bigger than that.

## How to see it for yourself

This sends the same long prompt with `num_ctx` set to 20000, once to `/v1` like graphify does and once to Ollama's own `/api/chat`:

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, urllib.request
long = "word " * 12000
def post(path, body):
    r = urllib.request.Request("http://localhost:11434" + path, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(r))
m = "qwen2.5:14b"
a = post("/v1/chat/completions", {"model": m, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": long}], "max_tokens": 10, "options": {"num_ctx": 20000}})
print("/v1:", a["usage"]["prompt_tokens"])
b = post("/api/chat", {"model": m, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": long}], "stream": False, "options": {"num_ctx": 20000, "num_predict": 10}})
print("/api/chat:", b["prompt_eval_count"])
EOF
```

I got `/v1: 4096` and `/api/chat: 12030`.

## Proof it's the cause

Same 2 docs (requests' README and quickstart, about 5.5k tokens), same model. The only change was making a copy of the model with the bigger context built in (`PARAMETER num_ctx 12288` in a Modelfile):

- normal qwen2.5:14b: cut to 4,096 tokens, plain text back 3 times, empty graph after about 12 minutes
- copy with 12k context: all 6,316 tokens read, proper JSON first try, done in 3 minutes

## What should happen

The context size graphify works out should actually reach Ollama, so chunks bigger than Ollama's default don't get cut off.

Also, when this happens the message says it's usually "a rate limit, a transport hiccup, a refusal, or a model that answered in prose". That sent me looking in the wrong places. If the tokens in are exactly Ollama's context size, it would help to say the prompt was probably cut off.

Related: #3982 saw part of this. They asked for 14000 and got their server's 11000.

---

**Version:** graphify 0.9.87 · Ollama 0.17.5 · macOS 26.4.1 · Python 3.14

title: fix: send ollama requests to /api/chat so the context size is used
body:
Fixes #4413.

## What this fixes

graphify works out a context size for each Ollama request, but it sends it to Ollama's `/v1` address, which ignores it. So Ollama cut every prompt at its default (4096 for me), the model lost the part asking for JSON, and docs came back empty.

## What changed

- Ollama requests now go to Ollama's own `/api/chat`, which actually uses the context size. Same for the output limit, seed and the disable thinking setting.
- This covers both places graphify talks to Ollama: reading files and naming communities.
- If a server doesn't have `/api/chat` (like LM Studio or llama.cpp behind the ollama backend), graphify says so once and goes back to `/v1` like before.
- If you set your own `extra_body` in `providers.json`, nothing changes, it still goes through `/v1`.
- Timeouts and retries work the same, it uses the same client as before.

## How I tested it

With my local qwen2.5:14b, nothing else changed:

- reading the same 2 docs: before, cut at 4,096 tokens and an empty graph after about 12 minutes. After, all 6,316 tokens read, JSON first try, about 4 minutes.
- naming communities on rich (312 communities): before, the first batch was cut at 4,096 tokens and it took 8 requests. After, the full 7,468 tokens went through and it took 4 requests. All communities got names both times, the old code just needed extra retries to get there.

I also checked against my real Ollama:
- a server with only `/v1` is tried once, then graphify sticks to `/v1`
- a model that doesn't exist still gives a clear "not found" error
- disable thinking works on qwen2.5 and qwen3.5
- works with openai 1.x and 3.x

Tests:
- added tests for all of the above. They fail on current `v8` and pass with this change, apart from the ones checking that other setups aren't affected
- updated the existing Ollama tests to check the `/api/chat` request instead of the `/v1` one
- full test suite passes

## Heads up

graphify's 30 min keep alive now actually reaches Ollama too. Before it was ignored and Ollama's own setting applied, so now the model unloads after 30 min idle unless you set `GRAPHIFY_OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE`.

title: [Bug]: C#: names that differ only by a leading underscore or by case collapse (`Action()` / `_Action()`, `Pair` / `_Pair`), and `this.Put()` binds to `_Put()`
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`ids.py:make_id` strips leading and trailing underscores from every id part and casefolds. In C#, `_Name` is the
usual spelling of a private member, and the language is case-sensitive. Two things go wrong.

**1. Declarations in one file collapse.** In one type, `Action()` and `_Action()`, `Size` and `_Size`, or `Load()`
and `load()` mint the same id; so do the types `Pair` and `_Pair` in one namespace. `add_node` keeps the first
declaration and drops the second:

* The dropped method is missing from the graph. Its calls are credited to the survivor, so `_Action()` calling
  `Action()` becomes a self-loop on `Action()`.
* A dropped type's members hang off the other type (`_Pair.Stop()` is listed as a member of `Pair`).
* A dropped property or enum member is missing; the existing comment on the enum member branch already names the
  case-only collision (`enum E { Value, value }`).

This is the collision of #3302 in C#. The fix for #3302 (v0.9.55) is scoped to Python.

**2. The C# member-call resolver ignores `_` and case.** `_resolve_csharp_member_calls` keys method and type names
with `_key()`, which keeps only `[a-zA-Z0-9]` and lowercases. `Put` and `_Put` are one key, so `this.Put()` in a
class whose nearer base declares `_Put()` binds to `_Put()` (EXTRACTED), not to `Put()` further up. Type names
are keyed the same way, so `Token` and `TOKEN`, or `Spec` and `_Spec`, are one key: a receiver declared as one of
them can be typed as the other.

**Expected:**

```text
Host   1 node(s) [['.Action()', '.Load()', '._Action()', '.load()', 'Size', '_Size']]
Pair   1 node(s) [['.Go()']]
_Pair  1 node(s) [['.Stop()']]
calls: Host._Action() -> Host.Action()
calls: Record.Save() -> BaseStore.Put()
```

**Scale.** A proprietary C# corpus of eight graphs, built twice from the same source tree: graphifyy 0.9.89 from
PyPI, and the same files with a fix for both points (PR follows). Compared is graphify's own output, no
post-processing.

* Declarations dropped by 0.9.89: 224 (189 methods, 33 properties, 2 types), in all eight graphs. Unit: a
  (source file, label) pair of a C# node, deduplicated, present with the fix and absent in 0.9.89. 197 of them
  differ from their survivor by an underscore, 27 only by case.
* `calls` edges whose target name is not called on the edge's source line, while a name that differs only by a
  leading or trailing underscore is: 319, in four of the eight graphs (source line read for every edge). Some of
  them exist because the method actually called had been dropped (point 1), the others come from the resolver key
  (point 2). With the fix: 0.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir -p underscore-collide && cd underscore-collide

cat > Demo.csproj <<'EOF'
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup><TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework></PropertyGroup>
</Project>
EOF

# Case 1: names that differ only by a leading underscore or by case, in one file.
cat > Host.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo
{
    public class Host
    {
        public bool Action() { return true; }
        private bool _Action() { return Action(); }
        public int Size { get; set; }
        private int _Size { get; set; }
        public void Load() { }
        public void load() { }
    }
    public class Pair { public void Go() { } }
    public class _Pair { public void Stop() { } }
}
EOF

# Case 2: a member call binds to an underscore sibling on a nearer base class.
cat > Records.cs <<'EOF'
namespace Demo
{
    public class BaseStore
    {
        public virtual bool Put(string name, object value) { return true; }
    }
    public class CachedStore : BaseStore
    {
        protected bool _Put(string name, object value) { return true; }
    }
    public class Record : CachedStore
    {
        public void Save() { this.Put("A", 1); }
    }
}
EOF

graphify update .

python - <<'EOF'
import json
g = json.load(open("graphify-out/graph.json", encoding="utf-8"))
edges = g.get("links") or g.get("edges")
nodes = {n["id"]: n for n in g["nodes"]}
members, owner = {}, {}
for e in edges:
    if e["relation"] in ("method", "defines"):
        members.setdefault(e["source"], []).append(nodes[e["target"]]["label"])
        owner[e["target"]] = nodes[e["source"]]["label"]
for label in ("Host", "Pair", "_Pair"):
    found = [sorted(members.get(n["id"], [])) for n in g["nodes"] if n["label"] == label]
    print(f"{label:6} {len(found)} node(s) {found}")
for e in edges:
    if e["relation"] == "calls" and nodes[e["source"]]["label"] in (".Save()", ".Action()", "._Action()"):
        s, t = e["source"], e["target"]
        print(f"calls: {owner.get(s)}{nodes[s]['label']} -> {owner.get(t)}{nodes[t]['label']}")
EOF
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Host   1 node(s) [['.Action()', '.Load()', 'Size']]
Pair   1 node(s) [['.Go()', '.Stop()']]
_Pair  0 node(s) []
calls: Host.Action() -> Host.Action()
calls: Record.Save() -> CachedStore._Put()


No warning is printed; the build exits 0.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.89

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

pip

### Additional Environment Details

Windows 11. graphifyy 0.9.89 from PyPI, installed with `uv pip install` into a fresh virtual environment with
Python 3.13.14.

### Additional context

A PR follows. For point 1 it applies the rule of #3302 to C#: a pre-scan groups the declared names of a file that
share an id; when exactly one name of a group has no leading underscore, it keeps the plain id, and every other name
gets an id salted with a hash of the name. For point 2 the resolver key keeps `_` and case.

Related, as of today:

* #3302 (Python) is fixed in v0.9.55; that fix is scoped to Python.
* #2810 (open) describes same-file collisions for JS/TS/Python.
* PR #3322 (open since 2026-09-03, in no release) adds a generic census for same-file collisions in the shared
  engine. It covers C# methods and types, but not C# properties, and not the member-call resolver key (point 2).

This issue is independent of #4411: that one is about two files whose stems collide, this one about names inside
one file and about the resolver key.

title: fix(csharp): keep names that differ only by _ or case apart, in ids and in member-call keys (#4415)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4415.

Two C# defects with one root: `ids.py:make_id` strips leading/trailing underscores and casefolds, while C# is
case-sensitive and spells private members `_Name`.

**1. Declarations in one file collapsed** (`graphify/extractors/engine.py`). `Action()` / `_Action()`, `Size` /
`_Size`, `Load()` / `load()` in one type, and `Pair` / `_Pair` in one namespace, minted one id; `add_node` kept the
first declaration and dropped the second, and the dropped method's calls were credited to the survivor. This PR
applies the rule of #3302 (Python, v0.9.55) to C#:

* A new pre-scan, `_csharp_pre_scan_name_collisions`, groups the declared names of a file that would share an id:
  types (class, struct, interface, record, enum), and per type its methods, properties and enum members. Types are
  keyed exactly as the walk mints them (namespace, arity, #4249); members under the type's final id, so the members
  of a salted type are grouped under the salted id. It enters only namespace and type bodies and `#if` wrappers,
  so its recursion depth is the nesting depth of declarations.
* The existing `_python_underscore_salted_nid` is renamed to `_underscore_salted_nid` and used for both languages,
  unchanged: when exactly one name of a group has no leading underscore, it keeps the plain id; every other name
  gets `sha1(name)[:6]` appended. A type, method, property or enum member without a colliding sibling keeps its
  id exactly, and the result does not depend on declaration order.
* In-file type references go through the same rule (`ensure_named_node` and the `base_list` lookup), so
  `class Z : _Pair` in the same file reaches `_Pair`, not `Pair`.
* The arity fold of #4249 moves into a helper, `_csharp_type_name_for_id`, shared by the walk and the pre-scan.

**2. The member-call resolver ignored `_` and case** (`graphify/extract.py`). `_resolve_csharp_member_calls`
keyed names with `[^a-zA-Z0-9]` removed and lowercased, so `this.Put()` bound to `_Put()` on a nearer base class,
and type names such as `Token` / `TOKEN` or `Spec` / `_Spec` were one key. The key now removes only
non-word characters (the label decoration of `.Put()`), keeping `_` and case.

Two existing tests asserted the old first-wins result for a case-only pair (`enum Odd { Value, value }`, properties
`Count` / `count`); they now assert one node and one edge per member.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** in a C# file, two declarations with different names never share a node id because of `_` or case;
a declaration with no such sibling keeps the id it had before. A C# member call binds only to a method whose name
equals the called name.

**Persisted state:** node ids change only for C# declarations that have a colliding sibling in the same file
(salted, as for Python since #3302). No node metadata or cache format change. I did not bump `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA`:
the AST cache is namespaced by package version, so a release re-extracts anyway; say if you want the bump in this PR.

**Determinism:** the salt is a function of the declared name; the group a name falls in does not depend on the
order of declarations.

**Effect on a real corpus.** A proprietary C# corpus of eight graphs, each built twice from the same source tree:
graphifyy 0.9.89 from PyPI, and the same files with this change. Compared is graphify's own output (`graphify
extract`), no post-processing. Unit, unless stated otherwise: a pair of (source file, label) of both ends of an edge,
deduplicated, per relation.

* C# nodes: none lost in any graph; 224 new (189 methods, 33 properties, 2 types), in all eight graphs. 197 differ
  from their former survivor by an underscore, 27 only by case.
* `calls` edges whose target name is not called on the edge's source line, while a name that differs only by a
  leading or trailing underscore is (source line read for every edge): 319 -> 0, in four of the eight graphs.
* Lost pairs, all classified: `calls` 1029, `references` 115, `method` 2, `contains` 1.
  * 784 (669 `calls`, 115 `references`): the same edge, now starting at the restored sibling, i.e. the edge comes
    from the body of `_X()`, which 0.9.89 had merged into `X()`. 5 sampled by hand: in each, the call line is
    below the declaration of `_X()`.
  * 340 (337 `calls`, 2 `method`, 1 `contains`): the same edge, now ending at the sibling with the same name up to
    `_` / case (the method actually called, or the restored declaration).
  * 23 `calls`, each checked against its source line. 22 were wrong in 0.9.89 and are gone: the target's name
    differs from the called name only by underscores (e.g. `x.Run()` bound to `_Run()`, `this.Re_Do()` bound to
    `__ReDo()`), or a bare call such as `_Hide()` bound to another class's method of that name because the
    caller's own `_Hide()` had been dropped, or the receiver was typed through a collapsed type key (a parameter
    of type `TOKEN` typed as the class `Token`; a field of type `Spec` left untyped because `Spec` and `_Spec` were
    one key, after which the field's own name matched an unrelated type). 1 is a call between two methods that
    call each other: with `_X()` restored they are one node pair, and `graph.json` keeps one edge per pair.
* New pairs: `calls` +1344, `references` +282, `method` +189, `defines` +35, `dispatches_to` +2, `contains` +1.
* Not from this change: 8 `.sql` file nodes appear only in the branch build (my branch environment has the optional
  SQL grammar from `uv sync --all-extras`, the PyPI install does not), and one HTML file whose output also varies
  between two builds of the same version.

## Limitations

* Fields are still not nodes (#3006); this PR does not change that.
* The Swift, Python, TypeScript, C++ and Objective-C member-call resolvers define the same `_key()`. I changed only
  the C# one.
* `_csharp_receiver_type_name` accepts only type names that start with an upper-case letter, so a receiver of type
  `_Pair` is never typed. Not changed here.
* Nested type ids omit the enclosing type (as before); the pre-scan follows that, so `Host.Item` and `_Item` nested
  in another type of the same file form one group and are salted apart. Two nested types with the SAME name under
  different outers still share an id, as before. PR #4287 (open, in no release) prefixes nested type ids with the
  enclosing type; if it lands, the pre-scan's key for nested types has to follow (`_visit` passes the namespace
  only). If the two keys ever diverge, a nested type's collision is only missed (no salt), never salted wrongly.
* PR #3322 (open, in no release) adds a generic census for same-file collisions in the shared engine. If it lands,
  the C# pre-scan here overlaps with it for methods and types; it does not cover C# properties, enum members or the
  resolver key.

## How was this tested?

```text
$ uv run pytest tests/test_csharp_underscore_collisions.py tests/test_csharp_enum_members.py tests/test_csharp_member_nodes.py tests/test_python_underscore_resolution.py -q
  47 passed

$ uv run pytest tests/test_csharp_underscore_collisions.py tests/test_csharp_enum_members.py tests/test_csharp_member_nodes.py -q   # with graphify/ from v8
  18 failed, 20 passed  (16 of the 17 new tests, and the 2 changed ones; the overload test passes on v8 by design)

$ uv run pytest tests                                      # this branch and v8 (e8eb76e), same machine
  this branch: 7 failed, 7860 passed, 73 skipped
  v8:          7 failed, 7844 passed, 73 skipped
  The same 7 fail on both (Windows-specific):
    test_language_override_lifecycle.py::test_watch_relative_roots_receive_config_events_without_rebasing_source_paths[src]
    test_non_regular_files.py::test_char_device_is_rejected
    test_resolve_memoization.py::test_absolute_path_lookup_skips_getcwd
    test_skillgen_input_path_injection.py::test_step1_still_resolves_a_legitimate_path (3 parameters)
    test_source_key_memoization.py::test_absolute_path_lookup_skips_getcwd

$ uv run --isolated --no-project --python 3.10 --with-editable . --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_csharp_underscore_collisions.py tests/test_csharp_enum_members.py tests/test_csharp_member_nodes.py tests/test_python_underscore_resolution.py -q
  47 passed

$ uv run ruff check .
  All checks passed!

$ uv run pyright
  964 errors on v8 and on this branch; no new findings

$ git diff --check
  clean
```

Pair   1 node(s) [['.Go()']]

title: feat(mimo): add Xiaomi MiMo Code agent integration
body:
## Summary
Adds support for **Xiaomi MiMo Code** (`graphify mimo install|uninstall|status [--project]`), enabling the AI assistant to inspect the codebase knowledge graph and inject focused graph context prior to responses.

## Key Changes
- **CLI Commands**: Added `mimo` dispatcher supporting `install`, `uninstall`, and `status` with both global and `--project` scoping.
- **Skill & Instructions**:
  - Configures skill destinations (`.mimocode/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` or global config directory).
  - Wires persistent graph guidance into `AGENTS.md`.
- **Plugin Hook**:
  - Drops `.mimocode/plugins/graphify.js` handling `chat.message` and `tool.execute.before`.
  - Securely queries `graphify-out/graph.json` with budget caps and timeouts.
- **Security & Reliability Hardening**:
  - **Safe Binary Resolution**: Validates executable paths against absolute locations outside the workspace directory to prevent untrusted execution.
  - **Surgical JSONC Preserving**: Properly handles trailing comments in `mimocode.jsonc` without appending commas inside comments.
  - **Strict Validation**: Validates `plugin` value types explicitly rather than silently overwriting unexpected structures.
- **Tests**:
  - Added dedicated test suite in `tests/test_mimo_install.py` covering skill routing, JSONC comment handling, type rejection, and lifecycle flows.

## Verification
- [x] Ran `pytest tests/test_mimo_install.py -v` (All 4 tests passed)

title: [Bug]: C#: a member call on a chained or invoked receiver binds to the caller's own same-named method
body:
### What happened?

A C# member call whose receiver has no capturable name binds to the **caller's own same-named method** as an `EXTRACTED` `calls` edge. This covers a member chain (`run.Sequence.Apply()`, `s.Items.Count()`), an invocation (`Pick().look.LateUpdate()`) and a `new X(...).M()`. The receiver's type is ignored.

In `extractors/engine.py`, the C# defer rule is:

```python
_csharp_defer = (
    config.ts_module == "tree_sitter_c_sharp"
    and is_member_call and member_receiver
)
```

It only fires when `member_receiver` was captured. That happens for a plain identifier, `this`, `base`, `this.field` or a cast. For every other receiver shape, the call falls through to `label_to_nid.get(callee_name)`, the per-file bare-name map, and lands on whatever method in the file shares the name. For a typed chain this happens even though `receiver_chain` (#4246) was computed and would have resolved it correctly.

Expected: no edge from the bare-name map for a C# member call. A typed chain should resolve through `receiver_chain`, and anything untypable should get no edge (fail-closed, as #1609 intended).

This is the C# twin of #4082 (TypeScript).

### Steps to reproduce

```python
import os, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract

os.chdir(tempfile.mkdtemp())
Path("Model.cs").write_text(
    "namespace Demo {\n"
    "    public class Sequence { public void Apply() { } }\n"
    "    public class Run { public Sequence Sequence; }\n"
    "}\n")
Path("Controller.cs").write_text(
    "namespace Demo {\n"
    "    public class Controller {\n"
    "        public void Apply() { }\n"
    "        public void Tick(Run run) { run.Sequence.Apply(); }\n"
    "        public void LateUpdate() { Pick().look.LateUpdate(); }\n"
    "        object Pick() { return null; }\n"
    "    }\n"
    "}\n")
r = extract([Path("Model.cs"), Path("Controller.cs")], cache_root=Path(".cache"))
label = {n["id"]: n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]}
for e in r["edges"]:
    if e["relation"] == "calls":
        print(label[e["source"]], "->", label[e["target"]], f"({e['target']})", e["confidence"])
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
.Tick() -> .Apply() (controller_demo_controller_apply) EXTRACTED          <- wrong class: should be Sequence.Apply
.LateUpdate() -> .LateUpdate() (controller_demo_controller_lateupdate) EXTRACTED   <- false self-loop
.LateUpdate() -> .Pick() (controller_demo_controller_pick) EXTRACTED
```

On a 1,512-file Unity C# codebase (game code plus vendored UniTask, LeanTween and MsgPack), 309 of the 516 `calls` self-loops came from this path. Typical cases:
- LINQ `s.cats.Count(...)` bound to a local `Count()`;
- `transform.gameObject.SetActive(...)` bound to a local `SetActive()`;
- `anim.Play(...)` bound to a local `Play()`.

### Graphify version

0.9.89 (v8 `e8eb76e`)

### Operating System

Windows (11)

### Python Version

3.14

### Installation Method

uv / pip (`graphifyy`)

title: [Bug]: C#: `new X()` binds to a method named X, and `new Outer.X()` is guessed by path proximity
body:
### What happened?

A C# `new X(...)` is resolved against every definition named `X`, **methods included**, so a construction can bind to a method that merely shares the type's name:

- **Same file:** inside `static Bounds Bounds(int a) => new Bounds(a);`, where `Bounds` is Unity's type and outside the corpus, the construction becomes an `EXTRACTED` self-loop on the `Bounds()` helper.
- **Across files:** `new List<int>()` binds to an unrelated `Market.List()` method as an `INFERRED` edge. On a real codebase this turns one `List()` method into a hub with a false caller for every `new List<T>()` in the corpus. The cross-file pass already excludes enum members and fields/properties for `csharp_new` (#3815, #4245), but not methods.

A related guess appears once those method candidates are gone. A **qualified nested construction** `new QuickSlotsBar.Slot()`, with several bare-name `Slot` classes in the corpus, goes to `disambiguate_ambiguous_candidates`. Its path-proximity tie-break ignores the qualifier and picks the `Slot` next to the caller. `_resolve_csharp_qualified_calls` (#2997) only handles namespace qualifiers, so a type qualifier is never consulted. Before, a same-named method candidate often made the tie unresolvable, which hid the guess.

Expected: `new X()` never binds to a method. A qualified nested construction takes the candidate nested in the named outer type, or gets no edge.

### Steps to reproduce

```python
import os, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract

os.chdir(tempfile.mkdtemp())
Path("Market.cs").write_text(
    "namespace Demo { public class Market { public static int List(int a) { return a; } } }\n")
Path("Use.cs").write_text(
    "namespace Demo { public class Use { public void Run() { var xs = new List<int>(); } } }\n")
Path("Box.cs").write_text(
    "namespace Demo { public class Box { static Bounds Bounds(int a) { return new Bounds(a); } } }\n")
r = extract([Path("Market.cs"), Path("Use.cs"), Path("Box.cs")], cache_root=Path(".cache"))
label = {n["id"]: n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]}
for e in r["edges"]:
    if e["relation"] == "calls":
        print(label[e["source"]], "->", label[e["target"]], f"({e['target']})", e["confidence"])
```

The qualified case:

```python
import os, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract

os.chdir(tempfile.mkdtemp())
for d in ("UI", "Editor"):
    Path(d).mkdir()
Path("UI/Bar.cs").write_text(
    "namespace Game.UI { public class QuickSlotsBar { public class Slot { public int kind; } } }\n")
Path("Editor/Towers.cs").write_text(
    "namespace Game.Tools { public class Towers { class Slot { public string texture; } } }\n")
Path("Editor/Hud.cs").write_text(
    "using Game.UI;\n"
    "namespace Game.Tools { public class Hud {"
    " public void Ensure() { var s = new QuickSlotsBar.Slot { kind = 1 }; } } }\n")
files = [Path("UI/Bar.cs"), Path("Editor/Towers.cs"), Path("Editor/Hud.cs")]
r = extract(files, cache_root=Path(".cache"))
node = {n["id"]: n for n in r["nodes"]}
for e in r["edges"]:
    if e["relation"] == "calls":
        t = node[e["target"]]
        print(node[e["source"]]["label"], "->", t["label"], "in", t.get("source_file"), e["confidence"])
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
.Bounds() -> .Bounds() (box_demo_box_bounds) EXTRACTED      <- self-loop: `new Bounds(..)` is not a call to the helper
.Run() -> .List() (market_demo_market_list) INFERRED        <- `new List<int>()` is not Market.List()

.Ensure() -> Slot in Editor/Towers.cs INFERRED              <- source says QuickSlotsBar.Slot (UI/Bar.cs)
```

On a 1,512-file Unity C# codebase, 156 false `calls` edges came from this. Examples:
- Unity's `new WaitForSeconds()` bound to UniTask's `WaitForSeconds()` method (41 callers);
- `new Rect()` bound to a `Rect()` UI helper (23 callers);
- `new Stack<T>()` bound to a `Stack()` method.

### Graphify version

0.9.89 (v8 `e8eb76e`)

### Operating System

Windows (11)

### Python Version

3.14

### Installation Method

uv / pip (`graphifyy`)

title: [Feature]: C#: type `foreach` loop variables for receiver resolution
body:
### Problem

A C# `foreach` loop variable gets no binding in the method-scoped receiver table (`_csharp_method_receiver_types`), so a call on it, or a chain starting at it, never resolves across files:

```csharp
foreach (var a in agents.Values) a.look.Animate();   // agents: Dictionary<string, Agent>
foreach (var a in list) a.Step();                     // list: List<Agent>
foreach (Agent a in xs) a.Step();                     // even an explicitly typed loop variable
```

All three produce no `calls` edge when `Agent` and `Look` live in another file. In Unity code this is the usual shape for per-frame work (`foreach (var a in agents.Values) a.look.LateUpdate();`), so the calls that matter most for performance questions are missing from the graph.

### Reproduction

```python
import os, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract

os.chdir(tempfile.mkdtemp())
Path("Model.cs").write_text(
    "namespace Demo {\n"
    "    public class Look { public void Animate() { } }\n"
    "    public class Agent { public Look look; public void Step() { } }\n"
    "}\n")
Path("Crowd.cs").write_text(
    "using System.Collections.Generic;\n"
    "namespace Demo {\n"
    "    public class Crowd {\n"
    "        readonly Dictionary<string, Agent> agents = new Dictionary<string, Agent>();\n"
    "        readonly List<Agent> list = new List<Agent>();\n"
    "        public void Tick() { foreach (var a in agents.Values) a.look.Animate(); }\n"
    "        public void Walk() { foreach (var a in list) a.Step(); }\n"
    "        public void Typed(IEnumerable<object> xs) { foreach (Agent a in xs) a.Step(); }\n"
    "    }\n"
    "}\n")
r = extract([Path("Model.cs"), Path("Crowd.cs")], cache_root=Path(".cache"))
label = {n["id"]: n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]}
calls = [(label[e["source"]], label[e["target"]]) for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "calls"]
print("calls from Crowd:", [c for c in calls if c[0] in (".Tick()", ".Walk()", ".Typed()")])
```

```text
calls from Crowd: []
```

### Proposed behavior

Bind the loop variable inside its loop:
- to its explicit type (`foreach (Agent a in ...)`);
- for `var`, to what the iterated class field or property yields: the element of a `T[]` or a sequence type (`List<T>`, `IEnumerable<T>`, `HashSet<T>`...), and a dictionary's value or key type for `f.Values` / `f.Keys`.

Stay untyped (no guess) for:
- iterating a dictionary itself (`KeyValuePair`);
- nested collections and type parameters;
- a loop over a name that a local or parameter shadows.

### Alternatives

Typing the iterated expression in general (locals, method return types, chains such as `s.modules`) would cover more loops. This proposal keeps to fields and properties, where the declared type is already recorded per class, and leaves the rest untyped.

### Compatibility

Additive: the change only creates `calls` edges that are missing today, and in the patch it adds no edges anywhere else. On a 1,512-file Unity C# codebase, it added 58 `calls` edges and removed none.

Graphify 0.9.89 (v8 `e8eb76e`), Windows 11, Python 3.14.

title: fix(csharp): never bind a nameless member-call receiver to a same-named method in the file
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4418.

A C# member call whose receiver has no capturable name reached the per-file bare-name map, because the C# defer rule required `member_receiver`. This covers a member chain (`run.Sequence.Apply()`, `s.Items.Count()`), an invocation (`Pick().look.LateUpdate()`) and a `new X(...).M()`. The call then bound to the caller's own same-named method as an `EXTRACTED` edge:
- a false self-loop;
- LINQ `Count()` bound to a local `Count()`;
- a typed chain landing on the wrong class instead of reaching the `receiver_chain` resolution from #4246.

Changes:
- `_csharp_defer` now covers every C# member call, so no member call uses the bare-name map. A typed chain still resolves through `receiver_chain`, and anything untypable gets no edge (fail-closed, the intent of #1609).
- `new X(...).M()` (#1770) used to get its edge from that same bare-name fallback. Its receiver is now typed from the construction (`receiver_chain = [X]`), so `test_method_chained_off_new_expression_resolves` keeps passing for the right reason.

title: feat(csharp): type `foreach` loop variables for receiver resolution
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4420.

A C# `foreach` loop variable had no binding in `_csharp_method_receiver_types`, so a call on it, or a chain starting at it, never resolved across files. For example, `foreach (var a in agents.Values) a.look.Animate();` produced no edge.

Changes:
- **Binding the loop variable.** It is bound inside its loop (the `foreach_statement` range):
  - to its explicit type (`foreach (Agent a in xs)`);
  - for `var`, to what the iterated class field or property yields.
- **What a field or property yields.** This is recorded per class next to the existing `name[]` element entries (#4246), under `name{}`, `name.Values{}` and `name.Keys{}`:
  - the element of a `T[]` or a sequence type (`List`, `IList`, `IReadOnlyList`, `IEnumerable`, `ICollection`, `IReadOnlyCollection`, `HashSet`, `ISet`, `SortedSet`, `Queue`, `Stack`, `LinkedList`);
  - a dictionary's value or key type for `f.Values` / `f.Keys`.
- **Shadowing.** `var` loops are typed after the walk, once every local and parameter is bound. A loop over a name that a local or parameter shadows at that point stays untyped.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a loop variable is typed only from evidence written in source, never guessed. The evidence is its declared type or the declared type of the field or property it iterates. Everything else stays untyped, so the existing no-binding / no-edge behavior is unchanged there.

title: [Feature]: Step 5 labels: generate the community keys and check each label against its community
body:
### Problem or use case

Step 5 asks the agent to write the community labels as a dict literal by hand ("Replace `LABELS_DICT` with the actual dict you constructed"). Nothing checks that each label belongs to the community it is keyed to.

On a 210-community code graph, the hand-written `LABELS_DICT` skipped two communities near id 128, so every later label was shifted by two (for example, id 184 got the label meant for 186). It was caught only by re-reading the community listing.

A second shape on a content graph: labels inferred from community membership marked some communities as unaligned because none of their members was a skill node. Checked against the graph's actual edges, several of them were aligned to skills that had clustered elsewhere. A label is read as a finding, so a claim inside it needs the same check as any other claim.

### Proposed solution

In Step 5, have the agent print a per-community summary keyed by id, write labels as an id-to-label file, and then assert in code that the label keys equal the community keys.

For each label, spot-check that at least one word in it appears in that community's top node or file names. Any qualifier in a label ("unaligned", "tests", "deprecated") is derived from or checked against edges rather than inferred from membership.

Above roughly 50 communities, suggest labelling only the communities with at least N nodes and keeping "Community N" for the thin tail.

### Alternatives considered

PR #3618 (size-aware labeling) changes how many representative nodes the LLM labeling path in `graphify/llm.py` samples per community and how communities are batched; #2101 addresses mislabeling from truncated member lists. Neither checks that a hand-written Step 5 map's keys and values line up. PR #3609 preserves labels by membership across rebuilds, a different problem. #4309 covers shell injection through `LABELS_DICT`, and its open fix, PR #4344, already moves Step 5 labels into an id-keyed JSON file (`.graphify_labels_in.json`); it does not check that the keys equal the community keys or that each label fits its community. This request builds on that change.

### Area

Skills or assistant integrations

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

No, I just wanted to request it

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Instruction change to Step 5 in `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md` (the split skills, including `graphify/skill.md`, regenerate from it) and the same Step 5 instruction in the monolith fragments (`tools/skillgen/fragments/core/aider.md` line 514, `core/devin.md` line 579), whose Step 5 code blocks differ slightly from core.md, plus an optional key-equality assertion in each Step 5 code block. No API change.

### Additional context

Seen with graphifyy 0.9.73, the version installed on the day of both runs. Re-checked at upstream HEAD `e8eb76e` (2026-10-13): `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md` line 484 and the generated `graphify/skill.md` line 555 still say "Replace `LABELS_DICT` with the actual dict you constructed" (fetched with `gh api repos/Graphify-Labs/graphify/contents/<path>`).

title: [Feature]: Step 2: offer to exclude committed bundles that detect() does not already skip
body:
### Problem or use case

A single-file server bundle (a ~35k-line `.mjs` produced by a bundler and committed beside the source for deployment, outside any `dist/` or `build/` directory) went through AST extraction alongside the source it was built from. Every bundled function became a second node next to its source definition.

The result was about 15 mirror communities (for example, a bundle copy of a source community under a near-identical label), a duplicate god node (a database helper appeared twice, once from the bundle), and 49 collapsed import edges from the bundle into a single package in the health diagnostics. Nothing in Step 2 flagged the file, and once extracted, the duplicates read as real architecture.

### Proposed solution

After detection in Step 2, list code files that look like committed build output but sit outside the directories `detect()` already prunes: a `.min.` name, a bundler banner comment, or a single very large `.mjs`/`.cjs`/`.js` file. Offer to exclude them before extraction, and name the effect when offering: mirror communities and duplicate god nodes.

### Alternatives considered

`detect()` already drops `dist/`, `build/`, `target/` and similar directories by name, which does not cover a bundle committed elsewhere. #728 reports a bundled `cli.mjs` (a sourcemap/vendor artifact) that alone produced 1,341 isolated nodes, and suggests filtering synthetic files at extraction time; #3237 (class 3) asks for minified artifacts to be detected and skipped; #2479 is the opposite failure (real `build/` directories dropped). #728 and #3237 ask for automatic filtering in code, and #2479 asks for directory pruning to require evidence and be reported. This asks for a Step 2 check that shows the user a likely bundle and offers to exclude it, which also catches unminified bundles a heuristic might keep.

### Area

Skills or assistant integrations

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

No, I just wanted to request it

### Compatibility / behavior impact

An extra confirmation step in Step 2 (`tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md`, from line 66; the monolith fragments `core/aider.md` and `core/devin.md` carry their own Step 2) only when such files are present. No API change.

### Additional context

Seen with graphifyy 0.9.73: the graph had 7,627 nodes in 210 communities, of which about 15 communities came only from the bundle. Re-checked at upstream HEAD `e8eb76e`: Step 2's instructions have no check for bundled or minified files, and `detect.py` has no `.min.` rule and no size rule for code files (its only per-file size cap, 50 MiB, guards PDF and Office parsing).

title: [Feature]: Query flow: report code that reimplements a hub instead of calling it ("bypasses")
body:
### Problem or use case

A suggested question asked why a shared date utility bridges many communities. The graph answered the literal question well: the neighbour listing showed every consumer (82 edges), and the source confirmed each one wraps the helper.

The useful finding, though, in the checkout that was scanned, was two server modules that should have used the helper and did not: they reimplemented it with a hard-coded UTC offset. Those modules have no edge to the hub, so the hub's neighbour listing cannot show them, and nothing in the traversal output marks them as doing the hub's job. A text search for the reimplemented constant found them.

Separately, the helper had been clustered into the community of its heaviest consumer, so the community label named the consumer (a calendar component), which made the question read as if the component were the bridge.

### Proposed solution

In the query flow, for a bridge or god-node question: after listing consumers, grep for reimplementations of what the hub does (its literal constants, the API it wraps) in files that have no edge to it, and report them separately as "bypasses".

Also note in the answer that a shared utility's community label may name its biggest consumer rather than the utility itself.

### Alternatives considered

The closest existing issue is #1220 (a literal/identifier usage index, or a `graphify grep` that maps text hits to graph nodes), which would make the hard-coded constant findable from the graph. This request is narrower and needs no new index: a query-flow step that looks for reimplementations of a hub and reports them as bypasses. #1595 (missing client/server contract edges) and #2460 (false name-only edges) are related but different. For the label point, #2298 and #2542 cover adjacent community-labelling problems.

### Area

Skills or assistant integrations

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

No, I just wanted to request it

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Instruction change to the query flow in `tools/skillgen/fragments/references/query/default.md` (Step 1, Traversal), which regenerates into the split platforms' `references/query.md`; the aider and devin monolith skills carry their own query section in `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/aider.md` and `core/devin.md` and would need the same edit. No API or `graph.json` change.

### Additional context

Seen with graphifyy 0.9.73. Re-checked at upstream HEAD `e8eb76e`: the query flow has no step for finding code that duplicates a hub without an edge to it.

title: [Feature]: Step 1: warn when the input repo is behind its default branch, and pass built_at_commit into the skill's report
body:
### Problem or use case

`/graphify` was run on a git checkout that was behind its default branch (it was missing at least one merged PR). A follow-up trace reported two files as live bugs. When a fix was started from a fresh worktree of the default branch, one of the two had already been fixed there; the other was real. The graph described code that was no longer deployed, and graphify gave no sign that the checkout was behind.

`graph.json` already carries `built_at_commit`, and `report.generate()` renders a "Graph Freshness" section when it is given one, as `graphify update` does. But the skill's own `generate()` calls in Step 4 and Step 5 (`tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md` lines 394 and 470) do not pass it, so the `GRAPH_REPORT.md` from a `/graphify` build carries no commit.

### Proposed solution

In Step 1, when the input path is a git repository, print the current branch and how many commits HEAD is behind its upstream or the remote default branch (`git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/<default>`). If it is behind, warn and offer to scan a fresh worktree of the default branch instead.

In Steps 4 and 5, pass `built_at_commit` to `generate()` so the report states the commit the graph was built from, and label query findings with it, so a "this is live" claim can be checked against the deployed branch before it is reported.

### Alternatives considered

#2841 covers a stale or partially built `graphify-out/` (the output going stale). This is the input being behind when it is first scanned. #2008 is about locating the graph across worktrees. The MCP server's "graph may be stale" line covers a later HEAD move, not a checkout that was behind from the start.

### Area

Skills or assistant integrations

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

No, I just wanted to request it

### Compatibility / behavior impact

One extra git call and an optional prompt in Step 1 (`tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md` line 62, and the monolith fragments `core/aider.md` and `core/devin.md`) for git inputs only. Passing `built_at_commit` uses an existing parameter. No API change.

### Additional context

Seen with graphifyy 0.9.73. Re-checked at upstream HEAD `e8eb76e`: Step 1 installs graphify and does not check the input's revision, and the Step 4 and Step 5 `generate()` calls do not pass `built_at_commit`.

title: fix(csharp): `new X()` never binds to a method that shares X's name
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4419.

A C# `new X(...)` was resolved against every definition named `X`, methods included:
- **Same file:** `static Bounds Bounds(..) => new Bounds(..)` (Unity's `Bounds`, outside the corpus) became an `EXTRACTED` self-loop.
- **Across files:** the bare-name pass bound every `new List<T>()` to an unrelated `List()` method, minting an `INFERRED` hub.

Changes:
- **Same file (`engine.py`):** a construction whose bare-name target is a method (`tgt_nid in method_owner`) is deferred to the cross-file pass.
- **Cross file (`extract.py`):** for `csharp_new` calls, method candidates are dropped next to the existing enum-member and property exclusion (#3815, #4245). It reuses the lazily built `_csharp_method_owner` map. A real type with the same name still wins.
- **Qualified nested constructions:** dropping those candidates removes ties that used to hide a separate guess. With several bare-name `Slot` classes, `new QuickSlotsBar.Slot()` went to `disambiguate_ambiguous_candidates`, whose path proximity ignores the qualifier and picks the `Slot` next to the caller. A qualified construction now skips that tie-break. It takes the single candidate nested (`contains`) in a type named by the qualifier's last segment, or gets no edge. Namespace qualifiers stay with `_resolve_csharp_qualified_calls` (#2997).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariants:
- `new X()` constructs a type and never binds to a method.
- A qualified construction is resolved by its qualifier, never by path proximity over the bare name.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test**: 5 tests in `tests/test_csharp_object_creation.py`. All 5 fail on `v8` (`e8eb76e`) and pass here.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Limitations:**
- A qualified construction with exactly one bare-name candidate binds as before, even when that candidate is not nested in the named outer type.
- The outer-type match uses the qualifier's last segment only, so it does not check the outer type's own namespace.

On a 1,512-file Unity C# codebase, this branch alone changes the `calls` edges as follows:
- 156 removed and 72 added;
- self-loops go from 516 to 454.

Removed examples:
- Unity's `new WaitForSeconds()` bound to UniTask's `WaitForSeconds()` method (41 false callers);
- `new Rect()` bound to a `Rect()` UI helper (23);
- `new Stack<T>()`.

Added examples:
- `new SkipUntil<T>(..)` inside the `SkipUntil()` factory now reaching the class;
- `new QuickSlotsBar.Slot` reaching the right `Slot`.

The qualified constructions that were already right (`new FarmWaves.Entry(..)` and similar) are kept.

## How was this tested?

```text

uv run pytest tests -k "csharp or cs_ or dotnet or razor or unity"   # 442 passed, 13 skipped

uv run pyright graphify/extractors/engine.py graphify/extract.py      # no new diagnostics
```

Full suite: 7610 passed, 15 failed, 247 skipped. All 15 failures also fail on an untouched `v8` checkout on the same machine (Windows 11, Python 3.14), so they come from the environment: `test_skillgen` ×11, `test_hooks` ×1, the two `*_memoization` tests and one `test_extract` checkout-path test.
