title: fix(build): sweep placeholders orphaned by re-extraction in build_merge
body:
Source-less placeholders (external types like `List`, namespace import stubs) that lose their last edge through **re-extraction** stayed in graph.json at degree 0 forever. `build_merge` drops a re-extracted file's old nodes/edges by `source_file`, and placeholders have none. The #2807 orphan sweep only ran under `prune_sources`, and its "already isolated" set was taken after the old edges were already gone.

**What changed** (`build_merge` only):
- Before the rebind, snapshot the source-less nodes that are isolated in the graph **as loaded from disk**, plus any the fresh chunks themselves emit with no edge (a from-scratch build keeps those too).
- Run the #2807 sweep after every merge, sparing that snapshot and any node referenced by a hyperedge (members live in `G.graph`, not as edges, so degree 0 doesn't mean unreferenced). Same rule as before otherwise: no `source_file`, degree 0.
- When no files are pruned, the sweep only removes machine-made placeholders: `file_type == "code"` stubs and #2873 external import stubs (`_is_external_stub`). A source-less semantic/curated node is never removed by a plain merge. On the prune path such a node is only removed if the prune itself isolated it, same as v8.
- Removed nodes that were on disk are counted in `_pruned_node_count`, so the #3774 shrink check still adds up.

**Testing**
- New `tests/test_merge_sweeps_reextract_orphans.py`: stale per-file stubs left behind by a rebind get removed (Path 1), a shared placeholder is removed when an edit drops its last reference (Path 2), the namespace external stub is removed, a placeholder that's still referenced is kept, a node already isolated on disk is kept, a freshly emitted isolated node is kept, source-less semantic nodes are left alone (including on the prune path when re-extraction, not the prune, stranded them), and hyperedge members are never swept. 3 of these fail on current v8. The existing #2807 tests still pass.
- Full suite on 3.10 / 3.12 / 3.13 / 3.14: no new failures (the remaining failures happen on unmodified v8 too). ruff is clean.
- Ran the issue's repros live (C# A.cs/B.cs). Node counts:

| | v8 | this PR | from-scratch control |
|---|---|---|---|
| Path 1: 0.9.70 graph → `extract --force --code-only` | 9 (`a_cs_list`, `b_cs_list` at degree 0) | 7 | 7 |
| Path 1: then an incremental run | 9 | 7 | 7 |
| Path 2: edit A+B to drop `List`, incremental run | 7 (`list`, `system_collections_generic` at degree 0) | 5 | 5 |

This complements #3342, which handles `merge_raw_extraction` for JS/TS import stubs and doesn't touch `build_merge`. I tested #3342 as-is against both repros and it still leaves the degree-0 nodes.

Graphs that already contain orphans from an earlier run aren't cleaned up automatically, since those nodes were already isolated on disk. A one-off manual prune or a fresh rebuild clears them.

Fixes #4399

_AI disclosure: written with help from an AI assistant (Grok Bot). I reviewed the change and ran the tests and repros above._

title: feat(skill): warn when the input checkout is behind and pass built_at_commit to the report
body:
Fixes #4427

## What changed

- **Step 1** (`core/core.md`, plus the `core/aider.md` and `core/devin.md` monoliths): after install, a small python block runs git against the scan root from `.graphify_root`. It prints `git: on <branch>, N commit(s) behind <base>`, where `<base>` is the branch's upstream, or `origin/HEAD` if there's no upstream. When N > 0 it prints a WARNING and the skill tells the agent to offer scanning a fresh worktree of the default branch. It prints nothing when the path isn't a git repo or has no upstream/remote. I wrote it in python, not bash, so the PowerShell (windows) render translates it the same way as the other blocks.
- **Steps 4 and 5**: `generate()` now gets `built_at_commit`. It's read from graph.json, falling back to `watch._git_head()` on the input path, same as `graphify update` does. So GRAPH_REPORT.md from a `/graphify` build now has the Graph Freshness section.
- Regenerated all rendered skills and `expected/` snapshots with `python -m tools.skillgen --bless` (`--check` passes). I added a sanctioned-diff predicate in `gen.py` for the new monolith lines so the aider/devin round-trip test accepts them.
- New `tests/test_skill_behind_default_branch.py`: checks every rendered skill has the check and both `built_at_commit` calls. It also runs the rendered Step 1 snippet against temp repos: behind by 2, up to date, non-git, and no remote.

## Testing

- ruff clean.
- Full suite on 3.10 / 3.12 / 3.13 / 3.14: 16 failures on each, and they're the same 16 (`test_dm_*`, `test_security`) as unmodified v8 on the same interpreter. Nothing new fails.
- Live: ran the rendered Step 1 block on a real clone of pallets/itsdangerous that was reset behind origin, and it printed `git: on main, 8 commit(s) behind origin/main` plus the warning. On an up-to-date clone it printed `0 commit(s) behind origin/main`. A non-git dir and a repo with no remote printed nothing. I also ran the rendered Step 2/4/5 blocks on the behind clone, using the AST extractor in place of the LLM Step 3. GRAPH_REPORT.md showed `## Graph Freshness` / `Built from commit: 31f46a34`, which matches that clone's HEAD.

Limitation: it compares against the last-fetched remote refs and doesn't fetch, so a clone that hasn't been fetched in a while can under-report how far behind it is.

AI disclosure: written with help from an AI assistant (Grok Bot); I reviewed the changes and test results.

title: [Bug]: skill full build (SKILL.md Step 4/5) still uses build_from_json and skips entity dedup, so the next --update re-shapes untouched files (skill counterpart of #769)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

The skill's full build still calls `build_from_json()` directly (SKILL.md Step 4 and the Step 5 re-export), so it never runs `deduplicate_entities()`. Every other build path does:

- `graphify extract` full rebuild: `build([merged], dedup=True)` (fixed in #769, commit 579e1cc, "making it symmetric with the incremental path")
- skill `--update`: `build_merge(..., dedup=True)` (default)

So the same extraction gives a different graph depending on which path built it. In practice the first skill `--update` after a skill full build silently merges nodes that belong to files the update never touched, and `graph.json` changes topology for reasons unrelated to the edit. This is the skill-side counterpart of #769.

Expected: the skill full build produces the same graph as `graphify extract` and as a subsequent `--update` would, i.e. Step 4 and Step 5 build through `build([extraction], dedup=True, root=..., directed=...)`.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir reproB && cd reproB
python - <<'EOF'
import copy
from graphify.build import build_from_json, build, build_merge
from graphify.cluster import cluster
from graphify.export import to_json
import os

def frag(stem):
    src = f"docs/{stem}.md"
    e = lambda s, t: {"source": s, "target": t, "relation": "references",
                      "confidence": "EXTRACTED", "confidence_score": 1.0, "source_file": src}
    return {"nodes": [
        {"id": f"docs_{stem}", "label": f"{stem}.md", "file_type": "document", "source_file": src},
        {"id": f"docs_{stem}_contract_446", "label": "Contract No. 446", "file_type": "concept", "source_file": src},
        {"id": f"docs_{stem}_acme_corp", "label": "ACME Corp.", "file_type": "concept", "source_file": src}],
        "edges": [e(f"docs_{stem}", f"docs_{stem}_contract_446"),
                  e(f"docs_{stem}_contract_446", f"docs_{stem}_acme_corp")],
        "hyperedges": []}

A, B = frag("lot_a"), frag("lot_b")
merged = {"nodes": A["nodes"] + B["nodes"], "edges": A["edges"] + B["edges"], "hyperedges": []}

# 1) skill full build (SKILL.md Step 4)
G1 = build_from_json(copy.deepcopy(merged), root=".", directed=False)
print("skill full build (build_from_json):", G1.number_of_nodes())

# 2) graphify extract full rebuild path
G2 = build([copy.deepcopy(A), copy.deepcopy(B)], root=".", directed=False)
print("CLI extract (build):", G2.number_of_nodes())

# 3) skill --update after only lot_b.md changed (references/update.md)
os.makedirs("graphify-out", exist_ok=True)
to_json(G1, cluster(G1), "graphify-out/graph.json")
G3 = build_merge([copy.deepcopy(B)], graph_path="graphify-out/graph.json", root=".", directed=False)
print("skill --update (build_merge):", G3.number_of_nodes())
EOF
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
skill full build (build_from_json): 6
[graphify] Deduplicated 2 node(s) (2 exact).
[graphify] Replaced 3 node(s) from re-extracted source file(s).
CLI extract (build): 4
[graphify] Deduplicated 2 node(s) (2 exact).
skill --update (build_merge): 4
```

(stderr and stdout interleave, so the "Replaced" line belongs to step 3.)

In step 3 only `lot_b.md` was re-extracted, yet `docs_lot_b_contract_446` / `docs_lot_b_acme_corp` were folded into the `lot_a` nodes, an effect the full build never applied.

Real-world numbers: on a 465-node docs graph (three sibling cost estimates sharing a contract, an object code, and the people who signed them), `deduplicate_entities` collapses 8 nodes (7 exact, 1 fuzzy) that the skill full build had left split across files. Those 8 merges would appear only on the next `--update`, attributed to whatever file happened to change.

### Graphify version

0.9.89 (also `v8` at e8eb76e7)

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider keys set; semantic extraction done by the host agent (Claude Code skill flow).

### Additional context

- Related: #769 (same asymmetry, fixed for the CLI only), #296 (cross-file canonicalization), #3094 (cross-file guard semantics that `build()` already applies).
- The #479 shrink guard needs no special handling: Step 5 re-exports the same extraction through the same builder, so the node count matches Step 4.

title: [Bug]: node-ID rule 'only [a-z0-9_]' still contradicts ids.py for non-ASCII paths in 0.9.89, in both llm.py and extraction-spec.md (#3103 closed without a fix)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

#3103 (closed by its author as completed, no linked commit) reported that the node-ID rule in the extraction prompt contradicts `graphify/ids.py` for non-ASCII paths. On 0.9.89 / `v8` the wording is unchanged, and it is in **two** prompts, not one:

- `graphify/llm.py` `_EXTRACTION_SYSTEM` (used by `graphify extract --backend ...`): `Node ID format: lowercase, only [a-z0-9_], no dots or slashes.` plus `stem = full repo-relative path with the extension dropped`
- `graphify/skills/*/references/extraction-spec.md` line 61 (skill subagents): same rule

For a file named in Cyrillic the two halves cannot both be satisfied: the canonical stem from `make_id(_file_stem(path))` keeps Cyrillic, e.g. `docs/tz/ЛЗ4_обоснование_с_листом_Расчет_Кдог.md` -> `docs_tz_лз4_обоснование_с_листом_расчет_кдог`. The model therefore improvises a different stem per chunk and per run, and `_semantic_id_remap` does not reconcile any of them.

Expected: every semantic node from one file carries the canonical stem that `ids.py` derives, regardless of the script the path is written in.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# corpus: Russian-named markdown files, e.g.
#   docs/tz/ЛЗ4_обоснование_с_листом_Расчет_Кдог.md
#   docs/tz/СРЗ КП18-С301   ЛЗ2 (105) - 12.10.2026.md
#   docs/tz/СРЗ КП18-С303   ЛЗ5 (105) - 12.10.2026.md   (large, split across chunks)
graphify extract . --backend claude-cli --force --allow-dedup-shrink

# canonical stems
python -c "
from graphify.ids import make_id
from graphify.extractors.base import _file_stem
from pathlib import Path
for p in ['docs/tz/ЛЗ4_обоснование_с_листом_Расчет_Кдог.md',
          'docs/tz/СРЗ КП18-С301   ЛЗ2 (105) - 12.10.2026.md',
          'docs/tz/СРЗ КП18-С303   ЛЗ5 (105) - 12.10.2026.md']:
    print(make_id(_file_stem(Path(p))))
"

# the remap leaves model-invented stems alone
python -c "
from graphify.build import _semantic_id_remap
sf = 'docs/tz/ЛЗ4_обоснование_с_листом_Расчет_Кдог.md'
print(_semantic_id_remap([
  {'id': 'docs_tz_lz4_obosnovanie_kdog', 'label': 'f', 'file_type': 'document', 'source_file': sf},
  {'id': 'docs_tz_lz4_obosnovanie_kdog_raschet5_fot', 'label': 'x', 'file_type': 'concept', 'source_file': sf},
], None))
"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
canonical stems (ids.py):
docs_tz_лз4_обоснование_с_листом_расчет_кдог
docs_tz_срз_кп18_с301_лз2_105_12_10_2026
docs_tz_срз_кп18_с303_лз5_105_12_10_2026

node ids per file in graph.json after ONE extract run (claude-cli backend, 0.9.89):
ЛЗ4_обоснование_с_листом_Расчет_Кдог.md  15 nodes: 9  docs_tz_lz4_obosnovanie_kdog_*  (transliterated + abbreviated)
                                                    6  no file stem at all: gnb_directional_drilling, lz4_smeta_11559, ...
СРЗ КП18-С301   ЛЗ2 (105) - 12.10.2026.md 28 nodes: 4  docs_tz_srz_kp18_s301_lz2_*  (transliterated, date dropped)
                                                    24 no file stem: s301_totals, srz_dogovor_446s001s, concept_kp18_s301, ...
СРЗ КП18-С302   ЛЗ4 (105) - 12.10.2026.md 59 nodes: 32 docs_tz_srz_kp18_s302_lz4_105_12_10_2026_*
                                                    27 no file stem: s302_obj_ktp21, s302_contract, concept_kp18_s302, ...
СРЗ КП18-С303   ЛЗ5 (105) - 12.10.2026.md 82 nodes: 73 docs_tz_srz_kp18_s303_lz5_105_12_10_2026_*
                                                    9  docs_tz_срз_кп18_с303_лз5_105_12_10_2026_*  (canonical, another chunk)
ТКП Монтаж МКС ЛЗ-2,4,5 ver.04.md          8 nodes: 8  docs_tz_ткп_монтаж_мкс_лз_2_4_5_ver_04_*  (canonical)

_semantic_id_remap: {}
```

So the model does not just transliterate: for many nodes it gives up on `{stem}_{entity}` entirely, which also makes ids like `concept_gesn_norms` free to collide across files.

Consequences:

1. The stem is not stable: it differs between chunks of one file in the same run and between runs. A cross-file edge cached for file X that targets a node of file Y dangles as soon as Y is re-extracted under another spelling, and `build_from_json` drops such an edge silently (checked: an edge to a missing id yields 0 edges, no stub).
2. Stemless ids (`concept_*`, `s301_*`) are not scoped to their file, so two files can mint the same id for different things and fall into the cross-file collision path.
3. Logic keyed on the canonical stem (the file's own node in `_id_prefixes`, `_doc_twin_remap`, `_disambiguate_defining_collisions`) never recognises these nodes.
4. A skill-subagent run on the same corpus (prompt from `extraction-spec.md`) produced canonical Cyrillic stems only because each subagent noticed the conflict and called `graphify.ids.make_id` itself; following the prompt literally gives the `docs______________doc` collapse #3103 describes.

### Graphify version

0.9.89 (also `v8` at e8eb76e7)

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

Backend `claude-cli` (Claude Code 2.1.296), no provider keys set.

### Additional context

Two possible fixes, either removes the drift:

- Prompt: state the charset as `\w` with Unicode semantics in both `_EXTRACTION_SYSTEM` and `extraction-spec.md` (the fix #3103 suggested), and give a non-ASCII example such as `docs/отчёт.md` -> `docs_отчёт`.
- Code: `_semantic_id_remap` already computes `new_stem` from `source_file`; for a non-AST node whose id does not start with `new_stem`, it could re-key it to `new_stem` + the id's entity part, so the stored id stops depending on the model's spelling. The entity part is the hard part, since the model's stem has no fixed length; using the node `label` for the entity part is one way around that.

title: fix(skill): run entity dedup in the skill's full build like graphify extract
body:
Fixes #4431

## What changed

- Step 4 and Step 5 in `core/core.md` now build with `build([extraction], dedup=True, root='INPUT_PATH', directed=IS_DIRECTED)` instead of `build_from_json(...)`, keeping the same args. So `deduplicate_entities()` runs like it does in the `graphify extract` full build (`build([merged], dedup=True, root=target)`, #769).
- The aider/devin monoliths get the same change in Step 4/5 and in their Step 6–7c rebuilds (HTML/Obsidian/SVG/GraphML/Neo4j), so those stay in line with graph.json and its community ids. Their own `--update` section is untouched.
- No second dedup after `--update`. The lean `--update` runbook hands `build_merge`'s output, which is already deduped with untouched nodes kept apart (#3477), back to Step 4. `references/update.md` now marks it with `'_merged_by_build_merge': True`, and Step 4/5 rebuild a marked extraction with `build_from_json` like before.
- Dedup shrink on a full rebuild. Rebuilding over a graph.json from an older skill build that skipped dedup shrinks it by exactly the merged duplicates. Step 4 now writes with `force=True` only when `0 < old_nodes - new_nodes <= dedup_collapsed`, and prints a note saying so. Any bigger shrink still hits the #479 guard and is refused, same as before. This differs from the CLI, which refuses any dedup shrink unless you pass `--allow-dedup-shrink`. The skill has no such flag, and the shrink is fully explained by dedup.
- The comments I added inside the double-quoted `python -c "..."` blocks have no backticks or `$` (an earlier version had a backtick pair, which bash ran as a command).
- Regenerated all rendered skills plus `expected/`, and `skillgen --check` passes. In `gen.py` I added a sanctioned-diff predicate for the new monolith lines, and updated the anchor line in one `test_skillgen` test.

## Testing

- New `tests/test_skill_build_dedup.py` runs the rendered Step 4/5 bash blocks from `skill.md`, `skill-aider.md` and `skill-devin.md`. A fake `graphify` on PATH fails the test if any block shells out to it.
  - The reporter's fixture gives 4 nodes, same as `build()` (the skill gave 6 before). Step 5 doesn't re-shape Step 4's graph, and a following `build_merge` leaves the untouched file's edges alone.
  - Edge cases: an empty extraction still stops with no write, no-duplicate input is unchanged, and same-label code symbols in different files stay separate.
  - Hyperedges get remapped, `--directed` is kept, and after `--update` there's no re-dedup of #3477-protected nodes.
  - A rebuild over an un-deduped graph.json succeeds, while a genuine shrink is still refused.
  - It also scans every rendered `.md` for backticks or unescaped `$` inside `python -c "..."` blocks. Two v8 comment lines already have this and are allowlisted.
- Against the previous commit, 22 of these fail, including the backtick case.
- Full suite on 3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14: same 16 failures as unmodified v8 (`test_dm_*`, `test_security`), nothing new. ruff clean.
- Live run with a real `graphify` CLI on PATH (editable install of this branch):
  - Setup: a 3-doc corpus with shared entities and a hand-written extraction in place of the LLM step.
  - Rendered Steps 2/4/5 give 8 nodes, the same as `build()` (the v8 skill gave 18).
  - The rendered `update.md` merge block followed by Step 4 matches `build_merge`, and the untouched docs' edges are unchanged.
  - A rebuild over the v8 skill's 18-node graph.json writes 8 nodes with the note.

title: fix(extract): give the model each file's real id stem (#4432)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4432. #3103 reported the same thing and was closed without a fix.

The extraction prompts say node ids use "only `[a-z0-9_]`". `graphify/ids.py` keeps Unicode letters. For a path like `docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md` the model cannot follow both, so it invents a stem, and the stem differs between chunks and between runs. `_semantic_id_remap` only strips stems it already knows, so none of them get fixed.

This PR states the real rule and gives the model each file's stem, computed in code.

```diff
 graphify extract (llm.py)
-  <untrusted_source path="docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md" sha256="...">
+  <untrusted_source path="docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md" sha256="..." stem="docs_tz_лз4">

 skill, Part B
   check_semantic_cache(...)
     writes .graphify_uncached.txt              # unchanged
+    writes .graphify_uncached_stems.txt        # path<TAB>stem, same order
   Step B1: FILE_LIST lines
-    /abs/docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md
+    /abs/docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md<TAB>docs_tz_лз4       # falls back to the old file if missing

 rule text (llm.py + both extraction-spec fragments)
-  Node ID format: lowercase, only [a-z0-9_], no dots or slashes.
+  Node ID format: lowercase. Letters and digits of any script are kept as written
+  (never transliterated to ASCII); every run of any other character becomes one _.
+  ...use the given stem character for character as the id prefix.
```

Both paths use one new helper, `file_id_stem(path, root)` in `graphify/extractors/base.py`. It returns `make_id(_file_stem(...))` of the root-relative path. The skill computes the stems in the same Python step that already runs the cache check. No path is pasted into code, and no agent types a stem.

I left `_semantic_id_remap` alone. A made-up stem has no known length, so a repair can't tell where the stem ends and the entity begins. The #4281 prototype also showed that re-keying a node from its `source_file` moves a node that mentions another file under the wrong file.

### Before / after

Same id, two different stems:

```text
before:  ids.py stem      docs_tz_лз4_обоснование_с_листом_расчет_кдог
         model's stem     docs_tz_lz4_obosnovanie_kdog            (from the issue; changes per run)
         remap            {}                                      (nothing reconciled)

after:   prompt carries   stem="docs_tz_лз4_обоснование_с_листом_расчет_кдог"
         page node id     docs_tz_лз4_обоснование_с_листом_расчет_кдог   (same string, tested)
```

Read literally, the old rule turns that path into `docs_tz_4_`. That result comes from running the rule as code, not from a model run.

Tests, `tests/test_unicode_id_rule.py`:

```text
before fix:  43 failed, 2 passed   (the 2 are the host-count guards)
after fix:   45 passed
```

### Merge danger

**Door:** two-way. No stored format changes. The only new file is a temp file that Part B cleans up, and reverting means one commit.

**Blast radius:** medium. Every semantic extraction prompt changes:

- **Cache:** the semantic cache is keyed on the prompt text, so every existing entry misses once. This hits `graphify extract` users and all 14 skill hosts, including ASCII-only repos. Reverting causes one more miss.
- **ASCII paths:** the chunk prompt is byte-identical apart from the added `stem="..."` (tested). File-node ids do not change for any path.
- **Skill hosts:** 14 hosts get the regenerated skill and spec. Aider and devin are not touched. They never stated the `[a-z0-9_]` rule.
- **#4344:** one-line conflict. Both PRs touch the same `check_semantic_cache` line in `core.md`. Whichever merges second changes `root = 'INPUT_PATH'` to `root = read_scan_root()`.

### Not covered

- Nothing enforces the id. The model can still ignore the stem it is given, and then ids drift as before. Enforcing it means having code mint the ids, which is a larger change.
- Nodes with no file stem at all (`concept_*`, `s301_totals` in the issue).
- On the skill path, a symlinked doc whose target is outside the scan root gets no stem and falls back to the rule text.
- The aider and devin monolith skills.

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature

- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: the stem the model is told to use is the same string the document pass mints for that file's node, whatever script the path is in.

- `test_file_id_stem_is_the_prefix_the_pipeline_mints` runs a Cyrillic and an ASCII document through the real `extract()`. The page-node id equals `file_id_stem`, the chunk prompt carries that stem, and `_semantic_id_remap` leaves a node under it alone.
- `file_id_stem` is tested with an absolute path and root `"."`, with a path outside the root (returns `""`), and with `"`, `<` and `>` in the name. The stem holds only letters, digits and `_`, so it cannot break out of the attribute.
- The Part B step is extracted from the generated `graphify/skill.md` and run. It writes the expected `path<TAB>stem` lines, with `INPUT_PATH` substituted once.
- The rule wording is checked in `llm.py` and in all 14 generated specs, with exact host counts so a dropped host fails the test.
- Generated state this invalidates: the semantic cache (once), plus 14 skill files and 14 specs, which are regenerated with `--bless`.

title: fix(extract): keep edges between kept nodes when edge source_file is undispatched (#2276)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Related to #2276.

When an incremental semantic extraction re-extracts two files (e.g. `page_a.md` and `page_b.md`), the model can stamp an edge between their kept nodes with a `source_file` that resolves to a real corpus file not dispatched in the current batch (e.g. `log.md`). Both out-of-scope filters (`extract_corpus_parallel` in `graphify/llm.py` and `scope_semantic_result` in `graphify/cache.py`) previously dropped any edge whose own `source_file` resolved outside the dispatched allowlist before checking its endpoints, and `build_merge` then replaced the prior edge contribution for the re-extracted files, losing the edge between the two kept nodes.

- In `extract_corpus_parallel` (`graphify/llm.py`), record `kept_ids` during the node pass and retain an edge whose own `source_file` is out of scope when both `source` and `target` are in `kept_ids` (and neither is in `dropped_ids`).
- In `scope_semantic_result` (`graphify/cache.py`), retain an edge whose own `source_file` resolves outside `allowed_source_files` when both endpoints are in `kept_ids`; the post-pass still prunes any edge referencing an exclusively dropped node id.
- Add `test_edge_between_kept_nodes_survives_when_source_file_was_not_dispatched` in `tests/test_chunking.py` covering `extract_corpus_parallel`, `scope_semantic_result`, and `build_merge`.

title: fix(python): walk enclosing scopes for module member calls (#2447)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Related to #2447 (resolves Cause C only).

In `_resolve_python_member_calls` (`graphify/extract.py`), the typed-receiver arm already climbs `contains` and `method` edges via `_file_node(caller)` to find the caller's enclosing file node, while the module arm (`mod.func()`) read `file_of_node.get(caller)` directly. Because a class method hangs off its class via a `method` edge rather than a `contains` edge from the file node, and a nested function's `contains` parent is its enclosing function rather than the file node, `file_of_node.get(caller)` missed the file node's `imported_by_filenode` entry for calls inside methods and nested functions (Cause C in #2447).

- Use `caller_file = _file_node(caller)` in the module arm of `_resolve_python_member_calls` while keeping `file_of_node` built from `contains` edges only so the `t not in file_of_node` filter on contained functions is unchanged.
- Add `test_python_module_qualified_call_resolves_from_enclosing_scopes` in `tests/test_extract.py` covering `mod.func()` calls from a method and a nested function, while verifying that an unresolvable root-level `import mod` when `mod.py` lives only in a subdirectory (Cause A) remains unlinked.

title: fix(go): normalize a generic receiver type before building its id
body:
## What does this PR do?

While verifying the already-merged Go member-call resolution (`deca9fa3`, cherry-picked as `1695efae` — "resolve member calls through the receiver's declared type") against the edge cases from #3368, I found one gap it left behind: **a generic type's methods attach to a node disconnected from the type's own declaration.**

`func (b *Box[T]) Get() T` reads its receiver's `type` field as `Box[T]` verbatim (after stripping the leading `*`). But `type Box[T any] struct {...}` captures `[T any]` as a separate `type_parameter_list` — never part of the name — so the type declaration's own id is keyed on the bare `Box`. Without stripping the instantiation before that text turns into an id, `walk()`'s method-attachment code (`parent_nid = _make_id(pkg_scope, receiver_type)`) produces a *different* id than the type declaration's own `type_nid`. The practical effect: `Box`'s own node ends up with **zero `method` edges** — `graphify explain Box`, graph.html, and any god-node/structural analysis walking from the type see no methods at all, even on a trivial generic type.

This didn't show up as a missing `calls` edge in most cases because the already-merged resolver's self-reference path (`self_type`) happens to still find the phantom node by label match for same-method self-calls — but the type's own node identity stays wrong, and a chain through a generic receiver's own *concrete*-typed field only resolves by coincidence of how the lookup is shaped, not because the ids agree.

### Fix

Adds `_go_strip_generic_args(type_text)` — drops everything from the first `[` onward — and applies it at **both** places a receiver's raw type text is turned into an id:
- the live `walk()` pass that attaches a method to its owner (`parent_nid`)
- the separate case-collision pre-scan (`_receiver_type_of`, feeding `_plain_symbol_nid`/`case_groups`), which has to compute the *same* id or case-only-collision salting (`Run`/`run`) silently stops matching for generic types

After the fix, `Box`'s own node (and the case-collision table) agree on one id, so a generic type's methods attach to the type itself — the same node a non-generic type would get.

Fixes the generic-type gap in #3368.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Purely a normalization fix to an id computation that was already happening — no new edge types, no new confidence tiers, nothing added to the public shape of a node or edge. Before the fix, a generic type's methods minted a *second*, disconnected `_callable_class` node (labeled `Box[T]`) alongside the type's own (`Box`); after the fix there is exactly one.

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue: confirmed against current `v8` HEAD (post-`0.9.89`) that `Box`'s own node has no `method` edges for a trivial `type Box[T any] struct { val T }; func (b *Box[T]) Get() T`, before writing the fix.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary: one small helper, applied at exactly the two places receiver-type text becomes an id in `graphify/extractors/go.py`. No other file touched.
- [x] Added **regression tests** (`tests/test_go_generic_receiver_methods.py`, 4 cases): pointer and value receivers both attach to their own type, exactly one `_callable_class` node is minted for a generic type with multiple methods, and a chain through a generic receiver's concrete field still resolves to the right target among an ambiguous corpus-wide name.

title: [Bug]: Rust: `use` edges target a bare name, and since 0.9.63 the stub they leave makes `affected`/`explain` ambiguous
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

A Rust `use` adds an `imports_from` edge whose target is the bare, case-folded name it imports (`invoice` for `use crate::model::Invoice;`), not the declaration's id. Nothing resolves that target directly. It reaches the declaration only when a sourceless node with the same id exists for `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` to remap, which is what an unresolved type annotation such as `fn f(i: &Invoice)` creates. When the type is only constructed, called or not used at all, or when its annotations resolve straight to the declaration, no such node exists and the edge dangles.

Up to 0.9.62 the dangling edge was dropped, so the import was silently lost. Since 0.9.63 (#2873) its target is minted as an `external` stub labelled `invoice`, which ties with the real `Invoice` in name lookups: `graphify affected Invoice` prints `No unique node match for Invoice` and exits 0, and `graphify explain Invoice` reports `Ambiguous: 'Invoice' matches 2 nodes in different files.`

Expected: the edge lands on `Invoice` in `src/model.rs`, no stub is minted, and both commands resolve the name.

### Steps to reproduce

```toml
# Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "repro"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
```

```rust
// src/lib.rs
pub mod billing;
pub mod model;

// src/model.rs
pub struct Invoice(pub u64);

// src/billing.rs
use crate::model::Invoice;

pub fn make() -> u64 {
    Invoice(1).0
}
```

```sh
graphify extract . --code-only --cargo --force
graphify cluster-only . --no-viz --no-label
graphify affected Invoice
graphify explain Invoice
```

Annotating the type instead, with `pub fn total(i: &Invoice) -> u64 { i.0 }` in `billing.rs`, removes the stub and lands the edge on `src_model_invoice`.

### Error output or graph output

| graphify | external stub | `imports_from` target | `affected Invoice` | `explain Invoice` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.9.62 | none | edge dropped | resolves | resolves |
| 0.9.63 | `id: invoice`, `label: invoice`, `type: external`, `source_file: ""` | `invoice`, the stub | `No unique node match for Invoice`, exit 0 | `Ambiguous: 'Invoice' matches 2 nodes in different files.` |
| 0.9.89 | same | same | same | same |

On a private ~440-file Cargo workspace, 0.9.89 mints 1,007 external stubs. 426 share a case-folded label with a real declaration, 407 of them with exactly one candidate, and 403 names that `affected` resolves on 0.9.62 no longer resolve. Annotations do not rescue them there: one of those types is annotated at 13 sites, its 9 `references` edges land on the declaration directly, and all 7 of its `imports_from` edges point at its stub.

### Graphify version

0.9.63 through 0.9.89, the latest. 0.9.62 is not affected.

### Operating System

macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)

### Python Version

3.14.7

### Installation Method

uv: `uv tool run --from 'graphifyy==<version>' graphify …`

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables are set, every run uses `--code-only`, and the repro is a clean directory holding only the four files above.

### Additional context

From the 0.9.89 source:

- `graphify/extractors/rust.py`, `use_declaration` branch: `add_edge(file_nid, _make_id(<last path segment>), "imports_from", …)` for each `use` and each binding of a grouped `use`.
- `graphify/extract.py`, `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes`: remaps sourceless nodes, so an edge whose target no node carries is never considered. Instrumented on the repro: with the annotation, a sourceless `invoice` node is present and the import edge moves from `invoice` to `src_model_invoice`; without it, there is no such node and the edge stays on `invoice`.
- `graphify/build.py`, `_mint_external_stub` (#2873): mints the dangling `invoice` as the `type: "external"` node that collides.

Related: #4134 makes `affected` prefer source-backed nodes. On the workspace graph above it resolves 401 of the 403 names to their declarations and none wrongly, the other 2 being genuine same-name declarations, but `explain` keeps the tie. #330 proposed resolving Rust `use` targets with a cross-file pass, and #2280 (Python) and #3565 (Elixir) are the same unresolved-import class in other extractors.

title: Windows: graph_stats hangs under MCP hosts — _git_head runs git without stdin=DEVNULL (export.py, watch.py)
body:
## Summary

On Windows, the `graph_stats` MCP tool (and the `graphify://stats` resource) can hang indefinitely when the server is run by an MCP host such as Claude Code. Root cause: `graphify.export._git_head` and `graphify.watch._git_head` run `git rev-parse HEAD` via `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, timeout=3)` **without `stdin=`**, so the git child inherits the server's stdin — the MCP stdio pipe. Under asyncio/libuv hosts that pipe is an overlapped-mode pipe, and git blocks on it.

`prs.py` already passes `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` to every `gh`/`git` call; these two call sites were missed.

**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.89, mcp 1.30.0, Python 3.12 (uv tool install), Windows 11, Git for Windows.

## Observed

- Under a plain Python `mcp` client, the 3s timeout fires: `graph_stats` takes a constant **3.0s** and the `Built at commit:` staleness line silently loses its `HEAD` comparison (because `_git_head` returns `None`). Measured on two graphs (5,497 and 22,709 nodes).
- Under Claude Code (Windows), the kill-after-timeout never returns: `graph_stats` hung for **592s** until the user interrupted. The host log then shows the correct result arriving as `Received a response for an unknown message ID`.
- Only graphs with a `built_at_commit` trigger it (the git call is skipped otherwise), which initially made it look like a "large graph" problem.
- With `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` added: **0.03s**, and the staleness line is correct (`HEAD is fe5410b, graph built at abd900b: graph may be stale`).

## Reproduction

1. Build a graph inside a git repo so `graph.json` carries `built_at_commit`.
2. Run `graphify-mcp --graph <that>/graph.json` as an MCP server from an asyncio-based client on Windows (e.g. `mcp.client.stdio.stdio_client`).
3. `call_tool("graph_stats", {})` → 3.0s (timeout path). Under Claude Code → hangs.

In-process bisect: calling `_git_head()` from a plain script in the same interpreter takes 0.03s; the same call inside the running MCP server hits the timeout; injecting `stdin=DEVNULL` into that `subprocess.run` makes it 0.03s inside the server too. `_filter_blank_stdin` is not a factor (same result with it disabled).

## Fix (two one-line changes)

```diff
--- a/graphify/export.py
+++ b/graphify/export.py
@@ def _git_head(cwd=None):
         r = _sp.run(
-            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=3,
+            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], stdin=_sp.DEVNULL, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=3,
             cwd=str(cwd) if cwd is not None else None,
         )
```

Same change in `graphify/watch.py` `_git_head`. Any other `subprocess.run` reached from a tool handler without `stdin=` has the same exposure on Windows.

Related background on the general hazard: python/cpython bpo-44527 and alexalexalex222/frontend-design-loop-mcp#1 (same mechanism: child inherits the MCP stdio pipe, kill after timeout never returns).

Happy to open a PR with the two-line change if useful.

title: fix(mcp): don't hand git the server's stdin in _git_head
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4440.

`graph_stats` asks git for `HEAD` so it can say whether the graph is stale. `_git_head` ran `git rev-parse HEAD` without `stdin=`, so the child inherited the server's stdin, which under an MCP stdio host is the protocol pipe. On Windows git blocks on that pipe: the call sits on the 3s timeout and the staleness line loses its `HEAD` comparison, or it hangs outright under Claude Code.

`prs.py` already passes `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` to every `gh`/`git` call (#3318). The two `_git_head` copies in `export.py` and `watch.py` were missed, so this adds it there.

I went through the other `subprocess` calls in `graphify/`. `export._git_head` is the only unguarded one a tool handler reaches (`serve.py` imports it for `graph_stats`). `watch._git_head` is the same function for the CLI path, so I changed it too rather than leave the two copies different.

Invariant: a subprocess started by the server never inherits the MCP stdio pipe.

title: test(ingest): compare the symlink target against what readlink returned before
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4435.

`test_binary_captures_skip_existing_entries` ends its symlink cases with `occupied.readlink() == sentinel`. On Windows `readlink()` returns the target in extended-length form (`\\?\C:\...`), so that comparison is false for `dangling_link-False`, `dangling_link-True` and `live_link-True`, even though the capture left the link alone.

The test now reads the target right after it creates the link and compares against that value at the end. That is what "the existing link is untouched" means, and it doesn't depend on how a platform spells the path, so there is no prefix stripping and no separate UNC case.

Test only, no change under `graphify/`.

title: fix(rust): land a `use` on the declaration it imports
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4439.

A Rust `use` adds an `imports_from` edge whose target is the bare, case-folded name it imports (`invoice` for `use crate::model::Invoice;`). That only reached the declaration when a type annotation somewhere had left a sourceless node under the same id for `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` to remap. When the type is only constructed or called, the edge dangled, and since 0.9.63 build mints the target as an external stub that ties with the real declaration, so `graphify affected Invoice` and `graphify explain Invoice` stop resolving.

What changes:

- The `use` edge carries the imported name as written (`_rust_use_name`, stripped before output like the other `_rust_use_*` markers), because the id has already folded its case and the rewire matches case-sensitively.
- Right before the rewire, each imported name that has no node gets a sourceless one lent to it. The lent nodes are never kept: an import with no unique declaration dangles exactly as it does today, and build mints it as before.
- Only a path rooted at `crate`, `self` or `super` is resolved. `use serde::Serialize;` or `use std::fs::File;` names another crate's item, never the corpus's own `Serialize` or `File` (second commit, after the review bot's finding).
- An incremental build re-extracts only the changed files, so the rewire now also takes `resolution_context_nodes` as candidates. Without that, `watch` resolved less than a full build and `test_incremental_builds_match_full_builds` caught it.
- AST cache schema 15 -> 16, since cached edges don't have the name.

I first tried emitting the stub from the extractor. That changed other passes (in-file call resolution bound to it, and the colliding-id pass renamed existing stubs), so the node only exists for the duration of the rewire.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: the only thing that moves is the target of a Rust `imports_from` edge whose name has exactly one declaration.

I checked that on a real corpus, the RustDesk source tree (289 `.rs` files), comparing `extract()` output before and after:

```text
imports_from edges retargeted to a declaration: 489
other edges added or removed:                   0
nodes added or removed:                         0
confidence changes on existing edges:           0
```

Limitations:

- Resolution is by name, the same rule type annotations already get. A name declared twice stays unresolved even when the `use` path says which one is meant (`test_a_use_of_a_name_declared_twice_stays_unresolved`).
- The edge target is a shared id, so once one file imports the crate's own `Config` through `crate::`, a `use other_crate::Config;` elsewhere follows it. On RustDesk about 38 of the 489 edges come from a path that is not rooted at `crate`/`self`/`super`, mostly `hbb_common::` and `scrap::`, which are workspace crates there. An annotation naming the type does the same today.
- Workspace crates are not resolved on their own: `use hbb_common::Foo;` only lands when something else already resolved that name.
- Three existing expectations in `tests/test_rust_use_trees.py` pinned the bare target (`parse`, `render`) and now expect the declaration id. That is the behaviour change this PR is about, but it does edit tests that were written on purpose, so please look at those.
- The `resolution_context_nodes` change is on a path every language shares. The full suite passes; I have no incremental corpus for other languages to compare.

title: [Bug]: Ignore patterns leak from home directory when an invalid .git marker is present
body:
Description

Graphify can discover ignore patterns from a user's home directory when scanning a temporary project that is not inside a valid Git repository.

On Windows, my home directory (C:\Users\vishn) contains a .git directory that Git does not recognize as a valid repository. However, _find_vcs_root() in graphify/detect.py treats the presence of this directory as a VCS root.

My home-level .gitignore contains node_modules. When Graphify scans a pytest temporary directory, this unrelated ignore pattern is loaded, causing the ignore-pattern count to be incorrect.

Steps to reproduce

Use Windows with Python and pytest.

Have a home directory containing an invalid or incomplete .git directory.

Add node_modules to the home-level .gitignore.

Run:

uv run pytest tests/test_detect.py::test_graphifyignore_excludes_file -vv

Observe the assertion failure.

Expected behavior

Graphify should not load unrelated ignore patterns from a home directory that is not a valid VCS repository. The test should count only the two patterns declared in the temporary project's .graphifyignore.

Actual behavior

The test expects graphifyignore_patterns == 2, but receives 3. The additional pattern is node_modules, inherited from the home-level .gitignore.

Environment

OS: Windows

Python: 3.11.9

Test framework: pytest

Affected code: graphify/detect.py, _find_vcs_root() and ignore-pattern discovery

Suggested direction

Consider how VCS root discovery should handle invalid or incomplete repository markers, while preserving support for legitimate repositories and the existing VCS-boundary tests.

title: global add takes one source, so the CLI cannot use global_add_many's one-pass batch
body:
## Summary

`global_add_many` (#3433 / #3434) composes a batch of project graphs in one pass over the global
graph — one load, one cross-repo pass, one save — turning the O(K²) of K sequential `global add`
calls into O(K). But the CLI `graphify global add` still takes exactly one source, so from the
command line adding K repos is still K separate invocations, each paying the whole-graph load /
cross-repo link / save that `global_add_many` was built to pay once. The batch API is reachable
only from Python.

Extra positional arguments are silently dropped today (`cli.py`), so there is not even a diagnostic
when someone tries `global add a b c`.

## Proposed

`graphify global add <graph.json> [<graph.json> ...] [--as <tag>]` routing every positional source
through one `global_add_many` call.

- `--as` stays valid only when exactly one source is given: it names one repo, and with several it
  would tag all but one by inference anyway (or, if applied to all, prune every repo down to one
  tag). Passing `--as` with several sources is rejected rather than guessed.
- Untagged sources are named in a single `distinct_repo_tags` pass so its collision widening spans
  the batch. A per-source call sees one directory name at a time, hands two same-named repos the
  same tag, and the second prunes the first.

Depends on #3434 (the `global_add_many` API). PR follows.

title: feat(cli): add several sources in one 'global add'
body:
Fixes #4445.

## Stacked on #3434

This builds on the `global_add_many` API from #3434. Until that merges, this PR's diff
also shows its two commits (`perf(global-graph): add global_add_many …` and `Pin the order
the external-label index is read in`) — review those on #3434, not here. Draft until #3434
lands, after which I will rebase so only the CLI commit remains.

## Summary

`graphify global add` took one source, so adding K repos from the command line meant K
invocations, each paying the whole-graph load / cross-repo link / save that `global_add_many`
pays once. `global add a b c` now routes every positional source through one `global_add_many`
pass.

- `--as` still names a single source; passing it with several sources is rejected rather than
  guessed.
- Untagged sources are named in one `distinct_repo_tags` call so its collision widening spans the
  batch — a per-source call hands two same-named repos the same tag and the second prunes the
  first. (This also keeps the existing `""` → `repo` degradation.)

Deliberately minimal: no per-source `--as`, no directory-to-`graph.json` resolution. Those are
easy to add if wanted, but they widen the surface past what #4445 asks for.

## Tests

`tests/test_global_add_tag_inference.py`, three added, no existing assertion changed:

- `test_several_sources_add_in_one_batch` — two sources land under their inferred tags in one pass.
- `test_several_same_named_repos_get_distinct_tags` — the one-pass inference; fails if inference is
  done per source.
- `test_as_tag_is_rejected_for_several_sources` — `--as` with several sources exits non-zero and
  writes nothing.

`ruff check` clean.

title: update.md: code-only --update never writes .graphify_extract.json (FileNotFoundError or silently dropped AST)
body:
## Summary

In the skill's `--update` runbook (`references/update.md`), the code-only branch never produces `graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json`, but the incremental merge step that follows reads it unconditionally. Following the runbook literally after a normal full build therefore either fails with `FileNotFoundError`, or, if the agent applies the "only deletions" guard, silently merges an empty extraction and discards the re-extracted AST.

Seen in the opencode skill as installed by v0.9.86. The same text is unchanged in `graphify/skills/opencode/references/update.md` on `v8` (v0.9.90). Other platforms are likely affected too, since the skill files are generated from shared sources.

## Steps (as written in the runbook)

1. Run a full build (`/graphify .`). Step 9 cleanup deletes `.graphify_extract.json`, `.graphify_ast.json` and `.graphify_semantic.json`.
2. Change one code file and run `/graphify . --update`.
3. `code_only` is True, so the runbook says: *"run only Step 3A (AST) on the changed files, skip Step 3B entirely (no subagents), then go straight to merge and Steps 4–8."*
4. Step 3A (SKILL.md Part A) writes only `.graphify_ast.json`. Nothing writes `.graphify_extract.json`:
   - Part C, which would merge AST and semantic output into it, is not mentioned on the code-only path.
   - Part C would itself fail, because it reads `.graphify_semantic.json` unconditionally, and that file is only written by Part B's "Fast path", which was skipped.
5. The merge block reads `new_extraction = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(...))` → `FileNotFoundError`.

The guard just above the merge (`if [ ! -f graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json ]` → write an empty extraction) is documented as being for "only deletions". If an agent runs it on the code-only path to get past step 5, the merge succeeds but with zero new nodes, so the changed files' fresh AST is silently dropped.

## Expected

On the code-only path, after Step 3A, write the empty semantic file (Part B "Fast path") and run Part C, so `.graphify_extract.json` contains the new AST before the incremental merge. Alternatively, make the merge read `.graphify_ast.json` directly when `code_only` is True.

## Notes

- The CLI `graphify update .` (watch-based rebuild) works correctly. This only affects agents following the skill's `--update` runbook.
- Related, but separate: an update that only prunes deleted files is then routed through Step 4, whose `to_json` shrink guard (#479) refuses to write a smaller graph. So a validated deletion can't be persisted without `force=True`.

title: JS: parameters of a file-scope anonymous callback are not shadowed, so a callback argument fabricates an indirect_call to any same-named function in the corpus
body:
## Behavior

When JS code sits inside an anonymous callback with no named enclosing function (the AngularJS `.controller('X', function ($scope) { ... })` shape, `items.forEach(function (value) { ... })` at file scope, a test's `it('...', () => { ... })`), a bare identifier that is one of that callback's own parameters, passed on as a call argument, is resolved against the corpus-wide label index. It produces an `indirect_call` edge (INFERRED, 0.85, context `argument`) from the file node to an unrelated same-named function in another file, including a module-private function in a separate package that the caller never imports.

The same code inside a named function is handled correctly.

Observed with `graphify 0.9.90`.

## Minimal reproduction

`a.js`:

```js
items.forEach(function (value) { s.on(value); });
```

`b.js`:

```js
function value(x) { return x; }
```

```sh
graphify extract . --code-only
```

Result:

```text
a.js --indirect_call [INFERRED, context=argument]--> value()
```

`value` at that location is the callback's parameter, not a reference to `b.js`'s function.

## Variants (all on 0.9.90, two-file corpus as above)

| `a.js` | edge to `value()` |
|---|---|
| `items.forEach(function (value) { s.on(value); });` | **fabricated** |
| `items.forEach(function (value) { emit(value); });` | **fabricated** |
| `m.c(function (s) { items.forEach(function (value) { s.on(value); }); });` | **fabricated** |
| `function run(items){ items.forEach(function (value) { s.on(value); }); }` | none (correct) |
| `function run(items){ items.forEach(function (value) { emit(value); }); }` | none (correct) |
| `function run(items){ items.forEach(value); }` (real reference, control) | kept (correct) |

The target does not have to be in the same package or language. With the target in a separate TypeScript package as a module-private function:

`app/package.json`: `{ "name": "app", "type": "module" }`

`app/src/transport.ts`:

```ts
async function value(response: Response): Promise<unknown> {
  return response.json();
}
export async function load(response: Response): Promise<unknown> {
  return value(response);
}
```

`legacy/controller.js`:

```js
angular.module('app').controller('ListCtrl', function ($scope) {
	angular.forEach($scope.events, function (value) {
		$scope.$on(value, function () {});
	});
});
```

Result: `controller.js --indirect_call [INFERRED, argument]--> value()` in `transport.ts`. The function is not exported and nothing imports the file.

## Expected

No edge. A parameter of the enclosing closure shadows the name, exactly as it already does when the closure sits inside a named function (#2241).

## Probable cause (read, not patched)

The #3124 path in `extractors/engine.py` (inside the `expression_statement` branch that #3408 added) collects each topmost closure of a module-level call statement and queues it for the call walk as `function_bodies.append((file_nid, closure_body))`. It queues the closure's *body*, so the closure's own parameters never enter `closure_locals_by_body`, and `local_bound_names` has no entry for `file_nid`. Inside a named function the same closure is reached through the `walk_calls` boundary branch instead, which folds `_js_local_bound_names(node, source)` into `extra_locals`, so the shadow works there.

Seeding `closure_locals_by_body[id(closure_body)]` with `_js_local_bound_names(closure, source)` at that append looks like the fix for the direct case. I have not traced why the nested variant (third row) still fabricates, so that row is worth its own regression test.

## Impact

On a 33k-node mixed PHP / AngularJS / React-TS repository this produced 110 phantom edges from AngularJS controllers into the separate React apps, almost all from generic callback parameter names: `slug` (34), `value` (27), `entry` (25), `scope` (16), `row`, `item`, `title`. The two apps are separate bundles and cannot call each other. The edges also moved targets into the wrong community: the TypeScript `value()` above was clustered into the AngularJS "Admin Learning Controllers" community.

Related but distinct: #2606 (block-scoped `for...of` binding in object shorthand), #2569 (unparenthesised arrow parameter), #2517 (catch bindings).

## Suggested regression test

The two-file corpus above: assert no `indirect_call` from `a.js` to `b_value` for the three file-scope rows, and keep the `run() -> value()` edge for the control row.

title: File node takes the label of a module-level variable when a same-stem sibling file exists (x.mjs + x.sql, const sql)
body:
### Summary

When a JS file and a file with another extension share the same stem in one directory (`x.mjs` + `x.sql`), the `.mjs` file node gets the disambiguated id `<dir>_<stem>_mjs_<dir>_<stem>`. If the `.mjs` also declares a module-level variable whose name equals the sibling's extension (`const sql = ...`), that variable is minted with the same id. Dedup keeps the variable and drops the file node, so the file node ends up labelled `sql` and cannot be found by its filename.

### Reproduction (graphify 0.9.33 and 0.9.90, `--code-only`, with `[sql]` extra)

```sh
mkdir -p repro/esquema && cd repro && git init -q
printf 'import postgres from "postgres";\nconst sql = postgres(process.env.U);\nasync function prueba(){ return sql`select 1` }\n' > esquema/x.mjs
echo 'create table t(a int);' > esquema/x.sql
graphify extract . --code-only
```

Output:

```
[graphify] note: node 'esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x' was extracted twice from 'esquema/x.mjs' under different labels — keeping 'sql', dropping 'x.mjs'.
```

Resulting nodes:

```
esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x | sql      <- should be the file node "x.mjs"
esquema_x_prueba        | prueba()
esquema_x_sql_esquema_x | x.sql
esquema_x_t             | t
```

`graphify explain "x.mjs"` → `No node matching 'x.mjs' found.`

### Controls

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `x.mjs` with `const db = postgres(...)` + `x.sql` | OK: file node `esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x` labelled `x.mjs` |
| `x.mjs` with `const sql = postgres(...)`, no `x.sql` | OK: file node `esquema_x` (`x.mjs`), variable `esquema_x_sql` (`sql`) |
| `x.mjs` with `const sql = postgres(...)` + `y.sql` | OK, same as above |
| `x.mjs` with `const sql = 1` (literal) + `x.sql` | OK: the literal is not emitted as a node |

So the trigger is: a same-stem sibling file (which turns on the extension-tagged id scheme) plus a module-level symbol named like the sibling's extension.

### Expected

The file node keeps its own label (`x.mjs`) and the variable gets a distinct id.

### Impact

This is common in database repos, where a migration runner `foo.mjs` sits next to `foo.sql` and uses the `postgres` client conventionally named `sql`. In our repo it hits 3 of 3 such pairs.

title: fix(cluster): keep a community label when membership overlap stays a majority (#2298)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Keep a saved community label when the nodes it still shares are a strict majority of both the previous membership and the current membership.

`remap_communities_to_previous` already puts the old community id on the overlapping community. After that, `cluster-only` in `graphify/cli.py` and `_rebuild_code` in `graphify/watch.py` kept the label only when `community_member_sigs` matched exactly. One added node changed the digest, so the hub name replaced the saved name even though the community count stayed the same. With no `.sig` file, a changed community count dropped every label, including communities whose members did not change.

`label_still_applies` (next to `remap_communities_to_previous`) keeps the equal-signature fast path. Otherwise the label stays only when `overlap * 2 > len(saved)` and `overlap * 2 > len(current)`.

Related to #2298. A `label` run and a later `update` can still emit different community counts; this PR only stops discarding a label whose overlap is a strict majority.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A saved label stays on the community that still contains a strict majority of its previous members, and for which those shared nodes are a strict majority of the current set. An equal membership signature still keeps the label. A one-node fragment of a large community does not, even when remap reuses the old id.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

- Reproduced on v8 at `041771b`: `tests/test_labeling.py::test_cluster_only_keeps_label_on_majority_membership_overlap` failed with `assert 'auth_hub' == 'Auth Engine'`. stderr: `2 saved labels, 2 communities now; renamed 1`.
- Decoy: a 200-node community split into singletons must not keep `Big Service`. Remap puts the old id on exactly one singleton. A fix that keeps every remapped id fails this.
- Left alone: `cluster()`, `community_member_sigs`, Leiden `randomness`, and the order that writes labels before the `.sig` file.
- Limitations: a 50/50 split keeps neither name. A community that more than doubles does not keep the name, because the overlap is not a strict majority of the new set. If no current community holds a majority, the hub name still fills the gap. This does not force `label` and `update` to emit the same community count.

## How was this tested?

Python 3.13.3. Python 3.10 was not available in this environment.

```text
PYTHONPATH=/Users/srijansrivastava/graphify-worktrees/2298-community-label-majority \
  /Users/srijansrivastava/graphify-worktrees/3581-reclone-manifest/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/test_labeling.py::test_cluster_only_keeps_label_on_majority_membership_overlap -q --tb=short
```

title: fix(extract): keep a symbol that spells a sibling's file id (#4449)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4449.

When a JS file and a file with another extension share a stem in one folder (`x.mjs` plus `x.sql`) and the `.mjs` declares a variable named like the sibling's extension (`const sql = ...`), the `.mjs` file node ends up labelled `sql`. `graphify explain "x.mjs"` finds nothing.

`extract()` renames each file's old file-level id (its path with the extension: `esquema_x_sql` for `esquema/x.sql`) to the canonical one (`esquema_x`). It did that on every node, edge endpoint and raw call that spells the string, whichever file it belonged to. The JS variable `sql` is minted `{stem}_{name}`, which is also `esquema_x_sql`. So it was renamed too, salted next to the file node, and dedup dropped one of the two.

This PR renames a key only for the file that minted it, and only when another file's own symbol carries the same id. Every other key renames exactly as before.

```diff
 extract.py, the id_remap pass          (key esquema_x_sql -> esquema_x, minted by x.sql)

   node   sql           (x.mjs)  id esquema_x_sql
-    renamed to esquema_x         (its file did not mint the key)
+    kept as esquema_x_sql

   edge   contains  x.mjs -> sql        endpoint esquema_x_sql, source_file x.mjs
-    renamed: now x.mjs -> x.mjs, a self-loop
+    kept: still points at the sql variable

   edge   imports_from  x.mjs -> x.sql  endpoint esquema_x_sql, target_file x.sql
     renamed (x.sql minted the key), then salted onto the x.sql file node

   edge   imports  main.pas -> util.pas   (no target_file, main.pas holds no such node)
     renamed, as before
```

A key is contested only when a node of a different file carries it as one of that file's own symbol ids. For a contested key, an item is renamed if its file minted the key, kept if its file holds a node with that id, and renamed otherwise. Which file an item belongs to: a node, its `source_file`; an edge source, the edge's `source_file`; an edge target, the `target_file` stamp if there is one, else the edge's `source_file`; a `raw_calls` `caller_nid`, the record's `source_file`. Paths are compared resolved. Swift extension `nid`s and Objective-C field-table keys follow the same rule.

The later `ext_id_remap` pass already has an ownership guard (`owned_ids`, from #2231 and #2243). The first pass lacked it.

### Before / after

The issue's repro, `graphify extract . --code-only`:

```text
before:  [graphify] note: node 'esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x' was extracted twice from 'esquema/x.mjs'
         under different labels (keeping 'sql', dropping 'x.mjs').
         5 nodes, 4 edges
         esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x | sql          <- should be the file node "x.mjs"
         esquema_x_prueba        | prueba()
         esquema_x_sql_esquema_x | x.sql
         esquema_x_t             | t

after:   no note.   6 nodes, 5 edges
         esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x | x.mjs
         esquema_x_sql           | sql
         esquema_x_prueba        | prueba()
         esquema_x_sql_esquema_x | x.sql
         esquema_x_t             | t
```

Tests, `tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py`:

```text
before fix:  8 failed, 6 passed   (the 6 are guards that must not move)
after fix:   14 passed
```

The same cause hit other pairs. Each is a test:

- `x.ts` + `x.css` (`export const css = ...`): `css` took the file node's id, and nothing was salted because `x.css` has no nodes.
- `x.js` + `x.js.map` (`const js_map`): the variable was renamed to the id of `x.js.map`, a node that does not exist.
- `x.py` + `x.sql` (`def sql()`): the function was lost and its `calls` edge started at the file node.
- `x.swift` + `x.sql` with `struct sql` and `extension sql`: without the Swift hunk the fix would delete both file nodes, so the hunk is required, and a test covers it.

### Merge danger

**Door:** two-way. No stored format changes. Reverting is one commit.

**Blast radius:** narrow. The rename changes only for a key that a node of another file also carries as its own symbol id; every other key takes the old path.

- **Ids:** a corpus with no such clash gets the same ids as before. An affected corpus gets its swallowed symbol back under its own id, with its edges. An unchanged affected file keeps its old state in an existing `graph.json` until it is re-extracted.
- **Caches and skills:** the semantic cache key, the AST cache and the generated skill files do not change. `.mjs`, `.js`, `.ts` and similar are never in the AST cache (`_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`).
- **Cost:** one extra pass over `all_nodes` before the rename loop, dictionary lookups and memoized path resolution.
- **Open PRs:** none of #4344, #4353, #4371 touches `graphify/extract.py`.

### Not covered

- The Objective-C hunk has no test that reaches it. I could not build a case where an Objective-C class node holds a contested id. It runs only when some key is contested (`if contested:`), and the 5 existing objc tests pass with it.
- Unstamped cross-file imports to a same-stem file (for example Pascal `uses util` next to `util.js`) already end on a node that does not exist after salting, with or without this bug. A contested key now behaves like an uncontested one there. That dangling edge is not repaired.
- A symbol named like its own file's extension (`const js` in `x.js`, `def py()` in `z.py`) is lost. The same file owns the key, so this rename fix does not touch it. It needs its own issue.
- Stub nodes: I scanned graphify's own repo and its test fixtures for a node whose file did not mint the key. The one hit is `sample` in `tests/fixtures/sample.lpk`, a Lazarus unit reference minted with `sample.pas`'s old id. Before this fix it collided with the lpk's own file node; now it keeps its own id and its edge follows. Other languages and extractors were not scanned.
- Through `graphify extract .`, only siblings of a supported type (such as `.sql`) trigger the bug. `collect_files` skips `.css` and `.map`, so those two pairs need an explicit `extract([...])` call.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a symbol is never renamed because of a file it does not belong to, and everything that refers to a file node still ends on that file node.

- The issue repro runs with relative and absolute paths: three distinct ids for the file node, the variable and the `x.sql` file node.
- After `build()`, the labels `x.mjs`, `sql` and `x.sql` all exist.
- With `import raw from "./x.sql"` in `x.mjs`: `imports_from` ends on the `x.sql` file node, `contains` and `calls` end on the variable, and there is no self-loop.
- An unstamped Pascal import on a contested key ends exactly where the same edge ends with no clashing variable.
- Controls from the issue (`const db`, `const sql = 1`, no sibling, a sibling with another stem), and a Lazarus stub from a different stem, keep their ids.
- Gating only the node rename, and leaving edge endpoints on the old id-only rule, was tried and does not work: it leaves a `contains x.mjs -> x.mjs` self-loop and a `calls` edge that starts at the file node.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

## How was this tested?

Run with `PYTHONPATH=/var/tmp/wt-4449` and the repo venv's Python, so the code under test is this branch and not an editable install of another checkout. `graphify.__file__` was checked to be inside the worktree.

```text
# the issue repro (in /var/tmp/scratch-4449/repro2)
python -m graphify extract . --code-only
  before: 5 nodes, 4 edges, "extracted twice ... keeping 'sql', dropping 'x.mjs'"
  after:  6 nodes, 5 edges, no note

python -m pytest tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt-4449 -p no:cacheprovider
  before fix: 8 failed, 6 passed, 12 warnings in 1.61s
  after fix:  14 passed, 12 warnings in 2.31s

python -m pytest tests/test_swift_cross_file_calls.py tests/test_objc_field_table_remap.py -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt-4449b -p no:cacheprovider
  22 passed, 21 warnings in 1.55s

python -m pytest <the 18 covering files> -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt-4449c -p no:cacheprovider
  1183 passed, 295 warnings in 38.41s
  (test_extract, test_incremental, test_js_import_resolution, test_node_id_canonical,
   test_file_node_id_spec, test_astro_import_ids, test_extract_path_memo,
   test_cross_extension_reexport_self_cycle, test_id_normalization_contract,
   test_objc_field_table_remap, test_dotnet, test_languages, test_incomplete_build_guard,
   test_extraction_spec_ids, test_jsconfig_baseurl, test_package_json_subpath_imports,
   test_cjs_module_extension, test_typescript_module_extensions)

python -m pytest -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt-4449-full -p no:cacheprovider
  8011 passed, 14 skipped, 2055 warnings in 541.55s (0:09:01)

ruff check graphify/extract.py tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py
  All checks passed!
pyright graphify/extract.py
  131 errors, same as upstream/v8 (041771be); tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py: 0
```
