title: query answers repeat each node's file path; a compact form gives the same answer in ~1.7x fewer tokens
body:
## What happens

Every `NODE` line in a `graphify query` answer repeats the node's full source path. On a graph built without clustering, it also carries an empty `community=`. Measured on SWE-bench Lite answers (12 repos, AST-only graphs, default BFS and 2,000-token budget):

| part of an answer | share of its characters |
|---|---|
| NODE lines | 87% |
| the repeated `src=` paths | 36% |
| empty `community=` | 12% |
| EDGE lines | 3% |

A file with five nodes in the answer pays for its path five times. Agents read these answers on every query, so the repetition is spent over and over.

## Proposal

Add an opt-in compact form of the same answer. Write each file once, in the order of its first node, with its nodes beneath it in their original order. Leave out empty fields. Change nothing else: the budget cut, the notices and the order.

```
FILE django/db/models/query.py
  QuerySet L280
  filter() L1203
FILE django/db/models/sql/where.py
  WhereNode L14
```

On 600 answers (300 SWE-bench Lite issues x 2 queries), this gives the same files in the same order in 600 of 600, at 1.74x fewer tokens. A PR follows.

title: feat(query): --compact writes the same answer in ~1.7x fewer tokens (#4469)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4469. It adds `compact` to `graphify query` (CLI `--compact`, MCP `query_graph` `compact: true`): the same answer in about 1.7x fewer tokens.

The budget cut, the truncation notices and the node order are decided exactly as today. Only the `NODE` lines that survive the cut are rewritten:

- each source file appears once, in the order of its first node, with its nodes beneath it in their original order;
- the community most of a file's nodes share goes on the `FILE` line, and a node names its own community only when it differs;
- empty fields (an empty `community=`, no location) are left out;
- a file's own node (its label is the file name, at L1) is dropped when the `FILE` line already says everything it would. It stays when it carries a different community or a learning or attrs annotation.

```
FILE django/db/models/query.py community=Query API
  QuerySet L280
  filter() L1203
  Prefetch L2148 community=Prefetching
FILE (none)
  os
```

Default output is unchanged. `compact` defaults to false everywhere.

## Measured

300 SWE-bench Lite issues x 2 queries (the issue title, and the title plus 400 characters), 12 repos, default BFS depth 2, 2,000-token budget:

| graphs | answers | default | compact | saving | same files, same order |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AST-only (`update --no-cluster`) | 600 | 1,588 tokens | 912 tokens | **1.74x** (1.63–2.02x per repo) | 600 of 600 |
| clustered (`cluster-only`), 5 repos | 48 | 1,522 tokens | 1,030 tokens | **1.48x** | 48 of 48 |

Tokens are characters divided by 4. "Same files, same order" compares the distinct `src=` paths in printed order with the `FILE` lines.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** compact changes how the chosen nodes are written, never which nodes are chosen or in what file order.

`_subgraph_to_text` (31 callers) is untouched. Compaction is a separate pure pass, `_compact_answer(text, token_budget)`, over the answer `_subgraph_to_text` already rendered: same cut, same notices, same order. Only `_render_query` calls it, and only when `compact=True`. Every field it rewrites was already passed through `sanitize_label`. If any NODE line does not parse, the answer is returned unchanged. A complete answer that was over budget only in its default form loses the over-budget notice once its compact form fits.

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added an isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly. The gain is smaller on clustered graphs (1.48x), since communities differ more within a file there. Agents that parse `NODE ` lines keep the default.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run python -m pytest -q tests/test_query_compact.py        # 10 passed
uv run python -m pytest -q tests/test_query_*.py tests/test_benchmark_real_query.py   # 73 passed
uv run python -m pytest -q tests                              # 7815 passed, 7 failed: test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py,
                                                              # the same 7 fail on v8 without this change here
uv run ruff check graphify/serve.py graphify/cli.py tests/test_query_compact.py   # clean
```

The new tests check four things:
- `compact=False` returns the default answer;
- compact gives the same files in the same order and is shorter;
- labels and locations are kept, and empty fields are dropped;
- the file-node and community rules hold, a truncated answer compacts exactly the nodes the default shows, under the same notice, and learning and attrs annotations survive;
- a NODE line that does not parse leaves the whole answer unchanged.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] No skill fragments changed, so there are no generated artifacts to bless.
- [x] AST/structural extraction is untouched. The change is rendering only and deterministic.
- [x] No shell or Python interpolation; every field is already sanitized before compaction.
- [x] No API keys or local graph data included.
- [x] AI authorship disclosed in the commit message.

---

This comes from the same SWE-bench Lite study of `graphify query` as the seed-order fix (#4358) and `--seed` (#4289). It covers which files the query finds, in what order, and at what token cost. I have a few more measured changes to the query path from that work. I'd be glad to go through them with you, or to share the evaluation harness if it would help you judge query changes in general.

title: Inline explain reverses incoming canonical links and drops parallel relationships
body:
The shared `/graphify explain` fallback reverses incoming canonical links and drops parallel relationships

Graphify 0.9.91 exports canonical graph JSON with `directed: false`, while link `source`/`target` (or legacy `_src`/`_tgt`) retain the relationship direction. The shared query reference loads that JSON as an undirected NetworkX graph, then prints every neighbor as outgoing and chooses only the first parallel edge.

A synthetic graph with `Caller -> Center` relations `calls` and `uses` demonstrates both problems: explaining Center reports an outgoing relationship to Caller and omits one relation. The CLI already forces directed loading, but the shared skill fallback does not. A self-loop must also appear once, and the printed source location should come from the relationship's call site.

Reproduced on v8 commit `10130e79ed9caf8f60d998073e097531eaa1a395` and the shared fragment in PR #4370 at `84bd0c3c`. That PR fixes directed input but explicitly retains the old renderer for `directed: false`, leaving the canonical export case affected.

Expected: the shared explanation fallback follows stored link direction, retains every parallel relationship, deduplicates the self-loop, and displays available edge source locations. No real project graph or external provider is needed for reproduction.


Minimal synthetic input (`graphify-out/graph.json`):

```json
{
  "directed": false, "multigraph": true, "graph": {},
  "nodes": [{"id": "caller", "label": "Caller"}, {"id": "center", "label": "Center"}],
  "links": [
    {"source": "caller", "target": "center", "key": 0, "relation": "calls", "confidence": "EXTRACTED"},
    {"source": "caller", "target": "center", "key": 1, "relation": "uses", "confidence": "EXTRACTED"}
  ]
}
```

Run the inline Python fallback under `## For /graphify explain` in `graphify/skills/codex/references/query.md`, with `NODE_NAME` replaced by `Center`. It currently prints only one relationship, pointing from Center to Caller. Both stored relationships are incoming to Center and should be listed. Changing only `directed` to true is a control for the related PR's branch. The same shared fragment is rendered to the other progressive-host references.

This report contains only synthetic node names; no private graph or source code is needed.

title: fix(skills): preserve canonical explain direction and parallel edges
body:
The shared skill explanation fallback treats Graphify's canonical `directed: false` JSON as undirected, reversing incoming relationships and hiding parallel edges. Load the stored links directionally, as the CLI already does, and enumerate incoming/outgoing keyed edges while respecting legacy `_src` direction and deduplicating self-loops. Show edge call sites instead of neighboring definitions.

The change updates the authoritative shared query fragment and regenerates its 14 progressive-host references and expected snapshots. It leaves the independently maintained Aider/Devin monolith sources unchanged. PR #4370 is related, but preserves the broken canonical-input renderer; the synthetic regression fails on its current head too.

Validation: regression fails on unmodified v8 and the canonical case also fails on #4370; all 111 affected workflow tests pass. Final full suite: 7,835 passed, 170 skipped. All repository Ruff and generator checks pass. Added-test Pyright is clean; whole-repository Pyright retains the same 685 errors /6 warnings as unmodified v8. The owning refresh/network suites additionally pass all 136 tests with normal environment flags. No real graph generation, provider calls, installation changes, or private project material is involved.

Fixes #4471.

Size: 30 files, 635 insertions / 116 deletions (net +519): +55 regression-test lines and +464 documentation lines, mostly regenerated host references and snapshots.

title: JS/TS: class members whose names differ only by `_`, `$` or `#` collapse to one node (Go, C# and Python no longer do)
body:
## Summary

On v0.9.91, two JS/TS class members whose names normalize to the same id (`updateHash` / `_updateHash`, `close` / `#close`,
`set` / `$set`, `onBegin` / `_onBegin`) produce a single node. The first declaration wins and the second has no node at all.
Edges that belong to it are credited to the survivor: its body's outgoing calls, and its callers' incoming calls.

Go, C# and Python give two nodes for the same pairs (output below), so JS/TS is the remaining extractor with this behavior.
This is the JS/TS part of #2810, re-checked on the current release.

## Reproduction

Clean checkout of v0.9.91. One file per case; prints the member nodes:

```python
import pathlib, tempfile
from graphify.extract import extract

CASES = [
    ("JS  class { _onBegin; onBegin }", "a.js", "export class R { _onBegin(a) { return a; } onBegin(b) { return b; } }\n"),
    ("JS  class { #close; close }", "a.js", "export class W { #close(a) { return a; } close(b) { return this.#close(b); } }\n"),
    ("TS  class { $set; set }", "a.ts", "export declare class Q { $set(a: number): void; set(b: number): void; }\n"),
    ("JS  class { updateHash; _updateHash }", "a.js", "export class A {\n  updateHash() { return 1; }\n  _updateHash() { return 2; }\n}\n"),
    ("Py  class { _run; run }", "a.py", "class C:\n    def _run(self):\n        return 1\n    def run(self):\n        return 2\n"),
    ("Go  func Run; func run", "a.go", "package a\nfunc Run() int { return 1 }\nfunc run() int { return 2 }\n"),
    ("C#  class { Foo; _Foo }", "a.cs", "class A { public int Foo() { return 1; } public int _Foo() { return 2; } }\n"),
]
for name, fn, src in CASES:
    d = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    (d / fn).write_text(src, encoding="utf-8")
    r = extract([d / fn], cache_root=d, parallel=False)
    members = [n["label"] for n in r["nodes"] if n["label"].startswith(".") or n["label"].endswith("()")]
    print(f"{name:40} -> {members}")

# a caller of the lost member
d = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
(d / "a.js").write_text(
    "export class A {\n  updateHash() { return 1; }\n  _updateHash() { return 2; }\n}\n"
    "export function f() {\n  const a = new A();\n  return a._updateHash();\n}\n", encoding="utf-8")
r = extract([d / "a.js"], cache_root=d, parallel=False)
label = {n["id"]: n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]}
print("f() calls:", [label[e["target"]] for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "calls" and label[e["source"]] == "f()"
                     and label[e["target"]].endswith("()")])
```

Output:

```
JS  class { _onBegin; onBegin }          -> ['._onBegin()']
JS  class { #close; close }              -> ['.#close()']
TS  class { $set; set }                  -> ['.$set()']
JS  class { updateHash; _updateHash }    -> ['.updateHash()']
Py  class { _run; run }                  -> ['._run()', '.run()']
Go  func Run; func run                   -> ['Run()', 'run()']
C#  class { Foo; _Foo }                  -> ['.Foo()', '._Foo()']
f() calls: ['.updateHash()']
```

Expected: two member nodes in the four JS/TS rows, and `f()` calling `._updateHash()`.

## A real file

webpack 5.111.1 (`c47e84fc`), `lib/graph/ExportsInfo.js`. Both `ExportsInfo` and `ExportInfo` define a public `updateHash()`
(L1017, L1995) that delegates to `_updateHash()` (L1028, L2005):

```python
import pathlib, shutil, sys, tempfile
from graphify.extract import extract

src = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])  # webpack/lib/graph/ExportsInfo.js
d = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
shutil.copy(src, d / src.name)
r = extract([d / src.name], cache_root=d, parallel=False)
label = {n["id"]: n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]}
print("nodes:", sorted((n["source_location"], n["label"]) for n in r["nodes"] if "pdateHash" in n["label"]))
print("calls from L1028-1050 (the _updateHash body):",
      sorted((e["source_location"], label[e["source"]], label[e["target"]], e["target"]) for e in r["edges"]
             if e["relation"] == "calls" and e["source_location"] and 1028 <= int(e["source_location"][1:]) <= 1050))
```

```
nodes: [('L1017', '.updateHash()'), ('L1995', '.updateHash()')]
calls from L1028-1050 (the _updateHash body): [('L1032', '.updateHash()', '.hasInfo()', 'exportsinfo_exportinfo_hasinfo'), ('L1036', '.updateHash()', '.updateHash()', 'exportsinfo_exportinfo_updatehash')]
```

Neither `_updateHash` has a node. The call at L1032, inside `_updateHash`, is an edge from `.updateHash()`. At L1036,
`this._sideEffectsOnlyInfo._updateHash(...)` (that field is `new ExportInfo(...)`, L236) targets `ExportInfo.updateHash`
instead of `ExportInfo._updateHash`.

## Related

- #2810 (open): the same collision across JS, TS and Python on v0.9.45, including the discussion of which member should
  keep the plain id per axis.
- #3738 (open PR): TS/JS symbols that differ only by case (#3726), a different axis. Its branch head gives the same output
  as above for the four JS/TS rows.

title: fix(hooks): drop MERGE_HEAD guard from post-merge so real merges rebuild (#4463)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4463. The post-merge hook never rebuilt after a merge that makes a merge commit (`--no-ff`, diverged branches, `git pull`). Only fast-forward merges rebuilt.

`_MERGE_SCRIPT` exits early if `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists. On git 2.54, MERGE_HEAD is still on disk while post-merge runs, and git deletes it after the hook returns. A fast-forward never writes it, which is why those merges still worked. I reproduced this on Linux with git 2.54.0, so it isn't specific to Windows.

What the hook sees while it runs:

| Merge | MERGE_HEAD during post-merge | v8 hook |
|---|---|---|
| fast-forward | absent | rebuilds |
| `--no-ff` | present | exits |
| diverged branches | present | exits |
| `git pull` (diverged) | present | exits |

So the #2418 cleanup (removing symbols the union merge driver brings back) never ran on a real merge.

**Before** (`sh -x` on the installed hook, `git merge --no-ff feat`):

```text
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-merge ']'
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-apply ']'
+ '[' -f .git/MERGE_HEAD ']'
+ exit 0
```

**After:**

```text
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-merge ']'
+ '[' -d .git/rebase-apply ']'
+ '[' -f .git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD ']'
...
[graphify] Merge completed - launching background rebuild (log: ...)
```

```diff
 _MERGE_SCRIPT
-# This hook only fires after a merge completed cleanly, so MERGE_HEAD is
-# already gone by the time it runs -- ...
+# git leaves MERGE_HEAD on disk while post-merge runs and deletes it only
+# after the hook returns, so it must not be checked here (#4463). ...
 [ -d "$GIT_DIR/rebase-merge" ] && exit 0
 [ -d "$GIT_DIR/rebase-apply" ] && exit 0
-[ -f "$GIT_DIR/MERGE_HEAD" ] && exit 0
 [ -f "$GIT_DIR/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD" ] && exit 0
```

Git only runs post-merge after a successful merge, so the check never protected anything there. The same check in post-commit and post-checkout is unchanged. There it keeps those hooks quiet while a conflicted merge is being resolved.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Every merge that changes the tree triggers one post-merge rebuild. Hooks still stay quiet mid rebase or cherry-pick.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. One line removed from a generated hook script, no schema, cache or file-format change. Existing installs pick it up on the next `graphify hook install`.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Only the post-merge hook changes. After this, every `--no-ff`, diverged or `git pull` merge launches one detached background rebuild, which is what the hook was written to do. Users who merge often will see that rebuild run where it silently didn't before. `GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK=1` still turns it off.

**Limitations**

- Hooks already installed keep the old guard until the user re-runs `graphify hook install`.
- If an older git deletes MERGE_HEAD before running post-merge, the new test passes there even without the fix. I haven't checked which git versions behave that way.

## How was this tested?

Added `test_post_merge_hook_runs_after_a_real_merge`. It installs the hooks in a temp repo, runs `git merge --no-ff`, and checks that the hook prints the launch line. It fails on v8 and passes with the fix.

```text
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_hooks.py -q --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt   -> 147 passed
  same test on unchanged hooks.py                                                    -> 1 failed (new test)
.venv/bin/ruff check graphify/hooks.py tests/test_hooks.py                             -> All checks passed
```

I didn't run the full suite. The change is confined to the post-merge hook script.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (N/A: no skill fragments touched.)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.

title: query never uses the work memory: a question already answered, asked in other words, starts from scratch
body:
## What happens

`graphify save-result --outcome useful` and `graphify reflect --graph` already record which nodes answered which questions: the `.graphify_learning.json` sidecar keeps each lesson's provenance questions. `graphify query` only uses that memory to label nodes (`learning=...`). It never uses it to decide where to start. So a question that was already answered, asked again in other words by a teammate or the next session, starts from scratch. Keyword seeding often misses it, because the new wording doesn't name the same symbols.

On SWE-bench Lite (12 repos), with the older half of each repo's issues saved as useful answers (question = issue title, cited node = the fixed file) and each one asked again by its issue body, the default query puts the right file first for 26 of 140.

## Proposal

Add an opt-in mode that reads the sidecar. Nodes whose useful provenance questions are well covered by the new question's query terms become start nodes ahead of the keyword seeds:
- no embeddings, using the same `_query_terms`;
- stale lessons skipped, using the existing code fingerprint;
- explicit `--seed` values never overridden.

In the same setup it puts the right file first for 98 of 140, while new, never-taught questions are unchanged in the top 5. A PR follows.

title: feat(query): --learned starts from nodes that past useful answers to a similar question cited (#4477)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4477. It adds `learned` to `graphify query` (CLI `--learned`, MCP `query_graph` `learned: true`): the query starts from nodes that past useful answers to a similar question cited. This closes the loop `save-result` and `reflect` already open: the memory steers where the traversal starts, instead of only labelling nodes.

`_learned_seeds(G, question)` reads the work-memory overlay (the `.graphify_learning.json` sidecar from `graphify reflect --graph`). A node qualifies when all of these hold:
- its lesson is **preferred or tentative**, never contested, and dead-end provenance is ignored;
- its lesson is **not stale**: the existing code fingerprint says the code it was learned on is unchanged;
- one of its **useful** provenance questions has at least **40%** of its query terms covered by the new question, sharing at least two of them (or all of a shorter question's).

Up to 3 such nodes become start nodes ahead of the keyword seeds. They're ranked by coverage, then shared terms, then lesson score, then node id, so the order is deterministic. The header names them: `Learned (past useful answers): [...]`. Explicit `--seed` values are never overridden.

A running MCP server picks up new memory too. The graph cache keyed each graph on graph.json's stat, and `reflect` writes only the sidecar, so a server started before a `reflect` kept its old memory. The cache now also stats the sidecar, and when only the sidecar changed it re-reads the overlay onto the cached graph without reloading the graph. This also keeps the existing `learning=` annotations current.

No embeddings: the terms are `_query_terms`, the same ones keyword seeding uses. `_subgraph_to_text` is untouched. `learned` defaults to false, and the CLI only reads the sidecar when it's set, so default output is unchanged.

## Measured, end to end through the real pipeline

SWE-bench Lite, 12 repos, default BFS depth 2, 2,000-token budget.
- **Teaching:** for each repo, the older half of the issues went through `save_query_result(question=title, source_nodes=[the fixed file's node], outcome="useful")`, then `reflect(..., graph_path=...)`.
- **Asking:** each taught issue by its **body** (the same issue in other words), and each newer issue by its **title** (never taught).

| questions | right file first: default → learned | top 5: default → learned |
|---|---|---|
| same issue in other words (140) | 26 → **98** | 50 → **105** |
| new, never taught (145) | 44 → 42 | 70 → 70 |

**Where the 40% comes from:** the same issue in other words covers a median 0.44–0.50 of the taught question's terms, and a different issue covers 0.20–0.25. I chose 0.4 on django and checked it on sympy and matplotlib, which it wasn't tuned on.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariants:**
- without `learned`, the output is unchanged;
- with it, a node enters only on a fresh, positive lesson whose question the new one largely covers;
- explicit seeds win.

The sidecar is still a derived, read-only overlay: nothing is written to graph.json, and the query never writes the sidecar.

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added isolated boundary tests and an end-to-end test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly:
  - lexical matching only, so a rewording that shares under 40% of the taught question's terms is not recognised;
  - on new questions the right-file-first count moved 44 → 42 across 145, with the top 5 unchanged.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run python -m pytest -q tests/test_query_learned.py      # 10 passed
uv run python -m pytest -q tests -k "query or reflect or learning or memory or lesson or mcp or serve or ingest or save_result"
                                                            # 792 passed, 9 skipped
uv run ruff check graphify/serve.py graphify/cli.py tests/test_query_learned.py   # clean
```

The new tests cover:
- a question in other words finds the cited node, and an unrelated one doesn't;
- a single shared term is not enough;
- stale, contested, dead-end and vanished nodes never count;
- the ranking and the cap;
- the query starts from the learned node and names it in the header;
- `learned=False` gives the default answer even with a memory;
- explicit seeds are never overridden;
- the real pipeline, `save_query_result` → `reflect --graph` → query;
- a running server's cached graph sees a `reflect` done after it loaded (fails without the cache fix).

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] No skill fragments changed.
- [x] AST/structural extraction untouched; deterministic ordering throughout.
- [x] No shell or Python interpolation; header labels are taken from the graph, as for the existing `Start:` line.
- [x] No API keys or local graph data included.
- [x] AI authorship disclosed in the commit message.

---

This continues the same SWE-bench Lite work on `graphify query`: #4358 (seed order), #4289 (`--seed`) and #4470 (`--compact`). I'm happy to walk through the evaluation or extend it, for example to weigh `preferred` lessons more, or to make this the default once the memory loop is in wider use.

title: fix(js): keep class members that differ only by _, $ or # as separate nodes
body:
Fixes #4475

`make_id` strips `_`, `$` and `#`, so in a JS/TS class `updateHash` / `_updateHash`, `close` / `#close` and `set` / `$set` ended up with the same id. The second member got dropped, and its calls were credited to the one that survived. On webpack's `ExportsInfo.js` this hid both `_updateHash` methods.

This uses the same rule Python and C# already follow (`_underscore_salted_nid`, which now takes the private prefixes as a parameter, `_`/`$`/`#` for JS). Within each class body, names that collide are grouped. The one public name keeps its plain id and the other names get a salted id, so the result doesn't depend on declaration order. Members with no collision keep their current ids. Getter/setter pairs and overloads share a single name, so they're unaffected. The rule covers methods, TS signatures and abstract signatures, and arrow-function fields.

I also had to touch the TS cross-file member resolver. It looked up methods by the stripped key, so once the members were split, `c.set()` could resolve to `$set`. It now tries the exact member name first and falls back to the old key only when that misses. If more than one member normalizes to that key (e.g. `c._close()` on a class with `close` and `#close`), it emits no edge instead of guessing. Loose hits with a single candidate behave as before.

No cache bump is needed, because JS/TS files skip the AST cache (`_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`).

Tests: `tests/test_js_member_collisions.py` adds 24 tests, and 19 of them fail on v8. The full suite on 3.10, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 has the same 16 failures as unmodified v8 (`test_dm_*`, `test_security`). ruff is clean. I also ran `graphify extract --code-only` on a small TS project plus webpack's `ExportsInfo.js`. On v8 the private members are gone; with this change they show up as separate nodes with the right call edges.

Not covered here: static and instance members with the same name still share an id, which was already the case, and `Foo.prototype.x` assignments aren't included.

AI disclosure: I wrote this with help from an AI assistant (Grok Bot). I reviewed and tested all of it myself.

title: [Feature]: query: lead with the file that matches a natural-language question best, not the single best-scoring node
body:
### Problem or use case

On a natural-language question, `graphify query` starts from the single best-scoring node, and the renderer prints the start nodes first. On a question of three or more words, that node is often a test, whose name repeats the words of the bug report, or a same-named helper in another file. The file the question is about usually matches through several of its nodes at once, each scoring a little lower, so it ends up behind them. An agent reading the answer starts in the wrong file.

Measured on SWE-bench Lite: 285 issues across 12 repos, graphs from `graphify update`, default BFS depth 2, 2,000-token budget, with the fix's changed files as the key.
- Asked by the issue title, the fixed file is printed first for 78 of 285.
- Of the 207 misses, the first file is a test 58 times, a file in the same folder 41 times, and a file elsewhere 108 times.
- The fixed file is among the 50 best-scored nodes in 113 of those 207, so the ranking already holds it; it just doesn't lead.

### Proposed solution

For a question of three or more terms:
- sum the scores of the 50 best-scored candidates per file;
- put the best node of the best file first among the start nodes, and keep the other seeds in their order behind it;
- let a test file lead only when the question names tests, or when nothing else matches.

Short queries (identifier lookups) keep their exact match first. Explicit `--seed` values are untouched.

Fixed file printed first / in the first 3 / in the first 5 files, out of 285:

| | by title | by title + 400 characters |
|---|---|---|
| v8 today | 78 / 115 / 131 | 67 / 99 / 122 |
| proposed | **88 / 121 / 136** | **80 / 117 / 140** |

The constants were chosen on django and sympy. On the 10 other repos alone, right file first goes 24 → 27 by title and 20 → 29 by title + 400.

### Alternatives considered

- **The per-file sum alone** (test files may lead): 73 / 120 / 135 and 45 / 104 / 128. Test files gather many matching nodes, so the top-1 gets worse.
- **The test rule alone** (the best non-test node leads): 83 / 115 / 132 and 76 / 100 / 122. It helps the first file but not the top five.
- **Ranking the whole answer by file**: worse, at 27 / 75 / 97 by title.
- **Excluding test paths from seeding** (#2381): related. This proposal keeps test nodes as seeds and only stops one from leading a question that isn't about tests.

### Area

Graph building or querying

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

title: feat(query): a natural-language question leads with its best-matching file (#4480)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4480. On a natural-language question, the query now starts from the file that matches the question best, instead of the single best-scoring node. The renderer prints the start nodes first, so this is the file an agent reads first.

`_lead_by_file(G, ranked, terms)` runs on questions of three or more terms:
- it sums the scores of the 50 best-scored candidates per file;
- the best node of the best file becomes the first start node, and the other seeds from `_pick_seeds` keep their order behind it;
- a test file (`graphify.paths._is_test_path`) leads only when the question names tests (`test`, `pytest`, `fixture`, `spec`, …), or when only test files match;
- ties break by path, so the choice is deterministic.

Short queries return None and are unchanged, so an identifier lookup keeps its exact match first. Explicit `--seed` values never reach this code. `_pick_seeds`, `_score_query` and `_subgraph_to_text` are untouched.

## Measured

SWE-bench Lite: 285 issues across 12 repos, graphs from `graphify update`, default BFS depth 2, 2,000-token budget. Each count is how often the fix's changed file is printed first, in the first 3 files, and in the first 5:

| | by title | by title + 400 characters |
|---|---|---|
| v8 (0.9.91) | 78 / 115 / 131 | 67 / 99 / 122 |
| this PR | **88 / 121 / 136** | **80 / 117 / 140** |
| per-file sum alone | 73 / 120 / 135 | 45 / 104 / 128 |
| test rule alone | 83 / 115 / 132 | 76 / 100 / 122 |

Neither part works alone. Test files gather many matching nodes, so summing without the test rule makes the first file worse. The test rule without the sum fixes the first file but not the top five.

The constants (50 candidates, 3 terms) were chosen on django and sympy. On the 10 other repos alone, right file first goes 24 → 27 by title and 20 → 29 by title + 400.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariants:**
- a query of fewer than three terms renders exactly as before;
- the lead is always a node the ranking already scored, so a question that matches nothing still says so;
- the lead is deterministic: ties break by path;

  - in 94 of the 207 title misses on v8, the fixed file isn't among the 50 best-scored nodes at all, so no reordering can help those.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run python -m pytest -q tests/test_query_lead_file.py            # 10 passed
uv run python -m pytest -q tests -k "query or reflect or learning or memory or lesson or mcp or serve or ingest or save_result or benchmark"
                                                                    # 799 passed, 9 skipped
```

The new tests cover:

title: Godot support: one place for #535, #697, #2152 and the open GDScript PRs
body:
### Problem or use case

Godot projects still come out as a docs-only graph. `.gd`, `.tscn`, `.tres` and `project.godot` aren't in `CODE_EXTENSIONS`, so none of the game code reaches an extractor. On my Godot 4 project (27 scripts, 37 scenes/resources, 5 autoloads) the graph is all Markdown, and `explain`, `path` and `affected` can't see a single script.

This has come up three times (#535, #697, #2152), and there are six PRs for it: #669, #699, #1242, #1836, #1929, #3750. Five are still open and most of them conflict with `v8` by now. Each one covers part of the problem, and they answer the open questions differently. @A-Levin asked the main one in #535 (should this add a dependency?) and nobody has answered it yet. I'd like to pull all of it into one place so there's a single thing to say yes or no to.

### Proposed solution

One PR on current `v8` that combines them, with these answers:

1. **No new dependency.** `tree-sitter-language-pack==0.11.0` is already pinned for the `r` and `erlang` extras, and it bundles the GDScript grammar. A new `gdscript` extra points at the same pin. (`tree-sitter-gdscript` 6.1.0 is on PyPI now, but it only ships wheels for Linux x86_64, macOS arm64 and Windows x64.)
2. **Scenes don't need a grammar.** `.tscn`, `.tres` and `project.godot` share a small INI-like format. A line parser, like the fallback in #1929, can link a scene to its scripts and sub-scenes, a `[connection]` to the handler method on the attached script, and an autoload to its script.
3. **Cross-file lookups in a `LanguageResolver`, not in the per-file pass.** #3750 has the most complete semantics (autoloads, `class_name`, preload aliases, inherited methods and signals, `super`). But it reads the other scripts from disk while extracting one file, and keeps that index in module-level dicts. A cached `grunt.gd` result doesn't change when `actor.gd` gains or loses a method, and a long-running `graphify watch` never sees a new `class_name` or autoload. Doing the same lookups in a registered resolver over the whole corpus avoids both, and incremental builds get them through `resolution_context_nodes` like the other languages.
4. **Bare calls stay out of the shared name matcher.** A bare call in GDScript can only reach the script's own methods or an ancestor's. If it goes to the shared pass (#1836 does that), `refresh()` binds to an unrelated script that happens to define `refresh()`.
5. **Fail closed.** A `class_name` or autoload name only binds when exactly one script has it. Engine classes and builtins (`Node`, `add_child`, `print`) produce no edge and no stub.

### Alternatives considered

- Merging one of the existing PRs as it is. Each covers only part of this (scripts only, or scenes through a second grammar), and they would conflict with each other.
- A generic fallback for unknown extensions (option 2 in #535). Bigger blast radius, and it wouldn't give any structure.

### Area

Extraction / AST

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes. I've put it together and will link it here. Every earlier PR's author is a co-author on the commit.

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Only new extensions. IDs, cache entries and output for existing languages don't change. `.gd` needs `graphifyy[gdscript]`; without it, the existing missing-extra warning names the extra. Scenes and `project.godot` work with no extra.

### Additional context

Known gaps I'd leave for later: an autoload that points at a scene (`Hud="*res://hud.tscn"`) doesn't resolve calls to the scene's root script, `uid://` references are skipped, and `$Node` / `get_node()` receivers aren't resolved.

title: TS workspace: `exports["."]` pointing only into dist/ never falls back to src/ (gap left by #3834)
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.91 (macOS, Python 3.14, pnpm workspace, TypeScript)

## What happens

A workspace package whose `exports["."]` is a condition object pointing only into `dist/` never resolves to its source:

- **With a local build (`dist/` present):** `@acme/contracts` resolves to `packages/contracts/dist/index.js`. `dist/` is gitignored and outside the corpus, so every import becomes an external stub (`packages_contracts_dist_index_<symbol>`).
- **Clean clone (no `dist/`):** nothing resolves, and the import falls back to `ref_acme_contracts`.

In both cases, the app → package edges into `src/` never appear.

This is the same problem as #3834, but on the `exports` path. #3834 added the build-output fallback for `main`/`types`. When `exports["."]` is a dict, `_package_entry_candidates` returns only the `_exports_candidates(...)` list and never appends `src/index` / `index`. `_resolve_workspace_import` can then only choose between `dist/` files: it uses `build_fallback` when they exist and returns `None` when they don't. `tsc`-built workspace packages commonly use this `package.json` shape.

## Minimal repro

```
pnpm-workspace.yaml               packages: ['packages/*', 'apps/*']
.gitignore                        dist/
packages/contracts/package.json   {"name":"@acme/contracts","type":"module","main":"dist/index.js","types":"dist/index.d.ts",
                                   "exports":{".":{"import":"./dist/index.js","types":"./dist/index.d.ts"}}}
packages/contracts/src/index.ts   export * from './deal.js';
packages/contracts/src/deal.ts    export interface DealDto { id: string }
                                  export function makeDeal(id: string): DealDto { return { id }; }
apps/api/package.json             {"name":"@acme/api","dependencies":{"@acme/contracts":"workspace:*"}}
apps/api/src/route.ts             import { makeDeal, type DealDto } from '@acme/contracts';
                                  export function route(): DealDto { return makeDeal('1'); }
```

`graphify update .`. Edges from `apps_api_src_route`:

| state | edges |
|---|---|
| `dist/index.js` + `dist/index.d.ts` present | `imports_from packages_contracts_dist_index` (external), `imports packages_contracts_dist_index_dealdto` (external), `imports packages_contracts_dist_index_makedeal` (external) |
| no `dist/` | `imports_from ref_acme_contracts` only |
| with the fix below | `imports_from packages_contracts_src_index`, `imports packages_contracts_src_deal_dealdto`, `imports packages_contracts_src_deal_makedeal`, `calls packages_contracts_src_deal_makedeal` |

In a real 4-package pnpm repo, the fix took api ↔ contracts edges from 0 to 591, api ↔ db from 1 to 1,203, and web ↔ contracts from 2 to 68.

## Suggested fix

In `_package_entry_candidates`, after the `exports` candidates, append the source twin of each build-output candidate (`dist/foo.js` / `dist/foo.d.ts` → `src/foo`). For the root entry, also append `src/index` and `index`. `_resolve_workspace_import` already prefers non-build-output paths, so these win when they exist, and `dist/` stays the fallback. The same applies to subpath exports (`"./sub": {"import": "./dist/sub.js"}`).

This is a local monkey-patch of `_package_entry_candidates` that does exactly that, and it works:

```python
def patched(package_dir, subpath, platform=None):
    cands = list(orig(package_dir, subpath, platform))
    extra = [twin for c in cands if (twin := source_twin(c, package_dir))]  # dist/x(.d).ts|.js -> src/x
    if not subpath:
        extra += [package_dir / "src/index", package_dir / "index"]
    return cands + [e for e in extra if e not in cands]
```

Note for anyone patching in-process: `graphify update` re-execs itself as `python -m graphify` to pin `PYTHONHASHSEED` (#3641). That drops any monkey-patch unless `PYTHONHASHSEED` is already set.

title: TS barrel imports: original `<barrel>_<symbol>` edge survives the #1983 repoint and mints a phantom external stub
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.91 (macOS, Python 3.14, TypeScript)

## What happens

A named import through an `export *` barrel produces two `imports` edges:

1. the repointed edge to the defining symbol, `packages_contracts_src_deal_makedeal`, which is correct (#1983);
2. the original edge to `packages_contracts_src_index_makedeal`. That id is never defined, because the barrel defines nothing, so build mints it as an external stub.

The leftover edge is not removed after the repoint. Every barrel-imported symbol therefore gets a phantom external twin named after the barrel.

## Minimal repro

The same layout as the repro in #4485. Edges from `apps_api_src_route`, taken from `extract()` directly (resolver fixed so the import reaches `src/index.ts`):

```
packages/contracts/src/index.ts   export * from './deal.js';
packages/contracts/src/deal.ts    export interface DealDto { id: string }
                                  export function makeDeal(id: string): DealDto { return { id }; }
apps/api/src/route.ts             import { makeDeal, type DealDto } from '@acme/contracts';
```

```
imports packages_contracts_src_index_makedeal   (dangling → external stub)
imports packages_contracts_src_index_dealdto    (dangling → external stub)
imports packages_contracts_src_deal_makedeal
imports packages_contracts_src_deal_dealdto
```

## Scale

In a real repo (two apps, two workspace packages, ~1,000 files), the leftover edges added about 1,200 duplicate edges and about 380 phantom `*_src_index_*` external nodes. Those stubs then attract community membership and betweenness that belong to the real symbols.

## Suggested fix

When the barrel repoint succeeds for (source, symbol), drop the original edge to `<barrel_id>_<symbol>`. Alternatively, rewrite it in place instead of adding a second edge. When the chain ends in a third-party package (`export { eq } from 'drizzle-orm'`), keeping the external stub is reasonable.

title: fix(llm): pin source_file to the dispatched file in the extraction prompt
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #3377
Refs #2270, #2297, #2217, #3982, #2276

The native-backend extraction prompt (`_EXTRACTION_SYSTEM`) never says what `source_file` means. Its only guidance is the schema placeholder `"source_file":"relative/path"`. When a document cites, links, or describes another file (a `*Source: other.md*` line, a "Related:" list, a wiki link, a class a design doc specifies), the model often attributes the document's *own* entities to that file. What happens next depends on the run:

- **Incremental run, cited file not dispatched:** the #1895 out-of-scope filter drops the nodes, and the document silently loses them (#2297, #3377).
- **Cited file is code:** a doc-described API is attributed to the code file (#2270).
- **Path reconstructed from a mention:** a path that doesn't exist on disk reaches the graph (#2217).

The skill path already has a `source_file RULE (every node, edge, and hyperedge)` in `extraction-spec.md`. This adds the native-backend equivalent, just before the node-ID rules:

- `source_file` is the `path` attribute of the enclosing `<untrusted_source>` block, or the listed `source_file` for an image, copied character-for-character.
- A file named, linked, cited or described inside a source is a reference, not the source, and is never used as `source_file`.
- The reference is modelled as a node attributed to the enclosing file, linked by a `references` or `cites` edge. That avoids the foreign stub nodes #3947 describes.
- `source_file` is never invented, shortened, rewritten, or omitted (edges included, cf. #3982).

The #1895 filter is unchanged and remains the safety net. This lowers how often it has to fire.

**Why `Closes` for #3377:** its own suggested fix (b) is this change: "bias `source_file` attribution toward the literal file path being processed… over any path mentioned/linked within the document body".

**Why only `Refs` for the others:**
- **#2270:** this stops new doc-described APIs being attributed to the code file (the issue's fix 1), but the issue is about reconciliation. Semantic nodes already on a code file are never reconciled against its AST on `update`, and they're tagged `EXTRACTED`. A prompt can't fix either.
- **#2297:** it proposes keeping edges to nodes that already exist. This change keeps the content but doesn't link it to existing AST nodes.
- **#2217:** it asks for code-side enforcement, which is #2260.
- **#3982 and #2276:** they include code-path problems that a prompt can't fix.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

title: fix(js): drop the barrel-named import edge once the import resolves past it
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4486.

A named import through a barrel gets two `imports` edges. The structural extractor adds one to `<barrel>_<symbol>`, and `_apply_symbol_resolution_facts` adds another to the defining symbol. The barrel defines nothing, so with `export * from` the first edge dangles and build mints it as an external stub. With a named re-export (`export { x } from`), the first edge got repointed onto the defining symbol later, so the same import came out as two identical edges.

After the facts loop, the structural edge is dropped when its import resolves past the barrel to exactly one symbol the corpus owns. `exported_candidates` decides that, not `resolve_exported_origin`, so a barrel that exports one name from two modules keeps its edge on the barrel instead of guessing (`test_ambiguous_barrel_reexport_chain_does_not_guess` still holds). A chain that ends in a third-party package (`export { eq } from 'drizzle-orm'`) keeps its edge too, as the issue suggests.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: only an `imports` edge whose target names the barrel's own symbol disappears, and only when the same import already has its edge to the defining symbol. No edge is added and no node changes.

Checked on the tRPC monorepo (`packages/`, 511 `.ts` files, 48 barrels), comparing `extract()` before and after:

```text

edges added                                 0
imports edges removed, target undefined     767   (the phantom stubs)
imports edges removed, duplicate of a kept  243   (named re-export barrels)
imports edges removed, other                4     (see below)
```

The 4 others were the same phantom edge landing on a real node by id collision: `import { RootConfig } from '@trpc/server/unstable-core-do-not-import'` produced `packages_server_src_unstable_core_do_not_import_rootconfig`, which is the file node of `unstable-core-do-not-import/rootConfig.ts`. title: fix(js): fall back to src/ when a workspace package's exports name only dist/
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4485.

#3834 lets a workspace import whose `main`/`types` point into `dist/` fall through to `src/index`. When `exports["."]` is a condition object, `_package_entry_candidates` returns only the `exports` targets, so that fallback is never reached. For the common tsc-built shape

```json
"exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" } }
```

the import resolves to `dist/` (outside the corpus, so an external stub) when the package is built, and to nothing on a clean clone.

`_with_source_twins` appends, after the `exports` candidates, each build-output target's source twin (`dist/sub.js` / `dist/sub.d.ts` -> `src/sub`) and, for the root entry, `src/index` and `index`, the same pair the `main` path already tries. It applies to the root entry, `exports` given as a string, and subpath / wildcard entries, as the issue suggests. The twins come last, and `_resolve_workspace_import` already prefers a file outside build output, so source wins when it exists and `dist/` stays the fallback when it doesn't.

title: [Bug]: hooks never rebuild after a clean cherry-pick, a rebase, or git pull --rebase
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

After a clean `git cherry-pick`, a `git rebase` or a `git pull --rebase`, the hooks from `graphify hook install` never launch a rebuild. `graph.json` keeps describing the old code until the next plain commit or branch switch. There are two causes:

1. **Cherry-pick.** `post-commit` exits on `[ -f "$GIT_DIR/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD" ] && exit 0` (`graphify/hooks.py:448`). git still has `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` on disk while `post-commit` runs, even when the pick finished cleanly. This is the same pattern as #4463 with `MERGE_HEAD`. For a range (`git cherry-pick A..B`), every pick hits it, the last one included.
2. **Rebase.** During a rebase, `post-checkout` (`hooks.py:538`) and every `post-commit` (`hooks.py:445`) see `rebase-merge/` and exit. That part is intended. But git's hook for "the rebase is finished" is `post-rewrite`, and `install()` never installs one (`hooks.py:1031-1034` installs post-commit, post-checkout and post-merge only). So nothing rebuilds at the end. `git pull --rebase` goes the same way.

- A conflicted single pick works today: when you finish it with `--continue` or `git commit`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` is already gone, so `post-commit` rebuilds. Only the clean pick is broken.
- `git commit --amend` works: `post-commit` rebuilds once.

Expected: every git operation that changes the tree launches one rebuild when it finishes.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
git init -q -b main demo && cd demo
mkdir graphify-out && echo '{}' > graphify-out/graph.json
echo 'def a(): pass' > a.py && git add . && git commit -qm init
graphify hook install

# clean cherry-pick
export GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK=1
git checkout -qb side && echo 'def b(): pass' > b.py && git add . && git commit -qm b
git checkout -q main
unset GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK
git cherry-pick side 2>&1 | grep -c "launching background rebuild"   # 0

# rebase
export GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK=1
git checkout -qb feat && echo 'def f(): pass' > f.py && git add . && git commit -qm f
git checkout -q main && echo 'def m(): pass' > m.py && git add . && git commit -qm m
git checkout -q feat
unset GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK
git rebase main 2>&1 | grep -c "launching background rebuild"        # 0

# control
echo 'def z(): pass' > z.py && git add z.py
git commit -qm z 2>&1 | grep -c "launching background rebuild"       # 1
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Rebuild launch lines in git's output, v8 10130e79:

operation              rebuilds launched
plain commit           1
git commit --amend     1
git cherry-pick X      0
git cherry-pick A..B   0
git rebase main        0
git pull --rebase      0

State files on disk while each hook runs (probe hook, git 2.54.0):

operation           hook                       on disk
cherry-pick X       post-commit                CHERRY_PICK_HEAD
cherry-pick A..B    post-commit (every pick)   CHERRY_PICK_HEAD sequencer/
rebase main         post-checkout              rebase-merge/
                    post-commit (every pick)   rebase-merge/ CHERRY_PICK_HEAD
                    post-rewrite, $1=rebase    rebase-merge/
commit --amend      post-commit                none
                    post-rewrite, $1=amend     none
```

### Graphify version

0.9.91

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

git 2.54.0. No provider environment variables needed: the bug is in the shell hooks, before Python runs. Reproduced on a clean worktree of v8 10130e79.

### Additional context

Found while writing #4476 (the #4463 fix).

The probe shows two traps for a fix:
- A new `post-rewrite` hook can't copy the existing `rebase-merge` check, because `rebase-merge/` is still on disk when it runs.
- It must ignore `$1 = amend`, because `post-commit` already rebuilt.

Simply dropping the `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` check is not safe. With a tracked `graphify-out/graph.json`, a rebuild between picks dirties it. A later pick that touches it is then refused with `error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: graphify-out/graph.json`. v8 completes the same sequence.

What I tested locally, with 7 launch-count tests, 12 edge cases and `tests/test_hooks.py`, all passing:
- `post-commit`: skip while `sequencer/todo` has more than one line. On the last pick, diff from `$(cat "$GIT_DIR/sequencer/head")` (the HEAD before the sequence started) instead of `HEAD~1`. A range then gets one rebuild covering every pick, and nothing rebuilds mid-sequence.
- A `post-rewrite` hook that acts only on `$1 = rebase`.
- Results are the same stacked on #4476.

Two gaps remain, on v8 and with the fix: `--skip` on the last pick and `--quit`. git runs no hook when a sequence ends that way.

Side notes:
- `git commit --amend` on a repo's first commit never rebuilds. `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD` has no parent to diff against, and the fallback diff is empty.
- The comment "git exports GIT_DIR to hooks" doesn't hold in a normal repo. `GIT_DIR` was empty in every probe, so the `git rev-parse` fallback runs on every hook.

title: fix(hooks): rebuild after cherry-pick, rebase and pull --rebase (#4490)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4490. After a clean `git cherry-pick`, a `git rebase` or a `git pull --rebase`, the hooks never launched a rebuild, so `graph.json` described the old code until the next plain commit.

There are two causes:
- **Cherry-pick.** `post-commit` exited on `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, which git leaves on disk while the hook runs. This is the same trap as `MERGE_HEAD` in #4463.
- **Rebase.** `post-commit` and `post-checkout` skip while `rebase-merge/` exists, and no hook rebuilt at the end.

**Before** (the issue's repro, v8 `10130e79`):

```text
git cherry-pick side   -> 0 rebuilds
git rebase main        -> 0 rebuilds
git commit (control)   -> 1 rebuild
```

**After:**

```text
git cherry-pick side   -> 1 rebuild
git rebase main        -> 1 rebuild
git commit (control)   -> 1 rebuild
```

```text
post-commit:
  drop the CHERRY_PICK_HEAD exit
  if sequencer/todo exists and its first line is the commit just made:
    more than one step left  -> skip (mid range pick or revert)
    last step                -> CHANGED = diff sequencer/head..HEAD   (one rebuild covers the range)
  else: a stale sequencer/ (left by git reset --hard) is ignored -> normal HEAD~1 rebuild

post-rewrite (new hook):
  $1 = rebase -> launch an unscoped rebuild, like post-merge
  $1 = amend  -> exit (post-commit already rebuilt)
  no rebase-merge check: rebase-merge/ is still on disk when post-rewrite runs
```

Why only the last step rebuilds: if `graphify-out/graph.json` is tracked, a rebuild between picks rewrites it, and git then refuses a later pick that touches it (`Your local changes ... would be overwritten by merge: graphify-out/graph.json`). Just dropping the `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` check hit exactly that.

```diff
 graphify/hooks.py
   _HOOK_SCRIPT (post-commit)
-    [ -f "$GIT_DIR/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD" ] && exit 0
+    sequencer/todo check: skip mid-sequence, last step diffs from sequencer/head,
+    stale sequencer/ ignored
+  _REWRITE_SCRIPT (new), _REWRITE_HOOK_MARKER / _END
   install / uninstall / status
+    post-rewrite, same append/preserve handling as the other hooks
 graphify/__main__.py
   hook install help line names post-rewrite
```

### Existing tests this PR changes

| Test | Before | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_hooks_reuse_git_dir_from_env` | every script in `_HOOK_SCRIPTS` must contain `GIT_DIR=${GIT_DIR:-` | required only when the script reads `$GIT_DIR` | the new post-rewrite hook never reads `$GIT_DIR`; adding an unused line would be dead code |
| `_HOOK_SCRIPTS` parametrize list | 3 hooks | adds `post-rewrite` | the nohup, detach, worker-cap and quote-safety tests now cover the new hook too |

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Every git operation that changes the tree launches one rebuild when it finishes, and no hook rebuilds in the middle of a pick, revert or rebase sequence.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Shell hook scripts and one new hook file. No schema, cache or file-format change.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. This changes when the hooks launch a rebuild, not what a rebuild does:
- A clean cherry-pick, a rebase and `pull --rebase` now rebuild once.
- A range pick or revert rebuilds once at the end. A revert range used to rebuild after every step, with the same final graph.
- Plain commits, amends, checkouts and merges behave as before.
- `graphify hook install` now also writes `.git/hooks/post-rewrite`, appending to a user's existing one like the other hooks. `GRAPHIFY_SKIP_HOOK=1` turns it off.

**Limitations**

- `--skip` on the last pick and `--quit` still leave the graph stale, as on v8. git runs no hook when a sequence ends that way.
- If you edit the commit message while resolving a pick, or revert a `Revert "..."` commit, the todo line no longer matches HEAD. That step is then treated as a stale sequencer and rebuilds mid-sequence. It never skips a rebuild. This comes from reading the logic, not a test.
- Hooks already installed keep the old behaviour until `graphify hook install` is run again.
- This PR doesn't touch `post-merge`. #4476 fixes that, and the two merge cleanly in either order. Merged together, the hook tests give 184 passed.

## How was this tested?

New `tests/test_hooks_rewrite.py` runs real git operations against the installed hooks and counts rebuild launches. Four of its tests run a real build and check the graph contents. Against v8's hooks it gives 8 failed and 4 passed. The 4 that pass are behaviours v8 already gets right: the plain-commit control, amend, the tracked-graph sequence, and the abandoned pick. They're there to prove this PR doesn't break those cases.

- `test_single_cherry_pick_rebuilds_once`, `test_range_cherry_pick_rebuilds_once`, `test_rebase_rebuilds_once`, `test_pull_rebase_rebuilds_once`, `test_conflicted_rebase_continues_and_rebuilds_once`
- `test_range_cherry_pick_lands_every_new_function`, `test_skip_mid_range_rebuilds_the_picks_that_landed`, `test_revert_range_rebuilds_once_and_removes_the_functions`
- `test_tracked_graph_range_pick_with_conflict_completes` (fails if a rebuild runs between picks)
- `test_abandoned_range_pick_does_not_silence_later_commits` (a `sequencer/` left by `git reset --hard`)

`tests/test_hooks.py` adds install, uninstall, status and append/preserve tests for post-rewrite. It also adds hook-level tests for the sequencer logic: skip mid-sequence, the diff from `sequencer/head` covering every picked file, and the stale-todo cases.

```text
  tests/test_hooks_rewrite.py against v8 hooks.py                                         -> 8 failed, 4 passed
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q                                                 -> 8087 passed, 14 skipped
merged with #4476: tests/test_hooks.py tests/test_hooks_rewrite.py                         -> 184 passed
.venv/bin/ruff check graphify/hooks.py tests/test_hooks.py tests/test_hooks_rewrite.py     -> All checks passed
```

I also ran 12 hand-made edge cases (conflicted single pick, revert range, `--skip`, `--abort`, `--quit`, `rebase --exec`, tracked graph) against v8 and this branch, one run each. No case is worse than on v8. Two are fixed (`--skip` mid-range, `rebase --exec`), and the two gaps listed above are unchanged. Not tested: Windows, and a clean range racing the rebuild.

title: ID collision: a node with no source_file beats a sourced node with the same id (dedup._collision_rank)
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.91 (unchanged since at least 0.9.49)

When two nodes share an id that neither node's file encodes, so that `_defines_id` is False for both, `_collision_rank` ties them on every key but the reversed path. An empty `source_file` gives `()`, which sorts before any real path. So the source-less node always survives, and the sourced one is dropped:

```python
from graphify.dedup import deduplicate_entities, _collision_rank
sourced = {"id": "x", "label": "X", "source_file": "a.md"}
blank = {"id": "x", "label": "X"}
print(_collision_rank(sourced))   # (True, 1, 1, 'X', ('a.md',))
print(_collision_rank(blank))     # (True, 1, 1, 'X', ())
nodes, _ = deduplicate_entities([sourced, blank], [], communities={})
print(nodes)                      # [{'id': 'x', 'label': 'X'}]
```

It is the same in either arrival order, and graphify warns "keeping 'X' from '', dropping 'X' from 'a.md'". Source-less semantic nodes reach dedup because the out-of-scope filter (#1895) returns early on an empty `source_file`, and since such a node is never in the per-file semantic cache, every incremental merge carries it forward.

#3775/#3786 made "a real `source_file` beats none" the rule in `_pick_winner`. The exact-ID path does not have it (its reversed-path tie-break dates from #2532's fix in 0.9.36). A key such as `not node.get("source_file")` right after `not _defines_id(node)` would match. It changes no collision between two sourced nodes.

title: fix of module.import inheritence
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes: Graphify did not create `inherits` relationships for Python classes using a module-qualified base, for example:

    ```python
    import base as Module
    
    class Child(Module.BaseClass):
        pass
    ```

The extractor now records the qualified base and resolves it only through the matching import edge to a uniquely matching class in the imported file.

This prevents unsafe global bare-name matching: `external.BaseClass` does not link to an unrelated local `BaseClass`.

The protected invariant is: a module-qualified Python base may create an `inherits` edge only when its module qualifier resolves through the importing file’s matching `import` edge to exactly one source-backed class. Unresolved or ambiguous bases must not bind to an unrelated same-named class.
