title: fix: keep a wiki page relabelled only by case (#4508)
body:
Fixes #4508. A community relabelled only by case keeps its wiki article on case-insensitive filesystems. ## Summary On APFS (macOS) and NTFS (Windows), `groups.md` and `Groups.md` are one file. When a community's label changes from `groups` to `Groups`, the export writes into the existing entry, and the entry keeps its old case. The end-of-run orphan sweep compared names case-sensitively, so it deleted the page the run had just written. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Before B1["write Groups.md
(lands in groups.md)"] --> B2{"sweep: 'groups.md' in produced?"} B2 -- "no (case differs)" --> B3["unlink groups.md
index.md links to missing file"] end subgraph After A1["write Groups.md
(lands in groups.md)"] --> A2{"sweep: same device+inode
as a produced page?"} A2 -- yes --> A3["keep, rename to Groups.md"] A2 -- no --> A4["unlink stale page"] end ``` The sweep now matches files by identity (device and inode) instead of by name. A page this run wrote is kept, and its entry is renamed to the produced case. A stale page that is a separate file is still removed. Case-folding the names was the other option in the issue. It was rejected because on Linux `groups.md` and `Groups.md` are two real files, so folding would keep a stale page. Changed: `graphify/wiki.py` (the sweep block plus a `_file_id` helper, 21 lines added, 1 removed). New: `tests/test_wiki_case_only_relabel.py` (2 tests). ## Evidence - **Before:** `to_wiki` relabel `groups` → `Groups` on upstream `v8`: `['Groups.md', 'index.md', 'other.md']`, but `Groups.md` is not a readable file. `index.md` links to it. The test `test_case_only_relabel_keeps_article_on_case_insensitive_fs` fails with `AssertionError` on `Groups.md` `is_file()`. - **After:** same run on this branch: `Groups.md` is readable and `index.md` links to it. Test passes. ```text upstream v8 test_case_only_relabel_keeps_article_on_case_insensitive_fs FAILED test_case_only_relabel_drops_old_page_on_case_sensitive_fs passed this branch test_case_only_relabel_keeps_article_on_case_insensitive_fs passed test_case_only_relabel_drops_old_page_on_case_sensitive_fs passed wiki suites (test_wiki, link_filename_parity, idempotent_writes, path_length) 70 passed, 3 skipped full suite (tests/) 8394 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed ruff check graphify/wiki.py + new test All checks passed ``` The case-insensitive test simulates APFS and NTFS with a symlink, because the test machine runs Linux. The test helper `_case_insensitive_write` documents this. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way. The change touches only the orphan sweep. No file format, schema or cache key changes. Reverting restores the name-based sweep. **Blast radius:** wiki export (`to_wiki`). It runs on every `graphify` export that writes a wiki. Output is unchanged unless a case-only relabel happens. The sweep now calls `stat` on each `*.md` in the wiki folder, which is one extra call per page. A stat failure on a dangling symlink still removes the link as before. ## What does this PR do? Fixes #4508. On a case-insensitive filesystem, a relabel that changes only case used to delete the new article and leave `index.md` pointing at it. The sweep now keeps any page this run wrote, even when its on-disk name has the old case, and renames the entry to the new case. - Single-case runs are unchanged. Each produced page still gets one file. - A stale page that is a different file is still removed on every platform. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Documentation - [x] Tests or CI - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Security fix ## Verification & Invariants Invariant: after an export, every page `index.md` links to exists, and the sweep never deletes a page the run wrote. - [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide. - [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant. - [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary. - [x] Added a **regression test** that fails on upstream `v8` and passes here. - [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation. - [x] Documented **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly. ## How was this tested? ```text PYTHONPATH=/var/tmp/wt-4508 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp=/var/tmp/... -q tests/test_wiki_case_only_relabel.py -> 2 passed (this branch); 1 failed, 1 passed (upstream v8) full suite: 8394 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed ``` ## Limitations - Not run on a real APFS or NTFS volume. The test simulates one with a symlink. - Windows `st_ino` values were not checked on Python 3.14. On Windows the sweep relies on device and inode numbers that Python reports for each file. - `to_obsidian` has a similar case-only collision (#2650). This PR does not change it. ## Graphify-specific checklist - [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts. N/A: no skill fragments changed. - [x] AST/structural extraction is deterministic. N/A: wiki export only. - [x] I reviewed security implications: no shell or Python interpolation added. - [x] No API keys or local-only graph data are included. - [ ] I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages. N/A: no AI attribution in the commits.

title: graphify tree renders an empty viewer on any merged graph — merge-graphs drops source_file from every node
body:
## `graphify tree` renders an empty viewer on any merged graph — merge-graphs drops `source_file` from every node

### Summary

`graphify merge-graphs` produces a merged graph.json whose nodes carry `src`/`source` but **no `source_file`**. `graphify tree` filters on `source_file` (tree_html.py `build_tree`: `file_nodes = [n for n in nodes if n.get("source_file")]`), so running `tree` against a merged graph — the primary cross-repo use case for merge-graphs — always produces the "(empty graph)" viewer: title `(empty graph) — graphify tree viewer`, 15 KB output, zero hierarchy.

### Reproduction (graphify 0.9.92, Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.12)

```bash
# two normal per-repo extractions — both carry source_file:
$ graphify extract repo-a --code-only && graphify extract repo-b --code-only
$ python3 -c "import json; g=json.load(open('repo-a/graphify-out/graph.json')); \
    print(sum(1 for n in g['nodes'] if n.get('source_file')), '/', len(g['nodes']))"
3248 / 3461          # fine

# merge them:
$ graphify merge-graphs repo-a/graphify-out/graph.json repo-b/graphify-out/graph.json --out world/graphify-out/graph.json
$ python3 -c "import json; g=json.load(open('world/graphify-out/graph.json')); \
    print(sum(1 for n in g['nodes'] if n.get('source_file')), '/', len(g['nodes']))"
0 / 3607             # source_file gone on every node

$ graphify tree --graph world/graphify-out/graph.json --output WORLD_TREE.html
$ grep -o "<title>[^<]*</title>" WORLD_TREE.html
<title>(empty graph) — graphify tree viewer</title>
```

Merged node shape after the merge (attrs renamed, `source_file` dropped):

```json
{"id": "src_engine_dashboard_corvusdashboard_physicsbody", "label": "PhysicsBody",
 "type": "code", "community": 25, "community_name": "Dashboard Physics Engine",
 "src": "src/engine/dashboard/CorvusDas...", "origin": "ast", "source": "corvus-colony"}
```

Per-repo input node shape (what tree_html needs):

```json
{"id": "...", "label": "PhysicsBody", "_callable": true, ..., "source_file": "src/engine/dashboard/...", ...}
```

### Expected

`graphify tree` on a merged graph shows the full cross-repo hierarchy (repo-tag roots → dirs → symbols), the same way it does for a single-repo graph. Either:

- merge-graphs preserves `source_file` (repo-relative, as inputs store it), or
- `build_tree` falls back to `src`/`source` when `source_file` is absent.

### Workaround we're running

Re-derive `source_file` from `src` post-merge, then run `tree` without `--root` (paths are repo-relative so an absolute `--root` matches 0/134 files and raises):

```python
for n in g["nodes"]:
    if not n.get("source_file") and (n.get("src") or n.get("source")):
        n["source_file"] = str(n.get("src") or n.get("source"))
```

After this patch the same merged graph renders a correct 259 KB tree with both repo roots.

### Environment

- graphify 0.9.92 (`pip install --user graphifyy`), networkx merge path via `nx.compose` + `_prefix`
- Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.12.10
- Also worth noting: `--root` with an absolute path fails on merged graphs because stored paths are repo-relative ("error: --root ... matched 0 of 134 source files"), which compounds this — there's no way to anchor a merged tree without knowing each input's relative layout.

Real-world corpus: corvus-colony (3461 AST nodes) + semantic vault graph (164 nodes) = 3607-node merged world graph.

title: [Bug]: graphify tree ignores the repo tag on merged graphs: no per-repo roots, and identical relative paths from different repos collapse together
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

On a graph produced by `graphify merge-graphs`, `graphify tree` does not use the `repo` attribute that merge-graphs sets on every node. As a result:

1. There are no per-repo roots. The root is the common prefix of the repo-relative `source_file` values, which is empty when the repos differ, so the viewer title is "/".
2. Files that share a repo-relative path in different repos (e.g. `src/engine.py` in both) collapse into ONE file node with all of their symbols interleaved.

Expected: each repo tag is a top-level root with its own directory/file hierarchy built from that repo's relative paths. This would also fix `--root` on merged graphs, since each repo subtree would be anchored by its tag rather than an absolute path.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
1. Create two graph.json files (repo-a, repo-b) whose nodes have source_file "src/engine.py".
2. graphify merge-graphs repo-a/graphify-out/graph.json repo-b/graphify-out/graph.json --out world/graphify-out/graph.json
3. graphify tree --graph world/graphify-out/graph.json --output WORLD_TREE.html
4. Or inspect directly: python3 -c "import json; from graphify.tree_html import build_tree; print(build_tree(json.load(open('world/graphify-out/graph.json'))))"

Merged nodes do carry `repo: "repo-a"` / `"repo-b"` and `local_id`, so the data needed to group by repo is present. tree_html.py never reads `repo`.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
build_tree output (name, total_count), both repos sharing src/engine.py:

engine.py (8)
  src (8)
    engine.py (8)
      Cls (1) x4
      fn (1) x4

Symbols from repo-a and repo-b are mixed under one file node. Viewer title: "/".
```

### Graphify version

0.9.92

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables set. Reproduced on a fresh shallow clone of main at the 0.9.92 release commit.Also reproduced with a fresh uv venv; same result.”

### Additional context

Suggested fix: in build_tree (tree_html.py), if nodes carry `repo`, group by it first and build each repo's subtree independently under a root named after the tag. A test in tests/test_tree_html.py with two repos sharing a relative path would cover it.

Related to #4522 (merged-graph tree rendering), but a different cause: here source_file is intact and the `repo` tag is simply unused by `tree`.

title: fix(tree): group merged graphs by repo tag so repos get their own roots
body:
## What does this PR do?

`graphify tree` ignored the `repo` tag that `merge-graphs` / `global add` set on every node. On a merged graph that meant no per-repo roots, and files sharing a repo-relative path in different repos (e.g. `src/engine.py` in both) fused into one file node with their symbols interleaved.

When a graph carries two or more distinct `repo` tags, `build_tree` now builds one top-level root per repo, each with its own directory tree. Graphs with fewer than two tags are built exactly as before.

Fixes #4524 . Related to #4522 (different cause: there `source_file` is reported missing; here it is intact and the `repo` tag is simply unused by `tree`).

- Single-repo and untagged graphs render exactly as before (fewer than two distinct tags takes the old path).
- An explicit `--root` that matches no file still fails closed (#2534), now counted across all repos.
- Output is deterministic: repo roots are sorted by tag, no ambient state is read.

**State that could be invalidated:** none. `tree` only reads `graph.json` and writes an HTML file; no cache, graph, or generated artifact is touched.

title: fix(extract): route extern "C" headers to the C++ extractor
body:
## What does this PR do?

A C-API header written in the usual way:

```c
#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif
...
#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

has no `class ` / `namespace ` / `template` / `::` / access-specifier marker, so `_is_cpp_header` leaves it on `extract_c`. The tree-sitter C grammar rejects the `extern "C"` linkage block, and the header extracts **zero symbols**. graphify warns `syntax errors ... no symbols extracted`.

Real-world case: in whisper.cpp, `include/whisper.h` and `include/parakeet.h`, the project's whole public API, contributed nothing to the graph. The same happened to `src/coreml/whisper-encoder.h` and `src/openvino/whisper-openvino-encoder.h`.

The fix adds `b'extern "C"'` to `_CPP_HEADER_MARKERS`, so these headers go to `extract_cpp`. ObjC sniffing still takes priority, and plain C headers without the marker keep their `extract_c` routing.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a `.h` file is routed to an extractor whose grammar can parse it. A plain C header (`cpp_samedir/plain.h`) must stay on `extract_c`, and an ObjC header must stay on `extract_objc`.

On whisper.cpp (`src/` + `include/`):

| Header | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `include/whisper.h` | 0 symbols | 132 symbols |
| `include/parakeet.h` | 0 symbols | 47 symbols |

Graph result: 1134 → 1312 nodes. `whisper_full_params` became the 2nd most connected node, and `src/*.cpp → include/*.h` references now resolve.

Limitations:
- Bare function prototypes are still not emitted as nodes. Neither `extract_c` nor `extract_cpp` does that today, and this PR doesn't change it.
- A C header that uses `extern "C"` and also uses C++ keywords as identifiers would now go through the C++ grammar. That is the same trade-off the existing `class ` marker already makes.

title: extract_pdf_text returns "" silently on extraction failure (indistinguishable from an empty PDF)
body:
`extract_pdf_text` wraps its entire `PdfReader` loop in `except Exception: return ""`, so a malformed, encrypted, or otherwise unreadable PDF is **indistinguishable from a PDF with no text**. Downstream consumers (knowledge-graph builders, RAG indexers) count the document as "empty" rather than "failed" — in our pipeline this was a coverage-audit blind spot: files producing zero nodes with no trace anywhere, undetectable without re-running extraction manually.

**Suggested shape:** a warning to stderr naming the file and the exception class before returning (or a distinct sentinel), and a separate warning when the result is near-empty (so scanned/image-only PDFs are visible in logs rather than silently skipped — related: the OCR gap in #181).

We implemented both locally (a warning on failure; a near-empty-result warning; an optional OCR fallback for the latter case) and they turned silent data loss into visible, countable events. Small patch, happy to PR.

Environment: graphifyy 0.9.92, Python 3.13, pypdf (pdf extra).

title: feat(cli): show elapsed time and ETA in the semantic chunk progress line (#3179)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Step 1 of #3179 (https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/issues/3179#issuecomment-6235358169): the semantic extraction progress line now shows elapsed time and an estimate of the time left.

Before:
    [graphify extract] chunk 12/87 done
After:
    [graphify extract] chunk 12/87 done · 4m10s elapsed · ~26m left

- `N` is now the number of completed chunks, not `idx + 1`. With `max_concurrency > 1`, `on_chunk_done` fires in completion order, so the index of the chunk that just finished did not say how many were done.
- The time left is extrapolated from the average time per completed chunk. It is hidden while fewer than two chunks are done, because one sample is too noisy, and once all chunks are done.
- The clock starts right before `extract_corpus_parallel` is called.
- The formatting lives in a small pure function, `format_chunk_progress(done, total, elapsed_seconds)`, in `graphify/cli.py`, so it can be tested without a backend.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

- The progress line keeps its `[graphify extract] chunk N/total done` prefix. Only a suffix is added.
- `N` never goes backwards and ends at the number of successful chunks, even when chunks finish out of order. A regression test covers an out-of-order completion sequence.
- `_chunk_stats["succeeded"]`, which drives the "all chunks failed" exit and the partial-graph guard, is unchanged.
- No persisted or generated state is touched: no cache, manifest, graph.json or skill artifacts.

Limitations:
- `on_chunk_done` only fires for successful chunks. When some chunks fail, `done` never reaches `total`, and the estimate counts failed chunks as still pending. In that case the last line still shows `~Xm left`, followed by the existing failure summary. Counting failures as completed needs a hook in `llm.py`; I left that for a later step.
- Failure lines on stderr still print the chunk index (`chunk 5/87 failed`), while the progress line prints the completed count.

title: Node confidence is not normalized by the build (edges and hyperedges are)
body:
A consistency gap in the confidence handling: `_fold_confidence` normalizes the `confidence`/`confidence_score` pair on **edges** (build.py ~L540) and **hyperedges** (~L1223), but **nodes** get no equivalent fold. Node dicts pass through the build verbatim (validate.py checks only {id, label, file_type, source_file}; unknown fields are preserved), so when a prompt schema emits per-node confidence (as ours now does) the values reach graph.json unnormalized: a model emitting "extracted" (lowercase), a bare float, or a drifted string lands as-is, while the same drift on an edge is folded to the enum + score.

Suggested shape: fold nodes in the same place node aliases are folded (`_fold_node_aliases`), so nodes and edges share one normalization contract. No behavior change for graphs without node confidence.

Environment: graphifyy 0.9.92, Python 3.13. Found wiring node-level confidence through an extraction pipeline; our extractor carries a local backstop fold meanwhile.

title: fix(detect): warn when a PDF cannot be read instead of returning "" silently (#4527)
body:
Fixes #4527.

## What does this PR do?

`extract_pdf_text` wrapped its whole `PdfReader` loop in `except Exception: return ""`, so a malformed, truncated or encrypted PDF looked exactly like a PDF with no text. The file dropped out of the graph with no trace.

It still returns `""` (callers depend on that), but first it prints a warning naming the file and the error:

    [graphify] WARNING: could not extract text from docs/x.pdf (PdfStreamError: Stream has ended unexpectedly); it contributes no content to the graph.

The warning fires once per path. `detect()` counts words through this function and the semantic pass reads the file again, so without dedup one bad file would warn twice. This uses the same per-key set pattern as `_warned_ignore_encodings`. A readable PDF with no text layer is not a failure and stays silent.

title: fix(prs): read StatusContext state when classifying CI
body:
## What does this PR do?

`gh pr list --json statusCheckRollup` returns two kinds of entries:

- **CheckRun** (GitHub Actions and other check apps): `status` + `conclusion`
- **StatusContext** (commit statuses posted by external CI such as Jenkins, CircleCI or Buildkite): only `state`, one of `SUCCESS`, `FAILURE`, `ERROR`, `PENDING`, `EXPECTED`

`_parse_ci` only read `conclusion` and `status`, so every StatusContext entry was invisible:

    [StatusContext FAILURE]                      -> NONE     (should be FAILURE)
    [StatusContext ERROR]                        -> NONE     (should be FAILURE)
    [CheckRun SUCCESS, StatusContext FAILURE]    -> SUCCESS  (should be FAILURE)
    [StatusContext PENDING]                      -> NONE     (should be PENDING)

A PR whose external CI is red was classified READY instead of CI-FAIL in `graphify pr list`/`triage` and in the MCP `list_prs`/`triage_prs` tools, which all go through `_parse_ci`.

This folds `state` into the set of conclusions. `ERROR` counts as a failure, and `PENDING`/`EXPECTED` count as pending. Every existing `TestParseCi` case behaves the same.

title: fix(detect): classify extensionless scripts whose shebang names a versioned interpreter
body:
## What does this PR do?

Extensionless executables are classified by their shebang (`_shebang_interpreter` → `_SHEBANG_CODE_INTERPRETERS` in detect, `_SHEBANG_DISPATCH` in extract). The parser returned the interpreter exactly as written, and both tables list only generic names, so a script that names a specific version was dropped from the scan without a word:

    #!/usr/bin/env python3      -> python3     -> CODE
    #!/usr/bin/env python3.12   -> python3.12  -> None   (dropped)
    #!/usr/local/bin/python3.11 -> python3.11  -> None   (dropped)
    #!/usr/bin/python2.7        -> python2.7   -> None   (dropped)
    #!/usr/bin/lua5.4           -> lua5.4      -> None   (dropped)

Versioned shebangs are common in venv-installed and distro-packaged CLIs.

This adds `_strip_interpreter_version` and applies it in `_shebang_interpreter`, so detection and extractor dispatch both see the same name. It tries the name with its major version (`python3.12` → `python3`), then the bare name (`lua5.4` → `lua`, `php8.2` → `php`), and keeps the original when neither is a known code interpreter. An unknown `mytool2.1` stays `mytool2.1` and stays unclassified.

## Type of change

title: fix(export): export GraphML from a graph loaded as a MultiGraph
body:
## What does this PR do?

Since #4500, `to_json` writes `"multigraph": true` whenever graph.json holds parallel edges (for example `imports` and `calls` between the same two nodes), and `graphify export` loads such a file as an `nx.MultiGraph`. `to_graphml`'s attribute-coercion loop then crashed:

    for u, v in H.edges():
        for key, val in list(H.edges[u, v].items()):   # ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 3, got 2)

title: --update runbook: graph.json backup instruction comes after the diff that needs it, so the graph diff never runs
body:
**Version:** 0.9.92 (`v8` at 86c57be); also present in 0.9.91. All 14 split-platform `references/update.md` runbooks, plus the aider and devin monoliths.

## Problem

The `--update` runbook ends with a "show the graph diff" block that runs after Step 4. It compares `graphify-out/.graphify_old.json`, a backup of the pre-update `graph.json`, with the merged extraction. The instruction that creates that backup sits *after* the diff block, at the end of the section:

```
After Step 4, show the graph diff:
  ...diff block reads .graphify_old.json...
Before the merge step, save the old graph: `cp graphify-out/graph.json graphify-out/.graphify_old.json`
Clean up after: `rm -f graphify-out/.graphify_old.json`
```

An agent that follows the runbook from top to bottom reaches the backup sentence only after Step 4 has rewritten `graph.json`. By then it's too late:

- If the agent never takes the backup, the diff block's `if old_data:` has no `else`, so the diff prints nothing at all. The user gets no diff and no sign that one was skipped.
- If it takes the backup on reaching the sentence, the "old" graph is already the new one, and the diff reports no changes.

## Repro

1. Build a graph, change a code file, and run `/graphify . --update`, following `references/update.md` in order.
2. After Step 4 the diff block runs before any `.graphify_old.json` exists, and it prints nothing.

## Expected

The backup is taken before the merge, and the diff block says so when the backup is missing instead of skipping silently.

title: fix(skill): take the --update graph.json backup before the merge (#4539)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4539. The `--update` runbook told the agent to back up `graph.json` to `.graphify_old.json` only *after* the post-Step-4 diff block, at the end of the section. An agent following the runbook from top to bottom reached that sentence after Step 4 had already rewritten `graph.json`. So the diff block either found no backup and printed nothing (`if old_data:` had no `else`), or compared the new graph with itself.

What changed:
- **Backup moved:** the backup sentence now leads the merge block, in `fragments/references/shared/update.md` (14 split-platform hosts) and in the aider and devin monoliths. It also says why: Step 4 rewrites `graph.json`.
- **Missing backup reported:** the diff block now prints `No pre-update backup at ... - graph diff skipped.` instead of skipping in silence.
- **Cleanup line:** the trailing line is now only the cleanup instruction, "Clean up after the diff".
- **Round-trip guard:** `gen.py` adds `_is_graph_diff_backup_order_fix_line` to `_SANCTIONED_MONOLITH_DIFFS`, so `--monolith-roundtrip` accepts the monolith change. It matches only this fix's lines: the old and new backup sentences, the cleanup line, the notice `print`, and the one bare `else:` line. A bare `else:` can't be narrowed further, because the round-trip compares lines one at a time.
- **Paths unchanged:** aider keeps its backup in the project root, as before.

Fixes #4524. Refs #4522.

## Problem

- **#4524:** `graphify tree` never read the `repo` tag that `merge-graphs` puts on every node. The root became the empty common prefix of repo-relative paths, so the title was `/`. Worse, `src/engine.py` in two repos collapsed into a single file node with both repos' symbols mixed together.
- **#4522:** I couldn't reproduce the merge step on current v8, because `merge-graphs` keeps `source_file` (a test now pins that). The reported node shape (`src` / `origin` / `source`, where `source` holds a repo name) isn't written anywhere in graphify. The real problem is that a graph where no node has a `source_file` rendered a blank `(empty graph)` viewer with no explanation.

## Change (`graphify/tree_html.py`)

- `build_tree` groups file nodes by `repo`. Each repo gets its own top-level root, built from that repo's paths. A graph with no `repo` tags builds exactly as before.
- An explicit `--root` now applies inside each repo. The zero-match guard from #2534 counts matches across all repos.
- A non-empty graph where no node has a `source_file` now raises `ValueError`, and the CLI exits 1 with the reason, the same way an unmatched `--root` does. A truly empty graph still returns `(empty graph)`.
- I did **not** add a fallback to `src`/`source`: in #4522's data, `source` is a repo name, not a path, so the fallback would guess wrong.

## Tests (`tests/test_tree_html.py`)

- Two repos sharing `src/engine.py` produce two separate file nodes with their own symbols, under per-repo roots.
- The root label, `--root` on a merged graph (zero match raises; a repo-relative root matches in each repo), and the no-`source_file` error.
- End to end: `merge-graphs` keeps `source_file`, and `tree` on its output draws both repo roots.
- 5 of the new tests fail on the old code. All 13 tests in the file pass.

`ruff` and `pyright` are clean on the touched files. On the full suite (Windows), 18 tests fail both with and without this change, in modules unrelated to tree (`test_ext_tagged_id_clash`, `test_skillgen_input_path_injection`, memoization and getcwd tests, and others), so they come from the environment.

title: fix(cache): read and write AST cache entries via extended-length paths on Windows
body:
## Problem

On Windows, `graphify extract` fails outright when the project sits under a deep path:

```
[graphify extract] AST extraction failed: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'C:\Users\...\graphify-out\cache\ast\v0.9.92-s17-ga8b351668dbe\893e91a9…e84647.yd0um411.tmp'
```

The AST cache path `<root>\graphify-out\cache\ast\v<ver>-s<schema>-g<grammars>\<64 hex>.json` adds about 120 characters to the root. `save_cached`'s `mkstemp` temp name (`<hash>.<random>.tmp`) adds 8 more. When the root is about 140 characters or longer, the path passes the 260-character MAX_PATH limit and the write raises. A long user name under the default `%TEMP%` is enough to trigger it. In my repro the temp path was 268 characters; the same project under `Desktop\` worked.

## Change

- Move `detect._os_path`, the `\?\` extended-length helper from #1655, to `paths.os_long_path` so `cache.py` can share it. `detect._os_path` stays as an alias, so its callers and the tests in `test_long_path_hashing.py` are unchanged.
- `save_cached` creates the temp file and writes the entry through the extended-length path. `load_cached` reads the entry, and the legacy fallback entry, the same way.
- Cache keys don't change: `_normalize_path` still strips the prefix.
- On other platforms `os_long_path` returns the path unchanged.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_cache_long_paths.py` (Windows only, like the MAX_PATH test in `test_atomic_writes.py`). It saves and loads an AST entry whose path is past MAX_PATH while its folder can still be created, and checks that no `.tmp` file is left behind. It fails without the fix (`FileNotFoundError` in `tempfile.mkstemp`) and passes with it.
- Manual check: `graphify extract` in the deep folder now writes `graph.json`, and a second run reports `1 files cached/unchanged`.
- `ruff` is clean. `pyright` reports the same 14 existing errors in `detect.py` as untouched v8.
- Full suite on Windows: 17 tests fail. They also fail on untouched v8 on the same machine (`test_ext_tagged_id_clash`, `test_skillgen_input_path_injection`, the memoization getcwd tests, and others). No new failures.

## Not covered

Only `load_cached`/`save_cached` use the long-path form. Other cache writers (the stat index, `cached_files`'s glob) write into the cache folder rather than to a 64-hex file name, so they stay under the limit in this case.

title: fix: stop silent semantic-extraction loss on the ollama and skill paths (#3982, #3988, #2225, #1758)
body:
Fixes the silent-loss paths in #3982, #2225 and #1758, and the remaining JSON-mode gap in #3988. Each fix is its own commit, so they can be reviewed (or split out) separately.

## Problem

All four issues are the same failure: semantic work is produced and paid for, then lost without a message, and the loss is never retried.

- **#3982 (library / ollama path):** `save_semantic_cache` keys every item by `source_file` and skips items without one. A small local model fills it on nodes but leaves it off most edges (99% vs 4% in the report). It also invents paths that name no real file. Either way the items vanished from the cache, and a chunk "succeeded" while persisting almost nothing.
- **#2225 (skill path):** the Read tool returns at most 2000 lines per call and doesn't say when it stops early. A subagent with 20-25 files skimmed the dense ones. The partial extraction then replaced the file's complete nodes, and the manifest stamped the file done.
- **#1758 (skill path):** with chunks sized only by file count, a dense chunk's single JSON write overran the ~64k output-token limit. The chunk file was never written, and Step B3 blamed a read-only dispatch.
- **#3988:** there was no way to constrain ollama to valid JSON. The reporter measured 39 nodes without the constraint and 73 with it on the same input.

## Implementation

**`fix(cache)` — #3982** (`graphify/cache.py`, `save_semantic_cache`)
- An edge with no `source_file` takes its source node's file, else its target's. A hyperedge takes its members' file only when they all agree. Whatever is still unkeyed is counted in one `RuntimeWarning`.
- When the chunk dispatched exactly **one** file, a `source_file` that names no real file can only be that file, so the group is attributed to it. A path that *is* a real undispatched file stays out of scope (#1757). With several dispatched files nothing is guessed: the group is skipped, as before.
- The #2973 basename recovery also tries a case-insensitive match, still only on a unique candidate.
- Groups that resolve to the same file (a recovered group plus the group that named the file correctly) are folded into one before writing. Before, the second write replaced the first unless `merge_existing` was set. This also closes the same hole in the existing #2973 recovery.
- A scoped write that loses some (not all) groups now warns with a count. The all-skipped warning names model-invented paths as a second cause.
- `test_save_semantic_cache_drops_edges_to_ghost_file_nodes` now dispatches two files so it keeps testing #1916's dangling-edge pruning. With a single dispatched file, the ghost path is now attributed instead of skipped. That is the intended behaviour change.

**`feat(llm)` — #3988** (`graphify/llm.py`)
- Opt-in `GRAPHIFY_OLLAMA_JSON=1` sends `format: "json"` on the native `/api/chat` request and `response_format: {"type": "json_object"}` on the `/v1` fallback. It is opt-in, like `GRAPHIFY_OLLAMA_SEED`, because the `/v1` servers behind this backend (LM Studio, llama.cpp) do not all accept `response_format`. It applies to extraction only, not to labeling or dedup calls.

**`fix(skill)` — #1758, plus the aider/devin side of #2225** (`tools/skillgen/fragments/…`, regenerated)
- v8 has since landed its own #2225 fix (8a982c4a): Step B1's line budget, the read-every-file rule, and the `coverage` report that Step B3.5 checks. The merge takes v8's text for those, so this PR no longer changes Step B1 or the shared read rule.
- Step B3 now gives the output-token cap as the other cause of a missing chunk file. It re-splits that chunk into thirds and keeps splitting any part that fails, never resending a chunk unchanged. A chunk that is already one file is not retried: the run warns, leaves it out, and the file is re-queued next run.
- The extraction prompts (verbose and compact) ask for compact JSON, so the output limit is spent on content.
- The aider and devin monoliths, which v8's fix did not touch, get the line-bounded chunking, the full-read rule and the Step B3 change. Those lines are sanctioned in `gen.py` (`_is_chunk_budget_fix_line`).

## Already on v8 (not changed here)

- **#2658:** pypdf is already floored at `>=6.16.1` and locked at 6.18.1, so all six advisories are cleared. This PR leaves it alone.
- **#3988:** the `extra_body` merge (69d87e0f) and the opt-in seed (`GRAPHIFY_OLLAMA_SEED`) are already on v8.
- **#3982 point 4:** ollama now talks to the native `/api/chat` (#4413), which honours `num_predict`.

## Limitations / not covered

- #3982 point 2 (`on_chunk_done` receiving the chunk's allowlist) is not changed. With the backfill and single-file attribution in the library, a caller no longer needs to re-persist a corrected chunk.
- The #3982 fixes apply to the semantic **cache**. `graph.json` itself still carries whatever `source_file` the model returned, as before.
- On Windows, a recovered group's rewritten `source_file` is the absolute, case-folded path. The existing #2973 recovery produces the same spelling. Not touched here.
- #3988's request for a supported extraction-prompt hook is out of scope.
- The #2225/#1758 changes are prompt and runbook rules, not a machine check. Nothing verifies that a returned chunk covered each file to its end. That would need a coverage signal the chunk JSON doesn't carry today.
- I did not run a live ollama or a live Claude Code skill run. The ollama request shape is covered by the request-capture tests, and the skill text by the skillgen tests.

## Verification

Commands run (Windows 10, Python 3.12, `uv run --frozen`):

- `pytest tests/test_semantic_cache_source_file_backfill.py`: 7 passed. Without the cache fix, 5 of 7 fail; the other 2 are guard tests for unchanged behaviour.
- `pytest tests/test_llm_backends.py -k "json_mode or seed"`: passed. Without the llm change, both JSON-mode tests fail.
- `pytest tests/test_skillgen.py`: 69 passed. With the fragments reverted, both new tests fail.
- `pytest tests`: 8281 passed, 127 skipped, 13 failed. The same 13 fail on unmodified `upstream/v8` in this environment: my Windows home path contains a space, and bash resolves paths through WSL (`/mnt/c/...`). None of them touches a changed file.
- `ruff check .`: all checks passed.
- `pyright graphify/cache.py graphify/llm.py tools/skillgen/gen.py`: 16 errors. All are already on v8 (`cache.py` has 5 both before and after), and none is in a changed line.
- `python -m tools.skillgen --check`, `--monolith-roundtrip`, `--audit-coverage`, `--schema-singleton`, `--always-on-roundtrip`: all OK.

title: feat(cli): add cochange, check (with SARIF) and dead-code graph analyses
body:
## What does this PR do?

It adds three read-only analysis commands over `graph.json`. Each lives in its own module with its own tests, and they share only the CLI wiring. They're bundled here at my request; I'm happy to split them into three PRs if reviewers prefer.

| Command | Module | Answers |
|---|---|---|
| `graphify cochange` | `graphify/cochange.py` | Which files change together but share no graph edge (hidden coupling)? Which files are high-churn hubs? |
| `graphify check` | `graphify/rules.py` | Does the code break the architecture rules in `graphify-rules.json`? Exits non-zero and can emit SARIF for GitHub code scanning |
| `graphify dead-code` | `graphify/deadcode.py` | Which callables does no live code reach? |

**Prior art check:** I searched open and closed PRs and issues for co-change/churn/hotspots, SARIF/architecture rules/forbidden imports, and dead code/reachability. Nothing overlaps. The closest items are Graphify-Labs/graphify#2950 (ingesting *external* OpenGrep findings, the opposite direction from `check`) and Graphify-Labs/graphify#2649 (removing some unused code by hand rather than adding an analysis).

All three outputs below come from running the commands on this repository.

---

### `graphify cochange`

```
$ graphify cochange --top 3
Co-change analysis: 489 commits (11 bulk commits skipped)

Hidden coupling (change together, no graph edge):
  CHANGELOG.md <-> pyproject.toml  26 commits, confidence 0.87
  graphify/cache.py <-> graphify/extractors/engine.py  7 commits, confidence 0.33
  graphify/cli.py <-> graphify/extractors/engine.py  7 commits, confidence 0.19

Hotspots (commits x linked files):
  graphify/extract.py  101 commits x 263 linked files
  CHANGELOG.md  35 commits x 67 linked files
  graphify/build.py  20 commits x 102 linked files
```

- Runs `git log --no-merges --relative --name-only` as an argv list, with no shell. `--relative` lines up a graph built from a subdirectory with git's paths, and `core.quotepath=false` keeps non-ASCII paths readable. The record separator uses git's `%x1e` escape because a raw control byte in argv breaks on Windows.
- **Corpus boundary:** only files already present as a graph `source_file` are considered, so detection and `.graphifyignore` stay the single definition of the corpus.
- Nothing is written back to `graph.json`: co-change is a statistical signal, never an edge.
- Options: `--since`, `--max-commits` (default 500), `--min-count` (3), `--max-files-per-commit` (30), `--top` (20), `--graph`, `--json`.
- Limitations: renames are not followed; bulk commits are skipped; any edge between two files counts as linked, including doc→code mentions.

### `graphify check`

```json
{
  "forbid": [
    {"from": "src/ui/*", "to": "src/db/*", "message": "UI must go through the service layer"},
    {"from": "src/core/*", "to": "src/plugins/*", "relations": ["imports_from"]}
  ],
  "no_import_cycles": true,
  "max_cycle_length": 5,
  "include_inferred": false
}
```

```
$ graphify check --sarif graphify.sarif
graphify check: 1 violation
  src/ui/view.py:12  [graphify/forbidden-dependency] src/ui/view.py -> src/db/repo.py (calls): UI must go through the service layer
```

- Exit codes: `0` no violations, `1` violations, `2` unreadable graph or invalid rules file. `--sarif PATH` writes SARIF 2.1.0 that `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` accepts. The rules file defaults to `<root>/graphify-rules.json`; use `--rules` to point elsewhere.
- The rules file is validated at the trust boundary (unknown keys, wrong types). Forbid rules default to `affected.DEFAULT_AFFECTED_RELATIONS` minus `defines`. Cycle checks reuse `analyze.find_import_cycles`, so the deferred and type-only exclusions still apply.
- **Fail-closed by default:** only `EXTRACTED` code-to-code edges count. `"include_inferred": true` opts in `INFERRED` edges; `AMBIGUOUS` edges and document mentions never count. Why: on graphify's own graph, a `graphify/* → tests/*` rule that counted every edge produced 45 bogus violations (31 INFERRED doc references and 12 INFERRED `indirect_call` resolutions). The default produces 0.
- Limitations: globs are `fnmatch` on repo-relative POSIX paths, and `*` also matches `/`. Unindexed files and unresolved calls can't violate a rule. SARIF URIs are relative to the scanned root.

### `graphify dead-code`

```
$ graphify dead-code
161 dead-code candidates (unreached callables; verify before deleting):
  graphify/build.py
     L1947  _norm_label()
     L1955  deduplicate_by_label()
  graphify/callflow_html.py
      L911  node_in_section()
  ...
```

- Walks usage edges forward (calls, references, imports, inheritance, …) starting from non-callable code nodes, such as files and modules whose top-level code runs on import, and from callables shaped like entry points. A callable the walk never reaches is a candidate. Unlike a zero-callers scan, this also catches **islands**: functions that only call each other.
- On graphify itself it surfaces `deduplicate_by_label`, `prune_dangling_edges`, `_auto_follow_symlinks` and `node_in_section`; a repo-wide grep confirms none of them has a caller. This PR doesn't delete them.
- It stays conservative wherever the AST pass is known to leave calls unresolved. I found these cases by running it on this repo: the first naive version flagged about 650 symbols, mostly nested helpers. In the current version:
  - a live function keeps its nested functions live
  - a live class keeps its methods live
  - methods that override a supertype member (via `affected._overridden_members`), dunders, `main` and `test*` names, and anything in a test file are never candidates
  - documents never make code live
  - `AMBIGUOUS` edges still count as usage
- Limitations: the output is *candidates*, never proof. Framework dispatch the AST can't see makes live code look dead: decorators, reflection, functions passed as values, packaging entry points. Public library API is reported, and dead methods of a live class are not.

---

## Verification

```
uv run pytest tests/test_cochange.py tests/test_check_rules.py tests/test_dead_code.py tests/test_cli_help.py tests/test_affected_cli.py -q
# 49 passed
uv run pytest tests -q
# 8056 passed, 305 skipped, 17 failed - every one of the 17 also fails on unmodified v8 (same environment); none touch these modules
uv run ruff check graphify tests/test_cochange.py tests/test_check_rules.py tests/test_dead_code.py tests/test_cli_help.py
# All checks passed
uv run pyright graphify/cochange.py graphify/rules.py graphify/deadcode.py tests/test_cochange.py tests/test_check_rules.py tests/test_dead_code.py
# 0 errors
```

`pyright graphify/cli.py` reports "dispatch_command is too complex to analyze". That error is identical on unmodified `v8` and not introduced here.

Determinism: every output is sorted on stable keys (file, line, label). No command writes graph or cache state.

title: [Enhancement]: Version and help checks should never rewrite skill files
body:
## Request

Please make informational invocations such as `graphify --version`, `graphify -v`, `graphify version`, `graphify --help`, `graphify -h`, and subcommand help read-only with respect to installed skills and integrations.

They should not replace `SKILL.md`, refresh references, create skill backups, or update `.graphify_version`, even when an installed skill is older than the package and automatic refresh is otherwise enabled.

## Confirmed observation

Environment: `graphifyy==0.9.92`, Python 3.14, macOS on Apple Silicon.

An existing Graphify skill for Gemini CLI had a `.graphify_version` marker of `0.9.91`. During package verification, running `graphify --version` printed `graphify 0.9.92` but also automatically refreshed that skill and its version marker, preserving the old skill in `SKILL.md.bak`.

In this particular case, the instruction-file difference was harmless: two backticks were removed around `graphify update` in a code comment. I am **not** claiming functional damage or settings corruption. The concern is that merely inspecting the package version performed writes to assistant instructions.

The files were restored. A launcher that sets `GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1` now prevents the writes in our setup; the opt-out works.

**Evidence boundary:** the write was observed during `--version`. I did not run an unguarded `--help` against the live skill directory. Source inspection of `_run_cli()` in the installed 0.9.92 package shows `_refresh_stale_skills()` and `_refresh_v1_opencode_plugins()` running before the top-level version/help early returns. Help is included in the requested read-only contract, not presented as a separately reproduced live incident.

## Why this matters

Version/help checks are used by diagnostics, health checks, package managers, and automation to inspect an installation. They should be safe to run without preparing an environment-variable workaround or anticipating changes to assistant instructions.

Locally customized or centrally managed skills may intentionally differ from the package. A backup is useful, but it does not make a metadata query read-only.

I understand that automatic refresh is intentional and addresses stale instructions after a package upgrade (#1805). This request is narrower: exempt informational invocations, without removing the refresh feature from normal operational commands.

## Suggested implementation and regression checks

Handle version/help requests before any integration-refresh routine that can write files. Existing read-only staleness warnings could remain.

For tests, use disposable home/project directories with stale skill markers and locally modified skill text; no installer needs to run. For each informational invocation, assert that:

- Existing skill files, references, and version stamps retain their bytes.
- No backup, lock, or replacement skill/reference files are created as a side effect of auto-refresh.
- Normal version/help output and exit behavior remain intact.
- This holds without `GRAPHIFY_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1`, including when its inherited value is `0`.
- Representative Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini skill destinations are covered.

## Related issues

- #1805: why stale-skill detection/refresh is valuable.
- #3144: preserving customized skills during installation; related concern, but this request concerns informational commands rather than an explicit install.
- #821: earlier help-flag execution behavior; this request specifically concerns integration auto-refresh before informational early returns.

No changes to graph schemas, extraction behavior, cache semantics, or the content of generated skills are requested.

title: GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING is ignored by the claude backend, so thinking eats max_tokens and extraction truncates
body:
## Summary

`GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING` is honoured by the OpenAI-compatible and Ollama paths but not by the native Claude backend (`--backend claude`). `_call_claude` in `graphify/llm.py` sends no `thinking` parameter at all, so on Claude models that think by default the thinking tokens count against the response's `max_tokens` (16384 from `BACKENDS["claude"]`), and extraction truncates or comes back hollow.

## Version

graphifyy 0.9.92, `anthropic` 1.15.0, Python 3.14, `graphify extract . --backend claude --model claude-haiku-5-5 --force` (headless, in CI).

## What happens

Claude Haiku 5.5 runs adaptive thinking by default. With `_call_claude` sending no `thinking` setting, a full extraction of a docs-heavy repo (347 semantic files) logged:

- 38 chunks `truncated at depth N, splitting into halves`, 11 of them `still truncated at recursion depth 3 (max 3) — partial result kept`;
- 3 hollow responses, one of them `content=no nodes/edges, output_tokens=13347` — almost all of the 16384 spent on thinking;
- `64/347 dispatched file(s) produced no nodes`, after which the shrink guard (correctly) refused to overwrite the existing graph.

Setting `GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING=1` changes nothing on this path, because `_thinking_disabled_via_env()` is read in the OpenAI-compatible and Ollama request builders but not in `_call_claude` (nor in the `claude` branch of the labelling call).

## Expected

`GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING=1` sends `thinking={"type": "disabled"}` on the Claude backend too, in both `_call_claude` and the labelling call, as it does elsewhere. Claude Haiku 5.5 accepts disabled thinking at its default effort. Optionally, a way to set `output_config.effort` (for example `GRAPHIFY_CLAUDE_EFFORT`) would let users keep thinking on but bounded.

## Workaround we are using

`GRAPHIFY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=21000` plus `--token-budget 15000`, so each smaller chunk's response, thinking included, fits. It works around the symptom; it does not stop thinking being billed on a structured-extraction task that does not need it.

## Related

#730 (hardcoded max_tokens), #2880 (hollow responses), #3671 (labelling discards `finish_reason='length'`).

title: Semantic extraction cannot tell a file with no entities from an omitted file, so empty files arm the shrink guard
body:
## Summary

Semantic extraction cannot tell "the model found no entities in this file" from "the model omitted this file". Both end up in `uncovered_files`, both make the extraction count as incomplete, and both keep the shrink guard armed, so a file that legitimately has nothing to extract (a `robots.txt`, an HTML shell, a short compose file) fails a headless `graphify extract` exactly as a dropped file does, on every run.

## Version

graphifyy 0.9.92, `graphify extract . --backend claude --model claude-haiku-5-5 --force` in CI.

## What happens

In `llm.py`, after the chunks are merged, a dispatched file is "uncovered" when no returned node has it as `source_file`:

```
uncovered = sorted(p for p in dispatched if p.resolve() not in {c.resolve() for c in covered})
...
WARNING: N/M dispatched file(s) produced no nodes and are absent from the graph ... The model returned a response but omitted them; a re-run will retry them.
```

The extraction schema in `_EXTRACTION_SYSTEM` has no way for the model to say "I read this file and there is nothing to extract": the response is only `nodes`, `edges` and `hyperedges`, and nothing asks for one acknowledgement per file. So absence of nodes is the only signal, and it means two different things.

On our run, 18 of 330 files were uncovered with no truncation and no hollow responses ("the model returned complete, well-formed responses that simply did not address every file"). The ones named include `README.md`, `docker-compose.yml` and two `index.html` files; HTML shells and compose files may well have nothing worth a node. The guard then refused the write, which is correct for omitted files and wrong for empty ones, and a re-run with the same inputs reproduces it.

Two smaller points in the same place:

- The warning prints five names and "+N more"; the full list is not written anywhere a CI job can read after the run (it lives in memory as `uncovered_files`).
- A node the model mis-attributes to another file's `source_file` also leaves the real file uncovered, which is a third case behind the same signal.

## Expected

One of:

1. A per-file acknowledgement in the schema (for example `"files": [{"path": "...", "entities": 0}]`, or a required file-level node per dispatched file), so "read, nothing to extract" is distinguishable from "not addressed", and only the latter counts as incomplete; or
2. A file-level node always minted for each dispatched document (as the AST pass does for code), so coverage is never zero for a file the model actually read.

And the full uncovered list written to a file in `graphify-out/` (or printed in full under a flag), so CI can report it.

## Workaround we are using

Keeping non-markdown files out of the semantic pass with `.graphifyignore` patterns, and a smaller `--token-budget` so fewer files share a chunk.

## Related

#3412 (the unverified-semantic-shrink guard has no verification path), #4546 (thinking on the claude backend).

title: fix(python): Stop counting binary media as text
body:
## TLDR

Stop counting binary media as text. This avoids unnecessary file reads and bogus corpus word counts while keeping media discoverable. Includes regression tests and documentation.

## AI Generated explanation

### What does this PR do?

`count_words()` previously decoded binary images as text, producing meaningless word counts and unnecessary processing. Cached counts could preserve those incorrect totals.

This patch:
- Returns zero for supported binary image, audio and video files without reading them.
- Bypasses their legacy cached word counts during detection.
- Preserves media discovery, SVG text handling and PDF/Office conversion.

Related: #1110 and #3261.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor

title: Metal/CUDA GPU qualifiers (kernel, __global__, device, ...) mint sourceless god nodes
body:
### Version
v8 @ 0.9.92 (86c57be8)

### Problem
Metal (`.metal`) and CUDA (`.cu`/`.cuh`) are C++-derived GPU languages and route through the C++ extractor. Their address-space / execution-space / function qualifiers are not part of the C++ grammar, so tree-sitter-cpp parses a leading qualifier as the declaration's `type_identifier` (the real type is pushed into an `ERROR` node). `_cpp_collect_type_refs` then emits the qualifier as a type reference, and each one becomes a **sourceless, corpus-shared god node** that every shader/kernel `references`.

This violates the provenance invariant (a node with no `source_file`), and the hubs pollute god-node rankings in `analyze`.

### Reproduce
Extract the shipped fixtures:

```python
from graphify.extract import extract_cpp
r = extract_cpp("tests/fixtures/sample.metal")
print(sorted({n["label"] for n in r["nodes"] if not n.get("source_file")}))
# -> ['constant', 'device', 'kernel', 'uint']
r = extract_cpp("tests/fixtures/sample.cu")
print(sorted({n["label"] for n in r["nodes"] if not n.get("source_file")}))
# -> ['__device__', '__global__', ...]  (ids normalize to global/device/host)
```

### Expected vs actual
- Expected: `kernel`, `device`, `constant`, `__global__`, `__device__`, `__host__`, ... are language keywords, not corpus symbols, and should not become nodes. The genuine struct `Vec3` should still resolve.
- Actual: each qualifier is a sourceless god node with a false `references` edge.

### Notes
These words are legal identifiers in plain C++/CUDA (e.g. a user type named `device`), so any filter must be keyed by the GPU-dialect file extension, not applied to `.cpp`/`.cc`/`.h`.

title: Swift 5.9 macro declarations are dropped entirely (and #name calls are lost)
body:
### Version
v8 @ 0.9.92 (86c57be8)

### Problem
Swift 5.9 macros never enter the graph. `macro stringify(...) = #externalMacro(...)` parses as a `macro_declaration` (freestanding or attached), which is in neither the Swift `function_types` nor `class_types`, so the whole declaration is dropped — the symbol is invisible. A freestanding call site `#stringify(...)` parses as a `macro_invocation` (not a `call_expression`), so its call edge is lost too.

### Reproduce
```python
from graphify.extract import extract_swift
# macro stringify<T>(_ v: T) -> (T, String) = #externalMacro(module: "M", type: "S")
# func use() { let x = #stringify(1 + 1) }
```
The `stringify` macro node is absent and `use() -> stringify` is not an edge.

### Expected vs actual
- Expected: the macro declaration is a node; a freestanding `#name(...)` call resolves to it; calls inside the macro's arguments still resolve.
- Actual: declaration dropped; invocation unresolved.

### Notes
`macro_declaration` has no `name` field — the name is a bare `simple_identifier` child (already covered by Swift's `name_fallback_child_types`). Attached-macro *usage* (`@AddCompletion` on a type) is an attribute, not a `macro_invocation`, and can stay unresolved (fail-closed).

title: C# delegate declarations dropped, so in-file references mint a sourceless god node
body:
### Version
v8 @ 0.9.92 (86c57be8)

### Problem
A C# `delegate` is a named type, but `delegate_declaration` is in neither `class_types` nor `function_types`, so the declaration is dropped. A field or parameter typed as the delegate still resolves the name through `ensure_named_node`, which mints a **sourceless** stub and points the `references` edge at it — even though the delegate is declared in the same file.

That violates the provenance invariant: a real source-backed declaration must not lose to a sourceless god node (and the bare-id stub becomes a cross-file hub shared by every same-named reference in the corpus).

### Reproduce
```csharp
public delegate int BinOp(int a, int b);
public class Calc {
    public BinOp Op;
    public int Apply(BinOp f, int x) { return f(x, x); }
}
```
`BinOp` appears as a node with empty `source_file`, and `Calc`/`Apply` reference that sourceless node.

### Expected vs actual
- Expected: `BinOp` is a sourced node in the declaring file; references bind to it.
- Actual: `BinOp` is sourceless; references bind to the stub.

### Notes
`delegate_declaration` has a `name` field and no body, so it emits a clean empty type node (no phantom members). Delegate parameter/return type refs and delegate-instance invocation resolution are out of scope.

title: fix(cpp): don't mint sourceless god nodes for Metal/CUDA GPU qualifiers
body:
Closes #4550.

### Problem
Metal (`.metal`) and CUDA (`.cu`/`.cuh`) are C++-derived GPU languages that route through the C++ extractor, but their qualifiers are not part of the C++ grammar:

- Metal address-space / function qualifiers: `device`, `constant`, `threadgroup`, `thread`, `kernel`, `vertex`, `fragment`, ...
- CUDA execution-space / memory qualifiers: `__global__`, `__device__`, `__host__`, `__shared__`, `__constant__`, `__forceinline__`, ...

tree-sitter-cpp parses a leading qualifier as the declaration's `type_identifier` (the real type is pushed into an `ERROR` node), and `_cpp_collect_type_refs` emitted it as a type reference. Each qualifier then became a sourceless, corpus-shared god node that every shader/kernel `references` (e.g. `kernel`/`device`/`constant` on `sample.metal`, `__global__`/`__device__`/`__host__` on `sample.cu`). That is a provenance violation (a node with no `source_file`), and the hubs pollute god-node rankings in `analyze`.

### Implementation
- Add a fixed, per-extension set of GPU-dialect qualifier keywords (`_CPP_DIALECT_TYPE_QUALIFIERS`, keyed by `.metal` / `.cu` / `.cuh`).
- Thread a `dialect_quals` skip set into `_cpp_collect_type_refs` (the single choke point for every `type_identifier` emission) and compute it once per file from the extension.
- Plain `.cpp`/`.cc`/`.h` are untouched — there these words are legal identifiers and still resolve as real user types.

Genuine user types in the shader/kernel (the `Vec3` struct) are preserved.

### Verification
- New regressions in `tests/test_languages.py`: `test_metal_qualifiers_do_not_mint_sourceless_god_nodes`, `test_cuda_execution_space_qualifiers_do_not_mint_sourceless_god_nodes` (both fail on pre-fix v8, pass after).
- `uv`/venv commands run:
  - `python -m pytest tests/ -q --ignore=tests/test_security.py` → 8331 passed, 15 skipped (deselecting the live-DNS security tests and the built-wheel test that need a network/packaged wheel).
  - `ruff check .` → clean.
  - `pyright graphify/extractors/engine.py` → unchanged from baseline (0 added).

### Limitations
`constant Foo* p` buries the real `Foo` type inside the `ERROR` node, so `Foo` is not recovered; this change only removes the bogus qualifier node, it does not add the lost type reference. Metal scalar vector types (`uint`, `float4`) are left as-is (they are types, not qualifiers).

title: fix(swift): extract macro declarations and resolve freestanding macro calls
body:
Closes #4551.

### Problem
Swift 5.9 macros were dropped entirely. `macro stringify(...) = #externalMacro(...)` parses as a `macro_declaration` (freestanding or attached), which was in neither `function_types` nor `class_types`, so the symbol never entered the graph. A freestanding call `#stringify(...)` parses as a `macro_invocation`, not a `call_expression`, so its call edge was lost too.

- Add `macro_invocation` to `call_types` and give it a callee branch in `walk_calls`: a freestanding macro is a free top-level symbol, resolved by bare name with no `self` receiver. Calls inside the macro's arguments (`#stringify(helper())`) still resolve because `walk_calls` recurses into the invocation's children.

title: fix(llm): honour GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING on the claude backend (#4546)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4546.

`GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING` reaches the OpenAI-compatible and Ollama requests, but `_call_claude` and the `claude` branch of `_call_llm` (labelling) sent no `thinking` setting at all. On Claude models that think by default, such as Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Opus 5, the thinking tokens come out of `max_tokens`, so extraction truncates or comes back hollow and the flag changes nothing.

Both calls now go through `_create_claude_message`, which adds `thinking={"type": "disabled"}` when the flag is set. With the flag unset the request is exactly as before.

Not every Claude model accepts that. Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and the Fable models answer `disabled` with a 400 (on Sonnet 5.5 the off switch is `{"type": "between_tools"}`), and a gateway behind `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` may reject the field too. The flag is a single environment variable, so someone who set it for deepseek would otherwise get a 400 on every chunk after switching to one of those models. So on a 400 the call is retried once without `thinking`. If that succeeds, the model is remembered for the rest of the run and a one-line note goes to stderr. If the retry fails as well, the 400 had another cause and is raised as before. This mirrors how `_OLLAMA_NO_NATIVE` remembers servers without `/api/chat`.

I left `GRAPHIFY_CLAUDE_EFFORT` (the optional part of the issue) out. It's a separate knob, and on Opus 5.5, where thinking can't be turned off, it's the only control there is, so it may be worth its own PR.

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation

- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: with `GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING` unset, the Claude request is unchanged; with it set, no Claude model that worked before starts failing.

- A model that 400s on it is answered by the retry without `thinking`, and the next call skips straight to that (3 requests for 2 calls, not 4).
- A 400 for another reason still raises and doesn't mark the model.

title: Obsidian wikilinks prefixed with the scan folder name are dropped (no references edge)
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.48, `graphify update . --force` on an Obsidian vault folder.

**Problem:** `_vault_lookup` in `graphify/extractors/markdown.py` resolves `[[Note]]` and `[[wiki/Note]]`, but a vault-root style link that starts with the scan folder's own name, such as `[[Corp/wiki/Delta|alias]]` or `[[Corp/wiki/Fox]]` (scan root is `Corp/`), never becomes a `references` edge. Obsidian vaults whose scan root is a sub-folder of the vault commonly link this way, because Obsidian shows the vault-relative path. The path suffix `Corp/wiki/Fox.md` never matches the root-relative index entry `wiki/Fox.md`, so the edge is dropped silently.

**Repro:**
```
Corp/Alpha.md      [[Bravo]] [[wiki/Charlie]] [[Corp/wiki/Delta|alias]] [[Corp/wiki/Fox]]
Corp/Bravo.md
Corp/wiki/{Charlie,Delta,Fox}.md
cd Corp && graphify update . --force
```
Expected: 4 references edges from Alpha. Actual: 2 (Bravo, Charlie).

On a real vault folder this meant about 119 `references` edges against about 10,000 `contains` edges; after the fix the same folder produced about 1,500.

**Suggested fix:** in `_vault_lookup`, when no candidate matches and the first path segment equals the scan root's folder name, retry with that segment stripped:
```python
if not matches and len(parts) > 1 and parts[0] == _nfc(Path(root).name):
    suffix2 = "/".join(parts[1:])
    matches = [c for c in candidates if c[1] == suffix2 or c[1].endswith("/" + suffix2)]
```

title: fix(markdown): resolve wikilinks that start with the scan root's own folders (#4559)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4559.

Obsidian writes a wikilink's path from the vault root. When graphify scans a folder below the vault, links from inside that folder start with the folder's own name, e.g. `[[Corp/wiki/Fox]]` while scanning `Corp/`. `_vault_lookup` matches path-qualified targets as suffixes of root-relative paths (`wiki/Fox.md`), so `Corp/wiki/Fox.md` never matched and the `references` edge was dropped.

When the existing lookup finds nothing, `_vault_lookup` now drops the longest leading run of path segments that equals the end of the scan root's own path, and matches the rest exactly as a root-relative path. That covers the issue's case and a scan root more than one level below the vault (`[[Projects/Corp/wiki/Fox]]`). The issue suggested matching the rest as a suffix again; I made it exact, since after the root's folders are dropped the rest is anchored at the root, so `[[Corp/Fox]]` does not land on `Corp/wiki/Fox.md`. Anything the lookup resolved before resolves the same way, because the new branch only runs when there was no match.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

title: [Feature]: Preserve callflow HTML when staging a replacement fails
body:
### Problem or use case

Regenerating a callflow HTML report currently writes directly over the destination. If writing or closing the file fails after it has been opened, the previous usable report can be lost or left incomplete.

This is a source-backed improvement proposal for `v8` at `86c57be8204673c2a1b9849a3292a7dd3ab373d8`, not a report of a production incident. The final write in `graphify/callflow_html.py` uses `Path.write_text`.

### Proposed solution

Write the rendered HTML to a temporary file before replacing the destination, using the existing text-writing helper. A handled temporary write or close failure before replacement starts should leave the previous report intact and use the helper's existing best-effort temporary-file cleanup.

Keep successful HTML content, the returned path, and CLI output unchanged on the same platform. Cover failure handling with injected write and close errors.

### Alternatives considered

Exporting to a different filename preserves the old report but requires users to manage replacement themselves. Keeping the direct write leaves the same failure window.

### Area

CLI or installation

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

This concerns callflow HTML output only. It does not change graph schemas, node or edge IDs, caches, generated skills, MCP output, or incremental extraction.

Replacing a file can change its inode and hard-link behavior. Owner, ACLs, extended attributes, timestamps, and exact permissions are not guaranteed to stay the same; permission errors can also differ from an in-place write. The proposal inherits the existing helper's symlink handling and Windows fallback. It does not promise protection from power loss, process termination, or a second failure during restoration.

### Additional context

The scenario is regenerating an existing report through `write_callflow_html`, `python -m graphify.callflow_html`, or `graphify export callflow-html`; all reach the same final writer. A controlled regression test can start with known destination bytes and inject a temporary write or close error before replacement, then verify the original bytes and temporary-file cleanup.
