title: hooks: last-resort `python3` probe launches the Microsoft Store redirector on Windows (visible console flash, exit 9009)
body:
**Where**: `graphify/hooks.py`, `_PYTHON_DETECT`, the "Last resort" block — `python3 -c "$_GFY_PROBE"` is tried before `python -c …` (0.9.92: L131–135; same order back to 0.8.36 L64–68).

**What happens on Windows**: with the Microsoft Store app-execution alias enabled (the Windows 10/11 default) and no Store Python installed, `command -v python3` in Git Bash resolves to `/c/Users/<me>/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WindowsApps/python3` — the `AppInstallerPythonRedirector.exe` stub. Running it opens a visible console window for ~1.1 s, then exits 9009. So on any machine where the pinned interpreter, `.graphify_python`, the launcher shebang and the uv-tools scan all miss (removed venv, graphify moved to another env, GUI git client with a minimal PATH), every commit flashes a terminal window before the hook falls through to `python`.

**Environment**: Windows 11 Home 23H2 (build 22631), Git for Windows, Windows Terminal 1.24 as default terminal, CPython 3.11.9 (per-user install under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Python`, not the Store build), graphifyy 0.8.36 (probe block unchanged in 0.9.92).

**Repro** (Git Bash, alias on, no Store Python):
```bash
command -v python3          # -> /c/Users/<me>/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WindowsApps/python3
time python3 --version      # console window appears for ~1.1 s; exit code 9009
```
Measured three times from a hidden launcher: ~1.1 s each, one `AppInstallerPythonRedirector.exe` + `OpenConsole.exe` per call.

**Caveat**: on my machine the hook never reached this branch (the pinned interpreter has graphify), so this is measured on the alias directly, not through a hook run.

**Suggested fix** (either):
- on Windows (`uname -s` = MINGW*/MSYS*/CYGWIN*) probe `python` before `python3`; or
- skip a `python3` whose resolved path contains `/WindowsApps/` (`case "$(command -v python3)" in */WindowsApps/*) ;; esac`).

Related: #287 noted the WindowsApps stub's exit code for the AGENTS.md command; #1416 touches the `python3` fallback in skill-claw.md. Neither covers the hook probe or the window flash. The console-window burst from `DETACHED_PROCESS` is #2253 (fixed in 0.9.29) and is a different mechanism.

title: [Bug]: Rust: a `use` rooted at a child module (`pub use item::X;`) still mints a stub that makes `affected`/`explain` ambiguous
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Follow-up to #4439, which ef1d256e and 5faa05c8 fixed in 0.9.91 for `use` paths rooted at `crate`, `self` or `super`. A `use` whose path starts at a child module declared beside it, such as `pub use item::Invoice;` next to `mod item;`, is still not named for the stub rewire. When nothing else lends the rewire a node under the bare id, the `imports_from` edge dangles, build mints the `external` stub `invoice`, and `affected` and `explain` tie on it exactly as #4439 described.

Expected: the edge lands on `Invoice` in `src/model/item.rs`, no stub is minted, and both commands resolve the name.

### Steps to reproduce

```toml
# Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "repro"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
```

```rust
// src/lib.rs
pub mod model;

// src/model.rs
mod item;
pub use item::Invoice;

// src/model/item.rs
pub struct Invoice(pub u64);
```

```sh
graphify extract . --code-only --cargo --force
graphify cluster-only . --no-viz --no-label
graphify affected Invoice
graphify explain Invoice
```

Spelling the re-export `pub use self::item::Invoice;` makes both commands resolve.

### Error output or graph output

| graphify | external stub | `imports_from` target | `affected Invoice` | `explain Invoice` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.9.62 | none | edge dropped | resolves | resolves |
| 0.9.91, 0.9.92 | `id: invoice`, `label: invoice`, `type: external`, `source_file: ""` | `invoice`, the stub | `No unique node match for Invoice`, exit 0 | `Ambiguous: 'Invoice' matches 2 nodes in different files.`, exit 3 |

### Graphify version

0.9.91 and 0.9.92, the latest. 0.9.63 to 0.9.90 mint the same stub through #4439 itself, and 0.9.62 is not affected.

### Operating System

macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)

### Python Version

3.15.0

### Installation Method

uv: `uv tool run --from 'graphifyy==<version>' graphify …`

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables are set, every run uses `--code-only`, and the repro is a clean directory holding only the four files above.

### Additional context

From the 0.9.92 source:

- `graphify/extractors/rust.py`, `use_declaration` branch: `name_use` sets `_rust_use_name` only when the path's first segment is `crate`, `self` or `super`, so `item::Invoice` gets none and `extract.py` lends the rewire no node for it.
- A larger repro can hide this. When another file imports the same item from `crate::` and that edge is still on the bare id at the rewire, its lent node rescues the re-export's edge too. On the private ~440-file Cargo workspace from #4439, those imports reach `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` on per-file placeholder ids (`<file>_rs_<name>`) instead, so the re-export's edge stays alone on the bare id.
- On that workspace, 90 names that 0.9.62 resolves still tie with an external stub on 0.9.92, down from 444 on 0.9.89. 83 of them are left on the stub only by child-module paths: 103 edges, all in a `mod.rs`, `lib.rs` or `main.rs`, 93 of them `pub use` re-exports.

A rule that should not reopen the `serde::Serialize` concern behind 5faa05c8: also name a `use` whose first segment is a `mod` declared in the same scope, unless the path starts with `::`. Rust resolves such a segment to the local module before a crate of that name. With `serde` as a dependency and `mod serde { pub struct Local; }` declared, `use serde::Serialize;` fails with E0432 on rustc 1.97.1, while `use ::serde::Serialize;` reaches the crate. Two details for the check: `name_use` strips a leading `::` before it reads the first segment, and an inline `mod` block is a scope of its own, so a `use serde::…` inside `mod tests { … }` still names the crate.

Related: @liam-mcelhaney122's comment on #4439 covers the same re-export from the importing side (`pub use item::Stack` in `core/src/lib.rs`). #4134 would mask this for `affected` but not for `explain`.

title: fix(extract): let the model acknowledge empty files so they don't arm the shrink guard (#4547)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4547. A file the model read and found empty (a `robots.txt`, an HTML shell, a short compose file) failed `graphify extract` on every run, the same way a file the model skipped does.

A file sent for semantic extraction counts as covered only if a returned node has it as `source_file`. Zero nodes puts it in `uncovered_files`, which sets `_extraction_incomplete`. That turns off `force`, so any run where the graph shrinks is refused and exits non-zero. The response format has only `nodes`, `edges` and `hyperedges`, so the model has no way to say "read it, nothing here." A retry sends the same file and gets the same answer.

A file the model read and found empty also failed a second way. A chunk holding only that file got an empty response, which `_response_is_hollow` treats as hollow. It was retried at 2 s and 8 s, then marked partial, which also arms the guard.

What changes, per file sent:

| Model's response for the file | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| nodes | covered | covered |
| no nodes, listed with `entities: 0` | uncovered, guard armed | `empty_files`, guard not armed |
| no nodes, not listed | uncovered | uncovered |
| no nodes, listed with `entities > 0` | uncovered | uncovered |
| no `files` key at all | uncovered | uncovered |
| in a truncated or hollow chunk | partial | partial, whatever it says |

```diff
 _EXTRACTION_SYSTEM schema
-{"nodes":[...],"edges":[...],"hyperedges":[...],"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0}
+{"nodes":[...],"edges":[...],"hyperedges":[...],"files":[{"path":"relative/path","entities":0}],...}

 _extract_with_adaptive_retry
   result = extract_files_direct(chunk)
+  _take_acks(result)        # keep 0-entity acks for paths in THIS chunk -> _empty_files
+                            # acks name only some files and no items -> hollow, normal retry

 _response_is_hollow
-  return not nodes and not edges and not hyperedges
+  no items and every acknowledged file has entities == 0 -> not hollow

 extract_corpus_parallel
-  uncovered = dispatched - covered
+  empty_files = (dispatched - covered) & acked_empty - partial
+  uncovered   = dispatched - covered - empty_files
```

The CLI also writes the full uncovered list to `graphify-out/uncovered_files.txt`, with paths relative to the corpus root, and removes a stale copy at the start of the next extract. Before this, the warning named five files and "+N more", and the rest were only in memory. The llm.py warning no longer says a re-run will retry the files. They are re-sent every run, but with the same `--token-budget` the model usually skips the same ones.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Only a file the model left out, or one from a truncated or hollow chunk, arms the shrink guard. A file the model read and acknowledged as empty does not.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. `files` is optional and is read only by the coverage check. It is popped before anything reaches the cache or `graph.json`. A response without it behaves exactly as on v8. Reverting the commit restores the old behaviour, and no stored data needs migrating.

**Blast Radius:** moderate. Every semantic extraction prompt gains the `files` rule, so each response gets slightly longer (one short entry per file). Runs that failed only because of empty files now write the graph. The guard now trusts a model's 0 for a file that comes back with no nodes.

**Limitations**

- If the model writes nodes for some files and falsely lists the others as `entities: 0`, those files won't arm the guard. The case in #4547 (files never mentioned) is still caught.
- If a large document is split into slices and one slice acknowledges 0 while another slice is never mentioned, the file counts as empty.
- `references/extraction-spec.md` has no `files` rule, so skill-driven extraction is unchanged.
- Empty files are still re-sent on every run. #2927 deliberately keeps zero-node results out of the semantic cache, and I left that rule alone. Caching an acknowledged 0 can be a follow-up if wanted.

## How was this tested?

New file `tests/test_empty_file_ack.py`, 11 tests. They patch out the model call and the hollow-retry sleep, so they make no network calls and run in about a second.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| acknowledged-empty file is not uncovered | fail | pass |
| chunk with only an empty file succeeds, no retry | fail | pass |
| files-only response is not hollow; empty and junk `files` still are | fail | pass |
| `extract` keeps `force=True` when an empty file is acknowledged | fail | pass |
| `uncovered_files.txt` holds every path, removed on a clean run | fail | pass |
| unacknowledged file stays uncovered | pass | pass |
| no `files` key behaves as before | pass | pass |
| `entities > 0` with no node stays uncovered | pass | pass |
| ack for a path outside the chunk is ignored | pass | pass |
| truncated chunk that acknowledges stays partial | pass | pass |
| files-only response that misses a file is still hollow | pass | pass |

The six that pass on v8 guard the existing behaviour.

```text

pytest tests/test_empty_file_ack.py -q (this branch)                        -> 11 passed
pytest tests/test_empty_file_ack.py tests/test_chunking.py \
       tests/test_hollow_chunks_arm_shrink_guard.py -q                       -> 51 passed
pytest -q (full suite, --basetemp=/var/tmp)                                  -> 8403 passed, 14 skipped
ruff check graphify/llm.py graphify/cli.py tests/test_empty_file_ack.py     -> All checks passed
```

title: fix(extract): redact credential-shaped text from rationale labels
body:
## Problem
Docstrings and `# WHY:` / `# NOTE:` style comments become `rationale` node labels. `_shorten_rationale_label()` only collapses whitespace and truncates, so a credential pasted into a comment is stored verbatim and then written to `graph.json`, `graph.html`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md` and the AST cache — the artifacts the README suggests committing and sharing.

Repro (0.9.86 / 0.9.87):
```
printf 'def f():\n    # WHY: prod token is ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789\n    pass\n' > s.py
graphify update . && grep -rl ghp_abcdefgh graphify-out/
# graph.json, graph.html, GRAPH_REPORT.md, cache/ast/*.json
```

## Change
- `security.redact_secrets()`: shape-based redaction to `[redacted]` — vendor-prefixed tokens (AWS, GitHub, Slack, Stripe, OpenAI/Anthropic-style, Google), PEM private-key headers, JWTs, and the password part of `scheme://user:pass@host` (host kept).
- Applied in `_shorten_rationale_label()` **before** truncation so a cut cannot leave a partial token. That helper is shared by the Python and JS/TS rationale extractors, so one call site covers both.

## Tests
- 5 tests in `tests/test_rationale.py` (comment, docstring, truncation boundary, persisted graph JSON, ordinary rationale untouched) and 3 in `tests/test_security.py`.
- The 3 that exercise the leak fail on `v8` without the change and pass with it.
- Full suite: only `tests/test_skillgen.py` fails (11), identically on an unmodified `v8` checkout of mine — I believe because my clone is shallow; please confirm in CI. `ruff` clean; pyright count unchanged (134 before/after on the touched modules).

## Scope / limits
- Related to #2781 (document text sent to LLM backends unredacted) but intentionally narrow: this does **not** touch `detect()` or the semantic pass, and does not address #2781's proposal.
- Shape-based matching is risk reduction, not a guarantee. Name/value (`password = ...`) redaction is not included here to keep false positives out of prose labels.
- Existing `cache/ast` entries written before this change keep their old labels until the file is re-extracted; an AST cache schema bump would force that — I left it out of this PR; happy to add it if you want it here.
- Other rationale-like sources (e.g. non-Python/JS extractors) not covered by `_shorten_rationale_label` were not audited.

title: fix(rust): name a use rooted at a sibling mod so it reaches its declaration (#4564)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4564. A Rust `use` rooted at a child module declared beside it, such as `pub use item::Invoice;` next to `mod item;`, left its `imports_from` edge dangling. Build then minted an `external` stub `invoice`, and `affected` and `explain` tied on it.

The #4439 fix lends `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` a temporary node for every edge that carries `_rust_use_name`. `name_use` sets that only when the path's first segment is `crate`, `self` or `super`, so that `use serde::Serialize` never lands on a corpus `Serialize` (5faa05c8). `item::Invoice` starts with `item`, which looks the same as `serde::` to that check, so it got no lent node.

Rust settles which one a first segment means. A `mod` declared in the same scope shadows a crate of the same name, and only a leading `::` reaches the crate. Checked with `cargo check` on rustc 1.95.0, using a stand-in `serde` crate:

| Code | Result |
|---|---|
| `mod serde { … }` + `use serde::Serialize;`, same scope | E0432 |
| `mod serde;` (file module) + `use serde::Serialize;` | E0432 |
| `mod serde` + `use ::serde::Serialize;` | compiles, reaches the crate |
| top-level `mod serde` + `mod tests { use serde::Serialize; }` | compiles, reaches the crate |

So the rule is exact: a first segment that names a sibling `mod_item` is this crate's, unless the path starts with `::`.

```diff
 use_declaration
+  scope_mods = names of mod_item siblings of this use     # either order; an inline mod is its own scope
   name_use(written, path)
-    if first segment in (crate, self, super)
+    if first segment in (crate, self, super)
+       or (first segment in scope_mods and path does not start with "::")
       edge._rust_use_name = written
```

`_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes from 17 to 18, so a cached 0.9.92 result without the name is not served.

**Before** (the issue's four files, `extract --code-only --cargo --force`, `cluster-only`):

```text
graph.json   NODE invoice  type=external  source_file=''
             EDGE src_model -> invoice
affected Invoice   No unique node match for Invoice                      (exit 0)
explain Invoice    Ambiguous: 'Invoice' matches 2 nodes in different files.   (exit 3)
```

**After:**

```text
graph.json   EDGE src_model -> src_model_item_invoice    (no external node)
affected Invoice   Affected nodes for Invoice …
explain Invoice    Node: Invoice  ID: src_model_item_invoice  Source: src/model/item.rs L1
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A Rust `use` reaches its declaration whenever Rust resolves the path inside this crate. A path Rust resolves to another crate never lands on a corpus declaration.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. One extra condition in `name_use` and a cache schema bump. No graph format, id or manifest change. Reverting restores v8 behaviour. The schema bump costs one re-extract of cached Rust files on the next forced run.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Only Rust `use` edges rooted at a sibling `mod` change, and only from a dangling stub to the real declaration. `use` paths rooted at `crate`, `self`, `super`, `::` or an outside crate behave as on v8. Bumping `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` invalidates the whole AST cache, not only Rust entries, so the first forced run after upgrading re-extracts every code file once.

**Limitations**

- An incremental `graphify extract` (no `--force`) skips a file whose content hash matches `manifest.json` before it reads the AST cache (`detect_incremental`). The schema bump never reaches those files, so an existing graph keeps the stub until `--force` or an edit to the file. The same is true of every schema bump, #4439's included, because the manifest does not record the extractor version or schema.
- `_make_id("Invoice as Bill")` puts the alias in the raw target id (`invoice_as_bill`), for `crate::`, `self::` and bare paths alike. The rewire hides it whenever it resolves the edge. Not changed here.
- A `use` inside a fn body gets no edge (the extractor does not visit fn bodies), and `r#item` paths are not matched. Both are unchanged from v8.
- In `pub use item::{self as items, Invoice};`, `Invoice` lands, but the `self as items` binding names a module, which has no declaration node, so it stays a stub as on v8.

## How was this tested?

15 new tests in `tests/test_rust_use_trees.py`, next to the #4439 tests:

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_a_use_rooted_at_a_child_mod_lands_on_the_declaration` [plain, use_first, pub_crate, rename, self_alias_group] | 5 fail | pass |
| `test_the_issue_repro_builds_without_an_external_stub` (build level) | fail | pass |
| `test_a_group_and_a_nested_path_from_a_child_mod_land_on_the_declarations` | fail | pass |
| `test_a_use_of_a_mod_declared_inline_lands_on_the_declaration` | fail | pass |
| `test_a_use_rooted_at_a_local_mod_named_like_a_crate_lands_on_the_local_declaration` | fail | pass |
| `test_a_cache_entry_from_before_child_mod_names_is_not_served` | fail | pass |
| `test_a_use_of_another_crate_still_does_not_land_on_a_same_named_declaration` [leading_colons, inner_scope, outside_crate] | pass | pass |
| `test_a_second_import_of_the_same_item_does_not_change_the_result` | pass | pass |
| `test_two_types_with_one_name_stay_two_nodes_and_are_not_swapped` | pass | pass |

The five that pass on v8 guard the serde concern, the second-import case that can hide this bug in larger repos, and two distinct `Invoice` types that must not be cross-linked. The cache test fails on this branch with the schema set back to 17 (`assert ['invoice'] == ['src_model_item_invoice']`) and passes with 18.

```text
pytest tests/test_rust_use_trees.py -q (new tests, on v8 86c57be8)    -> 10 failed, 5 passed
pytest tests/test_rust_*.py -q (this branch)                          -> 98 passed
pytest -q (full suite, --basetemp=/var/tmp)                           -> 8407 passed, 14 skipped
ruff check graphify/extractors/rust.py graphify/cache.py tests/test_rust_use_trees.py -> All checks passed
```

A separate session that did not write the fix also ran 20 end-to-end cases (`extract`, `cluster-only`, `affected`, `explain`) against v8 and this branch, with `cargo check` as ground truth for each. Fixed: the issue's repro, the `use` before the `mod`, a group, a nested path, an inline `mod`, `pub(crate) use` and `as Bill`. Unchanged and never landing on a corpus `Serialize`: `use ::serde::Serialize;`, `use ::serde::{Serialize};` (the group binding reaches `name_use` as `::serde::Serialize`), the `mod tests` inner scope and a plain `use serde::Serialize;`.

## Graphify-specific checklist

title: fix(hooks): try python before python3 under Git for Windows so the Store alias never runs (#4563)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4563. When the hook's interpreter probes 1 to 4 all miss, its last resort tried `python3` before `python`. On Windows 10/11, `python3` is usually the Microsoft Store App Execution Alias in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps`, because python.org's installer ships `python.exe` but no `python3.exe`. Running the alias opens a console window for about 1.1 s and exits 9009. The hook then falls through to the real `python`, so it works, but every commit, checkout and merge flashes a window and blocks before the detached rebuild starts.

The last resort is reached when the pinned interpreter, `.graphify_python`, the launcher and the uv-tools scan all miss: a removed venv, graphify moved to another env, or a GUI client with a minimal PATH.

Under Git for Windows the last resort now tries `python` first. The Windows check is the one `hooks.py` already uses for its pipe-handle handling.

```diff
 # Last resort: try python3 / python (works for system/venv installs on PATH).
+# Under Git for Windows `python3` is usually the Microsoft Store App Execution Alias
+# ... Try `python` first there (#4563).
 if [ -z "$GRAPHIFY_PYTHON" ]; then
-    if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && python3 -c "$_GFY_PROBE" 2>/dev/null; then
-        GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="python3"
-    elif command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1 && python -c "$_GFY_PROBE" 2>/dev/null; then
-        GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="python"
+    if [ -n "${WINDIR:-}" ] || [ -n "${MSYSTEM:-}" ]; then
+        _GFY_FIRST="python"; _GFY_SECOND="python3"
+    else
+        _GFY_FIRST="python3"; _GFY_SECOND="python"
+    fi
+    if command -v "$_GFY_FIRST" >/dev/null 2>&1 && "$_GFY_FIRST" -c "$_GFY_PROBE" 2>/dev/null; then
+        GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="$_GFY_FIRST"
+    elif command -v "$_GFY_SECOND" >/dev/null 2>&1 && "$_GFY_SECOND" -c "$_GFY_PROBE" 2>/dev/null; then
+        GRAPHIFY_PYTHON="$_GFY_SECOND"
     else
```

Probes 1 to 4, the probe command, the interpreter names, the "could not locate a Python" message and `exit 0` are unchanged. All four generated hooks splice in the same `_PYTHON_DETECT`, so one edit covers post-commit, post-checkout, post-merge and post-rewrite.

I did not take the issue's second suggestion, skipping a `python3` under `*/WindowsApps/*`. A real Store Python also lives there, so skipping it would remove the last resort for Store-Python users.

**Before** (v8 probe block, a fake `WindowsApps/python3` that logs, sleeps 1 s and exits 9009, ahead of a real `python`):

```text
calls:  python3 (stub), python
chose:  python          1.07 s
```

**After** (`MSYSTEM=MINGW64`):

```text
calls:  python
chose:  python
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Under Git for Windows, the hook never runs `python3` while `python` can import graphify. Everywhere else the probe order is unchanged.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. A probe-order change inside a generated hook script. No schema, cache or file-format change. Existing installs pick it up on the next `graphify hook install`.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. Only the last-resort branch changes, and only when `WINDIR` or `MSYSTEM` is set. Linux and macOS keep `python3` then `python`. If `WINDIR` or `MSYSTEM` leaks into a non-Windows shell (for example WSL with `WSLENV`), the only effect is that `python` is tried before `python3`.

**Limitations**

- Not run on Windows. The behavioural tests use `sh`-script fakes and skip on `nt`. The reporter's measurements (about 1.1 s, exit 9009, one `AppInstallerPythonRedirector.exe` per call) are the Windows evidence.
- Hooks already installed keep the old order until `graphify hook install` is run again.
- If `python` is itself a Store stub (no real Python on PATH), it still runs once before the warning.
- If `python` lacks graphify, `python3` is still probed after it.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_hooks.py`. They run the emitted `_PYTHON_DETECT` under a real `sh`, with a temp `HOME` so probes 1 to 4 miss, and only two fake directories on PATH: `WindowsApps/python3` and `bin/python`. Each fake logs its call.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_windows_never_runs_the_store_python3_alias_when_python_works` [msystem] | fail: calls `python3, python` | pass: calls `python` |
| `test_windows_never_runs_the_store_python3_alias_when_python_works` [windir] | fail: same | pass |
| `test_windows_falls_back_to_python3_when_python_lacks_graphify` | fail: calls `python3` | pass: calls `python, python3`, picks `python3` |
| `test_outside_windows_python3_is_still_tried_first` | pass | pass |
| `test_windows_with_no_working_python_still_fails_loudly_and_exits_zero` | pass | pass |
| `test_every_hook_embeds_the_probe_chain_unchanged` (4 hooks) | pass | pass |

The ones that pass on v8 guard existing behaviour: the Linux/macOS order, the warning path, and that every hook carries the tested block.

The same block also ran under `dash` (`debian:stable-slim`) and BusyBox ash (`alpine:3.20`) with podman. Both parse it, and both give the same call order as above, with and without `MSYSTEM`.

```text

title: package.json dependencies produce two unlinked nodes with the same label
body:
### Summary

For each entry under `dependencies` / `devDependencies` / `peerDependencies`, `extractors/json_config.py` emits two nodes with the same label:

- the generic key node `<stem>_dependencies_react`, created by `walk_object` and reached through `dependencies --contains-->`
- the external ref node `ref_react`, created by the dependency branch and reached through `package.json --imports-->`

No edge connects them. Source files that import the package (`import React from "react"`) resolve to `ref_react`, so the manifest's own entry for the dependency is cut off from the code that uses it.

### Reproduction (graphifyy 0.9.84; `json_config.py` is identical in 0.9.92)

`package.json`:
```json
{
  "name": "demo",
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^19.0.0"
  }
}
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extractors.json_config import extract_json
r = extract_json(Path("package.json"))
```

Nodes (stem shortened):
```
<stem>_package_json            'package.json'  code
<stem>_package_name            'name'          code
<stem>_package_dependencies    'dependencies'  code
<stem>_package_dependencies_react  'react'     code     <- key node
ref_react                      'react'         concept  <- ref node
```

Edges:
```
<stem>_package_json         -contains-> <stem>_package_name
<stem>_package_json         -contains-> <stem>_package_dependencies
<stem>_package_dependencies -contains-> <stem>_package_dependencies_react
<stem>_package_json         -imports->  ref_react
```

Neither `react` node has an edge to the other.

### Impact on a real graph

On a small Vite + React project, community detection put the two `react` nodes (and the two `react-dom` nodes) in different communities: the key nodes went to "package manifest" and the ref nodes to "SPA entry" with `main.tsx`. Each `@types/*` devDependency also got a near-isolated key node, so `suggest_questions` lists them as weakly connected ("possible documentation gaps"). Cross-community bridge scores for `devDependencies` / `index.html` are inflated by the split.

### Cause

The #1764 fix (comment at the `parent_key in _DEP_KEYS` branch) moved the `imports` edge source from `key_nid` to `file_nid`, to avoid the self-referential-looking `react --imports--> react`. That edge was the only link between the key node and the ref node, so they are now disconnected.

### Suggested fix

Link the two nodes again, with a relation that does not read as a self-import:

```python
dep_nid = _make_id("ref", key)
if dep_nid:
    add_node(dep_nid, key, line, file_type="concept")
    add_edge(file_nid, dep_nid, "imports", line, context="import")
    add_edge(key_nid, dep_nid, "declares", line)  # reconnect the manifest entry
```

The node ids still differ, so the J-4 namespacing and the #1764 self-loop concern both hold. An alternative is to skip creating the key node for pairs under a `_DEP_KEYS` parent, so that `ref_*` is the only node per dependency, but that drops the version-range location.

title: [Bug]: vbnet: cross-file and VB -> C# calls produce no calls edges (Module functions, typed locals, C# statics)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

In a mixed C# / VB.NET solution, the graph contains `calls` edges between VB.NET methods only when caller and callee are in the same file. These call forms produce no edge:

1. **An unqualified call to a `Module` function declared in another file** (`LogIt("x")`). In VB.NET, `Module` members are in scope without qualification, so this is the most common call form in legacy VB code.
2. **A module-qualified call to a function declared in another file** (`Helpers.LogIt("x")`). #3909 fixed this for a module in the caller's own file. It lists "a type declared only in another file" as a limitation. In this repro `Helpers.LogIt` has exactly one candidate in the whole corpus.
3. **A call through a local whose type is declared in the same statement** (`Dim w As New Worker()` then `w.Save()`). C# resolves the equivalent form by the receiver's declared type (`csharp_member_calls`, #1609). VB.NET leaves it unresolved.
4. **A VB.NET call to a C# static method** (`CsRules.IsLocked(1)`). The reverse direction works: a C# call to a VB `Module` function (`Helpers.LogIt("x")` from a `.cs` file) does get a `calls` edge.

Expected: a `calls` edge for each of the four cases above, since each has exactly one candidate target in the corpus.

Impact: in a VB.NET codebase most calls cross files, so `affected`, `path` and `explain` miss most real callers. Callers of C# code from VB code are invisible, even though the opposite direction is present.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
Four files in one folder:

`Helpers.vb`

Public Module Helpers
    Public Sub LogIt(msg As String)
    End Sub
End Module


`Worker.vb`

Public Class Worker
    Public Sub Save()
    End Sub
End Class


`Caller.vb`

Public Class Caller
    Public Sub A_SameFileSelf()
        B_Target()
    End Sub
    Public Sub B_Target()
    End Sub
  %
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
FOUND   A_ -> B_Target
MISSING C_ -> LogIt
MISSING D_ -> LogIt
MISSING E_ -> Save
MISSING F_ -> IsLocked
FOUND   G_ -> LogIt
```

### Graphify version

0.9.92

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

`GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none`, `--code-only`; no provider API keys set. Reproduced in a fresh folder that contains only the four files above.

### Additional context

- `resolve_vbnet_partial_calls` (registered as `vbnet_partial_calls`) is the only cross-file resolver for `.vb`. VB raw calls that are not partial-type calls appear to stay unresolved after extraction.
- Related: #3717 (VB.NET extractor), #3909 (type/module-qualified calls, with the documented limitation for types declared in another file).
- Not related: #1232 (`.vb` files not recognised in v0.8.36).

title: fix(json_config): link a package.json dependency's manifest entry to its ref node (#4569)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4569. Each package.json dependency produced two nodes labelled `react` with no edge between them:

- the manifest entry `<stem>_dependencies_react` (type code, carries the version-range line), reached through `dependencies --contains-->`;
- the ref node `ref_react` (type concept), reached through `package.json --imports-->`. Code imports (`import React from "react"`) resolve here.

5711e9d2 (#1764 follow-up) moved the `imports` edge from `key_nid` to `file_nid` so it would stop reading as `react --imports--> react`. That edge was the only link between the two nodes. On v8 the manifest entry is 4 hops from the code that imports the package, the two land in different communities, `explain react` exits 3 ("Ambiguous: 'react' matches 2 nodes in package.json"), and `affected react` prints "No unique node match".

The manifest entry now has a `declares` edge to the ref node and is labelled `name@range`:

```diff
 elif parent_key in _DEP_KEYS and val_text.strip():
     dep_nid = _make_id("ref", key)
     add_node(dep_nid, key, line, file_type="concept")
     add_edge(file_nid, dep_nid, "imports", line, context="import")
+    add_edge(key_nid, dep_nid, "declares", line)
+    version = one line of val_text, capped at 40 chars ("...")
+    relabel key_nid to f"{key}@{version}"   # only if its source_location is this line
```

The ref node keeps the bare name that imports resolve to, so the two nodes no longer share a label: no `react -> react` edge, and `react` resolves to one node. A blank range (`"   "`) now behaves like `""`: bare label, no ref, no edge. `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes from 17 to 18.

The relabel checks `source_location` because a key node id carries only the immediate parent key. In a v2 lockfile, `dependencies.semver` under two `node_modules/*` entries mints one node; `add_node` keeps the first, so relabelling every pair would put the later range on the first line (4 of 44 relabelled nodes on a 340-package lockfile).

**Before** (the issue's package.json):

```text
dependencies --contains--> react [code]
package.json --contains--> dependencies
package.json --contains--> name
package.json --imports--> react [concept]
```

**After:**

```text
dependencies --contains--> react@^19.0.0 [code]
package.json --contains--> dependencies
package.json --contains--> name
package.json --imports--> react [concept]
react@^19.0.0 --declares--> react [concept]
```

I chose this after writing tests for the wanted behaviour and running four candidates against them:

| | A: `declares` edge | A2: `references` edge | B: no key node | C: edge + `name@range` (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| entry connected to importing code | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| no edge between same-label nodes (#1764) | no | no | yes | yes |
| `explain` / `affected` resolve `react` | no | no | yes | yes |
| unimported devDependency not flagged isolated | yes | yes | no | yes |
| existing tests pass | yes | yes | no (`test_extract_json_nested_contains`) | yes |

A2 also makes `affected` list the manifest line as a consumer, since `references` is in `DEFAULT_AFFECTED_RELATIONS`. `declares` is not, and nothing in graphify whitelists relation names.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A package.json dependency's manifest entry is connected to the code that imports the package, and no edge joins two nodes with the same label.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. One edge and one relabel in the `_DEP_KEYS` branch, plus a cache schema bump. No id changes. Reverting restores v8 output after one re-extract.

**Blast Radius:** moderate. Every manifest entry under a dependency block changes label (`react` becomes `react@^19.0.0`), and anything keyed on that label sees the new text. The ref node keeps `react`, so searching for the package still finds it. Bumping `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` invalidates the whole AST cache, so the first forced run after upgrading re-extracts every code file once.

**Limitations**

- A v2 `package-lock.json` already takes this path on v8 (its top-level `dependencies` key makes it config JSON). Its nested entries get the new label and edge too: 99 `declares` edges on a 340-package lockfile. v3 lockfiles are skipped as data JSON. I did not change `_is_config_json`.
- npm reads `""` and `"   "` as `*`. graphify has never linked `""`, unchanged here; `"   "` used to mint `ref_react` and an `imports` edge and now matches `""`.
- A small community named after its hub can now carry a range, e.g. `left-pad@workspace:*`.
- Obsidian note names drop the caret (`react@19.0.0.md`); the existing numeric-suffix dedup handles collisions.
- With two package.json files, each manifest's ref id is file-qualified (`a_package_json_ref_react`) while code imports a separate `ref_react`, so in a monorepo the manifest and the code still don't connect. Separate bug, recorded as a strict xfail.
- The issue says the `@types/*` key nodes show as isolated. On v8 they are already exempt (#4205); the flagged node is the ref node, which this PR now connects.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_extract.py`, next to the existing json_config tests. The build-level tests run `extract` + `build_from_json` on a package.json and a `.tsx` that imports `react`. The manifest entry is found by structure (`contains` from the dependency block), not by label, so a relabel can't pass them on its own.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| entry within 2 hops of the importing code | fail: 4 hops | pass |
| every dependency block (×4) | fail | pass |
| stale cache entry not served (fails with schema 17) | fail | pass |
| one node labelled with the bare name | fail: 2 | pass |
| `explain` / `affected` resolve the package name | fail: ambiguous | pass |
| unimported devDependency not reported isolated | fail | pass |
| label carries a one-line capped range (×8) | fail | pass |
| blank range: bare name, no ref, no edge | fail | pass |
| key shared by two sibling blocks labelled with the range on its own line | fail | pass |
| no same-label `imports`, no self-loop | pass | pass |
| no edge of any relation between same-label nodes | pass | pass |
| `utils` dependency stays a namespaced `ref_` | pass | pass |
| declaring line recorded | pass | pass |
| two manifests keep their own lines | pass | pass |
| non-dependency keys unchanged | pass | pass |
| ref node keeps the bare name | pass | pass |
| empty range unchanged | pass | pass |
| non-string values unchanged | pass | pass |
| two-manifest corpus reaches its entry | xfail | xfail (strict) |

The ones that pass on v8 guard #1764, J-4 and existing output.

title: [Bug]: Swift: an extension of a type outside the corpus (`private extension String`) captures every reference to that type
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

A Swift `extension` of a type that is not defined in the corpus (here `private extension String`) becomes the node that every other `String` in the corpus resolves to. A struct field `let name: String` in another file gets a `references` edge to the extension node in `Helpers.swift`.

Expected: references to `String` should not land on an extension that happens to live in the repo. Leaving them unresolved, or pointing them at an external `String` node, would both be fine.

Impact on a mid-sized SwiftUI app: one `private extension String` collected about 940 edges. It became the top cross-community bridge in `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and the first suggested question was about it.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir ext-repro && cd ext-repro && git init -q
cat > Helpers.swift <<'EOF'
private extension String {
    var trimmed: String { trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces) }
}
EOF
cat > Models.swift <<'EOF'
struct Person {
    let name: String
}
EOF
graphify update .
python3 -c "
import json; g = json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); L = g.get('links', g.get('edges'))
lab = {n['id']: n['label'] for n in g['nodes']}
print([(n['id'], n.get('source_file')) for n in g['nodes'] if n['label'] == 'String'])
print(sorted((lab.get(e['source']), e['relation'], lab.get(e['target'])) for e in L if 'String' in (lab.get(e['source']), lab.get(e['target']))))
"
```

### Error output or graph output

```
[('helpers_string', 'Helpers.swift')]
[('Helpers.swift', 'contains', 'String'), ('Person', 'references', 'String'), ('String', 'method', '.trimmed')]
```

The only `String` node is the extension in `Helpers.swift`, and `Person` (in `Models.swift`) references it.

### Graphify version

0.9.92

### Operating System

macOS 26.5.2 (Apple silicon)

### Python Version

3.12.13

### Installation Method

`uv tool install graphifyy`

### Additional Environment Details

No provider API keys set. Reproduced in a clean directory with only the two files above. tree-sitter 0.25.2, tree-sitter-swift 0.7.4.

### Additional context

The docstring of `_merge_swift_extensions` says extensions of types outside the corpus are left untouched, which is right. But the untouched extension node keeps the label `String`, so the later by-label type-reference resolution seems to treat it as the only `String` definition. I didn't trace the resolver itself. A possible fix: never resolve a reference to a node that only exists as an extension, or skip `_LANGUAGE_BUILTIN_GLOBALS` names in that resolution the way the extension merge already does.

Related: #2538 (cross-file `extension Foo` handling).

_This report and its reproduction were prepared with the help of an AI assistant and checked by running the steps above._

title: [Bug]: Swift: same-named nested types in one file collapse into one node (e.g. two `CodingKeys` enums)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Two Swift types nested in different parents in the same file, with the same name, collapse into one node. The common case is `Codable` structs that each declare `enum CodingKeys`. The node ID is `{file_stem}_{name}` with no enclosing type, so both enums become `models_codingkeys`. That one node is then `contains`-ed by both structs and carries the cases of both enums.

Expected: one node per nested type, for example `models_person_codingkeys` and `models_place_codingkeys`.

Impact on a mid-sized SwiftUI app: 23 `CodingKeys` enums in one file became a single node with about 150 edges. It ranked #3 among the god nodes and was its own large, low-cohesion community.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir nested-repro && cd nested-repro && git init -q
cat > Models.swift <<'EOF'
struct Person: Codable {
    let name: String
    enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey { case name = "full_name" }

title: fix(python): resolve `module.func()` to the child named exactly `func`
body:
## What does this PR do?

The module arm of `_resolve_python_member_calls` (#1883) resolves `module.func()` to the child of the imported module whose `_key` matches the callee. `_key` drops every non-alphanumeric character and folds case, so `dataclass_schema()` and `class DataclassSchema` share one key. Python names are case-sensitive and `_` is significant, but any such pair made the lookup ambiguous and **the call was dropped**.

That shape is everywhere in pydantic-core: each `def x_schema()` in `core_schema.py` sits beside its `class XSchema(TypedDict)`. So no `core_schema.int_schema()`, `core_schema.model_field()`, `core_schema.dataclass_schema()`… call got an edge.

Change (`graphify/extract.py`, module arm only): when several children share the folded key, keep the one whose label (minus `()` / a leading `.`) is **exactly** the callee. The exact names come from an index built next to the folded one, so the tie-break is O(1) per call. A per-call scan was O(N²) for N calls to N same-key names: 2,000 case-variant calls took 1.7 s, against 0.85 s on v8 (and 0.98 s indexed, while resolving all 2,000). The pydantic graph is identical either way. A unique folded match resolves as before, and a name that matches only after folding (`computevalue` vs `compute_value` / `ComputeValue`) still gets no edge.

This is resolver-level, so no AST cache schema bump is needed.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: fail closed on genuine ambiguity, but don't treat two names that differ in Python as the same name. The change is strictly additive: it only acts where the old code bailed with more than one candidate, and only resolves to an exact-name match.

- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Out of scope: the class arm's `method_index` uses the same folded key (`get_x` vs `getX` on one class), which I didn't touch.

## How was this tested?

- New `tests/test_python_module_call_exact_name.py`: a function beside a same-key class resolves by its exact name; the class itself resolves when called by its exact name; an aliased module import (`import core_schema as cs`) resolves the same way; a fold-only match stays unresolved. 3 fail on v8 and 1 is a guard.

I verified **all 591** against the source: the call site contains `.<name>(` and the target module defines exactly `def <name>` / `class <name>`. title: fix(python): extract explicit type aliases as type nodes
body:
## What does this PR do?

A module-level `type Vector = list[float]` (PEP 695), `Matrix: TypeAlias = …` and `UserId = NewType("UserId", int)` each declare a type name, but the Python extractor emitted no node for them. Every annotation using the name, **even in the same module**, resolved to a **sourceless stub** that the corpus rewire can grow into a cross-file hub.

Changes (`graphify/extractors/engine.py`):
- `_python_alias_name` recognizes the three explicit forms on a module-level statement: `type X = …` / `type X[T] = …`, `X: TypeAlias = …` (also `typing.` / `typing_extensions.`), and `X = NewType(…)`.
- The walk gives each one a type node contained by its module, then walks the statement as usual. The node is minted under the same `_underscore_salted_nid` rule as module-level classes, and the names join `_python_pre_scan_underscore_collisions` (#2810), so `type Vector` and `def vector()` stay separate nodes.
- **Boundaries:** a bare `JsonValue = Union[…]` is an alias by convention only, and treating every capitalized assignment as a type would be a guess, so it isn't one. Class- or function-level aliases are out of scope. A same-name re-export (`Field: TypeAlias = core.Field`, `type Field = core.Field[int]`, or a bare `Field: TypeAlias = Field` after `from core import Field`, the case the graphify-labs bot flagged) denotes the original type and declares no new name, so it emits no node: references keep resolving to the one real `Field`. My Go alias PR follows the same rule; there a re-export node measurably regressed uber-go/zap.
- `graphify/cache.py`: AST cache schema 20 → 21 (the branch includes v8 at 0.9.93). Cached Python results lack these nodes.

title: fix(go): extract `type A = B` aliases as type nodes
body:
## What does this PR do?

tree-sitter-go parses `type A = B` as a `type_alias` node, not a `type_spec`, and `extract_go` walked `type_spec` only. The alias was dropped, so:
- a field, parameter or return typed with it, **even below the declaration**, resolved to a **sourceless stub** that the corpus rewire can grow into a cross-file hub, or bind to an unrelated same-named type elsewhere;
- a method on an alias receiver (`func (a Alias) M()`) minted the alias's node at the *method's* line.

Changes (`graphify/extractors/go.py`):
- A `type_alias` becomes a type node on its own line, with the same id (`type_symbol_nid`), collision census (`_scan_type_names`) and conversion semantics (`ID("x")` like `Name("y")`) as a defined type. Its right-hand side is not walked.
- **Same-name re-exports are deliberately left out.** `type Field = zapcore.Field` (or `pkg.Field[...]`) denotes the original type and declares no new name. Giving it a node made `Field` non-unique corpus-wide. On uber-go/zap that turned 0 sourceless `Field` stubs into 19 (62 edges): references that v8 correctly rewired to `zapcore.Field` started tying between the alias and the original. `_go_alias_re_exports` detects a `qualified_type` (optionally inside a `generic_type`) whose name equals the alias's, and those emit no node, exactly as on v8. A pointer alias (`*pkg.Field`) or a renamed one (`type Field = pkg.Entry`) is a new name and gets a node.
- `graphify/cache.py`: AST cache schema 20 → 21 (the branch includes v8 at 0.9.93). Cached Go results lack these nodes.

title: fix(cpp): extract namespace-scope `using` and `typedef` aliases as type nodes
body:
## What does this PR do?

The C++ extractor emitted no node for an alias declaration (`using X = …;`) or a `typedef`. A field, parameter or return typed with one, **even in the declaring header**, therefore resolved to a **sourceless stub**, which the corpus rewire can grow into a hub or bind to an unrelated same-named symbol elsewhere.

Changes (`graphify/extractors/engine.py`, in `_cpp_extra_walk`):
- A **namespace- or file-scope** `alias_declaration` / `type_definition` becomes a type node contained by its file. Every declarator of a typedef counts: `typedef int Handle, *HandlePtr;`, `typedef int (*Fn)(int);`, `typedef int Arr[4];` (`_cpp_declarator_type_name` walks pointer, function, parenthesized and array declarators). Alias templates (`template <class T> using Ptr = T*;`) count too. The handler returns `False`, so the walk continues and a typedef'd struct body still gets its own node and fields.
- **Not declarations here, on purpose:**
  - **Member aliases** (`using value_type = T;`, `typedef … size_type;` in a class). They sit in every container, and C++ member ids aren't class-qualified, so they would fold into one hub node. Scope is checked structurally (parent is `translation_unit` or a namespace `declaration_list`, looking through `template_declaration` and through `#ifndef`/`#if`/`#ifdef`/`#else` wrappers, which tree-sitter models as `preproc_*` nodes: an include guard is not a scope, as the graphify-labs bot pointed out). A member alias inside a conditional in a class body is still a member.
  - **The struct a C-style `typedef struct Foo {…} Foo;` names**: the struct's own node is it.
  - **Same-name re-exports** (`using Bar = ns::Bar;`), which denote the original type and declare no new name. My Go alias PR uses the same rule; there a re-export node measurably regressed uber-go/zap.
- Declarator names are de-duplicated with a set: one typedef can declare thousands of names, and a list `in` check was O(N²) (a 40,000-name typedef took 6.2 s; now 1.1 s, most of it emitting the 40,000 nodes v8 dropped).
- C++ never populates `namespace_stack`, so the id is `_make_id(stem, name)`, the one `ensure_named_node` looks up for a name declared in the file.
- `graphify/cache.py`: AST cache schema 20 → 21 (the branch includes v8 at 0.9.93).

**Two existing tests updated** (`test_cpp_nested_and_cli.py`): `typedef enum { A, B } Flag;` / `typedef union {…} Anon;` asserted that `Flag` / `Anon` are not nodes. Their stated concern is a *nameless* node and the anonymous specifier's members. They now expect `Flag` / `Anon` as alias nodes owning none of the members, and still forbid a nameless node and the members (`A`, `a`, `b`).

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a source-backed declaration wins over a sourceless stub, without making a previously unique, correct resolution ambiguous.

- **User-visible:** a name declared in two files is now honestly ambiguous. On fmt, `graphify explain test_string` used to pick compile-test.cc's struct silently. It now refuses with "Ambiguous: matches 2 nodes" (exit 3), because `util.h` declares `using test_string = …` too. That's the existing fail-closed behaviour, now fed by the real declarations.
- **Persisted state invalidated:** AST cache schema bump (first build after upgrading re-extracts code files once).

Limitations: the anonymous specifier named by a typedef still contributes no members (pre-existing). C (`.c` with the C config) models no types at all, so C typedefs are a separate feature.

## How was this tested?

- New `tests/test_cpp_type_alias.py` (9 tests): sourced alias nodes on their lines for every form, `contains` edges, field references binding to the aliases, member aliases not emitted, the C-style `typedef struct Foo {…} Foo;` resolving to the struct, the re-export boundary, a cross-file reference rewired onto the alias, aliases inside an include guard and `#if`/`#elif`/`#else`/`#ifdef` blocks, and a guarded member alias staying a member. 4 fail on v8 (0.9.93) and 5 are guards; the conditional test also fails on this branch's earlier revision.

  - **google/leveldb** (132 files): sourceless nodes 644 → 630, edges into sourceless 1,440 → 1,393, **47 stub → real, 0 real → stub, 0 moved, 0 lost.**
  - **fmtlib/fmt** (73 files): edges 12,251 → 12,373, sourceless nodes 1,112 → 987, edges into sourceless 2,271 → 1,958, **311 stub → real, 0 real → stub, 0 moved.** fmt keeps many aliases inside `#if` blocks (`enable_if_t`, `conditional_t`, `basic_format_context`, …). I checked all 12 edge sites that exist only on v8:
    - 4 are `#include <variant>` / `<any>` hitting the same external stub, whose label had been taken over by a case-folded type stub `Variant`/`Any`;
    - 1 was gtest.h's `Print(const Optional<T>&)` wrongly bound to gmock.h's *function* `Optional()`, now bound to the `using Optional = …` alias in gtest.h itself;

title: fix(rust): extract `type` aliases and `union` items as type nodes (#4285)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4285 (item 5, "Missing node kinds": `type`, `union`).

`extract_rust` emitted nodes for `struct`/`enum`/`trait` only. A field, parameter or return typed with a `type` alias or a `union` declared in the same file therefore resolved through `ensure_named_node` to a **sourceless stub**, which the corpus rewire can grow into a cross-file hub. A file holding only aliases was even reported as "yielded no symbols". The common `pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>;` in an `error.rs` was hit worst: `-> Result<u8>` in that file pointed at a global sourceless `Result`.

Changes (`graphify/extractors/rust.py`):
- `union_item` and `type_item` go through the same branch as struct/enum/trait. Each becomes a type node in its declaring file, with a `contains` edge from the file and the `_rust_declaration_count` that the cross-file tie-break reads.
- A union's named fields reference their types, as a struct's do. An alias is a bare node; its right-hand side is not walked, to keep the change narrow.
- Both kinds are added to the per-file collision census (`_scan_type_items`) as types, so same-id collisions follow the existing #3302/#3782 salting rule.
- An associated type in an `impl` body (`type Output = Meters;`) is also a `type_item`, but it's not a file-level item. It's skipped structurally (grandparent is `impl_item`); otherwise every `impl Add` would create a colliding `Output` node.
- Declaration nodes are now found through a `node_by_id` index, filled at the only two places nodes are appended (both guarded by `seen_ids`, so ids are unique). The old `next(n for n in nodes if n["id"] == ...)` was a linear scan per declaration, already on v8, so quadratic in file size. With aliases and unions going through it, a synthetic 3,000-alias + 3,000-union file went from 0.57 s to 3.2 s before the index. The `impl` lookup uses the same index.
- `graphify/cache.py`: AST cache schema 20 → 21 (the branch includes v8 at 0.9.93). Cached Rust results lack the new nodes.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a source-backed declaration wins over a sourceless stub (provenance). A reference is never dropped, and resolves only to something that becomes a node.

- Two existing #3782 tests asserted that an alias or union is *not* a node. They now expect the reference to land on the declaration. The function-local struct, undeclared name and impl-only generic cases still assert a stub.
- **Persisted state invalidated:** AST cache schema bump, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts code files once. An incremental `extract` without `--force` carries unchanged files forward from the manifest, as with every earlier bump.
- **Id change in one case:** a file with both `type HANDLE` and `struct Handle` (same folded id) now salts both apart under the existing collision rule, so the struct's id changes in that file.
- **Conflict note:** my other open PRs also bump the schema 20 → 21. Whichever merges later needs a one-line rebase.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Limitations: an alias's right-hand side is not walked. An alias or union inside a function body is not emitted, the same as structs there today.

## How was this tested?

- New `tests/test_rust_type_alias_union.py` (6 tests). 4 fail on v8 and 2 are guards. Reverting only `rust.py` and `cache.py` makes those 4 fail, plus the 2 updated #3782 tests.
- Edge cases on the committed code: `type Result<T>` gets a node and `parse()` references it; `impl Iterator { type Item = T; }` creates no `Item`; an alias inside an inline `mod` becomes a node; output is identical under CRLF, a UTF-8 BOM and tab indentation.
- ripgrep (110 files): sourceless nodes named after a local alias/union went from 11 (14 edges) to 8 (8 edges). `BagOfWords`, `PatternSetPoolFn` and `FnVisitor` now resolve. The remainder are associated types and generics, correctly left out.
- Performance: ripgrep full `extract()` 2.75 s → 2.78 s, peak memory 29.7 → 29.8 MiB. At 1×/2×/4× synthetic input both v8 and this branch grow ~2.1× per doubling (linear). The constant factor is the nodes v8 dropped.

```text

# tests/test_rust_type_alias_union.py on v8 (0.9.93): 4 of 6 fail; on this branch: 6 passed
# Full suite: per Python, `uv sync --all-extras --frozen`, then `uv run pytest tests/ -q --tb=short`.
#   this branch on v8 0.9.93 — 3.13: 8468 passed

uv run graphify --help && uv run graphify install   # in a throwaway HOME

When four suites ran in parallel I also saw timing flakes in the watch tests (`test_language_override_lifecycle.py`, `test_pr10_watch_overrides.py`). Those tests touch no Rust code, and they passed 10/10 unloaded on both v8 and this branch.

title: fix(dart): extract typedefs as aliases, not variables of type `typedef`
body:
## What does this PR do?

The Dart extractor turned `typedef` lines into **variables of type `typedef`**, which minted one sourceless node labelled `typedef` and a `references` edge to it from each file using the keyword:

- The typedef pattern accepted no parentheses, so a function-type alias (`typedef Callback = void Function(int);`, the most common modern form) never matched it.
- An alias of a builtin (`typedef JsonMap = Map<String, dynamic>;`) matched, but was skipped entirely.
- Both then fell through to the variable pattern, which read `typedef Callback = …` as a variable `Callback` of type `typedef`. The existing `JsonMap` assertion in `test_dart.py` was passing only through this path.
- The legacy form (`typedef int Compare(Object a, Object b);`) matched nothing.

On felangel/bloc (13 files with typedefs, 24 declared typedefs): **18 edges into a sourceless `typedef` node, and only 13 of 24 typedefs extracted.** After this PR: 0 such edges, 24 of 24 extracted.

Changes (`graphify/extractors/dart.py`):
- The `=` form now takes any right-hand side up to `;` (function types, records, nullable, multi-line). A second pattern covers the legacy function-typedef form. Every alias becomes a node, with one `defines` edge from the file.
- The existing `references` (context `typedef`) edge is kept, but only for a plain named, non-builtin target (`typedef Lookup = Repo;` → `Repo`, `pkg.Remote<int>` → `Remote`). A function type's leading name is its return type, not an aliased type, so it gets no edge.
- The variable and method passes skip lines starting with `typedef`. Those are declared in step 2.5, so the variable pass no longer invents a `typedef` type, and the method pass no longer double-defines `typedef void onTap();`.
- The legacy pattern reads the return type as whitespace-separated tokens that can't contain whitespace (`(?:[\w<>,.?]+[ \t]+)*?`), and doesn't cross lines. A first version used `[\w<>,.?\s]+?\s+`, whose overlapping classes backtrack: 1.74 s on a 0.8 MB file of `typedef a a a …` lines that never reach `(`, against 104 ms on v8.
- Files that never say `typedef` skip both typedef scans (one substring test), and the variable/method passes use a precompiled `_TYPEDEF_LINE` guard. Without this, a typedef-free test file ran 3–10% slower than v8; bloc's 616 files now run at v8's speed or better (0.79–0.83 s vs 0.78–0.90 s over 3 rounds).
- `graphify/cache.py`: AST cache schema 17 → 18. Cached Dart results carry the bogus edge.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a source-backed declaration wins over a sourceless stub. A language keyword is never a node.

- **Persisted state invalidated:** AST cache schema bump, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts code files once.
- **Conflict note:** #4567 and my Rust alias/union PR also bump the schema 17 → 18. Whichever merges later needs a one-line rebase.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Known limitation, pre-existing and unchanged: `_read_source_text` deliberately keeps a UTF-8 BOM, so in a BOM-prefixed `.dart` file the `^\s*` patterns miss **any** declaration on line 1. A `class First {}` on line 1 is lost on v8 too. This PR behaves the same way. It's a separate fix, not folded in here.

## How was this tested?

- New `tests/test_dart_typedef.py`. 4 of its 5 tests fail on v8; the fifth guards the kept `Lookup → Repo` edge. Reverting only `dart.py` and `cache.py` makes the 4 fail again.
- Edge cases: record, nullable, prefixed-generic and multi-line aliases; legacy form with generic return types (`List<int>`, `Map<String, int>`); indented legacy form. Output is identical under CRLF and tab indentation.
- Performance: bloc extractor-only 1.18 s → 1.17 s; full `extract()` within run-to-run noise (interleaved rounds 4.17–4.76 s on v8, 3.79–4.29 s here); peak memory unchanged (18.9 MiB). On a pathological 1 MB `typedef a a a …` file: 47 ms → 99 ms, and linear (2.0–2.1× per doubling).

title: fix(kotlin): model a type alias as a node, not a sourceless stub (#4553)
body:
Fixes #4553.

`type_alias` was in neither Kotlin's `class_types` nor `function_types`, so the declaration itself got no node. A property or parameter typed as the alias still resolved the name through `ensure_named_node`, which minted a sourceless stub and pointed every `references` edge at that stub instead of the real, same file declaration — turning a bare id into an unintended cross file hub, exactly the provenance violation the issue describes.

Adds `type_alias` to `_KOTLIN_CONFIG.class_types`. It has no body of its own, so the shared class handling emits a clean, empty, sourced node with no phantom members, the same shape Scala and TypeScript already model their own type aliases as. Confirmed via the grammar itself (`tree_sitter_kotlin`) that `type_alias`'s name child is a plain `identifier`, already covered by the existing `name_fallback_child_types`, and that it has no body field or fallback body child type, so `_find_body` returns `None` and no member walk runs.

Reproduced the issue's exact repro against a clean v8 checkout before the fix (confirmed the alias comes back with `source_file: ''` under a bare `clickhandler` id, with both the property and the parameter referencing that stub), then verified both the property and the parameter now reference one real, sourced node after the fix. Added regression tests in a new `tests/test_kotlin_type_alias.py`.

Ran the full suite plus `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`; the only failures are the pre-existing ones already present on a clean v8 checkout, unrelated to this change.

fix(csharp): model a delegate declaration as a node, not a sourceless stub (#4552)
body:
Fixes #4552.

`delegate_declaration` was in neither C#'s `class_types` nor `function_types`, so the declaration itself got no node. A field or parameter typed as the delegate still resolved the name through `ensure_named_node`, which minted a sourceless stub and pointed every `references` edge at that stub instead of the real, same file declaration — turning a bare id into an unintended cross file hub, exactly the provenance violation the issue describes.

Adds `delegate_declaration` to `_CSHARP_CONFIG.class_types`. Confirmed via the grammar itself (`tree_sitter_c_sharp`) that `delegate_declaration` has a `name` field (a plain `identifier`), already covered by the existing field lookup, and no `declaration_list` child (C#'s own body fallback type), so `_find_body` returns `None` and no member walk runs — a clean, empty, sourced node, matching the issue's own note. Delegate parameter/return type refs and delegate instance invocation resolution stay out of scope, as the issue says.

Reproduced the issue's exact repro against a clean v8 checkout before the fix (confirmed `BinOp` comes back with `source_file: ''` under a bare `binop` id), then verified both the field and the parameter now reference one real, sourced node after the fix. Added regression tests in a new `tests/test_csharp_delegate_type.py`.

title: fix(cpp): blank Metal and CUDA qualifiers tree sitter cpp cannot parse (#4550)
body:
Fixes #4550.

Metal (`.metal`) and CUDA (`.cu`/`.cuh`) are C++ derived GPU dialects that route through the C++ (`tree-sitter-cpp`) extractor, but their address space, execution space, and function qualifiers (`kernel`, `device`, `constant`, `__global__`, `__device__`, ...) are not part of the C++ grammar it actually parses with. Left in place, the grammar reads the qualifier itself as the declaration's type (a `type_identifier`) and pushes the real type into an adjacent `ERROR` node — confirmed directly by dumping the parse tree for `kernel void saxpy(device const float* x, ...)` — so the qualifier becomes a sourceless, corpus-wide god node every shader/kernel using it "references" by name.

This adds a `_normalize_gpu_qualifiers` source normalization step to `extract_cpp`, following the exact same byte-length-preserving blanking contract `_normalize_cpp_cli` already uses: each known qualifier is overwritten with spaces (keeping line breaks) before parsing, so every reported source location for everything else in the file stays accurate. The qualifier lists are keyed by the file's own extension — `.metal` gets Metal's vocabulary, `.cu`/`.cuh` get CUDA's — so a plain `.cpp`/`.cc`/`.h` file is never touched, and a genuine C++ type literally named `device` (a legal identifier) still resolves normally.

Confirmed by dumping the parse tree before and after: blanking turns `kernel void saxpy(device const float* x, ...)` into a clean function signature with zero `ERROR` nodes, for both the shipped `sample.metal` and `sample.cu` fixtures. Reproduced the issue's exact repro against a clean v8 checkout before the fix (`['constant', 'device', 'kernel', 'uint']` / `['__device__', '__global__']` sourceless), then verified none of the qualifier keywords appear as nodes at all after the fix. `uint` stays as is — it is a genuine Metal built-in type with no in-file declaration, a different, separate concern (recognizing GPU dialect built-ins the way `_C_PRIMITIVE_TYPE_NODES` already does for C) that the issue's own "Expected vs actual" section does not ask this fix to cover.

Added regression tests in `tests/test_languages.py` next to the existing CUDA/Metal tests: both dialects' fixtures mint no node at all (sourced or not) for their known qualifiers, and a plain `.cpp` file with a type named `device` is unaffected.

Ran the full suite plus `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`; the only failures are the pre-existing ones already present on a clean v8 checkout, unrelated to this change.

title: fix(swift): model a macro declaration and its freestanding call (#4551)
body:
Fixes #4551.

`macro stringify(...) = #externalMacro(...)` (Swift 5.9) parses as `macro_declaration`, which was in neither Swift's `function_types` nor `class_types`, so the whole declaration was dropped and the symbol was invisible. A freestanding call site `#stringify(...)` parses as `macro_invocation`, a different node type from an ordinary `call_expression`, so even a declared macro's own call edge was lost.

This adds `macro_declaration` to `function_types`. Confirmed via the grammar itself (`tree_sitter_swift`) that its name is a bare `simple_identifier` child, already covered by the existing `name_fallback_child_types`, so no special casing is needed to read it. Adds `macro_invocation` to `call_types` and a dedicated branch for it in the call walker, since the name sits as a sibling of the leading `#` token rather than at `children[0]` the way an ordinary call's receiver or name would be — not treated as a member call or an implicit `self.` call either, since a macro resolves by its own name alone. Calls nested inside a macro's own arguments already resolve through the walker's existing, unconditional recursion into every node's children, so no change was needed there (verified directly).

Attached macro usage stays out of scope, as the issue asks: an attribute like `@AddCompletion` on a type is not a `macro_invocation` at all and stays unresolved (fail closed, verified it mints no spurious node).

Reproduced the issue's exact repro against a clean v8 checkout before the fix (confirmed `stringify` is entirely absent and there's no `calls` edge), then verified the declaration gets a node and the freestanding call resolves to it after the fix. Added regression tests in a new `tests/test_swift_macro_declarations.py`.

Ran the full suite plus `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`; the only failures are the pre-existing ones already present on a clean v8 checkout, unrelated to this change.

title: [Bug]: vbnet: no calls edge through field receivers or With blocks (WinForms-style forms)
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Follow-up to #4570 / #4573, as suggested in the PR discussion. With #4573 (`0fcda3a129`), a VB.NET call through a parameter or a typed local gets its `calls` edge. A call through a **field**, or through a **`With` block**, still gets none. #4573 records both as expected-failure tests (`field`; `With` on a local).

In WinForms-style VB these are the usual shapes. A form holds its collaborators in fields, often initialised in the declaration or declared in the other half of a partial class (`Form1.Designer.vb`), and uses `With` blocks on them. So in a form most outgoing calls to other classes have no edge, and `affected` / `path` miss those callers.

This repro covers the shapes beyond the two in #4573's tests, one method per case:

- F1: field initialised in its declaration (`As New`)
- F2: field assigned in `Sub New`
- F3: `Me._field.Method()`
- F4: field typed as a C# class
- F5: field declared in the other partial file (`OrderForm.Designer.vb`)
- W1–W4: `With` on a field, a typed local, `New Repository()`, and a C#-typed field
- P1: parameter (control, already resolved by #4573)

Expected: a `calls` edge for each case. In each, the receiver's type is declared in the same statement or field declaration and names exactly one type in the corpus. The C# equivalent, `private Store _store = new Store();` then `_store.Save()`, does get an edge.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
Four files in one folder:

`Repository.vb`
Public Class Repository
    Public Sub Load(id As Integer)
    End Sub
    Public Sub Save()
    End Sub
End Class

`PriceRules.cs`
namespace Shop.Rules
{
    public class PriceRules
    {
        public decimal Total(int id) { return 0m; }
    }
}

`OrderForm.Designer.vb`
Partial Class OrderForm
    Inherits System.Windows.Forms.Form

    Friend Archive As New Repository()
End Class

`OrderForm.vb`
Partial Class OrderForm
    Private _repository As New Repository()
    Private _rules As New Shop.Rules.PriceRules()
    Private _late As Repository

    Public Sub New()
        _late = New Repository()
    End Sub

    Public Sub F1_FieldNew()
        _repository.Load(1)
    End Sub
    Public Sub F2_FieldAssignedLater()
        _late.Save()
    End Sub
    Public Sub F3_MeField()
        Me._repository.Save()
    End Sub
    Public Sub F4_FieldCSharp()
        _rules.Total(1)
    End Sub
    Public Sub F5_FieldInOtherPartialFile()
        Archive.Save()
    End Sub

    Public Sub W1_WithField()
        With _repository
            .Load(2)
        End With
    End Sub
    Public Sub W2_WithLocal()
        Dim r As New Repository()
        With r
            .Save()
        End With
    End Sub
    Public Sub W3_WithNew()
        With New Repository()
            .Load(3)
        End With
    End Sub
    Public Sub W4_WithFieldCSharp()
        With _rules
            .Total(2)
        End With
    End Sub

    Public Sub P1_Parameter(x As Repository)
        x.Save()
    End Sub
End Class

GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none graphify extract fields-repro --code-only

`graphify explain` on each case method shows whether it has an outgoing `calls` edge:

graphify explain "F1_FieldNew()" --graph fields-repro/graphify-out/graph.json    # only the <-- OrderForm [method] edge
graphify explain "P1_Parameter()" --graph fields-repro/graphify-out/graph.json   # --> Save() [calls] [INFERRED]
```

### Additional Environment Details

### Additional context

## What this changes
Two small additions, docs only:
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`:** an optional subsection under *Working with AI Coding Agents*, on giving a contributor's

Work on this repository repeats. In the 12 months to October 2026, 1,134 fix commits touched only 91 distinct files,

remembers where past answers were, saves most in exactly that situation.

I replayed the last 50 fix commits on `v8`. Each was asked against its parent commit, in the words of the commit

|---|---|---|
| right file first | 12 (24%) | 19 (38%) |
| right file in the top 5 | 36 (72%) | 40 (80%) |
| a changed line in the top 5 | 11 (22%) | — |

With 50 fixes, these shares can move by about ±14 points by chance.

modeld forecast .                 # git history only

Each worktree gets its own storage directory. `GRAPHIFY_OUT` still takes priority, and existing behavior is unchanged unless the feature is enabled

Also fixes source-root lookup for external graphs and adds regression tests
