title: fix(csharp): give each method overload its own node and bind calls by argument count
body:
Fixes #4584

C# overloads all got the same node id, so the graph only kept the first one. Every caller pointed at it, and the later overloads' own calls were credited to it. On the issue's repro, `TwoArgs()` showed up as calling `Banner(int)`, and `Banner(int)` showed up as calling `Pad`.

What changed:
- The first overload keeps the id it already had. Each other signature gets an id salted with its parameter signature, the same way #3302/#4415 salt colliding names. Methods without overloads keep the same ids.
- C# method nodes now carry their parameter count in metadata (`arity`, plus `min_arity`/`variadic` for optional/`params`/extension parameters, and `signature`). A call binds to the overload its argument count fits. If more than one fits (e.g. `M(int)` vs `M(string)`), it binds to the first declared one, same as before.
- This is wired into the in-file call walk, the receiver-typed member-call resolver, the bare-name cross-file pass, and interface dispatch (interface overloads pair with the implementation of the same signature/arity). The new metadata keys are forwarded on incremental (watch) rebuilds.
- `test_overloads_stay_one_node` asserted the old behaviour, so it now checks that overloads still aren't treated as an underscore collision. Two comments in the dispatch tests that described the old single-node behaviour are updated.

Testing:
- New `tests/test_csharp_overloads.py`: the issue repro, unchanged ids for methods without overloads, in-file and instance calls, same-count overloads, optional/`params`, same-file partial halves, a duplicate signature behind `#if`, interface dispatch, and ids that don't change with whitespace or CRLF.
- Ran the full suite on 3.10/3.12/3.13/3.14 against unmodified v8. Same pre-existing failures, no new ones.
- Ran `graphify extract <dir> --code-only --no-label` on the issue's repro. Before: one `Banner` node and both callers going to it. After: two nodes (L5/L10), `OneArg -> Banner(int)`, `TwoArgs -> Banner(int, string)`, `Banner(int) -> Format`, `Banner(int, string) -> Pad`.

Known limit: only the argument count is used, not the argument types, so overloads with the same count still go to the first one.

Written with help from Grok Bot; I reviewed and tested it.

title: fix(detect): read ignore-pattern escapes and [^...] the way git does
body:
## What does this PR do?

`.gitignore` / `.graphifyignore` patterns are matched with `fnmatch`, which differs from git in two ways that change which files get indexed:

- No backslash escape. `\*`, `\?`, `\[`, `\!`, `\ ` and `\\` keep the backslash as a literal character, so the pattern never matches. GitHub's VisualStudio.gitignore has `Generated\ Files/`, so graphify indexes the generated code under `Generated Files/` that git ignores. `\!important.py` and `app/\[id\].py` fail the same way.
- `[^a]` is read as the set {`^`, `a`} rather than "not `a`", so `[^a]b.py` ignores `ab.py`, which git keeps.

Repro with the VisualStudio template (graphify 0.9.92 from PyPI):

```text
$ git check-ignore -v "Generated Files/winrt/base.h"
.gitignore:62:Generated\ Files/	Generated Files/winrt/base.h

$ python -c 'from graphify.detect import detect; ...'   # code files
0.9.92:  ['Generated Files/winrt/base.h', 'src/main.cpp']
branch:  ['src/main.cpp']
```

`graphify update` on the same tree adds `generated_files_winrt_base*` nodes on 0.9.92, and none on this branch.

The fix matches each path component with a small translation of git's wildmatch rules: backslash escapes, `[!...]` / `[^...]` negation, ranges, and an unclosed `[` matching nothing, as in git. `**`, anchoring, directory-only patterns, negation, NFC handling and the Windows case-insensitive name match are unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a path is ignored exactly when git would ignore it, with the documented exceptions (inline `#` comments, stripped leading whitespace).

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test**.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Differential check against git: random trees (1,800 of them) with random `.gitignore` files, some nested, built from a vocabulary of escapes, sets, `**`, anchors and negations. Each file's result compared with `git check-ignore --no-index`. Before: 19-37 mismatches per 150 trees; after: 0. Those runs left out two cases that differ on purpose or by encoding: leading whitespace, which graphify strips, and multi-byte names against single-character sets, where git matches bytes.

Limitations: POSIX classes such as `[[:digit:]]` are still not supported (they weren't before either).

## How was this tested?

title: fix(csharp): give each overload its own node, location and calls (#4584)
body:
Fixes #4584.

A C# method name declared twice on one type, with different parameters, minted ONE node at the first declaration's location. The second overload had no node at all: every caller of either overload got a `calls` edge to the same survivor, the second overload's own outgoing calls were credited to the first instead, and the second overload's own location was simply lost — matching all three bullets in the issue's own "What happened" list.

Underscore salting (`_underscore_salted_nid`) never caught this, since every overload shares one literal spelling, not a name/underscore-variant pair, and so is never more than one entry in that collision check's own raw-name set. This extends `_csharp_pre_scan_name_collisions` to also count each method declaration by its own EXACT name (deliberately not the folded id `_Action`/`Action` already collapse onto, which is a different, unrelated collision); a name declared two or more times salts every one of its own node ids by that declaration's own parameter signature (confirmed via the grammar that two overloads always differ there), so the outcome never depends on which overload the walk visits first, and a type with no overloads keeps its ids exactly as before.

The cross-file member call resolver (`Type.Method()`, the capitalized-receiver tier in `_resolve_csharp_member_calls`) now reads back each overload's own parameter count — stamped on the node at extraction time — and the call's own argument count, read from its `argument_list` at the same point its receiver and callee are. A call naming an overloaded method binds to the one overload whose arity it actually matches. Two overloads sharing one arity but different parameter types cannot be told apart this way (that would need real argument expression type inference this extractor does not attempt), so such a call stays unresolved rather than guessing — matching the project's existing fail-closed philosophy, and covered by its own test. An override still shadows its base class chain whether or not a specific overload under it is resolvable, unchanged from before.

Two existing tests asserted the OLD, now intentionally-changed behavior directly and needed updating, not removing: `test_csharp_underscore_collisions.py::test_overloads_stay_one_node` (renamed, now asserts each overload gets its own node — the dedicated repro moved to the new file below) and `test_csharp_interface_dispatch.py::test_overloads_collapsed_into_one_node_still_link` (renamed, now asserts the dispatch guard correctly treats a genuinely-ambiguous overloaded implementer as a tie rather than linking to what used to be a single, blended node).

Reproduced the issue's exact two-file repro against a clean v8 checkout before the fix (confirmed only one `Banner` node, at L5, swallowing both overloads' calls), then verified both overloads get their own node/location, each keeps its own outgoing calls, and `OneArg`/`TwoArgs` each bind to the correctly-arity-matched overload after the fix. Added regression tests in a new `tests/test_csharp_overloads.py`.

Ran the full suite plus `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`; the only failures are the pre-existing ones already present on a clean v8 checkout, unrelated to this change.

title: [Bug]: JS/TS: member call binds to a same-named function in the file, so delegating wrappers become false self-loops (#4082 still reproduces on 0.9.93)
body:
## Summary

In JS and TS, a member call `receiver.name(...)` is resolved to a function called `name` declared in the **same file**, ignoring the receiver. Inside a same-named wrapper, this becomes a `calls` self-loop marked `EXTRACTED`.

This is the bug in #4082, which was closed by its reporter after they pruned the edges in their own repo. It still reproduces on **0.9.93**, in plain `.js` as well as `.ts`, including #4082's own `window.confirm` example.

## Repro (0.9.93, AST only)

`app.js`:

```js
import { createHistory } from "./history.js";
const history = createHistory();

export function appendFrame(entry) {
  return history.appendFrame(entry);   // delegates to the history object
}

export function confirm(message) {
  return window.confirm(message);      // the #4082 case
}
```

`history.js`:

```js
export function createHistory() {
  return { appendFrame: (e) => e };
}
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract
root = Path("repro").resolve()
r = extract(sorted(root.glob("*")), cache_root=root, root=root)
print([e["source"] for e in r["edges"]
       if e.get("relation") == "calls" and e["source"] == e["target"]])
# 0.9.92 and 0.9.93, .js and .ts alike: ['app_appendframe', 'app_confirm']
```

The collision is with any function of that name in the file, not only the enclosing one. With `function appendFrame` declared elsewhere in the file and a wrapper `addFrame` calling `history.appendFrame()`, the graph records `addFrame -> appendFrame`, which is also wrong.

For comparison: if no function of that name exists in the file, the member call produces no edge. Python does not have this problem; `history.append_frame()` inside `def append_frame` produces no self-loop.

## Impact in a real project

The repo is a JS frontend whose `app.js` is a composition root: about 220 wrappers of the form `function x(...) { return someController.x(...); }`. That file alone yields **219 false self-loops**, 92% of all self-loops in a 7.7k-node graph, and `graphify diagnose` cannot tell them from real recursion.

The bigger problem is the lost edge, not the extra one. Each wrapper's real dependency on the controller method disappears. So "who calls the controller's `appendFrame`?" misses every caller that goes through the wrapper, and BFS from the wrapper never reaches the module that does the work.

## Expected

For `receiver.name()` where `receiver` is not `this`/`self`:

- **Never** bind it to a same-file function by bare name. In particular, never to the enclosing function: a member call cannot be direct recursion.
- If the receiver can be followed, resolve the method there. Here `receiver` is a module-level `const` initialised from an imported factory.
- Otherwise emit no edge, or an `INFERRED`/`AMBIGUOUS` one, rather than an `EXTRACTED` edge to the wrong node.

## Related

- #4082: same bug, TS, closed without a code change
- #4418: the same pattern in C#
- #2041, #2023: member calls in general

title: fix(swift): keep same-named nested types under different outers apart
body:
Fixes #4575.

Two Swift types nested in different parents in the same file, with the same name, collapsed into one node. The node id was the file stem plus the bare name, with no enclosing-type component, so e.g. `struct Person { enum CodingKeys }` and `struct Place { enum CodingKeys }` in one file both minted `models_codingkeys`. That one node ended up `contains`-ed by both structs and carried the union of both enums' own cases.

0.9.92 already fixed the identical same-file-id-collision shape for Python (folding the immediate enclosing class into a nested class's id once a parent is known, via `_extract_generic` in `graphify/extractors/engine.py`). This applies the same fix for Swift: when a class/struct/enum/protocol/actor declaration has an enclosing type (`parent_class_nid` is set), its id becomes that type's own id plus its name, instead of the file stem plus the bare name. A top-level type (no enclosing type) is completely unaffected, since the new branch only fires when a parent exists. Case/member ids (`case_of` edges) already derive from their owner's id, so each `CodingKeys` enum's own cases automatically land on the correct, now-distinct enum node with no separate change needed.

Reproduced the issue's exact repro against a clean v8 checkout before the fix (confirmed one shared `CodingKeys` node), then verified two distinct nodes after the fix, each contained by only its own struct and keeping only its own case. Added regression tests in `tests/test_languages.py`: the issue's repro end-to-end, and a control confirming a top-level (non-nested) type's id is unchanged.

Ran the full suite plus `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`; both clean.

title: fix(swift): stop an extension of an outside type absorbing every same-named reference
body:
Fixes #4574.

`_merge_swift_extensions` correctly leaves an `extension` of a type with no declaration anywhere in the corpus untouched — there is nothing real to fold it into. But the untouched node still carries the label of the extended type (e.g. `String`), and the separate, generic bare-reference resolver (`_rewire_unique_stub_nodes`) matches purely by label when it has exactly one node sharing that label. With no other `String` declared anywhere, that one extension node became the unique "real" definition every other `String`-typed field in the corpus bound onto — a `private extension String` in one file silently absorbed every reference to the builtin type.

A class node built from a Swift `extension` declaration now carries a `swift_extension` metadata marker at creation. Any node still carrying it after `_merge_swift_extensions` runs is, by construction, one the merge could not fold into a real declaration — either the extended type lives outside the corpus, or its label was ambiguous (multiple real candidates, which the merge already refuses to guess between). `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` now skips any such node when building its pool of candidate real definitions, mirroring the exclusion the extension merge itself already applies when looking for something to fold an extension into.

An extension of a type the corpus *does* define is unaffected: that extension node gets folded into the real type by the merge and never survives to be seen by the rewire pass at all, so ordinary cross-file extension resolution (calls, references) keeps working exactly as before.

Reproduced the issue's exact two-file repro against a clean v8 checkout before the fix (confirmed the one `String` node, the extension, absorbing `Person.name`'s reference). After the fix, that reference lands on an ordinary unresolved builtin stub instead, and a control case (extension of an in-corpus type) still folds into one node with references resolving normally. Added regression tests for both in `tests/test_swift_cross_file_calls.py`.

Ran the full suite plus `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`; both clean.

title: [Bug]: test_the_pool_hands_its_workers_the_overrides never resets _ACTIVE_SCAN_ROOT, so 9 tests fail in a different order
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

`test_the_pool_hands_its_workers_the_overrides` in
tests/test_language_overrides.py leaves `_ACTIVE_SCAN_ROOT` set to its own
tmp dir after it finishes. Any test that runs after it and expects
`active_scan_root()` to be None fails: 2 tests in
test_extractor_scan_root_context.py and 7 XAML tests in test_dotnet.py.

The default test order never runs those files right after the leaking test,
so a normal `pytest` run passes. A different order fails in one serial
process, with no xdist.

The test swaps `ProcessPoolExecutor` for a `ThreadPoolExecutor` subclass so
it can record the pool's initializer. The 25 extractions then run as threads
in the test process. Each one goes through `_safe_extract_with_xaml_root`
in graphify/extract.py:

```python
previous_root = set_active_scan_root(root.resolve())
try:
    return _safe_extract(extractor, path, scan_root=root)
finally:
    set_active_scan_root(previous_root)
```

`_ACTIVE_SCAN_ROOT` is one module global in graphify/extractors/base.py, so
the threads share it. When two calls overlap, the second saves the first
one's root as `previous_root` and restores it last:

```text
thread A: previous = None, set root
thread B: previous = root, set root
thread A: restore None
thread B: restore root      <- still set after extract() returns
```

With the pool forced to one thread, the global ends as None (3 of 3 runs).
With the default thread count, it ends as the tmp dir (3 of 3 runs).

Expected: the global is None again after the test, whatever order the
tests run in.


### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# graphify v8 at 86c57be8, from a source checkout, serial (no -n)
pytest -p no:randomly \
  "tests/test_language_overrides.py::test_the_pool_hands_its_workers_the_overrides" \
  tests/test_extractor_scan_root_context.py tests/test_dotnet.py
# -> 9 failed, 42 passed   (3 of 3 runs)

pytest -p no:randomly tests/test_extractor_scan_root_context.py tests/test_dotnet.py
# -> 50 passed             (3 of 3 runs)

# Full suite in random order, serial:
pytest -p randomly --randomly-seed=2
# -> 9 failed, 8383 passed, 14 skipped: the same 9 tests
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
FAILED tests/test_extractor_scan_root_context.py::test_active_scan_root_defaults_to_none
FAILED tests/test_extractor_scan_root_context.py::test_active_scan_root_set_get_restore_nested
FAILED tests/test_dotnet.py  (7 XAML tests: viewmodel and DataContext linking,
       the CommunityToolkit link, prune-noise-dirs, non-UTF-8 code-behind)

active_scan_root() after the leaking test:
/var/tmp/.../test_the_pool_hands_its_worker0
```

### Graphify version

0.9.92

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables involved. Reproduced on a clean checkout
of v8 with a fresh venv.


### Additional context

Only the test is affected. Real runs extract through `ProcessPoolExecutor`,
and each worker process has its own copy of the global. I found no thread
pool on that path.

Two ways to fix it:
- In the test, run the pool with `max_workers=1`, or reset `_ACTIVE_SCAN_ROOT`
  afterwards with `monkeypatch`.
- In the code, make the scan root a `contextvars.ContextVar`, so each thread
  has its own value. This also protects any later caller that runs
  `extract()` from several threads.

Found while timing the suite. Under `pytest -n` it shows up on whichever
worker runs these files after the leaking test.

title: [Bug]: install and wheel tests write into the package and the repo build/, so a killed or concurrent run breaks the checkout
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

Two test fixtures write into folders that every process shares: the
installed package and the repo's own `build/`. One serial pytest run passes.
A killed run, or two runs on the same checkout, break in ways the suite
doesn't report.

**1. The real `graphify/skills/claude` bundle is moved out of the package.**

The `fake_bundle` fixture in tests/test_install_references.py (lines 31-64),
and `test_hard_fail_when_bundle_dir_present_but_references_missing` (line
180), do this:

```text
shutil.move(graphify/skills/claude -> a mkdtemp() backup)
write a fake bundle in its place
run the test
move the real bundle back      <- in finally
```

`finally` doesn't run when the process gets SIGTERM, which is what `kill`
and `timeout` send. Python has no handler for it, so the process ends where
it is. The fake bundle stays in the package, the real files stay in a
backup under the temp dir, and `git status` shows them as deleted and
modified. Ctrl-C (SIGINT) is fine: Python raises `KeyboardInterrupt`, and
the fixture restores the bundle on the way out.

While the bundle is moved away, any other process that reads the package
fails. That includes a second pytest run on the same checkout.

**2. Wheel builds share the repo's `build/` folder.**

The `wheel_namelist` fixture in tests/test_wheel_packaging.py (lines 55-66)
runs `python -m build --wheel --no-isolation --outdir <tmp> <repo>`. The
wheel lands in `<tmp>`, but setuptools still works in `<repo>/build/`. Two
builds at once on one checkout delete each other's files. The fixture then
calls `pytest.skip` for every dependent test, so the run that lost reports
133 skips and no failure.

Expected: a killed or concurrent test run leaves the checkout unchanged,
and a broken wheel build shows up as a failure, not a skip.


### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# graphify v8 at 86c57be8, from a source checkout, serial (no -n)

# 1a. Kill pytest during a fake_bundle test.
#     pause.py pauses inside the test, after the fixture has moved the bundle:
cat > /tmp/pause.py <<'EOF'
import os, time, pytest
@pytest.hookimpl(hookwrapper=True)
def pytest_runtest_call(item):
    open("/tmp/paused", "w").write(str(os.getpid()))
    time.sleep(60)
    yield
EOF
rm -f /tmp/paused
PYTHONPATH=/tmp pytest -p pause -p no:randomly \
  "tests/test_install_references.py::test_install_stages_references_sidecar" &
while [ ! -f /tmp/paused ]; do sleep 0.2; done
kill -TERM "$(cat /tmp/paused)"
git status --short graphify/skills/claude     # D and M lines
pytest -p no:randomly tests/test_install_references.py tests/test_install.py
# -> 3 failed, 133 passed, 1 skipped   (intact checkout: 136 passed, 1 skipped)
git checkout -- graphify/skills/claude        # restore

# 1b. Two serial runs on one checkout at the same time.
for i in $(seq 30); do pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/test_install_references.py; done &
for i in $(seq 30); do pytest -q -p no:randomly tests/test_install.py; done

# 2. Two wheel-test runs at the same time.
rm -rf build
pytest -rs -p no:randomly tests/test_wheel_packaging.py --basetemp=/tmp/w1 &
pytest -rs -p no:randomly tests/test_wheel_packaging.py --basetemp=/tmp/w2
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
1a. Stopped while the fake bundle is in place, 3 runs each:
    SIGINT      exit 2    bundle restored
    SIGTERM     exit 143  fake bundle left behind
    SIGKILL     exit 137  fake bundle left behind
    timeout 30  exit 124  fake bundle left behind (1 run)

    git status:  D graphify/skills/claude/references/add-watch.md
                 D graphify/skills/claude/references/exports.md
                 M graphify/skills/claude/references/extraction-spec.md
                 D graphify/skills/claude/references/github-and-merge.md
                 D graphify/skills/claude/references/hooks.md
                 M graphify/skills/claude/references/query.md
                 D graphify/skills/claude/references/transcribe.md
                 D graphify/skills/claude/references/update.md
    leftover:    <TMPDIR>/tmpXXXXXXXX/bundle_backup

    Follow-up run on that checkout: 3 failed, 133 passed, 1 skipped

2.  5 of 5 times, one run skipped all 133 tests and the other passed:

    Two runs one after the other: 133 passed both times.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.92

### Operating System

Linux

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables involved. Reproduced on a clean checkout
of v8 with a fresh venv, using an editable install of that checkout.
`graphify.__file__` pointed into the checkout, so the fixture moved the
checkout's own `graphify/skills/claude`.

Each run had a single pytest process, except 1b and 2, where two serial
processes ran at the same time. Under `pytest -n` both problems show up in
one command: install tests fail with the same `shutil.Error`, and about 110
wheel tests are skipped.

A CI job that hits its time limit gets SIGTERM, so it can leave a cached
checkout in the 1a state. A `graphify install` from that checkout would then
copy the fake references, and a wheel built from it ships them
(`test_built_wheel_ships_the_full_skill_payload` fails on that checkout).

Possible fixes:
- Bundle: monkeypatch the package dir the install code reads to a copy
  under `tmp_path`, so nothing in the real package moves.
- Wheel: build from a copy of the repo under `tmp_path`, so `build/` is
  private. Separately, fail instead of skipping when `python -m build` is
  available but the build fails. The `_has_build()` check already covers
  machines without `build`.

title: fix(build): rewire doc-to-code edges whose endpoint was replaced by re-extraction (#1711)
body:
Fixes #1711.

`build_merge`'s and `merge_raw_extraction`'s replace-per-source step correctly drops a re-extracted file's own stale nodes/edges, keyed on the item's OWN `source_file`. An edge owned by an UNCHANGED file (e.g. a doc referencing a function) survives that filter untouched, since the edge's own `source_file` wasn't re-extracted — but if the edge's *target* lives in a file that WAS re-extracted, that target node was just dropped by the same filter. Extraction is not id-stable across runs (#1695), so the re-extracted file's new node for the same symbol often gets a different id (e.g. requalified with a file-stem prefix). The surviving edge keeps naming the old id, which no longer exists.

That dangling reference then either vanishes silently in `build_from_json`'s generic dangling-edge drop (the `build_merge` path) or rides along as an unresolvable raw reference (`merge_raw_extraction`, the `--no-cluster` incremental path). Because the surviving endpoint's own file was never re-extracted, nothing ever re-emits the edge against the target's new id on a later run either — the loss is permanent, not just until the next rebuild, matching what both the original report and the independent production-corpus comment on the issue describe.

## Fix

Both functions now re-resolve a dropped endpoint by `(source_file, label)` against the fresh chunk — the same identity `build_from_json`'s own ghost-merge already trusts for AST/LLM twin detection — and rewrite the edge onto the one fresh node that claims that pair. Matching both the raw `source_file` string and its `_norm_source_file` form, same as the rest of this replace machinery.

Conservative by construction: an edge is only rewired when EXACTLY ONE fresh node matches; zero or 2+ candidates leave it exactly as before, so it still reaches the ordinary dangling-edge drop rather than guessing. A genuinely deleted endpoint (via `prune_sources`) is unaffected — the new logic only ever looks at nodes dropped for being *replaced*, never ones dropped for being *pruned* — so deletion still removes the edge as before.

`merge_raw_extraction`'s own docstring already states its replace/prune semantics "mirror `build_merge` exactly, so the raw and clustered incremental paths can't drift" — it has the identical bug via the identical mechanism, so this fixes both rather than just the one the issue's own repro exercises.

Out of scope, left as a documented follow-up: the issue's "residual hyperedge gap" (item 2 of its proposed fix) — a dropped hyperedge whose full member set is still resolvable in the merged graph. That's a related but separate carry-forward mechanism from ordinary edges and deserves its own focused change.

## Verification

- Reproduced the issue's own minimal repro against current `v8` before the fix: a doc→code edge disappears entirely after re-extracting only the code file (0 edges after, where 1 is expected).
- Verified via `git show`+file-swap (never `git stash`) that the pre-fix code reproduces this exactly, and that restoring the fixed file is byte-identical to the working tree.
- Added `tests/test_build_merge_edge_survival.py`: the repro for both `build_merge` and `merge_raw_extraction`, an ambiguous-candidates control (left unresolved), a genuine-deletion control (still pruned), and a no-op-update control (nothing spuriously rewritten).
- Full suite (`python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`) and `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check` both clean.

title: fix(js): never bind a nameless member-call receiver to a same-named method in the file
body:
Fixes #4598.

In JS/TS, a member call `receiver.name(...)` reached the per-file bare-name map the same way an unqualified call does, ignoring the receiver entirely. Inside a delegating wrapper (`function appendFrame(e) { return history.appendFrame(e); }`) this fabricated an EXTRACTED `calls` self-loop; more generally it could bind to any other same-named function in the file instead of the receiver's own method (`window.confirm()` binding to a local `confirm`, as in #4082). Reproduced the issue's own two-file example and confirmed both the self-loop and the lost real dependency it describes.

This mirrors #4422's fix for the identical pattern in C# (`f41ec2ec`): every JS/TS member call whose receiver is not `this`/`self` now defers instead of falling back to the bare-name map. The deferred call still reaches the existing cross-file member-call resolver, which binds it correctly when the receiver's declared type is known (a TypeScript annotation, a constructor parameter property, etc.), and otherwise leaves it unresolved rather than guessing — fail closed, like every other language this project already handles this way.

One case needed its own, narrower exception rather than deferring: a method assigned onto a local factory object calling a sibling through that same object (`store.get()` from inside `store.set = (k, v) => store.get(k)`, the existing #1322/#3408 pattern). The cross-file resolver only sees whole-file state and could still bind that call to an unrelated object's same-named member, so this one case is resolved directly off the caller's own owner id instead, which the receiver name reconstructs exactly, not off the file-wide bare-name map.

Verified the fix against the issue's exact repro (self-loop gone, no fabricated edge), a general wrong-sibling-binding case, and three controls: a bare unqualified call still resolves by name, `this.m()` calls are untouched, and a TypeScript-typed receiver still resolves through its declared type. Added regression tests in a new `tests/test_js_member_call_bare_name_fallback.py`.

Ran the full suite (unrelated pre-existing failures only, identical set before and after this change) plus `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`, both clean.

title: fix(dedup): merge a concept re-mentioned with a trailing qualifier
body:
Fixes #3568.

A concept re-mentioned from a saved memory file (`graphify-out/memory/query_*.md`) keeps its own name but can grow a trailing parenthetical gloss naming where it was mentioned from — the issue's own example is `Registry Resolver` becoming `Registry Resolver (port-registry-resolution doc concept)`. The node-ID rule derives the id straight from the label, so that gloss forks a second id for a concept that already has one, and an edge that should have landed on the original lands on the fork instead, with nothing in the existing dedup pipeline catching it afterward — the cross-file concept merge in `deduplicate_entities` already exists specifically to unify a `concept` node mentioned from more than one file, but it groups by an *exact* normalized-label match, which a label with an extra gloss appended fails.

This strips one trailing `(...)` group from a `concept` node's label before computing that group key in `deduplicate_entities`'s exact-normalization pass, so the gloss no longer changes which group the node falls into. Every later safety check — the file-anchored guard, the entropy floor, the cross-file "concept only" rule — is unchanged, so a node still only actually merges when those already decide it should; widening the grouping key only widens who is eligible to be considered, not who merges. The strip is scoped to `concept` nodes alone, so an unrelated node type whose label happens to end in parentheses (a document heading, for instance) keeps its existing, intentionally stricter, file-anchored behavior.

Reproduced the issue's exact scenario against a clean v8 checkout (confirmed two nodes survive and the duplicate's edge dangles on it instead of the canonical node), then verified the fix merges them and rewires the edge to the survivor, verified a genuinely different concept that also carries a qualifier still stays separate, and verified the strip has no effect outside `concept` nodes. Added regression tests to `tests/test_dedup.py` covering all three.

Ran the full suite plus `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`; both clean.

title: [Bug]: markdown mentions: a bare lowercase word in a code span links to an unrelated method that carries that name
body:
### What happened?

`resolve_markdown_mentions` links a bare code span (no `()`, no qualifier) to the corpus's single `_callable` that carries that label, and methods qualify. A word that is prose, not a reference, then becomes `heading --references--> SomeClass.word()` at INFERRED 0.95.

Expected: no edge. A parenthesis-less lowercase word in a code span (`redis` the server, `data`, `message`, `request`, `current`) is not evidence of a reference to a method on whichever unrelated class happens to define it.

On a real corpus (about 1,400 classes, 12 READMEs) 44 of 1,906 resolved mention edges were words of this kind: `data`, `message`, `request`, `previous`, `current`, `integrations`, `signature`, `moved`.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
d=$(mktemp -d)
printf 'class Cache:\n    def redis(self):\n        return "connection"\n' > $d/cache.py
printf '# Queue\n\nJobs run on `redis` (the server, not our code).\n' > $d/README.md
python - <<PY
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract
d = Path("$d")
r = extract([d / "cache.py", d / "README.md"], parallel=False, cache_root=d / "cache", root=d)
labels = {n["id"]: n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]}
print([(labels[e["source"]], labels[e["target"]], e["confidence"]) for e in r["edges"] if e.get("relation") == "references"])
PY
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
[('Queue', '.redis()', 'INFERRED')]
```

### Proposed fix

In the bare branch of `resolve_markdown_mentions` (`graphify/markdown_resolution.py`), when the span has no trailing `()` and no qualifiers and the candidate is a method (not `_callable_class`), keep the match only if the method's owner class (the `method` edge's source) is itself the target of a mention in the same document. `successWithWarnings` written next to `HandlerResult` keeps its edge; `redis` with no owner cited does not. The raw call already carries the span text in `context`, so the resolver can tell `redis` from `redis()`.

A stricter alternative is to require parentheses for any method match.

I have this running downstream as a post-pass and can open a PR with a regression test if you prefer that to a patch from the maintainers.

Related: #3561 (the feature that added code-span mentions).

Graphify version 0.9.93 (also 0.9.92), macOS, Python 3.14, installed with `uv tool`.

title: [Bug]: markdown mentions: `Ns\Class` and `Class::method()` are not recognised as symbol mentions (PHP, Rust, C++ docs)
body:
### What happened?

`_code_span_mention` (`graphify/extractors/markdown.py`) accepts the dotted form (`pkg.Name`) and the path-qualified form (`path.py::Name`), but not the separators other languages' docs use: `App\Services\Mailer` (backslash namespaces, PHP) and `Mailer::send()` (`Type::member`, PHP, Rust, C++). `_MD_BARE_MENTION_RE` allows only dots, and `_MD_PATH_MENTION_RE` needs a file extension before `::`, so both spans are dropped before the resolver sees them.

Expected: edges to `Mailer` and `.send()`, as the dotted and bare forms get.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
d=$(mktemp -d)
printf '<?php\n\nnamespace App\\Services;\n\nfinal class Mailer\n{\n    public function send(): void\n    {\n    }\n}\n' > $d/Mailer.php
printf '# Mail\n\nSee `App\\Services\\Mailer` and `Mailer::send()`.\n' > $d/README.md
python - <<PY
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract
d = Path("$d")
r = extract([d / "Mailer.php", d / "README.md"], parallel=False, cache_root=d / "cache", root=d)
labels = {n["id"]: n["label"] for n in r["nodes"]}
print([(labels[e["source"]], labels[e["target"]]) for e in r["edges"] if e.get("relation") == "references"])
PY
# control: same class, README says `Mailer` and `Mailer.send()`
printf '# Mail\n\nThe `Mailer` class and `Mailer.send()`.\n' > $d/README.md   # then run the same script
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
[]                                                  # `App\Services\Mailer` and `Mailer::send()`
[('Mail', 'Mailer'), ('Mail', '.send()')]            # control: bare and dotted forms
```

### Proposed fix

In `_code_span_mention`, treat `\` and `::` as qualifier separators the way `.` already is: `App\Services\Mailer` gives `["App", "Services", "Mailer"]`, `Mailer::send()` gives `["Mailer", "send"]`. The resolver already holds a dotted match to evidence (each qualifier must be an owner label or a path segment of the candidate), so no resolver change is needed. Two cases to leave out: `Foo::CONST` and `Foo::class` have no node to land on. A project namespace root such as `App\` that maps to the scan directory has no path segment and must be droppable (PSR-4 style).

Downstream, on a 12-README PHP corpus this adds 517 edges. I read a random sample of 30 resolver-only edges (both kinds mixed) and found none wrong; it is a sample, not an audit.

I can open a PR with a regression test if that is easier for you.

Related: #3561 (code-span mentions), #2615 (PHP support, consolidated).

Graphify version 0.9.93 (also 0.9.92), macOS, Python 3.14, installed with `uv tool`.

title: docs(skill): tell Gemini free-tier runs which quota error to stop on (#2840)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #2840.

A free-tier Gemini key can fail with two different quota errors, and only one of them clears when you retry:

- `generate_content_free_tier_input_token_count` is the per-minute input-token cap. It clears after about 60s, and a lower `max_concurrency` helps.
- `generate_content_free_tier_requests` is the per-day request cap. Retrying, backing off, or lowering concurrency does not clear it, and each attempt uses up another of the day's requests.

The skill named neither error, so the agent kept retrying the daily cap before falling back to subagents.

This PR adds a note to Step 3 of the core skill fragment that:
- names both error strings,
- says to stop calling `extract_corpus_parallel` on the daily cap and finish the remaining uncached files with subagents,
- explains that this switch re-extracts the files Gemini already finished.

The last point is true because semantic cache entries are keyed by the prompt fingerprint (#1939). The Gemini path stamps entries with `_extraction_system()` (`llm.py`, `_checkpoint_chunk`), while subagents use `references/extraction-spec.md`.

I only documented that behaviour. Sharing the cache key between the two prompts, the issue's option (b), is out of scope.

title: docs(skill): state the thin-community cutoff and offer .graphifyignore for large corpora (#2842)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Refs #2842. Fixes two of the four documentation gaps in that issue.

1. **Thin-community cutoff (item 1).** `report.generate()` only gives a community its own section in the report when it has at least `min_community_size` (default 3) real nodes. File, concept and rationale nodes don't count. Smaller communities are counted as "thin omitted". Step 5 never said this. It now states the cutoff and notes that those communities are still in `graph.json` and the visualizer.
2. **Large corpus: excluding a folder (item 3).** When the large-corpus warning fires, Step 2 only offered to narrow the run to one subfolder. If one of the biggest folders isn't project content (agent session logs, scratch, build output), it is better to exclude it. Step 2 now also offers to add that folder to `.graphifyignore`, which `detect()` already reads. The issue suggested surfacing `detect(extra_excludes=...)`, but I used `.graphifyignore` because it is the user-facing setting and reuses the existing ignore rules, as CONTRIBUTING asks.

Not included:
- **Item 2** (a typical dangling-edge rate): I have no measured data to back a number, so I didn't publish one.
- **Item 4** (a labeling strategy for hundreds of communities): it overlaps #4424 and the open docs PR #3926.

So this PR does not close #2842.

**Limitation:** the aider and devin skills are separate files that `--monolith-roundtrip` freezes against their pinned `v8` baseline.
