title: fix: fold SQL table stubs across files and bind schema-qualified names (#4653)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4653. A SQL table got one node per file that read it. A schema-qualified read like `dbo.Customers` never bound to the `CREATE TABLE` in another file, and a plain read like `Invoices` bound to a Python class of the same name.

There were three causes, all in the cross-file pass in `extract()`:

1. Stubs with the same id and no `source_file` are salted apart by `origin_file` in `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids`. So each file gets its own `dbo.Orders`.
2. `_is_type_like_definition` rejects any label with a `.`. A SQL table is `schema.name`, so `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` never binds `dbo.Customers` to its definition.
3. `.sql` is not in `_LANG_FAMILY_BY_EXT`, so the cross-language guard treats SQL as unknown and lets the Python class win.

This PR fixes all three in that pass. It doesn't touch the SQL extractor:

```diff
 _LANG_FAMILY_BY_EXT
+  ".sql": "sql"

 _is_type_like_definition(node)
-  dotted label -> not a definition
+  dotted label -> not a definition, unless the node comes from a .sql file

 _rewire_unique_stub_nodes
   remap each stub to its unique definition
+  for each stub from a .sql file
+    drop the remap if the definition is in another language
+    if it binds to nothing, group it by _norm_ident(label)
+  fold each group into its smallest id (so file order doesn't matter)
```

**Before** (v8, the issue's repro):

```text
dbo.ActiveCustomers  reads_from  dbo_customers                      (a stub, not the table)
dbo.LateOrders       reads_from  views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders
dbo.OpenOrders       reads_from  views_open_orders_sql_dbo_orders   (a second dbo.Orders)
dbo.Recent           reads_from  app_models_invoices                (the Python class)
```

**After:**

```text
dbo.ActiveCustomers  reads_from  tables_customers_dbo_customers     (the CREATE TABLE)
dbo.LateOrders       reads_from  views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders
dbo.OpenOrders       reads_from  views_late_orders_sql_dbo_orders   (one dbo.Orders)
dbo.Recent           reads_from  invoices                           (a SQL stub)
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Each SQL table is one node across the project. A read binds to the `CREATE TABLE` when exactly one file defines it, and never to a definition in another language.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Per-file extraction doesn't change, so the AST cache needs no bump. A revert brings back the per-file stubs on the next build.

**Blast Radius:** SQL nodes, and any edge between SQL and another language. On `microsoft/sql-server-samples` `wide-world-importers/wwi-ssdt` (336 `.sql` files):

| | v8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| nodes | 739 | 645 |
| table-like nodes | 172 | 79 |
| tables split across several nodes | 25 | 0 |
| non-`contains` edges | 146 | 146 |
| time (median of 3) | 5.5 s | 5.4 s |

`application.cities` goes from 7 nodes to 1, and `application.deliverymethods` from 10 to 1. 94 stub ids go away and none are added.

- **Other languages:** with `.sql` in the families, a call or reference between SQL and another language is no longer a candidate in `_cross_language_candidate`, the function-merge guard, or the cross-file call loop. No test depended on that.
- **Dotted labels in C#, Elixir and Julia:** the fixtures (`Demo.ViewModels`, `MyApp.Accounts.User`, `Base.Threads`) give the same nodes and edges, by sha256, on v8 and on this PR.
- **Saved graphs:** I built wwi-ssdt with v8, then ran this PR in the same folder. `graph.json` has 0 dangling edges and none of the 94 old stub ids. The same holds after editing a view and running `graphify update .` again.

**Limitations**

- **Bracket names:** a stub from `[dbo].[Orders]` and one from `dbo.Orders` fold only after #4649, because on v8 the parser's label is `dbo].[Orders`. A bracketed `CREATE TABLE` does bind (covered by a test).
- **Unqualified names:** `Orders` and `dbo.Orders` stay two tables. The default schema isn't known.
- **Two definitions:** when two files both `CREATE TABLE dbo.Orders`, reads go to one shared stub, not to either definition.
- **Old stub ids:** nothing maps an old per-file stub id to the merged node. A saved semantic edge that points at an old id won't follow it.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_sql_cross_file_tables.py` run `extract()` on small projects and compare node ids and `reads_from` targets. None of them calls a private helper.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| an undefined table read from two files is one node (`dbo.Orders`, `Orders`) | fail, fail | pass |
| reads bind to a table defined in another file (`dbo.Orders`) | fail | pass |
| reads bind to a table defined in another file (`Orders`) | pass | pass |
| `[dbo].[Orders]` defined, `dbo.Orders` read in another file | fail | pass |
| a SQL read of `Orders` doesn't bind to a Python `class Orders` | fail | pass |
| guard: a same-file definition still binds | pass | pass |
| guard: `dbo.Orders` and `sales.Orders` stay two tables | pass | pass |

```text
pytest tests/test_sql_cross_file_tables.py (tests on v8)    -> 5 failed, 3 passed
pytest tests/test_sql_cross_file_tables.py (this branch)    -> 8 passed
pytest test_multilang.py test_pg_introspect.py test_extract.py test_ejs_extractor.py -> 463 passed
pytest -q -p no:randomly (full suite, serial)               -> 8479 passed, 14 skipped
ruff check (changed files)                                  -> All checks passed
```

Running `extract()` with the file list reversed gives the same ids. With three files in all 6 orders, the merged node is always `a_sql_dbo_orders`.

title: fix(serve): accept the bracketed Host header of an IPv6 HTTP bind
body:
## What does this PR do?

Started with `python -m graphify.serve --transport http --host ::1`, the Streamable HTTP server rejects every request with **421**.

`_build_http_app()` builds the DNS-rebinding allowlist from the raw bind address, producing `::1` and `::1:8080`. A client that reaches the server at `http://[::1]:8080` sends `Host: [::1]:8080` (RFC 3986 brackets IPv6 literals), and the MCP SDK's `TransportSecuritySettings` compares Host headers exactly, so nothing matches:

```text
::1 Host: [::1]:8080      -> 421   (Invalid Host header: [::1]:8080)
::1 Host: [::1]           -> 421
127.0.0.1 Host: 127.0.0.1:8080 -> 200
```

The fix brackets an IPv6 literal before it goes into the allowlist. IPv4, hostname and wildcard binds behave as before.

## Type of change

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: on a non-wildcard bind, the server accepts exactly the Host headers a client uses to reach that address (plus the localhost aliases) and rejects all others. The new tests cover both directions: `[::1]:8080` and `[::1]` are accepted, and `evil.example:8080` still gets 421 on a `::1` bind. No persisted state is involved.

title: fix(ingest): never write a text capture through an existing entry
body:
## What does this PR do?

`graphify add <url>` has two capture paths with different collision rules:

- **Binary captures** (PDF, images) choose a free filename with `lstat()`, so they never replace any existing directory entry, including a symlink (#4393).
- **Text captures** (webpages, tweets, arXiv) still used `Path.exists()`. It follows symlinks, so a dangling symlink named like the capture (`raw/example_org_page.md -> /elsewhere/file`) reports "free", and `write_text()` follows the link and creates or overwrites its target outside the corpus. The loop also stopped after 999 numbered names and then overwrote `<stem>_999.md`.

This PR moves the existing `lstat()` loop into `_free_capture_path()` and uses it for both paths. Binary behaviour is unchanged; text captures now follow the same rule.

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant (already enforced for binaries by #4393): a capture never replaces, or writes through, an existing directory entry in the target directory. The new `test_text_captures_skip_existing_entries` covers a regular file and a dangling symlink. It fails on v8 for the symlink case: the write lands in the symlink's target. With the fix the capture goes to `_1.md`, the symlink is untouched, and its target is never created. The existing binary-capture tests pass unchanged.

title: docs: say the query log is opt-in, in the README and every translation
body:
## What does this PR do?

The README's privacy section says:

> every `graphify query`, `graphify path`, `graphify explain`, and MCP `query_graph` call is logged to `~/.cache/graphify-queries.log` ... Set `GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG_DISABLE=1` to opt out, or `GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG=/dev/null` to silence ...

Since #1797 the code does the opposite. `graphify/querylog.py::_log_path()` returns `None`, meaning no log, unless `GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG_ENABLE=1` (default path) or `GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG=<path>` is set. The README text appears to predate that change and survived the README trim. Readers are told their queries are recorded when they aren't, and they never learn how to switch logging on.

This PR rewrites that one bullet to match `querylog.py`:
- logging is off by default;
- `GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG_ENABLE=1` enables it at the default path;
- `GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG=<path>` enables it at a custom path;
- `GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG_RESPONSES=1` adds full responses;
- `GRAPHIFY_QUERY_LOG_DISABLE=1` forces it off.

The same bullet is updated in all 31 `docs/translations/README.*.md` files. Each keeps its translated label and only replaces the sentence body. The translations were written by hand for this one line, not regenerated; a native-speaker check or your usual regeneration pass is welcome.

title: docs(security): describe MCP graph-path handling as implemented
body:
## What does this PR do?

Two security docs promise a guard that the MCP server no longer has:

- `SECURITY.md` threat table: *"Path traversal in MCP server | `security.validate_graph_path()` resolves paths and requires them to be inside `graphify-out/`."*
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` Security list: *"Graph file paths → `validate_graph_path()` (must resolve inside `graphify-out/`)"*

`serve.py` stopped calling `validate_graph_path()` in 0.3.26 (6d394320, *fix MCP server path validation security issue*). It is now referenced only by tests. What the server actually does (`_read_graph()`, `_resolve_graph_path()`, `call_tool()`):

- it loads only `.json` files, rejecting anything over `check_graph_file_size_cap()`;
- it serves the graph it was started with, or, when a client passes `project_path`, `<project_path>/<GRAPHIFY_OUT>/graph.json` from **any** directory the process can read;
- a missing or corrupt client-selected graph becomes a tool error rather than stopping the server.

This PR rewrites the threat-table row and the ARCHITECTURE bullet to say exactly that. It also states the consequence for a shared HTTP server: any client holding the API key can query every graph the process can read.

The PR also fixes one line in "What graphify does NOT do". It said the `--transport http` option is "documented in the README", but that README section was removed in the README trim (565b22bc). The line now points to `python -m graphify.serve --help` and the `Dockerfile`, which do document it.

No code change. This PR does **not** propose re-adding path confinement: per-project serving is intended. It only makes the docs match the behaviour.

title: feat(label): accept externally-named communities via --from <path> (#3808)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3808. An external tool that names communities itself (e.g. [jev-graphify](https://github.com/190ibrahim/jev-graphify), which picks hub/candidate names with no LLM key) had to reimplement `graphify.cluster.community_member_sigs` byte-for-byte to produce a `.graphify_labels.json.sig` that a later `cluster-only`/`label` run would trust. Any drift between that copy and the real hash silently turned every external name back into a hub name, with no error — exactly the risk the issue describes.

This implements the issue's second proposed solution: `graphify label --from names.json` (also works on `cluster-only --from`) takes a `{community_id: name}` JSON map, applies it to the current clustering, and writes `.graphify_labels.json` **and its `.sig`** itself through the existing persistence path. An outside tool now only ever hands over names — never the hash.

## Behavior

- A community id missing from the map falls back to its deterministic hub label (same behavior as an unlabeled community today), so the output file is always complete.
- An id in the map that doesn't match any current community (e.g. stale ids after re-clustering) is ignored with a warning, not an error.
- Malformed/missing `--from` files, a non-object payload, or a non-string/empty name end in a clean CLI error, not a traceback.
- `--from` reuses the exact same write path (`write_json_atomic` for the labels, `write_text_atomic` for the `.sig`) that `cluster-only`/`label` already use, so there's no new persistence format to keep in sync with `community_member_sigs`.

## Testing

New `tests/test_label_from_file.py` (8 tests): every community named, hub-label fallback for an unnamed one, unknown-id warning, and the four error paths (missing file, malformed JSON, non-object payload, non-string name) — plus a check that `--from` works on `cluster-only` too, not just the `label` alias.

Also ran the full `test_labeling.py`, `test_cluster*.py`, `test_community_hub_labels.py`, `test_community_labels_skill.py`, `test_no_cluster_run_only_keys.py`, `test_cli_export.py`, `test_pin_hash_seed.py`, `test_cli_help.py` suites (172 passed, 2 skipped) to confirm no regression in the existing `cluster-only`/`label` paths.

title: fix(codex): quote a spaced exe path in the PreToolUse hook command
body:
The claude and gemini hooks (since #522/#1987) double-quote a resolved graphify path containing spaces, but `_install_codex_hook` embedded the resolver output raw. On a checkout path like `D:/Project V2/.venv/Scripts/graphify.EXE`, every shell that runs the hook (Git Bash on Windows → cmd.exe → POSIX sh) word-splits the command at the first space: the guard can never fire, and #2165's subcommand-parsing test splits at the same space and fails.

Mirror `_claude_pretooluse_hooks`/`_gemini_hook` with the same two-line guard: bare-name (project-scoped, #3129) installs are unaffected, as is any absolute path without spaces. `test_codex_hook_command_is_a_real_cli_subcommand` now parses hook commands with `shlex.split` instead of naive `.split()`, and a new regression test installs all three hosts under a spaced resolver output, proves `argv[0]` survives intact, and re-verifies uninstall recognition of the quoted entry.

## What does this PR do?

Codex hook installers were the only ones among the three JSON-hook hosts (claude, gemini, codex) that embedded `_resolve_graphify_exe()` output **unquoted** into the hook `command`. On any machine whose checkout/venv path contains a space (e.g. `D:/Project V2/.venv/Scripts/graphify.EXE`), every shell that executes hook commands word-splits the string at the first space: the PreToolUse guard is invoked as `D:/Program …` / `D:/Project …` and can never fire — the hook is permanently dead and `graphify uninstall`/reinstall cycles keep rewriting the same bad string.

This PR:

1. adds the same two-line quoting guard `_claude_pretooluse_hooks` and `_gemini_hook` already use since #522/#1987 (`graphify/install.py`, `_install_codex_hook`);
2. makes the #2165 subcommand-parsing test quote-aware (`shlex.split`, matching shell behavior);
3. adds `test_hook_commands_quote_a_spaced_resolved_exe`, a parametrization-free regression test exercising **claude + gemini + codex** under a spaced resolved path (`C:/Program Files/...`), asserting `argv[0] == spaced_exe` after `shlex.split` — under the old codex form this starts at `'C:/Program'`, proving the old failure — and re-verifying that a quoted entry is still recognized as graphify's own (uninstall/reinstall invariant).

Project-scoped installs (bare `graphify`, #3129) and space-free absolute paths are byte-identical to before.

body:
Three hook tests execute graphify's emitted scripts via `["sh", "-c", ...]` but were the only ones in `test_hooks.py` without the `skipif` guard the other probe tests already use. On Windows without a POSIX shell they fail with a bare `FileNotFoundError` instead of skipping, dirtying any Windows contributor's run. Separately, one watch-lifecycle test compared graphify's emitted POSIX-joined source keys against a `Path()`-rendered expectation, which on Windows looks for `src\page.tpl` where graphify writes `src/page.tpl`.

1. **`tests/test_hooks.py`** — adds the file's own established decorator to the 3 tests that missed it (the other probe tests already carry it at lines 890/911/928/941/1676):

   Each test's docstring already declares it proves *behavior* by "running the real emitted script under sh", so the skip is faithful to intent — on any machine with `sh` (all CI platforms) these tests run exactly as before, byte-for-byte.

2. **`tests/test_language_override_lifecycle.py`** — `test_watch_relative_roots_receive_config_events_without_rebasing_source_paths [src]` asserted `paths == {str(Path(argument) / "page.tpl")}`. title: fix(install): stage fake bundles in temp package root; fail-loud wheel builds
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4603. Two test fixtures mutated shared state outside the sandbox, so a killed (SIGTERM/SIGKILL runs no `finally` blocks) or concurrent pytest run left the checkout dirty or silently skipped 133 tests:

1. **`fake_bundle` / the hard-fail test in `tests/test_install_references.py`** moved the real `graphify/skills/claude` bundle out of the package and back on teardown. If the process died mid-test, the fake bundle stayed in the package (checkout shows D/M lines) and any concurrent run on the same checkout read a package with its bundle missing. Now the fixtures stage a **throwaway mini package root under `tmp_path`** (skill bodies, `always_on/`, the skills tree, then the fake/missing claude references) and point `graphify.install.__file__` at it via `patch`, so the real package is never touched and nothing can be left behind, no matter how the process dies. `test_install_from_read_only_package_dir` now chmod's the staged copy's references.
2. **`wheel_namelist` in `tests/test_wheel_packaging.py`** ran `python -m build` against the repo, whose shared `build/` dir made two concurrent runs on one checkout clobber each other, and the loser turned a broken build into 133 green `pytest.skip`s. Now the build is serialised by an `flock` on a temp-dir lock file keyed by the repo path (shared across processes on the same checkout, nothing added to the checkout; OS-released even if the holder is killed; no-op without `fcntl`), and a **failed wheel build is a failure, not a skip** — the missing-`build`-module skip stays.

title: feat(install): add DeepSeek Harness (dsh) platform target
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a `dsh` platform target for **DeepSeek Harness** (`graphify install --platform dsh`, aliases `deepseek` and `deepseek-harness`, plus `graphify dsh install|uninstall`). DSH is a Cordis-based agent harness whose skills come from a provider registry and whose versioned app profiles are composed from a user-global patch layer; because that layout is unlike any existing host, the integration needs both halves:

- **Skill** — copied to DSH's filesystem skill-provider root, `<DSH_HOME>/skills/graphify/` for a user install (default `~/.dsh/skills`) and `./.dsh/skills/graphify/` for `--project`. The target reuses the committed generic `agents` bundle, whose standard `name`/`description` frontmatter DSH's registry requires, so no new generated artifact is added.
- **MCP server** — registered in DSH's user-global loader patch layer, `<DSH_HOME>/cordis.patch.yml`, as an `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` stdio entry running `python -m graphify.serve <graph.json>`. DSH composes that file after every bundle and after the profile's own patch, so the graph tools appear as `mcp__graphify__*` without editing a profile.

The existing SDK harnesses use `AGENTS.md`-derived always-on instructions; DSH has no project-scoped configuration layer, so `--project` installs only the skill and points at the user-scope command for the graph server.

## The invariant this protects

A `graphify`-owned configuration block in a file the user also edits must be **additive, idempotent, and removable without collateral damage**:

- The entry is wrapped in `# >>> graphify MCP ... >>>` / `# <<< graphify MCP <<<` markers. Installing twice leaves exactly one block; uninstalling removes only that block and leaves every other patch entry byte-for-byte intact (`test_install_platform_dsh_preserves_user_patch_entries`).
- A patch file holding only `[]` (the shipped empty-layer form) is **replaced** rather than appended to; appending a block sequence after `[]` is invalid YAML (`test_install_platform_dsh_replaces_empty_document_patch`). The generated file parses as one top-level sequence.
- Paths (interpreter, graph) are emitted as single-quoted YAML scalars, so a project path containing spaces, `'`, or `#` stays literal (`test_mcp_block_quotes_paths_with_spaces`).
- Uninstall deletes the file when graphify's block was its only content, and otherwise re-emits the rest (`test_dsh_subcommand_install_uninstall_roundtrip`).
- `DSH_HOME` relocates both the skill root and the patch layer, matching the harness (`test_dsh_user_destination_honours_dsh_home`, `test_install_platform_dsh_custom_home_writes_both_roots`); `GRAPHIFY_OUT` relocates the served graph like every other read command (`test_graphify_out_env_is_honoured`).

## Limitations, stated explicitly

- The MCP entry is user-global by construction: DSH has no per-project configuration layer. A user-scope install (re)points the server at the registering project's `graphify-out/graph.json`; serving a different repository means re-running the install there, or passing DSH's per-call project argument.
- Serving requires the `mcp` extra. The installer detects that the configured interpreter cannot `import mcp` and prints the exact `graphifyy[mcp]` remediation instead of failing; the skill half still installs.
- The entry records an absolute `sys.executable` path, the same lifetime contract as the other hook installers: re-run the install after moving or recreating that environment.
- Windows is untested for this target (no DSH Windows profile was exercised).

## Regression-test coverage

`tests/test_dsh_install.py` (16 tests): destination map, `DSH_HOME` resolution, user vs `--project` scope, idempotent re-install, user-entry preservation, `[]` replacement, quoted paths, `GRAPHIFY_OUT`, the dedicated subcommand round trip, and alias resolution. `tests/conftest.py` now clears `DSH_HOME` in the autouse HOME sandbox so a developer running the suite inside DSH cannot have their real `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` mutated.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv sync --all-extras --frozen
uv run python -m pytest tests/ -q                      -> 8489 passed, 14 skipped
uv run python -m pytest tests/test_dsh_install.py -q   -> 16 passed
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --check                -> OK
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --audit-coverage       -> OK
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --schema-singleton     -> OK
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --monolith-roundtrip   -> OK
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --always-on-roundtrip  -> OK
uv run ruff check .                                    -> All checks passed
uv run graphify --help && uv run graphify install      -> both OK (isolated HOME)
```

End-to-end against the real harness: a `graphify install --platform dsh` run into a throwaway `DSH_HOME` produced the patch file; `dsh --profile headless --dump-config` on DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2` composed the `mcp-graphify` entry into the tree; an MCP `initialize` + `tools/list` handshake with the generated command returned `graphify 0.9.93` and the 10 graph tools; `graphify dsh uninstall` removed the skill and the entry.

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] No generated skill artifacts change: the target reuses the committed `agents` bundle, and the rendered skill bodies do not enumerate platform flags, so no `tools.skillgen --bless` output differs (`--check` is clean).
- [x] Extraction determinism is untouched; the change is confined to install/uninstall code paths.
- [x] Security review: the written file is YAML the user owns; all interpolated values (interpreter path, graph path) are quoted scalars, never shell- or Python-interpolated. The installer opens no network connection.
- [x] No API keys or local graph data are included.

title: ObjC category files (Foo+Cat.h/.m) leak the absolute checkout path into node ids
body:
## Summary

For an ObjC category/extension file (`Foo+Cat.h` / `Foo+Cat.m`), the class and
method node ids keep the **absolute checkout path** instead of the repo-relative
form. The same source therefore produces a different `graph.json` depending on
where it was checked out, so the graph is not reproducible and any downstream that
keys off node ids (e.g. an incremental Neo4j import) churns on every build machine.

Verified on `graphifyy==0.9.93` and on current `v8` (0.9.89).

## Reproduction

Extract the same ObjC source from two different directories and compare the id sets
(they should be identical):

```bash
unset GRAPHIFY_OUT
make_src() { mkdir -p "$1"; cat > "$1/Foo.h" <<'E'
#import <Foundation/Foundation.h>
@interface Foo : NSObject
- (void)bar;
@end
E
cat > "$1/Foo+Ext.h" <<'E'
#import "Foo.h"
@interface Foo (Ext)
- (void)baz;
@end
E
cat > "$1/Foo+Ext.m" <<'E'
#import "Foo+Ext.h"
@implementation Foo (Ext)
- (void)baz {}
@end
E
}
A=$(mktemp -d)/checkoutA/src; B=$(mktemp -d)/checkoutB/src
make_src "$A"; make_src "$B"
graphify extract "$A" --code-only --no-cluster --out "$A.out" >/dev/null 2>&1
graphify extract "$B" --code-only --no-cluster --out "$B.out" >/dev/null 2>&1
python3 - "$A.out/graphify-out/graph.json" "$B.out/graphify-out/graph.json" <<'E'
import json, sys
a, b = ({n["id"] for n in json.load(open(p))["nodes"]} for p in sys.argv[1:])
print("only in A:", sorted(a - b)); print("only in B:", sorted(b - a))
E
```

Actual — the `-baz` id differs per checkout dir and embeds the absolute path:

```
only in A: ['private_<tmpA>_checkouta_src_foo_foo_baz']
only in B: ['private_<tmpB>_checkoutb_src_foo_foo_baz']
```

Expected: identical id sets; `-baz` should be `foo_foo_baz`.

A category whose directory has no sibling base header leaks its **class** node id
too (e.g. `plug/Engine+Ads.h` with no `Engine.h` beside it →
`private_<tmp>_plug_engine_engine`).

## Root cause

A category keys its class/method nodes off the **base** stem
(`_objc_category_base_stem`: `Foo+Ext` → `Foo`, #1556), so those ids are built with
the base stem as prefix. The `extract()` id-remap post-pass that strips the absolute
path relativizes each file's ids by that file's **own** file-stem prefix — for
`Foo+Ext.h` that is `foo_ext` (`_file_node_id`). A base-stem-prefixed id
(`<abs>_foo_foo_baz`) does not start with `<abs>_foo_ext_`, so it is never rewritten
and the absolute prefix survives.

The class node escapes this in the same-directory case only because
`_merge_decl_def_classes` folds it onto `Foo.h`'s already-relativized node; a method
node has no such twin, and neither does the class node when there is no sibling
`Foo.h`.

This is distinct from #3407 (fixed by #1504/#1522), which made `_file_stem` preserve
every path segment and salted colliding symbol ids: that covers symbols built from
the *file* stem, but not the ObjC-category case where the id prefix is the *base*
stem.

## Fix

Register the base-stem prefix alongside the file-stem prefix for ObjC source files
(`.h`/`.m`/`.mm`) in the id-remap pass, so the relativization reaches category class
and method nodes. The pass is already `source_file`-gated, and the base stem only
matches ids actually built from it, so non-category and non-ObjC files are
untouched. PR to follow.

title: fix(extract): keep ObjC category node ids free of the absolute checkout path
body:
Fixes #4666.

An ObjC category/extension keys its class and method nodes off the base-class stem
(`Foo+Ext` → `Foo`, #1556), so those ids carry the base stem as prefix. The
`extract()` id-remap post-pass relativizes each file's ids by its **own** file-stem
prefix (`foo_ext` for `Foo+Ext.h`), which a base-stem-prefixed id
(`<abs>_foo_foo_baz`) never matched — so the absolute checkout path leaked into
category node ids and the same source produced a different `graph.json` per checkout
directory.

This registers the base-stem prefix alongside the file-stem prefix for ObjC source
files (`.h`/`.m`/`.mm`) so the relativization reaches category class and method
nodes. The pass stays `source_file`-gated to the file, and the base stem only
matches ids actually built from it, so non-category and non-ObjC files are
untouched.

Distinct from #3407 (fixed by #1504/#1522): that relativizes ids built from the
*file* stem; this covers the ObjC-category case where the prefix is the *base* stem.

## Tests

`tests/test_objc_category_id_reproducible.py`:
- id sets are identical across two checkout directories;
- the category method hangs on the base class with canonical id `foo_foo` / `foo_foo_baz`;
- a category with no sibling base header still gets a clean (non-absolute) class id.

Ran the ObjC + id-remap suites (`test_objc_*`, `test_node_id_canonical`,
`test_file_node_id_spec`, `test_id_normalization_contract`,
`test_semantic_id_remap_root`, `test_carried_hyperedge_remap`): all green. The 7
pre-existing failures in `test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py` (#4449) are present on clean
`v8` and unchanged by this PR.

title: cross_repo_calls: edge source_file is the caller node's file (the .h) while source_location is the call-site line (in the .m)
fix(cross-repo): point a cross-repo call edge at its call site, not the caller's header
body:
## Summary

Closes #4668.

A cross-repo `calls` edge pointed `source_file:source_location` into the wrong file. `source_file` came from the caller node (an ObjC method node lives at its `@interface` in the `.h`) while `source_location` is the call-site line (in the `.m`), so the pair landed past the end of a short header.

- `_park_unresolved_member_call` now records the call-site `file` next to `line`.
- The extract-time `source_file` relativization pass relativizes the parked `file` too, so it never leaks the absolute checkout path into `graph.json` (consistent with the parking payload carrying names only, #3150).
- `link_cross_repo_member_calls` prefers the parked `file`, falling back to the caller node's `source_file` for graphs built before the field existed.

## Testing

- New `tests/test_parked_call_site_file.py`: the parked `file` is the repo-relative call-site `.m`, never absolute.
- New cross-repo edge cases: the edge `source_file` is the call site, and a pre-#3152 entry without `file` falls back to the caller's file.
- Updated the Go/PHP/TS parked-payload assertions to tolerate the new additive `file` key (its exact value depends on a root those unit cases extract without).
- `pytest -k "objc or cross_repo or parked or receiver"` green apart from 7 failures in `test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py` that are pre-existing on `v8` (#4449), unrelated to this change. `ruff` clean.

Based on `v8`.

title: extract --no-cluster: imports that the clustered path resolves to a real file land on an external stub (finalize_raw_graph_endpoints lacks build_from_json's ghost/basename resolution)
body:
### What happens

The same corpus produces different import edges under `--no-cluster` than under the clustered (default) path, for a framework-style `#import <Module/Header.h>` that resolves to a real header in the tree:

- clustered: `#import <Kit/ToolEvent.h>` attaches to the real file node `kit_event_toolevent`;
- `--no-cluster`: the same edge lands on an external stub `toolevent`, and an extra `external: true` stub node appears.

Two write paths of one extractor disagree, and a downstream `build_from_json` on the raw graph cannot recover it: the stub is already declared, so endpoint resolution leaves the edge on it.

### Minimal reproduction

```bash
W=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$W/r/Kit/Event"
printf '#import <Foundation/Foundation.h>\n@interface ToolEvent : NSObject\n@end\n' > "$W/r/Kit/Event/ToolEvent.h"
printf '#import <Kit/ToolEvent.h>\n@interface Holder : NSObject\n@end\n' > "$W/r/Kit/Holder.h"
graphify extract "$W/r" --code-only --no-cluster --out "$W/raw" >/dev/null 2>&1
graphify extract "$W/r" --code-only --out "$W/clu" >/dev/null 2>&1
for d in raw clu; do python3 - "$W/$d/graphify-out/graph.json" "$d" <<'PY'
import json, sys
d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); L = d.get("links") or d.get("edges")
print(sys.argv[2], [(e["source"], e["target"]) for e in L if e["relation"] == "imports"],
      "| stubs:", [n["id"] for n in d["nodes"] if n.get("external")])
PY
done
```

Actual:

```
raw [('kit_event_toolevent', 'foundation'), ('kit_holder', 'toolevent')] | stubs: ['foundation', 'toolevent']
clu [('kit_event_toolevent', 'foundation'), ('kit_holder', 'kit_event_toolevent')] | stubs: ['foundation']
```

Expected: `raw` imports and stubs match `clu`.

### Root cause — and why the obvious reorder is not enough

`finalize_raw_graph_endpoints` (build.py ~266) calls `mint_external_stubs_in_data(data)` first, then re-points an endpoint that differs from a declared id only by `_normalize_id`.

Reordering those two alone does **not** fix it. The raw edge target is `toolevent`; the real node is `kit_event_toolevent`. They are **not** normalization-equivalent, so `norm_to_id` would never attach them even if minting ran afterward. `build_from_json` resolves `toolevent` -> `kit_event_toolevent` through its **ghost-node / basename alias** pass (the import target's label is the header basename `toolevent`, which matches the real file node's label), removing the ghost and registering `norm_to_id[ghost_id] = canonical_id`. `finalize_raw_graph_endpoints` has only the bare normalization map, not that alias resolution.

### Suggested fix

`finalize_raw_graph_endpoints` must mirror `build_from_json`'s endpoint resolution — the ghost/basename alias pass, not just `_normalize_id` — to re-point import targets onto the real file node they name, and only then mint stubs for whatever is still genuinely external (e.g. `foundation`). Factoring that resolution into a shared helper both paths call would keep them from drifting again. A stub carried over from an earlier graph that no edge references after re-pointing should still be dropped (as the function already does for orphans).

Regression to preserve: a truly external import (`<Foundation/Foundation.h>`) must still mint a stub (#2873).

(No PR yet — filing so the mechanism is recorded; the fix touches the shared build path and wants its own review.)

title: #2543 heal re-queues declined-by-design code files (data JSON) on every incremental
body:
## Summary

`extract`'s #2543 heal (`_zero_node_stamped_code_sources` in `graphify/cli.py`) re-queues any manifest-stamped code file that has a registered extractor but zero nodes in `graph.json`, on the assumption that such a row is a *poisoned* stamp (extraction failed, hashes stamped anyway). But a file the extractor **declines by design** — a data JSON like an `.xcassets/Contents.json` (#1224/#2879) — is also stamped with live hashes and also contributes zero nodes. The heal cannot tell the two apart, so it re-queues the declined file on **every** incremental run, forever.

## Reproduce

```
project/src/app.py
project/src/Assets.xcassets/Contents.json
project/src/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/Contents.json
```

```
graphify extract src --out out --no-cluster   # run 1: full scan
graphify extract src --out out --no-cluster   # run 2
graphify extract src --out out --no-cluster   # run 3
```

Runs 2 and 3 print:

```
[graphify extract] re-queuing 2 manifest-stamped code file(s) with no nodes in graph.json (prior failed extraction, #2543)
```

The two `Contents.json` files are re-queued every run even though nothing changed and their extraction is behaving exactly as intended.

## Root cause

`extract()` already separates these cases: a `skipped` result (`_res.get("skipped")`, the data-JSON decline from #2879) is deliberately kept *out* of `failed_sources`, so the file is stamped normally. A non-skipped zero-node file *is* added to `failed_sources` and gets `clear_ast`'d (unstamped). So after a clean run, the only stamped-with-live-hash / zero-node / has-extractor rows are the declined-by-design ones.

The heal gates solely on `_get_extractor(p) is not None` plus absence from the graph, which both of those classes satisfy — it has no signal for "declined by design", so it treats the legitimate empty as a poisoned stamp.

`#2879` fixed the same forever-requeue on the `failed_sources` path; the heal (added later) reintroduced it for the skipped class.

## Proposed fix

Give the manifest a persistent, positive marker for "declined by design": `extract()` surfaces the skipped files, `save_manifest` records `ast_empty: true` on their row (preserved across unchanged incrementals, dropped once the file starts producing nodes), and the heal skips rows carrying the marker. Genuinely poisoned rows (failed, wrongly stamped) never carry the marker, so #2543's recovery is unchanged; a pre-fix manifest simply re-queues the file once more, re-stamps the marker, and settles.

PR to follow (base `v8`).

title: fix(extract): stop re-queuing declined-by-design code files every incremental
body:
Fixes #4671.

## Problem

The #2543 heal (`_zero_node_stamped_code_sources`) re-queues any manifest-stamped code file with a registered extractor but zero nodes in `graph.json`, assuming a poisoned stamp. A file the extractor **declines by design** (data JSON such as `.xcassets/Contents.json`, #1224/#2879) is stamped yet legitimately empty — the same shape — so the heal re-queued it on every incremental run forever. #2879 fixed the identical forever-requeue on the `failed_sources` path; the heal, added later, reintroduced it for the skipped class.

## Fix

A persistent, positive manifest marker distinguishes "declined by design" from "poisoned stamp":

- `extract()` surfaces the declined files as `skipped_sources` (a run-only key, alongside `failed_sources`).
- `save_manifest` records `ast_empty: true` on those rows. The marker is set when the extractor declined the file this run, inherited across unchanged incrementals exactly like `ast_hash`, and dropped once a file starts producing nodes. A genuine AST failure (`clear_ast`) drops it.
- `_zero_node_stamped_code_sources` loads the manifest and skips rows carrying the marker.

Genuinely poisoned rows never carry the marker, so #2543's recovery is intact. A pre-fix manifest has no marker, so such a file is re-queued exactly once, re-stamped with the marker, and left alone thereafter — a one-cycle migration, consistent with the heal's existing no-wedge property.

## Test

`test_declined_by_design_file_is_not_requeued_every_run` (in `tests/test_extract_cli.py`): a declined-by-design file is stamped with `ast_empty: true` and not re-queued on runs 2/3; a pre-#2879 manifest (marker stripped) re-queues it once, then settles.

Verified: full `test_extract_cli.py` / `test_detect.py` / `test_zero_node_no_cache.py` / `test_incremental.py` suites green; ruff clean.

title: ObjC member calls drop when a class splits header/impl across directories
fix(extract): resolve ObjC member calls when a class splits across header/impl dirs
body:
Fixes #4673.

## Problem

`_merge_decl_def_classes` folds an ObjC `@interface`/`@implementation` pair into one node only when both live in the **same directory** (the id embeds the directory path, #1556). A class whose `.h` sits in `include/` and `.m` in `src/` therefore mints two same-labelled nodes that never merge, so the member-call resolver sees two type-def candidates, trips its single-definition god-node guard (`if len(type_defs) != 1: continue`), and emits **no** edge. Header/impl directory splits are a common layout, so this hit ordinary code.

## Fix

Replace the three per-arm god-node bails with a shared `_resolve_member_target` that:

- unions the candidates' members, and
- binds the selector to the **sole candidate that DEFINES it** — an `@implementation` in `.m`/`.mm`, or a merged node carrying `definition_file`. A header-only node is a bare declaration and does not count.

So a split decl/def pair resolves to its one real definition, while two *unrelated* same-named classes that each define the selector still yield two definitions and stay ambiguous — the guard holds for the case it was meant for.

## Tests

Added `test_objc_class_split_across_header_and_impl_dirs_resolves_members`: asserts two `Widget` nodes (unmerged across dirs), one `-render` definition in `.m`, and a single `-go -> -render` `calls` edge (INFERRED) pointing at the definition.

`test_objc_same_named_categories_in_different_directories_stay_distinct` (the genuinely-ambiguous case) stays green, along with the rest of the ObjC member-call suites. Pre-existing failures in the tree are environmental (missing optional `tree_sitter_sql`, wheel/skill packaging) and unrelated to this change.

title: fix(build): resolve a raw-graph import target through the same alias index the clustered path uses
body:
Closes #4670.

`--no-cluster` and the clustered path build the same graph two different ways, and one of the ways only knew half the endpoint rules. `finalize_raw_graph_endpoints` re-pointed an edge endpoint through `_normalize_id` alone; `build_from_json` also consults a pre-migration alias index derived from each node's old stem forms. `Kit/Event/ToolEvent.h` is therefore reachable as `toolevent` in the clustered graph but not in the raw one, so `#import <Kit/ToolEvent.h>` bound to the real file node in one path and to a freshly minted external stub in the other.

The index construction moves into `_endpoint_alias_index` and both callers use it, which is the part that keeps them from drifting apart again. In the raw path, stub minting now runs after endpoint resolution instead of before: a target that resolves through the alias layer is a declared node and must not be minted, while a target that still resolves to nothing on an import-family relation is genuinely external and still gets its stub (#2873). The orphan-stub sweep at the end is unchanged.

Verified with the issue's corpus:

```
raw [('kit_event_toolevent', 'foundation'), ('kit_holder', 'kit_event_toolevent')] | stubs: ['foundation']
clu [('kit_event_toolevent', 'foundation'), ('kit_holder', 'kit_event_toolevent')] | stubs: ['foundation']
```

The regression test asserts exactly that, plus that no endpoint stays undeclared in either output. It fails on the previous commit and passes here. `tests/test_no_cluster_undeclared_endpoints.py`, `tests/test_external_stub_endpoints.py` and `tests/test_merge_sweeps_reextract_orphans.py` are green (27 passed).

title: fix(build): resolve a raw graph's import endpoints through the alias index (#4670)
body:
## Summary

`graphify extract --no-cluster` and the clustered path disagreed on where a framework-style `#import <Kit/ToolEvent.h>` lands. The clustered path re-pointed the edge at the header's real file node (`kit_event_toolevent`); the raw path minted an external stub for the header's bare basename (`toolevent`) and left the edge on it.

Two write paths of one extractor produced different graphs for the same corpus, and a downstream `build_from_json` on the raw graph could not recover it: the stub was already declared, so endpoint resolution left the edge on it.

```
raw [('kit_event_toolevent', 'foundation'), ('kit_holder', 'toolevent')] | stubs: ['foundation', 'toolevent']
clu [('kit_event_toolevent', 'foundation'), ('kit_holder', 'kit_event_toolevent')] | stubs: ['foundation']
```

Fixes #4670.

## Root cause

`finalize_raw_graph_endpoints` (`graphify/build.py`) only had a `_normalize_id` map. Normalization cannot bridge `toolevent` and `kit_event_toolevent` — they are not the same string modulo case and punctuation — so re-pointing was impossible.

`build_from_json` resolves it through the pre-migration alias index, which maps a file's old-stem spellings onto its canonical id (#1504/#1509). That index was inlined in `build_from_json` and never shared.

Reordering the two steps alone does not fix it, as the issue notes: the raw edge target is `toolevent`, the real node is `kit_event_toolevent`, and they are not normalization-equivalent.

## The change

- Move the alias index into a shared `_alias_index` helper and call it from both `build_from_json` and `finalize_raw_graph_endpoints`, so the two paths resolve an endpoint the same way.
- `finalize_raw_graph_endpoints` now re-points endpoints **before** it mints stubs, so an import that names a real file is no longer frozen onto a stub minted for its unresolved spelling. Only a genuinely external import (`<Foundation/Foundation.h>`) still mints one (#2873 preserved).

An alias is committed only when exactly one node claims it, so two files sharing a bare stem stay ambiguous and the import keeps its stub rather than binding to whichever same-stem file was seen first.

## Tests

`tests/test_no_cluster_undeclared_endpoints.py`:

- `test_finalize_raw_graph_endpoints_resolves_an_old_stem_alias` — an import naming a real file by its bare basename lands on that file, and no stub is minted for it.
- `test_finalize_raw_graph_endpoints_keeps_an_ambiguous_alias_unresolved` — two files with the same bare stem leave the alias ambiguous, so it is not used.
- `test_extract_no_cluster_resolves_a_framework_import_like_the_clustered_path` — end-to-end: `extract --no-cluster` and the clustered path agree on the import target, the `toolevent` stub is gone, and `foundation` still gets its stub.

The two new behavioural tests fail without this change (verified by reverting `graphify/build.py`).

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_no_cluster_undeclared_endpoints.py tests/test_external_stub_endpoints.py` — 20 passed.
- Full suite: 8135 passed, 9 failed. The same 9 fail on a pristine `upstream/v8` checkout (shell/env issues in `test_code_only_update_all_hosts.py`, `test_hooks.py`, `test_install_references.py`, `test_resolve_memoization.py`, `test_source_key_memoization.py`, `test_unmapped_at_alias_resolution.py`) — no regressions from this change.
- `ruff check --config pyproject.toml graphify/ tests/` — clean.
- `python -m tools.skillgen --check` — 134 artifacts match.

title: fix(sql): recover CREATE TABLE statements dropped into ERROR nodes by unsupported column defaults
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4613: on MySQL/MariaDB schemas, any `CREATE TABLE` using `DEFAULT current_timestamp()` or `ON UPDATE current_timestamp()` (with parentheses) produced **no node at all**. tree-sitter-sql rejects the parentheses, the whole statement lands in an `ERROR` node, `walk()` never dispatches on it, and the pre-pass never registers the name — so the table vanished and other tables' `REFERENCES` to it resolved to a sourceless stub. On a real dump, every table from the first failing one onward was missing.

## Change (`graphify/extractors/sql.py`)

Tables get the same recovery treatment routines and triggers already have:

- New `_TABLE_RECOVERY_RX`, sibling to `_ROUTINE_RECOVERY_RX` / `_TRIGGER_RECOVERY_RX`, sharing the delimited-identifier atom (`_TRIGGER_IDENT`): matches `CREATE [OR REPLACE|OR ALTER] TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] <name>` including quoted and bracketed names. The label is the bare name (a table is not callable, so no `()` suffix).
- When the parse failed, recovered table names are pre-registered in `table_nids` from the comment-masked source (same `_scan_sql` + identifier-span guard as the existing recoveries), so forward/backward `REFERENCES` resolve to the real sourced id instead of a stub, and the global REFERENCES fallback can emit the recovered table's own FK edges.
- In the `has_error` fallback, the recovered tables' nodes are emitted via `_add_node` (which dedupes by id, so cleanly parsed tables keep their walk-emitted node untouched).

The scan only runs on files whose parse already failed, over the masked source — commented-out or single-quoted `CREATE TABLE` text cannot fabricate a node.

## Tests

Two regression tests in `tests/test_multilang.py`:

- `test_sql_mysql_current_timestamp_parens_table_is_recovered` — the issue's repro: `foo` is recovered as a sourced node next to `after_table`, and `after_table`'s FK resolves onto it.
- `test_sql_commented_out_create_table_is_not_recovered` — a commented-out `CREATE TABLE` in an error-bearing file mints no node.

## Verification

- Issue repro before the fix: `['after_table', 'repro.sql']`; after: `['after_table', 'foo', 'repro.sql']`.
- FK cases: a good table referencing the recovered table, and a recovered table's own `REFERENCES`, both emit edges to the real nodes.
- A 5-table MariaDB-style dump where every table uses `current_timestamp()` recovers all 5.
- Byte-identical extractor output (nodes + edges) before/after the patch on clean schemas (basic FK/view/index/ALTER, MySQL backtick + `IF NOT EXISTS`, Postgres function+trigger, T-SQL bracketed procedure, Firebird computed column) — the change only adds previously dropped tables.
- The new recovery test fails on the unpatched code and passes with the patch; neighboring trigger/procedure recovery tests pass unchanged.

title: feat(heal): add graph-guided test failure triage and healing engine
body:
# What does this PR do?

Introduces `graphify heal "<test-cmd>"`, a native test failure triage and autonomous healing engine that leverages Graphify's architectural knowledge graph to isolate failure blast radiuses and synthesize targeted code repairs.

### Problem
Raw test runner stack traces only reveal the symptom at the point of assertion, omitting structural context like upstream callers, downstream callees, and imported contracts. Developers and agents spend considerable manual effort mapping which connected components are affected across the codebase.

### Solution
`graphify heal` directly links test execution failures to the knowledge graph:
1. **Failure Interception:** Executes user test suites and parses failing test targets and assertion errors.
2. **Blast Radius Slicing:** Extracts a localized ego-subgraph around the failing module from `graph.json` using NetworkX shortest paths with path normalization.
3. **Contextual Patch Synthesis:** Dispatches the failure traceback, graph neighborhood, and target source code to Graphify's native `_call_llm` dispatcher.
4. **Iterative Verification:** Applies patches and re-runs the suite until passing or until `--max-iters` is reached.
5. **Non-Destructive Inspection:** Supports `--dry-run` and `--json` for read-only architectural triage without modifying code.

---

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

---

## Verification & Invariants

### Invariants Protected
* **Zero Disruption to Existing Pipeline:** The change is strictly additive. No existing extraction routines (`graphify extract`), clustering algorithms, or MCP server handlers were modified.
* **Zero Dependency Footprint:** Introduces no new dependencies. It exclusively uses Graphify's existing core `networkx>=3.4` and internal `graphify.llm` dispatchers.
* **Stream Hygiene:** Diagnostic logs route strictly to `stderr` when `--json` is specified, preventing JSON stdout stream corruption in automated pipelines.
* **Dry-Run Safety:** `--dry-run` guarantees zero write operations or file mutations on disk.

### Checklist
- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

### Limitations / Unsupported Cases
* Optimized for test runners following standard failure reporting conventions (e.g., `pytest`).
* Requires a pre-indexed `graph.json` to extract structural neighbors (exits gracefully with exit code 1 if missing).

---

## How was this tested?

### Unit & Integration Suite
* Subgraph blast radius extraction and 2-hop boundary traversal (`test_extract_blast_radius_subgraph`).
* Prompt assembly and context injection (`test_build_healing_prompt`).
* Markdown fence code stripping and file application (`test_extract_code_patch`, `test_apply_patch_to_file`).
* CLI arguments, `--dry-run`, passing test detection, missing graph errors, and missing LLM backend fallbacks (`test_heal_cli_*`).

### Live Synthetic E2E Verification
* Tested on an isolated temporary environment with a real broken module, failing test, and `graph.json`. Verified both human-readable blast radius reporting and machine-readable `--json` output.
* Validated clean syntax compilation across `graphify/cli.py`, `graphify/heal/`, and test modules using `python3 -m py_compile`.

```text
# 1. Bytecode compilation / syntax verification
python3 -m py_compile graphify/cli.py graphify/heal/*.py tests/test_heal_*.py

# 2. Complete heal unit & integration test suite (9/9 passed)
pytest tests/test_heal_engine.py tests/test_heal_cli.py -v

# 3. Live end-to-end dry-run and JSON stream verification (isolated tempdir)
python3 -c '
import subprocess, sys, tempfile, json, networkx as nx
from pathlib import Path

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    tmp = Path(tmpdir)
    src = tmp / "calculator.py"; src.write_text("def add(a, b):\n    return a - b\n")
    tst = tmp / "test_calculator.py"; tst.write_text("from calculator import add\ndef test_add():\n    assert add(2, 3) == 5\n")
    G = nx.DiGraph()
    G.add_node(str(tst), source_file=str(tst), label="test_add", node_type="function")
    G.add_node(str(src), source_file=str(src), label="add", node_type="function")
    G.add_edge(str(tst), str(src), relation="CALLS")
    (tmp / "graph.json").write_text(json.dumps(nx.node_link_data(G)))

    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "graphify", "heal", f"{sys.executable} -m pytest {tst}", "--graph", str(tmp / "graph.json"), "--dry-run", "--json"]
    res = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=tmpdir)
    assert res.returncode == 0
    data = json.loads(res.stdout)
    assert data[0]["blast_radius_nodes"] == 2
'

title: `graphify extract` aborts with `ValueError: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component` when pnpm-workspace.yaml has an inline comment after a glob (Python 3.12)
body:
### Summary

The JS/TS import resolver reads `pnpm-workspace.yaml` with a hand-written line parser
(`graphify/extractors/resolution.py`, `_pnpm_workspace_globs`). It strips the quotes around a
package glob but **keeps an inline YAML comment**, so

```yaml
packages:
  - "apps/*"
  - "services/runner/stg/**" # staging runner infrastructure
```

yields the glob `services/runner/stg/**" # staging runner infrastructure`. `_load_workspace_packages`
then calls `root.glob(pattern)` on it without guarding, and on **Python 3.12** `pathlib` raises

```
ValueError: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component
```

because the last component is `**" # staging …`, not a bare `**`. The resolver runs for every
JS/TS file, so every file is reported as `warning: skipped <file> (ValueError: Invalid pattern: …)`
and the run ends with `[graphify extract] AST extraction failed: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be
an entire path component` (exit 1) — the whole repository produces no graph.

On Python 3.13+ `glob.translate` accepts the broken glob silently (it just matches nothing), so
the bug only shows on 3.12 and older.

### Version

- `graphifyy` 0.9.93 (`graphify --version` → `graphify 0.9.93`); the same parser and unguarded
  `root.glob(pattern)` are on `v8` at `v0.9.94` / `v1.0.0` (`graphify/extractors/resolution.py`,
  `_pnpm_workspace_globs` and `_load_workspace_packages`, line ~468).
- Python 3.12.15 (`python:3.12-slim-bookworm`), Debian 12, x86_64. Not reproducible on 3.14.

### Minimal reproducer

```bash
mkdir -p repro/services/runner/stg && cd repro
cat > pnpm-workspace.yaml <<'EOF'
packages:
  - "apps/*"
  - "services/runner/stg/**" # staging runner infrastructure
EOF
echo '{"name":"root","private":true}' > package.json
echo 'export const a = 1;' > services/runner/stg/main.ts
python3.12 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install "graphifyy==0.9.93"
.venv/bin/graphify extract . --code-only
```

Output (3.12.15):

```
[graphify extract] AST extraction on 1 code files...
  warning: skipped /…/repro/services/runner/stg/main.ts (ValueError: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component)
[graphify extract] AST extraction failed: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component
```

The parser alone:

```python
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from graphify.extractors.resolution import _workspace_globs
>>> _workspace_globs(Path("."))
['apps/*', 'services/runner/stg/**" # staging runner infrastructure']
>>> list(Path(".").glob(_workspace_globs(Path("."))[-1]))
ValueError: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component
```

Removing the trailing `# staging runner infrastructure` from the YAML makes the extraction
succeed, which pins the cause to the comment handling rather than to `**` itself (a bare
`stg/**` works).

### Traceback (production run, `graphify extract . --code-only`, 598 code files)

```
  warning: skipped /work/services/vault/main.ts (ValueError: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component)
  warning: skipped /work/services/vault/setup.js (ValueError: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component)
  … (107 files)
  AST extraction: 598/598 uncached files (100%) [8 workers]
[graphify extract] AST extraction failed: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component
```

### Expected

Workspace globs parsed as pnpm parses them (inline comments are valid YAML), and a glob the
resolver cannot use should be skipped with a warning — one bad workspace entry should never
abort the extraction of the whole repository.

### Suggested fix

1. In `_pnpm_workspace_globs`, strip an inline comment before stripping quotes (or parse the
   file with the YAML loader already used elsewhere): a `#` preceded by whitespace outside the
   quotes ends the value.
2. Guard `root.glob(pattern)` in `_load_workspace_packages` with `except (ValueError,
   NotImplementedError)` (pathlib also raises `NotImplementedError("Non-relative patterns are
   unsupported")` for an absolute glob) and log the offending pattern once instead of failing
   every file — `package.json` `"workspaces"` globs go through the same call and a `tools/**-cli`
   style entry fails identically.

Happy to send a PR for either part.

title: detect: a linked git worktree that sits next to its main checkout is indexed as a second copy when the scan root is not a git repo (follow-up to #1810)
body:
### What happened?

When the scan root is a plain workspace folder (not itself a git repo) that holds a repo *and* a
linked worktree of that same repo as siblings, `detect()` indexes both checkouts. Every file
appears twice and the graph roughly doubles.

#1810 fixed the nested case by reading `.git/info/exclude`, and #947 / #1023 skip worktrees by
folder name (`.worktrees/`, `<dot-dir>/worktrees/`). Neither covers this layout:

- the workspace root has no `.git`, so there is no `info/exclude` to read (`_find_vcs_root` returns
  `None`);
- `git worktree add ../<any-name>` places the worktree next to the repo under an arbitrary name,
  so the name-based rules don't match.

Yet the worktree is unambiguous on disk: its `.git` is a file containing
`gitdir: <main>/.git/worktrees/<name>`, and that gitdir's `commondir` points back to `<main>/.git`,
whose working tree is already inside the scan root.

Real-world impact: a multi-repo workspace (`Toolbooks-back/`, `Toolbooks-front/`, `docs/`) where an
agent session created `Toolbooks-back-lote-e/` with `git worktree add`. The next
`graphify update .` added ~13,800 nodes of duplicate backend code (18% of the resulting ~78k-node
graph), and `GRAPH_REPORT.md`'s community hubs started listing files from the copy, e.g.
`Toolbooks-back-lote-e/database-repo/src/modules/exports.ts`.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
mkdir -p ws/app/src && cd ws/app
git init -q
printf 'export function hello() { return 1 }\n' > src/a.ts
git add . && git -c user.email=x@x -c user.name=x commit -qm init
git worktree add -q ../app-feature
cd ..                      # ws/ is NOT a git repo
python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.detect import detect
r = detect(Path('.'))
print(sorted(f for v in r['files'].values() for f in v))
"
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
['.../ws/app-feature/src/a.ts', '.../ws/app/src/a.ts']
```

Expected: only `ws/app/src/a.ts`, with `ws/app-feature/` listed in `pruned_noise_dirs` (it is a
second checkout of a repo that is already in the scan).

Not expected to change:
- scanning the worktree itself (`detect(Path('ws/app-feature'))`) still indexes it;
- a worktree whose main checkout is *outside* the scan root is still indexed (it's the only copy);
- submodules (`.git` file pointing to `<super>/.git/modules/<name>`, no `commondir`) are untouched.

I have a PR ready that prunes such a directory during the walk (and in the `_ignored` predicate
used for incremental/watch updates), records it in `pruned_noise_dirs`, and adds regression tests
with real `git worktree add` checkouts.

### Graphify version

0.9.94 (also checked against `v8` at the time of filing: same behaviour, no sibling-worktree check
in `detect.py`)

### Operating System

Linux (WSL2, Ubuntu 22.04); same layout seen on Windows 11.

title: query: "get" survives stopwording and exact-matches framework hubs like a NestJS `Get` decorator, hijacking BFS seeds (follow-up to #1602)
body:
### What happened?

"get" is one of the most common verbs in natural-language questions ("how does X get
authorized", "where do we get the totals"), but it is not in `_QUERY_STOPWORDS`. In codebases
whose framework exports a symbol named `Get` (NestJS `@Get()`, many HTTP routers), that symbol is
a node imported by nearly every controller. The query term `get` exact-matches its label and
receives `_EXACT_MATCH_BONUS`, so the decorator becomes a BFS seed for any question that contains
"get", and the traversal spends its budget in the controller layer.

#1602 guarded against a generic term exact-matching a *short, low-degree leaf*. Here the matched
node is the opposite, a high-degree hub, so that guard doesn't apply. The `work`/`works`/`working`
entries already handle the same pattern for "how does X work".

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
python -c "from graphify.serve import _query_terms; print(_query_terms('how does payroll.approve get authorized'))"
# ['payroll', 'approve', 'get', 'authorized']

graphify query "how does payroll.approve get authorized" --budget 400
```

### Error output or graph output

On a ~36k-node NestJS + Next.js graph:

```text
Graph: graphify-out/graph.json (35775 nodes) | Traversal: BFS depth=2 | Start: ['AUTHORIZED', 'Payroll', 'Get', 'approve-bill-dialog.tsx'] | 168 nodes found
NODE Get [src= loc= community=QueryLogsDto]
```

`Get` (the NestJS decorator import) is one of four seeds. Expected: no seed chosen for "get".

### Proposed fix

Add `get`, `gets`, `got`, `getting` to the English part of `_QUERY_STOPWORDS`, with a comment like
the `work` one. The all-stopwords fallback in `_query_terms` keeps a bare `graphify query "get"`
working, and `explain "Get"` / `find_node` are unaffected because node text is never filtered.
Trade-off: a question about the HTTP verb ("GET /invoices") loses the term "get", but keeps its
content terms ("invoices").

I have a PR ready with the stopword change and regression tests (term filtering, the all-stopword
fallback, and a seed-selection test with a high-degree `Get` hub).

### Graphify version

0.9.94 (also checked against `v8` at the time of filing: "get" not in `_QUERY_STOPWORDS`)

### Operating System

Linux (WSL2, Ubuntu 22.04)

title: fix(detect): skip a linked worktree whose main checkout is in the same scan
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4683. Extends #1810 / #947.

When the scan root is a plain workspace folder (not itself a git repo) holding a repo `repo/` and a
linked worktree of it with an arbitrary name, `repo-feature/` (what `git worktree add ../repo-feature`
produces), `detect()` indexes both checkouts. There is no `.git/info/exclude` above the root to read
(#1810's fix) and the name-based rules (`.worktrees/`, `<dot-dir>/worktrees/`) don't match.

This PR reads the candidate's `.git` file (`gitdir: …`) and that gitdir's `commondir`, and prunes the
directory when the common directory exists, is named `.git`, and its main working tree is inside the
scan root and is not the directory itself. The pruned directory is recorded in `pruned_noise_dirs`
like other noise dirs. `ignored_predicate` (used by `watch.py`) applies the same rule, so an
incremental update does not re-add what a full scan pruned; it caches the per-directory result for
the lifetime of each predicate instance (watch creates a fresh predicate per rebuild). Windows
extended-length prefixes (`\\?\C:\…`, `\\?\UNC\…`) are normalized before the containment checks.

Unchanged: a worktree scanned as the root, a worktree whose main checkout is outside the scan root,
submodules (no `commondir`), independent nested repos (`.git` directory), and any unreadable or
malformed metadata (fails open: indexed).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: for canonical input paths, the full scan and the incremental/watch predicate agree on
which linked checkouts are redundant, and only readable metadata pointing at an existing `.git`
directory of a distinct main tree inside the scan root can prune anything.

Regression tests (`tests/test_detect.py`, real `git worktree add` fixture with ambient `GIT_*`
settings cleared and global/system config isolated): sibling layout pruned and listed in
`pruned_noise_dirs`; worktree as root indexed; main outside root indexed; fake submodule indexed;
predicate/full-scan agreement; relative metadata with a symlinked root; malformed and unreadable
metadata; `commondir` pointing at a missing directory or a regular file (both entry points);
extended drive/UNC prefixes on either side (`PureWindowsPath`, runs on Linux, no `os.name` mocking);
per-directory caching and refresh with a fresh predicate. The sibling regression fails without the
fix; each fix-round regression was confirmed failing before its change.

Cost: on a 10,000-path / six-shared-ancestor workload the predicate makes 6 classification calls
(first pass) and 0 (warm), and its time matches the predicate with the new check disabled
(~0.56 s vs ~0.60 s, local WSL, predicate-only timing). The walk classifies each directory once.

**Limitations**
- The main working tree is identified by a common directory named `.git`; bare or custom common
  directories keep their worktrees indexed.
- The rule does not check that the main checkout actually contributes files: if `.graphifyignore`
  excludes the main tree, the sibling worktree is still pruned. Scan the worktree itself to index it.
- As before this change, `ignored_predicate` expects canonical paths; a path spelled through a
  symlinked scan root can be treated as outside the root.
- A predicate's classifications are a snapshot; a fresh predicate observes metadata changes.
- Native Windows filesystems were not exercised; Windows prefix handling is covered with pure-path tests.

title: fix(query): drop "get" filler verbs from query terms
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4684.

Questions such as "how does payroll.approve get authorized" keep the term `get`. In codebases whose
framework exports a symbol named `Get` (a NestJS `@Get()` decorator import, HTTP routers), that
symbol is a high-degree hub: the term exact-matches its label, gets `_EXACT_MATCH_BONUS`, and
becomes a BFS seed, so the traversal starts in the controller layer instead of at the content
words. #1602's guard covers short, low-degree leaves, not hubs.

This adds `get`, `gets`, `got`, `getting` to the English part of `_QUERY_STOPWORDS`, next to
`work`/`works`/`working`, which exist for the same reason, and extends the comment above the set.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Only query *terms* change. Node text, `_find_node`/`explain`/`path`/`get_node` resolution,
`affected` seed resolution, scoring constants and the all-stopwords fallback are unchanged. The
CLI, the MCP `query_graph` tool and the benchmark's real-graph mode all go through `_query_terms`
and inherit the change. No persisted graph, cache or generated artifact is affected.

Regression tests (`tests/test_serve.py`):
- `test_query_terms_drops_get_question_filler`: `['payroll', 'approve', 'get', 'authorized']` → `['payroll', 'approve', 'authorized']`.
- `test_query_terms_drops_get_variants`: `gets` / `got` / `getting`.
- `test_query_terms_get_only_falls_back_to_unfiltered`: `"get"` → `['get']`, `"how do I get it"` → `['how', 'get']`.
- `test_pick_seeds_get_question_ignores_framework_hub`: 20 controllers importing a `Get` hub; seeds were `['get', 'approve']` before the fix, `get` is absent after it, and `_find_node(G, "Get")` still resolves the hub.

With the stopword line removed, the new term and seed tests fail (seeds `['get', 'approve']`); with it, they pass.

**Limitations.** The filter applies to every question, not only bare HTTP-verb queries: in a mixed
question the word is dropped and the remaining terms drive seeding, e.g. `GET endpoint` →
`['endpoint']`, `get user` → `['user']`, `got request` → `['request']`. That loses the GET-vs-POST
distinction and a literal function or package named `get`/`got` in mixed questions. The
all-stopwords fallback only restores the term when nothing else is left. Identifiers that merely
contain the word (`getter`, `getValue`, `get_user`) are single tokens and unaffected, and
`explain "Get"` still finds the symbol.

title: fix: drop inline comments from pnpm workspace globs and skip globs pathlib rejects (#4681)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4681. An inline YAML comment after a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` glob stayed in the glob, so the workspace package was never found and imports of it stayed unresolved. On Python 3.12 a `**` glob with a comment also made `Path.glob` raise, and the error escaped `extract()`, so the whole run failed with no graph.

```yaml
packages:
  - "services/runner/stg/**" # staging runner infrastructure
```

`_pnpm_workspace_globs` read that line as `services/runner/stg/**" # staging runner infrastructure`.

- **3.12:** `ValueError: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component`. Exit 1, and the Python files in the run are lost too.
- **3.13:** no crash, but the glob matches nothing. A plain `pk/*` with a comment fails the same way on every version.
- **Absolute globs:** `Path.glob` raises `NotImplementedError` on every version, from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or from `package.json` `"workspaces"`.

This PR fixes both parts in `resolution.py`:

```diff
 _pnpm_workspace_globs
   for each "- value" line under packages:
-    strip quotes from both ends
+    if quoted: take the text up to the closing quote (skip the item if there is none)
+    else: cut at the first `#` that follows whitespace
     skip empty and `!` values

 _load_workspace_packages
   for each glob
-    root.glob(pattern)
+    try root.glob(pattern)
+    except ValueError, NotImplementedError: warn and skip this glob
```

`"a#b/*"` and unquoted `a#b/*` stay as written, because YAML only starts a comment at a `#` after whitespace.

**Before** (v8, the issue's repro plus a package `@x/svc` under `services/runner/stg/`):

```text
3.12: warning: skipped .../libs/consumer.ts (ValueError: Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component)
      [graphify extract] AST extraction failed: ...   exit 1, no graph.json
3.13: exit 0, 19 nodes, 14 edges, consumer.ts imports_from ref_x_svc (unresolved)
```

**After:**

```text
3.12: exit 0, 18 nodes, 16 edges, consumer.ts imports_from svc/index.ts
3.13: exit 0, 18 nodes, 16 edges, consumer.ts imports_from svc/index.ts
```

These are the same counts v8 gives for the repro with the comment removed.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A workspace glob means what pnpm reads from the YAML, and one glob that `Path.glob` can't use never stops the extraction of the rest of the repository.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. No ids or cache formats change. JS/TS files skip the AST cache (`_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`), so no schema bump is needed.

**Blast Radius:** JS/TS workspace import resolution. Only lines under `packages:` that hold a comment, or a quote left open, read differently. A glob that used to crash the run is now skipped.

**Limitations**
