title: JS/TS: after #4634, `class A extends X` with `const X = require('./m')` gets no `inherits` edge at all
body:
## Summary

#4621 was closed as fixed in 0.9.94 (#4634), which stops creating a module-scope node for `const X = require(...)`. `new X()` now resolves to the required class. But the other shape in #4621, `class A extends X`, went from "edge on the binding node in the importing file" to "no edge", so the expected result of #4621 (the edge ends on the class in the required file) is still not met for `extends`. The same change also removes the `calls` edge for `new Plugin()` when the specifier is an external package (`require('some-package')`), where there is no file to resolve to.

Checked on clean checkouts of `v0.9.93` and `v0.9.94`.

## Reproduction

Script (writes the files itself, run from the checkout):

```python
import pathlib, tempfile
from graphify.extract import extract

GEN = "class Generator { run() {} }\nmodule.exports = Generator;\n"
USE = "const Generator = require('./gen');\nclass A extends Generator { go() {} }\n"
EXT = "const Plugin = require('some-plugin');\nfunction cfg() { return new Plugin(); }\n"

d = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
(d / "gen.js").write_text(GEN, encoding="utf-8")
(d / "use.js").write_text(USE, encoding="utf-8")
(d / "ext.js").write_text(EXT, encoding="utf-8")
r = extract([d / "gen.js", d / "use.js", d / "ext.js"], cache_root=d / "_cache", root=d, parallel=False)
n = {x["id"]: x for x in r["nodes"]}
where = lambda x: pathlib.Path(n[x]["source_file"]).name
print("A inherits:", sorted((n[e["target"]]["label"], where(e["target"])) for e in r["edges"]
                            if e["relation"] == "inherits" and n[e["source"]]["label"] == "A"))
print("cfg() calls:", sorted((n[e["target"]]["label"], where(e["target"])) for e in r["edges"]
                             if e["relation"] == "calls" and n[e["source"]]["label"] == "cfg()"))
```

Output on `v0.9.93`:

```
A inherits: [('Generator', 'use.js')]
cfg() calls: [('Plugin', 'ext.js')]
```

Output on `v0.9.94`:

```
A inherits: []
cfg() calls: []
```

On `v0.9.93` the `inherits` edge ends on the binding in `use.js` (wrong target, the bug in #4621). On `v0.9.94` there is no edge. Expected: `('Generator', 'gen.js')`.

## A real repository

`webpack/webpack` at `c28d144bc4be7993307718fd74c7f62f9d097bad`, the same two files as in #4621: `lib/asset/AssetGenerator.js` has `const Generator = require("../module/Generator"); ... class AssetGenerator extends Generator`, and `lib/module/Generator.js` defines `class Generator`. Extracting just these two files (`python script.py <path to the webpack checkout>`):

```python
import pathlib, sys, tempfile
from graphify.extract import extract

root = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()  # a webpack checkout at the commit above
r = extract([root / "lib/module/Generator.js", root / "lib/asset/AssetGenerator.js"],
            cache_root=pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()), root=root, parallel=False)
n = {x["id"]: x for x in r["nodes"]}
for e in r["edges"]:
    if e["relation"] == "inherits":
        t = n[e["target"]]
        sf = pathlib.Path(t["source_file"])
        print(n[e["source"]]["label"], "inherits", t["label"], "in", (sf.resolve().relative_to(root) if sf.is_absolute() else sf).as_posix())
```

`v0.9.93`:

```
ByTypeGenerator inherits Generator in lib/module/Generator.js
AssetGenerator inherits Generator in lib/asset/AssetGenerator.js
```

`v0.9.94`:

```
ByTypeGenerator inherits Generator in lib/module/Generator.js
```

`AssetGenerator` has no `inherits` edge on `v0.9.94`. It should end in `lib/module/Generator.js`.

Over every `.js` file under `lib/` of the same checkout (one `extract` call), the number of `inherits` edges is 336 on `v0.9.93` (all 336 end in the subclass's own file, on the binding) and 8 on `v0.9.94` (all 8 in the subclass's own file, i.e. class declarations in the same file).

<details>
<summary>count script</summary>

```python
import pathlib, sys, tempfile
from graphify.extract import extract

root = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
files = [p for p in (root / "lib").rglob("*.js") if "node_modules" not in p.parts and ".git" not in p.parts]
r = extract(files, cache_root=pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()), root=root, parallel=False)
n = {x["id"]: x for x in r["nodes"]}
inh = [e for e in r["edges"] if e["relation"] == "inherits"]
same = sum(1 for e in inh if n.get(e["target"], {}).get("source_file") == n[e["source"]]["source_file"])
print("inherits total:", len(inh), "| ending in the same file as the subclass:", same)
```

</details>

## Expected

- When the specifier resolves to a file in the corpus, `extends X` (and `new X()`) ends on the class that file exports, as for an ESM default import.
- When it does not resolve (external package), the use stays visible: an edge to the binding, or to an external-package node, instead of no edge.

## Related

#4621 (closed), #4634.

title: fix(hooks): run the rebuild from the checkout's top level (#3258)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the remaining part of #3258: the git hooks now run the rebuild from the checkout's top level instead of from whatever cwd git started them in.

The rebuild body reads `graphify-out/` and its `.graphify_root` relative to the cwd. Git doesn't always start hooks at the top level. With `GIT_DIR` exported and no `GIT_WORK_TREE` (a nested git call from another hook or tool), git takes the caller's cwd as the work tree, and even `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` echoes that subdirectory. A stray `graphify-out/` left there by an earlier run then roots the rebuild at that subdirectory. #3265 already rejects a `..` marker, but the fallback `Path('.')` is the same subdirectory. For `.claude/worktrees/` that means every linked worktree: in the incident in #3258 that was ~130k files, 16 GB RAM and a frozen machine on 0.8.39. A minimal repro still triggers on 0.9.94; it's in [this comment](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/issues/3258#issuecomment-6354183857).

The change adds one shared shell snippet, `_TOPLEVEL_ANCHOR`, placed right after `_WORKTREE_GUARD` in all four hooks. It reuses the guard's absolute `_GFY_GITDIR` / `_GFY_COMMONDIR`:

- In the standard layout (common dir named `.git`, no `GIT_WORK_TREE`), the top level is the parent of the common `.git` dir. This is right even when git itself was told cwd is the work tree.
- Otherwise (`GIT_WORK_TREE`, `--separate-git-dir`), it keeps git's own `--show-toplevel` answer.
- It `cd`s there, or exits the graphify block if nothing resolves.
- It rewrites `GIT_DIR` to its absolute form (it doesn't newly export it), so a relative inherited `GIT_DIR` keeps working for the git calls after the `cd`.

Everything runs inside the existing `( ... )` subshell, so the `cd` doesn't leak into hooks chained after graphify's block. A linked worktree still exits at the guard, before the anchor.

Correction to my comment on #3258: I first suggested `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"`. That isn't enough in exactly this case, because `--show-toplevel` returns the cwd when `GIT_DIR` is exported without `GIT_WORK_TREE`. Hence the common-dir-based anchor.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a hook-triggered rebuild only ever reads `graphify-out/` (and the saved root) of the repository's own top level, never of the directory git happened to start the hook in.

- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Tests added in `tests/test_hooks.py`:

- `test_hooks_anchor_to_the_top_level_after_the_worktree_guard` (all four hooks): the anchor is present exactly once, after `_WORKTREE_GUARD`, and before the interpreter is chosen and the rebuild is launched.
- `test_toplevel_anchor_runs_from_the_top_when_git_starts_the_hook_in_a_subdir`: end to end against a real repo with a linked worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`. The guard + anchor snippet must run at the top for cwd = top, cwd = subdir, and cwd = subdir with `GIT_DIR=../../.git`. A `git rev-parse HEAD` after the `cd` must still work. The linked worktree must still be skipped.
- I confirmed the end-to-end test fails without the fix (with the anchor replaced by a no-op `:`): `AssertionError: subdir: did not run at the top`.

Limitations / unchanged behaviour:

- The cheap "is there a graph here?" early exits in post-checkout, post-merge and post-rewrite (`[ ! -d "graphify-out" ]`) still run before the anchor, so they test the start cwd. That direction is safe, because at worst a rebuild is skipped. I left them in place to keep the diff narrow and to avoid extra git execs on repos without a graph.
- `detect` still doesn't prune `worktrees/` when the scan root itself is `<dot-dir>/worktrees` (see the table in the #3258 comment). That is a separate concern and isn't touched here.
- Existing installs pick this up on the next `graphify hook install`.

## How was this tested?

All 33 full-suite failures also fail on unmodified `v8` (c588b72) on this Windows machine:
- the 11 `tests/test_hooks.py` bash-harness tests above;
- 22 in `test_skillgen.py`, `test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py`, `test_code_only_update_all_hosts.py`, `test_source_key_memoization.py` and `test_resolve_memoization.py`, which were checked by re-running those files on unmodified `v8`.

None of the failing tests exercise the hook scripts.

- Before: the rebuild indexed only `wt1/`, `wt2/` and `wt3/`, and rewrote the stray marker to `.`.
- After: both rebuilds ran at the top level ("No code-graph topology changes detected"), the top graph kept only `src/`, and the stray directory was left untouched.

title: Cross-repo ObjC call drops when @interface/@implementation are split across repositories
body:
## Summary

A cross-repo member call to an Objective-C class whose `@interface` (`.h`) and `@implementation` (`.m`) live in **different repositories** is silently dropped, even though exactly one of the merged type nodes DEFINES the selector.

This is the cross-repo analog of #4673 (same-repo, fixed in 0.9.94). That fix handled the split surfacing **within one build**; this one handles the same class split **across a repo boundary**, which `link_cross_repo_member_calls` resolves separately.

## Root cause

`_merge_decl_def_classes` folds an `@interface`/`@implementation` pair into one class node only when they share a directory — the node id embeds the directory path (#1556). When the `.h` lives in repo A and the `.m` in repo B, the two never fold, so the merged graph carries **two same-named `Greeter` type nodes**.

A parked member call (`[g greet]` with receiver typed `Greeter`) then reaches `link_cross_repo_member_calls` and hits:

```python
if len(candidates) != 1:
    # two repos declaring the same name is an ambiguity, not a hit.
    continue
```

Two candidates → the guard trips → the `calls` edge is dropped, even though only **one** of them (the `.m`) defines `-greet`; the other is a bare header declaration.

## Impact

- ObjC is the affected language: the `.h`/`.m` split is idiomatic, and splitting a library's public header from its implementation across repositories (SDK header package + impl package, vendored headers, etc.) is common.
- The edge exists when the same code sits in one repo but vanishes once the header and impl are merged from two repos — exactly the kind of edge a merged call graph is supposed to recover.
- No wrong edges today; the symptom is a missing edge (false negative), not a fabricated one.

## Suggested fix

Scope a branch to `lang == "objc"` in `link_cross_repo_member_calls`: when more than one same-named candidate survives, union their members and bind the selector to the **sole candidate that DEFINES it** (a method node with `definition_file` set, or a `.m`/`.mm` source). If two candidates both define it, they are two unrelated classes and stay ambiguous — the single-definition guard still catches the collision it was meant to.

Other languages, the C# visibility-resolver path, and the single-candidate path are unchanged. Mirrors the same-repo resolution in #4673.

PR to follow.

title: fix(cross-repo): bind ObjC split decl/impl across repos to its definition
body:
Fixes #4690.

## Problem

A cross-repo member call to an ObjC class whose `@interface` (`.h`) and `@implementation` (`.m`) live in different repositories is dropped, even though exactly one merged type node DEFINES the selector. Cross-repo analog of #4673 (same-repo, 0.9.94).

`_merge_decl_def_classes` folds a decl/impl pair only within a directory (the id embeds the directory, #1556), so a `.h` in repo A and a `.m` in repo B surface as two same-named `Greeter` nodes. `link_cross_repo_member_calls` then trips its `len(candidates) != 1` single-definition guard and drops the `calls` edge — even though only the `.m` defines `-greet`.

## Fix

Scoped to `lang == "objc"`: when more than one same-named candidate survives, union their members and bind the selector to the sole candidate that DEFINES it (a method node with `definition_file` set, or a `.m`/`.mm` source). Two candidates that both define it stay ambiguous — the guard still catches the collision it was meant to. Other languages, the C# resolver path, and the single-candidate path are unchanged.

## Tests

- `test_an_objc_class_split_decl_impl_across_repos_binds_to_the_definition` — split across repos now emits one edge to the `.m` definition.
- `test_two_objc_definitions_of_the_same_class_still_bind_nothing` — two full definitions stay ambiguous (guard holds).

Full suite green aside from pre-existing environmental failures unrelated to this change (`tree_sitter_sql not installed`, wheel-packaging, skill backtick). `ruff` clean.

title: fix(no-cluster): resolve basename import targets to the real file node
body:
Fixes #4670.

## Problem

Under `extract --no-cluster` (and the incremental raw write path), a framework-style `#import <Kit/ToolEvent.h>` that resolves to a real header in the tree lands on an external stub `toolevent` instead of the real file node `kit_event_toolevent`, and an extra `external: true` stub node appears. The clustered (default) path attaches the same edge to the real node. A downstream `build_from_json` on the raw graph cannot recover it — the stub is already declared, so endpoint resolution leaves the edge on it.

```
raw [('kit_event_toolevent', 'foundation'), ('kit_holder', 'toolevent')]          | stubs: ['foundation', 'toolevent']
clu [('kit_event_toolevent', 'foundation'), ('kit_holder', 'kit_event_toolevent')] | stubs: ['foundation']
```

## Root cause

`finalize_raw_graph_endpoints` minted stubs first, then re-pointed endpoints only by `_normalize_id`. The raw target `toolevent` and the real id `kit_event_toolevent` are **not** normalization-equivalent. The clustered path bridges them through `build_from_json`'s **basename/old-stem alias pass** (the import target's label is the header basename `toolevent`, matching the real file node's label) — resolution that `finalize_raw_graph_endpoints` did not have.

## Fix

Factor that alias pass into a shared `_register_file_stem_aliases` that both `build_from_json` and `finalize_raw_graph_endpoints` call, and re-point endpoints through it **before** minting, so only a genuinely external import (`<Foundation/Foundation.h>`, #2873) still mints a stub. One implementation keeps the two write paths from drifting again. Orphan stubs carried over from an earlier graph are still dropped.

## Tests

- `test_finalize_raw_graph_endpoints_binds_a_basename_import_to_the_real_header` — unit-level: bare-basename import re-points to the file node, external import still stubs.
- `test_extract_no_cluster_objc_framework_import_matches_clustered` — end-to-end: raw imports and stubs now equal the clustered path.

`build_from_json`'s existing alias behavior is unchanged (the shared helper is the same logic it ran inline). Full suite green aside from pre-existing environmental failures unrelated to this change (`tree_sitter_sql not installed`, wheel-packaging, skill backtick). `ruff` clean.

title: pillow 12.x has no patched release for Python 3.10, so the svg, all and leiden extras stay vulnerable there
body:
The `svg` and `all` extras pin `pillow>=12.3.0; python_version < '3.11'`, and `matplotlib` (pulled in by `svg`, `graspologic` and `seaborn`) brings pillow in transitively. On Python 3.10, pip and uv resolve pillow 12.3.0, which has no patched release: the first fixed version of every open pillow advisory below is 13.0.0, and pillow 13 requires Python 3.11 or newer.

Open advisories against pillow 12.3.0 (GitHub advisory database, as of 2026-10-23): 4 Critical (GHSA-332p-7hrc-92wf, GHSA-8g5g-8vmr-9782, GHSA-v9pv-5gc8-w2m6, GHSA-w889-685w-c8fh) and 23 High, all with first fixed version 13.0.0. A dependency scan of `uv.lock` therefore reports them on the Python 3.10 branch, and a Python 3.10 user of the `svg`, `all` or `leiden` extras cannot get a patched pillow.

Options: drop Python 3.10 from the lock and the `pillow` pin (`[tool.uv] environments = ["python_full_version >= '3.11'"]`), raise `requires-python` to `>=3.11`, or document that these extras on Python 3.10 carry unpatched pillow advisories. A downstream fork took the first option for the lock only, so a plain `pip install` on 3.10 is unchanged.

title: fix: make the ambient scan root thread-isolated via ContextVar
body:
Fixes #4602. diagnosis by @Deepjyoti-Sarmah, who pinned the mechanism precisely.

## Root cause

`_ACTIVE_SCAN_ROOT` was a module global. Extraction runs concurrently -
`test_the_pool_hands_its_workers_the_overrides` forces the pool onto
threads, and production uses process pools. so overlapping
save/restore pairs in `_safe_extract_with_xaml_root` interleaved:

```
thread A: previous = None, set root
thread B: previous = root, set root
thread A: restore None
thread B: restore root      <- still set after extract() returns
```

Any test running after the leak in a different order failed; a plain
serial run passed, which is why it looked order-dependent rather than
concurrent.

## Fix

Replace the module global with a `contextvars.ContextVar` (stdlib,
Python ≥ 3.10 per pyproject). Each thread. and each async task. gets
its own value, so save/restore pairs nest correctly by construction and
the `set_active_scan_root` / `active_scan_root` API is unchanged. No
lock, no new dependency.

## Regression proof (per CONTRIBUTING #7)

New `tests/test_scan_root_contextvar.py`:

- `test_concurrent_save_restore_pairs_do_not_leak`. two threads with
  overlapping barriers; asserts each thread sees **its own** root at
  the peak and the outer `None` after restore. **Fails on the module
  global, passes with this fix.**
- `test_concurrent_workers_see_their_own_root`. per-thread isolation
  under a real thread pool.

The issue's repro command now passes 3/3 (verified over five repeats):
`51 passed` where it previously failed `9, 2 of 3 runs`.

## Verification

- The repro from #4602: `51 passed` × 5 repeats
- Full relevant suite: `107 passed, 2 skipped` (overrides, scan-root
  context, dotnet, contextvar, language overrides)
- Broader extractor smoke: no regressions

title: fix(markdown): recognise backslash namespaces and Type::member code-span mentions (#4610)
body:
Fixes #4610

## What

`_code_span_mention` accepted only the dotted and path-qualified forms, so the separators other languages' docs write were dropped before the resolver saw them — `App\\Services\\Mailer` (PHP namespaces) and `Mailer::send()` (PHP, Rust, C++ type-qualified members). Both are now qualifier separators the way `.` already is:

- `App\\Services\\Mailer` → `["App", "Services", "Mailer"]`, `Mailer::send()` → `["Mailer", "send"]` (a trailing `()` is dropped from the last name, like the dotted form),
- `Foo::CONST` and `Foo::class` are left out — neither has a node to land on,
- a span that is only a namespace root (`App\\`) is dropped as the non-mention it is.

On the resolution side, a PSR-4 namespace root maps to the scan directory and has no path segment, so when no candidate accounts for the whole chain the resolver drops the leading qualifiers a candidate cannot account for and falls back to the unique bare-name match. The fallback fires only when strict matching found nothing, so a qualifier that *does* match keeps discriminating: `Mailer::send()` still picks the right `send` over a same-named method on another class. Dotted mentions are untouched — they keep the strict evidence check (`time.sleep`, `pyproject.toml` still resolve to nothing).

## Verification

The issue's exact repro (PHP corpus) now prints the expected:

```text
[('Mail', 'Mailer'), ('Mail', '.send()')]     # was [] before
```

`tests/test_markdown_code_spans.py` extended with classification cases (`App\\Services\\Mailer`, `Mailer::send()`, `Foo::CONST`, `Foo::class`, `App\\`, `C:\\Users\\me`) and an end-to-end case mirroring the repro (namespace-root drop + `Mailer::send()` disambiguation against a second `send`). Full file: 16 passed; with `tests/test_symbol_resolution.py`: 58 passed.

> The issue offered to open a PR with a regression test — happy to hand this over or adjust the shape if you'd rather drive it from your 12-README corpus numbers.

title: fix(report): keep community hub wikilinks matching their exported filename
body:
GRAPH_REPORT.md's "Community Hubs" section, when generated with `--obsidian`, emits an Obsidian wikilink `[[_COMMUNITY_<name>|<label>]]` meant to point at the real `_COMMUNITY_<name>.md` note that `export.to_obsidian` writes for the same community. Both sides sanitize the raw community label into a filesystem-safe stem, but `report.py` kept its own, separate, partial copy of that logic (`_safe_community_name`) instead of calling the export's own `_obsidian_safe_stem`, and the two had drifted apart.

Found this by auditing the core report/export machinery directly (not from a filed issue) and noticing the docstring's own claim — "mirrors export.safe_name so community hub filenames and report wikilinks always agree" — wasn't actually true anymore. Confirmed by calling both functions side by side on a handful of inputs:

- `report.qmd` -> export strips the `.qmd` suffix to `report`; the report kept the full `report.qmd`, so the link named a file that was never written.
- `@@@` (no word characters) -> export falls back to `unnamed`; the report kept the literal punctuation.
- A label starting with `.` -> export prefixes `dot-` (Obsidian hides dot-files); the report didn't.
- A label over 200 UTF-8 bytes -> export truncates and appends a hash suffix; the report didn't cap at all.
- A label containing a control character other than `\r`/`\n` -> export folds every C0 control character to a space; the report only handled `\r`/`\n`.

A community's label isn't always a short, clean phrase — the deterministic naming fallback uses a community's highest-degree member, which can be a plain source file, so a label that looks exactly like `report.qmd` is a realistic, not contrived, case.

Fix: `_safe_community_name` now delegates straight to `export._obsidian_safe_stem`, so the two can never drift apart again. The one thing this still can't match exactly is the MAX_PATH-aware length budget the export computes from the real output directory at export time (`stem_filename_budget`), since `generate()` has no output path to recover that from — that's a pre-existing, separately tracked limitation (see #3351), not something this PR changes or worsens.

Added two regression tests in `tests/test_report.py` covering the `.qmd`-suffixed label and the punctuation-only label, both confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the fix. Ran the full suite and `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`; both clean.

title: fix(robot): give each duplicate test case name its own node
body:
No existing issue — found while auditing the Robot Framework extractor directly, since it carries no open PRs and was worth a closer look.

`graphify/extractors/robot.py` keys a test case node id as `_make_id(stem, node.name)` — qualified by file, not by anything that distinguishes two test cases *in the same file*. Robot Framework allows two test cases in one suite to share a name: it only warns ("Multiple test cases with name 'X' executed in suite 'Y'"), it does not reject the file the way it rejects a duplicate keyword definition. Given:

```
*** Test Cases ***
Login Test
    Click Button

Login Test
    Open Browser
```

the extractor mints exactly one `Login Test` node at line 2, and both `Click Button` and `Open Browser` end up as its outgoing `calls` edges — the second test's own call gets attributed to the first test's node and location, and the graph has no way to show two tests with that name even exist. This is the same collision-by-collapsed-id shape that #4575 and #4574 fixed for Swift earlier this week, just for a different extractor.

The fix adds a quick pre-scan counting test case names within the file before the main visitor runs. A name used once keeps the exact id it always had. A name used two or more times salts every one of its own ids by its own line number, so each occurrence gets its own node, its own location, and keeps only the calls its own body actually makes — and the outcome does not depend on which occurrence is visited first.

User keyword nodes are untouched: the extractor already, deliberately, merges same-named keywords across the whole corpus into one node, and that is correct — Robot itself rejects a duplicate keyword definition as a real conflict, unlike a repeated test case name, which it tolerates.

Reproduced the collapse against the exact snippet above on a clean v8 checkout before touching anything, confirmed via a safe `git show`+file swap that the regression test fails on the pre-fix extractor, then restored it byte for byte. Added two tests: the duplicate case gets separate nodes/locations/calls, and a control confirming a file with no duplicate name keeps its exact previous id.

Ran the full suite plus `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`; both clean.

title: affected <path> returns 'No unique node match' for a file with a shared basename and a module docstring
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.94 (also 0.9.47). **OS:** Windows 11, Python 3.12.

## What happens

`graphify affected <path>` answers `No unique node match for <path>` for a file whose basename is shared with another file **and** which has a second node on `L1` (for example, a module docstring, which becomes a `rationale` node). Asking by the file node's id works, so the graph is fine; only the path lookup misses.

In our real repository, this affects 404 of 4,771 files (about 1 in 12). Every per-agent `callbacks/before_tool.py`-style file with a docstring falls into it. Callers that script `affected <path>` get an error that reads like "this file is not in the graph".

## Minimal repro

```
app/__init__.py
app/main.py          from app.alpha.hooks import check
                     def handle(request): return check(request)
app/alpha/__init__.py
app/alpha/hooks.py   """Checks a request before it runs."""
                     (two blank lines)
                     def check(request): return bool(request)
app/beta/__init__.py
app/beta/hooks.py    same as app/alpha/hooks.py
```

```
graphify update . --force
graphify affected app/alpha/hooks.py   # -> No unique node match for app/alpha/hooks.py
graphify affected app_alpha_hooks      # -> lists main.py and handle(), as expected
```

Controls (same layout, each one changed):

| Case | `affected app/alpha/hooks.py` |
|---|---|
| shared basename + docstring | **No unique node match** |
| shared basename, `# comment` instead of a docstring | works |
| unique basename (no `app/beta`) + docstring | works |

## Why

`resolve_seed` matches the path against `source_file`, which correctly finds every node of `app/alpha/hooks.py`, then calls `_prefer_file_node` to pick the file node. All three of its passes miss:

1. **The label equals the basename and is on L1.** Label disambiguation has renamed the file node's label to `alpha/hooks.py`, so it no longer equals `hooks.py`.
2. **The only node on L1.** The file node and the docstring's `rationale` node (`app_alpha_hooks_rationale_1`) are both on `L1`.
3. **The label equals the basename.** This misses for the same reason as the first pass.

Nodes for the file:

```
app_alpha_hooks              | alpha/hooks.py                    | L1 | code
app_alpha_hooks_rationale_1  | Checks a request before it runs.  | L1 | rationale
app_alpha_hooks_check        | check()                           | L4 | code
```

## Suggested fix

In `_prefer_file_node`, also accept a label that is a path suffix of the query, so a disambiguated label still counts as the file's own name:

```python
query_norm = _normalize_label(query)

def _is_file_label(label: str) -> bool:
    label = _normalize_label(label)
    return label == query_basename or query_norm == label or query_norm.endswith("/" + label)

exact_file_nodes = [
    node_id for node_id in node_ids
    if str(graph.nodes[node_id].get("source_location", "")) == "L1"
    and _is_file_label(str(graph.nodes[node_id].get("label", "")))
]
```

A smaller alternative is to leave `rationale` nodes out of the `l1_nodes` fallback. The suffix match seems more robust, though, because any other L1 node (a decorator, a one-line import-time call) would cause the same tie.

The same `_prefer_file_node` logic is on `main` today.

title: Rust: `use` of an external crate item resolves to an unrelated same-named local symbol (false `imports_from` edges, phantom import cycles)
body:
## Summary

In Rust code, when a file imports a symbol from an external crate (e.g. `use serde_json::Value;`), the AST extractor links the import to any local symbol that happens to have the same name, including an enum *variant* in an unrelated crate. The edge is marked `EXTRACTED`, so it looks certain. Downstream this produces phantom import cycles, inflated god nodes and wrong cross-community bridges.

## Minimal reproduction

```
a/src/lib.rs
    pub enum Field {
        Value(String),
    }

b/src/lib.rs
    use serde_json::Value;

    pub fn get(v: &Value) -> Option<&Value> {
        v.get("x")
    }
```

```python
from graphify.extract import extract
from pathlib import Path
r = extract([Path("a/src/lib.rs"), Path("b/src/lib.rs")], cache_root=Path("."))
```

Output (relevant edges):

```
imports_from b_src_lib     -> a_src_lib_field_value  | a/src/lib.rs L2 | EXTRACTED
references   b_src_lib_get -> a_src_lib_field_value  | a/src/lib.rs L2 | EXTRACTED   (x2)
```

**Expected:** `serde_json::Value` is not defined in the corpus, so no edge to `Field::Value`. At most, an external/unresolved reference node, or an edge marked `AMBIGUOUS`.

**Actual:** `b` "imports" the variant `Field::Value` from `a`, with confidence `EXTRACTED`.

## Impact on a real workspace

On a ~30-crate Cargo workspace (graph has 2376 nodes), the import cycle report listed 6 cycles. Checking each edge against the source showed that 5 of the 6 cycles do not exist:

| Reported edge | Actual source line |
|---|---|
| `types/src/lib.rs` → `plugin/src/http.rs::Value` | `use serde_json::{Map, Value};` |
| `plugin/src/proxy.rs` → `plugin/src/http.rs::Value` | `use serde_json::Value;` |
| `server/src/api/mod.rs` → `plugin/src/http.rs::Response` | `use axum::response::{IntoResponse, Response};` |
| `plugin/src/lib.rs` → `server/src/api/mod.rs::Config` | `use osiris_types::{CollectionResult, Config, Manifest};` |

Several of these cycles are impossible: Cargo rejects cyclic crate dependencies, and e.g. the `types` crate does not depend on `plugin` at all. The `Value(String)` variant became the #2 god node (89 edges) and a top "cross-community bridge" in the suggested questions, almost entirely from `serde_json::Value` imports.

The last case is slightly different. `osiris_types::Config` is a crate-qualified path to a crate in the same workspace, yet it resolves to a different crate's `Config` struct. So the crate path segment seems to be ignored even when it names a local crate.

## Suggested fix

- Use the path prefix of a `use` item when resolving it. A path rooted at an external crate (`serde_json::`, `axum::`, `std::`) should not resolve to a corpus symbol, and a path rooted at a workspace crate should resolve only within that crate's files.
- Never resolve an imported *type* to an enum variant.
- If resolution falls back to a name-only match, mark the edge `INFERRED` or `AMBIGUOUS`, not `EXTRACTED`.
- Optionally, use `Cargo.toml` dependencies as a sanity check: drop any cross-crate edge whose target crate is not a dependency of the source crate.

## Related

- #2774: same bare-name collision family, but for call/function nodes rather than `use` imports.
- #4285: covers lossy `use`-list parsing (dropped items), not resolution of the imported path to a wrong local symbol.

## Environment

- graphify 0.9.86 (installed via the `graphify` CLI)
- Python 3.10.21
- Linux (CachyOS)

title: fix(js): resolve class extends through CJS require bindings
body:
Fixes #4688.

### What was wrong

#4634 stopped creating a module-scope node for `const X = require('./m')` so `new X()` could reach the required class. That fixed the shadowing half of #4621, but `class A extends X` went through the same missing binding and ended up with **no** `inherits` edge at all (webpack `AssetGenerator extends Generator` is the real-world case).

### What changed

In the JS/TS symbol-resolution facts pass:

- Treat whole-module `const`/`let`/`var X = require('./m')` (and TS `import X = require('./m')`) as a default import alias, same shape as ESM `import X from './m'`.
- Record `module.exports = Name` / `exports.X = …` as export facts so that alias can resolve to the class in the required file.
- Do **not** recreate the old local binding node.

Follow-up after review: only `module.exports = …` mints a default export (bare `exports = X` is ignored), and chained assignments walk to the final RHS so `module.exports = exports = Foo` exports `Foo`.

Destructured / `require('./m').y` forms are left alone — they already have structural `imports` edges, and minting symbol-import facts for them regresses the EXTRACTED call path.

### External `require('pkg')`

Checked against ESM: `import X from 'some-plugin'` also has no `calls`/`inherits` edge today, only `imports_from` to a `ref_…` id. Restoring a local stub would undo #4634. So unresolved package requires stay without a use edge, matching ESM / #4634.

### Tests

- New regressions in `tests/test_js_extends_require_4688.py` (10 cases: local require extends, let/var/ts, ESM control, `import = require`, renamed require, `new` no-regression, external CJS vs ESM, bare `exports =` ignored, chained `module.exports = exports = Foo`).
- Full suite on 3.10 / 3.12 / 3.13 / 3.14 vs unmodified `v8`: same pre-existing failures on both trees, no new ones.
- Live CLI e2e on the issue repro + webpack `Generator.js` / `AssetGenerator.js` under `/workspace/e2e-4688` — before: no `A inherits`, no `AssetGenerator inherits`; after: both land on `Generator` in the required file.

### Limitations

- Destructured `const { X } = require('./m')` / `require('./m').X` extends is not covered here (structural imports already exist; whole-module was the #4688 gap).
- Unresolved external packages still get no `calls`/`inherits` edge (same as ESM after #4634).

Written with help from Grok Bot; I reviewed and tested it.
created by error - sorry

title: fix(js): keep a require of an external package visible on its binding node
body:
Fixes the remaining gap in #4688 that PR #4700 leaves open.

#4700 fixes `class A extends X` through a resolvable `const X = require('./m')` binding. This PR covers the other shape from the same issue: a `require` of an **external** package (`require('some-plugin')`), where #4634's node suppression left the use with no edge at all, a real regression from 0.9.93 (which pointed at the binding node, wrong but present) to 0.9.94 (nothing). The issue's own "Expected" section asks for this case specifically: "an edge to the binding, or to an external-package node, instead of no edge."

Scoped to `graphify/extractors/engine.py` only, independent of #4700's `resolution.py` changes (verified no file overlap, no conflict).

What changed: the require-binding node is now suppressed only when the specifier actually resolves to a file in the corpus. An external package's specifier doesn't, so it keeps its binding node exactly as it did before #4621/#4634, and a call through it (`new Plugin()`) stays visible instead of vanishing.

Verified against the issue's own repro and reproduced pre-fix via `git show`+file-swap (no stash) that the new test fails on `HEAD` and passes after the fix, with byte-identical restoration confirmed afterward. Full suite: same pre-existing failures as a clean `v8` checkout, no new ones. `tools.skillgen --check` clean (no skill-generation changes in this PR).

title: feat(skill): report code that reimplements a hub instead of calling it
body:
Fixes #4426.

A bridge/god-node question's neighbour listing only shows code that already has an edge to the hub, so a module that reimplements the hub's own job instead of calling it never shows up there even though it depends on the exact same behavior. The issue's own real case: two server modules hard-coded a shared date utility's UTC offset instead of calling the helper - the most useful finding, invisible to the traversal output because neither module has an edge to the hub.

The query flow (`references/query/default.md`, which regenerates into every split platform's `references/query.md`) now adds a check scoped to hub/bridge questions: after the normal answer, grep the corpus for one or two literal, distinctive things the hub does (a hard-coded constant, a specific string, the exact computation in its body) in files with no edge to the hub in the traversed subgraph, and report hits separately as "Bypasses". It also asks the answer to flag when a shared utility's own community label actually names its heaviest consumer instead - the issue's second observation, a labelling quirk that otherwise reads as if the consumer were the bridge.

The `aider`/`devin` monolith skills carry their own copy of this query section (no sidecar `references/` to point at), so the same paragraph was added there too, right after their own answer step and before `save-result` - verified via `--monolith-roundtrip` with a new sanctioned-diff predicate.

Two commits: the fragment/generator source change, and the regenerated skill artifacts (`python -m tools.skillgen` + `--bless`).

Ran the full suite and every `tools.skillgen` check (`--check`, `--audit-coverage`, `--schema-singleton`, `--monolith-roundtrip`, `--always-on-roundtrip`); all clean, only pre-existing unrelated flakes (confirmed identical on a clean `v8` checkout) remain.

title: feat(objc): extract NS_CLOSED_ENUM declarations as enums
body:
## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #4401, from [this suggestion](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/pull/4401#issuecomment-6143846714).

**Problem:** Graphify skips Objective-C enums declared with `NS_CLOSED_ENUM`. Their type and members never reach the graph. `NS_CLOSED_ENUM` is a Foundation macro that declares an enum, like `NS_ENUM`.

**Change:** `NS_CLOSED_ENUM` is added to the macro-name check in `extract_objc` (`graphify/extractors/objc.py`). These enums now get the same type node, member nodes, `case_of` edges and source locations as `NS_ENUM` and `NS_OPTIONS`. The comment that lists the handled macros is updated too.

Only enum-declaring macros pass the name check. The shape checks after it are the same for every accepted name, so a malformed `NS_CLOSED_ENUM` declaration is still rejected.

In `tests/test_objc_enum_declarations.py`:
- `NS_CLOSED_ENUM` is added to the cache test (`.h`, `.m`, `.mm`) and the member-attributes test.
- `typedef NS_CLOSED_ENUM(NSInteger, Broken) { Bad };` is removed from the reject list. It is a valid declaration that the old check rejected only by name.

Limitations and unsupported cases:
- Other enum macros, such as `CF_ENUM`, are still rejected.
- I did not bump `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` in `graphify/cache.py`. Files cached before this change keep their old result until the schema is bumped.
- CHANGELOG, version and `uv.lock` are left to the maintainer.
- These are parser tests. No Objective-C compiler or SDK was used.

title: fix(detect/extract): structurally extract .yaml/.yml config files (#2214)
body:
Fixes #2214.

## Problem

`.yaml` / `.yml` were classified as **documents**, so any AST-only / code-only run (`graphify update`, `--code-only`) produced **zero nodes** from them. Helm charts, Kubernetes manifests, and CI pipelines therefore contributed nothing to the graph, even though `.json` has had a deterministic structural extractor (`extract_json`) for the same reason.

## Fix

Treat YAML like JSON:

- Add `graphify/extractors/yaml_config.py`, a PyYAML-based `extract_yaml()` that emits a file node plus `contains` edges to top-level and nested keys.
- Register `.yaml` / `.yml` in `_DISPATCH`.
- Add both suffixes to `CODE_EXTENSIONS`; remove from `DOC_EXTENSIONS` and `_SPLITTABLE_TEXT_SUFFIXES` (they no longer reach the semantic pass).
- Update `tests/test_manifest_ingest.py` classification assertion.

### Safety limits

- 1 MiB max file size.
- 500 pairs / depth 6 cap, mirroring `extract_json`, so data-heavy YAML cannot explode into orphan nodes.
- Scalar documents return `skipped` rather than minting noise.
- IDs are derived deterministically from the file path; repeated runs produce identical node IDs.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_yaml_extraction.py`: classification, top-level/nested keys, `contains` edges, stable IDs, scalar/empty documents.
- Updated oversized-document slicing test: `.yaml`/`.yml` are code now, not semantic documents.
- Updated language-override lifecycle test to use the `markdown` alias for its document-override case.
- Verified locally: code-only build on a YAML-only corpus now yields nodes (previously an empty graph). 919 relevant tests pass.

## Verification

- `python -m graphify . --code-only` on `deployment.yaml` + `values.yaml` produces 7 nodes / 5 edges (was: empty graph).
- Deterministic: two `extract_yaml` runs produce identical IDs.

title: fix(extract): don't promote module-imported same-named calls to EXTRACTED (#2945)
body:
Fixes #2945.

## Problem

When an ambiguous bare call resolved to a candidate **solely because the caller imported the candidate's source module** (`from b import other`), the resolver promoted the resulting `calls` edge to `EXTRACTED`. That falsely certifies a same-named symbol that was never imported. Example: `_make_id` defined in both `a.py` and `b.py`, with the caller importing only `other` from `b`.

This is the module-level half of #2945. The symbol-level half (a direct `from a import _make_id`) already resolves correctly on `v8` because a symbol-level `imports` edge lands in `symbol_matches` first.

## Fix

In the ambiguous-name branch of the shared cross-file pass, the `module_matches` path now sets `has_import_evidence = False`. The edge is still emitted (for graph connectivity) but stays `INFERRED`. Symbol-level imports (`from X import Y`) still promote to `EXTRACTED`.

## Tests

- New regression test in `tests/test_extract.py`: `test_module_import_does_not_promote_unimported_same_named_call`.
  - Fails on the pre-fix tree (edge is `EXTRACTED`).
  - Passes with the fix (edge is `INFERRED`).
- `tests/test_extract.py` + `tests/test_symbol_resolution.py`: 386 passed.

## Verification

- Module-only import repro: `c_caller -> b_make_id` is now `INFERRED`.
- Symbol-import repro (`from a import _make_id`): `c_caller -> a_make_id` remains `EXTRACTED`.

title: fix: block multicast and unspecified IPs in _ip_is_blocked
body:
`_ip_is_blocked` in security.py checks private, reserved, loopback, link-local and the CGN range, but not multicast or unspecified. `validate_url` accepts `http://224.0.0.1/` and `http://[ff02::1]/` today. Small gap in the blocklist, cheap to close.

Fix: add `ip.is_multicast` and `ip.is_unspecified` to the check.

Verified locally: `_ip_is_blocked` now returns True for 224.0.0.1, 239.1.1.1, ff02::1 and 0.0.0.0, and still returns False for public addresses like 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1.

title: fix: sanitize obsidian frontmatter tag values
body:
In `to_obsidian`, the frontmatter comment says all scalars pass through `_yaml_str`, and source_file, type, community and location do. The tags list does not. `file_type` and the dominant confidence are interpolated raw into `  - graphify/{value}` lines, so a value with a newline lands at column 0 in the frontmatter as a new YAML key. The standard pipeline folds file_type and confidence to enums before export, so this needs a hand-built graph or a future writer that skips the fold, but the exporter should not rely on that.

Fix: build both tag values through `_obsidian_tag`, the same sanitizer the community tag already uses.

Verified locally: a graph with file_type set to `document` plus a newline plus `injected_key: pwned` now produces one indented tag line; the injected key never appears at column 0 in the frontmatter.

title: fix: use full YAML scalar escaping for shortcut frontmatter
body:
`_safe_yaml_str` in google_workspace.py is a short copy of the F-009 YAML escaper. It handles backslash, quote, LF and CR, but not tab, NUL and other C0 controls, and not the Unicode line breaks U+2028, U+2029 and U+0085. The full `_yaml_str` in ingest.py and export.py exists because of exactly those characters: a shortcut url or file id containing one breaks out of the quoted scalar in the converted sidecar's frontmatter and injects sibling keys when the file is later parsed without PyYAML (which is not a declared dependency).

Fix: give `_safe_yaml_str` the same escaping as `_yaml_str`, plus U+0085.

Verified locally: a url containing U+2028, a tab and U+0085 now comes out with the `\L`, `\t` and `\x85` escapes and no raw separator characters.

title: TS: parenthesized decorator `@(fn().method())` with a line break before `.method` is flagged a syntax error, dropping later symbols
body:
## Summary

A parenthesized decorator `@( ... )` whose expression is a **call expression followed by a line break before `.member`** is rejected by the TypeScript AST extractor. The file is reported as having a syntax error and every symbol after the decorator is dropped from the graph.

`tsc` accepts the same file without a single diagnostic.

This formatting is what Prettier produces for chained decorator factories, so it is common in decorator-heavy codebases (NestJS, TypeORM, and in my case [`@sqb/connect`](https://github.com/panates/sqb)).

## Minimal reproduction

`x.ts` — 7 lines, clean under `tsc --noEmit`:

```ts
declare function Link(): any;

export class C {
  @(Link()
    .toMany())
  a: unknown;
}
```

```
$ graphify update .
  warning: 1 file(s) had syntax errors and may be partially extracted: x.ts (first error at line 4, 1 symbol(s) extracted)
```

Only `C` is extracted; the property `a` is lost.

## What exactly triggers it

I bisected the construct. The line break before `.` only matters when the receiver is a **call expression**:

| # | Decorator | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `@(Link().toMany())` — one line | ✅ clean |
| 2 | `@(Link\n    .toMany())` — line break, **identifier** receiver | ✅ clean |
| 3 | `@(\n  Link().toMany()\n)` — line break after `@(`, expression on one line | ✅ clean |
| 4 | `@(Link()\n    .toMany())` — line break, **call** receiver | ❌ **syntax error** |
| 5 | `@(Link({ a: 1 })\n    .toMany(() => X, {})\n    .toOne(() => Y, {}))` | ❌ **syntax error** |
| 6 | `const v = Link()\n  .toMany();` — same chain, plain statement | ✅ clean |

Rows 2 and 3 show parenthesized decorators are supported in general, and row 6 shows multi-line call chains are fine outside decorator position — so this is specific to a call-expression receiver continuing onto the next line *inside* a decorator.

Line breaks inside the **argument list** are fine; it is only the break before the `.`:

```ts
// clean
@(Link({ exclusive: true }).toMany(
  async () => (await import('./country.entity.js')).Country,
  { sourceKey: 'code' },
))
```

## Secondary issue: the reported line number points at the wrong decorator

In my real file ([`continent.entity.ts`](https://github.com/panates/sqb/blob/dev/packages/connect/test/_support/continent.entity.ts), 43 lines, 3 decorated properties) the warning says:

```
warning: 1 file(s) had syntax errors and may be partially extracted:
  packages/connect/test/_support/continent.entity.ts (first error at line 14, 4 symbol(s) extracted)
```

Line 14 is a decorator of the **row-1/argument-list shape above, which parses fine in isolation**. The actual culprit is the chained decorator at lines 33–41. Deleting lines 33–42 makes the file extract cleanly (9 nodes, no warning); deleting the line-14 decorator instead does not help.

So the "first error at line N" position is taken from a tree-sitter ERROR node that starts well before the construct that actually fails, which sent me to the wrong place for a while. Reporting the position of the failing node — or the whole ERROR range — would make these warnings much more actionable.

## Environment

- graphifyy **0.9.94** (also reproduces on 0.9.53)
- tree-sitter-typescript **0.23.2** — which is the latest release on PyPI, so there is no newer grammar to bump to; the parse failure likely needs either an upstream grammar fix or a workaround in the extractor
- tree-sitter 0.25.2, Python 3.14.5
- macOS 26.7.1 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64, installed via `uv tool install graphifyy`

## Impact

Low severity, but silent: the warning says "may be partially extracted" and the run otherwise succeeds, so the missing symbols and relations are easy to miss. In my case the `@Link` relations of one entity are simply absent from the graph, which is exactly the kind of edge the graph is for.

Possibly related: #3597 (`export type *` partial extraction, also tree-sitter-typescript predating current TS syntax).

title: fix(rust): scope a `use` to the crate it names (#4699)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4699. A Rust `use` could bind to a same-named definition in another crate. On `tokio-rs/axum` @ `86aa615`, `examples/customize-extractor-error/src/custom_extractor.rs` says `use serde_json::Value`, and both its import and a `Value` reference bound to a variant in `axum-core/src/response/into_response_parts.rs`. The graph showed a cross-crate dependency the source never had.

Three causes, all in the Rust extractor and the corpus rewire:

1. `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` bound a sourceless stub to the only node with that label anywhere in the corpus. The crate the `use` names was not part of the decision.
2. The extractor recorded the imported name (`_rust_use_name`) only for paths rooted in this crate, so an external `use` carried no scope.
3. A scoped binding and a label-only guess both reported `EXTRACTED`.

```diff
 extractors/rust.py
   use binding
+    record the first path segment on the stub (`_rust_use_roots`)
+    record a bare `pub use` as a re-export (`_rust_pub_use`)

 extract.py
-  _rewire_unique_stub_nodes(nodes, edges)
+  _rewire_unique_stub_nodes(nodes, edges, root)
+    resolve each .rs file's crate from the nearest Cargo.toml
     bind a stub to a unique same-label definition
+    consider only candidates in a crate the `use` names
+    follow `pub use` re-exports across crates
+    leave the stub unbound when the named crate is outside the scan
+    mark a rewire with no resolving `use` as INFERRED

 cargo_introspect.py
+  package_name(manifest)   # reuses the module's TOML loader
```

**Before** (v8, the reported file):

```text
imports_from  custom_extractor.rs  ->  Value @ axum-core/.../into_response_parts.rs
references    handler()            ->  Value @ axum-core/.../into_response_parts.rs
```

**After:**

```text
imports_from  custom_extractor.rs  ->  Value  (a local sourceless stub)
references    handler()            ->  Value  (a local sourceless stub)
```

The re-export handling keeps edges the scoping would otherwise drop. `axum-extra/src/extract/cached.rs` (`use axum::extract::FromRequestParts`) and `axum/src/extract/connect_info.rs` (`use super::{.., FromRequestParts}`) still reach `axum-core/src/extract/mod.rs`, and a `use axum_core::..` edge stays `EXTRACTED`.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A Rust name binds only inside a crate its `use` names. A crate outside the scan binds to nothing. A cross-crate re-export counts as the named crate. A binding made by label alone is `INFERRED`.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. The per-file AST payload gained two markers, so the cache schema moves from 22 to 24 and cached `.rs` extractions re-run on the next build. A revert brings back the label-only binding on the next build. No migration, no config change.

**Blast Radius:** Rust cross-file resolution.

On `tokio-rs/axum` @ `86aa615` (302 `.rs` files):

| | v8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| nodes | 4036 | 4141 |
| edges | 10326 | 10326 |
| cross-crate `imports_from` | 125 | 163 |
| cross-crate `references` | 122 | 168 |
| bug-signature edges (target label is an external `use` of the source file) | 22 | 13 |
| confidence | 10195 EXTRACTED / 131 INFERRED | 9828 EXTRACTED / 498 INFERRED |
| import cycles | 20 | 20 |
| time (median of 3) | 2.05 s | 1.97 s |

The node count rises because a scoped stub that binds to nothing stays as a sourceless node instead of being dropped. Cross-crate edges rise because a name with several same-named definitions can now resolve to the one in the crate it names instead of staying ambiguous. Bug-signature edges drop from 22 to 13. The 20 cycles do not change; the reported `Value` edge was not part of one.

- **Other languages:** scoping only applies when `origin_file` ends in `.rs`, so no other extractor changes. The full-suite failure set is identical to v8.
- **Saved graphs:** the cache bump forces a re-extraction, so an existing `graph.json` keeps its old Rust edges until the next build. A rebuild produces the scoped result.
- **Determinism:** crate resolution reads only paths and `Cargo.toml` files, with no environment or ordering input.

**Limitations**

- **No manifest:** a file with no `Cargo.toml` above it keeps v8's label-only binding and is marked `INFERRED`. Scoping needs a crate.
- **Glob re-exports:** `pub use core::*;` is not followed; only a named `pub use` is.
- **Renamed dependencies:** `foo = { package = "bar" }` in `Cargo.toml` is not mapped, so `use foo::..` stays unbound.
- **Macros:** a re-export produced by a macro is invisible to the extractor.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_rust_crate_use_scope.py` run `extract()` on small Cargo projects and compare node ids, edge targets, and confidence. None of them calls a private helper.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| an external `use` plus an annotation does not reach a local crate (enum variant) | fail | pass |
| an external `use` plus an annotation does not reach a local crate (struct) | fail | pass |
| a grouped external `use` does not reach a local crate | fail | pass |
| an annotation with no `use` does not reach a local crate | fail | pass |
| `use a::Value` reaches `a`, not a namesake in `c` | fail | pass |
| `use osiris_types::Config` does not reach `server`'s `Config` | fail | pass |
| `use osiris_types::Config` reaches `osiris-types` when both define it | fail | pass |
| a `use` of a re-exporting crate reaches the defining crate, not an unrelated namesake | fail | pass |
| `pub(crate) use` does not leak out of its crate | fail | pass |
| a manifest-less binding is `INFERRED`, not `EXTRACTED` | fail | pass |
| guard: external `use` with no reference, `std`, `crate::`, same-name types without a `use` | pass | pass |
| guard: `use super::Item` through a re-export reaches the defining crate | pass | pass |
| guard: a scanned-crate `use` keeps `EXTRACTED` | pass | pass |

```text
pytest tests/test_rust_crate_use_scope.py (v8)             -> 10 failed, 9 passed
pytest tests/test_rust_crate_use_scope.py (this branch)    -> 19 passed
pytest test_rust_* test_extract.py test_cache.py test_grammar_cache_key.py test_cargo_* \
                                                           -> 576 passed, 4 skipped
pytest -q -p no:randomly (full suite, serial)              -> v8:      39 failed, 7988 passed, 361 skipped
                                                              this PR:  39 failed, 8007 passed, 361 skipped
                                                              (failure sets identical)
```

- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).

title: fix: resolve affected <path> for disambiguated file labels (#4698)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4698. `graphify affected <path>` answered `No unique node match for <path>` for a file whose basename is shared with another file and that has a second node on `L1`, for example a module docstring.

A path query matches every node in the file, so resolution ends in `_prefer_file_node`. Three of its passes pick the file node:

1. the label equals the query basename and sits on `L1`
2. the file node is the only node on `L1`
3. the label equals the basename

#2032 relabels colliding basenames to their shortest unique path suffix (`alpha/hooks.py`), which retires passes 1 and 3. The rationale pass creates one node per docstring at the docstring's own line, so a docstring on line 1 puts a second node on `L1` and retires pass 2. A one-line top-level definition does the same. Either precondition alone is harmless. Both together resolve to `None`.

The fact the resolver needs is already in the graph: a file node's label is a path form of its own `source_file`. `_is_file_node_label` encodes exactly that and `build`/`analyze` already use it.

```diff
 graphify/affected.py
   _prefer_file_node()
     pass 1: label equals the basename and is on L1
+    pass 2: label names this node's own source_file
+            (_is_file_node_label, imported lazily from graphify.build)
+            checked before the "only node on L1" fallback
     pass 3: only node on L1
     pass 4: label equals the basename
```

No graph schema change and no re-extraction. The relabelled node is already in `graph.json`; only the lookup changes.

**Before** (v8, the issue's repro):

```text
$ graphify affected app/alpha/hooks.py
No unique node match for app/alpha/hooks.py
$ echo $?
0
```

**After:**

```text
$ graphify affected app/alpha/hooks.py
Affected nodes for alpha/hooks.py
Relations: calls, indirect_call, references, imports, imports_from, dynamic_import, re_exports, inherits, extends, implements, uses, mixes_in, embeds, defines, requires
Depth: 2
- main.py [imports_from] app/main.py:L1
- handle() [calls] app/main.py:L5
```

The same graph resolves both files by path:

```text
app/alpha/hooks.py                  -> alpha/hooks.py
app/beta/hooks.py                   -> beta/hooks.py
./app/alpha/hooks.py                -> alpha/hooks.py
/abs/path/app/alpha/hooks.py        -> alpha/hooks.py
alpha/hooks.py   (the label)        -> alpha/hooks.py
app_alpha_hooks  (the node id)      -> alpha/hooks.py
hooks.py         (ambiguous)        -> still no unique match
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A path seed resolves to the node that names the file: the `L1` node whose label is the file's basename or a trailing path suffix of its own `source_file`. Extra `L1` nodes do not change the result. When two nodes both claim that shape, resolution still refuses to guess.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. No cache schema change, no extractor change. A revert restores the miss on the next run, and an existing `graph.json` works without a rebuild.

**Blast Radius:** path seed resolution.

`resolve_seed` is shared by the `affected` CLI and the `serve`/MCP lookup path, so both gain the fix. The new pass runs only when a path query already matched more than one node, and it compares the label to that node's own `source_file`, so it cannot bind to another file. Single-file graphs, unique basenames, and node-id seeds take the same path as before. The full-suite failure set is identical to v8.

**Limitations**

- **Exit code:** `affected` still prints the failure to stdout and exits 0 when nothing matches. That is a separate defect and is not fixed here.
- **Docstring text:** a docstring whose text is literally a path suffix of the file (for example `alpha/hooks.py`) and lands on `L1` would compete with the file node. Two candidates still return no match rather than guessing.
- **Graphs before #2032:** a label that is still the bare basename resolves through the existing pass, unchanged.
- **Not attempted:** marking file nodes explicitly at extraction time, which would remove the heuristic entirely. This PR keeps the read-side predicate.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_affected_path_file_node.py` build the exact node shapes and run the issue's repro end to end through `python -m graphify update` and `graphify affected`. None of them calls a private helper.

| Test | v8 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| disambiguated label plus a docstring rationale on L1 | fail | pass |
| disambiguated label plus a one-line definition on L1 | fail | pass |
| absolute-path seed with `root=` resolves the same node | fail | pass |
| two nodes claiming the same path form still return no match | pass | pass |
| end to end: shared basename with a docstring lists `main.py` | fail | pass |
| control: comment instead of a docstring, definition below L1 | pass | pass |

```text
pytest tests/test_affected_path_file_node.py (v8)          -> 4 failed, 2 passed
pytest tests/test_affected_path_file_node.py (this branch) -> 6 passed
pytest test_affected_cli.py test_affected_defines.py test_affected_member_seed.py \
       test_affected_overrides.py test_explain_cli.py test_explain_same_file_tie.py \
       test_js_dynamic_import_affected.py test_lookup_exit_codes.py \
       test_query_seed_order.py test_query_seeds.py        -> 111 passed
pytest test_serve.py test_analyze.py                       -> 232 passed, 1 skipped
pytest test_build.py                                       -> 97 passed
pytest -q -p no:randomly (full suite, serial)              -> v8:      39 failed, 7988 passed, 361 skipped
                                                              this PR:  39 failed, 7994 passed, 361 skipped
                                                              (failure sets identical)
```

The pass-count difference is the six new tests. The 39 failures are the same environment failures on v8 and on this branch.

title: fix: recover chained TS decorators and report the lossy parse region (#4711)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4711. A TypeScript decorator whose expression is a call chain (`@(Link().toMany())`) contributed no `references` edge to the graph, and the partial-parse warning pointed at a line that was not the one costing extraction.

tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2 cannot parse a member access on a call in decorator position. `@Link().toMany()` fails on one line, without parentheses, and with the dot moved to the next line, so no formatting change avoids it. The parser recovers by wrapping `Link().` in an ERROR and parsing `toMany()` as a sibling inside the parentheses. `_ts_decorator_name` returned `None` for every `parenthesized_expression`, so the whole decorator was skipped.

The warning also reported the first ERROR in document order. In `continent.entity.ts` that is line 14, a single-line recovery that keeps every symbol; the multiline region at line 33 is the one that lost edges.

```diff
 graphify/extractors/engine.py
+  _ts_decorator_target_name()
+    unwrap a parenthesized decorator
+    name the outermost call the parser recovered
+    name nothing for a recovered non-call expression (`@(A, B)`)
+
+  _first_multiline_error_line()
+    line of the earliest ERROR that spans more than one line

 graphify/extract.py
-  first_error_line
+  lossy_error_line, falling back to first_error_line
+  "error region at line N" instead of "first error at line N"
```

**Before** (v8, `continent.entity.ts` from the issue):

```text
warning:  ... continent.entity.ts (first error at line 14, 6 symbol(s) extracted)
decorator edges: column, entity, primarykey
```

**After:**

```text
warning:  ... continent.entity.ts (error region at line 33, 8 symbol(s) extracted)
decorator edges: column, tomany, toone, entity, primarykey
```

The two new edges add their stub targets, which is where the two extra nodes come from.

The 7-line `x.ts` from the issue goes from no decorator edge to:

```text
x_c -> tomany [references, context=decorator]
```

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A decorator's `references` edge targets the outermost call of its expression, whether or not the expression is parenthesized. A recovered expression that is not a call (an invalid `@(A, B)`) gets no name rather than a guessed one. The warning line names the region the warning gate selects on: the earliest multiline ERROR, or the first error when the file yielded nothing but its file node.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. No cache schema change. Cached per-file results without `lossy_error_line` keep the old first-error line until they are re-extracted; the graph itself is unchanged by that key.

**Blast Radius:** TS/JS decorator edges and the partial-parse warning text.

Parenthesized decorators in every language now resolve a name where they previously resolved none. Plain decorators (`@Component`, `@ng.Component()`, `@Injectable`) take the same path as before, and the 320 TS/JS tests pass. The warning wording changed from `first error at line N` to `error region at line N`, which is user-visible; four existing expectations were updated with it. The full-suite failure set is identical to v8.

**Limitations**

- **Grammar:** the parse error remains. tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2 is the newest release on PyPI, and TSX and JS grammars fail on the same construct. No source rewrite tried (paren stripping, double parens, computed access, sequence, optional chain, line continuation) parses.
- **Unparenthesized chains:** `@Link().toMany()` still attributes only `Link`, because the parser ends the decorator at `@Link()` and parses the rest as a separate expression.
- **One target per decorator:** only the outermost call is named, so `Link` gets no edge from `@(Link().toMany())`.
- **Repeated targets:** two decorators with the same target collapse into one edge, since edges are deduplicated by endpoints and relation.
- **Warning:** it still says "may be partially extracted" even when every symbol survived; the parser cannot tell whether the lost part was a decorator edge or a symbol.

## How was this tested?

New tests in `tests/test_ts_decorator_chains.py` run `extract()` on small TS files: the two recovered shapes, the clean identifier-receiver shape, the invalid-sequence guard, and the warning line for a file with an earlier single-line error.

```text
pytest tests/test_ts_decorator_chains.py (v8)      -> 4 failed, 1 passed
pytest tests/test_ts_decorator_chains.py (this PR) -> 5 passed
pytest test_ts_*.py test_js_*.py test_python_decorators.py \
       test_partial_extraction_warning.py          -> 320 passed
pytest -q -p no:randomly (full suite, serial)      -> v8:      39 failed, 7988 passed, 361 skipped
                                                      this PR:  39 failed, 7993 passed, 361 skipped
                                                      (failure sets identical)
```

Verified on the issue's files with `graphify update --force`:

| file | v8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `x.ts` | no decorator edge | `x_c -> tomany` |
| `continent.entity.ts` | 3 decorator edges, warning at line 14 | 5 decorator edges, warning at line 33 |

body:
Fixes #3859.

## Base

Based on `upstream/v8` at `c588b72d` (0.9.94), the latest release at the time of writing. Re-verified against that tree, not the 0.9.69 version in the report.

## Problem

The README did not document the labeling/rendering limits, and several behaviors were easy to misread:

- `--batch-size` defaults to 100 communities per call, sized for a ~16k-token context. An 8k model overflows; context overflow is not split-retried, so the batch keeps hub-derived names.

- `export html` defaults to a 5,000-node limit and does not read `GRAPHIFY_VIZ_NODE_LIMIT`, unlike `cluster-only`/`update`/`watch`.
- The README described clustering as Leiden without noting the silent Louvain fallback when the `leiden` extra is absent.

## Change

- `README.md`: add a compact "Labeling and rendering limits" section covering the five points above.
- `graphify/__main__.py`: CLI help now states the ~16k sizing for `--batch-size` and the 5,000 default for `export html --node-limit`.

Docs and help strings only; no behavior change.
