title: graph.html is hard to move on a dense graph
body:
## Problem

`graph.html` is the page a person opens after `graphify extract` and `graphify cluster-only`. On a dense graph it is unpleasant to move around.

Upstream v8 makes a drag or a zoom feel lighter by setting `hideEdgesOnDrag` and `hideEdgesOnZoom`. The edges disappear while the pointer is down and come back when it is released. That is a different picture from the graph at rest. On top of that, the nodes change size while the view moves, a hover in a dense cluster stalls, and opening the same graph again re-runs the force solver from scratch.

The aim is a page that stays the graph people already have, and stays that graph while it is moving.

## Constraints

These were the rules for the change. They are why the patch looks the way it does.

- Do not hide edges during a drag, a pan, or a zoom. The frame in motion has to be the frame at rest.
- Do not change a node's size because the pointer went down or the camera moved.
- Hover highlights only the edge or the node under the pointer. It does not dim the rest of the graph. Dimming is a click.
- The sidebar still classifies communities by colour and by name. The name box filters that list. It is not a second list.
- A small graph stays on vis-network's own drawing. The extra path is only for a drawn graph over 800 nodes, and arrowheads wait until hover only over 1,500 edges.
- Graphs over the existing 5,000 node limit still become the community summary. This does not raise that limit.
- No new renderer, no new dependency, no change to extraction, clustering, or `graph.json`.

## Why this is not a WebGL renderer

vis-network 9.1.6 draws on a 2D canvas. It has no WebGL mode. A replacement was tried: sigma.js on the same graph (1,886 nodes, 3,876 edges), on a real GPU, not software WebGL. Pan went from about 5 fps on the shipped page to about 90â€“110 fps.

That spike was rejected. The picture was not the graph this page already is. Community colours, the smooth curves, the sidebar, hover, and click would all have been reimplemented, and the result still looked like a different product. Speed that changes the graph people open is not the goal.

The cost was also not "canvas cannot do this". It was specific work on the canvas path:

- one `stroke()` per edge per frame (about 3,876 strokes, ~30 ms, on that graph)
- one border stroke per node per frame
- `network.setOptions()` during a gesture, which forces a full synchronous redraw
- a hover that wrote the edge DataSet and pulled a hub's edges back out of any batch
- the canvas waiting on the compositor before the next frame could be presented (interaction-to-next-paint about 166 ms, down to about 55 ms once the context is `desynchronized: true`)

All of that can be fixed inside the existing page. WebGL stays available later if a graph is so large that even the on-screen strokes cannot hold a frame rate. It is not required for the graphs this viewer is asked to draw, and anything over 5,000 nodes is already the community summary.

## What changed

One runtime file, `graphify/exporters/html.py`. `export html`, `cluster-only`, and watch all call `to_html` there, so every new `graph.html` gets this. Against current `v8` the file is +1,192 / âˆ’81. The behaviour tests are a new file, `tests/test_html_perf_levers.py`.

What every graph gets:

- The canvas context is created with `desynchronized: true`.
- The layout is saved in `localStorage` after the solver finishes. Opening the same graph again skips the 200-iteration solve. The positions are that graph's own positions.
- The community list has a colour strip and a name filter. "All" resets it.
- Hover is on. It highlights the edge under the pointer (and that edge's arrowhead) or the node under the pointer. It does not dim neighbours, and hovering a node does not fan arrowheads onto every incident edge. That fan-out was the stall in a dense cluster. Click still focuses and dims what is not connected.

What a drawn graph over 800 nodes also gets:

- Solid edges are stroked in groups of the same colour and width, one `stroke()` per group, with the same curve vis was already drawing. Dashed, selected, hovered, and arrowed edges stay on vis's own draw.
- While zoomed in, if most edges are off screen, each visible edge is stroked on its own. A colour group can be hundreds of curves spanning a huge path, and stroking that whole path is what made zoomed-in panning hitch.
- Node discs keep one radius for the life of the gesture. The radius is stored on the node so a DataSet write during a drag cannot snap it back, and hover or select does not halve it.

What a graph over 1,500 edges also gets:

- Arrowheads are not drawn on every edge every frame. Direction is still there: hover the edge and its arrowhead is drawn. Below the threshold the arrowheads stay as they are today.

## What this does not include

The branch this was developed on also has lab notes, screenshots, a sigma.js prototype, and older unrelated commits. None of that is in the patch. The pull request is the exporter and the tests that pin it.

## How it was checked

`tests/test_html_perf_levers.py` pins the behaviour above: edges stay in the page during a gesture, the edge batch groups by colour and width and leaves dashes to vis, off-screen curves are dropped, hover never dims, the families panel has one row per community and a name filter, node size is not rewritten on a gesture, and the desynchronized patch is emitted before the vis script. The existing `to_html` tests (search, legend, theme, script breakout, `showInfo`) still apply.

By hand, the same folder was built the way a person builds a graph, once with upstream `v8` and once with this file:

- A code graph of 918 nodes and about 2,400 edges (under the 5,000 cap, over the 800 node threshold, so the zoom path is in the page). At rest the two pages are the same kind of graph. v8 hides edges while dragging and the sidebar says "Select All". This page keeps the edges and the sidebar has the colour strip and the name filter.
- A larger repo that goes over 5,000 nodes. Both versions draw the community summary, which is under 800 nodes, so that page has the sidebar and the saved layout, and does not include the zoom culling. That is the existing node limit, not a new one.
- On a 1,597 node / 3,651 edge graph, the first open was not faster (10.7 s against 8.1 s for v8). The second open was 0.7 s against 9.7 s, because the solver result had been saved.

Before and after, the same graph, upstream v8 beside this branch. The recording is the drag and the zoom, not a still of the first frame.

https://youtu.be/pSgp00Xr-jA

## Pull request

The patch is #4723, on `perf/html-render-qol`, based on current `v8`, commit `d67b1022`.

title: perf(html): keep graph.html smooth without hiding edges
body:
Fixes #4722

## Problem

On a dense graph, `graph.html` is only comfortable to drag and zoom because v8 sets `hideEdgesOnDrag` and `hideEdgesOnZoom`. The edges vanish while the view moves. Nodes also change size during the gesture, a hover in a dense cluster stalls, and reopening the same file runs the force solver again.

## Fix

The change is `graphify/exporters/html.py`. `cluster-only`, `export html`, and watch all call `to_html`, so this is the page everyone gets. No new dependency and no change to extraction or `graph.json`.

- Edges stay drawn during a drag, pan, and zoom.
- Over 800 nodes, solid edges are stroked in colour/width groups, and while zoomed in only the on-screen edges are stroked. Dashed, selected, hovered, and arrowed edges stay on vis's own draw.
- Over 1,500 edges, arrowheads are drawn when an edge is hovered, not on every edge every frame.
- Node discs keep their radius while the view moves, including on hover and select.
- Hover highlights the edge or the node under the pointer. It does not dim the rest. Dimming stays a click.
- The community sidebar has a colour strip and a name filter.
- The solved layout is saved, so the next open of the same graph skips the solver.
- The canvas context is `desynchronized: true`.

A WebGL replacement (sigma.js) was faster on a pan and was not used. vis-network has no WebGL mode, and the replacement did not look like this page. The cost was specific canvas work, described in #4722.

Before and after, the same graph:

https://youtu.be/pSgp00Xr-jA

## Testing

- `tests/test_html_perf_levers.py` pins the behaviour above.
- Existing `to_html` coverage still applies: theme, `showInfo`, legend, script breakout, search.
- Same folder, both builds, the way a person runs graphify: a 918-node code graph. v8 hides edges while dragging and the sidebar says "Select All". This page keeps the edges, and the sidebar has the colour strip and the name filter. On a 1,597-node graph the first open was not faster (10.7 s vs 8.1 s); the second open was 0.7 s vs 9.7 s.

Local check of the HTML tests: `tests/test_html_perf_levers.py`, `tests/test_html_theme.py`, `tests/test_html_script_breakout.py`, and `tests/test_export.py` â€” 130 passed after the theme and script-tag fixes. Full `uv run pytest tests/ -q` is the pre-PR run for this branch.

title: fix(watch): bound each watch rebuild with GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT, with a Timer fallback where SIGALRM is missing (#2173)
body:
**Defect**
On `v8` (92741d1), `graphify/watch.py` contains 0 references to `SIGALRM`, `threading.Timer` or `GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT`. `graphify/hooks.py` contains 2 of each, one per embedded rebuild body. A rebuild that hangs inside `graphify watch` therefore blocks the watch loop with no upper bound. This is the remaining half of #2173.

**Root cause**
`graphify/watch.py:2850` calls `_rebuild_code(watch_path)` outside any timeout guard. The hooks guard the same call at `graphify/hooks.py:200-228`: `signal.alarm` where `SIGALRM` exists, a `threading.Timer` where it does not (#2148). `watch.py` has neither path.

**Fix**
I added `_rebuild_timeout()` to `graphify/watch.py` and wrapped the loop's `_rebuild_code` call in it. It has the two paths the hooks have:
- `SIGALRM` available: the handler kills `multiprocessing.active_children()`, then raises `TimeoutError`. The loop prints `[graphify watch] <message>` and keeps watching. The previous handler is restored on exit.
- `SIGALRM` unavailable (Windows): a daemon `threading.Timer` kills the children and calls `os._exit(1)`. The watcher process exits.
- `GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT=0` disables the guard. The default is `600`, as in the hooks.

**Evidence**
```
pytest tests/test_hooks.py -q                              178 passed   (after rebase onto 92741d1)
pytest tests/test_hooks.py -q -k watch_rebuild_timeout     1 failed, 172 deselected   (watch.py reverted to v8)
pytest tests/ -q                                           8265 passed, 200 skipped, 7 failed   (before rebase; not rerun on 92741d1)
ruff check .                                               All checks passed!
```
- The new test, `test_watch_rebuild_timeout_arms_a_timer_without_sigalrm`, parses `watch.py` with `ast`. It asserts that the `Timer` fallback sits in the else-branch of the `SIGALRM` check, that `_bail` kills children before `os._exit`, and that `watch()` references `_rebuild_timeout`.
- The 7 failures are all in `tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py`. The same file gives `7 failed, 7 passed` on `v8` with this change stashed.
- `pyright` reports errors in my environment. `watchdog` is not installed, so `graphify/watch.py` reports 3 unresolved `watchdog.*` imports. Other files report errors unrelated to this change. No error falls on a changed line. I did not compare the total against `v8`.

**Behavior change**
POSIX `graphify watch` now has a 600 s default rebuild timeout where it had none. This matches the `600` default in the hooks. On timeout the POSIX watcher logs and continues, and the Windows watcher exits. `GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT=0` restores the previous behavior.

**Boundaries and trade-offs**
- I did not run the Windows path on a Windows host. The test is structural, like the hook tests it follows.
- I did not reproduce a hung rebuild, so I have no timing for the timeout firing.
- I left the hook bodies untouched. They are string literals inside a shell `-c` argument, and a shared import would change that carrier. A second copy of the 25 lines in `watch.py` was the alternative; a context manager was shorter and restores the handler.
- The Timer path uses `os._exit(1)` because no other call interrupts a main thread blocked in a rebuild when `SIGALRM` is missing.

**Question**
I kept the 600 s default to match the hooks. Do you want `watch` to default to `0` instead, so POSIX behavior stays unchanged? I can change the default or split the Windows fallback into its own PR.

title: fix(python): resolve calls through injected fields and method results
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fix four missing Python method-call edges in a small task-service project:

```text
TaskService.create_task   -> TaskRepository.add
TaskService.complete_task -> TaskRepository.get
TaskService.complete_task -> Task.complete
TaskService.pending_tasks -> TaskRepository.all
```

The service receives `repository: TaskRepository` and assigns `self.repository = repository`. The extractor previously lost that binding, so calls through the field stayed unresolved. In `task = self.repository.get(key); task.complete()`, the local receiver also lost the resolved method's `-> Task` annotation.

This change carries unchanged typed bindings into fields and links a local method result to its exact producer call span. The resolver uses the producer's single-class return annotation, while preserving caller file/line provenance and `INFERRED` confidence. CLI and watch rebuilds retain unchanged return-type references as resolution context, and AST cache schema 26 retires cached calls without these markers.

## Verification & Invariants

A receiver must resolve to one class before a call edge is added. Unknown, rebound, shadowed, container-valued, or ambiguously typed results stay unresolved. A nested argument call on the same line cannot substitute for the assigned producer; there is no bare-method-name fallback.

The new tests cover all four edges, source locations, negative cases, cold/warm caches, schema invalidation, changed-file extraction, and actual CLI/watch rebuilds.

Limits: this does not add general data-flow inference. Changing a producer's return annotation still requires a full rebuild to recompute inferred relationships for unchanged callers.

title: feat(global): add commit-provenance manifest, settle guard, and status/sync subcommands
body:
## Why (Rationale & Problem)

In multi-repository workspaces (`~/.graphify/global-graph.json`), `graphify global add` previously recorded only `added_at`, `source_path`, `node_count`, `edge_count`, and `source_hash` in `~/.graphify/global-manifest.json`. That left three operational blind spots:
1. **No Commit Provenance or Staleness Visibility**: There was no record of which git commit each registered repository's graph represented, making it impossible to tell whether a repository had advanced by 1 commit or 100 commits since its last merge into the global union.
2. **Race Condition with Background Hook Rebuilds**: `graphify hook install` (`post-commit` / `post-checkout`) triggers incremental graph rebuilds in the background. Running `graphify global add` immediately after a commit could read a `graph.json` mid-write or stamp a newer git `HEAD` than the bytes actually merged.
3. **No Bulk Union Refresh**: Updating an N-repository workspace required manually re-running `graphify global add <path> --as <tag>` for every repository one by one.

## What For (Use Cases & Value)

- **CI / Pre-Flight Currency Gates (`graphify global status --strict --json`)**: Allows multi-repo orchestrators and agent pre-flight checks to verify in `<100ms` that every registered repository's global graph slice matches its on-disk `graph.json` and git `HEAD`, failing closed when any member repository is stale or missing.
- **One-Command Safe Multi-Repo Refresh (`graphify global sync --settle 5`)**: Re-merges only the repositories whose `graph.json` changed, automatically waiting for background post-commit hooks to finish writing before reading, and skipping unchanged repositories.

## How (Implementation & Invariants)

1. **Commit Provenance in `~/.graphify/global-manifest.json` (`built_at_commit` vs `head_at_merge` + `commit_basis`)**:
   - `global_add()` samples the repository's git `HEAD` (`head_at_merge`, honoring `.graphify_root` when present) **before** reading/merging `source_path` and extracts `built_at_commit` from `graph.json`, recording `built_at_commit`, `head_at_merge`, and `commit_basis` (`"built_at_commit" | "head_at_merge" | None`) so extracted graph provenance remains visibly separate from the git `HEAD` fallback.
2. **In-Flight Background Write-Stability Guard (`settled()` & `--settle <seconds>`)**:
   - `settled(source_path, budget_s)` returns immediately when a file has been quiet for `> 2.0s` (zero overhead on the normal path) and otherwise polls `(st_size, st_mtime_ns)` across consecutive samples until stable. If still changing after `budget_s`, `global_add(..., settle_s=...)` returns `skipped=True, unsettled=True` and leaves both `global-graph.json` and `global-manifest.json` untouched.
3. **`graphify global status [--strict] [--json] [--only <substr>]` & `graphify global sync [--only <substr>] [--settle <seconds>]`**:
   - `global_status()` inspects each registered repo in `global-manifest.json`, comparing its on-disk `source_hash` against `manifest_hash` and computing git commit distance (`commits_behind` via `git rev-list --count`) from the merged commit to current `HEAD`.
   - `global_sync()` iterates over all registered repositories in `global-manifest.json`, re-merging modified graphs, skipping unchanged ones, and explicitly reporting any missing or unsettled repositories.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

- **Provenance separation & pre-merge sampling invariant (`CONTRIBUTING.md` #2 & #4)**: `head_at_merge` is sampled before reading/merging `source_path` (so a concurrent commit during merge cannot stamp a newer `HEAD` than the merged content), and `built_at_commit` is stored separately with `commit_basis` explicitly stating which stamp is authoritative.
- **No partial/mid-write overwrite (`CONTRIBUTING.md` #1 & #6)**: When `settle_s > 0` and a background hook is actively writing `graph.json`, `global_add` refuses to read or overwrite `global-graph.json` / `global-manifest.json`.
- **Fail-closed status & sync (`CONTRIBUTING.md` #5)**: Missing `source_path` entries and `--only` filters that match zero registered repositories fail loudly rather than succeeding vacuously.

title: fix(prs): treat every unfinished CheckRun status as pending CI
body:
## What does this PR do?

`graphify prs` classifies CI from `statusCheckRollup`. GitHub's `CheckStatusState` has six values: `REQUESTED`, `QUEUED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`, `WAITING`, `PENDING`. Only `COMPLETED` carries a conclusion. `_parse_ci` only matched `IN_PROGRESS` and `QUEUED`. So:

- a `WAITING` CheckRun (a job held by a deployment protection rule / required reviewer on an environment), a `REQUESTED` one, or a `PENDING` one read as `NONE` on its own, and
- next to any sibling check that already passed, it read as `SUCCESS`. `_classify` then marked the PR `READY` while a gated job had not run.

The fix treats every non-`COMPLETED` status as pending (`_CI_PENDING_STATUSES`). StatusContext handling and the failure precedence are unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a check that has not finished never counts as passed CI.

title: fix(build): coerce numeric hyperedge members under the members/node_ids aliases
body:
## What does this PR do?

`_coerce_non_string_ids` (#2326) turns numeric ids from a loose backend into str: node ids, edge endpoints (including the legacy `from`/`to` aliases), and the hyperedge member list, but only under the canonical `nodes` key.
```text
[graphify] WARNING: hyperedge 'h' uses field 'members' instead of 'nodes'; normalizing.
[graphify] WARNING: dropping hyperedge 'h' — none of its members [1, 2, 3] match built nodes.
```

The identical extraction keyed `nodes` survives. The fix coerces the alias lists in the same loop, as the `from`/`to` endpoint aliases already are. It doesn't change behaviour for str members or for the canonical key.

title: fix(llm): evidence-check a code node whose confidence is a mis-cased EXTRACTED
body:
## What does this PR do?

`_bind_node_evidence` marks a semantic `code` node `verification: "unverified"` when none of its identifiers occur in the source the model read. It only does that for nodes the model presented as solid, and the check is case-sensitive:

```python
if n.get("confidence") in (None, "", "EXTRACTED") and not n.get(_VERIFICATION_FIELD):
```

`build._fold_confidence` treats a case variant as that enum value and corrects its spelling (#4529, #4495). The fix upper-cases a string confidence before the comparison. A hedged value in any case (`inferred`, `ambiguous`) is still left alone. A control test pins that.

title: fix(python): bind a member call to the method it spells, not a folded twin
body:
## What does this PR do?

A public wrapper next to a private implementation is a common Python shape:

```python
class Worker:
    def run(self): ...
    def _run(self): ...
```

#3302 gave the two methods separate node ids, but `_resolve_python_member_calls` still indexes methods by `_key(label)`, which strips `_` and folds case. Both land on one `method_index` entry, the later `method` edge overwrites the earlier one, and every member-call arm resolves `run()` to `_run()`. On v8:

| call | expected target | actual target |
|---|---|---|
| `Worker.run(None)` (class arm) | `.run()` | `._run()` |
| `w.run()` with `w: Worker` (typed receiver) | `.run()` | `._run()` |
| `self.run()` in a subclass in another file (inherited arm) | `.run()` | `._run()` |
| `Worker.Run(None)` (matches neither exactly) | no edge | `._run()` |

The fix keeps every method under the folded key. When several share it, the one named exactly as the call wins, and an inexact match is no edge. That's the same rule the module arm already applies (#4577), and the one C# got in #4415. When only one method has the key, the lookup is unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a resolved call edge points at the definition the call names. A guess between folded twins is no edge (fail closed).

title: Add ZCode platform support (graphify install --platform zcode)
body:
## Summary

ZCode (docs: https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/skill) discovers skills from `~/.zcode/skills/` (user) and `.zcode/skills/` (project), reads AGENTS.md natively as its workspace instruction file, and dispatches parallel subagents through an Agent tool — the same shape as Claude Code, which makes it a natural `--platform` target riding claude's split skill bundle (like codebuddy/kimi).

Proposed shape, mirroring the codex/opencode wiring:

- `_PLATFORM_CONFIG["zcode"]`: `skill_file: skill.md` (claude bundle), `skill_dst: .zcode/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` — the generic `_platform_skill_destination` fallthrough already yields `~/.zcode/skills` (global) and `./.zcode/skills` (project), so no destination branch is needed.
- Project install joins the AGENTS.md platforms (`skill + _agents_install`), since ZCode loads AGENTS.md into every session; global install stays skill-only like codex.
- Bare `graphify uninstall` removes the `~/.zcode/skills` user skill (mirrors the amp/agents user-scope removals).

No skillgen changes: zcode reuses the committed claude bundle and references as-is (verified with `python -m tools.skillgen --check`).

PR incoming with tests (`tests/test_zcode_platform.py`) covering destinations, global/project install, idempotency, uninstall, and the bare-uninstall user-scope removal.

title: feat(install): add zcode platform (claude skill bundle + AGENTS.md + SessionStart reminder hook)
body:
Refs #4736.

## What

Adds `zcode` as an installable platform: `graphify install --platform zcode` (global, `~/.zcode/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`) and `graphify install --project --platform zcode` (`./.zcode/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` + the `## graphify` AGENTS.md always-on section + a SessionStart reminder hook in `.zcode/config.json`).

ZCode (https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/skill) discovers skills from `~/.zcode/skills` and `.zcode/skills`, loads AGENTS.md natively, and dispatches parallel subagents through an Agent tool — so the platform rides claude's split bundle (`skill.md` + claude references, like codebuddy/kimi) and wires AGENTS.md like codex/opencode:

- `_PLATFORM_CONFIG["zcode"]` entry only; the generic `_platform_skill_destination` fallthrough already resolves both scopes, so no destination branch was added.
- `_project_install`/`_project_uninstall` join the AGENTS.md platform tuple (`.zcode` gets a git-add hint like codex/opencode).
- Bare `uninstall` removes the `~/.zcode/skills` user skill (mirrors the amp/agents user-scope removals).
- No skillgen changes — the platform reuses the committed claude bundle unchanged (`python -m tools.skillgen --check` passes: 134 artifacts match).

## SessionStart reminder hook (second commit)

AGENTS.md alone proved skippable in practice: on a real repo with daily ZCode use, query-first graphify usage died within days of relying only on the always-on section, and came back the moment a session-start reminder fired. So a `--project` install now also registers a SessionStart hook in `.zcode/config.json`:

- `graphify hook-guard zcode <dir>` prints `{"additionalContext": "<nudge>"}` when a graph exists — strict-JSON stdout (ZCode validates the hook output schema), silent exit 0 otherwise, no stdin contract. The dir arg arrives as `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` expanded by the hook runner, with a guard for unexpanded literals that falls back to the env vars / cwd; `GRAPHIFY_OUT` is honored.
- `_install_zcode_hook`/`_uninstall_zcode_hook` merge into `.zcode/config.json` through the shared settings helpers: foreign top-level keys and foreign SessionStart hooks are preserved, re-installs replace rather than duplicate, `.graphify-bak` backup, and `hooks.enabled: true` is set with a visible note (ZCode config-file hooks are off by default). Uninstall strips the entry and prunes empty `hooks` containers.
- Project installs only — a global install stays skill-only, mirroring the opencode plugin's project scope (the knowledge graph is per-project). Like a project-scoped Claude/Codex hook (#3129), the committed config carries the bare `graphify` command + the `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` template variable, never an installing-machine path.
- ZCode snapshots hook config per session, so the reminder first fires in the session after install.

## Tests

`tests/test_zcode_platform.py` (16 tests): user/project destinations, global install (skill + references + version stamp, no AGENTS.md, no hook anywhere), project install (skill + AGENTS.md + SessionStart hook with `hooks.enabled=true`), hook merge preserves foreign keys and foreign SessionStart hooks, idempotent double install (one section, one hook entry), project uninstall (skill + section + hook; prunes empty containers; keeps foreign keys/hooks), bare-uninstall user-scope removal, and `hook-guard zcode` end-to-end (nudge with a graph, incl. the unexpanded-literal fallback; silent without one).

Validation run:
- `uv run pytest tests/test_zcode_platform.py` — 16 passed
- `uv run pytest tests/test_install.py tests/test_gemini_hook.py tests/test_hook_guard.py tests/test_install_hook_identity.py tests/test_hook_guard_token_match.py tests/test_hook_out_of_project_paths.py` — 327 passed, 5 skipped
- `uv run ruff check --config pyproject.toml` — clean
- `uv run python -m tools.skillgen --check` — OK (134 artifacts match)
- `uv run pyright graphify` — no new errors vs the base branch (455 pre-existing on both; the one `too complex` error in the CLI module pre-dates this change and only shifts lines)
- Manual CLI run on Windows in a scratch repo: install merges the hook under a pre-existing `plugins` key; `hook-guard zcode` is silent without a graph and emits strict JSON with one; uninstall prunes back to the foreign keys.

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek output cap silently ignored
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

# DeepSeek output cap silently ignored

`_call_openai_compat` sends `max_completion_tokens` to every OpenAI-compatible backend. DeepSeek documents only `max_tokens`, and **silently ignores `max_completion_tokens`** — so the configured 16,384 cap is never applied and the provider's default governs.

DeepSeek's documented defaults are `8K` in non-thinking mode and `64K` in thinking mode. Setting `GRAPHIFY_DISABLE_THINKING=1` therefore drops the effective output budget from 64K to 8K, and extraction JSON truncates constantly:

| | `DISABLE_THINKING=1` | default (thinking on) |
|---|---|---|
| Truncation events | 30+, cascading to recursion depth 3 | 5 |
| Chunks producing no nodes | several (partial results kept) | 0 |

`graphify/llm.py` already documents that disabling thinking causes truncation — the mechanism above is *why*, and it is worse than the note implies because the configured cap never reaches the provider.

Suggested fix: map `max_completion_tokens` → `max_tokens` for the `deepseek` backend (or send both), so `GRAPHIFY_*_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` actually takes effect.


### Steps to reproduce

```shell
Just use the official hosted deepseek and the bug materialises (api.deepseek.com).
```

```text
None
```

title: `graphify update` on a cloned checkout re-extracts every file and rebuilds the whole graph (3 to 7 min, ~6 GB) even with zero changes
body:
**Use case.** One large monorepo, many git worktrees (one per branch / agent). The map is built once on a canonical checkout of `main`; each worktree gets a copy of `graphify-out/graph.json` (and `manifest.json`, and in one run `cache/`). We wanted each worktree to run `graphify update` so its map reflects the branch's changes. Correctness was fine: a new file and its function appeared. Cost was the blocker.

**Environment.** graphifyy 0.9.92 (pipx, Python 3.14.5), macOS, Apple M5 Max, 18 cores, 48 GB. Graph: 184,314 nodes, 463,239 edges, 4,610 communities, `graph.json` 258 MB, 19,397 code files. AST only (no LLM key set). Command each time: `GRAPHIFY_OUT=<worktree>/graphify-out graphify update <worktree>`.

| run | change since the copy | wall | peak RSS | log |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | none | 6m 12s | 6.3 GB | rebuilt, same counts |
| 2 | 49 files (42 modified/deleted, 1 new) | 7m 2s | 5.7 GB | rebuilt, correct |
| 3 | none | 3m 12s | 6.1 GB | `AST extraction: 19397/19397 uncached files (100%)` then `No code-graph topology changes detected; outputs left untouched.` |
| 4 | 1 file, canonical `cache/` (5,108 AST entries, 94 MB) copied in with the copy | 5m 58s | 6.2 GB | `19300/19397 uncached files (99%)`, full rebuild |

**What looks wrong.**
1. Run 3 and 4: the AST cache misses almost every file on a copied checkout. `cache.file_hash` documents keys as content + root-relative path for portability across checkout directories (#2199), so a copied cache should hit for unchanged files. Possibly the stat-index fast path misses (different inode/mtime on the copy) and something downstream counts the fallback as "uncached"; we have not traced further.
2. Run 1 and 4: with no or one changed file, `update` still re-clusters and rewrites `graph.json`, `graph.html` and `GRAPH_REPORT.md` in full. Run 3 shows a "no topology changes" short-circuit exists; it would help if it also applied before re-extraction, and if a small change patched the graph instead of rebuilding it.

**Ask.** An incremental update whose cost scales with the changed files: re-extract only files whose content changed, patch their nodes and edges into the existing graph, skip re-clustering and the HTML/report when topology changes are local (or behind flags like `--no-html --no-report`). Related: #2406 (cross-file edges lost on incremental re-extract), #3763 (AST-only update drops semantic edges).

Happy to run a patched build against this corpus and report timings.

title: fix(dart): detect an unnamed extension declaration
body:
An extension declared without a name - `extension on String { ... }`, the common unnamed-extension idiom - never matched the pattern meant to catch it, so it never minted a node or an `extends` edge at all. Found while auditing lesser-used language extractors for unreported bugs; no existing issue or PR covers this.

Root cause: `ext_pattern = r"^\s{0,4}extension\s+(\w+)?(?:<[^>]+>)?\s+on\s+(\w+)"` - the name's trailing whitespace was written as its own separate `\s+` run, demanding at least one space of its own before `on`, in addition to the `\s+` already required right after `extension`. With no name present, the single space between `extension` and `on` can only satisfy one of those two runs, so the whole regex simply never matched the anonymous form. The fallback label (`f"{stem}_anonymous_extension"`) this code already carries for exactly this case was dead code - it was written for a shape the regex could never actually produce a match for.

Fix: fold the name's trailing whitespace into the same optional group as the name itself (`(?:(\w+)\s*(?:<[^>]+>)?\s+)?on`), so nothing demands that space when the name is absent. A named extension's own match is unaffected.

Added two tests: the anonymous case now mints its node and `extends` edge, and a control confirming a named extension still resolves to its own declared name rather than the anonymous fallback.

Verified pre-fix behavior via `git show HEAD:<path>` + a temporary file swap (never `git stash`), confirmed byte-identical restoration afterward. Full suite and `tools.skillgen --check` both clean (only pre-existing, unrelated flakes present on a clean checkout too).

title: fix(detect): prune MSBuild obj/ and bin/ output on build evidence
body:
A C# project scanned after `dotnet build` pulled generated sources (GlobalUsings.g.cs, AssemblyInfo.cs) and build-copied config from obj/ and bin/ into the graph; `dotnet new` writes no .gitignore to stop it.

bin/ is real source in Rust and script trees, so gate both names on MSBuild artifacts as out/ is (#3347): restore output or FileListAbsolute.txt for obj/, *.deps.json, *.runtimeconfig.json or *.pdb for bin/. Ignore obj/ and bin/ under tests/fixtures, which C# editor tooling creates by restoring the fixture projects.

title: fix(extract): report AST cache hit rate over the file total, not uncached set (#4740)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4740. `graphify update` reported its AST cache progress against the uncached set, so the last line always read `N/N uncached files (100%)` and looked like a 100% hit rate. #4740 read it as "the copied cache missed almost every file"; the real rate was never printed anywhere.

That line counts progress through the work the run has to do, so its denominator is the work, not the corpus. This adds a separate line whose denominator is the file total, and leaves the existing progress lines alone.

**Before** (warm run across 100 `.py` + 20 `.ts`, cache already warmed, v8 `92741d16`):

```text
  AST extraction: 20/20 uncached files (100%) [12 workers]
```

20 of the 120 files were re-extracted, and the only line shown says 100%.

**After:**

```text
cold:  AST cache: 0/120 files served from cache (0%); 120 to extract
warm:  AST cache: 100/120 files served from cache (83%); 20 to extract
       AST extraction: 20/20 uncached files (100%) [12 workers]
```

```diff
 graphify/extract.py
+  _PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 100    hoisted to module scope, shared by all three sites
   extract()
+    cache_hits / no_extractor counters in the Phase 1 cache loop
+    print(f"  AST cache: {cache_hits}/{total} files served from cache "
+          f"({cache_hits * 100 // total}%); {len(uncached_work)} to extract"
+          + f"; {no_extractor} without an extractor")
+    gated on total >= _PROGRESS_INTERVAL, like the progress lines
   _extract_parallel / _extract_sequential
-    _PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 100    dropped, both read the module constant now
 tests/test_extract.py
+  test_extract_reports_ast_cache_hit_rate_over_file_total
```

No existing test changes. `tests/test_extract.py:5660` pins the `100/100 uncached files (100%)` format and still passes unmodified.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The cache summary reports against the files the run was asked to extract, so its denominator cannot shrink to the uncached set. The progress lines keep counting the uncached work, and their format stays pinned by `tests/test_extract.py:5660`.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Two counters, one `print`, one test. No schema, cache or file-format change, no persisted state, nothing to migrate back.

**Blast Radius:** narrow, and limited to stdout:
- The line prints on the runs that already print progress, meaning any `extract()` call asked to extract `_PROGRESS_INTERVAL` (100) files or more. Small batches, which is what `watch`, the hooks and the MCP server pass on a rebuild, stay quiet. Anything parsing that stdout strictly will see one extra line on the large runs. The gate came out of review: the first version printed on every call, so a one-file watch rebuild logged a 0% rate that is trivially true and carries no information.
- The counts come from the existing Phase 1 loop. Extraction, caching and the graph are untouched.
- Files with no extractor were invisible in every printed total before this. They now show as a suffix, so the 5 `.ets` files in the existing 105-file test are accounted for instead of silently absent.

**Limitations**

- The `uncached files` lines are unchanged. A reader still sees `20/20 uncached files (100%)`; the new line is what supplies the correct denominator. I left them because their format is asserted by an existing test, and rewriting them is outside this fix.
- On a TS-heavy repo the rate will read low or zero, because the JS/TS suffixes bypass the AST cache (`_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`). That is the second half of #4740 and this PR does not touch it.
- The `; N without an extractor` suffix is not asserted by a test. The path is exercised, since the existing 105-file test's `.ets` files have no extractor, but nothing pins the suffix text.
- Nothing prints when the path list is empty, or when it holds fewer than `_PROGRESS_INTERVAL` (100) files.
- Once warm `update` runs pass only the changed batch (the incremental path in #4740's other half), this line goes quiet on the runs someone might use to check whether the cache helped. If that visibility is wanted, it belongs behind a flag or an environment variable rather than unconditional stdout.

## How was this tested?

New `tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_reports_ast_cache_hit_rate_over_file_total` drives the real `extract()` over 100 `.py` + 5 `.ts` and reads captured stdout, no mocking. The corpus is sized past 100 files on purpose: the final progress line only prints when `total_files >= 100` (`extract.py:9263`), so a smaller corpus cannot show the two lines side by side. It covers three runs:

- cold, cacheable-only corpus -> `0/100`, `100 to extract`
- warm, same corpus -> `100/100`, `0 to extract`
- mixed, after warming -> `100/105`, `5 to extract`, while asserting the progress line still reads `5/5 uncached files (100%)` and that `105/105 uncached files` never appears

The gate was measured directly, in a scratch checkout, against the real `extract()` and through `_rebuild_code(changed_paths=[one file])`:

```text
    1 file  -> no line
   99 files -> no line
  100 files -> prints
  605 files -> prints
one-file watch rebuild -> no line, only the usual watch message

tests/test_extract.py with the gate     -> 373 passed, 1 xfailed
tests/test_extract.py without the gate  -> 373 passed, 1 xfailed
```

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly \
  tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_reports_ast_cache_hit_rate_over_file_total \
  tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_progress_final_line_uses_consistent_denominator
  -> 2 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
  -> 8727 passed, 15 skipped, 1 xfailed, 2225 warnings in 402.12s (0:06:42)
```

Both Before/After blocks come from real `graphify update` runs on the same corpus, with the fix stashed and then applied.

Environment note, not fixed here: the full suite needs `tests/test_skillgen_input_path_injection.py` to install `graphifyy` through `uv`, so it hangs without network. The step-1 script tries `uv tool run` / `uv tool install` before it ever reads the `graphify` shebang. With `graphify` on PATH and an offline `uv` that fails fast, that file's 30 tests pass in 8s.

Not tested: Windows. The change is a `print` of integers.

title: fix: resolve XAML codebehind independently of directory order
body:
## What does this PR do?

`_xaml_codebehind_path` resolves a XAML file's codebehind. When the exact
`<name>.xaml.cs` is absent it falls back to scanning siblings for a
case-insensitive match:

```python
for sibling in path.parent.iterdir():
    if sibling.name.casefold() == expected.name.casefold():
        return sibling
```

On a case-sensitive filesystem more than one sibling can match at once, for
example `App.xaml.cs` alongside `app.xaml.CS`. `iterdir()` yields them in
filesystem order, so the function returned whichever came first:

```
iterdir order ['app.xaml.cs', 'App.xaml.CS'] -> app.xaml.cs
iterdir order ['App.xaml.CS', 'app.xaml.cs'] -> App.xaml.CS
```

The resolved file is handed to `extract_csharp`, so the symbols and edges taken
from it, and the node ids built on them, changed with directory layout rather
than with the inputs.

The fix sorts the siblings before matching, keyed on `p.name`.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant is the one in CONTRIBUTING: AST extraction, symbol identity and
traversal order must not depend on filesystem ordering. This path depended on it.

The sort key is load-bearing and not cosmetic. `WindowsPath` comparison is
case-insensitive, so a bare `sorted(path.parent.iterdir())` leaves `App.xaml.CS`
and `app.xaml.cs` comparing equal, and Python's stable sort then hands back the
original filesystem order. That version looks correct and fixes nothing on
Windows; I had it that way first and the regression test caught it. Sorting on
the name string compares case-sensitively on every platform.

No persisted or generated state is invalidated: the change only affects which of
two case-variant files is chosen, and only where both exist.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Limitations: this only orders the ambiguous case deterministically, it does not
decide which casing is "right", because nothing in the inputs says. The other two
unsorted `iterdir()` call sites I checked, `detect._auto_follow_symlinks` and the
project-extension probe in `extract.py`, both feed `any()`, so order cannot change
their result; left alone to keep this narrow.

## How was this tested?

```text
$ uv run pytest tests/test_dotnet.py -q
47 passed

$ uv run ruff check graphify/extract.py tests/test_dotnet.py
All checks passed!

# the regression test demonstrates the old failure, not just the new code:
$ git stash push -- graphify/extract.py
$ uv run pytest tests/test_dotnet.py -k order -q
E   AssertionError: codebehind resolution changed with directory order: ['app.xaml.cs', 'App.xaml.CS']
E   assert 'app.xaml.cs' == 'App.xaml.CS'
1 failed

# full suite, same checkout, before and after this change:
$ uv run pytest tests/ -q
17 failed, 8586 passed, 138 skipped, 1 xfailed
```

The test patches `iterdir` to return a fixed order rather than creating
case-variant files on disk, so it runs identically on a case-insensitive
filesystem where those two files cannot coexist. It asserts on `got.name` rather
than on the `Path` for the same reason the fix uses `key=p.name`: comparing
`Path` objects would pass on Windows even when the two orders resolved to
different files.

Environment: Windows 11, Python 3.13, `uv sync --all-extras`. This change moves
`tests/test_dotnet.py` from 46 to 47 passing and touches nothing else. The 17
failures in the full run are pre-existing on this platform and unrelated to this
change; happy to open a separate issue for them if they are not already known.

No skill fragments were touched, so there was nothing to regenerate. AI authorship

title: perf(update): skip extraction when no relevant inputs changed (#4740)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4740. `graphify update` had exactly one no-change exit, and it sat at the far end of the pipeline: detect → extract → build → cluster → compare topology. A run where nothing changed still paid for all of it. On this repo that is 36 s and 1.0 GB of RSS.

This moves the decision to the front, before extraction. `detect()` is not moved or duplicated; the gate classifies the result `_rebuild_code` already computed.

```diff
 _rebuild_code(watch_path, ...)
   detect(watch_path)
   code_files = detected["files"]["code"]
+  if changed_paths is None and not force:
+    if _inputs_unchanged(...) and _build_state_matches(...):
+      print("No relevant changes; graphify-out left untouched.")
+      return True
   extract(...)
   build_from_json(...)
   cluster(...)
-  compare topology   <- was the only no-change exit
```

The work is in the skip key. A skip is sound only if the key covers every input that reaches the graph, and the failure modes are asymmetric: a wrong "changed" costs time, a wrong "unchanged" ships a stale graph. So the key is:

```text
scanned files      every detected bucket, compared by content (ast_hash), not mtime
                   (detect_incremental's existing loop, shared)
in-scope path set  digest of the scanned paths plus the resolution inputs
                   (catches adds, deletes, renames and ignore-rule edits)
resolution inputs  tsconfig*/jsconfig/package.json, already ordinary scan input,
                   and package-lock/yarn.lock/pnpm-lock, which detect() skips by
                   name and now records separately so they can be stamped
extractor          v{version}-s{schema}-g{grammar}, the AST cache namespace
                   (a graph an older extractor wrote is not one this one wrote)
build config       scan root, follow_symlinks, no_cluster, gitignore, --exclude,
                   .graphifyrc digest
output shape       GRAPHIFY_VIZ_NODE_LIMIT, GRAPHIFY_AMBIGUOUS_SCALE
outputs            graph.json size + mtime_ns, graph.html presence, .graph.html.stale
was full           the last rebuild passed changed_paths=None
```

Most of that list is not theoretical. The first full-suite run failed 11 existing tests, and every one was a second rebuild on an unchanged tree that still had work to do: healing a graph an older version wrote, honouring a `.gitignore` eviction the incremental path deliberately skips (#2495), a subdir invocation after a root one, a pending HTML re-render. I grew the key until each passed again. No existing test was changed.

```diff
 graphify/detect.py
~  detect_incremental's classify loop -> classify_manifest_files(file_buckets, manifest, *, kind, unstamped_is_changed=True)
+  called from detect_incremental (behaviour unchanged) and from the gate
+  detect() records the resolution inputs it skips by name in detected["resolution_inputs"]
 graphify/watch.py
+  _inputs_unchanged, _scan_digest, _extractor_epoch, _current_build_state
+  _graph_json_is_complete, _write_build_state, _build_state_matches
+  graphify-out/.graphify_build_state.json
+  _ast_manifest_files() stamps a resolution_inputs bucket
 tests/test_update_no_change_gate.py
+  new, 19 tests
```

### The stamp only describes outputs that are fully on disk

A stamp is a promise that the next run may skip, so it is only allowed to exist when the outputs it names are complete. `_write_build_state` used to read graph.json's size and mtime from `stat()` without looking at the bytes. The atomic replace exists so a crash mid-write cannot leave a truncated graph.json (#2689), but its non-atomic fallback can land part of the bytes and report success. Forcing that:

```text
run2 returned True
graph.json now 40 bytes; parses: False (Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 38)
stamp records size=40 | on disk 40 | match=True
_build_state_matches says: True
run3 skipped: True              <- truncated graph served forever
```

The writer now refuses to stamp unless graph.json is a whole JSON object and no `.graph.html.stale` marker is pending. Both refusals fail closed, so the next run takes the full path and reports the problem instead of skipping over it:

```text
stamp records size=1246 | on disk 40 | match=False
_build_state_matches says: False
run3 skipped: False
```

Before finding that, I tried the failure points a reviewer would expect, each with a topology-changing edit so the run had real work: `cluster`, the graph publish, the report write, `save_manifest`, and the HTML reconcile. None of them produced a skip on the next run, and the graph was never stale. Every stamp site is already the last statement before its `return True`, so anything written afterwards would only cause a mismatch. The `--no-cluster` `same_graph` case is safe for the same reason: graph.json is not rewritten, and the stamp stats it at stamp time, so the recorded size and mtime always describe what is on disk.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (performance; the report is a cost bug)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A skip happens only when the key covers every input that reaches the graph, and a stamp exists only when the outputs it names are complete. Anything that cannot be proven takes the full path.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. One new JSON file under `graphify-out/` and a set of comparisons. No graph schema, cache-key or file-format change, and deleting the stamp reverts behaviour to a full run.

**Blast Radius:** moderate, because the gate decides whether a rebuild happens at all:

- A missing, unreadable or mismatched stamp falls back to the full path, so the worst case is the old cost rather than a wrong graph.
- `detect()` gains a `resolution_inputs` key and the manifest a matching bucket, so lock files are hashed on every rebuild. That is the cost this PR adds, bounded by how many lock files the corpus has.
- `classify_manifest_files()` defaults to the old `detect_incremental` semantics: a row-less or blank-hash file still re-queues on the incremental path, and only the gate treats it as unchanged.
- An explicit `changed_paths` and `--force` both bypass the gate.
- `_write_build_state` can now decline to write. A declined stamp is not an error; the next run simply rebuilds.

**Limitations**

- A **copied** `graphify-out` does not skip. The stamp is a new file, so a checkout that copies `graph.json`/`manifest.json`/`cache/` (the issue's runs 1–3) has no stamp and takes the full path. The steady-state rerun is what this makes cheap, which is why it only partly addresses #4740. The incremental patch path is a later PR.
- A source whose extraction previously failed, and whose content is then fixed with no other change, is picked up on the next rebuild instead of by the gate. Its row is blanked by design (#2543), and closing that needs a per-file stamp of unstamped sources.
- The completeness check reads the first and last non-whitespace byte of graph.json rather than parsing it. A full `json.load` would answer more, but the cap is 512 MiB and the rebuild is still holding its own copy of the graph, so a second parse can add about a gigabyte of peak RSS. Mid-file corruption moves mtime, which the stat comparison already catches.
- A retained `.graph.html.stale` marker means the `--no-cluster` path cannot stamp, since that path never touches HTML. It takes the full path until a clustered run consumes the marker.
- A new input that affects the output (another env knob, another resolution file) means extending `_current_build_state()`. Nothing enforces that.
- Hooks and the watcher go through the same gate.

## How was this tested?

`tests/test_update_no_change_gate.py` drives the real `_rebuild_code` and spies on `extract()`. It covers the unchanged tree, a new file, a deleted file, an edited `tsconfig.json`, an edited `package.json`, an edited lock file, an mtime bump with identical bytes, an explicit `changed_paths`, `--force`, a missing manifest, a scanned file with no manifest row, the scan digest, a rebuild that fails at each of three write points, a partially published graph.json, and both writer refusals.

Against pristine v8 (`92741d16`) the whole file gives **8 failed, 11 passed**. The 11 that pass include every "the full path is still taken" guard, so they are the proof this PR did not change existing behaviour. The 8 failures are the skip itself, the two digest and row-tolerance tests, and the three stamp refusals.

Against the pre-hardening stamp (`79c812d0`), the 6 tests added for it give **3 failed, 3 passed**. The 3 failures are its contracts: a partial publish, a truncated graph, a pending marker. The 3 `never_finishes` cases pass either way; they pin the ordering so a later refactor cannot move a stamp in front of a write.

```text
tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_progress_final_line_uses_consistent_denominator
                                                                 -> 1 passed
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/ tests/test_update_no_change_gate.py
                                                                 -> All checks passed
.venv/bin/python -m pyright graphify/watch.py graphify/detect.py  -> 29 errors, 3 warnings
   identical to the pre-change count on the same two files; no new errors
```

Wall time and peak RSS for `graphify update .` on this repo, 605 tracked code files and a 22.8k node / 47.7k edge graph, with the tree untouched between runs:

| run | wall | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| before, no change | 36.1 s | 1,007,716 KB |
| after, no change | 1.4–2.1 s | 53,260 KB |
| after, `--force` | 37.7 s | 1,008,724 KB |

It drives the real watcher through a monkeypatched `time.sleep`, so it is timing-sensitive.

title: graphify update silently skips .md files classified as paper (no option to disable)
body:
### Summary

A Markdown file whose first 3,000 characters match 3 of the 13 `_PAPER_SIGNALS` (e.g. an arXiv ID, the word "arxiv" and an "Abstract" heading) is classified as `paper`. `graphify update` (AST-only rebuild) re-extracts only the `code` bucket and AST-extractable `document` files, so such a `.md` gets **zero nodes** — while a similar `.md` without those signals gets its headings extracted. Nothing warns about it, and there is no setting or env var to opt out of paper classification for `.md`.

In our knowledge-base repo this silently dropped 6 Markdown notes (summaries/full texts of arXiv papers) from the graph, so `graphify query` could not reach them.

### Reproduce (0.9.95, also 0.9.68)

    mkdir repro && cd repro
    printf '# Notes on a paper\n\narXiv 2501.00001\n\n## Abstract\n\nWe study X.\n' > paper_notes.md
    printf '# Plain notes\n\n## Section\n\nSome text.\n' > plain_notes.md
    PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python -m graphify update .

Result (`graph.json` nodes by `source_file`): `plain_notes.md` 3, `paper_notes.md` 0. Exit code 0; the only hint is the generic "For doc/paper/image changes run /graphify --update in your AI assistant."

### Where (0.9.95)

- `detect.py:260-275` `_PAPER_SIGNALS` / `_PAPER_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD = 3`, `:324` `_looks_like_paper`, `:565` the `.md` → `PAPER` branch in `classify_file`
- `watch.py:1796` (`code`) and `:1830` (`document`) — the only buckets `_rebuild_code` reads

### Expected

Any of these would fix it for us (in order of preference):

1. Keep the AST quick-scan for `.md`/`.txt` files even when they are classified as `paper` (the Markdown extractor works fine on them).
2. A config/env option to disable paper classification for text documents.
3. At minimum, a warning listing files skipped by the AST-only update because they were classified as `paper`.

### Workaround we use

A launcher that replaces `graphify.detect._looks_like_paper` with a function returning `False` for `.md`, then calls `graphify.__main__.main()` (requires `PYTHONHASHSEED` to be set, otherwise `_pin_hash_seed_if_needed` re-execs and the patch is lost). It works on 0.9.68 and 0.9.95 but depends on private names.

title: fix(watch): quick-scan Markdown that detect() classifies as a paper (#4750)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4750 with the reporter's preferred option (1): documents that `detect()` classifies as `paper` and that have an AST extractor (`.md`, `.mdx`, `.qmd` today) now get the same quick-scan as other documents in the AST-only rebuild.

`classify_file` reclassifies a text document as `paper` when its first 3,000 characters match `_PAPER_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD` of the `_PAPER_SIGNALS` (an arXiv id, "arxiv" and an "Abstract" heading are enough). `_rebuild_code`, the path behind `graphify update` and the git hooks, reads only the `code` and `document` buckets. So those notes got zero nodes, with no warning, while a near-identical file kept its heading structure.

The change feeds `detected['files']['paper']` through the same `_get_extractor` filter that `document` files already go through:

- **Markdown papers** (`.md`, `.mdx`, `.qmd`) have an AST extractor and are quick-scanned.
- **Formats without an AST extractor** (`.pdf`, and also plain `.txt`/`.rst`) stay out, exactly as before. A paper-classified `.txt` still gets zero nodes on `update`, as on `v8`; giving `.txt` an extractor is out of scope here.
- **Paper docs with a semantic layer** are still excluded from the quick-scan by the existing #1915 gate, whose node `file_type` set already includes `paper`. So a full `/graphify` build that extracted the paper semantically is not double-represented.

title: fix(llm): don't report a failed chunk's files as model omissions (#3616)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3616. When a semantic chunk raises, `extract_corpus_parallel()` already prints `chunk N/M failed: …` and counts it in `failed_chunks`. The #1890 dispatch/return reconciliation then explained every uncovered file with one sentence: "The model returned a response but omitted them". For a chunk that raised (a provider error, a missing optional SDK) no response existed, so the last line contradicted the failure above it and sent the operator to debug model output instead of the actual error.

The change:

- records the files of every chunk that raises (`unit_path` of each item, so a `FileSlice` maps to its file), in both the serial and the thread-pool path;
- splits the uncovered set by cause:
  - files from failed chunks: "… produced no nodes and are absent from the graph: X. Their chunk failed before returning a response (see errors above); a re-run will retry them."
  - every other uncovered file keeps the existing omission wording, unchanged.
- leaves `merged["uncovered_files"]` as it was (both groups), so downstream consumers and re-dispatch behave exactly as before.

title: fix(zig): stop a call crossing between a method and a free function
fix(dedup): no id-collision warning for shared module nodes
body:
## What does this PR do?

Every Swift file that imports a module (`import Foundation`) mints the same module node id by design, and the extractors already exempt module and namespace nodes from collision disambiguation. `deduplicate_entities` still reported each such group as a lost-node ID collision, so a build printed one spurious `WARNING: node '...' is minted by two different files` for every extra importing file. That noise teaches users to ignore the real data-loss warning.

`_report_id_collision` now stays silent only when every node in the group is a `module` (or `namespace`) node of the same type under the same label. A module colliding with a namespace, with any other node type, or with a differently named module still warns.

Refs #4754

Found during the work on #4754 (it is Phase 5 of the RFC in that Swift PR), but independent of it: this PR does not depend on the Swift PR, and the Swift PR does not depend on this one.

title: fix(python): member-call pass binds only Python callers and targets
body:
## What does this PR do?

`_resolve_python_member_calls` folds labels across the whole corpus, so in a mixed corpus it binds member calls across languages:

- a Swift `Inner.go()` binds a Python class `Inner`;
- a Python `Inner.go()` binds a Swift `Inner`;
- a Python `SwiftArray.make()` binds a Swift node labelled `Swift.Array`, because the label key drops the dot;
- a Swift class with the same name as a Python class counts as a second definition in the single-definition guard, so a correct Python-to-Python member call binds nothing.

The fix: the pass skips callers and targets whose effective suffix (`.graphifyrc` language overrides honoured) belongs to another extractor, and counts only Python classes for the single-definition guard. Unknown suffixes and raw calls that name no file still pass, as before. Other languages bind their member calls in their own passes.

Extensionless files (shebang scripts) are decided by their shebang, in a second commit (`fix(python): keep extensionless non-Python scripts out of the member-call pass`): a script whose interpreter maps to another extractor (`#!/usr/bin/env node`, `ruby`, `bash`) is not Python, a `python` shebang is Python, and a file with no shebang or an interpreter no extractor claims stays unknown and passes. The shebang is read from the path given to `extract()` or from the scan root for unchanged context files, never relative to the working directory, and kept in a map for the pass only (context nodes are not changed). The Python pass also runs when the only changed file is an extensionless script.

Found during the Swift cross-file work (#4754), but independent of it: this PR does not depend on the Swift PR, and the Swift PR does not depend on this one.

Invariant: no member-call edge between language families from the Python pass, and a definition in another language does not change what the Python pass binds. The change only removes wrong edges or restores Python-to-Python ones; it touches no cache or persisted state, so no schema bump.
