title: feat(swift): resolve type references across files through a Swift type index
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4574
Fixes #4575
Fixes #4754

**Problem.** In a Swift corpus many type references never reach the declaration of the type they name. Swift has no per-type imports inside a module, so every cross-file type name starts as a sourceless stub that the label-based passes have to repair, and several ordinary patterns defeat them:

- a type declared next to its own same-file `extension` and also extended in another file (#4754, case 1);
- an extension of a type declared outside the corpus (`extension View`, `private extension String`) that absorbs every same-named reference (#4574);
- qualified nested paths (`Catalog.Item.ID`) cut to their first segment (#4754, case 2), and same-named nested types under different parents collapsing into one node (#4575);
- cross-file constructor calls `Widget(...)` dropped because a Swift file never imports a type from its own module (#4754, case 3).

The root causes (RC1-RC5), the design and the decisions are in `docs/swift-cross-file-type-resolution-rfc.md`, added by this PR.

**Approach.** Deterministic, fail-closed Swift name lookup, in the RFC's phases. Phases 1-4 depend on each other (the RFC explains why Phase 3 cannot ship without Phases 2 and 4), so they are one PR.

- **Phase 1, real declarations (#4574, #4754 case 1).** `swift_extensions[]` records carry `declared`, and a node built only from `extension` blocks carries `_swift_extension_only`. Such a node is never a canonical merge or rewire target; the real declaration is, even when it has a same-file extension. `graphify update` keeps the marker on context nodes (`cli.py`, `watch.py`).
- **Phase 2, Swift type index and lexical lookup (#4754 case 2).** Swift type nodes carry `_swift_qualified` paths, reference edges carry `_swift_scope`, and `swift_type_table` gains `scopes`. A new `_resolve_swift_type_references` pass binds a reference by its written path (`Catalog.Item.ID` stays dotted) through `_swift_type_index` / `_swift_lookup`, before the bare-label rewire: the innermost scope that declares the name wins, two candidates at that level are ambiguous and bind nothing, and a name declared nowhere keeps its dotted stub label. Extension targets resolve through the same lookup.
- **Phase 3, nested type identity (#4575).** A nested type gets an id under its enclosing type, so `A.State` and `B.State` (or two `CodingKeys`) in one file stay two nodes. The id is salted only on a collision with a member of the same slug.
- **Phase 4, constructor calls (#4754 case 3).** `Widget(...)` binds as an `INFERRED` `calls` edge with `context="constructor"` when the lexical lookup finds exactly one type. A same-file constructor call to a nested type, or to a label shared by several Swift types in the file, goes through the same pass. `serve.py`: the "callers of X" question keeps `context="constructor"` edges, otherwise these edges would be invisible to it.
- **Member calls.** `x.go()` binds through a per-file receiver table that records each name's type and enclosing scope. When two writes of one name in a file disagree on type or scope, the name binds nothing and is not parked for cross-repo resolution.

Wrong bindings fixed on the way, each with a regression test:

- A dotted label such as `Item.ID` resolves only through the Swift lookup; it no longer binds a concatenated `ItemID` through the member-call fallback or the stub rewire.
- An extension of the sugar forms `[T]`, `[K: V]`, `T?` extends `Swift.Array` / `Swift.Dictionary` / `Swift.Optional` instead of folding onto `T`.
- A member call whose receiver type is an extension-only node emits no type-only `references` edge to it when the method is not defined in the extension.
- The Swift member-call pass handles only Swift callers (by effective suffix, so a `.graphifyrc` override counts) and binds only `.swift` / `.m` / `.mm` / `.h` targets.

Fixed after review (the first three in commits `fix(swift): dotted refs to nested types, ObjC-owned callers, extension-only ctor targets` and `fix(swift): resolve same-file dotted type names by lexical lookup`; the others name their commit), each with a regression test:

- A dotted reference such as `Action.Delegate` slugged to the id of a same-file `case delegate` (ids are caseless; the case keeps the plain id and the nested type is salted), so it pointed at the enum case; and a same-file shortcut by absolute path ignored lexical scope, so `Model.Item` written inside `Outer` could bind a top-level `Model.Item` instead of `Outer.Model.Item`. A dotted Swift name no longer takes the same-file id shortcut: it stays a stub and the Phase 2 lookup binds it with the reference's scope (`test_dotted_reference_reaches_nested_type_not_same_slug_enum_case`, `test_dotted_reference_uses_lexical_scope_over_same_named_top_level`, both declaration orders).
- A Swift extension of an Objective-C class folds onto the Objective-C node, which has no Swift path, so `Item()` inside that extension lost the constructor edge v8 has. A non-Swift owner now gives file scope (`test_constructor_call_in_extension_of_objc_class_binds`).
- The generic constructor fallback still accepted an extension-only node, so `External()` of a library type bound to `extension External` (as on v8). Swift calls now drop such candidates (`test_constructor_call_does_not_bind_extension_only_node`).
- `fix(swift): do not bind Swift calls to C/C++ declarations in .h headers`: the member-call target gate admitted every `.h` target, so `Inner.go()` could bind a C++ `Inner::go` declared in a header, and a missing method fell back to a type-only `references` edge to the C++ class. A `.h` target now binds only when it is an Objective-C method (its label carries the `-` / `+` sigil) or a type that owns one (`test_swift_type_call_does_not_bind_cpp_class_method_in_h`, `test_swift_call_to_cpp_class_emits_no_reference_in_h`, `test_swift_instance_call_still_binds_objc_instance_method_in_h`).
- `fix(swift): honour language overrides in Swift suffix checks`: six checks (the constructor branch, its extension-only candidate filter, the dotted-stub guard, the Swift type index, the type-reference source set and the type-reference file selection) tested the raw file name, so a file remapped to Swift in `.graphifyrc` lost or gained edges, and a corpus of `.SWIFT` files skipped the type-reference pass. One helper now decides by the effective suffix, ignoring case (`test_constructor_in_language_override_file_binds_lexical_type`, `test_uppercase_swift_suffix_corpus_binds_type_reference`).
- `fix(swift): keep nested type ids distinct from same-file top-level declarations`: a nested type's id joins its parent's id and its name, so `Outer.State` and a file-level `Outer_State` or `outer_state()` minted one id and the second node was dropped. A nested type now yields that id to any member or function and to any type of the same or a shallower depth, and is salted, independent of declaration order (`test_nested_type_does_not_swallow_toplevel_underscore_type`, `test_nested_type_does_not_swallow_toplevel_function`).
- `fix(swift): bind nothing for receivers whose written type is unproven`: a receiver typed with a name that something else in the file shadows (a `typealias`, an `associatedtype`, a generic parameter or pack, a type declared inside a function body, a `Self.`-qualified path, a generic-constrained prefix or a generic argument) bound the call to a same-named type elsewhere. Such a write now makes the name bind nothing in that file, for properties (every name of a multi-binding declaration), parameters, typed locals, typed closure parameters, file-scope bindings and initializers or factories called through such a type, also when the binding is annotated; nothing is parked, and `var x: A; x.go()` still binds `A.go` (`tests/test_swift_receiver_fail_closed.py`).

Three commits change no behaviour. `refactor(swift): tidy the new Swift resolution helpers` removes duplication in the new helpers (one shared navigation-path walk, one shared relation set, one redundant check dropped), and `docs(swift): use generic examples in the RFC and fixtures` only renames examples in the RFC, test fixtures and comments. The third, `refactor(swift): split Swift call binding out of walk() for pyright`, only moves the new Swift branches of `_extract_generic`'s `walk()` into small nested helpers, with no behaviour change: they had pushed `walk()` past pyright's complexity limit, so pyright stopped checking the whole function.

**Cache and upgrade.** `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes from 25 to 26, once for all phases, because per-file Swift output changes. The first build after the upgrade re-extracts every file. Nested Swift types get new ids, so saved queries and `--seed` ids that name a nested Swift type have to be updated. On a large Swift corpus the dedup shrink guard may refuse the first graph if it is smaller than the old one; `--allow-dedup-shrink` lets it through.

**Related PRs and issues.**

- #4600 also targets #4574. This PR uses a different marker: only a node built purely from extensions is marked, so a declaration with its own same-file extension stays a merge target (the #4754 case 1 layout). If this PR is accepted, it supersedes #4600.
- #4599 also targets #4575 with a similar parent-qualified id for nested types. This PR overlaps with it on nested type identity and adds the lookup that resolves `Outer.Inner` written in another file; if this PR is accepted, it supersedes #4599.
- #4639 adds file-scope `typealias` nodes. It is complementary and not included here; both change the Swift extractor, so whichever lands second may need a rebase.

**Split out.** Two small fixes found during this work are separate PRs and do not depend on this one or on each other: #4756 (no dedup collision warning for shared module nodes, RFC Phase 5) and #4757 (the Python member-call pass binds only Python callers and targets).

## Notes for maintainers

- This PR bumps `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 25 -> 26 because it changes per-file Swift output; feel free to adjust the number or fold it into your release bump.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariants: extraction stays deterministic (no ambient state, no file reads in the resolvers); ambiguity binds nothing instead of guessing (fail-closed); no binding across language families; a sourceless stub never wins over a sourced declaration; an extension of a type outside the corpus is never treated as its declaration. Persisted state this invalidates: the AST cache (schema bump) and any saved id of a nested Swift type.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary (Phases 1-4 depend on each other; see the RFC).
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

## How was this tested?

New test files: `tests/test_swift_type_index.py`, `test_swift_type_resolution.py`, `test_swift_nested_constructor_calls.py`, `test_swift_member_call_scopes.py`, `test_swift_member_call_target_gate.py`, `test_swift_extension_only_member_calls.py`, `test_swift_sugar_extensions.py`, `test_swift_dotted_label_key.py`, `test_swift_language_override.py`, `test_swift_nested_id_collision.py`; additions to `test_swift_cross_file_calls.py` and `test_serve.py`.

On this branch at its current head (rebased on v8 `92741d16`):

```text
uv sync --all-extras
uv run pytest tests                  # 8885 passed, 16 skipped, 1 xfailed
uv run ruff check .                  # All checks passed!   (v8: All checks passed!)
uv run pyright                       # 656 errors   (v8: 657)
```

Pyright: the error sets compared by file and message (line stripped) show 0 new errors.

Regression tests fail on v8: the new and changed test files copied into a v8 `92741d16` checkout and run against v8 code give 55 failed and 1 collection error in the Swift and serve files (the same run also held the test files of the two split-out PRs, which account for its other 6 failures; 216 tests passed in total). The failures include `test_extension_of_outside_type_does_not_absorb_references` (#4574), `test_same_file_nested_types_get_distinct_ids` (#4575), `test_declaration_with_same_file_extension_absorbs_cross_file_extension` (#4754 case 1), `test_cross_file_constructor_call_emits_inferred_call` (#4754 case 3) and `test_callers_question_keeps_constructor_call_edges` (serve). `test_swift_type_index.py` cannot be collected on v8 because it imports `_swift_type_index` / `_swift_lookup`. The 216 that pass are the controls.

Real-project check: a SwiftUI app with several hundred Swift files, built with `graphify extract <app> --code-only`, `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none`, no API keys set. These numbers were measured on an earlier revision of this change set, before the rebase onto `92741d16`, against v8 `c588b72d` (0.9.94). Since that measurement the branch changed only by the rebase, the `walk()` refactor above (no behaviour change), the removal of the Python-pass change that now ships as #4757, and the review fixes above; the real-app check was not rerun after those fixes.

| metric | before (`c588b72d`) | after |
|---|---|---|
| one struct referenced from many other files: `affected <declaration id>`, depth 1, other files / uses | 0 / 0 | 30 / 127 |
| the same struct: `affected "<name>"` (label) | `No unique node match` | 427 hits in 36 files |
| references left on a stub although the corpus has exactly one declaration of that name | 600 | 66 |
| `INFERRED` constructor `calls` | 0 | 3705 (0 to a stub) |
| dotted label collapsed onto a concatenated name (`Item.ID` -> `ItemID`) | 0 | 0 |
| cross-language `calls` / `references` | 0 | 0 |
| `EXTRACTED` `calls` | 10065 | 9859 |

The total of Swift references that end on a stub rises (4836 -> 7040). That is by design: references to an extension-only type (`View`, `NSEvent`) no longer bind to the extension (#4574), and dotted names stay dotted stubs instead of binding a lookalike.

The drop in `EXTRACTED` `calls` was checked per call site (caller, file, line, callee name), not by node id, since nested types now get parent-qualified ids. Of the 370 call sites that lost an `EXTRACTED` `calls` edge, 314 still have an edge to the same target: 248 are in-file constructor calls of nested types that are now recorded as `INFERRED`, and 66 collapsed into an existing `references` edge on the same node pair, since the graph keeps one edge per pair. Another 26 were wrong bindings that are now gone (self-recursion through a receiver of a different type, a receiver of an external type bound to a same-named local method, and one call bound to an extension-only node that now binds to the real type). The remaining 30 are real losses, listed under limitations: 21 member calls whose receiver is written several times in the same file, 6 qualified nested-type constructors `Outer.Inner(...)`, and 3 self-loops from a type's static property calling its own initializer. On the other side, 164 `EXTRACTED` calls were added, 142 of them cross-file `Type.member(...)` calls whose receiver type was checked to match the target's owner.

## Known limitations / unsupported cases

- A receiver name written more than once in one file with a different type or in a different scope binds nothing (fail-closed), even when both writes name the same type in two enclosing types or spell it `Outer.T` and `T`. 21 correct same-file member calls on the app above are lost this way. A narrower rule is follow-up work.
- A qualified nested-type constructor call `Outer.Inner(...)` reaches only `Outer` (a `references` edge) or nothing; the `calls` edge to `Inner` is not emitted (6 calls on the app above, plus 3 self-loop initializer calls).
- An Objective-C class in a `.h` header that owns no Objective-C method (for example an `@interface` that declares only properties) is no longer a target of a Swift type-only `references` edge, since the gate cannot tell it from a C or C++ type (accepted loss of the `.h` fix above).
- A method declared only on a superclass or protocol is not found by the member-call resolver (no inheritance walk); the call gets a type-only `references` edge.
- The receiver table is flat per file: a name written once binds by that write's type label, without flow analysis.
- The receiver check does not yet see `if let` / `guard let` / `for` bindings with a type annotation or tuple patterns (`let (x, y): (State, Int)`), and a local bound by a resolvable factory can still shadow a typed parameter of the same name, so such a receiver can bind to a same-named type elsewhere, as on v8 (follow-up).
- The same receiver check does not yet follow generic constructors (`let x = Box<Int>()` through `typealias Box<T> = Other<T>`), wrapped initializers (`try Box.make()`, `(Box.make())`) or nested factory paths, and sees only shadowing declarations in the current file (a `typealias` declared in a type in another file, used from an extension of that type), so these receivers can still bind to a same-named type, as before this change (follow-up).
- The fail-closed receiver rule is file-wide: one unproven write of a name drops that name's member calls in the whole file, including correct ones in other functions.
- A dotted receiver path is shortened to its first segment when the corpus has any type table, so `Outer.Inner.go()` binds `Outer.go`, as on v8 (follow-up).
- An extension written before its declaration in the same file (`extension Outer.State` above `struct Outer`) creates the node with the dotted label, so `State()` binds a top-level `State`, as on v8 (follow-up).
- A static factory is chosen by bare label, so a nested factory that shadows a same-named top-level one binds `make()` but not the member call on its result (fail-closed; follow-up: choose the factory by lexical lookup).
- In one file, a typed member call can still bind by bare label in the extractor before the scoped resolver runs, as on v8 (follow-up).
- A same-file dotted reference to a type that exists only as an extension (no declaration in the corpus) stays on its stub (fail-closed).
- tree-sitter-swift parse errors that swallow a declaration (#3542) are not addressed.
- An incremental re-extraction (the watch and post-commit hook paths) does not re-resolve references in unchanged files when a declaration changes elsewhere (pre-existing, all languages).
- The corpus is treated as one Swift module; per-target scoping (SwiftPM / Xcode targets) is an open question in the RFC.
- Out of scope: nested receivers (`a.b.go()`), protocol-extension default implementations and conditional conformances.

title: docs(contributors): graph who has worked on each core area, with a title per contributor
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `docs/CONTRIBUTORS.md`, generated by `python -m tools.contributors` from the git history:

- a graph joining each core contributor to the core areas they have commits in, with commit counts;
- a table giving each one a title: the area of their first core commit. The author of the repository's first commit is its Creator.

The areas follow the pipeline in CONTRIBUTING.md (detect → extract → build → cluster → analyze → report → export), plus cache and updates, the MCP server, security, agent skills, and the CLI and install. Which files belong to which area is one table at the top of `tools/contributors.py`. A core contributor has at least 10 commits that change `graphify/` or `tools/skillgen/`; tests, docs and release files are not counted.

People who commit with several emails are counted once. `tools/contributors.mailmap` maps 87 emails to 79 GitHub logins, each taken from the account GitHub's commits API attributes those commits to. Only this tool reads it: there is no root `.mailmap`, so `git shortlog` and blame are unchanged. The 4 emails GitHub does not link to an account are left as they are.

## Type of change

- [x] Documentation

- The tool reads only the local git history: no network, no environment. The same commit renders the same file, and the tests check that.
- Nothing ships in the wheel; it is a build-time tool like `tools.skillgen`.
- Limits: titles come from which files a commit changed, not from judging the work. The page is a snapshot, regenerated with one command; it is not wired into CI. The thresholds are constants at the top of the tool, if you want different ones.

title: feat(query): read project budget and depth defaults
body:
## What does this PR do?

Projects can set `query_budget` and `query_depth` in `.graphifyrc`, so repeated queries can use the same defaults. Explicit CLI options override each setting independently; projects without settings keep budget 2000 and depth 2. Both `--depth N` and `--depth=N` accept 1 through 6. Existing explicit budget values, including zero and negative numbers, retain their behavior.

Configuration belongs to the selected graph's project, including when `--graph` points outside the working directory. Invalid project configuration produces one warning and falls back to built-in defaults while retaining explicit options. Execution and query logging use the same resolved values.

title: fix: size the ollama context properly for other languages and the real instructions
body:
Follow up to #4414, picking up @nothariharan's review.

## What this fixes

Now that the context size actually reaches Ollama, how graphify works it out matters. Two parts were off:

- it guessed 4 characters per token, which is fine for English and code but way off for other languages. With qwen2.5, Chinese text came out 2.8x bigger than the guess and Hindi 3.7x. So a Chinese doc got too small a context and Ollama cut it.
- it kept 400 tokens for graphify's own instructions, but they're really about 760.

## What changed

- characters from other scripts (Chinese, Hindi, Russian, Arabic and so on) now count as a token each. English, code and accented Latin text are worked out the same as before.
- graphify's instructions are now measured instead of assumed to be 400.
- added a test that runs against a real Ollama, only when you ask for it:
  `GRAPHIFY_TEST_OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen2.5:14b pytest tests/test_ollama_live.py`

## How I tested it

Real token counts from qwen2.5:14b vs the old and new guess:

| text | real | old guess | new guess |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chinese only | 3,440 | 1,244 | 4,552 |
| Hindi only | 5,555 | 1,500 | 5,100 |
| Chinese README | 4,463 | 3,000 | 4,200 |
| Japanese README | 4,738 | 3,000 | 4,780 |
| Russian README | 4,046 | 3,000 | 5,790 |
| Arabic README | 4,210 | 3,000 | 5,085 |
| English README | 3,540 | 3,000 | 3,060 |
| code | 3,387 | 3,000 | 3,004 |
| graphify's instructions | 755 | 400 | 828 |

Hindi still comes out a bit under, but the room kept for the reply covers that.

The real Ollama test sends a Chinese chunk through graphify and checks that the whole thing got to the model. On 0.9.95 with qwen2.5-coder:14b, Ollama cuts it at 8,192 of 12,338 tokens, with this change it gets all 12,338. The English one passes on both. It's slow, about 10 min per run on my Mac.

Tests:

- full test suite passes

## Not in this one

title: fix(skill): stop substituting the scan path into code and commands
body:
## Summary

The skill instructs the agent to substitute `INPUT_PATH` literally into Python
source code, e.g.:

```python
result = detect(Path('INPUT_PATH'))
```

A scan path containing a single quote breaks out of the string literal. A
directory named `x');__import__('os').system('...')#` - plausible via a cloned
repo - turns the pasted code into arbitrary Python execution on the user's
machine. The same applies to every other block that pastes `INPUT_PATH`
(`generate(...)`, `detect_incremental(...)`) and to the `--watch` command line,
where an unquoted `INPUT_PATH` would be interpreted by the shell.

## Fix

The path now never enters code or shell text at all.

Step 1 (and each independent entry-point flow - `add`, `--update`, `--watch`,
`--cluster-only`) instructs the agent to write the resolved absolute path to a
file named `.graphify_input_path` using its file-writing tool. The agent writes
the exact bytes; no quoting, escaping, or parsing ever touches the value, so
delimiter collisions and quoting bugs are impossible by construction.

Every Python block then reads it back:

```python
SCAN_ROOT = Path('.graphify_input_path').read_text().rstrip('\n')
result = detect(Path(SCAN_ROOT))
```

and the `--watch` command takes it as a quoted substitution from the file:

```bash
python3 -m graphify.watch "$(cat .graphify_input_path)" --debounce 3
```

Why a file rather than an environment variable: an env var exported in Step 1
is invisible to blocks running in separate shells, breaks on runtimes without
persistent shell state, and silently expands to an empty argument in the watch
command. A file at the working root survives across shells and sessions, and
each entry-point flow writes its own target path (`add` writes `./raw`
resolved to absolute before running `--update`; `--update`, `--watch`, and
`--cluster-only` instructions say to write their target first).

The `INPUT_PATH` placeholder is gone entirely - there is nothing left to
substitute anywhere.

## Files changed

- `graphify/skill.md` - Step 1 instruction added; Steps 2, 4, 5 and the
  `--update` block read `.graphify_input_path`; `--watch` reads it via `cat`;
  `add`, `--update`, `--watch`, and `--cluster-only` sections tell the agent
  to write their target path first
- `skills/graphify/skill.md` - identical changes (the two copies carry the
  same blocks)

Docs-only change; no package code touched.

## Test

Docs-only, but the mechanism was exercised end to end:

- A directory named `x');__import__('os').system('touch /tmp/pwn')#` written
  to `.graphify_input_path` is read back intact, `Path()` resolves it
  correctly, and no payload executes.
- A directory whose name contains an interior newline survives the same round
  trip - the case that would defeat any pasted-into-shell transport.
- `$(cat .graphify_input_path)` passes the path to argv as a single quoted
  argument.
- A block reading the file in a fresh shell works, confirming there is no
  cross-block environment dependency.

title: fix(skill): require consent before installing graphifyy, never touch system Python
body:
## Problem

Step 1 of `graphify/skill.md` ran:

```bash
python3 -c "import graphify" 2>/dev/null || pip install graphifyy -q --break-system-packages 2>&1 | tail -3
```

Two problems with this:

1. **No consent.** `graphifyy` is a third-party PyPI package. The skill installed it silently on first invocation, without asking the user or telling them their environment was about to change. A skill should not silently install third-party packages.

2. **`--break-system-packages` mutates system Python.** On PEP 668-managed systems (Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, and others) this flag exists specifically to override the protection that keeps `pip` out of the OS interpreter. Installing into system Python can break distro tooling that depends on it. The skill should never reach for it, even as a fallback.

## Fix

Step 1 now gates installation behind explicit user consent:

- If no interpreter can `import graphify`, the block prompts `graphifyy is not installed. Install/upgrade from PyPI now? (y/N)` on a TTY (bounded by a 120s timeout so a pty-backed agent shell can't hang) and installs only on `y`/`yes` — the answer is normalized for case and stray whitespace. Anything else, including timeout or empty input, aborts cleanly.
- In non-interactive sessions there is no one to confirm, so the block does not install. It prints the exact manual command and stops. The skill text also instructs the agent to ask the user in chat first, since agent shells typically run non-interactively; after a chat-consented install the agent re-runs the Step 1 block, which finds the new interpreter and writes `.graphify_python` before Step 2 can run.
- The only supported installers are `uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy` (preferred) and `pipx install --upgrade graphifyy` (`--upgrade` so a present-but-broken install heals rather than no-ops). If neither is available, the block prints instructions to install uv and stops — no pip fallback into the system interpreter, and `--break-system-packages` is gone entirely.
- Because `uv tool`/`pipx` installs live in their own venvs (system `python3` cannot import them), Step 1 now detects the interpreter that can actually import graphify: uv tool dir first (probing both `bin/python` and the Windows `Scripts/python.exe` layout), then the shebang of the `graphify` CLI on PATH, then a `python3` fallback. The resolved interpreter is written atomically to `.graphify_python`, and every later bash block calls `"$(x=$(cat .graphify_python 2>/dev/null); echo "${x:-python3}")"` instead of `python3`.

### Why the `python3` fallback matters

Several flows skip Step 1 entirely (`--cluster-only`, `query`, `path`, `explain`, `add`, `--update`, `--watch`), so `.graphify_python` may not exist — most importantly for graphs built by the previous version of this skill, whose system-python install means `python3` can still import graphify. The `${x:-python3}` fallback also covers an empty or truncated file, preserving the old behavior in every degraded case; quoting keeps interpreter paths containing spaces working.

`.graphify_python` holds a machine-specific absolute path, so the skill notes it should not be committed (suggest `.gitignore` next to `graphify-out/`).

## Files changed

- `graphify/skill.md` — Step 1 rewritten (consent gate + interpreter detection); all subsequent bash blocks switched from `python3` to the guarded `.graphify_python` expansion; `.gitignore`/Windows note added; MCP config note added for non-system interpreters.
- `skills/graphify/skill.md` — same changes (the repo ships two copies).

## Known limitations

- **Windows, partially covered:** uv-tool detection now probes both `bin/python` and `Scripts/python.exe`, before and after a consented install. A pipx install on Windows still resolves only via the `graphify` CLI shebang, which `.exe` launchers don't carry — that path can still dead-end. The surrounding skill is POSIX-bash throughout, so this PR adds probing plus a caveat rather than restructuring.
- **pipx installed but not on PATH:** detection finds pipx installs via the `graphify` CLI shebang; if the pipx bin dir is off PATH a working install is invisible and `pipx install --upgrade` re-runs it rather than locating the existing interpreter. The user can still run the printed manual path.

## Merge note

Sibling PR #4762 touches adjacent lines in the same Step 1 region; whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

## Verification

- All ```bash blocks extracted from both files pass `bash -n`.
- Pty-tested the gate: `yes ` and `Yes` (normalized) install; `n`, empty Enter, and a no-input timeout decline cleanly with exit 1; non-interactive abort prints the manual command.
- Stub-`uv` consented install end to end, including a `Scripts/python.exe` (Windows-layout) venv being detected and persisted.
- Simulated a standalone flow in a fresh directory with no `.graphify_python` and with an empty one: the call sites fall back to `python3` and run (previously exit 127 / `: command not found`).
- Interpreter path containing spaces (`/tmp/dir with space/python`) resolves correctly through the quoted expansion.
- `grep` confirms no `pip install graphifyy`, `--break-system-packages`, `uv tool run`, or unguarded installer invocation remains in either file.

title: fix: word the hook reminders as facts, not orders
body:
Fixes #2202.

## What this fixes

The graphify hook adds a reminder before searches and file reads. It was written as an order: "MANDATORY... You MUST run graphify", and the read one also said "include it in every subagent prompt". That shows up in the middle of the agent's tool output, so it looks just like a prompt injection. Agents in the issue flagged it as one and ignored it, which means the reminder did nothing.

## What changed

- the search and read reminders now just say what's there: the project has a graph, and `graphify query` / `explain` / `path` usually gets you the right files in far fewer tokens than grepping or reading files one by one
- dropped "include it in every subagent prompt". Subagents already get their own reminder from the per agent budget (#3435), so they don't need to pass it on
- strict mode still blocks the first read like before, I only took out the line asking to copy it into subagent prompts
- the stale reminder was already worded as a fact, so it's unchanged

New reminders, as the hook prints them:

> graphify: this project has a knowledge graph at graphify-out/graph.json. `graphify query "<question>"` returns the files and relations that matter for a question, usually in far fewer tokens than grepping raw files. Grep works best once the graph or an earlier read has pointed to the exact file and lines.

> graphify: this project has a knowledge graph at graphify-out/graph.json. `graphify query "<question>"` (scoped subgraph), `graphify explain "<concept>"` and `graphify path "<A>" "<B>"` show which files and lines matter — usually in far fewer tokens than reading source files one by one. Reading a file directly works best once the graph has pointed to the exact lines.

## How I tested it

- added tests that check the reminders, both as written and as the hook actually prints them, don't contain "MANDATORY", "MUST" or ask to be copied into subagent prompts. They fail on current `v8` and pass with this change
- the existing hook tests looked for the word "MANDATORY" to tell a reminder fired, so I switched them to a phrase that's in the new reminders
- all 621 hook tests pass
- full test suite: 8,423 passed. The 8 that fail (7 in `test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py`, 1 in `test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py`) fail the same way on `v8` without this change

## Heads up

- #3756 (reminder repeats on every call) looks already handled by #3435. I ran the hook 8 times in one session: reminders on the first 5, then silent, and with `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_NUDGE_CAP=1` only the first one. So it could probably be closed.
- the Cursor rule file `graphify install` writes still says "MANDATORY". I left it, since that's an instructions file the user installs, not text that shows up in tool output.

title: fix: save graphify extract token usage to cost.json
body:
Fixes #1769.

## What this fixes

`graphify-out/cost.json` is meant to be a running log of how many tokens each build used. Only the skill ever wrote to it. `graphify extract` printed the tokens for the run and then just dropped them, so if you refresh your graph with `extract` (on a schedule, say) the log stays stuck on the first build and you can't tell what refreshes cost you.

## What changed

- `graphify extract` now adds each run to `cost.json` the same way the skill does: date, input and output tokens, file count, plus the running totals
- works with and without `--no-cluster`, and honours `--out`
- an existing log from the skill is kept and added to
- a run that used no tokens (code only, nothing sent to a model) doesn't touch it
- if `cost.json` is broken and can't be read, it's left alone with a warning instead of being replaced with a fresh one-run log

## How I tested it

- ran it for real with Ollama (qwen2.5-coder:7b) on a small folder, changed a doc, ran it again. Before: `cost.json` never got written by `extract`. After: both runs are in it and the totals add up
- added `tests/test_extract_cost_ledger.py`. The three that check runs get added fail on current `v8` and pass with this change, the other two check a broken log and a no-token run are left alone
- full test suite: 8,422 passed. The 8 that fail (7 in `test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py`, 1 in `test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py`) fail the same way on `v8` without this change

## Not in this one

- a run that gets stopped by the shrink guard still spent tokens but isn't logged, since it exits before the tokens are printed. Happy to add that if you want it counted
- the issue also mentions `cluster-only` and labelling, I kept this one to `extract`

title: [Feature]: Bound directory entries with tree --max-children
body:
### Problem or use case

When generating a tree for a directory with many immediate files or subdirectories, `tree --max-children N` still includes every directory entry. The limit currently applies only to symbols beneath file nodes. This makes it difficult to keep a wide repository tree, or a merged tree containing many repositories, within a chosen breadth.

### Proposed solution

Apply the nonnegative limit to each directory's immediate entries, including the tree root and repository groups in merged trees. Keep the current ordering and show one `(+K more)` entry when children are omitted. Its label should count omitted immediate entries, while its total should include all descendant leaves behind them. Ancestor totals should continue to describe the complete tree.

Keep the existing limit and omission behavior for symbols beneath files. A zero limit should show only an omission entry for a nonempty directory; negative limits should be rejected consistently.

### Alternatives considered

A lower `--max-children` value currently reduces file symbols but does not reduce directory breadth. Generating separate trees for smaller roots can help, but loses the combined overview.

### Area

CLI or installation

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

This would change which entries are visible in `GRAPH_TREE.html`, while retaining complete totals and the existing tree data fields. It would not change graph node or edge IDs, `graph.json`, caches, incremental updates, generated skills, or MCP output.

### Additional context

This request is based on source inspection at `v8` commit `92741d162b2094ffc2fed58cfbd8ee823e9da62c`, rather than a measured performance problem. For example, a directory with `a.py`, `b.py`, and `c.py` still exposes all three entries with `--max-children 2`; the proposed result would retain two entries and show `(+1 more)`.

The producer is [`graphify/tree_html.py`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/92741d162b2094ffc2fed58cfbd8ee823e9da62c/graphify/tree_html.py). This request covers single and merged trees, including nested directories and untagged repository groups.

title: fix(js): keep nested functions scoped so same-named calls don't bind to them
body:
## What this fixes

Since #2653, a JS/TS function declared inside another function gets its own node, which is great. But it also went into the file-wide name lookup, so a call to that name from anywhere in the file could get linked to it, even from outside the function it lives in. Two ways this goes wrong:

- two functions that each have their own inner `run`: both get linked to the last one
- a function with an inner `helper` steals the callers of a top-level or imported `helper`

So the graph says things call functions they can't even see.

## How to recreate

```bash
mkdir repro && cd repro
cat > x.ts <<'EOF'
export function helper() { return 0; }
export function a() { function helper() { return 1; } return helper(); }
export function b() { return helper(); }
EOF
graphify extract . --code-only --no-cluster
python -c "import json; g=json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); [print(e['source'], e['relation'], e['target']) for e in g['edges'] if e['relation'] == 'calls']"
```

Before:

```
x_a calls x_a_helper
x_b calls x_a_helper
```

`b()` is linked to the `helper` hidden inside `a()`. After:

```
x_a calls x_a_helper
x_b calls x_helper
```

Same thing with two inner functions of the same name:

```ts
export function first() { function run() { return 1; } return run(); }
export function second() { function run() { return 2; } return run(); }
```

Before, `first()` calls `x_second_run`. After, each calls its own.

## What changed

Python already handles this the right way (#3405), so I reused the same approach for JS/TS:

- each inner function is recorded under the function it's declared in
- a call (or a function passed by name, like `register(run)`) looks in its own scope first, then the outer ones
- inner functions are kept out of the file-wide lookup, since they can't be called from outside anyway

Top-level functions, imports and methods are looked up the same as before.

## How I tested it

- added `tests/test_js_nested_function_scope.py` with the cases above, an inner function named like an import, siblings and deeper nesting, and inner functions inside arrow components. The four that check the wrong links fail on current `v8` and pass with this change, the siblings one checks those still resolve
- ran it on five of my own JS/TS projects before and after. Four didn't change at all. The fifth has a minified Prisma runtime full of one-letter names, where calls that pointed into other functions' inner functions now don't
- all 1,256 JS/TS related tests pass
- full test suite: 8,422 passed. The 8 that fail (7 in `test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py`, 1 in `test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py`) fail the same way on `v8` without this change, they need the SQL parser which my local setup doesn't have

## Not in this one

- in the import example, `a()` also gets a `calls lib_helper` link from the separate import pass, which doesn't know about inner functions. That's on `v8` too, so I left it for now
- inner functions written as `const helper = () => {}` still don't get nodes at all (#2143). I have that fix ready and will open it after this one, since it builds on this

title: feat(tree): cap directory children while retaining full totals
body:
## What does this PR do?

`tree --max-children N` currently limits symbols beneath files but leaves directory entries unbounded. Apply the limit to each logical directory in single and merged trees: retain up to N real children, then one `(+K more)` entry for omitted children.

The omission label counts hidden immediate entries; its `total_count` includes their full descendant leaves. Ancestors keep complete totals, and file-symbol limits remain unchanged. Zero retains only the omission entry for a nonempty directory; negative values raise `ValueError`, including for an empty graph.

title: perf(update): re-extract only the files whose content changed (#4740)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #4740, and the half that makes `graphify update` cheap for a warm tree.

The command's cost had nothing to do with what changed. Seven stages run, and only the first two read source text:

```text
scan ──> extract ──> build ──> cluster ──> analyze ──> report ──> export
disk     parse       graph     communities  findings     md/html
```

Everything downstream works on the graph, so a run with two edited files paid for all seven stages: 54.7 s and 1.08 GB on a 1,046-file corpus, and 34.0 s of that even with nothing edited.

The engine for a partial rebuild already existed. `_rebuild_code` has taken `changed_paths` since the hook work, and the only caller that ever passed a list was git: `post-commit` diffs HEAD and forwards the touched paths. `graphify update` called it with the argument unset, which the function documents as "the full code corpus". So the missing piece was a change set that does not depend on git. The manifest already holds one per-file content hash, so this reads it:

```diff
 _rebuild_code(watch_path, incremental=True)
   detect(watch_path)
+  changed_paths = manifest diff of the scan
+                  files whose ast_hash moved, plus rows whose file is gone
   if changed_paths is not None:
     extract only those
     preserve every other file's nodes
     hand the unchanged corpus's AST nodes to extract() as resolution context
-  else: extract the whole corpus        <- what `update` always did
   extract -> build -> cluster -> analyze -> report -> export
```

The manifest is written with paths relative to the scan root, so it survives being copied. That is what makes the reporter's workflow answerable, since their copy carries a usable baseline.

### The rule the change set is built on

A false "changed" costs time. A false "unchanged" ships a graph that describes code the reader no longer has. Every uncertain answer therefore resolves to "changed":

| question | answer |
|---|---|
| has this file changed? | content hash, never mtime alone. A checkout or `rsync --times` moves mtime with identical bytes; a same-second rewrite leaves it put |
| no row for it? | changed. Nothing describes it, so it was not in the last build |
| manifest missing, unreadable, or naming another tree? | full path. Unknown is not "nothing changed" |
| file gone from disk? | changed, and it must reach the deleted branch, or its nodes survive and the shrink guard refuses the write |

### Four commits

```text
bdc08b66  refactor(detect): expose the changed set for a root
d0a90eb5  feat(watch): derive changed_paths from the manifest in _rebuild_code (#4740)
e149ad02  feat(cli): use the incremental path for update (#4740)
48988034  fix(watch): keep cross-file resolution edges for the changed set (#4740)
0d4371a8  test(watch): make the default-path assertion robust to the no-change gate (#4740)
```

The split is deliberate. The refactor is behaviour-neutral and provable as such. The capability is default-off, so the watcher and the post-checkout hook are untouched. The CLI flag is its own commit, so reverting it returns `update` to full-corpus while the capability stays.

The last two commits are correctness fixes, and the new caller is what exposed them. Deriving a change set means only the changed files are parsed, so a call from a changed file into an unchanged one can lose its edge (#2406/#3763). v8 answers that by passing the unchanged corpus's AST nodes as resolution context, and commit `48988034` fixes the case where that context came back empty. The membership test anchored stored paths via `identity()`, which resolves against the tree recorded in `graphify-out/.graphify_root`, while the set it was compared against was built with `absolute_identity(..., project_root)`. On a copied checkout the marker still names the original tree, so every stored node read as corpus-absent. Two lines, same anchoring on both sides.

## Overlap with #4748, read before merging

This branch was cut from `v8` at `92741d16`, same as #4748, and it is not textually independent of it. `git merge-tree` gives:

```text
perf/4740-update-early-exit <-> perf/4740-incremental-update
  CONFLICT graphify/detect.py     (6 hunks)
  CONFLICT graphify/watch.py      (1 region)
  clean:      graphify/cli.py, tests/test_update_no_change_gate.py, tests/test_update_incremental.py
```

Both PRs need a function that does not exist on v8 yet: compare a scan against the manifest and say what changed. #4748 needs it for its gate, this one needs it for its change set, so both add `classify_manifest_files`. Both also insert into `_rebuild_code` at the same point, immediately after the `#3511` unclassified-file warning, because both read the same `detected` dict.

Worth knowing: if git ever merges these two cleanly, that is worse than a conflict. You would have two definitions of `classify_manifest_files` and Python would silently keep the later one.

The resolution, verified end to end:

| piece | keep |
|---|---|
| `classify_manifest_files` | #4748's, which is a superset (it adds `unstamped_is_changed`) |
| `classify_manifest_deletions` | this branch's; #4748 has no equivalent |
| `detect_incremental` | both call sites |
| the `_rebuild_code` insertion point | #4748's gate first, then this change set |

One detail the conflict markers do not show: #4748 folds `resolution_inputs` into the scanned set inside that loop, because its lock-file rows carry manifest entries while staying out of the scan corpus. The shared helper has to keep doing that or those rows read as excluded on every run.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [x] Refactor (the first commit only)
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

A partial rebuild is sound only if its key covers every input that reaches the graph, and the cost of being wrong is asymmetric: over-reporting costs time, under-reporting ships a stale graph.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. No schema, cache-key or file-format change. Reverting the CLI commit alone returns `update` to full-corpus rebuilds.

**Blast Radius:** moderate, because this decides what gets re-extracted:

- The change set is content-addressed, so a false "unchanged" needs identical bytes plus a matching manifest row. Everything else falls back to the full path.
- A new file has no row and therefore always re-extracts.
- A deleted file is carried into the change set so its nodes are evicted and the shrink guard can attribute the loss.
- `incremental` defaults to off, so the watcher, the post-checkout hook and every existing caller keep the full path.
- The first commit is a pure refactor. `detect_incremental` calls the factored helpers with the same arguments, and I checked the output matches the inline version on a corpus with an edit, a delete and an add, for both `kind="ast"` and `kind="semantic"`.
- `graphify update --force` still means a full rebuild. An explicit `changed_paths` still wins over the derived set.
- If both this and #4748 land, the gate runs first. On a tree the gate can skip, the user sees its message; the change set is only computed when the gate declines.

**Limitations**

- **An incremental rebuild is not byte-identical to a full one on a large corpus.** On 1,046 files it keeps one sourceless `any` node and seven edges that a full rebuild drops. This is **not** introduced here: v8 with an explicit `changed_paths` produces the same 21715 nodes / 46389 edges against 21714 / 46382 for a full rebuild, same node, same edges. It is pre-existing `changed_paths` behaviour that this PR makes reachable from the CLI, and it deserves its own issue.
- **The pipeline after extraction is still whole-graph.** Extraction was about a third of the cost. Rebuild, cluster, analyze and report still run over every node, which is why the two-file case lands at 35.9 s rather than seconds. That is the rest of #4740.
- **A source that never extracts re-queues on every run** by design (#2543), so a corpus containing one can never reach the pure-skip case. This repo has one (`worked/rsl-siege-manager/graph.json`), which is why `graphify update .` here still re-extracts a handful of files. On a corpus without one, an unchanged copied checkout reaches the skip.
- **On a copied checkout, deletions and renames are not evicted.** `graphify-out/.graphify_root` still names the original tree, so stored source paths resolve there and the fail-closed sweep reads the removed file as alive-out-of-scan and preserves it. The full path behaves identically, so this predates the PR; I deliberately did not test around it, which is why this branch's deletion test uses a same-directory tree.
- **No incremental rebuild for the semantic path.** This only covers `graphify update` (AST). `graphify extract` already had its own incremental mode.
- The change set is not persisted, so it is recomputed per run. It costs one manifest read against a scan that already happened.

## How was this tested?

`tests/test_update_incremental.py` is new and has 17 tests. Fifteen drive the real `_rebuild_code` with a spy on `extract()`: an unchanged copied checkout, two edited files reduced to the changed subset, an mtime bump with identical bytes, an added file, a deleted file and the eviction that follows, the default path, `--force`, an explicit `changed_paths`, a missing manifest, an unreadable manifest, a manifest anchored elsewhere, incremental output equal to a full rebuild on the same tree, the lock path, the non-blocking queue behaviour, and a cross-file call edge surviving an incremental update both in place and on a copied checkout. Two run the real CLI as a subprocess: `update` end to end, and `update --force`.

Against this branch the 17 give 17 passed. Against commit 1 alone they give 10 failed and 1 passed, which is the expected shape for a new keyword that does not exist yet.

The assertion in `test_default_is_the_full_path` is the one that had to change to survive #4748, and it is worth checking because a test that passes in both worlds can be vacuous. The corpus now carries one change before the second run, which is sound in either world: a correct no-change gate cannot skip a tree that changed. I confirmed the assertion still has teeth by mutating the derivation guard in a scratch copy to fire even when `incremental` is unset. It then fails in both worlds, with and without the gate:

```text
E  AssertionError: assert [['a.py']] == [['a.py', 'b.py', 'c.py', 'uses.py']]
```

Verification of the combination with #4748, since that is the risk this PR carries. I materialised the merged tree read-only (`git archive` of the resolved branch) and ran both test files against it with the tree on `PYTHONPATH`, so the subprocess tests loaded the combined code rather than the installed package:

```text
tests/test_update_incremental.py + tests/test_update_no_change_gate.py
  -> 36 passed          (17 here + 19 from #4748)
full suite on the merged tree
  -> 8762 passed, 15 skipped, 1 xfailed in 453.00s
  8726 (v8) + 17 (this PR) + 19 (#4748) = 8762
```

Gates, all with `PYTHONPATH` set to the repo so `sys.executable -m graphify` children load this tree:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q                                              -> 8743 passed, 15 skipped, 1 xfailed in 429.73s
tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_progress_final_line_uses_consistent_denominator  -> 1 passed
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .                                           -> All checks passed
.venv/bin/python -m pyright graphify/detect.py graphify/watch.py graphify/cli.py
  -> 30 errors, 3 warnings, identical to v8 on the same three files; no new errors
```

Wall time and peak RSS for `graphify update`, one process per run, v8 baseline executed from a worktree of `92741d16`, on 1,046 scanned files (570 code files) copied from this repo's tracked sources:

| | wall | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| unchanged copied checkout, before (v8) | 33.99 s | 991,000 KB |
| unchanged copied checkout, after | 1.74 s | 124,820 KB |
| two files edited, before (v8) | 54.70 s | 1,080,020 KB |
| two files edited, after | 35.93 s | 539,940 KB |

The same unchanged-copy measurement on a corpus that contains a never-extracting source gives 35.53 s to 15.51 s, which is the honest floor when the change set cannot be empty.

Not tested: Windows. The change set uses paths from `detect()` and the manifest's existing anchoring rules, and nothing here adds new path construction.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (N/A: no skill fragments touched.)
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). (Extraction is untouched. The change set is a content-hash comparison against the manifest, and mtime is only ever used to decide whether to hash.)
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [ ] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages. (No trailer in the commit messages.)

title: fix(install): give gemini its own global skill dir on Windows (#2800)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #2800. On Windows, `graphify install --platform gemini` wrote its user-global skill to `~/.agents/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`, the same path the `agents` platform uses. The two platforms ship different files (`skill.md` vs `skill-agents.md`), so installing one overwrote the other, and `graphify uninstall` for either one deleted the other's `SKILL.md`, `references/` and version stamp.

The issue asked which layout is intended. The Windows branch came from #368 (v0.4.15), on the belief that Gemini CLI prefers `~/.agents/skills` on Windows. Gemini CLI's own docs ([docs/cli/skills.md](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/cli/skills.md)) list the user tier as "`~/.gemini/skills/` or the `~/.agents/skills/` alias" with nothing OS-specific. Both paths are read on every OS, and the alias wins a name clash. The #368 report itself was a missing `--platform` flag. So this takes option 2 from the issue: gemini uses `~/.gemini/skills/graphify` everywhere.

Since the alias wins a name clash, a copy that an older Windows gemini install left in `~/.agents/skills/graphify` would hide the fresh one. `gemini install` now prints a note naming that folder. It does not delete it, because it may be a real `agents` install.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: two platforms never share one skill destination, so one platform's install or uninstall cannot touch another's files.

- [x] Reproduced: on v8, both new tests fail. `test_windows_gemini_install_and_uninstall_leave_the_agents_skill` fails because the gemini skill lands in `~/.agents` over the planted agents skill. `test_gemini_and_agents_own_separate_skill_dirs[Windows]` fails because the destination is `.agents/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`.
- [x] Smallest fix: one branch removed, plus the shadowing note.
- [x] Regression tests added in `tests/test_uninstall_scope.py` and `tests/test_skill_auto_refresh.py`.
- [x] `test_a_directory_shared_by_two_platforms_is_not_guessed` relied on the collision itself (it asserted gemini == agents on Windows), so it is replaced by the destination test above. The shared-dir guard it exercised is still covered by the copilot/vscode and symlink tests beside it.
- Limitation: an existing Windows user's old copy in `~/.agents/skills/graphify` is left in place. They get the note instead.

## How was this tested?

On Windows 11 with Python 3.12, the only OS where the old branch is reachable (CI is ubuntu-only).

```text
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_uninstall_scope.py tests/test_skill_auto_refresh.py tests/test_install_references.py tests/test_install.py -q
  -> 204 passed, 4 skipped
same new tests with graphify/install.py reverted to v8 -> 2 failed (the Windows cases)
uv run --frozen pytest tests/ -q -> 7 failed, 8651 passed, 86 skipped. The same 7 tests fail on unmodified v8 on this machine (8648 passed): aider/devin code-only update, a shebang parse test, a watch relative-roots test, two getcwd memoization tests, one alias-resolution test. None is new.
```

title: fix(install): write the global OpenCode plugin to ~/.config/opencode (#3398)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3398. A global (non-`--project`) `graphify install --platform opencode` called `_install_opencode_plugin(Path("."))`, and the helper joined `.opencode/plugins/graphify.js` onto that base. The "global" plugin therefore landed in whatever directory the command ran from, and loaded only for that project. The issue explains why swapping the base path alone would not work: OpenCode's global plugin dir is `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`, with no `.opencode/` segment.

The plugin helpers now take the OpenCode config dir itself, chosen by a new `_opencode_dir()`: `<project>/.opencode` for a project install, `~/.config/opencode` for a global one. To keep install and uninstall symmetric:

- `graphify uninstall` also removes the global plugin. Before, the misplaced plugin sat in `./.opencode`, which uninstall already cleaned.
- The OpenCode 2 plugin auto-refresh (#3554/#3732) also checks `~/.config/opencode`, alongside the cwd and home `.opencode` dirs where older installs wrote.
- The legacy `.opencode/plugins/graphify.js` entry that older releases wrote into `opencode.json` is still matched by its old string.

The slash-command half of #3398 no longer applies: v8 has no `_install_opencode_command`.

This takes the same approach as #3459 by @nikhilsaxena04, which now conflicts with v8. This branch is built on current v8, including the auto-refresh and `opencode.json` cleanup that landed after that PR. The diagnosis is theirs and the issue's.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a global install writes only under the user's config dir, never under the cwd, and a project install writes only under its project.

The project-scope guard `test_opencode_project_install_keeps_plugin_in_project` passes on both.
- [x] Existing project-scope opencode tests are unchanged and pass.
- Limitation: a plugin that an older global install already dropped into some project's `.opencode/` stays there. It behaves as a project plugin for that project.

title: fix(skill): record unreported subagent usage as unknown, not zero (#2786)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #2786. The skill has the parent agent copy each subagent's `usage` over the chunk's placeholder zeros. Codex returns a subagent's completion text with no machine-readable usage, so a semantic run there ended with `Token cost: 0 input · 0 output` in GRAPH_REPORT.md and a zero-cost run in `cost.json`. That says the work was free, not that it went unmeasured.

This makes token accounting tri-state, as the issue proposes:

- **Measured**: integers, summed as today.
- **Unknown**: the skill now tells the parent to write `null` for a chunk whose host reported no usage. `null` then stays unknown through every step that reads it:
  - The B3 chunk merge (core, aider and devin fragments) writes null totals and prints `token usage unavailable`.
  - The `cost.json` tracker records the run with null counts, keeps the all-time totals as the sum of measured runs, and counts the rest in a new `unmeasured_runs` field.
  - `graphify merge-chunks` and `build()` carry `null` through. Before, merge-chunks coerced it to 0 and build raised `TypeError`.
  - GRAPH_REPORT.md says `Token cost: unavailable (the host did not report token usage)`. The issue pointed at `report.py` rendering `0` here.
- **Zero**: still means a run that did no semantic work. A chunk with no token keys still counts as 0, as before.

The aider and devin monoliths gain a sanctioned-diff predicate in `tools/skillgen/gen.py` (`_is_unknown_token_usage_fix_line`) that covers exactly these lines.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: the report and `cost.json` never state a number the host did not give, and never turn "unmeasured" into 0.

- [x] Reproduced on v8 with `tests/test_token_usage_unknown.py`: 9 of its 13 tests fail. The cost tracker and the report raise `TypeError` on `null`, `build()` raises `TypeError`, and `merge-chunks` drops the null chunk and reports 1,200 tokens. The 4 guard tests (reported usage still sums, a code-only run still prints 0) pass on both.
- [x] The tests run the skill's own merge and cost snippets, extracted from `skill-codex.md`, `skill-aider.md` and `skill-devin.md`, not copies of them.
- [x] Regenerated with `python -m tools.skillgen` and `--bless`. Only the intended lines changed in the 17 skill artifacts and their `expected/` copies.

## How was this tested?

Windows 11, Python 3.12.

```text
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_token_usage_unknown.py -q -> 13 passed
same file with graphify/ and tools/ reverted to v8 -> 9 failed, 4 passed
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_report.py tests/test_merge_chunks_validation.py tests/test_skill_codex_semantic_merge.py tests/test_skill_semantic_all_cached.py tests/test_skillgen.py tests/test_build.py -q -> all passed
uv run --frozen python -m tools.skillgen --check | --audit-coverage | --schema-singleton | --monolith-roundtrip | --always-on-roundtrip -> all OK
uv run --frozen pytest tests/ -q -> the 7 tests that already fail on unmodified v8 on this machine, plus two that did not. test_claude_install_ships_lean_core_and_references was real: skill.md reached 802 lines against its 800-line cap, so the snippets were compacted (skill.md is now 798, v8 is 793). test_path_runs_without_error passes on rerun and was load flakiness. After the compaction, every skill-reading test file (tests/test_skill*.py, tests/test_code_only*.py, tests/test_install*.py) passes except the 2 aider/devin code-only tests that also fail on v8.
uv run --frozen ruff check (changed files) -> All checks passed
uv run --frozen pyright graphify/report.py graphify/build.py graphify/cli.py -> no errors beyond the ones v8 already has
```

title: fix(extract): resolve module.func values in Python dispatch tables (#1566)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #1566. A dispatch table of bare function names already gets `indirect_call` edges. The same table written with the module prefix, the usual shape of a plugin registry, got no edge at all, because only bare identifiers counted as table values:

```python
from payments import card
import payments.cash as cash

PROVIDERS = {"card": card.card_charge, "cash": cash.cash_charge}

def pay(provider, amount):
    table = {"card": card.card_charge, "cash": cash.cash_charge}
    return table[provider](amount)
```

On v8 neither `pay()` nor `checkout.py` links to `card_charge` or `cash_charge`. This came up in a user report about a plugin-style payments module.

**How it resolves.** A `module.func` value in a dict, list, set or tuple literal becomes an `indirect` member raw call. The existing Python member-call resolver then binds it, through its **module arm only** (#1883): the receiver must be a module imported into the caller's own file, and that module must hold exactly one callable of that name. The edge is the same INFERRED `indirect_call` (0.85, context `collection`) that the bare-name path emits.

It does not guess:

- No edge for a class used as a value (`card.CardGateway`, #2137).
- No edge when a parameter or local shadows the module name.
- No edge for a module the file never imports.
- When two modules define the same function name, the imported module's function is the only target. There's no fallback to bare-name proximity.
- A direct `card.card_charge()` call to the same target keeps the precise `calls` edge, whether it comes before or after the table. Indirect raw calls resolve after direct ones.
- A file-level `from payments.card import card_charge` (an `imports` edge to the same symbol) does not hide the edge. Indirect edges only dedup against `calls` / `indirect_call` pairs, as the generic resolver's `call_like_pairs` does.

A module-level table resolves from the file node. `_file_node()` returns `None` for a file node, so the module arm treats an indirect caller with no parent and with import edges as the file itself. That special case covers only `indirect` raw calls. Direct module-level calls (`card.card_charge(1)` at top level) still get no edge, as on v8. Changing that would add edges outside this PR's scope.

`_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` goes to 26 so cached Python extractions re-run.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: an `indirect_call` is emitted only to a callable the caller's own imports pin down to exactly one definition. Otherwise nothing is emitted.

- [x] Regression tests in `tests/test_indirect_dispatch_module_attr.py` (10). On v8, the 4 positive tests fail: function-level table, module-level registry, same-name-in-two-modules, and the file-level `imports` edge. The 6 guard tests pass on both: class value, shadowing parameter, unimported module, direct call not duplicated, table-before-call ordering, and both spellings giving one edge.
- [x] Graph diff, v8 vs this branch, built with `graphify update --no-cluster`:
  - `tests/fixtures`: 849 nodes / 970 edges, identical.
  - Graphify's own `graphify/` package as a corpus: 4,787 nodes / 10,144 edges, identical. That code has many `local.attr` dict values (`path.name`, `st.st_size`, `imported.local_name`), and none gained an edge.
  - A plugin-registry demo: exactly 4 new edges (`pay()` and `checkout.py` to `card_charge` / `cash_charge`), nothing removed.
  - Two builds of each corpus on this branch are identical.
- [x] Found in review and fixed before opening: a table listed before a direct call hid the `calls` edge, and a file-level `imports` edge suppressed the indirect edge. Both have tests.

**Known pre-existing gaps, not changed here.** The new path inherits these from the bare-name path's shared guard. Each one reproduces on v8 with bare names:

- A name rebound by `except ... as` (or a module-level `with`) is not treated as shadowing, so `except E as card_charge: [card_charge]` still gets an edge.
- A function inside an `isinstance` tuple counts as a table value.
- When the generic pass has already emitted a bare-name `indirect_call`, a later direct `module.func()` call to the same target loses its `calls` edge.
- `module.func` passed as a call argument, assigned, or returned (`pool.submit(card.card_charge)`) is still unsupported. Only table values are handled here.

## How was this tested?

Windows 11, Python 3.12.

```text
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_indirect_dispatch_module_attr.py -q -> 10 passed
same file with graphify/ reverted to v8 -> 4 failed, 6 passed
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_indirect_dispatch*.py tests/test_indirect_call*.py tests/test_python*.py tests/test_cache*.py tests/test_extract.py -q -> all passed
uv run --frozen pytest tests/ -q -> 7 failed, 8658 passed, 86 skipped. The same 7 tests fail on unmodified v8 on this machine: aider/devin code-only update, a shebang parse test, a watch relative-roots test, two getcwd memoization tests, one alias-resolution test. None is new.
uv run --frozen ruff check graphify tests/test_indirect_dispatch_module_attr.py -> All checks passed
uv run --frozen pyright graphify/extract.py graphify/extractors/engine.py graphify/cache.py -> no errors beyond the ones v8 already has
```

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] No generated skill artifacts touched.
- [x] AST extraction stays deterministic: two builds per corpus are identical, and nothing depends on the environment.
- [x] No shell/Python interpolation added.
- [x] No API keys or local graph data included.

title: fix(verilog): model a SystemVerilog class task method like a function one
body:
Found while auditing lesser-tested language extractors for unreported bugs — no existing issue covers this.

`graphify/extractors/verilog.py`'s `_augment_systemverilog_semantics` scans a SystemVerilog class body with regexes to extract its methods, fields, and type references (tree-sitter-verilog nests class internals in a shape this extractor doesn't walk directly). The method scan only ever looked for a `function` header (`_SV_FUNC_RE`), so a class method declared `task` instead — a method that needs to consume simulation time or has non-blocking statements, a routine SystemVerilog shape — got no node and no `method` edge at all. Silently dropped, not even an error.

The same code stripped only `function...endfunction` bodies before scanning what's left for class field declarations (`<type> <name>;`). A task method's own local variable declarations were never stripped, so a locally-declared variable of a custom type inside a task body read as a false `references`/`field` edge on the enclosing class — a field that doesn't exist.

```systemverilog
class Packet;
  function void set_data(int d); ... endfunction  // gets a node, as before

  task run_sim();
    Config cfg;   // a LOCAL variable, not a field
    ...
  endtask          // got NO node at all; `Config` leaked as a false field ref
endclass
```

Fix: added `_SV_TASK_RE`, a task-header pattern mirroring the function one minus the return type (tasks have none), and harvest task methods the same way functions already are (node, `method` edge, parameter-type references). Also strip `task...endtask` bodies out of the field-scan text the same way `function...endfunction` bodies already are, so a task's own locals stop leaking into the class's field references.

Verified the exact repro above directly against `extract_verilog`, then via the shared `tests/fixtures/sample.sv` fixture already used by the rest of this extractor's test suite. Verified pre-fix behavior via `git show HEAD:<path>` + a temporary file swap (never `git stash`) — both new tests fail on the unmodified file, confirmed byte-identical restoration afterward. Full suite (8609 passed) and `tools.skillgen --check` both clean; the only 3 failures are the same pre-existing, unrelated flakes already present on a clean checkout (erlang/R/skill-backtick, confirmed this session).

title: feat(opencode): install a native /graphify command
body:
## What this changes

`graphify install --platform opencode` writes the OpenCode skill and the `.opencode/plugins/graphify.js` hook, but no command. OpenCode does not expose skills as slash commands — they are loaded on demand through its `skill` tool — so typing `/graphify` in a session (as the README's platform table implies) is answered with an unknown command, and the only way to reach the skill is an explicit mention or the agent deciding to load it.

This adds the missing piece the same way the Kilo install already does it: a packaged command template, written to the directory OpenCode reads commands from.

## Implementation

- New `graphify/command-opencode.md`: front-matter `description`, then an instruction to invoke the `graphify` skill through the `skill` tool and pass `$ARGUMENTS` through unchanged (`. ` as the target when no arguments were supplied). Shipped in `package-data` next to `command-kilo.md`.
- `graphify/install.py`

title: fix(build): count label-only AST file twins in the shrink guard (#4778)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4778, the `cluster-only` follow-up that @jxamen reported on #4389.

#4391 taught `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes()` about the `(source_file, label)` fold from `build_from_json()` Pass 2. Pass 2b (#3344) is a second fold: when a document mentions a file, the semantic node has the file's path as its label and the document as its `source_file`, and Pass 2b merges it into the single AST file node that label names. On `cluster-only`, the reload performs that fold. The write is then refused twice:

1. The guard reports the folded node as a lost semantic node.
2. `to_json()`'s count check (`new_n < existing_n`) refuses as well, because the saved graph held the mention and its twin as two nodes.

Changes:
- `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes()` mirrors Pass 2b. A missing semantic node whose label names exactly one AST file node in the new graph counts as folded, not lost. If it names two or more, it is still lost, since Pass 2b leaves it unmerged.
- The helper takes an optional `folded` dict and records each fold as `saved id -> twin id`. Pass 2 folds are recorded too.
- `to_json()` subtracts from the count check only the folds whose twin was **already in the saved graph**. A twin that is new in this run does not offset the loss of some other node.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant (#479/#2229): a write must not lose a saved semantic node or shrink the graph without an explanation. A fold into an AST twin is one node, not a lost one. The exemption is exactly as narrow as Pass 2b: a unique AST file-node match, with the strict `_origin == "ast"` check. Two negative tests guard that it doesn't loosen further: an ambiguous label is still lost, and a new twin doesn't hide another loss.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant (the #4778 graph on graphifyy 0.9.94 exits 1 with the warning above).
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test**. On `v8` (92741d16) without the fix, 4 of the 5 new tests fail. The ambiguous-label test is a negative control and passes on both. `test_to_json_new_twin_does_not_offset_another_loss` also fails on `v8`, but there it fails on the semantic-loss message, before it reaches the count check it is meant to guard.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly:
  - The `graphify update` path (`watch._check_shrink`) gets the helper's Pass 2b exemption, but its count accounting (`rebuilt_sources`) does not change. I did not reproduce a count refusal there.
  - I did not determine how a fresh extraction ends up with an unfolded mention in the saved graph. The fix only makes reload/recluster accept the fold.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_lost_saved_semantic_nodes.py tests/test_cli_export.py::test_cluster_only_accepts_file_mention_folded_into_ast_twin

     test_language_override_lifecycle [src], test_resolve_memoization / test_source_key_memoization getcwd); Windows env
uv run ruff check .   -> All checks passed
uv run pyright graphify/build.py graphify/export.py tests/test_lost_saved_semantic_nodes.py
  -> 17 errors before and after (all pre-existing, none on changed lines)
graphify cluster-only . --no-label on the #4778 graph -> refused before; see test_cluster_only_accepts_file_mention_folded_into_ast_twin for after
```
