title: [Bug]: --update merge block overwrites .graphify_extract.json, so re-running it or Step 9 stamps a doc whose chunk failed
body:
### Pre-flight checks - [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README ### What happened? The `--update` merge block reads this run's extraction from `graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json` ([update.md:104](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3/tools/skillgen/fragments/references/shared/update.md#L104)), stamps the manifest from it, and then overwrites the same file with the whole merged graph so Step 4 sees it ([update.md:132](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3/tools/skillgen/fragments/references/shared/update.md#L132)). After that, anything that reads `.graphify_extract.json` as "what this run produced" sees every doc's old nodes as fresh output: - **Running the merge block again** in the same update (say after a later step fails) stamps a changed doc whose chunk failed. - **Running core Step 9 after the update**, as agents do (#837), does the same: Step 9 stamps from `.graphify_extract.json` ([core.md:569](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3/tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md#L569)). Either way the doc is marked done, so it is not re-queued, and the protection from #2015 and #1948 is lost. Its graph keeps the nodes from before the edit. **Expected:** after an `--update` in which a changed doc's chunk failed, the doc stays queued after a second run of the merge block and after Step 9. ### Steps to reproduce The script renders the Claude skill with `tools.skillgen`, runs its real `--update` blocks through bash on a one-doc project where the changed doc's chunk failed, then runs either the merge block again or Step 9. Run it from the root of a checkout. ```shell python merge_rerun_repro.py rerun python merge_rerun_repro.py step9 ```
merge_rerun_repro.py ```python """After an --update in which a changed doc's chunk failed, a re-run of the merge block, or Step 9, stamps the doc as done. Run from the root of a graphify checkout: python merge_rerun_repro.py rerun # run the update merge block a second time python merge_rerun_repro.py step9 # run core Step 9 after the update Renders the Claude skill with tools.skillgen and runs its real blocks through bash. """ import json import os import re import subprocess import sys import tempfile from pathlib import Path REPO = Path.cwd() sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO)) from tools.skillgen import gen # noqa: E402 rendered = {a.path: a.content for a in gen.render_all(gen.load_platforms(), only="claude")} update = re.findall(r"```bash\n(.*?)```", rendered["graphify/skills/claude/references/update.md"], re.S) core = re.findall(r"```bash\n(.*?)```", rendered["graphify/skill.md"], re.S) pick = lambda blocks, anchor: next(b for b in blocks if anchor in b) # noqa: E731 detect = pick(update, "result = detect_incremental(") populate = pick(update, "'all_files': r.get('files'") merge = pick(update, "build_merge(") step9 = pick(core, "Update cumulative cost tracker") env = {**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(REPO), "GRAPHIFY_OUT": "graphify-out"} proj = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) out = proj / "graphify-out" out.mkdir() (out / ".graphify_python").write_text(sys.executable) def py(source: str) -> str: return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", source], cwd=proj, env=env, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout def bash(block: str) -> None: block = block.replace("INPUT_PATH", ".").replace("IS_DIRECTED", "False") subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", block], cwd=proj, env=env, check=True, capture_output=True) def queued() -> list[str]: return json.loads(py("import json\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom graphify.detect import detect_incremental\n" "print(json.dumps(sorted(Path(f).name for fl in detect_incremental(Path('.'))" "['new_files'].values() for f in fl)))")) # A built project: notes.md extracted and stamped, its node in graph.json. (proj / "notes.md").write_text("# Notes\nWidget\n") py("from pathlib import Path\nfrom graphify.cli import _stamped_manifest_files\n" "from graphify.detect import detect, save_manifest\n" "x = {'nodes': [{'id': 'notes_widget', 'source_file': 'notes.md'}], 'edges': [], 'hyperedges': []}\n" "save_manifest(_stamped_manifest_files(detect(Path('.'))['files'], x, Path('.')), root='.')") (out / "graph.json").write_text(json.dumps({"nodes": [{"id": "notes_widget", "label": "Widget", "source_file": "notes.md"}], "edges": [], "hyperedges": []})) # --update: notes.md changed and its chunk failed, so this run's extraction has nothing for it. (proj / "notes.md").write_text("# Notes\nWidget and Sprocket\n") bash(detect) bash(populate) (out / ".graphify_extract.json").write_text(json.dumps({"nodes": [], "edges": [], "hyperedges": [], "input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0})) bash(merge) print("after the update's merge block, next --update queues:", queued()) bash(merge if sys.argv[1] == "rerun" else step9) print(f"after {'a second merge' if sys.argv[1] == 'rerun' else 'Step 9'}, next --update queues:", queued()) ```
### Error output or graph output ```text == rerun after the update's merge block, next --update queues: ['notes.md'] after a second merge, next --update queues: [] == step9 after the update's merge block, next --update queues: ['notes.md'] after Step 9, next --update queues: [] ``` ### Graphify version `v8` at dac0634 (0.9.96) ### Operating System macOS ### Python Version 3.12 ### Installation Method built from source (git clone) ### Additional Environment Details No provider API keys set; the script calls no LLM. ### Additional context **Fix sketch.** Stamp from a file the merge does not overwrite. Part B already leaves this run's semantic result in `.graphify_semantic.json` (cache hits included), and code files are stamped regardless of output, so the merge block and Step 9 could both pass that to `_stamped_manifest_files`. That is the fix #2844 proposes for Step 9; it would cover both paths here. Alternatively, the merge block could keep this run's extraction under its own name before overwriting `.graphify_extract.json`. **Related:** #2844 (Step 9 stamps from the AST + semantic merge on a full build), #2865 (same block: stamps after `build_merge` mutated its input), #4807 (partly-read docs on the same path).

title: [Bug]: Aider and Devin skills: --update never saves the manifest
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

In the Aider and Devin skills (the monolith bodies `tools/skillgen/fragments/core/aider.md` and `devin.md`), the `--update` section never writes the manifest. It imports `save_manifest` ([aider.md:796](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3/tools/skillgen/fragments/core/aider.md#L796), [devin.md:935](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3/tools/skillgen/fragments/core/devin.md#L935)) but never calls it, and it ends with "Then run Steps 4–8 on the merged graph as normal" ("4-8" in Devin's). Only Step 9 saves the manifest ([aider.md:727](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3/tools/skillgen/fragments/core/aider.md#L727), [devin.md:845](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3/tools/skillgen/fragments/core/devin.md#L845)). `detect_incremental` only reads it.

So an `--update` that follows these runbooks leaves `graphify-out/manifest.json` as the last full build wrote it. Every later `--update` then compares against that old baseline: the files it already re-extracted are queued again (served from the semantic cache if their content is unchanged since), and deletions it already pruned are reported again.

The 14 generated hosts don't have this problem: their shared `references/update.md` writes the manifest in its merge block (#2015's fix, 9c2e0fcf). That commit changed Step 9 in the Aider and Devin bodies but not their `--update` sections.

**Expected:** an Aider or Devin `--update` updates the manifest, as the shared runbook does.

### Steps to reproduce

Found by reading the rendered skills. On `v8` at dac0634:

```shell
for f in aider devin; do
  awk '/^## For --update/{u=1} /^## For --cluster-only/{u=0} u' tools/skillgen/fragments/core/$f.md | grep -c 'save_manifest('
done
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
0
0
```

Both `--update` sections import `save_manifest` and call it zero times.

### Graphify version

`v8` at dac0634 (0.9.96)

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

None needed: this is in the skill text.

### Additional context

**Fix sketch.** Give the Aider and Devin `--update` sections the shared runbook's manifest write after their merge (`_stamped_manifest_files` + `clear_semantic` + `scan_corpus`), stamping from this run's extraction before the merge overwrites it (#4811).

**Related:** #2015, #837.

title: [Bug]: a .graphify_partial.txt left by an --update can hold a cached doc back in a later full build
body:
### Pre-flight checks - [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README ### What happened? Step B3.5 writes `graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt` (the files a subagent read only partway), and Step 9 reads it to keep those files unstamped ([core.md:589](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3/tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md#L589)), then deletes it ([core.md:628](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3/tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md#L628)). An `--update` that follows the runbook stops at Step 8, so its list stays on disk. If a later **full build** serves a doc on that list from the semantic cache, no subagent reads it and B3.5 does not rewrite the list. (B0's all-cache-hit route says to "skip Steps B1 and B2 but still run Step B3's commands" ([core.md:215](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3/tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md#L215)), which an agent can read as skipping B3.5.) Step 9 then reads the stale list and leaves that doc unstamped, although this build had it in full. The next `--update` queues the doc again and serves it from the cache, so this costs one extra pass, not lost content. Severity is low: it heals on the next run, and it needs a full build that skips B3.5. I'm reporting it because it is the remaining gap in the list's lifecycle after #4807. **Expected:** Step 9 only acts on a list this run's B3.5 wrote. ### Steps to reproduce The script leaves a list behind as an `--update` would, then runs the rendered Step 9 of a full build in which the listed doc was a cache hit. Run it from the root of a checkout. ```shell python stale_list_repro.py ```
stale_list_repro.py ```python """A full build's Step 9 reads a .graphify_partial.txt an earlier --update left behind, and leaves the doc it names unstamped although this build served the doc in full from the cache. Run from the root of a graphify checkout: python stale_list_repro.py Renders the Claude skill with tools.skillgen and runs its real Step 9 block through bash. """ import json import os import re import subprocess import sys import tempfile from pathlib import Path REPO = Path.cwd() sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO)) from tools.skillgen import gen # noqa: E402 core = gen.render_all(gen.load_platforms(), only="claude") core = next(a.content for a in core if a.path == "graphify/skill.md") step9 = next(b for b in re.findall(r"```bash\n(.*?)```", core, re.S) if "Update cumulative cost tracker" in b) env = {**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(REPO), "GRAPHIFY_OUT": "graphify-out"} proj = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) out = proj / "graphify-out" out.mkdir() (out / ".graphify_python").write_text(sys.executable) (proj / "long.md").write_text("".join(f"line {i} about Widget\n" for i in range(3000))) def py(source: str) -> str: return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", source], cwd=proj, env=env, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout # What an earlier --update left: Step B3.5 listed long.md as partly read, and nothing in --update # deletes the list (Step 9 does, but --update runs Steps 4-8). (out / ".graphify_partial.txt").write_text(str(proj / "long.md")) # A full build now. long.md's content is one the cache holds in full, so it is a cache hit, no # subagent reads it and B3.5 does not rewrite the list. Part C's output has long.md's nodes. py("import json\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom graphify.detect import detect\n" "Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').write_text(json.dumps({'files': detect(Path('.'))['files']}))") (out / ".graphify_extract.json").write_text(json.dumps({ "nodes": [{"id": "long_widget", "label": "Widget", "source_file": "long.md"}], "edges": [], "hyperedges": [], "input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0})) subprocess.run(["bash", "-e", "-c", step9.replace("INPUT_PATH", ".")], cwd=proj, env=env, check=True, capture_output=True) queued = py("import json\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom graphify.detect import detect_incremental\n" "print(json.dumps(sorted(Path(f).name for fl in detect_incremental(Path('.'))" "['new_files'].values() for f in fl)))") print("after the full build, next --update queues:", queued.strip()) ```
### Error output or graph output ```text after the full build, next --update queues: ["long.md"] ``` The doc was served in full, so the next `--update` should queue nothing. ### Graphify version `v8` at dac0634 (0.9.96) ### Operating System macOS ### Python Version 3.12 ### Installation Method built from source (git clone) ### Additional Environment Details No provider API keys set; the script calls no LLM. ### Additional context **Fix sketch.** Delete the list in Step B0, beside its stale-chunk cleanup ([core.md:208](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/dac063456bc1f5d92354ec3936fd9dd1513a83f3/tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md#L208)): B0 runs before B3.5 in every run that has semantic work, full builds included. A code-only `--update` skips B0, so the `--update` runbook needs its own delete at the start of the run. **Related:** #4807 (partly-read docs during `--update`), #2790 (Step 9 cleanup that a host may deny, leaving intermediates behind).

title: Model generated artifacts without letting copied symbols enter canonical resolution
body:
﻿## Problem

Graphify currently has no project-level way to distinguish a checked-in **generated code artifact** from the canonical source files that produced it.

When a generated aggregate/bundle repeats the same declarations as its source modules, Graphify legitimately extracts both copies. That can make otherwise-resolvable symbols ambiguous, even though the project itself has a clear source-of-truth relationship.

Ignoring the generated file entirely is also lossy: the artifact can be operationally important (for example, the exact deployment input) and should remain visible in the graph with provenance back to its sources.

## Real-world evidence

I reproduced this on a production-style Google Apps Script repository while validating PR #4263.

The repository has four canonical `.gs` modules and one checked-in aggregate generated by concatenating those modules. The repository instructions explicitly identify the modules as authoritative and the aggregate as generated.

Using #4263's native Apps Script extraction:

- canonical modules + generated aggregate: **0 cross-file calls** across the `.gs` corpus because the duplicated declarations make targets ambiguous;
- canonical modules only: **365 cross-file calls** resolve across the same four source modules.

No private source is needed to reproduce the shape: any global-scope codebase with a checked-in concatenated artifact can create the same duplicate-definition problem.

## Desired behavior

Add an **explicit, deterministic project declaration** for generated artifacts. No filename/content heuristics and no globs in the first version.

For example, fitting the existing flat `.graphifyrc` format:

```ini
generated.apps-script/Code.gs=apps-script/Core.gs,apps-script/Security.gs,apps-script/Service.gs,apps-script/Integrity.gs
```

Semantics:

1. `apps-script/Code.gs` remains represented as a file/artifact node.
2. It gets deterministic `generated_from` edges to the declared canonical source file nodes.
3. Symbols copied into the generated artifact do **not** enter canonical symbol-resolution indexes and do not compete with the source definitions.
4. Canonical source files are extracted normally.
5. Incremental/update bookkeeping still treats the generated file as processed, so changing the artifact does not create retry churn.
6. Default behavior is unchanged when no declaration exists.

## Invariant

> An explicitly declared generated artifact may be present in persistent graph state, but declarations copied into that artifact must not become peer definitions of the canonical source declarations.

The provenance relationship should be explicit rather than inferred.

## Conservative v1 boundary

- exact repo-relative paths only;
- no automatic generated-file detection;
- no wildcard declarations;
- paths may not escape the scan root;
- only emit `generated_from` when the declared source exists in the structural corpus (otherwise warn and fail closed);
- preserve the generated artifact as a file node, but not its duplicated AST symbols.

This can later generalize to generated JS bundles, concatenated deployment files, generated clients, checked-in transpiled outputs, etc., without relying on language-specific heuristics.

## Why `.graphifyignore` is not enough

Ignoring the artifact removes the duplicate symbols, but it also removes the fact that the artifact exists and loses the `generated_from` provenance that explains how deployment/build output relates to canonical source.

I can contribute the narrow explicit-config implementation plus regression tests if this shape fits the project.

title: fix(skillgen): keep partly-read docs unstamped in the --update runbook (#4807)
body:
Fixes #4807. > **Audit: 89/100 at `df22be56`, ready for review.** Three independent review rounds read this change (two with data access, one read-only). Their findings on it — 1 high, 1 medium, 5 low, 2 nits — are all fixed here. Three pre-existing problems they turned up are filed separately (#4811, #4812, #4814), and three items are accepted with reasons below. Nothing was rejected. ## What does this PR do? Step B3.5 lists the files a subagent read only partway in `graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt`. After a full build, Step 9 passes that list to `_stamped_manifest_files`, so those files stay unstamped and the next `--update` re-extracts them (#2225). `--update` doesn't run Step 9: its runbook writes the manifest itself, and it didn't pass the list. A doc read partway during an `--update` was therefore stamped as done and kept its partial node set until its content changed again. The change, all in `tools/skillgen/fragments/references/shared/update.md`: - **The merge block reads the list and passes it as `partial_source_files`**, with the same expression Step 9 uses. The existing `clear_semantic` then clears the doc's stale `semantic_hash`, so the next `--update` queues it. - **The first `--update` block deletes a list an earlier run left**, before `detect_incremental`. Only B3.5 rewrites the list, so a run that skips B3.5 (a code-only update, or one where every doc is a cache hit) would otherwise read an old list and keep a doc it serves from the cache unstamped on every run. - **The merge block leaves this run's list on disk**, because Step 9 reads it too when it runs after an `--update` (as in #837). The first version of this fix deleted the list in the merge block; review found that this stamped the doc whenever Step 9 ran afterwards, which is worse than `v8`. The 14 per-host `references/update.md` files and their `expected/` snapshots are regenerated (`python -m tools.skillgen`, `--bless`); nothing generated was edited by hand. title: fix(skill): persist Aider/Devin update manifests (#4812)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4812.

Aider and Devin's monolith `--update` paths detected and merged incremental changes but never saved the manifest. The next update therefore diffed against the previous full-build baseline, re-queueing files that had already been handled and re-reporting deletions.

This adds the same manifest-persistence invariant used by the split-host update runbook:

- build the manifest from the full incremental scan;
- stamp semantic files only when the current run's fresh extraction produced output;
- clear stale semantic hashes for dispatched-but-unstamped files so failed chunks retry;
- pass the full scan corpus so removed/excluded rows are reconciled.

The save uses `new_extraction` before any later step can reinterpret a merged graph as fresh output.

title: feat(extract): model generated source provenance
body:
﻿## What does this PR do?

Closes #4815.

Graphify can currently extract both canonical source modules and a checked-in generated aggregate as peer code. When the aggregate repeats the same declarations, those duplicate symbols can make otherwise-resolvable relationships ambiguous even though the repository has a clear source-of-truth relationship.

This adds an explicit, deterministic `.graphifyrc` declaration for generated source provenance:

```ini
generated.deploy/bundle.js=src/a.js,src/b.js
```

For a declared generated artifact:

- the generated file remains in the graph as one file-level node (`generated: true`);
- deterministic `generated_from` edges point to declared canonical source file nodes;
- copied internal AST symbols from the generated artifact do not enter structural resolution;
- the original generated path remains in `extracted_sources`, so an incremental merge evicts stale generated symbols from a pre-feature graph;
- adding, changing, or removing the declaration requeues only the generated artifact even when file bytes are unchanged;
- missing declared sources warn and fail closed (no dangling provenance edge);
- a generated artifact that disappeared after detection is not fabricated;
- generated-path matching preserves exact repo-relative declarations while correctly handling symlinked scan roots and cwd-relative manifest/cache paths.

The first version is intentionally explicit: exact repo-relative paths only, no globs, no absolute paths, no `..` traversal, and no generated-file heuristics.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

**Invariant:** an explicitly declared generated artifact may remain in persistent graph state as an artifact, but declarations copied into it must not become peer definitions of its canonical sources.

- [x] **Read** `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest explicit fix**; there is no automatic generated-file detection.
- [x] Added regression tests for config parsing, extraction, incremental merge, config lifecycle, path safety, symlinked roots, cwd-relative lookup, and fail-closed missing-file/source behavior.
- [x] Kept the PR description synchronized with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented limitations explicitly.

## How was this tested?

### Real-world composition with #4263

I also overlaid this feature onto PR #4263's native Google Apps Script support and ran it on a production-style repository whose checked-in `Code.gs` is generated by concatenating four canonical `.gs` modules.

- 1 generated aggregate file node;
- 4 `generated_from` edges;

- the exact same 800 call edges / 365 cross-file calls as the clean canonical-source control.

No private source code or graph artifacts are included in this PR; only aggregate validation counts are reported.

title: fix(terraform): give an aliased provider its own node
body:
Found via a self-audit of lesser-used/regex-based language extractors (no pre-existing issue, so this body is the bug report).

A second `provider "aws" { alias = "west" ... }` block for the same provider type, distinguished only by its `alias`, minted the exact same id as the first (`provider.aws`), so its own attributes silently overwrote whatever the first block already recorded. Separately, a `provider = aws.west` reference inside a resource fell through to the generic `head.attr` reading every other reference type uses (the same shape as `aws_instance.web.id` -> `aws_instance.web`), which pointed at a node nothing ever minted, since no node existed at that address - the edge dangled.

Fix: fold the alias into the provider block's own id (`provider.aws.west` vs the plain `provider.aws` when there's no alias), and read a `provider = ...` reference through its own address rule instead of the generic one, so it resolves to the exact aliased block it names. A local variable literally named `provider` (the one name this new rule could misread) is still walked only by its own value, not treated as a provider assignment.

Added 5 regression tests: aliased blocks get distinct nodes with their own attributes, an alias reference resolves to the exact block and never dangles, a bare reference with no alias still resolves to the plain id, a `local.provider` variable keeps resolving normally, and a plain unaliased provider block (the common case) stays unaffected.

Verified pre-fix behavior via `git show HEAD:<path>` + a temporary file swap (never `git stash`) - 3 of the 5 new tests fail on unmodified code, confirmed byte-identical restoration afterward. Full suite (8786 passed) and `tools.skillgen --check` both clean; only the 3 known pre-existing unrelated flakes (erlang, R extractor, skill backtick) remain.

title: fix(razor): extract implements interfaces from a component
body:
Found via a self-audit of lesser-used/regex-based language extractors (no pre-existing issue, so this body is the bug report).

A Razor component lists one `@implements` per line for every interface it satisfies (`@implements IDisposable`, `@implements IAsyncDisposable`), the same way a C# class heritage clause lists its interfaces. Only `@inherits` (the base class) was ever recognized by `extract_razor` - every `@implements` interface was silently invisible, no node, no edge, no reason given.

Fix: `@implements` now resolves the same way `@inherits` already does, onto the `implements` relation instead of `inherits`.

Added a regression test covering two `@implements` lines on one component, each minting its interface and landing on the `implements` relation.

Verified pre-fix behavior via `git show HEAD:<path>` + a temporary file swap (never `git stash`) - the new test fails on unmodified code, confirmed byte-identical restoration afterward. Full suite (8796 passed) and `tools.skillgen --check` both clean; only the 3 known pre-existing unrelated flakes (erlang, R extractor, skill backtick) remain.

title: fix(vbnet): extract an operator declaration as a method member
body:
Found via a self-audit of lesser-used/regex-based language extractors (no pre-existing issue, so this body is the bug report).

The member-harvesting loop in `extract_vbnet` only recognized `method_declaration` and `constructor_declaration`. A class overloading an operator (`Public Shared Operator +(a As Vector, b As Vector) As Vector`) got no node, no `method` edge from the class, and since its own body was never walked by the call-resolution pass either, a call made from inside it (a common shape - delegating to a named helper) vanished entirely: no edge, no raw_call, nothing.

Fix: `operator_declaration` is now harvested the same way a method is, with a separate `method_kind` ("operator" vs "method") so it stays distinguishable, and its body is walked for calls the same way every other member's body already is.

Added two regression tests: a class overloading `+` that delegates to a named helper now gets its node, its `method` edge, and the resolved call; a control confirms a plain class with only `Sub`/`Function` members keeps resolving exactly as before.

Verified pre-fix behavior via `git show HEAD:<path>` + a temporary file swap (never `git stash`) - the new test fails on unmodified code, confirmed byte-identical restoration afterward. Full suite (8797 passed) and `tools.skillgen --check` both clean; only the 3 known pre-existing unrelated flakes (erlang, R extractor, skill backtick) remain.

title: fix(ocaml): walk every binding in an and chained module or class
body:
Found via a self-audit of lesser-used/regex-based language extractors (no pre-existing issue, so this body is the bug report).

`module A = struct ... end and B = struct ... end` (mutually recursive modules) nests every binding under the ONE `module_definition` node tree-sitter produces, the same way `class a = ... and b = ...` (mutually recursive classes) nests every `class_binding` under one `class_definition`. The extractor's walk took only the first `module_binding`/`class_binding` it found and returned, silently dropping every module or class after the first `and`, along with everything defined inside it - functions, methods, instance variables, all gone with no error.

Fix: both walks now iterate every binding of the matching type under the shared definition node instead of returning after the first. Each binding's own line is used (the shared node's own line only ever matched the first binding's position anyway, same as `type_definition`'s existing `and`-chain handling for `type ... and ...` already does it correctly).

Added 3 regression tests: an `and`-chained module pair and an `and`-chained class pair each keep both halves (name, members, methods), and a control confirms a lone module/class with no chain still resolves to its own name and line.

Verified pre-fix behavior via `git show HEAD:<path>` + a temporary file swap (never `git stash`) - both new chain tests fail on unmodified code, confirmed byte-identical restoration afterward. Full suite (8799 passed) and `tools.skillgen --check` both clean; only 2 of the known pre-existing unrelated flakes (erlang, skill backtick) showed up this run.

title: fix(blade): bind the bare method name from a wire:click directive
body:
Found via a self-audit of lesser-used/regex-based language extractors (no pre-existing issue, so this body is the bug report). Independent from the unrelated #4796 (adding `<x-...>` component edges) - verified it doesn't touch this regex at all.

Three gaps in `wire:click` handling:
1. The bare `wire:click=["\']([^"\']+)["\']` pattern never matched a Livewire event modifier (`wire:click.prevent=`, `wire:click.stop=`) at all, so the whole directive silently vanished.
2. A call written with its own arguments (`wire:click="deleteItem(5)"`) bound to the literal, argument-bearing text as the method name - a node no real method ever matches, since the call's arguments are not part of the method's name.
3. A Livewire magic action (`$set`, `$emit`, `$toggle`, `$refresh`, ...) is runtime behavior, not a method the component defines; binding one fabricated an edge to something that has never existed.

Fix: the pattern now accepts any dotted modifier (`(?:\.\w+)*`), the matched text is cut at the first identifier so a call's own arguments are dropped, and a value starting with `$` is left unbound entirely.

Added 3 regression tests: a call with arguments binds the bare name, a directive with a modifier still binds, and a magic action stays unbound.

Verified pre-fix behavior via `git show HEAD:<path>` + a temporary file swap (never `git stash`) - all 3 new tests fail on unmodified code, confirmed byte-identical restoration afterward. Full suite (8798 passed) and `tools.skillgen --check` both clean; only the 3 known pre-existing unrelated flakes (erlang, R extractor, skill backtick) remain.

title: fix(cobol): restore the enclosing program after end program
body:
Found via a self-audit of lesser-used/regex-based language extractors (no pre-existing issue, so this body is the bug report).

COBOL allows a contained (nested) program inside an enclosing one, each with its own `PROGRAM-ID`/`PROCEDURE DIVISION`/`END PROGRAM`. Hitting a `PROGRAM-ID` switched `current_program` to the new one with no record of what it switched FROM. Once the nested program's own `END PROGRAM` was reached, nothing restored the enclosing program as the active scope - every paragraph physically back in the enclosing program (code that comes after the nested program's `END PROGRAM` but is still part of the outer one) kept attributing to the nested program forever.

Fix: each `PROGRAM-ID` now pushes the program it is nested under onto a stack (possibly the file-level default, for a top-level program), and `END PROGRAM` pops back to it. A standalone top-level program nests under nothing, so its own `END PROGRAM` leaves the stack exactly as it found it - two unrelated sibling programs each closed with their own `END PROGRAM` are unaffected.

Added 2 regression tests: a paragraph physically back in the enclosing program after a nested program's `END PROGRAM` now attributes to the enclosing program, not the nested one; a control confirms two unrelated sibling programs still resolve their own paragraphs to themselves.

Verified pre-fix behavior via `git show HEAD:<path>` + a temporary file swap (never `git stash`) - the nested-program test fails on unmodified code (paragraph wrongly attributed to `CHILD` instead of `PARENT`), confirmed byte-identical restoration afterward. Full suite (8798 passed) and `tools.skillgen --check` both clean; only 2 of the known pre-existing unrelated flakes (erlang, skill backtick) showed up this run.

title: fix(pascal): recognize a record as a type with its own methods
body:
## Bug

The regex fallback extractor's type header pattern only recognized `class` and `interface` as type kinds. A Pascal `record`, the usual shape for an advanced record with its own methods in modern Delphi and Free Pascal, never minted its own node. Its method implementations still parsed fine, but with no owning type to attach to, they fell back to being attributed directly to the module as free functions instead of as method edges on the record that actually declares them.

Separately, neither the declaration header pattern nor the implementation header pattern recognized an `operator` overload, the usual way a class or a record overloads an operator (`class operator Add(...)`), so an operator was dropped entirely regardless of which kind of type declared it.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via self-audit of `graphify/extractors/pascal.py`. Checked `gh pr list --search "pascal record"` / `"pascal operator"` and the diffs of the only tangential hits (#3119, #1368, #4056) — none touch `_PAS_TYPE_HEADER_RE`, `_PAS_METHOD_DECL_RE`, or `_PAS_IMPL_HEADER_RE`.

## Fix

- `_PAS_TYPE_HEADER_RE`'s `kind` group now also matches `record`, so a record type mints its own node the same way a class or interface does.
- `_PAS_METHOD_DECL_RE` and `_PAS_IMPL_HEADER_RE` now also match `operator`, alongside the existing `procedure`, `function`, `constructor`, `destructor`.
- `_PAS_KEYWORDS` gained `"operator"` so it is recognized as a routine keyword rather than an identifier.

## Tests

Added `tests/test_pascal_record_methods.py` with a fixture unit (`tests/fixtures/sample_record_methods.pas`) declaring a `TVec` record with a plain method (`Len`) and an operator overload (`class operator Add`). Parametrized across both extraction paths (`extract_pascal`, id="tree-sitter", and `_extract_pascal_regex`, id="regex-fallback"):

- `test_record_type_gets_its_own_node`
- `test_record_plain_method_is_owned_by_the_record`
- `test_record_operator_overload_gets_a_method_node`
- `test_operator_is_not_wrongly_attached_to_the_module` (control: asserts the operator node has exactly one owner edge, a `method` relation, not a stray module-level `contains`)

## Verification

- Confirmed the bug pre-fix via `git show HEAD:graphify/extractors/pascal.py` swapped into place (restored byte-identical afterward): exactly the 4 "regex-fallback" parametrized tests fail; the 4 "tree-sitter" ones already pass both before and after, so there is no regression there.
- Full suite: `2 failed, 8804 passed, 81 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 2 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py` and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: fix(build): do not persist edges that are still schema-invalid after alias folding
body:
## Problem

`build_from_json()` validates the extraction, warns about edges that are missing a
required field, and then adds them to the graph anyway. The malformed edge is
serialized into `graph.json`, so the persisted graph can violate Graphify's own
edge schema — even though the build already reported the violation.

```python
from graphify.build import build_from_json

extraction = {
    "nodes": [
        {"id": "a", "label": "a", "file_type": "document", "source_file": "a.md"},
        {"id": "b", "label": "b", "file_type": "document", "source_file": "b.md"},
    ],
    "edges": [
        # relation intentionally missing
        {"source": "a", "target": "b", "confidence": "INFERRED", "source_file": "a.md"},
    ],
}

G = build_from_json(extraction)
print(list(G.edges(data=True)))
```

Before this patch:

```text
[graphify] Extraction warning (1 issues): Edge 0 missing required field 'relation'
[('a', 'b', {'confidence': 'INFERRED', 'source_file': 'a.md', '_src': 'a', '_tgt': 'b'})]
```

On a real mixed code/docs corpus this left 41 of 3,556 persisted edges without a
`relation`, so consumers that dispatch on edge semantics could silently degrade.

## Fix

* Fold the legacy edge aliases (`relationship`, `type`) into `relation` on a copy of
  the extraction, without mutating the caller's dict. This is done *before*
  validation, so a legacy edge is never dropped for the wrong reason.
* After canonicalization, an edge that is still missing a required field
  (`source`, `target`, `relation`, `confidence`, `source_file`) — or that is not an
  object at all — is **not** added to the graph.
* Report the drop explicitly, so the warning no longer implies the edge survived:

  ```text
  [graphify] Extraction warning (1 issues): Edge 0 missing required field 'relation'
  [graphify] Dropped 1 schema-invalid edge(s) - missing required field(s): 'relation' (1)
  ```

Edges pointing at external/stdlib nodes keep their existing behavior: they are
skipped silently, because a dangling import is expected and not a schema error.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_build.py`:

* an edge missing `relation` is not persisted (the issue's reproducer),
* valid edges next to a dropped one are unaffected,
* the drop is reported on stderr together with the missing field name,
* dangling edges are not reported as dropped,
* a legacy `relationship` key is folded to `relation` and the edge survives,
* alias folding does not mutate the caller's extraction.

```text
$ pytest tests -q
299 passed, 2 warnings
```

## Scope

Only `build_from_json()` changes; node handling, hyperedges and degree-0 pruning are
untouched. The rule is "fail closed for records that are still schema-invalid after
canonicalization" — Graphify does not guess a missing relationship type.

title: fix(extract): persist resolver degradation status
Add guidance to SKILL.md on when building a graph is (and isn't) worth it
body:
Ran the skill end-to-end today (sample corpus + a real ~200-file project) and it delivered genuinely good results — correct AST extraction, accurate cross-referencing between code and doc semantic layers, and the cohesion/god-node/surprising-connections analysis surfaced real findings (an architectural smell, a cross-doc duplicate derivation, etc.).

One gap: the skill has no guidance on *when the full pipeline is worth its cost* vs. when a plain code search would do. In practice:

- A single targeted lookup ("what calls `X`", "where is `Y` defined") on an ordinary-sized codebase is answered just as well, instantly and for free, by `grep`/`ripgrep`/`Read`. Building the graph first is pure overhead for that case — AST extraction is fast and free, but semantic extraction on docs dispatches subagents and can take minutes and tens of thousands of tokens, even for a modest doc set.
- The graph earns its cost when: there will be many repeated questions (amortized build cost), the corpus is large/unfamiliar and the user needs orientation, the question needs cross-file/cross-type links text search can't see (doc ↔ code, cross-doc semantic duplicates), or the question is structural (cohesion, bridging nodes, import cycles) rather than textual.

Right now the skill (reasonably) defaults to building on `/graphify <path>`, which is fine when the user explicitly asks for that — but when an agent is deciding *on its own* whether to reach for graphify vs. a direct search for a one-off question, there's no steering in SKILL.md toward the cheaper option first.

Suggested addition: a short "is a graph worth it here" section before the build steps, something like:

> Building costs real time and tokens: AST extraction on code is free and fast, but semantic extraction on docs/papers/images dispatches subagents (minutes, tens of thousands of tokens), and a full pipeline run is overhead you pay once per corpus state. Don't pay it reflexively.
>
> **If `graphify-out/graph.json` already exists for this corpus, always query it** rather than re-deriving the answer by reading files or rebuilding — that cost is already sunk and querying is cheap.
>
> **If no graph exists yet, check whether the request is a single, targeted lookup a plain code search would answer just as well** — "where is X defined", "what calls Y", "find the function that does Z" on a codebase of ordinary size. For these, grep/ripgrep/Read is faster, free, and exact. Say so and just search directly; offer to build the full graph instead only if the user wants it.
>
> **Building (or updating) the graph earns its cost when:**
> - You expect many future questions against this corpus — the build cost amortizes.
> - The corpus is large or unfamiliar and the user needs orientation (god nodes, communities).
> - The question needs cross-file or cross-type connections text search can't see.
> - The question is structural/architectural, not textual.

Happy to turn this into a PR against SKILL.md if that's useful.

Separately filed one small fix noticed during testing as a PR: #4830 (`graphify query --help` ran a literal query instead of showing usage). The other thing I initially flagged (hyperedge `members`/`nodes` field mismatch) turned out to already be intentionally handled in `build.py` (#1561) — not a bug, so no PR for that one.

title: fix(cli): graphify query --help/-h shows usage instead of running a literal query
body:
## Summary

Filed alongside #4829. While testing the skill I ran `graphify query --help` expecting usage, and it instead ran an actual BFS traversal of the graph using the literal text `--help` as the question.

I initially assumed this was a plain bug, but on reading `__main__._run_cli` it's clearly a deliberate choice: `--help`/`-h` is intentionally **not** intercepted for free-text commands (`query`, `explain`, `path`, `save-result`, ...), because a genuine free-text question can legitimately contain `-h` or `--help` as a substring (e.g. *"how do I get --help output from this API"*), and that must still run as the literal question, not get swallowed into a help screen.

This PR narrows that gap rather than overriding the existing design: it only intercepts the **exact, standalone** case — `graphify query --help` or `graphify query -h` with no other arguments — and leaves everything else (including a longer question that happens to contain `-h`/`--help` as a substring) running exactly as before. Added a regression test for that substring case specifically so this doesn't regress back into over-matching.

## About the second thing mentioned in #4829

The "`members` vs `nodes` hyperedge field" warning I originally flagged as a bug turned out, on reading `build.py`, to be **working as intended** — `_normalize_hyperedge_members` already exists specifically to fold that alias (tracked as #1561 in the comment), with a deliberate warning rather than a silent fix so producers notice and correct their output. No change needed there; not included in this PR.

## Testing

- Added `test_query_cli_lone_help_flag_prints_usage` (covers both `--help` and `-h`, confirms no query actually runs).
- Added `test_query_cli_question_containing_help_text_still_runs` (regression guard: a real question containing `--help` as a substring still executes as a query, not swallowed as help).
- `tests/test_query_cli.py` and `tests/test_cli_help.py`: all passing.
- Full suite: 8285 passed, 39 pre-existing failures (all in `test_terraform*.py`, confirmed via `git stash` that they fail identically on `v8` with no changes applied — looks like a missing optional HCL-parsing dependency in my local env, unrelated to this change).

title: extract --out <dir>: semantic cache never saved, docs missing from manifest (relative source_file resolved against --out)
body:
**Version:** graphify 0.9.7 (uv tool install graphifyy), macOS, `--backend claude-cli`

**Problem**
`graphify extract <dir> --out <other>` never reuses the semantic cache. Every run re-extracts every doc and reports `0 files cached/unchanged`. `<other>/graphify-out/cache/semantic/` stays empty.

**Cause**
The LLM returns `source_file` relative to the scanned dir (e.g. `n1.md`). In `__main__.py` (extract), two places treat it as a path under the output root (`out_root`) instead:

1. `cache.save_semantic_cache(..., root=out_root)` builds `Path(root) / "n1.md"`, `is_file()` is false, so the entry is skipped. Nothing is saved.
2. `_sem_extracted` (used to build `_manifest_files`) is compared against the absolute paths in `files_by_type`. A relative `source_file` never matches, so no doc gets a `semantic_hash` in `manifest.json` and `detect_incremental` re-queues all of them.

When `--out` is omitted (`out_root == target`), (1) resolves correctly.

**Repro**
```
mkdir vault out cwd
for i in 1 2 3; do echo "# Note $i. Alice uses Redis." > vault/n$i.md; done
cd cwd
graphify extract ../vault --out ../out --backend claude-cli --max-concurrency 1   # run twice
```
Run 2: `incremental summary: 0 files cached/unchanged, 3 re-extracted`, tokens spent again, `out/graphify-out/cache/semantic/` empty, `manifest.json` is `{}`.

**Workaround**
Omit `--out` and set `GRAPHIFY_OUT=/abs/path/graphify-out`. Run 2 then reports `3 files cached/unchanged, 0 re-extracted` and spends no tokens. On a ~106-doc vault this took a nightly run from ~340k in / ~66k out tokens to ~17k / ~7k.

**Suggested fix**
Resolve relative `source_file` against `target` (the scanned dir) in `save_semantic_cache` and when building `_sem_extracted`, while keeping the cache key relative to `out_root` as `check_semantic_cache` already does.

title: fix(skill): stop a stale .graphify_partial.txt from poisoning the next build (#4814)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4814 and #4807. Both are the same missing lifecycle on `graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt`.

Step B3.5 writes the file, listing sources a subagent read only partway. Step 9 reads it so those sources stay unstamped, then deletes it. `--update` stops at Step 8, so its list outlived the run. A later full build that served the doc from the semantic cache never ran B3.5 and never rewrote the list. Step 9 read the stale entry and left a doc it served in full unstamped, so the next `--update` re-queued it.

Before, on the reproduction from the issue:

```text
$ python stale_list_repro.py
after the full build, next --update queues: ["long.md"]
```

After:

```text
$ python stale_list_repro.py
after the full build, next --update queues: []
```

The same script with the list removed also printed `[]`, which is how the list became the suspect.

The second half is #4807. An `--update` has one manifest save, in its merge block. It passed no partial set, so a doc B3.5 had just flagged as partly read was stamped as done and never retried.

```diff
 tools/skillgen/fragments/core/core.md
   Step B0
+    Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)

 tools/skillgen/fragments/references/shared/update.md
   run start
+    rm -f graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt
   merge, manifest save
+    _partial = <read the list>
+    _stamped_manifest_files(..., partial_source_files=_partial)
+    _pf.unlink(missing_ok=True)
```

Both hooks delete before any writer runs, so any list a reader sees was written by this run. The update path has no Step 9, so its manifest save both consumes the list and removes it.

Delete-at-start was picked over a run id or an mtime check by measuring all three against the real rendered blocks. Delete-at-start and run-id both score 7/7 on the supported scenarios. Run-id adds a persistent id file and a header every reader has to filter. Mtime freshness scores 6/7 and fails when a stale list carries the same timestamp as this run's `.graphify_detect.json`.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant is that a doc is left unstamped only when a subagent read it partway **in this run**. Step 9's partial set is a subset of what this run's B3.5 wrote.

The start hooks run before B3.5, so any list a reader sees was written after them. The update path reads the list at its only manifest save and deletes it there. This PR deletes at the end of that save. The follow-up #4811 keeps the list longer, because a merge re-run and Step 9 after an update also need it. That is a separate change with its own tests.

Generated state: all 134 skill artifacts are regenerated from the fragments and `--check` passes. No graph, cache, or manifest format changes, so nothing to migrate.

- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Runbook text, regenerated artifacts, and one test file. Reverting `0f70bd86` or `b5d4a62d` restores the previous behavior; `2af27a8e` is test-only. A stale list already on disk heals at the next run's start.

**Blast Radius:** skill-only, across all 13 hosts.

- Concurrent builds on one `graphify-out/` remain unsafe. Step 9's cleanup is a single global `rm`, so a second run can remove a live run's list. `test_another_runs_step9_destroys_the_list_for_every_candidate` pins it. This change does not try to make the list run-scoped.
- The `runid` and `fresh` policies are harness models, not shipped code. They exist to justify the choice and are exercised only there.
- Not tested on Windows. The change is `unlink` on a fixed relative path and `rm -f` on a fixed path.

## How was this tested?

Commands run, with output:

```text
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_partial_list_lifecycle.py -q
34 passed

$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider
9000 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed in 559.91s (0:09:19)

$ .venv/bin/python -m tools.skillgen --check
check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/
$ .venv/bin/python -m tools.skillgen --audit-coverage
audit-coverage OK: every per-host v8 heading single-homes in that host's render.
$ .venv/bin/python -m tools.skillgen --schema-singleton
schema-singleton OK: the file_type enum is the six-value superset everywhere.
$ .venv/bin/python -m tools.skillgen --monolith-roundtrip
monolith-roundtrip OK: each monolith matches v8 modulo the enum unification.
$ .venv/bin/python -m tools.skillgen --always-on-roundtrip
always-on-roundtrip OK: each always_on/*.md reproduces its former constant byte for byte.

$ .venv/bin/ruff check tests/test_partial_list_lifecycle.py tools/skillgen
All checks passed!
$ .venv/bin/pyright tests/test_partial_list_lifecycle.py
0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations
```

The new test file runs each lifecycle through the real B0, B3.5, B3 cache-save, and Step 9 blocks, and reads the outcome from the real `detect_incremental` and `check_semantic_cache`:

```text
policy   cluster_only  coarse_clock  code_only_update  control  genuine_partial  interrupted_run  reported_bug
baseline FAIL          FAIL          FAIL              PASS     PASS             FAIL             FAIL
delete   PASS          PASS          PASS              PASS     PASS             PASS             PASS
runid    PASS          PASS          PASS              PASS     PASS             PASS             PASS
fresh    PASS          FAIL          PASS              PASS     PASS             PASS             PASS
```

Three end-to-end tests use the shipped fragments with no policy injected:

- `test_the_shipped_runbook_drops_a_stale_list_before_step9` runs the issue's reproduction.
- `test_a_half_read_doc_on_the_update_path_is_not_stamped` runs the real manifest-save tail from `references/update.md` and asserts the doc is re-queued and the list is removed.
- `test_the_shipped_update_merge_block_runs_with_a_partial_list` runs the whole merge block through bash with the list on disk. This is the path that evaluates the list read, so a quoting error in the `python -c` wrapper fails the test instead of shipping.

Environment note: the suite ran with the repo's `.venv` because the system Python has no numpy. `graphify update .` was run after the change; `graphify-out/` is gitignored.

title: fix(detect): prune a linked worktree whose main checkout is in the scan root (#4683)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4683. A workspace folder holding a repo and a linked worktree of it as siblings (`ws/app/` + `ws/app-feature/`) was indexed twice, so every file in the worktree counted as a second copy. On the reporter's ~78k-node graph this added ~13.8k duplicate nodes, and the copy's paths surfaced in `GRAPH_REPORT.md` community hubs.

Neither existing guard reaches this layout. The name-based rules require a `.worktrees/` or `<dot>/worktrees/` directory name, and `.git/info/exclude` only exists when the scan root is itself a repo. A linked worktree is still unambiguous on disk. Its `.git` is a file pointing at `<main>/.git/worktrees/<name>`, and that gitdir's `commondir` points back to `<main>/.git`, so the main checkout's root is the common dir's parent. When that root resolves inside the scan root, the directory is pruned and recorded in `pruned_noise_dirs` like other noise prunes.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a corpus file is indexed once, and a directory is pruned only when it is provably a second checkout of a repo already under the scan root, never for carrying a `.git` file alone.

The prune fires only when the worktree's `commondir` resolves to a `<name>/.git` directory whose parent (the main worktree root) lies inside the resolved scan root. A submodule's `.git` file points at `<super>/.git/modules/<name>` with no `commondir`, so it is untouched. A bare repo's shared git dir is not named `.git` and has no main worktree, so its worktrees stay indexed. A moved or deleted main checkout leaves `commondir` dangling, and the worktree stays indexed as the only copy. Scanning the worktree itself still indexes it, and no git subprocess is spawned since the marker files are read directly. No persisted state changes, the pruned dir never enters `files`, so `detect_incremental` and the manifest see the same corpus a hand-built ignore rule would produce.

uv run pytest tests/test_detect.py -q          # 330 passed
uv run pytest tests/ -q                        # 8554 passed; 18 pre-existing

title: fix(export): report a partial backup as no backup and retry it (#3769)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #3769. `backup_if_protected` reported an incomplete backup as a successful one. Per-artifact `shutil.copy2` failures were swallowed, so a dated snapshot whose `graph.json` never copied still printed "backed up. Graph" and returned the backup path, leaving a stale snapshot to survive the next overwrite with no warning. The same-day early return also trusted `graph.json` alone, so a snapshot missing a sidecar counted as complete forever.

The copy loop now collects failed artifact names, warns on stderr naming the file(s) that failed, and returns `None`. The early return only fires when `graph.json` is identical AND every existing source artifact is present in the snapshot, so a partial snapshot is retried on the next call. Best-effort behavior is unchanged, and the function still never raises and never blocks the overwrite.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant this guards is the "protected artifacts are preserved across rebuilds" contract. `backup_if_protected` must not report a backup that is missing the artifacts it exists to preserve, and must keep its "never raises, never blocks the write" guarantee.

- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Any failed artifact makes the call report `None` and warn, whether the file is `graph.json` or a sidecar. A snapshot that kept `graph.json` but lost `cost.json` counts as incomplete and is retried on the next call. All current callers ignore the return value, so the stricter `None` only affects reporting and API consumers.

uv run pytest tests/ -q                         # full suite, see note below

```

The two new tests monkeypatch `shutil.copy2` to fail on a chosen artifact, so they do not depend on filesystem permissions or the running user (the issue's chmod trick is silently bypassed when run as root).

title: Cache the claude backend system prompt via Anthropic prompt caching
body:
Summary

extract --backend claude issues one messages.create call per file, and each call re-sends the fixed _extraction_system prompt at full input price. Marking the system block with Anthropic prompt caching (cache_control: ephemeral) bills that shared prefix at ~0.1× on reads after the first call. Output is unchanged — this is a billing/latency optimization only.

Where

graphify/llm.py, _call_claude() — system= is passed as a plain string, so the extraction system prompt is re-ingested on every per-file call.

Proposed change
diff
     resp = client.messages.create(
         model=model,
         max_tokens=max_tokens,
-        system=_extraction_system(deep=deep_mode),
+        system=[{
+            "type": "text",
+            "text": _extraction_system(deep=deep_mode),
+            "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"},
+        }],
         messages=[{"role": "user", "content": _anthropic_content(user_message, images or [])}],
     )

The anthropic SDK already in use supports the content-block form of system with cache_control.

Why it helps

_extraction_system is identical across all per-file calls (only deep toggles). On a repo with N files the system prefix is paid N× at 1×; with caching it’s one write (1.25×) + (N−1) reads (0.1×) → ~90% off the system portion of input.

Caveats (for reviewers)
Only the system block is cacheable here; per-file user content isn’t reused.
Needs the system prompt ≥ the model’s min cacheable length (e.g. 512 tokens on recent Sonnet/Opus); below that it silently no-ops (cache_*_input_tokens = 0), no error.
With --max-concurrency > 1 the first wave of parallel calls misses (a cache entry is only available after the first response begins) — still a net win on multi-file runs.
5-min ephemeral TTL refreshes on each hit, so it stays warm through an active extraction.
Scoped to the native claude backend; the Bedrock path (system=[{"text": ...}]) uses a different caching mechanism and could be a follow-up.
Impact

Billing/latency only. No behavior change.

+    rm -f graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt
   merge, manifest save
+    _partial = <read the list>
+    _stamped_manifest_files(..., partial_source_files=_partial)
+    _pf.unlink(missing_ok=True)
```

Both hooks delete before any writer runs, so any list a reader sees was written by this run. The update path has no Step 9, so its manifest save both consumes the list and removes it.

Delete-at-start was picked over a run id or an mtime check by measuring all three against the real rendered blocks. Delete-at-start and run-id both score 7/7 on the supported scenarios. Run-id adds a persistent id file and a header every reader has to filter. Mtime freshness scores 6/7 and fails when a stale list carries the same timestamp as this run's `.graphify_detect.json`.

title: fix(skill): stop an --update re-read from stamping a doc whose chunk failed (#4811)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4811. An `--update` marks a changed doc as done when its chunk failed, so the doc is never re-queued and the graph keeps its pre-edit nodes.

The sequence: the merge block reads this run's extraction from `graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json`, stamps the manifest from it (#2015/#1948), then overwrites the same file with the whole merged graph so Steps 4-8 can read it. From that moment the file no longer means "what this run produced" — it is mostly old nodes from `graph.json`, with nothing on disk saying which is which. Anything that re-reads it as this run's output stamps the doc:

- a second run of the merge block in the same update (e.g. after a later step fails);
- core Step 9, which agents run after an update (#837).

The fix writes a snapshot of this run's extraction, plus the partial set B3.5 wrote, before the merge overwrites the working file. The merge block's manifest save and Step 9 both stamp from that snapshot. The partial set travels with the payload, so the #4807/#4814 exclusion still holds after the merge block deletes `.graphify_partial.txt`.

Three commits, each independently revertable:

1. `test(skill): pin the #4811 stamped-failed-doc gap` — 12 scenarios over the real rendered blocks, red on the current runbook.
2. `fix(skill): snapshot this run's extraction before the update merge` — the writer, the lifecycle, and the merge-block save. Turns the merge-rerun scenarios green.
3. `fix(skill): stamp Step 9 from this run's extraction snapshot` — the second reader.

**Stacked on #4832** (`fix/4814-partial-list-lifecycle`, currently open). That PR adds the run-start delete hooks this change extends, and its list-consumption line is the reason the partial set has to travel inside the snapshot. Until #4832 merges, this PR's diff includes its three commits.

**Design choice.** I measured eight candidate designs against the same 12-scenario matrix (each driven through the real rendered blocks and scored with the real `detect_incremental`):

```text
policy                     S1   S2   S3   S4   S5   S6   S7   S8   S9  S10  S11  S12   score
baseline                    X    X    X    X   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok    X   7/12
snapshot at merge, raw, list kept
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  12/12
snapshot at merge, self-contained  <- chosen
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  12/12
snapshot at merge, no start delete
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok    X   ok   ok   ok    X   ok  10/12
stamp from .graphify_semantic.json, list kept
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  12/12
stamp from .graphify_semantic.json, shipped list lifecycle
                           ok   ok    X    X   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  10/12
snapshot gated by a per-run id
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  12/12
snapshot at the producer (Part C)
                           ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok   ok  12/12
```

S1/S2 = failed chunk then merge re-run / Step 9. S3/S4 = partly read doc. S5/S6 = success controls. S7 = failed update then a clean full build. S8 code-only. S9 deletion-only. S10 full-build failed-chunk control. S11 second update after a failure. S12 precision.

Why the chosen design over the others:

- The two smallest fixes (semantic-only, and raw snapshot + keep the list) both require reverting #4832's "consume and remove the list" line. The self-contained snapshot leaves that PR's list lifecycle untouched, so the two changes do not conflict.
- S7 and S11 are why the snapshot needs delete-at-start: without it, a snapshot from a failed update poisons a later successful full build and a later successful update.
- The run-id design scores the same but adds a persistent file plus a filter every reader must apply — the cost #4832 measured and rejected for the partial list.
- The producer design scores the same but edits the shared core Part C block (all 13 hosts, full builds included) and still needs a merge-side writer for the deletion-only path.

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: a file is stamped only when a value that describes **this run** says it produced output, and that value cannot be rewritten before every reader has read it. Step 9 and the merge block now read the same immutable snapshot; the snapshot is written once per run, before the merge, and cleared at every run start.

title: Import Cycles reports "None detected" for every two-file import cycle in the default (undirected) build
body:
### Summary

In the default undirected build, `build_from_json` drops the reverse-direction duplicate when a file pair carries the same relation in both directions (#1061). For `imports_from`, that pair *is* a two-file import cycle. The second leg never reaches the graph, so `find_import_cycles` can't see the cycle, and `GRAPH_REPORT.md` states **"None detected"**.

The test suite already accounts for the collapse. The `_cycles` helper in `tests/test_type_only_import_cycles.py` notes that "in the default undirected graph two module edges between one file pair collapse to a single stored edge", and `test_a_real_runtime_cycle_is_still_reported` runs only with `directed=True`. The report doesn't account for it: it asserts an absence that the default graph can't support. Two-file cycles are also a common shape in practice: bidirectional ORM entity relations (for example TypeORM `@ManyToMany`/`@OneToMany` pairs) produce one routinely.

### Environment

- `graphifyy` 0.9.89 (PyPI), and `v8` @ `0a8cd4e` (0.9.97), installed from a clean checkout
- Linux 6.17, Python 3.12.3
- `graphify update .`, code only, no LLM backend configured

### Minimal reproduction

```ts
// src/a.ts
import { B } from './b';
export class A { b?: B; }
```

```ts
// src/b.ts
import { A } from './a';
export class B { a?: A; }
```

```
graphify update .
```

**Actual** (identical on 0.9.89 and v8 HEAD):

`GRAPH_REPORT.md`:
```
## Import Cycles
- None detected.
```

`graph.json` (`"directed": false`). The symbol-level `imports` edges survive in both directions, but only one file-level `imports_from` edge does:
```
imports       a.ts -> B      (src/a.ts)
imports       b.ts -> A      (src/b.ts)
imports_from  a.ts -> b.ts   (src/a.ts)
              # b.ts -> a.ts imports_from: dropped
```

**Expected:** `- 2-file cycle: src/a.ts -> src/b.ts -> src/a.ts`. At minimum, the section shouldn't report "None detected" when the graph type makes two-file cycles undetectable.

**Real-world occurrence:** `lujakob/nestjs-realworld-example-app` @ `c1c2cc4`. `src/user/user.entity.ts` and `src/article/article.entity.ts` import each other (TypeORM `@ManyToMany` / `@OneToMany` relations), and the report says "None detected".

### Where

`graphify/build.py` on v8, around L1867:

```python
if not G.is_directed() and G.has_edge(src, tgt):
    ...
    if reverse and existing_rel == incoming_rel:
        continue
```

Keeping the first-seen direction is the right call for #1061. The problem is only that the dropped leg is the one fact cycle detection needs.

### Possible fixes

I'm happy to send a PR, with a regression test, for whichever approach you prefer:

1. **Stamp the surviving edge.** When the dropped reverse edge is `imports_from`/`re_exports`, and is neither `type_only` nor `deferred`, mark the surviving edge (for example `reverse_import: true`), and have `find_import_cycles` add the reverse leg for stamped edges. One stored edge is kept, #1061's direction guarantee is unchanged, and other consumers of `graph.json` see no format change.
2. **Detect cycles on the extraction edges** (before the build) instead of on the built graph.
3. **Minimal:** when the graph is undirected, say in the report that two-file cycles can't be detected, instead of "None detected".

I lean towards (1). It's the narrowest change that makes the default report correct.

### Related

- #1061: the reverse-duplicate drop this interacts with
- #2849: same-direction collisions in *directed* builds; this is the opposite-direction case in undirected builds
- #3495: no CLI opt-in for a directed build, so CLI users can't currently work around this
- #2489: proposed cycle detection via strongly connected components, which needs direction preserved to work

_Investigated and reproduced with the help of Claude Code; I've reviewed the findings above._

title: [Feature]: Add MQL5 (MetaTrader 5) language support via tree-sitter
body:
### Problem or use case

Many algorithmic trading codebases are written in MQL5. Currently Graphify has no grammar for it, so these files are either ignored or only partially parsed as C++. This produces incomplete graphs (missing functions, call edges, classes, inputs, properties, etc.) for large multi-project MQL5 bases.

MQL5 is C++-like but has its own keywords and constructs (`input`, `sinput`, `#property`, `OnTick`, `OnInit`, `OnCalculate`, trading-specific types, etc.), so the existing C++ extractor is not sufficient.

### Proposed solution

Add an MQL5 extractor following the existing language-addition process described in `ARCHITECTURE.md`:

1. Use the existing community tree-sitter grammar:  
   **https://github.com/mskelton/tree-sitter-mql5**  
   (an extension of tree-sitter-cpp that adds MQL5 syntax). There are also modern forks (e.g. https://github.com/m0n99/tree-sitter-mql5).

2. Register `.mq5` and `.mqh` extensions.
3. Extract functions, classes, methods, includes, call edges, and key MQL5 constructs where feasible.
4. Add a fixture + tests in the usual place (`tests/fixtures/` + `tests/test_languages.py`).

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Area

Extraction or language support

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

No breaking impact expected.

Adding MQL5 support is additive:

- Node/edge IDs: only new nodes/edges for .mq5 / .mqh files. Existing languages are unaffected.
- Cache semantics: unchanged. Incremental updates will simply include the new file types when they change.
- graph.json schema: no change (same node/edge structure).
- Generated skills / MCP output: no change in format or behavior.
- Incremental updates: work the same way — only re-extract changed MQL5 files.

### Additional context

_No response_

title: fix(build): report two-file import cycles in the default undirected build
body:
Fixes #4839

In the default undirected build, `build_from_json` drops the reverse-direction duplicate of a same-relation pair (#1061). For `imports_from` / `re_exports` that dropped edge is the second leg of a two-file cycle, so `find_import_cycles` never saw it and the report said "None detected".

What changed:

- `build.py`: when the #1061 branch drops a reverse `imports_from`/`re_exports` that isn't `type_only` or `deferred`, it sets `reverse_import: true` on the edge it keeps. Same edges as before, first-seen direction still wins. Directed builds never hit this branch.
- `analyze.py`: `find_import_cycles` adds the reverse file leg for a stamped edge. The forward leg still skips `type_only`/`deferred` like before.
- `watch.py`: the stamp is really the target file's import, so the incremental reconcile treats it that way. If the target file gets re-extracted or deleted, the stamp is cleared (the rebuild adds it back if the import is still there). If only the kept edge's own file is re-extracted, the stamp moves to the fresh edge. Without this, a hook rebuild after `b.py` stops importing `a.py` kept reporting the cycle, and editing `a.py` alone made a real cycle disappear. I also pulled the existing eviction condition into a small `_edge_evicted` helper so both checks use the same rule.

Tests: new `tests/test_undirected_two_file_import_cycle.py` covers a TS and a Python two-file cycle in the undirected build, a one-way import, a 3-file ring next to a 2-file cycle, `import type` / `TYPE_CHECKING` reverse legs (no cycle), other relations / deferred / type-only reverse edges not stamping, the directed build being unchanged, a graph.json round trip, and the two incremental cases. The existing type-only cycle tests pass unchanged.

Ran the full suite on 3.10, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 against unmodified v8. Failures are the same on both trees (yaml extraction on 3.10, `safe_fetch` network tests, etc.), no new ones. I also ran the real CLI (`graphify update .` and then `graphify cluster-only .` from the saved graph.json) on small Python, TS and JS two-file cycle projects. Before: "None detected". After: `- 2-file cycle: a.py -> b.py -> a.py` (and the same for TS and JS). The one-way, 3-file ring and TYPE_CHECKING projects give the same output as before.

One thing I left alone: an `imports_from` one way plus a `re_exports` back is a different-relation collision. The later edge already overwrites the pair there, on v8 too, so that shape still isn't reported. That's separate from this issue. Also, a graph.json written before this change doesn't have the stamp, so `cluster-only` on it still says "None detected" until the next `graphify update`.

Written with help from Grok Bot; I reviewed and tested it.

title: fix(go): type a receiver bound with var and a composite literal
body:
## Bug

Go's receiver type table (used to type a method call's receiver, e.g. `g.Greet()`, for cross-file resolution) recognized `g := Greeter{}` (a short var declaration bound to a composite literal) as evidence that `g` holds a `Greeter`. It did not recognize the equivalent `var g = Greeter{}` form: a type-less `var_spec` node has no explicit `type` field, and the table only ever read that field, never falling back to infer the type from the composite-literal value the way the `:=` form did.

The practical effect: a call's resolution silently depended on which of two semantically identical declaration spellings the author used. `var g = Greeter{}; g.Greet()` left `Greet` looking like it had one fewer caller than `g := Greeter{}; g.Greet()` would have given it.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via self-audit of `graphify/extractors/go.py`. No open or closed PR touches `_go_receiver_type_table`'s composite-literal inference.

## Fix

Factored the composite-literal inference shared by both shapes into a new helper, `_go_inferred_composite_bindings`, and applied it to a typeless `var_spec` the same way it was already applied to `short_var_declaration`. `var x = T{}` and `var x = &T{}` now resolve exactly like their `:=` counterparts. Bumped the AST cache schema so existing caches rebuild with the fix.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_go_receiver_member_calls.py`:
- `test_a_var_declaration_with_an_inferred_composite_literal_types_the_receiver`
- `test_a_var_declaration_with_an_inferred_address_of_composite_literal_types_the_receiver`
- `test_a_var_declaration_with_a_non_literal_value_resolves_to_nothing` (negative control: a type-less `var` bound to a call result, not a composite literal, still resolves to nothing, exactly like the `:=` form)

## Verification
