title: fix(pascal): recognize inherited and inline form component blocks
body:
## Bug

The Lazarus/Delphi form (`.lfm`/`.dfm`) nesting parser only treated a line starting with `object` as opening a component block. Real form files also declare components with `inherited` (an ancestor form overriding one of its own components) and `inline` (an embedded frame), using the identical `Name: Class ... end` shape. Those blocks never pushed onto the containment stack, so their closing `end` either silently did nothing or, worse, popped a level the block never opened — misattaching every sibling that followed to the wrong ancestor, and letting event handlers declared inside the block bind to the wrong component.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via self-audit of `graphify/extractors/pascal_forms.py`. Checked `gh pr list` for pascal_forms/lazarus/delphi form/lfm/dfm — the only related open PR (#3119) is about resolving calls through a global singleton, unrelated to form-block parsing.

## Fix

`obj_re` in both `extract_lazarus_form` and `extract_delphi_form` now matches `object`, `inherited`, or `inline` as the block-opening keyword, so all three correctly push onto the containment stack.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_pascal.py`, covering both `extract_lazarus_form` and `extract_delphi_form` with a shared fixture (new `tests/fixtures/sample_inherited.lfm` / `.dfm`) containing an inherited block, an inline frame, and a plain object sibling after both:
- Asserts the sibling still nests under the right parent.
- Asserts an event handler declared inside the inherited block binds to that block, not to an ancestor.

## Verification

- Confirmed the bug pre-fix: an `inherited`/`inline` block's contents and trailing siblings misattached without the fix.
- Full suite: `2 failed, 8894 passed, 81 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 2 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py` and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: fix(commonlisp): bind a forward referenced superclass to its local node
body:
## Bug

`ensure_class_ref` (resolving a Common Lisp superclass name to a node id) checked a candidate only against `seen_ids`, which fills in as `_walk_forms` reaches each `defclass` form in file order. A subclass listed above its own parent in the same file — e.g. `(defclass child (parent) ())` appearing before `(defclass parent () ())` — asked before the parent's node existed, so the check wrongly treated the parent as an external, cross file class and minted a sourceless stub for it instead of binding to the real local class.

The real `parent` class then got added later under a different, file qualified id, splitting one class into two disconnected nodes with the `inherits` edge pointing at the wrong (stub) one.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via self-audit of `graphify/extractors/commonlisp.py`. Checked the open commonlisp PRs (#3543, #3544, #3545) and closed #3001/#3131 — all of them call `ensure_class_ref` for a different use (specializer resolution in `defmethod` parameters, or its original introduction); none touch the forward reference ordering in the check itself.

## Fix

Added `_prescan_class_names`, which walks the file up front to collect every name defined via `defclass`, mirroring `_walk_forms`'s own recursion rule (stop at a recognized top level form, descend into anything else) so it finds a `defclass` nested in a wrapper macro the same way the real walk later will. `ensure_class_ref` now also treats a name in that set as local, so a forward referenced same file superclass binds correctly regardless of where in the file its `defclass` form sits. A true cross file superclass still correctly mints a sourceless stub.

## Tests

Added `test_cl_forward_referenced_superclass_binds_to_local_node` to `tests/test_languages.py`: a subclass listed above its own parent, asserting the parent mints exactly one node and that the `inherits` edge targets that local node (not a stub).

## Verification

- Confirmed the bug pre-fix: before the fix, the forward referenced parent split into two nodes, with the `inherits` edge pointing at the sourceless stub.
- Full suite: `2 failed, 8891 passed, 81 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 2 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py` and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: fix(solidity): emit uses edges for a free function using set
body:
## Bug

The `using_directive` branch (building `uses` edges for Solidity's `using X for T;` syntax) only read direct children of the directive node to find the name to link to. That covers `using Lib for T;`, where the name sits directly under the directive as a `type_alias`/`identifier`/`user_defined_type`. But Solidity >=0.8.13 also allows binding free functions directly: `using {f1, f2} for T;`. tree-sitter-solidity wraps each name here in its own `using_alias` child instead, one level deeper, so the direct-child scan saw nothing and silently dropped the whole directive — no edge at all, for either function.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via self-audit of `graphify/extractors/solidity.py`/`sln.py`. `sln.py`'s only relevant open-area bug (solution-folder detection) is already covered by PR #3270 — no independent fix was written there. Searched `gh pr list`/`gh issue list` for "solidity", "using for", "using_directive", "using_alias" and found nothing touching this code path.

## Fix

In the `using_directive` branch, also collect `type_alias`/`identifier`/`user_defined_type` grandchildren nested under any `using_alias` child, then emit a `uses` edge for every name found (not just the first). The single-library form is untouched — same code path, no `using_alias` wrapper present for it.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_solidity_extractor.py`:
- `test_solidity_using_free_function_set_emits_uses_edges`: `using {freeAdd, freeSub} for uint;` now produces both `uses` edges.
- A control assertion added to the existing `test_solidity_types_imports_inheritance_overloads_and_modifiers` confirming the pre-existing `using Lib for uint;` single-library form still produces its `uses` edge.

## Verification

- Confirmed the bug pre-fix via a raw tree-sitter parse dump and `extract_solidity()` before/after: the free-function `using` set produced zero edges.
- Full suite: `2 failed, 8891 passed, 81 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 2 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py` and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: fix(powershell): strip the extension from a using module or assembly name
body:
## Bug

PowerShell's `using` statement handler (`extract_powershell`) took the last dotted segment of the value for all three forms: `using namespace X.Y`, `using module X`, `using assembly X`. That's correct for `namespace` (a dotted hierarchy where the last segment is the piece wanted), but wrong for `module`/`assembly`, whose value is a file or library name with an extension, not a namespace path. `using module Helpers.psm1` resolved the import edge to `psm1` (the extension) instead of `helpers`, and `using assembly System.Data.dll` resolved to `dll`.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via self-audit of `graphify/extractors/powershell.py` (`objc.py` had no genuine bug after a full read). Searched `gh pr list`/`gh issue list` for "using module"/"using namespace"/"module_tokens" — nothing claims this.

## Fix

Branch on the leading keyword: keep last-segment splitting for `namespace`, but strip the trailing extension for `module`/`assembly`, matching the convention already used elsewhere in this file for `Import-Module` and dot-sourcing.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_languages.py`:
- `test_powershell_using_module_with_extension_resolves_to_stem`
- `test_powershell_using_assembly_with_extension_resolves_to_stem`
- `test_powershell_using_namespace_keeps_last_segment` (control, confirms `namespace` behavior is unchanged)

## Verification

- Confirmed the bug pre-fix: `using module Helpers.psm1` resolved to `psm1`, `using assembly System.Data.dll` resolved to `dll`.
- Full suite: `2 failed, 8893 passed, 81 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 2 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py` and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: fix(verilog): give a SystemVerilog constructor its own node
body:
## Bug

`_SV_FUNC_RE` (SystemVerilog's function header regex) required an explicit return type before the method name (`function TYPE NAME(...)`). A `new` constructor never has one, and a plain `function foo(...);` with an implicit one-bit return also omits it, so `function new(...)` — the single most common method in a SystemVerilog class — matched nothing at all: no node, no `method` edge, and its parameter types were never extracted either.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via self-audit of `graphify/extractors/verilog.py` (`zig.py` had no genuine bug after a full read). Checked the two open verilog PRs (#3324, #3332) and closed #1218 for `_SV_FUNC_RE`/`function new` — zero hits.

## Fix

Made the return-type group in `_SV_FUNC_RE` optional, and guarded the return-type reference emission with `if return_type:` so it only runs when one was actually captured. Bumped the AST cache schema to 30 so existing caches rebuild with the fix.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_languages.py` (with a `function new(Config cfg);` constructor added to `tests/fixtures/sample.sv`):
- `test_systemverilog_constructor_method_gets_a_node` (regression: asserts the `method` edge and a `parameter_type` reference for the constructor)
- `test_systemverilog_explicit_return_type_function_still_works` (control for the adjacent working case, also asserting the return type isn't swallowed into the method name)

## Verification

- Confirmed the bug pre-fix via a standalone temp-file repro against the unmodified extractor: `function new(...)` produced no node at all.
- Full suite: `3 failed, 8891 passed, 81 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 3 failures are pre-existing flakes (`test_erlang_extractor.py`, `test_r_extractor.py`, the skill backtick test), unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: test(extract): cover --out semantic cache reuse and root pairing (#4831)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds regression coverage for #4831. No behaviour change: one line in `cli.py` makes an existing pair of roots explicit, everything else is tests.

The bug was a root mix-up. `extract <dir> --out <other>` passed `root=out_root` to both semantic cache calls. `save_semantic_cache` resolved the model's corpus-relative `source_file` against the output root, so `is_file()` failed for every group and nothing was written. The manifest join failed the same way, so no doc got a `semantic_hash` and run 2 re-extracted the whole docs corpus. The code fixes landed upstream in 0.9.17 (manifest stamping) and 0.9.20 (`root=target, cache_root=out_root`).

Two coverage gaps were left behind:

```text
                                                      existing suite
save path writes entries under --out                  covered, indirectly (#2927)
check path reads what the save wrote                  uncovered
a new caller omits cache_root                         uncovered
two runs with --out spend nothing on run 2            uncovered
```

The two additions map to the reporter's shapes:

```text
run 1                              run 2
3 docs dispatched                  no source change:       0 dispatched
3 entries under --out              doc rows removed:       0 dispatched, 3 cache hits
corpus stays clean                 both runs:              every doc stamped
```

and to the call sites:

```diff
 _check_semantic_cache(sem_paths_file, root=target, cache_root=out_root)
 _save_semantic_cache(nodes, root=target, cache_root=out_root, ...)
-check_semantic_cache(files, root, mode=cache_mode, ...)
+check_semantic_cache(files, root=root, cache_root=root, mode=cache_mode, ...)
```

### Commits

```text
3559d763  test(extract): assert --out reuses the semantic cache across runs (#4831)
d76d11cf  test(cache): pin both roots on every semantic cache call site (#4831)
```

## Evidence

Mutate the historical call shape back into `cli.py` (`root=out_root`, `cache_root` dropped) and run this branch:

| mutation | existing suite | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| save call, both roots dropped | 1 failure, incidental (#2927) | 3 failures |
| check call only | **0 failures** (56 green) | 2 failures |
| a new caller omits `cache_root` | 0 failures (35 green) | guard fails |

The check-side row is the gap: nothing in the suite consumed a cache entry the manifest had not already stamped, so the read path was never exercised under `--out`.

```text
tests/test_extract_out_semantic_cache.py   2 passed
tests/test_semantic_cache_call_sites.py    3 passed
full suite                                8971 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed (8m35s)
```

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: a path that names a source file resolves against the corpus root, the cache lives under the output root, and every call site states both. The runtime tests prove the composite behaviour; the static guard proves the pairing at call sites that runtime tests never reach.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.

- [x] Added a **regression test** or isolated boundary test.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Nothing persisted changes shape. No cache key, manifest key, schema, or file format is touched, so a revert restores the exact previous test count and behaviour.

**Blast Radius:** narrow. This is test-only apart from one explicit keyword pair.

- `cache-check` passes the corpus as both roots. It has no `--out`, so the call is byte-identical in effect; the keywords make the two roles visible.
- `save_semantic_cache` and `check_semantic_cache` keep their signatures. The 32 call sites inside generated skill snippets (single root, no `--out`) stay valid.

title: fix(pdf): scope converted text cache to the resolved source path

title: fix(analyze): preserve two-file import cycles in undirected graphs
body:
﻿## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4839.

The default undirected build intentionally keeps only one same-relation edge for a node pair (#1061). For a bidirectional `imports_from` / `re_exports` pair, that meant the reverse runtime import disappeared before `find_import_cycles()` ran, so a real two-file cycle was reported as `None detected`.

This keeps the existing undirected graph representation and preserves only the missing fact needed for analysis:

- when `build_from_json()` drops a reverse same-relation **runtime** `imports_from` / `re_exports` edge, it stamps the surviving edge with `reverse_runtime_import: true`;
- `find_import_cycles()` restores that reverse runtime direction in its temporary directed file graph;
- type-only and deferred reverse imports are not stamped as runtime dependencies;
- a surviving type-only/deferred edge can still carry a real runtime import in the opposite direction without manufacturing a cycle.

No graph schema version or public graph type changes.

## Verification & invariant

**Invariant:** if extraction contains runtime imports `A -> B` and `B -> A`, cycle analysis must retain enough information to report the two-file cycle even when the persisted NetworkX graph is undirected.

```text

FAILED: assert 0 == 1
```

GREEN:

```text

24 passed

188 passed
```

title: fix(go): resolve member calls on receivers typed from another package (#3368)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Refs #3368. The member-call fix for that issue (1695efae, `feat(go): resolve member calls through the receiver's declared type`, 0.9.89) resolves a receiver only when its type is declared in the **same package**. A receiver typed from **another package** still gets no `calls` edge, and that is the shape the issue is about: in Go, a dependency held as a field almost always has a type from another package (`*plugincontext.Provider`, `plugins.Client`).

Rebased onto v8 `f5155bad` (0.9.100), which has since landed fdd25f7b (a field typed through a struct declared in a sibling file), 61e864a7 (method values as `indirect_call`) and 1c4c3f2c (package-level `var` initialiser calls). This PR now also covers the combination of fdd25f7b and a cross-package field type, which is the layout Grafana actually uses.

### Why #3368 is not resolved on v8 (`f5155bad`)

`_go_single_type_name` drops a `qualified_type` on purpose:

> a `qualified_type` (`pkg.Greeter`) names a type no bare local name can stand for

So `pkg.T` enters neither the per-file type table nor the sibling-file struct fields (`_go_fields`, from fdd25f7b, which use the same helper), and every call through such a receiver is skipped. That reasoning is right for a bare-name lookup. But the file's import of `pkg` already gives exact evidence of which `T` is meant, and the extractor already records it (`go_imports`).

Repro 1, same file, on v8 `f5155bad`:

```go
// go.mod: module example.com/gomini
// plugincontext/plugincontext.go
package plugincontext
type Provider struct{}
func (p *Provider) GetWithDataSource(name string) string { return name }

// api/server.go
package api
import "example.com/gomini/plugincontext"
type HTTPServer struct{ pluginContextProvider *plugincontext.Provider }
func (hs *HTTPServer) check(name string) string {
	return hs.pluginContextProvider.GetWithDataSource(name) // no calls edge
}
func ViaParam(p *plugincontext.Provider) string { return p.GetWithDataSource("x") } // no calls edge
```

Repro 2, struct in one file and method in a sibling file, the Grafana layout (`pkg/api/datasources.go:860` `hs.pluginClient.CheckHealth(...)`, with `HTTPServer` declared in `http_server.go` and `pluginClient plugins.Client`):

```go
// go.mod: module example.com/app
// plugins/client.go
package plugins
type Client interface {
	CheckHealth(uid string) error
}

// api/server.go
package api
import "example.com/app/plugins"
type HTTPServer struct {
	pluginClient plugins.Client
}

// api/datasources.go  (does not import plugins itself)
package api
func (hs *HTTPServer) checkDatasourceHealth() error {
	return hs.pluginClient.CheckHealth("x") // no calls edge
}
```

| Receiver | type in same package | type from another package |
|---|---|---|
| struct field via the method's receiver | edge | **no edge** |
| struct field, struct declared in a sibling file | edge (fdd25f7b) | **no edge** |
| parameter | edge | **no edge** |
| `var x T` / `x := &T{}` | edge | **no edge** |
| interface-typed field | – | **no edge** |

Before this rebase, the PR's first version linked repro 1 but not repro 2: the sibling-file field had no import of `plugins` in the caller's file to read the qualifier from.

On Grafana @ `23f3e93` (92 non-test files from `plugincontext`, `expr`, `api`, `query`, `ngalert/writer`, `liveplugin`, `plugins`), `Provider.GetWithDataSource` gets 0 incoming `calls` edges on v8.

### The change

1. **`extractors/go.py`:**
   - `_go_single_type_name` keeps a qualified type as written (`pkg.T`, `*pkg.T`), so the per-file type table holds it.
   - A sibling-file struct field (`_go_fields` on the declaring file's node) is stored as `<import path>.T`, settled by the **declaring** file's imports. The method file reading it need not import `pkg` (repro 2). A qualifier with no matching import is dropped.
   - Each Go type node carries its own import path (`_go_package_path`), computed by the existing `_go_import_path_for_file` from its `go.mod`.
2. **`extract.py` `_resolve_go_member_calls`:** for `pkg.T` from the caller's table, look `pkg` up in the caller file's `go_imports`; for `<import path>.T` from a sibling file's fields, use that path directly. Then keep only the `T` declarations whose node carries that import path. The single-definition and single-method guards are unchanged. No match (stdlib, or a module outside the corpus) stays unresolved as before; it is not parked.
3. **`watch.py`, `cli.py`:** `_go_package_path` is forwarded in the incremental resolution context next to `_go_fields`, so on an update an unchanged declaring file still answers.
4. **`cache.py`:** `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 33 → 34, so cached Go extractions re-run with the new table values and markers.

Compared with the first version of this PR: the per-file `go_package_path` result key is gone. The path now rides on the type node instead, because the first version read it only from files extracted in the current run, so `graphify update` dropped the edge whenever the declaring file was unchanged (covered by the new rebuild test below).

Because the match is on the full import path, the qualifier also settles the case the bare-name path must bail on: two packages that both declare `T`.

title: JS file/class ID collision drops class Js and emits self-contains edges (0.9.87)
body:
## Summary

In graphifyy 0.9.87, a JavaScript file and a class inside it can receive the same node ID. For example, `bundle.min.js` and its `class Js` both become `bundle_min_js`. The class node is silently dropped, the surviving file node acquires `_callable` / `_callable_class`, and extraction emits a self-referencing `contains` edge. Method ownership consequently points at the file instead of a distinct class.

Related: #2810 (same-file symbol normalization collisions), #4281 (file-derived ID collisions). This report isolates a **file-versus-class collision within one file**, rather than two sibling symbols or two files.

## Minimal reproduction (no files written)

```python
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch
from graphify.extract import extract_js

with patch.object(Path, "read_bytes", return_value=b"class Js { run() { return 1; } }"):
    result = extract_js(Path("bundle.min.js"))

print(result)
```

Verified result, abbreviated:

```python
{
    'nodes': [
        {'id': 'bundle_min_js', 'label': 'bundle.min.js',
         'source_location': 'L1', '_callable': True, '_callable_class': True},
        {'id': 'bundle_min_js_run', 'label': '.run()', '_callable': True},
    ],
    'edges': [
        {'source': 'bundle_min_js', 'target': 'bundle_min_js', 'relation': 'contains'},
        {'source': 'bundle_min_js', 'target': 'bundle_min_js_run', 'relation': 'method'},
    ],
    'raw_calls': [],
}
```

There is no separate `Js` class node.

## Real-world reproduction

Observed in Magento 2 source files:

- `lib/web/hugerte/hugerte.min.js`: `class Js`, line 7.
- `lib/web/chartjs/Chart.min.js`: `class js`, line 13.

Calling upstream `graphify.extract.extract()` on these two actual files with `root` set to the Magento root, a fresh temporary `cache_root`, and `parallel=False` also reproduces the issue. Extraction returned 913 nodes, 2531 edges, and an empty `failed_sources` list. The resulting self-contains IDs were `lib_web_hugerte_hugerte_min` and `lib_web_chartjs_chart_min`.

Our separate downstream canonical-graph integrity gate rejects self-containment and refuses publication. That gate/error wording is **not** an upstream Graphify CLI error; the malformed nodes and edges already exist in upstream extraction output, independently of the downstream adapter. Without such a gate, the lost class and incorrect ownership can go unnoticed.

## Root-cause investigation in installed 0.9.87

- `extractors/engine.py` generates file IDs with `_make_id(str(path))` and class IDs with `_make_id(stem, namespace, class_name)`.
- Shared ID normalization collapses separators and case: the file extension `js` collides with the class name `Js`/`js`.
- The same-file `seen_ids` check drops the class record while later edge generation and callable-class marking still use its colliding ID.
- Global extraction subsequently remaps the surviving file ID, retaining the self-edge.

By the time a consumer sees the merged output, the separate class record and endpoint identities have already been lost. Dropping self-contains edges alone would therefore hide rather than repair the data loss.

## Expected behavior

File and symbol identities must remain distinct before deduplication. The result should contain a file node, a separate `Js` class node, and a method node, with `file -> class` containment and `class -> method` ownership. The file must not acquire callable-class flags merely because its ID collided.

A fix should preserve consistency across reference/import resolution and ID remapping, invalidate affected cached extraction results where necessary, and produce equivalent fresh/cache-hit output. It should not require excluding minified sources or suppressing integrity checks.

## Environment

- graphifyy: 0.9.87
- Python: 3.12.11
- macOS, ARM64
- tree-sitter: 0.25.2
- tree-sitter-javascript: 0.25.0

No Graphify source patch was applied for this report. A locally patched PHP grammar binding is installed for unrelated PHP syntax support; the minimal JavaScript reproduction above does not invoke it. Claims here concern the installed 0.9.87 release, not untested current upstream HEAD.

title: fix(extract): keep file and declaration IDs distinct (#4854)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4854. A file and a declaration inside it no longer share an id.

The file id is the extensionless stem, a declaration id is `make_id(stem, name)`, and the parse-time file id is `make_id(path)`. When a declaration's normalized name equals the file extension, both recipes land on one string, and `add_node` silently keeps the first:

```text
a.js   class Js

before
  file id     make_id("a.js")      -> a_js
  class id    make_id("a", "Js")   -> a_js      same string
  add_node(class)                  -> a_js in seen_ids, return
  add_edge(file, class, contains)  -> a_js -> a_js
  flags on class_nid               -> file becomes _callable_class
  method id   make_id(a_js, run)   -> a_js_run   owned by the file

after
  registry.resolve(a_js, "Js", "type")
    a_js is reserved by the file
    -> a_js_b692bab43393
  decl_node adds the class under the salted id
    -> a_js -> a_js_b692bab43393 contains
    -> a_js_b692bab43393 -> a_js_b692bab43393_run method
```

Two invariants are enforced:

```text
unique    an id is assigned only after an availability check against the
          file id, the taken node ids, and the ids assigned to declarations
stable    the same declaration resolves to its assigned id on a re-walk
          (reopened classes, cfg twins), and unaffected files keep their ids
referenced a reference to the declaration uses the declared id, not a
          per-file id derived from the referring file
```

The registry keys ownership by the id the declaration would have used, so `Foo` and `_Foo`, or `Base` in two namespaces, stay distinct. A lookup by name only answers when one declaration in the file spells it.

Cross-file references needed a second change. `ensure_named_node` is per file, so a reference in `b.ts` to `Ts` in `a.ts` was minted from `b.ts`'s stem, which is `b.ts`'s own file id:

```diff
 b.ts   import { Ts } from "./a";  @Ts class Other {}

 before
-  Other --references--> b.ts        (the referring file)
   no edge to the class

 after
+  Other --references--> Ts (a.ts)
   corpus map: (resolved path, normalized name) -> declared id
   import fact selects the module, path-keyed, so two modules may declare Ts
```

## Evidence

The test commit is red on the base tree. The implementation commits flip it green, one concern at a time:

| commit | new test file |
|---|---|
| `1517f89e` tests only, base code | 61 failed, 9 passed |
| `bcea646b` registry and mint sites | 2 failed, 68 passed (`Other -> b.ts` remains) |
| `6755a5a7` corpus map | 1 failed, 69 passed (schema pin) |
| `9290d9fc` schema 30 | 70 passed, 1 skipped |

The cases that failed on the experiment branch and now pass:

```text
class Js {} + export const $b692bab43393 = 1     before: const dropped
                                                after:  both nodes, distinct ids

a.ts export class Ts
b.ts @Ts class Other                            before: Other -> references -> b.ts
                                                after:  Other -> references -> Ts (a.ts)

a1.ts, a2.ts both export Ts
b.ts imports a1 and @Ts                         after:  binds a1's Ts, not a2's
```

Full suite, no env var:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly
9036 passed, 18 skipped, 1 xfailed, 2398 warnings in 556.48s

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_file_id_collision_4854.py
70 passed, 1 skipped   (twice in a row, cold and warm)
```

The 71 parametrized cases cover JS, TS, Python, Java, PHP, Ruby, C++, C headers, Rust, Go, C#, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, and Julia. One skip: C++ namespace declarations are not modeled by the extractor, confirmed by the control name.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: a node id is unique in the corpus, a declaration's id is stable across runs, and every reference to that declaration uses it. The tests assert behaviour (labels, source files, edges, build labels), not the helper.

- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented the **limitations** below.

## How was this tested?

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_file_id_collision_4854.py
  70 passed, 1 skipped

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_extract.py tests/test_build.py \
    tests/test_cache.py tests/test_dedup.py tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py \
    tests/test_file_node_id_spec.py
  624 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:randomly
  9036 passed, 18 skipped, 1 xfailed in 556.48s
```

The targeted extraction, build, cache, dedup, and existing id-collision tests ran after the fix. The full suite ran on the final tree with no environment variables set.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. A revert restores the previous ids for the colliding declarations only; unaffected files keep the same ids before and after. The one persisted change is the AST cache schema, and reverting the code makes the schema-30 entries miss and re-extract, which is safe.

**Blast Radius:** narrow, but corpus-wide in code paths. The behaviour change applies to every language that mints declaration ids through the engine, plus Rust, Go, and Julia. It only fires when a declaration name normalizes to the file extension (`Js` in `.js`, `Ts` in `.ts`, `Java` in `.java`, and so on), so ordinary files produce byte-identical ids. `build()` keeps the file and the declaration for each fixture; no self-contains edges remain.

**Schema:** `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` is 30 (base 29). Cached per-file results under 29 carry the dropped declaration, so they are ignored and re-extracted. An existing `graph.json` built before this change keeps the missing class until a full rebuild: `graphify update` only re-extracts changed files, so delete `graphify-out/` or pass a fresh `--out` once after upgrading.

**Limitations**

- Cross-file references: decorator and inheritance are covered. `new Ts()` and TS type annotations do not emit a cross-file reference edge in this extractor today, so no test claims them.
- Standalone extractors: rust, go, and julia use the registry at their choke points. Apex, Bash, Dart, DM, Elixir, Erlang, Fortran, Markdown, Objective-C, OCaml, Pascal/Pascal Forms, PowerShell, R, Robot, Solidity, SQL, VB.NET, Verilog, Zig, and the YAML/JSON/Terraform config extractors still mint from the file stem and are not covered here. title: Terraform/HCL node ids embed the absolute build directory when the AST cache is reused from another location (0.9.92)
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.92 (macOS, Python 3.13)

## Summary
A Terraform/HCL file's node ids depend on the **absolute directory** where its AST cache entry was first written. If a project (or its `graphify-out/cache`) is reused from another location, `graphify update` emits ids that contain the old absolute path. They differ from the ids a clean build produces for the same content.

## Reproduce
```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/a/repo/deploy && cd /tmp/a/repo
printf 'variable "REGISTRY" {\n  default = "example"\n}\n' > deploy/bake.hcl
git init -q && git add . && git commit -qm x
graphify update . --force                       # clean build in /tmp/a

cp -R /tmp/a/repo /tmp/b/repo && cd /tmp/b/repo  # same content, cache copied
graphify update . --force

cp -R /tmp/a/repo /tmp/c/repo && rm -rf /tmp/c/repo/graphify-out && cd /tmp/c/repo
graphify update . --force                       # same content, no cache
```

**Ids of `var.REGISTRY`** (absolute part shortened):
- `/tmp/a` (clean): `terraform_deploy_<hash>_var_registry`
- `/tmp/c` (clean, copied): `terraform_deploy_<hash>_var_registry`, the same as `/tmp/a`
- `/tmp/b` (cache reused): `terraform_<…>_tmp_a_repo_deploy_<other hash>_var_registry`, with the old absolute path inside the id

Python and the other extractors we use showed no such difference.

## Cause (from reading the 0.9.92 source)
- `extract_terraform` scopes ids with `_scope_id(path.parent.resolve().as_posix())`, i.e. the absolute directory. That result is stored in the per-file AST cache, which is keyed on content plus tool, schema and grammar versions, not on the path.
- `prepare_terraform` (called for every per-file result, cached or fresh) rewrites only ids that start with `_scope_id(<current absolute directory>)`.
- A cache entry written under another root carries that root's scope, so `nid.startswith(old + "_")` is false and the absolute id is kept.
- The docstring says "Make cached directory-scoped IDs portable"; this holds only when the cache was written at the same absolute path.

## Suggested fixes (any one)
- Store the portable form in the cache: run the relative re-scoping before `save_cached`, or scope by the path relative to the scan root from the start.
- In `prepare_terraform`, recognise any absolute scope by storing the absolute directory (or its scope id) in the cached result, instead of recomputing it from the current location.
- Include the scan-root path in the Terraform cache key.

## Impact
- Builds that run in a fresh directory each time (CI, blue-green build directories) get ids that change between runs and differ from a clean build.
- Lookups by id then miss the node.
- No crash, so it goes unnoticed.

title: ID collision: a doc whose path prefixes a code node's id outranks the AST node on label length, and its next re-extract deletes the code node
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

When a semantic (doc) node and an AST code node share an id, and the doc's own path is a prefix of that id, `_defines_id` returns True for both. `_collision_rank` then has no provenance key left to separate them: the next keys are "has a source_file" (both do), the lifecycle penalty (equal), and then label length. A doc node with a shorter label than the code node wins.

The code node then carries the doc as its `source_file`. On the next `--update` that re-extracts the doc without that node, `build_merge` replaces the doc's nodes and the code node is deleted, although the code file never changed.

Layout that triggers it: `pkg.md` beside `pkg/test_x.py`. The AST id for the file is `pkg_test_x`. The extraction spec asks doc subagents to reuse the AST id for a code entity they describe, so `pkg.md` emits `pkg_test_x`, and `pkg_` is also a prefix of `pkg.md`'s own path.

Checked directly on 0.9.97:

```
Tests              | defines: code True doc True | rank code (False, False, 1, 9) doc (False, False, 1, 5)  | winner doc
test_x.py (tests)  | defines: code True doc True | rank code (False, False, 1, 9) doc (False, False, 1, 17) | winner code
```

So the outcome depends on how briefly the doc names the file. This is not #4738 (reference stubs between documents, fixed by #4743, landed in 0.9.96; the skill's extraction spec does not ask subagents for that marker) and not #4281 (dropped extensions). The definer-wins rule (`_defines_id` as the first rank key) holds whenever only one side's path prefixes the id. The gap is the case where both do.

Expected: the AST/code-tier node keeps the id, since it is extracted fact and the doc's copy is an inference about it (CONTRIBUTING: "Keep inference visibly separate from extracted fact"). The doc node's edges then attach to the code node.

Possible fix: in `_collision_rank`, add a key right after the defining key that prefers `_origin == "ast"` over `_origin == "semantic"` when both sides define the id. It changes no collision where only one side defines it.

### Steps to reproduce

Self-contained, no corpus needed (writes a temp graph.json):

```python
"""A doc whose own path prefixes a code node's id takes that node over in build_merge,
and the doc's next re-extract deletes it."""
import json, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import graphify
from graphify.build import build_merge
from networkx.readwrite import json_graph

d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
code = {"id": "pkg_test_x", "label": "test_x.py", "file_type": "code",
        "source_file": "pkg/test_x.py", "source_location": "L1", "_origin": "ast"}
other = {"id": "pkg_test_x_run", "label": "run()", "file_type": "code",
         "source_file": "pkg/test_x.py", "source_location": "L3", "_origin": "ast"}
g = {"directed": False, "multigraph": False, "graph": {}, "hyperedges": [],
     "nodes": [code, other],
     "links": [{"source": "pkg_test_x", "target": "pkg_test_x_run", "relation": "contains",
                "confidence": "EXTRACTED", "source_file": "pkg/test_x.py", "_origin": "ast"}]}
(d / "graph.json").write_text(json.dumps(g))

# --update re-extracts only the doc pkg.md; its subagent gives the code file's node the AST id,
# as the extraction spec asks
doc = {"nodes": [{"id": "pkg_test_x", "label": "Tests", "file_type": "code",
                  "source_file": "pkg.md", "_origin": "semantic"},
                 {"id": "pkg_overview", "label": "Overview", "file_type": "document",
                  "source_file": "pkg.md", "_origin": "semantic"}],
       "edges": [{"source": "pkg_overview", "target": "pkg_test_x", "relation": "describes",
                  "confidence": "EXTRACTED", "source_file": "pkg.md", "_origin": "semantic"}],
       "hyperedges": []}
G = build_merge([doc], graph_path=d / "graph.json")
print("graphify", graphify.__version__ if hasattr(graphify, "__version__") else "")
print("1) after merge: pkg_test_x source_file =", G.nodes["pkg_test_x"].get("source_file"))

(d / "graph2.json").write_text(json.dumps(json_graph.node_link_data(G, edges="links")))
doc2 = {"nodes": [{"id": "pkg_overview", "label": "Overview", "file_type": "document",
                   "source_file": "pkg.md", "_origin": "semantic"}], "edges": [], "hyperedges": []}
G2 = build_merge([doc2], graph_path=d / "graph2.json")
print("2) after pkg.md is re-extracted without that node: pkg_test_x present =", "pkg_test_x" in G2)
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
[graphify] WARNING: node 'pkg_test_x' is minted by two different files — keeping 'Tests' from 'pkg.md', dropping 'test_x.py' from 'pkg/test_x.py'. An ID is derived from the source path plus the entity name, so this one does not identify a single entity and the dropped node is lost. To keep them distinct, run 'graphify extract' per subfolder and merge with 'graphify merge-graphs'.
[graphify] Replaced 2 node(s) from re-extracted source file(s).
graphify 
1) after merge: pkg_test_x source_file = pkg.md
2) after pkg.md is re-extracted without that node: pkg_test_x present = False
```

With the doc label `"test_x.py (tests)"` (longer than `test_x.py`) the code node survives and step 2 prints `True`.

### Graphify version

0.9.97

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

pip

### Additional Environment Details

graphifyy 0.9.97 installed with pip on Windows 11, Python 3.12. `graphify/dedup.py` at `v8` HEAD is byte-identical to the 0.9.97 wheel's copy (`curl` of the raw file, then `cmp`, 2026-10-29).

### Additional context

Found while running the skill's `--update` path on a corpus mixing docs and code; worked around locally by dropping semantic nodes whose id an AST code node from another file already owns, before `build_merge`.

title: Relative JS imports with a query string (`./foo.js?v=123`) are not resolved
body:
**Version:** graphify 0.9.93 (`graphifyy`), `extract --code-only`, `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none`

**Description**
ES module imports that include a cache-busting query string are not resolved to the target file:

```js
import { foo } from './lib/foo.js?v=134';
```

Instead of an `imports_from` edge to `lib/foo.js`, graphify creates a phantom node (e.g. `ref_foo_js_v_134`) and the real file gets no inbound edge. Symbol imports and cross-file `calls` are lost as well, since they depend on the module resolving.

**Impact (real project, 93 JS files)**
- Phantom `_v_` nodes: 96 → 0 after stripping the suffix
- Inbound imports_from edges for the most-used module: 0 → 29
- Symbol imports: 30 → 413
- About 400 cross-file `calls` edges recovered

**Root cause**
`extractors/resolution.py`, lines 855-856 (`_resolve_js_module_path`): relative specifiers are resolved with `start_dir / raw` without stripping the `?query` / `#fragment` part. The Markdown extractor already strips it (`extractors/markdown.py:289`), so applying the same normalization to relative JS/TS specifiers should fix it.

Also present on `v8` (default branch) as of 0a8cd4e1e342235fe53e881fb5d591bf0460071f (`resolution.py` lines 868-869).

**Current workaround**
Copy the tree to a temp dir, strip the suffix with `sed -E 's/(\.js)\?v=[0-9]+/\1/g'`, and extract from the copy.

**Expected behavior**
`./foo.js?v=123` resolves to `./foo.js`, as browsers and bundlers do for module resolution.

**Related:** #2849 lists one `../styles.css?url` import under "Resource-query import is unresolved". It looks like the same root cause.

title: fix(terraform): preserve cached IDs across project moves (#4858)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4858.

Terraform/HCL AST caches copied between checkout directories could retain the original absolute scope in node IDs. A cached rebuild then produced different IDs from a clean build of the same project.

The extractor now records its original scope in internal _terraform_scope metadata. The existing preparation pass consumes it to normalize node IDs and edge endpoints against the current scan root. Module-source resolution still uses the current permitted corpus.

AST cache schema 30 retires entries without scope metadata. This causes a one-time AST re-extraction across languages; semantic caches are unchanged. Existing graphs with stale Terraform IDs require a full code rebuild:

    graphify extract . --code-only --force

No public function signatures, CLI flags, or exported graph schema change.

- [x] Tests or CI

- [ ] Security fix

The invariant is that moving a project together with its AST cache produces the same node IDs and reference edges as a clean build, while preserving module isolation.

The CLI reproduction compares a fresh build in A, a build in B using A's copied cache, and a clean build in C. Before the fix, B retains A's absolute scope. After the fix, all three agree, with a 100% AST cache hit in B.

The 16 new cases cover copied caches without parsing, root/nested directories, .tf/.hcl/.tfvars, actual parallel workers, cross-file references, distinct module scopes, module topology, idempotent preparation, and old-cache invalidation.

title: feat(html): add Hide orphans toggle to graph.html
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a "Hide orphans" checkbox to `graph.html`, next to "Select All" in the Communities panel. When checked, nodes with degree 0 in the rendered graph are hidden. It is off by default, so the default output looks the same as before.

Community filtering and the new toggle both set the vis `hidden` flag, so they now share one predicate, `isNodeHidden(n)`:

```js
hiddenCommunities.has(n.community) || (hideOrphans && n.degree === 0)
```

The per-community checkbox and `toggleAllCommunities()` call `isNodeHidden()` and no longer write `hidden: !cb.checked` / `hidden: hide` directly. Without this, re-showing a community would un-hide its orphans while the toggle is on.

Hyperedge hulls already skip hidden nodes (`network.getPositions` returns nothing for them), so they need no change.

title: feat(html): run physics while dragging a node in graph.html
body:
## What does this PR do?

`graph.html` turns physics off once the initial layout stabilizes. After that, a dragged node stays wherever it is dropped. Its neighbours do not react, so a node can be dropped on top of another or dragged far away from its group.

This PR turns physics back on while a node is dragged:
- Nodes pushed too close repel each other (existing `forceAtlas2Based` repulsion and `avoidOverlap`).
- Edges pull a node dragged too far back toward its neighbours (existing springs).
- Physics turns off again on the next `stabilized` event after the drag ends.

```js
let draggingNode = false;
network.on('dragStart', params => {
  if (!params.nodes.length) return;
  draggingNode = true;
  network.setOptions({ physics: { enabled: true } });
});
network.on('dragEnd', () => { draggingNode = false; });
network.on('stabilized', () => {
  if (!draggingNode) network.setOptions({ physics: { enabled: false } });
});
```

Notes from the vis-network 9.1.6 source (the pinned version):
- `Network.setOptions({physics})` only emits `startSimulation`. It does not re-run stabilization or refit the view, so the camera does not jump on drag.
- `dragStart` also fires for view pans, with `params.nodes` empty. The guard keeps pans from enabling physics.
- `stabilized` can fire while a node is still held, if the user pauses mid-drag. `draggingNode` keeps physics on until the drag ends.

Solver parameters and the initial `stabilizationIterationsDone` freeze are unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Physics runs only during the initial layout and while a node drag is settling. It is off at rest and during view pans.

Limitations:
- A drag simulates every visible node. On graphs near the viz node limit the page does more work until the layout settles.
- Orphan nodes have no springs, so the repulsion from a nearby drop can push them away from the group.

fix(go): type a receiver's field when its struct is declared in a sibling file (#3368)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Refs #3368. On v8, a Go method that calls through a field of its own receiver (`s.field.M()`) gets no `calls` edge when the struct is declared in a **different file of the same package**, even when the field's type is a same-package type. That is the usual Go layout: the struct and its constructor in one file, the methods spread over others.

### Why #3368 is not resolved yet on v8

1695efae (`feat(go): resolve member calls through the receiver's declared type`, 0.9.89) types a receiver through `go_type_table`, which is built **per file** by `_go_receiver_type_table`. For `s.field.M()` the resolver looks `field` up in the table of the caller's own file. When the struct is declared in another file, the caller's file has no `field` binding, the lookup returns nothing, and the call is dropped. This is independent of the receiver's type being in the same package or not.

Minimal repro on v8 (`0a8cd4e1`):

```go
// svc/greeter.go
package svc
type Greeter struct{}
func (g *Greeter) Greet() {}

// svc/types.go
package svc
type App struct{ greeter *Greeter }

// svc/run.go
package svc
func (a *App) Run() { a.greeter.Greet() } // no calls edge to Greeter.Greet
```

Move `type App` into `run.go` and the edge appears, which is the existing `test_a_struct_field_types_the_receiver_through_the_methods_own_receiver`.

On Grafana (`pkg/router`, 45 non-test files), `GrafanaRouter` is declared in `router.go` and its methods live in `discovery_status.go`, `reconcile.go` and others. v8 has 488 `calls` edges there. With this change it has 492, and all 4 new edges match the source:

| caller | call (line) | target |
|---|---|---|
| `GrafanaRouter.groupStatus` | `r.discoveryCache.lookup(...)` (discovery_status.go:210) | `discoveryCache.lookup` |
| `GrafanaRouter.publish` | `r.discoveryCache.retain(snap)` (reconcile.go:375) | `discoveryCache.retain` |
| `GrafanaRouter.Run` | `r.loader.Notify(ctx)` (reconcile.go:68) | `RoutesLoader.Notify` |
| `GrafanaRouter.reconcile` | `r.loader.Load(ctx)` (reconcile.go:185) | `RoutesLoader.Load` |

No edge was removed.

### The change

1. **`extractors/go.py`**: `_go_struct_field_types` records, for each struct the file declares, `field -> TypeName` under the same rule the flat table uses (`_go_single_type_name`, so only `T` / `*T`). The map is stored on the **file node** as `_go_fields`, keyed by struct id. A raw call `s.field.M()` rooted at the method's own receiver also carries `field_owner` (the receiver's type).
2. **`extract.py` `_resolve_go_member_calls`**: when the caller file's table has no binding for the field, look it up in the fields of `field_owner`, only when that owner resolves to a single type node that a single file declares fields for. The rest of the path is unchanged: the single-definition and single-method guards, INFERRED / 0.85, and parking for an undeclared type.
3. **`watch.py` / `cli.py`**: `_go_fields` is added to the persisted resolver markers, so an incremental rebuild that re-extracts only the method's file still sees the unchanged struct file's fields.
4. **`cache.py`**: `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 29 → 30, so cached Go extractions pick up the new field and marker.

Why the file node and not the struct node: every file that holds a method of `App` emits the `App` node id too, so on an incremental rebuild of `run.go` the fresh copy of `App` from `run.go` shadows the declaring file's copy in the resolution context. The file node's id is unique to the declaring file.

This is independent of #4853 (receivers typed from another package, `pkg.T`, through the caller's `go_imports`). That PR changes how a qualified type enters the tables. This one changes which file's fields a self-rooted chain can read. Each applies on v8 without the other. Grafana's `hs.pluginContextProvider.GetWithDataSource` in `pkg/api/datasources.go` needs both, because the field type is `*plugincontext.Provider` and `HTTPServer` is declared in `http_server.go`. Both PRs bump `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` to 30, so whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase to 31.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a Go member call binds only to a method of the one type its receiver is declared as. For `s.field.M()`, the field's type comes from the declaration of `s`'s own struct, wherever in the package that struct is declared, and never from a same-named field of another struct.

- `test_a_sibling_files_field_of_another_struct_does_not_type_the_receiver`: `greeter` is a field of `Other`, not of `App`, so no edge is created.
- The existing negative cases still pass unchanged: a chain not rooted at the method's receiver, a package-qualified type, two packages that declare the same type.
- Persisted state: the new `_go_fields` attribute is written to `graph.json` on Go file nodes. The cache schema bump retires extractions cached without it.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Not covered (unchanged):**
- A qualified field type (`*pkg.T`). See #4853.
- A chain not rooted at the method's own receiver (`p.field.M()` with `p` a parameter), excluded by design in 1695efae.
- An embedded (promoted) field.
- A struct whose file name matches its type name (`app.go` with `type App`): on v8 the file node and the type node get the same id, so an incremental rebuild of a method file loses the declaring file's node, and this field data with it. A full build resolves. This is a separate id collision and is not changed here.

## How was this tested?

Run on Windows 11, Python 3.12, in the environment `uv run --all-extras` syncs (`.venv`; the later runs call `.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest` directly because `uv run` rewrites `uv.lock` on Windows).

```text

  # 16 passed (on unchanged v8: 2 failed, 14 passed; the negative test passes on both)
uv run --all-extras pytest tests/test_go_*.py tests/test_sql_go_batches.py tests/test_languages.py tests/test_cache*.py -q
  # 696 passed
uv run --all-extras pytest tests -q
  # 8877 passed, 10 failed, 99 skipped. All 10 are in files that fail on unchanged v8 on Windows
  # (test_code_only_update_all_hosts x2, test_hooks, test_language_override_lifecycle,
  # test_resolve_memoization, test_source_key_memoization, test_unmapped_at_alias_resolution).
  # test_hooks.py run alone gives the same result on this branch and on v8 (1 failed, the same test).
uv run ruff check graphify/extractors/go.py graphify/extract.py graphify/cache.py graphify/watch.py graphify/cli.py tests/test_go_receiver_member_calls.py
  # All checks passed!
```

title: fix(go): credit calls in a package-level var initialiser to the file (#2360)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Refs #2360. On v8 the Go extractor walks only function and method bodies for calls. A call made in a **package-level `var` initialiser** is never walked, so it produces no edge and the callee loses that caller. The most common form is a closure kept in a package variable as a swappable hook:

```go
// cmd/migrate.go
package cmd

import "example.com/m/dbimpl"

var resourceDBProvider = func(name string) string {
	return dbimpl.ProvideResourceDB(name) // no edge to ProvideResourceDB
}
```

The same happens for a plain initialiser call such as `var registry = newRegistry()`.

### Why #2360 is not resolved yet on v8

#2360 is about package-level `var`/`const` declarations missing from the graph. On v8, `extract_go`'s `walk` dispatches on `function_declaration`, `method_declaration`, `type_declaration` and `import_declaration` only. A `var_declaration` is recursed into and never registered as a body, so `walk_calls` never sees the calls in it. The two open PRs for the issue (#2364, #3098) add nodes for the declared names, but neither walks the initialiser for calls: #2364's `var_declaration` branch mints the nodes and returns. So the calls stay missing with either of them.

On Grafana, `pkg/cmd/grafana-cli/commands/resource_db_migrate.go:22-23` holds exactly this shape:

```go
var resourceDBProvider = func(cfg *setting.Cfg) (db.DBProvider, error) {
	return dbimpl.ProvideResourceDB(nil, cfg, nil)
}
```

Extracting `pkg/api`, `pkg/api/routing`, `pkg/cmd/grafana-cli/commands` and `pkg/storage/unified/sql/db/dbimpl` (74 non-test files):

- v8: `dbimpl.ProvideResourceDB` (`dbimpl.go:41`) has 0 incoming `calls` edges, and `resource_db_migrate.go` has no edge at lines 22-23.
- With this change: 426 → 430 `calls` edges, none removed. All 4 new edges are package-init calls that are in the source:

| file | line | call |
|---|---|---|
| `resource_db_migrate.go` | 23 | `dbimpl.ProvideResourceDB(nil, cfg, nil)` inside `var resourceDBProvider = func(...)` |
| `commands.go` | 95 | `runPluginCommand(installCommand)` in `var pluginCommands = []*cli.Command{...}` |
| `commands.go` | 130 | `runRunnerCommand(resetPasswordCommand)` in `var adminCommands` |
| `commands.go` | 151 | `runDbCommand(datamigrations.EncryptDatasourcePasswords)` in `var adminCommands` |

### The change

`extractors/go.py`: a `var_declaration` whose parent is the `source_file` (a package-level one) is registered as a body owned by the **file node** and is walked by the existing `walk_calls`. That includes the bodies of closures in it, since `walk_calls` stops only at function and method declarations. The file is the owner because the initialiser runs at package init and has no enclosing function. That matches how other extractors handle module-level code: the JS scan of #3408, for example, attaches what a module-level closure defines to the file node. A `var` declared inside a function is not affected: it is still walked as part of that function.

`cache.py`: `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 29 → 30, so cached Go extractions re-run.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: every call site in a Go file is attributed to the innermost named owner that runs it: a function, a method, or the file for package-level code. No call is credited to a function that does not contain it.

- `test_a_var_declared_inside_a_function_stays_with_the_function`: a local `var x = helper()` keeps `Run -> helper` and adds no file-level edge.
- Resolution is unchanged: the new raw calls go through the same in-file label match and cross-file import-evidence pass as any other Go call.

- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Not covered (unchanged):**
- The `var` itself is still not a node, so a call *through* it (`resourceDBProvider(cfg)` in a function) still links nothing. That is the node half of #2360 (#2364, #3098). If var nodes land, the var node is a more precise owner for its initialiser's calls than the file, and this branch would be the place to switch it.
- `const` declarations are not walked: a constant initialiser cannot call a function.

## How was this tested?

Run on Windows 11, Python 3.12, in the environment `uv run --all-extras` syncs (`.venv`; the later runs call `.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest` directly because `uv run` rewrites `uv.lock` on Windows).

```text
  # 3 passed (on unchanged v8: 2 failed, 1 passed; the local-var negative passes on both)
uv run --all-extras pytest tests/test_go_*.py tests/test_sql_go_batches.py tests/test_languages.py tests/test_cache*.py -q
  # 696 passed
uv run --all-extras pytest tests -q
  # 8877 passed, 10 failed, 99 skipped. All 10 are in files that fail on unchanged v8 on Windows\n  # (test_code_only_update_all_hosts x2, test_hooks, test_language_override_lifecycle,\n  # test_resolve_memoization, test_source_key_memoization, test_unmapped_at_alias_resolution).\n  # test_hooks.py run alone gives 1 failure (test_shebang_parse_requires_leading_hash_bang), the same on v8.
uv run ruff check graphify/extractors/go.py graphify/cache.py tests/test_go_package_var_calls.py
  # All checks passed!
```

title: fix(go): link a method value passed as an argument as an indirect_call (#1566)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Refs #1566. In Go, a handler or callback is registered by passing a **method value**: `routing.Wrap(hs.CheckDatasourceHealth)`, `r.Get("/health", s.Health)`, `pool.Submit(w.run)`. On v8 such a method gets no edge from the registration site. The call walk only looks at what a call expression invokes, not at its arguments. A handler that is reached only through its route registration therefore shows no caller, and `affected` does not reach it.

Minimal repro on v8 (`0a8cd4e1`):

```go
// routing/routing.go
package routing
type Handler func(string) string
func Wrap(h Handler) Handler { return h }

// api/server.go
package api
type Server struct{}
func (s *Server) Health(name string) string { return name }

// api/routes.go
package api
import "example.com/m/routing"
func (s *Server) Register() routing.Handler {
	return routing.Wrap(s.Health) // Register -> Wrap only; nothing reaches Health
}
```

On Grafana, `pkg/api/api.go:420` registers `routing.Wrap(hs.CheckDatasourceHealth)`. With `pkg/api` extracted on v8, `HTTPServer.CheckDatasourceHealth` (`pkg/api/datasources.go:829`) has no incoming `calls` or `indirect_call` edge.

Extracting `pkg/api`, `pkg/api/routing`, `pkg/cmd/grafana-cli/commands` and `pkg/storage/unified/sql/db/dbimpl` (74 non-test files):

- v8: 426 `calls` edges, 0 `indirect_call`; `HTTPServer.CheckDatasourceHealth` has 0 incoming edges.
- With this change: 426 `calls` edges (none added or removed), 176 `indirect_call` edges. `CheckDatasourceHealth` gets `HTTPServer.registerRoutes -> CheckDatasourceHealth` at `api.go:420`.
- I checked all 176 new edges against their source line. Each line holds `x.Method` not followed by `(`. 175 targets are `HTTPServer` methods; 151 come from `registerRoutes` (`routing.Wrap(hs.X)` route registrations); the others are callbacks such as `cookies.DeleteCookie(c.Resp, name, hs.CookieOptionsFromCfg)` (`login.go:125`) and `authn.HandleLoginRedirect(..., hs.ValidateRedirectTo, ...)` (`login_oauth.go:66`).

### Why #1566 is not resolved yet on v8

#1566 tracks `indirect_call` (a function passed by name, or listed in a dispatch table, is linked as an INFERRED `indirect_call` so `affected` reaches it). The slices that shipped cover Python (call arguments, dispatch tables, assignments and returns, `getattr`) and JS/TS (callbacks and dispatch tables). Go has none of them: `extractors/go.py` never emits an `indirect` raw call, and `_resolve_go_member_calls` only emits `calls`.

### The change

1. **`extractors/go.py`**: in `walk_calls`, each argument of a call that is a selector `x.M` on a plain identifier (not an imported package) is recorded as a raw member call with `indirect: True` and `context: "argument"`. Its receiver is typed exactly as a direct `x.M()` call is: the method's own receiver, or the enclosing function's parameter/local type.
2. **`extract.py` `_resolve_go_member_calls`**: an `indirect` raw call resolves through the same path as a direct member call (receiver type, single declaration, single method of that name), and is emitted as `indirect_call`, INFERRED, 0.85, which matches the Python/JS `indirect_call`. It is **never parked** as an unresolved call for a merge: `f(x.y)` is just as often a field read as a method value, so an unknown type here is not evidence of a missing call.
3. **`cache.py`**: `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 29 → 30.

The shared cross-file pass skips every `is_member_call`, so it does not see these entries. An existing direct `calls` edge between the same pair still takes precedence, so no pair gets both.

This is independent of #4853 (receivers typed from another package). It only adds a second kind of entry to the resolver #4853 also changes. A method value on a receiver typed `*pkg.T` resolves once both are in.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: an `indirect_call` from a Go function to a method is emitted only when the argument names a method of the one type its receiver is declared as. A field passed as an argument, a package function value, or a receiver of unknown type links nothing and parks nothing.

- `test_a_field_passed_as_an_argument_links_nothing_and_parks_nothing`
- `test_a_package_function_value_is_not_read_as_a_method_value`

- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Not covered (unchanged):**
- A function value (`Wrap(handler)`, `Wrap(pkg.Handler)`): the free-function half of the Go slice of #1566.
- A method value through a field chain (`Wrap(s.svc.Handle)`) or a method expression (`(*Server).Health`).
- Method values outside a call's argument list (`h := s.Health`, struct literals, maps).

## How was this tested?

Run on Windows 11, Python 3.12, in the environment `uv run --all-extras` syncs (`.venv`; the later runs call `.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest` directly because `uv run` rewrites `uv.lock` on Windows).

```text
  # 4 passed (on unchanged v8: 2 failed, 2 passed; the two negatives pass on both)
uv run --all-extras pytest tests/test_go_*.py tests/test_sql_go_batches.py tests/test_languages.py tests/test_cache*.py tests/test_indirect*.py -q
  # 796 passed (with tests/test_indirect*.py)
uv run --all-extras pytest tests -q
  # 8878 passed, 10 failed, 99 skipped. All 10 are in files that fail on unchanged v8 on Windows\n  # (test_code_only_update_all_hosts x2, test_hooks, test_language_override_lifecycle,\n  # test_resolve_memoization, test_source_key_memoization, test_unmapped_at_alias_resolution).\n  # test_hooks.py run alone gives 1 failure (test_shebang_parse_requires_leading_hash_bang), the same on v8.
uv run ruff check graphify/extractors/go.py graphify/extract.py graphify/cache.py tests/test_go_method_value_indirect_calls.py
  # All checks passed!
```

title: fix(extract): strip query/fragment from relative JS imports
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4860. Relative JS/TS imports with a Vite-style query string or fragment (`./foo.js?v=134`, `./foo.js#section`) resolved to the literal suffixed path, which does not exist on disk, so the import-target layer minted a phantom node instead of the real file, losing symbol imports and cross-file `calls` edges.

The fix strips the `?query` / `#fragment` suffix from relative specifiers in `_resolve_js_module_path` before resolution, mirroring the markdown link resolver (same split order, so `./foo.js?v=134#s` and `./foo.js#s?v=1` both collapse to `./foo.js`). `#`-subpath imports, bare specifiers, tsconfig aliases, and workspace packages are untouched, and the stripped specifier resolves to the byte-identical path as the plain specifier, so it shares the same cache entry and node id (no phantom).

Documented limitation: a query/fragment on a tsconfig alias or `@/`-prefixed specifier is not stripped. Such specifiers never resolved before either, so nothing regresses; extending the strip there would need an alias-layer decision and is left for a follow-up. No skill fragments were changed, so no skillgen regen applies.

title: fix(serve): a name spelled exactly wins a lookup tie that is only case
body:
## What does this PR do?

Since 0.9.45 (#2779) the Go extractor keeps two symbols that differ only by case apart: `Run` keeps the plain id and `run` gets a hash suffix. The graph is right. But no node lookup can reach either of them by name: `get_node`, `get_neighbors`, `explain`, `path` and `query --seed` all refuse the name as ambiguous, **even when it is spelled exactly like one of the two labels**.

Minimal repro on v8 (`0a8cd4e1`), `graphify update .` on:

```go
// api/datasources.go
package api
type HTTPServer struct{}
func (hs *HTTPServer) CheckDatasourceHealth(name string) string { return hs.checkDatasourceHealth(name) }
func (hs *HTTPServer) checkDatasourceHealth(name string) string { return name }
```

```text
get_node {"label": "CheckDatasourceHealth"}
Ambiguous: 'checkdatasourcehealth' matches 2 nodes in api/datasources.go.
  L9
    id: api_httpserver_checkdatasourcehealth
  L13
    id: api_httpserver_checkdatasourcehealth_efb2ee
Retry with the full node id.
```

`checkDatasourceHealth` and `.checkDatasourceHealth()` get the same answer. A `path::symbol` form cannot help because both symbols are in the same file. The only way in is the opaque id. Grafana has many such pairs: in a 132-file subset of `pkg/`, all 16 same-file case-only pairs are kept as two nodes on v8 (for example `HTTPServer.CheckDatasourceHealth` / `checkDatasourceHealth` in `pkg/api/datasources.go`, `Router.handle` / `Handle` in `pkg/web/router.go`, `NewBackendPlugin` / `newBackendPlugin` in `pkg/plugins/backendplugin/grpcplugin/client.go`). Each of them can only be looked up by id.

### Why it is not resolved yet on v8

#2779 fixed the **ids**, but lookup still folds case in two places:

1. `_find_node_tiers` matches labels and ids case-insensitively, so both nodes land in the `exact` tier and `_tier_refusal` refuses the same-file tie.
2. The MCP `get_node` / `get_neighbors` handlers call `raw.lower()` before resolving, so the spelling the caller typed is lost before the resolver sees it.

### The change

`serve.py`:

1. In `_find_node_tiers`, when the `exact` tier holds several nodes whose labels are all the **same name up to case**, and exactly one label equals the query as written (ignoring the `.` / `()` decoration), that node is the `exact` tier. The others move to the front of `prefix`, so they still appear in search results.
2. `get_node` / `get_neighbors` pass the label as written. Every comparison in the tiers already folds case on its own, so this changes nothing except the new rule.

Nothing changes when the spelling does not settle the tie:
- A query in neither spelling (`checkdatasourcehealth`) is still refused as ambiguous.
- The same spelling in two files (`CheckHealth` in `api/server.go` and in `web/router.go`) is still refused across files, because two nodes match as written.
- A tie between labels that differ by more than case is untouched.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a lookup resolves to a node only when the query names that node and no other one equally well; otherwise it fails closed with the candidates. An exact-case spelling names one node better than its case twin does. It never overrides a tie between two nodes that both match as written.

- `test_a_case_tie_neither_spelling_matches_stays_ambiguous`
- `test_an_exact_spelling_does_not_break_a_tie_between_two_files`
- `test_get_node_and_get_neighbors_agree_on_ambiguous_label` (existing) still passes.
- No persisted state is touched: this is read-side only.

- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Not covered:** `affected` resolves its seed through its own lookup, which also rejects `path::symbol` (#4792, #4797). This PR does not change it.

## How was this tested?

Run on Windows 11, Python 3.12, in the environment `uv run --all-extras` syncs (`.venv`; the later runs call `.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest` directly because `uv run` rewrites `uv.lock` on Windows).

title: fix(dedup): prefer an AST node over a semantic one in a defining collision
body:
Fixes #4859.

## Bug

When a semantic (doc) node and an AST code node share an id, and the doc's own path is a prefix of that id, `_defines_id` returns True for both. `_collision_rank`'s first key (definer wins) then ties, and nothing after it spoke to tier either, so the comparison fell through "has a source_file" (both do) and the lifecycle penalty (equal) straight to label length. A doc node with a shorter label than the code node it describes could then win.

The code node then carried the doc as its `source_file`. On the next `--update` that re-extracts the doc without that node, `build_merge` replaces the doc's nodes and the code node is deleted outright, although the code file never changed.

Layout that triggers it: `pkg.md` beside `pkg/test_x.py`. The AST id for the file is `pkg_test_x`. The extraction spec asks doc subagents to reuse the AST id for a code entity they describe, so `pkg.md` emits `pkg_test_x`, and `pkg_` is also a prefix of `pkg.md`'s own path — so both sides define the id.

Reported in #4859 with a self-contained repro and a suggested fix; I independently reproduced it and verified the fix. No open or closed PR touches `_collision_rank`'s return tuple.

## Fix

Added a key to `_collision_rank`'s tuple right after the first (definer) key: an AST-tier node now beats a semantic-tier one, read via `_is_ast_tier` (imported locally from `graphify.build` to avoid a circular import, mirroring the existing lazy-import pattern between these two modules). This mirrors the project convention that extracted fact outranks inference about it (`CONTRIBUTING.md`: "Keep inference visibly separate from extracted fact"). It changes no collision where the two sides already differ on the first key.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_dedup.py`:
- `test_ast_node_survives_a_defining_doc_namesake_order_independent`: the exact scenario from #4859 — an AST code node with a longer label survives a defining doc namesake with a shorter one, in both arrival orders.
- `test_semantic_reference_still_loses_to_a_defining_doc` (control): a semantic node that only *references* the id still loses to a doc that *defines* it, tier aside — confirming the new key only matters once the first key ties.

## Verification

- Reproduced the bug pre-fix with the issue's own repro script (`build_merge` twice: once to merge, once to re-extract the doc without the node) — confirmed the code node was lost both times, and that the new regression test fails against the unmodified `_collision_rank` (restored byte-identical after).
- Checked every existing `_collision_rank`/`_defines_id` test in `tests/test_dedup.py`: none sets `_origin` or an AST-shaped `source_location`, so the new key ties for all of them and changes no existing outcome.
- Full suite: `2 failed, 8892 passed, 81 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 2 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py` and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: fix(dedup): keep an AST definer's id when another file's node also defines it (#4859)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4859.

When a doc's own path prefixes a code entity's id (`pkg.md` beside `pkg/test_x.py`, id `pkg_test_x`), both colliding nodes pass the definer key of `_collision_rank`, and the survivor came down to label length. A short doc label kept the id, the code node took `pkg.md` as its `source_file`, and the next re-extract of `pkg.md` deleted it although the code file never changed.

A new helper, `_outranked_by_ast`, lists the non-AST definers of an id that an AST node from a file with a different full stem also defines, when the non-AST node's own file has no AST definer. `_collision_rank` ranks those right behind the other definers. The set is built once per dedup call, so the rank stays a total order (#1851). The check is strict on `_origin == "ast"`, like the ghost pass in `build.py`, because fresh semantic chunks arrive unstamped.

Unchanged:
- collisions with at most one definer;
- a file's AST node and its same-file semantic enrichment (#2091), even when another file also has an AST definer;
- same-stem twins (`x.py`/`x.html`, or slug twins such as `pkg/service.py` and `pkg_service.py`), whether or not the twin rename pass splits them.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: extracted fact is kept separate from inference. A code node keeps its id and `source_file` against another file's non-AST copy, so that copy's re-extract cannot delete it.

Limitations:
- A graph already damaged by this bug (code node carrying the doc as `source_file`) is only repaired when the code file is re-extracted or the graph is rebuilt.
- A twin can still be outranked by an AST node from a third file with a different stem, like any other definer.
- With x.py (AST), x.html, and a third-file definer that wins the twin pass's rank, the twin split is skipped and one twin is dropped. This is the same as on v8 and is not tested here.
- The rule trusts `_origin`. Nothing strips a model-supplied `_origin` from semantic chunks today. That gap predates this PR and could be a separate issue.

- [ ] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [ ] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [ ] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [ ] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.
