title: docs: fix stale language count and Claude-only wording in how-it-works
body:
﻿`docs/how-it-works.md` still said "25 languages supported" and described semantic extraction as Claude-only. This PR fixes both against `v8` @ 0a8cd4e1 (v0.9.97). Docs only, 6 lines changed.

## Changes
- Pass 1: "25 languages" becomes **about 40 languages: 33 via tree-sitter and 7 via built-in parsers** (Dart, Apex, COBOL, Razor, Blade, Pascal, Robot Framework), with a note about optional extras (`graphifyy[sql]`, ...). This matches README.md:119/336 ("~40 languages").
- Pass 3, INFERRED row, similarity edges and the parallel section: "Claude" becomes model-neutral wording, mentioning `graphify extract --backend` (graphify/llm.py:2, `BACKENDS` at graphify/llm.py:140: claude, kimi, ollama, gemini, openai, deepseek, ...).

## Language-count evidence
Two counts were going around: "33 tree-sitter + 7 built-in, 10 extras incl. Robot Framework" and "34 tree-sitter, 9 extras". Both come from the same source; they just count differently.
- **Tree-sitter, 33 languages.** 24 core grammars in pyproject.toml dependencies: python, javascript, typescript, go, rust, java, groovy, c, cpp, ruby, c-sharp, kotlin, scala, php, swift, lua, zig, powershell, elixir, objc, julia, verilog (which also covers .sv, graphify/extractors/verilog.py:242), fortran and bash. tree-sitter-json is counted as config, not a language. The other 9 come from extras: sql (pyproject.toml:101), dm (:113), terraform/hcl (:114), ocaml (:117), commonlisp (:120), vbnet (:125), r (:129), erlang (:130) and solidity (:131).
- **Pascal is the +1.** The `pascal` extra (pyproject.toml:106) is only an optional tree-sitter upgrade. Without it, Pascal falls back to a regex parser (comment near graphify/extract.py:9013, "rather than falling back like Pascal does"). Counting it as tree-sitter gives 34.
- **Built-in, non-tree-sitter parsers (7):** Dart (graphify/extractors/dart.py:15, "using regex"), Apex (graphify/extractors/apex.py:11, "no tree-sitter grammar on PyPI"), COBOL, Razor, Blade (graphify/extract.py:9146), Pascal (fallback) and Robot Framework (`robot.api`, extra `robotframework>=4.0` at pyproject.toml:124).
- **Extras: 10 vs 9.** `_EXTRA_FOR_EXTENSION` (graphify/extract.py:9013) hard-requires 10 extras: vbnet, r, solidity, erlang, sql, terraform, dm, ocaml, commonlisp and robot. Nine are tree-sitter grammars; robot is not. "9" is the tree-sitter-only count.

The docs therefore use the conservative 33 + 7 ≈ 40.

Note: `main` on this repo is stale; this PR targets the default branch `v8`.

title: [Bug]: Java/Kotlin imports do not resolve to the class node, so `affected` silently omits dependents
body:
### What happened?

In a mixed Java/Kotlin repository, references across the two languages do not reach the class node of the referenced symbol, so `graphify affected <Class>` returns an incomplete list with no warning. This makes impact analysis look complete when it is not.

Three cases, all from the minimal example below:

1. **Kotlin imports a Java class:** the edge targets the file node (`Logger.java`), while Java importers also get an edge to the class node. `affected "Logger"` lists `JavaUser.java` but not `KotlinUser.kt`.
2. **Java imports or extends a Kotlin class:** the edges target a separate source-less stub named after the fully qualified name (`com.example.ui.BaseScreen`). `affected "BaseScreen"` and `affected "BaseScreen.kt"` both omit `JavaUser`; only the fully qualified name finds it.
3. **Kotlin calls a Java method:** no `calls` edge is created from `KotlinUser.run()` to `Logger.info()`, while the Java caller gets one.

Expected: `affected "Logger"` and `affected "BaseScreen"` each list both `JavaUser` and `KotlinUser`.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# src/com/example/util/Logger.java
package com.example.util;
public class Logger { public static void info(String m) { System.out.println(m); } }

# src/com/example/ui/BaseScreen.kt
package com.example.ui
open class BaseScreen { fun show() {} }

# src/com/example/app/JavaUser.java
package com.example.app;
import com.example.util.Logger;
import com.example.ui.BaseScreen;
public class JavaUser extends BaseScreen { public void run() { Logger.info("java"); } }

# src/com/example/app/KotlinUser.kt
package com.example.app
import com.example.util.Logger
import com.example.ui.BaseScreen
class KotlinUser : BaseScreen() { fun run() { Logger.info("kotlin") } }

graphify update .
graphify affected "Logger" --depth 1
graphify affected "Logger.java" --depth 1
graphify affected "BaseScreen" --depth 1
graphify affected "com.example.ui.BaseScreen" --depth 1
```

### Graph output

```text
affected "Logger"       -> JavaUser.java [imports], .run() [calls]              (KotlinUser missing)
affected "Logger.java"  -> KotlinUser.kt [imports], JavaUser.java [imports]
affected "BaseScreen"   -> KotlinUser.kt [imports], KotlinUser [inherits]       (JavaUser missing)
affected "com.example.ui.BaseScreen" -> JavaUser.java [imports], JavaUser [inherits]

Edges in graph.json:
KotlinUser.kt  imports  Logger.java (file node)
JavaUser.java  imports  Logger.java (file node)
JavaUser.java  imports  Logger (class node)
KotlinUser.kt  imports  BaseScreen (class node)
JavaUser.java  imports  com.example.ui.BaseScreen (stub, no source_file)
JavaUser       inherits com.example.ui.BaseScreen (stub, no source_file)
KotlinUser     inherits BaseScreen (class node)
JavaUser.run() calls    Logger.info()
(no calls edge from KotlinUser.run())
```

### Environment

- Graphify version: 0.9.92 and 0.9.97
- Operating system: Windows
- Python: 3.14
- Installation method: uv tool install
- No provider API keys set

### Additional context

Same output on 0.9.92 and 0.9.97. Also seen in a private mixed Android project, where a widely used Java class lost all of its Kotlin importers in `affected`.

Possibly related: #2322 (Kotlin cross-file import resolution). #1718 keeps calls from binding across language families; Java and Kotlin share the JVM and call each other directly, so that rule may not fit this pair.

title: feat(plugins): add extractor plugins, so a language can be added by installing a package
body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets a language be added by installing a package, instead of editing `extract.py` and `detect.py`.

**Why I built it.** graphify has no AST extractor for q/kdb+, so q files fall through to the LLM pass, which is slow, costs tokens and isn't deterministic. I wrote qlens (not published yet), a q extractor that uses q's own `parse` as the parser (no LLM, no tree-sitter grammar) and puts a confidence score on every node and edge. I wanted it to feed graphify's AST step for `.q` files, but not by hard-wiring q into `extract.py`. A plugin hook means it ships as its own package, and the next language that doesn't fit the built-in tables can do the same.

A package registers an extractor under the entry-point group `graphify.extractors`. It says which files it handles (suffix, filename, glob or shebang) and gives either a per-file `extract(path)` or a batch `extract_batch(paths, ctx)` that sees all its files at once. Batch exists because some extractors resolve names across files; I wanted this for q/kdb+, where that matters.

`GRAPHIFY_PLUGINS=module:attr` loads a plugin that isn't installed as a package. `graphify plugins` lists what's loaded. The contract is in `docs/PLUGINS.md`.

Built-in extractors still win unless a plugin sets `override_builtin`. With no plugins installed, nothing changes.

If a plugin crashes or returns malformed nodes/edges, the file goes into `failed_sources` and the reason is printed. There is no fallback to another extractor.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI

## Verification & Invariants

- The AST cache key includes the plugin's name and `cache_key`, so changing a plugin's output invalidates its cached files. Batch plugins skip the per-file cache, like JS/TS.
- A plugin's `confidence` is kept as given. If it omits one, it defaults to `EXTRACTED`, so a plugin that infers should say so.
- Plugins load only from installed entry points or `GRAPHIFY_PLUGINS`, never from a project's `.graphifyrc`, because that file belongs to the repo being scanned.
- Extraction depends on which plugins are installed. That's inherent to plugins, and opt-in.

Limits: `register()` is per-process, so spawn workers don't see it (entry points and `GRAPHIFY_PLUGINS` work in workers). Plugins are discovered once per process.

## How was this tested?

`tests/test_plugins.py` adds 31 tests, including a real run through the worker pool.

```text
tests/test_plugins.py                        31 passed
11 existing test files (detect, extract,     1124 passed, 22 skipped, 1 xfailed
  watch, cache, language overrides, ...)       (same files on untouched v8: 1093 passed)
ruff on touched files                        clean
pyright                                      0 errors on plugins.py and on lines this PR changes
```

I also installed a real q/kdb+ extractor as a plugin and ran a mixed Python/YAML/q repo: Python and YAML went through the worker pool, `.q` through the batch plugin.

`tests/test_plugins.py` and `tests/test_detect.py` also pass on Python 3.10 and 3.13 (361 each), besides 3.14.

Not run: the full suite with `--all-extras` (lean environment) and any platform besides macOS.

Existing flake, unrelated: `test_active_scan_root_defaults_to_none` and `test_active_scan_root_set_get_restore_nested` fail when run after `test_extract_cache_location.py`. They fail the same way on untouched `v8`.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] N/A: no skill fragments changed.
- [x] Built-in AST extraction is unchanged and still deterministic.
- [x] No unsafe interpolation; plugins can't be loaded from scanned-repo config.
- [x] No API keys or local-only graph data included.
- [x] AI authorship disclosed: written with AI assistance (Claude).

title: fix(extract): resolve relative JS/TS imports with a ?query or #fragment (#4860)
body:
## Problem
Relative ES module imports that carry a cache-busting query string or fragment
are not resolved:

    import { foo } from './lib/foo.js?v=134';

Instead of an `imports_from` edge to `lib/foo.js`, graphify creates a phantom
node (`ref_lib_foo_js_v_134`) and the real file gets no inbound edge. The
dependent per-symbol `imports` edges and cross-file `calls` are lost too, since
they depend on the module resolving first.

## Root cause
`_resolve_js_module_path` (`graphify/extractors/resolution.py`) resolves a
relative specifier with `start_dir / raw` without stripping the `?query` /
`#fragment` part, so the path never matches a real file. The Markdown extractor
already strips these (`graphify/extractors/markdown.py`).

## Fix
Strip the `?query` / `#fragment` from the relative specifier before resolving,
mirroring the Markdown extractor. Only the relative (`.`-prefixed) branch is
touched; bare and alias specifiers are unchanged.

## Verification
Commands run locally (Python 3, `uv`):
- `uv run pytest tests/test_import_extension_resolution.py` -> 45 passed
  (6 new regression tests; the 4 core ones fail without the fix, confirming the
  phantom `ref_..._v_134` node, and pass with it).
- `uv run ruff check .` -> clean.
- `uv run pyright` -> no new errors introduced by this change (project baseline
  unchanged).
- Full suite `uv run pytest tests` -> 8653 passed. The 7 failures in
  `test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py` are pre-existing on `v8` HEAD (identical with
  this change reverted) and unrelated to this fix.

## Scope / limitations
- Applies to relative specifiers only, matching the issue's root-cause analysis.
- Likely also resolves the `../styles.css?url` case noted in #2849.

Fixes #4860

title: [Bug]: Cypher re-import treats display label changes as new nodes
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README.

### What happened?

The generated Cypher includes the display `label` property in node `MERGE` identity. If a graph keeps the same node ID and file type but updates its display label, the next import matches a different property map. Neo4j can then create a second logical node, or reject the import when that type has an ID uniqueness constraint. ID-only edge matches can also multiply relationships.

Expected: a sequential refresh updates the existing node's display label while retaining one node and one relationship for unchanged IDs and edge properties.

### Steps to reproduce

Generate two exports with only the display label changed:

```python
import networkx as nx
from graphify.export import to_cypher

graph = nx.DiGraph()
graph.add_node("pkg_fn", file_type="code", label="before")
graph.add_node("pkg_peer", file_type="code", label="peer")
graph.add_edge("pkg_fn", "pkg_peer", relation="CALLS", confidence="EXTRACTED")
to_cypher(graph, "before.cypher")
graph.nodes["pkg_fn"]["label"] = "after"
to_cypher(graph, "after.cypher")
```

Import `before.cypher` and then `after.cypher` into a disposable Neo4j database, keeping the database between imports. Compare the number of `Code` nodes with `id = 'pkg_fn'`, their labels, and the `CALLS` relationship count. Repeat in a separate clean database with a `Code.id` uniqueness constraint.

### Error output or graph output

The editable installation generated these statements for those inputs:

```cypher
MERGE (n:Code {id: 'pkg_fn', label: 'before'});
MERGE (n:Code {id: 'pkg_fn', label: 'after'});
```

Both properties participate in matching. The generator output was reproduced on the pinned source below. A database replay has not yet been run, so duplication and constraint failure are consequences of the matching properties rather than claimed database observations.

### Graphify version

`v8` at `0a8cd4e1e342235fe53e881fb5d591bf0460071f`.

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

macOS with Python 3.12.11. The checkout was pinned to the commit below and installed with `uv sync --all-extras`; the editable CLI reports `graphify 0.9.97`. No provider or API configuration is involved. Database execution results are not claimed.

### Additional context

The shared generated-file producer is [`to_cypher`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/0a8cd4e1e342235fe53e881fb5d591bf0460071f/graphify/export.py#L558-L583). Matching the typed node by ID and assigning its display label separately would preserve the intended identity. Historical duplicate cleanup, file-type migration, and concurrent imports are outside this report.

title: fix(extract): resolve Java/Kotlin imports and calls across the JVM (#4874)
body:
## Summary

Java and Kotlin share package names, class names, and call sites. Graphify built its cross-file type index from one extension at a time, so each language could not see the other:

```text
before
KotlinUser.kt --imports--> Logger.java              (file node)
JavaUser.java --imports--> com.example.ui.BaseScreen (source-less stub)
JavaUser     --inherits--> com.example.ui.BaseScreen (source-less stub)
KotlinUser.run() --/--> Logger.info()

after
KotlinUser.kt --imports--> Logger      (class node)
JavaUser.java --imports--> BaseScreen  (class node)
JavaUser     --inherits--> BaseScreen  (class node)
KotlinUser.run() --calls--> Logger.info()
```

This PR builds one JVM-wide package and type index and uses it before the shared call-evidence pass runs. That gives imports, inheritance, references, and member calls one place to resolve the same namespace.

Closes #4874.

## What does this PR do?

- Adds `_jvm_package_name`, `_jvm_imports_by_file`, and `_resolve_jvm_references` in `graphify/extract.py`.
- Indexes sourced Java and Kotlin type nodes by `(package, type name)`.
- Repoints Java and Kotlin import, inheritance, and reference edges only when the written FQN names exactly one sourced type.
- Keeps file-level import edges where they already exist, so `affected <File>` still reaches importers.
- Lets `_resolve_kotlin_member_calls` accept JVM receiver types instead of only `.kt` and `.kts` files.
- Leaves external imports on their stubs. A bare or same-named local class is never chosen.
- Adds a regression suite that uses the issue's four-file project plus external, ambiguous, and non-JVM controls.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Evidence

**Before:** `affected "Logger"` returned only `JavaUser.java`. `affected "BaseScreen"` returned only `KotlinUser.kt`.

**After:**

```text
affected "Logger"
  KotlinUser.kt [imports]
  JavaUser.java [imports]
  .run() [calls] JavaUser.java
  .run() [calls] KotlinUser.kt

affected "BaseScreen"
  KotlinUser.kt [imports]
  JavaUser.java [imports]
  JavaUser [inherits]
  KotlinUser [inherits]
```

The regression suite is 9 tests:

```text
tests/test_4874_jvm_resolution.py    9 passed
```

Full suite:

```text
8975 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed in 510.20s
```

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: if a Java or Kotlin file imports a type that exists in the scanned corpus, and exactly one sourced declaration matches the written package and type name, the edge must reach that declaration node. If the candidate is missing or ambiguous, the reference stays unresolved.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue on clean `0.9.97` (`0a8cd4e1`) before changing code.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** that covers both directions of the JVM namespace.
- [x] Added a **regression test** for each failure and for the controls.
- [x] Kept the PR description synchronized with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented limitations below.

The exact FQN is the only key used. Source-less stubs are not candidates, and two candidates produce no edge. That keeps these existing behaviours:

- `org.springframework.stereotype.Component` does not bind to a local `Component`.
- `a.Logger` and `b.Logger` are separated by the import package.
- A Kotlin call cannot bind to a same-named Python class.

No AST cache schema changes. Resolution runs on every extraction, so a full rebuild is enough to heal an existing graph.

Known limitations:

- Nested JVM types are not indexed as `package.Outer.Inner` yet.
- The shared index reads this run's `per_file` results. Unchanged JVM declarations still need to be added through `resolution_context_nodes` for warm updates to resolve exactly like a cold build.
- Java package and import facts are read from source with a small regex instead of a second tree-sitter parse. The tests cover the normal declaration forms, not every legal Java formatting variant.

## How was this tested?

```text
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_4874_jvm_resolution.py
9 passed

PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
8975 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed in 510.20s

graphify update <fixture>
graphify affected Logger --depth 2
graphify affected BaseScreen --depth 2
```

The CLI output matches the expected result in #4874.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Reverting the branch restores the previous edges, and no persisted schema or cache format changes.

**Blast Radius:** resolver. Mixed Java/Kotlin repositories get new class-level edges. Single-language repositories and non-JVM languages keep their existing behaviour.

A graph built before this change may keep its old edges until a full rebuild. A warm `--update` is not guaranteed to repair it.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments.
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).

title: fix(serve): print confidence_score in path, explain and neighbors output
body: ## What does this PR do? `graph.json` stores a `confidence_score` on INFERRED edges. For example, C# interface dispatch (`interface_dispatch.py`, `_dispatch_confidence`) writes 0.85, 0.75 or 0.65 depending on how many implementers there are. The text renderers printed only the bare tag, though, so `[INFERRED]` didn't tell you whether an edge was a strong or a weak inference. This adds one shared helper, `_confidence_tag()` in `serve.py`. Wherever an edge's confidence is printed in `path`, `explain` and neighbors output, it now shows `[INFERRED 0.75]` when the edge has a score: - CLI `path` (`cli.py`) - CLI `explain` (`cli.py`) - MCP `shortest_path` (`serve.py` `_shortest_path_text`) - MCP `get_neighbors` (`serve.py` `_neighbor_lines`) Repro from the issue (`Report.cs`, then `graphify update .`): ```text before: --> .Build() [dispatches_to] [INFERRED] Report.cs:L2 after: --> .Build() [dispatches_to] [INFERRED 0.75] Report.cs:L2 before: .Run() --calls [INFERRED]--> .Build() --dispatches_to [INFERRED]--> .Build() after: .Run() --calls [INFERRED 0.85]--> .Build() --dispatches_to [INFERRED 0.75]--> .Build() ``` I've since merged v8 (0.9.98) into this branch. The score now sits alongside what landed there: the weaker `also_seen` evidence shows as `[AMBIGUOUS 0.40/INFERRED 0.75]`, and the weakest-hop `Path confidence:` line gets the score too. EXTRACTED hops still print no score. The test expectations now use the new C# owner labels, like `PdfReport.Build()`. The `query` EDGE lines and `affected` (#2352) are out of scope and unchanged. Fixes #4882 ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Tests or CI - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Security fix ## Verification & Invariants Invariant: inference stays visibly separate from extracted fact, and the output never shows more precision than `graph.json` actually stores. - A score is printed only for a non-EXTRACTED edge whose stored `confidence_score` is a finite int or float. EXTRACTED edges stay `[EXTRACTED]` because they are 1.0 by definition, and showing that everywhere would only add noise. - A missing, `None`, string, boolean or NaN score leaves the bare tag. The fallback is the old output, not a guessed number. - Scores are formatted as `{:.2f}`, which matches the two-decimal tiers in the extraction rubric. - Display only: no persisted graph or cache state changes, and no AST cache schema bump is needed. - [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide. - [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant. - [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary. - [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test. - [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation. - [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly. Limitation: a score stored as a numeric string (for example `"0.75"`) is not coerced and renders bare. ## How was this tested? `tests/test_confidence_score_output.py` runs the issue's `Report.cs` repro through `extract` → `build_from_json` → `to_json`. It asserts the stored scores (0.85 and 0.75), then checks CLI `explain`, CLI `path`, MCP `shortest_path` and MCP `get_neighbors`. It also has parametrized boundary cases for `_confidence_tag`. On v8 without the fix, the four output tests fail. ```text uv run pytest tests/test_confidence_score_output.py -q # 15 passed uv run pytest tests/ -q # 9161 passed, 18 skipped, 1 xfailed (after merging v8 0.9.98) uv run ruff check . # All checks passed uv run pyright # no new errors (667 vs 668 on v8 base) graphify update /tmp/repro && graphify explain report_ireport_build && graphify path report_exporter_run report_pdfreport_build ``` ## Graphify-specific checklist - [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. title: fix(csharp): label C# methods with their owning type (#4883)
body: ## What does this PR do? Every C# method node was labeled `.Name()`, so on the #4883 repro the interface method and both implementations all printed as `.Build()` and only the line number told them apart: ```text Node: .Build() --> .Build() [dispatches_to] [INFERRED] Report.cs:L2 --> .Build() [dispatches_to] [INFERRED] Report.cs:L3 <-- .Run() [calls] [INFERRED] Report.cs:L7 ``` After this change (`graphify update .` then `graphify explain report_ireport_build`): ```text Node: IReport.Build() ID: report_ireport_build <-- IReport [method] [EXTRACTED] Report.cs:L1 --> PdfReport.Build() [dispatches_to] [INFERRED] Report.cs:L2 --> CsvReport.Build() [dispatches_to] [INFERRED] Report.cs:L3 <-- Exporter.Run() [calls] [INFERRED] Report.cs:L7 ``` Node IDs and edges are unchanged; only the display label changes. **Where the label is assigned.** The `.Name()` shape is load-bearing during extraction: the direct-call label index, the C# member-call resolvers, interface dispatch (`interface_dispatch.method_label`), and the build method-ghost passes all match on it. So extraction still emits `.Name()`. The owner-qualified label is applied as the last step of `build_from_json` and in both `--no-cluster` writers (`watch._rebuild_code`, `cli`). This is the same placement and contract as the #2032 file-label disambiguation. The owner comes from the source of the method's `method` edge, read through `_src`/`_tgt` on undirected graphs. **Reading persisted labels back.** Code that reads labels from an existing `graph.json` now converts `Owner.Name()` back to `.Name()` through one helper, `bare_csharp_method_label`: - `extract()` normalizes `resolution_context_nodes` on intake. The caller's dicts are copied, never mutated. Without this, an incremental rebuild of only the caller loses the `calls` edge into an unchanged file. - `build._alias_index` (the `_` alias) and the #3705 method-ghost index in `build_from_json`. - `analyze._is_file_node`, so C# methods stay out of god nodes and knowledge-gap reporting. The issue's refs (`extractors/csharp.py` ~49/~126) are the type-def index and namespace lookup. Both already reject dotted labels and never see method labels, so they need no change. Fixes #4883 ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Tests or CI - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Security fix ## Verification & Invariants Invariants protected: - **Node identity:** IDs and the edge set are unchanged. The test compares the built graph against raw `extract()` output. - **Resolver contract:** `extract()` still returns `.Name()` for C# methods. - **Incremental = full build:** with only the caller re-extracted, the `calls` and `dispatches_to` edges and the labels match a full rebuild. - **Idempotent:** labels are derived from the bare form, so rebuilding from an already-qualified graph never produces `PdfReport.PdfReport.Build()`. - **Fail-closed:** a method with no owner, with owners carrying different labels, or with a non-plain owner label (for example a dotted namespace) keeps `.Name()`. - **Language gate:** the change applies only to files whose `effective_suffix` is `.cs`. Java and Swift labels are unchanged (tested). Persisted state: existing graphs pick up the new C# labels on the next build. Extraction output and the per-file AST cache are unchanged, so no cache schema bump is needed. Community names derived from C# method labels (for example in `GRAPH_REPORT.md` or the wiki) may change text accordingly. - [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide. - [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant. - [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary. - [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test. - [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation. - [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly. Each added piece was shown to be necessary by reverting it on its own and re-running `tests/test_csharp_method_owner_labels.py`: - Build/writer wiring reverted: 6 tests fail (issue repro clustered and `--no-cluster`, incremental, context normalization, god nodes, ghost collapse). - `extract()` context normalization reverted: 2 tests fail (incremental rebuild, context normalization). - `analyze` predicate reverted: 1 test fails (god nodes). - Build ghost-index normalization reverted: 1 test fails (#3705 ghost collapse). - Build alias-index normalization reverted: 1 test fails (class-segment-less alias). **Limitations / unsupported cases** - **Swift has the same problem** (`protocol Report`, `PdfReport`, `CsvReport` all show `.build()`). It is not changed here. Swift needs the same treatment plus its own checks: extension members merged across files by `_merge_swift_extensions`, and the Swift member-call and protocol-dispatch resolvers reading context labels. The helpers here are suffix-gated, so a follow-up can extend them, but that is a separate concern with its own tests. - Razor (`.razor` / `.cshtml`) methods keep `.Name()`. Only `.cs` (including rcfile-mapped suffixes) is relabeled. - Nested types show their immediate owner only (`Inner.Deep()`, not `Outer.Inner.Deep()`). ## How was this tested? ```text # repro from the issue (Report.cs), before and after graphify update . graphify explain report_ireport_build uv run pytest tests/test_csharp_method_owner_labels.py -q # 19 passed uv run pytest tests -q # 8985 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed uv run ruff check . # All checks passed uv run pyright graphify/extractors/csharp.py graphify/build.py graphify/analyze.py \ graphify/extract.py graphify/watch.py graphify/cli.py tests/test_csharp_method_owner_labels.py # no new diagnostics vs. upstream v8 (remaining errors are pre-existing) ``` ## Graphify-specific checklist - [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. *(N/A: no skill fragments touched)* - [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). - [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python). - [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included. - [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

title: fix(path): resolve Type.Method to the member, not the type (#4884)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4884.

`graphify path "Exporter.Run" "PdfReport.Build"` answered with a route to the `PdfReport` class, not to its method. The labels are `PdfReport` and `.Build()`, so `Type.Method` matches no label and goes to the scorer, which settles on the type.

`_resolve_python_qualified` now tries `Type.Method` through the type's `method`/`contains` edge, after the module path lookup, so `pkg.mod.func` (#4366) still wins when both match. It sits under `_find_node_tiers`, so `explain` and `get_node` get it too.

- two types with that name, or overloads in one file: refused with candidates, by the existing `_tier_refusal`
- a known type with no such member (`PdfReport.Nope`): `No node matching 'PdfReport::Nope' found; PdfReport defines no 'Nope'.`, the same fail closed as `file::symbol` (#4264)

Limitations:

- only the segment right before the member is checked. the graph has no namespaces, so `Ns.PdfReport.Build` and `Wrong.PdfReport.Build` both find `PdfReport.Build`
- inherited members aren't found. `CsvReport.Inherited` with the method on a base class gets the "defines no" message, where it used to give the class

title: fix(build): keep a collapsed edge's weaker evidence in also_seen (#4881)
body: ## What does this PR do? Fixes #4881. When two edges with the same relation land on the same node pair, `build_from_json` keeps the higher-confidence one (#3711, `graphify/build.py` at the `_CONFIDENCE_RANK` comparison) and throws the other away. The usual case is a semantic-pass edge duplicating an AST edge. An AMBIGUOUS or INFERRED duplicate therefore left no trace in `graph.json`, even though `path` already shows tag unions such as `[EXTRACTED/INFERRED]` for parallel edges. This change keeps the winner exactly as before and adds the loser's provenance to it: - **`also_seen`**: the surviving edge lists every other copy's `confidence`, `confidence_score`, `source_file` and `source_location`, weakest first. An entry that only repeats the winner's own provenance, or another entry, is dropped. That keeps a rebuild that re-feeds `graph.json` (the `update` path) idempotent. A malformed `also_seen` read back from disk is reduced to its valid scalar fields. - **No leaked fields from the loser**: `G.add_edge(**attrs)` merges attribute dicts. When a stronger edge without a score replaced a scored INFERRED one, the loser's `confidence_score` stayed on the EXTRACTED winner. Provenance fields that only the displaced edge carried are now removed from the stored edge, and that edge's own values go into `also_seen` instead. - **The weakest tag is shown**: `graphify path` and the MCP `shortest_path` tool include `also_seen` tags in the hop label, as they already do for parallel edges. For example: `--dispatches_to [AMBIGUOUS/INFERRED]-->`. This is a one-line change at each of the two hop-formatting sites. - `docs/how-it-works.md` documents the new optional edge field. Repro from the issue: build `Report.cs` (`IReport.Build()`, `PdfReport`/`CsvReport` implementing it, `Exporter.Run()` calling `_report.Build()`) together with a weaker same-relation duplicate of the `report_ireport_build -> report_pdfreport_build` `dispatches_to` edge, for example AMBIGUOUS 0.4 from a notes file. Before: the stored edge is `INFERRED 0.75 L2` and the AMBIGUOUS copy is gone. After: the same winner, plus `also_seen: [{confidence: AMBIGUOUS, confidence_score: 0.4, source_file: notes.md, source_location: L12}]`, in either arrival order. #4885's path-confidence summary is stacked on this branch as PR B ([branch `cursor/4885-path-confidence-b0a3`](https://github.com/SyedFahad7/graphify/pull/6)). **Overlap with #4882 / PR #4888:** that PR rewrites the same `confs = sorted(...)` hop-tag line in `serve.py` and `cli.py`. Whichever lands second needs a one-line merge per file: `sorted({_confidence_tag(e) for d in datas for e in edge_evidence(d) if e.get("confidence")})`. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [x] Documentation - [ ] Tests or CI - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Security fix ## Verification & Invariants **Invariant:** collapsing same-relation duplicates must not erase provenance (CONTRIBUTING, "Preserve provenance" and "Keep inference visibly separate from extracted fact"). The winner's `relation`, `confidence`, `confidence_score`, `source_file` and `source_location` are decided exactly as before. Only the loser's record is added. A field the winner does not carry no longer survives from the loser. **Persisted state:** `graph.json` edges may gain an optional `also_seen` list. Old graphs load unchanged. A rebuild over a graph that already has `also_seen` does not duplicate entries (covered by a test). Neo4j/FalkorDB pushes already skip non-scalar properties, GraphML JSON-encodes them, and Cypher export only reads `confidence`. title: feat(path): report path confidence as the weakest hop (#4885)
body:
## What does this PR do? Fixes #4885. > **Stacked on PR A** (`fix/4881-keep-weaker-evidence`, [#4881 / also_seen](https://github.com/SyedFahad7/graphify/pull/5)). This branch is cut from that branch and targets `v8`, so until PR A merges the diff also shows PR A's commit `3304de16`. This PR's own change is the single commit `6e6e68a2`. Review or merge PR A first. `graphify path` and the MCP `shortest_path` tool label each hop separately. A path with one INFERRED or AMBIGUOUS hop among EXTRACTED hops therefore reads as a list of independent tags, and nothing marks the path as a whole as uncertain. Both now end with one summary line. Repro from the issue (`Report.cs`: `IReport.Build()`, `PdfReport`/`CsvReport` implementing it, `Exporter.Run()` calling `_report.Build()`; `graphify update .`): ```text $ graphify path report_exporter_run report_pdfreport_build Shortest path (2 hops): .Run() --calls [INFERRED]--> .Build() --dispatches_to [INFERRED]--> .Build() Path confidence: INFERRED (weakest hop 2: dispatches_to, score 0.75) ``` The MCP `shortest_path` result ends with the same line. How the summary is computed (`_path_confidence_line` in `graphify/serve.py`, also called by the CLI path in `graphify/cli.py`): - A hop's strength is the weakest evidence it carries. That includes all of its parallel edges and, from PR A, its `also_seen` entries. - Hops are compared by `_CONFIDENCE_RANK` (`graphify/build.py`) first, then by the lowest `confidence_score`. A missing score never counts as weaker than a present one. On a tie, the first such hop is named. - `, score X` is printed only when the weakest evidence has a score. - A hop with no recognised confidence tag makes the result `Path confidence: unknown (hop N: has no confidence tag)`. The other hops cannot vouch for it. - The `shortest_path` tool description and the README sentence about `graphify path` mention the new line. ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [x] Documentation - [ ] Tests or CI - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Security fix ## Verification & Invariants **Invariant:** a path is never reported as more certain than its least certain hop (CONTRIBUTING, "Keep inference visibly separate from extracted fact"). The existing hop segments are byte-identical. The only output change is one extra line after them, so anything matching `Shortest path (N hops):` or hop substrings is unaffected. Nothing is persisted, so no graph or cache state changes. - [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide. - [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant. - [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary. - [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test. - [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation. - [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly. **Limitations:** - The summary covers only the single shortest path that `path` returns. Comparing several routes to the same target is not attempted. - #4882 (PR #4888, scores printed in hop tags) edits the same `confs = sorted(...)` hop-tag line in `serve.py` and `cli.py`. Whichever lands second has a trivial one-line merge per file. This PR's own additions (`hop_datas`, the summary line, the helper) are outside those lines. ## How was this tested? `tests/test_path_confidence.py` (7 tests) covers: - the exact repro line through the CLI and through the MCP `_shortest_path_text`; - tier taking precedence over score; - the lowest score breaking a tier tie, and a missing score not counting as weaker; - all-EXTRACTED paths naming the first hop; - parallel edges and `also_seen` counting toward their hop; - a hop with no tag making the path unknown. On PR A's commit, without this change, the module fails (`_path_confidence_line` does not exist), and the repro output has no summary line. ```text uv run pytest tests/test_path_confidence.py tests/test_edge_also_seen.py tests/test_path_cli.py tests/test_serve.py -q # 215 passed uv run pytest tests -q # 8983 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed uv run ruff check . # All checks passed uv run pyright # 667 errors, identical to the upstream v8 baseline (no new ones) graphify update . && graphify path report_exporter_run report_pdfreport_build # output above ``` ## Graphify-specific checklist - [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (No fragments touched.) - [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). - [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python). - [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included. - [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

title: fix(path): resolve a Type.Member endpoint to the member, not the type (#4884)
body:
## What does this PR do? Fixes #4884. When `graphify path` got an endpoint in `Type.Method` form, it resolved it to the class and printed a misleading route. A member's label is `.Build()`, so `PdfReport.Build` matched none of `_find_node_tiers`' exact tiers. `_resolve_path_endpoint` then fell through to token scoring, which picked the `PdfReport` class. With the issue's `Report.cs`: - `path "Exporter.Run" "PdfReport.Build"` printed `Exporter <--contains-- Report.cs --contains--> PdfReport`, a route between two classes through the file, presented as if it joined the two methods. - `path "Run" "PdfReport.Build"` found no path, because no edge leads from a method back up to a class. The change: - `_find_node_tiers` now resolves `Type.Member` and `Outer.Inner.Member` (an optional trailing `()` is allowed) by walking the owner type's `method`, `defines` and `contains` edges. This only runs after the dotted-Python form (#4366) finds nothing, and only when no node is literally labelled with the query. The hits are returned as the exact tier, so `path`, `explain`, get_node and `query` all get them. Several hits go through the existing refusal with their candidate ids, rather than one being guessed: the same member name in two files, or overloads in one type. - `_resolve_path_endpoint` fails closed when the type exists but declares no member of that name, the way a `file::symbol` miss does (#4264). It returns not-found (exit 4) instead of scoring its way to the type. - Membership direction comes from the stored arc, or from the `_src`/`_tgt` markers (#2309). So `Inner.Outer` does not resolve just because `Outer` contains `Inner`. After the fix, both commands from the issue print `.Run() --calls--> .Build() --dispatches_to--> .Build()` (2 hops). `IReport.Build` and `CsvReport.Build()` resolve to their own methods. `PdfReport.Missing` is refused with `no type 'PdfReport' declares 'Missing'`. This does not depend on the label change in #4883. It matches on the label as it is stored today (`.Build()`), and would keep matching a bare `Build()` or `Build` label too. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Documentation - [x] Tests or CI - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Security fix ## Verification & Invariants The invariant is the README contract: "a name that matches several nodes is refused with the candidates listed rather than guessed". A `Type.Member` endpoint now resolves to that member or is refused. It never resolves silently to the type. What stays the same: - A node whose label literally equals the dotted query still wins, because the new lookup is skipped when `_label_has_literal_exact_match` holds. - `pkg.mod.func` still resolves through the module file first. - A dotted query whose owner is not a type with members still goes to ordinary scoring. - No persisted state, cache or extraction output changes. This is lookup-only code in `serve.py`. Limitations / unsupported cases: - A namespace qualifier (`Acme.Io.Outer.Go`) cannot narrow the match. The file owns the type, not the namespace node, so there is no edge to walk. Such a query is refused, and the refusal lists the bare type's same-named members with their ids for a retry. - Only `.`-separated forms are handled. `Type::Member` is still read as `path::symbol`. - [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide. - [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant. - [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary. - [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test. - [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation. - [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly. ## How was this tested? `tests/test_path_type_member.py` extracts the issue's `Report.cs` with the real C# extractor and runs the CLI and the MCP `shortest_path` tool against it. It also uses synthetic graphs for: - the same member in two files - same-type overloads - nested types and edge direction - a namespace qualifier - a missing member - a literal dotted label - an owner that is not a type Without the `serve.py` change, 11 of the 12 tests fail. The one that still passes guards the unchanged fall-through behaviour. ```text uv sync --all-extras --frozen graphify update . # in a scratch dir holding the issue's Report.cs, then the two `graphify path` commands above uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_path_type_member.py -q # 12 passed (11 failed with serve.py reverted) uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_path_type_member.py tests/test_path_cli.py tests/test_serve.py tests/test_lookup_exit_codes.py -q # 227 passed uv run --frozen pytest tests/ -q --tb=short # 8978 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed uv run --frozen ruff check . # All checks passed uv run --frozen pyright graphify/serve.py tests/test_path_type_member.py # 67 errors, same as v8 before the change; none in the new code ``` ## Graphify-specific checklist - [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. (No skill fragments touched.) - [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables). - [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python). - [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included. - [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.
  
### Update (follow-up commit c3ad1778, addressing bot review) - Lookup order: the `Type.Member` lookup now runs only after exact node id, label and source-path matches find nothing, and never for a query that names a source file (`utils.py` was previously refused; `config.json` previously resolved to a `Config.Json()` member). - Direction: owner/member direction comes from `_src`/`_tgt` edge markers, else the stored arc in a directed graph; undirected edges without markers are skipped. - Limitations: a query that is also a file name resolves to the file (the member stays reachable by node id); unmarked undirected edges are not used for member lookup. - Tests: +5 (utils.py endpoint, config.json vs Config.Json(), exact dotted id, undirected with/without markers); `tests/test_path_type_member.py` 17 passed; full suite 8983 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed.

title: fix(extract): link PHP Scope::MEMBER accesses in class-level initializers (#4648)
body:
## Problem
PHP `Scope::MEMBER` accesses (enum cases / class constants) in **class-level
initializers** produce no edge:

```php
enum Role { case Viewer; }

class Perms {
    private const array MAP = ['posts.read' => Role::Viewer];   // const value
    private Role $fallback = Role::Viewer;                       // property default
    public function __construct(private Role $default = Role::Viewer) {}  // param default
}
```

Only accesses inside a function or method body get a `references_constant`
edge, so these common shapes (permission catalogs, state-machine maps,
config-like classes) are silently missing from the graph.

## Root cause
The `class_constant_access_expression -> references_constant` edge is emitted in
the per-function-body call-walk, where the source is the enclosing callable.
Class-level initializers (const values, property defaults, parameter defaults,
including promoted constructor properties) are never inside a function body, so
that walk never visits them.

## Fix
Emit `references_constant` edges for `class_constant_access_expression` nodes
found in class-level initializer positions during the structural walk, attributed
to the enclosing class (consistent with how PHP property/parameter *type*
references are already attributed). Const values and property defaults are handled
where those declarations are walked; parameter defaults are handled alongside the
existing PHP formal-parameters pass.

## Verification
Commands run locally (Python 3, `uv`), rebased onto current `v8` (0.9.99):
- `uv run pytest tests/test_php_class_const_initializer_refs.py` -> 5 passed.
  5 new regression tests cover all four positions plus a method-body control;
  the four initializer tests fail without the change and pass with it.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -k php` -> 108 passed, 10 skipped.
- `uv run ruff check .` -> clean.
- `uv run pyright` -> 690 errors, identical to the parent commit (no new errors).
- Full suite `uv run pytest tests` -> 8879 passed. The 7 failures in
  `tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py` are pre-existing on `v8` HEAD (JS/Swift
  id-collision tests), unrelated to this PHP-only change.

## Scope / limitations
- Resolution matches the existing `references_constant` behavior; the scope class
  is resolved by name, so an access to a class only reachable cross-file resolves
  through the same stub path as other PHP references.
- Edges are deduplicated per declaration/parameter.

Fixes #4648

title: watch liveness check resolves relative source identities against process CWD instead of watch root
body:
Version 0.9.93, macOS, daily job under launchd.

SYMPTOM: incremental code rebuild refuses to overwrite (fail-closed, saved semantic nodes missing) only when run under the scheduler; the same rebuild from a shell rooted at the watch root succeeds.

ROOT CAUSE: the alive check does Path(identity).exists() where identity is a watch-root-relative source path. Under launchd with WorkingDirectory set to the home dir, existing files (e.g. memory slash plan docs) resolve to a nonexistent absolute path, are judged deleted, their semantic nodes are evicted, and fail-closed correctly refuses the write. Manual runs succeed only because the shell CWD happens to equal the watch root.

SUGGESTED FIX: resolve against the watch root at the call site (watch_root.joinpath(relative_id).exists()), not bare Path(relative_id).exists(). Prefer this over storing absolute identities (keeps watches relocatable, avoids leaking home-dir layout into stored state).

REGRESSION TEST: parametrize CWD (project tmp dir vs home dir), assert an existing file stays alive and a truly-deleted file still trips refusal.

title: fix(fortran): emit an inherits edge for a derived type extends clause
body:
## Bug

The `derived_type_definition` handler only ever read the `type_name` child of a `derived_type_statement` and ignored the sibling `base_type_specifier` node that holds Fortran's `type, extends(base) :: derived` inheritance syntax. Every other OOP-capable language extractor in this codebase (C++, Ruby, C#, Java, Kotlin, Scala, PHP, Swift, ObjC, Julia, PowerShell, Groovy, Apex, Razor, SystemVerilog, Common Lisp) emits an `inherits` edge for its own inheritance syntax — Fortran was the one silent gap, so Fortran OOP hierarchies (abstract base types, polymorphic dispatch via `class(base)`) never got an inherits edge at all, with zero existing tests covering it.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via self-audit of `graphify/extractors/fortran.py`. Checked the one open Fortran PR (#4450, "link Fortran modules and submodule procedures") — its diff touches `derived_type_definition` only for submodule/`module_procedure` bookkeeping, never reads `base_type_specifier` or emits `inherits`. No overlap.

## Fix

In the `derived_type_definition` branch, after locating `type_name`, also look for a `base_type_specifier` child of `derived_type_statement`, read its `identifier` child as the base type name, resolve it via the existing `ensure_named_node` helper (so a cross-module base type still becomes the standard sourceless stub, consistent with the file's existing type-bound-procedure/generic-interface handling), and emit `type_nid --inherits--> base_nid`.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_languages.py`:
- `test_fortran_derived_type_extends_emits_inherits_edge` — regression for a plain `extends(shape)` clause.
- `test_fortran_abstract_extends_also_emits_inherits_edge` — the combined `abstract, extends(...)` specifier still works.
- `test_fortran_plain_derived_type_has_no_inherits_edge` — control: a bare `type :: name` with no `extends()` must not gain a spurious inherits edge.

## Verification

- Confirmed the bug pre-fix via `git show upstream/v8:...` swapped into place (restored byte-identical afterward): exactly the 2 regression tests fail; the control passes both before and after.
- Full suite: `2 failed, 9117 passed, 82 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 2 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py` and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: AST mode: opt-in to index data JSON skipped by _is_config_json (since 0.8.37)
body:
## Summary

Since 0.9.70, `graphify update` (AST mode) skips any JSON file that `_is_config_json` does not classify as a config or manifest. For repositories whose configuration lives in plain JSON files with project-specific keys, those files drop out of the graph, and no flag, environment variable or rc key brings them back. Could AST mode get an opt-in to index them?

## Measurement (0.8.30 vs 0.9.97, same commit, `graphify update . --force`, fresh copy per run)

| Version | Nodes | Edges | Distinct source files | JSON sources |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0.8.30 | 9996 | 13367 | 775 | 57 |
| 0.9.97 | 9538 | 14262 | 731 | 2 |

55 JSON files indexed by 0.8.30 are absent in 0.9.97. They are framework configuration (allowlists, registries, gate definitions, a hooks settings template), with object roots and project-specific keys. Only `package.json` and an `mcp.json` remain.

## Where it happens

- `extractors/json_config.py:293-294` returns `{"nodes": [], "edges": [], "skipped": "data json (not a config/manifest)"}` when `_is_config_json` is false.
- `_is_config_json` accepts only names in `_CONFIG_JSON_NAMES`, a few rc suffixes, or a root key in `_CONFIG_JSON_KEYS`.
- `extract.py:8855-8859` says data JSON is left to the LLM semantic pass (#1224).

## What I checked for an override

- CLI flags of `update` and `extract`: none mention JSON.
- `.graphifyinclude`: removed (#2112), so it now only warns.
- `.graphifyignore` / `.gitignore` `!` patterns: these act at detection, and the files are already detected.
- `language.json=...` in the rc file only maps the suffix.
- `GRAPHIFY_*` environment variables: none relate to JSON.

## Request

An opt-in for AST mode, for example `--include-data-json`, a `json.index=all` rc key, or an include glob list, that bypasses `_is_config_json` for matching paths. The current default could stay as it is. Without the opt-in, the alternatives are a deep (LLM) pass for files that need no LLM, or keeping the 0.8.x line.

title: fix(dart): resolve every superclass constraint in a mixin on clause
body:
## Bug

A Dart mixin's `on` clause may list several comma-separated superclass constraints (`mixin Selectable on Comparable<T>, State<X> {}`), unlike `extends`, which only ever has one target since Dart classes have single inheritance. The class-header parser in `extract_dart` only ever captured the single type name immediately after `extends`/`on` via a regex with no comma handling. For `extends` that's correct; for `on` it silently dropped every constraint after the first — no node, no edge, and the leftover `, State<X>` text was neither consumed nor matched by the later `with`/`implements` checks, so it just vanished.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via self-audit of `graphify/extractors/dart.py` (`csharp.py` had nothing demonstrable after a thorough read). The only open PR touching the same class-header block (#2249, "reduce Dart extraction noise") refactors the mixin/interface cleanup helper but does not touch the `extends`/`on` comma-list parsing itself — no overlap. Three other open PRs (#3651, #2114, and closed #415) are full tree-sitter rewrites that would eventually replace this regex extractor entirely, but none are merged, so this interim fix is still worth landing.

## Fix

Refactored the `extends`/`on` parsing into a `_consume_generic_args` helper plus a loop that, only when the keyword is `on`, keeps consuming further comma-separated `, TypeName<Generics>` entries into a `base_entries` list. `extends` still only ever reads one entry, so its behavior is unchanged. The later "map inheritance relation" block now iterates every entry in `base_entries` instead of a single `base_class`/`generics` pair, so each constraint gets its own `inherits` edge and its generic argument still surfaces as a `references` edge.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_dart.py`:
- `test_mixin_on_clause_with_multiple_superclass_constraints` — regression: asserts both constraints get `inherits` edges, and the second one's generic argument still surfaces as a `references` edge.
- `test_mixin_on_clause_with_single_superclass_constraint_is_unaffected` — control: a single-constraint `on` clause still resolves exactly as before.

## Verification

- Confirmed the bug pre-fix via `git show upstream/v8:...` swapped into place (restored byte-identical afterward): the regression test fails (only the first constraint got an edge), the control passes both before and after.
- Full suite: `3 failed, 9115 passed, 82 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 3 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py`, `test_r_extractor.py`, and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: fix(elixir): scope a bare call to the caller's own module first
body:
## Bug

The in-file resolver for an unqualified (bare) Elixir call built one flat `label_to_nid` dict mapping bare function name to node id across the entire file, with a later-walked definition silently overwriting an earlier one while the table was built. In a file with two modules that each define a same-named function (e.g. `ModuleA.process/1` and `ModuleB.process/1`), a bare call to `process(x)` made inside `ModuleA`'s own `go/1` resolved to whichever module's `process` was walked last, not to the caller's own sibling function — misattributing the call edge to a completely unrelated module.

This is the same class of bug issue #4001 (fixed by merged PR #4015) addressed for the CROSS-FILE resolver (scoping bare calls to `import`/`use`), but that fix only patched `extract.py`'s cross-file `raw_calls` path via `elixir_call_scope`; it never touched this file's own in-file `label_to_nid` lookup, so the identical mis-binding still happens for same-file multi-module collisions.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via self-audit of `graphify/extractors/elixir.py` (`erlang.py` had nothing beyond the known pre-existing flaky test, which is unrelated and untouched). Checked #4001/#4015 and #4206/#4213 (both merged, different bugs) and the two open elixir-touching PRs (#2970, #2717) — neither touches `label_to_nid` or `module_defs`. No overlap.

## Fix

Removed the flat `label_to_nid` table entirely. Extended `module_defs` (already used for qualified `Mod.fun()` resolution) to also register top-level (no-module) defs, keyed by `(container, func_name)` where `container` is the def's own enclosing module or the file node. Bare-call resolution now checks the caller's own container's defs first, then walks the same `_call_scope_for` import/use chain already used by the cross-file pass — so it only ever binds within actual lexical scope, the same invariant #4001's fix already enforces across files, just applied to the in-file path too.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_elixir_unqualified_call_scope.py`:
- `test_same_file_sibling_module_does_not_steal_a_bare_call` — the exact scenario above. Both candidate targets share the identical label `process()`, so a label-pair assertion (the pattern the rest of this file uses) can't tell them apart and would pass regardless of which one won; this asserts on the resolved target's node id directly instead.
- `test_same_file_own_module_call_still_resolves` (control): a bare call to a genuine sibling within the same module, with no other same-named def anywhere in the file, still resolves.

## Verification

- Directly reproduced the bug against `extract_elixir()` and the full `extract()` pipeline with explicit node ids (not just labels): pre-fix, `go()` resolved to `ModuleB`'s `process()`; post-fix, to `ModuleA`'s own.
- Full suite: `2 failed, 9116 passed, 82 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 2 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py` and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: fix(r): recognize contains as a class inheritance keyword
body:
## Bug

`add_class_members` (shared by `setClass`/`setRefClass` and `R6Class`-family class definitions) only ever recognized the key `inherit` when looking for a class's superclass argument. That's R6Class's own spelling. But `setClass` and `setRefClass` (S4/R5 classes) both spell the identical argument `contains` instead — e.g. `Derived <- setRefClass("Derived", contains = "Base", ...)`. Since only `inherit` was checked, every S4/R5 inheritance relationship was silently dropped — no `inherits` edge emitted at all, with no error.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via self-audit of `graphify/extractors/r.py` (`markdown.py` had nothing unclaimed — it's extremely heavily iterated, and every plausible gap checked was already fixed and documented with an issue number). Checked the open R-touching PRs (#2150, #2065 — no overlap; #1759 is a stale, pre-tree-sitter regex-based R extractor proposal that predates and doesn't touch the current implementation) — no overlap.

## Fix

Changed the single-key check to a set membership check: `if key in {"inherit", "contains"}`, reusing the exact same base-name lookup, external-class node creation, and `inherits` edge emission already in place for `inherit`. `add_class_members` is only ever called from the two `setClass`/`setRefClass`/R6-constructor call sites, so there's no risk of `contains` meaning something unrelated elsewhere.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_r_extractor.py`:
- `test_r_setrefclass_contains_inheritance_is_recognised` — regression: a `setRefClass` that inherits via `contains = "Base"` now gets its `inherits` edge.
- `test_r6class_inherit_still_recognised` (control): R6Class's own `inherit` keyword still works unchanged alongside the new `contains` handling.

## Verification

- Confirmed the bug pre-fix via `git show upstream/v8:...` swapped into place (restored byte-identical afterward): the regression test fails, the control passes both before and after.
- Full suite: `2 failed, 9116 passed, 82 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 2 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py` and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: fix(hooks): decode git rev-parse paths as UTF-8
body:
## What does this PR do?

On Windows, `graphify hook install` in a linked worktree whose path has a non-ASCII character writes the hooks into a mangled copy of the path, so git never runs them:

```text
post-commit: installed at C:\Users\...\cafÃ©\main\.git\hooks\post-commit
```

The real hooks directory is `C:\Users\...\café\main\.git\hooks`, and the `cafÃ©` tree is created from scratch. To reproduce with Git for Windows:

```sh
git init café/main
git -C café/main commit --allow-empty -m x
git -C café/main worktree add ../wt
cd café/wt && graphify hook install
```

`_hooks_dir` and `_rev_parse_path` run `git rev-parse` with `text=True` and no `encoding`, so Python decodes the output with the locale codec. That's cp1252 on Windows, but Git for Windows prints paths as UTF-8. In the main checkout git answers with the relative `.git/hooks`, so it's the absolute paths a linked worktree gets back that break.

The fix passes `encoding="utf-8"` to both calls. I left out `errors="replace"`, since a replaced character would still give a wrong path. Linux and macOS already decode as UTF-8. Same decode fix as #1505 (`llm.py`) and #1980 (`prs.py`).

- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Hooks are written to the directory git reads them from. The other `text=True` git calls in `hooks.py` read config values or stderr, not paths, and aren't changed here.

title: A type and a function named `Foo` / `foo` in one file share one node id (JS, TS, Kotlin, C++, PHP, Ruby, Swift)
body:
## Summary

When one file declares a type (class, interface, enum, type alias, namespace) and a top-level function or arrow function whose names differ only in case, both get the same node id and only one node is kept. The other declaration's edges are attributed to the survivor, and which one survives depends on declaration order. Python, Go and Rust are not affected.

The cause is in `DeclIdRegistry.resolve` and is shared by all affected languages. #3726 reports the TypeScript instance (`interface FallListe` / `function fallListe`); the reproduction below shows the same collapse in six more languages.

## Reproduction

Run from a clean checkout of the tag. Each file declares `Foo` and `foo` in the same file and calls `Foo` from `foo`:

```python
import pathlib
import tempfile

from graphify.extract import extract

CASES = {
    "a.js": "class Foo {\n  run() { return 1 }\n}\n\nfunction foo() {\n  return new Foo().run()\n}\n",
    "a.ts": "class Foo {\n  run(): number { return 1 }\n}\n\nfunction foo(): number {\n  return new Foo().run()\n}\n",
    "a.kt": "class Foo { fun run(): Int = 1 }\n\nfun foo(): Int = Foo().run()\n",
    "a.cpp": "class Foo { public: int run() { return 1; } };\n\nint foo() { Foo f; return f.run(); }\n",
    "a.php": "<?php\nclass Foo { function run() { return 1; } }\n\nfunction foo() { return (new Foo())->run(); }\n",
    "a.rb": "class Foo\n  def run; 1; end\nend\n\ndef foo; Foo.new.run; end\n",
    "a.swift": "struct Foo { func run() -> Int { 1 } }\n\nfunc foo() -> Int { Foo().run() }\n",
    "a.py": "class Foo:\n    def run(self):\n        return 1\n\n\ndef foo():\n    return Foo().run()\n",
    "a.go": "package p\n\ntype Foo struct{}\n\nfunc (f *Foo) Run() int { return 1 }\n\nfunc foo() int {\n\treturn (&Foo{}).Run()\n}\n",
    "a.rs": "struct Foo;\nimpl Foo { fn run(&self) -> i32 { 1 } }\n\nfn foo() -> i32 { Foo.run() }\n",
}

for name, code in CASES.items():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        root = pathlib.Path(d)
        src = root / name
        src.write_text(code)
        g = extract([src], cache_root=root / ".cache", root=root, parallel=False)
    labels = {n["label"] for n in g["nodes"]}
    print(f"{name:8} Foo node: {'Foo' in labels!s:5}  foo() node: {'foo()' in labels}")
```

Output on v0.9.99:

```
a.js     Foo node: True   foo() node: False
a.ts     Foo node: True   foo() node: False
a.kt     Foo node: True   foo() node: False
a.cpp    Foo node: True   foo() node: False
a.php    Foo node: True   foo() node: False
a.rb     Foo node: True   foo() node: False
a.swift  Foo node: True   foo() node: False
a.py     Foo node: True   foo() node: True
a.go     Foo node: True   foo() node: True
a.rs     Foo node: True   foo() node: True
```

In `a.js` the edges show what is lost: `foo()` has no node, so the call it makes is attributed to the class and appears as a self-loop `Foo -calls-> Foo`. If the function is declared first, `Foo` is the missing node and `.run()` is attached to `foo()` as a method.

In TypeScript the same happens for `interface Foo`, `type Foo = ...`, `enum Foo` and `namespace Foo`, each next to `function foo`, and for `class Foo` / `interface Foo` next to `const foo = () => ...`. The two declarations get one id (for example `kollision_fallliste` for #3726's `FallListe` / `fallListe`).

Expected: `foo()` gets its own node, is contained in the file, and `foo() -calls-> Foo`.

## Cause

Declaration ids are built from the normalized name, so `Foo` and `foo` produce the same id. In `DeclIdRegistry.resolve` (`graphify/ids.py`, v0.9.99), a declaration whose id is already owned by another real declaration reuses that id. The comment on that branch describes it as meant for the same declaration seen twice (a prototype owner, a redeclared name), but it also fires when the owner is a declaration of a different kind.

## Suggested direction

Take the reuse branch only when the owner is of the same kind, and bump the AST cache schema:

```diff
--- a/graphify/ids.py
+++ b/graphify/ids.py
-        if (nid in taken and owner is not None and owner[0] != "file"
-                and nid not in self._salted):
+        if (nid in taken and owner is not None and owner[0] != "file"
+                and owner[0] == kind and nid not in self._salted):
             return nid
```

```diff
--- a/graphify/cache.py
+++ b/graphify/cache.py
-_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA = 31  # ...
+_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA = 32  # ...
```

Checked on v0.9.99 with these changes:

- The script above reports `foo() node: True` for all ten files, and `a.js` has `foo() -calls-> Foo` with no self-loop.
- The TypeScript variants separate as well: `interface`, `type`, `enum` and `namespace` next to a function, and `interface` next to an arrow function. In #3726's file, `FallListe` and `fallListe()` get distinct ids.
- The declaration that already had a node keeps its id. The other one gets a salted id (`a.js`: `Foo` stays `a_foo`, `foo()` becomes `a_foo_0beec7b5ea3f`; with the order reversed, `foo()` stays `b_foo` and `Foo` becomes `b_foo_201a6b3053cc`).
- Redeclaring the same name twice (`function foo` twice, `class Foo` twice) still produces one node.
- The full test suite gives the same result with the `ids.py` change as on the unmodified tag: 13 failed, 9099 passed, the same 13 tests failing in both runs. The cache and id tests (`test_cache.py`, `test_file_id_collision_4854.py`, `test_csharp_partial_classes.py` and the cache, schema, decl and collision tests in `test_extract.py`) pass with both changes: 183 passed, 1 skipped.

The schema bump is needed for the non-JS languages. With a Kotlin file extracted once on the unmodified tag, the patched code with the schema left at 31 served the old result from the cache (`1/1 files served from cache`, no `foo()` node). After the bump to 32 the file was re-extracted and `foo()` appeared. JS and TS suffixes bypass the AST cache, so they do not need it.

This change does not cover two declarations of the same kind. These still share one id with or without it: `class Foo` / `class FOO`, `function foo` / `function Foo` (TS and JS), `interface Foo` / `interface foo`, and `class Foo` / `interface foo`.

## Related

- #3726 (open): the TypeScript instance of this collapse, `interface FallListe` / `function fallListe`.
- #3738 (open PR for #3726): salts case-only collisions of TS/JS top-level declarations in a pre-scan in `engine.py`. It does not touch `ids.py` and is limited to JS and TS.
- #2810 (open): same-file symbols that collapse after id normalization. Its reported pairs are class members and pairs of top-level functions, not a class together with a function.
- #4854 (closed): a declaration taking the id of its own file node. A different pair, handled by `DeclIdRegistry`.

title: graphify update never finishes on TypeScript projects: _apply_symbol_resolution_facts is O(imports × edges)
body:
### What happened?

`graphify update .` never finishes on a mid-size TypeScript project. It stays at 100% of one core after `AST extraction: 100%`, with no error and no output. This happens on every run, even after a one-line change, so the graph can't be kept up to date.

The cause is a nested loop in `_apply_symbol_resolution_facts` (`graphify/extractors/resolution.py`, around line 1406, unchanged on `v8`). For each JS/TS import fact it walks **all** edges and builds a `Path` for each one, so the cost is imports × edges:

```python
for fact in facts.imports:
    ...
    for edge in edges:
        if _js_source_path(str(edge.get("source_file") or ""), root) != source_path:
            continue
```

Sampling the main thread showed it on line 1407 at 120, 135 and 150 seconds.

### Steps to reproduce

Self-contained script. It generates `n` TypeScript files, each with 10 imports, and times `extract()`:

```python
# python repro.py <n_files>
import shutil, sys, tempfile, time
from pathlib import Path

def main():
    n = int(sys.argv[1])
    root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="gfy-repro-"))
    (root / "src").mkdir()
    for i in range(n):
        lines = [f'import {{ f{(i + k) % n}_{k} }} from "./m{(i + k) % n}";' for k in range(1, 11)]
        lines += [f"export function f{i}_{k}() {{ return 1; }}" for k in range(1, 11)]
        lines.append("export const all = () => [" + ", ".join(f"f{(i + k) % n}_{k}()" for k in range(1, 11)) + "];")
        (root / "src" / f"m{i}.ts").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    from graphify.extract import extract
    t = time.time()
    r = extract(sorted((root / "src").glob("*.ts")), cache_root=root, root=root)
    print(f"n={n}: {time.time() - t:.1f}s, {len(r['nodes'])} nodes, {len(r['edges'])} edges")
    shutil.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### Error output or graph output

There is no error. Timings from the script above:

| Files | Edges | 0.9.99 | With the change below |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | 8,200 | 35.2 s | 1.6 s |
| 400 | 16,400 | 141.6 s | 1.9 s |
| 800 | 32,800 | not finished at 60 s (cut off) | 3.1 s |

Doubling the files multiplies the time by 4.

On a real private repository (1,922 files, about 96,700 edges, roughly 970 TS/TSX), the run was still going when stopped after 14 minutes. With the change below the same run takes 39 seconds.

### Suggested fix

Index the `references` edges by source file once, before the loop. The filters are the same and only the lookup changes:

```diff
         node_by_id = {node.get("id"): node for node in nodes}
+        references_by_file: dict[Path | None, list[dict]] = {}
+        for edge in edges:
+            if edge.get("relation") == "references":
+                references_by_file.setdefault(
+                    _js_source_path(str(edge.get("source_file") or ""), root), []
+                ).append(edge)
         for fact in facts.imports:
             ...
-            for edge in edges:
-                if _js_source_path(str(edge.get("source_file") or ""), root) != source_path:
-                    continue
-                if edge.get("relation") != "references":
-                    continue
+            for edge in references_by_file.get(source_path, ()):
                 if edge.get("target") == target_nid:
                     continue
```

The loop only changes `edge["target"]`, not `source_file` or `relation`, so the index stays valid while it runs.

On a generated 120-file project, the sorted node ids and `(source, target, relation)` edges were identical with and without the change (same SHA-256). That is the only equivalence check I ran. I did not run the project's test suite.

### Graphify version

0.9.99

### Operating System

macOS 27.2 (arm64)

### Python Version

3.14

### Installation Method

pip (Homebrew Python)

### Additional context

Reproduced with the script above and on the private repository, both from a clean run with no cache. Found and measured with the help of Claude Code.

title: docs(skill): say when a graph is worth building (#4829)

Fixes #4829.

The skill goes straight to its build steps, so an agent choosing its own tool for a one-off lookup gets no steering toward a plain search. title: fix(ids): keep a type and a function differing only in case apart
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #4904

`class Foo` and `function foo` in one file normalize to the same id, and `DeclIdRegistry.resolve` treated the second one as a duplicate of the first. One node got dropped and its edges went to the survivor, so `foo()` calling `Foo` showed up as a `Foo -> Foo` self loop.

Now an id is only reused when the declaration has the same kind or the exact same spelling. The other one gets a salted id, and the AST cache schema goes to 32 so old cache entries don't hide the fix.

This is a bit different from the diff in the issue. Kind alone also splits `class Foo` + `namespace Foo` in TS, which is one merged declaration, so same spelling across kinds still counts as a duplicate. There's a test for it and it fails with the kind-only check.

Limitation, also in the issue: two declarations of the same kind still collapse (`class Foo` / `class FOO`, `function foo` / `function Foo`). Should cover the `FallListe` / `fallListe` pair from #3726 too since that's a type and a function, I didn't run that file. #3738 is a pre-scan for that one in TS and JS only, this doesn't touch it.
