title: Full code rebuild spends ~100 s in path and string work with nothing changed (0.9.48, 21.5k nodes)
body:
## Summary

A full code rebuild (`_rebuild_code(Path('.'))`, the path `graphify watch` and `graphify update` take) on a 21.5k-node TypeScript repo takes 105 s when nothing has changed and every file is in the extraction cache. Parsing is 5 s of that. The rest is Python-side path and string work in four places, each of which recomputes the same values per node or per file.

## Environment

- graphifyy 0.9.48, CPython 3.12.13 (uv), macOS 15 on Apple Silicon (arm64)
- repo: a pnpm monorepo, 2,624 scanned files, mostly TypeScript; graph.json 21.5k nodes after build
- run: `python -c "from graphify.watch import _rebuild_code; from pathlib import Path; _rebuild_code(Path('.'))"` under cProfile, second run with a warm cache and no file changed

## Profile (cumulative, warm cache, nothing changed)

```
total                                                           104.97 s
extract.extract                                                  71.4 s
  resolution._augment_symbol_resolution_edges                    35.8 s
    resolution._collect_js_symbol_resolution_facts               28.8 s   (_walk_js_tree: 25.6M calls, 14.9 s)
    resolution._apply_symbol_resolution_facts                     6.7 s
  resolution._disambiguate_colliding_node_ids                    22.2 s
    resolution._source_key (143,032 calls)                       21.8 s
  extract._extract_parallel (the parsing, all cached)             5.6 s
detect.detect                                                    17.0 s
  detect._is_ignored (2,624 calls, 6 ms each)                    15.7 s
    detect._eval (11,016 calls)                                  15.4 s
watch._reconcile_existing_graph                                   9.8 s
  watch.identity / absolute_identity (150k calls each)            5.4 s
build.build_from_json                                             3.2 s
```

Clustering did not run in this profile (same topology, early exit); on a run where it does, `cluster.cluster` is about 5 s.

## What the numbers say

1. `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids` calls `_source_key` once per node (143k calls for 21.5k nodes, so several times per node) and each call does path normalisation. Memoising `_source_key` per node id, or computing it once per file, would take this from 22 s to well under a second.
2. `_collect_js_symbol_resolution_facts` walks every JS/TS syntax tree again (25.6M `_walk_js_tree` calls) even though the per-file extraction is cached. The facts it collects depend only on the file, so they could be cached beside the per-file extraction result and only recomputed for files whose hash changed.
3. `_is_ignored` costs 6 ms per file: `_eval` is called 4 times per file and the ignore patterns look like they are re-evaluated (and the file path re-split) on every call. Compiling the pattern set once per run, and short-circuiting on directory prefixes, would make detection a fraction of a second for 2.6k files.
4. `_reconcile_existing_graph` resolves `identity` / `absolute_identity` 150k times for what are 21.5k distinct paths; a dict from node id to normalised path would do it once.

Together these four are about 95 of the 105 seconds. None of them depends on the size of the change, so the whole cost is paid on every rebuild, which is what makes a watch on an active repo expensive (we measured 98 rebuilds in a day, about three hours of CPU, on a merge-triggered schedule).

I am happy to run the same profile on a branch or share the full cProfile dump if useful.

title: _rebuild_code(changed_paths=[unchanged file]) drops the file's external-module nodes
body:
## Summary

`watch._rebuild_code(root, changed_paths=[one file])` on a file whose content did not change produces a graph with fewer nodes than the full rebuild of the same tree: the external-module nodes that the file imports (`fastify`, `ioredis`, `node:crypto` in our case) disappear, with their edges.

## Environment

- graphifyy 0.9.48, CPython 3.12.13 (uv), macOS 15 on Apple Silicon (arm64)
- repo: a pnpm TypeScript monorepo, 2,624 scanned files, 21.5k nodes after a full build

## Steps

1. `_rebuild_code(Path('.'))` (full). Note `len(graph.json nodes)` and edges.
2. Without touching any file, `_rebuild_code(Path('.'), changed_paths=[Path('<one .ts file that imports fastify, ioredis and node:crypto>')])`.
3. Compare graph.json.

## Observed

- Step 1: N nodes, E edges.
- Step 2: N - 19 nodes, E - 40 edges. All 19 missing nodes are external-module nodes referenced from the given file (`fastify`, `ioredis`, `node:crypto`, and the rest of its imports); the file's own function and class nodes are intact.
- A third full rebuild brings the 19 nodes back.

## Expected

An incremental rebuild for an unchanged file should be a no-op on the graph, or at least keep the external-module nodes that the file's import edges point at. It looks like the incremental path re-extracts the file's own nodes and edges but then drops the edge targets that live outside the scanned tree, because those nodes are created by the full-tree resolution pass and not by the per-file extraction.

Until this is fixed we run only full rebuilds, which is what motivated the profile in the other issue I opened today.

title: feat(json): add scoped json.include for project configs (#4898)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4898.

Since v0.8.37, `_is_config_json()` has accepted only a short filename list, a few suffixes, and nine root keys. Framework configs such as `allowlist.json`, `registry.json`, `gates.json`, and `settings.template.json` fall outside that list, so they return zero nodes. The manifest still stamps them, and `graphify update` reports success.

The loss is broader than `update`. `.json` is in `CODE_EXTENSIONS`, and the semantic pass only receives documents, papers, and images. A full `graphify extract` with an LLM does not index these files either.

This change adds an explicit policy:

```text
# .graphifyrc
json.include=config/**/*.json
json.include=hooks/**/*.json
```

```bash
graphify update . --include-json 'config/**/*.json'
graphify extract . --code-only --include-json 'hooks/**/*.json'
```

The default stays unchanged. A matching path bypasses only `_is_config_json()`. `.gitignore`, `.graphifyignore`, the secret filter, and JSON Schema rejection still win. `json.include=all` is the explicit whole-repo escape hatch.

Policy changes invalidate the AST cache and the manifest gate. The include patterns are hashed into `cache_salt()`, which the manifest already stores under its generic `language` field. Enabling or removing the policy therefore works on unchanged files without `--force`.

The change also prints one summary line when JSON is skipped, so the decision is visible:

```text
skipped 5 JSON file(s) as data/config; set json.include=<glob> in .graphifyrc to index matching paths (#4898).
```

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Evidence

**Before:** default policy on the regression fixture.

```text
nodes 12, edges 14, communities 2
config/allowlist.json absent
graphify query "allowlist" -> No matching nodes found.
```

**After:** scoped `config/**/*.json`.

```text
nodes 21, edges 21
graphify query "allowlist" -> 6 nodes found.
allowlist.json --contains--> roles, paths, enabled
```

The full test fixture also includes `hooks/**/*.json`:

```text
nodes 25, edges 24, communities 5
```

The same fixture under `json.include=all`:

```text
nodes 536, edges 533, communities 164
```

One 300-key data fixture added 501 nodes. That is the #1224 failure shape, which is why `all` is an escape hatch and the glob is the recommended path.

**Tests:**

```text
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_json_include_4898.py -q
19 passed

$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
9209 passed, 18 skipped, 1 xfailed in 666.38s

$ .venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/rcfile.py graphify/cli.py \
    graphify/extractors/json_config.py graphify/extract.py \
    tests/test_json_include_4898.py tests/test_language_overrides.py
All checks passed!
```

## Verification & Invariants

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

The invariant: every detected JSON source is either indexed, explicitly excluded by the user, or reported as skipped with a way to change the decision.

The tests pin:

- Default skip and warning.
- Direct and nested glob matches.
- `*` does not cross a slash; `**/` matches zero or more directories.
- Absolute paths and `..` are rejected.
- `all` indexes data JSON but still respects ignore and secret filters.
- JSON Schema files stay out under `all` (#2255).
- Enabling the policy reindexes unchanged files without `--force`.
- Removing the policy evicts the nodes without `--force`.
- The policy reaches process-pool workers.
- The CLI override wins over `.graphifyrc`.

Known limitations:

- `json.include=all` can recreate #1224 on repos with large data fixtures. Scoped globs are the safe form.
- JSON Schema documents remain skipped even under `all`.
- `--include-json` is available on `update` and `extract`. `watch` reads `.graphifyrc`.
- The glob matcher supports `*`, `?`, and `**`. It does not support brace expansion or character classes.

## How was this tested?

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_json_include_4898.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/rcfile.py graphify/cli.py \
  graphify/extractors/json_config.py graphify/extract.py \
  tests/test_json_include_4898.py tests/test_language_overrides.py
.venv/bin/python -m graphify update .
```

Branch `fix/4898-json-include` is based on `upstream/v8` (`a0946f96`, v0.9.99).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way.

The default path is unchanged. No cache schema bump and no graph format change. The policy salt is added only when `json.include` is active, so existing manifests without it re-extract the affected JSON once. Removing the include evicts the previously added nodes on the next rebuild.

**Blast Radius:** Config indexing.

The main risk is a user choosing `json.include=all` on a data-heavy repo and getting the #1224 noise again. The warning and the measured 164-community result document that cost. Ignore rules, secret filtering, and JSON Schema protection are unchanged.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. No source fragments changed.
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python). Include globs cannot escape the scan root and cannot bypass secret filtering.
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.

title: [Bug]: Updates retain linked-worktree sources excluded by a fresh scan
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

A workspace can contain a main Git checkout and a linked worktree as siblings. A fresh scan already excludes the linked copy when the main checkout is inside the same scan root. Updating a graph that still contains sources from that linked copy can retain them instead.

This is a source-inspection report against `v8` at `a0946f962af31b19bff941b453f6dae9a7077c7a`, not a claim of a completed runtime reproduction. `ignored_predicate()` does not check the linked-worktree boundary used by `detect()`. Reconciliation therefore lacks positive exclusion evidence for those still-existing files. It also discovers ignored source identities from nodes only, so a stored edge or hyperedge with its own excluded source can survive when no node owns that source.

Expected: when a rebuild reaches reconciliation, positively excluded linked-worktree sources should be removed consistently across stored nodes, edges and hyperedges. Main-checkout records and live sources absent from the corpus without positive exclusion evidence should remain protected.

### Steps to reproduce

The following fixture checks the scan/predicate mismatch on the named source. It has not been executed for this report:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from graphify.detect import detect, ignored_predicate

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    workspace = (Path(directory) / "workspace").resolve()
    main = workspace / "app"
    (main / "src").mkdir(parents=True)
    (main / "src" / "a.py").write_text("x = 1\n")
    def git(*args):
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(main), *args], check=True)
    git("init", "-q")
    git("add", ".")
    git("-c", "user.name=Repro", "-c", "user.email=repro@example.com",
        "commit", "-q", "-m", "fixture")
    linked = workspace / "app-feature"
    git("worktree", "add", "-q", str(linked))
    target = linked / "src" / "a.py"
    scanned = {Path(p) for group in detect(workspace)["files"].values() for p in group}
    print("included by scan:", target in scanned)
    print("excluded by predicate:", ignored_predicate(workspace)(target))
```

For the persisted-graph case, start with a legacy graph containing records owned by `app-feature/src/a.py`, then run an ordinary full update that reaches reconciliation. Include an edge and a hyperedge owned by that source whose endpoint/member nodes belong to `app/src/a.py`, with no node owned by the linked source. Those source-owned records should be evicted along with linked-owned nodes. Keep an equivalent live, unexplained corpus-absent source as a preservation control.

### Error output or graph output

No runtime output is attached. Source inspection predicts `False` / `False` for the two printed checks; the consistent result would be `False` / `True`. In the persisted case, the incorrect result is retained linked-source records after reconciliation.

This report does not claim that a same-version no-change update necessarily reaches reconciliation, or that excluded-only watch events immediately clean an existing graph.

### Graphify version

`v8` at `a0946f962af31b19bff941b453f6dae9a7077c7a`

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

The environment fields describe the inspection host, using Python 3.13.5. Graphify has not been installed or executed for this report, and no clean-checkout runtime reproduction is claimed. No provider configuration is needed for the proposed AST-only fixture.

### Additional context

This is the persistent-update residual of #4683, which is already closed. The fresh-scan behavior is covered by the existing linked-worktree tests.

Source references at the inspected commit:

- [Scan exclusion and its boundaries](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/a0946f962af31b19bff941b453f6dae9a7077c7a/graphify/detect.py#L2261)
- [Per-path exclusion predicate](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/a0946f962af31b19bff941b453f6dae9a7077c7a/graphify/detect.py#L1973)
- [Stored-source reconciliation](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/a0946f962af31b19bff941b453f6dae9a7077c7a/graphify/watch.py#L1129)

title: perf(resolve): index reference edges by source (#4909)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Refs #4909.

The current full rebuild is O(imports times edges) in `_apply_symbol_resolution_facts`. On a 21k-node TypeScript corpus it takes 14 minutes. The pass added for #4854 loops over every edge for every import so it can rewrite a reference edge from a sourceless stub to the imported declaration.

The index is keyed by the same `_js_source_path(...)` value the old comparison computed. The per-edge checks stay the same:

- relation must be `references`
- target must be a sourceless stub
- stub label must match the imported or local name

No graph schema, cache schema, or manifest field changes. The written graph is identical on the 200-file fixture.

This does not close the rest of #4909. `_collect_js_symbol_resolution_facts` still re-parses every JS/TS tree, and the original 0.9.48 profile has other costs. This removes the current regression that makes a full rebuild worse than the reported version.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [x] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Evidence

**Before:** current `v8` at `a0946f96`.

```text
200 files / 3,200 nodes:     25.3 s
1,312 files / 20,992 nodes: 847.0 s  (14 m 7 s)
```

**After:** branch `fix/4909-reference-index`.


Scaling:

```text
before:  25.3 -> 847.0     33.5x
after:    4.24 -> 24.32     5.7x
```

The before path is quadratic. The after path is close to linear.


**After:**

```text
1 passed
```

The test counts `_js_source_path` calls and requires a linear budget. It does not measure wall time, so it will not flake on a busy CI machine.

**Graph equality on the 200-file corpus:**

```text

links: 5,400 both
node ids equal: yes
node field diffs: 0
edge set equal: yes
missing edges: 0
extra edges: 0
```

- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

The invariant: the cost of reference binding scales with nodes, edges, and imports, not with imports times edges. A per-import full scan fails the new test.

Limitation: the index holds reference edges grouped by source file for the duration of this pass. That is one list per file, not a second graph. Memory is proportional to the reference edge count.

**Blast Radius:** JS/TS reference binding.

The main risk is a subtle change in which edges are rewritten. The index uses the same source path and the same checks as the old loop. The 200-file graph comparison found identical nodes, fields, and edges, and all #4854 tests pass. A revert restores the old behavior and the old cost.

title: Deletion-only --update unstamps all semantic files from the manifest
body:
**Repro (the documented deletion-only `--update` path):**

1. Build a graph with docs in the corpus; semantic cache is populated and the manifest stamps the docs.
2. Delete a doc, then run the `references/update.md` deletion-only flow: `new_total == 0`, so the flow writes an **empty extraction** (`.graphify_extract.json = {nodes:[],edges:[]}`) and calls the merge step.
3. The merge step's manifest save calls `_stamped_manifest_files(incremental['files'], new_extraction, root)` with the empty extraction.

**Expected:** the deletion prunes the deleted file's nodes; unchanged docs keep their manifest stamps, so the next `--update` treats them as unchanged.

**Actual:** `_stamped_manifest_files` gates semantic stamps on the extraction having output for the file (per #2015's anti-lost-content rule), and the extraction is empty — so **every unchanged semantic file is unstamped** (or cleared via `clear_semantic`). The next `--update` re-queues the whole doc corpus for semantic extraction, even though nothing changed and the cache would have served all of it.

**Observed impact:** a single-file deletion prune caused the next update to re-dispatch 5+ unchanged docs (cache hits saved the tokens, but the pipeline still re-ran detection, chunking, and merge, and produced node-ID churn because replacements re-extracted files that needed no replacement).

**Suggested fix:** in the deletion-only path, pass the previous run's manifest state (or a `preserve_stamps` set of scan-corpus files minus `deleted_files`) into `save_manifest`, so a deletion prune only removes the deleted file's row instead of unstamping everything semantic.

Version: graphifyy (pip) as of 2026-10-31. Happy to provide the full repro transcript.

title: update never finishes on a large JS repo: quadratic loop in _apply_symbol_resolution_facts
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?


**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.99, Python 3.13, Linux

**What happens**
`graphify update . --no-cluster` on a JavaScript repo with ~12,900 code files finishes AST extraction in about 15 minutes, then runs for over 90 minutes on one core and never writes `graph.json`.

**Where** (from `py-spy dump`)
```
_js_source_path (graphify/extractors/resolution.py:1260)
_apply_symbol_resolution_facts (graphify/extractors/resolution.py:1407)
_augment_symbol_resolution_edges (graphify/extractors/resolution.py:2976)
extract (graphify/extract.py:10019)
```

**Cause**
In `_apply_symbol_resolution_facts`, for every JS/TS import fact the code loops over **all** edges and resolves each edge's `source_file` path to filter by the importing file. Cost is imports x edges (plus a path resolve per pair), so it grows quadratically with repo size.

**Fix we applied locally**
Build an index of `references` edges by resolved source path once, before the imports loop, and loop over only that file's edges:

```python
_refs_by_src = {}
for _e in edges:
    if _e.get("relation") == "references":
        _refs_by_src.setdefault(_js_source_path(str(_e.get("source_file") or ""), root), []).append(_e)
for fact in facts.imports:
    ...
    for edge in _refs_by_src.get(source_path, ()):
        if edge.get("target") == target_nid:
            continue
        ...
```
The filter on `source_path` and `relation == "references"` is the same, so the result does not change.

**Result:** with the patch, the same `update --no-cluster` finished in 13 min 19 s (extraction included): 129,212 nodes, 518,589 edges. Without it, two runs were stopped after 90+ minutes with no graph written.


### Steps to reproduce

```shell
1. A JavaScript repo with about 12,900 code files (ES modules, many relative imports).
2. pip install "graphifyy[sql]==0.9.99"
3. graphify update . --no-cluster
4. AST extraction finishes in ~15 min, then the process runs on one core for 90+ min and never writes graph.json.

Cause: graphify/extractors/resolution.py, _apply_symbol_resolution_facts loops over ALL edges for EVERY JS/TS import fact (imports x edges, plus a path resolve per pair).

Fix that works for us: index "references" edges by resolved source path once, before the imports loop, then loop only over that file's edges:

    _refs_by_src = {}
    for _e in edges:
        if _e.get("relation") == "references":
            _refs_by_src.setdefault(_js_source_path(str(_e.get("source_file") or ""), root), []).append(_e)
    for fact in facts.imports:
        ...
        for edge in _refs_by_src.get(source_path, ()):
            if edge.get("target") == target_nid:
                continue
            ...

With the patch the same run finishes in 13 min 19 s (extraction included): 129,212 nodes, 518,589 edges.
```

```text
_js_source_path (graphify/extractors/resolution.py:1260)
_apply_symbol_resolution_facts (graphify/extractors/resolution.py:1407)
_augment_symbol_resolution_edges (graphify/extractors/resolution.py:2976)
extract (graphify/extract.py:10019)
_rebuild_code (graphify/watch.py:2447)
```

0.9.99

### Operating System

Linux

3.13

pip

title: [Bug]: C++: out-of-line methods are not attached to their class when the header is in another directory, so unqualified own-member calls bind to same-named functions in other files
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

When a C++ class is declared in a header that lives in a **different directory** from its `.cpp` (the common `include/` + `src/` layout, and Unreal's `Public/` + `Private/`), the out-of-line definitions (`void Foo::run() { ... }`) are not attached to the class. They stay as file-level `Foo::run()` / `Foo::say()` nodes, and an unqualified call to the class's own member inside them (`say(...)` in `Foo::run`) gets an INFERRED `calls` edge to a same-named function in **another file**, even one with internal linkage (anonymous namespace).

**Expected:** `say("hello")` inside `Foo::run()` resolves to `Foo::say` (the definition or the `.say()` declaration in `foo.h`), or produces no edge. It should not link to `say` in `bar.cpp`.

**Actual:** `Foo::run() --calls [INFERRED]--> say() (src/bar.cpp:L3)`.

With the same three files in one directory, the definitions are attached to the class (`.run()` / `.say()`) and the wrong edge is not produced, so the directory split is what triggers it. It is not specific to Unreal macros: the repro below is plain C++, and adding `UCLASS()` / `GENERATED_BODY()` / `MYGAME_API` gives the same result.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# include/foo.h
#pragma once

class Foo
{
public:
    void run();
private:
    void say(const char* text);
};

# src/foo.cpp
#include "foo.h"

void Foo::say(const char* text)
{
}

void Foo::run()
{
    say("hello");   // calls Foo::say
}

# src/bar.cpp
namespace
{
    int say(const char* text) { return 0; }
}

int bar() { return say("x"); }

# run from the directory that contains include/ and src/
uvx --isolated --python 3.13 --from graphifyy==0.9.99 graphify extract . --code-only --out ../out
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Split layout (include/ + src/), all `calls` edges in graph.json:
bar()      (src/bar.cpp:L6) --calls [EXTRACTED]--> say() (src/bar.cpp:L3)
Foo::run() (src/foo.cpp:L9) --calls [INFERRED]--> say() (src/bar.cpp:L3)   <-- wrong

Nodes / structural edges (split):
Foo     - method   -> .run()      include/foo.h
Foo     - method   -> .say()      include/foo.h
foo.cpp - contains -> Foo::run()  src/foo.cpp     (not attached to Foo)
foo.cpp - contains -> Foo::say()  src/foo.cpp     (not attached to Foo)

Same three files in one directory:
bar()      (bar.cpp:L6) --calls [EXTRACTED]--> say() (bar.cpp:L3)
foo.cpp - contains -> .run() / .say()  (attached; no wrong edge, but also no run -> say edge)
```

### Graphify version

0.9.99

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables are set (no GEMINI/GOOGLE/OPENAI/ANTHROPIC/KIMI/DEEPSEEK keys); `--code-only`. Reproduced in a fresh isolated environment (`uvx --isolated --from graphifyy==0.9.99`) as well as in my uv tool install. `v8` HEAD at the time of testing was `a0946f962a` (the 0.9.99 version bump).

### Additional context

On a real Unreal Engine 5 module (249 C++ files, `Public/` + `Private/` layout) I checked every INFERRED `calls` edge against the source: 81 of 1,753 bind an unqualified call to a same-named function in another file instead of the caller's own class member. They also inflate the god-node ranking of those same-named functions. Possibly related: 4 more bind `AddWarning()` called inside Unreal automation tests (inherited from an engine base class outside the scanned tree) to a same-named member of an unrelated game class.

Related: #2348 (qualified calls to UCLASS methods; the comment near `qualified_method_nids` in `extract.py` describes the file-contained `Class::method()` fallback node), PR #4252 (binds unqualified calls to the caller's own class, its bases and enclosing classes declared in the file), #3215. Local lambdas / local variables, which misbind in both layouts, are filed separately as #4917.

My workaround is a post-processing step on graph.json that repoints these edges to the caller's own class member, followed by `graphify cluster-only .`.

This report was prepared with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code); the repro was run and the numbers were checked against the source.

title: [Bug]: C++: calls to a local lambda or local std::function variable are INFERRED-linked to same-named symbols in other files
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

In C++, a call to a **local lambda** (`auto box = [](int x) {...}; box(1);`) or a **local `std::function` variable** (`std::function<void()> job = ...; job();`) gets an INFERRED `calls` edge to a same-named symbol in another file: a free function `box()`, or even a struct **field** `job`.

**Expected:** no `calls` edge for these two calls, since both names are locals declared just above the call.

**Actual:** `run() --calls [INFERRED]--> box() (bar.cpp:L3)` and `run() --calls [INFERRED]--> job (bar.cpp:L5)`, where `job` is the field `std::function<void()> job;` of `struct Task`.

This happens with all files in one directory, so it is independent of the header-layout issue #4916.

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# foo.cpp
#include <functional>

int run()
{
    auto box = [](int x) { return x; };
    std::function<void()> job = [] {};
    job();
    return box(1);
}

# bar.cpp
#include <functional>

int box(int x) { return x; }

struct Task { std::function<void()> job; };

# run from the directory that contains both files
uvx --isolated --python 3.13 --from graphifyy==0.9.99 graphify extract . --code-only --out ../out
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
All `calls` edges in graph.json:
run() (foo.cpp:L7) --calls [INFERRED]--> job   (bar.cpp:L5)   <-- local variable bound to a struct field
run() (foo.cpp:L8) --calls [INFERRED]--> box() (bar.cpp:L3)   <-- local lambda bound to another file's function
```

### Graphify version

0.9.99

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

### Additional Environment Details

No provider environment variables are set; `--code-only`. Reproduced in a fresh isolated environment (`uvx --isolated --from graphifyy==0.9.99`) as well as in my uv tool install. `v8` HEAD at the time of testing was `a0946f962a` (the 0.9.99 version bump).

### Additional context

On a real Unreal Engine 5 module (249 C++ files) I checked every INFERRED `calls` edge against the source: 65 of 1,753 bind a call to a local lambda to a same-named symbol in another file, and 1 binds a local `TFunction` variable to a struct field of the same name. Local helper lambdas with short names (`Box`, `At`) are common in UI paint code, so these edges pile up on unrelated symbols.

Related: #4916 (out-of-line methods not attached to their class when the header is in another directory).

title: docs: make the agent query workflow consistent and prefer exact node IDs
body:
## What does this PR do?

Refs #3768. The agent query instructions disagreed across AGENTS.md, the skill, the always-on fragments and the query reference. This makes them say one thing:

- An exact node name or ID may be queried directly.
- A natural-language question first runs `graphify reflect --if-stale`, reads `LESSONS.md` and maps the question onto the graph's vocabulary, then traverses.
- Match ranking is described as tiers combined with field weights and term coverage, not a strict "exact, then prefix, then substring" order, matching `references/query/default.md`.

The inline sample query flows (aider, devin, and the CLI-unavailable fallback in the query reference) now choose an exact-ID match before exact-label matches, then apply the start-node cap. Before, a node whose ID matched the query could be dropped when three other nodes had that text as their label.

All generated skills were regenerated from the fragments; nothing generated was hand-edited.

title: Hook rebuild ignores `--code-only` scope: code-only graph becomes full graph
body:
## Summary
When a graph is built with `--code-only`, the git hooks installed by
`graphify hook install` rebuild it as a **full** graph (code + docs)
on the next commit / branch switch. The rebuild does not preserve the
scope the graph was originally built with.

## Repro
1. `graphify extract . --code-only` — code-only graph (in my repo: 675
nodes, 1356 edges, 20 communities; 70 code files, 335 docs skipped).
2. `graphify hook install` (installs post-commit / post-checkout /
post-merge / post-rewrite).
3. Make a commit (or switch branches).
4. The hook rebuilds the graph — it now includes docs: 2325 nodes,
2701 edges, 364 communities (403 files extracted, including 333 docs).

## Expected
A rebuild should preserve the scope the graph was built with. A
code-only graph should stay code-only across hook-triggered rebuilds
(unless the user explicitly changes the scope).

## Actual
`_rebuild_code` has no code-only parameter. When called without
`changed_paths` (post-checkout / post-merge / post-rewrite do a full
rebuild), it extracts every file it can parse — code and docs alike.
The original `--code-only` flag is silently dropped. There is also no
record of the extraction scope in the graph metadata (e.g.
`graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json` / `manifest.json`), so the
rebuild has no way to know the graph was code-only.

## Suggested fix
Record the extraction scope (e.g. `code_only: true`) in the graph
metadata at `extract` time, and have `_rebuild_code` respect it (or
accept a `code_only` parameter that the hooks pass through).
Alternatively, add a `--code-only` flag to the hook install / a
`code_only` key in `.graphifyrc`.

## Environment
- graphify 0.9.99 (via `uv tool install graphifyy`)
- Python 3.12, Linux
- No LLM API key configured (AST-only extraction)

## Related observations
- The CLI and the hook disagree about docs without an API key:
`graphify extract .` (no `--code-only`, no key) refuses with "no LLM
API key found (335 doc/paper/image file(s) need semantic extraction)",
while the hook's `_rebuild_code` extracts docs via AST with no key. A
`--ast-only` CLI mode (full extraction, no LLM) would match the hook's
behavior.
- `graphify-out/manifest.json` changes on every rebuild (mtime/seen
timestamps) even when the graph topology is unchanged, which dirties
the working tree for repos that commit the graph. It would help if the
manifest were stable when nothing meaningful changed.

title: `graphify update` waits forever on Windows when the filesystem has no byte-range locks (e.g. `\wsl.localhost`)
body:
### What happened?

On Windows, `graphify update .` never finishes when the repo lives on a filesystem that does not support byte-range locks. The one I hit is the WSL share (`\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\...`), i.e. a repo inside WSL opened from Windows.

`_rebuild_lock` (`graphify/watch.py`) takes the Windows lock with `msvcrt.locking(fd, LK_NBLCK, 1)`. On the WSL share that call raises `OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument` every time, not only under contention. The Windows branch treats any `OSError` as "another rebuild holds the lock":

- `blocking=True` (what the `graphify update` CLI uses, `block_on_lock=True` in `cli.py`) retries in a `while True` with `time.sleep(0.05)` and no limit, so the process sleeps forever.
- `blocking=False` (the git hooks, which call `_rebuild_code` with the default) yields `False`: the hook queues its change, prints "Rebuild already in progress … changes queued" and returns. No lock holder ever exists to drain that queue, so nothing gets rebuilt.

The POSIX branch only treats `BlockingIOError` as contention; other errors propagate. The asymmetry is what turns "this filesystem can't lock" into an infinite wait on Windows.

On my machine a SessionEnd hook that runs `graphify update . --force` hung like this 3 times out of 3 when the repo was opened from Windows through `\\wsl.localhost`: one run never logged an exit, one was killed after 4.5 h, and one ran for 33 h until I killed it. The same rebuild run inside WSL finishes in about 2 minutes.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows with WSL, create a small repo inside the distro, e.g. 40 one-function `.py` files under `/home/<user>/repro/pkg/`.
2. From Windows (PowerShell), `cd \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\<user>\repro` and run `graphify update . --force`.
3. It prints the startup lines and then sits there. After 240 s it had used 0.7 s of CPU in total.

Control: the same repo copied to `C:` finishes in 4 s. Run inside WSL, it also finishes normally.

The lock call on its own, no graphify involved:

```python
import msvcrt
fh = open(r"\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\<user>\repro\t.lock", "a+")
fh.seek(4096)
msvcrt.locking(fh.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_NBLCK, 1)   # OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument
```

On `C:` or `D:` the same call succeeds. A real contended lock (a second handle on a locked byte) raises `[Errno 13]` (EACCES), so the two cases can be told apart.

### Error output or graph output

No error. A `faulthandler.dump_traceback_later` dump of the stuck process (0.9.94 line numbers):

```text
File "...\graphify\watch.py", line 286 in _rebuild_lock
File "...\contextlib.py", line 137 in __enter__
File "...\graphify\watch.py", line 1728 in _rebuild_code
File "...\graphify\cli.py", line 2838 in dispatch_command
File "...\graphify\__main__.py", line 1101 in _run_cli
```

### Graphify version

Hit on 0.9.94. The code is unchanged on `v8` at 0.9.100 (`watch.py` lines 283-296).

### Operating System

Windows 11 Pro (Insider build 26340), WSL 3.0.3, Ubuntu distro.

### Python Version

3.11

### Installation Method

pip

### Additional context

Related: #3881 / #3883 added the msvcrt lock; #4273 is the POSIX-side lock fix. I have a fix with a regression test and will open a PR.

title: `file_hash` opens the lowercased path on Windows, so files with uppercase names fail on case-sensitive dirs (`\wsl.localhost`)
body:
### What happened?

On Windows, `file_hash` (`graphify/cache.py`) normalizes the path with `_normalize_path`, which calls `os.path.normcase` and so lowercases it, and then uses that lowercased path for the file itself: `p.is_file()`, the stat fastpath and the read. On a case-sensitive directory, a file with uppercase letters in its name is then "not a file", and the rebuild fails.

I hit it on the WSL share (`\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\...`), which is case-sensitive. `README.md` becomes `...\readme.md`, which does not exist there:

```text
warning: worker failed for \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\<user>\repro\README.md: file_hash requires a file, got: \\wsl.localhost\ubuntu\home\<user>\repro\readme.md
[graphify watch] Rebuild failed: file_hash requires a file, got: \\wsl.localhost\ubuntu\home\<user>\repro\readme.md
Nothing to update or rebuild failed — check output above.
```

`graphify update` exits 1.

The lowercasing makes sense for the cache key (stable keys across Windows path spellings, #629), but it should not be the path used to open the file.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows with WSL, a repo inside the distro with any file with an uppercase letter (here `README.md` plus 40 `.py` files).
2. From PowerShell, `cd \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\<user>\repro` and run `graphify update . --force`.

Today this step hangs first because of #4924; with that fix applied, it fails as above in about 10 s.

### Graphify version

title: fix(watch): don't wait forever when msvcrt.locking is unsupported (#4924)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4924.

On Windows, `_rebuild_lock` treated every `OSError` from `msvcrt.locking` as "another rebuild holds the lock". On a filesystem that cannot byte-range lock at all, such as the WSL share `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\...` (where the call raises `EINVAL` every time), that made the blocking `graphify update` CLI (`block_on_lock=True`) sleep in a `while True` forever. The non-blocking git hooks queued their change and returned "Rebuild already in progress", with no lock holder ever left to drain the queue.

The Windows branch now looks at the errno:

- `EACCES` / `EDEADLK` is contention, and behaves as before: blocking callers wait and retry every 50 ms, non-blocking callers get `False`.
- Any other errno is treated as "locking unsupported on this filesystem". The rebuild proceeds without a lock (`yield True`, like the existing fallback when neither `fcntl` nor `msvcrt` exists), and a warning on stderr names the lock file.

In that unsupported case the caller does **not** take over `.rebuild.lock`: it writes no PID into it and does not unlink it on release. On a WSL-share repo the file can belong to a WSL-side `flock` holder. Overwriting its PID, or unlinking the path, would let the next WSL-side caller `flock` a fresh inode while the first is still rebuilding (the #4273 race). If this call created the file only to try the lock, it removes that still-empty file again before the rebuild starts, so no stale lock is left behind (GH-858).

The POSIX branch is unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariants:

1. A rebuild waits on `_rebuild_lock` only for another holder, never for a condition that cannot change.
2. Contention keeps its existing semantics.
3. A caller that could not take the lock never modifies or removes a lock file another process may hold.

- [x] **Read** the CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test**.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Tests, in `tests/test_watch.py`. They run the msvcrt branch on any OS through a stand-in `msvcrt`, with `fcntl` hidden. `time.sleep` is replaced so a loop that never ends fails the test instead of hanging it.

| Test | origin/v8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_rebuild_lock_blocking_does_not_spin_when_filesystem_cannot_lock` | fails | passes |
| `test_rebuild_lock_non_blocking_proceeds_when_filesystem_cannot_lock` | fails | passes |
| `test_rebuild_lock_unsupported_filesystem_leaves_another_holders_lock_file_alone[True/False]`: a pre-existing `.rebuild.lock` with a foreign PID must keep its content and inode | fails | passes |
| `test_rebuild_lock_blocking_still_waits_while_msvcrt_lock_is_contended` | passes | passes |
| `test_rebuild_lock_non_blocking_still_yields_false_while_msvcrt_lock_is_contended` | passes | passes |

The "leaves another holder's lock file alone" test also fails on an earlier version of this branch, which wrote its PID and unlinked the file in the unsupported case. I checked that the real two-OS race it guards against exists:

- WSL process L1 holds the `flock`.
- A Windows process runs on the same `graphify-out` through `\\wsl.localhost`.
- A second WSL process L2 then tries the lock.

With that earlier version, L2 got the lock while L1 still held it. With this PR, L1's PID and the file stay intact, and L2 gets `False` until L1 releases.

Limitations:

- On a filesystem without byte-range locks, Windows-side rebuilds of the same graph are not serialized: not with each other, and not with WSL-side rebuilds. The warning says so. For Windows-vs-Windows, that is the pre-#3883 behaviour (#3881), now limited to filesystems where locking cannot work at all. Before this PR they hung forever instead. Keeping Windows-side serialization there would need a separate lock on a local path (e.g. under the temp dir, keyed by the resolved `graphify-out`); I left that out to keep this to one concern.
- Classification is by errno only. I verified `EACCES` for a contended lock and `EINVAL` on `\\wsl.localhost`. I have not tested an SMB share; a filesystem that reported contention with some other errno would now proceed unlocked instead of waiting.
- With this fix, `graphify update` from Windows on a `\\wsl.localhost` repo no longer hangs, but it can still fail on files with uppercase names. That is a separate bug in `file_hash` path normalization, reported in #4925; this PR does not touch it.

## How was this tested?

On Windows, `uv run` could not fetch dependencies on this machine (TLS interception: `invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer`). The Windows runs therefore used an existing venv of this project (CPython 3.13.5) with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at this branch; I checked that `graphify.watch` was imported from this branch. The Linux runs used `uv run` in WSL (CPython 3.10.12, separate venv).

```text
# lock tests, Windows, Python 3.13.5
python -m pytest tests/test_watch.py -q -k rebuild_lock
  this PR:    11 passed, 1 skipped
  origin/v8:  4 failed (the regression tests above), 7 passed, 1 skipped

# lock tests, Linux (WSL), Python 3.10.12
uv run python -m pytest tests/test_watch.py -q -k rebuild_lock
  this PR:    12 passed
  origin/v8:  4 failed (same 4), 8 passed

# all of tests/test_watch.py, Linux:  205 passed, 3 skipped

# full suite, Windows, Python 3.13.5
python -m pytest tests -q
  this PR:    12 failed, 8983 passed, 286 skipped, 1 xfailed
  origin/v8:  18 failed, 8971 passed, 286 skipped, 1 xfailed
  # no failure is new: all 12 also fail on origin/v8 (Windows-environment failures,
  # e.g. test_absolute_path_lookup_skips_getcwd, test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py).
  # The other 6 base failures, test_copied_ast_cache_preserves_terraform_ids[parallel-*],
  # passed in this run but failed in an earlier run of this branch too, so they look flaky.
  # 8983 = 8971 + the 6 new tests + those 6.

# lint / types on the touched files (Linux)
uv run ruff check graphify/watch.py tests/test_watch.py   -> All checks passed!
uv run pyright graphify/watch.py   -> 12 errors, all already on origin/v8 (which has 20);
                                      none new

# real case: `graphify update . --force` from Windows on a 40-file repo under \\wsl.localhost
#   before (installed 0.9.94, same lock code): hung, killed after 240 s with 0.7 s of CPU
#   after (this branch): prints the warning, gets past the lock, and the whole run ends in ~10 s
#   (exit 1 on #4925)
```

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts — n/a, no skill fragments touched.
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (not touched: the change is limited to `_rebuild_lock`).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications.
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [x] I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

title: fix(build): preserve independently sourced semantic file evidence (#4896)
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #4896 and the Pass 2b shrink-guard work in #4778/#4779. An AST file-self node with a unique filename can absorb multiple distinct semantic nodes from unrelated source documents purely by matching their label. Their ID, source_file and independent rationale then disappear on clustered rebuilds.

This is not a scheduler-CWD failure: a synthetic watch-root-relative graph reproduces it under both the watch root and home directory as CWD. In 0.9.93 the loss triggered fail-closed; in 0.9.99/0.9.100 the changed shrink guard permits the write, but still loses the independent source explanations.

## Change

- Reuse the existing build Pass 2b, but limit its label-only fold to evidence-free file mentions. Semantic records with nonempty rationale, source_url, author, contributor, captured_at or metadata remain distinct source-backed records.
- Apply the same predicate to _lost_saved_semantic_nodes so the shrink guard never exempts a record the builder intentionally preserves.
- Keep existing same-path (source_file, label) merge behavior unchanged.
- Add tests for two independently explained mentions of the same filename, edge preservation, ordinary evidence-free mention folding, shrink-guard negative control, and repeated serialization/cold-load integrity.
- Document the conservative rule in ARCHITECTURE.md.

No new schema, Store, persistence layer, or production configuration.

## Verification

- Isolated Python 3.11 E2E: unpatched graphifyy 0.9.100 loses two synthetic semantic IDs on clustered update under both CWDs; patched source preserves both and writes successfully. Non-clustered updates preserve both before and after.
- Targeted build/lost-semantic/cluster-only tests: 119 passed before the final serialization test.
- Expanded test_watch.py, test_build.py, test_lost_saved_semantic_nodes.py, test_cli_export.py: 386 passed, 146 warnings before the final serialization test.
- Follow-up provenance/serialize tests: 20 passed.
- ruff check .: all checks passed.
- Broad suite with test dependencies added: **6,268 passed, 111 skipped, 1 xfailed**, then stopped at tests/test_provider_registry.py::test_custom_provider_add_list_show_remove. This test also fails in isolation against the **unpatched upstream 0.9.100 wheel**, with the same assertion, so it is not a regression introduced by this patch. The earlier SQL parser and Python build dependency blockers passed after installing tree-sitter-sql and build/setuptools.
- git diff --check: passed.

## Boundaries and risks

- Deliberately conservative: a richly annotated file mention may remain separate even if it is ultimately semantically equivalent to the AST file node. A future evidence-preserving fold could merge it explicitly.
- This does not solve all semantic duplicate forms or same-source AST/semantic merges; it addresses the cross-source label-only fold identified in #4896.
- No production graph was overwritten, no --force was used, and no launchd job was changed.

## AI assistance

The implementation and regression tests were materially assisted by OpenAI ChatGPT (GPT-6); the isolated reproductions and test commands above were executed on macOS.

## Follow-up: full-rebuild YAML AST migration (#4896)

The first **real production** full update using the previous candidate did **not** overwrite graph.json: Graphify's fail-closed guard detected 10 saved semantic file-node IDs missing from the candidate. All 10 relate to existing, non-ignored YAML sources and were introduced or reprocessed by the newer YAML AST extractor. The production graph and manifest SHA256 were unchanged.

This revealed two more requirements:
1. **Same-source AST twins also cannot erase independently evidenced semantic YAML nodes.** The previous patch guarded only cross-source label-only folding; it is now extended to the exact (source_file,label) pass for reviewed semantic records.
2. **Plain same-source YAML file-self twins need a safe shrink-accounting match when AST disambiguation path-qualifies the visible label.** The guard now matches an exact normalized source identity, and does not confuse a separate same-basename file with a legitimate fold.

A 10-YAML test with the **real source paths and IDs** and ephemeral local copies of the YAML data, plus duplicate basenames, reproduces the original full-update fail-closed warning on unpatched v0.9.100. The amended candidate completes the full clustered rebuild, retains both reviewed rationales, and accounts for the evidence-free twins. The test runs in TemporaryDirectory and never changes production data.

Added end-to-end full-YAML regression in tests/test_watch.py; targeted tests updated:
- Scope: **391 passed**, 147 warnings.
- Python 3.10: **23 passed**, focused YAML tests.
- Python 3.13: **23 passed**, focused YAML tests.
- Full-repository Ruff: **PASS**.
- Earlier unrelated upstream provider-registry full-suite baseline failure remains disclosed above.

**Production status:** source backup intact, production graph unchanged following initial full-update refusal; candidate not promoted to production until a full guarded update and post-deployment provenance gate pass.

## Follow-up: same-ID AST/semantic overwrites and fail-closed provenance (#4896)

A full production rebuild with the prior commit completed successfully but exposed a **distinct data-integrity regression** in post-run read-only provenance gates: 111 independently evidenced saved semantic IDs remained in the graph but were replaced by AST-tier nodes with the **same ID**, dropping rationale (109 nodes), author (2 nodes), or captured_at (2 nodes). The deployed output was archived as a private local diagnostic and the production graph, manifest and sidecars were atomically restored from checksum-verified backup. No private graph or source data is included in this PR.

The new follow-up commit protects those same-ID collisions in the existing reconciliation path: a saved semantic node keeps its ID and metadata, while a fresh colliding AST node gets a stable source-qualified AST ID and its AST-only links are retargeted. It also avoids evicting semantic nodes when the source is incrementally re-extracted, and introduces a same-ID metadata downgrade check in the existing fail-closed shrink guard (node-count growth alone no longer permits semantic provenance loss). Sourceless AST placeholders are handled without borrowing the semantic source identity.

Local verification:
- Existing + added scoped suite: **395 passed**, 149 warnings, Ruff PASS.
- Python 3.10 / 3.13 focused suite: 25 passed on each.
- Read-only re-reconciliation of the **111 actual colliding IDs** from the local baseline and rejected candidate: **111 stable AST aliases, 0 semantic metadata losses**.
- End-to-end isolated full and incremental YAML AST/semantic ID collision regressions: PASS.
- The previous production candidate is not promoted; a new guarded production rebuild is undergoing post-update provenance validation with automatic rollback on failure.

No --force, no disabling of safety checks, and no Graphify global-version replacement.

title: fix(cpp): suppress INFERRED calls edges for local lambdas/std::function variables (#4917)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4917.

Calls to local lambdas (`auto box = [...]...; box(1);`) and local
`std::function` variables (`std::function<void()> job = ...; job();`)
were getting phantom INFERRED `calls` edges to same-named symbols in
other files. Local variable declarations never emit nodes, so they were
absent from `label_to_nid` and the call fell through to `raw_calls`,
where cross-file resolution bound it to an unrelated same-named symbol.

## Changes

- `graphify/extractors/engine.py`: Add `_cpp_local_bound_names()` to
  collect locally-declared variable names per C++ function body, and
  skip `raw_calls` for bare C++ calls whose callee matches a local
  binding — mirroring the existing Python `is_py_local_data` guard.
  Legitimate cross-file calls to non-local symbols are unaffected.
- `tests/test_cpp_method_declarations.py`: Regression test covering both
  local lambda and local `std::function` calls against same-named
  symbols in another file.

## Verification

- Reproduction case from #4917 now produces zero `calls` edges
- Legitimate cross-file INFERRED calls (e.g. to a function only defined
  in another file) still work
- All 36 C++ tests pass (35 existing + 1 new)

## Relationship to #4916

Independent of the header-layout issue #4916 — reproduced with all files
in one directory.

title: fix(python): resolve imports across PEP 420 namespace packages under src/
body:
## What does this PR do?

On v8, a Python monorepo of **PEP 420 namespace distributions** loses every import that crosses from one distribution to another. Each distribution has its own `src/`, and no directory has an `__init__.py`.

```text
pkgsql/src/airflow/sql/hooks/sql.py          class DbApiHook: def strip_sql_string(self, sql) ...
                                             def free_fn() ...
pkgpresto/src/airflow/presto/hooks/presto.py from airflow.sql.hooks.sql import DbApiHook, free_fn
                                             class PrestoHook(DbApiHook):
                                                 def get_records(self, sql):
                                                     free_fn()
                                                     return self.strip_sql_string(sql)
```

On v8 (`f5155bad`), this gives:

- `imports_from` dangles at `airflow_sql_hooks_sql` instead of reaching `sql.py`.
- `PrestoHook` gets no resolved base, so the inherited `self.strip_sql_string()` call has **no `calls` edge**.
- `free_fn()` is only an `INFERRED` name match.

Add `__init__.py` to the target's directories and both calls become `EXTRACTED`. So this is a namespace-package gap, not a missing feature.

### Why it happens

`_repoint_python_package_imports` maps a dotted module id (`airflow_sql_hooks_sql`) to the real file node. To find the module path, it walks up the contiguous run of `__init__.py` directories above the file. A namespace package has none, so the walk stops at once (`levels == 0`) and the file is skipped (`# not inside a package (namespace pkg / loose module)`). `_resolve_python_module_path` doesn't recover it either: it probes the scan root and the importing file's own ancestors, and another distribution's `src/` is neither.

### The change

When no `__init__.py` is found, the nearest `src/` ancestor is taken as the import root. `pkgsql/src/airflow/sql/hooks/sql.py` then aliases to `airflow.sql.hooks.sql`, the same module path Python would import it by. Three guards:

- **Ambiguity:** a module path claimed by two `src/` roots still stays unresolved, through the existing single-claimant guard (`test_ambiguous_namespace_submodule_does_not_bind_calls` and a new test cover it).
- **Loose modules:** a module directly under `src/` (`src/helpers.py`) is not aliased, since a bare `import helpers` may name a third-party package.
- **Stdlib names:** a namespace named like a stdlib module (`src/logging/...`) is not aliased (#4261).

Files with an `__init__.py` chain take the old path unchanged.

Related: #2174 is a broader rework of Python import resolution in monorepos, including namespace packages. This is a small, separate fix for the one case above. #2280 and #3272 are different import forms.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: a Python absolute import whose module exists in the corpus, at exactly one path, is linked to that file whatever the package layout. Ambiguous module paths are never guessed. Nothing persisted changes shape; graphs built from these layouts gain the missing `imports_from` and `calls` edges.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly. Namespace packages that are not under a `src/` directory are still not aliased.

## How was this tested?

```text
uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_src_layout_import_resolution.py -q
  12 passed (3 new)
New headline test with the extract.py change reverted:
  FAILED ... AssertionError: {('.get_records()', 'free_fn()', 'INFERRED')}
Full suite on Linux (WSL), isolated HOME:
  uv sync --all-extras --frozen && uv run --frozen pytest tests/ -q --tb=short
  9364 passed, 28 skipped, 1 xfailed, 1 failed:
  test_install_references.py::test_install_skill_references_ignores_precreated_predictable_tmp_symlink_to_dir
  It fails only in the full run. Run alone, it passes on both this branch and f5155bad (it reuses a predictable /tmp path).
uv run --frozen python -m tools.skillgen --check   ok
uv run --frozen bandit -r graphify -ll             same findings as f5155bad (4 high, 8 medium), none in the changed lines
```

title: feat(connect): one command to add the Graphify MCP server to Cursor, Claude Code, Codex and VS Code
body:
## Why

`graphify install` sets up skills and rules, but it never writes MCP config. To use the hosted Graphify server (`https://api.graphify.com/mcp`) or the local `graphify-mcp` server, users currently copy JSON or TOML into each client by hand, and every client uses a different shape: `mcpServers` vs `servers`, `type: "http"` or not, TOML for Codex. Both docs troubleshooting tables and support questions show the same failures: invalid JSON, the wrong URL, a server configured in two scopes ("every tool appears twice"), and no sign-in.

This PR adds one command that writes the right entry into every installed agent, safely and idempotently, and then tells the user how to sign in and check it worked.

## What it does

`graphify connect`:

1. **Detects clients.** Cursor, Claude Code, Codex and VS Code are found via their config dir or CLI on `PATH`. `--client` overrides.
2. **Shows a plan.** One line per client and server: the file or CLI, and whether it will add, update, remove or make no change. `--dry-run` also prints a unified diff of every file and every CLI call, and writes nothing.
3. **Asks once**, then backs up, writes and verifies the result. Without a TTY it requires `--yes`.
4. **Prints next steps.** Each client's sign-in step, plus a link to [Check it's working](https://docs.graphify.com/platform/verify-connection).

The command name is set in one place (`graphify/connect.py: COMMAND_NAME`). If we pick a different name (see the decisions below), the rename is a one-line change; help text and tests read the constant.

### Per-client behaviour

| Client | User scope | Project scope | Entry |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (file merge; Cursor has no add CLI) | `.cursor/mcp.json` | `mcpServers.graphify = {"url": …}` |
| Claude Code | `claude mcp add --transport http --scope user graphify <url>`. An update runs `claude mcp remove … --scope user` and then add. We never edit `~/.claude.json` ourselves, because Claude Code rewrites it constantly. With no `claude` on PATH, the client is skipped and the entry to add by hand is printed. | `.mcp.json` (file merge, the same shape `claude mcp add --scope project` writes) | `{"type": "http", "url": …}` |
| Codex | A fresh add uses `codex mcp add graphify --url <url>`. Update and remove edit only our table in `~/.codex/config.toml`. Honors `CODEX_HOME`. | `.codex/config.toml` (Codex reads it for trusted projects) | `[mcp_servers.graphify]` `url = …` |
| VS Code | A fresh add uses `code --add-mcp '{"name":"graphify","type":"http","url":…}'`, except on Windows (a JSON argument through a `.cmd` shim isn't safe). Otherwise the default-profile `mcp.json` is merged. | `.vscode/mcp.json` | `servers.graphify = {"type": "http", "url": …}` |

The local server (`--server local|both`) is a stdio entry named `graphify-local`: `<absolute graphify-mcp> --graph <absolute graph.json>`. Both paths are absolute: GUI clients often start without the shell's `PATH`, and `graphify-mcp`'s default graph path is relative to the working directory. When `graphify-mcp` isn't on PATH, it falls back to `<python> -m graphify.serve`.

### Flags

`--client cursor,claude,codex,vscode|all` (default: every client detected) · `--server hosted|local|both` (default: hosted) · `--scope user|project` (default: user for hosted, project for local) · `--graph PATH` · `--dry-run` · `--yes/-y` · `--remove` · `--with-skills` (also runs `graphify install` for each client) · `--json` (the plan and log go to stderr; the result object goes to stdout).

## Safety guarantees (each one has a test)

- **Merge, never overwrite.** Only the `graphify` / `graphify-local` entries change. Other servers, other top-level keys, the file's indent and its line endings (CRLF stays CRLF) are kept.
- **On update,** only the connection keys (`url`/`type`/`command`/`args`) are replaced. Keys the user added, such as `headers`, are kept.
- **Codex TOML:** no TOML writer is added as a dependency. Only our `[mcp_servers.graphify]` table and its sub-tables are edited as text; comments and every other table stay byte-for-byte. The result is re-parsed with `tomllib` and must differ from the original only at our key, or nothing is written. An entry written inline or with dotted keys is left alone, and the user is told to edit it by hand. Remove after add restores the original file exactly.
- **Idempotent.** A re-run with nothing to change writes nothing, makes no backup and calls no CLI. `--remove` twice is fine.
- **Unparseable files are skipped.** This includes JSON with comments. The file is never written, the entry to add by hand is printed, and the command exits 1 at the end.
- **Backups:** before each file change, `<file>.graphify.<timestamp>.bak` is written, and two runs in the same second don't overwrite each other's backup. Writes are an atomic temp file + rename, and a symlinked config is written through to its target. Changes made through a client's own CLI are not backed up; that client owns the file.
- **Duplicate warning:** a warning is shown when the same server name is already configured in the other scope (or in Claude Code's per-project "local" scope). The docs list "every tool appears twice" as a common setup problem.
- **Cursor plugin:** if the Graphify Cursor plugin is installed and already provides `graphify`, Cursor is skipped, to avoid a duplicate server.
- **No secrets are written.** The hosted server uses OAuth inside each client.
- **A user-scope local server needs an explicit `--graph`.** A local server needs an existing graph; otherwise it fails with `graphify update .` as the fix.

## How to test manually

```bash
# Nothing is written:
graphify connect --dry-run
graphify connect --client all --server both --dry-run

# In a throwaway HOME, so your real configs are untouched:
export HOME=$(mktemp -d); cd "$(mktemp -d)"
graphify connect --client cursor,vscode,codex --yes
graphify connect --client cursor,vscode,codex --yes      # every line: no-change
graphify connect --client cursor,vscode,codex --remove --yes
```

I also ran it end to end against the real `claude` (Claude Code) and `codex` CLIs in a temporary HOME. Claude: add → no-change → remove, checked in `~/.claude.json`. Codex: add via `codex mcp add` → no-change → URL drift is updated in the file with a backup → remove. Real `codex mcp list` showed `graphify  https://api.graphify.com/mcp  enabled  OAuth`.

## Test results

- `tests/test_connect.py`: **34 passed** (new)
- `tests/test_install*.py` + `tests/test_uninstall*.py` + `tests/test_connect.py`: **363 passed, 1 skipped**
- Full suite: **9130 passed, 215 skipped, 1 xfailed, 8 failed**. The same 8 fail on untouched `v8` @ `f5155ba` (7 in `tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py`, 1 in `tests/test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py`), so none comes from this PR. Run on macOS, Python 3.12.
- `ruff check`: clean. `pyright graphify/connect.py tests/test_connect.py`: 0 errors.

All tests run against a temporary HOME and an empty `PATH`. Client CLIs are stubbed via an injected runner.

## Decisions this PR made (open for review)

| Question | Options | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Command name | `graphify connect` / `graphify setup` / `graphify mcp add` | `connect`: it matches the docs' "Connect your agent" wording and leaves `install` for skills. A rename touches one constant. |
| Default server | hosted only / both | **hosted**. `local` needs a built graph and the `mcp` extra, so it's opt-in via `--server local\|both`. |
| Default scope | user / project | **user for hosted** (one setup for every repo), **project for local** (the graph belongs to this checkout). |
| Install skills by default | yes / no | **no**. Opt in with `--with-skills`. MCP config and skills are separate concerns, and `install` already exists. |
| Token via env var for headless/CI | `--token-env` | **not included**. Each client's env-interpolation syntax still needs verifying (follow-up). |

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `--token-env VAR` for headless/CI, writing a header that references an env var, never the literal token. The syntax differs per client; Codex has `bearer_token_env_var`.
- Read the hosted endpoint from the server's MCP Server Card (SEP-2127, `https://api.graphify.com/mcp/server-card`) once that endpoint is live. The URL constant stays as the fallback.
- More clients: OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Zed.
- VS Code: non-default profiles are reached through `code --add-mcp` for adds, but update and remove only edit the default profile's `mcp.json`.
- A `--verify` option that runs each client's own list command (`claude mcp list`, `codex mcp list`) after writing.
- Docs: a short "Connect with one command" section on the quickstart and integration pages.

## Handoff for reviewer

- **Merge order:** independent of any other PR. No migrations, no new dependencies (`tomli` was already required on Python 3.10).
- **Deploy:** nothing to deploy. It ships with the next CLI release.
- **Release note** (for the changelog at release time): `Feat: **connect** new \`graphify connect\` adds the Graphify MCP server (hosted, local, or both) to Cursor, Claude Code, Codex and VS Code in one step: merge-only edits with backups, idempotent re-runs, \`--dry-run\`, \`--remove\`, \`--json\`.`
- **Files:** `graphify/connect.py` (new), `graphify/__main__.py` (dispatch + help; `connect` parses its own `--help`), `tests/test_connect.py` (new), `README.md` (a short section).
- **Things worth a second look:**
  - The Claude Code update path runs remove then add. If the add fails after the remove, the entry is gone and the error is reported.
  - The Cursor plugin check scans `~/.cursor/plugins` at most 5 levels deep.

title: fix(go): link a method value reached through a receiver field (#1566)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Refs #1566. 61e864a7 (`fix(go): link a method value passed as an argument as an indirect_call`) links `routing.Wrap(s.Health)` to `Server.Health`. It does not link a method value reached through a field of the receiver, which is how Go code usually registers a handler held as a dependency:

```go
// api/handler.go
package api

type ContextHandler struct{}

func (h *ContextHandler) Middleware(next int) int { return next }

// api/http_server.go
package api

type Macaron struct{}

func (m *Macaron) UseMiddleware(f func(int) int) {}

type HTTPServer struct {
	ContextHandler *ContextHandler
}

func (hs *HTTPServer) addMiddlewares(m *Macaron) {
	m.UseMiddleware(hs.ContextHandler.Middleware) // no edge to Middleware
}
```

On v8 (`f5155bad`, 0.9.100) the call edges are only `addMiddlewares -> UseMiddleware (calls)` plus `references`; there is no edge to `ContextHandler.Middleware`. Same result when `HTTPServer` is declared in a sibling file of the package. The real-world shape is Grafana `pkg/api/http_server.go:732`, `m.UseMiddleware(hs.ContextHandler.Middleware)`.

### Root cause

In `extract_go`'s `walk_calls`, the method-value loop over call arguments added in 61e864a7 skips any `selector_expression` argument whose operand is not an `identifier`. `hs.ContextHandler.Middleware` has a `selector_expression` operand (`hs.ContextHandler`), so no raw call was recorded. The direct-call branch already handles the same shape (`hs.ContextHandler.Middleware()`) by recording the field as `member_receiver` and the receiver's type as `field_owner`, and `_resolve_go_member_calls` already types that through the caller's table or, for a struct declared in a sibling file, the owner's `_go_fields` (#3368).

### The change

`graphify/extractors/go.py` only: the argument loop also accepts `self.field.M` when `self` is the enclosing method's own receiver, and records it with `member_receiver = field`, `receiver_type = None`, `field_owner = self_type`, the same values the direct-call branch uses. Resolution, guards and the emitted edge (`indirect_call`, `context: "argument"`, INFERRED, 0.85) are unchanged code in `_resolve_go_member_calls`. A chain rooted at anything other than the method's own receiver is still skipped, as for direct calls.

### Scope

- Covered: field typed by a type of the same package, struct declared in the same file or in a sibling file.
- Not covered here: a field typed from another package (`*contexthandler.ContextHandler`, the Grafana case). `_go_single_type_name` drops a `qualified_type`, so the field has no type on v8; that is what #4853 adds, and this PR does not duplicate it. I applied #4853's source diff together with this change in a scratch worktree: the cross-package repro then also gets `addMiddlewares -> ContextHandler.Middleware (indirect_call)` with no further change.
- No AST cache schema bump: Go extraction output changes, so a cached Go file keeps the old raw calls until it is re-extracted. Left to the batch bump, as with the other recent Go fixes; happy to add one if preferred.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a Go method value binds only to a method of the single type its receiver is declared as, and a value whose type is unknown links nothing and parks nothing (it may be a field, not a method). The new path goes through the same resolver and guards as a direct `s.field.M()` call, so it can only add an edge where the direct-call form would get one.

New tests in `tests/test_go_method_value_indirect_calls.py`:

- `test_a_method_value_through_a_receiver_field_is_an_indirect_call`: same file; asserts `indirect_call`, INFERRED, no `calls` edge to `Middleware`, and the `UseMiddleware` call unchanged.
- `test_a_method_value_through_a_field_declared_in_a_sibling_file`: struct declared in another file of the package.
- `test_a_method_value_through_a_field_of_unknown_type_links_and_parks_nothing`: field typed `*Missing` (declared nowhere): no `indirect_call`, no `unresolved_calls` on the caller.

title: fix(go): reference the types a package-level var initialiser names (#2360)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #2360 (commit 1c4c3f2c), which credits calls in a Go package-level `var` initialiser to the file. The types named in the same place were still dropped, so a file that only holds a google/wire set referenced nothing.

Minimal repro (`go.mod`: `module example.com/app`):

```go
// validator/validator.go
package validator

type DataSourceRequestValidator interface{ Validate() error }
type OSSDataSourceRequestValidator struct{}
func (v *OSSDataSourceRequestValidator) Validate() error { return nil }
func ProvideValidator() *OSSDataSourceRequestValidator { return &OSSDataSourceRequestValidator{} }
```

```go
// server/wire.go
package server

import (
	"github.com/google/wire"
	"example.com/app/validator"
)

var wireSet = wire.NewSet(
	validator.ProvideValidator,
	wire.Bind(new(validator.DataSourceRequestValidator), new(*validator.OSSDataSourceRequestValidator)),
)
```

On v8 (f5155bad), `extract(...)` warns `1 code file(s) yielded no symbols ... server/wire.go`, and `wire.go` has only its two `imports_from` edges: nothing to `DataSourceRequestValidator` or `OSSDataSourceRequestValidator`. The same shape is Grafana's `pkg/server/wire.go`.

Root cause: in `extract_go`, `walk` hands a package-level `var_declaration` to `walk_calls` (#2360), which only looks at `call_expression`s. Type references are emitted only for struct fields, interface elements and signatures (`emit_go_method_refs`). Nothing reads the types in a `var` declaration's declared type, a composite literal, or a `new`/`make` type argument.

The change: a new `emit_go_package_var_type_refs`, called from the same `var_declaration` branch, walks the declaration and collects:

- the `var_spec` declared type (`var x pkg.T`, `var _ Iface = ...`),
- a `composite_literal` type (`pkg.T{}`, `&T{}`, `[]*T{{}}`),
- an `argument_list` child that parses as a type node (`new(T)`, `new(*pkg.T)`, `make(map[string]pkg.T)`).

Each type goes through the same `_go_collect_type_refs` + `ensure_named_node` path a struct field uses. The file node gets a `references` edge with context `variable_type`, or `generic_arg` for a generic instantiation's type argument (`pkg.List[T]{}`), as on a field. That file node is the owner #2360 already gives these calls. Because the path is shared, `pkg.T` resolves through the file's import in `_resolve_go_type_references`. An external type such as `http.Client` is parked on its import path (`net/http.Client`), the same as an external field type, and is never bound to a same-named local type. `wire.NewSet` / `wire.Bind` are unchanged and add no nodes or edges. With the patch, the repro gives `wire.go -references-> DataSourceRequestValidator` and `wire.go -references-> OSSDataSourceRequestValidator`, both on the nodes declared in `validator/validator.go`, and the "no symbols" warning goes away.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a type named in Go source gets a `references` edge from its owner, and that edge goes to the declaration the import names, or to a parked external stub. It never goes to a same-named local type. Struct fields already worked this way. A package-level initialiser's owner is the file (#2360).

Scope limits, stated explicitly:
- A closure body inside the initialiser (`var f = func() { _ = &T{} }`) is function code. It emits no body type references, like any other function body; a test locks this in.
- A package-qualified function value passed as an argument (`validator.ProvideValidator` above) is still not linked. The #1566 method-value path covers only non-package receivers, and `test_a_package_function_value_is_not_read_as_a_method_value` keeps a package function value from becoming an `indirect_call`. Changing that would also affect function bodies, so it is left out here.
- A conversion such as `var _ Iface = (*Impl)(nil)` links `Iface` (the declared type) but not `Impl`, because the grammar parses `(*Impl)` as an expression.
- `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` is not bumped. Cached Go extractions keep the old output until the next schema bump. I left that for the release batch, the way the recent schema bumps were done.
