title: fix(python): don't resolve a bare call in a method to a method
body:
## What does this PR do?

In Python, a bare call inside a method body was linked to a method with the same name, usually the enclosing method itself. The call should have been linked to the imported or module-level function it actually names. Python never resolves a bare name to a method. Methods are only reachable through `self`, `cls`, or the class. A bare name goes local -> enclosing function -> module globals (including imports) -> builtins.

Minimal repro (v8 at f5155bad, 0.9.100):

```python
# tpl/build_api.py
def get_build_status(c, b):
    return 1

# tpl/main.py
from tpl.build_api import get_build_status

class AsyncTemplate:
    @classmethod
    def get_build_status(cls, b):
        return get_build_status(None, b)
```

v8 emits a false self-loop:

```text
calls  .get_build_status()@tpl/main.py -> .get_build_status()@tpl/main.py  EXTRACTED
```

Expected (and emitted with this PR):

```text
calls  .get_build_status()@tpl/main.py -> get_build_status()@tpl/build_api.py  EXTRACTED
```

The same thing happens with a plain (non-classmethod) method. It also happens with a same-file module function: `def helper(): ...` at module level plus `class C: def helper(self): return helper()` linked `.helper()` to itself. The real-world case where this shows up is the E2B SDK's `AsyncTemplate.get_build_status` (`template_async/main.py`), which calls the imported `get_build_status`.

**Root cause.** In `_extract_generic` (`graphify/extractors/engine.py`), the call walk first resolves a Python bare call through the lexical scope chain (`lexical_nids_by_scope`), then falls back to the file-wide `label_to_nid` map. That map is built from every node label, methods included (`.get_build_status()` normalises to `get_build_status`). Its entries are overwritten in file order, so a method can also replace a same-named module function. The fallback therefore landed on the method. That is an in-file hit, so the call never reached `raw_calls`, and the cross-file import resolution never saw it.

**Change.** While building `label_to_nid`, also build `python_free_label_to_nid`: the same map with Python method nodes (targets of `method` edges) left out. In the Python bare-call branch, if the fallback hit is a method and the call does not sit directly in that method's class body, look the name up in the method-free map instead. With no in-file hit, the call goes to `raw_calls`, and the existing cross-file resolver binds it through the import. Code that is not Python is untouched. `self.m()` / `cls.m()` / `super().m()` take the `_self_call_target` branch, which is untouched. A module function that calls itself by bare name still resolves to itself, because it is not a method.

I found no existing issue or PR for this. #2366 is about module-qualified `mod.f()` calls from methods, which is a different path.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a Python bare call `f()` made from a method body never resolves to a method. It resolves to a nested function, a module-level definition, or an import, or else it gets no in-file edge.

Kept as before:
- Genuine module-function recursion (`def fact(n): ... fact(n - 1)`) still links to itself.
- `self.b()` still links to the sibling method.
- A nested function inside a method still resolves through the lexical scope chain first.

Persisted state: this changes Python extraction output (it removes false self-loop `calls` edges and adds the correct cross-file/module edges). Cached Python AST extractions from earlier builds keep the old edges until they are re-extracted. I did not bump `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA`, because recent fix PRs leave that to the maintainer's batched bump. I can add it here if you prefer.

title: feat(go): dispatch interface method calls to implicit implementers
body:
## What does this PR do?

A Go call through an interface-typed field lands on the interface's method node, which is correct. But nothing links that interface method to the concrete types that implement it. So the concrete method loses every caller that goes through the interface, and a directed walk stops at the interface.

Repro on v8 (`f5155bad`, 0.9.100). `go.mod` is `module example.com/app`.

```go
// plugincontext/provider.go
package plugincontext

type Provider struct{}

func (p *Provider) GetWithDataSource(uid string) error { return nil }
```

```go
// expr/nodes.go
package expr

type pluginContextProvider interface {
	GetWithDataSource(uid string) error
}

type DSNode struct {
	provider pluginContextProvider
}

func (d *DSNode) Execute() error {
	return d.provider.GetWithDataSource("x")
}
```

v8 emits `calls .Execute() -> expr_plugincontextprovider_getwithdatasource` (the interface method). Nothing reaches `plugincontext_provider_getwithdatasource`, before or after `build_from_json`. Grafana has the same shape: `pkg/expr/nodes.go` calls `GetWithDataSource` through `pkg/expr`'s local `pluginContextProvider`, and `plugincontext.Provider.GetWithDataSource` loses those callers.

**Why.** `graphify.interface_dispatch` (#3003, shared with the Swift pass) already links `interface_method --dispatches_to--> implementing_method`. It is driven by `implements` edges. Go satisfies interfaces implicitly, so the Go extractor emits no `implements` edges and the mechanism never runs.

**Change.**

- `graphify/extractors/go.py` stamps each interface type node with `metadata: {"language": "go", "kind": "interface"}`. Without it the output cannot tell an interface's method requirements from a struct's methods, because both hang off their owner by a `method` edge. `language` and `kind` are already among the metadata keys that the incremental `update`/`watch` context forwards for unchanged nodes, so the stamp survives an incremental rebuild.
- New `graphify/go_dispatch.py`, registered next to the C# and Swift passes. It infers implementers from method sets: named type T implements interface I when T's methods include every method name I requires, counting I's own methods and the methods of interfaces it embeds. T can be a struct or any other named type with methods. Value and pointer receivers both count, because the extractor hangs both off T's node. The pass hands those pairs to `resolve_interface_dispatch` and keeps only the `dispatches_to` edges that come back. The inferred `implements` pairs are not added to the graph.
- `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` 33 -> 34, so cached Go extractions re-run and pick up the stamp.

The C# and Swift edges keep their shape and tiers: `INFERRED`, `context: "call"`, 0.85 for one implementer, 0.75 for two, 0.65 floor, and the per-implementer single-owner guard. The edge is additive, so the `calls` edge to the interface method stays.

**Matching rule and guards**

- Matching is by name only. Method nodes carry no parameter list, and Go has no overloads to tell apart. Adding arity would mean new metadata on every Go method node, so I left it out.
- Both ends must be declared in a `.go` file. This is the same suffix gate as the C# and Swift passes.
- An interface with no methods (`interface{}`, `any`) is skipped. Every type satisfies it.
- A type-set interface (`~int | ~string`, which the extractor marks as a `type_constraint` reference) is skipped. It is a generics constraint, not something a call goes through.
- When an interface embeds another, the embedded interface's methods are required too. If an embedded interface is not declared in the corpus (`io.Reader`), the method set is unknown, so the interface is skipped. Matching on part of the method set would admit types that do not implement it.
- An unexported requirement (`run()`) can only be implemented in the interface's own package. When the interface requires one, only types in the same directory count.
- **Cap.** The shared mechanism has no fan-out cap, because declared `implements` cannot explode. Name-only structural matching can. An interface matched by more than 10 types (`_MAX_IMPLICIT_IMPLEMENTERS`) is skipped entirely. It is not truncated, because which ten to keep would be arbitrary. On Grafana `pkg/` (5715 Go files, 1056 interfaces), 160 interfaces go over the cap. The largest are `Runnable`/`BackgroundService`/`Elector`-style interfaces, with 436 matching types each, and `Validator`-style ones, with 333 each. Without the cap they would add thousands of 0.65 edges that say little.
- **Common names (`Error`, `String`).** These get no special case. The builtin `error` and `fmt.Stringer` are not corpus nodes, so they never match. A local redeclaration (`type stringer interface{ String() string }`) is a real interface that calls go through. It gets edges like any other interface, and the cap covers the case where the name is everywhere.

**Effect on Grafana `pkg/`:** 6637 `dispatches_to` edges (680 at 0.85, 1502 at 0.75, 4455 at 0.65). `expr.pluginContextProvider.GetWithDataSource` now dispatches to `plugincontext.Provider.GetWithDataSource` and to the in-package test fake, at 0.75. The pass took about 3 s on that corpus with the cap disabled.

**Limitations**

- Struct embedding is not followed. If a type gets a method from an embedded field, the type does not own that method node, so it is not matched.
- Name-only matching can pair a type whose method has the same name but a different signature. Confidence tiers and the cap limit this; they do not remove it.
- Test fakes and mocks implement interfaces too, so they count as implementers and lower the tier for the production type. That is structurally correct, but it is noisier than C#, where a mock usually comes from a framework rather than from source.
- Interfaces declared outside the corpus (stdlib, dependencies) get no edges, because they have no method nodes.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a `dispatches_to` edge joins a Go interface method only to a same-named method of a Go type that has every method the interface requires. The edge is additive (the `calls` edge to the interface stays), carries an `INFERRED` tier, and is never emitted for an interface whose method set is unknown or empty.

fix(hook): drop the self-claimed exemption from the search nudge
body:
## Problem

The search nudge ends with:

> Grep works best once the graph or an earlier read has pointed to the exact file and lines.

An agent can apply the "earlier read" half to any grep, because it decides for itself what counts as a prior read. In practice the agent read the sentence as permission for the grep the nudge had just flagged, including the first exploratory search of a session (the case the nudge exists for), and then for the greps after it. The sentence ended up excusing exactly the behavior it was meant to redirect.

## Change

The last sentence of `_SEARCH_NUDGE` now says what each tool is for, with no exemption the agent can grant itself:

> Finding where something lives is what the graph answers; grep finds exact text in files the graph has already named.

It stays a statement of fact rather than a command (#2202), and `tests/test_hook_nudge_wording.py` still passes. The read nudges are unchanged; their "once the graph has pointed to the exact lines" condition does not name a self-claimable "earlier read".

## Verification

- `uv run pytest -q tests/test_hook_nudge_wording.py tests/test_hook_guard.py tests/test_install_strings.py`: 133 passed.
- `uv run ruff check graphify/cli.py`: clean.
- `uv run pytest -q tests`: 9068 passed, 7 failed. All 7 are in `tests/test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py` and fail the same way on `upstream/v8` without this change.
- Ran `graphify hook-guard search` on a project with a graph, feeding it a Grep tool payload. It printed the new text.

## Limitations

This is wording only. A nudge still arrives with or after the search it comments on, so it can redirect later searches but not the one that fired it.

title: fix(cache): keep Windows cache keys case-preserving (#4925)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4925.

On Windows, `file_hash()` ran the caller path through `_normalize_path()`, which called `os.path.normcase()`. That lowercased the path used for `is_file()`, `stat()` and `read_bytes()`. On a case-sensitive WSL share, `README.md` became `readme.md`, so the rebuild failed.

The same value was also the cache key. Lowercasing made `README.md` and `readme.md` share a digest and a semantic cache entry. When both files exist, that turns the crash into a wrong cache hit.

This change separates the path used for I/O from the path used for the cache key:

```diff
- p = _normalize_path(path)
- p.is_file(); p.stat(); p.read_bytes()
+ src = os_long_path(path)
+ src.is_file(); src.stat(); src.read_bytes()

  key = _normalize_path(path)
- return Path(os.path.normcase(s))
+ return Path(os.path.normpath(s))
- salt = walked_rel.as_posix().lower()
+ salt = walked_rel.as_posix()
```

`_normalize_path()` now keeps case. `file_hash()` and `cached_word_count()` use `os_long_path()` for the filesystem path. The stat-index key is case-preserving.

On POSIX, `_normalize_path()` still returns the path unchanged. On Windows, a case-only spelling change may now miss the cache. That is safer than returning another file's cache entry.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Evidence

**Before:** on `v8` at 0.9.100.

```text
tests/test_cache_windows_case_4925.py
8 failed in 3.35s
```

The reported failure:

```text
file_hash requires a file, got: ...\readme.md
```

The quieter failure, with both `README.md` and `readme.md` present:

```text
file_hash(README.md) == file_hash(readme.md)
load_cached(readme.md) returned the entry saved for README.md
```

**After:**

```text
tests/test_cache_windows_case_4925.py
8 passed

cache-focused suites
146 passed, 1 skipped

full suite
9396 passed, 18 skipped, 1 xfailed in 1092.49s
```

The full suite was run with `PYTHONPATH=.` so subprocess CLI tests imported this worktree instead of the installed package.

## Verification & Invariants

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

The invariant: a cache key may miss, but it must not name a different file.

The tests pin:

- Uppercase files and uppercase roots hash and cache correctly.
- `save_cached()` and `load_cached()` round trip an uppercase path.
- Two case variants with the same content get different hashes.
- Two case variants do not share a semantic cache entry.
- Hardlink and symlink aliases keep distinct hashes.
- `cached_word_count()` writes and uses the stat index for an uppercase path.

Known limitations:

- On a case-insensitive volume, alternate case spellings may miss the cache. That costs a rebuild, not correctness.
- `Path.relative_to()` on Windows compares case-insensitively. Two WSL directories differing only by case can still be conflated. That is separate hardening and is not required for this issue.
- Old lowercased cache entries on Windows become unreachable and are rebuilt. No graph data is lost.
- No cache schema bump and no graph format change.

## How was this tested?

```text
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_cache_windows_case_4925.py -q
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp=/var/tmp/gf4925-full6
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/cache.py tests/test_cache_windows_case_4925.py
.venv/bin/python -m graphify update .
```

Branch `fix/4925-windows-case-sensitive-path` is based on `upstream/v8` (`32e5efe9`, v0.9.100). It has four commits:

```text
bcd81af5 test(cache): pin Windows case-sensitive path handling (#4925)
78448a04 fix(cache): keep Windows cache keys case-preserving (#4925)
54e6ba23 fix(cache): open hashed files through os_long_path (#4925)
002d31e3 fix(cache): open word-count files through os_long_path (#4925)
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way.

The default path is unchanged. No cache schema bump and no graph format change. Reverting restores the old cache keys.

**Blast Radius:** Cache.

After merge, old lowercased cache entries on Windows become unreachable and are rebuilt. A user who spells the same file with different case may see a cache miss. That costs time and returns the correct result. Ignore rules, secret filtering, extraction and graph writing are unchanged.

title: fix(hook): count sed and awk run on files as searches
body:
## Problem

The Bash search guard (`_bash_invokes_search`) matches grep, rg, find, fd, ack, ag and `git grep`. An agent that has been nudged can keep searching or reading the codebase with `sed -n 4085,4145p src/x.php` or `awk 'NR>=10 && /warn/' src/x.php`, and those calls are never nudged. This came up in a real session: once the agent switched to sed and awk for its searches and reads, those calls were never nudged.

## Change

`sed` and `awk` now count as searches when they open files themselves. Two cases stay quiet, so the change doesn't bring back the false positives #3121 removed:

- **On the receiving end of a pipe** (`ps aux | awk '{print $2}'`, `git log | sed -n 1,5p`): there they only reshape another command's output. The segment split now keeps its operators so each segment knows whether it reads a pipe. `||` is not treated as a pipe.
- **In place** (`-i`, `--in-place`, or a sed flag cluster such as `-Ei`): that's an edit, not a search.
- **With no file operand** (`awk 'BEGIN{…}'`, `sed -n 1,5p`): the program reads stdin. Quoted spans now become one placeholder word, so a quoted program still counts as an operand.

A pipe carries over the empty segments that `|&` and a pipeline continued on the next line leave behind.

## Verification

- Wrote the new cases in `tests/test_hook_guard_token_match.py` first. The four that should fire failed on `upstream/v8` and the five quiet cases passed. With the change, all pass.
- `uv run pytest -q tests/test_hook_guard_token_match.py tests/test_hook_guard.py tests/test_hook_nudge_wording.py`: 175 passed (after the review follow-up).
- `uv run ruff check graphify/cli.py tests/test_hook_guard_token_match.py`: clean.
- `uv run pyright graphify/cli.py`: 1 error ("Code is too complex to analyze" at `cli.py:1456`), which is also present on `upstream/v8` without this change.
- Ran `graphify hook-guard search` with a `sed -n ... src/x.php` Bash payload in a project with a graph: it printed the search nudge.

## Limitations

- `xargs sed ...` after a pipe stays quiet, because the segment reads a pipe.
- `cat file` and `head`/`tail` on files are not covered.

title: fix(rebuild): keep a --code-only graph code-only on rebuilds (#4923)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4923.

A graph built with `graphify extract . --code-only` grows `.md`, `.mdx` and `.qmd` nodes on the next git hook, `graphify update` or `graphify watch` rebuild. `_rebuild_code` has no `--code-only` flag and nothing recorded the scope, so it re-detects the repo and adds every markdown-family file that has an AST extractor (the #4750 doc quick-scan).

This PR records the scope when `extract --code-only` runs, and `_rebuild_code` reads it back.

```diff
 extract . --code-only
   detect -> skip docs
+  write .graphify_build.json {"code_only": true}

 _rebuild_code        (hooks, update, watch all land here)
   _read_build_gitignore
+  _read_build_code_only
   detect
-  add .md/.mdx/.qmd to the AST quick-scan
+  add .md/.mdx/.qmd to the AST quick-scan, unless code_only
```

- `code_only` sits in `.graphify_build.json` next to `excludes` and `gitignore` (#1886, #1971). `_rebuild_code` gets no new parameter, so every rebuild entry point is covered without touching the hooks.
- `code_only` is part of the build state the #4740 no-change gate compares, so flipping the scope on unchanged files is not skipped as "No relevant changes".
- A flagless `extract` clears the scope only when it goes on to ingest docs, meaning it got past the API key check. An aborted run, or a repo with no docs, leaves it alone.
- Doc nodes already in the graph are kept, the same way `--code-only` already keeps the semantic layer (#2923).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Evidence

**Before** (`upstream/v8` at `32e5efe9`): scratch repo with 2 `.py` and 3 `.md` files.

```text
$ graphify extract . --code-only
nodes 5, edges 7, from .md: 0
$ graphify update .
nodes 17, edges 16, from .md: 12
```

**After:**

```text
$ graphify extract . --code-only
nodes 5, edges 7, from .md: 0
$ graphify update .
nodes 5, edges 7, from .md: 0
```

The issue's own steps are covered by a test that installs the real post-commit hook, commits a changed `.py` and `.md`, waits for the new code symbol to land, then checks for doc nodes.

**Tests:**

```text
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_code_only_scope_4923.py -q
14 passed

$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
1 failed, 9401 passed, 18 skipped, 1 xfailed in 868.46s
FAILED tests/test_language_override_lifecycle.py::test_watch_root_config_lifecycle_rebuilds_and_refreshes_event_mapping[create]

$ .venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/watch.py graphify/cli.py \
    tests/test_code_only_scope_4923.py tests/test_extract_code_only_cli.py
All checks passed!
```

The one failure is a file-watcher timing test that does not touch this change. It failed 1 run in 5 on the unmodified base (`32e5efe9`), and it passes 5 of 5 on this branch when run alone.

`tests/test_extract_code_only_cli.py::test_explicit_exclude_replaces_persisted_setting_with_custom_out` asserted the whole `.graphify_build.json` equals `{"excludes": [...]}` after a `--code-only` run. The file now also carries `"code_only": true`, so the expectation includes it. The test still checks what it was written for: an explicit `--exclude` replaces the persisted list.

## Verification & Invariants

- [ ] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

The invariant: a rebuild keeps the scope the graph was built with. A code-only graph stays code-only until the user runs a flagless `extract` that ingests docs.

The tests drive the real CLI and assert on the resulting graph. They pin:

- The scope survives a full rebuild (checkout, merge, rewrite), an incremental rebuild (commit), `graphify update`, and a new doc added later.
- A rebuild of a code-only graph still picks up new code and drops deleted code.
- A graph with no recorded scope still gets doc nodes (#4750 unchanged).
- Doc nodes already in the graph survive turning the scope on.
- An aborted flagless `extract` and a flagless `extract` on a repo with no docs keep the scope.
- A flagless `extract` that ingests docs clears it.
- The build state differs by scope.

Known limitations:

- A graph built before this change has no recorded scope. Run `extract --code-only` once to record it.
- Doc nodes already in the graph are not evicted when the scope turns on, and a rebuild no longer refreshes them.
- The two side notes in the issue (the CLI and the hook disagreeing about docs without a key, and `manifest.json` changing on every rebuild) are not part of this PR.
- The reset-on-flagless-extract test reaches the backend through a dead local Ollama port, not a real LLM backend.

## How was this tested?

```text

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/watch.py graphify/cli.py \
  tests/test_code_only_scope_4923.py tests/test_extract_code_only_cli.py
```

Branch `test/4923-code-only-scope` is based on `upstream/v8` (`32e5efe9`, v0.9.100). It is five commits, and each one passes its own tests: the tests (red by design), the recorded scope, the rebuild fix, the no-change gate, and the reset.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way.

A graph with no `code_only` key rebuilds exactly as before. No cache schema bump and no graph format change. Reverting leaves a stray `code_only` key in `.graphify_build.json`, which older code ignores.

**Blast Radius:** Rebuild scope.

The change only affects graphs built with `--code-only`. Someone who built one and still wanted doc headings from hook rebuilds will stop getting them until they run a flagless `extract`.

title: Shrink-guard refuses a valid merge when exact-duplicate dedup drops nodes the saved cache references
body:
### Summary

During an incremental semantic `--update` on a project graph, `to_json` (via `build_merge`) refuses to write with:

```
[graphify] Replaced 23 node(s) from re-extracted source file(s).
[graphify] Deduplicated 2 node(s) (2 exact).
[graphify] WARNING: Refusing to overwrite — saved semantic node(s) are missing from the new graph: glossary_first_contact, glossary_the_nudge.
graph.json written: False
```

The two "missing" nodes ARE present in the freshly extracted chunk that was passed to `build_merge` — they are then dropped by the immediately preceding **exact-duplicate dedup** ("Deduplicated 2 node(s) (2 exact)"), and the shrink-guard (#479) afterwards compares the saved cache against the post-dedup graph and counts them as missing. The guard's refusal discards a healthy merged graph.

### Reproduction shape

1. Project graph previously built with semantic nodes from a doc chunk that covered **two files at once** (chunk = `CLAUDE.md` + `GLOSSARY.md` in one extraction).
2. Later `--update`: the chunk set changes so `GLOSSARY.md` is re-extracted **alone** (cache-first: `save_semantic_cache` run before `build_merge`, prompt_file consistent).
3. `build_merge([extraction], graph_path=..., root='.', ast_sources=[...])` replaces the `GLOSSARY.md`-sourced nodes (23 replaced) and dedups 2 exact duplicates (the two nodes whose ids/labels collide with nodes still present from the old two-file chunk's provenance handling).
4. `to_json` refuses: the deduped nodes are counted as "saved semantic node(s) missing from the new graph".

Observed on graphify 0.9.97 (installed via `uv tool install graphifyy`), Python 3.12, Linux. The refusal is deterministic across retries, including with a fully cache-first flow (the skill's documented Part-B order).

### Impact

The writer refuses a valid merge, so the on-disk graph silently stays stale (new concept nodes from the re-extracted doc never land), and the operator is invited to re-run — but re-running re-extracts and re-refuses identically. In an agent workflow this is expensive: each "retry" is another full LLM extraction of unchanged documents.

### Expected behavior

Nodes removed by the merge's own dedup step should not count as "missing" in the #479 shrink-guard comparison — the guard should compare against the pre-dedup node set (or dedup should preserve one copy of an "exact duplicate" whose id the saved cache references).

### Workaround

Accept the refusal, keep the previous on-disk `graph.json`, and let the next full rebuild (or `graphify update . --force` for AST-only content) pick up the missing concept nodes. Works, but the doc-side semantic content lags until a full rebuild.

Happy to provide the full extraction chunk + graph.json pair if useful.

title: Build alias index binds a live Dart variable_type reference to a Java file node across languages (0.9.100)
body:
## Summary

`extract()` correctly leaves an unresolved Dart type reference as a dangling stub (`punchtype`), but `build_from_json()` then resolves that endpoint through `_alias_index()` to an unrelated **Java file node**, because the alias is committed when exactly one node claims the old-stem spelling — with no language check. On a real repo this produces the only cross-language code edge, and it is an articulation edge that dominates betweenness.

## Environment

- graphifyy 0.9.100 (pip), Python 3.10, Windows 11
- fresh AST cache (0/3 files served), no LLM involved

## Minimal reproduction

Three files:

```dart
// mobile/lib/domain/punch.dart
enum PunchType { checkIn, checkOut }          // L3

class PunchDraft {
  final String employeeId;
  final PunchType type;                       // L27 - the reference
}
```

```java
// backend/.../PunchType.java
public enum PunchType { CHECK_IN, CHECK_OUT }
```

```java
// backend/.../AttendancePunch.java  (present so the enum has a same-corpus user)
public record AttendancePunch(UUID deviceId, PunchType type) {}
```

```python
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.extract import extract
from graphify.build import build_from_json

files = [
    Path('mobile/lib/domain/punch.dart'),
    Path('backend/.../PunchType.java'),
    Path('backend/.../AttendancePunch.java'),
]
r = extract(files, cache_root=<fresh dir>, root=Path('.'))
# raw edge: mobile_lib_domain_punch --references--> punchtype   (dangling, correct)
G = build_from_json(r, root='.', directed=False)
```

### Actual (built)

```
mobile_lib_domain_punch --references [EXTRACTED, context=variable_type, L27]-->
  backend_src_main_java_ec_smartlocalizador_attendance_punchtype
```

where the target node is labeled `PunchType.java` with `source_file=backend/.../PunchType.java`.

### Expected

```
mobile_lib_domain_punch --references--> mobile_lib_domain_punch_punchtype
```

(label `PunchType`, defined in the same Dart file at L3), or a dangling stub if same-language cross-file resolution is unavailable. It should never bind to `PunchType.java`.

## Where it happens

- `extract()` emits target `punchtype` (dangling stub) — correct.
- `build.py::_alias_index` (around L1142–1218, applied at L1793) registers `_old_file_stems(rel)` for every node with a `source_file`. For `backend/.../PunchType.java` those forms are `attendance_punchtype` and the bare `punchtype`. The Dart endpoint `punchtype` matches the bare alias; the alias has exactly one claimant, so the `norm_to_id.setdefault(...)` commit binds it to the Java file node.
- The uniqueness rule protects against ambiguity *between corpus files*, but not against a same-named node in a different language. The comment at L1767–1777 already flags "silent cross-file (and cross-language) merge" as the hazard that uniqueness is meant to prevent — it does not prevent this case, because the correctly-named same-language node is not a claimant of the alias.

## Relationship to existing issues

- #1749 described this exact family (unresolved imports/references binding by name across language boundaries) and suggested gating both `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes` and the build alias index on language compatibility. It is closed as completed, but the alias branch here still has no language gate in 0.9.100.
- #2343 covers the type/class branches of `_absorb_stubs` in `extract.py`. This report is the separate build-layer alias path, so it is not addressed by that fix either.

## Impact (real repo: 1006 nodes / 1513 edges)

- This is the **only** `dart -> java` edge among all 1513 edges (scanned across dart/java/ts/kotlin).
- It is an articulation edge: removing the `PunchType` node splits the main connected component `771 -> 232 + 536`, where the 232-node side is the entire Flutter app lobe.
- Betweenness inflated: `PunchType` 0.2495, `punch.dart` 0.2532, `AttendancePunch` 0.2493, `PunchType.java` 0.2468 — all on this one chain. graphify's own GRAPH_REPORT surfaced it as a top God Node and "surprising connection".
- Mobile and backend couple over HTTP, never by import; the graph should not connect them here.

## Suggested fix

Gate alias resolution on language/extension compatibility at the edge-resolution site (where the edge's `source_file` is known), reusing the `_lang_family` helper already used in `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes`: when looking up an endpoint alias, skip candidates whose `source_file` language family differs from the edge source's family. Uniqueness is the wrong safety property when the correct answer is "none of the above" — the same conclusion as #1749.

An alternative narrow rule: only honor cross-language aliases for endpoints that are demonstrably stale pre-migration ids (they match a node's `_old_file_stems` form in the edge's own language), never for bare type names emitted as live references.

I can test a patch against the repro above if useful.

title: Write graph.json one element per line (deterministic, line-friendly)
body:
## Summary

`graphify update` writes `graphify-out/graph.json` as compact JSON on a single line. In medium-sized code repositories that line is several MB long. When the graph is committed to the repository (a common workflow so that agents and teammates get the graph without regenerating it), this layout causes two practical problems:

1. **Line-oriented tooling breaks or degrades.** Tools that scan staged files in fixed-size windows split on whitespace. In code-heavy repos (for example Go), node ids and paths contain no spaces, so windows of 100 KB or more without any whitespace are common. We hit a pre-commit secret scanner that loops forever on such a file and blocks `git commit`.
2. **Diffs are unreadable.** Every refresh rewrites one huge line, so code review shows the whole file as changed and Git stores a full new blob instead of small line deltas.

## Proposal

Add an option (or make it the default for `graph.json`) to write the graph deterministically with one element per line:

- object keys in a stable order;
- `nodes` sorted by `id`, `links` sorted by `(source, target, relation)`;
- one node or link per line, plus a trailing newline;
- content-equal to today's JSON (`json.loads` gives the same object), so readers do not change.

In our measurements across 20 repositories this grows the file by only about 0.3% (one newline per element), the longest line drops to about 1.2 KB, and refresh diffs show only the nodes that changed.

## Workaround we use today

We post-process the file after `graphify update`:

```python
import json

def normalize_graph(path: str) -> None:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        graph = json.load(f)
    nodes = sorted(graph.get("nodes", []), key=lambda n: str(n.get("id")))
    links = sorted(graph.get("links", []), key=lambda l: (str(l.get("source")), str(l.get("target")), str(l.get("relation"))))
    rest = {k: v for k, v in graph.items() if k not in ("nodes", "links")}
    dump = lambda o: json.dumps(o, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    lines = ["{"]
    for k in sorted(rest):
        lines.append(f"{json.dumps(k)}:{dump(rest[k])},")
    lines.append('"nodes":[')
    lines += [dump(n) + ("," if i < len(nodes) - 1 else "") for i, n in enumerate(nodes)]
    lines.append('],"links":[')
    lines += [dump(l) + ("," if i < len(links) - 1 else "") for i, l in enumerate(links)]
    lines.append("]}")
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
```

The post-commit hook installed by `graphify hook install` regenerates the single-line file, so the workaround has to be repeated after every update. Native support in the writer would remove that step.

Tested with graphifyy 0.9.92. Happy to open a PR if you agree with the approach.

title: [Bug]: interrupted FileSlice extraction marks an incomplete file as fully cached
body:
## What happened

An interrupted extraction can cache one successful `FileSlice` as the complete parent file.
A later semantic cache check then reports no uncached files, although later slices never completed.
This can silently omit content after the interruption.

Expected: a strict cache check must keep the parent file uncached until every required slice completes successfully.

## Environment and scope

- Reproduced twice with the installed `graphifyy==0.9.82` package, Python 3.13.11, macOS arm64, installed through `uv tool`.
- The example uses the native `extract_corpus_parallel` and `check_semantic_cache` functions.
- Only `extract_files_direct` is mocked. No model request, API key, provider response, or private source is required.
- The first call returns a complete result for its slice. The second call raises `KeyboardInterrupt`.
- This is an installed-package repro. I did not run the current upstream checkout or its full test suite.

## Steps to reproduce

Run this script with the Python interpreter that contains Graphify.

```python
import tempfile,json
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch
from importlib.metadata import version
from graphify import llm
from graphify.cache import check_semantic_cache
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
 root=Path(directory);p=root/'guide.md';p.write_text('# Early\nEarly fact.\n'+'filler '*6000+'\n# Tail\nTAIL_ASSERTION must remain visible.\n');calls=[]
 def endpoint(files,**kwargs):
  calls.append(len(files))
  if len(calls)>1:raise KeyboardInterrupt()
  return {'nodes':[{'id':'early','label':'Early fact.','source_file':str(p),'source_location':'Early'}],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[],'input_tokens':1,'output_tokens':1,'finish_reason':'stop','model':'fixture'}
 try:
  with patch.object(llm,'extract_files_direct',endpoint):llm.extract_corpus_parallel([p],backend='openai',root=root,cache_root=root/'out',max_concurrency=1,token_budget=1,max_retry_depth=0)
 except KeyboardInterrupt:pass
 nodes,edges,hyp,miss=check_semantic_cache([str(p)],root=root,cache_root=root/'out',prompt=llm._extraction_system())
 entries=list((root/'out/graphify-out/cache/semantic').rglob('*.json'));data=json.loads(entries[0].read_text()) if entries else {}
 print(json.dumps({'version':version('graphifyy'),'attempted_chunks':len(calls),'successful_chunks':1,'cache_entries':len(entries),'partial_flag':data.get('partial',False),'warm_uncached_files':len(miss),'warm_nodes':len(nodes),'tail_present':any('TAIL_ASSERTION' in str(n) for n in nodes)}))
```

## Actual output

```json
{"version": "0.9.82", "attempted_chunks": 2, "successful_chunks": 1, "cache_entries": 1, "partial_flag": false, "warm_uncached_files": 0, "warm_nodes": 1, "tail_present": false}
```

The displayed `successful_chunks: 1` value is a fixture constant, not a separate measured counter.
This repro exercises only the serial branch (`max_concurrency=1`).

The cache contains one entry with `partial_flag: false`.
`warm_uncached_files: 0` means the native checker treats the entire file as cached.
The tail assertion is absent because extraction stopped before its slice completed.

## Source investigation

The current `v8` source at commit `32e5efe935e6844ef39a5e33409e4efe848f2172` appears to retain the relevant mechanism.
This is source inspection, not a runtime reproduction on that commit.

[`_checkpoint_chunk`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/32e5efe935e6844ef39a5e33409e4efe848f2172/graphify/llm.py#L2867-L2910) maps each slice to its parent path with `unit_path`.
It calls `save_semantic_cache` with `merge_existing=True`.
Its partial set comes from `_partial_source_files(result)`, which does not establish completion of sibling slices.
A successful individual slice can therefore produce an authoritative entry for an incomplete file.

A possible fix is to track completion per parent file and keep interim checkpoints partial.
Any fix also needs native API finalization and final-save protection when one required slice fails.
Existing entries from interrupted runs may need targeted invalidation because their metadata can falsely claim completeness.
These are proposed fix requirements. No patch is included.

## Related issues checked

- #1870 fixed a `FileSlice.rel` access error that prevented checkpoints. Here the checkpoint succeeds but incorrectly represents file completeness.
- #4547 concerns empty-file acknowledgements and omitted sources. This repro returns a nonempty successful slice before interruption.
- #4814 concerns stale partial-state instructions. This repro demonstrates a native semantic cache entry that lacks the partial marker.

I checked the README Troubleshooting section and its linked documentation before reporting this issue.

title: fix(rust): resolve module-qualified calls (revives #2135)
body:
Revives #2135 by @okinoxis, rebased onto current v8 with authorship kept, plus review follow-ups.

## Problem
A Rust call written with a module path (`crate::formatter::format_line()`, `formatter::format_line()`, `super::formatter::format_line()`) never became a `calls` edge, so `explain` showed 0 callers. A user reported this on a 100k-line Rust repo, and I reproduced it on v8 32e5efe9.

## Change
- **okinoxis's commit (from #2135):** enqueue scoped calls with their qualifier. Resolve one only when the qualifier matches the candidate's file path right to left and exactly one candidate survives. This addresses both false positives from the July review (`std::fs::read` vs a local `fs.rs`, and Rust `b::helper()` vs Python `b.py`), with 11 tests. Rebase note: v8 now has its own `use_roots` (sets, aware of crate-local `mod`s), so I dropped the PR's copy and ported its scoped-call step onto v8's.
- **Follow-ups:**
  - a candidate must be in the caller's crate (nearest `Cargo.toml`, else the directory above `src`), so `crate::util::f()` can't reach another workspace crate;
  - `crate::b::helper()` in `a.rs` no longer binds to `a.rs`'s own `helper`. A module-path call binds in-file only for `self::f()` or an inline `mod m { }`;
  - `_`-prefixed module names are accepted;
  - methods are skipped as candidates. Its test passes with or without the guard, so treat it as protection against regressions.

## Evidence
- Repro crate: 0 → 3 caller edges for the three path forms. Two builds give identical graphs.
- 15 tests in `tests/test_rust_scoped_call_resolution.py`. The new ones fail with the follow-up reverted, except the method guard.
- Full suite: 9006 passed. The 14 failures also fail on plain v8 on this Windows machine (`test_ext_tagged_id_clash`, `test_code_only_update_all_hosts[devin/aider]`, the memoization getcwd tests, and a flaky `test_partial_extraction_warning`). Ruff is clean, and the pyright count is unchanged from v8.
- I didn't bump the AST cache schema, so it can go into the next batch bump.

Not covered: `m::f()` inside a macro (see the macro-argument PR). The scoped resolution is also still duplicated across `extract.py` and `symbol_resolution.py`. That was already the case in #2135, and a shared edge builder would be a follow-up.

Supersedes #2135.

title: fix(rust): link calls written inside macro arguments
body:
## Problem
Tree-sitter keeps a Rust macro's arguments as raw tokens, so `println!("{}", f(x))`, `assert_eq!(f(), 1)` and `vec![f()]` produced no edge. A function used only inside formatting or assert macros showed no callers.

## Change
Scan for `name(...)` in the token tree of the std and `log` macros whose arguments are plain expressions (`println!`, `format!`, `assert*!`, `vec!`, `dbg!`, `panic!`, `write!`, `info!`, and so on):
- skip names after `.`, `::`, `#` or `$`, names followed by `!`, UpperCamelCase constructors, and names on the existing builtin and trait-method blocklists;
- an in-file match is **INFERRED 0.85**, since it's a token pattern rather than a parsed call. Anything else goes to the cross-file pass as a bare call;
- macro edges are added after the bodies are walked, so a real parsed call to the same target keeps its EXTRACTED edge;
- DSL macros (`table!`, `quote!`, `html!`) are not scanned, and `macro_rules!` bodies are untouched.

## Evidence
- 9 tests in `tests/test_rust_macro_argument_calls.py`. The positive cases, the dedupe case and the DSL case fail without the fix.
- Repro crate: `in_macro() -> via_macro_target()` now appears across files. Two builds give identical graphs.
- Full suite: 9000 passed. The 14 failures are the same ones plain v8 has on this machine. Ruff and pyright are clean.
- I didn't bump the AST cache schema, so it can go into the batch bump.

title: fix(cpp): bind x.m() by the receiver's type (builds on #3240)
body:
Builds on #3240 by @abhay-codes07, cherry-picked with authorship kept (it applies cleanly to v8), and fixes the case #3240 doesn't fix on its own.

## Problem
In C++, `void render(Base* b) { b->draw(); }` in a file that defines `Derived::draw` produced an **EXTRACTED** edge to `Derived::draw`, which is the method the static type rules out, and no edge to `Base::draw`. A member call with a variable receiver fell through to the file-wide bare-name map. This came up in a public C++ firmware benchmark that reported calls into overridden functions weren't linked.

## Change
1. **#3240:** type receivers from parameters and class fields.
2. Defer `x.m()` / `x->m()` to `_resolve_cpp_member_calls`, as JS/TS have done since #4598, **but only when the receiver is typed**. Untyped receivers (`auto`, smart pointers, range-for) keep their v8 in-file binding, so they don't lose edges. `this->m()` and `Foo::m()` are unchanged.
3. Each function's receivers are now typed from its own locals and parameters. The file table was first-write-wins, so `Response r` in one function retyped `Request& r` in another. A name typed differently in two places, or a field typed differently in two classes, is dropped as ambiguous instead of guessed.

`b->draw()` now reaches `Base::draw` (INFERRED).

## Evidence
- `tests/test_cpp_member_call_by_receiver_type.py`: 5 tests. The base-pointer, cross-function retype and `auto` cases each fail without the commit that fixes them.
- 495 C/C++ tests pass. Full suite: 9002 passed, with the same 14 failures plain v8 has on this machine. Ruff is clean, and the pyright count is unchanged from v8.

Not included: an edge from `Derived::draw` to the `Base::draw` it overrides. The schema has no such relation today, so adding one is a design decision.

title: fix(llm): cache a sliced file only once every slice has succeeded (#4943)
body:
Fixes #4943.

## Problem
An oversized document is split into `FileSlice`s, and each slice's checkpoint was saved under the parent file with `merge_existing=True`. Nothing recorded which sibling slices were still pending, so after the first slice the parent had a complete-looking entry. An interrupted run then served the head of the file as the whole file, and `check_semantic_cache` reported 0 uncached. I reproduced this with the issue's script on v8 32e5efe9.

There's a second path to the same bug. When a slice **raises**, the other slices' nodes make the parent look covered, so the CLI's final save wrote it as complete.

## Change (`graphify/llm.py`)
- A sliced parent's results are held until its last slice returns, then written in one save. They're joined in chunk order, not completion order, so the entry is deterministic (#1632). Whole files are still checkpointed right away.
- A failed slice adds its parent to `_partial_files`, so the final save stamps it partial and the next run retries it.
- I didn't simply stamp interim checkpoints `partial`, because `partial` is sticky across merges and would leave the file uncached forever.

## Evidence
- Issue script: `warm_uncached_files` goes from 0 to 1.
- `tests/test_slice_checkpoint_completeness.py`: 5 tests. The interrupt, failed-slice and ordering tests fail without the fix.
- Full suite: 8996 passed, with the same 14 failures plain v8 has on this machine. Ruff is clean, and the pyright count is unchanged from v8.

Not covered: entries already written by earlier interrupted runs still look complete. A semantic-cache prompt or schema bump would invalidate them, and that's your call.

title: fix(llm): stamp sliced-file checkpoints partial when some slices never complete
body:
## What does this PR do?

An oversized splittable file is dispatched as several `FileSlice` chunks (`expand_oversized_files` → per-chunk `_checkpoint_chunk` saves). If the run is interrupted before every slice's chunk returns (crash, kill, or a `KeyboardInterrupt`-style abort), the checkpoint written by the slices that *did* finish is stamped clean, so the parent file sits in the semantic cache looking complete. `check_semantic_cache` then reports zero uncached files and the content that was never extracted (everything past the completed slice) is silently omitted from every later graph.

Fixes #4943. `_checkpoint_chunk` now stamps a sliced file `partial: True` whenever this chunk does not contain all of the file's slices (`FileSlice.index`/`total`), merged with the existing `_partial_source_files` truncation set. Interrupted runs leave a partial entry that `load_cached`/`check_semantic_cache` treat as a miss, so the whole file re-dispatches next run. A fully completed run is unaffected: checkpoints stay conservative (same contract an LLM-truncated slice already has), and the final full save of a completed run — the non-merge `save_semantic_cache` call the CLI makes after the corpus run — overwrites the stamp with a clean complete entry.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Tests or CI

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: a semantic cache entry for a file may only be served as complete when every slice of that file completed; otherwise the entry must carry `partial: True`.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary (one call site, no schema or cache-format change — the `partial` flag machinery already existed for truncated responses).
- [x] Added a **regression test** (`test_interrupted_multi_slice_checkpoint_is_partial_and_missed_on_reload`); verified it fails with `AssertionError` on the pre-fix `llm.py` and passes with the fix.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly (see below).

## How was this tested?

Reproduced #4943's report first on the plain `v8` checkout with the issue's mock harness (system Python 3.13-compatible interpreter, `extract_files_direct` patched; one slice succeeds, the second raises `KeyboardInterrupt`):

```text
before fix: {"attempted_chunks": 2, "cache_entries": 1, "partial_flag": false, "warm_uncached_files": 0, "tail_present": false}
after fix:  {"attempted_chunks": 2, "cache_entries": 1, "partial_flag": true,  "warm_uncached_files": 1, "tail_present": false}
```

Then:

1. New regression test `test_interrupted_multi_slice_checkpoint_is_partial_and_missed_on_reload` (in `tests/test_chunking.py`): passes with the fix, `AssertionError` without it.
2. Existing checkpoint tests re-run after the change and still pass: `test_checkpoint_scopes_cache_writes_to_chunk_files`, `test_truncated_chunk_is_cached_partial_and_missed_on_reload` (driven individually, since the full pytest suite is not runnable in my environment — the only stubbed import was `tree_sitter`, which these paths do not execute; the mocked-endpoint paths above are unaffected by it).
3. Success-path guard (no regression for completed runs): a two-slice corpus where every chunk succeeds, followed by the CLI's final full save, leaves a clean non-partial entry that `check_semantic_cache` serves warm, including the tail-section nodes.

Limitations: the partial stamp makes a killed-after-chunks-but-before-final-save run re-extract the sliced files next run — conservative by design, same recovery cost a truncated-response slice already incurs. No cache-format change, so old entries remain readable.

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [ ] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. — N/A: `graphify/llm.py`'s `_checkpoint_chunk` is runtime code, not a skillgen source fragment (verified the generated `skill-*.md` artifacts do not embed this region), so no artifact regeneration is needed.
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages (`Co-authored-by` trailer, per the repo's authorship convention).

title: fix(build): gate the alias index on language family
body:
Fixes #4941.

## Bug

`extract()` correctly leaves an unresolved Dart type reference as a dangling stub (`punchtype`), but `build_from_json()` then resolves that endpoint through `_alias_index()` to an unrelated **Java file node**. `_alias_index` registers every node's old-stem id forms as aliases (`#1504` migration-compat) and commits an alias only when exactly one node claims it — but the uniqueness check protects against two same-stem files racing within one language, never against a same-named node whose real identity is in another language entirely. On a real repo this produced the only `dart -> java` edge among 1513 edges, an articulation edge that split the graph's main connected component and dominated betweenness.

Reported in #4941 with a precise repro, root-cause analysis down to the exact lines, and a suggested fix (gate on language family via the existing `_lang_family` helper, reusing the pattern already used by `_rewire_unique_stub_nodes`). I independently reproduced it and verified the fix against the exact repro. No open or closed PR touches `_alias_index`'s commit logic with a language gate — the PR that introduced `_alias_index` (#4676, merged) added no such gate.

## Fix

Kept the alias index separate from the main normalized-id map (`norm_to_id`) instead of merging it in directly. Added `_alias_lang_compatible(edge_source_file, alias_source_file)`, consulted only when an endpoint falls back to the alias layer: it skips the alias candidate when the edge's own file and the candidate's file are both in a known, *different* language family (via `_lang_family`, imported locally to avoid a circular import with `extract.py`). It's permissive whenever either side's family is unknown, so a legitimate same-language or provenance-less alias still resolves exactly as before — this changes no existing alias-resolution test.

Applied at both places the alias index is consulted: `build_from_json` (the clustered path) and `finalize_raw_graph_endpoints` (the raw `--no-cluster` write path, per #4670), so they keep resolving endpoints identically.

## Tests

- `tests/test_build.py::test_build_from_json_unambiguous_old_stem_alias_still_needs_language_match` — the clustered path, using the exact Dart/Java shape from the issue.
- `tests/test_no_cluster_undeclared_endpoints.py::test_finalize_raw_graph_endpoints_rejects_a_cross_language_alias` — the raw `--no-cluster` path.

Both assert the dangling edge is never re-pointed at the cross-language file.

## Verification

- Reproduced the bug with the issue's own repro shape (relative paths from a CWD root, matching their exact invocation): confirmed pre-fix `build_from_json` produces the `dart -> java` edge; post-fix it does not.
- Confirmed both new tests fail against the unmodified `build.py` (restored byte-identical afterward) and pass against the fix.
- Checked every existing alias test in `tests/test_build.py` and `tests/test_no_cluster_undeclared_endpoints.py` (same-language unambiguous/ambiguous old-stem cases, framework-header imports): none sets a cross-language `source_file` pairing, so the new gate changes no existing outcome.
- Full suite: `2 failed, 9313 passed, 83 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 2 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py` and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change.
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: fix(watch): preserve semantic evidence across AST id collisions
body:
## Problem
An AST-only update silently discards saved cross-file semantic evidence when a freshly extracted AST node takes its id. Reproduced while auditing tracked semantic graphs, including a CodeRabbit concept in Leveret.

## Change
- Retain sourced semantic evidence during AST reconciliation and namespace cross-file collisions through the existing reference alias helper.
- Scope preservation to AST updates; full-build deduplication keeps its existing definer rules, and fresh AST facts remain authoritative for same-source ids.
- Preserve authored AST links, semantic links, hyperedges, confidence, and opaque document-version attributes.
- Allocate a free alias when the usual citing-file namespace is occupied. Cover clustered and --no-cluster updates.

Only graph.json carries portable provenance. No extraction cache is tracked, and no cache-based freshness requirement or commit/push hook policy is introduced.

## Verification
- Initial regression failed in both output modes: https://github.com/andrebrait/integration-ci/actions/runs/41446031700
- Review counterexamples failed before correction: https://github.com/andrebrait/integration-ci/actions/runs/41448006199
- Expanded integration gate including existing watch and dedup suites: **533 passed, 3 skipped**: https://github.com/andrebrait/integration-ci/actions/runs/41449467347
- A real installed-CLI smoke preserved a colliding semantic node and document-version attribute through freshness refresh and commit, kept the AST identity, avoided an occupied alias, and retrieved the semantic motivates relationship. Only graph.json was staged among graph outputs.
- Condensed adversarial review findings resolved and independently re-probed. Deployed through the integration script at pfBlockerNG/graphify@bfb3e31f6540d84266a1661560501389dc9b9984 with leiden and gdscript extras.

Full upstream CI was not run on the fork because its Actions are disabled. No upstream bot review requests were posted because the authenticated account has read-only permission in the base repository.

title: fix(cpp): bind alias references by exact spelling, keep a salted alias's contains edge
body:
## What does this PR do?

Two follow-ups to the declaration-id registry (#4854, #4904/#4908). Both show up on C++ aliases on today's v8.

**1. A type reference to an alias binds to a function whose name differs only in case.**

```cpp
using Session = int;            // or: typedef int Session;
void session() {}
struct Holder { Session s; };   // v8: Holder --references--> session()
```

Since #4904, `Session` and `session()` are two nodes. But `DeclIdRegistry.lookup` normalizes the name and walks the kinds in a fixed order (`type`, `fn`, `var`, `ns`, `alias`), so the `fn` wins and `Session s;` lands on `session()`. `lookup` now first looks across the requested kinds for the one declaration spelled exactly like the reference, and returns it. When there is no such declaration, or more than one, the kind order decides, as before.

Registering C++ aliases as `type` instead doesn't work. `resolve` lets declarations of the same kind share an id, so an alias would merge with a same-kind case twin: doctest's `using string = basic_string<...>` and `class String` collapsed into one node when I tried it.

**2. An alias whose id spells its file's id gets no `contains` edge.** In `a.cpp`, `using cpp = int;` makes `_make_id("a", "cpp")`, which is the file's own id, so the registry salts the alias's id (#4854). The alias site decided whether to emit `contains` by checking the unsalted id against `seen_ids` before the call. It found the file node there, so the edge was skipped and the alias node was left without a parent. The site now checks `seen_ids` after `decl_node_fn`, as the Swift alias site in #4639 does.

Changes:
- `graphify/ids.py`: `lookup` prefers the exact spelling. `resolve` also records the spelling of a salted id, so a salted declaration can be found by its exact spelling too.
- `graphify/extractors/engine.py`: the C++ alias site in `_cpp_extra_walk`. If no registry is passed, it now mints the node itself, like the Swift site. No caller takes that path today.
- `graphify/cache.py`: AST cache schema 34 → 35, so cached extractions re-run.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: when exactly one declaration in the file is spelled like the reference, the reference binds to it; normalization and kind order don't override that. When none or several are, behavior is unchanged.

- **Where the lookup change reaches:** `DeclIdRegistry.lookup` is the per-file lookup used by `ensure_named_node`, the PHP `Scope::MEMBER` path and the JS/TS walk, so every language on the generic engine. The Go, Rust and Julia extractors don't call it. A result changes only when exactly one declaration is spelled like the reference and the kind order would pick another one, or none (when an earlier kind held two ids).
- **Persisted state invalidated:** AST cache schema bump, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts code files once.
- **Conflict note:** my open variadic (#4638), Swift (#4639) and Dart (#4641) PRs also bump the schema 34 → 35. Whichever merges later needs a one-line rebase.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Limitation: when two declarations are spelled exactly like the reference (the same name in two C++ namespaces of one file), the lookup still falls back to the kind order, as on v8.

## How was this tested?

- `tests/test_cpp_type_alias.py`: 3 new tests. `Session s;` lands on the alias for both the `using` and the `typedef` form, and `using cpp = int;` in `a.cpp` is contained by its file and referenced by a field. All 3 fail on v8 (32e5efe9); the 9 existing tests still pass.
- **Real repos, full-graph diff v8 → this branch** (every edge keyed by its source, relation, site and target):

title: fix(guard): don't refuse a write when dedup folded a saved node into a twin (#4940)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4940.

The #479 write guard in `to_json` calls a saved node lost when its id is missing from the new graph. Entity dedup also removes ids. It folds a re-extracted node into a twin, and the content lives on under the twin's id. So an `--update` that re-extracted `GLOSSARY.md` alone was refused, and `graph.json` stayed stale. A full rebuild that merged the same twins was refused the same way.

This change has dedup report which ids it merged away, carries that map to `to_json`, and lets the guard count a merged id as present when its survivor is in the new graph:

```diff
  build_merge
    build
-     deduplicate_entities
+     deduplicate_entities(remap_out=remap)
+     G.graph["_dedup_remap"] = remap
  to_json
+   dedup_remap = take_dedup_remap(G)      # also keeps it out of graph.json
    _lost_saved_semantic_nodes(saved, new)
+     saved id in remap and survivor in new graph -> not lost
    node-count check
+     allowance: N merged ids = N-1 if the survivor is new, N if it is saved
```

```text
saved:  claude_the_nudge   glossary_the_nudge
fresh:                     glossary_the_nudge   (GLOSSARY.md alone)
dedup:  glossary_the_nudge -> claude_the_nudge
guard:  before  "glossary_the_nudge missing"          -> refuse
        after   survivor claude_the_nudge is present  -> write
```

A survivor that is itself gone excuses nothing. A real loss next to a merge is still refused, and only that id is named.

The node-count check needed the same allowance. When two saved ids merge into one survivor that is new this run, the count drops by one with nothing lost, and the id check alone still refused it.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Evidence

**Before:** on `upstream/v8` (`32e5efe9`), the issue's scenario.

```text
[graphify] Deduplicated 2 node(s) (2 exact).
[graphify] WARNING: Refusing to overwrite — saved semantic node(s) are missing from the new graph: glossary_first_contact, glossary_the_nudge.
graph written: False
```

```text
tests/test_shrink_guard_dedup_merge_4940.py
9 failed, 8 passed
```

**After:**

```text
graph written: True, one node per concept,
an edge that pointed at the merged id now points at the survivor

tests/test_shrink_guard_dedup_merge_4940.py
17 passed

full suite
9405 passed, 18 skipped, 1 xfailed in 1689.87s
```

The full suite ran serially with `PYTHONPATH=/var/tmp/wt-4940-fix`, so subprocess CLI tests imported this worktree and not the installed package.

## Verification & Invariants

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

The invariant: the guard may refuse a write, but only when content is gone, never because an id was merged into a twin that is still there.

The tests assert on what reaches `graph.json` and on whether `to_json` wrote, so they hold for any fix of this bug. They pin:

- Re-extracting a doc alone writes when dedup folds it into the untouched twins.
- An edge to the merged-away id is kept and rewired.
- Same-file exact duplicates do not block the write.
- Two saved ids folded into one new survivor write.
- The updated graph has one node per concept.
- A full rebuild that merges the same twins writes.
- A real loss next to a merge is refused and only that id is named.
- A survivor that is itself gone excuses nothing.
- A saved node that vanished, and a re-extracted node dropped after the merge, are still refused. These two pass before and after.
- The map is never written into `graph.json`.

I tried two other fixes against the same scenarios. Comparing against the pre-dedup node set turns the guard off, because `build_merge`'s input already holds every saved node. Keeping dedup from dropping ids that `graph.json` holds leaves the twins unmerged, and the next full rebuild hits the same refusal.

Known limitations:

- `watch._check_shrink` has its own copy of the guard. It works on dicts and has no graph to carry the map, so a `graphify update` that goes through it can still refuse a merge. That needs a separate change.
- The extract CLI keeps its own dedup-shrink policy (`--allow-dedup-shrink`, #3774). It is not touched.
- I did not trace how the reporter's graph came to hold both twins. The refusal reproduces with a graph that does.
- No cache schema bump and no graph format change.

## How was this tested?

```text
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_shrink_guard_dedup_merge_4940.py -q
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt4940-full
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/build.py graphify/dedup.py graphify/export.py tests/test_shrink_guard_dedup_merge_4940.py
```

Branch `fix/4940-shrink-guard-dedup-merge` is based on `upstream/v8` (`32e5efe9`). It has four commits:

```text
54423fc2 test(guard): pin that the #479 write guard still refuses a real loss (#4940)
89f34e14 feat(dedup): report which ids deduplicate_entities merged away (#4940)
268513af feat(build): carry the dedup merge map on the built graph (#4940)
4c3b38ba fix(guard): a saved node dedup folded into a twin is not a lost node (#4940)
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way.

The default path is unchanged when dedup merges nothing. No cache schema bump and no graph format change. Reverting restores the old guard.

**Blast Radius:** Write guard.

Every graph written through `to_json` passes this guard, so a mistake here either blocks a good write or lets a bad one through. The guard excuses an id only when its survivor is in the new graph, and the control tests pin the refusals. After merge, a graph that dedup has already shrunk by merging twins is written instead of refused, so an `--update` that was stuck on a stale `graph.json` now lands. Extraction, ignore rules and secret filtering are unchanged.
