title: fix(build): excuse an exact duplicate dedup fold from the shrink guard
body:
Fixes #4940.

## Bug

During an incremental semantic `--update`, `build_merge` (via `build`) can replace a re-extracted file's nodes and then run `deduplicate_entities`'s exact-duplicate pass, which collapses a same-label, same-file near-duplicate pair onto one survivor id. When the *saved* node's id is the one folded away (not the survivor), `to_json`'s `#479` shrink guard — specifically `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes` — has no way to know the concept actually survived under a different id. It reports the saved id as missing and refuses the write outright, even though nothing was lost. Retrying re-extracts the same unchanged documents and refuses identically.

The accounting for this already half-exists: `build()` computes `_dedup_collapsed` (the total node-count drop from dedup) and stashes it on `G.graph`, and `to_json` calls `take_shrink_accounting(G)` to pop it — but the call site in `export.py` discards the return value entirely (confirmed: `take_shrink_accounting` has exactly one other caller in the whole codebase, `cli.py`, and neither ever consumes the dict needed to exclude a *specific* id). The count was never wired into the `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes` check that actually produces the refusal.

No existing issue or PR covers this; found via the issue tracker (#4940, well-documented with an exact repro shape). Checked PR #3623 (open, "excuse dedup-explained node drops from the #479 shrink guard") — it addresses a *different* mechanism (`build_from_json`'s #1145 ghost-merge count, `_ghost_dedup_count`), not `deduplicate_entities`'s exact-duplicate `remap`. No overlap.

## Fix

- `dedup.py`: `deduplicate_entities` gains an optional `node_remap: dict[str, str] | None` out-param, filled in place with every merged id's survivor id — mirroring the existing `hyperedges` out-param precedent exactly ("Optional and mutating rather than returned so existing two-tuple callers are unaffected").
- `build.py`: `build()` passes a fresh dict as `node_remap=` and stashes it on `G.graph["_dedup_node_remap"]` next to the existing `_dedup_collapsed`. `take_shrink_accounting` now pops and returns it too (3-tuple; its one other caller, `cli.py`, is updated to match). `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes` gains a `dedup_remap` parameter: a saved id whose remap target is present in the new graph is excused (and recorded into `folded`, so downstream node-count math stays consistent), checked before the existing AST-twin/file-twin fold checks.
- `export.py`: `to_json` now captures the remap from `take_shrink_accounting` and passes it through to `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes`.
- `cli.py`: the extract CLI's own early `take_shrink_accounting(G)` call pops this map before `to_json` runs; when `to_json`'s own internal guard will still execute (`force=False`, the partial-extraction path), the map is put back onto `G.graph` first so `to_json` can retrieve it again.

Checked `watch.py`'s `_rebuild_code`/`_check_shrink` (the `--update` incremental path) separately — that path writes the raw merged extraction directly, never through `build_from_json`/`deduplicate_entities`, so this specific gap doesn't apply there.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_lost_saved_semantic_nodes.py`:
- `test_dedup_remap_target_present_is_not_lost` / `test_dedup_remap_target_absent_is_still_lost` — the `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes` unit-level behavior.
- `test_no_dedup_remap_given_is_unaffected` — control confirming the existing no-remap call shape (every other caller) is unchanged.
- `test_to_json_writes_after_exact_duplicate_dedup` — end-to-end with `build()` + `to_json()`, reproducing the issue's exact shape (a saved concept re-extracted alongside a same-label, same-file near-duplicate under a shorter id, collapsed by the exact-duplicate pass).

## Verification

- Reproduced the bug with the issue's exact message shape (`Deduplicated 1 node(s) (1 exact).` / `Refusing to overwrite — saved semantic node(s) are missing...` / `graph.json written: False`), then confirmed the fix resolves it (`graph.json written: True`).
- Confirmed all 4 new tests fail against the unmodified code (either a genuine assertion failure or the expected `TypeError` from the not-yet-existing `dedup_remap` parameter) and pass against the fix; restored byte-identical afterward.
- Ran `tests/test_dedup.py` (153), `tests/test_merge_sweeps_reextract_orphans.py` (the only other `take_shrink_accounting` caller, uses index-based unpacking so the 3-tuple doesn't break it), and the CLI-level shrink-guard tests (`test_incomplete_build_guard.py`, `test_hollow_chunks_arm_shrink_guard.py`, `test_dedup_shrink_refuses_force_write.py`) — all pass.
- Full suite: `3 failed, 9314 passed, 83 skipped, 1 xfailed` — the 3 failures are the pre-existing flakes in `test_erlang_extractor.py`, `test_r_extractor.py`, and the skill backtick test, unrelated to this change. (An earlier run under host memory pressure showed spurious unrelated failures — a clean rerun after the pressure cleared confirmed this baseline.)
- `python3 -m tools.skillgen --check`: `check OK: 134 artifact(s) match committed output and expected/.`

title: docs(readme): hook install already covers git pull
body: The README told people to run `graphify update .` by hand after `git pull` and pointed to a "Recommended workflow" section that no longer exists. `graphify hook install` sets up post-merge and post-rewrite hooks next to post-commit and post-checkout (see `hooks.py`), so a pull, whether it merges or rebases, already rebuilds the graph. This changes that one comment in the README and in the translated READMEs, where the line was still in English.

title: [Bug]: build_merge(dedup=False) refuses a no-op merge: #479 guard counts intentional ghost merges (#1145, #3344) as drops
body:
### What happened?

On 0.9.100, `build_merge(..., dedup=False)` raises the #479 `ValueError` on existing graphs even when the new chunk is empty, so nothing was re-extracted or pruned.

The nodes it reports as dropped are not lost by accident. They are removed by the intentional ghost-merge passes in `build_from_json`: #1145 (same `source_file` and label) and #3344 (a document node whose label names a file). The guard in `build_merge` only excuses the #1799 doc-twin case, so it counts these merges as unexplained drops.

The result is that a graph containing such twins can't be updated through `build_merge(dedup=False)` at all. This is a different case from #4019, whose reproducer now passes for me (5 -> 5).

Two things make this confusing:

- `build_from_json(..., dedup=False)` on the first case below keeps both nodes (2 -> 2), while `build_merge(..., dedup=False)` merges them. From reading the code, I think nodes loaded from disk get classified as AST by shape, which would skip the `not dedup` check at the top of Pass 2. I haven't confirmed that.
- The message suggests passing `prune_sources`, but no source was meant to be removed here.

### Steps to reproduce

```python
import json
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from graphify.build import build_merge

EMPTY = {"nodes": [], "edges": [], "hyperedges": [], "input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0}


def node(id_, label, source_file, loc):
    return {"id": id_, "label": label, "file_type": "code", "source_file": source_file, "source_location": loc}


CASES = {
    "same file, same label (#1145 path)": [
        node("src_client", "client.py", "src/client.py", "L1"),
        node("client_py", "client.py", "src/client.py", None),
    ],
    "doc mentions the file by name (#3344 path)": [
        node("src_client", "client.py", "src/client.py", "L1"),
        node("plan_client", "src/client.py", "docs/plan.md", None),
    ],
}

for name, nodes in CASES.items():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
        graph = Path(t) / "graph.json"
        graph.write_text(json.dumps({"directed": False, "multigraph": False, "graph": {}, "nodes": nodes, "links": []}), encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            G = build_merge([dict(EMPTY)], graph_path=str(graph), dedup=False)
            print(f"{name}: 2 -> {G.number_of_nodes()}")
        except ValueError as ex:
            print(f"{name}: ValueError: {ex}")
```

### Error output or graph output

0.9.100:

```
same file, same label (#1145 path): ValueError: graphify: build_merge would drop 1 node(s) from sources that were neither re-extracted nor pruned this run (e.g. 'src_client_py'); graph would go 2 → 1 nodes. Pass prune_sources explicitly if you intend to remove them. (#479)
doc mentions the file by name (#3344 path): ValueError: graphify: build_merge would drop 1 node(s) from sources that were neither re-extracted nor pruned this run (e.g. 'docs_plan_client'); graph would go 2 → 1 nodes. Pass prune_sources explicitly if you intend to remove them. (#479)
```

0.8.31:

```
same file, same label (#1145 path): 2 -> 2
doc mentions the file by name (#3344 path): 2 -> 2
```

### Graphify version

0.9.100 (compared with 0.8.31)

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Python Version

3.14.3

### Installation Method

pip, in an isolated venv

### Additional context

Impact on real graphs: I ran the same empty-chunk merge on copies of 9 real graphs built with 0.8.31. All 9 pass on 0.8.31 with no IDs lost. On 0.9.100, 6 of the 9 are refused:

| Nodes on disk | Node count in the refusal message |
|---:|---:|
| 6809 | 6614 |
| 4025 | 3865 |
| 935 | 927 |
| 339 | 330 |
| 54 | 49 |
| 29 | 25 |

Removing the nodes that match these two patterns before merging lets 3 of the 6 pass. The other three still report 1, 21 and 9 nodes. I haven't reduced those, so there may be a third path. My filter only approximates the passes, so it may also just be missing some of them.

Re-keying the graph first with `build_from_json` + `to_json(force=True)` doesn't help: `build_merge` still refuses the result.

The guard itself is doing something useful, since it stops the write and nothing is lost. The problem is that there's no way through. Would you prefer that `dedup=False` also skips these two passes for nodes loaded from disk, or that the guard excuses them as it does for #1799? Either would unblock us. I can test a patch against these graphs.

Note: I only tested the library calls above. I didn't run a full semantic re-extraction on 0.9.100.

title: fix(kotlin): resolve overloaded and init-block calls, drop unreachable inherited calls (#4935)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4935.

Three Kotlin/Java `calls` edges were missing or wrong, each for a different reason. They are three commits that do not depend on each other.

**1. Calls to overloaded methods.** Java gives every overload the same node id, because the id has no parameter types, so a class holds two `method` edges to one target. `_resolve_kotlin_member_calls` counted list entries, read the two as an ambiguous name, and wrote no edge. It now counts distinct ids.

```diff
-        candidates = [m for m in methods_by_type.get(type_nids[0], []) if label matches]
+        candidates = list(dict.fromkeys(m for m in methods_by_type.get(type_nids[0], []) if label matches))
         if len(candidates) != 1:
             continue
```

**2. Calls inside `init { }`.** The block parses as `anonymous_initializer`, which the engine never visited, so its calls had no source to attach to. It now goes to `initializer_nodes` the way a property initializer does (#2565), with the same owner: the enclosing class, or the file node for a nested one.

```diff
+        if kotlin and t == "anonymous_initializer":
+            initializer_nodes.append((parent_class_nid or file_nid, node))
+            return
         if kotlin and t == "property_declaration":
             ...
             initializer_nodes.append((owner_nid, child))
```

**3. Inherited external methods.** `class KotlinScreen : Activity()` calling `getString(1)` bound to the only `getString` in the corpus, `Prefs.getString`, a method of an unrelated class. A bare call can only name a member of the caller's own class, a superclass or an enclosing class, and `Activity` is outside the corpus, so nothing says where `getString` lives.

```text
bare call in a Kotlin/Java class
  walk the caller's class chain: own class, in-repo bases, enclosing classes
  does any base in the chain have no source file (declared outside the repo)?
    no  -> unchanged
    yes -> keep a candidate only if it
             is not a class member (a top-level function), or
             belongs to a class in the chain, or
             is imported by name (import pkg.Obj.member, import static)
```

This mirrors the unresolved-base guard the C# resolver already has.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Evidence

**Before:** the repro from the issue on `upstream/v8` (`8e6a6d21`).

```text
KotlinCaller.kt  .callSingle()  -> Logger.java  .single()      [EXTRACTED]
KotlinScreen.kt  .title()       -> Prefs.java   .getString()   [INFERRED]   (unrelated class)
missing: KotlinCaller.callOverloaded -> Logger.overloaded
missing: KotlinInit (init block)     -> Logger.single
```

```text
tests/test_kotlin_java_call_edges_4935.py
10 failed, 7 passed
```

**After:** the same repro.

```text
JavaCaller.java  .callOverloaded()  -> Logger.java  .overloaded()  [EXTRACTED]
JavaCaller.java  .callSingle()      -> Logger.java  .single()      [EXTRACTED]
KotlinCaller.kt  .callOverloaded()  -> Logger.java  .overloaded()  [EXTRACTED]
KotlinCaller.kt  .callSingle()      -> Logger.java  .single()      [EXTRACTED]
KotlinInit.kt    KotlinInit         -> Logger.java  .single()      [EXTRACTED]
(no edge to Prefs.getString)

tests/test_kotlin_java_call_edges_4935.py
17 passed

full suite
9580 passed, 18 skipped, 1 xfailed in 794.61s
```

The full suite ran serially with `PYTHONPATH` set to this worktree, so subprocess CLI tests imported this code and not the installed package.

## Verification & Invariants

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

The invariant: a call edge points at a method the caller can reach, and a resolver guard that counts candidates counts distinct methods, not list entries.

The commits go in this order, and each fix commit's tests fail without it:

- Controls first: a call to a non-overloaded Java method, a property-initializer call, two same-named classes staying ambiguous, and inherited in-repo members in Kotlin and Java. All pass before and after.
- Overloads: a Kotlin call to an overloaded Java method and to an overloaded Kotlin `object` method.
- `init`: the call attaches to the class, a call to an overloaded method, a class with both a property and an `init`, a nested class (checked against a property initializer of the same shape), and `object` and companion blocks.
- Inherited external methods: Kotlin and Java classes with an external base, an in-repo base that itself extends an external class, a top-level function and a member imported by name (Kotlin and Java), which must survive the guard.

Before choosing, I ran five variants (each fix alone, fixes 1 and 2 together, and two rules for fix 3) against 21 call shapes. The alternative for fix 3 dropped every class member the caller's chain does not contain, with no external-base condition. It also fixed a class with no base calling an unrelated `getString`, but it removed two edges that exist today (an object member imported by name, and a call inside `with(p) { getString() }`) and failed `test_jvm_interop_kotlin_call_to_java_still_resolves`. The external-base condition fixes the three shapes in the issue and breaks none of those.

Known limitations:

- A class with no external base that calls an unrelated class's method by bare name still gets the edge. It is not in the issue and not changed.
- A wildcard import (`import pkg.Obj.*`) of an object member, called bare from a class with an external base, loses its edge, because nothing in the graph records which names the wildcard brings in. A `with(p) { ... }` receiver lambda in such a class loses it too.
- Three older gaps remain: a bare call to an own member inside an initializer, calls in a secondary constructor body, and the `KotlinInit` owner for a companion `init`, which depends on layout.
- The reporter's 121 `getString` edges were not checked; I do not have their project.
- No cache schema bump. Fix 2 changes extractor output, so cached Kotlin results keep missing `init` edges until the usual maintainer bump.

## How was this tested?

```text
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_kotlin_java_call_edges_4935.py -q
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt4935-full2
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/extract.py graphify/extractors/engine.py tests/test_kotlin_java_call_edges_4935.py
```

Branch `fix/4935-kotlin-java-call-edges` is based on `upstream/v8` (`8e6a6d21`). It has four commits:

title: fix(build): don't treat intentional ghost folds as drops in build_merge (#4955)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4955.

`build_from_json` folds three kinds of duplicate on purpose: a semantic ghost into its AST twin (#1145), a document node whose label names a file into that file (#3344), and a bare method into its AST method (#3705). The #479 guard in `build_merge` excuses only the #1799 doc twin, so it read these folds as nodes lost from sources nobody re-extracted or pruned. A graph that holds such a twin could not be updated through `build_merge(dedup=False)`, even with an empty chunk, and the error pointed at `prune_sources`, which was not what the caller wanted.

`dedup=False` does not stop the fold. Nodes loaded from disk are stamped `_origin` by shape, which makes the AST twin the canonical node, and `test_ast_twin_remains_canonical_despite_semantic_location_drift` pins that an AST twin wins even with `dedup=False`. So the fold is intended, and the guard has to know about it.

This change reports the ghost folds on the `{merged-away id: survivor id}` channel entity dedup already uses (#4940), and lets the `build_merge` guard read it:

```diff
  build_from_json
    Pass 2 / Pass 2b / method branch -> _ghost_remap
+   G.graph["_dedup_remap"].update(_ghost_remap)
  build
-   G.graph["_dedup_remap"] = _dedup_remap
+   G.graph.setdefault("_dedup_remap", {}).update(_dedup_remap)
  build_merge  (#479 guard)
    _in_new_graph(saved node)
+     folded into a survivor that is still in G -> not lost
  to_json
    take_dedup_remap(G)      # already excuses it, and keeps it out of graph.json
```

```text
saved:   src_client (L1, ast)    client_py (no loc, semantic)    same file + label
fold:    client_py -> src_client
guard:   before  "client_py dropped"            -> ValueError
         after   survivor src_client is present -> write
```

A survivor that is itself gone excuses nothing.

`to_json` has its own guard. It re-derives the #1145 and #3344 folds from labels but never learned the #3705 method fold, so with only the `build_merge` change a saved method ghost would pass the merge and then be refused on write. Feeding it the real fold map fixes that, and removes the need for it to guess.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Evidence

**Before:** on `upstream/v8` (`8e6a6d21`), the issue's two cases with an empty chunk and `dedup=False`.

```text
same file, same label (#1145 path): ValueError: graphify: build_merge would drop 1 node(s) ... graph would go 2 → 1 nodes. (#479)
doc mentions the file by name (#3344 path): ValueError: graphify: build_merge would drop 1 node(s) ... graph would go 2 → 1 nodes. (#479)
```

An ordinary update raises too: a re-extracted file brings a new AST node while a saved semantic twin of it exists.

```text
tests/test_build_merge_ghost_fold_4955.py
8 failed, 6 passed
```

**After:**

```text
same file, same label: written, 1 node (src_client)
doc mentions the file: written, 1 node (src_client)
method ghost (.run() + run): build_merge ok, to_json writes
an edge that pointed at the ghost now points at the survivor

tests/test_build_merge_ghost_fold_4955.py
14 passed

full suite
9577 passed, 18 skipped, 1 xfailed in 503.72s
```

The full suite ran serially with `PYTHONPATH=/var/tmp/wt-4955-A`, so subprocess CLI tests imported this worktree and not the installed package.

## Verification & Invariants

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

The invariant: the guard may refuse a write, but only when content is gone, never because `build_from_json` folded a node into a twin that is still there.

The tests assert on what `build_merge` returns and what reaches `graph.json`, so they hold for any fix of this bug. They pin:

- The issue's two cases, a directory-qualified file label, and a method ghost no longer raise, and each leaves one node.
- An edge into a folded ghost is kept and lands on the survivor.
- An ordinary update with a new AST node next to a saved semantic twin folds and writes.
- `build_merge(dedup=False)` followed by `to_json` round-trips all three folds.
- A clean graph, semantic duplicates under `dedup=False`, a ghost with its own rationale (#4896), an ambiguous file label and `prune_sources` behave as before. These pass before and after.
- The fold map is never written into `graph.json`.

I tried a second fix against the same shapes: under `dedup=False`, skip Pass 2 and 2b for nodes loaded from disk. It leaves the nodes at 2 → 2, as 0.8.31 did, but it breaks `test_ast_twin_remains_canonical_despite_semantic_location_drift`, which pins the opposite on purpose. So I kept the fold and fixed the guard.

Known limitations:

- `dedup=False` still merges an AST twin with its ghost, as the existing test pins. Nothing here changes node counts, only whether the guard refuses.
- `watch._check_shrink` calls `_lost_saved_semantic_nodes` without the fold map. A `graphify update` through it could still refuse a #3705 method fold. I did not reproduce that, and it needs a separate change.
- The fold map is keyed on the id after semantic rekeying. A saved id that is rekeyed and then folded in the same run might not match. The rekey-only and fold-only shapes pass, and I did not build the combination.
- The reporter's three graphs that still fail after filtering these patterns are unexplained. I could not reproduce them without one of their graphs.
- No cache schema bump and no graph format change.

## How was this tested?

```text
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_build_merge_ghost_fold_4955.py -q
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp=/var/tmp/pt4955-full3
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check graphify/build.py tests/test_build_merge_ghost_fold_4955.py
```

Branch `fix/4955-merge-guard-ghost-folds` is based on `upstream/v8` (`8e6a6d21`). It has four commits:

```text
8d3c88f9 test(build): pin the build_merge guard behaviours that already hold (#4955)
2e6831e8 fix(build): report ghost folds on the dedup remap channel (#4955)
9839bc9a fix(build): don't count intentional ghost folds as drops in build_merge (#4955)
539fc628 test(build): cover edge repoint, incremental update and write-back for ghost folds (#4955)
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way.

When `build_from_json` folds nothing the default path is unchanged. No cache schema bump and no graph format change. Reverting restores the old guard.

**Blast Radius:** Write guard.

Every graph written after a merge passes the `build_merge` guard and `to_json`, so a mistake here either blocks a good write or lets a bad one through. A fold is excused only when its survivor is in the new graph, and the control tests pin the refusals. After merge, a graph holding these twins can be updated through `build_merge(dedup=False)` instead of being refused with no way out. Extraction, ignore rules and secret filtering are unchanged.

title: perf(resolve): hold one parsed file at a time in symbol resolution
body:
## What does this PR do?

**Problem.** Symbol resolution kept every file's source and syntax tree until its last pass finished, so it held the whole corpus in memory. Part of #3011.

**Fix.** Each file is parsed once and released before the next.
- **JS/TS and Python:** the passes over a file now run in one loop. They fill different fact lists, so each list keeps its order. Class-member uses go to a separate list appended at the end, as before.
- **Java:** pass 2 needs a name index built after pass 1, but from each file it only needs the imports. Pass 1 now keeps those rows instead of the tree, so nothing is parsed twice.

**Result on Next.js** (28,465 code files, main process peak, cold cache):

| | Peak | Time |
|---|---:|---:|
| `v8` | 3.17 GB | 69 s |
| This PR | 1.77 GB | 67 s |

Nodes and edges are identical: 166,514 and 373,606, same SHA-256 over both lists.

title: perf(extract): release edge keys and per-file rows once they are used
body:
## What does this PR do?

**Problem.** `extract()` kept data after its last use. Alias de-duplication stored one JSON string per edge in the corpus, and the per-file rows and raw calls stayed alive for the rest of the function. Part of #3011.

**Fix.**
- `_edge_key` returns a 16-byte BLAKE2b digest of the same JSON. It is only compared for equality, so the full string isn't needed.
- The de-duplication tables are deleted when it ends.
- `per_file` and `all_raw_calls` are deleted after the language resolvers, their last use.

Nodes and edges are identical: 166,514 and 373,606, same SHA-256 over both lists.

## Type of change

- [x] Refactor

Invariant: de-duplication keeps and drops the same edges. A digest collision is the only way that could change, which at 128 bits is not a practical risk.

title: perf(load): do not hold graph.json rows and the graph at once
body:
## What does this PR do?

**Problem.** Loading `graph.json` held the parsed rows and the finished graph at the same time, because networkx copies each row while the input list stays alive. Each repeated id, path and relation name was also a separate string. Every `query`, `path`, `explain` and `affected` call and the MCP server pay for this.

**Fix.**
- `read_graph_json` shares repeated strings through a table local to the read. It doesn't use `sys.intern`, because interned strings are never freed on Python 3.12, which would leak in a long-running server.
- `consumed` hands each row to networkx and releases it, so rows and graph don't peak together. It's only used for data the loader read itself; a dict passed in by a caller is left untouched.
- The `except TypeError` retry is removed at these sites. `networkx>=3.4` is required, so the retry only ever fired on a bad row, and retrying over consumed rows would return a partial graph. A bad row now raises.

**Result on a Next.js graph** (168,833 nodes, 349,786 edges, 189 MB file), `load_node_link_graph`:

| | Peak | Time |
|---|---:|---:|
| `v8` | 1.15 GB | 2.5 s |
| This PR | 0.77 GB | 2.1 s |

The loaded nodes and edges are identical, with the same SHA-256.

## Type of change

- [x] Refactor

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: the loaded graph has the same nodes, edges, order and stored arc direction, and a malformed file never loads partially.

title: Go same-file member calls can resolve to a method on the wrong receiver type
Default-imported object literal methods have nodes but no cross-file call edges
body:
Tested on v8 at 32e5efe935e6844ef39a5e33409e4efe848f2172.

`native.ts`:
```ts
export default { toast() { return 1; } };
```

`use.ts`:
```ts
import native from './native';
export function Use() { return native.toast(); }
```

Extracting both files produces nodes for `toast()` and `Use()`, but no `Use -> toast` call edge. The default-export parser does not expose an identity for an anonymous object literal that the imported member call can bind to.

Expected: resolve a statically named member through its directly default-exported object and the source module. A different module's same-named method must not answer the call. Imported aliases should work, while shadowed bindings, unknown members and dynamic keys should remain unresolved unless supported by explicit evidence.

This report concerns cross-file binding to existing method nodes, rather than adding new callable nodes or changing decorator relations.

Scope: the caller and target must be available to the same extraction or its resolution context, and existing import resolution must locate the module. This does not request rerunning default-object import resolution during `global add` of independently extracted repository graphs.

title: extract silently omits ignored directories without showing the detection summary
body:
Tested on v8 at 32e5efe935e6844ef39a5e33409e4efe848f2172.

Consider a parent Git repository with `.gitignore` containing `Developments/`. Under that directory, place a separate Git repository containing tracked source code. Running `graphify extract . --code-only` at the parent root respects the parent's ignore rule and can finish successfully after indexing only the parent shell.

Respecting ignore rules is expected. The problem is that the CLI reports discovered and unclassified files without surfacing the detector's existing `ignored` records, so the user has little indication why the nested repository is absent.

Expected: show a bounded summary of ignored paths and explain how to inspect the corpus boundary. `--no-gitignore` should be described specifically as bypassing VCS ignore rules; explicit `.graphifyignore` and `--exclude` rules must continue to apply.

The summary should reuse detector output and preserve directory pruning. It should not recursively walk ignored trees or automatically change which files are included.

title: fix(go): resolve same-file member calls through receiver types
body:
`a.apply()` could bind to `B.apply` even when `a` was declared as `*A`; method declaration order chose the target. A method could also capture a bare call to a package-level function. Route member calls through receiver-aware resolution and exclude methods from local/global bare-call candidates.

Receiver types follow lexical scope and declaration order. Unknown local bindings block package-variable fallback, fields resolve through their owning struct, and direct calls take priority over method-value references. Generic receiver bindings and explicit `T.M(t)` / `(*T).M(t)` expressions use their declared types. Unknown or ambiguous receivers remain unresolved.

Same-file member calls now carry `INFERRED` confidence, matching cross-file receiver resolution; same-file bare function calls retain `EXTRACTED`. AST cache schema advances from 36 to 37. The historical schema regression keeps a lower bound without requiring an old issue number in the current assignment's comment.

Scope: this improves extraction within the visible corpus. It does not add complete Go package/import resolution, package-qualified type inference or general return-type inference. `global add` continues to use existing parked-call hints rather than rerunning receiver inference.

title: Python: calls on module-level class instances get no calls edge (g = Svc(); def f(): g.m()), incl. lowercase class rebound to instance
body:
**Version:** graphifyy 0.9.101 (latest), code-only, `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none`

### Summary
A method call on a class instance created at **module scope** gets no `calls` edge when it's made inside a function. This covers a plain singleton (`g = Svc()`) and a lowercase class rebound to its own instance (`svc = svc(app)`, a common Flask-style pattern). It's the Python version of #3101 (Pascal) and #1698 (Kotlin).

On a ~1,300-file production backend this drops most calls into core service classes: 102 such rebinds across 57 files. A core write method showed 0 callers where grep finds 8+, and the top-degree nodes came out as schema base classes.

### Repro
```python
# pkg/__init__.py  (empty)

# pkg/svc.py
class Svc:
    def create(self): return 1

class lower_svc:
    def __init__(self, app): self.app = app
    def create(self): return 2

# pkg/caller.py
from .svc import Svc, lower_svc

g = Svc()
lower_svc = lower_svc(None)

def a(): g.create()          # expected: calls -> Svc.create
def b(): lower_svc.create()  # expected: calls -> lower_svc.create
def c():
    x = Svc(); x.create()    # control
```
`GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none graphify update . --no-cluster`

**Actual `calls` edges:** only `c() -> Svc` and `c() -> .create()`. `a()` and `b()` get nothing.

### Likely cause (reading `v8`)
- `_python_local_class_bindings` (`extractors/engine.py`) collects bindings only from a function's own params and locals. Module-scope assignments never set `receiver_type`.
- With no `receiver_type`, `_resolve_python_member_calls` (`extract.py` ~5331–5364) falls back to two branches. The class branch requires `receiver[:1].isupper()`, so a lowercase class never takes it. The module branch only matches imported *modules*. Both miss.
- An `X = X(...)` rebind would also hit the "import + constructor" poisoning rule.

### Suggested fix
Collect module-scope `name = ClassName(...)` bindings and let functions inherit them unless they shadow the name locally. Treat `X = X(...)`, where the right-hand `X` resolves to exactly one class, as an instance of that class. Emit these edges as `INFERRED`, like the existing typed-receiver branch.

title: fix(hooks): include dedicated Grep in the strict orientation gate
body:
## Problem

`graphify hook-guard search` remains advisory even with `--strict` or `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT=1`. Dedicated Grep calls therefore bypass the existing first-read orientation gate. Unlike compound Bash commands, a dedicated Grep request has an explicit search target.

## Change

- Dedicated Grep shares Read's existing once-per-session deny marker and recent-query bypass; directory searches do not require an indexed-file match, while a Grep pinned to a single file is denied only when the graph indexes that file (Read's existing `_target_is_indexed` check).
- Bash searches and Glob remain advisory. Grep searches outside the project or inside graph output are silent in both soft and strict mode, matching Read's scope, and do not consume the deny. A `needs_update` marker, absent graph/session, malformed input, or marker error cannot trigger denial.
- Strict Claude Code installs now pass `--strict` to the search hook as well as the read hook. Existing strict installs need a reinstall or `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT=1`. Pi/OMP continue to use the same CLI policy through their inherited environment.
- Update help, README, and changelog. No per-agent state, new configuration, or Bash parser changes.

This is intentionally narrower than Graphify-Labs/graphify#3291: it preserves today's shared session marker and query-stamp semantics instead of replacing them or enforcing compound Bash searches.

## Verification

- Regression tests were executed unchanged against base production and then the fix. Initial focused producer run: 14 failed / 13 passed to 27 passed. After review added soft-mode and non-Grep boundary cases, the independent reviewer repeated the gate: **19 failed / 13 passed at base; 32 passed with the fix**.
- Real CLI smoke: extract a tiny project, deny its first dedicated Grep, allow the retry, run an actual graph query, then allow Grep in another session through the existing query stamp.
- `env -u GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT uv run --frozen ruff check .`: passed.
- With the declared SQL extra installed: `env -u GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q --tb=short` — **9385 passed, 168 skipped, 1 xfailed**, before the test-only review additions. Final focused regression/strict checks: **50 passed**; after the single-file review fix, the adjacent hook and install suites: **384 passed, 4 skipped**. The initial run without the SQL extra had seven missing-parser failures; installing the dependency resolved them without code/test changes.
- `uv run --frozen pyright`: **702 errors, 4 warnings**, the same totals independently observed on pristine `8e6a6d2`. No type-check settings or thresholds changed.

## Limits

The gate intentionally remains self-limiting: one denial shared with Read per session, then advisory guidance. Bash/Glob behavior is unchanged. Existing project-wide query stamps remain project-wide.

title: fix(hooks): check extraction hashes before declaring newer files stale
body:
## Problem

When a checkout writes a tracked `graph.json` before source files, those source mtimes can be newer even though their bytes still match the extracted snapshot. The read hook currently calls them stale and softens strict mode to a nudge based on timestamps alone.

## Change

Only when a source mtime is newer than the graph, check the exact path's saved extraction hashes in the configured output directory's manifest. A match means the normal read guidance and strict gate still apply.

The check reuses the manifest writer's streamed MD5 helper, not the separate path-salted SHA256 cache digest. Every populated AST/semantic tier must agree with current contents. Legacy `{hash: ...}` rows remain supported. Missing, malformed, oversized, unreadable, unknown-path or invalid-hash evidence retains the conservative stale nudge; `needs_update` always wins. Older files are not hashed.

Hook documentation is updated in the authoritative fragment and regenerated with skillgen, including its expected artifacts.

## Verification

- Frozen tests execute the real `save_manifest` writer. Producer red: 10 failed / 22 passed; green: 32 passed. Parent independently reproduced the failures on pristine base production and verified the same test file hash with the fix. After a test-only Unicode review addition, the independent reviewer repeated the gate: **11 failed / 22 passed at base; 33 passed with the fix**.
- Coverage includes unchanged later mtimes, same-size content edits, AST/semantic/both manifests, legacy rows, exact-path collisions, custom output, errors, invalid metadata, and `needs_update` precedence.
- Real CLI smoke: extract a tiny project, advance its source mtime without changing bytes and observe strict denial; change one byte without changing length and observe the stale advisory instead.
- `env -u GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT uv run --frozen ruff check .`: passed.
- `uv run --frozen python -m tools.skillgen --check`: passed after regeneration.
- With the declared SQL extra installed: `env -u GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests -q --tb=short` — **9391 passed, 168 skipped, 1 xfailed**, before the test-only review addition. Final focused regression/strict checks: **52 passed**. An initial run without the SQL extra had seven missing-parser failures; installing the dependency resolved them without code/test changes.
- `uv run --frozen pyright`: **702 errors, 4 warnings**, the same totals independently observed on pristine `8e6a6d2`. No type-check settings or thresholds changed.

## Limits

This corrects checkout timestamp false positives, not every possible stale-graph case. It does not hash older files, trust the stat-index as extraction evidence, or override an explicit update-pending marker. The existing indexed-file check is not NFC-aware, so decomposed filenames can receive normal guidance without strict denial; this change only corrects their freshness guidance.

title: fix(install): remove the global skill registration on uninstall
body:
## What does this PR do?

A global Claude or CodeBuddy install adds a `# graphify` block to the user's global instructions file. Uninstall deleted the skill but left that block behind.

| Install | Block written to |
|---|---|
| `graphify install --platform claude` (or `windows`) | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, or `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CLAUDE.md` when that is set |
| `graphify install --platform codebuddy` | `~/.codebuddy/CODEBUDDY.md` |

`graphify uninstall`, `graphify claude uninstall` and `graphify codebuddy uninstall` all leave it. Claude Code and CodeBuddy read that file in every session, so after uninstalling they kept being told to use a skill that no longer exists:

```text
$ graphify install --platform claude && graphify uninstall
  skill removed    ->  ~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md
$ cat ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
# graphify
- **graphify** (`~/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`) - any input to knowledge graph. Trigger: `/graphify`
When the user types `/graphify`, use the installed graphify skill or instructions before doing anything else.
```

The project-scoped uninstall already removes its own registration (`_remove_claude_skill_registration`); only the global path was missing it.

Changes (`graphify/install.py`):
- `claude_uninstall` and `codebuddy_uninstall` remove the global registration wherever they remove the global skill: a bare call, and `uninstall_all` (`remove_user_skill=True`). In `codebuddy_uninstall` it runs before the project-file checks, which return early when the project has no `CODEBUDDY.md`.
- **Only graphify's own block goes.** The global files belong to the user, and every `graphify uninstall` now visits them, even for users who never installed the skill there (a codex-only user, say). So in those files a `# graphify` section is removed only when it carries the registration bullet graphify has written in every version: `- **graphify** (`…`)` with the `/graphify` trigger. A section the user wrote under `# graphify` stays. A file holding both is left as is, with a hint, rather than guessed at.
- Uninstall resolves the global file with a new `_claude_global_registration()`, which makes the same choice as `install()`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` included (#2694). `install()` itself is unchanged, to stay clear of #4803, which refactors that block. Instead, a test runs a real install with and without `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and asserts the helper names the file it wrote.
- The removal logic moves from `_remove_claude_skill_registration` into `_remove_skill_registration(target, prefix, *, only_graphify_written=False)`, shared by both paths. It keeps the existing rules:
  - only the exact `# graphify` H1 heading, never a user's `## graphify` (#2062);
  - line endings are kept (#4360);
  - a symlinked file is edited in place, and the output names its target (#3805);
  - the file is deleted only when nothing else was in it.

  It also handles three edge cases:
  - A BOM no longer hides a block on the file's first line, and is written back as found.
  - A file without the heading is never decoded, so an unrelated non-UTF-8 file draws no warning.
  - Like install (#3474), an unreadable or unwritable file is skipped with a hint instead of raising. A `CLAUDE.md` that nix/home-manager links into a read-only store no longer aborts the uninstall before later platforms are cleaned.

The project-scoped call keeps its existing matching (any exact `# graphify` section); it only gains the BOM and degrade handling.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: after an uninstall that removes a skill, nothing graphify wrote still points at that skill, and nothing the user wrote is changed. User content stays byte for byte.

- **Scope (#2215):** a project-scoped uninstall (`claude_uninstall(project_dir)`, `graphify claude uninstall --project`, `graphify uninstall --project`) keeps the global skill, so it keeps the global registration too. A test covers this.
- **No persisted graph state** is touched: no cache schema change and no generated skill files.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

Limitations:
- **Pre-existing, unchanged:** graphify's block runs to the next H1, so text a user adds directly *below* it, with no H1 of their own in between, goes with it. Install already behaves this way; that is #3791.
- If `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` changes between install and uninstall, uninstall cleans the profile it currently points at.
- A file holding graphify's block *and* a hand-written `# graphify` section keeps both, with a hint naming the file.

## How was this tested?

- New `tests/test_uninstall_global_registration.py`, 29 tests. They install and uninstall for real inside the suite's sandboxed HOME (#2168).
  - The block is removed for `claude` and `windows`, through `graphify uninstall` and `graphify claude uninstall`.
  - CodeBuddy's block is removed through both `graphify uninstall` and `graphify codebuddy uninstall`, including when the project has no `CODEBUDDY.md` (the early-return path).
  - The user's own content survives, byte for byte under LF and CRLF, and with a BOM.
  - `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is honored, and the default profile is not touched.
  - A symlinked `CLAUDE.md` is kept, with its target cleaned.
  - A user's `## graphify` heading survives.
  - In both global files, a hand-written `# graphify` section survives. That includes one with its own `- **graphify** (`…`)` bullet but no trigger.
  - A file mixing both kinds of section is left as is, with a hint.
  - Blocks written by older versions (the em-dash and hyphen forms, with a leading blank line) are removed.
  - An unwritable `CLAUDE.md` is skipped with a hint, and the rest of the uninstall still runs.
  - An unrelated non-UTF-8 file is left alone without a warning.
  - A project-scoped uninstall leaves the global registration.
  - A second uninstall changes nothing.
  - Uninstall resolves the file install wrote.

  On v8 (8e6a6d21), 20 fail. The other 9 are guards that pass there because v8 never touches these files: project scope, repeat uninstall, the six hand-written-section cases, and the non-UTF-8 file.
- **Mutations**, each caught:

  | Change | Tests that fail |
  |---|---|
  | drop the Claude removal | 15 |
  | drop the CodeBuddy removal | 4 |
  | move the CodeBuddy removal after the early return | 4 |
  | remove sections without the signature check | 5 |
  | remove a mixed file anyway | 1 |
  | require the current wording only (no older blocks) | 1 |
  | ignore the trigger in the signature | 2 |
  | drop the BOM handling | 1 |
  | drop the heading pre-check | 1 |
  | catch nothing on `OSError` | 1 |
  | resolve the path without `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | 1 |

- **CLI, throwaway HOME** (`graphify install --platform X`, then `graphify uninstall`):
  - for `claude`, `windows` and `codebuddy`, a global file graphify created is deleted;
  - user notes (LF, CRLF, with a BOM, or in `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) come back unchanged;
  - a codex-only user's hand-written `# graphify` notes in either global file are untouched;
  - an older version's block leaves exactly the user's notes;
  - a mixed file is untouched, with the hint printed;
  - `graphify claude uninstall --project` leaves the global block.

```text
uv run pytest tests/test_uninstall_global_registration.py -q   # 29 passed (also on 3.12 and 3.14)
uv run pytest tests/test_install.py tests/test_install_line_endings.py tests/test_uninstall_symlink.py tests/test_codebuddy.py tests/test_home_sandbox.py -q   # plus every other install/uninstall test file: 473 passed, 1 skipped
# Full suite: `uv sync --all-extras --frozen`, then `uv run pytest tests/ -q --tb=short`.
#   this branch on v8 8e6a6d21 — 3.10: 9583 | 3.13: 9583 passed (v8 itself: 9554, counting one watch-harness flake that failed on plain v8 in that run; +29 new)
#   only the 7 DNS-dependent test_security tests fail (no network here)
uv run python -m tools.skillgen --check / --audit-coverage / --schema-singleton / --monolith-roundtrip / --always-on-roundtrip   # all OK
uv run ruff check .
uv run pyright graphify/install.py        # the same 4 (Windows msvcrt) errors as v8; none new. The new test file: 0
uv run bandit -r graphify -ll             # 12 findings, identical to v8
GRAPHIFY_TEST_CLI=.venv/bin/graphify bun test tests/pi.test.ts   # 20/20
```

## Graphify-specific checklist

- [x] I updated generated skill artifacts (`uv run python -m tools.skillgen --bless`) when changing their source fragments. *(No source fragments touched; `--check` passes.)*
- [x] I confirmed that AST/structural extraction remains deterministic (no ambient state dependencies like ENV variables).
- [x] I reviewed changes for security implications (no unsafe interpolation into shell/Python).
- [x] I confirmed no API keys or local-only graph data are included.
- [x] (If applicable) I disclosed AI authorship in my commit messages.

title: fix(extract): preservar plantillas e imports de tipo en TypeScript
body:
## ¿Qué hace este PR?

Corrige dos casos válidos de TypeScript que la gramática actual de tree-sitter puede interpretar con errores: una plantilla etiquetada con un tipo genérico de objeto-arreglo, como `sql<{ id: string }[]>` seguida de una plantilla, y una anotación genérica calificada como `import("mod").Context<Env>`. El segundo caso podía absorber declaraciones posteriores y dejar fuera del grafo una función exportada.

La extracción normaliza sólo candidatos reconocidos por el árbol sintáctico, en memoria y con la misma longitud en bytes y saltos de línea. También evita registrar el `import` de tipo reparado como una carga dinámica ejecutable. No modifica el archivo fuente. Los offsets de los imports se convierten de bytes a texto con saltos de línea normalizados en una sola pasada, y el patrón de etiquetas evita volver a empezar dentro de un identificador. Ambas observaciones de la revisión automática se reprodujeron antes del arreglo y tienen pruebas de regresión.

## Tipo de cambio

- [x] Corrección de error
- [x] Pruebas de regresión

## Verificación e invariantes

- [x] Leí la guía de contribución y la arquitectura.
- [x] Reproduje los dos problemas en la base `v8`: cuatro pruebas de regresión fallaron antes de aplicar el parche y pasaron después.
- [x] Las pruebas comprueban declaraciones y llamadas posteriores, ubicaciones, TS y TSX, saltos de línea, literales, comentarios, comparaciones e importaciones dinámicas reales, incluso después de caracteres multibyte.
- [x] La extracción sigue siendo local y determinista; no agrega llamadas de red ni escribe sobre el archivo analizado.
- [x] El diff no incluye claves, datos del corpus local ni artefactos generados. La asistencia de IA está declarada en el commit.
- [x] No se cambiaron fuentes de skills ni artefactos generados de skills.

## ¿Cómo se probó?

- 153 pruebas focalizadas de compatibilidad TypeScript, importaciones dinámicas y resolución de imports: aprobadas.
- `ruff check graphify/extract.py tests/test_ts_typed_template_and_annotation.py`: aprobado.
- Extracción directa de los diez archivos que reprodujeron el problema: sin avisos; la función exportada que faltaba quedó presente.
- Reconstrucción AST aislada de un corpus local, con la rama de este PR y `--code-only`: 4.899 archivos de código detectados, 31.947 nodos, 97.402 relaciones y 561 comunidades. Los 288 archivos SQL versionados quedaron representados; se recuperaron la función afectada y una prueba reciente. No hubo avisos de sintaxis ni faltó el parser YAML o SQL. No se utilizó ningún adaptador local ni modelo.
- La ejecución excluyó 2 archivos considerados potencialmente sensibles y 2.418 archivos no correspondientes a código; 256 archivos no se clasificaron y 318 archivos de código no aportaron símbolos. Por eso la evidencia cubre la extracción AST de los archivos admitidos, no la extracción semántica de documentación ni los archivos excluidos.
- Como comprobación adicional, la corrección equivalente sobre la versión instalada 0.9.72 completó `graphify update .` sobre el mismo corpus sin los diez avisos: 40.075 nodos, 106.042 relaciones y 288 archivos SQL representados. Esta cifra corresponde a esa versión instalada, no a la rama `v8`.

Verificación completa adicional del commit actual en entornos aislados y sin credenciales:

- Python 3.13 y Bash 5: **9.568 aprobadas, 27 omitidas y 1 fallo esperado**. Python 3.10 y Bash 5: **9.568 aprobadas, 27 omitidas y 1 fallo esperado**. Se ejecutó `pytest tests/ -q --tb=short --disable-warnings` en ambas versiones; se registraron 2.632 y 2.645 advertencias, respectivamente.
- Una primera corrida con Bash 3.2 tuvo un fallo en el control de trazado de comandos; se reprodujo igual en la base y desapareció en ambas versiones con Bash 5. El archivo afectado pasó sus 163 pruebas con Bash 5.
- `ruff check .`: aprobado.
- `pyright`: **683 errores en la base y 683 en el PR, sin diagnósticos adicionales** al comparar archivo, regla y mensaje. El chequeo global no está en verde por los diagnósticos existentes.
- El [workflow de CI](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/actions/runs/41648708440) del commit actual figura como `action_required` y no mostró jobs ejecutados; los controles de gestión no sustituyen esa ejecución. El normalizador de plantillas cubre el patrón observado de objeto-arreglo sin llaves anidadas; no pretende normalizar arbitrariamente todos los argumentos de tipo posibles. La extracción semántica de documentos queda fuera de esta prueba.

title: [Bug]: Generated git hooks break when CDPATH is exported (dash's cd prints the resolved dir), silently skipping every rebuild
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

## What happened?

Every git hook that `graphify hook install` generates fails at its top-level anchor whenever the committing shell exports `CDPATH` (common in zsh setups, e.g. `export CDPATH=".:~:$HOME/go/src"`). The hook prints a `cd` error on every commit and then takes the `|| exit 0` path, so **the detached rebuild is never launched and `graphify-out/` silently goes stale** while the commits themselves keep succeeding.

The cause is in `graphify/hooks.py`, `_WORKTREE_GUARD` (the block spliced into all four hook templates):

```sh
_GFY_GITDIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null && pwd)
_GFY_COMMONDIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null && pwd)
```

`git rev-parse --git-dir` answers the relative `.git`, so the absolute form is obtained by `cd`-ing into it and calling `pwd`. When `CDPATH` is set and contains `.`, the shell `cd` builtin **also writes the resolved directory to stdout** (dash, and bash outside posix mode; `/bin/sh` is dash on Debian/Ubuntu). The `2>/dev/null` guards stderr only, so the capture becomes a two-line string:

```text
/abs/path/.git
/abs/path/.git
```

`_TOPLEVEL_ANCHOR`, which runs next, then mis-derives the checkout root:

```sh
if [ -z "${GIT_WORK_TREE:-}" ] && [ "${_GFY_COMMONDIR##*/}" = ".git" ]; then
    _GFY_TOP=${_GFY_COMMONDIR%/*}
```

`${_GFY_COMMONDIR##*/}` still ends in `.git` on the doubled value, so the branch is taken, but `%/*` strips at the last slash of the **second** copy, producing `<abs>/.git` newline `<abs>`. The next line fails and exits:

```sh
[ -n "$_GFY_TOP" ] && cd "$_GFY_TOP" || exit 0
```

Two side effects worth noting:

1. The failure is silent by design (`|| exit 0`), so a repo can run for months with the hook installed and never rebuild, with only a stray line on stderr at each commit as the trace.
2. `_WORKTREE_GUARD`'s own comparison (`_GFY_GITDIR != _GFY_COMMONDIR`) only still works because both captures are doubled *identically*. Its correctness there is accidental rather than structural.

## Steps to reproduce

```shell
mkdir /tmp/gfy-repro && cd /tmp/gfy-repro
git init -q .
graphify hook install
printf 'print("hello")\n' > m.py
git add m.py
# CDPATH as an interactive zsh/bash config would export it
CDPATH=".:$HOME" git commit -m "feat: m"
```

To reproduce against the un-patched 0.9.101 template only the guard matters; the minimal shell shape is:

```shell
env CDPATH=. dash -c 'mkdir -p /tmp/d/.git && cd /tmp/d && G=$(cd .git 2>/dev/null && pwd); printf "G=[%s]\n" "$G"'
# G=[/tmp/d/.git
# /tmp/d/.git]        <- two lines

env CDPATH=. dash -c 'unset CDPATH; mkdir -p /tmp/d2/.git && cd /tmp/d2 && G=$(cd .git 2>/dev/null && pwd); printf "G=[%s]\n" "$G"'
# G=[/tmp/d2/.git]    <- one line
```

## Error output or graph output

With the shipped 0.9.101 hook (note the second line: it is the tail of the same `cd` argument, the value contains a newline):

```text
$ CDPATH=".:$HOME" git commit -q -m "feat: m"
.git/hooks/post-commit: 38: cd: can't cd to /tmp/gfy-repro/.git
/tmp/gfy-repro
commit exit=0
```

`git commit` succeeds, `~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log` gains **zero** lines, and `graphify-out/` is never created in that repo. The graph in a real checkout therefore keeps its old `built_at_commit` indefinitely.

With the two-line fix below applied to the same generated hook, same `CDPATH`:

```text
$ CDPATH=".:$HOME" git commit -q -m "feat: n"
[graphify hook] launching background rebuild (log: ~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log)
commit exit=0

$ tail -3 ~/.cache/graphify-rebuild.log
[graphify watch] Rebuilt: 1 nodes, 0 edges, 1 communities
[graphify watch] graph.json, graph.html and GRAPH_REPORT.md updated in graphify-out
```

## Graphify version

0.9.101 (the current release on PyPI at report time; `graphifyy 0.9.101`, installed with `uv tool install`, and the template in the installed package matches the `v8` source).

## Operating System

Linux (Ubuntu, `/bin/sh` -> `dash`)

## Python Version

3.14 (the hook runs the rebuild through the tool's own interpreter; the failing part is the `/bin/sh` hook body, which is independent of the interpreter)

## Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

## Additional Environment Details

- `CDPATH` is exported from the user's shell config: `export CDPATH=".:~:$HOME/go/src:$HOME/Documents/MyProjects:$HOME/Documents/Projects:"`. The trailing `.`/`:` entries are what make `cd .git` resolve through `CDPATH` and print.
- `git version 2.43.0`. `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE` are both **unset** in the hook environment here, so the failure is in the fallback path, not a worktree or `core.hooksPath` layout.
- Reproduces in a clean, throwaway `git init` repo (yes, clean-checkout repro), and in a large real checkout: `post-commit`, `post-checkout`, `post-merge` and `post-rewrite` all carry the same `_WORKTREE_GUARD` + `_TOPLEVEL_ANCHOR` splice, so all four are affected.
- No provider API keys are involved; this is the code-only hook path.

## Additional context

**Suggested fix** (verified end-to-end in the repro above; keeps the intent of the comment about resolving relative `GIT_DIR` absolutely):

```diff
-_GFY_GITDIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null && pwd)
-_GFY_COMMONDIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null && pwd)
+unset CDPATH
+_GFY_GITDIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)
+_GFY_COMMONDIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)
```

`unset CDPATH` is safe inside the hook body because every `cd` graphify performs afterwards is given an absolute path (`$_GFY_TOP` from `%/*` or from `--show-toplevel`), so nothing relies on `CDPATH` lookup.

A cleaner variant, if the minimum supported git is 2.31 or newer, is to drop the shell `cd` from the capture entirely and let git do it:

```sh
_GFY_COMMONDIR=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)
```

with a fallback to the existing form for older git. That also removes the accidental-equality dependency in the worktree guard.

**Regression test** in the spirit of `tests/test_hook_guard.py` and the `tests/test_<issue>_<slug>.py` convention (CONTRIBUTING point 7, prove the old failure): render the hook body, then run it under `dash` with `CDPATH=.` exported and assert (a) stderr contains no `cd: can't cd to` line, and (b) the run reaches the launcher (the `[graphify hook] launching background rebuild` line / the `Popen`) instead of exiting at `_TOPLEVEL_ANCHOR`. A narrower variant is to source the guard and assert `$_GFY_TOP` is exactly one line, which fails today with two.

**Local workaround applied on our side**, so the hooks are not broken while this is open: the four hooks in `.git/hooks/` and the `_WORKTREE_GUARD` constant in the installed `graphify/hooks.py` were patched as above (with `hooks.py.bak` kept). Note this is a site-packages patch, so it is reverted by any `uv tool upgrade graphifyy` / reinstall.

**Not tested:** Windows/MSYS `cd` (it does not print on `CDPATH` as far as I know, but the `>/dev/null` half of the fix is inert there anyway), and a git configuration where hooks are executed by `zsh` rather than `dash`/`bash`.

title: perf(update): `_reconcile_existing_graph` re-sniffs every `.h` file once per node — up to ~200 GB of redundant reads after the AST phase
body:
## Summary

After AST extraction finishes (in parallel), `graphify update .` enters a single-threaded phase at 100% of one core. During part of that phase the main process re-reads the same C/C++ header files thousands of times. In this repository that costs about 66 s per reconcile pass; a per-file cache brings it to 0.23 s.

Cause: two pieces of code interact.

1. `_reconcile_existing_graph()` (`graphify/watch.py`, line 1204 on `v8` @ 8e6a6d2 and in 0.9.101) calls `_get_extractor(Path(source_file))` **once per node** in the existing graph. The result is not cached per file. The `alive` and `ignored` checks next to it already are cached (`_alive_cache`, `_ignored_cache`).
2. For a `.h` path, `_get_extractor()` calls `_is_objc_header()` and then `_is_cpp_header()` (`graphify/extract.py`). Each of them runs `path.read_bytes()[:256 * 1024]`. That loads the **whole file** before slicing, so a C/C++ header is read in full twice per call.

So the cost of one reconcile pass is about `2 × Σ(nodes_in_file × file_size)` over all `.h` files, not `Σ file_size`.

## Measurements (Linux, Python 3.13, graphify 0.9.101)

The repository vendors several C/C++ projects (llama.cpp and forks, whisper.cpp). Each of them carries its own copy of `miniaudio.h`.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Nodes in existing `graph.json` | 642,814 |
| Nodes whose `source_file` is `.h` or `.m` | 130,624 (3,215 distinct files) |
| Estimated bytes read per reconcile pass (2 reads per node, upper bound) | ~223 GB |
| `miniaudio.h` alone (4.1 MB, 3,361 nodes, 4 vendored copies) | ~27.6 GB per copy |
| Observed main-process `rchar` during the post-AST phase | >60 GB, up to ~3 GB/s, 100% of one core |
| Regular files open in the main process during that phase (319k `/proc/<pid>/fd` samples over 8 s) | ~9,900 of ~9,910 hits were `.h` files; 459 distinct files |

| Per-node `_get_extractor()` over all 130,624 `.h`/`.m` nodes, uncached (extrapolated from a 4,000-node random sample) | ~66 s |
| Same loop with a per-file cache (fix 1 below), full pass | 0.23 s |

A single pass of `_get_extractor()` over all 1,293 vendored headers (32 MB) takes about 98 ms. So the per-file loops in `extract()` are not the problem. The per-**node** loop is.

The whole single-threaded phase lasted longer than these 66 s, so other work in that phase also costs time. This issue covers only the repeated header reads.

(py-spy could not attach on this host, so the call site was found by reading the code and confirmed by the numbers above.)

## Proposed fix

1. In `_reconcile_existing_graph()`, cache the extractor lookup per source file, the same way `_alive_cache` works:

   ```python
   _extractor_known: dict[str, bool] = {}
   ...
   key = identity or source_file
   has_extractor = _extractor_known.get(key)
   if has_extractor is None:
       has_extractor = _get_extractor(Path(source_file)) is not None
       _extractor_known[key] = has_extractor
   if not has_extractor:
       ...
   ```

2. In `_is_objc_header()` and `_is_cpp_header()`, read only the bytes that are used:

   ```python
   with open(path, "rb") as f:
       head = f.read(256 * 1024)
   ```

   Optionally share one cached head per `(path, st_mtime_ns, st_size)` between the two sniffers, so a `.h` file is opened at most once per run.

Either change alone removes almost all of the redundant I/O in this repository. With (1) the reconcile pass reads each header at most twice. With (2) each read is capped at 256 KB instead of the full 4 MB.

## Related

- #3045 (open): `graphify update .` stalls after the AST phase. Same symptom, root cause not identified there. It may be this.
- #4150, #4909 (closed): other cases of per-node work repeated in the update path.

title: perf(resolution): `_resolve_cross_file_imports` scans every edge in the graph once per Python file (O(files × edges))
body:
## Summary

In `graphify/extractors/resolution.py`, `_resolve_cross_file_imports()` loops over the per-file results (`for file_result, path in zip(per_file, paths):`, line 3049 in 0.9.101). For each file that has `import_targets`, the type-reference repoint step (#3252) then iterates **all** edges of the whole corpus:

```python
if all_edges and import_targets:
    for edge in all_edges:
        if edge.get("source_file") not in file_srcs:
            continue
        ...
```

(lines 3224–3226 on `v8` @ 8e6a6d2, the same in 0.9.101.)

Only the edges whose `source_file` belongs to the current file can match. So the work is O(files × edges) instead of O(edges).

## Measurements (Linux, Python 3.13, graphify 0.9.101)

`py-spy record -r 50` on a full `graphify update .` (wall time 3 min 31 s; the main process was active for 171 s):

| Frame | Time | Share of active main-process time |
|---|---|---|
| `_resolve_cross_file_imports` (inclusive) | 56 s | 33% |
| lines 3225–3226 (self: the `for edge in all_edges` scan and the `source_file` check) | 39 s | 23% |

Corpus: 4,115 Python files and 360,996 edges in the resulting graph.

## Proposed fix

Group the edges by `source_file` once, before the per-file loop, and only visit the current file's edges:

```python
edges_by_source: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
if all_edges:
    for edge in all_edges:
        edges_by_source.setdefault(edge.get("source_file"), []).append(edge)
...
if all_edges and import_targets:
    for src in file_srcs:
        for edge in edges_by_source.get(src, ()):
            if edge.get("relation") not in TYPE_REPOINT_RELATIONS:
                continue
            ...
```

The repoint changes only `edge["target"]`, not `source_file`, so the index stays valid while the loop runs. `all_edges` itself is not appended to inside the function (new edges go to `new_edges`).

### Measured with this patch

Two `graphify update .` runs, one after the other, on two identical copies of the same `graphify-out` (via `GRAPHIFY_OUT`) and the same corpus. The only difference: the patched run used a copy of the package with the change above.

| Run | Wall time | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| 0.9.101 as released | 3:36.3 | 5.9 GB |
| 0.9.101 + patch | **2:55.3** (−41 s, −19%) | 5.9 GB |

Both runs ended with `No code-graph topology changes detected; outputs left untouched.`, so the patched run produced the same graph topology as the existing graph.

## Related

- #4978: per-node `.h` re-sniffing in `_reconcile_existing_graph`, a separate hot spot in the same `update` run.
- #3868: unbounded edge allocation in cross-file import resolution (a different problem in the same function).

title: perf(resolution): index edges by source file for the #3252 repoint (#4980)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4980.

The #3252 repoint step in `_resolve_cross_file_imports()` (`graphify/extractors/resolution.py`) scanned **every edge in the corpus once per Python file** that has import targets:

```python
if all_edges and import_targets:
    for edge in all_edges:
        if edge.get("source_file") not in file_srcs:
            continue
```

So the pass cost files × edges. This PR indexes the edges by `source_file` once, the first time a file needs it, and visits only the importing file's edges.

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: for each importing file, the repoint visits the same edges, in the same order, and makes the same `target` changes as before. Only the cost changes.

- **Same edges:** the old loop skipped every edge whose `source_file` was not in `file_srcs`. The index lookup returns exactly the edges whose `source_file` is in `file_srcs`.
- **Same order:** each index entry keeps the edge's position in `all_edges`, and a file's entries are sorted by it before the loop.
- **Index stays valid:** the loop only rewrites `edge["target"]`. `source_file` is never changed, and `all_edges` is not appended to inside the function (new edges go to `new_edges`).
- **Same point of first contact:** the index is built inside the same `if all_edges and import_targets:` branch where the old code first touched every edge. A corpus where no file has import targets still never iterates `all_edges` there.

title: feat(query): rank source above tests and docs, and answer file-first
body:
Closes #4983

## What does this PR do?

I noticed `graphify query` kept starting from tests and docs. A test named after a bug repeats the bug's words in its own name, so it wins the exact-name match, and the real source file ends up 6th or later or gets cut by the budget. On 177 SWE-bench Lite questions, 43% of the start nodes were tests.

This PR changes `query` only, in two ways:

1. Tests, docs, config and nodes with no source file count x0.3 when picking seeds. If the question mentions tests ("test", "tests", "testing", "testcase", "unittest") or docs ("doc", "docs", "documentation", "readme"), those keep full weight. Tests are detected with the existing `paths._is_test_path`, plus a `testing/` folder and `conftest.py`.
2. The answer is listed file by file, best-scoring file first. Nodes the question did not match keep the old order after them.

`path`, `explain`, traversal, depth and the token budget do not change. The new arguments default to `None`, so every other caller runs the old code. The per-term seed guarantee still holds, because the weight is applied to the per-term score too. Nothing new is stored, so `graph.json` and the cache do not change.

Diff: `graphify/serve.py` +83 / -10, `tests/test_query_source_first.py` (9 new tests).

### Numbers

I measured with `graphify benchmark --questions` (#4342) at the MCP defaults (BFS, depth 3, 2,000-token budget) on 293 SWE-bench Lite + Verified questions from 9 Python repos, each against the graph of its own base commit. "Top-5" means a file the real fix changed is in the first 5 files of the answer.

| | top-1 | top-3 | top-5 | anywhere | median tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v8 | 27% | 40% | 49% | 67% | 2,193 |
| this PR | 30% | 48% | **56%** | 62% | 2,197 |

Top-5 paired: 26 questions gained, 4 lost (McNemar p = 6e-5). I picked the 0.3 weight and the file-first order on the Django questions only; on the other 8 repos, which I did not tune on, it still goes up (Lite 49% to 56%, Verified 59% to 65%).

The cost: "anywhere" drops from 67% to 62%. In 28 of the 30 questions that lost it, v8 had shown the right file only 6th to 32nd, so an agent would rarely have read it anyway.

Data, scripts and the per-repo table: [research/query/](https://github.com/rohit-jsfreaky/graphify/tree/claude/query-study/research/query).

### Overlap

Other open PRs try similar things: #2403 (exclude tests from seeds), #3417 (demote tests and vendor, sort by relevance), #4601 (file-type weights), #4481 (lead with the best file), and #3284 / #1782 / #1658 (relevance order). On the same 177 Lite questions the best of them reached 51% top-5. This PR also makes a small `serve.py` conflict with #3284, #3636, #3866, #4478, #4576 and #4601.

- [ ] Documentation

- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Kept: `path` / `explain` scoring is unchanged (test 6), the per-term seed guarantee still seeds every matched term (test 7), and seeds are still the first lines of the answer, so truncation keeps them. No persisted state changes.

title: [Feature]: query starts from tests and docs instead of the code the question is about
body:
### Problem or use case

`graphify query` often starts from tests, docs and config instead of the code the question is about, and then lists nodes by hop and degree, so the right file is cut off by the budget.

`query` scores node names only. A test named after a bug repeats the question's words in its own name (`UsernameValidatorsTests`, `test_sqlmigrate_for_non_transactional_databases`), so it wins the exact-name tier.

Measured with `graphify benchmark --questions` (#4342) on 177 SWE-bench Lite issues (question = issue title, answer = non-test files of the gold patch): 43% of start nodes were tests, and an expected file is in the first 5 files shown only 49% of the time on v8 (293 Lite + Verified questions).

### Proposed solution

Inside `query` only:
1. Rank source above tests, docs and config (x0.3 weight via the existing `paths._is_test_path`), unless the question asks about tests or docs. The per-term seed guarantee stays.
2. List the answer file by file, best file first, so the budget keeps the most relevant files.

`path`, `explain`, traversal and the budget are unchanged. Result on 293 questions: top-5 49% -> 56% (26 gained, 4 lost, paired p = 6e-5), same answer size. PR: #4982.

### Alternatives considered

Indexing words inside function bodies gives a much larger gain (top-5 ~73% on held-out questions, smaller answers) but stores ~15% more in graph.json; better as a separate follow-up on top of this. Open ranking PRs (#3417, #2403, #4504, ...) were measured on the same questions; the best reached 51% top-5.

### Area

Graph building or querying

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, PR #4982 is open.

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Only the `query` answer order and its seeds change. No change to node/edge ids, graph.json, cache, MCP tool signatures, `path`, `explain` or incremental builds. An agent that relied on tests appearing first in `query` sees source first unless the question mentions tests.

### Additional context

Benchmark questions and scripts: SWE-bench Lite + Verified issues, one graph per base commit, `graphify benchmark --questions` from #4342.

title: [Bug]: Solidity: an import with ../ points at a dangling stub instead of the real file
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

A Solidity import that goes up a folder (`import {Errors} from "../utils/Errors.sol";`) gets an `imports_from` edge to a node that does not exist. The path is joined to the importer's folder without being normalised, so from `contracts/proxy/Clones.sol` the target becomes `contracts/proxy/utils/errors.sol` instead of `contracts/utils/Errors.sol`. That dangling target's id also keeps the absolute checkout path (e.g. `c_users_..._contracts_proxy_utils_errors_sol`), so graph.json is not portable.

Because the import never reaches the real file, everything that resolves names through imports (type references, and qualified names like `Errors.FailedCall`) cannot see the imported file.

On OpenZeppelin Contracts v5.4.0, only 87 of 681 Solidity `imports_from` edges reach a real file; the other 594 (every `../` import) dangle.

### Steps to reproduce

```
mkdir -p contracts/utils contracts/proxy
echo 'library Errors { error FailedCall(); }' > contracts/utils/Errors.sol
printf 'import {Errors} from "../utils/Errors.sol";\nlibrary Clones { function clone() internal {} }\n' > contracts/proxy/Clones.sol
graphify update .
```

Then look at the `imports_from` edge from `Clones.sol` in `graphify-out/graph.json`.

### Error output or graph output

```
imports_from Clones.sol -> c_users_..._contracts_proxy_utils_errors_sol   (no such node; no source_file)
```
Expected: `imports_from Clones.sol -> contracts_utils_errors_sol` (the real `Errors.sol` file node).

### Graphify version

0.9.101 (v8 @ 8e6a6d21)

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

title: fix(solidity): resolve ../ imports to the real file
body:
Closes #4984

## What does this PR do?

While checking Solidity calls on OpenZeppelin I saw most imports going nowhere. The extractor joined the import path to the file's folder without normalising it, so `import "../utils/Errors.sol"` in `contracts/proxy/Clones.sol` pointed at `contracts/proxy/utils/errors.sol`, a stub that does not exist, and that stub's id even kept my checkout's absolute path.

title: perf(update): stop re-reading headers once per node during reconcile
body:
## What does this PR do?

```diff
 _reconcile_existing_graph
   for node in nodes
-    _get_extractor(Path(source_file))
-      .h: _is_objc_header  -> read_bytes()[:256 KiB]   whole file, twice, per node
-      .h: _is_cpp_header   -> read_bytes()[:256 KiB]
+    _ast_owned(identity or source_file)                dict hit after the first node
+      _get_extractor(..., sniff_headers=False)          once per file, reads nothing for .h
```

The reconcile loop asked a per-file question once per node. For a `.h` path, `_get_extractor` ran two header probes, and each probe called `read_bytes()` before slicing to 256 KiB. The `is None` test cannot change for `.h`, because every dialect resolves to an extractor.

This branch asks the weaker "is this source AST-owned" question once per file, keyed by identity. It also reads only the sniff head and shares that head between the two probes. Reconcile now resolves `source_file` through `identity` first, so a relative path no longer makes both header probes swallow an `OSError` and misclassify `.m` sources when the process CWD is outside the project. Fixes #4978.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant is that reconcile work per node is constant, and a per-file fact is computed once per file. The suite asserts call and byte counts per variant, and asserts the frozen survivor set from `8e6a6d21` is unchanged. No generated or persisted state changes, because the survivor set is byte-identical.

- [x] Confirmed the frozen survivor set matches `8e6a6d21`.

Limitations: `sniff_headers=False` answers "is this source AST-owned" only, and must never pick a grammar for a real parse, because a C++ header resolves to `extract_c` that way. The sniff window is still 256 KiB, so a marker past that is invisible; that is the pre-existing behavior, not something this PR changes. The memo is local to one `_reconcile_existing_graph` call, so `watch` re-reads a header after an edit.
