title: fix(hooks): keep the toplevel anchor working when CDPATH is exported
body:
## Problem

An exported `CDPATH` (common in zsh/bash setups) makes the `cd` builtin print the resolved directory to stdout. `_WORKTREE_GUARD` only silences stderr, so the `git rev-parse --git-dir` / `--git-common-dir` captures became two-line values. `_TOPLEVEL_ANCHOR` then derived a malformed root and took the `|| exit 0` path, so every generated hook silently skipped its detached rebuild and `graphify-out/` went stale.

## Implementation

Prefix both `cd` calls in the shared guard with `CDPATH=` so they resolve the absolute git dirs without emitting the CDPATH echo. This is a two-line change in `graphify/hooks.py` and applies to all four generated hooks.

## Verification

- New regression `tests/test_hooks.py::test_worktree_guard_survives_exported_cdpath` runs the real `_WORKTREE_GUARD` + `_TOPLEVEL_ANCHOR` under `CDPATH=.:$HOME` and asserts the anchor reaches the checkout root.
- On the unmodified guard the test fails: the anchor exits before printing (`cd: ...\.git\n/tmp/...: No such file or directory`). With the change it passes.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_hooks.py -q`: 159 passed, 21 skipped, 1 failure — `test_shebang_parse_requires_leading_hash_bang`, a pre-existing Windows drive-letter path-case assertion unrelated to this change.

## Limitations

None known; `CDPATH=` is POSIX and works in dash, bash and Git for Windows' sh.

Fixes #4977

title: Python: a builtin used without import is linked to a package class of the same name (e.g. NotImplementedError), sometimes tagged EXTRACTED
body:
**Version:** `graphifyy==0.9.102` from PyPI, Python 3.12, `graphify extract . --code-only`, `GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none`, empty `HOME`.

### What happens

A package defines a class with the name of a builtin, `class NotImplementedError(Exception)`. A module that does **not** import it uses the builtin, `raise NotImplementedError(...)`. Graphify links that call to the package's class.

### Minimal reproduction

```
pkg/__init__.py   (empty)
pkg/errors.py     class NotImplementedError(Exception):
                      pass
pkg/a.py          def todo():
                      raise NotImplementedError("x")        # no import: this is builtins.NotImplementedError
pkg/b.py          from pkg.errors import NotImplementedError
                  def todo2():
                      raise NotImplementedError("x")        # control: this one is the package class
```

`graph.json`:

```
pkg/b.py:todo2() -> pkg/errors.py:NotImplementedError [calls EXTRACTED]   # correct
pkg/a.py:todo()  -> pkg/errors.py:NotImplementedError [calls INFERRED]    # wrong: a.py never binds the name
```

Expected: no link from `todo()`. Without an import or an assignment in `a.py`, the name is the builtin.

A function homonym is **not** affected: with `def open(path)` in `pkg/files.py`, a bare `open("f")` in another module gets no link. So this looks specific to class targets.

### Seen on a real tree

On a 280-file Python repo, five calls to the builtin `NotImplementedError` in three files that never import the package's class all link to it:
- `analysis/__init__.py` L185;
- `ml/__init__.py` L10 and L14;
- `indicators/base.py` L147 and L157. That file imports a *different* name from the same `exceptions` module.

Three links are tagged `INFERRED`. The two from `indicators/base.py` are tagged **`EXTRACTED`**, "explicit in the source". I did not isolate what makes the tag differ; the minimal tree gives `INFERRED`.

`BENCHMARKS.md` says the resolver "prefers no edge over a wrong one" on production cross-file edges. This is a production cross-file edge that should not exist. Exception classes named like builtins are a common pattern in Python packages (`NotImplementedError`, `TimeoutError`, `ConnectionError`…), so this probably reaches beyond one repo.

Context: this came out of a hands-on comparison on a pinned tree, written up with every pre-registered expectation and the re-check above: https://github.com/kogriv/codemap/blob/main/research/tools/graphify.md (§1, §3). Happy to be told if I misread the intent.

title: fix(markdown): don't drop a dotted mention whose method name is a language builtin
body:
## Summary
A dotted code-span mention whose method name collides with a language builtin — e.g. `` `Repository.open` `` — is silently dropped, producing **no `references` edge**, even though its qualifier proves the reference.

## Root cause
In `graphify/markdown_resolution.py`, the builtin-exclusion runs for *every* non-path mention, before qualifier evidence is considered:
```python
callee = names[-1]
if callee in _LANGUAGE_BUILTIN_GLOBALS:   # fires for `Repository.open` too
    return None, "INFERRED", 0.95
```
So `Repository.open` is discarded because `open` is a builtin — contradicting the module's own contract ("a candidate survives only when every qualifier is a label on its contains/method owner chain… `Widget.render` picks the render that `Widget` owns"). Builtin-named methods (`open`, `get`, `set`, `list`, `map`, `filter`, `update`, `type`, `sum`, `next`…) are pervasive, so many real cross-references vanish; `Repository.connect` (non-builtin) resolves fine.

## Fix
Apply the builtin filter only to **bare** single-name mentions:
```python
if len(names) == 1 and callee in _LANGUAGE_BUILTIN_GLOBALS:
    return None, "INFERRED", 0.95
```
A dotted mention proceeds to normal candidate matching, which still requires the qualifier to be a label on the owner chain (so `time.sleep` still won't bind to a repo's own `sleep`).

## Testing
Added `test_dotted_mention_resolves_when_method_name_is_a_builtin`: a `Repository` class with a builtin-named `.open()` method and a doc citing `Repository.open`.
- Before: `.open()` yields no edge (only `.connect()` resolves) — test fails.
- After: both resolve. Full `tests/test_markdown_code_spans.py` → 16 passed; `test_language_resolvers.py` green; the `time.sleep` negative control still refuses to bind.

title: test(hooks): isolate ambient venv and PATH in _detect_run
body:
## Problem

`tests/test_hooks.py::test_shebang_parse_requires_leading_hash_bang` fails for a contributor who follows CONTRIBUTING and runs the suite with `uv run pytest`. `_detect_run` inherits the ambient environment, so `VIRTUAL_ENV` points at the project `.venv` and `PATH` puts that venv's `python` first. The emitted detector then adopts the project interpreter instead of the uv-tool venv the `_broken_uv_machine` fixture constructs, and the test's `RESOLVED=` assertion fails. The repository rule "Tests must not depend on the contributor's ambient environment" is violated by the helper.

## Implementation

In `_detect_run`, after copying `os.environ`:

- Remove `VIRTUAL_ENV`, `PYTHONHOME`, `PYTHONPATH` and `CONDA_PREFIX`.
- Rebuild `PATH` from the fixture's stub bin plus `os.defpath` instead of prepending to the ambient PATH.

No production code changes.

- `uv run ruff check tests/test_hooks.py` (no new findings).

## Limitations

The helper is test-only; the emitted detector's preference for an active venv is intentional runtime behaviour and is not changed.

title: TypeScript import() type annotations emit false dynamic_import edges and virtual source_file paths
body:
TypeScript `import()` type expressions produce false runtime `dynamic_import` edges and external stub nodes with a package name in `source_file`.

Reproduced with `graphifyy` **0.9.82** and **0.9.101**, CPython 3.13 on macOS arm64. The example uses only native AST extraction. No LLM or API key is required.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from importlib.metadata import version
from graphify.extract import extract_js

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "example.ts"
    path.write_text(
        "export function accept(page: import('@playwright/test').Page): void {}\n"
    )
    graph = extract_js(path)

print(version("graphifyy"))
print([e["relation"] for e in graph["edges"]
       if e["relation"] == "dynamic_import"])
print([n["source_file"] for n in graph["nodes"]
       if n.get("source_file") == "@playwright/test"])
```

Both versions return:

```text
['dynamic_import']
['@playwright/test']
```

Expected: no runtime `dynamic_import` edge. An explicitly typed reference could still represent the type dependency. A package specifier should not act as a local source path.

The [TypeScript module reference](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/modules/reference.html#import-types) describes `import()` types as type syntax for referring to a module without an import declaration.

The tree-sitter parse has no errors. The matched `import` token is under `type_annotation` and `required_parameter`. `_rescue_js_dynamic_imports()` scans the original source with a regex and emits an edge without this AST context. `_emit_rescued_import()` also creates the stub with `source_file="@playwright/test"`.

In a full 0.9.82 corpus, the same false edge and stub reached `graph.json`. A strict local-source validator then rejected the package specifier. A native replay reproduced the entire graph from the semantic cache. Suppressing only this verified type-only rescue removed exactly the false edge and isolated stub. Every retained node, edge, and hyperedge remained identical. The real static import at line 1 remained present. No model calls were needed for that replay.

A runtime control, `export async function load() { return await import('@playwright/test'); }`, still emits import edges on both versions. A fix should preserve real runtime imports while excluding type positions from the runtime rescue pass.

Related: https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/issues/3210 addresses runtime imports removed by the type normalizer. This case adds a false runtime dependency from a type annotation instead.

title: a
[Bug]: Python calls from _main() are also attributed to main()
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

When a Python file defines both main() and _main(), Graphify's underscore normalization causes their base node IDs to collide. The primary extractor keeps their declaration nodes distinct, but with an imported call inside _main(), the import-aware resolution pass also attributes that call to main().

The extra calls edge is marked EXTRACTED and points at a line inside _main(), so graph consumers see a high-confidence relationship that is not present in the source.

Expected: distinct function nodes and correctly attributed calls, without the extra edge.

This also affects other top-level names that normalize to the same ID, such as invoke_scheduler() and _invoke_scheduler().

### Steps to reproduce

```shell
# In an empty directory, create targets.py:
cat > targets.py <<'PY'
def alpha():
    return 1

def beta():
    return 2
PY

# Create cli.py:
cat > cli.py <<'PY'
from targets import alpha, beta

def _main():
    return beta()

def main():
    return alpha()
PY

# Build the graph:
GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none graphify update . --no-cluster

# Open graphify-out/graph.json and inspect the "calls" edges.
# Resolve their source and target node IDs to function names.
# The observed and expected edges are listed in the next field.
```

### Error output or graph output

```text
Observed on unpatched Graphify:

Caller     Target     Location     Confidence    Result
_main()    beta()     cli.py:L4    EXTRACTED     Correct
main()     beta()     cli.py:L4    EXTRACTED     INCORRECT
main()     alpha()    cli.py:L7    EXTRACTED     Correct

Expected:
_main() -> beta()     cli.py:L4
main()  -> alpha()    cli.py:L7

The patched version produces exactly these two expected calls edges, with both function declaration nodes retained.
```

### Graphify version

0.9.102

### Operating System

WSL

### Python Version

3.13

### Installation Method

built from source (git clone)

### Additional Environment Details

Python 3.14.4

Reproduced under WSL/Linux using a clean checkout of Graphify's upstream development branch (v8), commit 59b5ab1151e031fb42e39cfc9a50bf96f2d57ae0.

Dependencies installed using uv sync --all-extras --frozen. Reproduction uses GRAPHIFY_BACKEND=none; no external model backend is required.


### Additional context

**Cause**

The primary AST extractor distinguishes colliding function names by adding a short hash to their node IDs (related to #3302). The later import-aware resolution pass reconstructs top-level caller IDs without applying the same policy.

In [`_python_top_level_function_bodies()`](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify/blob/59b5ab1151e031fb42e39cfc9a50bf96f2d57ae0/graphify/extractors/resolution.py#L3137-L3147), the unpatched code uses:

`bodies.append((_make_id(stem, _read_text(name_node, source)), body))`

Because `_make_id(stem, "_main") == _make_id(stem, "main")`, the second pass gives `_main()`'s body the ID of the existing `main()` node.

**Verification**

- Minimal reproduction: 3 `calls` edges before the fix (1 incorrect), 2 afterward (both correct).
- Seven regression tests: 6 failed and 1 passed before the fix (the passing test was the no-collision control); all 7 passed afterward.
- Full upstream pytest suite, neighboring Python tests, Ruff and skill-generation check passed with the fix applied.
- Pyright: zero new diagnostics relative to unmodified upstream.

**Scope**

I've verified this path for top-level functions. I have not comprehensively audited methods, nested functions or other secondary resolution paths.

When applying the patch without changing the installed Graphify version, an update on unchanged source files can retain old incorrect edges. An explicit rebuild with `graphify update . --force` re-extracts the source.

The fix and regression tests are available in [my fork](https://github.com/geirp/graphify/tree/fix/python-imported-call-caller-collision).

title: fix(yaml): give earlier map precedence in a << merge sequence
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a YAML merge-key **precedence** bug in the structural YAML extractor
(`graphify/extractors/yaml_config.py`, `_mapping_pairs`).

For a sequence merge `<<: [*a, *b]`, the YAML 1.1 merge spec gives the **earlier**
map precedence over the later one, and PyYAML's `safe_load` / `flatten_mapping`
honor this (flatten reverses the submerge so the first map's keys win). The
extractor instead fed the merge sources forward into a last-write-wins dict, so a
key defined in both anchors ended up resolving to the **later** map's value and
line — the opposite of the spec and of `safe_load`.

Concretely, given:

```yaml
x-a: &a
  common:
    from_a: 1
x-b: &b
  common:
    from_b: 2
services:
  web:
    <<: [*a, *b]
```

`yaml.safe_load(...)["services"]["web"]["common"]` is `*a`'s mapping (`from_a`,
whose key is at L2), but the extractor was emitting the `web.common` node at `*b`'s
line (L5).

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant protected: the extractor's "keys as written" view
(`_mapping_pairs` over the composed node tree) must agree with the value PyYAML
actually constructs via `safe_load`. The fix feeds the merge sources in reverse,
mirroring `flatten_mapping`, so the earliest map keeps the final value/line.

Fail-pre / pass-post evidence (new test
`tests/test_yaml_extraction.py::test_merge_key_sequence_earlier_map_wins`):

Before the fix (test fails):

```text
>       assert web_common["source_location"] == "L2"
E       AssertionError: assert 'L5' == 'L2'
E         - L2
E         + L5
tests/test_yaml_extraction.py:220: AssertionError
1 failed in 0.12s
```

After the fix (full file passes, incl. the existing merge test):

```text
..................                                                       [100%]
18 passed in 0.23s
```

title: test(reflect): characterize _is_stale across changed/unchanged/vanished sources
body:
## What

Adds three characterization tests for the learning-overlay staleness check `_is_stale` in `graphify/reflect.py`. These lock in the **existing, correct** behavior at the helper level — complementing the loader-level tests already in `tests/test_reflect.py` that exercise the same logic end-to-end through `load_learning_overlay`.

This is **not a bug fix**. No production code is touched; the behavior under test is already correct. The tests simply pin it down so future refactors of the fingerprint/resolution path can't silently regress it.

## Behavior characterized

`_is_stale` recomputes the source file's content hash and compares it to the fingerprint the writer stored, using the same file resolution + hash as the writer (`_code_fingerprint`):

- **unchanged source** (stored fingerprint still matches) -> fresh (`False`)
- **changed source content** -> stale (`True`)
- **vanished / unresolvable source path** -> stale (`True`) — the deliberate over-flagging (safe) direction for a re-verify hint

Each test seeds the stored fingerprint via the writer's own `_code_fingerprint`, documenting that writer and reader agree on an unchanged file, then asserts the baseline before mutating.

## Verification

```
$ uv run pytest tests/test_reflect.py -q
62 passed in 2.90s

$ uv run pytest tests/test_reflect.py -q -k is_stale
3 passed, 59 deselected in 0.20s

$ uv run ruff check
All checks passed!
```

Tests only; no runtime/behavior change.

title: fix(resolution): attribute a call inside `_main` to `_main`, not `main`
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4994.

When a module declares both `main()` and `_main()`, a call on an imported symbol made from inside `_main()` was emitted twice: once correctly from `_main()`, and once more from `main()` — marked `EXTRACTED`, pointing at a line inside `_main()`.

`ids.py:make_id` strips the underscore edges off each part, so `_main` and `main` collapse onto one plain id. The AST extractor already handles that: `_python_pre_scan_underscore_collisions` salts the colliding group apart (#3302) and leaves the plain id on the unique public spelling, so `main()` keeps `cli_main` and `_main()` gets `cli_main_<hash>`. The import-aware symbol pass (`_apply_symbol_resolution_facts`) walked the top-level defs on its own and rebuilt each caller id straight from the bare name, so `_main` arrived as `cli_main` too — the public sibling's node.

The fix resolves the caller against the graph at that point in the pipeline: node ids, edges and `raw_calls` are all final there, so when the id is shared by more than one declaration, the one whose `source_location` encloses the call line is the caller. A name with no collision never enters the branch, so it keeps exactly the behaviour it had.

I left `_python_top_level_function_bodies` returning the plain id on purpose rather than re-deriving the salt there: the fact collector is otherwise node-identity-blind, and duplicating the id policy in a second place is what drifted in the first place. The docstring says so.

Scope: top-level functions, matching the report. Nested functions and methods go through different id paths and I did not touch them. On an incremental rebuild over unchanged files the old edges can survive — `graphify update . --force` re-extracts.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The invariant: a `calls` edge carries the id of the declaration whose body actually contains the call site. Underscore-normalized siblings may share a plain id, but they never share a body, so the caller is decidable from `(source_file, line)` — this change only ever moves a caller onto another node the graph already has, in the same file.

title: fix(python): don't bind bare builtin calls to same-named package classes (#4989)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4989.

A bare Python name resolves through the caller module's own bindings. The cross-file call resolver matched bare callees by label across the whole corpus. A module that never bound `NotImplementedError` linked to a package class with that name. The only builtin guard was `_LANGUAGE_BUILTIN_GLOBALS`, which contains `open` but not the builtin exception classes.

The same wrong edge could be tagged `EXTRACTED` when the caller imported some other name from the file that defines the class, because module-level import evidence counted as proof for the symbol.

This change gives builtin-named Python callees one rule:

```text
resolve(bare_python_call)
  candidates = label_index[callee]
  tgt = unique candidate (or tie-breaker winner)
+ if callee is a Python builtin and tgt was not imported as a symbol by this file
+   emit no edge
  emit calls(tgt)
```

The builtin list is `_PYTHON_BUILTIN_NAMES` in `graphify/extractors/base.py`. It stays separate from `_LANGUAGE_BUILTIN_GLOBALS` because that set gates extraction, where dropping the raw call would also drop the evidence for an imported class that shares a builtin name.

```text
graphify/extractors/base.py   # fixed Python builtin name set
graphify/extract.py           # direct-symbol-import gate for builtin names
tests/test_python_builtin_call_shadowing_4989.py
```

```text

pkg/base.py | todo3() -> NotImplementedError @ pkg/errors.py | EXTRACTED   # imported a different name from the same module
pkg/a.py    | todo()  -> NotImplementedError @ pkg/errors.py | INFERRED
```

**After:**


**Tests:**

```text
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_python_builtin_call_shadowing_4989.py -q
```

The tests pin:

title: [Bug]: Solidity: emit E() and revert Err() get no edge to the event / error they name
fix(solidity): link emit, revert and require to the event or error they name
body:
Closes #5000

## What does this PR do?

While measuring Solidity calls against the compiler I found that no function is ever linked to the event or error it uses. `emit E(..)` and `revert Err(..)` are statements, not `call_expression`s, so the body walk in `extract_solidity` skipped them.

I link them as `calls` edges, the same way Python links `raise Err()` (a call of the class):

1. **Same contract:** events and errors go into the same `(name, arity)` table as functions, so `revert NotOwner(x)` and `emit Withdrawn(a, b)` bind like a normal call. `require(cond, Err(..))` is a plain call of the error, so it resolves too.
2. **Base contract:** if the name is not declared in the caller's contract, it goes through the existing linearized-bases pass (`resolve_solidity_inherited_calls`), like an inherited call.
3. **Qualified, other file:** `revert Errors.InsufficientBalance(..)` looks up `Errors` among the types the caller's file declares or imports directly (the same scope `resolve_solidity_type_references` uses), then the member by name and arity.

Every step fails closed: no edge when the name or the (name, arity) pair is ambiguous. Event and error nodes now carry `metadata.arity`. Node ids do not change. AST cache schema 37 -> 38 because Solidity output changes.

Diff: `graphify/extractors/solidity.py` +90 / -8, 3 new tests in `tests/test_solidity_extractor.py`.

### Numbers

OpenZeppelin Contracts v5.4.0 (319 files), compared with the solc 0.8.28 AST (`referencedDeclaration`):

| link kind | compiler | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `revert Err()` / `require(c, Err())` -> error | 403 | 0 | **401** |
| `emit E()` -> event | 119 | 0 | **119** |
| same-contract / inherited / super / modifier calls | 936 / 268 / 176 / 113 | 778 / 268 / 173 / 113 | unchanged |
| all links | 2,521 | 53% | **73%** |

### Limitations

- A qualified error inside `require(c, Errors.X())` still goes through the member-call path and is not linked (the 2 remaining `revert` misses).
- Named arguments `emit E({a: 1, b: 2})` count as one argument, like other calls. If an event has a one-argument overload, that could pick the wrong one.
- About 41 new edges start from the wrong function because `_grantRole` and `grantRole` already share one node id (an existing id issue, not changed here).

title: [Bug]: C#: an #if block can close the class early, so later members lose their class and their calls
fix(csharp): blank preprocessor directives and #if branches that derail parsing
body:
Closes #5002

## What does this PR do?

tree-sitter-c-sharp parses `#if` / `#elif` / `#else` / `#endif` with every branch in place. Around a directive its error recovery can close the enclosing class early, so every later member loses its class (repro in the issue).

Before parsing, `extract_csharp` now rewrites the source:

1. Every directive line is blanked (`#if`, `#else`, `#region`, `#pragma`, `#nullable`, `#define`, ...).
2. The first branch of each `#if` group is always kept.
3. A later `#elif` / `#else` branch is also kept, so members that exist only there stay in the graph (#2631, its test in `tests/test_dotnet.py` passes unchanged). It is blanked only when keeping it would derail the parse:
   - its `{}` or `()` do not net to zero on their own (`class A : B {` / `#else` / `class A {`), or
   - it declares a member (name + arity) that a kept branch of the same group already declares (`void Write(Span<char> s)` / `#else` / `void Write(string s)` sharing one body).

Nested groups are decided first. Blanked bytes become spaces and CR/LF are kept, so every byte keeps its line and column. A `#` line inside a comment or a multi-line string is not treated as a directive.

AST cache schema 37 -> 38 because C# output changes. (#5001 also bumps it to 38. Whichever lands second takes 39.)

Diff: `graphify/extract.py` +277 / -3, 5 new tests in `tests/test_csharp_member_calls.py`.

### Numbers

`calls` links that Roslyn resolves on Newtonsoft.Json, Dapper and AutoMapper, and how many graphify finds:

| kind | Roslyn | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| same class | 2819 | 2497 | **2586** |
| inherited | 422 | 302 | **376** |
| static | 948 | 807 | **830** |
| typed receiver | 986 | 680 | **838** |
| generic | 321 | 263 | 264 |
| ctor | 710 | 478 | 474 |
| extension / interface / other | 871 / 188 / 84 | 1 / 104 / 71 | unchanged |
| **total** | 7349 | 5203 (70.8%) | **5544 (75.4%)** |
| wrong `calls` edges | | 288 | **264** |

Per project: Newtonsoft.Json 72.8% -> 79.0%, Dapper 81.2% -> 81.7%, AutoMapper unchanged (55.3%).

The `ctor` drop (-4) comes from five `new JValue(...)` calls inside the partial class `JValue`. Those methods now correctly belong to `JValue`, and the graph keeps one edge per node pair, so the `JValue -> method` edge takes the place of the `calls` edge.

I also tried keeping only the first branch. It scores one link more (5545) but drops `#else`-only members, which breaks #2631.

### Limitations

- 5 of the 40 files with tree-sitter errors still have one. Their leftover spots are balanced alternatives with no member, like `bool Ignored` then `=> false;` / `#else` / `{ get; }` in AutoMapper. They cost no Roslyn links here.
- The duplicate-member check is a text scan of the branch, not a parse.
- Calls inside a kept `#else` branch that the net8.0 build does not compile now show up as edges. That is expected when both branches are kept.

## Verification & Invariants

Invariant: the rewrite never moves a byte. It only turns directive lines and derailing branches into spaces, so every node keeps its real `source_location`. Members in any balanced, non-duplicate branch stay in the graph.

body:
Closes #5004

> Built on #5001 (emit/revert), because it reuses the `qualified` lookup that PR adds. Only the last commit, 28f882c, is new here. I'll rebase onto v8 once #5001 lands.

## What does this PR do?

`Recv.f(..)` with a plain identifier receiver is now parked as a `qualified` call, the same kind `revert Errors.Err()` uses in #5001. It binds through the one library or contract of that name that the caller's file declares or imports directly (named import, whole-file import, or alias `{A as B}`), and then through the member by arity.

Also:
- Free functions resolve qualified calls too. The resolver no longer needs the caller to sit inside a contract, and a function is never linked to itself.
- `require(c, Lib.Err(..))` binds the library error (the 2 `revert` misses left in #5001).
- `!Lib.f(x)` works. The grammar parses it as a call of `(!Lib).f`, so `_callee_text` now strips the unary operator, the same way it already handles `a || b.f()`.

Fails closed: no edge when the name or the (name, arity) pair is ambiguous. A value receiver (`token.transfer()`) names no type, so it gets no edge. Node ids do not change. AST cache schema 38 -> 39.

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `Lib.f()` library call | 208 | 0 | **181** |

| same / inherited / super / modifier / emit | 936 / 268 / 176 / 113 / 119 | 778 / 268 / 173 / 113 / 119 | unchanged |
| `using X for Y` / typed receiver (out of scope) | 221 / 71 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

- Import scope is the existing one: any type in the caller's file or in a file it imports directly. That is slightly wider than a named import allows, and whole-file imports are not followed transitively.
- Aliases match by name only, so `{A as B}` plus a local `A` is ambiguous and gets no edge.

title: [Bug]: Swift: a local with same name as a modifier (prefix, open, final...) used in a switch case body gives a syntax-parse error from tree-sitter-swift
body:
### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

### What happened?

**Summary:**
`tree-sitter-swift` 0.7.4 cannot parse a local value whose name is a Swift contextual modifier when it is used as `return name <operator>` or `return name.member` inside a `switch` case. The grammar reads the identifier as a declaration modifier waiting for a declaration, and the surrounding code collapses into ERROR nodes. Graphify warns about a syntax-parse error at line: X and extracts the file only partially.

Related but distinct: #3540 (another tree-sitter-swift parse failure, `if let x = await ...`).

The trigger is a modifier-named identifier at the start of an expression statement inside a `case` body, followed by an operator or member access.

**Limits and unfixed exceptions** (the fix doesn't cover these, so behavior is unchanged: partial extraction plus the warning):
1. A function parameter named like a modifier. Renaming it would change the argument label and every call site.
2. A closure parameter, as in `xs.map { prefix in ... }`.
3. Tuple destructuring, as in `let (prefix, b) = t`.
4. A file with any other syntax error, because the rewrite is accepted only if the whole file then parses cleanly.
5. Names I haven't tested. The list is only what I verified.

**Covered:** `if let prefix = x`, and a type-scope property with the same name.

**Code change:** added six names that also fail to `extract.py`, the test parametrization, and the changelog: `distributed`, `nonmutating`, `public`, `private`, `internal` and `fileprivate`. 

**Validation:** The Swift tests pass, 36 of 36 in the two files I re-ran after the change. I did not re-run the full suite because it had 8 failures before this change, and they also fail without this fix.

`static`, `class` and `inout` also error, but they are reserved keywords, so `let class = 1` isn't valid Swift.

### Steps to reproduce

**Minimal repro**

let prefix = "x"
switch kind {
case 0:
    return prefix + "a"   // error


| Case body | Result |
|---|---|
| `return prefix + "a"` | **error** |
| `return prefix.count > 0 ? "a" : "b"` | **error** |
| `return prefix` | ok |
| `print(prefix)` | ok |
| `let y = prefix` | ok |
| `x = prefix + "a"` | ok |
| `return "a" + prefix` | ok |
| `return pfx + "a"` (local renamed) | ok |
| `return prefix + "a"` inside `if k == 0 { ... }` instead of a `switch` | ok |
| `return prefix + "a"` after the `switch`, outside any case | ok |

### What happened?

In a long Claude Code session, the graph nudge stops for good. `_nudge_allowed` counts nudges per `session_id` and stops at `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_NUDGE_CAP` (default 5, #3435). When Claude Code compacts the conversation (auto-compact or `/compact`), the session id stays the same, but the model loses the earlier nudges and everything it knew about the graph. The budget is already spent, so for the rest of the session Claude reads raw files and never hears about the graph again.

This hits exactly the users with the longest sessions. In one of my own long sessions on a project with a fresh graph, after a couple of compactions Claude was grepping and reading files with no mention of graphify. The 24h marker clean-up doesn't help inside a working day. Telling users to start a new session isn't a real fix.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
mkdir -p demo/src demo/graphify-out && cd demo
printf 'def run():\n    return 1\n' > src/app.py
echo '{"nodes":[],"links":[]}' > graphify-out/graph.json
R='{"session_id":"s1","hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"Read","tool_input":{"file_path":"'"$PWD"'/src/app.py"}}'
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do echo "$R" | graphify hook-guard read | cut -c1-60; echo; done
# Claude Code now compacts the conversation: same session_id, empty context
echo "$R" | graphify hook-guard read
```

### Error output or graph output

```
reads 1-5: nudge
read 6:    nothing (cap reached, correct)
after compaction: nothing, and nothing for the rest of the session
```
Expected: after a compaction the model starts from an empty context, so it should get the nudge again (still capped).

### Graphify version

0.9.102

### Operating System

Windows

### Python Version

3.12

### Installation Method

uv tool install (recommended)

title: fix(hook): restore the nudge budget after a Claude Code compaction
body:
Closes #5007

## What does this PR do?

After a compaction, Claude Code fires `SessionStart` with `"source": "compact"` and the same `session_id`. I add a Claude Code `SessionStart` hook with matcher `compact` that runs `graphify hook-guard compact`. For that session it:

1. **Resets the nudge budget:** it deletes the session's `<key>.nudges` and every subagent counter `<key>-<16 hex>.nudges`. The match is exact, so other sessions are never touched.
2. **Re-arms strict mode once:** it deletes `<key>.denied`, so `--strict` can redirect one more time. The compacted model lost the first redirect too. It is still at most one deny per compaction.
3. **Prints one short reminder** as `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` (supported for SessionStart, no blocking) when a graph exists, naming `graphify query` / `explain` / `path`.

Sources `startup`, `resume`, `clear` and `fork`, and any other event, reset nothing. The cap, the per-agent keys and the query stamp rules from #3435 are unchanged. Any error prints nothing and exits 0.

`graphify install` adds the entry the same way it merges the PreToolUse entries. The user's own SessionStart hooks are kept, re-install doesn't duplicate it, and `uninstall` removes it from both `settings.json` and `settings.local.json`. Global `graphify install` still writes no hooks, as on v8.

Diff: `graphify/cli.py` +61 / -1, `graphify/install.py` +40 / -7, one README sentence, 21 tests in the new `tests/test_hook_compact.py`.

### Before / after (the issue's repro)

| step | v8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Read 1-5, main session and subagent | nudge | nudge |
| Read 6 | nothing | nothing |
| SessionStart `startup` / `resume`, then Read | nothing | nothing |
| SessionStart `compact` | nothing | reminder |
| Read, main session and subagent | nothing | **nudge** |
| Read with `--strict` | nothing | **deny** (once) |

I checked the session-id assumption in my own Claude Code session. After a compaction, the `SessionStart` hook with source `compact` fired, and the session kept the same id and transcript file.

### Limitations

- If a future Claude Code version gave a compacted session a new id, that session would already start with a fresh budget, so this hook would do no harm.
- Existing installs need `graphify claude install` again to get the new hook.

title: fix(hook): give Bash file reads (cat, head, sed -n, ...) the read nudge
body:
Closes #5009

## What does this PR do?

A Bash command that runs a file reader now goes through the same Read path as the Read tool: the same read nudge with the file hint, the stale variant, and the same per-agent budget (`GRAPHIFY_HOOK_NUDGE_CAP`). The readers are `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `nl`, `less`, `more`, `bat`, and `sed` with `-n` / `--quiet` / `--silent`. They must run in an executed position and target an existing in-project code file.

To find the reader and its file, I moved the existing command parsing out of `_bash_invokes_search` into a shared `_bash_commands` helper. That is the parsing that skips comments and quoted text and only looks at executed positions (#3121). Search detection is unchanged. The new parts are `_bash_read_target` and a small dispatch in `_run_hook_guard`.

It never blocks. Bash stays nudge-only, also with `--strict`, `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT=1`, or a missing `tool_name`. The Read tool is still denied as before.

It stays silent (and spends no budget) for:
- doc files: `cat README.md` (the existing v8 tests pin this), `.txt`, `.rst`, `.mdx`, and `cat package.json`
- writes: `cat > src/x.py`, `sed -i ...`
- piped stdin: `echo x | cat`
- `graphify-out/` and files outside the project (#1840, #4961)

Diff: `graphify/cli.py` +157 / -38 (most of it is the moved parser), a few README words, 51 tests in the new `tests/test_hook_bash_read.py`.

### Before / after (the issue's repro)

| command | v8 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `cat src/app.py` | nothing | read nudge, the same text as a Read of that file (with its node hint when the graph has nodes for it) |
| `sed -n 1,80p src/app.py` | search nudge, no hint | read nudge + hint |
| `head -50` / `tail` / `nl` / `less` / `more` / `bat` on `src/app.py` | nothing | read nudge + hint |
| `cat README.md`, `cat > src/x.py`, `sed -i`, `echo x \| cat`, `cat graphify-out/graph.json`, outside file | nothing | nothing |
| `grep -rn run src` | search nudge | search nudge (unchanged) |

### Limitations

- `cd src && cat app.py`: a `cd` earlier in the same command is not tracked, so it stays silent.
- Quoted paths (`cat "src/app.py"`) and globs (`cat src/*.py`) are not detected. The shared parser blanks quoted text before reading arguments.
- When a reader and a search share one command (`cat a.py | grep x`), the read nudge wins.
- Bash skips the doc extensions (`.md`, `.txt`, `.rst`, `.mdx`) that the Read tool nudges on, to keep the existing `cat README.md` behaviour.

title: fix(install): write the pi project skill to .pi/skills, where Pi reads it (#5011)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #5011

`graphify install --project --platform pi` wrote the skill to `./.pi/agent/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`. That is the user-scope shape (`~/.pi/agent/skills`). Pi reads project skills from `.pi/skills/` (its configuration docs list `.pi/skills/` as "Project skills and supporting files"), so the installed skill never loaded and there was no error: no `/skill:graphify`, and the model reported no graphify skill.

Cause: `_platform_skill_destination()` falls through to `(project_dir or Path(".")) / cfg["skill_dst"]` for `pi`, and `_PLATFORM_CONFIG["pi"]["skill_dst"]` is the `$HOME` path. `gemini`, `opencode`, `hermes`, `devin` and `amp` each special-case the project path; `pi` did not. Same class as #1040 and #2319.

## Change

- `graphify/install.py`: a `pi` branch in `_platform_skill_destination()`: project scope resolves to `.pi/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`, user scope stays `~/.pi/agent/skills/graphify/SKILL.md`. Install, uninstall and the version stamp all go through this resolver, so they agree.
- `graphify/detect.py`: comment only. The `(".pi", "agent")` entry in `_NESTED_SKILL_HOLDERS` stays, because projects installed before this change still carry `.pi/agent/skills/graphify/` and it must stay pruned; `.pi/skills/graphify/` is already pruned by the generic hidden-holder rule.

## Tests

`tests/test_pi_install.py`, four cases: project install lands in `.pi/skills` and creates no `.pi/agent`; user install still lands in `~/.pi/agent/skills`; `_remove_skill_file` resolves the same project path after install; the resolver itself for both scopes.

I could not run `uv run pytest` here; the tests follow `tests/test_devin.py` and I am relying on CI for the run.

## Checked by hand

Reporter's repro: with the installer's path Pi lists `obsidian, superdesign, treg`; after moving the same file to `.pi/skills/graphify/` it lists `graphify` too. The change produces that second path directly.

title: [Feature]: Opt-in Firecrawl fetcher for `graphify add <url>` on JavaScript-rendered pages
body:
Hey, I'm Juampi from the Firecrawl team.

### Problem or use case

`graphify add <url>` saves generic webpages through `_fetch_webpage` in `graphify/ingest.py`, which downloads the HTML with `safe_fetch_text` and converts it with markdownify. Pages that render their content with JavaScript come back as an empty shell. For example, `graphify add https://hn.algolia.com/` saves 85 characters of page text, the title plus "This page will only work with JavaScript enabled", so the next graph update has almost nothing to extract from that source.

### Proposed solution

An opt-in fetcher for generic webpages, chosen per call with `graphify add <url> --fetcher firecrawl`.

- The flag is the only switch. Without it, `safe_fetch_text` plus markdownify stays the path, and no environment variable changes behavior on its own.
- With the flag, `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` is read. A missing key, an HTTP error or a response with `success: false` exits with a clear error and writes nothing, with no fallback to the default fetcher.
- `validate_url` still runs first. The request goes to Firecrawl /v2/scrape with `formats: ["markdown"]`, `onlyMainContent: true` and `origin: "graphify"`. The returned Markdown is treated as untrusted text and saved with the same frontmatter, 12,000 character cap and filename logic as `_fetch_webpage`.
- Firecrawl fetches the page from its own servers, so the URL goes to a third party and DNS and redirects resolve there. The flag's help text, the README Privacy section and the optional network calls list in SECURITY.md would say so.
- An unknown `--fetcher` value exits with an error, since `graphify add` ignores unknown flags today.
- Tweets, arXiv, PDFs, images and YouTube keep their current handlers.

### Alternatives considered

A local headless browser also renders the page, but it is a heavy install and a larger untrusted surface on the user's machine. Selecting Firecrawl automatically whenever the key is set was ruled out, because ambient environment state would then change what gets saved.

### Area

CLI or installation

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

Yes, I can work on this

### Compatibility / behavior impact

Nothing changes unless the flag is passed. ID rules, cache semantics, the `graph.json` schema and MCP output stay the same, and the saved file keeps its format. Only the captured text differs, which can change the nodes and edges extracted from that source. `ingest()` gains an optional `fetcher` argument that defaults to today's behavior. Generated skills stay as they are; letting `/graphify add` pass the flag would mean editing `add-watch.md` and running skillgen, which I'd leave for a second PR. Tests would stub the HTTP call (success, missing key, HTTP error, `success: false`, URL rejected before any request) and clear `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, so they stay offline and independent of the contributor's shell.

### Additional context

Firecrawl /scrape docs: https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/scrape?utm_source=graphify&utm_medium=integration

Happy to change the flag name or scope to whatever fits the CLI.

title: [Bug]: graphify update skips or partially rebuilds a missing graph when the manifest survives
body:
### Reproduction

Confirmed on `v8` at `59b5ab11` (0.9.102), Python 3.12 on Windows. No LLM or API credentials are needed.

1. Put `def first(): return 1` in `first.py` and `def second(): return 2` in `second.py` in a clean directory.
2. Run `graphify update . --no-cluster`.
3. Delete only `graphify-out/graph.json`. Leave `graphify-out/manifest.json` in place.
4. Run the same update again. Repeat after changing just `first.py`.

### Actual behavior

With no source changes, update exits successfully without recreating the file. With one changed source, it creates a graph containing only that source. The manifest identifies changed bytes but cannot supply unchanged nodes and edges.

### Expected behavior

Recreate the complete AST graph using the existing full rebuild path whenever the output graph is absent.

This is a follow-up to the manifest-derived update path in #4801.

title: [Bug]: incremental update leaves stale TypeScript imports after an alias-only change
body:
### Reproduction

Confirmed on `v8` at `59b5ab11` (0.9.102), Python 3.12 on Windows. No LLM or API credentials are needed.

1. Put `export function target() {}` in both `old/target.ts` and `new/target.ts`.
2. In `main.ts`, import `target` from `@app/target` and call it from an exported function.
3. Set `compilerOptions.baseUrl` to `.` and `compilerOptions.paths` to `{"@app/*":["./old/*"]}` in `tsconfig.json`.
4. Run `graphify update . --no-cluster`. Change only the alias to `./new/*` and run the same command.

### Actual behavior

The `imports_from` edge still points to `old/target.ts`. Adding or deleting the config also leaves the unchanged importer unresolved or attached to the old file.

### Expected behavior

The edge should match a fresh rebuild after the resolver input changes, even when the importer bytes are unchanged.

This is a follow-up to #4801. It uses the resolution-input classification introduced for the no-change gate in #4748.

title: [Bug]: concurrent graphify add captures can overwrite each other
body:
### Reproduction

Confirmed on `v8` at `59b5ab11` (0.9.102), Python 3.12 on Windows. No LLM or API credentials are needed.

Call `graphify.ingest.ingest` concurrently for `https://example.org/report.pdf?capture=1` and `https://example.org/report.pdf?capture=2` in the same output directory. For an offline reproduction, stub `validate_url` and `safe_fetch` and pause both calls immediately after `Path.lstat()` reports that `example_org_report_pdf.pdf` is absent. The regression also reproduces the same race for captured Markdown.

### Actual behavior

Both callers select and return the same path. Only one payload survives even though both calls report success.

### Expected behavior

Each capture should save its own bytes. The later claimant should use the next available numbered filename.

This covers the concurrent case explicitly left open by the sequential fixes in #4394 and #4657.

title: [Bug]: malformed learning sidecar data can hide valid annotations
body:
### Reproduction

Confirmed on `v8` at `59b5ab11` (0.9.102), Python 3.12 on Windows. No LLM or API credentials are needed.

Next to `graph.json`, save `.graphify_learning.json` containing `{"nodes":{"bad":{"source_file":["app.py"]},"good":{"status":"preferred","score":2}}}`. Call `graphify.reflect.load_learning_overlay` with the graph path. A second reproduction is a sidecar containing JSON `null` or `[]`.

### Actual behavior

A non-string source raises `TypeError` while resolving a path. The MCP loader catches the exception and drops the entire overlay, including healthy entries. A non-object JSON root raises `AttributeError` before entries are read.

### Expected behavior

Treat a malformed root as an empty optional overlay, and keep healthy entries when an individual row is malformed.

The change concerns sidecar input handling. The staleness characterization in #4996 exercises the existing behavior for well-formed entries.

title: [Bug]: valid JSON with the wrong global-manifest shape bypasses recovery
body:
### Reproduction

Confirmed on `v8` at `59b5ab11` (0.9.102), Python 3.12 on Windows. No LLM or API credentials are needed.

In a disposable home directory, create `~/.graphify/global-manifest.json` with `null` and run `graphify global list`. Repeat with `{"repos":[]}` or `{"repos":{"example":"invalid"}}`.

### Actual behavior

The JSON decoder succeeds, but consumers receive the wrong shape. Depending on the value, a command crashes or reports an empty graph without preserving the malformed manifest as a recovery backup.

### Expected behavior

Use the same backup and warning path as for invalid JSON syntax. A well-formed manifest should continue to load unchanged.

This extends the recovery added in #1207 to JSON that parses successfully but has the wrong shape.

4. Run `graphify update . --no-cluster`. Change only the alias to `./new/*` and run the same command.

title: fix(cache): keep the \\?\ long-path spelling out of cache identity
body:
## What does this PR do?

Since 0.9.101, every `graphify update` on Windows that re-extracts something prints

```text
RuntimeWarning: stat index switched from cache root '\\\\?\\E:\\...\\repo' to 'E:\\...\\repo' within one process; ... (#3989)
```

and writes `graphify-out/cache/stat-index.json` with absolute keys, so a moved or copied checkout re-hashes every file (#2199). There's no issue for it. I found it running the test suite on Windows, where three tests in `test_stat_index_portability.py` and `test_file_hash_is_order_independent_across_roots` fail on v8. CI only runs on Linux, where `os_long_path()` and `_normalize_path()` return the path unchanged, so it doesn't show up there.

It comes from 99b8da7/ff8ddf5 (#4925, #4937). Opening files through `os_long_path()` is right, but the `\\?\` spelling also reached cache identity:

- `file_hash()` and `cached_word_count()` bound the stat index to the prefixed root. `extract()` passes the plain `cache_root`, so one root looked like two: the warning above, plus a flush and reload mid-run. No key was relative to the prefixed anchor, so every key was written absolute.
- The walked-parent check in `file_hash()` compared a plain path with the prefixed root and never matched. Under a junctioned or symlinked scan root, an in-root alias got its target's salt and digest, which is the #2832 case again.
- The out-of-root salt picked up a `//?/` prefix.
- `_normalize_path()` only strips `\\?\`, so the UNC form `\\?\UNC\server\share` turned into a relative `UNC\server\...` key that the flush pruned as missing. A corpus on a network or WSL share always wrote an empty stat index.

This binds the stat index to the normalized root again (as before 0.9.101), normalizes the resolved path and root before they're used as keys, salts or comparisons, and maps `\\?\UNC\` back to `\\`. File I/O still goes through `os_long_path()`.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

Cache identity uses the normalized spelling and `\\?\` is only for I/O, which is what 99b8da7's own message says ("The stat-index key comes from the normalized identity"). One project root binds the stat index once, on-disk keys stay relative to the corpus, and an alias keeps its own walked salt.

Persisted state: changed keys and salts only cause cache misses. Absolute stat-index keys written by 0.9.101/0.9.102 still load and are rewritten relative on the next flush, which `test_legacy_absolute_index_migrates_gracefully` covers. Limitations: under a junctioned or symlinked scan root, an AST entry that 0.9.101/0.9.102 wrote under an alias's shared digest stays in place for the target until that file changes. A schema bump would clear it. I didn't bump `_AST_CACHE_SCHEMA` here since you batch those. stat-index.json itself is still opened by its plain path, as before 0.9.101.

```text
FAILED tests/test_stat_index_portability.py::test_deleted_entries_are_pruned_on_flush
FAILED tests/test_stat_index_portability.py::test_legacy_absolute_index_migrates_gracefully

All checks passed!

python -m pytest tests/ -q -n 4        (uv venv, pytest-xdist)
```

All 20 full-suite failures also fail on v8 and are unrelated Windows or environment test issues: POSIX path literals in tests, `bash` resolving to the WSL launcher, parallel extract/terraform tests that pass when run serially, and so on.

Also checked by hand:

title: [Bug]: query drops a distinct node that has the same label as a seed, and the per-term seed guarantee does not hold
body:
## Pre-flight checks
- [x] I have checked the Troubleshooting section in the README

## Graphify version
0.9.102 (latest release; `v8` branch has the same `serve.py`)

## What happened?
`_pick_seeds` removes any seed candidate whose normalized label is already a seed (#1766). This also applies to the "one seed for each query term" step (#1445).

Two different nodes can share a label. Example: two classes named `PreToolUse` in two different plugins. When their scores are close, only the higher one is a seed. The other is dropped, even when it is the only node that matches one of the query terms.

In the repro below, the query names `alpha`. Only the `alpha` node matches that term (`best_seed_by_term["alpha"] == "alpha_pre"`). That node has a lower score (29.11 against 29.81), so it is dropped. The result has no seed for `alpha`, and the node is not in the output.

The docstring of `_pick_seeds` says the step "guarantees at least one seed per distinct query term that has any match at all". The label cap breaks this guarantee.

I expect #1766 to stay. It prevents many `GET()` handlers from filling the seeds. I ask for a narrower rule.

## Steps to reproduce
Create `graph_a.json`:

```python
import json
def node(i, label, src):
    return {"id": i, "label": label, "source_file": src, "file_type": "code"}
nodes = [
    node("hooks_pre", "PreToolUse", "plugins/core/lib/core_hooks/handler/pre_tool_use.rb"),
    node("hooks_run", ".run", "plugins/core/lib/core_hooks/handler/pre_tool_use.rb"),
    node("alpha_pre", "PreToolUse", "plugins/core-alpha/lib/alpha/pre_tool_use.rb"),
]
links = [{"source": "hooks_pre", "target": "hooks_run", "relation": "contains", "confidence": "EXTRACTED"}]
json.dump({"directed": False, "multigraph": False, "graph": {}, "nodes": nodes, "links": links},
          open("graph_a.json", "w"))
```

```shell
graphify query "core alpha PreToolUse hook handler" --graph graph_a.json
grep -c alpha <(graphify query "core alpha PreToolUse hook handler" --graph graph_a.json --budget 5000)
```

## Error output or graph output
```text
| Traversal: BFS depth=2 | Start: ['PreToolUse', '.run'] | 2 nodes found

NODE PreToolUse [src=plugins/core/lib/core_hooks/handler/pre_tool_use.rb ...]
NODE .run [src=plugins/core/lib/core_hooks/handler/pre_tool_use.rb ...]
```

No `plugins/core-alpha/...` node is in the output, and the `grep -c alpha` count is 0.

In-process, with `_score_query` and `_pick_seeds`:

```text
29.81 hooks_pre
29.11 alpha_pre
 2.08 hooks_run
best_seed_by_term: {'core': 'hooks_run', 'pretooluse': 'hooks_pre', 'hook': 'hooks_run',
                    'handler': 'hooks_run', 'alpha': 'alpha_pre'}
seeds: ['hooks_pre', 'hooks_run']
```

Expected: `alpha_pre` is a seed, because it is the best match for the term `alpha` and no other seed covers that term.

## Source reference
`graphify/serve.py`, `_pick_seeds`: the `seen_labels` check in the first loop, and the `key not in seen_labels` check in the per-term loop.

## Suggested direction (optional)
Apply the label cap only to a candidate that adds no uncovered query term. A candidate that is the best match for a term with no seed yet should be kept.

## Related
- #1766 (adds the label de-duplication)
- #1445 (per-term seed guarantee)
- #1303 (tied scores in seed selection)

## Environment
- Operating System: Linux
- Python Version: 3.12
- Installation Method: `uv tool install` (graphifyy 0.9.102)

title: fix(query): preserve per-term seed guarantee when distinct node shares label (#5027)
body:
## Summary
Fixes #5027.

In `_pick_seeds()`, seed candidates are deduplicated by normalized label to prevent generic symbols (e.g. repeated `GET()` route handlers) from consuming all BFS seed slots (#1766). However, the deduplication cap was also unconditionally applied in the per-term seed guarantee loop (#1445). When two distinct nodes in different packages share a label (such as `PreToolUse` in core vs an extension) and one of them is the best (or sole) match for an uncovered query term, it was discarded because the normalized label had already been seen from the other node. Consequently, the per-term seed guarantee failed and the query returned zero matches for that term.

## Changes
- In `graphify/serve.py` (`_pick_seeds`): Track `covered_terms` in the per-term guarantee loop. Only apply the `seen_labels` cap when the candidate covers no uncovered query terms (`key not in seen_labels or term not in covered_terms`).
- In `tests/test_serve.py`: Added `test_pick_seeds_preserves_per_term_guarantee_for_distinct_node_with_shared_label` reproducing the Issue #5027 case with two `PreToolUse` nodes and verifying that #1766 generic-symbol flooding protection continues to hold.

## Test Plan
- `pytest tests/test_serve.py -k "seed or 1766 or 5027"`: all 37 passed.
- `pytest tests/test_serve.py`: 180 passed, 1 skipped.

title: fix(query): keep a same-label seed when it is the only match for a query term (#5027)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5027.

In `_pick_seeds()`, seed candidates are deduplicated by normalized label so that generic symbols (e.g. repeated `GET()` route handlers) cannot take every BFS seed slot (#1766). The same cap was also applied, unconditionally, in the per-term seed guarantee loop (#1445). When two distinct nodes share a label (such as `PreToolUse` in two different plugins) and one of them is the only match for a query term, that node was dropped because its label was already seeded. The term was left with no seed, and the query never reached that node.

## Changes

- In `graphify/serve.py` (`_pick_seeds`): the label cap in the per-term loop now applies only when the term is part of the shared label (`key not in seen_labels or term not in key`). In that case the already-seeded node matches the term through the same label, so the term is covered. Otherwise the candidate won the term through its path, rationale or attributes, so it is kept. The first loop is unchanged. The comments and docstring are updated.
- In `tests/test_serve.py`, I added two tests:
  - `test_pick_seeds_keeps_same_label_node_that_is_only_match_for_a_term`: the issue's 3-node `PreToolUse` repro. It fails before the fix and passes after.
  - `test_pick_seeds_per_term_still_caps_same_label_winner_of_a_label_term`: a second `GET` that wins the term `get` (degree tie-break) is still capped, so the #1766 flooding protection holds. This test fails if the cap is removed entirely. The existing #1766 per-term test cannot catch that, because its winner is already the first-loop seed.

## Test Plan

- `uv run pytest tests/test_serve.py tests/test_query_seed_order.py -q`: 187 passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/ -q`: 10092 passed. 23 failed, the same 23 pre-existing Windows failures as `v8`, so nothing new.

title: graphify watch on Linux: self-sustaining inotify overflow loop on trees with more than ~4,000 directories (most real changes are lost)
body:
## Summary

On Linux, `graphify watch` stops working on any tree with more than roughly 4,000 directories. The inotify event queue
overflows during the initial watch setup. watchdog then rebuilds all recursive watches, which overflows the queue
again, and so on indefinitely. The process stays near 100% CPU and real file changes are mostly lost: in a controlled
test a real write to a `.ts` file reached the handler in only 2 of 8 runs.

The trigger is that `watch()` schedules the observer **without an `event_filter`**. watchdog therefore asks the kernel
for `IN_OPEN` and `IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE` too. The directory walk that watchdog performs to register recursive watches
generates exactly those events, so they flood the queue. Graphify already discards these events in the handler
(`_is_read_only_event`), but by then they have already filled the kernel queue.

Passing `event_filter` to `observer.schedule()` removes those events from the inotify mask and fixes the problem:
with it there were 0 overflows and changes were detected, even with 45,000 directories.

## Environment

- graphifyy 0.9.103 (`pip install graphifyy`, Python venv)
- watchdog 7.1.0
- Python 3.12.3
- Linux 7.0.0-42-generic (Ubuntu), default inotify limits:
  `fs.inotify.max_queued_events = 16384`, `fs.inotify.max_user_watches = 65536`

## What I observed with the real workspace

`graphify watch .` run as a systemd user service on a parent folder with several repositories (50,585 directories
in total, most of them in `node_modules`). A `.graphifyignore` limited the scope to five repositories.

- The process registered 45,885 inotify watches. I counted them in `/proc/<pid>/fdinfo`, and they include ignored
  paths, because `.graphifyignore` is only checked inside the event handler.
- The log repeated these two lines several times per second:
  ```
  Inotify queue overflowed; filesystem events were lost
  Inotify queue overflowed; reconciling recursive watches below b'/home/<user>/sviluppo'
  ```
- CPU stayed at about 95%.
- Almost nothing was written to disk during that time (checked with `find -newermt`), so the overflow was not caused
  by real file activity.

## Minimal reproduction (no Graphify needed, same `schedule()` call as `graphify/watch.py`)

```bash
python3 -m venv /tmp/wd && /tmp/wd/bin/pip install -q watchdog==7.1.0
mkdir -p /tmp/wdtree && (cd /tmp/wdtree && seq 1 5000 | xargs mkdir)
```

```python
# probe.py: python probe.py /tmp/wdtree graphify|filtered
import sys, time, logging, os
from watchdog.observers import Observer
from watchdog.events import (FileSystemEventHandler, FileCreatedEvent, FileModifiedEvent, FileDeletedEvent,
    FileMovedEvent, FileClosedEvent, DirCreatedEvent, DirDeletedEvent, DirMovedEvent)

overflows = 0
class CountOverflows(logging.Handler):
    def emit(self, record):
        global overflows
        if "overflowed" in record.getMessage():
            overflows += 1
logging.getLogger("watchdog").addHandler(CountOverflows())
logging.getLogger("watchdog").setLevel(logging.WARNING)

received = set()
class Handler(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_any_event(self, event):
        received.add(event.event_type)

event_filter = None if sys.argv[2] == "graphify" else [
    FileCreatedEvent, FileModifiedEvent, FileDeletedEvent, FileMovedEvent, FileClosedEvent,
    DirCreatedEvent, DirDeletedEvent, DirMovedEvent]

observer = Observer()
observer.schedule(Handler(), sys.argv[1], recursive=True, event_filter=event_filter)
observer.start()
time.sleep(3)
with open(os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "1", "probe.ts"), "w") as f:   # one real change
    f.write("x")
time.sleep(3)
print(f"{sys.argv[2]:9s} overflows: {overflows:4d} | events received: {sorted(received)}")
observer.stop(); observer.join()
```

Results:

| Directories | `event_filter` | Overflows in 6 s | Real write delivered |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 / 3,000 | none (as Graphify) | 0 | yes |
| 5,000 | none (as Graphify) | 126–132 | **lost in 6 of 8 runs** (`[]`) |
| 45,000 | none (as Graphify) | 26 | **no** (`[]`, 1 run) |
| 5,000 | write events only | 0 | yes (`closed`, `created`, `modified`) |
| 45,000 | write events only | 0 | yes (`closed`, `created`, `modified`) |

The loop also happens with nobody touching the tree. With 10,000 directories and no access at all I got 238
overflows in 15 seconds and zero delivered events.

## Root cause

I instrumented `watchdog.observers.inotify_c.InotifyFD.read_events` on the 5,000-directory tree:

- Events received **before the first overflow**: `IN_OPEN|IN_ISDIR` = 8,193, `IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE|IN_ISDIR` = 8,192.
  That is 16,385 events, exactly the queue size plus the overflow marker. There were no write events at all.
- `_get_or_create_watch` was called 175,035 times in 4 seconds on 5,000 directories, which means about 35 full
  rebuilds of the watch tree.

The sequence:

1. `graphify/watch.py` calls `observer.schedule(handler, str(watch_root_for_ignore), recursive=True)` without
   `event_filter`. In that case `InotifyEmitter.get_event_mask_from_filter()` returns `WATCHDOG_ALL_EVENTS`, which
   includes `IN_OPEN` and `IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE`.
2. To add recursive watches, watchdog walks the tree with `os.walk`. Every `opendir`/`closedir` produces
   `IN_OPEN|IN_ISDIR` and `IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE|IN_ISDIR` on the parent watch, and on the directory's own watch once it
   exists. That is about 4 events per directory, so around 4,000 directories are enough to exceed 16,384 queued events.
3. On `IN_Q_OVERFLOW`, `InotifyWatchGroup.on_queue_overflow()` removes every callback and calls
   `_add_all_callbacks(self.path)`, walking the whole tree again. That walk overflows the queue again, so the
   loop never ends.
4. Real events are dropped with each overflow, so whether a change reaches the handler is a matter of timing
   (2 of 8 runs on 5,000 directories).

`_is_read_only_event()` (filtering `opened` and `closed_no_write`) and the early `.graphifyignore` check in
`on_any_event` keep the *handler* cheap. They act after the kernel has already queued the events, so they cannot
prevent the overflow.

## Suggested fix

Pass an `event_filter` that matches what the handler actually uses, so read-only events never reach the inotify
mask. This also makes `_is_read_only_event()` redundant on Linux.

```python
from watchdog.events import (
    FileCreatedEvent, FileModifiedEvent, FileDeletedEvent, FileMovedEvent, FileClosedEvent,
    DirCreatedEvent, DirDeletedEvent, DirMovedEvent,
)

_WATCH_EVENT_FILTER = [
    FileCreatedEvent, FileModifiedEvent, FileDeletedEvent, FileMovedEvent, FileClosedEvent,
    DirCreatedEvent, DirDeletedEvent, DirMovedEvent,
]

observer.schedule(handler, str(watch_root_for_ignore), recursive=True, event_filter=_WATCH_EVENT_FILTER)
```

`event_filter` is a parameter of `BaseObserver.schedule()` (verified on watchdog 7.1.0), so `PollingObserver` (macOS)
accepts it as well.

## Related problem (separate, lower priority): ignored directories still get watches

Even with the fix above, `watch` places one inotify watch on **every** directory under the root, including those
excluded by `.graphifyignore` and `.gitignore` (`node_modules/`, `.venv/`, `dist/`, unrelated projects). On my
workspace that was 45,885 watches. `max_user_watches` is per user, and VS Code (12,669) plus another IDE (6,528)
were already using part of it, so the total came close to the 65,536 limit. Past that limit, `inotify_add_watch`
fails with ENOSPC, and editors stop seeing file changes too.

Possible approaches:

- schedule non-recursive watches only on directories that `ignored_predicate()` keeps (walking the tree with the same
  pruning that `detect()` uses), and add watches for newly created directories that are not ignored;
- or document the limitation and suggest `graphify update` from a timer/cron for large trees.

## Workaround in use

A systemd user timer running `graphify update .` every 10 minutes: AST only, no LLM, about 12–23 s per run on
23,000 nodes. It is reliable, but changes reach the graph only every 10 minutes.

title: Windows: stat index stores absolute keys again, breaking cache portability
body:
## Summary

On clean `v0.9.103` on Windows, `file_hash` writes an absolute key for a file inside the corpus to `graphify-out/cache/stat-index.json`. The index should use a root-relative key so it can be reused after the corpus is copied or moved. As a result, the copied index's entries still point at the old checkout and do not provide the intended cache hits in the new location.

This is a regression of the portability behavior addressed in #2199. The three existing portability tests listed below fail on the clean tag.

## Reproduction

Run from a clean checkout on Windows. This script creates the entire corpus and cache in a temporary directory:

```python
import json
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

from graphify import cache

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    root = Path(tmp) / "a"
    root.mkdir()
    source = root / "example.py"
    source.write_text("x = 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    old = time.time_ns() - 10_000_000_000
    os.utime(source, ns=(old, old))  # permit the stat fast path
    original_digest = cache.file_hash(source, root)
    cache._flush_stat_index()
    data = json.loads((root / "graphify-out/cache/stat-index.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    print("absolute key:", any(os.path.isabs(k) for k in data))
    print("relative key:", "example.py" in data)

    copy = Path(tmp) / "b"
    shutil.copytree(root, copy, copy_function=shutil.copy2)
    # Simulate a fresh process loading the copied index.
    cache._stat_index_root = None
    cache._stat_index_anchor = None
    cache._stat_index = {}
    cache._stat_index_dirty = False
    original_read = Path.read_bytes
    reads = []
    def counting(path):
        reads.append(path.name)
        return original_read(path)

    with patch.object(Path, "read_bytes", counting):
        copied_digest = cache.file_hash(copy / "example.py", copy)
    print("digests equal:", original_digest == copied_digest)
    print("source reads after copy:", reads.count("example.py"))
```

Observed on clean `v0.9.103`:

```text
absolute key: True
relative key: False
digests equal: True
source reads after copy: 1
```

On clean `v0.9.100`, the same script reports `absolute key: False`, `relative key: True`, `digests equal: True`, and `source reads after copy: 0`. The file is backdated and copied with metadata preserved so the warm stat-cache fast path is eligible. The digest remains correct in this example; the demonstrated regression is the extra content read after copying the corpus.

The existing upstream tests also reproduce it:

```text
python -m pytest tests/test_stat_index_portability.py -q
3 failed, 4 passed
```

The failures are `test_cache_hits_survive_corpus_move`, `test_deleted_entries_are_pruned_on_flush`, and `test_legacy_absolute_index_migrates_gracefully`. The latter two fail their relative-key assertions; this alone does not establish that deletion pruning is broken.

## Cause

`file_hash` passes a long-path-prefixed root to `_ensure_stat_index`, which stores it in `_stat_index_anchor`. The in-memory key is normalized separately and has no prefix. On the tested Windows setup, these are two spellings of the same location, for example anchor `\\?\C:\...\a` and key `C:\...\a\example.py`.

When `_flush_stat_index` passes them to `_stat_key_to_relative`, `os.path.relpath` raises `ValueError` because Windows treats `\\?\C:` and `C:` as different mounts. The exception handler leaves the key absolute, so the copied index retains the old path.

The same script was tested on the two adjacent commits: parent `5c4a8589` writes the relative key and performs zero source reads after copying; `99b8da78` writes the absolute key and performs one. Commit `99b8da78` changes `file_hash` to pass `root_src` through `_os_long_path` while normalizing the key separately. This identifies the observed regression without proposing a fix for other path forms.

## Environment

Windows 11, Python 3.12, clean `v0.9.103` checkout on a local NTFS volume.

title: Pending-queue test compares Windows paths with POSIX-only strings
body:
## Summary

On clean `v0.9.103` on Windows, `tests/test_update_lock_contention.py::test_i4_pending_full_and_pending_changes_keep_their_semantics` fails when comparing `str(Path(...))` with hardcoded forward-slash strings. The actual drained paths have Windows separators; the reproduced failure does not establish that queue semantics are wrong.

## Reproduction

The following script creates its own output directory and calls the same queue functions:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from graphify.watch import _drain_pending, _queue_pending

with TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    out = Path(tmp) / "out"
    out.mkdir()
    _queue_pending(out, [Path("/x/a.py"), Path("/x/a.py"), Path("/y/b.py")])
    actual = [str(p) for p in _drain_pending(out)]
    print("matches test's strings:", actual == ["/x/a.py", "/y/b.py"])
    print("after separator normalization:", [p.replace("\\", "/") for p in actual])
```

On Windows, the first comparison is `False` and the normalized list is `['/x/a.py', '/y/b.py']`. The existing upstream test also fails on the same assertion:

```text
python -m pytest tests/test_update_lock_contention.py::test_i4_pending_full_and_pending_changes_keep_their_semantics -q
1 failed
```

Expected: the test should compare platform-appropriate paths while continuing to verify ordering and deduplication.

## Environment

Windows 11, Python 3.12, clean `v0.9.103`. This report concerns the assertion, not the queue's behavior under real lock contention.

title: test: compare pending-queue paths as Path objects for Windows (#5039)
body:
## Summary
Fixes #5039.

`test_i4_pending_full_and_pending_changes_keep_their_semantics` compared drained paths with `str(p)` against hardcoded POSIX strings. On Windows, `_queue_pending` writes via `os.fspath`, so the round-tripped paths use backslashes and the assertion fails even though queue ordering/dedup is correct.

Compare `Path` objects instead so the check is separator-agnostic while still pinning order and deduplication.
